mula_pali: 1. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā mallesu viharati anupiyaṃ nāma anuppiyaṃ nāma (syā.) mallānaṃ nigamo. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya anupiyaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Atha kho bhagavato etadahosi – ‘‘atippago kho tāva anupiyāyaṃ anupiyaṃ (ka.) piṇḍāya carituṃ. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ yena bhaggavagottassa paribbājakassa ārāmo, yena bhaggavagotto paribbājako tenupasaṅkameyya’’nti.
mula_english:
1. Thus have I heard.

Once, the Blessed One (bhagavān) was staying among the Mallas in a Malla town called Anupiya (anupiyaṃ nāma mallānaṃ nigamo).

Then, in the morning, having dressed and taken his bowl and robe, the Blessed One entered Anupiya for alms (piṇḍāya pāvisi).

Then the Blessed One thought: "It is still too early to walk for alms in Anupiya (anupiyāyaṃ piṇḍāya carituṃ)."

"Suppose I were to visit the hermitage of the wanderer Bhaggava-gotta (bhaggavagottassa paribbājakassa ārāmo), or rather, visit the wanderer Bhaggava-gotta himself (bhaggavagotto paribbājako)?"
commentary_pali: 1.Evaṃme sutaṃ…pe… mallesu viharatīti pāthikasuttaṃ. Tatrāyaṃ apubbapadavaṇṇanā. Mallesu viharatīti mallā nāma jānapadino rājakumārā, tesaṃ nivāso ekopi janapado ruḷhīsaddena ‘‘mallā’’ti vuccati, tasmiṃ mallesu janapade. ‘‘Anupiyaṃ nāma mallānaṃ nigamo’’ti anupiyanti evaṃnāmako mallānaṃ janapadassa eko nigamo, taṃ gocaragāmaṃ katvā ekasmiṃ chāyūdakasampanne vanasaṇḍe viharatīti attho. Anopiyantipi pāṭho. Pāvisīti paviṭṭho. Bhagavā pana na tāva paviṭṭho, pavisissāmīti nikkhantattā pana pāvisīti vutto. Yathā kiṃ, yathā ‘‘gāmaṃ gamissāmī’’ti nikkhanto puriso taṃ gāmaṃ apattopi ‘‘kuhiṃ itthannāmo’’ti vutte ‘‘gāmaṃ gato’’ti vuccati, evaṃ. Etadahosīti gāmasamīpe ṭhatvā sūriyaṃ olokentassa etadahosi. Atippago khoti ativiya pago kho, na tāva kulesu yāgubhattaṃ niṭṭhitanti. Kiṃ pana bhagavā kālaṃ ajānitvā nikkhantoti? Na ajānitvā. Paccūsakāleyeva hi bhagavā ñāṇajālaṃ pattharitvā lokaṃ volokento ñāṇajālassa anto paviṭṭhaṃ bhaggavagottaṃ channaparibbājakaṃ disvā ‘‘ajjāhaṃ imassa paribbājakassa mayā pubbe katakāraṇaṃ samāharitvā dhammaṃ kathessāmi, sā dhammakathā assa mayi pasādappaṭilābhavasena saphalā bhavissatī’’ti ñatvāva paribbājakārāmaṃ pavisitukāmo atippagova nikkhami. Tasmā tattha pavisitukāmatāya evaṃ cittaṃ uppādesi.
commentary_english:
1. Thus it was heard by me…pe… he was dwelling among the Mallas, this is the Pāthika Sutta. Herein is an explanation of the *apubbapadavaṇṇanā*.

*Mallesu viharati* means: *Mallā* were the name of royal princes of the country. Their residence, even a single district, is called *Mallā* by convention, in that *Mallā* district.

"*Anupiyaṃ nāma mallānaṃ nigamo*" means: *Anupiya* is the name of a market town of the Mallas' country. Having made that a pasture village, he was dwelling in a certain grove endowed with shade and water, is the meaning. *Anopiyaṃ* is also a reading.

*Pāvisī* means: he entered. But the Blessed One had not yet entered; he was said to have entered because he had departed intending to enter. How is it? Just as a man who has set out, saying, "I will go to the village," is said to have "gone to the village" even if he has not reached that village when asked, "Where is so-and-so?". Thus it is.

*Etadahosī* means: while standing near the village and looking at the sun, this thought occurred to him.

*Atippago kho* means: it is very early, the rice gruel meal is not yet finished in the families.

But did the Blessed One set out without knowing the time? No, not without knowing. For in the early morning, the Blessed One, having spread the net of knowledge, surveyed the world. Seeing Bhaggava Gotra, the hidden wanderer, enter within the net of knowledge, he thought, "Today, having gathered the cause formerly made by me for this wanderer, I will preach the Dharma. That Dharma talk will be fruitful for him because of gaining faith in me," and knowing thus, intending to enter the wanderer's park, he set out very early. Therefore, because of the desire to enter there, he produced such a thought.

mula_pali: 2. Atha kho bhagavā yena bhaggavagottassa paribbājakassa ārāmo, yena bhaggavagotto paribbājako tenupasaṅkami. Atha kho bhaggavagotto paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘etu kho, bhante, bhagavā. Svāgataṃ, bhante, bhagavato. Cirassaṃ kho, bhante, bhagavā imaṃ pariyāyamakāsi yadidaṃ idhāgamanāya. Nisīdatu, bhante, bhagavā, idamāsanaṃ paññatta’’nti. Nisīdi bhagavā paññatte āsane. Bhaggavagottopi kho paribbājako aññataraṃ nīcaṃ āsanaṃ gahetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho bhaggavagotto paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘purimāni, bhante, divasāni purimatarāni sunakkhatto licchaviputto yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā maṃ etadavoca – ‘paccakkhāto dāni mayā, bhaggava, bhagavā. Na dānāhaṃ bhagavantaṃ uddissa viharāmī’ti. Kaccetaṃ, bhante, tatheva, yathā sunakkhatto licchaviputto avacā’’ti? ‘‘Tatheva kho etaṃ, bhaggava, yathā sunakkhatto licchaviputto avaca’’.
mula_english:
2. Then the Blessed One went to the hermitage of the wanderer Bhaggava-gotta, and approached the wanderer Bhaggava-gotta.

Then the wanderer Bhaggava-gotta said this to the Blessed One: "Come, Blessed Lord. Welcome, Blessed Lord! It has been long, Blessed One, since you arranged to come here. Be seated, Blessed One, this seat is prepared."

The Blessed One sat down on the prepared seat.

The wanderer Bhaggava-gotta also took a low seat, sat down on one side.

Sitting to one side, the wanderer Bhaggava-gotta said this to the Blessed One: "Some days ago Sunakkhatta the Licchavi came to me and said: 'Bhaggava, I have renounced the Blessed One. I am no longer under the Lord’s rule.'"

"Is that as it is, venerable sir, just as Sunakkhatta the Licchavi said?" "It is just as Sunakkhatta the Licchavi said, Bhaggava."
commentary_pali: 2.Etadavocāti bhagavantaṃ disvā mānathaddhataṃ akatvā satthāraṃ paccuggantvā etaṃ etu kho, bhantetiādikaṃ vacanaṃ avoca. Imaṃ pariyāyanti imaṃ vāraṃ, ajja imaṃ āgamanavāranti attho. Kiṃ pana bhagavā pubbepi tattha gatapubboti? Na gatapubbo, lokasamudācāravasena pana evamāha. Lokiyā hi cirassaṃ āgatampi anāgatapubbampi manāpajātikaṃ āgataṃ disvā ‘‘kuto bhavaṃ āgato, cirassaṃ bhavaṃ āgato, kathaṃ te idhāgamanamaggo ñāto, kiṃ maggamūḷhosī’’tiādīni vadanti. Tasmā ayampi lokasamudācāravasena evamāhāti veditabbo. Idamāsananti attano nisinnāsanaṃ papphoṭetvā sampādetvā dadamāno evamāha. Sunakkhatto licchaviputtoti sunakkhatto nāma licchavirājaputto. So kira tassa gihisahāyo hoti, kālena kālaṃ tassa santikaṃ gacchati. Paccakkhātoti ‘‘paccakkhāmi dānāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ na dānāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ uddissa viharissāmī’’ti evaṃ paṭiakkhāto nissaṭṭho pariccatto.
commentary_english:
2. " *Etadavocā* ti": Having seen the Blessed One, without making a show of pride, having gone to greet the teacher ( *satthāraṃ*), he spoke these words beginning with "*etu kho, bhante*."
"*Imaṃ pariyāya*nti": This turn ( *vāraṃ*), today is the turn for arrival ( *āgamanavāraṃ*), this is the meaning.
What, was the Blessed One there before? No, he was not there before; however, he spoke thus according to worldly custom ( *lokasamudācāravasena*).
For worldly people ( *lokiyā*) having seen an agreeable person who has arrived after a long time or who has not arrived before say, "From where have you come, you have come after a long time, how was the path to here known by you, have you lost your way?" and so on.
Therefore, he also spoke thus according to worldly custom; this should be understood.
"*Idamāsana*nti": Having prepared and offered his own sitting place ( *nisinnāsanaṃ*), he spoke thus.
"*Sunakkhatto licchaviputto*ti": Sunakkhatta was the name of the Licchavi prince ( *licchavirājaputto*).
It seems he was a householder friend ( *gihisahāyo*) of his; he goes to his presence from time to time.
"*Paccakkhāto*ti": "I reject ( *paccakkhāmi*) giving, venerable sir, to the Blessed One; I will live intending the Blessed One" - thus, he was rejected ( *paṭiakkhāto*), cast out ( *nissaṭṭho*), abandoned ( *pariccatto*).

mula_pali: 3. Purimāni, bhaggava, divasāni purimatarāni sunakkhatto licchaviputto yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā maṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho, bhaggava, sunakkhatto licchaviputto maṃ etadavoca – ‘paccakkhāmi dānāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ. Na dānāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ uddissa viharissāmī’ti. ‘Evaṃ vutte, ahaṃ, bhaggava, sunakkhattaṃ licchaviputtaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘api nu tāhaṃ, sunakkhatta, evaṃ avacaṃ, ehi tvaṃ, sunakkhatta, mamaṃ uddissa viharāhī’ti? ‘No hetaṃ, bhante’. ‘Tvaṃ vā pana maṃ evaṃ avaca – ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ uddissa viharissāmī’ti? ‘No hetaṃ, bhante’. ‘Iti kira, sunakkhatta, nevāhaṃ taṃ vadāmi – ehi tvaṃ, sunakkhatta, mamaṃ uddissa viharāhīti. Napi kira maṃ tvaṃ vadesi – ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ uddissa viharissāmīti. Evaṃ sante, moghapurisa, ko santo kaṃ paccācikkhasi? Passa, moghapurisa, yāvañca yāva ca (ka.) te idaṃ aparaddha’nti.
mula_english:
3.  “Bhaggava, a few days ago, Sunakkhatta the Licchavi came to me, saluted me, and sat down to one side.

Sitting to one side, Bhaggava, Sunakkhatta the Licchavi said this to me: ‘I renounce the Blessed One, Bhante (venerable sir).

And I will no longer live under the authority of the Blessed One, Bhante.’

“When this was said, I said this to Sunakkhatta the Licchavi: ‘Sunakkhatta, did I ever say to you, "Come, Sunakkhatta, live under my authority?"’ ‘No, Bhante.’

“Or did you ever say this to me: ‘I will live under the authority of the Blessed One, Bhante’?” ‘No, Bhante.’

“So, Sunakkhatta, I never said to you, ‘Come, Sunakkhatta, live under my authority.’

And you never said to me, ‘I will live under the authority of the Blessed One, Bhante.’

This being so, foolish man, who are you renouncing? Look, foolish man, how much wrong (*aparaddha*) has been done by you.”
commentary_pali: 3.Bhagavantaṃ uddissāti bhagavā me satthā ‘‘bhagavato ahaṃ ovādaṃ paṭikaromī’’ti evaṃ apadisitvā. Ko santo kaṃ paccācikkhasīti yācako vā yācitakaṃ paccācikkheyya, yācitako vā yācakaṃ. Tvaṃ pana neva yācako na yācitako, evaṃ sante, moghapurisa, ko santo ko samāno kaṃ paccācikkhasīti dasseti. Passa moghapurisāti passa tucchapurisa. Yāvañca te idaṃ aparaddhanti yattakaṃ idaṃ tava aparaddhaṃ, yattako te aparādho tattako dosoti evāhaṃ bhaggava tassa dosaṃ āropesinti dasseti.
commentary_english:
3. *bhagavantaṃ uddissā* means "Bhagavān is my teacher; thus, having indicated, 'I will follow the advice of the Bhagavān.'"

*ko santo kaṃ paccācikkhasī* means, "Should a beggar refuse a borrowed object, or should a borrower refuse a beggar?"

It indicates, "You are neither a beggar nor a borrower; thus, foolish man, who are you to refuse someone?"

*passa moghapurisā* means "See, foolish man."

*yāvañca te idaṃ aparaddha* means, "However much this is your fault, Bhaggava, to that extent I will attribute blame to him."

mula_pali: 4. ‘Na hi pana me, bhante, bhagavā uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ karotī’ti. ‘Api nu tāhaṃ, sunakkhatta, evaṃ avacaṃ – ehi tvaṃ, sunakkhatta, mamaṃ uddissa viharāhi, ahaṃ te uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ karissāmī’ti? ‘No hetaṃ, bhante’. ‘Tvaṃ vā pana maṃ evaṃ avaca – ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ uddissa viharissāmi, bhagavā me uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ karissatī’ti? ‘No hetaṃ, bhante’. ‘Iti kira, sunakkhatta, nevāhaṃ taṃ vadāmi – ehi tvaṃ, sunakkhatta, mamaṃ uddissa viharāhi, ahaṃ te uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ karissāmī’ti; napi kira maṃ tvaṃ vadesi – ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ uddissa viharissāmi, bhagavā me uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ karissatī’ti. Evaṃ sante, moghapurisa , ko santo kaṃ paccācikkhasi? Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, sunakkhatta, kate vā uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriye akate vā uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriye yassatthāya mayā dhammo desito so niyyāti takkarassa sammā dukkhakkhayāyā’ti? ‘Kate vā, bhante, uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriye akate vā uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriye yassatthāya bhagavatā dhammo desito so niyyāti takkarassa sammā dukkhakkhayāyā’ti. ‘Iti kira, sunakkhatta, kate vā uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriye, akate vā uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriye, yassatthāya mayā dhammo desito, so niyyāti takkarassa sammā dukkhakkhayāya. Tatra, sunakkhatta, kiṃ uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ kataṃ karissati? Passa, moghapurisa, yāvañca te idaṃ aparaddha’nti.
mula_english:
4. ”Well, Lord *bhante*, the Blessed One *bhagavā* does not perform superhuman *uttarimanussa* marvels *iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ*.”

“And did I ever say to you: ‘Come under my rule, Sunakkhatta, and I will perform superhuman *uttarimanussa* marvels *iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ* for you?’” “No, Lord *bhante*.”

“Or did you ever say to me: ‘Lord *bhante*, I will be under your rule if you will perform superhuman *uttarimanussa* marvels *iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ* for me?’” “No, Lord *bhante*.”

“Then it appears, Sunakkhatta, that I made no such promises – ‘Come under my rule, Sunakkhatta, and I will perform superhuman *uttarimanussa* marvels *iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ* for you’ – and you made no such conditions – ‘Lord *bhante*, I will be under your rule if you will perform superhuman *uttarimanussa* marvels *iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ* for me.’”

“That being the case, foolish man *moghapurisa*, who are you contradicting? What do you think, Sunakkhatta, whether superhuman *uttarimanussa* marvels *iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ* are performed or not, the Dharma *dhamma* I have taught leads whoever practices it to the total destruction of suffering *dukkhakkhayāya*.” “Whether superhuman *uttarimanussa* marvels *iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ* are performed or not, Lord *bhante*, the Dharma *dhamma* the Blessed One *bhagavatā* has taught leads whoever practices it to the total destruction of suffering *dukkhakkhayāya*.”

“So, Sunakkhatta, whether superhuman *uttarimanussa* marvels *iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ* are performed or not, the Dharma *dhamma* I have taught, leads whoever practises it to the total destruction of suffering *dukkhakkhayāya*.

Then what purpose would the performance of superhuman *uttarimanussa* marvels *iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ* serve? Look, foolish man *moghapurisa*, how far you have gone wrong!”
commentary_pali: 4.Uttarimanussadhammāti pañcasīladasasīlasaṅkhātā manussadhammāuttari. Iddhipāṭihāriyanti iddhibhūtaṃ pāṭihāriyaṃ. Kate vāti katamhi vā. Yassatthāyāti yassa dukkhakkhayassa atthāya. Soniyyāti takkarassāti so dhammo takkarassa yathā mayā dhammo desito, tathā kārakassa sammā paṭipannassa puggalassa sabbavaṭṭadukkhakkhayāya amatanibbānasacchikiriyāya gacchati, na gacchati, saṃvattati, na saṃvattatīti pucchati. Tatra sunakkhattāti tasmiṃ sunakkhatta mayā desite dhamme takkarassa sammā dukkhakkhayāya saṃvattamāne kiṃ uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ kataṃ karissati, ko tena katena attho. Tasmiñhi katepi akatepi mama sāsanassa parihāni natthi, devamanussānañhi amatanibbānasampāpanatthāya ahaṃ pāramiyo pūresiṃ, na pāṭihāriyakaraṇatthāyāti pāṭihāriyassa niratthakataṃ dassetvā ‘‘passa, moghapurisā’’ti dutiyaṃ dosaṃ āropesi.
commentary_english:
4. *Uttarimanussadhammā*: *manussa-dhammā* that are superior, enumerated as the five precepts and the ten precepts.

*Iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ*: miraculous power (*iddhi*) is a miracle (*pāṭihāriyaṃ*).

*Kate vā*: or in which one?

*Yassatthāyā*: for the sake of the cessation of which suffering?

*So niyyāti takkarassā*: that *dhamma*, just as the *dhamma* has been taught by me, goes for the sake of the cessation of all rounds of suffering, for the realization of deathless liberation (*amatanibbānasacchikiriyāya*) for the individual who is properly practicing it, to the one who does it (*kārakassa*). Does it go, does it not go, does it lead, does it not lead, he asks.

*Tatra sunakkhattā*: In that *dhamma* taught by me, Sunakkhatta, while it leads to the proper cessation of suffering for the one who does it, what superior human qualities (*uttarimanussadhammā*) or miracle of power (*iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ*) has been done or will be done, what is the purpose with that having been done?

Indeed, whether that has been done or not done, there is no decline of my teaching (*sāsana*). For the sake of leading gods and humans to deathless liberation (*amatanibbānasampāpanatthāya*), I have fulfilled the perfections (*pāramiyo*), not for the sake of doing miracles (*pāṭihāriyakaraṇatthāya*), thus having shown the meaninglessness of miracles, he imputed a second fault, saying, "Look, foolish men!"

mula_pali: 5. ‘Na hi pana me, bhante, bhagavā aggaññaṃ paññapetī’ti paññāpetīti (pī.)? ‘Api nu tāhaṃ, sunakkhatta, evaṃ avacaṃ – ehi tvaṃ, sunakkhatta, mamaṃ uddissa viharāhi, ahaṃ te aggaññaṃ paññapessāmī’ti? ‘No hetaṃ, bhante’. ‘Tvaṃ vā pana maṃ evaṃ avaca – ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ uddissa viharissāmi, bhagavā me aggaññaṃ paññapessatī’ti? ‘No hetaṃ, bhante’. ‘Iti kira, sunakkhatta, nevāhaṃ taṃ vadāmi – ehi tvaṃ, sunakkhatta, mamaṃ uddissa viharāhi, ahaṃ te aggaññaṃ paññapessāmīti. Napi kira maṃ tvaṃ vadesi – ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ uddissa viharissāmi, bhagavā me aggaññaṃ paññapessatī’ti. Evaṃ sante, moghapurisa, ko santo kaṃ paccācikkhasi? Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, sunakkhatta, paññatte vā aggaññe, apaññatte vā aggaññe, yassatthāya mayā dhammo desito, so niyyāti takkarassa sammā dukkhakkhayāyā’ti? ‘Paññatte vā, bhante, aggaññe, apaññatte vā aggaññe, yassatthāya bhagavatā dhammo desito, so niyyāti takkarassa sammā dukkhakkhayāyā’ti. ‘Iti kira, sunakkhatta, paññatte vā aggaññe, apaññatte vā aggaññe, yassatthāya mayā dhammo desito, so niyyāti takkarassa sammā dukkhakkhayāya. Tatra, sunakkhatta, kiṃ aggaññaṃ paññattaṃ karissati? Passa, moghapurisa, yāvañca te idaṃ aparaddhaṃ’.
mula_english:
5. ‘But surely, venerable, the Blessed One does not teach about the origin (aggaññaṃ paññapetī)’? ‘And did I ever say to you, Sunakkhatta: “Come, Sunakkhatta, live under my guidance, and I will teach you about the origin (aggaññaṃ paññapessāmī)?”’ ‘No, venerable.’

‘Or did you ever say to me: “Venerable, I will live under the Blessed One’s guidance, and the Blessed One will teach me about the origin (aggaññaṃ paññapessatī)?”’ ‘No, venerable.’

‘Then, Sunakkhatta, it seems that neither did I say to you: “Come, Sunakkhatta, live under my guidance, and I will teach you about the origin (aggaññaṃ paññapessāmīti)," nor did you say to me: “Venerable, I will live under the Blessed One’s guidance, and the Blessed One will teach me about the origin (aggaññaṃ paññapessatī).”’

Such being the case, foolish man (moghapurisa), who are you to renounce what? What do you think, Sunakkhatta, whether the origin (aggaññe) is taught or not taught (apaññatte vā aggaññe), the Dhamma I teach leads one who practices it rightly to the complete destruction of suffering (dukkhakkhayāyā)’? ‘Whether the origin (aggaññe) is taught or not taught (apaññatte vā aggaññe), venerable, the Dhamma taught by the Blessed One leads one who practices it rightly to the complete destruction of suffering (dukkhakkhayāyā).’

‘Then, Sunakkhatta, whether the origin (aggaññe) is taught or not taught (apaññatte vā aggaññe), the Dhamma I teach leads one who practices it rightly to the complete destruction of suffering (dukkhakkhayāya).

So what origin (aggaññaṃ) will be taught? Look, foolish man (moghapurisa), how very wrong you are!’
commentary_pali: 5.Aggaññanti lokapaññattiṃ. ‘‘Idaṃ nāma lokassa agga’’nti evaṃ jānitabbampi aggaṃ mariyādaṃ na taṃ paññapetīti vadati. Sesamettha anantaravādānusāreneva veditabbaṃ.
commentary_english: 5. aggaññanti lokapaññattiṃ. It is a designation of the world called *aggañña*. ‘‘idaṃ nāma lokassa agga’’nti evaṃ jānitabbampi aggaṃ mariyādaṃ na taṃ paññapetīti vadati. Saying "this is called the highest in the world," one does not make known the limit ( *maryādā*) of what should be known in this way. sesamettha anantaravādānusāreneva veditabbaṃ. The rest should be understood according to the immediately preceding statement.

mula_pali:
6. ‘Anekapariyāyena kho te, sunakkhatta, mama vaṇṇo bhāsito vajjigāme – itipi so bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavāti. Iti kho te, sunakkhatta, anekapariyāyena mama vaṇṇo bhāsito vajjigāme.

‘Anekapariyāyena kho te, sunakkhatta, dhammassa vaṇṇo bhāsito vajjigāme – svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo sandiṭṭhiko akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṃ veditabbo viññūhīti. Iti kho te, sunakkhatta, anekapariyāyena dhammassa vaṇṇo bhāsito vajjigāme.

‘Anekapariyāyena kho te, sunakkhatta, saṅghassa vaṇṇo bhāsito vajjigāme – suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, ujuppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, ñāyappaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, sāmīcippaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, yadidaṃ cattāri purisayugāni aṭṭha purisapuggalā, esa bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, āhuneyyo pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ lokassāti. Iti kho te, sunakkhatta, anekapariyāyena saṅghassa vaṇṇo bhāsito vajjigāme.

‘Ārocayāmi kho te, sunakkhatta, paṭivedayāmi kho te, sunakkhatta. Bhavissanti kho te, sunakkhatta, vattāro, no visahi sunakkhatto licchaviputto samaṇe gotame brahmacariyaṃ carituṃ, so avisahanto sikkhaṃ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattoti. Iti kho te, sunakkhatta, bhavissanti vattāro’ti.

Evaṃ pi kho, bhaggava, sunakkhatto licchaviputto mayā vuccamāno apakkameva imasmā dhammavinayā, yathā taṃ āpāyiko nerayiko.

Korakkhattiyavatthu
mula_english:
6. “Sunakkhatta, in many ways you have spoken in praise of me among the Vajjis, saying: ‘Indeed, the Blessed One is an *arhat*, a fully enlightened Buddha, endowed with knowledge and conduct, the Well-Farer, knower of the worlds, incomparable leader of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, enlightened, blessed.’ In these ways, Sunakkhatta, you have spoken in praise of me among the Vajjis.

‘Sunakkhatta, in many ways you have spoken in praise of the *dharma*, saying: ‘Well-proclaimed by the Blessed One is the *dharma*, visible here and now, timeless, inviting inspection, leading onward, to be realized by the wise, each one for himself.’ In these ways, Sunakkhatta, you have spoken in praise of the *dharma* among the Vajjis.

‘Sunakkhatta, in many ways you have spoken in praise of the *saṃgha*, saying: ‘Well-trained is the order of the Lord’s disciples, trained in uprightness, methodically trained, excellently trained is the order of the Lord’s disciples, that is, the four pairs of men, the eight classes of individuals. This is the order of the Lord’s disciples, worthy of respect, worthy of homage, worthy of gifts, worthy of salutation, an unsurpassed field in the world for merit.’ In these ways, Sunakkhatta, you have spoken in praise of the *saṃgha* among the Vajjis.

‘I declare to you, Sunakkhatta, I make known to you, Sunakkhatta, there will be those who will say: ‘Sunakkhatta the Licchavi was unable to maintain the holy life (*brahmacariya*) under the ascetic Gotama, and being thus unable he abandoned the training (*śikṣā*) and reverted to a base life.’ That, Sunakkhatta, is what they will say.

Even so, Bhaggava, Sunakkhatta the Licchavi, when spoken to by me, simply departed from this *dharma* and discipline (*vinaya*), like one condemned to hell.

The Korakkhattiya Account
commentary_pali:
6.Anekapariyāyena khoti idaṃ kasmā āraddhaṃ. Sunakkhatto kira ‘‘bhagavato guṇaṃ makkhessāmi, ‘‘dosaṃ paññapessāmī’’ti ettakaṃ vippalapitvā bhagavato kathaṃ suṇanto appatiṭṭho niravo aṭṭhāsi.

Atha bhagavā – ‘‘sunakkhatta, evaṃ tvaṃ makkhibhāve ṭhito sayameva garahaṃ pāpuṇissasī’’ti makkhibhāve ādīnavadassanatthaṃ anekapariyāyenātiādimāha. Tattha anekapariyāyenāti anekakāraṇena. Vajjigāmeti vajjirājānaṃ gāme, vesālīnagare no visahīti nāsakkhi. So avisahantoti so sunakkhatto yassa pubbe tiṇṇaṃ ratanānaṃ vaṇṇaṃ kathentassa mukhaṃ nappahoti, so dāni teneva mukhena avaṇṇaṃ katheti, addhā avisahanto asakkonto brahmacariyaṃ carituṃ attano bālatāya avaṇṇaṃ kathetvā hīnāyāvatto. Buddho pana subuddhova, dhammo svākkhātova, saṅgho suppaṭipannova. Evaṃ tīṇi ratanāni thomentā manussā tuyheva dosaṃ dassessantīti. Iti kho teti evaṃ kho te, sunakkhatta, vattāro bhavissanti. Tato evaṃ dose uppanne satthā atītānāgate appaṭihatañāṇo, mayhaṃ evaṃ doso uppajjissatīti jānantopi puretaraṃ na kathesīti vattuṃ na lacchasīti dasseti. Apakkamevāti apakkamiyeva, apakkanto vā cutoti attho. Yathātaṃ āpāyikoti yathā apāye nibbattanāraho satto apakkameyya, evameva apakkamīti attho.

anekapariyāyenā anekapariyāyenā Vajjigāme no visahī So avisahanto Iti kho te Apakkamevā Yathā taṃ āpāyiko

commentary_english:
6.  Why was this begun by saying "<hi rend="bold">anekapariyāyena kho</hi> ti"? Sunakkhatta, after rambling on to this extent, "I will disparage the Blessed One's virtues, I will point out his faults," stood there distressed, without support, and without shelter while listening to the Blessed One's teaching.

 Then the Blessed One said, "Sunakkhatta, in this way, remaining in a state of disparagement, you will only incur blame yourself." To show the danger in disparagement, he began with "<hi rend="bold">anekapariyāyenā</hi> ti," and so on.

 There, <hi rend="bold">anekapariyāyenā</hi> ti means with many reasons (anekakāraṇena).

 <hi rend="bold">Vajjigāme</hi> ti means in the village of the Vajji kings; in the city of Vesālī, <hi rend="bold">no visahī</hi> ti means he was not able (nāsakkhi).

 <hi rend="bold">So avisahanto</hi> ti means that Sunakkhatta, whose mouth was previously insufficient to describe the virtues of the three jewels ( tiṇṇaṃ ratanānaṃ), now speaks disparagingly with that very mouth. Indeed, being unable to practice the holy life (brahmacariyaṃ carituṃ), he has regressed to a lower state, having spoken disparagingly due to his own foolishness (bālatāya avaṇṇaṃ kathetvā hīnāyāvatto).

 The Buddha, however, is well-awakened (subuddhova), the Dharma is well-proclaimed (svākkhātova), and the Saṅgha is well-practiced (suppaṭipannova).

 Thus, people praising the three jewels will only show your faults (tuyheva dosaṃ dassessantīti).

 <hi rend="bold">Iti kho te</hi> ti means in this way, Sunakkhatta, they will be speakers (vattāro bhavissanti).

 Therefore, when such a fault arises, the Teacher, whose knowledge is unobstructed in the past and future (atītānāgate appaṭihatañāṇo), shows that you will not be able to say, "Even though he knew that such a fault would arise in me, he did not speak beforehand (puretaraṃ na kathesīti)."

 <hi rend="bold">Apakkamevā</hi> ti, having departed, or the meaning is: "having fallen away" (cuto ti attho).

 <hi rend="bold">Yathā</hi> <hi rend="bold">taṃ āpāyiko</hi> ti, just as a being worthy of being born in the lower realms (apāye nibbattanāraho satto) would depart (apakkameyya), so too, he departed (evameva apakkamīti attho).

7. ‘‘Ekamidāhaṃ, bhaggava, samayaṃ thūlūsu bumūsu (sī. pī.) viharāmi uttarakā nāma thūlūnaṃ nigamo. Atha khvāhaṃ, bhaggava, pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sunakkhattena licchaviputtena pacchāsamaṇena uttarakaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisiṃ. Tena kho pana samayena acelo korakkhattiyo kukkuravatiko catukkuṇḍiko catukuṇḍiko (sī. pī.) catukoṇḍiko (syā. ka.) chamānikiṇṇaṃ bhakkhasaṃ mukheneva khādati, mukheneva bhuñjati. Addasā kho, bhaggava, sunakkhatto licchaviputto acelaṃ korakkhattiyaṃ kukkuravatikaṃ catukkuṇḍikaṃ chamānikiṇṇaṃ bhakkhasaṃ mukheneva khādantaṃ mukheneva bhuñjantaṃ. Disvānassa etadahosi – ‘sādhurūpo vata, bho, ayaṃ arahaṃ (sī. syā. pī.) samaṇo catukkuṇḍiko chamānikiṇṇaṃ bhakkhasaṃ mukheneva khādati, mukheneva bhuñjatī’ti.

‘‘Atha khvāhaṃ, bhaggava, sunakkhattassa licchaviputtassa cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya sunakkhattaṃ licchaviputtaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘tvampi nāma, moghapurisa, samaṇo sakyaputtiyo moghapurisa sakyaputtiyo (sī. syā. pī.) paṭijānissasī’ti! ‘Kiṃ pana maṃ, bhante, bhagavā evamāha – ‘tvampi nāma, moghapurisa, samaṇo sakyaputtiyo moghapurisa sakyaputtiyo (sī. syā. pī.) paṭijānissasī’ti? ‘Nanu te, sunakkhatta, imaṃ acelaṃ korakkhattiyaṃ kukkuravatikaṃ catukkuṇḍikaṃ chamānikiṇṇaṃ bhakkhasaṃ mukheneva khādantaṃ mukheneva bhuñjantaṃ disvāna etadahosi – sādhurūpo vata, bho, ayaṃ samaṇo catukkuṇḍiko chamānikiṇṇaṃ bhakkhasaṃ mukheneva khādati, mukheneva bhuñjatī’ti? ‘Evaṃ, bhante. Kiṃ pana, bhante, bhagavā arahattassa maccharāyatī’ti? ‘Na kho ahaṃ, moghapurisa, arahattassa maccharāyāmi. Api ca, tuyhevetaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ, taṃ pajaha. Mā te ahosi dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāya. Yaṃ kho panetaṃ, sunakkhatta, maññasi acelaṃ korakkhattiyaṃ – sādhurūpo ayaṃ samaṇoti maññasi ‘‘acelo korakhattiyo sādhurūpo arahaṃ samaṇoti’’ (syā.). So sattamaṃ divasaṃ alasakena kālaṅkarissati. Kālaṅkato kālakato (sī. syā. pī.) ca kālakañcikā kālakañjā (sī. pī.), kālakañjikā (syā.) nāma asurā sabbanihīno asurakāyo, tatra upapajjissati. Kālaṅkatañca naṃ bīraṇatthambake susāne chaḍḍessanti. Ākaṅkhamāno ca tvaṃ, sunakkhatta, acelaṃ korakkhattiyaṃ upasaṅkamitvā puccheyyāsi – jānāsi, āvuso korakkhattiya acela korakhattiya (ka.), attano gatinti? Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, sunakkhatta, vijjati yaṃ te acelo korakkhattiyo byākarissati – jānāmi, āvuso sunakkhatta, attano gatiṃ; kālakañcikā nāma asurā sabbanihīno asurakāyo, tatrāmhi upapannoti.

moghapurisa sakyaputtiyo (sī. syā. pī.) moghapurisa sakyaputtiyo (sī. syā. pī.) maññasi ‘‘acelo korakhattiyo sādhurūpo arahaṃ samaṇoti’’ (syā.) kālakato (sī. syā. pī.) kālakañjā (sī. pī.), kālakañjikā (syā.) acela korakhattiya (ka.)

‘‘Atha kho, bhaggava, sunakkhatto licchaviputto yena acelo korakkhattiyo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā acelaṃ korakkhattiyaṃ etadavoca – ‘byākato khosi, āvuso korakkhattiya, samaṇena gotamena – acelo korakkhattiyo sattamaṃ divasaṃ alasakena kālaṅkarissati. Kālaṅkato ca kālakañcikā nāma asurā sabbanihīno asurakāyo , tatra upapajjissati. Kālaṅkatañca naṃ bīraṇatthambake susāne chaḍḍessantī’ti. Yena tvaṃ, āvuso korakkhattiya, mattaṃ mattañca bhattaṃ bhuñjeyyāsi, mattaṃ mattañca pānīyaṃ piveyyāsi. Yathā samaṇassa gotamassa micchā assa vacana’nti.
mula_english:
7. ‘Once, Bhaggava, I was staying among the Thūlūs at a place called Uttaraka, a town of theirs.

In the early morning I went with robe and bowl into Uttaraka for alms, with Sunakkhatta of the Licchavis as my attendant.

And at that time the naked ascetic Korakkhattiya the "dog-man" was going round on all fours, sprawling on the ground, and chewing and eating his food with his mouth alone.

Sunakkhatta of the Licchavis saw the naked ascetic Korakkhattiya the "dog-man" going round on all fours, sprawling on the ground, and chewing and eating his food with his mouth alone.

Sunakkhatta thought: “Now that is a real *śramaṇa*, who goes round on all fours, sprawling on the ground, and chewing and eating his food with his mouth alone."

Then I, Bhaggava, knowing with my mind the thoughts in the mind of Sunakkhatta of the Licchavis, said to Sunakkhatta of the Licchavis: ‘So you too, misguided man, claim to be a *śramaṇa*, a follower of the Śākyas!’ ‘But why, lord, does the Blessed One say this to me: “So you too, misguided man, claim to be a *śramaṇa*, a follower of the Śākyas?" ’ ‘Sunakkhatta, did you not, on seeing that naked ascetic Korakkhattiya the "dog-man" going around on all fours, think: "Now that is a real *śramaṇa*, who goes round on all fours, sprawling on the ground, and chewing and eating his food with his mouth alone?" ’ ‘Yes, lord.

But why, lord, is the Blessed One jealous of *arhat*-ship?’ ‘I am not jealous of *arhat*-ship, misguided man.

However, this evil view has arisen in you. Abandon it, lest it should be to your harm and sorrow for a long time!

That naked ascetic Korakkhattiya whom you think is a real *śramaṇa*—he will die in seven days from indigestion.

And when he is dead he will reappear among the Kālakañjika *asuras*, who are the very lowest grade of *asuras*. And his body will be cast aside on a heap of *bīraṇa*-grass in the charnel-ground.
If you want to, Sunakkhatta, you can go to the naked ascetic Korakkhattiya, approach him and ask: ‘Do you know, friend Korakkhattiya, your destiny?’ And it is possible, Sunakkhatta, that the naked ascetic Korakkhattiya will explain to you: ‘I know, friend Sunakkhatta, my destiny. I have been reborn among the *Kālakañjika* demons (*asura*), the very lowest order of demons; that is where I have arisen.’

Then, Bhaggava, Sunakkhatta the Licchavi would approach the naked ascetic Korakkhattiya, and having approached, he would say this to the naked ascetic Korakkhattiya: ‘Friend Korakkhattiya, you have been declared by the ascetic Gotama: “The naked ascetic Korakkhattiya will die in seven days due to indigestion. And having died, he will be reborn among the *Kālakañjika* demons (*asura*), the very lowest order of demons; that is where he will arise. And after death, they will throw him onto a heap of *bīraṇa* grass in the charnel ground.”’ Therefore, friend Korakkhattiya, be very careful what you eat and drink, so that the ascetic Gotama’s words may be proved false!”
commentary_pali:
7.Ekamidāhanti iminā kiṃ dasseti? Idaṃ suttaṃ dvīhi padehi ābaddhaṃ iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ na karotīti ca aggaññaṃ na paññapetīti ca. Tattha ‘‘aggaññaṃ na paññapetī’’ti idaṃ padaṃ suttapariyosāne dassessati. ‘‘Pāṭihāriyaṃ na karotī’’ti imassa pana padassa anusandhidassanavasena ayaṃ desanā āraddhā.

Tattha ekamidāhanti ekasmiṃ ahaṃ. Samayanti samaye, ekasmiṃ kāle ahanti attho. Thūlūsūti thūlū nāma janapado, tattha viharāmi. Uttarakā nāmāti itthiliṅgavasena uttarakāti evaṃnāmako thūlūnaṃ janapadassa nigamo, taṃ nigamaṃ gocaragāmaṃ katvāti attho. Aceloti naggo. Korakkhattiyoti antovaṅkapādo khattiyo. Kukkuravatikoti samādinnakukkuravato sunakho viya ghāyitvā khādati, uddhanantare nipajjati, aññampi sunakhakiriyameva karoti. Catukkuṇḍikoti catusaṅghaṭṭito dve jāṇūni dve ca kappare bhūmiyaṃ ṭhapetvā vicarati. Chamānikiṇṇanti bhūmiyaṃ nikiṇṇaṃ pakkhittaṃ ṭhapitaṃ. Bhakkhasanti bhakkhaṃ yaṃkiñci khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ. Mukhenevāti hatthena aparāmasitvā khādanīyaṃ mukheneva khādati, bhojanīyampi mukheneva bhuñjati. Sādhurūpoti sundararūpo. Ayaṃ samaṇoti ayaṃ arahataṃ samaṇo ekoti. Tattha vatāti patthanatthe nipāto. Evaṃ kirassa patthanā ahosi ‘‘iminā samaṇena sadiso añño samaṇo nāma natthi, ayañhi appicchatāya vatthaṃ na nivāseti, ‘esa papañco’ti maññamāno bhikkhābhājanampi na pariharati, chamānikiṇṇameva khādati, ayaṃ samaṇo nāma. Mayaṃ pana kiṃ samaṇā’’ti? Evaṃ sabbaññubuddhassa pacchato carantova imaṃ pāpakaṃ vitakkaṃ vitakkesi.

ekamidāha Samaya Thūlūsū Uttarakā nāmā Acelo Korakkhattiyo Kukkuravatiko Catukkuṇḍiko Chamānikiṇṇa Bhakkhasa Mukhenevā Sādhurūpo Ayaṃ samaṇo vatā

Etadavocāti bhagavā kira cintesi ‘‘ayaṃ sunakkhatto pāpajjhāsayo, kiṃ nu imaṃ disvā cintesī’’ti? Athevaṃ cintento tassa ajjhāsayaṃ viditvā ‘‘ayaṃ moghapuriso mādisassa sabbaññuno pacchato āgacchanto acelaṃ arahāti maññati, idheva dānāyaṃ bālo niggahaṃ arahatī’’ti anivattitvāva etaṃ tvampi nāmātiādivacanamavoca. Tattha tvampi nāmāti garahatthe pikāro. Garahanto hi naṃ bhagavā ‘‘tvampi nāmā’’ti āha. ‘‘Tvampi nāma evaṃ hīnajjhāsayo, ahaṃ samaṇo sakyaputtiyoti evaṃ paṭijānissasī’’ti ayañhettha adhippāyo. Kiṃ pana maṃ, bhanteti mayhaṃ, bhante, kiṃ gārayhaṃ disvā bhagavā ‘‘evamāhā’’ti pucchati. Athassa bhagavā ācikkhanto ‘‘nanu te’’tiādimāha. Maccharāyatīti ‘‘mā aññassa arahattaṃ hotū’’ti kiṃ bhagavā evaṃ arahattassa maccharāyatīti pucchati. Na kho ahanti ahaṃ, moghapurisa, sadevakassa lokassa arahattappaṭilābhameva paccāsīsāmi, etadatthameva me bahūni dukkarāni karontena pāramiyo pūritā, na kho ahaṃ, moghapurisa, arahattassa maccharāyāmi. Pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigatanti na arahantaṃ arahāti, arahante ca anarahantoti evaṃ tassa diṭṭhi uppannā. Taṃ sandhāya ‘‘pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigata’’nti āha. Yaṃ kho panāti yaṃ etaṃ acelaṃ evaṃ maññasi. Sattamaṃ divasanti sattame divase. Alasakenāti alasakabyādhinā. Kālaṅkarissatīti uddhumātaudaro marissati.

Etadavocā tvampi nāmā tvampi nāmā Kiṃ pana maṃ, bhante Maccharāyatī Na kho aha Pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigata Yaṃ kho panā Sattamaṃ divasa Alasakenā Kālaṅkarissatī

Kālakañcikāti tesaṃ asurānaṃ nāmaṃ. Tesaṃ kira tigāvuto attabhāvo appamaṃsalohito purāṇapaṇṇasadiso kakkaṭakānaṃ viya akkhīni nikkhamitvā matthake tiṭṭhanti, mukhaṃ sūcipāsakasadisaṃ matthakasmiṃyeva hoti, tena oṇamitvā gocaraṃ gaṇhanti. Bīraṇatthambaketi bīraṇatiṇatthambo tasmiṃ susāne atthi, tasmā taṃ bīraṇatthambakanti vuccati.

Kālakañcikā Bīraṇatthambake

Tenupasaṅkamīti bhagavati ettakaṃ vatvā tasmiṃ gāme piṇḍāya caritvā vihāraṃ gate vihārā nikkhamitvā upasaṅkami. Yena tvanti yena kāraṇena tvaṃ. Yasmāpi bhagavatā byākato, tasmāti attho. Mattaṃmattanti pamāṇayuttaṃ pamāṇayuttaṃ. ‘‘Mantā mantā’’tipi pāṭho, paññāya upaparikkhitvā upaparikkhitvāti attho. Yathā samaṇassa gotamassāti yathā samaṇassa gotamassa micchā vacanaṃ assa, tathā kareyyāsīti āha. Evaṃ vutte acelo sunakho viya uddhanaṭṭhāne nipanno sīsaṃ ukkhipitvā akkhīni ummīletvā olokento kiṃ kathesi ‘‘samaṇo nāma gotamo amhākaṃ verī visabhāgo, samaṇassa gotamassa uppannakālato paṭṭhāya mayaṃ sūriye uggate khajjopanakā viya jātā. Samaṇo gotamo amhe, evaṃ vācaṃ vadeyya aññathā vā. Verino pana kathā nāma tacchā na hoti, gaccha tvaṃ ahamettha kattabbaṃ jānissāmī’’ti vatvā punadeva nipajji.

Tenupasaṅkamī Yena tva Mattaṃ matta Yathā samaṇassa gotamassā
commentary_english:
7. " *Ekamidāha*nti": What does this mean? " *Iminā kiṃ dasseti*?" This *sutta* is bound by two *padas*, meaning it does not perform the miracle of power (*iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ*) and does not explain the origin of the world (*aggaññaṃ*).
There, “does not explain the origin of the world (*aggaññaṃ na paññapeti*)” — this *pada* will show at the end of the *sutta*.
"Does not perform the miracle of power (*pāṭihāriyaṃ na karoti*)" — this teaching (*desanā*) began in accordance with the connectional way of seeing of this *pada*.

There, "*ekamidāha*nti": I was in one.
"*Samaya*nti": At one time, it means.
"*Thūlūsū*ti": *Thūlū* is the name of a country (*janapado*); there, I live (*viharāmi*).
"*Uttarakā nāmā*ti": By way of the feminine gender (*itthiliṅgavasena*), *Uttarakā* is a town (*nigamo*) of the country (*janapadassa*) of the *Thūlūs*; it means having made that town a pasture village (*gocaragāmaṃ katvāti attho*).
"*Acelo*ti": Naked (*naggo*).
"*Korakkhattiyo*ti": A Khattiya whose feet are inside the *vaṅka* (*antovaṅkapādo khattiyo*).
"*Kukkuravatiko*ti": One who has undertaken the dog duty (*samādinnakukkuravato*), he eats having smelled like a dog (*sunakho viya ghāyitvā khādati*), lies down in another place (*uddhanantare nipajjati*), and does just the action of a dog (*aññampi sunakhakiriyameva karoti*).
"*Catukkuṇḍiko*ti": One who is assembled on four sides (*catusaṅghaṭṭito*), having placed two knees (*dve jāṇūni*) and two elbows (*dve ca kappare*) on the ground (*bhūmiyaṃ ṭhapetvā*), he wanders (*vicarati*).
"*Chamānikiṇṇa*nti": Strewn on the ground (*bhūmiyaṃ nikiṇṇaṃ*), thrown, established.
"*Bhakkhasa*nti": Food (*bhakkhaṃ*), whatever is edible (*yaṃkiñci khādanīyaṃ*), enjoyable (*bhojanīyaṃ*).
"*Mukhenevā*ti": Without touching with the hand (*hatthena aparāmasitvā*), he eats the edible (*khādanīyaṃ*) just with the mouth (*mukheneva khādati*), he enjoys the enjoyable (*bhojanīyampi*) just with the mouth (*mukheneva bhuñjati*).
"*Sādhurūpo*ti": Beautiful form (*sundararūpo*).
"*Ayaṃ samaṇo*ti": This is a *samaṇa* of the *arahats*, it means.
There, "*vatā*ti": It is a particle (*nipāto*) in the sense of desire (*patthanatthe*).
Thus, there was a desire in him: “There is no other *samaṇa* like this *samaṇa* (*iminā samaṇena sadiso añño samaṇo nāma natthi*), because this one, due to having few desires (*appicchatāya*), does not wear clothes (*vatthaṃ na nivāseti*), thinking ‘this is proliferation (*esa papañco*ti maññamāno*)’, does not even care for a begging bowl (*bhikkhābhājanampi na pariharati*), he eats just what is strewn on the ground (*chamānikiṇṇameva khādati*), this is a *samaṇa*!
But what are we, *samaṇas*?" Thus, while walking behind the all-knowing Buddha (*sabbaññubuddhassa pacchato carantova*), he pondered (*vitakkesi*) this evil thought (*imaṃ pāpakaṃ vitakkaṃ*).

"*Ekamidāha*, *samaya*, *thūlūsū*, *uttarakā nāmā*, *acelo*, *korakkhattiyo*, *kukkuravatiko*, *catukkuṇḍiko*, *chamānikiṇṇa*, *bhakkhasa*, *mukhenevā*, *sādhurūpo*, *ayaṃ samaṇo*, *vatā*." "*Etadavocā*ti": The Blessed One (*bhagavā*) thought: “This *Sunakkhatta* is of evil intent (*pāpajjhāsayo*), what did he think after seeing this (*kiṃ nu imaṃ disvā cintesī*)?” Then, while thinking thus (*athevaṃ cintento*), having known his intention (*tassa ajjhāsayaṃ viditvā*): "This empty man (*ayaṃ moghapuriso*), while coming behind the all-knowing one like me (*mādisassa sabbaññuno pacchato āgacchanto*), thinks that the naked one is an *arhat* (*acelaṃ arahāti maññati*), right here this fool is worthy of restraint (*idheva dānāyaṃ bālo niggahaṃ arahatī*)!" Without turning away, he spoke this word beginning with "*tvampi nāmā*ti*".
There, "*tvampi nāmā*ti": The *pikāro* is in the sense of reproach (*garahatthe*).
Indeed, the Blessed One (*bhagavā*), while reproaching him (*garahanto hi naṃ*), said: "*Tvampi nāmā*ti."
“You too, with such a base intention (*tvampi nāma evaṃ hīnajjhāsayo*), will declare yourself to be a *samaṇa*, a son of the *Sakyas* (*ahaṃ samaṇo sakyaputtiyoti evaṃ paṭijānissasī*)?" This is the intention here (*ayañhettha adhippāyo*).
"*Kiṃ pana maṃ, bhante*ti": Having seen what is blameworthy in me (*mayhaṃ, bhante, kiṃ gārayhaṃ disvā*), Reverend Sir (*bhagavā*) asks, "Why did you say this (*evamāhā*ti pucchati)?"
Then the Blessed One (*bhagavā*), explaining to him (*athassa bhagavā ācikkhanto*), said that which begins with "Surely not you (*nanu te*)" etc.
"*Maccharāyatī*ti": "May *arahatship* not be for another (*mā aññassa arahattaṃ hotū*)!" Why does the Blessed One (*bhagavā*) ask thus, being jealous (*maccharāyati*) of *arahatship* (*arahattassa*)?
"*Na kho aha*nti": I (*ahaṃ*), empty man (*moghapurisa*), only expect the attainment of *arahatship* for the world together with the *devas* (*sadevakassa lokassa arahattappaṭilābhameva paccāsīsāmi*); for this purpose alone, with me doing many difficult things (*etadatthameva me bahūni dukkarāni karontena*), the perfections (*pāramiyo*) were fulfilled (*pūritā*), I (*ahaṃ*) am not jealous (*maccharāyāmi*) of *arahatship* (*arahattassa*), empty man (*moghapurisa*)!
"*Pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigata*nti": He is not an *arhat*, and among the *arahats* there is a non-*arhat*—thus, his view (*diṭṭhi*) arose (*uppannā*).
With reference to that (*taṃ sandhāya*), he said: "evil view (*pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigata*)."
"*Yaṃ kho panā*ti": Whatever naked one (*yaṃ etaṃ acelaṃ*) you think thus (*evaṃ maññasi*).
"*Sattamaṃ divasa*nti": On the seventh day (*sattame divase*).
"*Alasakenā*ti": By the disease of *alasaka* (*alasakabyādhinā*).
"*Kālaṅkarissatī*ti": One with a swollen belly will die (*uddhumātaudaro marissati*).
"*Etadavocā*"

mula_pali: 8. ‘‘Atha kho, bhaggava, sunakkhatto licchaviputto ekadvīhikāya sattarattindivāni gaṇesi, yathā taṃ tathāgatassa asaddahamāno. Atha kho, bhaggava, acelo korakkhattiyo sattamaṃ divasaṃ alasakena kālamakāsi. Kālaṅkato ca kālakañcikā nāma asurā sabbanihīno asurakāyo, tatra upapajji. Kālaṅkatañca naṃ bīraṇatthambake susāne chaḍḍesuṃ.
mula_english:
8. Then, Bhaggava, Sunakkhatta, the Licchavi's son, counted the seven days and nights, thinking that the Tathāgata's words would prove false.

Then, Bhaggava, the naked ascetic Korakkhattiya died of indigestion on the seventh day.

Having died, he was reborn among the *kālakañcikā* asuras, the lowest of the asura hosts.

And after his death, his body was thrown on a heap of *bīraṇa* grass in the charnel ground.
commentary_pali:
8.Ekadvīhikāyāti ekaṃ dveti vatvā gaṇesi. Yathā tanti yathā asaddahamāno koci gaṇeyya, evaṃ gaṇesi. Ekadivasañca tikkhattuṃ upasaṅkamitvā eko divaso atīto, dve divasā atītāti ārocesi. Sattamaṃ divasanti so kira sunakkhattassa vacanaṃ sutvā sattāhaṃ nirāhārova ahosi. Athassa sattame divase eko upaṭṭhāko ‘‘amhākaṃ kulūpakasamaṇassa ajja sattamo divaso gehaṃ anāgacchantassa aphāsu nu kho jāta’’nti sūkaramaṃsaṃ pacāpetvā bhattamādāya gantvā purato bhūmiyaṃ nikkhipi. Acelo disvā cintesi ‘‘samaṇassa gotamassa kathā tacchā vā atacchā vā hotu, āhāraṃ pana khāditvā suhitassa me maraṇampi sumaraṇa’’nti dve hatthe jaṇṇukāni ca bhūmiyaṃ ṭhapetvā kucchipūraṃ bhuñji. So rattibhāge jīrāpetuṃ asakkonto alasakena kālamakāsi. Sacepi hi so ‘‘na bhuñjeyya’’nti cinteyya, tathāpi taṃ divasaṃ bhuñjitvā alasakena kālaṃ kareyya. Advejjhavacanā hi tathāgatāti.

Bīraṇatthambaketi titthiyā kira ‘‘kālaṅkato korakkhattiyo’’ti sutvā divasāni gaṇetvā idaṃ tāva saccaṃ jātaṃ, idāni naṃ aññattha chaḍḍetvā ‘‘musāvādena samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ niggaṇhissāmā’’ti gantvā tassa sarīraṃ valliyā bandhitvā ākaḍḍhantā ‘‘ettha chaḍḍessāma, ettha chaḍḍessāmā’’ti gacchanti. Gatagataṭṭhānaṃ aṅgaṇameva hoti. Te kaḍḍhamānā bīraṇatthambakasusānaṃyeva gantvā susānabhāvaṃ ñatvā ‘‘aññattha chaḍḍessāmā’’ti ākaḍḍhiṃsu. Atha nesaṃ valli chijjittha, pacchā cāletuṃ nāsakkhiṃsu. Te tatova pakkantā. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘bīraṇatthambake susāne chaḍḍesu’’nti.

Bīraṇatthambake
commentary_english:
8. *Ekadvīhikāyā* means: he counted saying, "one, two."

*Yathā ta* means: as someone counting without conviction might count, so he counted.

And after approaching three times in one day, he announced, "One day has passed, two days have passed."

*Sattamaṃ divasa* means: he, having heard Sunakkhatta's words, fasted for a week.

Then on the seventh day, an attendant of his said, "Today is the seventh day for our family-supporting ascetic, who has not come to the house. Has something unpleasant happened?" Having had pig's meat cooked, he took the food, went, and placed it on the ground in front of him.

Seeing the naked one, he thought, "The words of the ascetic Gotama, whether true or untrue, may they be. Having eaten the food, may my death be a good death for one who is satisfied." Having placed both hands and knees on the ground, he ate his fill.

Unable to digest it during the night, he died of tympanites.

Even if he were to think, "I will not eat," nevertheless, having eaten that day, he would die of tympanites.

Indeed, the words of the *tathāgata* are not double-tongued.

*Bīraṇatthambake* means: the heretics, having heard that Korakkhattiya was dead, counted the days. "This much is true. Now, having thrown him elsewhere, we will discredit the ascetic Gotama with false speech." Going, binding his body with creepers, and dragging him, they went, saying, "We will throw him here, we will throw him here."

Every place they went was a courtyard.

While they were dragging him, they went to the *bīraṇatthambaka* cemetery itself. Knowing it was a cemetery, they dragged him, saying, "We will throw him elsewhere."

Then their creeper broke, and afterward, they were unable to move him.

They departed from there.

Therefore it was said, "Throw him in the *bīraṇatthambaka* cemetery."

*Bīraṇatthambake*

mula_pali: 9. ‘‘Assosi kho, bhaggava, sunakkhatto licchaviputto – ‘acelo kira korakkhattiyo alasakena kālaṅkato bīraṇatthambake susāne chaḍḍito’ti. Atha kho, bhaggava, sunakkhatto licchaviputto yena bīraṇatthambakaṃ susānaṃ, yena acelo korakkhattiyo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā acelaṃ korakkhattiyaṃ tikkhattuṃ pāṇinā ākoṭesi – ‘jānāsi, āvuso korakkhattiya, attano gati’nti? Atha kho, bhaggava, acelo korakkhattiyo pāṇinā piṭṭhiṃ paripuñchanto vuṭṭhāsi. ‘Jānāmi, āvuso sunakkhatta, attano gatiṃ. Kālakañcikā nāma asurā sabbanihīno asurakāyo, tatrāmhi upapanno’ti vatvā tattheva uttāno papati paripati (syā. ka.).
mula_english:
“I heard, venerable, that Sunakkhatta of the Licchavis said: ‘The naked ascetic Korakkhattiya died wretchedly and was thrown on the heap of biraṇa-grass in the charnel ground.’"

Then, venerable, Sunakkhatta of the Licchavis went to the heap of biraṇa-grass in the charnel ground where the naked ascetic Korakkhattiya was; having gone there, he struck the naked ascetic Korakkhattiya three times with his hand, saying: “Friend Korakkhattiya, do you know your destiny?”

Then, venerable, the naked ascetic Korakkhattiya, wiping his back with his hand, arose. “I know, friend Sunakkhatta, my destiny. I have been reborn among the *Kālakañjika* asuras (*kālakāñcikā nāma asurā*), the very lowest grade of asuras." And having spoken thus, he fell back there on his back.
commentary_pali: 9.Tenupasaṅkamīti kasmā upasaṅkami? So kira cintesi ‘‘avasesaṃ tāva samaṇassa gotamassa vacanaṃ sameti, matassa pana uṭṭhāya aññena saddhiṃ kathanaṃ nāma natthi, handāhaṃ gantvā pucchāmi. Sace katheti, sundaraṃ. No ce katheti, samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ musāvādena niggaṇhissāmī’’ti iminā kāraṇena upasaṅkami. Ākoṭesīti pahari. Jānāmi āvusoti matasarīraṃ uṭṭhahitvā kathetuṃ samatthaṃ nāma natthi, idaṃ kathaṃ kathesīti? Buddhānubhāvena. Bhagavā kira korakkhattiyaṃ asurayonito ānetvā sarīre adhimocetvā kathāpesi. Tameva vā sarīraṃ kathāpesi, acinteyyo hi buddhavisayo.
commentary_english:
9. "Why did he approach *him* (tenupasaṅkamī)?" He approached, thinking, "The rest of the words of the renunciant Gotama (śramaṇa Gautama) agree, but there is no such thing as a dead man rising and speaking with another. Come, I will go and ask him. If he speaks truly, it is excellent (sundaraṃ). But if he does not speak truly, I will convict the renunciant Gotama of lying (*musāvādena niggaṇhissāmī*)." It was for this reason that he approached him.

"*Ākoṭesī* means he struck."

"*Jānāmi āvuso* [I know, friend]," but there is no such thing as a dead body rising up and being able to speak. "How did *he* speak this?" By the power of the Buddha (buddhānubhāvena). The Blessed One (bhagavā) brought Korakkhattiya from the womb of an Asura, infused [him] into the body, and made [him] speak. Or he made that very body speak; for the domain of the Buddha (buddhavisayo) is inconceivable (*acinteyyo*).

mula_pali:
10. ‘‘Atha kho, bhaggava, sunakkhatto licchaviputto yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā maṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhaggava , sunakkhattaṃ licchaviputtaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘taṃ kiṃ maññasi, sunakkhatta, yatheva te ahaṃ acelaṃ korakkhattiyaṃ ārabbha byākāsiṃ, tatheva taṃ vipākaṃ, aññathā vā’ti? ‘Yatheva me, bhante, bhagavā acelaṃ korakkhattiyaṃ ārabbha byākāsi, tatheva taṃ vipākaṃ, no aññathā’ti. ‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, sunakkhatta, yadi evaṃ sante kataṃ vā hoti uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ, akataṃ vāti? ‘Addhā kho, bhante, evaṃ sante kataṃ hoti uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ, no akata’nti. ‘Evampi kho maṃ tvaṃ, moghapurisa, uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ karontaṃ evaṃ vadesi – na hi pana me, bhante, bhagavā uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ karotīti. Passa, moghapurisa, yāvañca te idaṃ aparaddha’nti. ‘‘Evampi kho, bhaggava, sunakkhatto licchaviputto mayā vuccamāno apakkameva imasmā dhammavinayā, yathā taṃ āpāyiko nerayiko.

Acelakaḷāramaṭṭakavatthu
mula_english:
10. Then, Bhaggava, Sunakkhatta, son of the Licchavis, approached me; having approached, he paid homage to me and sat down to one side.

As he was sitting to one side, Bhaggava, I said to Sunakkhatta, son of the Licchavis: ‘What do you think, Sunakkhatta? Has what I explained to you regarding the naked ascetic Korakkhattiya come true, or is it otherwise?’ ‘Just as the Blessed One explained to me regarding the naked ascetic Korakkhattiya, so it has come to fruition, and not otherwise.’

‘What do you think, Sunakkhatta? If that is so, has a superhuman miracle ( *uttarimanussadhamma iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ*) been performed, or not?’ ‘Indeed, venerable sir (*bhante*), if that is so, a superhuman miracle has been performed, not not performed.’

‘Even so, foolish man (*moghapurisa*), when I perform a superhuman miracle, you say this: “Indeed, venerable sir, the Blessed One (*bhagavā*) does not perform a superhuman miracle."

Consider, foolish man, how great is your offense!’

Even so, Bhaggava, Sunakkhatta, son of the Licchavis, when spoken to by me, departed from this Dharma and Discipline (*dhammavinayā*), just like someone destined for misery and hell.

The Acelakaḷāramaṭṭakavatthu
commentary_pali:
10.Tatheva taṃ vipākanti tassa vacanassa vipākaṃ tatheva, udāhu noti liṅgavipallāso kato, tatheva so vipākoti attho. Keci pana ‘‘vipakka’’ntipi paṭhanti, nibbattanti attho.

Ettha ṭhatvā pāṭihāriyāni samānetabbāni. Sabbāneva hetāni pañca pāṭihāriyāni honti. ‘‘Sattame divase marissatī’’ti vuttaṃ, so tatheva mato, idaṃ paṭhamaṃ pāṭihāriyaṃ. ‘‘Alasakenā’’ti vuttaṃ, alasakeneva mato, idaṃ dutiyaṃ. ‘‘Kālakañcikesu nibbattissatī’’ti vuttaṃ, tattheva nibbatto, idaṃ tatiyaṃ. ‘‘Bīraṇatthambake susāne chaḍḍessantī’’ti vuttaṃ, tattheva chaḍḍito , idaṃ catutthaṃ. ‘‘Nibbattaṭṭhānato āgantvā sunakkhattena saddhiṃ kathessatī’’ti vutto, so kathesiyeva, idaṃ pañcamaṃ pāṭihāriyaṃ.

Acelakaḷāramaṭṭakavatthuvaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
That very result” means that the result of that statement is just so, or if not, a reversal of the sign has been made; just so is that result, is the meaning.

But some read ‘‘vipakka’’ntipi, the meaning is nibbattanti.

Having stood here, miracles should be brought together.
All of these five are miracles.
‘‘He will die on the seventh day’’ it was said, and he died just so; this is the first miracle.
‘‘By means of tympanites’’ it was said, and he died just so from tympanites; this is the second.
‘‘He will be reborn in the Kālakañcikas’’ it was said, and he was reborn just there; this is the third.
‘‘They will throw [him] into the Bīraṇatthambaka charnel ground’’ it was said, and he was thrown just there, this is the fourth.
‘‘Having come from the place of rebirth, he will speak with Sunakkhatta’’ it was said, and he spoke just so; this is the fifth miracle.

Description of the Acelakaḷāramaṭṭaka affair

mula_pali: 11. ‘‘Ekamidāhaṃ, bhaggava, samayaṃ vesāliyaṃ viharāmi mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṃ. Tena kho pana samayena acelo kaḷāramaṭṭako vesāliyaṃ paṭivasati lābhaggappatto ceva yasaggappatto ca vajjigāme. Tassa sattavatapadāni sattavattapadāni (syā. pī.) samattāni samādinnāni honti – ‘yāvajīvaṃ acelako assaṃ, na vatthaṃ paridaheyyaṃ, yāvajīvaṃ brahmacārī assaṃ, na methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭiseveyyaṃ, yāvajīvaṃ surāmaṃseneva yāpeyyaṃ, na odanakummāsaṃ bhuñjeyyaṃ. Puratthimena vesāliṃ udenaṃ nāma cetiyaṃ, taṃ nātikkameyyaṃ, dakkhiṇena vesāliṃ gotamakaṃ nāma cetiyaṃ, taṃ nātikkameyyaṃ, pacchimena vesāliṃ sattambaṃ nāma cetiyaṃ, taṃ nātikkameyyaṃ, uttarena vesāliṃ bahuputtaṃ nāma bahuputtakaṃ nāma (syā.) cetiyaṃ taṃ nātikkameyya’nti. So imesaṃ sattannaṃ vatapadānaṃ samādānahetu lābhaggappatto ceva yasaggappatto ca vajjigāme.
mula_english:
11. Once, Bhaggava, I was staying at Vesali, at the Gabled Hall in the Great Forest.

And at that time there was a naked ascetic living in Vesali called Kalaramutthaka who enjoyed great gains and fame in the Vajjian capital.

He had undertaken seven rules of practice: ”As long as I live l will be a naked ascetic *acelaka* (acelako assaṃ) and will not put on any clothes; as long as I live I will remain chaste *brahmacārī* (brahmacārī assaṃ) and abstain from sexual intercourse *maithuna dharma* (na methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭiseveyyaṃ); as long as I live I will subsist on strong drink and meat, abstaining from boiled rice and sour milk;

as long as I live l will never go beyond the Udena shrine *cetiya* (cetiyaṃ) to the east of Vesali, the Gotamaka shrine *cetiya* (cetiyaṃ) to the south, the Sattamba shrine *cetiya* (cetiyaṃ) to the west, nor the Bahuputta shrine *cetiya* (cetiyaṃ) to the north.

” And it was through having undertaken these seven rules that he enjoyed the greatest gains and fame of all in the Vajjian capital.
commentary_pali: 11.Kaḷāramaṭṭakoti nikkhantadantamattako. Nāmameva vā tassetaṃ. Lābhaggappattoti lābhaggaṃ patto, aggalābhaṃ pattoti vuttaṃ hoti. Yasaggappattoti yasaggaṃ aggaparivāraṃ patto. Vatapadānīti vatāniyeva, vatakoṭṭhāsā vā. Samattānīti gahitāni. Samādinnānīti tasseva vevacanaṃ. Puratthimena vesālinti vesālito avidūre puratthimāya disāya. Cetiyanti yakkhacetiyaṭṭhānaṃ. Esa nayo sabbattha.
commentary_english:
11. *Kaḷāramaṭṭako* means one whose teeth have come out a little.
Or it is just a name for that.
*Lābhaggappatto* means one who has attained the best gain, it is said to have attained the foremost gain.
*Yasaggappatto* means one who has attained fame, the best retinue.
*Vatapadānī* means just fences, or divisions of fences.
*Samattānī* means taken.
*Samādinnānī* is another word for that same thing.
*Puratthimena vesāli* means not far from Vesālī, in the eastern direction.
*Cetiya* means the place of a *yakṣa* shrine.
This method applies in each instance.

mula_pali: 12. ‘‘Atha kho, bhaggava, sunakkhatto licchaviputto yena acelo kaḷāramaṭṭako tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā acelaṃ kaḷāramaṭṭakaṃ pañhaṃ apucchi. Tassa acelo kaḷāramaṭṭako pañhaṃ puṭṭho na sampāyāsi. Asampāyanto kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātvākāsi. Atha kho, bhaggava, sunakkhattassa licchaviputtassa etadahosi – ‘sādhurūpaṃ vata bho arahantaṃ samaṇaṃ āsādimhase asādiyimhase (syā.). Mā vata no ahosi dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāyā’ti.
mula_english:
Now then, Bhaggava, Sunakkhatta, son of the Licchavis, went to the naked ascetic Kaḷāramaṭṭaka and asked him a question.

But the naked ascetic Kaḷāramaṭṭaka, when asked the question, could not answer.

Because he could not answer it, he showed anger, rage, and petulance.

Then, Bhaggava, Sunakkhatta, son of the Licchavis, thought: “I might cause this real *arhat* (*arhant*) ascetic offence.

I don’t want anything to happen that would be to my lasting harm and misfortune."
commentary_pali: 12.Yena acelakoti bhagavato vattaṃ katvā yena acelo kaḷāramaṭṭako tenupasaṅkami. Pañhaṃ apucchīti gambhīraṃ tilakkhaṇāhataṃ pañhaṃ pucchi. Na sampāyāsīti na sammā ñāṇagatiyā pāyāsi, andho viya visamaṭṭhāne tattha tattheva pakkhali. Neva ādiṃ, na pariyosānamaddasa. Atha vā ‘‘na sampāyāsī’’ti na sampādesi, sampādetvā kathetuṃ nāsakkhi. Asampāyantoti kabarakkhīni parivattetvā olokento ‘‘asikkhitakassa santike vuṭṭhosi, anokāsepi pabbajito pañhaṃ pucchanto vicarasi, apehi mā etasmiṃ ṭhāne aṭṭhāsī’’ti vadanto. Kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātvākāsīti kuppanākāraṃ kopaṃ, dussanākāraṃ dosaṃ, atuṭṭhākārabhūtaṃ domanassasaṅkhātaṃ appaccayañca pākaṭamakāsi. Āsādimhaseti āsādiyimha ghaṭṭayimha. Mā vata no ahosīti aho vata me na bhaveyya. Maṃ vata no ahosītipi pāṭho. Tattha manti sāmivacanatthe upayogavacanaṃ, ahosi vata nu mamāti attho. Evañca pana cintetvā ukkuṭikaṃ nisīditvā ‘‘khamatha me, bhante’’ti taṃ khamāpesi. Sopi ito paṭṭhāya aññaṃ kiñci pañhaṃ nāma na pucchissasīti. Āma na pucchissāmīti. Yadi evaṃ gaccha, khamāmi teti taṃ uyyojesi.
commentary_english:
12. "[Because] he did not go well" -- having made the Blessed One's round, he approached the naked ascetic Kaḷāramaṭṭaka.

"He asked a question" -- he asked a profound question that struck at the three characteristics.

"[Because] he does not go well" -- he does not go by means of right knowledge; like a blind man in an uneven place, he slips right there.

He did not see either the beginning or the end.

Then, "He does not go well" -- he did not accomplish it; having accomplished it, he was not able to speak.

"Not going well" -- turning his disheveled hair around, looking, saying, "You have gone forth near an uneducated person; even in an improper place, having gone forth, you wander about asking questions; go away, do not stand in this place!"

"He manifested anger, displeasure, and discontent" -- he made manifest anger in the manner of being angry, displeasure in the manner of being displeased, and discontent, which is of the nature of unhappiness, in the manner of being displeased.

"We assailed" -- we assailed, we struck.

"May it not be for us!" -- Oh, may it not be for me!

There is also the reading, "May it not be for me!"

There, "ma" means a word of use in the sense of ownership; the meaning is, "Oh, may it be mine!"

And further, having thought thus, squatting down, he propitiated him, saying, "Forgive me, venerable sir!"

He too, from here on, [said,] "You will not ask any other question by name."

"Yes, I will not ask."

"If so, go, I forgive you," he sent him away.

mula_pali:
13. ‘‘Atha kho, bhaggava, sunakkhatto licchaviputto yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā maṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhaggava, sunakkhattaṃ licchaviputtaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘tvampi nāma, moghapurisa, samaṇo sakyaputtiyo paṭijānissasī’ti! ‘Kiṃ pana maṃ, bhante, bhagavā evamāha – tvampi nāma, moghapurisa, samaṇo sakyaputtiyo paṭijānissasī’ti? ‘Nanu tvaṃ, sunakkhatta, acelaṃ kaḷāramaṭṭakaṃ upasaṅkamitvā pañhaṃ apucchi. Tassa te acelo kaḷāramaṭṭako pañhaṃ puṭṭho na sampāyāsi. Asampāyanto kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātvākāsi. Tassa te etadahosi – ‘‘sādhurūpaṃ vata, bho, arahantaṃ samaṇaṃ āsādimhase. Mā vata no ahosi dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāyā’ti. ‘Evaṃ, bhante. Kiṃ pana, bhante, bhagavā arahattassa maccharāyatī’ti? ‘Na kho ahaṃ, moghapurisa, arahattassa maccharāyāmi, api ca tuyhevetaṃ pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppannaṃ, taṃ pajaha. Mā te ahosi dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāya. Yaṃ kho panetaṃ, sunakkhatta, maññasi acelaṃ kaḷāramaṭṭakaṃ – sādhurūpo ayaṃ arahaṃ (syā.) samaṇoti, so nacirasseva parihito sānucāriko vicaranto odanakummāsaṃ bhuñjamāno sabbāneva vesāliyāni cetiyāni samatikkamitvā yasā nihīno yasānikiṇṇo (ka.) kālaṃ karissatī’ti.

‘‘‘Atha kho, bhaggava, acelo kaḷāramaṭṭako nacirasseva parihito sānucāriko vicaranto odanakummāsaṃ bhuñjamāno sabbāneva vesāliyāni cetiyāni samatikkamitvā yasā nihīno kālamakāsi.
mula_english:
13. ‘Then, Bhaggava, Sunakkhatta the Licchavi came to me, saluted me, sat down to one side.

Sitting to one side, I said to Sunakkhatta the Licchavi: ‘So, you, worthless man, claim to be a renunciate, a follower of the Śākyan clan!’ ‘Why, venerable sir, does the Blessed One say this to me: “So, you, worthless man, claim to be a renunciate, a follower of the Śākyan clan!”?’ ‘Well, Sunakkhatta, you approached the naked ascetic Kalaramutthaka and asked him a question.

But the naked ascetic Kalaramutthaka could not answer the question you asked him.

Because he could not answer it, he showed anger, rage and petulance.

Then you thought: “I might cause this real *arhat* ascetic offence.

I don’t want anything to happen that would be to my lasting harm and misfortune”?’
‘Yes, venerable sir.’

‘But, venerable sir, is the Blessed One jealous of *arhatship*?’ ‘I am not jealous of *arhatship*, worthless man, but such an evil view has arisen in you. Give it up!

Do not let it cause you misfortune and suffering for a long time!

Sunakkhatta, you think of the naked ascetic Kalaramutthaka: “This is a fine *samaṇa*.” But before long, surrounded by his followers, wandering about, eating rice gruel, passing by all the shrines in Vesālī, deprived of glory, he will die.’

‘‘Then, Bhaggava, the naked ascetic Kalaramutthaka, before long, surrounded by his followers, wandering about, eating rice gruel, passing by all the shrines in Vesālī, deprived of glory, died.

mula_pali:
14. ‘‘Assosi kho, bhaggava, sunakkhatto licchaviputto – ‘acelo kira kaḷāramaṭṭako parihito sānucāriko vicaranto odanakummāsaṃ bhuñjamāno sabbāneva vesāliyāni cetiyāni samatikkamitvā yasā nihīno kālaṅkato’ti. Atha kho, bhaggava, sunakkhatto licchaviputto yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā maṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhaggava, sunakkhattaṃ licchaviputtaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘taṃ kiṃ maññasi, sunakkhatta, yatheva te ahaṃ acelaṃ kaḷāramaṭṭakaṃ ārabbha byākāsiṃ, tatheva taṃ vipākaṃ, aññathā vā’ti? ‘Yatheva me, bhante, bhagavā acelaṃ kaḷāramaṭṭakaṃ ārabbha byākāsi, tatheva taṃ vipākaṃ, no aññathā’ti. ‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, sunakkhatta, yadi evaṃ sante kataṃ vā hoti uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ akataṃ vā’ti? ‘Addhā kho, bhante, evaṃ sante kataṃ hoti uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ, no akata’nti. ‘Evampi kho maṃ tvaṃ, moghapurisa, uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ karontaṃ evaṃ vadesi – na hi pana me, bhante, bhagavā uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ karotī’’ti. Passa, moghapurisa, yāvañca te idaṃ aparaddha’nti. ‘‘Eva’mpi kho, bhaggava, sunakkhatto licchaviputto mayā vuccamāno apakkameva imasmā dhammavinayā, yathā taṃ āpāyiko nerayiko.

Acelapāthikaputtavatthu
mula_english:
14. Bhaggava, Sunakkhatta, son of the Licchavis, heard: 'It seems that Kālāramattaka, the naked ascetic, having fallen from his glory, has died, after going about with his followers, eating rice gruel, and passing by all the shrines of Vesālī.'

Then, Bhaggava, Sunakkhatta, son of the Licchavis, went to me, and after paying homage to me, sat down at one side.

Sitting at one side, I, Bhaggava, said to Sunakkhatta, son of the Licchavis: 'What do you think, Sunakkhatta? Has what I told you about Kālāramattaka, the naked ascetic, come about, or not?' 'It has come about just as the Blessed One told me about Kālāramattaka, the naked ascetic, Lord, it has come about just so, not otherwise.'

'What do you think, Sunakkhatta, when this is so, is the superhuman power and miracle performed, or not performed?' 'Indeed, Lord, when this is so, the superhuman power and miracle is performed, not unperformed.'

'Well then, you foolish man (moghapurisa), do you still say to me, after I have performed such a superhuman power and miracle: 'Well, Lord (bhante), the Blessed One (bhagavā) does not perform any superhuman power and miracle'?'

Consider, you foolish man, how far the fault is yours.

Even so, Bhaggava, when I spoke thus, Sunakkhatta, son of the Licchavis, departed from this Dhamma and discipline, like one condemned to hell.

The story of the naked ascetic Pāthika's son (acelapāthikaputtavatthu).
commentary_pali:
14.Parihitoti paridahito nivatthavattho. Sānucārikoti anucārikā vuccati bhariyā, saha anucārikāya sānucāriko, taṃ taṃ brahmacariyaṃ pahāya sabhariyoti attho. Odanakummāsanti surāmaṃsato atirekaṃ odanampi kummāsampi bhuñjamāno. Yasā nihīnoti yaṃ lābhaggayasaggaṃ patto, tato parihīno hutvā. ‘‘Kataṃ hoti uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriya’’nti idha sattavatapadātikkamavasena satta pāṭihāriyāni veditabbāni.

Acelapāthikaputtavatthuvaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
"parihito" means "paridahito nivatthavattho".
"sānucāriko" means anucārikā is said to be bhariyā, saha anucārikāya sānucāriko, taṃ taṃ brahmacariyaṃ pahāya sabhariyoti is the meaning.
"odanakummāsa" means atirekaṃ exceeding surāmaṃsato, odanampi and kummāsampi, bhuñjamāno while enjoying.
"yasā nihīno" means yaṃ lābhaggayasaggaṃ patto, tato parihīno hutvā, having declined from that.
"kataṃ hoti uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriya" means idha here, sattavatapadātikkamavasena due to the transgression of the vows, satta pāṭihāriyāni seven miracles, veditabbāni should be known.

acelapāthikaputtavatthuvaṇṇanā

mula_pali: 15. ‘‘Ekamidāhaṃ, bhaggava, samayaṃ tattheva vesāliyaṃ viharāmi mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṃ. Tena kho pana samayena acelo pāthikaputto pāṭikaputto (sī. syā. pī.) vesāliyaṃ paṭivasati lābhaggappatto ceva yasaggappatto ca vajjigāme. So vesāliyaṃ parisati evaṃ vācaṃ bhāsati – ‘samaṇopi gotamo ñāṇavādo, ahampi ñāṇavādo. Ñāṇavādo kho pana ñāṇavādena arahati uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ dassetuṃ. Samaṇo gotamo upaḍḍhapathaṃ āgaccheyya, ahampi upaḍḍhapathaṃ gaccheyyaṃ. Te tattha ubhopi uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ kareyyāma. Ekaṃ ce samaṇo gotamo uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ karissati, dvāhaṃ karissāmi. Dve ce samaṇo gotamo uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyāni karissati, cattārāhaṃ karissāmi . Cattāri ce samaṇo gotamo uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyāni karissati, aṭṭhāhaṃ karissāmi. Iti yāvatakaṃ yāvatakaṃ samaṇo gotamo uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ karissati, taddiguṇaṃ taddiguṇāhaṃ karissāmī’ti.
mula_english: ‘Once, Bhaggava, I was staying at Vesali in the Gabled Hall in the Great Forest. And at that time there was a naked ascetic living in Vesali called Patikaputta, who enjoyed great gains and fame in the Vajjian capital. And he made this declaration in the assembly of Vesali: ”The ascetic Gotama claims to be a man of wisdom (*jñānavāda*), and I make the same claim. It is right that a man of wisdom (*jñānavāda*) should show it by performing miracles (*iddhi-prātihārya*). If the ascetic Gotama will come half-way to meet me, l will do likewise. Then we could both work miracles (*iddhi-prātihārya*). However many miracles (*iddhi-prātihārya*) he performs, I will perform twice as many!’
commentary_pali: 15.Pāthikaputtoti pāthikassa putto. Ñāṇavādenāti ñāṇavādena saddhiṃ. Upaḍḍhapathanti yojanaṃ ce, no antare bhaveyya, gotamo aḍḍhayojanaṃ, ahaṃ aḍḍhayojanaṃ. Esa nayo aḍḍhayojanādīsu. Ekapadavārampi atikkamma gacchato jayo bhavissati, anāgacchato parājayoti. Te tatthāti te mayaṃ tattha samāgataṭṭhāne. Taddiguṇaṃ taddiguṇāhanti tato tato diguṇaṃ diguṇaṃ ahaṃ karissāmi, bhagavatā saddhiṃ pāṭihāriyaṃ kātuṃ asamatthabhāvaṃ jānantopi ‘‘uttamapurisena saddhiṃ paṭṭhapetvā asakkuṇantassāpi pāsaṃso hotī’’ti ñatvā evamāha. Nagaravāsinopi taṃ sutvā ‘‘asamattho nāma evaṃ na gajjati, addhā ayampi arahā bhavissatī’’ti tassa mahantaṃ sakkāramakaṃsu.
commentary_english:
15. *Pāthikaputto* means "son of Pāthika."

*Jñāṇavādenā* means "together with the doctrine of knowledge (jñāna)."

*Upaḍḍhapatha* means: If a *yojana* ["a stage or Yojana"] could not be between them, Gotama [would be] half a *yojana*, [and] I [would be] half a *yojana*.

This is the way with half a *yojana*, and so on.

Even by transgressing one turn of the foot, victory will occur for the one going, defeat for the one not going.

*Te tatthā* means "we [are] in that place where we have assembled."

*Taddiguṇaṃ taddiguṇāha* means: "I will make it twice as much, twice as much from that." Even knowing the state of being incapable of performing a miracle together with the Blessed One, thinking "even for one not being able to establish [something] together with an excellent person, there is praise," thus he said.

The city dwellers, having heard that, [thought], "The incapable one does not roar like this. Surely, this one will also be an *arhat*." They made a great offering to him.

mula_pali:
16. ‘‘Atha kho, bhaggava, sunakkhatto licchaviputto yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā maṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho, bhaggava, sunakkhatto licchaviputto maṃ etadavoca – ‘acelo, bhante, pāthikaputto vesāliyaṃ paṭivasati lābhaggappatto ceva yasaggappatto ca vajjigāme. So vesāliyaṃ parisati evaṃ vācaṃ bhāsati – samaṇopi gotamo ñāṇavādo, ahampi ñāṇavādo. Ñāṇavādo kho pana ñāṇavādena arahati uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ dassetuṃ. Samaṇo gotamo upaḍḍhapathaṃ āgaccheyya, ahampi upaḍḍhapathaṃ gaccheyyaṃ. Te tattha ubhopi uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ kareyyāma. Ekaṃ ce samaṇo gotamo uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ karissati, dvāhaṃ karissāmi. Dve ce samaṇo gotamo uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyāni karissati, cattārāhaṃ karissāmi. Cattāri ce samaṇo gotamo uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyāni karissati, aṭṭhāhaṃ karissāmi. Iti yāvatakaṃ yāvatakaṃ samaṇo gotamo uttari manussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ karissati, taddiguṇaṃ taddiguṇāhaṃ karissāmī’’ti.

‘‘Evaṃ vutte, ahaṃ, bhaggava, sunakkhattaṃ licchaviputtaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘abhabbo kho, sunakkhatta, acelo pāthikaputto taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā mama sammukhībhāvaṃ āgantuṃ. Sacepissa evamassa – ahaṃ taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā samaṇassa gotamassa sammukhībhāvaṃ gaccheyyanti, muddhāpi tassa vipateyyā’ti.
mula_english:
‘Then Sunakkhatta, son of the Licchavis, came to me, and after paying homage to me, he sat down at one side.

‘Seated at one side, Sunakkhatta, son of the Licchavis, said to me: “Venerable sir, the naked Ājīvika Pāthikaputta is living in Vesālī, and he has gained the foremost gain and the foremost fame in Vajjigāma.

In Vesālī, in the assembly, he speaks thus: “The *śramaṇa* Gotama is a man of wisdom (*jñānavāda*), and I too am a man of wisdom (*jñānavāda*). It is right that a man of wisdom (*jñānavāda*) should show supernormal human states, the miracle of psychic power (*uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ*), through wisdom. If the *śramaṇa* Gotama will come half-way to meet me, l will do likewise. Then we could both work miracles, supernormal human states (*uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ*) there. However many miracles, supernormal human states (*uttari manussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ*) he performs, I will perform twice as many!”

‘When this was said, I said to Sunakkhatta, son of the Licchavis: ”Sunakkhatta, that naked ascetic Pāthikaputta is incapable of meeting me face to face unless he takes back his words, abandons that thought, and gives up that view. If he thinks otherwise—if he thinks: “Without taking back my words, abandoning that thought, and giving up that view, I will go to meet the *śramaṇa* Gotama”—his head will split in pieces.”’
commentary_pali:
16.Yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkamīti ‘‘sunakkhatto kira pāthikaputto evaṃ vadatī’’ti assosi. Athassa hīnajjhāsayattā hīnadassanāya cittaṃ udapādi.

So bhagavato vattaṃ katvā bhagavati gandhakuṭiṃ paviṭṭhe pāthikaputtassa santikaṃ gantvā pucchi ‘‘tumhe kira evarūpiṃ kathaṃ kathethā’’ti? ‘‘Āma, kathemā’’ti. Yadi evaṃ ‘‘mā bhāyittha vissatthā punappunaṃ evaṃ vadatha, ahaṃ samaṇassa gotamassa upaṭṭhāko, tassa visayaṃ vijānāmi, tumhehi saddhiṃ pāṭihāriyaṃ kātuṃ na sakkhissati, ahaṃ samaṇassa gotamassa kathetvā bhayaṃ uppādetvā taṃ aññato gahetvā gamissāmi, tumhe mā bhāyitthā’’ti taṃ assāsetvā bhagavato santikaṃ gato. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkamī’’ti. Taṃ vācantiādīsu ‘‘ahaṃ abuddhova samāno buddhomhīti vicariṃ, abhūtaṃ me kathitaṃ nāhaṃ buddho’’ti vadanto taṃ vācaṃ pajahati nāma. Raho nisīditvā cintayamāno ‘‘ahaṃ ‘ettakaṃ kālaṃ abuddhova samāno buddhomhī’ti vicariṃ, ito dāni paṭṭhāya nāhaṃ buddho’’ti cintayanto taṃ cittaṃ pajahati nāma. ‘‘Ahaṃ ‘ettakaṃ kālaṃ abuddhova samāno buddhomhī’ti pāpakaṃ diṭṭhiṃ gahetvā vicariṃ, ito dāni paṭṭhāya imaṃ diṭṭhiṃ pajahāmī’’ti pajahanto taṃ diṭṭhiṃ paṭinissajjati nāma. Evaṃ akaronto pana taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvāti vuccati. Vipateyyāti bandhanā muttatālapakkaṃ viya gīvato pateyya, sattadhā vā pana phaleyya.

Taṃ vāca Vipateyyā
commentary_english:
16. "I approached him" — he heard, "Sunakkhatta, it seems, Pāthika's son speaks thus."

Then, due to his inferior disposition, a thought arose in his mind for an inferior view.

Then, having made an opportunity for the Blessed One, when the Blessed One had entered the Gandhakuti, he went to Pāthika's son and asked, "Do you speak in such a way?" "Yes, I speak."

If so, "Do not be afraid, be confident, speak thus again and again. I am the attendant of the ascetic Gotama, I know his sphere, he will not be able to perform miracles with you. I will frighten the ascetic Gotama by speaking to him, and having taken him elsewhere, I will go away. Do not be afraid!" Having reassured him, he went to the Blessed One.

Therefore it was said, "I approached him."

Among the *taṃ vāca* etc., "I wandered about, being unawakened, thinking I was awakened, an untruth was spoken by me, I am not awakened," saying thus, he abandons that speech.

Having sat down in private, reflecting, "I wandered about for so long, being unawakened, thinking I was awakened; from now on, I am not awakened," thinking thus, he abandons that thought.

"I wandered about for so long, being unawakened, thinking I was awakened, having grasped an evil view; from now on, I will abandon this view," abandoning thus, he relinquishes that view.

But not doing thus, it is said that he does not abandon that speech, he does not abandon that thought, he does not relinquish that view.

*Vipateyya* means he might fall from the bond as a ripe palmyra fruit falls from its stem, or it might break into seven pieces.

*taṃ vāca vipateyyā*

mula_pali: 17. ‘Rakkhatetaṃ, bhante, bhagavā vācaṃ, rakkhatetaṃ sugato vāca’nti. ‘Kiṃ pana maṃ tvaṃ, sunakkhatta, evaṃ vadesi – rakkhatetaṃ, bhante, bhagavā vācaṃ, rakkhatetaṃ sugato vāca’nti? ‘Bhagavatā cassa, bhante, esā vācā ekaṃsena odhāritā ovāditā (ka.) – abhabbo acelo pāthikaputto taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā mama sammukhībhāvaṃ āgantuṃ. Sacepissa evamassa – ahaṃ taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā samaṇassa gotamassa sammukhībhāvaṃ gaccheyyanti, muddhāpi tassa vipateyyāti. Acelo ca, bhante, pāthikaputto virūparūpena bhagavato sammukhībhāvaṃ āgaccheyya, tadassa bhagavato musā’ti.
mula_english:
17. ‘Lord, let the Blessed Lord have a care what he says, let the Well-Farer have a care what he says!’

“But why do you say this to me, Sunakkhatta: ‘Lord, let the Blessed Lord have a care what he says, let the Well-Farer have a care what he says’?” ‘Because, lord, this statement has been definitively determined by the Blessed One—the naked ascetic Pāthika’s son is incapable of coming into my presence without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, without relinquishing that view.

If he thinks otherwise: “Without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, without relinquishing that view, I might go into the presence of the ascetic Gotama,” his head would split in pieces.’

And the naked ascetic Pāthika’s son might come into the Blessed One’s presence in an altered shape, and thus that would be a lie for the Blessed Lord!”
commentary_pali: 17.Rakkhatetanti rakkhatu etaṃ. Ekaṃsenāti nippariyāyena. Odhāritāti bhāsitā. Aceloca, bhante, pāthikaputtoti evaṃ ekaṃsena bhagavato vācāya odhāritāya sace acelo pāthikaputto. Virūparūpenāti vigatarūpena vigacchitasabhāvena rūpena attano rūpaṃ pahāya adissamānena kāyena. Sīhabyagghādivasena vā vividharūpena sammukhībhāvaṃ āgaccheyya. Tadassa bhagavato musāti evaṃ sante bhagavato taṃ vacanaṃ musā bhaveyyāti musāvādena niggaṇhāti. Ṭhapetvā kira etaṃ na aññena bhagavā musāvādena niggahitapubboti.
commentary_english:
17. "Rakkhatetaṃ" means "rakkhatu etaṃ," may it protect this.

"Ekaṃsenā" means without any alternative (nippariyāyena).

"Odhāritā" means spoken (bhāsitā).

"Acelo ca, bhante, pāthikaputto" means thus, certainly, mendicant, Pāthikaputta; thus, certainly, Pāthikaputta is defined by the word of the Blessed One,

"Virūparūpenā" means by a form that has vanished, by a form whose nature has ceased, by a form, having abandoned his own form, by a body that is invisible.

Or he might approach a state of confrontation with various forms such as a lion or a tiger.

"Tadassa bhagavato musā" means thus, in such a case, that word of the Blessed One would be false; therefore, he refutes by false speech.

Having set this aside, the Blessed One was never before refuted by false speech by another.

mula_pali:
18. ‘Api nu, sunakkhatta, tathāgato taṃ vācaṃ bhāseyya yā sā vācā dvayagāminī’ti? ‘Kiṃ pana, bhante, bhagavatā acelo pāthikaputto cetasā ceto paricca vidito – abhabbo acelo pāthikaputto taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā mama sammukhībhāvaṃ āgantuṃ. Sacepissa evamassa – ahaṃ taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā samaṇassa gotamassa sammukhībhāvaṃ gaccheyyanti, muddhāpi tassa vipateyyā’ti?

‘Udāhu , devatā bhagavato etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ – abhabbo, bhante, acelo pāthikaputto taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā bhagavato sammukhībhāvaṃ āgantuṃ. Sacepissa evamassa – ahaṃ taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā samaṇassa gotamassa sammukhībhāvaṃ gaccheyyanti, muddhāpi tassa vipateyyā’ti?
mula_english:
“Sunakkhatta, would the *tathāgata* utter speech that is duplicitous?”

“But, venerable sir, has the Blessed One known with his mind, having fully considered the mind [of]: ‘The *acela* Pāthikaputta is incapable of coming into my presence without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, without relinquishing that view’?

If he thinks, ‘Without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, without relinquishing that view, I will go into the presence of the *śramaṇa* Gautama,’ his head would split open.”
