“Or, have the *devatās* informed the Blessed One of this matter, [saying]: ‘Venerable sir, the *acela* Pāthikaputta is incapable of coming into the presence of the Blessed One without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, without relinquishing that view.’

If he thinks, ‘Without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, without relinquishing that view, I will go into the presence of the *śramaṇa* Gautama,’ his head would split open."
commentary_pali: 18.Dvayagāminīti sarūpena atthibhāvaṃ, atthena natthibhāvanti evaṃ dvayagāminī. Alikatucchanipphalavācāya etaṃ adhivacanaṃ.
commentary_english: 18. dvayagāminī (dvayagāminī) thus: by form, existence; by meaning, non-existence; thus, *dvayagāminī*. This is a designation for false, empty, and fruitless speech.

mula_pali:
19. ‘Cetasā ceto paricca vidito ceva me, sunakkhatta , acelo pāthikaputto abhabbo acelo pāthikaputto taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā mama sammukhībhāvaṃ āgantuṃ. Sacepissa evamassa – ahaṃ taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā samaṇassa gotamassa sammukhībhāvaṃ gaccheyyanti, muddhāpi tassa vipateyyā’ti.

‘Devatāpi me etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ – abhabbo , bhante, acelo pāthikaputto taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā bhagavato sammukhībhāvaṃ āgantuṃ. Sacepissa evamassa – ahaṃ taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā samaṇassa gotamassa sammukhībhāvaṃ gaccheyyanti, muddhāpi tassa vipateyyā’ti.

‘Ajitopi nāma licchavīnaṃ senāpati adhunā kālaṅkato tāvatiṃsakāyaṃ upapanno. Sopi maṃ upasaṅkamitvā evamārocesi – alajjī, bhante, acelo pāthikaputto; musāvādī, bhante, acelo pāthikaputto. Mampi, bhante, acelo pāthikaputto byākāsi vajjigāme – ajito licchavīnaṃ senāpati mahānirayaṃ upapannoti. Na kho panāhaṃ, bhante, mahānirayaṃ upapanno; tāvatiṃsakāyamhi upapanno. Alajjī, bhante, acelo pāthikaputto; musāvādī, bhante, acelo pāthikaputto; abhabbo ca, bhante, acelo pāthikaputto taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā bhagavato sammukhībhāvaṃ āgantuṃ. Sacepissa evamassa – ahaṃ taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā samaṇassa gotamassa sammukhībhāvaṃ gaccheyyanti, muddhāpi tassa vipateyyā’ti.

‘Iti kho, sunakkhatta, cetasā ceto paricca vidito ceva me acelo pāthikaputto abhabbo acelo pāthikaputto taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā mama sammukhībhāvaṃ āgantuṃ. Sacepissa evamassa – ahaṃ taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā samaṇassa gotamassa sammukhībhāvaṃ gaccheyyanti, muddhāpi tassa vipateyyāti. Devatāpi me etamatthaṃ ārocesuṃ – abhabbo, bhante , acelo pāthikaputto taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā bhagavato sammukhībhāvaṃ āgantuṃ. Sacepissa evamassa – ahaṃ taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā samaṇassa gotamassa sammukhībhāvaṃ gaccheyyanti, muddhāpi tassa vipateyyā’ti.

‘So kho panāhaṃ, sunakkhatta, vesāliyaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātappaṭikkanto yena acelassa pāthikaputtassa ārāmo tenupasaṅkamissāmi divāvihārāya. Yassadāni tvaṃ, sunakkhatta, icchasi, tassa ārocehī’ti.

Iddhipāṭihāriyakathā
mula_english:
19. 'Sunakkhatta, I know by my own mind, that Ācela Pāthikaputta is incapable of meeting me face to face without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, without abandoning that view. If he thinks otherwise – "I will not abandon that speech, I will not abandon that thought, I will not abandon that view," and yet comes to the *śramaṇa* Gautama – his head will split in pieces.’

'Also, a deity announced this matter to me: "Venerable sir, Ācela Pāthikaputta is incapable of meeting the Blessed One face to face without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, without abandoning that view." If he thinks otherwise – "I will not abandon that speech, I will not abandon that thought, I will not abandon that view," and yet comes to the *śramaṇa* Gautama – his head will split in pieces.’

'Ajita, the general of the Licchavis, who recently died, has been reborn in the company of the Thirty-Three Gods. He came to see me and told me: "Venerable sir, Ācela Pāthikaputta is an impudent liar!

Venerable sir, Ācela Pāthikaputta declared in the Vajjian capital: “Ajita, the general of the Licchavis, has been reborn in the great hell!”

But I have not been reborn in the great hell, venerable sir, but in the company of the Thirty-Three Gods. Venerable sir, Ācela Pāthikaputta is an impudent liar! Venerable sir, Ācela Pāthikaputta is a liar! And venerable sir, Ācela Pāthikaputta is incapable of meeting the Blessed One face to face without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, without abandoning that view. If he thinks otherwise – "I will not abandon that speech, I will not abandon that thought, I will not abandon that view," and yet comes to the *śramaṇa* Gautama – his head will split in pieces.’

'Thus, Sunakkhatta, I know by my own mind that Ācela Pāthikaputta is incapable of meeting me face to face without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, without abandoning that view. If he thinks otherwise – "I will not abandon that speech, I will not abandon that thought, I will not abandon that view," and yet comes to the *śramaṇa* Gautama – his head will split in pieces.’

‘A deity announced this matter to me: "Venerable sir, Ācela Pāthikaputta is incapable of meeting the Blessed One face to face without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, without abandoning that view. If he thinks otherwise – "I will not abandon that speech, I will not abandon that thought, I will not abandon that view," and yet comes to the *śramaṇa* Gautama – his head will split in pieces.’

'And now, Sunakkhatta, I will go into Vesali for alms. On my return, after I have eaten, I will go for my midday rest to Pāthikaputta’s park. You may tell him whatever you wish.’

The Discourse on the Miracle of Psychic Power
commentary_pali:
19.Ajitopi nāma licchavīnaṃ senāpatīti so kira bhagavato upaṭṭhāko ahosi, so kālamakāsi. Athassa sarīrakiccaṃ katvā manussā pāthikaputtaṃ pucchiṃsu ‘‘kuhiṃ nibbatto senāpatī’’ti? So āha – ‘‘mahāniraye nibbatto’’ti. Idañca pana vatvā puna āha ‘‘tumhākaṃ senāpati mama santikaṃ āgamma ahaṃ tumhākaṃ vacanamakatvā samaṇassa gotamassa vādaṃ patiṭṭhapetvā niraye nibbattomhī’’ti paroditthāti. Tenupasaṅkami divāvihārāyāti ettha ‘‘pāṭihāriyakaraṇatthāyā’’ti kasmā na vadati? Abhāvā. Sammukhībhāvopi hissa tena saddhiṃ natthi, kuto pāṭihāriyakaraṇaṃ, tasmā tathā avatvā ‘‘divāvihārāyā’’ti āha.

Iddhipāṭihāriyakathāvaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
19. Ajita also, it seems, was the name of a Licchavi general (licchavīnaṃ senāpatī). He was an attendant of the Blessed One (bhagavato upaṭṭhāko), and he died.

Then, having performed the obsequies for him, the people asked Pāthikaputta, "Where was the general reborn (kuhiṃ nibbatto senāpatī)?" He said, "He was reborn in the great hell (mahāniraye nibbatto)."

And further, having said this, he again said, "Your general, having come into my presence, because I did not value your words, but established the doctrine of Gotama the Samaṇa, has been reborn in hell (niraye nibbattomhī)," thus he lamented.

Why does he not say here, "He approached for the sake of the daytime abiding (tenupasaṅkami divāvihārāyā)" as "for the purpose of performing miracles (pāṭihāriyakaraṇatthāyā)"? Because it is not the case.

Even the state of being face-to-face with him does not exist, how much less the performance of miracles? Therefore, not speaking thus, he said, "for the sake of the daytime abiding (divāvihārāyā)."

Description of the miracle of psychic power (iddhipāṭihāriyakathāvaṇṇanā).

mula_pali:
20. ‘‘Atha khvāhaṃ atha kho svāhaṃ (syā.), bhaggava, pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya vesāliṃ piṇḍāya pāvisiṃ. Vesāliyaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātappaṭikkanto yena acelassa pāthikaputtassa ārāmo tenupasaṅkamiṃ divāvihārāya. Atha kho, bhaggava, sunakkhatto licchaviputto taramānarūpo vesāliṃ pavisitvā yena abhiññātā abhiññātā licchavī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā abhiññāte abhiññāte licchavī etadavoca – ‘esāvuso, bhagavā vesāliyaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātappaṭikkanto yena acelassa pāthikaputtassa ārāmo tenupasaṅkami divāvihārāya. Abhikkamathāyasmanto abhikkamathāyasmanto, sādhurūpānaṃ samaṇānaṃ uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ bhavissatī’ti . Atha kho, bhaggava, abhiññātānaṃ abhiññātānaṃ licchavīnaṃ etadahosi – ‘sādhurūpānaṃ kira, bho, samaṇānaṃ uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ bhavissati; handa vata, bho, gacchāmā’ti. Yena ca abhiññātā abhiññātā brāhmaṇamahāsālā gahapatinecayikā nānātitthiyā nānātitthiya (syā.) samaṇabrāhmaṇā tenupasaṅkami. Upasaṅkamitvā abhiññāte abhiññāte nānātitthiye nānātitthiya (syā.) samaṇabrāhmaṇe etadavoca – ‘esāvuso, bhagavā vesāliyaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātappaṭikkanto yena acelassa pāthikaputtassa ārāmo tenupasaṅkami divāvihārāya. Abhikkamathāyasmanto abhikkamathāyasmanto, sādhurūpānaṃ samaṇānaṃ uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ bhavissatī’ti. Atha kho, bhaggava, abhiññātānaṃ abhiññātānaṃ nānātitthiyānaṃ samaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ etadahosi – ‘sādhurūpānaṃ kira, bho, samaṇānaṃ uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ bhavissati; handa vata, bho, gacchāmā’ti.

‘‘Atha kho, bhaggava, abhiññātā abhiññātā licchavī, abhiññātā abhiññātā ca brāhmaṇamahāsālā gahapatinecayikā nānātitthiyā samaṇabrāhmaṇā yena acelassa pāthikaputtassa ārāmo tenupasaṅkamiṃsu. Sā esā, bhaggava, parisā mahā hoti parisā hoti (sī. syā. pī.) anekasatā anekasahassā.

parisā hoti (sī. syā. pī.)
mula_english:
20. Then, Bhaggava, having dressed in the early morning, I took my robe and bowl and went into Vesālī for alms. Having wandered for alms in Vesālī and on my return, after the meal, I went to the park of the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta for my midday rest.

Then, Bhaggava, Sunakkhatta, the Licchavi son, hurrying, entered Vesālī and went to the well-known Licchavis; having approached the well-known Licchavis, he said this: 'This, friends (āvuso), the Blessed One (bhagavā), having wandered for alms in Vesālī, after the meal, on his return from the alms round, has gone to the park of the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta for his midday rest. Come along, venerable ones (āyasmanto), come along, venerable ones! A superhuman state, a wonder of psychic power (iddhi-pāṭihāriyaṃ), will occur for the well-formed ascetics!'

Then, Bhaggava, it occurred to the well-known Licchavis: 'A superhuman state, a wonder of psychic power, will occur for the well-formed ascetics! Come, friends, let us go!'

And those well-known wealthy Brahmins (brāhmaṇamahāsālā), householders (gahapatinecayikā), and ascetics and Brahmins (samaṇabrāhmaṇā) of various schools (nānātitthiyā) went to him.

Having approached the well-known ascetics and Brahmins of various schools, he said this: 'This, friends, the Blessed One, having wandered for alms in Vesālī, after the meal, on his return from the alms round, has gone to the park of the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta for his midday rest. Come along, venerable ones, come along, venerable ones! A superhuman state, a wonder of psychic power will occur for the well-formed ascetics!'

Then, Bhaggava, it occurred to the well-known ascetics and Brahmins of various schools: 'A superhuman state, a wonder of psychic power will occur for the well-formed ascetics! Come, friends, let us go!'

Then, Bhaggava, the well-known Licchavis, the well-known wealthy Brahmins, the prominent householders, and the ascetics and Brahmins of various schools went to the park of the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta.

That assembly, Bhaggava, was a great assembly, numbering many hundreds, many thousands.
commentary_pali: 20.Gahapatinecayikāti gahapati mahāsālā. Tesañhi mahādhanadhaññanicayo, tasmā ‘‘necayikā’’ti vuccanti. Anekasahassāti sahassehipi aparimāṇagaṇanā. Evaṃ mahatiṃ kira parisaṃ ṭhapetvā sunakkhattaṃ añño sannipātetuṃ samattho natthi. Teneva bhagavā ettakaṃ kālaṃ sunakkhattaṃ gahetvā vicari.
commentary_english:
20. *Gahapatinecayikā*: *gahapati mahāsālā*.

Because they have stores of great wealth and grain; therefore, they are called "accumulators" (*necayikā*).

*Anekasahassā*: an unreckonable number, even by thousands.

Thus, having established such a great assembly, no one else is capable of convening Sunakkhatta.

Therefore, the Blessed One kept Sunakkhatta for so long.

mula_pali:
21. ‘‘Assosi kho, bhaggava, acelo pāthikaputto – ‘abhikkantā kira abhiññātā abhiññātā licchavī, abhikkantā abhiññātā abhiññātā ca brāhmaṇamahāsālā gahapatinecayikā nānātitthiyā samaṇabrāhmaṇā. Samaṇopi gotamo mayhaṃ ārāme divāvihāraṃ nisinno’ti. Sutvānassa bhayaṃ chambhitattaṃ lomahaṃso udapādi. Atha kho, bhaggava, acelo pāthikaputto bhīto saṃviggo lomahaṭṭhajāto yena tindukakhāṇuparibbājakārāmo tenupasaṅkami.

‘‘Assosi kho, bhaggava, sā parisā – ‘acelo kira pāthikaputto bhīto saṃviggo lomahaṭṭhajāto yena tindukakhāṇuparibbājakārāmo tenupasaṅkanto’ti tenupasaṅkamanto (sī. pī. ka.). Atha kho, bhaggava, sā parisā aññataraṃ purisaṃ āmantesi –

tenupasaṅkamanto (sī. pī. ka.)

‘Ehi tvaṃ, bho purisa, yena tindukakhāṇuparibbājakārāmo, yena acelo pāthikaputto tenupasaṅkama. Upasaṅkamitvā acelaṃ pāthikaputtaṃ evaṃ vadehi – abhikkamāvuso, pāthikaputta, abhikkantā abhiññātā abhiññātā licchavī, abhikkantā abhiññātā abhiññātā ca brāhmaṇamahāsālā gahapatinecayikā nānātitthiyā samaṇabrāhmaṇā, samaṇopi gotamo āyasmato ārāme divāvihāraṃ nisinno; bhāsitā kho pana te esā, āvuso pāthikaputta, vesāliyaṃ parisati vācā samaṇopi gotamo ñāṇavādo, ahampi ñāṇavādo. Ñāṇavādo kho pana ñāṇavādena arahati uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ dassetuṃ. Samaṇo gotamo upaḍḍhapathaṃ āgaccheyya ahampi upaḍḍhapathaṃ gaccheyyaṃ. Te tattha ubhopi uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ kareyyāma. Ekaṃ ce samaṇo gotamo uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ karissati, dvāhaṃ karissāmi. Dve ce samaṇo gotamo uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyāni karissati, cattārāhaṃ karissāmi. Cattāri ce samaṇo gotamo uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyāni karissati , aṭṭhāhaṃ karissāmi. Iti yāvatakaṃ yāvatakaṃ samaṇo gotamo uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ karissati, taddiguṇaṃ taddiguṇāhaṃ karissāmī’ti abhikkamasseva abhikkamayeva (sī. syā. pī.) kho; āvuso pāthikaputta, upaḍḍhapathaṃ. Sabbapaṭhamaṃyeva āgantvā samaṇo gotamo āyasmato ārāme divāvihāraṃ nisinno’ti.

abhikkamayeva (sī. syā. pī.)
mula_english:
21. Bhaggava, Pāthikaputta the ascetic heard: ‘The Licchavis are coming in great numbers; the wealthy brahmins and householders, followers of other sects, ascetics, and brahmins are coming in great numbers. The ascetic Gotama is sitting in my park for his midday rest.’ On hearing this, he was overcome with fear and trembling, and his hair stood on end. Then, Bhaggava, Pāthikaputta the ascetic, terrified and trembling, his hair standing on end, went to the Tinduka lodging of the wanderers.

Bhaggava, the assembled company heard that he had gone to the Tinduka lodging of the wanderers. Then, Bhaggava, that assembled company addressed a certain man:

‘Come, fellow, go to the Tinduka lodging of the wanderers, where Pāthikaputta the ascetic is. On arrival, tell Pāthikaputta the ascetic: “Friend Pāthikaputta, come along! The Licchavis are coming in great numbers; the wealthy brahmins and householders, followers of other sects, ascetics, and brahmins are coming in great numbers. The ascetic Gotama is sitting in Your Reverence’s park for his midday rest. Because you declared to the assembly at Vesali: ‘The ascetic Gotama claims to be a man of wisdom (jñānavāda), and I make the same claim. It is right that a man of wisdom (jñānavāda) should show it by performing miracles (uttarimanussadhamma iddhipāṭihāriya). If the ascetic Gotama will come half-way to meet me (upaḍḍhapatha), I will do likewise. Then we could both work miracles (uttarimanussadhamma iddhipāṭihāriya). However many miracles (uttarimanussadhamma iddhipāṭihāriya) he performs, I will perform twice as many!’” Friend Pāthikaputta, he is already half-way here. So now come half-way: the ascetic Gotama has already come half-way to meet you, and is sitting for his midday rest in Your Reverence’s park.’”
commentary_pali:
21.Bhayanti cittutrāsabhayaṃ. Chambhitattanti sakalasarīracalanaṃ. Lomahaṃsoti lomānaṃ uddhaggabhāvo. So kira cintesi – ‘‘ahaṃ atimahantaṃ kathaṃ kathetvā sadevake loke aggapuggalena saddhiṃ paṭiviruddho, mayhaṃ kho panabbhantare arahattaṃ vā pāṭihāriyakaraṇahetu vā natthi, samaṇo pana gotamo pāṭihāriyaṃ karissati, athassa pāṭihāriyaṃ disvā mahājano ‘tvaṃ dāni pāṭihāriyaṃ kātuṃ asakkonto kasmā attano pamāṇamajānitvā loke aggapuggalena saddhiṃ paṭimallo hutvā gajjasī’ti kaṭṭhaleḍḍudaṇḍādīhi viheṭhessatī’’ti. Tenassa mahājanasannipātañceva tena bhagavato ca āgamanaṃ sutvā bhayaṃ vā chambhitattaṃ vā lomahaṃso vā udapādi. So tato dukkhā muccitukāmo tindukakhāṇukaparibbājakārāmaṃ agamāsi. Tamatthaṃ dassetuṃ atha kho bhagavātiādimāha . Tattha upasaṅkamīti na kevalaṃ upasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā pana dūraṃ aḍḍhayojanantaraṃ paribbājakārāmaṃ paviṭṭho. Tatthapi cittassādaṃ alabhamāno antantena āvijjhitvā ārāmapaccante ekaṃ gahanaṭṭhānaṃ upadhāretvā pāsāṇaphalake nisīdi. Atha bhagavā cintesi – ‘‘sace ayaṃ bālo kassacideva kathaṃ gahetvā idhāgaccheyya, mā nassatu bālo’’ti ‘‘nisinnapāsāṇaphalakaṃ tassa sarīre allīnaṃ hotū’’ti adhiṭṭhāsi. Saha adhiṭṭhānacittena taṃ tassa sarīre allīyi. So mahāaddubandhanabaddho viya chinnapādo viya ca ahosi.

Assosīti ito cito ca pāthikaputtaṃ pariyesamānā parisā tassa anupadaṃ gantvā nisinnaṭṭhānaṃ ñatvā āgatena aññatarena purisena ‘‘tumhe kaṃ pariyesathā’’ti vutte pāthikaputtanti. So ‘‘tindukakhāṇukaparibbājakārāme nisinno’’ti vuttavacanena assosi.

Assosī
commentary_english:
21. "Fear" (bhaya) means fear and trembling of the mind (cittutrāsabhayaṃ).

"Agitation" (chambhitatta) means the movement of the entire body (sakalasarīracalanaṃ).

"Horripilation" (lomahaṃsa) means the rising of the hairs of the body (lomānaṃ uddhaggabhāvo).

He reflected: "How can I, being in conflict with the foremost individual (aggapuggalena) in the world (loke) with its gods (sadevake), speak (kathetvā) of something very great (atimahantaṃ)? I have no attainment of Arhatship (arahattaṃ) within me, nor any cause for performing miracles (pāṭihāriyakaraṇahetu), but the renunciate (samaṇo) Gotama will perform a miracle (pāṭihāriyaṃ karissati). Having seen his miracle, the great assembly (mahājano) will say, ‘Since you are now unable to perform a miracle, why, not knowing your own measure (attano pamāṇaṃajānitvā), did you roar (gajjasī) having become a rival (paṭimallo) to the foremost individual (aggapuggalena) in the world (loke)?’ They will harass (viheṭhessati) me with sticks, clods, staffs, and so on (kaṭṭhaleḍḍudaṇḍādīhi.”

Hearing (sutvā) of the arrival (āgamanaṃ) of the Blessed One (bhagavato), fear (bhayaṃ), agitation (chambhitattaṃ) or horripilation (lomahaṃso) arose (udapādi) in him due to that great assembly (mahājanasannipātañceva).

He, desiring to be freed from suffering ( dukkhā muccitukāmo), went to the Tindukakhāṇukaparibbājakārāma.

To show that meaning, he said, "Then, the Blessed One (atha kho bhagavā)" etc.

There, "approached" (upasaṅkamīti) means not only did he approach (upasaṅkami), but having approached (upasaṅkamitvā), he entered (paviṭṭho) the Paribbājakārāma, a distance of half a yojana (aḍḍhayojanantaraṃ).

Even there, not obtaining delight of mind (cittassādaṃ alabhamāno), wandering about in the interior (antantena āvijjhitvā), he discerned (upadhāretvā) a solitary (ekaṃ) dense (gahana) spot (ṭhānaṃ) at the edge of the park (ārāmapaccante) and sat down (nisīdi) on a stone slab (pāsāṇaphalake).

Then the Blessed One (bhagavā) thought (cintesi): “If this fool (bālo) were to go anywhere else (kassacideva kathaṃ gahetvā) from here (idhāgaccheyya), may the fool (bālo) not be lost (mā nassatu)!” He determined (adhiṭṭhāsi): “May the stone slab (nisinnapāsāṇaphalakaṃ) be stuck (allīnaṃ hotū) to his body (tassa sarīre)!”

With the thought of determination (adhiṭṭhānacittena), it stuck (allīyi) to his body (tassa sarīre).

He was like (viya) someone bound (baddho) by a great chain (mahāaddubandhana), or like (viya ca) someone with severed feet (chinnapādo).

"Heard" (assosīti): the assembly (parisā), seeking (pariyesamānā) Pāthikaputta here and there (ito cito ca pāthikaputtaṃ), went to (gantvā) his immediate vicinity (anupadaṃ), and having learned (ñatvā) the place where he was sitting (nisinnaṭṭhānaṃ), when it was said (vutte) by a certain man (aññatarena purisena) who had come (āgatena), “Whom are you seeking (tumhe kaṃ pariyesathā)?” they said, “Pāthikaputta.”

He heard (assosi) by the spoken word (vuttavacanena), "He is sitting (nisinno) in the Tindukakhāṇukaparibbājakārāma."

Heard (assosī).

mula_pali:
22. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhoti kho, bhaggava, so puriso tassā parisāya paṭissutvā yena tindukakhāṇuparibbājakārāmo, yena acelo pāthikaputto tenupasaṅkami. Upasaṅkamitvā acelaṃ pāthikaputtaṃ etadavoca – ‘abhikkamāvuso pāthikaputta, abhikkantā abhiññātā abhiññātā licchavī, abhikkantā abhiññātā abhiññātā ca brāhmaṇamahāsālā gahapatinecayikā nānātitthiyā samaṇabrāhmaṇā. Samaṇopi gotamo āyasmato ārāme divāvihāraṃ nisinno. Bhāsitā kho pana te esā, āvuso pāthikaputta, vesāliyaṃ parisati vācā – samaṇopi gotamo ñāṇavādo; ahampi ñāṇavādo. Ñāṇavādo kho pana ñāṇavādena arahati uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ dassetuṃ…pe… taddiguṇaṃ taddiguṇāhaṃ karissāmīti. Abhikkamasseva kho, āvuso pāthikaputta, upaḍḍhapathaṃ. Sabbapaṭhamaṃyeva āgantvā samaṇo gotamo āyasmato ārāme divāvihāraṃ nisinno’ti.

‘‘Evaṃ vutte, bhaggava, acelo pāthikaputto ‘āyāmi āvuso, āyāmi āvuso’ti vatvā tattheva saṃsappati saṃsabbati (ka.), na sakkoti āsanāpi vuṭṭhātuṃ. Atha kho so, bhaggava, puriso acelaṃ pāthikaputtaṃ etadavoca – ‘kiṃ su nāma te, āvuso pāthikaputta, pāvaḷā su nāma te pīṭhakasmiṃ allīnā, pīṭhakaṃ su nāma te pāvaḷāsu allīnaṃ? Āyāmi āvuso, āyāmi āvusoti vatvā tattheva saṃsappasi, na sakkosi āsanāpi vuṭṭhātu’nti. Evampi kho, bhaggava, vuccamāno acelo pāthikaputto ‘āyāmi āvuso, āyāmi āvuso’ti vatvā tattheva saṃsappati , na sakkoti āsanāpi vuṭṭhātuṃ.

saṃsabbati (ka.)
mula_english:
“Bhaggava, that man, having promised that to that assembly, approached the park of the wanderer Tindukakhāṇu, where the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta was. Approaching the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta, he said this: ‘Friend Pāthikaputta, come forth! The Licchavis have come, they are well-known, they are recognized; and the wealthy Brahmin householders and ascetics and Brahmins of various sects have come, they are well-known, they are recognized. The ascetic Gotama has also come and is sitting in Your Reverence’s park for his midday rest. This statement was spoken by you, friend Pāthikaputta, in the assembly at Vesālī: ‘The ascetic Gotama claims to be a man of wisdom; and I too am a man of wisdom. A man of wisdom should demonstrate superhuman powers and miracles to a man of wisdom… and I will do twice as much, twice as much as him.’ Just come halfway, friend Pāthikaputta. The ascetic Gotama has arrived before everyone else and is sitting in Your Reverence’s park for his midday rest.’

“When this was said, the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta, said ‘I’m coming, friend, I’m coming, friend,’ but he just wriggled about right there, and couldn’t even get up from his seat. Then that man said this to the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta: ‘Friend Pāthikaputta, are your feet stuck to the seat, or is the seat stuck to your feet? You say, “I’m coming, friend, I’m coming, friend,” but you just wriggle about right there, and can’t even get up from your seat!’

“And even when he was spoken to in this way, the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta said ‘I’m coming, friend, I’m coming, friend,’ but he just wriggled about right there, and couldn’t even get up from his seat.
commentary_pali: 22.Saṃsappatīti osīdati. Tattheva sañcarati. Pāvaḷā vuccati ānisadaṭṭhikā.
commentary_english: 22. *Saṃsappatī* means "it sinks down." There it moves around. *Pāvaḷā* is said to be the anus-bone (ānisadaṭṭhikā).

mula_pali:
23. ‘‘Yadā kho so, bhaggava, puriso aññāsi – ‘parābhūtarūpo ayaṃ acelo pāthikaputto. Āyāmi āvuso, āyāmi āvusoti vatvā tattheva saṃsappati, na sakkoti āsanāpi vuṭṭhātu’nti. Atha taṃ parisaṃ āgantvā evamārocesi – ‘parābhūtarūpo, bho parābhūtarūpo bho ayaṃ (syā. ka.), parābhūtarūpo (sī. pī.), acelo pāthikaputto. Āyāmi āvuso, āyāmi āvusoti vatvā tattheva saṃsappati, na sakkoti āsanāpi vuṭṭhātu’nti. Evaṃ vutte, ahaṃ, bhaggava, taṃ parisaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘abhabbo kho, āvuso, acelo pāthikaputto taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā mama sammukhībhāvaṃ āgantuṃ. Sacepissa evamassa – ‘ahaṃ taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā samaṇassa gotamassa sammukhībhāvaṃ gaccheyya’nti, muddhāpi tassa vipateyyāti.

Paṭhamabhāṇavāro niṭṭhito.
mula_english:
23. ‘And when that man realized that Pāthikaputta was defeated, he went back to the assembly and reported the situation.

‘I’m coming, friend, I’m coming‘, but he only wriggles and can’t get up from his seat.

Then he went to that assembly and announced: ‘Pāthikaputta the naked ascetic is defeated.

‘I’m coming, friend, I’m coming‘, but he only wriggles and can’t get up from his seat.

When this was said, I said to that assembly: ‘The naked ascetic Pāthikaputta is incapable of coming into my presence unless he abandons that statement, abandons that thought, and relinquishes that view.

And if he thinks: ‘Without abandoning that statement, without abandoning that thought, without relinquishing that view, I will come into the presence of the *śramaṇa* Gautama,’ his head would split open.’

The first *bhāṇavāra* is finished.
commentary_pali: 23.Parābhūtarūpoti parājitarūpo, vinaṭṭharūpo vā.
commentary_english: [23.] *Parābhūtarūpa*, means *parājitarūpa*, or *vinaṭṭharūpa*.

mula_pali:
24. ‘‘Atha kho, bhaggava, aññataro licchavimahāmatto uṭṭhāyāsanā taṃ parisaṃ etadavoca – ‘tena hi, bho, muhuttaṃ tāva āgametha, yāvāhaṃ gacchāmi paccāgacchāmi (?). Appeva nāma ahampi sakkuṇeyyaṃ acelaṃ pāthikaputtaṃ imaṃ parisaṃ ānetu’nti.

‘‘Atha kho so, bhaggava, licchavimahāmatto yena tindukakhāṇuparibbājakārāmo, yena acelo pāthikaputto tenupasaṅkami. Upasaṅkamitvā acelaṃ pāthikaputtaṃ etadavoca – ‘abhikkamāvuso pāthikaputta, abhikkantaṃ te seyyo, abhikkantā abhiññātā abhiññātā licchavī, abhikkantā abhiññātā abhiññātā ca brāhmaṇamahāsālā gahapatinecayikā nānātitthiyā samaṇabrāhmaṇā. Samaṇopi gotamo āyasmato ārāme divāvihāraṃ nisinno. Bhāsitā kho pana te esā, āvuso pāthikaputta, vesāliyaṃ parisati vācā – samaṇopi gotamo ñāṇavādo…pe… taddiguṇaṃ taddiguṇāhaṃ karissāmīti. Abhikkamasseva kho, āvuso pāthikaputta, upaḍḍhapathaṃ. Sabbapaṭhamaṃyeva āgantvā samaṇo gotamo āyasmato ārāme divāvihāraṃ nisinno. Bhāsitā kho panesā, āvuso pāthikaputta, samaṇena gotamena parisati vācā – abhabbo kho acelo pāthikaputto taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā mama sammukhībhāvaṃ āgantuṃ. Sacepissa evamassa – ahaṃ taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā samaṇassa gotamassa sammukhībhāvaṃ gaccheyyanti, muddhāpi tassa vipateyyāti. Abhikkamāvuso pāthikaputta, abhikkamaneneva te jayaṃ karissāma, samaṇassa gotamassa parājaya’nti.

‘‘Evaṃ vutte, bhaggava, acelo pāthikaputto ‘āyāmi āvuso, āyāmi āvuso’ti vatvā tattheva saṃsappati, na sakkoti āsanāpi vuṭṭhātuṃ. Atha kho so, bhaggava, licchavimahāmatto acelaṃ pāthikaputtaṃ etadavoca – ‘kiṃ su nāma te, āvuso pāthikaputta, pāvaḷā su nāma te pīṭhakasmiṃ allīnā, pīṭhakaṃ su nāma te pāvaḷāsu allīnaṃ ? Āyāmi āvuso, āyāmi āvusoti vatvā tattheva saṃsappasi, na sakkosi āsanāpi vuṭṭhātu’nti . Evampi kho, bhaggava, vuccamāno acelo pāthikaputto ‘āyāmi āvuso, āyāmi āvuso’ti vatvā tattheva saṃsappati, na sakkoti āsanāpi vuṭṭhātuṃ.
mula_english:
24. “Then, Bhaggava, a certain high-ranking Licchavi official, getting up from his seat, said to that assembly: ‘In that case, good sirs, wait just a moment, while I go to see whether I can bring Pāthikaputta to this assembly.’

“Then that high-ranking Licchavi official went to the Tinduka rest-house for wanderers, where Pāthikaputta was. Having gone there, he said to Pāthikaputta: ‘Come along, friend Pāthikaputta, it would be better for you to come along! The Licchavis, who are well-known and distinguished, have come; the wealthy and distinguished brahmins and householders have come, as well as ascetics and brahmins of various schools. The ascetic Gotama is sitting in Your Reverence’s park for his midday rest. And this statement has been made about you, friend Pāthikaputta, in the assembly at Vesālī: “The ascetic Gotama claims to be a man of wisdom… and I will make him twice as wise.” You have only come half-way, friend Pāthikaputta. The ascetic Gotama has come to Your Reverence’s park to take his midday rest before anyone else. And this statement was made by the ascetic Gotama in the assembly: “The naked ascetic Pāthikaputta is incapable of coming into my presence without abandoning that statement, without abandoning that thought, without abandoning that view. If he should think otherwise—that he could come into the presence of the ascetic Gotama without abandoning that statement, without abandoning that thought, without abandoning that view—his head would split in pieces.” Come along, friend Pāthikaputta, by coming we will make you the winner, and the ascetic Gotama the loser.’

“When this was said, Bhaggava, the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta, saying ‘I’m coming, friend, I’m coming,’ just wriggled about there, but was unable to get up from his seat. Then that high-ranking Licchavi official said to Pāthikaputta: ‘What’s the matter with you, friend Pāthikaputta? Is your bottom stuck to the seat, or is the seat stuck to your bottom? You say, “I’m coming, friend, I’m coming,” but you just wriggle about there and are unable to get up from your seat!’ Even when he was being told this, the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta, saying ‘I’m coming, friend, I’m coming,’ just wriggled about there, but was unable to get up from his seat.

mula_pali: 25. ‘‘Yadā kho so, bhaggava, licchavimahāmatto aññāsi – ‘parābhūtarūpo ayaṃ acelo pāthikaputto āyāmi āvuso, āyāmi āvusoti vatvā tattheva saṃsappati, na sakkoti āsanāpi vuṭṭhātu’nti. Atha taṃ parisaṃ āgantvā evamārocesi – ‘parābhūtarūpo, bho parābhūtarūpo (sī. pī.), parābhūtarūpo ayaṃ (syā.), acelo pāthikaputto āyāmi āvuso, āyāmi āvusoti vatvā tattheva saṃsappati, na sakkoti āsanāpi vuṭṭhātu’nti. Evaṃ vutte, ahaṃ, bhaggava, taṃ parisaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘abhabbo kho, āvuso, acelo pāthikaputto taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā mama sammukhībhāvaṃ āgantuṃ. Sacepissa evamassa – ahaṃ taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā samaṇassa gotamassa sammukhībhāvaṃ gaccheyyanti, muddhāpi tassa vipateyya. Sace pāyasmantānaṃ licchavīnaṃ evamassa – mayaṃ acelaṃ pāthikaputtaṃ varattāhi yāhi varattāhi (syā. ka.) bandhitvā goyugehi āviñcheyyāmāti āviñjeyyāmāti (syā.), āvijjheyyāmāti (sī. pī.), tā varattā chijjeyyuṃ pāthikaputto vā. Abhabbo pana acelo pāthikaputto taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā mama sammukhībhāvaṃ āgantuṃ. Sacepissa evamassa – ahaṃ taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā samaṇassa gotamassa sammukhībhāvaṃ gaccheyyanti, muddhāpi tassa vipateyyā’ti.
mula_english:
25. Furthermore, Bhaggava, when the Licchavi high official realized, "This naked ascetic, Pāthika's son, is in a state of defeat, [saying] 'I'm coming, friend, I'm coming,'" and wriggles right there, unable to rise even from his seat.

Then, coming to that assembly, he announced, "This naked ascetic, Pāthika's son, is in a state of defeat, [saying] 'I'm coming, friend, I'm coming,'" and wriggles right there, unable to rise even from his seat."

When this was said, I, Bhaggava, said to that assembly: "The naked ascetic Pāthika's son is incapable of coming into my presence without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, without relinquishing that view."

"If he were to think, 'Without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, without relinquishing that view, I will come into the presence of the *śramaṇa* Gotama,' his head would split."

"If the venerable Licchavis were to think, 'Let us bind the naked ascetic Pāthika's son with straps and drag him with a team of oxen,' either the straps would break or Pāthika's son [would break free]."

Moreover, the naked ascetic Pāthika's son is incapable of coming into my presence without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, without relinquishing that view.

"If he were to think, 'Without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, without relinquishing that view, I will come into the presence of the *śramaṇa* Gotama,' his head would split."
commentary_pali: 25.Goyugehīti goyuttehi satamattehi vā sahassamattehi vā yugehi. Āviñcheyyāmāti ākaḍḍheyyāma. Chijjeyyunti chindeyyuṃ. Pāthikaputto vā bandhaṭṭhāne chijjeyya.
commentary_english:
25. "With cows yoked," that is, with cows yoked, with hundreds yoked, or with thousands yoked.

"We might pull," that is, we might draw [it].

"They might be cut," that is, they might cut.

The son of Pāthika, or he might be cut in the place of binding.

mula_pali:
26. ‘‘Atha kho, bhaggava, jāliyo dārupattikantevāsī uṭṭhāyāsanā taṃ parisaṃ etadavoca – ‘tena hi, bho, muhuttaṃ tāva āgametha, yāvāhaṃ gacchāmi; appeva nāma ahampi sakkuṇeyyaṃ acelaṃ pāthikaputtaṃ imaṃ parisaṃ ānetu’’nti.

‘‘Atha kho, bhaggava, jāliyo dārupattikantevāsī yena tindukakhāṇuparibbājakārāmo, yena acelo pāthikaputto tenupasaṅkami. Upasaṅkamitvā acelaṃ pāthikaputtaṃ etadavoca – ‘abhikkamāvuso pāthikaputta, abhikkantaṃ te seyyo. Abhikkantā abhiññātā abhiññātā licchavī, abhikkantā abhiññātā abhiññātā ca brāhmaṇamahāsālā gahapatinecayikā nānātitthiyā samaṇabrāhmaṇā. Samaṇopi gotamo āyasmato ārāme divāvihāraṃ nisinno. Bhāsitā kho pana te esā, āvuso pāthikaputta, vesāliyaṃ parisati vācā – samaṇopi gotamo ñāṇavādo…pe… taddiguṇaṃ taddiguṇāhaṃ karissāmīti. Abhikkamasseva, kho āvuso pāthikaputta, upaḍḍhapathaṃ. Sabbapaṭhamaṃyeva āgantvā samaṇo gotamo āyasmato ārāme divāvihāraṃ nisinno. Bhāsitā kho panesā, āvuso pāthikaputta, samaṇena gotamena parisati vācā – abhabbo acelo pāthikaputto taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā mama sammukhībhāvaṃ āgantuṃ. Sacepissa evamassa – ahaṃ taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā samaṇassa gotamassa sammukhībhāvaṃ gaccheyyanti, muddhāpi tassa vipateyya. Sace pāyasmantānaṃ licchavīnaṃ evamassa – mayaṃ acelaṃ pāthikaputtaṃ varattāhi bandhitvā goyugehi āviñcheyyāmāti. Tā varattā chijjeyyuṃ pāthikaputto vā. Abhabbo pana acelo pāthikaputto taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā mama sammukhībhāvaṃ āgantuṃ. Sacepissa evamassa – ahaṃ taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā samaṇassa gotamassa sammukhībhāvaṃ āgaccheyyanti, muddhāpi tassa vipateyyāti. Abhikkamāvuso pāthikaputta, abhikkamaneneva te jayaṃ karissāma, samaṇassa gotamassa parājaya’nti.

‘‘Evaṃ vutte, bhaggava, acelo pāthikaputto ‘āyāmi āvuso, āyāmi āvuso’ti vatvā tattheva saṃsappati, na sakkoti āsanāpi vuṭṭhātuṃ. Atha kho, bhaggava, jāliyo dārupattikantevāsī acelaṃ pāthikaputtaṃ etadavoca – ‘kiṃ su nāma te, āvuso pāthikaputta, pāvaḷā su nāma te pīṭhakasmiṃ allīnā, pīṭhakaṃ su nāma te pāvaḷāsu allīnaṃ? Āyāmi āvuso, āyāmi āvusoti vatvā tattheva saṃsappasi, na sakkosi āsanāpi vuṭṭhātu’nti. Evampi kho, bhaggava, vuccamāno acelo pāthikaputto ‘‘āyāmi āvuso, āyāmi āvuso’’ti vatvā tattheva saṃsappati, na sakkoti āsanāpi vuṭṭhātunti.
mula_english:
26. “Then, Bhaggava, Jāliya, the pupil of the wooden-bowl ascetic, rose from his seat and said to that assembly: ‘In that case, good sirs, wait just a moment while I go; perhaps I might be able to bring Pāthikaputta, the naked ascetic, to this assembly.’”

“Then, Bhaggava, Jāliya, the pupil of the wooden-bowl ascetic, went to the Tinduka lodging of the wanderers, where Pāthikaputta, the naked ascetic, was. Having gone there, he said to Pāthikaputta, the naked ascetic: ‘Come along, friend Pāthikaputta, it is better for you to come. The eminent Licchavis have come, and the eminent wealthy *brāhmaṇas* and householders, the ascetics and *brāhmaṇas* of various schools have come. The *śramaṇa* Gotama is sitting in Your Reverence’s park for his midday rest. Because you declared to the assembly at Vesālī: “The *śramaṇa* Gotama claims to be a man of wisdom… and I will make that twice as much again.” You are already half way there, friend Pāthikaputta. The *śramaṇa* Gotama has come first, and is sitting in Your Reverence’s park for his midday rest. But this was declared by the *śramaṇa* Gotama to the assembly: “Pāthikaputta, the naked ascetic, is not capable of meeting me face to face without abandoning that statement, without abandoning that thought, without abandoning that view. And if he thinks otherwise, his head will split in pieces. If the good Licchavis were to think: ‘Let us bind Pāthikaputta, the naked ascetic, with thongs and try to drag him with yoked oxen!’, those thongs would burst or Pāthikaputta would. Pāthikaputta, the naked ascetic, is not capable of meeting me face to face without abandoning that statement, without abandoning that thought, without abandoning that view. And if he thinks otherwise, his head will split in pieces.” Come along, friend Pāthikaputta, if you come, we will make you the winner and let the *śramaṇa* Gotama be defeated.’"

“When this was said, Bhaggava, Pāthikaputta, the naked ascetic, said: ‘I’m coming, friend, I’m coming,’ but wriggled about on the spot, and was unable to get up from his seat. Then, Bhaggava, Jāliya, the pupil of the wooden-bowl ascetic, said to Pāthikaputta, the naked ascetic: ‘Friend Pāthikaputta, have you got coral stuck to your seat, or has the seat got coral stuck to you? You keep saying: “I’m coming, friend, I’m coming”, but you only wriggle and can’t get up from your seat.’ Even at these words, Bhaggava, Pāthikaputta, the naked ascetic, still wriggled about, but could not rise.
commentary_pali: 26.Dārupattikantevāsīti dārupattikassa antevāsī. Tassa kira etadahosi ‘‘tiṭṭhatu tāva pāṭihāriyaṃ, samaṇo gotamo ‘acelo pāthikaputto āsanāpi na vuṭṭhahissatī’ti āha. Handāhaṃ gantvā yena kenaci upāyena taṃ āsanā vuṭṭhāpemi. Ettāvatā ca samaṇassa gotamassa parājayo bhavissatī’’ti. Tasmā evamāha.
commentary_english:
Dārupattikantevāsī means a pupil of Dārupattika.

The thought then occurred to him: "Let the miracle be for now. The ascetic Gotama, the naked follower of the Pāthika, has said he will not rise from his seat.

Come now, I will go and by some means or other, I will make him rise from his seat.

By this much, the ascetic Gotama will be defeated."

Therefore, he spoke thus.

mula_pali:
27. ‘‘Yadā kho, bhaggava, jāliyo dārupattikantevāsī aññāsi – ‘parābhūtarūpo ayaṃ acelo pāthikaputto ‘āyāmi āvuso, āyāmi āvusoti vatvā tattheva saṃsappati, na sakkoti āsanāpi vuṭṭhātu’nti, atha naṃ etadavoca –

‘Bhūtapubbaṃ, āvuso pāthikaputta, sīhassa migarañño etadahosi – yaṃnūnāhaṃ aññataraṃ vanasaṇḍaṃ nissāya āsayaṃ kappeyyaṃ. Tatrāsayaṃ kappetvā sāyanhasamayaṃ āsayā nikkhameyyaṃ, āsayā nikkhamitvā vijambheyyaṃ, vijambhitvā samantā catuddisā anuvilokeyyaṃ, samantā catuddisā anuviloketvā tikkhattuṃ sīhanādaṃ nadeyyaṃ, tikkhattuṃ sīhanādaṃ naditvā gocarāya pakkameyyaṃ. So varaṃ varaṃ migasaṃghe migasaṃghaṃ (syā. ka.) vadhitvā mudumaṃsāni mudumaṃsāni bhakkhayitvā tameva āsayaṃ ajjhupeyya’nti.

migasaṃghaṃ (syā. ka.)

‘Atha kho, āvuso, so sīho migarājā aññataraṃ vanasaṇḍaṃ nissāya āsayaṃ kappesi. Tatrāsayaṃ kappetvā sāyanhasamayaṃ āsayā nikkhami, āsayā nikkhamitvā vijambhi, vijambhitvā samantā catuddisā anuvilokesi, samantā catuddisā anuviloketvā tikkhattuṃ sīhanādaṃ nadi, tikkhattuṃ sīhanādaṃ naditvā gocarāya pakkāmi. So varaṃ varaṃ migasaṅghe vadhitvā mudumaṃsāni mudumaṃsāni bhakkhayitvā tameva āsayaṃ ajjhupesi.
mula_english:
27. "When, venerable Bhaggava, Jāliya, the apprentice of Dārupatta, knew that Acela Pāthikaputta was defeated, [that] he was crawling on the very spot, saying, 'I am coming, venerable sir, I am coming, venerable sir,' and he was not able even to rise from his seat, then he said this to him:

'Once long ago, venerable Pāthikaputta, the lion, king of beasts, thought: ‘Suppose I were to make my lair near a certain jungle.
Then, having made my lair there, I could emerge in the evening, and having emerged from my lair, I could yawn, and having yawned, I could survey the four quarters all around, and having surveyed the four quarters all around, I could roar my lion’s roar three times, and having roared my lion’s roar three times, I could then make for the cattle-pasture.
I could then pick out the very best of the herd for my kill and, having had a good feast of tender meat, return to my lair.’

"Then, venerable sir, the lion, king of beasts, chose a lair near a certain jungle.
Having made his lair there, he emerged in the evening, and having emerged from his lair, he yawned, and having yawned, he surveyed the four quarters all around, and having surveyed the four quarters all around, he roared his lion’s roar three times, and having roared his lion’s roar three times, he then set out in search of game.
He then picked out the very best of the herd for his kill and, having had a good feast of tender meat, he returned to his lair.
commentary_pali: 27.Sīhassāti cattāro sīhā tiṇasīho ca kāḷasīho ca paṇḍusīho ca kesarasīho ca. Tesaṃ catunnaṃ sīhānaṃ kesarasīho aggataṃ gato, so idhādhippeto. Migaraññoti sabbacatuppadānaṃ rañño. Āsayanti nivāsaṃ. Sīhanādanti abhītanādaṃ. Gocarāyapakkameyyanti āhāratthāya pakkameyyaṃ. Varaṃ varanti uttamuttamaṃ, thūlaṃ thūlanti attho. Mudumaṃsānīti mudūni maṃsāni . ‘‘Madhumaṃsānī’’tipi pāṭho, madhuramaṃsānīti attho. Ajjhupeyyanti upagaccheyyaṃ. Sīhanādaṃ naditvāti ye dubbalā pāṇā, te palāyantūti attano sūrabhāvasannissitena kāruññena naditvā.
commentary_english:
27. *Sīhassā* means four lions: the grass-colored lion, the black lion, the pale lion, and the maned lion.

Of these four lions, the maned lion is considered the foremost, and that is what is intended here.

*Migarañño* means king of all quadrupeds.

*Āsaya* means dwelling place.

*Sīhanāda* means a fearless roar.

*Gocarāya pakkameyya* means should go forth for the sake of food.

*Varaṃ vara* means the most excellent, the coarsest, the most substantial.

*Mudumaṃsānī* means soft meats.

There is also the reading "madhumaṃsānī," meaning sweet meats.

*Ajjhupeyya* means should approach.

*Sīhanādaṃ naditvā* means having roared a lion's roar, with compassion relying on his own heroic nature, [thinking] "let those beings who are weak flee."

mula_pali:
28. ‘Tasseva kho, āvuso pāthikaputta, sīhassa migarañño vighāsasaṃvaḍḍho jarasiṅgālo jarasigālo (sī. syā. pī.) ditto ceva balavā ca. Atha kho, āvuso, tassa jarasiṅgālassa etadahosi – ko cāhaṃ, ko sīho migarājā. Yaṃnūnāhampi aññataraṃ vanasaṇḍaṃ nissāya āsayaṃ kappeyyaṃ. Tatrāsayaṃ kappetvā sāyanhasamayaṃ āsayā nikkhameyyaṃ, āsayā nikkhamitvā vijambheyyaṃ, vijambhitvā samantā catuddisā anuvilokeyyaṃ, samantā catuddisā anuviloketvā tikkhattuṃ sīhanādaṃ nadeyyaṃ, tikkhattuṃ sīhanādaṃ naditvā gocarāya pakkameyyaṃ. So varaṃ varaṃ migasaṅghe vadhitvā mudumaṃsāni mudumaṃsāni bhakkhayitvā tameva āsayaṃ ajjhupeyya’nti.

‘Atha kho so, āvuso, jarasiṅgālo aññataraṃ vanasaṇḍaṃ nissāya āsayaṃ kappesi. Tatrāsayaṃ kappetvā sāyanhasamayaṃ āsayā nikkhami, āsayā nikkhamitvā vijambhi, vijambhitvā samantā catuddisā anuvilokesi, samantā catuddisā anuviloketvā tikkhattuṃ sīhanādaṃ nadissāmīti siṅgālakaṃyeva anadi bheraṇḍakaṃyeva bhedaṇḍakaṃyeva (ka.) anadi, ke ca chave siṅgāle, ke pana sīhanādeti sīhanāde (?).

bhedaṇḍakaṃyeva (ka.) sīhanāde (?)

‘Evameva kho tvaṃ, āvuso pāthikaputta, sugatāpadānesu jīvamāno sugatātirittāni bhuñjamāno tathāgate arahante sammāsambuddhe āsādetabbaṃ maññasi. Ke ca chave pāthikaputte, kā ca tathāgatānaṃ arahantānaṃ sammāsambuddhānaṃ āsādanā’ti.
mula_english:
28. ‘Again, friend Pāthikaputta, the old jackal, fed on the leavings of the lion, the king of beasts, was both fierce and strong. Then, friend, the old jackal thought: ‘What difference is there between me and the lion, king of beasts? Suppose I were to make my lair near the jungle. Then I could emerge in the evening, yawn, survey the four quarters, roar my lion’s roar three times, and then make for the cattle-pasture. I could then pick out the very best of the herd for my kill and, having had a good feast of tender meat, return to my lair.’

‘So he chose a lair accordingly. Then, emerging in the evening, he surveyed the four quarters, and then thought: ‘Now I will roar a lion’s roar three times’, — and he gave out the howl of his kind, a jackal howl. For what has the wretched howl of a jackal in common with a lion’s roar?

‘In just the same way, Pāthikaputta, you are living off the achievements of the Well-Farer, feeding on the Well-Farer’s leavings, imagine you can set yourself up beside the *Tathāgatas*, *Arhats* and fully enlightened Buddhas. But what have wretched Pāthikaputtas in common with them?
commentary_pali:
28.Vighāsasaṃvaḍḍhoti vighāsena saṃvaḍḍho, vighāsaṃ bhakkhitā tirittamaṃsaṃ khāditvā vaḍḍhito. Dittoti dappito thūlasarīro. Balavāti balasampanno. Etadahosīti kasmā ahosi? Asmimānadosena.

Tatrāyaṃ anupubbikathā – ekadivasaṃ kira so sīho gocarato nivattamāno taṃ siṅgālaṃ bhayena palāyamānaṃ disvā kāruññajāto hutvā ‘‘vayasa, mā bhāyi, tiṭṭha ko nāma tva’’nti āha. Jambuko nāmāhaṃ sāmīti. Vayasa, jambuka, ito paṭṭhāya maṃ upaṭṭhātuṃ sakkhissasīti. Upaṭṭhahissāmīti. So tato paṭṭhāya upaṭṭhāti. Sīho gocarato āgacchanto mahantaṃ mahantaṃ maṃsakhaṇḍaṃ āharati. So taṃ khāditvā avidūre pāsāṇapiṭṭhe vasati. So katipāhaccayeneva thūlasarīro mahākhandho jāto. Atha naṃ sīho avoca – ‘‘vayasa, jambuka, mama vijambhanakāle avidūre ṭhatvā ‘viroca sāmī’ti vattuṃ sakkhissasī’’ti. Sakkomi sāmīti. So tassa vijambhanakāle tathā karoti . Tena sīhassa atireko asmimāno hoti.

Athekadivasaṃ jarasiṅgālo udakasoṇḍiyaṃ pānīyaṃ pivanto attano chāyaṃ olokento addasa attano thūlasarīratañceva mahākhandhatañca. Disvā ‘jarasiṅgālosmī’ti manaṃ akatvā ‘‘ahampi sīho jāto’’ti maññi. Tato attanāva attānaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘vayasa, jambuka, yuttaṃ nāma tava iminā attabhāvena parassa ucchiṭṭhamaṃsaṃ khādituṃ, kiṃ tvaṃ puriso na hosi, sīhassāpi cattāro pādā dve dāṭhā dve kaṇṇā ekaṃ naṅguṭṭhaṃ, tavapi sabbaṃ tatheva, kevalaṃ tava kesarabhāramattameva natthī’’ti. Tassevaṃ cintayato asmimāno vaḍḍhi. Athassa tena asmimānadosena etaṃ ‘‘ko cāha’’ntiādi maññitamahosi. Tattha ko cāhanti ahaṃ ko, sīho migarājā ko, na me ñāti, na sāmiko, kimahaṃ tassa nipaccakāraṃ karomīti adhippāyo. Siṅgālakaṃyevāti siṅgālaravameva. Bheraṇḍakaṃyevāti appiyaamanāpasaddameva. Ke ca chave siṅgāleti ko ca lāmako siṅgālo. Ke pana sīhanādeti ko pana sīhanādo siṅgālassa ca sīhanādassa ca ko sambandhoti adhippāyo. Sugatāpadānesūti sugatalakkhaṇesu. Sugatassa sāsanasambhūtāsu tīsu sikkhāsu. Kathaṃ panesa tattha jīvati? Etassa hi cattāro paccaye dadamānā sīlādiguṇasampannānaṃ sambuddhānaṃ demāti denti, tena esa abuddho samāno buddhānaṃ niyāmitapaccaye paribhuñjanto sugatāpadānesu jīvati nāma. Sugatātirittānīti tesaṃ kira bhojanāni dadamānā buddhānañca buddhasāvakānañca datvā pacchā avasesaṃ sāyanhasamaye denti. Evamesa sugatātirittāni bhuñjati nāma. Tathāgateti tathāgataṃ arahantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ āsādetabbaṃ ghaṭṭayitabbaṃ. Atha vā ‘‘tathāgate’’tiādīni upayogabahuvacanāneva. Āsādetabbanti idampi bahuvacanameva ekavacanaṃ viya vuttaṃ. Āsādanāti ahaṃ buddhena saddhiṃ pāṭihāriyaṃ karissāmīti ghaṭṭanā.

ko cāha Siṅgālakaṃyevā Bheraṇḍakaṃyevā Ke ca chave siṅgāle Ke pana sīhanāde Sugatāpadānesū Sugatātirittānī Tathāgate Āsādetabba Āsādanā
commentary_english:
28. *Vighāsasaṃvaḍḍho* means *saṃvaḍḍho* through *vighāsa*, [namely,] *vaḍḍhito* by eating *tirittamaṃsaṃ* after having eaten *vighāsaṃ*.

*Ditto* means *dappito thūlasarīro* (delighted, with a stout body).

*Balavā* means *balasampanno* (endowed with strength).

*Etadahosī* means why did it happen? Because of the fault of conceit (*asmimāna-dosa*).

There is the following graduated talk (*anupubbikathā*): One day, it seems, that lion, returning from his range (*gocara*), saw that jackal (*siṅgāla*) fleeing in fear. Having become full of compassion (*karuññajāta*), he said, “Friend (*vayasa*), do not fear! Stop! What, pray, is your name (*ko nāma tva*)?”

“[My] name is Jackal (*jambuko*), master (*sāmī*),” [he replied].

“Friend (*vayasa*), Jackal (*jambuka*), from here on, will you be able to attend upon me (*upaṭṭhātuṃ sakkhissasī*)?”

“[Yes,] I will attend upon [you] (*upaṭṭhahissāmi*),” [he said].

So, from then on, he attends upon [him] (*upaṭṭhāti*).

The lion, going to and coming from his range (*gocarato āgacchanto*), brings a large and great piece of meat (*maṃsakhaṇḍaṃ āharati*).

Having eaten that, he dwells on a stone slab not far away (*avidūre pāsāṇapiṭṭhe vasati*).

In just a few days (*katipāhaccayeneva*), he became stout-bodied (*thūlasarīro*), a great mass (*mahākhandho jāto*).

Then the lion said to him (*sīho avoca*): “Friend (*vayasa*), Jackal (*jambuka*), when I yawn (*vijambhanakāle*), standing not far away (*avidūre ṭhatvā*), will you be able to say, ‘Shine forth, master (*viroca sāmī*)’?”

“I am able, master (*sakkomi sāmī*),” [he said].

So, when he yawns (*vijambhanakāle*), he does so (*tathā karoti*).

Because of that, the lion has an extraordinary conceit (*atireko asmimāno hoti*).

Then, one day, the old jackal (*jarasiṅgālo*), drinking water in a pool (*udakasoṇḍiyaṃ pānīyaṃ pivanto*), seeing his reflection (*attano chāyaṃ olokento*), saw his own stout body (*thūlasarīratañceva*) and great mass (*mahākhandhatañca*).

Having seen [it], not making [it] a mind [that] ‘I am an old jackal’ (*jarasiṅgālosmī’ti manaṃ akatvā*), he thought (*maññi*), “I too have become a lion (*ahampi sīho jāto*)!”

Then, by himself (*attanāva*), he said this to himself (*attānaṃ etadavoca*): “Friend (*vayasa*), Jackal (*jambuka*), is it proper (*yuttaṃ nāma*) for you, with this selfhood (*iminā attabhāvena*), to eat another’s leftover meat (*parassa ucchiṭṭhamaṃsaṃ khādituṃ*)? Are you not a man (*kiṃ tvaṃ puriso na hosi*)? The lion also has four feet (*cattāro pādā*), two fangs (*dve dāṭhā*), two ears (*dve kaṇṇā*), and one tail (*ekaṃ naṅguṭṭhaṃ*). You too have all that (*tavapi sabbaṃ tatheva*). Only a mane (*kesarabhāramattameva*) is not there (*natthī*)!”

As he was thinking thus (*tassevaṃ cintayato*), his conceit (*asmimāno*) increased (*vaḍḍhi*).

Then, through that fault of conceit (*asmimānadosena*), this thought occurred to him (*etaṃ maññitamahosi*): “Who is he (*ko cāha*)?”

There, *ko cāha* means who am I (*ahaṃ ko*)? Who is the lion (*sīho*)? Who is the king of beasts (*migarājā ko*)? He is no relative (*na me ñāti*). He is no master (*na sāmiko*). Why should I do obeisance to him (*kimahaṃ tassa nipaccakāraṃ karomi*)?” is the intention (*adhippāyo*).

*Siṅgālakaṃyevā* means just the sound of a jackal (*siṅgālaravameva*).

*Bheraṇḍakaṃyevā* means just a disagreeable and unpleasant sound (*appiyaamanāpasaddameva*).

*Ke ca chave siṅgāle* means what sort of jackals are those (*ko ca lāmako siṅgālo*)?

*Ke pana sīhanāde* means what, pray, is a lion’s roar (*ko pana sīhanādo*)? What is the connection (*ko sambandho*) between the jackal (*siṅgālassa*) and the lion’s roar (*sīhanādassa ca*)?” is the intention (*adhippāyo*).

*Sugatāpadānesu* means in the qualities of the Sugata (*sugatalakkhaṇesu*).

In the three trainings (*tīsu sikkhāsu*) arisen in the Sugata’s dispensation (*sugatassa sāsanasambhūtāsu*).

How does he live there (*kathaṃ panesa tattha jīvati*)? Because [people], giving the four requisites to those *sambuddha* who are endowed with good qualities such as virtue (*sīlādiguṇasampannānaṃ*), give, [thinking,] “We give to the Buddhas (*buddhānaṃ demāti denti*)”, therefore, though he is not a Buddha (*abuddho samāno*), partaking of the requisites allotted to the Buddhas (*buddhānaṃ niyāmitapaccaye paribhuñjanto*), he lives in the Sugata’s legends (*sugatāpadānesu jīvati nāma*).

*Sugatātirittānī* means [people], giving those foods to the Buddhas (*buddhānañca*) and the Buddha’s disciples (*buddhasāvakānañca*), after having given [it], later (*pacchā*) give the remainder (*avasesaṃ*) at evening time (*sāyanhasamaye denti*).

Thus he enjoys (*bhuñjati*) the Sugata’s surplus (*sugatātirittāni nāma*).

*Tathāgate* means the *Tathāgata*, the *arhat*, the *sammāsambuddha* is to be assailed (*āsādetabbaṃ*), to be struck (*ghaṭṭayitabbaṃ*).

Or else, *tathāgate* and so on are just plurals of use (*upayogabahuvacanāneva*).

*Āsādetabba* means this too is just a plural, [though] stated as if a singular (*ekavacanaṃ viya vuttaṃ*).

*Āsādanā* means striking (*ghaṭṭanā*), [thinking,] “I will perform a miracle (*pāṭihāriyaṃ karissāmīti*) together with the Buddha (*buddhena saddhiṃ*)”.
ko cāha siṅgālakaṃyevā bheraṇḍakaṃyevā ke ca chave siṅgāle ke pana sīhanāde sugatāpadānesū sugatātirittānī tathāgate āsādetabba āsādanā

Someone said, "Just like a jackal," "Just like a bheraṇḍaka bird," "Who are similar corpses and jackals?" "Who then are the lion's roar?" In the Sugata's *apadāna* stories, what exceeds the Sugata is obtainable in the *Tathāgata*; [this is] an attainment.

mula_pali:
29. ‘‘Yato kho, bhaggava, jāliyo dārupattikantevāsī iminā opammena neva asakkhi acelaṃ pāthikaputtaṃ tamhā āsanā cāvetuṃ. Atha naṃ etadavoca –

‘Sīhoti attānaṃ samekkhiyāna,

Amaññi kotthu migarājāhamasmi;

Tatheva tameva (syā.) so siṅgālakaṃ anadi,

tameva (syā.)

Ke ca chave siṅgāle ke pana sīhanāde’ti.

‘Evameva kho tvaṃ, āvuso pāthikaputta, sugatāpadānesu jīvamāno sugatātirittāni bhuñjamāno tathāgate arahante sammāsambuddhe āsādetabbaṃ maññasi. Ke ca chave pāthikaputte, kā ca tathāgatānaṃ arahantānaṃ sammāsambuddhānaṃ āsādanā’ti.
mula_english:
29. ‘Then, Bhaggava, Jāliya, the resident of Dārupatta, being unable even with this parable to get the naked Pāthikaputta to rise from his seat, said this to him:

‘Like a lion, observing himself, the king of beasts thought, "Where is there another?"

Just so, he despised the jackal, saying, "What do wretched jackals have to do with the lion's roar?"’

‘In just the same way, Āvuso Pāthikaputta, you, living off the achievements of the Well-Farer, feeding on the Well-Farer’s leavings, imagine you can set yourself up beside the *Tathāgatas*, *Arhats* and Fully Enlightened *Buddhas*. But what have wretched Pāthikaputtas in common with them? And what is comparable to the attainment of the *Tathāgatas*, the *Arhats*, the Perfectly Awakened *Buddhas*?’
commentary_pali: 29.Samekkhiyānāti samekkhitvā, maññitvāti attho. Amaññīti puna amaññittha kotthūti siṅgālo.
commentary_english: 29. *Samekkhiyānā* means *samekkhitvā*, considering, meaning thinking. *Amaññī* means again, *amaññittha*, *kotthū* means jackal.

mula_pali:
30. ‘‘Yato kho, bhaggava, jāliyo dārupattikantevāsī imināpi opammena neva asakkhi acelaṃ pāthikaputtaṃ tamhā āsanā cāvetuṃ. Atha naṃ etadavoca –

‘Aññaṃ anucaṅkamanaṃ, attānaṃ vighāse samekkhiya;

Yāva attānaṃ na passati, kotthu tāva byagghoti maññati.

Tatheva so siṅgālakaṃ anadi;

Ke ca chave siṅgāle ke pana sīhanāde’ti.

‘Evameva kho tvaṃ, āvuso pāthikaputta, sugatāpadānesu jīvamāno sugatātirittāni bhuñjamāno tathāgate arahante sammāsambuddhe āsādetabbaṃ maññasi. Ke ca chave pāthikaputte, kā ca tathāgatānaṃ arahantānaṃ sammāsambuddhānaṃ āsādanā’ti.
mula_english:
30. “And, being unable even with this parable to get Patikaputta to rise from his seat, Jaliya the pupil of Dārupatta then said this to him:

‘Another pacing to and fro, considering oneself in a ruined state; as long as one does not see oneself, then one thinks one is a tiger.

Just so, he did not value the jackal; what have wretched jackals in common with the roar of a lion?’

In just the same way, Patikaputta, you are living off the achievements of the Well-Farer, feeding on the Well-Farer’s leavings, imagine you can set yourself up beside the *Tathāgatas*, *Arhats* and *sammāsambuddhas*.

But what have wretched Patikaputtas in common with them?
commentary_pali: 30.Attānaṃ vighāse samekkhiyāti soṇḍiyaṃ ucchiṭṭhodake thūlaṃ attabhāvaṃ disvā. Yāva attānaṃ na passatīti yāva ahaṃ sīhavighāsasaṃvaḍḍhitako jarasiṅgāloti evaṃ yathābhūtaṃ attānaṃ na passati. Byagghoti maññatīti sīhohamasmīti maññati, sīhena vā samānabalo byagghoyeva ahanti maññati.
commentary_english:
"Having thoroughly looked at himself in the refuse," seeing the coarse self-existence in the leftover water in a tipper.

"Until he sees himself," until he sees his real self, as I am a lion, grown up on scraps, an old jackal like this.

"A tiger" he thinks, "he considers," he thinks, "I am a lion," or he thinks, "I am a tiger, of equal strength to a lion."

mula_pali:
31. ‘‘Yato kho, bhaggava, jāliyo dārupattikantevāsī imināpi opammena neva asakkhi acelaṃ pāthikaputtaṃ tamhā āsanā cāvetuṃ. Atha naṃ etadavoca –

‘Bhutvāna bheke bhiṅge (ka.) khalamūsikāyo,

bhiṅge (ka.)

Kaṭasīsu khittāni ca koṇapāni kūṇapāni (syā.);

kūṇapāni (syā.)

Mahāvane suññavane vivaḍḍho,

Amaññi kotthu migarājāhamasmi.

Tatheva so siṅgālakaṃ anadi;

Ke ca chave siṅgāle ke pana sīhanāde’ti.

‘Evameva kho tvaṃ, āvuso pāthikaputta, sugatāpadānesu jīvamāno sugatātirittāni bhuñjamāno tathāgate arahante sammāsambuddhe āsādetabbaṃ maññasi. Ke ca chave pāthikaputte, kā ca tathāgatānaṃ arahantānaṃ sammāsambuddhānaṃ āsādanā’ti.
mula_english:
31. “And, being unable even with this parable to get Patikaputta to rise from his seat, Jaliya the pupil of Dārupatta then said to him:

‘Having eaten frogs, beetles, and field-mice, scraps thrown among the rushes and carrion, grown up in the great empty wilderness, the jackal thinks, “I am a king of beasts.”

So he disregards the jackal; what have wretched jackals in common with the lion’s roar?’

‘In just the same way, friend Patikaputta, you are living off the achievements of the Well-Farer, feeding on the Well-Farer’s leavings, [imagine] you can set yourself up beside the *tathāgatas*, *arhats*, and perfectly awakened *buddhas*. But what have wretched Patikaputtas in common with them, and what have the achievements of the *tathāgatas*, *arhats*, and perfectly awakened *buddhas* [in common with them]?”
commentary_pali:
31.Bhutvāna bheketi āvāṭamaṇḍūke khāditvā. Khalamūsikāyoti khalesu mūsikāyo ca khāditvā. Kaṭasīsu khittāni ca koṇapānīti susānesu chaḍḍitakuṇapāni ca khāditvā. Mahāvaneti mahante vanasmiṃ. Suññavaneti tucchavane. Vivaḍḍhoti vaḍḍhito. Tatheva so siṅgālakaṃ anadīti evaṃ saṃvaḍḍhopi migarājāhamasmīti maññitvāpi yathā pubbe dubbalasiṅgālakāle, tatheva so siṅgālaravaṃyeva aravīti . Imāyapi gāthāya bhekādīni bhutvā vaḍḍhitasiṅgālo viya lābhasakkāragiddho tvanti pāthikaputtameva ghaṭṭesi.

Nāgehīti hatthīhi. Mahābandhanāti mahatā kilesabandhanā mocetvā. Mahāviduggāti mahāviduggaṃ nāma cattāro oghā. Tato uddharitvā nibbānathale patiṭṭhapetvā.

Nāgehī Mahābandhanā Mahāviduggā

Aggaññapaññattikathāvaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
31. *bhutvāna bheke* means having eaten frogs in a well (*āvāṭamaṇḍūke khāditvā*).
*khalamūsikāyo* means having eaten mice in the threshing floor (*khalesu mūsikāyo ca khāditvā*).
*kaṭasīsu khittāni ca koṇapānī* means having eaten corpses thrown in the cemetery (*susānesu chaḍḍitakuṇapāni ca khāditvā*).
*mahāvane* means in a great forest (*mahante vanasmiṃ*).
*suññavane* means in an empty forest (*tucchavane*).
*vivaḍḍho* means grown (*vaḍḍhito*).
*tatheva so siṅgālakaṃ anadī* means just as he, even though he had grown up, thinking, "I am a lion, king of beasts," just as formerly at the time when he was a weak jackal, so he cried only the cry of a jackal (*evaṃ saṃvaḍḍhopi migarājāhamasmīti maññitvāpi yathā pubbe dubbalasiṅgālakāle, tatheva so siṅgālaravaṃyeva aravīti*).
Even with this verse, having eaten frogs etc., the jackal grown up like that, greedy for gain and honor, you struck just that Pāthika's son (*imāyapi gāthāya bhekādīni bhutvā vaḍḍhitasiṅgālo viya lābhasakkāragiddho tvanti pāthikaputtameva ghaṭṭesi*).

*nāgehī* means by elephants (*hatthīhi*).
*mahābandhanā* means having freed [them] from the great bondage of defilements (*mahatā kilesabandhanā mocetvā*).
*mahāviduggā* means the four great floods called *mahāviduggaṃ* (*mahāviduggaṃ nāma cattāro oghā*).
Having rescued them from that, having established them on the shore of nirvāṇa (*tato uddharitvā nibbānathale patiṭṭhapetvā*).

Elephants, great bondage, great fortress. The Aggañña-paññatti-kathā-vaṇṇanā.

mula_pali: 32. ‘‘Yato kho, bhaggava, jāliyo dārupattikantevāsī imināpi opammena neva asakkhi acelaṃ pāthikaputtaṃ tamhā āsanā cāvetuṃ. Atha taṃ parisaṃ āgantvā evamārocesi – ‘parābhūtarūpo, bho, acelo pāthikaputto āyāmi āvuso, āyāmi āvusoti vatvā tattheva saṃsappati, na sakkoti āsanāpi vuṭṭhātu’nti.
mula_english: ‘And, Bhaggava, being unable even with this parable to get the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta to rise from his seat, Jāliya Dārupatta's pupil then went to that assembly and announced: ‘The naked ascetic Pāthikaputta has been defeated, sir. I am going, friend; I am going, friend,’ and saying this, he just collapsed there and was unable even to get up from his seat.’

mula_pali: 33. ‘‘Evaṃ vutte, ahaṃ, bhaggava, taṃ parisaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘abhabbo kho, āvuso, acelo pāthikaputto taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā mama sammukhībhāvaṃ āgantuṃ. Sacepissa evamassa – ahaṃ taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā samaṇassa gotamassa sammukhībhāvaṃ gaccheyyanti, muddhāpi tassa vipateyya. Sacepāyasmantānaṃ licchavīnaṃ evamassa – mayaṃ acelaṃ pāthikaputtaṃ varattāhi bandhitvā nāgehi goyugehi (sabbattha) aṭṭhakathā passitabbā āviñcheyyāmāti . Tā varattā chijjeyyuṃ pāthikaputto vā. Abhabbo pana acelo pāthikaputto taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā mama sammukhībhāvaṃ āgantuṃ. Sacepissa evamassa – ahaṃ taṃ vācaṃ appahāya taṃ cittaṃ appahāya taṃ diṭṭhiṃ appaṭinissajjitvā samaṇassa gotamassa sammukhībhāvaṃ gaccheyyanti, muddhāpi tassa vipateyyā’ti.
mula_english:
Then, Bhaggava, I said to that assembly: 'It is not possible, Āvuso, that the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta, without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, without giving up that view, could come into my presence.

And if he were to think: 'Without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, without giving up that view, I shall go into the presence of the ascetic Gotama,' his head would split.

Even if the esteemed Licchavis were to think: 'Let us bind the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta with thongs and drag him here with oxen' (the commentary should be consulted everywhere regarding yoked oxen).

Those thongs would break, or rather Pāthikaputta would burst them.

But it is not possible that the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta, without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, without giving up that view, could come into my presence.

And if he were to think: 'Without abandoning that speech, without abandoning that thought, without giving up that view, I shall go into the presence of the ascetic Gotama,' his head would split."

mula_pali: 34. ‘‘Atha khvāhaṃ, bhaggava, taṃ parisaṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassesiṃ samādapesiṃ samuttejesiṃ sampahaṃsesiṃ, taṃ parisaṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṃsetvā mahābandhanā mokkhaṃ karitvā caturāsītipāṇasahassāni mahāviduggā uddharitvā tejodhātuṃ samāpajjitvā sattatālaṃ vehāsaṃ abbhuggantvā aññaṃ sattatālampi acciṃ aggiṃ (syā.) abhinimminitvā pajjalitvā dhūmāyitvā dhūpāyitvā (sī. pī.) mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṃ paccuṭṭhāsiṃ.
mula_english: “Then, Bhaggava, I instructed, inspired, fired, and delighted that assembly with a talk on the Dharma. Having delivered that company from the great bondage, thus rescuing eighty-four thousand beings from the great path of peril, I entered into the fire-element (tejodhātu) and rose into the air to the height of seven palm-trees (sattatālaṃ), and projecting a beam for the height of another seven so that it blazed and shed fragrance, I then reappeared in the Gabled Hall (kūṭāgārasālāyaṃ) in the Great Forest (mahāvane).

mula_pali:
35. ‘‘Atha kho, bhaggava, sunakkhatto licchaviputto yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā maṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhaggava, sunakkhattaṃ licchaviputtaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘taṃ kiṃ maññasi, sunakkhatta, yatheva te ahaṃ acelaṃ pāthikaputtaṃ ārabbha byākāsiṃ, tatheva taṃ vipākaṃ aññathā vā’ti? ‘Yatheva me, bhante, bhagavā acelaṃ pāthikaputtaṃ ārabbha byākāsi, tatheva taṃ vipākaṃ, no aññathā’ti.

‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, sunakkhatta, yadi evaṃ sante kataṃ vā hoti uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ, akataṃ vā’ti? ‘Addhā kho, bhante, evaṃ sante kataṃ hoti uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ, no akata’nti. ‘Evampi kho maṃ tvaṃ, moghapurisa, uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ karontaṃ evaṃ vadesi – na hi pana me, bhante, bhagavā uttarimanussadhammā iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ karotīti. Passa, moghapurisa, yāvañca te idaṃ aparaddhaṃ’ti.

‘‘Evampi kho, bhaggava, sunakkhatto licchaviputto mayā vuccamāno apakkameva imasmā dhammavinayā, yathā taṃ āpāyiko nerayiko.

Aggaññapaññattikathā
mula_english:
35. ‘Then, Bhaggava, Sunakkhatta, son of the Licchavis, came to me, and after paying homage to me, he sat down at one side.

Sitting at one side, I said to Sunakkhatta, son of the Licchavis: “What do you think, Sunakkhatta? Has what I told you about the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta come about, or not?” “Just as the Blessed One told me about the naked ascetic Pāthikaputta, so it has come about, and not otherwise.”

“What do you think, Sunakkhatta? Has a miracle of supernormal power beyond human ability been performed, or not?” “Indeed, venerable sir, in such a case a miracle of supernormal power beyond human ability has been performed, and not not performed.”

“Well then, you foolish man ( *moghapurisa*), do you still say to me, after I have performed a miracle of supernormal power beyond human ability: ‘Venerable sir, the Blessed One does not perform a miracle of supernormal power beyond human ability’? Consider, you foolish man, how great is your offense.”

“And at my words Sunakkhatta, son of the Licchavis, departed from this Dhamma and discipline, like one destined for misery and hell.

The Discourse on the Highest Knowledge

mula_pali: 36. ‘‘Aggaññañcāhaṃ, bhaggava, pajānāmi. Tañca pajānāmi ‘‘tañcapajānāmī’’ti idaṃ syāpotthakenatthi, tato ca uttaritaraṃ pajānāmi, tañca pajānaṃ pajānanaṃ (syā. ka.) aṭṭhakathāsaṃvaṇṇanā passitabbā na parāmasāmi, aparāmasato ca me paccattaññeva nibbuti viditā, yadabhijānaṃ tathāgato no anayaṃ āpajjati .
mula_english: “Bhaggava, I know the first beginning of things. And I know that, and what surpasses it; and knowing that, I do not cling to it. And not clinging, I have realized nirvāṇa for myself. The Tathāgata does not fall into perilous paths by that realization.
commentary_pali: 36. Iti ‘‘bhagavā ettakena kathāmaggena pāṭihāriyaṃ na karotī’’ti padassa anusandhiṃ dassetvā idāni ‘‘na aggaññaṃ paññāpetī’’ti imassa anusandhiṃ dassento aggaññañcāhanti desanaṃ ārabhi. Tattha aggaññañcāhanti ahaṃ, bhaggava, aggaññañca pajānāmi lokuppatticariyavaṃsañca. Tañca pajānāmīti na kevalaṃ aggaññameva, tañca aggaññaṃ pajānāmi. Tato ca uttaritaraṃ sīlasamādhito paṭṭhāya yāva sabbaññutaññāṇā pajānāmi. Tañca pajānaṃ na parāmasāmīti tañca pajānantopi ahaṃ idaṃ nāma pajānāmīti taṇhādiṭṭhimānavasena na parāmasāmi. Natthi tathāgatassa parāmāsoti dīpeti. Paccattaññevanibbuti viditāti attanāyeva attani kilesanibbānaṃ viditaṃ. Yadabhijānaṃ tathāgatoti yaṃ kilesanibbānaṃ jānanto tathāgato. No anayaṃ āpajjatīti aviditanibbānā titthiyā viya anayaṃ dukkhaṃ byasanaṃ nāpajjati.
commentary_english:
36. Having shown the connection of the word *iti* "the Blessed One does not perform miracles with such speech," now showing the connection of "he does not make known the highest knowledge," he began the teaching, *aggaññañcāha* "and he declared the highest knowledge."

Therein, *aggaññañcāha* "and he declared the highest knowledge" means, "I, Bhaggava, understand the highest knowledge, the lineage of the world's origin and conduct.

*tañca pajānāmī* "and I understand that" means, not only the highest knowledge, but I understand that highest knowledge.

And then, further, from morality and concentration, up to the knowledge of omniscience, I understand.

*tañca pajānaṃ na parāmasāmī* "and knowing that, I do not grasp it" means, even knowing that, I do not grasp it with craving, views, and pride, thinking, "I understand this."

*natthi tathāgatassa parāmāsoti dīpeti* means, he reveals that there is no grasping for the Tathāgata.

*paccattaññeva nibbuti viditā* "Nirvana is known only to oneself" means, by oneself, in oneself, the extinction of defilements is known.

*yadabhijānaṃ tathāgato* "whatever the Tathāgata has directly known" means, whatever extinction of defilements the Tathāgata knows.

*no anayaṃ āpajjatī* "he does not fall into misfortune" means, unlike those of other sects who do not know cessation, he does not fall into misfortune, suffering, and calamity.

mula_pali: 37. ‘‘Santi, bhaggava, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā issarakuttaṃ brahmakuttaṃ ācariyakaṃ aggaññaṃ paññapenti. Tyāhaṃ upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ vadāmi – ‘saccaṃ kira tumhe āyasmanto issarakuttaṃ brahmakuttaṃ ācariyakaṃ aggaññaṃ paññapethā’ti? Te ca me evaṃ puṭṭhā, ‘āmo’ti āmāti (syā.) paṭijānanti. Tyāhaṃ evaṃ vadāmi – ‘kathaṃvihitakaṃ pana kathaṃ vihitakaṃno pana (ka.) tumhe āyasmanto issarakuttaṃ brahmakuttaṃ ācariyakaṃ aggaññaṃ paññapethā’ti? Te mayā puṭṭhā na sampāyanti, asampāyantā mamaññeva paṭipucchanti. Tesāhaṃ puṭṭho byākaromi –
mula_english: ‘Bhaggava, there are some ascetics and Brahmins who declare as their doctrine that all things began with the creation by an Īśvara (Lord), or Brahmā. Approaching them, I say this: “Is it true that you, venerable sirs, declare that all things began with the creation by an Īśvara, or Brahmā?” And when they are questioned in this way by me, they acknowledge, "Yes." Then I say this: “But in what manner do you, venerable sirs, declare that all things began with the creation by an Īśvara, or Brahmā?” When questioned by me, they are unable to explain and instead they ask me questions. When questioned by them, I explain:
commentary_pali: 37. Idāni yaṃ taṃ titthiyā aggaññaṃ paññapenti, taṃ dassento santi bhaggavātiādimāha. Tattha issarakuttaṃ brahmakuttanti issarakataṃ brahmakataṃ, issaranimmitaṃ brahmanimmitanti attho. Brahmā eva hi ettha ādhipaccabhāvena issaroti veditabbo. Ācariyakanti ācariyabhāvaṃ ācariyavādaṃ. Tattha ācariyavādo aggaññaṃ. Aggaññaṃ pana ettha desitanti katvā so aggaññaṃ tveva vutto. Kathaṃ vihitakanti kena vihitaṃ kinti vihitaṃ. Sesaṃ brahmajāle vitthāritanayeneva veditabbaṃ.
commentary_english:
37. Now, to show what the Tīrthikas assert as the foremost knowledge (aggañña), [the text] begins with "santi bhaggavā," and so forth.

There, "issarakuttaṃ brahmakuttaṃ" means made by Īśvara, made by Brahmā; the meaning is created by Īśvara, created by Brahmā. For Brahmā himself here should be understood as Īśvara in the sense of having supremacy.

"ācariyakaṃ" means the state of a teacher, the doctrine of a teacher (ācariyavādaṃ). There, the doctrine of the teacher is the foremost knowledge (aggaññaṃ). But having made it taught here as the foremost knowledge (aggaññaṃ), he is indeed called the foremost knowledge (aggaññaṃ).

"kathaṃ vihitakaṃ" means by whom was it done? How was it done?

The rest should be understood in the same way as the method explained in the Brahma-jāla [Sutta].

mula_pali:
38. ‘Hoti kho so, āvuso, samayo yaṃ kadāci karahaci dīghassa addhuno accayena ayaṃ loko saṃvaṭṭati. Saṃvaṭṭamāne loke yebhuyyena sattā ābhassarasaṃvattanikā honti. Te tattha honti manomayā pītibhakkhā sayaṃpabhā antalikkhacarā subhaṭṭhāyino ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ tiṭṭhanti.

‘Hoti kho so, āvuso, samayo yaṃ kadāci karahaci dīghassa addhuno accayena ayaṃ loko vivaṭṭati. Vivaṭṭamāne loke suññaṃ brahmavimānaṃ pātubhavati. Atha kho atha (sī. syā. pī.) aññataro satto āyukkhayā vā puññakkhayā vā ābhassarakāyā cavitvā suññaṃ brahmavimānaṃ upapajjati . So tattha hoti manomayo pītibhakkho sayaṃpabho antalikkhacaro subhaṭṭhāyī, ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ tiṭṭhati.

atha (sī. syā. pī.)

‘Tassa tattha ekakassa dīgharattaṃ nivusitattā anabhirati paritassanā uppajjati – aho vata aññepi sattā itthattaṃ āgaccheyyunti. Atha aññepi sattā āyukkhayā vā puññakkhayā vā ābhassarakāyā cavitvā brahmavimānaṃ upapajjanti tassa sattassa sahabyataṃ. Tepi tattha honti manomayā pītibhakkhā sayaṃpabhā antalikkhacarā subhaṭṭhāyino, ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ tiṭṭhanti.
mula_english:
38. "There comes a time, friends, when, after the lapse of a long period, this world contracts. While the world is contracting, beings for the most part are reborn in the Ābhassara Brahma-world. There they dwell, mind-made, feeding on rapture, self-luminous, moving through the air, abiding in glory. And they continue thus for a long, long period of time.

‘There comes a time, friends, when, after the lapse of a long period, this world expands once again. While the world is expanding, an empty palace of Brahmā appears. Then some being or other, due to the exhaustion of his life-span or the exhaustion of his merit, passes away from the Ābhassara plane and is reborn in the empty palace of Brahmā. There he dwells, mind-made, feeding on rapture, self-luminous, moving through the air, abiding in glory. And he continues thus for a long, long period of time.

‘Because he has lived there alone for a long time, he begins to feel dissatisfied and agitated: “Oh, that other beings might come to this place!” Then other beings, due to the exhaustion of their life-span or the exhaustion of their merit, pass away from the Ābhassara plane and are reborn in the palace of Brahmā, in companionship with him. And there they dwell, mind-made, feeding on rapture, self-luminous, moving through the air, abiding in glory. And they continue thus for a long, long period of time.

mula_pali:
39. ‘Tatrāvuso, yo so satto paṭhamaṃ upapanno, tassa evaṃ hoti – ahamasmi brahmā mahābrahmā abhibhū anabhibhūto aññadatthudaso vasavattī issaro kattā nimmātā seṭṭho sajitā sañjitā (sī. pī.), sajjitā (syā. kaṃ.) vasī pitā bhūtabhabyānaṃ, mayā ime sattā nimmitā. Taṃ kissa hetu? Mamañhi pubbe etadahosi – aho vata aññepi sattā itthattaṃ āgaccheyyunti; iti mama ca manopaṇidhi. Ime ca sattā itthattaṃ āgatāti.

‘Yepi te sattā pacchā upapannā, tesampi evaṃ hoti – ayaṃ kho bhavaṃ brahmā mahābrahmā abhibhū anabhibhūto aññadatthudaso vasavattī issaro kattā nimmātā seṭṭho sajitā vasī pitā bhūtabhabyānaṃ; iminā mayaṃ bhotā brahmunā nimmitā. Taṃ kissa hetu? Imañhi mayaṃ addasāma idha paṭhamaṃ upapannaṃ; mayaṃ panāmha pacchā upapannāti.
mula_english:
"39. 'There, friend, the being who first arose thinks thus: "I am Brahmā, the Great Brahmā, the Conqueror, the Unconquered, the All-Seeing, the Wielder of Power, the Lord, the Maker, the Creator, the Best, the Ordainer, the Controller, the Father of all beings that have been and will be. These beings were created by me." What is the reason for this? Previously, this thought occurred to me: "Oh, that other beings would come into this existence!" Such was my heart's resolution (manopaṇidhi). And these beings have come into this existence.'

'And those beings who arose later, they also think thus: "This Brahmā, the Great Brahmā, the Conqueror, the Unconquered, the All-Seeing, the Wielder of Power, the Lord, the Maker, the Creator, the Best, the Ordainer, the Controller, the Father of all beings that have been and will be, was the one who created us." What is the reason for this? We saw this being arise here first; we arose later.'"

mula_pali:
40. ‘Tatrāvuso , yo so satto paṭhamaṃ upapanno, so dīghāyukataro ca hoti vaṇṇavantataro ca mahesakkhataro ca. Ye pana te sattā pacchā upapannā, te appāyukatarā ca honti dubbaṇṇatarā ca appesakkhatarā ca.

‘Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, āvuso, vijjati, yaṃ aññataro satto tamhā kāyā cavitvā itthattaṃ āgacchati. Itthattaṃ āgato samāno agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajati. Agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito samāno ātappamanvāya padhānamanvāya anuyogamanvāya appamādamanvāya sammāmanasikāramanvāya tathārūpaṃ cetosamādhiṃ phusati, yathāsamāhite citte taṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati; tato paraṃ nānussarati.

‘So evamāha – yo kho so bhavaṃ brahmā mahābrahmā abhibhū anabhibhūto aññadatthudaso vasavattī issaro kattā nimmātā seṭṭho sajitā vasī pitā bhūtabhabyānaṃ, yena mayaṃ bhotā brahmunā nimmitā. So nicco dhuvo sassato dīghāyuko (syā. ka.) sassato avipariṇāmadhammo sassatisamaṃ tatheva ṭhassati. Ye pana mayaṃ ahumhā tena bhotā brahmunā nimmitā, te mayaṃ aniccā addhuvā addhuvā asassatā (syā. ka.) appāyukā cavanadhammā itthattaṃ āgatā’ti. Evaṃvihitakaṃ no tumhe āyasmanto issarakuttaṃ brahmakuttaṃ ācariyakaṃ aggaññaṃ paññapethāti. ‘Te evamāhaṃsu – evaṃ kho no, āvuso gotama, sutaṃ, yathevāyasmā gotamo āhā’ti. ‘‘Aggaññañcāhaṃ, bhaggava, pajānāmi. Tañca pajānāmi, tato ca uttaritaraṃ pajānāmi, tañca pajānaṃ na parāmasāmi, aparāmasato ca me paccattaññeva nibbuti viditā. Yadabhijānaṃ tathāgato no anayaṃ āpajjati.

sassato dīghāyuko (syā. ka.) addhuvā asassatā (syā. ka.)
mula_english:
40. ‘In this case, *āvuso*, the being who re-arose there first possesses longer life, greater beauty, and greater authority (*mahā-ṛddhi*) than the beings who re-arose there after him. Those beings who arose later have shorter lives, are less beautiful and have less authority.

‘Now, *āvuso*, this comes to pass, that a certain being, after passing away from that plane (*kāya*), takes rebirth in this world (*itthattaṃ*). Having arisen in this world, he goes forth from the household life (*agāra*) into homelessness (*anagāriyaṃ*). Having gone forth from the household life into homelessness, by means of ardour (*ātappa*), exertion (*padhāna*), application (*anuyoga*), earnestness (*appamāda*) and right attention (*sammā-manasikāra*) he attains to such a degree of mental concentration (*ceto-samādhi*) that with his mind thus concentrated he recollects his immediately preceding life (*pūrve-nivāsa*), but none previous to that.

‘So he speaks thus: “That venerable Brahmā, the Great Brahmā (*mahā-brahmā*), the Conqueror (*abhibhū*), the Unconquered (*anabhibhūta*), the Universal Seer (*aññadatthudaso*), the Wielder of Power (*vasavattī*), the Lord (*īśvara*), the Maker (*kattā*) and Creator (*nimmātā*), the Supreme Being (*seṭṭho*), the Ordainer (*sajitā*), the Almighty (*vasī*), the Father (*pitā*) of all that are and are to be, by whom we were created; he is permanent (*nicca*), stable (*dhruva*), eternal (*saśvata*), not subject to change (*avipariṇāma-dharma*), and he will remain the same just like eternity itself.” But we, who were created by that Brahmā, we are impermanent (*anitya*), unstable (*adhruva*), short-lived (*alpāyuka*), fated to fall away (*cyavana-dharma*), and we have come to this world (*itthattaṃ*).” Thus it is that you, venerable sirs, teach the creation by Īśvara, the creation by Brahmā, the doctrine (*ācariyakaṃ*) of the beginning (*aggaññaṃ*)!’

‘They said: “It is just as you say, friend Gotama; thus have we heard it.”

‘‘Bhaggava, I know the first beginning of things (*aggañña*), and I know not only that, but what surpasses it in value. And I am not under the sway of what I know, and not being under its sway I have come to know for myself that quenching (*nirvṛti*), by the realisation of which the *Tathāgata* cannot fall into perilous paths (*anayaṃ āpajjati*).’

mula_pali: 41. ‘‘Santi, bhaggava, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā khiḍḍāpadosikaṃ ācariyakaṃ aggaññaṃ paññapenti.
