Tyāhaṃ upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ vadāmi – ‘saccaṃ kira tumhe āyasmanto khiḍḍāpadosikaṃ ācariyakaṃ aggaññaṃ paññapethā’ti? Te ca me evaṃ puṭṭhā ‘āmo’ti paṭijānanti. Tyāhaṃ evaṃ vadāmi – ‘kathaṃvihitakaṃ pana tumhe āyasmanto khiḍḍāpadosikaṃ ācariyakaṃ aggaññaṃ paññapethā’ti? Te mayā puṭṭhā na sampāyanti, asampāyantā mamaññeva paṭipucchanti, tesāhaṃ puṭṭho byākaromi –
mula_english:
41. There are, Bhaggava, some ascetics and Brahmins who declare that the beginning of things was due to corruption by pleasure ( *khiḍḍāpadosikaṃ ācariyakaṃ aggaññaṃ paññapenti*).

I went to them and asked them if this was their view: ‘Is it true that you, venerable sirs, declare that the beginning of things was due to corruption by pleasure?’ And when they were asked this question by me, they acknowledged, ‘Yes.’

Then I said this to them: ‘But in what way do you, venerable sirs, declare that the beginning of things was due to corruption by pleasure?’ When asked by me, they are unable to explain. Being unable to explain, they cross-question me. When questioned by them, I explain.
commentary_pali: 41.Khiḍḍāpadosikanti khiḍḍāpadosikamūlaṃ.
commentary_english: 41. khiḍḍāpadosikanti: The root of *khiḍḍāpadosika*.

mula_pali:
42. ‘Santāvuso, khiḍḍāpadosikā nāma devā. Te ativelaṃ hassakhiḍḍāratidhammasamāpannā hasakhiḍḍāratidhammasamāpannā (ka.) viharanti. Tesaṃ ativelaṃ hassakhiḍḍāratidhammasamāpannānaṃ viharataṃ sati sammussati, satiyā sammosā satiyā sammosāya (syā.) te devā tamhā kāyā cavanti.

‘Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, āvuso, vijjati, yaṃ aññataro satto tamhā kāyā cavitvā itthattaṃ āgacchati, itthattaṃ āgato samāno agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajati, agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito samāno ātappamanvāya padhānamanvāya anuyogamanvāya appamādamanvāya sammāmanasikāramanvāya tathārūpaṃ cetosamādhiṃ phusati, yathāsamāhite citte taṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati; tato paraṃ nānussarati.

‘So evamāha – ye kho te bhonto devā na khiḍḍāpadosikā te na ativelaṃ hassakhiḍḍāratidhammasamāpannā viharanti. Tesaṃ nātivelaṃ hassakhiḍḍāratidhammasamāpannānaṃ viharataṃ sati na sammussati, satiyā asammosā te devā tamhā kāyā na cavanti, niccā dhuvā sassatā avipariṇāmadhammā sassatisamaṃ tatheva ṭhassanti. Ye pana mayaṃ ahumhā khiḍḍāpadosikā te mayaṃ ativelaṃ hassakhiḍḍāratidhammasamāpannā viharimhā, tesaṃ no ativelaṃ hassakhiḍḍāratidhammasamāpannānaṃ viharataṃ sati sammussati, satiyā sammosā evaṃ sammosā eva (sī. pī.) sammosā te (syā. ka.) mayaṃ tamhā kāyā cutā, aniccā addhuvā appāyukā cavanadhammā itthattaṃ āgatāti. Evaṃvihitakaṃ no tumhe āyasmanto khiḍḍāpadosikaṃ ācariyakaṃ aggaññaṃ paññapethā’ti. ‘Te evamāhaṃsu – evaṃ kho no, āvuso gotama, sutaṃ, yathevāyasmā gotamo āhā’ti. ‘‘Aggaññañcāhaṃ, bhaggava, pajānāmi…pe… yadabhijānaṃ tathāgato no anayaṃ āpajjati.

sammosā eva (sī. pī.) sammosā te (syā. ka.)
mula_english:
‘Friends, there are gods called *khiḍḍāpadosikā* (corrupted by pleasure). They live indulging excessively in laughter, play, delight, and attachment to the Dhamma. When they live excessively indulging in laughter, play, delight, and attachment to the Dhamma, mindfulness is confused in them; due to the confusion of mindfulness, those gods fall away from that body.

‘It is possible, friend, that a certain being, having fallen away from that body, comes to this state; having come to this state, he goes forth from the household life into homelessness; having gone forth from the household life into homelessness, he, following ardour, following exertion, following application, following diligence, following right attention, touches a *ceto-samādhi* (concentration of mind) of such a kind that, with his mind well concentrated, he recollects that former dwelling place; but he does not recollect beyond that.

‘He speaks thus: “Those honourable gods who are not *khiḍḍāpadosikā* do not live excessively indulging in laughter, play, delight, and attachment to the Dhamma. When they live not excessively indulging in laughter, play, delight, and attachment to the Dhamma, mindfulness is not confused in them; due to the non-confusion of mindfulness, those gods do not fall away from that body; they are permanent, stable, eternal, not subject to change, and they will remain the same just like eternity itself.” Those of us who were *khiḍḍāpadosikā* lived excessively indulging in laughter, play, delight, and attachment to the Dhamma. When we lived excessively indulging in laughter, play, delight, and attachment to the Dhamma, mindfulness was confused in us; due to the confusion of mindfulness, we fell away from that body, we are impermanent, unstable, short-lived, subject to falling away, and we have come to this state.”

‘Is it in this way that you, venerable sirs, expound the teaching about those gods corrupted by pleasure and about the origin of the world?’

‘They spoke thus: “Yes, friend Gotama, we have heard it thus, just as the venerable Gotama says.”

‘‘Bhaggava, I understand the origin of the world… and the *Tathāgata* does not incur misfortune by realizing it."

mula_pali: 43. ‘‘Santi, bhaggava, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā manopadosikaṃ ācariyakaṃ aggaññaṃ paññapenti. Tyāhaṃ upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ vadāmi – ‘saccaṃ kira tumhe āyasmanto manopadosikaṃ ācariyakaṃ aggaññaṃ paññapethā’ti? Te ca me evaṃ puṭṭhā ‘āmo’ti paṭijānanti. Tyāhaṃ evaṃ vadāmi – ‘kathaṃvihitakaṃ pana tumhe āyasmanto manopadosikaṃ ācariyakaṃ aggaññaṃ paññapethā’ti? Te mayā puṭṭhā na sampāyanti, asampāyantā mamaññeva paṭipucchanti. Tesāhaṃ puṭṭho byākaromi –
mula_english:
‘There are some ascetics and Brahmins, Bhaggava, who propound the doctrine (ācariyakaṃ) that the beginning of things (aggaññaṃ) was due to corruption of mind (manopadosikaṃ).

I approach them and say: ‘Is it true that you, venerable sirs, propound the doctrine that the beginning of things was due to corruption of mind?’ And when they are questioned by me in this way, they acknowledge it, saying: ‘Yes.’

Then I say to them: ‘But in what way do you, venerable sirs, propound the doctrine that the beginning of things was due to corruption of mind?’ When questioned by me, they cannot explain, and being unable to explain, they cross-question me.

And when I am questioned, I explain:

mula_pali:
44. ‘Santāvuso, manopadosikā nāma devā. Te ativelaṃ aññamaññaṃ upanijjhāyanti. Te ativelaṃ aññamaññaṃ upanijjhāyantā aññamaññamhi cittāni padūsenti. Te aññamaññaṃ paduṭṭhacittā kilantakāyā kilantacittā. Te devā tamhā kāyā cavanti.

‘Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, āvuso, vijjati, yaṃ aññataro satto tamhā kāyā cavitvā itthattaṃ āgacchati. Itthattaṃ āgato samāno agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajati. Agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito samāno ātappamanvāya padhānamanvāya anuyogamanvāya appamādamanvāya sammāmanasikāramanvāya tathārūpaṃ cetosamādhiṃ phusati, yathāsamāhite citte taṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati, tato paraṃ nānussarati.

‘So evamāha – ye kho te bhonto devā na manopadosikā te nātivelaṃ aññamaññaṃ upanijjhāyanti. Te nātivelaṃ aññamaññaṃ upanijjhāyantā aññamaññamhi cittāni nappadūsenti. Te aññamaññaṃ appaduṭṭhacittā akilantakāyā akilantacittā. Te devā tamhā akilantacittā tamhā (ka.) kāyā na cavanti, niccā dhuvā sassatā avipariṇāmadhammā sassatisamaṃ tatheva ṭhassanti. Ye pana mayaṃ ahumhā manopadosikā, te mayaṃ ativelaṃ aññamaññaṃ upanijjhāyimhā. Te mayaṃ ativelaṃ aññamaññaṃ upanijjhāyantā aññamaññamhi cittāni padūsimhā padosiyimhā (syā.), padūsayimhā (?). Te mayaṃ aññamaññaṃ paduṭṭhacittā kilantakāyā kilantacittā. Evaṃ mayaṃ kilantacittāeva mayaṃ (sī. pī.), kilantacittā (ka.) tamhā kāyā cutā, aniccā addhuvā appāyukā cavanadhammā itthattaṃ āgatāti. Evaṃvihitakaṃ no tumhe āyasmanto manopadosikaṃ ācariyakaṃ aggaññaṃ paññapethā’ti. ‘Te evamāhaṃsu – evaṃ kho no, āvuso gotama, sutaṃ, yathevāyasmā gotamo āhā’ti. ‘‘Aggaññañcāhaṃ, bhaggava, pajānāmi…pe… yadabhijānaṃ tathāgato no anayaṃ āpajjati.

akilantacittā tamhā (ka.) padosiyimhā (syā.), padūsayimhā (?) kilantacittāeva mayaṃ (sī. pī.), kilantacittā (ka.)
mula_english:
44. “There are, friends, certain *devas* called Corrupted in Mind (*manopadosikā nāma devā*). They spend an excessive amount of time regarding each other with envy. As a consequence, their minds become corrupted. On account of their corrupted minds, they become weary in body and mind. And they fall from that place (*te devā tamhā kāyā cavanti*).

It can happen that a being, having fallen from that state, arises in this world (*itthattam āgacchati*). Having arisen in this world, he goes forth from the household life into homelessness. Having gone forth, by means of effort, exertion, application, diligence, and right reflection, he attains to such a degree of mental concentration that with his mind thus concentrated he recollects his immediately preceding life (*pubbenivāsaṃ*), but none previous to that.

He speaks thus: ‘Those honorable gods who are not corrupted by mind (*na manopadosikā*) do not contemplate each other with excessive envy. As a result, their minds do not become corrupted by anger towards one another. Their bodies and minds do not become exhausted. And so they do not fall from that state. They are permanent, stable, eternal, not subject to change, the same for ever and ever. But we, who are corrupted in mind (*manopadosikā*)… We contemplated each other with excessive envy. And as a result, our minds became corrupted by anger towards one another. When our minds were corrupted by anger, our bodies and minds became exhausted. We have fallen from that state, we are impermanent, unstable, short-lived, fated to fall away, and we have come to this world.’ That, Reverend Sits, is how it comes about that you teach that the beginning of things was due to corruption of mind. “ And they said: ”We have heard this, Reverend Gotama, as you have explained.” “I understand the most excellent knowledge (*aggaññaṃ*), Bhaggava... and I know not only that, but what surpasses it in value. And I am not under the sway of what I know, and not being under its sway I have come to know for myself that quenching, by the realisation of which the *Tathāgata* cannot fall into perilous paths.

mula_pali: 45. ‘‘Santi, bhaggava, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā adhiccasamuppannaṃ ācariyakaṃ aggaññaṃ paññapenti. Tyāhaṃ upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ vadāmi – ‘saccaṃ kira tumhe āyasmanto adhiccasamuppannaṃ ācariyakaṃ aggaññaṃ paññapethā’ti? Te ca me evaṃ puṭṭhā ‘āmo’ti paṭijānanti. Tyāhaṃ evaṃ vadāmi – ‘kathaṃvihitakaṃ pana tumhe āyasmanto adhiccasamuppannaṃ ācariyakaṃ aggaññaṃ paññapethā’ti? Te mayā puṭṭhā na sampāyanti, asampāyantā mamaññeva paṭipucchanti. Tesāhaṃ puṭṭho byākaromi –
mula_english:
"Bhaggava, there are some ascetics and Brahmins who declare as their doctrine that all things began by chance (*adhiccasamuppannaṃ ācariyakaṃ aggaññaṃ paññapenti*).

Then I go to them and say, 'Is it true that you, venerable sirs, declare as your doctrine that all things began by chance?' And when I ask them this, they acknowledge it.

Then I say to them, 'In what way do you, venerable sirs, declare as your doctrine that all things began by chance?' But when I ask them this, they cannot explain, and so they ask me in return.

And I replied:

mula_pali:
46. ‘Santāvuso, asaññasattā nāma devā. Saññuppādā ca pana te devā tamhā kāyā cavanti.

‘Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, āvuso, vijjati. Yaṃ aññataro satto tamhā kāyā cavitvā itthattaṃ āgacchati. Itthattaṃ āgato samāno agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajati. Agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito samāno ātappamanvāya padhānamanvāya anuyogamanvāya appamādamanvāya sammāmanasikāramanvāya tathārūpaṃ cetosamādhiṃ phusati, yathāsamāhite citte taṃ idaṃ padaṃ brahmajālasutte na dissati. evaṃ (pī. ka.) saññuppādaṃ anussarati, tato paraṃ nānussarati.

idaṃ padaṃ brahmajālasutte na dissati. evaṃ (pī. ka.)

‘So evamāha – adhiccasamuppanno attā ca loko ca. Taṃ kissa hetu? Ahañhi pubbe nāhosiṃ, somhi etarahi ahutvā santatāya sattakāya (sī. pī.), sattāya (ka. sī.) pariṇatoti. Evaṃvihitakaṃ no tumhe āyasmanto adhiccasamuppannaṃ ācariyakaṃ aggaññaṃ paññapethā’ti? ‘Te evamāhaṃsu – evaṃ kho no, āvuso gotama, sutaṃ yathevāyasmā gotamo āhā’ti. ‘‘Aggaññañcāhaṃ, bhaggava, pajānāmi tañca pajānāmi, tato ca uttaritaraṃ pajānāmi, tañca pajānaṃ na parāmasāmi, aparāmasato ca me paccattaññeva nibbuti viditā. Yadabhijānaṃ tathāgato no anayaṃ āpajjati.

sattakāya (sī. pī.), sattāya (ka. sī.)
mula_english:
46. “There are, friends, certain *devas* called Non-percipient Beings (*asaññasattā nāma devā*). As soon as a perception arises in them, those *devas* pass away from that plane (*saññuppādā ca pana te devā tamhā kāyā cavanti*).

‘And it can happen, friends, that a being, having fallen from that state, arises in this world (*yaṃ aññataro satto tamhā kāyā cavitvā itthattaṃ āgacchati*). Having come to this world (*itthattaṃ āgato samāno*), he goes forth from the household life into homelessness (*agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajati*). Having gone forth from the household life into homelessness (*agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajito samāno*), by means of effort (*ātappamanvāya*), exertion (*padhānamanvāya*), application (*anuyogamanvāya*), earnestness (*appamādamanvāya*) and right attention (*sammāmanasikāramanvāya*) he attains to such a degree of mental concentration (*tathārūpaṃ cetosamādhiṃ phusati*) that with his mind thus concentrated (*yathāsamāhite citte*) he recalls his last existence (*saññuppādaṃ anussarati*), but none before that (*tato paraṃ nānussarati*).

‘He speaks thus: ‘The self (*attā*) and the world (*loko*) originate fortuitously (*adhiccasamuppanno*). What is the reason for that (*taṃ kissa hetu*)? Because formerly I did not exist (*pubbe nāhosiṃ*), [but] now I am, having come into being from non-being (*ahutvā santatāya pariṇatoti*).’

“Do you, venerable sirs, teach a theory of the origin by chance (*adhiccasamuppannaṃ ācariyakaṃ aggaññaṃ paññapethā’ti*)?"

"They say thus: ‘Thus, friend Gotama, have we heard, just as the venerable Gotama says (*evaṃ kho no, āvuso gotama, sutaṃ yathevāyasmā gotamo āhā’ti*)."

‘‘Bhaggava, I know the first beginning of things (*aggaññañcāhaṃ, bhaggava, pajānāmi tañca pajānāmi*), and I know what surpasses it in value (*tato ca uttaritaraṃ pajānāmi*). And I am not under the sway of what I know (*tañca pajānaṃ na parāmasāmi*), and not being under its sway I have come to know for myself that quenching (*aparāmasato ca me paccattaññeva nibbuti viditā*), by the realization of which the *Tathāgata* cannot fall into perilous paths (*yadabhijānaṃ tathāgato no anayaṃ āpajjati*).

mula_pali:
47. ‘‘Evaṃvādiṃ kho maṃ, bhaggava, evamakkhāyiṃ eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā asatā tucchā musā abhūtena abbhācikkhanti – ‘viparīto samaṇo gotamo bhikkhavo ca. Samaṇo gotamo evamāha – yasmiṃ samaye subhaṃ vimokkhaṃ upasampajja viharati, sabbaṃ tasmiṃ samaye asubhantveva asubhanteva (sī. syā. pī.) pajānātī’ti sañjānātīti (sī. pī.). Na kho panāhaṃ, bhaggava, evaṃ vadāmi – ‘yasmiṃ samaye subhaṃ vimokkhaṃ upasampajja viharati, sabbaṃ tasmiṃ samaye asubhantveva pajānātī’ti. Evañca khvāhaṃ, bhaggava, vadāmi – ‘yasmiṃ samaye subhaṃ vimokkhaṃ upasampajja viharati, subhantveva tasmiṃ samaye pajānātī’ti.

‘‘Te ca, bhante, viparītā, ye bhagavantaṃ viparītato dahanti bhikkhavo ca. Evaṃpasanno ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavati. Pahoti me bhagavā tathā dhammaṃ desetuṃ, yathā ahaṃ subhaṃ vimokkhaṃ upasampajja vihareyya’’nti.
mula_english:
47. “And I, Bhaggava, who teach this and declare this am wrongly, vainly, lyingly and falsely accused by some ascetics and Brahmins who say: ”The ascetic Gotama is on the wrong track, and so are his monks.
The ascetic Gotama has declared that whoever has attained to the stage of deliverance called ‘the Beautiful’ finds everything repulsive.”

But I, Bhaggava, do not say that whoever has attained to the deliverance called ‘the Beautiful’ finds everything repulsive.
What l say is that whenever anyone has attained to the stage of deliverance called ”the Beautiful”, he knows ‘that it is beautiful.’

“Indeed, Lord, they are on the wrong track themselves who accuse the Lord and his monks of error.
I am so delighted with the Lord
that I think the Lord is able to teach me the *dharma* in such a way that I can attain and remain in the deliverance called ”the Beautiful”.’
commentary_pali: 47.Asatāti avijjamānena, asaṃvijjamānaṭṭhenāti attho. Tucchāti tucchena antosāravirahitena. Musāti musāvādena. Abhūtenāti bhūtatthavirahitena. Abbhācikkhantīti abhiācikkhanti. Viparītoti viparītasañño viparītacitto. Bhikkhavo cāti na kevalaṃ samaṇo gotamoyeva, ye ca assa anusiṭṭhiṃ karonti, te bhikkhū ca viparītā. Atha yaṃ sandhāya viparītoti vadanti, taṃ dassetuṃ samaṇo gotamotiādi vuttaṃ. Subhaṃ vimokkhanti vaṇṇakasiṇaṃ. Asubhantvevāti subhañca asubhañca sabbaṃ asubhanti evaṃ pajānāti. Subhantveva tasmiṃ samayeti subhanti eva ca tasmiṃ samaye pajānāti, na asubhaṃ. Bhikkhavo cāti ye te evaṃ vadanti, tesaṃ bhikkhavo ca antevāsikasamaṇā viparītā. Pahotīti samattho paṭibalo.
commentary_english:
47. *Asatā* means by that which is non-existent, in the sense of not being found.

*Tucchā* means by that which is empty, devoid of inner essence.

*Musā* means by false speech (*mṛṣāvāda*).

*Abhūtenā* means by that which is devoid of truth.

*Abbhācikkhantī* means they accuse.

*Viparīto* means with perverted perception (*viparītasaṃjño*), with perverted mind (*viparītacitto*).

*Bhikkhavo cā* means not only the renunciate Gautama, but also those monks (*bhikṣu*) who do his teaching, those monks are also perverted.

Then, with reference to what do they say "perverted"? To show that, *samaṇo gotamo* etc. was said.

*Subhaṃ vimokkha* means color meditation (*varṇakasiṇa*).

*Asubhantvevā* means understanding thus, "Both the beautiful (*śubha*) and the unbeautiful (*aśubha*) are all unbeautiful (*aśubha*)."

*Subhantveva tasmiṃ samaye* means understanding thus, "Only the beautiful (*śubha*) at that time," not the unbeautiful (*aśubha*).

*Bhikkhavo cā* means those renunciates who speak thus, their renunciate disciples are perverted.

*Pahotī* means capable, competent.

mula_pali:
48. ‘‘Dukkaraṃ kho etaṃ, bhaggava, tayā aññadiṭṭhikena aññakhantikena aññarucikena aññatrāyogena aññatrācariyakena subhaṃ vimokkhaṃ upasampajja viharituṃ. Iṅgha tvaṃ, bhaggava, yo ca te ayaṃ mayi pasādo, tameva tvaṃ sādhukamanurakkhā’’ti. ‘‘Sace taṃ, bhante, mayā dukkaraṃ aññadiṭṭhikena aññakhantikena aññarucikena aññatrāyogena aññatrācariyakena subhaṃ vimokkhaṃ upasampajja viharituṃ. Yo ca me ayaṃ, bhante, bhagavati pasādo, tamevāhaṃ sādhukamanurakkhissāmī’’ti. Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamano bhaggavagotto paribbājako bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti.

Pāthikasuttaṃ pāṭikasuttantaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) niṭṭhitaṃ paṭhamaṃ.

pāṭikasuttantaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.)
mula_english:
48. “It is difficult, Bhaggava, for you, holding different views (*aññaditṭhikena*), being of different inclinations (*aññakhantikena*), of different tastes (*aññarucikena*), following a different discipline (*aññatrāyogena*), and having had a different teacher (*aññatrācariyakena*), to attain and abide in the deliverance called "the Beautiful" (*subhaṃ vimokkhaṃ*).

You must strive hard, Bhaggava, putting your trust (*prasāda*) in me, you must safeguard that trust (*sādhukamanurakkhā*) in me."

"Lord (*bhante*), even if it is hard for me to attain and abide in the deliverance called "the Beautiful" (*subhaṃ vimokkhaṃ*), with different views (*aññadiṭṭhikena*), different inclinations (*aññakhantikena*), different tastes (*aññarucikena*), a different discipline (*aññatrāyogena*), and a different teacher (*aññatrācariyakena*), still I will place my trust (*prasāda*) in the Blessed One (*bhagavati*), I will carefully safeguard that trust (*sādhukamanurakkhissāmi*)."

Thus it was said by the Blessed One (*bhagavā*).

Bhaggava of the Bhaggava clan, the wanderer (*paribbājako*), was delighted and rejoiced at the Blessed One's (*bhagavato*) words (*bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti*).

The *Pāthikasuttaṃ* is finished, the first.
commentary_pali:
48.Dukkaraṃ khoti ayaṃ paribbājako yadidaṃ ‘‘evaṃpasanno ahaṃ, bhante’’tiādimāha, taṃ sāṭheyyena kohaññena āha. Evaṃ kirassa ahosi – ‘‘samaṇo gotamo mayhaṃ ettakaṃ dhammakathaṃ kathesi, tamahaṃ sutvāpi pabbajituṃ na sakkomi, mayā etassa sāsanaṃ paṭipannasadisena bhavituṃ vaṭṭatī’’ti. Tato so sāṭheyyena kohaññena evamāha. Tenassa bhagavā mammaṃ ghaṭṭento viya ‘‘dukkaraṃ kho etaṃ, bhaggava tayā aññadiṭṭhikenā’’tiādimāha. Taṃ poṭṭhapādasutte vuttatthameva. Sādhukamanurakkhāti suṭṭhu anurakkha.

Iti bhagavā pasādamattānurakkhaṇe paribbājakaṃ niyojesi. Sopi evaṃ mahantaṃ suttantaṃ sutvāpi nāsakkhi kilesakkhayaṃ kātuṃ. Desanā panassa āyatiṃ vāsanāya paccayo ahosi. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānatthamevāti.

Sumaṅgalavilāsiniyā dīghanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Pāthikasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
"Difficult indeed ( *dukkaraṃ kho* )": This mendicant ( *paribbājaka* ) said this, beginning with "I am pleased in this way, venerable sir ( *evaṃpasanno ahaṃ, bhante* )", deceitfully and hypocritically ( *sāṭheyyena kohaññena* ).

Thus it occurred to him: “The *śramaṇa* Gautama ( *samaṇo gotamo* ) spoke this much discourse on the *dharma* ( *dhammakathaṃ* ), but having heard it, I am not able to go forth as a renunciate ( *pabbajituṃ na sakkomi* ); it is fitting that I be one who is similar to one committed to his teaching ( *etassa sāsanaṃ paṭipannasadisena bhavituṃ vaṭṭatī* )."

Then he said thus deceitfully and hypocritically ( *sāṭheyyena kohaññena evamāha* ).

Because of that, the Blessed One ( *bhagavā* ), as if touching a vital spot ( *mammaṃ ghaṭṭento viya* ), said, "Difficult indeed is this ( *dukkaraṃ kho etaṃ* ), Bhaggava, for you, holding another view ( *tayā aññadiṭṭhikenā* )."

That is just the meaning as stated in the Poṭṭhapāda Sūtra ( *taṃ poṭṭhapādasutte vuttatthameva* ).

"Well guarded ( *sādhukamanurakkhā* )": Guard well ( *suṭṭhu anurakkha* ).

Thus, the Blessed One ( *bhagavā* ) directed the mendicant ( *paribbājakaṃ niyojesi* ) in guarding only his own serenity ( *pasādamattānurakkhaṇe* ).

Even he, having heard such a great *sūtra* ( *mahantaṃ suttantaṃ sutvāpi* ), was not able to make an end to the afflictions ( *nāsakkhi kilesakkhayaṃ kātuṃ* ).

The teaching ( *desanā* ), however, was a condition for the development of his disposition in the future ( *āyatiṃ vāsanāya paccayo ahosi* ).

The rest is clear throughout ( *sesaṃ sabbattha uttānatthamevāti* ).

The Pāthikasuttavaṇṇanā is finished.

mula_pali: 49. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati gijjhakūṭe pabbate. Tena kho pana samayena nigrodho paribbājako udumbarikāya paribbājakārāme paṭivasati mahatiyā paribbājakaparisāya saddhiṃ tiṃsamattehi paribbājakasatehi. Atha kho sandhāno gahapati divā divassa divādivasseva (sī. syā. pī.) rājagahā nikkhami bhagavantaṃ dassanāya. Atha kho sandhānassa gahapatissa etadahosi – ‘‘akālo kho bhagavantaṃ dassanāya. Paṭisallīno bhagavā. Manobhāvanīyānampi bhikkhūnaṃ asamayo dassanāya. Paṭisallīnā manobhāvanīyā bhikkhū. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ yena udumbarikāya paribbājakārāmo, yena nigrodho paribbājako tenupasaṅkameyya’’nti. Atha kho sandhāno gahapati yena udumbarikāya paribbājakārāmo, tenupasaṅkami.
mula_english:
49. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One (bhagavā) was dwelling at Rājagaha on the Vulture Peak (Gijjhakūṭa) Mountain.

At that time, the wanderer Nigrodha was staying at the Udumbarika rest-house for wanderers, with a large company of some three hundred wanderers.

Then Sandhāna, the householder (gahapati), one morning, left Rājagaha in order to see the Blessed One (bhagavantaṃ) .

Then Sandhāna, the householder, thought: "It is not the proper time to see the Blessed One (bhagavantaṃ). The Blessed One (bhagavā) is in retreat. It is not the proper time to see even the monks worthy of esteem. The monks worthy of esteem are in retreat. Perhaps I should go to the Udumbarika rest-house for wanderers, and visit Nigrodha, the wanderer."

Then Sandhāna, the householder, went to the Udumbarika rest-house for wanderers.
commentary_pali:
49.Evaṃme sutanti udumbarikasuttaṃ. Tatrāyamapubbapadavaṇṇanā – paribbājakoti channaparibbājako. Udumbarikāya paribbājakārāmeti udumbarikāya deviyā santake paribbājakārāme. Sandhānoti tassa nāmaṃ. Ayaṃ pana mahānubhāvo parivāretvā vicarantānaṃ pañcannaṃ upāsakasatānaṃ aggapuriso anāgāmī bhagavatā mahāparisamajjhe evaṃ saṃvaṇṇito –

‘‘Chahi, bhikkhave, aṅgehi samannāgato sandhāno gahapati tathāgate niṭṭhaṅgato saddhamme iriyati. Katamehi chahi? Buddhe aveccappasādena dhamme aveccappasādena saṅghe aveccappasādena ariyena sīlena ariyena ñāṇena ariyāya vimuttiyā. Imehi kho, bhikkhave, chahi aṅgehi samannāgato sandhāno gahapati tathāgate niṭṭhaṅgato saddhamme iriyatī’’ti (a. ni. 6.120-139).

So pātoyeva uposathaṅgāni adhiṭṭhāya pubbaṇhasamaye buddhappamukhassa saṅghassa dānaṃ datvā bhikkhūsu vihāraṃ gatesu ghare khuddakamahallakānaṃ dārakānaṃ saddena ubbāḷho satthu santike ‘‘dhammaṃ sossāmī’’ti nikkhanto. Tena vuttaṃ divā divassa rājagahā nikkhamīti. Tattha divā divassāti divasassa divā nāma majjhanhātikkamo, tasmiṃ divasassāpi divābhūte atikkantamatte majjhanhike nikkhamīti attho. Paṭisallīnoti tato tato rūpādigocarato cittaṃ paṭisaṃharitvā nilīno jhānaratisevanāvasena ekībhāvaṃ gato. Manobhāvanīyānanti manavaḍḍhakānaṃ. Ye ca āvajjato manasikaroto cittaṃ vinīvaraṇaṃ hoti unnamati vaḍḍhati.

divā divassa rājagahā nikkhamī divā divassā Paṭisallīno Manobhāvanīyāna
commentary_english:
49. Thus, I have heard: the Uḍumbarika Sūtra.

Here follows a word-by-word explanation of the beginning: *Paribbājaka* means a wandering mendicant. *Udumbarikāya paribbājakārāme* means in the monastery of the wandering mendicants belonging to Uḍumbarikā. *Sandhāno* means his name.

Now, this great and powerful Sandhāna, surrounded by and attending to five hundred lay followers, the foremost, a non-returner, was thus praised by the Blessed One in the great assembly:

"Sandhāna, householder, is endowed with six qualities, has put down his anchor in the Tathāgata, and fares on in the true Dhamma. Which six? He has unwavering faith in the Buddha ( *buddhe aveccappasādena*), unwavering faith in the Dhamma ( *dhamme aveccappasādena*), unwavering faith in the Saṅgha ( *saṅghe aveccappasādena*), noble morality ( *ariyena sīlena*), noble knowledge ( *ariyena ñāṇena*), and noble liberation ( *ariyāya vimuttiyā*). Sandhāna, householder, endowed with these six qualities, has put down his anchor in the Tathāgata, and fares on in the true Dhamma" (A.
iii.
120-139).

In the morning, he would undertake the *uposatha* vows, and in the forenoon, having given alms to the Saṅgha, with the Buddha at its head, after the monks had gone to the monastery, he, overwhelmed by the noise of the young and old children in the house, would leave, thinking, "I will hear the Dhamma," to the presence of the Teacher.

Therefore, it was said: "He went out from Rājagṛha in the day."

There, *divā divassā* means during the day, namely after the passing of noon; the meaning is that he went out at midday, when the day had already become day.

*Paṭisallīno* means having withdrawn his mind from this and that, from objects such as forms, having secluded himself, having gone to a state of oneness through cultivating the pleasure of meditation. *Manobhāvanīyāna* means of those who increase the mind. And those who cultivate and apply their minds, the mind becomes free from hindrances, rises up, and increases.

He went out from Rājagṛha in the day. During the day. Secluded. Of those who increase the mind.

mula_pali: 50. Tena kho pana samayena nigrodho paribbājako mahatiyā paribbājakaparisāya saddhiṃ nisinno hoti unnādiniyā uccāsaddamahāsaddāya anekavihitaṃ tiracchānakathaṃ kathentiyā. Seyyathidaṃ – rājakathaṃ corakathaṃ mahāmattakathaṃ senākathaṃ bhayakathaṃ yuddhakathaṃ annakathaṃ pānakathaṃ vatthakathaṃ sayanakathaṃ mālākathaṃ gandhakathaṃ ñātikathaṃ yānakathaṃ gāmakathaṃ nigamakathaṃ nagarakathaṃ janapadakathaṃ itthikathaṃ sūrakathaṃ visikhākathaṃ kumbhaṭṭhānakathaṃ pubbapetakathaṃ nānattakathaṃ lokakkhāyikaṃ samuddakkhāyikaṃ itibhavābhavakathaṃ iti vā.
mula_english: At that time, Nigrodha the wanderer was sitting with a large assembly of wanderers, who were making an uproar, loudly and noisily talking many kinds of pointless talk ( *tiracchānakathaṃ* ). Namely: talk of kings (*rājakathaṃ*), talk of robbers (*corakathaṃ*), talk of high officials (*mahāmattakathaṃ*), talk of armies (*senākathaṃ*), talk of fear (*bhayakathaṃ*), talk of war (*yuddhakathaṃ*), talk of food (*annakathaṃ*), talk of drinks (*pānakathaṃ*), talk of clothing (*vatthakathaṃ*), talk of beds (*sayanakathaṃ*), talk of garlands (*mālākathaṃ*), talk of perfumes (*gandhakathaṃ*), talk of relatives (*ñātikathaṃ*), talk of vehicles (*yānakathaṃ*), talk of villages (*gāmakathaṃ*), talk of towns (*nigamakathaṃ*), talk of cities (*nagarakathaṃ*), talk of countries (*janapadakathaṃ*), talk of women (*itthikathaṃ*), talk of heroes (*sūrakathaṃ*), talk of street gossip (*visikhākathaṃ*), talk of wells (*kumbhaṭṭhānakathaṃ*), talk of deceased ancestors (*pubbapetakathaṃ*), talk of various things (*nānattakathaṃ*), world stories (*lokakkhāyikaṃ*), sea stories (*samuddakkhāyikaṃ*), talk of thus it is or thus it is not (*itibhavābhavakathaṃ*), and so on.
commentary_pali: 50.Unnādiniyātiādīni poṭṭhapādasutte vitthāritanayeneva veditabbāni.
commentary_english: The *unnādiniyā*, etc., should be understood just as they have been explained in detail in the *Poṭṭhapāda Sutta*.

mula_pali: 51. Addasā kho nigrodho paribbājako sandhānaṃ gahapatiṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvā sakaṃ parisaṃ saṇṭhāpesi – ‘‘appasaddā bhonto hontu, mā bhonto saddamakattha. Ayaṃ samaṇassa gotamassa sāvako āgacchati sandhāno gahapati. Yāvatā kho pana samaṇassa gotamassa sāvakā gihī odātavasanā rājagahe paṭivasanti, ayaṃ tesaṃ aññataro sandhāno gahapati. Appasaddakāmā kho panete āyasmanto appasaddavinītā , appasaddassa vaṇṇavādino. Appeva nāma appasaddaṃ parisaṃ viditvā upasaṅkamitabbaṃ maññeyyā’’ti. Evaṃ vutte te paribbājakā tuṇhī ahesuṃ.
mula_english: Then Nigrodha the wanderer saw the householder Sandhana approaching from afar. Seeing him, he called his followers to order, saying: "Be quiet, gentlemen, don’t make a noise, gentlemen! The householder Sandhana, a follower of the ascetic Gotama, is approaching. He is one of the number of white-robed householder followers of the ascetic Gotama in Rajagaha. These venerable ones are fond of quiet, trained in quiet, and speak in praise of quiet. Maybe, if he perceives our group as quiet, he will consider it worth his while to come our way.” When this was said, the wanderers fell silent.
commentary_pali: 51.Yāvatāti yattakā. Ayaṃ tesaṃ aññataroti ayaṃ tesaṃ abbhantaro eko sāvako, bhagavato kira sāvakā gihianāgāminoyeva pañcasatā rājagahe paṭivasanti. Yesaṃ ekekassa pañca pañca upāsakasatāni parivārā, te sandhāya ‘‘ayaṃ tesaṃ aññataro’’ti āha. Appeva nāmāti tassa upasaṅkamanaṃ patthayamāno āha. Patthanākāraṇaṃ pana poṭṭhapādasutte vuttameva.
commentary_english:
51. *yāvatā* means as many as; *yattakā.*

*ayaṃ tesaṃ aññataro* means this is one of them, an intimate disciple of the Blessed One. It is said that five hundred disciples of the Blessed One, all householders who would not return to this world, resided in Rājagaha.

With reference to those who each had five hundred lay followers ( *upāsaka*) in their retinue, he said, "This is one of them."

*appeva nāmā* means hoping for an opportunity to approach him, he said:

The reason for this aspiration has already been stated in the Poṭṭhapāda Sutta.

mula_pali: 52. Atha kho sandhāno gahapati yena nigrodho paribbājako tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā nigrodhena paribbājakena saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho sandhāno gahapati nigrodhaṃ paribbājakaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘aññathā kho ime bhonto aññatitthiyā paribbājakā saṅgamma samāgamma unnādino uccāsaddamahāsaddā anekavihitaṃ tiracchānakathaṃ anuyuttā viharanti. Seyyathidaṃ – rājakathaṃ…pe… itibhavābhavakathaṃ iti vā. Aññathā kho ca (sī. pī.) pana so bhagavā araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevati appasaddāni appanigghosāni vijanavātāni manussarāhasseyyakāni paṭisallānasāruppānī’’ti.
mula_english:
Then Sandhāna, the householder, approached Nigrodha the wanderer, and having approached, exchanged greetings with Nigrodha the wanderer. When the courteous and amiable talk was finished, he sat down at one side.

As he sat down at one side, Sandhāna the householder said to Nigrodha the wanderer: ‘Reverend sirs, the way the wanderers of another faith conduct themselves when they come together is one thing: they are noisy and loud, given to all kinds of frivolous talk, such as talk about kings (*rājakathaṃ*), …and talk about being and non-being (*itibhavābhavakathaṃ*).

The Blessed Lord’s way is different: he seeks a lodging in the forest (*araññavanapatthāni*), in the depths of the jungle, free from noise, with little sound, far from the madding crowd, undisturbed by men, well fitted for seclusion.’
commentary_pali: 52.Etadavocāti āgacchanto antarāmaggeyeva tesaṃ kathāya sutattā etaṃ aññathā kho imetiādivacanaṃ avoca. Tattha aññatitthiyāti dassanenapi ākappenapi kuttenapi ācārenapi vihārenapi iriyāpathenapi aññe titthiyāti aññatitthiyā. Saṅgamma samāgammāti saṅgantvā samāgantvā rāsi hutvā nisinnaṭṭhāne. Araññavanapatthānīti araññavanapatthāni gāmūpacārato muttāni dūrasenāsanāni. Pantānīti dūratarāni manussūpacāravirahitāni. Appasaddānīti vihārūpacārena gacchato addhikajanassapi saddena mandasaddāni. Appanigghosānīti avibhāvitatthena nigghosena mandanigghosāni. Vijanavātānīti antosañcārino janassa vātena vigatavātāni. Manussarāhasseyyakānīti manussānaṃ rahassakaraṇassa yuttāni anucchavikāni. Paṭisallānasāruppānīti ekībhāvassa anurūpāni. Iti sandhāno gahapati ‘‘aho mama satthā yo evarūpāni senāsanāni paṭisevatī’’ti añjaliṃ paggayha uttamaṅge sirasmiṃ patiṭṭhapetvā imaṃ udānaṃ udānento nisīdi.
commentary_english:
52. "Having said, `*etadavocā*,'" [it means that] while they were coming along the road, because of the conversation among themselves, they were excited, and he spoke this statement, "`*aññathā kho ime*,' etc."

There, "*aññatitthiyā*" means that by appearance, by manner, by fraud, by conduct, by dwelling, and by deportment, they are other *tīrthika*s, therefore, they are "*aññatitthiyā*."

"*saṅgamma samāgammā*" means having come together, having assembled, having become a heap, at a place where they were sitting.

"*araññavanapatthānī*" means forest and woodland resting places, remote dwellings, free from village vicinity.

"*pantānī*" means very distant, devoid of human resort.

"*appasaddānī*" means with little sound, due to the sound of those who go to the monastery vicinity, [and] even for the sake of the sound of travelers, they are places with subdued sound.

"*appanigghosānī*" means with indistinct noise, with indistinct sound, places with subdued noise.

"*vijanavātānī*" means the winds of people who travel inside, the winds that are free from wind.

"*manussarāhasseyyakānī*" means suitable and appropriate for people's secret deeds.

"*paṭisallānasāruppānī*" means corresponding to solitude.

Thus, Sandhāno the householder, thinking, "Oh, my teacher frequents such dwellings!" raised his joined palms (*añjali*) and having placed them on the top of his head, sat down uttering this solemn utterance (*udāna*).

mula_pali: 53. Evaṃ vutte nigrodho paribbājako sandhānaṃ gahapatiṃ etadavoca – ‘‘yagghe gahapati, jāneyyāsi, kena samaṇo gotamo saddhiṃ sallapati, kena sākacchaṃ samāpajjati, kena paññāveyyattiyaṃ samāpajjati? Suññāgārahatā samaṇassa gotamassa paññā aparisāvacaro samaṇo gotamo nālaṃ sallāpāya. So antamantāneva sevati antapantāneva (syā.). Seyyathāpi nāma gokāṇā pariyantacārinī antamantāneva sevati. Evameva suññāgārahatā samaṇassa gotamassa paññā; aparisāvacaro samaṇo gotamo; nālaṃ sallāpāya. So antamantāneva sevati. Iṅgha, gahapati, samaṇo gotamo imaṃ parisaṃ āgaccheyya, ekapañheneva naṃ saṃsādeyyāma saṃhareyyāma (ka.), tucchakumbhīva naṃ maññe orodheyyāmā’’ti.
mula_english:
Having spoken thus, Nigrodha the wanderer said this to Sandhāna the householder: "Come now, householder, would that you might know with whom the *śramaṇa* Gautama converses, with whom he engages in discussion, and through what he attains proficiency in wisdom (*prajñā*). The wisdom (*prajñā*) of the *śramaṇa* Gautama is ruined by solitary dwelling; the *śramaṇa* Gautama is unused to assemblies and is no good at conversation. He frequents only the outskirts."

"Just as bison circling around keep to the fringes, even so, the wisdom (*prajñā*) of the *śramaṇa* Gautama is ruined by solitary dwelling; the *śramaṇa* Gautama is unused to assemblies; he is no good at conversation. He frequents only the outskirts. Come now, householder, should the *śramaṇa* Gautama come to this assembly, we would confound him with a single question, we would, I think, knock him over like an empty pot."
commentary_pali:
53.Evaṃ vutteti evaṃ sandhānena gahapatinā udānaṃ udānentena vutte. Nigrodho paribbājako ayaṃ gahapati mama santike nisinnopi attano satthāraṃyeva thometi ukkaṃsati, amhe pana atthītipi na maññati, etasmiṃ uppannakopaṃ samaṇassa gotamassa upari pātessāmīti sandhānaṃ gahapatiṃ etadavoca.

Yaggheti codanatthe nipāto. Jāneyyāsīti bujjheyyāsi passeyyāsi. Kena samaṇo gotamo saddhiṃ sallapatīti kena kāraṇena kena puggalena saddhiṃ samaṇo gotamo sallapati vadati bhāsati. Kiṃ vuttaṃ hoti – ‘‘yadi kiñci sallāpakāraṇaṃ bhaveyya, yadi vā koci samaṇassa gotamassa santikaṃ sallāpatthiko gaccheyya, sallapeyya, na pana kāraṇaṃ atthi, na tassa santikaṃ koci gacchati, svāyaṃ kena samaṇo gotamo saddhiṃ sallapati, asallapanto kathaṃ unnādī bhavissatī’’ti.

Yagghe Jāneyyāsī Kena samaṇo gotamo saddhiṃ sallapatī

Sākacchanti saṃsandanaṃ. Paññāveyyattiyanti uttarapaccuttaranayena ñāṇabyattabhāvaṃ. Suññāgārahatāti suññāgāresu naṭṭhā, samaṇena hi gotamena bodhimūle appamattikā paññā adhigatā, sāpissa suññāgāresu ekakassa nisīdato naṭṭhā. Yadi pana mayaṃ viya gaṇasaṅgaṇikaṃ katvā nisīdeyya, nāssa paññā nasseyyāti dasseti. Aparisāvacaroti avisāradattā parisaṃ otarituṃ na sakkoti. Nālaṃ sallāpāyāti na samattho sallāpaṃ kātuṃ. Antamantānevāti koci maṃ pañhaṃ puccheyyāti pañhābhīto antamantāneva pantasenāsanāni sevati. Gokāṇāti ekakkhihatā kāṇagāvī. Sā kira pariyantacārinī hoti, antamantāneva sevati. Sā kira kāṇakkhibhāvena vanantābhimukhīpi na sakkoti bhavituṃ. Kasmā? Yasmā pattena vā sākhāya vā kaṇṭakena vā pahārassa bhāyati. Gunnaṃ abhimukhīpi na sakkoti bhavituṃ. Kasmā? Yasmā siṅgena vā kaṇṇena vā vālena vā pahārassa bhāyati. Iṅghāti codanatthe nipāto. Saṃsādeyyāmāti ekapañhapucchaneneva saṃsādanaṃ visādamāpannaṃ kareyyāma. Tucchakumbhīva nanti rittaghaṭaṃ viya naṃ. Orodheyyāmāti vinandheyyāma. Pūritaghaṭo hi ito cito ca parivattetvā na suvinandhanīyo hoti. Rittako yathāruci parivattetvā sakkā hoti vinandhituṃ, evameva hatapaññatāya rittakumbhisadisaṃ samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ vādavinandhanena samantā vinandhissāmāti vadati.

Sākaccha Paññāveyyattiya Suññāgārahatā Aparisāvacaro Nālaṃ sallāpāyā Antamantānevā Gokāṇā Iṅghā Saṃsādeyyāmā Tucchakumbhīva na Orodheyyāmā

Iti paribbājako satthu suvaṇṇavaṇṇaṃ nalāṭamaṇḍalaṃ apassanto dasabalassa parammukhā attano balaṃ dīpento asambhinnaṃ khattiyakumāraṃ jātiyā ghaṭṭayanto caṇḍālaputto viya asambhinnakesarasīhaṃ migarājānaṃ thāmena ghaṭṭento jarasiṅgālo viya ca nānappakāraṃ tucchagajjitaṃ gajji. Upāsakopi cintesi ‘‘ayaṃ paribbājako ati viya gajjati, avīciphusanatthāya pādaṃ, bhavaggaggahaṇatthāya hatthaṃ pasārayanto viya niratthakaṃ vāyamati. Sace me satthā imaṃ ṭhānamāgaccheyya, imassa paribbājakassa yāva bhavaggā ussitaṃ mānaddhajaṃ ṭhānasova opāteyyā’’ti.
commentary_english:
53.
"Thus spoken" means thus spoken by the householder, with such a combination of words, uttering a solemn utterance.

Nigrodha the wandering ascetic [thought:] "This householder, even sitting near me, praises and exalts his own teacher. He does not even acknowledge that we exist. Now I will vent the anger that has arisen in me upon the ascetic Gotama." Such was his intention when he spoke these words to the householder:

"Indeed!" is a particle indicating incitement.

"You should know" means you should understand, you should see.

"With whom does the *śramaṇa* Gotama converse?" means with what reason, with what individual does the *śramaṇa* Gotama converse, speak, and address.

What is said is this: "If there should be any cause for conversation, or if any conversationalist should go to the *śramaṇa* Gotama's presence, he would converse. But there is no cause, no one goes to his presence. So with whom does the *śramaṇa* Gotama converse? Not conversing, how will he become eloquent?"

Indeed! You should know! With whom does the *śramaṇa* Gotama converse?

"Having conversation" means association.

"Manifestation of wisdom" means the state of making wisdom clear through the method of question and answer.

"Habituated to solitary dwellings" means ruined in solitary dwellings. For the wisdom that the *śramaṇa* Gotama attained at the foot of the *bodhi* tree, though he was conscientious, was ruined when he lived alone in solitary dwellings. He shows that if he were to sit with a group and an assembly, as we do, his wisdom would not be ruined.

"Not frequenting assemblies" means he is unable to enter an assembly due to lack of confidence.

"Not competent for conversation" means not capable of making conversation.

"Only to the very ends" means because he is afraid that someone will ask him a question, being fearful of questions, he resorts only to remote forest resting places.

"Cow with a defect" means a one-eyed, injured, blind cow.

That cow, it is said, is accustomed to wandering on the periphery, she resorts only to the very ends.

That cow, it is said, is unable to face the forest edge because of being one-eyed.

Why? Because she fears being struck by a leaf or a branch or a thorn.

She is also unable to face the herds.

Why? Because she fears being struck by a horn or an ear or a tail.

"Indeed!" is a particle indicating incitement.

"We should cause him to be depressed" means by asking a single question, we should cause him to be dejected and to meet with misfortune.

"Like an empty pot, no" means like an empty vessel, no.

"We should obstruct" means we should ruin.

For a full pot, having been turned this way and that, is not easily ruined.

An empty one, having been turned as one pleases, is able to be ruined. Just so, with the ruin of wisdom, we will completely ruin the *śramaṇa* Gotama, who is like an empty pot, with the ruin of argument, so he says.

Having conversation, manifestation of wisdom, habituated to solitary dwellings, not frequenting assemblies, not competent for conversation, only to the very ends, cow with a defect, indeed!, we should cause him to be depressed, like an empty pot, no, we should obstruct.

Thus, the wandering ascetic, not seeing the golden-colored brow of the Teacher, turning his back on the strength of the Ten Powers, showing his own strength, harassing the unconfused Kṣatriya youth by [mentioning his] birth, like a *caṇḍāla*'s son, striking the unimpaired lion with a mane, roaring out various kinds of empty roars while striking the king of beasts with force, like an old jackal.

The lay follower also thought, "This wandering ascetic is roaring excessively, like someone stretching out his foot to touch *Avīci*, stretching out his hand to grasp the peak of existence [*Bhavāgra*], he is striving fruitlessly.

If my Teacher should come to this place, he would depose that wandering ascetic's flag of pride, raised up to the peak of existence, from its very place!"

mula_pali:
54. Assosi kho bhagavā dibbāya sotadhātuyā visuddhāya atikkantamānusikāya sandhānassa gahapatissa nigrodhena paribbājakena saddhiṃ imaṃ kathāsallāpaṃ. Atha kho bhagavā gijjhakūṭā pabbatā orohitvā yena sumāgadhāya tīre moranivāpo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā sumāgadhāya tīre moranivāpe abbhokāse caṅkami. Addasā kho nigrodho paribbājako bhagavantaṃ sumāgadhāya tīre moranivāpe abbhokāse caṅkamantaṃ. Disvāna sakaṃ parisaṃ saṇṭhāpesi – ‘‘appasaddā bhonto hontu, mā bhonto saddamakattha, ayaṃ samaṇo gotamo sumāgadhāya tīre moranivāpe abbhokāse caṅkamati. Appasaddakāmo kho pana so āyasmā, appasaddassa vaṇṇavādī. Appeva nāma appasaddaṃ parisaṃ viditvā upasaṅkamitabbaṃ maññeyya. Sace samaṇo gotamo imaṃ parisaṃ āgaccheyya, imaṃ taṃ pañhaṃ puccheyyāma – ‘ko nāma so, bhante, bhagavato dhammo, yena bhagavā sāvake vineti, yena bhagavatā sāvakā vinītā assāsappattā paṭijānanti ajjhāsayaṃ ādibrahmacariya’nti? Evaṃ vutte te paribbājakā tuṇhī ahesuṃ.

Tapojigucchāvādo
mula_english:
Now the Lord, with his divine-ear-faculty, purified and surpassing human range, heard this exchange between Sandhāna the householder and Nigrodha the wanderer.

Then the Lord, descending from Vulture Peak (Gijjhakūṭa), went to the Peacocks’ Feeding Ground (moranivāpo) beside the Sumāgadhā Tank; having arrived, he walked up and down (caṅkami) in the open air at the Peacocks’ Feeding Ground beside the Sumāgadhā Tank.

Then Nigrodha the wanderer saw the Lord walking up and down (caṅkamantaṃ) in the open air at the Peacocks’ Feeding Ground beside the Sumāgadhā Tank.

Seeing him, he called his company to order, saying: ‘Gentlemen, be quiet (appasaddā), be less noisy (mā saddamakattha)! The ascetic Gotama is walking up and down (caṅkamati) in the open air at the Peacocks’ Feeding Ground beside the Sumāgadhā Tank.

That venerable one is fond of quiet (appasaddakāmo), and speaks in praise of quiet (appasaddassa vaṇṇavādī).

Maybe, if he perceives our group as quiet (appasaddaṃ parisaṃ viditvā), he will consider it worthwhile to come our way (upasaṅkamitabbaṃ maññeyya).

If the ascetic Gotama comes to this company, we could ask him this question: “Lord (bhante), what is this doctrine (dhammo) in which the Blessed Lord (bhagavato) trains his disciples (sāvake vineti), and which those disciples (sāvakā) whom the Blessed Lord (bhagavatā) has so trained as to benefit from it (vinītā assāsappattā) recognise as their principal support (ajjhāsayaṃ), and the perfection of the holy life (ādibrahmacariya)?”’ When this was said, those wanderers were silent (tuṇhī ahesuṃ).

Discussion of loathing for asceticism (tapojigucchāvādo).
commentary_pali:
54. Bhagavāpi tesaṃ taṃ kathāsallāpaṃ assosiyeva. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘assosi kho imaṃ kathāsallāpa’’nti.

Sumāgadhāyāti sumāgadhā nāma pokkharaṇī, yassā tīre nisinno aññataro puriso padumanāḷantarehi asurabhavanaṃ pavisantaṃ asurasenaṃ addasa. Moranivāpoti nivāpo vuccati bhattaṃ, yattha morānaṃ abhayena saddhiṃ nivāpo dinno, taṃ ṭhānanti attho. Abbhokāseti aṅgaṇaṭṭhāne. Assāsapattāti tuṭṭhipattā somanassapattā. Ajjhāsayanti uttamanissayabhūtaṃ. Ādibrahmacariyanti purāṇabrahmacariyasaṅkhātaṃ ariyamaggaṃ. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – ‘‘ko nāma so, bhante, dhammo yena bhagavatā sāvakā vinītā ajjhāsayādibrahmacariyabhūtaṃ ariyamaggaṃ pūretvā arahattādhigamavasena assāsapattā paṭijānantī’’ti.

Sumāgadhāyā Moranivāpo Abbhokāse Assāsapattā Ajjhāsaya Ādibrahmacariya

Tapojigucchāvādavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
54. The Blessed One heard their conversation. Therefore, it was said, "He heard this conversation."

*Sumāgadhāya*: Sumāgadhā is the name of a pond on whose bank a certain man, sitting, saw an army of *asuras* entering the *asura* abode through the interior of lotus stalks.

*Moranivāpo*: *Nivāpo* is called food; the place where food was given to the peacocks along with safety, that is the meaning.

*Abbhokāse*: In an open place, in the courtyard.

*Assāsapattā*: Attained satisfaction, attained joy.

*Ajjhāsaya*: Being of excellent reliance.

*Ādibrahmacariya*: <pb ed="v" n="3. 0018"/> The Noble Path, known as the ancient holy life (brahmacariya). This is what was said – “What, venerable sir, is that *dharma* by which the disciples, being led by the Blessed One, having fulfilled the Noble Path, which is the basis of excellent reliance and the beginning of the holy life, acknowledge that they have attained satisfaction by way of attaining Arhatship?”

*Sumāgadhāya*, *Moranivāpo*, *Abbhokāse*, *Assāsapattā*, *Ajjhāsaya*, *Ādibrahmacariya* <pb ed="v" n="3. 0018"/>

Explanation of the Discourse on Austerity and Disgust.

mula_pali: 55. Atha kho bhagavā yena nigrodho paribbājako tenupasaṅkami. Atha kho nigrodho paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘etu kho, bhante, bhagavā, svāgataṃ, bhante, bhagavato. Cirassaṃ kho, bhante, bhagavā imaṃ pariyāyamakāsi yadidaṃ idhāgamanāya. Nisīdatu, bhante, bhagavā, idamāsanaṃ paññatta’’nti. Nisīdi bhagavā paññatte āsane. Nigrodhopi kho paribbājako aññataraṃ nīcāsanaṃ gahetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho nigrodhaṃ paribbājakaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – ‘‘kāya nuttha, nigrodha, etarahi kathāya sannisinnā, kā ca pana vo antarākathā vippakatā’’ti? Evaṃ vutte, nigrodho paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca, ‘‘idha mayaṃ, bhante, addasāma bhagavantaṃ sumāgadhāya tīre moranivāpe abbhokāse caṅkamantaṃ, disvāna evaṃ avocumhā – ‘sace samaṇo gotamo imaṃ parisaṃ āgaccheyya, imaṃ taṃ pañhaṃ puccheyyāma – ko nāma so, bhante, bhagavato dhammo, yena bhagavā sāvake vineti, yena bhagavatā sāvakā vinītā assāsappattā paṭijānanti ajjhāsayaṃ ādibrahmacariya’nti? Ayaṃ kho no, bhante, antarākathā vippakatā; atha bhagavā anuppatto’’ti.
mula_english:
Then the Blessed One approached Nigrodha the wanderer.

Then Nigrodha the wanderer said to the Blessed One: “Come, Blessed One, welcome, Blessed One!

It is long since the Blessed One found an opportunity to come here.

Be seated, Lord, a seat is prepared.”

The Blessed One sat down on the prepared seat (paññatte āsane).

And Nigrodha the wanderer took a low seat and sat down to one side.

Then the Blessed One said to Nigrodha the wanderer, who was sitting to one side: “Nigrodha, what was the subject of your conversation just now? What talk have I interrupted?”

When this was said, Nigrodha the wanderer said to the Blessed One, “Here, venerable sir, we saw the Blessed One walking up and down in the open air on the bank of the Sumāgadhā (river), at the Peacock Feeding Ground; and having seen (him), we spoke thus: ‘If the ascetic Gotama were to come to this assembly, we would ask him this question: “What, venerable sir, is that doctrine of the Blessed One by which the Blessed One trains his disciples, and through which the disciples trained by the Blessed One, having attained confidence, acknowledge the essence of the fundamental holy life (ādibrahmacariya)?” That, venerable sir, was the interrupted topic of our conversation; then the Blessed One arrived.’”
commentary_pali: 55.Vippakatāti mamāgamanapaccayā aniṭṭhitā, va hutvā ṭhitā, kathehi, ahametaṃ niṭṭhapetvā matthakaṃ pāpetvā dassemīti sabbaññupavāraṇaṃ pavāresi.
commentary_english: "Vippakatā" means unfinished due to my arrival; having become thus, he remains. "Tell [it], I will finish this, bring it to completion, and show [it]," he invited the *sabbaññupavāraṇa*.

mula_pali: 56. ‘‘Dujjānaṃ kho etaṃ, nigrodha, tayā aññadiṭṭhikena aññakhantikena aññarucikena aññatrāyogena aññatrācariyakena, yenāhaṃ sāvake vinemi , yena mayā sāvakā vinītā assāsappattā paṭijānanti ajjhāsayaṃ ādibrahmacariyaṃ. Iṅgha tvaṃ maṃ, nigrodha, sake ācariyake adhijegucche pañhaṃ puccha – ‘kathaṃ santā nu kho, bhante, tapojigucchā paripuṇṇā hoti, kathaṃ aparipuṇṇā’ti? Evaṃ vutte te paribbājakā unnādino uccāsaddamahāsaddā ahesuṃ – ‘‘acchariyaṃ vata bho, abbhutaṃ vata bho, samaṇassa gotamassa mahiddhikatā mahānubhāvatā, yatra hi nāma sakavādaṃ ṭhapessati, paravādena pavāressatī’’ti.
mula_english:
“Nigrodha, it is difficult for you, who hold different views, have different inclinations, different preferences, follow a different practice, and have a different teacher, to understand the doctrine which I teach my disciples... My disciples, having been trained by me, have attained confidence and acknowledge the essence of the holy life.

Therefore, Nigrodha, ask me a question concerning your own teacher's doctrine and ascetic practices: ‘How is asceticism perfected, venerable sir, and how is it not perfected?’" When this was said, those wanderers were excited, making a great noise: "It is wonderful, truly! It is amazing, truly! The ascetic Gotama has such great power and influence that he will establish his own doctrine and refute the doctrine of others!"
commentary_pali: 56.Dujjānaṃ khoti bhagavā paribbājakassa vacanaṃ sutvā ‘‘ayaṃ paribbājako mayā sāvakānaṃ desetabbaṃ dhammaṃ tehi pūretabbaṃ paṭipattiṃ pucchati, sacassāhaṃ āditova taṃ kathessāmi, kathitampi naṃ na jānissati, ayaṃ pana vīriyena pāpajigucchanavādo, handāhaṃ etasseva visaye pañhaṃ pucchāpetvā puthusamaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ laddhiyā niratthakabhāvaṃ dassemi. Atha pacchā imaṃ pañhaṃ byākarissāmī’’ti cintetvā dujjānaṃ kho etantiādimāha. Tattha sake ācariyaketi attano ācariyavāde. Adhijeguccheti vīriyena pāpajigucchanabhāve. Kathaṃ santāti kathaṃ bhūtā. Tapojigucchāti vīriyena pāpajigucchā pāpavivajjanā. Paripuṇṇāti parisuddhā. Kathaṃaparipuṇṇāti kathaṃ aparisuddhā hotīti evaṃ pucchāti. Yatra hi nāmāti yo nāma.
commentary_english:
56.
“*Dujjānaṃ kho*,” having heard the words of the wanderer, the Blessed One [said]: “This wanderer is asking me about the Dharma that should be taught to my disciples, the practice that should be fulfilled by them. If I were to explain it to him from the beginning, he would not understand what was said. However, this is a doctrine of disgust with evil through vigor. Let me ask him a question on this very subject and show the worthlessness of the views of various ascetics and Brahmins.”
Then, thinking, “I will explain this question later,” he spoke, beginning with “*Dujjānaṃ kho etaṃ*.”
There, "*sake ācariyake*," means in his own teacher's doctrine.
"*Adhijegucche*," means in the state of disgust with evil through vigor.
"*Kathaṃ santā*," means how are they?
"*Tapojigucchā*," means disgust with evil through vigor, avoidance of evil.
"*Paripuṇṇā*," means completely purified (*parishuddhā*).
"*Kathaṃ aparipuṇṇā*," means how are they not completely purified (*aparisuddhā*)? Thus he asks.
"*Yatra hi nāmā*," means whatever name.

mula_pali:
57. Atha kho nigrodho paribbājako te paribbājake appasadde katvā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘mayaṃ kho, bhante, tapojigucchāvādā tarojigucchaṃsārodā (ka.) tapojigucchāsārā tapojigucchāallīnā viharāma . Kathaṃ santā nu kho, bhante, tapojigucchā paripuṇṇā hoti, kathaṃ aparipuṇṇā’’ti?

‘‘Idha, nigrodha, tapassī acelako hoti muttācāro, hatthāpalekhano hatthāvalekhano (syā.), na ehibhaddantiko, na tiṭṭhabhaddantiko, nābhihaṭaṃ , na uddissakataṃ, na nimantanaṃ sādiyati, so na kumbhimukhā paṭiggaṇhāti, na kaḷopimukhā paṭiggaṇhāti, na eḷakamantaraṃ, na daṇḍamantaraṃ, na musalamantaraṃ, na dvinnaṃ bhuñjamānānaṃ, na gabbhiniyā, na pāyamānāya, na purisantaragatāya, na saṅkittīsu, na yattha sā upaṭṭhito hoti, na yattha makkhikā saṇḍasaṇḍacārinī, na macchaṃ, na maṃsaṃ, na suraṃ, na merayaṃ, na thusodakaṃ pivati, so ekāgāriko vā hoti ekālopiko, dvāgāriko vā hoti dvālopiko, sattāgāriko vā hoti sattālopiko, ekissāpi dattiyā yāpeti, dvīhipi dattīhi yāpeti, sattahipi dattīhi yāpeti; ekāhikampi āhāraṃ āhāreti, dvīhikampi dvāhikaṃpi (sī. syā.) āhāraṃ āhāreti, sattāhikampi āhāraṃ āhāreti, iti evarūpaṃ addhamāsikampi pariyāyabhattabhojanānuyogamanuyutto viharati. So sākabhakkho vā hoti, sāmākabhakkho vā hoti, nīvārabhakkho vā hoti, daddulabhakkho vā hoti, haṭabhakkho vā hoti, kaṇabhakkho vā hoti, ācāmabhakkho vā hoti, piññākabhakkho vā hoti, tiṇabhakkho vā hoti, gomayabhakkho vā hoti; vanamūlaphalāhāro yāpeti pavattaphalabhojī. So sāṇānipi dhāreti , masāṇānipi dhāreti, chavadussānipi dhāreti, paṃsukūlānipi dhāreti, tirīṭānipi dhāreti, ajinampi dhāreti, ajinakkhipampi dhāreti, kusacīrampi dhāreti, vākacīrampi dhāreti, phalakacīrampi dhāreti, kesakambalampi dhāreti, vāḷakambalampi dhāreti, ulūkapakkhampi dhāreti, kesamassulocakopi hoti kesamassulocanānuyogamanuyutto , ubbhaṭṭhakopi ubhaṭṭhakopi (syā.), ubbhaṭṭhikopi (ka.) hoti āsanapaṭikkhitto, ukkuṭikopi hoti ukkuṭikappadhānamanuyutto, kaṇṭakāpassayikopi hoti kaṇṭakāpassaye seyyaṃ kappeti, phalakaseyyampi kappeti, thaṇḍilaseyyampi kappeti, ekapassayikopi hoti rajojalladharo, abbhokāsikopi hoti yathāsanthatiko, vekaṭikopi hoti vikaṭabhojanānuyogamanuyutto, apānakopi hoti apānakattamanuyutto, sāyatatiyakampi udakorohanānuyogamanuyutto viharati. Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, nigrodha, yadi evaṃ sante tapojigucchā paripuṇṇā vā hoti aparipuṇṇā vā’’ti? ‘‘Addhā kho, bhante, evaṃ sante tapojigucchā paripuṇṇā hoti, no aparipuṇṇā’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ paripuṇṇāyapi kho ahaṃ, nigrodha, tapojigucchāya anekavihite upakkilese vadāmī’’ti.

hatthāvalekhano (syā.) dvāhikaṃpi (sī. syā.) ubhaṭṭhakopi (syā.), ubbhaṭṭhikopi (ka.)

Upakkileso
mula_english:
57. Then Nigrodha the wanderer, silencing those wanderers, said this to the Blessed One: "Venerable Sir, we are advocates of, hold essential, and adhere to the practice of higher austerities.

How, Venerable Sir, is the practice of higher austerities fulfilled, and how is it unfulfilled?"

"Here, Nigrodha, a certain ascetic is naked (*acelaka*), rejects conventions, licks his hands, does not come when asked, does not stop when asked; he does not accept food brought or food specially made or an invitation to a meal; he receives nothing from a pot, from a bowl, across a threshold, across a stick, across a pestle, from two eating together, from a pregnant woman, from a woman giving suck, from a woman lying with a man, from where food is advertised to be distributed, from where a dog is waiting, from where flies are buzzing; he accepts no fish or meat, he drinks no liquor, wine, or fermented brew; he keeps to one house, to one morsel; he keeps to two houses to two morsels; he keeps to seven houses, to seven morsels. He lives on one saucerful a day, on two saucerfuls a day on seven saucerfuls a day. He takes food once a day, once every two days once every seven days, and so on up to once every fortnight; he dwells pursuing the practice of taking food at stated intervals.

He is an eater of greens or millet or wild rice or hide-parings or moss or rice-bran or rice-scum or sesamum flour or grass or cow-dung. He lives on forest roots and fruits, he feeds on fallen fruits.

He wears coarse hemp or mixed material, shrouds from corpses, rags from the dust-heap, garments of bark-fibre, antelope-skins, grass, bark, shavings, blankets of human hair or horse-hair, the wings of owls. He is a plucker-out of hair and beard, devoted to this practice; he is one who stands continuously, rejecting seats. He is one who squats continuously, devoted to maintaining the squatting position. He is one who uses a mattress of spikes; he makes a mattress of spikes his bed. He dwells pursuing the practice of bathing in water three times daily including the evening.

What do you think, Nigrodha, is the higher austerity thereby fulfilled, or not?"

"Indeed, Venerable Sir, the higher austerity is thereby fulfilled, not unfulfilled."

"But, Nigrodha, I maintain that this higher austerity can be faulted in various ways."

Upakkileso [Defilement].
commentary_pali:
57.Appasaddekatvāti nirave appasadde katvā. So kira cintesi – ‘‘samaṇo gotamo ekaṃ pañhampi na katheti, sallāpakathāpissa atibahukā natthi, ime pana ādito paṭṭhāya samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ anuvattanti ceva pasaṃsanti ca, handāhaṃ ime nissadde katvā sayaṃ kathemī’’ti. So tathā akāsi. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘appasadde katvā’’ti. ‘‘Tapojigucchavādā’’tiādīsu tapojigucchaṃ vadāma, manasāpi tameva sārato gahetvā vicarāma, kāyenapimhā tameva allīnā, nānappakārakaṃ attakilamathānuyogamanuyuttā viharāmāti attho.

Upakkilesavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
57. Having made [them] *appasadde*, having made [them] *nirave appasadde*.

So, he considered – “The renunciant Gotama does not speak even a single question; he does not have very much conversational speech either; however, these ones follow the renunciant Gotama from the beginning, and they also praise [him]; come, I will make these ones silent and speak myself.”

This was done.

Therefore it was said, "Having made [them] *appasadde*."

In "[They are advocates of mortification, disgusted (jiguccha) with austerity (tapas)]," we speak of being disgusted with austerity (tapojiguccha), we roam about, even in mind, grasping it as essential; we are attached to that very thing even in body; meaning, we live engaged in various kinds of practices of self-mortification (*attakilamathānuyoga*).

Description of the defilements (*upakkilesavaṇṇanā*).

mula_pali:
58. ‘‘Yathā kathaṃ pana, bhante, bhagavā evaṃ paripuṇṇāya tapojigucchāya anekavihite upakkilese vadatī’’ti? ‘‘Idha, nigrodha, tapassī tapaṃ samādiyati, so tena tapasā attamano hoti paripuṇṇasaṅkappo. Yampi, nigrodha, tapassī tapaṃ samādiyati, so tena tapasā attamano hoti paripuṇṇasaṅkappo. Ayampi kho, nigrodha, tapassino upakkileso hoti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī tapaṃ samādiyati, so tena tapasā attānukkaṃseti paraṃ vambheti. Yampi, nigrodha, tapassī tapaṃ samādiyati, so tena tapasā attānukkaṃseti paraṃ vambheti. Ayampi kho, nigrodha, tapassino upakkileso hoti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī tapaṃ samādiyati, so tena tapasā majjati mucchati pamādamāpajjati madamāpajjati (syā.). Yampi, nigrodha, tapassī tapaṃ samādiyati, so tena tapasā majjati mucchati pamādamāpajjati. Ayampi kho, nigrodha, tapassino upakkileso hoti.

madamāpajjati (syā.)
mula_english:
58. “In what way, Lord (bhante), does the Blessed One (bhagavā) maintain that there are defilements (upakkilese) connected with rigorous asceticism (tapojigucchāya) which are described in various ways?”

“Here, Nigrodha, a self-mortifier (tapassī) undertakes a certain austerity (tapaṃ samādiyati), and as a result, he is pleased (attamano hoti) and satisfied at having attained his end (paripuṇṇasaṅkappo). Again, Nigrodha, a self-mortifier undertakes a certain austerity, and as a result, he is pleased and satisfied at having attained his end. And this is a fault (upakkileso hoti) in that self-mortifier (tapassino).

“Again, Nigrodha, a self-mortifier undertakes a certain austerity, and in so doing he elevates himself (attānukkaṃseti) and disparages others (paraṃ vambheti). Again, Nigrodha, a self-mortifier undertakes a certain austerity, and in so doing he elevates himself and disparages others. And this is a fault in that self-mortifier.

“Again, Nigrodha, a self-mortifier undertakes a certain austerity, and as a result, he has become intoxicated (majjati) with conceit, infatuated (mucchati) and therefore careless (pamādamāpajjati). Again, Nigrodha, a self-mortifier undertakes a certain austerity, and as a result, he has become intoxicated with conceit, infatuated and therefore careless. And this is a fault in that self-mortifier.
commentary_pali:
58.Tapassīti tapanissitako. ‘‘Acelako’’tiādīni sīhanāde (dī. ni. aṭṭha. 1.393) vitthāritanayeneva veditabbāni. Tapaṃ samādiyatīti acelakabhāvādikaṃ tapaṃ sammā ādiyati, daḷhaṃ gaṇhāti. Attamano hotīti ko añño mayā sadiso imasmiṃ tape atthīti tuṭṭhamano hoti. Paripuṇṇasaṅkappoti alamettāvatāti evaṃ pariyositasaṅkappo, idañca titthiyānaṃ vasena āgataṃ. Sāsanāvacarenāpi pana dīpetabbaṃ. Ekacco hi dhutaṅgaṃ samādiyati, so teneva dhutaṅgena ko añño mayā sadiso dhutaṅgadharoti attamano hoti paripuṇṇasaṅkappo. Tapassino upakkileso hotīti duvidhassāpetassa tapassino ayaṃ upakkileso hoti. Ettāvatāyaṃ tapo upakkileso hotīti vadāmi.

Attānukkaṃsetīti ‘‘ko mayā sadiso atthī’’ti attānaṃ ukkaṃsati ukkhipati. Paraṃ vambhetīti ‘‘ayaṃ na mādiso’’ti paraṃ saṃhāreti avakkhipati.

Attānukkaṃsetī Paraṃ vambhetī

Majjatīti mānamadakaraṇena majjati. Mucchatīti mucchito hoti gadhito ajjhāpanno. Pamādamāpajjatīti etadeva sāranti pamādamāpajjati. Sāsane pabbajitopi dhutaṅgasuddhiko hoti, na kammaṭṭhānasuddhiko. Dhutaṅgameva arahattaṃ viya sārato pacceti.

Majjatī Mucchatī Pamādamāpajjatī
commentary_english:
58. *Tapassī* means one who is dependent on austerity (*tapanissita*).

"Acelako" etc. [should be understood] according to the expanded method in the *Sīhanāda Sutta* (Dīgha Nikāya), Nikāya, Aṭṭha. 1. 393) as it has been explained in detail.

*Tapaṃ samādiyatī* means he properly undertakes austerity (*tapa*) beginning with the state of being naked (*acelakabhāva*), he firmly grasps [it].

*Attamano hotī* means he is delighted (*tuṭṭhamano*) thinking, "Who else is like me in this austerity (*tapas*)?"

*Paripuṇṇasaṅkappo* means his resolve is completely fulfilled (*pariyositasaṅkappo*) in this way, "Enough of loving-kindness," and this comes about through the influence of the Tīrthikas.

It should also be illuminated by one who is involved in the Buddha's teaching (*sāsanāvacarena*).

A certain person undertakes the practice of the ascetic observances (*dhutaṅgaṃ samādiyati*), and he is delighted (*attamano*) thinking, "Who else is like me, a possessor of the ascetic observances (*dhutaṅgadharo*)?" Thus, his resolve is completely fulfilled (*paripuṇṇasaṅkappo*).

*Tapassino upakkileso hotī* means this defilement (*upakkileso*) occurs to an ascetic (*tapassino*) who is devoid of two qualities (*duvidhassāpeta*).

I say that to this extent, austerity (*tapo*) becomes a defilement (*upakkileso hotīti*).

*Attānukkaṃsetī* means he praises himself (*attānaṃ ukkaṃsati ukkhipati*) thinking, "Who is like me?"

*Paraṃ vambhetī* means he disparages others (*paraṃ saṃhāreti avakkhipati*) thinking, "This one is not like me."

He lauds himself (*attānukkaṃsetī*) and disparages others (*paraṃ vambhetī*).

*Majjatī* means he is intoxicated (*majjati*) with the making of pride and arrogance (*mānamadakaraṇena*).

*Mucchatī* means he is infatuated (*mucchito hoti*), attached (*gadhito*), and completely devoted (*ajjhāpanno*).

*Pamādamāpajjatī* means he falls into negligence (*pamādamāpajjati*), considering this very thing to be the essence (*sāranti*).

Even if one has gone forth in the Buddha's teaching (*sāsane pabbajitopi*), he is purified by the ascetic observances (*dhutaṅgasuddhiko hoti*), but not purified by the meditation subject (*kammaṭṭhānasuddhiko*).

He regards the ascetic observances (*dhutaṅgameva*) as the essence (*sārato pacceti*), as if [they were] *arhatship* (*arahattaṃ viya*).

He is intoxicated (*majjatī*), infatuated (*mucchatī*), and falls into negligence (*pamādamāpajjatī*).

mula_pali:
59. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī tapaṃ samādiyati, so tena tapasā lābhasakkārasilokaṃ abhinibbatteti, so tena lābhasakkārasilokena attamano hoti paripuṇṇasaṅkappo. Yampi, nigrodha, tapassī tapaṃ samādiyati, so tena tapasā lābhasakkārasilokaṃ abhinibbatteti, so tena lābhasakkārasilokena attamano hoti paripuṇṇasaṅkappo. Ayampi kho, nigrodha, tapassino upakkileso hoti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī tapaṃ samādiyati, so tena tapasā lābhasakkārasilokaṃ abhinibbatteti, so tena lābhasakkārasilokena attānukkaṃseti paraṃ vambheti. Yampi, nigrodha, tapassī tapaṃ samādiyati, so tena tapasā lābhasakkārasilokaṃ abhinibbatteti, so tena lābhasakkārasilokena attānukkaṃseti paraṃ vambheti. Ayampi kho, nigrodha, tapassino upakkileso hoti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī tapaṃ samādiyati, so tena tapasā lābhasakkārasilokaṃ abhinibbatteti, so tena lābhasakkārasilokena majjati mucchati pamādamāpajjati. Yampi, nigrodha, tapassī tapaṃ samādiyati, so tena tapasā lābhasakkārasilokaṃ abhinibbatteti, so tena lābhasakkārasilokena majjati mucchati pamādamāpajjati. Ayampi kho, nigrodha, tapassino upakkileso hoti.
mula_english:
‘Again, Nigrodha, a self-mortifier undertakes austerity, and through that austerity, he gains, honour, and fame (lābhasakkārasilokaṃ abhinibbatteti). He is pleased with that gain, honour, and renown, and his intention is fulfilled (attamano hoti paripuṇṇasaṅkappo).

Or else, Nigrodha, a self-mortifier undertakes austerity, and through that austerity, he gains, honour, and fame. He is pleased with that gain, honour, and renown, and his intention is fulfilled.

And this, Nigrodha, is a fault (upakkileso) in that self-mortifier.

Again, Nigrodha, a self-mortifier undertakes austerity, and through that austerity, he gains, honour, and fame. Or else he elevates himself (attānukkaṃseti) and disparages others (paraṃ vambheti).

Or else, Nigrodha, a self-mortifier undertakes austerity, and through that austerity, he gains, honour, and fame. Or else he elevates himself and disparages others.

And this, Nigrodha, is a fault in that self-mortifier.

Again, Nigrodha, a self-mortifier undertakes austerity, and through that austerity, he gains, honour, and fame. Or else he becomes intoxicated with conceit (majjati), infatuated (mucchati) and therefore careless (pamādamāpajjati).

Or else, Nigrodha, a self-mortifier undertakes austerity, and through that austerity, he gains, honour, and fame. Or else he becomes intoxicated with conceit, infatuated and therefore careless.

And this, Nigrodha, is a fault in that self-mortifier.
commentary_pali: 59.Lābhasakkārasilokanti ettha cattāro paccayā labbhantīti lābhā, teyeva suṭṭhu katvā paṭisaṅkharitvā laddhā sakkāro, vaṇṇabhaṇanaṃ siloko. Abhinibbattetīti acelakādibhāvaṃ terasadhutaṅgasamādānaṃ vā nissāya mahālābho uppajjati, tasmā ‘‘abhinibbattetī’’ti vutto. Sesamettha purimavāranayeneva duvidhassāpi tapassino vasena veditabbaṃ.
commentary_english:
" *lābhasakkārasiloka* " means here that *lābha* refers to the four conditions that are obtained; *sakkāra* is the same thing, well made, having been obtained after reflection; *siloka* is the declaration of virtues.

"*abhinibbatteti*" means that, depending on the state of being an ascetic, etc., or undertaking the thirteen ascetic practices, great gain arises; therefore it is said “*abhinibbatteti*”.

The rest here should be understood in terms of the two kinds of ascetics, according to the method of the previous passage.

mula_pali:
60. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī bhojanesu vodāsaṃ āpajjati – ‘idaṃ me khamati, idaṃ me nakkhamatī’ti. So yañca yaṃ hi (sī. pī.) khvassa nakkhamati, taṃ sāpekkho pajahati. Yaṃ panassa khamati, taṃ gadhito gathito (sī. pī.) mucchito ajjhāpanno anādīnavadassāvī anissaraṇapañño paribhuñjati…pe… ayampi kho, nigrodha, tapassino upakkileso hoti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī tapaṃ samādiyati lābhasakkārasilokanikantihetu – ‘sakkarissanti maṃ rājāno rājamahāmattā khattiyā brāhmaṇā gahapatikā titthiyā’ti…pe… ayampi kho, nigrodha, tapassino upakkileso hoti.
mula_english:
Again, Nigrodha, a self-mortifier practises a certain discrimination in food, thinking: “This suits me, this does not suit me.”

And what does not suit him, he eagerly rejects. While what suits him, he consumes greedily, recklessly, passionately, without seeing the danger, and without wisdom leading to liberation... And this, Nigrodha, is a fault ( *upakkilesa*) in that self-mortifier.

Again, Nigrodha, a self-mortifier undertakes austerity for the sake of gain, honor, and fame, thinking: “Kings and their ministers, *kṣatriyas* (warrior caste), *brāhmaṇas* (priestly caste), householders, and ascetics will honor me." ... And this, Nigrodha, is a fault ( *upakkilesa*) in that self-mortifier.
commentary_pali: 60.Vodāsaṃ āpajjatīti dvebhāgaṃ āpajjati, dve bhāge karoti. Khamatīti ruccati. Nakkhamatīti na ruccati. Sāpekkho pajahatīti sataṇho pajahati. Kathaṃ? Pātova khīrabhattaṃ bhutto hoti. Athassa maṃsabhojanaṃ upaneti. Tassa evaṃ hoti ‘‘idāni evarūpaṃ kadā labhissāma, sace jāneyyāma, pātova khīrabhattaṃ na bhuñjeyyāma, kiṃ mayā sakkā kātuṃ, gaccha bho, tvameva bhuñjā’’ti jīvitaṃ pariccajanto viya sāpekkho pajahati. Gadhitoti gedhajāto. Mucchitoti balavataṇhāya mucchito saṃmuṭṭhassatī hutvā. Ajjhāpannoti āmise atilaggo, ‘‘bhuñjissatha, āvuso’’ti dhammanimantanamattampi akatvā mahante mahante kabaḷe karoti. Anādīnavadassāvītiādīnavamattampi na passati. Anissaraṇapaññoti idha mattaññutānissaraṇapaccavekkhaṇaparibhogamattampi na karoti. Lābhasakkārasilokanikantihetūti lābhādīsu taṇhāhetu.
commentary_english:
60.
" *vodāsaṃ āpajjati*" means he incurs a double share, he makes two shares.
" *khamatī*" means it pleases.
" *nakkhamatī*" means it does not please.
" *sāpekkho pajahatī*" means he gives up with craving ( *sataṇho pajahati*).
How? Early in the morning he has eaten milk-rice ( *khīrabhattaṃ*).
Then they bring him meat-food ( *maṃsabhojanaṃ*).
Then he thinks thus: "When shall we get such [food] now? If we had known, we would not have eaten milk-rice early in the morning. What can I do? Go, friend, you yourself eat it," thus, as if abandoning his life, he gives up with craving.
" *gadhito*" means one who is born of greed ( *gedhajāto*).
" *mucchito*" means one who is infatuated by strong craving, having become one of confused mindfulness ( *balavataṇhāya mucchito saṃmuṭṭhassatī hutvā*).
" *ajjhāpanno*" means one who is exceedingly attached to delicacies, without even inviting [others, saying] "Eat, friend!" he makes large mouthfuls ( *‘‘bhuñjissatha, āvuso’’ti dhammanimantanamattampi akatvā mahante mahante kabaḷe karoti*).
" *anādīnavadassāvī*" means he does not see even a little fault ( *ādīnavamattampi na passati*).
" *anissaraṇapañño*" means here he does not make even a little using with knowledge of measure, without escape, and with reflection.
" *lābhasakkārasilokanikantihetū*" means craving as the cause in gain, etc. ( *lābhādīsu taṇhāhetu*).

mula_pali:
61. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī aññataraṃ samaṇaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā apasādetā apasāretā (ka.) hoti – ‘kiṃ panāyaṃ sambahulājīvo bahulājīvo (sī. pī.) sabbaṃ saṃbhakkheti. Seyyathidaṃ – mūlabījaṃ khandhabījaṃ phaḷubījaṃ aggabījaṃ bījabījameva pañcamaṃ, asanivicakkaṃ dantakūṭaṃ, samaṇappavādenā’ti…pe… ayampi kho, nigrodha, tapassino upakkileso hoti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī passati aññataraṃ samaṇaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā kulesu sakkariyamānaṃ garukariyamānaṃ māniyamānaṃ pūjiyamānaṃ. Disvā tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘imañhi nāma sambahulājīvaṃ kulesu sakkaronti garuṃ karonti mānenti pūjenti. Maṃ pana tapassiṃ lūkhājīviṃ kulesu na sakkaronti na garuṃ karonti na mānenti na pūjentī’ti, iti so issāmacchariyaṃ kulesu uppādetā hoti…pe… ayampi kho, nigrodha, tapassino upakkileso hoti.
mula_english:
61. Furthermore, Nigrodha, a self-mortifier disparages some ascetic (*śramaṇa*) or *brāhmaṇa*, saying, “See how this abundant-liver eats everything! For example, [he consumes] root-seed (*mūlabīja*), stem-seed (*khandhabīja*), joint-seed (*phaḷubīja*), shoot-seed (*aggabīja*), and fifthly seed from seed (*bījabīja*), along with the thunderbolt wheel and tooth powder, all under the guise of ascetic pronouncements." And this, Nigrodha, is a defilement (*upakkilesa*) of that self-mortifier.

Furthermore, Nigrodha, a self-mortifier sees another ascetic (*śramaṇa*) or *brāhmaṇa* being made much of, honored, respected, and worshipped in families. Having seen this, he thinks, "Indeed, they honor, respect, esteem, and worship this abundant-liver in families. But they do not make much of, honor, respect, or worship me, a meager-livered ascetic (*tapasvin*) in families.” Thus, he generates envy and jealousy towards those families. And this, Nigrodha, is a defilement (*upakkilesa*) of that self-mortifier.
commentary_pali: 61.Saṃbhakkhetīti saṃkhādati. Asanivicakkanti vicakkasaṇṭhānā asaniyeva. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti ‘‘asanivicakkaṃ imassa dantakūṭaṃ mūlabījādīsu na kiñci na saṃbhuñjati. Atha ca pana naṃ samaṇappavādena samaṇoti sañjānantī’’ti. Evaṃ apasādeti avakkhipati. Idaṃ titthiyavasena āgataṃ. Bhikkhuvasena panettha ayaṃ yojanā, attanā dhutaṅgadharo hoti, so aññaṃ evaṃ apasādeti ‘‘kiṃ samaṇā nāma ime samaṇamhāti vadanti, dhutaṅgamattampi natthi, uddesabhattādīni pariyesantā paccayabāhullikā vicarantī’’ti. Lūkhājīvinti acelakādivasena vā dhutaṅgavasena vā lūkhājīviṃ. Issāmacchariyanti parassa sakkārādisampattikhīyanalakkhaṇaṃ issaṃ, sakkārādikaraṇaakkhamanalakkhaṇaṃ macchariyañca.
commentary_english:
61. *saṃbhakkhetī* means *saṃkhādati* (to chew thoroughly).
*asanivicakka* means like a thunderbolt in the form of a wheel.
This means: "The *asanivicakka* does not consume anything among roots, seeds, etc."
Furthermore, "they recognize him as a *śramaṇa* due to the talk of *śramaṇas*."
Thus, he disparages and rejects.
This came about through the influence of the *tīrthikas*.
Here, the connection is according to the way of a *bhikkhu*: He himself observes the *dhutaṅgas*, and he disparages another thus: "Are these truly *śramaṇas* who say 'we are *śramaṇas*?' They do not even have a bit of *dhutaṅga*; they wander about seeking food and other requisites, being full of attachments."
*lūkhājīvi* means one who lives a rough life, either by the way of the *acelakas*, etc., or by the way of the *dhutaṅgas*.
*issāmacchariya* means envy (*īrṣyā*), which is characterized by being displeased at another's attainment of offerings, etc.; and miserliness (*mātsarya*), which is characterized by being incapable of allowing offerings etc.

mula_pali:
62. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī āpāthakanisādī hoti…pe… ayampi kho, nigrodha, tapassino upakkileso hoti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī attānaṃ adassayamāno kulesu carati – ‘idampi me tapasmiṃ idampi me tapasmi’nti…pe… ayampi kho, nigrodha, tapassino upakkileso hoti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī kiñcideva paṭicchannaṃ sevati. So ‘khamati te ida’nti puṭṭho samāno akkhamamānaṃ āha – ‘khamatī’ti. Khamamānaṃ āha – ‘nakkhamatī’ti. Iti so sampajānamusā bhāsitā hoti…pe… ayampi kho, nigrodha, tapassino upakkileso hoti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī tathāgatassa vā tathāgatasāvakassa vā dhammaṃ desentassa santaṃyeva pariyāyaṃ anuññeyyaṃ nānujānāti…pe… ayampi kho, nigrodha, tapassino upakkileso hoti.
mula_english:
62. Again, Nigrodha, a self-mortifier sits in a prominent position…and this, Nigrodha, is a fault in that self-mortifier.

Again, Nigrodha, a self-mortifier goes round ostentatiously among the families, as if to say: “See, this is my way of renunciation!”…and this, Nigrodha, is a fault in that self-mortifier.

Again, Nigrodha, a self-mortifier behaves in an underhand way. On being asked: “Do you approve of this?” although he does not approve he says: “I do”, or if he approves he says “I do not.” In this way he becomes a conscious liar…and this, Nigrodha, is a fault in that self-mortifier.

Again, Nigrodha, a self-mortifier, when the *Tathāgata* or a disciple of the *Tathāgata* presents the *Dharma* in a way that should command his assent, withholds that assent…and this, Nigrodha, is a fault in that self-mortifier.
commentary_pali:
62.Āpāthakanisādīhotīti manussānaṃ āpāthe dassanaṭṭhāne nisīdati. Yattha te passanti, tattha ṭhito vaggulivataṃ carati, pañcātapaṃ tappati, ekapādena tiṭṭhati, sūriyaṃ namassati. Sāsane pabbajitopi samādinnadhutaṅgo sabbarattiṃ sayitvā manussānaṃ cakkhupathe tapaṃ karoti, mahāsāyanheyeva cīvarakuṭiṃ karoti, sūriye uggate paṭisaṃharati, manussānaṃ āgatabhāvaṃ ñatvā ghaṇḍiṃ paharitvā cīvaraṃ matthake ṭhapetvā caṅkamaṃ otarati, sammuñjaniṃ gahetvā vihāraṅgaṇaṃ sammajjati.

Attānanti attano guṇaṃ adassayamānoti ettha a-kāro nipātamattaṃ, dassayamānoti attho. Idampi me tapasminti idampi kammaṃ mameva tapasmiṃ, paccatte vā bhummaṃ, idampi mama tapoti attho. So hi asukasmiṃ ṭhāne acelako atthi muttācārotiādīni sutvā amhākaṃ esa tapo, amhākaṃ so antevāsikotiādīni bhaṇati. Asukasmiṃ vā pana ṭhāne paṃsukūliko bhikkhu atthītiādīni sutvā amhākaṃ esa tapo, amhākaṃ so antevāsikotiādīni bhaṇati.

Attāna adassayamāno Idampi me tapasmi

Kiñcidevāti kiñci vajjaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ vā. Paṭicchannaṃ sevatīti yathā aññe na jānanti, evaṃ sevati. Akkhamamānaṃ āha khamatīti aruccamānaṃyeva ruccati meti vadati. Attanā kataṃ atimahantampi vajjaṃ appamattakaṃ katvā paññapeti, parena kataṃ dukkaṭamattaṃ vītikkamampi pārājikasadisaṃ katvā dasseti. Anuññeyyanti anujānitabbaṃ anumoditabbaṃ.

Kiñcidevā Paṭicchannaṃ sevatī Akkhamamānaṃ āha khamatī Anuññeyya
commentary_english:
62. *āpāthakanisādī hotī*: He sits in a place visible to people.

Where they see, there he stands, practices the bat-vow (vaggulivataṃ carati), heats himself with the five fires (pañcātapaṃ tappati), stands on one foot (ekapādena tiṭṭhati), and worships the sun (sūriyaṃ namassati).
