Even having gone forth in the Dispensation (sāsane pabbajitopi), adhering to the ascetic practices (samādinnadhutaṅgo), having spent the whole night lying down (sabbarattiṃ sayitvā), he performs austerity (tapaṃ karoti) in the sight of people (manussānaṃ cakkhupathe), makes a leaf hut (cīvarakuṭiṃ karoti) only late in the afternoon (mahāsāyanheyeva), takes it apart (paṭisaṃharati) when the sun has risen (sūriye uggate), having learned of the arrival of people (manussānaṃ āgatabhāvaṃ ñatvā), having struck the gong (ghaṇḍiṃ paharitvā), having placed his robe on his head (cīvaraṃ matthake ṭhapetvā), he descends to the cloister walk (caṅkamaṃ otarati), having taken the broom (sammuñjaniṃ gahetvā), he sweeps the monastery courtyard (vihāraṅgaṇaṃ sammajjati).

*attāna* means not showing one's own good qualities (attano guṇaṃ adassayamāno). Here, the a- is merely a particle, the meaning is *dassayamānoti*.

*idampi me tapasmi* means this deed (idampi kammaṃ) is indeed mine in my austerity (mameva tapasmiṃ), in private or publicly (paccatte vā bhummaṃ), this too is my austerity, that is the meaning (idampi mama tapoti attho).

For, having heard things like, "In such and such a place (asukasmiṃ ṭhāne) there is a naked ascetic (acelako atthi) with a liberated lifestyle (muttācāroti)," he says things like, "This is our austerity (amhākaṃ esa tapo), he is our pupil (amhākaṃ so antevāsikoti)."

Or, having heard things like, "In such and such a place (asukasmiṃ vā pana ṭhāne) there is a rag-robe wearing monk (paṃsukūliko bhikkhu atthīti)," he says things like, "This is our austerity (amhākaṃ esa tapo), he is our pupil (amhākaṃ so antevāsikoti)."

*attāna adassayamāno idampi me tapasmi*

*kiñcidevā* means some fault or wrong view (kiñci vajjaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ vā).

*paṭicchannaṃ sevatī* means he practices it in such a way that others do not know (yathā aññe na jānanti, evaṃ sevati).

*akkhamamānaṃ āha khamatī* means he says, "It pleases me," even about what is unpleasant (aruccamānaṃyeva ruccati meti vadati).

Having made a very great fault (attanā kataṃ atimahantampi vajjaṃ) seem insignificant (appamattakaṃ katvā), he makes it known (paññapeti), and having made a mere wrong-doing (parena kataṃ dukkaṭamattaṃ) seem like an offense entailing defeat (pārājikasadisaṃ katvā), he shows it (dasseti).

*anuññeyya* means it should be permitted and approved (anujānitabbaṃ anumoditabbaṃ).

*kiñcidevā paṭicchannaṃ sevatī akkhaṇamānaṃ āha khamatī anuññeyya*

mula_pali:
63. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī kodhano hoti upanāhī. Yampi, nigrodha, tapassī kodhano hoti upanāhī. Ayampi kho, nigrodha, tapassino upakkileso hoti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī makkhī hoti paḷāsī palāsī (sī. syā. pī.) …pe… issukī hoti maccharī… saṭho hoti māyāvī… thaddho hoti atimānī… pāpiccho hoti pāpikānaṃ icchānaṃ vasaṃ gato… micchādiṭṭhiko hoti antaggāhikāya diṭṭhiyā samannāgato… sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī hoti ādhānaggāhī duppaṭinissaggī. Yampi, nigrodha, tapassī sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī hoti ādhānaggāhī duppaṭinissaggī. Ayampi kho, nigrodha, tapassino upakkileso hoti.

palāsī (sī. syā. pī.)

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, nigrodha, yadime tapojigucchā tapojigucchāya (?) upakkilesā vā anupakkilesā vā’’ti? ‘‘Addhā kho ime, bhante, tapojigucchā tapojigucchāya (?) upakkilesā upakkilesā hoti (ka.), no anupakkilesā. Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, bhante, vijjati yaṃ idhekacco tapassī sabbeheva imehi upakkilesehi samannāgato assa; ko pana vādo aññataraññatarenā’’ti.

tapojigucchāya (?) tapojigucchāya (?) upakkilesā hoti (ka.)

Parisuddhapapaṭikappattakathā
mula_english:
63. Furthermore, Nigrodha, a self-mortifier is angry and bad-tempered. And this, Nigrodha, is a fault in that self-mortifier.

Furthermore, Nigrodha, a self-mortifier is mean and spiteful… envious and jealous… crafty and deceitful… obstinate and proud… with evil desires and under their sway… with wrong views and given to extremist opinions; he is tainted with worldliness, holding on firmly, unwilling to give up. And this, Nigrodha, is a fault in that self-mortifier.

What do you think, Nigrodha? Are these things faults in the higher austerity (tapo-jigucchā), or not?” “Indeed, venerable sir, these are faults in the higher austerity (tapo-jigucchā), not *not* faults. It could happen that a single self-mortifier was possessed of all these faults, not to speak of just one or the other."

The Discourse on the Acceptance of Pure Conduct
commentary_pali:
63.Kodhanohoti upanāhīti kujjhanalakkhaṇena kodhena, veraappaṭinissaggalakkhaṇena upanāhena ca samannāgato. Makkhī hoti paḷāsīti paraguṇamakkhanalakkhaṇena makkhena, yugaggāhalakkhaṇena paḷāsena ca samannāgato.

Issukī hoti maccharīti parasakkārādīsu usūyanalakkhaṇāya issāya, āvāsakulalābhavaṇṇadhammesu maccharāyanalakkhaṇena pañcavidhamaccherena ca samannāgato hoti. Saṭho hoti māyāvīti kerāṭikalakkhaṇena sāṭheyyena, katappaṭicchādanalakkhaṇāya māyāya ca samannāgato hoti. Thaddhohoti atimānīti nissinehanikkaruṇathaddhalakkhaṇena thambhena, atikkamitvā maññanalakkhaṇena atimānena ca samannāgato hoti. Pāpiccho hotīti asantasambhāvanapatthanalakkhaṇāya pāpicchatāya samannāgato hoti. Pāpikānanti tāsaṃyeva lāmakānaṃ icchānaṃ vasaṃ gato. Micchādiṭṭhikoti natthi dinnantiādinayappavattāya ayāthāvadiṭṭhiyā upeto. Antaggāhikāyāti sāyeva diṭṭhi ucchedantassa gahitattā ‘‘antaggāhikā’’ti vuccati, tāya samannāgatoti attho. Sandiṭṭhiparāmāsītiādīsu sayaṃ diṭṭhi sandiṭṭhi, sandiṭṭhimeva parāmasati gahetvā vadatīti sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī. Ādhānaṃ vuccati daḷhaṃ suṭṭhu ṭhapitaṃ, tathā katvā gaṇhātīti ādhānaggāhī. Ariṭṭho viya na sakkā hoti paṭinissajjāpetunti duppaṭinissaggī. Yadimeti yadi ime.

Issukī hoti maccharī Saṭho hoti māyāvī Thaddho hoti atimānī Pāpiccho hotī Pāpikāna Micchādiṭṭhiko Antaggāhikāyā Sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī. ādhānaggāhī. duppaṭinissaggī. Yadime

Parisuddhapapaṭikappattakathāvaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
63. “He is *kodhano* (wrathful), *upanāhī* (bearing grudges)” means he is endowed with *kodha* (wrath) due to the characteristic of being angry, and with *upanāha* (grudge) due to the characteristic of not relinquishing enmity.

“He is *makkhī* (detractive), *paḷāsī* (domineering)” means he is endowed with *makkha* (detraction) due to the characteristic of disparaging others’ virtues and with *paḷāsa* (domineering) due to the characteristic of seizing upon the essential point.

“He is *issukī* (envious), *maccharī* (miserly)” means he is endowed with *issā* (envy) due to the characteristic of resenting others’ honor etc., and with the fivefold *macchariya* (miserliness) due to the characteristic of being miserly regarding dwellings, families, gains, praise, and [teachings of the] Dharma.

“He is *saṭho* (deceitful), *māyāvī* (fraudulent)” means he is endowed with *sāṭheyya* (deceitfulness) due to the characteristic of crookedness, and with *māyā* (fraudulence) due to the characteristic of concealing wrongdoings.

“He is *thaddho* (stubborn), *atimānī* (conceited)” means he is endowed with *thambha* (stubbornness) due to the characteristic of being unyielding, unkind, and pitiless, and with *atimāna* (conceit) due to the characteristic of thinking [himself] superior [to others].

“He is *pāpiccho* (of evil desires)” means he is endowed with *pāpicchatā* (evil desire) due to the characteristic of desiring the impossible.

“*Pāpikāna* (evil ones)” means he has come under the control of those base desires themselves.

“*Micchādiṭṭhiko* (of wrong view)” means he is possessed of an inaccurate view that arises in ways such as “there is no gift.”

“*Antaggāhikāyā* (holding to an extreme)” means that same view is called “*antaggāhikā*” because it grasps the extreme of annihilation; the meaning is that he is endowed with that.

"*Sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī* (addicted to [his own] views)” and so on: *sandiṭṭhi* is his own view; *sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī* means he clings to and speaks only of his own view, having grasped it.

*Ādhānaṃ* (adherence) is said to be firm, well-established; *ādhānaggāhī* means he grasps [things] having made them thus.

“Like an *ariṭṭha* fruit, it is not possible to make him relinquish it” means he is *duppaṭinissaggī* (difficult to relinquish).

*Yadime* means *yadi ime* (whatever these may be).

*issukī hoti maccharī saṭho hoti māyāvī thaddho hoti atimānī pāpiccho hotī pāpikāna micchādiṭṭhiko antaggāhikāyā sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī. ādhānaggāhī. duppaṭinissaggī. yadime*

Explanation of the attainment of pure perception

mula_pali:
64. ‘‘Idha, nigrodha, tapassī tapaṃ samādiyati, so tena tapasā na attamano hoti na paripuṇṇasaṅkappo. Yampi, nigrodha, tapassī tapaṃ samādiyati, so tena tapasā na attamano hoti na paripuṇṇasaṅkappo. Evaṃ so tasmiṃ ṭhāne parisuddho hoti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī tapaṃ samādiyati, so tena tapasā na attānukkaṃseti na paraṃ vambheti…pe… evaṃ so tasmiṃ ṭhāne parisuddho hoti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī tapaṃ samādiyati, so tena tapasā na majjati na mucchati na pamādamāpajjati…pe… evaṃ so tasmiṃ ṭhāne parisuddho hoti.
mula_english:
—14. ‘Now, Nigrodha, take the case of a certain self-mortifier (tapasvī) who practises a certain austerity (tapas). As a result, he is not pleased (attamano) and satisfied at having attained his end (na paripuṇṇasaṅkappo).

Again, Nigrodha, take the case of a certain self-mortifier (tapasvī) who practises a certain austerity (tapas). As a result, he is not pleased (attamano) and satisfied at having attained his end (na paripuṇṇasaṅkappo). In this respect (tasmiṃ ṭhāne) he is purified (parisuddho hoti).

Again, Nigrodha, a self-mortifier (tapasvī) undertakes austerity (tapaṃ samādiyati), but through that austerity (tena tapasā), he does not exalt himself (na attānukkaṃseti) nor disparage others (na paraṃ vambheti)... in this respect (tasmiṃ ṭhāne) he is purified (parisuddho hoti).

Again, Nigrodha, a self-mortifier (tapasvī) undertakes austerity (tapaṃ samādiyati), but through that austerity (tena tapasā), he neither immerses (na majjati) nor faints (na mucchati) nor falls into negligence (na pamādamāpajjati)... in this respect (tasmiṃ ṭhāne) he is purified (parisuddho hoti).
commentary_pali: 64.Idha, nigrodha, tapassīti evaṃ bhagavā aññatitthiyehi gahitaladdhiṃ tesaṃ rakkhitaṃ tapaṃ sabbameva saṃkiliṭṭhanti upakkilesapāḷiṃ dassetvā idāni parisuddhapāḷidassanatthaṃ desanamārabhanto idha, nigrodhātiādimāha. Tattha ‘‘na attamano’’tiādīni vuttavipakkhavaseneva veditabbāni. Sabbavāresu ca lūkhatapassino ceva dhutaṅgadharassa ca vasena yojanā veditabbā. Evaṃ so tasmiṃ ṭhāne parisuddho hotīti evaṃ so tena na attamanatā na paripuṇṇasaṅkappabhāvasaṅkhātena kāraṇena parisuddho nirupakkileso hoti, uttari vāyamamāno kammaṭṭhānasuddhiko hutvā arahattaṃ pāpuṇāti. Iminā nayena sabbavāresu attho veditabbo.
commentary_english:
64. Thus, the Blessed One, having shown the defiled aspects ( *saṃkiliṭṭha*) by presenting the chapter on defilements (*upakkilesapāḷiṃ*) through the acceptance of the doctrines (*gahitaladdhiṃ*) of other sects, and their protected austerities ( *rakkhitaṃ tapaṃ* ), beginning the discourse (*desanamārabhanto*) for the purpose of showing the pure aspects (*parisuddhapāḷidassanatthaṃ*), said "Here, Nigrodha, ascetic (*tapassī*)," etc.

There, "not content" and so on should be understood only by way of the opposite (*vuttavipakkhavaseneva*) .

And in all cases, the connection (*yojanā*) should be understood in terms of the harsh ascetic (*lūkhatapassino*) and the one who holds the practice of purification (*dhutaṅgadharassa*).

"Thus he is pure in that place" thus, by that cause consisting of not being content, and not having the nature of fully conceived thought (*paripuṇṇasaṅkappabhāvasaṅkhātena kāraṇena*), he is pure ( *parisuddho*), without defilements (*nirupakkileso*), striving further (*uttari vāyamamāno*), becoming purified in his object of meditation (*kammaṭṭhānasuddhiko hutvā*), he attains arhatship (*arahattaṃ pāpuṇāti*).

By this method, the meaning (*attho*) should be understood in all cases (*sabbavāresu*).

mula_pali:
65. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī tapaṃ samādiyati, so tena tapasā lābhasakkārasilokaṃ abhinibbatteti, so tena lābhasakkārasilokena na attamano hoti na paripuṇṇasaṅkappo…pe… evaṃ so tasmiṃ ṭhāne parisuddho hoti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī tapaṃ samādiyati, so tena tapasā lābhasakkārasilokaṃ abhinibbatteti, so tena lābhasakkārasilokena na attānukkaṃseti na paraṃ vambheti…pe… evaṃ so tasmiṃ ṭhāne parisuddho hoti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī tapaṃ samādiyati, so tena tapasā lābhasakkārasilokaṃ abhinibbatteti, so tena lābhasakkārasilokena na majjati na mucchati na pamādamāpajjati…pe… evaṃ so tasmiṃ ṭhāne parisuddho hoti.
mula_english:
65. Again, Nigrodha, a self-mortifier undertakes austerity; through that austerity, he produces gain, honor, and fame. He is not pleased with that gain, honor, and renown, and his intention is not fulfilled… thus, he is completely pure in that place.

Again, Nigrodha, a self-mortifier undertakes austerity; through that austerity, he produces gain, honor, and fame. He does not elevate himself and disparage others… thus, he is completely pure in that place.

Again, Nigrodha, a self-mortifier undertakes austerity; through that austerity, he produces gain, honor, and fame. He does not become intoxicated, infatuated, or careless… thus, he is completely pure in that place.

mula_pali:
66. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī bhojanesu na vodāsaṃ āpajjati – ‘idaṃ me khamati, idaṃ me nakkhamatī’ti. So yañca khvassa nakkhamati, taṃ anapekkho pajahati. Yaṃ panassa khamati , taṃ agadhito amucchito anajjhāpanno ādīnavadassāvī nissaraṇapañño paribhuñjati…pe… evaṃ so tasmiṃ ṭhāne parisuddho hoti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī na tapaṃ samādiyati lābhasakkārasilokanikantihetu – ‘sakkarissanti maṃ rājāno rājamahāmattā khattiyā brāhmaṇā gahapatikā titthiyā’ti…pe… evaṃ so tasmiṃ ṭhāne parisuddho hoti.
mula_english:
Again, Nigrodha, a self-mortifier in regard to foods does not divide his food into two heaps, thinking: “This suits me, that does not suit me.” (idaṃ me khamati, idaṃ me nakkhamatī’ti).

And what does not suit him, he abandons without longing.

But what suits him, he consumes without greed (agadhito), without being infatuated (amucchito), without being enslaved (anajjhāpanno), seeing the danger (ādīnavadassāvī), with the wisdom of escape (nissaraṇapañño)…pe… Thus, in that place, he is purified (parisuddho hoti).

Again, Nigrodha, a self-mortifier does not undertake austerity for the sake of gains, honors, and fame, thinking: “Kings, royal ministers, Kṣatriyas, Brahmins, householders, and ascetics will honor me" (sakkarissanti maṃ rājāno rājamahāmattā khattiyā brāhmaṇā gahapatikā titthiyā’ti)…pe… Thus, in that place, he is purified (parisuddho hoti).

mula_pali:
67. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī aññataraṃ samaṇaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā nāpasādetā hoti – ‘kiṃ panāyaṃ sambahulājīvo sabbaṃ saṃbhakkheti. Seyyathidaṃ – mūlabījaṃ khandhabījaṃ phaḷubījaṃ aggabījaṃ bījabījameva pañcamaṃ, asanivicakkaṃ dantakūṭaṃ, samaṇappavādenā’ti…pe… evaṃ so tasmiṃ ṭhāne parisuddho hoti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī passati aññataraṃ samaṇaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā kulesu sakkariyamānaṃ garu kariyamānaṃ māniyamānaṃ pūjiyamānaṃ. Disvā tassa na evaṃ hoti – ‘imañhi nāma sambahulājīvaṃ kulesu sakkaronti garuṃ karonti mānenti pūjenti. Maṃ pana tapassiṃ lūkhājīviṃ kulesu na sakkaronti na garuṃ karonti na mānenti na pūjentī’ti, iti so issāmacchariyaṃ kulesu nuppādetā hoti…pe… evaṃ so tasmiṃ ṭhāne parisuddho hoti.
mula_english:
67. Furthermore, Nigrodha, the ascetic does not disparage another *śramaṇa* or *brāhmaṇa*, [saying]: ‘Why does this abundant-liver eat everything?

Namely: root-seed (*mūlabīja*), stem-seed (*khandhabīja*), fruit-seed (*phaḷubīja*), tip-seed (*aggabīja*), seed-seed itself being the fifth, the thunderbolt wheel (*asanivicakka*), the tooth-peak (*dantakūṭa*), by way of the ascetic proclamation...pe... thus he is completely pure in that place.

Furthermore, Nigrodha, the ascetic sees another *śramaṇa* or *brāhmaṇa* being made much of by families, being honoured, respected, and worshipped.

Having seen this, he does not think thus: ‘Indeed, they make much of this abundant-liver in families, they honour, respect, and worship him. But me, an ascetic, a rough-liver, they do not make much of in families, they do not honour, respect, or worship.’ Thus, he does not create envy and jealousy because of those families…pe… thus he is completely pure in that place.

mula_pali:
68. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī na āpāthakanisādī hoti…pe… evaṃ so tasmiṃ ṭhāne parisuddho hoti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī na attānaṃ adassayamāno kulesu carati – ‘idampi me tapasmiṃ, idampi me tapasmi’nti…pe… evaṃ so tasmiṃ ṭhāne parisuddho hoti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī na kañcideva paṭicchannaṃ sevati, so – ‘khamati te ida’nti puṭṭho samāno akkhamamānaṃ āha – ‘nakkhamatī’ti. Khamamānaṃ āha – ‘khamatī’ti. Iti so sampajānamusā na bhāsitā hoti…pe… evaṃ so tasmiṃ ṭhāne parisuddho hoti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī tathāgatassa vā tathāgatasāvakassa vā dhammaṃ desentassa santaṃyeva pariyāyaṃ anuññeyyaṃ anujānāti…pe… evaṃ so tasmiṃ ṭhāne parisuddho hoti.
mula_english:
Again, Nigrodha, a self-mortifier is not one who is constantly dwelling near the crossroads... In this respect, he is purified.

Again, Nigrodha, a self-mortifier does not go about in families while making a show of himself, [saying] 'This too is in my austerity, this too is in my austerity.' In this respect, he is purified.

Again, Nigrodha, a self-mortifier does not cultivate any hidden practices; when asked if something is agreeable to him, if he does not approve, he says, “I do not approve.”

If he does approve, he says, “I approve.” Thus, he does not consciously lie. In this respect, he is purified.

Again, Nigrodha, a self-mortifier, when the Tathāgata or a disciple of the Tathāgata presents the *dharma*, acknowledges a teaching that inherently merits acknowledgement. In this respect, he is purified.

mula_pali:
69. ‘‘Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī akkodhano hoti anupanāhī. Yampi, nigrodha, tapassī akkodhano hoti anupanāhī evaṃ so tasmiṃ ṭhāne parisuddho hoti.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, nigrodha, tapassī amakkhī hoti apaḷāsī…pe… anissukī hoti amaccharī… asaṭho hoti amāyāvī… atthaddho hoti anatimānī… na pāpiccho hoti na pāpikānaṃ icchānaṃ vasaṃ gato… na micchādiṭṭhiko hoti na antaggāhikāya diṭṭhiyā samannāgato… na sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī hoti na ādhānaggāhī suppaṭinissaggī. Yampi, nigrodha, tapassī na sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī hoti na ādhānaggāhī suppaṭinissaggī. Evaṃ so tasmiṃ ṭhāne parisuddho hoti.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, nigrodha, yadi evaṃ sante tapojigucchā parisuddhā vā hoti aparisuddhā vā’’ti? ‘‘Addhā kho, bhante, evaṃ sante tapojigucchā parisuddhā hoti no aparisuddhā, aggappattā ca sārappattā cā’’ti. ‘‘Na kho, nigrodha, ettāvatā tapojigucchā aggappattā ca hoti sārappattā ca; api ca kho papaṭikappattā pappaṭikapattā (ka.) hotī’’ti.

pappaṭikapattā (ka.)

Parisuddhatacappattakathā
mula_english:
69. Again, Nigrodha, a *tapasvin* is not angry (*akrodhanaḥ*) and not harboring resentment (*anupanāhī*).

Furthermore, Nigrodha, when a *tapasvin* is not angry (*akrodhanaḥ*) and not harboring resentment (*anupanāhī*), in this respect, he is purified (*parisuddhaḥ*).

Again, Nigrodha, a *tapasvin* is not disparaging (*amakṣī*), not insolent (*apalāśī*)…pe…not envious (*anissukī*), not stingy (*amaccharī*)…not deceitful (*aśaṭho*), not fraudulent (*amāyāvī*)…not obstinate (*atrabdhaḥ*), not arrogant (*anatimānī*)…

…he is without evil desires (*na pāpiccho*), not under the sway of evil desires (*na pāpikānaṃ icchānaṃ vasaṃ gato*)…he is without wrong views (*na mithyādṛṣṭikaḥ*), not endowed with extremist opinions (*na antagrāhikāya dṛṣṭiyā samanvāgataḥ*)…he is not tainted with worldliness (*na sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī*), does not hold on firmly (*na ādhānagrāhī*) and is not unwilling to give up (*supratinissargī*).

Furthermore, Nigrodha, when a *tapasvin*

…he is not tainted with worldliness (*na sandiṭṭhiparāmāsī*), does not hold on firmly (*na ādhānagrāhī*) and is not unwilling to give up (*supratinissargī*).

Thus, in this respect, he is purified (*parisuddhaḥ*).

What do you think, Nigrodha, if that is so, is the higher austerity (*tapojigucchā*) purified (*parisuddhā*) or not purified (*aparisuddhā*)?" "Certainly, venerable sir, if that is so, the higher austerity (*tapojigucchā*) is purified (*parisuddhā*), not unpurified (*aparisuddhā*), it has attained the peak (*aggappattā*) and reached the essence (*sārappattā*)."

"No, Nigrodha, in this way, the higher austerity (*tapojigucchā*) does not attain the peak (*aggappattā*) and reach the essence (*sārappattā*); but rather, it has only reached the outer bark (*papaṭikappattā*)."

The talk on the attainment of purified inner bark (*parisuddhatacappattakathā*).
commentary_pali:
69.Addhā kho, bhanteti bhante evaṃ sante ekaṃseneva vīriyena pāpajigucchanavādo parisuddho hotīti anujānāti. Ito parañca aggabhāvaṃ vā sārabhāvaṃ vā ajānanto aggappattā sārappattā cāti āha. Athassa bhagavā sārappattabhāvaṃ paṭisedhento na kho nigrodhātiādimāha . Papaṭikappattā hotīti sāravato rukkhassa sāraṃ phegguṃ tacañca atikkamma bahipapaṭikasadisā hotīti dasseti.

Parisuddhatacappattādikathāvaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
69. Indeed, venerable sir, he acknowledges that, venerable sir, being so, the speech that rejects evil with energy is thoroughly purified. Furthermore, not knowing the nature of the best or the nature of the essence, he says, "They have attained the best, and they have attained the essence." Then, the Blessed One, refuting the attainment of the essence, spoke beginning with, "Not indeed, Nigrodha" . "He becomes one who has attained mere bark" thus he shows that, having surpassed the essence, the sapwood, and the bark of a tree that has essence, he is similar to mere outer bark.

Explanation of the discourse on attaining pure bark, etc.

mula_pali:
70. ‘‘Kittāvatā pana, bhante, tapojigucchā aggappattā ca hoti sārappattā ca? Sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā tapojigucchāya aggaññeva pāpetu, sāraññeva pāpetū’’ti. ‘‘Idha, nigrodha, tapassī cātuyāmasaṃvarasaṃvuto hoti. Kathañca, nigrodha, tapassī cātuyāmasaṃvarasaṃvuto hoti? Idha, nigrodha, tapassī na pāṇaṃ atipāteti atipāpeti (ka. sī. pī. ka.), na pāṇaṃ atipātayati, na pāṇamatipātayato samanuñño hoti . Na adinnaṃ ādiyati, na adinnaṃ ādiyāpeti, na adinnaṃ ādiyato samanuñño hoti. Na musā bhaṇati, na musā bhaṇāpeti, na musā bhaṇato samanuñño hoti. Na bhāvitamāsīsati na bhāvitamāsiṃ sati (sī. syā. pī.), na bhāvitamāsīsāpeti, na bhāvitamāsīsato samanuñño hoti. Evaṃ kho, nigrodha, tapassī cātuyāmasaṃvarasaṃvuto hoti.

‘‘Yato kho, nigrodha, tapassī cātuyāmasaṃvarasaṃvuto hoti, aduṃ cassa hoti tapassitāya. So abhiharati no hīnāyāvattati. So vivittaṃ senāsanaṃ bhajati araññaṃ rukkhamūlaṃ pabbataṃ kandaraṃ giriguhaṃ susānaṃ vanapatthaṃ abbhokāsaṃ palālapuñjaṃ. So pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātappaṭikkanto nisīdati pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā ujuṃ kāyaṃ paṇidhāya parimukhaṃ satiṃ upaṭṭhapetvā. So abhijjhaṃ loke pahāya vigatābhijjhena cetasā viharati, abhijjhāya cittaṃ parisodheti. Byāpādappadosaṃ pahāya abyāpannacitto viharati sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampī, byāpādappadosā cittaṃ parisodheti. Thinamiddhaṃ thīnamiddhaṃ (sī. syā. pī.) pahāya vigatathinamiddho viharati ālokasaññī sato sampajāno, thinamiddhā cittaṃ parisodheti. Uddhaccakukkuccaṃ pahāya anuddhato viharati ajjhattaṃ vūpasantacitto, uddhaccakukkuccā cittaṃ parisodheti. Vicikicchaṃ pahāya tiṇṇavicikiccho viharati akathaṃkathī kusalesu dhammesu, vicikicchāya cittaṃ parisodheti.

thīnamiddhaṃ (sī. syā. pī.)
mula_english:
70. ‘But to what extent, venerable sir, does austerity attain its peak and penetrate to the pith? It would be good, venerable sir, if the Blessed One were to cause my austerity to attain its peak, to penetrate to the pith.’

‘Here, Nigrodha, a self-mortifier observes the fourfold restraint (*cātuyāmasaṃvarasaṃvuto*).

And how, Nigrodha, does a self-mortifier observe the fourfold restraint? Here, Nigrodha, a self-mortifier does not kill any living being, nor does he cause any living being to be killed, nor does he approve of another killing; he does not take what is not given, nor does he cause what is not given to be taken, nor does he approve of another taking what is not given; he does not tell a lie, nor does he cause a lie to be told, nor does he approve of another telling a lie; he does not crave for sense-pleasures, cause others to do so, or approve of such craving. In this way, Nigrodha, a self-mortifier observes the fourfold restraint.

‘And through this restraint, through making this his austerity, he takes an upward course and does not fall back into lower things. He resorts to a secluded resting place: the forest, the foot of a tree, a mountain, a ravine, a hillside cave, a charnel ground, a jungle highland, the open air, a heap of straw. After his meal, on returning from his alms round, he sits down, crosses his legs, holds his body erect, and sets up mindfulness before him. Abandoning covetousness for the world, he abides with a mind free from covetousness; he purifies his mind from covetousness. Abandoning ill will and hatred, he abides with a mind free from ill will, compassionate for the welfare of all living beings; he purifies his mind from ill will and hatred. Abandoning sloth and torpor, he abides free from sloth and torpor, percipient of light, mindful and fully aware; he purifies his mind from sloth and torpor. Abandoning restlessness and remorse, he abides unagitated with a mind inwardly peaceful; he purifies his mind from restlessness and remorse. Abandoning doubt, he abides having gone beyond doubt, unperplexed about wholesome states; he purifies his mind from doubt.
commentary_pali:
70.Aggaṃpāpetūti desanāvasena aggaṃ pāpetvā desetu, sāraṃ pāpetvā desetūti dasabalaṃ yācati. Cātuyāmasaṃvarasaṃvutoti catubbidhena saṃvarena pihito. Na pāṇaṃ atipātetīti pāṇaṃ na hanati. Na bhāvitamāsīsatīti bhāvitaṃ nāma tesaṃ saññāya pañca kāmaguṇā, te na āsīsati na sevatīti attho.

Aduṃ cassa hotīti etañcassa idāni vuccamānaṃ ‘‘so abhiharatī’’tiādilakkhaṇaṃ. Tapassitāyāti tapassibhāvena hoti. Tattha so abhiharatīti so taṃ sīlaṃ abhiharati, uparūpari vaḍḍheti. Sīlaṃ me paripuṇṇaṃ, tapo āraddho, alamettāvatāti na vīriyaṃ vissajjeti. No hīnāyāvattatīti hīnāya gihibhāvatthāya na āvattati. Sīlato uttari visesādhigamatthāya vīriyaṃ karotiyeva, evaṃ karonto so vivittaṃ senāsanaṃ bhajati. ‘‘Arañña’’ntiādīni sāmaññaphale (dī. ni. aṭṭha. 1.216) vitthāritāneva. ‘‘Mettāsahagatenā’’tiādīni visuddhimagge vaṇṇitāni. Tacappattāti papaṭikato abbhantaraṃ tacaṃ pattā. Phegguppattāti tacato abbhantaraṃ phegguṃ pattā, pheggusadisā hotīti attho.

Aduṃ cassa hotī Tapassitāyā so abhiharatī No hīnāyāvattatī Tacappattā Phegguppattā
commentary_english:
70. **Aggaṃ**: "May [the teacher] lead [us] to the highest [attainment]," that is, by means of teaching. Having led [us] to the highest [attainment], may [the teacher] teach. Having led [us] to the essence, may [the teacher] teach—[thus] one implores the power of the ten perfections (daśabalaṃ yācati).
**Cātuyāmasaṃvarasaṃvuto**: [He is] cloaked by the fourfold restraint (catubbidhena saṃvarena pihito).
**Na pāṇaṃ atipātetī**: [He] does not kill living beings (prāṇaṃ na hanati).
**Na bhāvitamāsīsatī**: The five desirable sense objects (pañca kāmaguṇā) are nominally contemplated (bhāvitaṃ nāma teṣaṃ saññāya), but he does not long for them; he does not cultivate them; this is the meaning.

**Aduṃ cassa hotī**: This now being spoken, the characteristic of "he brings near," etc., [is present].
**Tapassitāyā**: [This] is through the state of asceticism (tapasvibhāvena hoti).
There, **So abhiharatī**: He brings near that *śīla* (so taṃ śīlaṃ abhiharati), he increases it more and more (uparūpari vaḍḍheti).
"[My] *śīla* is complete (śīlaṃ me paripuṇṇaṃ), austerity (*tapas*) has begun (tapo āraddhaḥ)," he does not abandon his energy, thinking, "enough of this (alamettāvatāti na vīriyaṃ vissajjeti)!"
**No hīnāyāvattatī**: He does not return to the inferior state, to the state of a householder (hīnāya gihibhāvatthāya na āvattati).
From *śīla*, for the sake of the higher attainment of distinction (śīlato uttari viśeṣādhigamatthāya), he exerts energy, thus acting, he cultivates a secluded dwelling place (evaṃ karonto so vivittaṃ senāsanaṃ bhajati).
"Forest," and so forth, [are] expanded in the general fruit (sāmaññaphale).
"Accompanied by loving-kindness (mettāsahagatenā)," and so forth, [are] described in the *Visuddhimagga* (visuddhimagge varṇitāni).
**Tacappattā**: Reaching the skin inside the scale (papaṭikato abbhantaraṃ tacaṃ pattā).
**Phegguppattā**: Reaching the core inside the skin (tacato abbhantaraṃ phegguṃ pattā), [being] similar to the core; this is the meaning (pheggusadisā hotīti attho).

**Aduṃ cassa hotī**, **Tapassitāyā**, **So abhiharatī**, **No hīnāyāvattatī**, **Tacappattā**, **Phegguppattā**.

mula_pali:
71. ‘‘So ime pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya cetaso upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati. Tathā dutiyaṃ. Tathā tatiyaṃ. Tathā catutthaṃ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ mettāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati. Karuṇāsahagatena cetasā…pe… muditāsahagatena cetasā…pe… upekkhāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati. Tathā dutiyaṃ. Tathā tatiyaṃ. Tathā catutthaṃ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ upekkhāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, nigrodha. Yadi evaṃ sante tapojigucchā parisuddhā vā hoti aparisuddhā vā’’ti? ‘‘Addhā kho, bhante, evaṃ sante tapojigucchā parisuddhā hoti no aparisuddhā, aggappattā ca sārappattā cā’’ti. ‘‘Na kho, nigrodha, ettāvatā tapojigucchā aggappattā ca hoti sārappattā ca; api ca kho tacappattā hotī’’ti.

Parisuddhaphegguppattakathā
mula_english:
71. Having abandoned these five hindrances (*nīvaraṇa*) and in order to weaken by insight the defilements (*upakkilesa*) of mind, he dwells, letting his mind, filled with loving-kindness (*maitrī-sahagatena cetasā*), pervade one quarter.
Likewise the second direction.
Likewise the third direction.
Likewise the fourth direction.
Thus above, below, around, everywhere, in its entirety, he dwells pervading the all-encompassing world with his heart imbued with loving-kindness (*maitrī-sahagatena cetasā*)—abundant, exalted, immeasurable (*appamāṇena*), without hostility (*averena*) and without ill will (*avyāpajjena*).
And he dwells, letting his mind, filled with compassion (*karuṇā-sahagatena cetasā*)…with sympathetic joy (*muditā-sahagatena cetasā*)…with equanimity (*upekkhā-sahagatena cetasā*), pervade one quarter.
Likewise the second direction.
Likewise the third direction.
Likewise the fourth direction.
Thus above, below, around, everywhere, in its entirety, he dwells pervading the all-encompassing world with a mind imbued with equanimity (*upekkhā-sahagatena cetasā*)—abundant, exalted, immeasurable (*appamāṇena*), without hostility (*averena*) and without ill will (*avyāpajjena*).

What do you think, Nigrodha?
If austerity of religious practice (*tapojigucchā*) is so purified (*parisuddhā*) or not purified (*aparisuddhā*)?”
“Certainly it is, venerable sir (*bhante*). If austerity of religious practice (*tapojigucchā*) is so purified (*parisuddhā*) and not purified (*aparisuddhā*), it attains its peak (*aggappattā*) and penetrates to the pith (*sārappattā*).”
“No, Nigrodha, it austerity of religious practice (*tapojigucchā*) does not attain its peak (*aggappattā*) and penetrates to the pith (*sārappattā*); it only reaches the outer bark (*tacappattā*).”

The Discourse on the Purification that Only Reaches the Fibres Surrounding the Pith.

mula_pali:
72. ‘‘Kittāvatā pana, bhante, tapojigucchā aggappattā ca hoti sārappattā ca? Sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā tapojigucchāya aggaññeva pāpetu, sāraññeva pāpetū’’ti. ‘‘Idha, nigrodha, tapassī cātuyāmasaṃvarasaṃvuto hoti. Kathañca, nigrodha, tapassī cātuyāmasaṃvarasaṃvuto hoti…pe… yato kho, nigrodha, tapassī cātuyāmasaṃvarasaṃvuto hoti, aduṃ cassa hoti tapassitāya. So abhiharati no hīnāyāvattati. So vivittaṃ senāsanaṃ bhajati…pe… so ime pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya cetaso upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe mettāsahagatena cetasā…pe… karuṇāsahagatena cetasā…pe… muditāsahagatena cetasā…pe… upekkhāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati. So anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati seyyathidaṃ – ekampi jātiṃ dvepi jātiyo tissopi jātiyo catassopi jātiyo pañcapi jātiyo dasapi jātiyo vīsampi jātiyo tiṃsampi jātiyo cattālīsampi jātiyo paññāsampi jātiyo jātisatampi jātisahassampi jātisatasahassampi anekepi saṃvaṭṭakappe anekepi vivaṭṭakappe anekepi saṃvaṭṭavivaṭṭakappe – ‘amutrāsiṃ evaṃnāmo evaṃgotto evaṃvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṃsukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto amutra udapādiṃ, tatrāpāsiṃ evaṃnāmo evaṃgotto evaṃvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṃsukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto idhūpapanno’ti. Iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, nigrodha, yadi evaṃ sante tapojigucchā parisuddhā vā hoti aparisuddhā vā’’ti? ‘‘Addhā kho, bhante, evaṃ sante tapojigucchā parisuddhā hoti, no aparisuddhā, aggappattā ca sārappattā cā’’ti. ‘‘Na kho, nigrodha, ettāvatā tapojigucchā aggappattā ca hoti sārappattā ca; api ca kho phegguppattā hotī’’ti.

Parisuddhaaggappattasārappattakathā
mula_english:
72. “But to what extent, venerable sir, is the higher austerity purified so as to reach its peak and penetrate to the pith? It would be good, venerable sir, if the Blessed One would lead me to the very peak of the higher austerity, lead me to the very pith!”

“Here, Nigrodha, a self-mortifier observes the fourfold restraint.

And how, Nigrodha, does a self-mortifier observe the fourfold restraint? …pe… When, Nigrodha, a self-mortifier observes the fourfold restraint, this is how his self-mortification occurs.

He takes an upward course and does not fall back into lower things.

He frequents a secluded lodging…pe… He abandons these five hindrances, corruptions of the mind that weaken wisdom, and dwells pervading one quarter with a mind imbued with loving-kindness…pe… with a mind imbued with compassion…pe… with a mind imbued with gladness…pe… with a mind imbued with equanimity, vast, exalted, measureless, without enmity, without ill-will.

He recollects his numerous past lives, that is, one birth, two births, three, four, or five births; ten, twenty, thirty, forty, or fifty births; a hundred births, a thousand births, a hundred thousand births; many aeons of world contraction, many aeons of world expansion, many aeons of world contraction and expansion, : ‘There I had such a name, belonged to such a clan, had such an appearance; such was my food, such my experience of pleasure and pain, such my span of life. Passing away from that, I re-arose there. There too I had such a name… such was my span of life. Passing away from there, I was reborn here.’

In this way he remembers various past births, their conditions and details.

“What do you think, Nigrodha, when this is so, is the higher austerity purified or not?” “Indeed, venerable sir, when this is so, the higher austerity is purified, not impure; it has reached its peak and penetrated to the pith.”

“No, Nigrodha, it does not attain its peak there, penetrating to the pith. It has only reached the fibres surrounding the pith.”

Account of the purification that attains the peak and penetrates to the pith.

mula_pali:
73. ‘‘Kittāvatā pana, bhante, tapojigucchā aggappattā ca hoti sārappattā ca? Sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā tapojigucchāya aggaññeva pāpetu, sāraññeva pāpetū’’ti. ‘‘Idha, nigrodha, tapassī cātuyāmasaṃvarasaṃvuto hoti. Kathañca, nigrodha, tapassī cātuyāmasaṃvarasaṃvuto hoti…pe… yato kho, nigrodha, tapassī cātuyāmasaṃvarasaṃvuto hoti, aduṃ cassa hoti tapassitāya. So abhiharati no hīnāyāvattati. So vivittaṃ senāsanaṃ bhajati…pe… so ime pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya cetaso upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe mettāsahagatena cetasā…pe… upekkhāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati. So anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati. Seyyathidaṃ – ekampi jātiṃ dvepi jātiyo tissopi jātiyo catassopi jātiyo pañcapi jātiyo…pe… iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati. So dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passati cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe sugate duggate, yathākammūpage satte pajānāti – ‘ime vata bhonto sattā kāyaduccaritena samannāgatā vacīduccaritena samannāgatā manoduccaritena samannāgatā ariyānaṃ upavādakā micchādiṭṭhikā micchādiṭṭhikammasamādānā. Te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapannā. Ime vā pana bhonto sattā kāyasucaritena samannāgatā vacīsucaritena samannāgatā manosucaritena samannāgatā ariyānaṃ anupavādakā sammādiṭṭhikā sammādiṭṭhikammasamādānā. Te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapannā’ti. Iti dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passati cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe sugate duggate, yathākammūpage satte pajānāti.

‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, nigrodha, yadi evaṃ sante tapojigucchā parisuddhā vā hoti aparisuddhā vā’’ti? ‘‘Addhā kho, bhante, evaṃ sante tapojigucchā parisuddhā hoti no aparisuddhā, aggappattā ca sārappattā cā’’ti.
mula_english:
73. "But to what extent, venerable sir, does the higher austerity reach its highest point and its essence? It would be good, venerable sir, if the Blessed One would lead me to the highest point and the very essence of the higher austerity."

"Here, Nigrodha, a self-mortifier observes the fourfold restraint (*cātuyāmasaṃvarasaṃvuto*).

And how, Nigrodha, does a self-mortifier observe the fourfold restraint (*cātuyāmasaṃvarasaṃvuto*)?...

…because, Nigrodha, a self-mortifier observes the fourfold restraint (*cātuyāmasaṃvarasaṃvuto*), this is considered his asceticism.

He takes an upward course and does not fall back into lower things.

He frequents a secluded lodging… He abandons these five hindrances, the corruptions of the mind, weaknesses of wisdom; and he dwells having pervaded one direction with a mind imbued with loving-kindness (*mettāsahagatena cetasā*)… and he dwells having pervaded one direction with a mind imbued with equanimity (*upekkhāsahagatena cetasā*), expansive, sublime, immeasurable, without hostility, without ill-will.

He recollects his manifold past lives.

That is to say, one birth, two births, three births, four births, five births… Thus he recollects his numerous past lives in their modes and their details.

With the divine eye (*dibbena cakkhunā*), purified and surpassing the human, he sees beings passing away and reappearing, inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate, and he understands how beings pass on according to their actions: ‘These beings, who were endowed with bad conduct of body (*kāyaduccaritena*), speech, and mind, who reviled the noble ones, held wrong views, and undertook actions governed by wrong views—

at the breaking-up of the body (*kāyassa bhedā*), after death, have reappeared in the plane of misery (*apāyaṃ*), the bad destinations (*duggatiṃ*), the lower realms (*vinipātaṃ*), in hell (*nirayaṃ*).

But these beings, on account of good conduct of body (*kāyasucaritena*), speech, and mind, not revilers of noble ones, right in their views, giving effect to right views in their actions,

at the dissolution of the body (*kāyassa bhedā*), after death, have reappeared in a happy destination (*sugatiṃ*), in the world of Heaven (*saggaṃ lokaṃ*).’

Thus with the divine eye (*dibbena cakkhunā*), purified and surpassing the human, he sees beings passing away and reappearing, inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate, and he understands how beings pass on according to their actions.

“What do you think, Nigrodha, is the higher austerity, under these circumstances, purified or unpurified?” “Indeed, venerable sir, under these circumstances the higher austerity is purified, not unpurified, it has reached its highest point and its very essence.”

mula_pali:
74. ‘‘Ettāvatā kho, nigrodha, tapojigucchā aggappattā ca hoti sārappattā ca. Iti kho, nigrodha iti nigrodha (syā.), yaṃ maṃ tvaṃ avacāsi – ‘ko nāma so, bhante, bhagavato dhammo, yena bhagavā sāvake vineti, yena bhagavatā sāvakā vinītā assāsappattā paṭijānanti ajjhāsayaṃ ādibrahmacariya’nti. Iti kho taṃ, nigrodha, ṭhānaṃ uttaritarañca paṇītatarañca, yenāhaṃ sāvake vinemi, yena mayā sāvakā vinītā assāsappattā paṭijānanti ajjhāsayaṃ ādibrahmacariya’’nti.

Evaṃ vutte, te paribbājakā unnādino uccāsaddamahāsaddā ahesuṃ – ‘‘ettha mayaṃ anassāma sācariyakā, na mayaṃ ito bhiyyo uttaritaraṃ pajānāmā’’ti.

Nigrodhassa pajjhāyanaṃ
mula_english:
‘So indeed it is, Nigrodha, that austerity (*tapo-jigucchā*) is so purified as to reach its peak (*agga-ppattā*) and penetrate to the pith (*sāra-ppattā*).

And so, Nigrodha, when you asked me: “What, Lord (*bhante*), is this doctrine (*dhammo*) of the Blessed One (*bhagavato*), in which the Blessed One trains his disciples (*sāvake vineti*), and which those disciples whom the Blessed One has so trained recognise as their principal support (*assāsa-ppattā*), and the perfection of the holy life (*ādi-brahmacariya*)?”

I say that it is by something more far-reaching and excellent (*uttaritarañca paṇītatarañca*) that I train them (*sāvake vinemi*), through which they…recognise as their principal support (*assāsa-ppattā*), and the perfection of the holy life.’

At this the wanderers (*paribbājakā*) made a great commotion and noise (*uccāsadda-mahāsaddā*), exclaiming: ‘We and our teacher are ruined! We know of nothing higher or more far-reaching than our teaching! ‘

Nigrodha's meditation.
commentary_pali:
74. ‘‘Ettāvatā, kho nigrodha, tapojigucchā aggappattā ca hoti sārappattā cā’’ti idaṃ bhagavā titthiyānaṃ vasenāha. Titthiyānañhi lābhasakkāro rukkhassa sākhāpalāsasadiso. Pañcasīlamattakaṃ papaṭikasadisaṃ. Aṭṭhasamāpattimattaṃ tacasadisaṃ. Pubbenivāsañāṇāvasānā abhiññā pheggusadisā. Dibbacakkhuṃ panete arahattanti gahetvā vicaranti. Tena nesaṃ taṃ rukkhassa sārasadisaṃ. Sāsane pana lābhasakkāro sākhāpalāsasadiso. Sīlasampadā papaṭikasadisā. Jhānasamāpattiyo tacasadisā. Lokiyābhiññā pheggusadisā. Maggaphalaṃ sāro. Iti bhagavatā attano sāsanaṃ onatavinataphalabhārabharitarukkhūpamāya upamitaṃ. So desanākusalatāya tato tacasārasampattito mama sāsanaṃ uttaritarañceva paṇītatarañca, taṃ tuvaṃ kadā jānissasīti attanodesanāya visesabhāvaṃ dassetuṃ ‘‘iti kho nigrodhā’’ti desanaṃ ārabhi . Te paribbājakāti te tassa parivārā tiṃsasatasaṅkhyā paribbājakā. Ettha mayaṃ anassāmāti ettha acelakapāḷiādīsu, idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti ‘‘amhākaṃ acelakapāḷimattampi natthi , kuto parisuddhapāḷi. Amhākaṃ parisuddhapāḷimattampi natthi, kuto cātuyāmasaṃvarādīni. Cātuyāmasaṃvaropi natthi, kuto araññavāsādīni. Araññavāsopi natthi, kuto nīvaraṇappahānādīni. Nīvaraṇappahānampi natthi, kuto brahmavihārādīni. Brahmavihāramattampi natthi, kuto pubbenivāsādīni. Pubbenivāsañāṇamattampi natthi, kuto amhākaṃ dibbacakkhu. Ettha mayaṃ saācariyakā naṭṭhā’’ti. Ito bhiyyo uttaritaranti ito dibbacakkhuñāṇādhigamato bhiyyo aññaṃ uttaritaraṃ visesādhigamaṃ mayaṃ sutivasenāpi na jānāmāti vadanti.

Nigrodhassapajjhāyanavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
74. "In this way, Nigrodha, the abhorrence of austerity is both the highest attainment and the attainment of essence." Thus spoke the Blessed One in reference to the ascetics.

For the ascetics, gain and honor are like the branches and leaves of a tree. A mere five precepts are like bark. A mere eight attainments are like sapwood. The higher knowledges ending with the knowledge of former abodes are like the pith. These people take the divine eye and go about thinking it is arahantship. Therefore, that for them is like the heartwood of the tree.

In the Dispensation, gain and honor are like branches and leaves. Accomplishment in virtue is like bark. Meditative attainments are like sapwood. Mundane higher knowledges are like the pith. The path and its fruit are the heartwood (sāro). Thus, the Blessed One compared his own Dispensation to a tree laden with the weight of fruits that are bent down and bowed low.

Because of skill in teaching and because of that attainment of the essence of the sapwood, my Dispensation is even more excellent and refined. When will you know this?"

To show the special nature of his own teaching, he began the teaching, "Thus, Nigrodha..."

"These wanderers" means these wanderers, who are his retinue, numbering thirty hundred.

"Here we are ruined" means that in the Acelakapāḷi and so on, it is said, "We do not even have the mere Acelakapāḷi, how much less the purified Pāḷi? We do not even have the mere purified Pāḷi, how much less the fourfold restraint and so on? There is not even the fourfold restraint, how much less dwelling in the forest and so on? There is not even dwelling in the forest, how much less the abandoning of the hindrances and so on? There is not even the abandoning of the hindrances, how much less the divine abodes (brahmavihāra) and so on? There is not even the mere divine abodes, how much less the knowledge of former abodes and so on? There is not even the mere knowledge of former abodes, how much less our divine eye? Here we are ruined together with our teachers."

"Beyond this, further and further" means, "Beyond this attainment of the divine eye knowledge, we do not know any other attainment that is further and further, even by way of listening." Thus they say.

Commentary on Nigrodha's Recitation

mula_pali: 75. Yadā aññāsi sandhāno gahapati – ‘‘aññadatthu kho dānime aññatitthiyā paribbājakā bhagavato bhāsitaṃ sussūsanti, sotaṃ odahanti, aññācittaṃ upaṭṭhāpentī’’ti. Atha atha naṃ (ka.) nigrodhaṃ paribbājakaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘iti kho, bhante nigrodha, yaṃ maṃ tvaṃ avacāsi – ‘yagghe, gahapati, jāneyyāsi, kena samaṇo gotamo saddhiṃ sallapati, kena sākacchaṃ samāpajjati, kena paññāveyyattiyaṃ samāpajjati, suññāgārahatā samaṇassa gotamassa paññā, aparisāvacaro samaṇo gotamo nālaṃ sallāpāya, so antamantāneva sevati; seyyathāpi nāma gokāṇā pariyantacārinī antamantāneva sevati. Evameva suññāgārahatā samaṇassa gotamassa paññā, aparisāvacaro samaṇo gotamo nālaṃ sallāpāya; so antamantāneva sevati; iṅgha, gahapati, samaṇo gotamo imaṃ parisaṃ āgaccheyya, ekapañheneva naṃ saṃsādeyyāma, tucchakumbhīva naṃ maññe orodheyyāmā’ti. Ayaṃ kho so, bhante, bhagavā arahaṃ sammāsambuddho idhānuppatto, aparisāvacaraṃ pana naṃ karotha, gokāṇaṃ pariyantacāriniṃ karotha, ekapañheneva naṃ saṃsādetha, tucchakumbhīva naṃ orodhethā’’ti. Evaṃ vutte, nigrodho paribbājako tuṇhībhūto maṅkubhūto pattakkhandho adhomukho pajjhāyanto appaṭibhāno nisīdi.
mula_english:
75. When the householder Sandhāna realized: ‘These wanderers of other views are actually listening and attending to the Blessed One’s words (bhāsitaṃ), and inclining their minds to the higher wisdom (aññācittaṃ upaṭṭhāpentī)’, then he said to Nigrodha the wanderer: ‘Reverend Nigrodha, you said to me: “Come now, householder, do you know whom the ascetic Gotama (samaṇo Gotamo) talks to? With whom does he converse (sākacchaṃ samāpajjati)? From whom does he get his lucidity of wisdom (paññāveyyattiyaṃ samāpajjati)? The wisdom (paññā) of Gotama (Gotamassa), the ascetic, is destroyed by the solitary life (suññāgārahatā), Gotama (Gotamo), the ascetic, is no good at conversation (aparisāvacaro), he is right out of touch (antamantāneva sevati); just as a crow frequents only the outskirts of a village (gokāṇā pariyantacārinī antamantāneva sevati).” His wisdom (paññā) is destroyed by the solitary life (suññāgārahatā), Gotama (Gotamo), the ascetic, is no good at conversation (aparisāvacaro); he is right out of touch (antamantāneva sevati); come now, householder (gahapati), should the ascetic Gotama (samaṇo Gotamo) come to this assembly (parisaṃ āgaccheyya), we would baffle him with a single question (ekapañheneva naṃ saṃsādeyyāma), and knock him over like an empty pot (tucchakumbhīva naṃ maññe orodheyyāmā’ti).’ So now that the Blessed One (bhagavā), the worthy one, the fully awakened one (arahaṃ sammāsambuddho) has come here (idhānuppatto), why don’t you treat him as one who is no good at conversation (aparisāvacaraṃ pana naṃ karotha), treat him as a crow that frequents the outskirts of a village (gokāṇaṃ pariyantacāriniṃ karotha), baffle him with a single question (ekapañheneva naṃ saṃsādetha), and knock him over like an empty pot (tucchakumbhīva naṃ orodhethā’’ti)?

When this was said, Nigrodha (Nigrodho), the wanderer (paribbājako), became silent (tuṇhībhūto), confused (maṅkubhūto), his form drooping (pattakkhandho), face turned down (adhomukho), unable to reply (appaṭibhāno), sat down (nisīdi).
commentary_pali:
75.Atha nigrodhaṃ paribbājakanti evaṃ kirassa ahosi ‘‘ime paribbājakā idāni bhagavato bhāsitaṃ sussūsanti, iminā ca nigrodhena bhagavato parammukhā kakkhaḷaṃ durāsadavacanaṃ vuttaṃ, idāni ayampi sotukāmo jāto, kālo dāni me imassa mānaddhajaṃ nipātetvā bhagavato sāsanaṃ ukkhipitu’’nti. Atha nigrodhaṃ paribbājakaṃ etadavoca. Aparampissa ahosi ‘‘ayaṃ mayi akathente satthāraṃ na khamāpessati, tadassa anāgate ahitāya dukkhāya saṃvattissati, mayā pana kathite khamāpessati, tadassa bhavissati dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāyā’’ti. Atha nigrodhaṃ paribbājakaṃ etadavoca. Aparisāvacaraṃ pana naṃ karothāti ettha panāti nipāto, atha naṃ aparisāvacaraṃ karothāti attho. ‘‘Aparisāvacareta’’ntipi pāṭho, aparisāvacaraṃ vā etaṃ karotha, gokāṇādīnaṃ vā aññataranti attho.

Gokāṇanti etthāpi gokāṇaṃ pariyantacāriniṃ viya karothāti attho. Tuṇhībhūtoti tuṇhībhāvaṃ upagato. Maṅkubhūtoti nittejataṃ āpanno. Pattakkhandhoti onatagīvo. Adhomukhoti heṭṭhāmukho.

Gokāṇa Tuṇhībhūto Maṅkubhūto Pattakkhandho Adhomukho
commentary_english:
75. Then, concerning Nigrodha the wanderer ( *nigrodhaṃ paribbājaka* ), it occurred to him: "These wanderers are now eager to hear the Blessed One's words. But that Nigrodha has spoken harsh and unapproachable words, turning away from the Blessed One. Now even he has become desirous to listen. Now is the time for me to cast down his banner of pride and raise up the Blessed One's teaching."

Then he said this to Nigrodha the wanderer.

Moreover, it occurred to him: "If this person does not ask the Teacher, he will not appease him, and that will lead to harm and suffering in the future. But if he asks, he will appease him, and that will lead to long-term welfare and happiness."

Then he said this to Nigrodha the wanderer.

"Do not make him an outsider" (*aparisāvacaraṃ pana naṃ karotha*)—here, *pana* is a particle; thus, the meaning is: "Do not make him an outsider."

There is also the reading "he should not be made an outsider" (*aparisāvacareta*); or, "Make him not an outsider, but one or another of the cow-eared ones, and so on" is the meaning.

*Gokāṇa* means here also: "Make him like a cow-eared one wandering about at the edge" is the meaning.

*Tuṇhībhūto* means one who has become silent (*tuṇhībhāvaṃ upagato*).

*Maṅkubhūto* means one who has come to a state of being without brightness (*nittejataṃ āpanno*).

*Pattakkhandho* means one with a lowered neck (*onatagīvo*).

*Adhomukho* means one with the face downwards (*heṭṭhāmukho*).

Cow-eared, silent, shaking, with lowered neck, face downwards.

mula_pali:
76. Atha kho bhagavā nigrodhaṃ paribbājakaṃ tuṇhībhūtaṃ maṅkubhūtaṃ pattakkhandhaṃ adhomukhaṃ pajjhāyantaṃ appaṭibhānaṃ viditvā nigrodhaṃ paribbājakaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘saccaṃ kira, nigrodha, bhāsitā te esā vācā’’ti? ‘‘Saccaṃ , bhante, bhāsitā me esā vācā, yathābālena yathāmūḷhena yathāakusalenā’’ti. ‘‘Taṃ kiṃ maññasi, nigrodha. Kinti te sutaṃ paribbājakānaṃ vuḍḍhānaṃ mahallakānaṃ ācariyapācariyānaṃ bhāsamānānaṃ – ‘ye te ahesuṃ atītamaddhānaṃ arahanto sammāsambuddhā, evaṃ su te bhagavanto saṃgamma samāgamma unnādino uccāsaddamahāsaddā anekavihitaṃ tiracchānakathaṃ anuyuttā viharanti. Seyyathidaṃ – rājakathaṃ corakathaṃ…pe… itibhavābhavakathaṃ iti vā. Seyyathāpi tvaṃ etarahi sācariyako. Udāhu, evaṃ su te bhagavanto araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti appasaddāni appanigghosāni vijanavātāni manussarāhasseyyakāni paṭisallānasāruppāni, seyyathāpāhaṃ etarahī’ti.

‘‘Sutaṃ metaṃ, bhante. Paribbājakānaṃ vuḍḍhānaṃ mahallakānaṃ ācariyapācariyānaṃ bhāsamānānaṃ – ‘ye te ahesuṃ atītamaddhānaṃ arahanto sammāsambuddhā , na evaṃ su nāssu (sī. pī.) te bhagavanto saṃgamma samāgamma unnādino uccāsaddamahāsaddā anekavihitaṃ tiracchānakathaṃ anuyuttā viharanti. Seyyathidaṃ – rājakathaṃ corakathaṃ…pe… itibhavābhavakathaṃ iti vā, seyyathāpāhaṃ etarahi sācariyako. Evaṃ su te bhagavanto araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti appasaddāni appanigghosāni vijanavātāni manussarāhasseyyakāni paṭisallānasāruppāni, seyyathāpi bhagavā etarahī’’’ti.

nāssu (sī. pī.)

‘‘Tassa te, nigrodha, viññussa sato mahallakassa na etadahosi – ‘buddho so bhagavā bodhāya dhammaṃ deseti, danto so bhagavā damathāya dhammaṃ deseti, santo so bhagavā samathāya dhammaṃ deseti, tiṇṇo so bhagavā taraṇāya dhammaṃ deseti, parinibbuto so bhagavā parinibbānāya dhammaṃ desetī’’’ti?

Brahmacariyapariyosānasacchikiriyā
mula_english:
Then the Blessed One, knowing that Nigrodha the wanderer was silent, crestfallen, with shoulders drooping, head down, pondering, and without ready wit, said this to Nigrodha the wanderer: “Is it true, Nigrodha, that you said these words?”

“Yes, venerable sir, it is true that I said those words, foolishly, mistakenly, and wickedly.”

“What do you think, Nigrodha? Have you ever heard it said by wanderers who were aged, venerable, the teachers of teachers, that those who in the past were *arhats*, perfectly awakened Buddhas, when they came together, used to talk by shouting and screaming and making a great clamor, and indulging in diverse kinds of inconsequential conversation, such as talk about kings, robbers… talk of being and non-being? Or is it like you right now, with your teachers? Or did those Blessed Ones frequent secluded forest and woodland retreats, free from noise and disturbance, far from the crowds, undisturbed by men, fit for solitude, just as I do now?”

“I have heard this, venerable sir. Those wanderers who were aged, venerable, the teachers of teachers, said that those who in the past were *arhats*, perfectly awakened Buddhas, did not, when they came together, talk by shouting and screaming and making a great clamor, and indulging in diverse kinds of inconsequential conversation, such as talk about kings, robbers… talk of being and non-being, but that those Blessed Ones frequented secluded forest and woodland retreats, free from noise and disturbance, far from the crowds, undisturbed by men, fit for solitude, just as the Blessed One does now."

“Nigrodha, intelligent, mindful, and aged as you are, did it never occur to you to think, ‘The Buddha, the Blessed One, teaches the *dharma* for enlightenment; the Buddha, the Blessed One, teaches the *dharma* for self-control; the Buddha, the Blessed One, teaches the *dharma* for appeasement; the Buddha, the Blessed One, teaches the *dharma* for crossing over; the Buddha, the Blessed One, teaches the *dharma* for *nirvāṇa*’?”

Spiritual life's ultimate realization.
commentary_pali:
76.Buddhoso bhagavā bodhāyāti sayaṃ buddho sattānampi catusaccabodhatthāya dhammaṃ deseti. Dantoti cakkhutopi danto…pe… manatopi danto. Damathāyāti aññesampi damanatthāya eva, na vādatthāya. Santoti rāgasantatāya santo, dosamohasantatāya sabba akusalasabbābhisaṅkhārasantatāya santo. Samathāyāti mahājanassa rāgādisamanatthāya dhammaṃ deseti. Tiṇṇoti cattāro oghe tiṇṇo. Taraṇāyāti mahājanassa oghanittharaṇatthāya. Parinibbutoti kilesaparinibbānena parinibbuto. Parinibbānāyāti mahājanassāpi sabbakilesaparinibbānatthāya dhammaṃ deseti.

Brahmacariyapariyosānādivaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
76. *Buddha*: that Blessed One is a Buddha for the sake of awakening; he himself is awakened and teaches the Dharma for the sake of the four noble truths for other beings as well.

*Subdued*: he is subdued with regard to the eye…and… he is subdued with regard to the mind.

*For the sake of subduing*: for the sake of subduing others as well, not for the sake of argument.

*Peaceful*: peaceful due to the peacefulness from attachment, peaceful due to the peacefulness from aversion and delusion, peaceful due to the peacefulness from all unwholesome and all intentional activities.

*For the sake of calming*: he teaches the Dharma for the sake of calming the great multitude from attachment, etc.

*Crossed over*: he has crossed over the four floods.

*For the sake of crossing over*: for the sake of the great multitude crossing over the flood.

*Completely extinguished*: completely extinguished by the complete extinction of defilements.

*For the sake of complete extinction*: he teaches the Dharma for the sake of the complete extinction of all defilements for the great multitude as well.

Description of the culmination of the holy life, etc.

mula_pali:
77. Evaṃ vutte, nigrodho paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘accayo maṃ, bhante, accagamā yathābālaṃ yathāmūḷhaṃ yathāakusalaṃ, yvāhaṃ evaṃ bhagavantaṃ avacāsiṃ. Tassa me, bhante, bhagavā accayaṃ accayato paṭiggaṇhātu āyatiṃ saṃvarāyā’’ti. ‘‘Taggha tvaṃ taṃ (sī. syā. pī.), nigrodha, accayo accagamā yathābālaṃ yathāmūḷhaṃ yathāakusalaṃ, yo maṃ tvaṃ evaṃ avacāsi. Yato ca kho tvaṃ, nigrodha, accayaṃ accayato disvā yathādhammaṃ paṭikarosi, taṃ te mayaṃ paṭiggaṇhāma. Vuddhi hesā, nigrodha, ariyassa vinaye, yo accayaṃ accayato disvā yathādhammaṃ paṭikaroti āyatiṃ saṃvaraṃ āpajjati. Ahaṃ kho pana, nigrodha, evaṃ vadāmi –

‘Etu viññū puriso asaṭho amāyāvī ujujātiko, ahamanusāsāmi ahaṃ dhammaṃ desemi. Yathānusiṭṭhaṃ tathā yathānusiṭṭhaṃ (?) paṭipajjamāno, yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti, tadanuttaraṃ brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharissati sattavassāni. Tiṭṭhantu, nigrodha, satta vassāni. Etu viññū puriso asaṭho amāyāvī ujujātiko, ahamanusāsāmi ahaṃ dhammaṃ desemi. Yathānusiṭṭhaṃ tathā paṭipajjamāno, yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti, tadanuttaraṃ brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharissati cha vassāni. Pañca vassāni… cattāri vassāni… tīṇi vassāni… dve vassāni… ekaṃ vassaṃ. Tiṭṭhatu, nigrodha, ekaṃ vassaṃ. Etu viññū puriso asaṭho amāyāvī ujujātiko ahamanusāsāmi ahaṃ dhammaṃ desemi. Yathānusiṭṭhaṃ tathā paṭipajjamāno, yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti, tadanuttaraṃ brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharissati satta māsāni. Tiṭṭhantu, nigrodha, satta māsāni… cha māsāni… pañca māsāni … cattāri māsāni… tīṇi māsāni… dve māsāni… ekaṃ māsaṃ… aḍḍhamāsaṃ. Tiṭṭhatu, nigrodha, aḍḍhamāso. Etu viññū puriso asaṭho amāyāvī ujujātiko, ahamanusāsāmi ahaṃ dhammaṃ desemi. Yathānusiṭṭhaṃ tathā paṭipajjamāno, yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti, tadanuttaraṃ brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharissati sattāhaṃ’.

yathānusiṭṭhaṃ (?)

Paribbājakānaṃ pajjhāyanaṃ
mula_english:
77. When this was said, Nigrodha the wanderer said to the Blessed One: “Lord, transgression overcame me, foolish, blind, and unskilled as I was, that I spoke thus of the Blessed One. May the Blessed One accept my transgression as a transgression, so that I may restrain myself in the future."

"Indeed, Nigrodha, transgression overcame you, foolish, blind, and unskilled as you were, that you spoke thus of me. But since you, Nigrodha, see your transgression as such and make amends according to the Dharma, we accept it of you. For, Nigrodha, it is growth in the Discipline of the Noble Ones when one sees one's transgression as such and makes amends and undertakes restraint in the future.

I, however, Nigrodha, say this: 'Let an intelligent man come, one who is not deceitful, not given to trickery, one who is upright. I will instruct him; I will teach him the Dharma. If he practices according to the instruction, then within seven years he will realize for himself with direct knowledge, and attain to, and dwell in that unsurpassed culmination of the holy life for which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness.'

Let alone seven years, Nigrodha. Let an intelligent man come, one who is not deceitful, not given to trickery, one who is upright. I will instruct him; I will teach him the Dharma. If he practices according to the instruction, then within six years he will realize for himself with direct knowledge, and attain to, and dwell in that unsurpassed culmination of the holy life for which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness. Five years… four years… three years… two years… one year. Let alone one year, Nigrodha.

Let an intelligent man come, one who is not deceitful, not given to trickery, one who is upright. I will instruct him; I will teach him the Dharma. If he practices according to the instruction, then within seven months he will realize for himself with direct knowledge, and attain to, and dwell in that unsurpassed culmination of the holy life for which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness. Let alone seven months, Nigrodha… six months… five months… four months… three months… two months… one month… half a month. Let alone half a month, Nigrodha.

Let an intelligent man come, one who is not deceitful, not given to trickery, one who is upright. I will instruct him; I will teach him the Dharma. If he practices according to the instruction, then within seven days he will realize for himself with direct knowledge, and attain to, and dwell in that unsurpassed culmination of the holy life for which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life into homelessness.'

The Recitation of the Wanderers
commentary_pali: 77.Accayotiādīni sāmaññaphale (dī. ni. aṭṭha. 1.250) vuttāni. Ujujātikoti kāyavaṅkādivirahito ujusabhāvo. Ahamanusāsāmīti ahaṃ tādisaṃ puggalaṃ anusāsāmi, dhammaṃ assa desemi. Sattāhanti sattadivasāni, idaṃ sabbampi bhagavā dandhapaññaṃ puggalaṃ sandhāyāha asaṭho pana amāyāvī ujujātiko taṃmuhutteneva arahattaṃ pattuṃ sakkhissati. Iti bhagavā ‘‘asaṭha’’ntiādivacanena saṭho hi vaṅkavaṅko, mayāpi na sakkā anusāsitunti dīpento paribbājakaṃ pādesu gahetvā mahāmerupādatale viya khipittha. Kasmā? Ayañhi atisaṭho, kuṭilacitto satthari evaṃ kathentepi buddhadhammasaṅghesu nādhimuccati, adhimuccanatthāya sotaṃ na odahati, kohaññe ṭhito satthāraṃ khamāpeti. Tasmā bhagavā tassajjhāsayaṃ viditvā ‘‘etu viññū puriso asaṭho’’tiādimāha. Saṭhaṃ panāhaṃ anusāsituṃ na sakkomīti.
commentary_english:
77. *Accayo* etc., are stated in the *sāmaññaphala* (Dī. Ni. Aṭṭha. 1. 250).

*Ujujātiko* means one who is without bodily crookedness (*kāyavaṅkādi*), upright in nature (*ujusabhāvo*).

*Ahamanusāsāmī* means I instruct such a person; I teach him the Dharma (*dhammaṃ assa desemi*).

*Sattāha* means seven days; all this the Blessed One said with reference to a person of slow wisdom (*dandhapaññaṃ puggalaṃ sandhāya*). But one who is without deceit (*asaṭho*), without trickery (*amāyāvī*), upright in nature (*ujujātiko*) will be able to attain *arahatship* in that very moment.

Thus, the Blessed One, by the statement beginning with “without deceit” (*asaṭha*), showing that a deceitful person is crooked (*vaṅkavaṅko*), and that he cannot be instructed by me, seized the wanderer by the feet and threw him as if at the foot of the Great Mount Meru (*mahāmerupādatale viya khipittha*).

Why? Because he is very deceitful (*atisaṭho*), with a crooked mind (*kuṭilacitto*), even when the Teacher speaks thus, he does not have conviction in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha (*buddhadhammasaṅghesu nādhimuccati*), he does not lend an ear (*sotaṃ na odahati*) for the purpose of conviction (*adhimuccanatthāya*), standing in hypocrisy (*kohaññe ṭhito*) he appeases the Teacher (*satthāraṃ khamāpeti*).

Therefore, the Blessed One, knowing his intention (*tassajjhāsayaṃ viditvā*) said, “Let a wise man come, without deceit” (*etu viññū puriso asaṭho*), etc.

But I am not able to instruct a deceitful person (*saṭhaṃ panāhaṃ anusāsituṃ na sakkomi*).

mula_pali: 78. ‘‘Siyā kho pana te, nigrodha, evamassa – ‘antevāsikamyatā no samaṇo gotamo evamāhā’ti. Na kho panetaṃ, nigrodha, evaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Yo eva vo te (sī. syā.) ācariyo, so eva vo ācariyo hotu. Siyā kho pana te, nigrodha, evamassa – ‘uddesā no cāvetukāmo samaṇo gotamo evamāhā’ti. Na kho panetaṃ, nigrodha , evaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Yo eva vo uddeso so eva vo uddeso hotu. Siyā kho pana te, nigrodha, evamassa – ‘ājīvā no cāvetukāmo samaṇo gotamo evamāhā’ti. Na kho panetaṃ, nigrodha, evaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Yo eva vo ājīvo, so eva vo ājīvo hotu. Siyā kho pana te, nigrodha, evamassa – ‘ye no dhammā akusalā akusalasaṅkhātā sācariyakānaṃ, tesu patiṭṭhāpetukāmo samaṇo gotamo evamāhā’ti. Na kho panetaṃ, nigrodha, evaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Akusalā ceva vo te dhammā vodhammā (ka.), te dhammā (syā.) hontu akusalasaṅkhātā ca sācariyakānaṃ. Siyā kho pana te , nigrodha, evamassa – ‘ye no dhammā kusalā kusalasaṅkhātā sācariyakānaṃ, tehi vivecetukāmo samaṇo gotamo evamāhā’ti. Na kho panetaṃ, nigrodha, evaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Kusalā ceva vo te dhammā hontu kusalasaṅkhātā ca sācariyakānaṃ. Iti khvāhaṃ, nigrodha, neva antevāsikamyatā evaṃ vadāmi, napi uddesā cāvetukāmo evaṃ vadāmi, napi ājīvā cāvetukāmo evaṃ vadāmi, napi ye vo dhammā napi ye kho dhammā (sī.), napi ye te dhammā (syā.), napi ye ca vo dhammā (ka.) akusalā akusalasaṅkhātā sācariyakānaṃ, tesu patiṭṭhāpetukāmo evaṃ vadāmi, napi ye vo dhammā napi ye kho dhammā (sī.), napi ye te dhammā (syā.), napi ye ca vo dhammā (ka.) kusalā kusalasaṅkhātā sācariyakānaṃ, tehi vivecetukāmo evaṃ vadāmi. Santi ca kho, nigrodha, akusalā dhammā appahīnā saṃkilesikā ponobbhavikā ponobhavikā (ka.) sadarā saddarā (pī. ka.), sadarathā (syā. ka.) dukkhavipākā āyatiṃ jātijarāmaraṇiyā, yesāhaṃ pahānāya dhammaṃ desemi. Yathāpaṭipannānaṃ vo saṃkilesikā dhammā pahīyissanti, vodānīyā dhammā abhivaḍḍhissanti, paññāpāripūriṃ vepullattañca diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharissathā’’ti.
mula_english:
78. "Nigrodha, you may think: 'The ascetic Gotama says this in order to get disciples.'
But, Nigrodha, it should not be regarded thus.
Let him who is your teacher remain your teacher. (yo eva vo ācariyo, so eva vo ācariyo hotu.)
Nigrodha, you may think: 'The ascetic Gotama says this in order to make us abandon our rules.'
But, Nigrodha, it should not be regarded thus.
Let your rules remain as they are.
Nigrodha, you may think: 'The ascetic Gotama says this in order to make us abandon our livelihood.'
But, Nigrodha, it should not be regarded thus.
Let your way of life remain as it was.
Nigrodha, you may think: 'The ascetic Gotama says this in order to establish us in things that are unwholesome and considered unwholesome by those of our persuasion.'
But, Nigrodha, it should not be regarded thus.
Let those things you consider unwholesome continue to be so considered.
Nigrodha, you may think: 'The ascetic Gotama says this in order to draw us away from things that are wholesome and considered wholesome by those of our persuasion.'
But, Nigrodha, it should not be regarded thus.
Let whatever you consider right continue to be so considered.
Nigrodha, I do not speak thus to get disciples, nor do I speak thus to make you abandon your rules, nor do I speak thus to make you abandon your livelihood, nor do I speak thus to establish you in things that are unwholesome and considered unwholesome by those of your persuasion, nor do I speak thus to draw you away from things that are wholesome and considered wholesome by those of your persuasion.
There are, Nigrodha, unwholesome things that have not been abandoned, defiled, leading to renewed existence, fearful, resulting in suffering, related to birth, aging, and death in the future, and for the abandonment of these things I teach the Dharma (dhamma).
If you practice accordingly, these defiled things will be abandoned, and the things that make for purification will develop and grow, and in this very life you will realize it for yourselves with direct knowledge, attain to it, and abide in the full perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāripūriṃ)."
commentary_pali: 78.Antevāsikamyatāti antevāsikamyatāya, amhe antevāsike icchanto. Evamāhāti ‘‘etu viññupuriso’’tiādimāha. Yo eva vo ācariyoti yo eva tumhākaṃ pakatiyā ācariyo. Uddesā no cāvetukāmoti attano anusāsaniṃ gāhāpetvā amhe amhākaṃ uddesato cāvetukāmo. Soeva vo uddeso hotūti yo tumhākaṃ pakatiyā uddeso, so tumhākaṃyeva hotu , na mayaṃ tumhākaṃ uddesena atthikā. Ājīvāti ājīvato. Akusalasaṅkhātāti akusalāti koṭṭhāsaṃ pattā. Akusalā dhammāti dvādasa akusalacittuppādadhammā taṇhāyeva vā visesena. Sā hi punabbhavakaraṇato ‘‘ponobbhavikā’’ti vuttā. Sadarathāti kilesadarathasampayuttā. Jātijarāmaraṇiyāti jātijarāmaraṇānaṃ paccayabhūtā. Saṃkilesikā dhammāti dvādasa akusalacittuppādā. Vodāniyāti, samathavipassanā dhammā. Te hi satte vodāpenti, tasmā ‘‘vodāniyā’’ti vuccanti. Paññāpāripūrinti maggapaññāpāripūriṃ. Vepullattañcāti phalapaññāvepullataṃ, ubhopi vā etāni aññamaññavevacanāneva. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti ‘‘tato tumhe maggapaññañceva phalapaññañca diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharissathā’’ti. Evaṃ bhagavā paribbājake ārabbha attano ovādānusāsaniyā phalaṃ dassento arahattanikūṭena desanaṃ niṭṭhapesi.
commentary_english: 78. *Antevāsikamyatā* means in wanting discipleship, desiring us as disciples. *Evamāhā* means "‘Let a discerning man come,’" etc., he said. *Yo eva vo ācariyo* means that he is naturally your teacher. *Uddesā no cāvetukāmo* means, having made us accept his teaching, he wants to remove us from our assignment. *So eva vo uddeso hotū* means, whatever is naturally your assignment, let that be yours; we do not need your assignment. *Ājīvā* means from living. *Akusalasaṅkhātā* means having attained to the state of unwholesome things. *Akusalā dhammā* means the twelve unwholesome states of mind, or especially craving. For it is called "leading to renewed existence" because it causes renewed existence. *Sadarathā* means associated with the anxieties of defilements. *Jātijarāmaraṇiyā* means being the cause of birth, old age and death. *Saṃkilesikā dhammā* means the twelve unwholesome states of mind. *Vodāniyā* means the qualities of serenity and insight. For they purify beings, therefore they are called "vodāniyā." *Paññāpāripūri* means the fulfillment of wisdom on the path. *Vepullattañcā* means the abundance of the wisdom of fruition, or both of these are indeed synonyms for each other. This is what was said: "Then you yourselves, in this very life, having realized and attained the wisdom of the path and the wisdom of fruition through direct knowledge, will abide therein." In this way, the Blessed One, in connection with the wandering ascetics, showing the fruit of his own instruction, concluded the teaching with the pinnacle of Arahantship.

mula_pali:
79. Evaṃ vutte, te paribbājakā tuṇhībhūtā maṅkubhūtā pattakkhandhā adhomukhā pajjhāyantā appaṭibhānā nisīdiṃsu yathā taṃ mārena pariyuṭṭhitacittā. Atha kho bhagavato etadahosi – ‘‘sabbe pime moghapurisā phuṭṭhā pāpimatā. Yatra hi nāma ekassapi na evaṃ bhavissati – ‘handa mayaṃ aññāṇatthampi samaṇe gotame brahmacariyaṃ carāma, kiṃ karissati sattāho’’’ti? Atha kho bhagavā udumbarikāya paribbājakārāme sīhanādaṃ naditvā vehāsaṃ abbhuggantvā gijjhakūṭe pabbate paccupaṭṭhāsi paccuṭṭhāsi (sī. syā. pī.). Sandhāno pana gahapati tāvadeva rājagahaṃ pāvisīti.

Udumbarikasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ dutiyaṃ.
mula_english:
79. At these words, the wanderers sat silent, upset, their shoulders drooping, they hung their heads and sat there downcast and bewildered, their minds so possessed by Māra.

Then the Lord thought: “Every one of these foolish men is possessed by the evil one.

So that not a single one of them thinks: “Let us now follow the holy life, *brahmacarya*, proclaimed by the ascetic Gotama, that we may learn it—for what do seven days matter?”’ Then the Lord, after uttering a lion’s roar *sīhanāda* in the alms-hall of the wanderers at Udumbarikā, rose into the sky and reappeared on Vulture Peak *Gijjhakūṭe pabbate*.

And the householder Sandhāna also returned to Rājagaha.

The Udumbarika Discourse is finished, the second.
commentary_pali:
79.Yathā taṃ mārenāti yathā mārena pariyuṭṭhitacittā nisīdanti evameva tuṇhībhūtā…pe… appaṭibhānā nisinnā.

Māro kira satthā ativiya gajjanto buddhabalaṃ dīpetvā imesaṃ paribbājakānaṃ dhammaṃ deseti, kadāci dhammābhisamayo bhaveyya, handāhaṃ pariyuṭṭhāmīti so tesaṃ cittāni pariyuṭṭhāsi. Appahīnavipallāsānañhi cittaṃ mārassa yathākāmakaraṇīyaṃ hoti. Tepi mārena pariyuṭṭhitacittā thaddhaṅgapaccaṅgā viya tuṇhī appaṭibhānā nisīdiṃsu. Atha satthā ime paribbājakā ativiya niravā hutvā nisinnā, kiṃ nu khoti āvajjanto mārena pariyuṭṭhitabhāvaṃ aññāsi. Sace pana tesaṃ maggaphaluppattihetu bhaveyya, māraṃ paṭibāhitvāpi bhagavā dhammaṃ deseyya, so pana tesaṃ natthi. ‘‘Sabbepi me tucchapurisā’’ti aññāsi. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘atha kho bhagavato etadahosi sabbepi me moghapurisā’’tiādi.

Tattha phuṭṭhā pāpimatāti pāpimatā mārena phuṭṭhā. Yatra hi nāmāti yesu nāma. Aññāṇatthampīti jānanatthampi. Kiṃ karissati sattāhoti samaṇena gotamena paricchinnasattāho amhākaṃ kiṃ karissati. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti ‘‘samaṇena gotamena ‘sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharissati sattāha’nti vuttaṃ, so sattāho amhākaṃ kiṃ apphāsukaṃ karissati. Handa mayaṃ sattāhabbhantare etaṃ dhammaṃ sacchikātuṃ sakkā, na sakkāti aññāṇatthampi brahmacariyaṃ carissāmā’’ti. Atha vā jānāma tāvassa dhammanti ekadivase ekavāraṃ aññāṇatthampi etesaṃ cittaṃ nuppannaṃ, sattāho pana etesaṃ kusītānaṃ kiṃ karissati, kiṃ sakkhissanti te sattāhaṃ pūretunti ayamettha adhippāyo. Sīhanādanti paravādabhindanaṃ sakavādasamussāpanañca abhītanādaṃ naditvā. Paccupaṭṭhāsīti patiṭṭhito. Tāvadevāti tasmiññeva khaṇe. Rājagahaṃ pāvisīti rājagahameva paviṭṭho. Tesaṃ pana paribbājakānaṃ kiñcāpi idaṃ suttantaṃ sutvā viseso na nibbatto, āyatiṃ pana nesaṃ vāsanāya paccayo bhavissatīti. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānamevāti.

phuṭṭhā pāpimatā Yatra hi nāmā Aññāṇatthampī Kiṃ karissati sattāho Sīhanāda Paccupaṭṭhāsī Tāvadevā Rājagahaṃ pāvisī

Sumaṅgalavilāsiniyā dīghanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Udumbarikasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
79. *yathā taṃ mārenā*ti: Just as they sit with their minds overcome by Māra, so too, they were silent… speechless.

Māra, it seems, having greatly roared, displaying the power of the Buddha, teaches the Dharma to these wanderers, [thinking,] "Perhaps there might be a realization of the Dharma." So, he overcame their minds.

Indeed, the mind of one who has not abandoned distorted perceptions is easily manipulated by Māra.

They too, with their minds overcome by Māra, sat silently, their bodies stiff and their limbs frozen, as if speechless.

Then, the Teacher, knowing that these wanderers were sitting very silently, reflecting, understood that they were overcome by Māra.

If, however, there were a cause for the arising of the path and its fruit in them, the Blessed One, even having repelled Māra, would teach the Dharma, but that does not exist in them.

"All of them are empty men to me," he realized.

Therefore, it was said, "Then, it occurred to the Blessed One, 'All of them are vain men to me,'" and so on.

There, *phuṭṭhā pāpimatā*ti: touched by Māra, the evil one.

*yatra hi nāmā*ti: in whom [there is] a name.

*aññāṇatthampī*ti: For the sake of ignorance also… for the sake of knowledge.

*kiṃ karissati sattāho*ti: What will the week do? [This means:] What will the week, defined by the ascetic Gotama, do to us?

This is what was said: "The ascetic Gotama said, 'Having directly experienced the higher knowledge himself, he will abide for a week,' what discomfort will that week cause us?"

Now, we are able to realize this Dharma within a week, or not able. Even for the sake of ignorance, we will live the holy life.

Or, we know his Dhamma for a moment, for one day, once; even for the sake of ignorance, this thought did not arise in them. What will the week do for these lazy ones? What will they be able to complete in a week? This is the meaning here.

*sīhanāda*nti: Having roared the lion's roar, [which is] the shattering of the doctrines of others and the raising up of one's own doctrine, [a roar] free from fear.

*paccupaṭṭhāsī*ti: Established.

*tāvadevā*ti: In that very moment.

*rājagahaṃ pāvisī*ti: He entered Rājagṛha itself.

Although no special [insight] arose in those wanderers from hearing this discourse, in the future, however, it will be a cause for their habit-energy.

The rest is clear throughout.

*phuṭṭhā pāpimatā* *yatra hi nāmā* *aññāṇatthampī* *kiṃ karissati sattāho* *sīhanāda* *paccupaṭṭhāsī* *tāvadevā* *rājagahaṃ pāvisī*

The Commentary on the Udumbarika Sutta is finished.

mula_pali:
80. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā magadhesu viharati mātulāyaṃ. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘bhikkhavo’’ti. ‘‘Bhaddante’’ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca – ‘‘attadīpā, bhikkhave, viharatha attasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā, dhammadīpā dhammasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā. Kathañca pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu attadīpo viharati attasaraṇo anaññasaraṇo, dhammadīpo dhammasaraṇo anaññasaraṇo? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Vedanāsu vedanānupassī…pe… citte cittānupassī…pe… dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu attadīpo viharati attasaraṇo anaññasaraṇo, dhammadīpo dhammasaraṇo anaññasaraṇo.

‘‘Gocare, bhikkhave, caratha sake pettike visaye. Gocare, bhikkhave, carataṃ sake pettike visaye na lacchati māro otāraṃ, na lacchati māro ārammaṇaṃ āramaṇaṃ (?). Kusalānaṃ, bhikkhave, dhammānaṃ samādānahetu evamidaṃ puññaṃ pavaḍḍhati.

āramaṇaṃ (?)

Daḷhanemicakkavattirājā
mula_english:
80. Thus have I heard:

Once the Blessed One was staying among the Magadhans at Mātulā.

There the Fortunate One addressed the monks, saying: “Monks!”

“Venerable sir,” those monks replied to the Blessed One.

The Blessed One said this: “Be islands unto yourselves, monks, refuges unto yourselves, seeking no external refuge; with the Dharma as your island, the Dharma as your refuge, seeking no other refuge.

And how, monks, does a monk live as an island unto himself, a refuge unto himself, seeking no other refuge; with the Dharma as his island, the Dharma as his refuge, seeking no other refuge? Here, monks, a monk abides contemplating the body as body, earnestly, clearly comprehending, and mindfully, having overcome desire and sorrow in regard to the world.

He abides contemplating feelings as feelings,… mind as mind,… mental objects as mental objects, earnestly, clearly comprehending, and mindfully, having put aside hankering and fretting for the world.

This is how, monks, a monk lives as an island unto himself, a refuge unto himself, seeking no other refuge; with the *dharma* as his island, the *dharma* as his refuge, seeking no other refuge.”

“Keep to your own preserves, monks, to your ancestral haunts.

If you conduct yourselves in your own preserves, in your own ancestral territory, Māra will find no opportunity, Māra will find no support.

It is just by the building-up of wholesome states (*kuśalānām dharmānām*), monks, that this merit (*puṇyaṃ*) increases.”

Support (?)

Daḷhanemicakkavattirājā
commentary_pali:
80.Evaṃme sutanti cakkavattisuttaṃ. Tatrāyamanuttānapadavaṇṇanā – mātulāyanti evaṃnāmake nagare. Taṃ nagaraṃ gocaragāmaṃ katvā avidūre vanasaṇḍe viharati. ‘‘Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesī’’ti ettha ayamanupubbikathā –
