Bhagavā kira imassa suttassa samuṭṭhānasamaye paccūsakāle mahākaruṇāsamāpattito vuṭṭhāya lokaṃ volokento imāya anāgatavaṃsadīpikāya suttantakathāya mātulanagaravāsīnaṃ caturāsītiyā pāṇasahassānaṃ dhammābhisamayaṃ disvā pātova vīsatibhikkhusahassaparivāro mātulanagaraṃ sampatto. Mātulanagaravāsino khattiyā ‘‘bhagavā āgato’’ti sutvā paccuggamma dasabalaṃ nimantetvā mahāsakkārena nagaraṃ pavesetvā nisajjaṭṭhānaṃ saṃvidhāya bhagavantaṃ mahārahe pallaṅke nisīdāpetvā buddhappamukhassa bhikkhusaṅghassa mahādānaṃ adaṃsu. Bhagavā bhattakiccaṃ niṭṭhāpetvā cintesi – ‘‘sacāhaṃ imasmiṃ ṭhāne imesaṃ manussānaṃ dhammaṃ desessāmi, ayaṃ padeso sambādho, manussānaṃ ṭhātuṃ vā nisīdituṃ vā okāso na bhavissati, mahatā kho pana samāgamena bhavitabba’’nti.

Atha rājakulānaṃ bhattānumodanaṃ akatvāva pattaṃ gahetvā nagarato nikkhami. Manussā cintayiṃsu – ‘‘satthā amhākaṃ anumodanampi akatvā gacchati, addhā bhattaggaṃ amanāpaṃ ahosi, buddhānaṃ nāma na sakkā cittaṃ gahetuṃ, buddhehi saddhiṃ vissāsakaraṇaṃ nāma samussitaphaṇaṃ āsīvisaṃ gīvāya gahaṇasadisaṃ hoti; etha bho, tathāgataṃ khamāpessāmā’’ti. Sakalanagaravāsino bhagavatā saheva nikkhantā. Bhagavā gacchantova magadhakkhette ṭhitaṃ sākhāviṭapasampannaṃ sandacchāyaṃ karīsamattabhūmipatthaṭaṃ ekaṃ mātularukkhaṃ disvā imasmiṃ rukkhamūle nisīditvā dhamme desiyamāne ‘‘mahājanassa ṭhānanisajjanokāso bhavissatī’’ti. Nivattitvā maggā okkamma rukkhamūlaṃ upasaṅkamitvā dhammabhaṇḍāgārikaṃ ānandattheraṃ olokesi. Thero olokitasaññāya eva ‘‘satthā nisīditukāmo’’ti ñatvā sugatamahācīvaraṃ paññapetvā adāsi. Nisīdi bhagavā paññatte āsane. Athassa purato manussā nisīdiṃsu. Ubhosu passesu pacchato ca bhikkhusaṅgho, ākāse devatā aṭṭhaṃsu, evaṃ mahāparisamajjhagato tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi.

Te bhikkhūti tatra upaviṭṭhā dhammappaṭiggāhakā bhikkhū. Attadīpāti attānaṃ dīpaṃ tāṇaṃ leṇaṃ gatiṃ parāyaṇaṃ patiṭṭhaṃ katvā viharathāti attho. Attasaraṇāti idaṃ tasseva vevacanaṃ. Anaññasaraṇāti idaṃ aññasaraṇapaṭikkhepavacanaṃ. Na hi añño aññassa saraṇaṃ hoti, aññassa vāyāmena aññassa asujjhanato. Vuttampi cetaṃ ‘‘attā hi attano nātho, ko hi nātho paro siyā’’ti (dha. pa. 160). Tenāha ‘‘anaññasaraṇā’’ti. Ko panettha attā nāma, lokiyalokuttaro dhammo. Tenāha – ‘‘dhammadīpā dhammasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā’’ti. ‘‘Kāye kāyānupassī’’tiādīni mahāsatipaṭṭhāne vitthāritāni.

Te bhikkhū Attadīpā Attasaraṇā Anaññasaraṇā

Gocareti carituṃ yuttaṭṭhāne. Saketi attano santake. Pettike visayeti pitito āgatavisaye. Caratanti carantānaṃ. ‘‘Caranta’’ntipi pāṭho, ayamevattho. Na lacchatīti na labhissati na passissati. Māroti devaputtamāropi, maccumāropi, kilesamāropi. Otāranti randhaṃ chiddaṃ vivaraṃ. Ayaṃ panattho leḍḍuṭṭhānato nikkhamma toraṇe nisīditvā bālātapaṃ tapantaṃ lāpaṃ sakuṇaṃ gahetvā. Pakkhandasenasakuṇavatthunā dīpetabbo. Vuttañhetaṃ –

Gocare Sake Pettike visaye Carata Na lacchatī Māro Otāra

‘‘Bhūtapubbaṃ, bhikkhave, sakuṇagghi lāpaṃ sakuṇaṃ sahasā ajjhappattā aggahesi. Atha kho, bhikkhave, lāpo sakuṇo sakuṇagghiyā hariyamāno evaṃ paridevasi ‘mayamevamha alakkhikā, mayaṃ appapuññā, ye mayaṃ agocare carimha paravisaye, sacejja mayaṃ gocare careyyāma sake pettike visaye, na myāyaṃ sakuṇagghi alaṃ abhavissa yadidaṃ yuddhāyā’ti. Ko pana te lāpa gocaro sako pettiko visayoti? Yadidaṃ naṅgalakaṭṭhakaraṇaṃ leḍḍuṭṭhānanti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, sakuṇagghi sake bale apatthaddhā sake bale asaṃvadamānā lāpaṃ sakuṇaṃ pamuñci gaccha kho tvaṃ lāpa, tatrapi gantvā na mokkhasīti.

Atha kho , bhikkhave, lāpo sakuṇo naṅgalakaṭṭhakaraṇaṃ leḍḍuṭṭhānaṃ gantvā mahantaṃ leḍḍuṃ abhiruhitvā sakuṇagghiṃ vadamāno aṭṭhāsi ‘‘ehi kho dāni me sakuṇagghi, ehi kho dāni me sakuṇagghī’’ti. Atha kho sā, bhikkhave, sakuṇagghi sake bale apatthaddhā sake bale asaṃvadamānā ubho pakkhe sannayha lāpaṃ sakuṇaṃ sahasā ajjhappattā. Yadā kho, bhikkhave, aññāsi lāpo sakuṇo bahuāgatā kho myāyaṃ sakuṇagghīti, atha kho tasseva leḍḍussa antaraṃ paccupādi. Atha kho, bhikkhave, sakuṇagghi tattheva uraṃ paccatāḷesi. Evañhi taṃ, bhikkhave, hoti yo agocare carati paravisaye.

Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, mā agocare carittha paravisaye, agocare, bhikkhave, carataṃ paravisaye lacchati māro otāraṃ, lacchati māro ārammaṇaṃ. Ko ca, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno agocaro paravisayo, yadidaṃ pañca kāmaguṇā. Katame pañca? Cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā, sotaviññeyyā saddā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā, ghānaviññeyyā gandhā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā, jivhāviññeyyā rasā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā, kāyaviññeyyā phoṭṭhabbā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā. Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno agocaro paravisayo.

Gocare, bhikkhave, caratha…pe… na lacchati māro ārammaṇaṃ. Ko ca, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno gocaro sako pettiko visayo, yadidaṃ cattāro satipaṭṭhānā. Katame cattāro? Idha bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ; vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ; citte cittānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ; dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ – ayaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno gocaro sako pettiko visayoti (saṃ. ni. 5.371).

Kusalānanti anavajjalakkhaṇānaṃ. Samādānahetūti samādāya vattanahetu. Evamidaṃ puññaṃ pavaḍḍhatīti evaṃ idaṃ lokiyalokuttaraṃ puññaphalaṃ vaḍḍhati, puññaphalanti ca uparūpari puññampi puññavipākopi veditabbo.

Kusalāna Samādānahetū Evamidaṃ puññaṃ pavaḍḍhatī

Daḷhanemicakkavattirājakathāvaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
80. Thus I have heard: the *Cakkavattisutta*.

Here follows an explanation of words that are not obvious: "*Mātulāya*" means "in a city called Evaṃnāmaka."

Having made that city a pasture-ground, he lived in a nearby forest grove.

“There, the Blessed One addressed the monks”– here follows a sequential account:

It is said that at the time of the origin of this *sūtra*, the Blessed One, at dawn, arising from the attainment of great compassion, while surveying the world, having seen the *dharma*-understanding of eighty-four thousand living beings dwelling in the city of Mātula through this *sūtra*-discourse illuminating the lineage of the future, arrived in the city of Mātula early in the morning, surrounded by a retinue of twenty thousand monks.

The *Kṣatriyas* dwelling in the city of Mātula, having heard "The Blessed One has arrived," went out to meet him, invited the One with Ten Strengths, and, having respectfully led [him] into the city, prepared a seat, had the Blessed One sit on a precious divan, and gave a great donation to the *bhikṣu-saṃgha* headed by the Buddha.

The Blessed One, having finished his meal, thought: "If I were to teach the *dharma* to these people in this place, this region is crowded; there will be no space for the people to stand or sit, but there should be a great gathering."

Then, without giving approval of the meal to the royal families, he took his bowl and left the city.

The people thought: "The Teacher goes without giving approval to us; truly, the meal was displeasing. It is not possible to grasp the mind of the Buddhas. Trusting the Buddhas is like grasping a cobra with raised hood by the neck; come, let us ask forgiveness of the *Tathāgata*."

All the city-dwellers departed together with the Blessed One.

While going, the Blessed One saw a single *mātula*-tree in the Magadha territory, standing, complete with branches and twigs, providing dense shade, with a surface of about the size of a hide, and thought, “If I sit down at the base of this tree, there will be space for the great assembly to sit and stand."

Having turned back and gone off the road, approaching the base of the tree, he looked at Ānanda Thera, the treasurer of the *dharma*.

The Thera, knowing from the sign of the glance alone that "the Teacher wishes to sit down," spread out the Sugata's great robe and gave [it to him].

The Blessed One sat down on the prepared seat.

Then the people sat down in front of him.

On both sides and in back was the *bhikṣu-saṃgha*; in the sky, the gods stood. Thus, in the midst of the great assembly, there the Blessed One addressed the *bhikṣus*.

"Those *bhikṣus*" means the *bhikṣus* sitting there, accepting the *dharma*.

"*Attadīpā*" means "live making yourselves a lamp, a refuge, a shelter, a destination, an ultimate support." This is the meaning.

"*Attasaraṇā*" – this is a synonym for that very [term].

"*Anaññasaraṇā*" – this is a term rejecting other refuges.

For another is not a refuge for another, because another's effort does not purify another.

And it was said, "Oneself is indeed one's own lord; who else could be the lord?" (Dhp. 160).

Therefore [he] said, "*Anaññasaraṇā*."

What here is the self (*ātmā*)? It is the mundane and supramundane *dharma*.

Therefore [he] said: "*dharma*-lamp, *dharma*-refuge, other-less refuge."

"Contemplating the body in the body," etc., are extensively explained in the *Mahāsatipaṭṭhāna*.

Those *bhikṣus* are lamps unto themselves, refuges unto themselves, and refuges with no other.

"*Gocare*" means "in a suitable place to wander."

"*Sake*" means "in one's own possession."

"*Pettike visaye*" means "in the ancestral realm."
" *carata*nti carantānaṃ:" "carata" means for those who wander.
"‘‘caranta’’ntipi pāṭho, ayamevattho:" "caranta" is also a reading, the meaning is the same.
" *na lacchatī*ti na labhissati na passissati:" "na lacchati" means he will not obtain, he will not see.
" *māro*ti devaputtamāropi, maccumāropi, kilesamāropi:" "*māra*" means he raised up the son of a god, he raised up death, he raised up defilements.
" *otāra*nti randhaṃ chiddaṃ vivaraṃ:" "*otāra*" means a hole, a gap, an opening.
ayaṃ panattho leḍḍuṭṭhānato nikkhamma toraṇe nisīditvā bālātapaṃ tapantaṃ lāpaṃ sakuṇaṃ gahetvā: Now, the meaning here is, having left the lump of earth, sitting at the archway, taking the young bird that was warming itself in the sun.
pakkhandasenasakuṇavatthunā dīpetabbo: It should be explained by the story of Pakkhandasena and the bird.
vuttañhetaṃ –

*gocare sake pettike visaye carata na lacchatī māro otāraṃ:*

“bhūtapubbaṃ, bhikkhave, sakuṇagghi lāpaṃ sakuṇaṃ sahasā ajjhappattā aggahesi: It has been said: A hawk, monks, suddenly attacked and seized a quail.
atha kho, bhikkhave, lāpo sakuṇo sakuṇagghiyā hariyamāno evaṃ paridevasi ‘mayamevamha alakkhikā, mayaṃ appapuññā, ye <pb ed="p" n="3.
0847"/> mayaṃ agocare carimha paravisaye, sacejja mayaṃ gocare careyyāma sake pettike visaye, na myāyaṃ sakuṇagghi alaṃ abhavissa yadidaṃ yuddhāyā’ti: Then, monks, as the quail was being carried off by the hawk, it lamented thus: ‘We are unlucky, we are without merit, because we wandered in a place that was not our own. If we were to wander in our own ancestral territory, this hawk would not be strong enough to fight with us.’
ko pana te lāpa gocaro sako pettiko visayoti? yadidaṃ <pb ed="m" n="3.
0031"/> naṅgalakaṭṭhakaraṇaṃ leḍḍuṭṭhānanti: What, quail, is your own ancestral territory? It is this: the place of the ploughshare and the lump of earth.
atha kho, bhikkhave, sakuṇagghi sake bale apatthaddhā sake bale asaṃvadamānā lāpaṃ sakuṇaṃ pamuñci gaccha kho tvaṃ lāpa, tatrapi gantvā na mokkhasīti: Then, monks, the hawk, not relying on its own strength, not trusting in its own strength, released the quail, saying: ‘Go now, quail, even going there you will not escape.’

atha kho <pb ed="v" n="3.
0028"/>, bhikkhave, lāpo sakuṇo naṅgalakaṭṭhakaraṇaṃ leḍḍuṭṭhānaṃ gantvā mahantaṃ leḍḍuṃ abhiruhitvā sakuṇagghiṃ vadamāno aṭṭhāsi ‘‘ehi kho dāni me sakuṇagghi, ehi kho dāni me sakuṇagghī’’ti: Then, monks, the quail, going to the place of the ploughshare and the lump of earth, climbing up a large lump of earth, stood calling out to the hawk: ‘Come now, hawk, come now, hawk!’
atha kho sā, bhikkhave, sakuṇagghi sake bale apatthaddhā sake bale asaṃvadamānā ubho pakkhe sannayha lāpaṃ sakuṇaṃ sahasā ajjhappattā: Then, monks, the hawk, relying on its own strength, trusting in its own strength, folding both wings, suddenly reached the quail.
yadā kho, bhikkhave, aññāsi lāpo sakuṇo bahuāgatā kho myāyaṃ sakuṇagghīti, atha kho tasseva leḍḍussa antaraṃ paccupādi: When, monks, the quail knew, ‘This hawk has come too close to me,’ then a gap in that very lump of earth appeared.
atha kho, bhikkhave, sakuṇagghi tattheva uraṃ paccatāḷesi: Then, monks, the hawk right there beat its breast.
evañhi taṃ, bhikkhave, hoti yo agocare carati paravisaye: Indeed, monks, it is like this for anyone who wanders in a place that is not their own.

tasmātiha, bhikkhave, mā agocare carittha paravisaye, agocare, bhikkhave, carataṃ paravisaye lacchati māro otāraṃ, lacchati māro ārammaṇaṃ: Therefore, monks, do not wander in a place that is not your own, for monks, wandering in a place that is not your own, Māra obtains an opportunity, Māra obtains a foothold.
ko ca, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno agocaro paravisayo, yadidaṃ pañca kāmaguṇā: And what, monks, is a monk's place that is not his own, another's territory? It is these five strands of sense pleasure.
katame pañca? cakkhuviññeyyā rūpā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā, sotaviññeyyā saddā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā, ghānaviññeyyā gandhā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā, jivhāviññeyyā rasā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā, kāyaviññeyyā phoṭṭhabbā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā piyarūpā kāmūpasaṃhitā rajanīyā: Which five? Forms cognizable by the eye that are wished for, desired, agreeable, likeable, connected with sensual desire and provocative of lust; sounds cognizable by the ear... odours cognizable by the nose... flavours cognizable by the tongue... tangibles cognizable by the body that are wished for, desired, agreeable, and likeable, connected with sensual desire and provocative of lust.
ayaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno agocaro paravisayo: This, monks, is a monk's place that is not his own, another's territory.

gocare, bhikkhave, caratha…pe… na lacchati māro ārammaṇaṃ: Wander in your own place, monks... and so on... Māra does not obtain a foothold.
ko ca, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno gocaro sako pettiko visayo, yadidaṃ cattāro satipaṭṭhānā: And what, monks, is a monk's own ancestral territory? It is these four foundations of mindfulness ( *satipaṭṭhāna*).
katame cattāro? idha bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ; vedanāsu vedanānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ; citte cittānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ; dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ – ayaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno gocaro sako pettiko visayoti (saṃ.

371): Which four? Here, monks, a monk abides contemplating the body as a body, ardent, clearly aware and mindful, having put aside hankering and fretting for the world; he abides contemplating feelings as feelings...; he abides contemplating mind as mind...; he abides contemplating mind-objects as mind-objects, ardent, clearly aware and mindful, having put aside hankering and fretting for the world. This, monks, is a monk's own ancestral territory.

*kusalāna*nti anavajjalakkhaṇānaṃ: "*kusalāna*" means of faultless characteristics.
*samādānahetū*ti samādāya vattanahetu: "*samādānahetū*" means the cause of undertaking and practice.
*evamidaṃ puññaṃ pavaḍḍhatī*ti evaṃ idaṃ lokiyalokuttaraṃ puññaphalaṃ vaḍḍhati, puññaphalanti ca uparūpari puññampi puññavipākopi veditabbo: "*evamidaṃ puññaṃ pavaḍḍhatī*" means in this way this worldly and supramundane fruit of merit increases; and the fruit of merit should be understood as both merit and the ripening of merit, one upon the other.

*kusalāna samādānahetū evamidaṃ puññaṃ pavaḍḍhatī*
daḷhanemicakkavattirājakathāvaṇṇanā: The description of the story of Daḷhanemi, the wheel-turning monarch.

mula_pali: 81. ‘‘Bhūtapubbaṃ , bhikkhave, rājā daḷhanemi nāma ahosi cakkavattī cakkavatti (syā. pī.) dhammiko dhammarājā cāturanto vijitāvī janapadatthāvariyappatto sattaratanasamannāgato. Tassimāni satta ratanāni ahesuṃ seyyathidaṃ – cakkaratanaṃu hatthiratanaṃ assaratanaṃ maṇiratanaṃ itthiratanaṃ gahapatiratanaṃ pariṇāyakaratanameva sattamaṃ. Parosahassaṃ kho panassa puttā ahesuṃ sūrā vīraṅgarūpā parasenappamaddanā. So imaṃ pathaviṃ sāgarapariyantaṃ adaṇḍena asatthena dhammena dhammena samena (syā. ka.) abhivijiya ajjhāvasi.
mula_english: Once, monks, there was a king named Daḷhanemi, a wheel-turning monarch ( *cakravartin* ), a righteous king who ruled by the Dharma ( *dharma*), master of the four quarters, all-victorious, who had stabilised his country and possessed the seven treasures ( *sapta ratnāni*). He had these seven treasures: namely, the Wheel-Treasure ( *cakra-ratna*), the Elephant-Treasure ( *hasti-ratna*), the Horse-Treasure ( *aśva-ratna*), the Jewel-Treasure ( *maṇi-ratna*), the Woman-Treasure ( *strī-ratna*), the Householder-Treasure ( *gṛhapati-ratna*), and the Counselor-Treasure ( *pariṇāyaka-ratna*) as the seventh. Moreover, he had more than a thousand sons who were heroes, of heroic stature, conquerors of the hostile army. He dwells having conquered this earth bounded by the ocean, without stick or sword, by the Dharma.
commentary_pali:
81. Tattha duvidhaṃ kusalaṃ vaṭṭagāmī ca vivaṭṭagāmī ca. Tattha vaṭṭagāmikusalaṃ nāma mātāpitūnaṃ puttadhītāsu puttadhītānañca mātāpitūsu sinehavasena mudumaddavacittaṃ. Vivaṭṭagāmikusalaṃ nāma ‘‘cattāro satipaṭṭhānā’’tiādibhedā sattatiṃsa bodhipakkhiyadhammā. Tesu vaṭṭagāmipuññassa pariyosānaṃ manussaloke cakkavattisirīvibhavo. Vivaṭṭagāmikusalassa maggaphalanibbānasampatti. Tattha vivaṭṭagāmikusalassa vipākaṃ suttapariyosāne dassessati.

Idha pana vaṭṭagāmikusalassa vipākadassanatthaṃ, bhikkhave, yadā puttadhītaro mātāpitūnaṃ ovāde na aṭṭhaṃsu, tadā āyunāpi vaṇṇenāpi issariyenāpi parihāyiṃsu. Yadā pana aṭṭhaṃsu, tadā vaḍḍhiṃsūti vatvā vaṭṭagāmikusalānusandhivasena ‘‘bhūtapubbaṃ, bhikkhave’’ti desanaṃ ārabhi. Tattha cakkavattītiādīni mahāpadāne (dī. ni. aṭṭha. 2.33) vitthāritāneva.
commentary_english:
81. Therein, twofold is the wholesome ( *kuśala*): *vaṭṭagāmī* and *vivaṭṭagāmī*.

Therein, *vaṭṭagāmikusalaṃ* means a tender and gentle mind due to affection between parents and children and between children and parents.

*vivaṭṭagāmikusalaṃ* means the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment (*bodhipakkhiyadhammā*), beginning with the four establishments of mindfulness (*cattāro satipaṭṭhānā*).

Among these, the result of *vaṭṭagāmipuññassa* is the glory and wealth of a wheel-turning monarch (*cakravartisirīvibhavo*) in the human world (*manussaloke*).

[The result] of *vivaṭṭagāmikusalassa* is the attainment (*sampatti*) of the path (*magga*), the fruit (*phala*), and *nirvāṇa*.

There, at the end of the discourse (*suttapariyosāne*), he will show the result (*vipākaṃ*) of *vivaṭṭagāmikusalassa*.

Here, monks (*bhikkhave*), in order to show the result (*vipāka*) of *vaṭṭagāmikusalassa*, when sons and daughters did not stand by the advice of their parents, then they declined in life (*āyu*), beauty (*vaṇṇa*), and power (*issariya*).

When they stood by [it], then, having said that they grew, he began the teaching (*desanaṃ*) with the connection of *vaṭṭagāmikusala* [saying], "Once upon a time, monks (*bhikkhave*)".

There, *cakkavattītiādīni* (wheel-turner etc.) are explained at length in the Mahāpadāna Sutta (Dīgha Nikāya, Aṭṭhakathā 2.33).

mula_pali: 82. ‘‘Atha kho, bhikkhave, rājā daḷhanemi bahunnaṃ vassānaṃ bahunnaṃ vassasatānaṃ bahunnaṃ vassasahassānaṃ accayena aññataraṃ purisaṃ āmantesi – ‘yadā tvaṃ, ambho purisa, passeyyāsi dibbaṃ cakkaratanaṃ osakkitaṃ ṭhānā cutaṃ, atha me āroceyyāsī’ti. ‘Evaṃ, devā’ti kho, bhikkhave, so puriso rañño daḷhanemissa paccassosi. Addasā kho, bhikkhave, so puriso bahunnaṃ vassānaṃ bahunnaṃ vassasatānaṃ bahunnaṃ vassasahassānaṃ accayena dibbaṃ cakkaratanaṃ osakkitaṃ ṭhānā cutaṃ, disvāna yena rājā daḷhanemi tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā rājānaṃ daḷhanemiṃ etadavoca – ‘yagghe, deva, jāneyyāsi, dibbaṃ te cakkaratanaṃ osakkitaṃ ṭhānā cuta’nti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, rājā daḷhanemi jeṭṭhaputtaṃ kumāraṃ āmantāpetvā āmantetvā (syā. ka.) etadavoca – ‘dibbaṃ kira me, tāta kumāra, cakkaratanaṃ osakkitaṃ ṭhānā cutaṃ. Sutaṃ kho pana metaṃ – yassa rañño cakkavattissa dibbaṃ cakkaratanaṃ osakkati ṭhānā cavati, na dāni tena raññā ciraṃ jīvitabbaṃ hotīti. Bhuttā kho pana me mānusakā kāmā, samayo dāni me dibbe kāme pariyesituṃ. Ehi tvaṃ, tāta kumāra, imaṃ samuddapariyantaṃ pathaviṃ paṭipajja. Ahaṃ pana kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissāmī’ti.
mula_english:
Monks, after many years, many hundreds of years, many thousands of years, King Daḷhanemi addressed a certain man: 'Good man, whenever you see the divine wheel-treasure has slipped, fallen from its place, then report it to me.'

'Very good, your majesty,' the man replied to King Daḷhanemi.

Monks, after many years, many hundreds of years, many thousands of years, the man saw the divine wheel-treasure had slipped, fallen from its place. Having seen it, he approached King Daḷhanemi and said: 'Your majesty, know that your divine wheel-treasure has slipped, fallen from its place.'

Then, monks, King Daḷhanemi had his eldest son, the prince, summoned and said: 'My dear prince, it seems the divine wheel-treasure has slipped, fallen from its place. And I have heard that when the divine wheel-treasure of a wheel-turning monarch slips and falls from its place, that king does not have long to live. I have had my fill of human pleasures (mānusakāma), now is the time for me to seek divine pleasures (dibba kāma). Come, dear prince, take over this ocean-bounded land (samuddapariyantaṃ pathaviṃ). But I shall shave off my hair and beard, put on the ochre robes, and go forth from the householder's life into homelessness (agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissāmi).'
commentary_pali:
82.Osakkitanti īsakampi avasakkitaṃ. Ṭhānā cutanti sabbaso ṭhānā apagataṃ. Taṃ kira cakkaratanaṃ antepuradvāre akkhāhataṃ viya vehāsaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Athassa ubhosu passesu dve khadiratthambhe nikhaṇitvā cakkaratanamatthake nemiabhimukhaṃ ekaṃ suttakaṃ bandhiṃsu. Adhobhāgepi nemiabhimukhaṃ ekaṃ bandhiṃsu. Tesu uparimasuttato appamattakampi ogataṃ cakkaratanaṃ osakkitaṃ nāma hoti, heṭṭhā suttassa ṭhānaṃ uparimakoṭiyā atikkantagataṃ ṭhānā cutaṃ nāma hoti, tadetaṃ atibalavadose sati evaṃ hoti. Suttamattampi ekaṅguladvaṅgulamattaṃ vā bhaṭṭhaṃ ṭhānā cutameva hoti. Taṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ ‘‘osakkitaṃ ṭhānā cuta’’nti.

Atha me āroceyyāsīti tāta, tvaṃ ajja ādiṃ katvā divasassa tikkhattuṃ cakkaratanassa upaṭṭhānaṃ gaccha, evaṃ gacchanto yadā cakkaratanaṃ īsakampi osakkitaṃ ṭhānā cutaṃ passasi, atha mayhaṃ ācikkheyyāsi. Jīvitañhi me tava hatthe nikkhittanti. Addasāti appamatto divasassa tikkhattuṃ gantvā olokento ekadivasaṃ addasa.

Atha me āroceyyāsī Addasā
commentary_english:
82. " *Osakkita* means even a little receding.

*ṭhānā cuta* means completely departed from the place.

That wheel-jewel stood in the sky as if struck by an axle at the gate of the inner city.

Then, having dug two *khadira* posts on both sides, they tied one thread-cord facing the rim on the top of the wheel-jewel.

Also on the lower part, they tied one facing the rim.

Among those, if the wheel-jewel, having gone down even a little from the upper thread, is said to be *osakkita*, the place of the lower thread, having gone beyond the upper edge, is said to be *ṭhānā cuta*, so it is when there is very strong fault.

Even a thread-cord, if it is fallen as much as one or two inches, it is indeed *ṭhānā cuta*.

Referring to that, this was said, “ *osakkitaṃ ṭhānā cuta*."

" *Atha me āroceyyāsī* ti tāta, *tvam ajja ādiṃ katvā divasassa tikkhattuṃ cakkaratanassa upaṭṭhānaṃ gaccha, evaṃ gacchanto yadā cakkaratanaṃ īsakampi osakkitaṃ ṭhānā cutaṃ passasi, atha mayhaṃ ācikkheyyāsi.*" Thus, father, you, having made a beginning today, go to the attendance of the wheel-jewel three times a day, thus going, when you see the wheel-jewel even a little *osakkita* and *ṭhānā cuta*, then you should tell me.

Indeed, my life is placed in your hand.

*Addasā* means, being unheedful, having gone three times a day, looking around, one day he saw.

*Atha me āroceyyāsī addasā*

mula_pali:
83. ‘‘Atha kho, bhikkhave, rājā daḷhanemi jeṭṭhaputtaṃ kumāraṃ sādhukaṃ rajje samanusāsitvā kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbaji. Sattāhapabbajite kho pana, bhikkhave, rājisimhi dibbaṃ cakkaratanaṃ antaradhāyi.

‘‘Atha kho, bhikkhave, aññataro puriso yena rājā khattiyo muddhābhisitto muddhāvasitto (sī. syā. pī.) evamuparipi tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā rājānaṃ khattiyaṃ muddhābhisittaṃ etadavoca – ‘yagghe, deva, jāneyyāsi, dibbaṃ cakkaratanaṃ antarahita’nti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, rājā khattiyo muddhābhisitto dibbe cakkaratane antarahite anattamano ahosi, anattamanatañca paṭisaṃvedesi. So yena rājisi tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā rājisiṃ etadavoca – ‘yagghe, deva, jāneyyāsi, dibbaṃ cakkaratanaṃ antarahita’nti. Evaṃ vutte, bhikkhave, rājisi rājānaṃ khattiyaṃ muddhābhisittaṃ etadavoca – ‘mā kho tvaṃ, tāta, dibbe cakkaratane antarahite anattamano ahosi, mā anattamanatañca paṭisaṃvedesi, na hi te, tāta, dibbaṃ cakkaratanaṃ pettikaṃ dāyajjaṃ. Iṅgha tvaṃ, tāta, ariye cakkavattivatte vattāhi. Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ vijjati, yaṃ te ariye cakkavattivatte vattamānassa tadahuposathe pannarase sīsaṃnhātassa sīsaṃ nahātassa (sī. pī.), sīsanhātassa (syā.) uposathikassa uparipāsādavaragatassa dibbaṃ cakkaratanaṃ pātubhavissati sahassāraṃ sanemikaṃ sanābhikaṃ sabbākāraparipūra’nti.

muddhāvasitto (sī. syā. pī.) evamuparipi sīsaṃ nahātassa (sī. pī.), sīsanhātassa (syā.)

Cakkavattiariyavattaṃ
mula_english:
"Then, monks, King Daḷhanemi, having duly instructed his eldest son, the prince, in kingship, shaved off his hair and beard, donned yellow robes, and went forth from the household life into homelessness.

And seven days after the royal sage (*rājisi*) had gone forth, the divine wheel-treasure (*cakkaratana*) disappeared.

"Then, monks, a certain man came to the anointed Khattiya king; having come, he said to the anointed Khattiya king: ‘Sire, you should know that the divine wheel-treasure has disappeared.’

Then, monks, the anointed Khattiya king, upon the disappearance of the divine wheel-treasure, was grieved and felt sad.

He went to the royal sage; having come, he said to the royal sage: ‘Sire, you should know that the divine wheel-treasure has disappeared.’

When this was said, monks, the royal sage said to the anointed Khattiya king: ‘My son, you should not grieve or feel sad at the disappearance of the divine wheel-treasure. The divine wheel-treasure is not an ancestral inheritance for you.

But now, my son, you must turn yourself to the Ariyan wheel-turning conduct (*ariye cakkavattivatte*).

And then it may come about that, if you are engaged in the Ariyan wheel-turning conduct, on the fast-day of the fifteenth, when you have bathed your head and gone up to the excellent verandah on top of your palace for the fast-day, the divine wheel-treasure will appear to you, thousand-spoked, complete with felloe, hub and all appurtenances.’"

Cakkavattiariyavattaṃ (The Ariyan Wheel-Turning Conduct)
commentary_pali:
83.Athakho, bhikkhaveti bhikkhave, atha rājā daḷhanemi ‘‘cakkaratanaṃ osakkita’’nti sutvā uppannabalavadomanasso ‘‘na dāni mayā ciraṃ jīvitabbaṃ bhavissati, appāvasesaṃ me āyu, na me dāni kāme paribhuñjanakālo, pabbajjākālo me idānī’’ti roditvā paridevitvā jeṭṭhaputtaṃ kumāraṃ āmantāpetvā etadavoca. Samuddapariyantanti parikkhittaekasamuddapariyantameva. Idaṃ hissa kulasantakaṃ. Cakkavāḷapariyantaṃ pana puññiddhivasena nibbattaṃ, na taṃ sakkā dātuṃ. Kulasantakaṃ pana niyyātento ‘‘samuddapariyanta’’nti āha. Kesamassunti tāpasapabbajjaṃ pabbajantāpi hi paṭhamaṃ kesamassuṃ ohārenti. Tato paṭṭhāya parūḷhakese bandhitvā vicaranti. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘kesamassuṃ ohāretvā’’ti.

Kāsāyānīti kasāyarasapītāni. Ādito evaṃ katvā pacchā vakkalānipi dhārenti. Pabbajīti pabbajito. Pabbajitvā ca attano maṅgalavanuyyāneyeva vasi. Rājisimhīti rājaīsimhi. Brāhmaṇapabbajitā hi ‘‘brāhmaṇisayo’’ti vuccanti. Setacchattaṃ pana pahāya rājapabbajitā rājisayoti. Antaradhāyīti antarahitaṃ nibbutadīpasikhā viya abhāvaṃ upagataṃ. Paṭisaṃvedesīti kandanto paridevanto jānāpesi. Pettikanti pitito āgataṃ dāyajjaṃ na hoti, na sakkā kusītena hīnavīriyena dasa akusalakammapathe samādāya vattantena pāpuṇituṃ. Attano pana sukataṃ kammaṃ nissāya dasavidhaṃ dvādasavidhaṃ vā cakkavattivattaṃ pūrentenevetaṃ pattabbanti dīpeti. Atha naṃ vattapaṭipattiyaṃ codento ‘‘iṅgha tva’’ntiādimāha. Tattha ariyeti niddose. Cakkavattivatteti cakkavattīnaṃ vatte.

Kāsāyānī Pabbajī Rājisimhī Antaradhāyī Paṭisaṃvedesī Pettika ariye Cakkavattivatte

Cakkavattiariyavattavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
83. *Atha kho, bhikkhave* means monks; then King Daḷhanemi, hearing that the "wheel-jewel has declined," felt a great sorrow and said, "I will not live long, my life is nearly over, this is not the time for me to enjoy pleasures, now is the time for me to renounce," and weeping and lamenting, he summoned his eldest son, the prince, and said this:

*Samuddapariyanta* means only as far as the sea surrounds. This is his ancestral property. But what extends to the limits of the *cakravāḷa* arises from the power of merit and cannot be given away. However, when handing over the ancestral property, he said, "as far as the sea surrounds."

*Kesamassu* means even those who renounce in the ascetic's renunciation first shave off their hair and beard. From then on, they tie up their overgrown hair and wander about. Therefore it was said - "having shaved off hair and beard."

*Kāsāyānī* means dyed with astringent flavors. Having done this from the beginning, they later wear bark garments as well.

*Pabbajī* means he renounced. And having renounced, he lived in his own auspicious park.

*Rājisimhī* means royal ascetic. Ascetics who are Brahmins are called *brāhmaṇisayo*. But having abandoned the white umbrella, royal renunciates are called *rājisayo*.

*Antaradhāyī* means disappeared, like a extinguished lamp flame, having gone to non-existence.

*Paṭisaṃvedesī* means he announced, weeping and lamenting.

*Pettika* means the inheritance that comes from the father is not obtained by one who is lazy, lacking in energy, and living by engaging in the ten unwholesome courses of action. But it is because of his own well-done deeds, relying on them, that he fulfills the ten or twelve duties of a wheel-turning monarch.

Then, urging him in the practice of those duties, he said, "Come now," etc.

There, *ariye* means faultless.

*Cakkavattivatte* means the duties of wheel-turning monarchs.

*Kāsāyānī, Pabbajī, Rājisimhī, Antaradhāyī, Paṭisaṃvedesī, Pettika, Ariye, Cakkavattivatte*

Description of the Noble Duties of a Wheel-Turning Monarch

mula_pali:
84. ‘‘‘Katamaṃ pana taṃ, deva, ariyaṃ cakkavattivatta’nti ? ‘Tena hi tvaṃ, tāta, dhammaṃyeva nissāya dhammaṃ sakkaronto dhammaṃ garuṃ karonto garukaronto (sī. syā. pī.) dhammaṃ mānento dhammaṃ pūjento dhammaṃ apacāyamāno dhammaddhajo dhammaketu dhammādhipateyyo dhammikaṃ rakkhāvaraṇaguttiṃ saṃvidahassu antojanasmiṃ balakāyasmiṃ khattiyesu anuyantesu anuyuttesu (sī. pī.) brāhmaṇagahapatikesu negamajānapadesu samaṇabrāhmaṇesu migapakkhīsu. Mā ca te, tāta, vijite adhammakāro pavattittha. Ye ca te, tāta, vijite adhanā assu, tesañca dhanamanuppadeyyāsi dhanamanuppadajjeyyāsi (sī. syā. pī.). Ye ca te, tāta, vijite samaṇabrāhmaṇā madappamādā paṭiviratā khantisoracce niviṭṭhā ekamattānaṃ damenti, ekamattānaṃ samenti, ekamattānaṃ parinibbāpenti, te kālena kālaṃ upasaṅkamitvā paripuccheyyāsi pariggaṇheyyāsi – ‘‘kiṃ, bhante, kusalaṃ, kiṃ akusalaṃ, kiṃ sāvajjaṃ, kiṃ anavajjaṃ, kiṃ sevitabbaṃ, kiṃ na sevitabbaṃ, kiṃ me karīyamānaṃ dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāya assa, kiṃ vā pana me karīyamānaṃ dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya assā’’ti? Tesaṃ sutvā yaṃ akusalaṃ taṃ abhinivajjeyyāsi, yaṃ kusalaṃ taṃ samādāya vatteyyāsi. Idaṃ kho, tāta, taṃ ariyaṃ cakkavattivatta’nti.

Cakkaratanapātubhāvo
mula_english:
“But what, your majesty, is the duty of an Āryan wheel-turning monarch?”

“It is this, my son: Yourself depending on the *dharma*, honouring the *dharma*, revering the *dharma*, cherishing the *dharma*, doing homage to the *dharma* and venerating the *dharma*, having the *dharma* as your badge and banner, acknowledging the *dharma* as your master, you should establish guard, ward and protection according to *dharma* for your own household, your troops, your nobles and vassals, for *brāhmaṇas* and householders, town and country folk, ascetics and *brāhmaṇas*, for beasts and birds.

Let no crime prevail in your kingdom, and to those who are in need, give property.

And whatever ascetics and *brāhmaṇas* in your kingdom have renounced the life of sensual infatuation and are devoted to forbearance and gentleness, each one taming himself, each one calming himself and each one striving for the end of craving, if from time to time they should come to you and consult you as to what is wholesome (*kuśala*) and what is unwholesome (*akuśala*), what is blameworthy (*sāvajja*) and what is blameless (*anavajja*), what is to be followed and what is not to be followed, and what action will in the long run lead to harm and suffering, or what action will in the long run lead to welfare and happiness, having listened to them, you should reject what is unwholesome and undertake and adopt what is wholesome. That, my son, is the duty of an Āryan wheel-turning monarch.”

Appearance of the Wheel-Jewel
commentary_pali:
84.Dhammanti dasakusalakammapathadhammaṃ. Nissāyāti tadadhiṭṭhānena cetasā tameva nissayaṃ katvā. Dhammaṃ sakkarontoti yathā kato so dhammo suṭṭhu kato hoti, evametaṃ karonto. Dhammaṃ garuṃ karontoti tasmiṃ gāravuppattiyā taṃ garuṃ karonto. Dhammaṃ mānentoti tameva dhammaṃ piyañca bhāvanīyañca katvā viharanto. Dhammaṃ pūjentoti taṃ apadisitvā gandhamālādipūjanenassa pūjaṃ karonto. Dhammaṃapacayamānoti tasseva dhammassa añjalikaraṇādīhi nīcavuttitaṃ karonto. Dhammaddhajodhammaketūti taṃ dhammaṃ dhajamiva purakkhatvā ketumiva ca ukkhipitvā pavattiyā dhammaddhajo dhammaketu ca hutvāti attho. Dhammādhipateyyoti dhammādhipatibhūto āgatabhāvena dhammavaseneva sabbakiriyānaṃ karaṇena dhammādhipateyyo hutvā. Dhammikaṃ rakkhāvaraṇaguttiṃ saṃvidahassūti dhammo assā atthīti dhammikā, rakkhā ca āvaraṇañca gutti ca rakkhāvaraṇagutti . Tattha ‘‘paraṃ rakkhanto attānaṃ rakkhatī’’ti (saṃ. ni. 5.385) vacanato khantiādayo rakkhā. Vuttañhetaṃ ‘‘kathañca, bhikkhave, paraṃ rakkhanto attānaṃ rakkhati. Khantiyā avihiṃsāya mettacittatā anuddayatā’’ti (saṃ. ni. 5.385). Nivāsanapārupanagehādīnaṃ nivāraṇā āvaraṇaṃ, corādiupaddavanivāraṇatthaṃ gopāyanā gutti, taṃ sabbampi suṭṭhu saṃvidahassu pavattaya ṭhapehīti attho. Idāni yattha sā saṃvidahitabbā, taṃ dassento antojanasmintiādimāha.

Tatrāyaṃ saṅkhepattho – antojanasaṅkhātaṃ tava puttadāraṃ sīlasaṃvare patiṭṭhapehi, vatthagandhamālādīni cassa dehi, sabbopaddave cassa nivārehi. Balakāyādīsupi eseva nayo. Ayaṃ pana viseso – balakāyo kālaṃ anatikkamitvā bhattavetanasampadānenapi anuggahetabbo. Abhisittakhattiyā bhadrassājāneyyādiratanasampadānenapi upasaṅgaṇhitabbā. Anuyantakhattiyā tesaṃ anurūpayānavāhanasampadānenapi paritosetabbā. Brāhmaṇā annapānavatthādinā deyyadhammena. Gahapatikā bhattabījanaṅgalaphālabalibaddādisampadānena. Tathā nigamavāsino negamā, janapadavāsino ca jānapadā. Samitapāpabāhitapāpā samaṇabrāhmaṇā samaṇaparikkhārasampadānena sakkātabbā. Migapakkhino abhayadānena samassāsetabbā.

Balakāyā

Vijiteti attano āṇāpavattiṭṭhāne. Adhammakāroti adhammakiriyā. Mā pavattitthāti yathā nappavattati, tathā naṃ paṭipādehīti attho. Samaṇabrāhmaṇāti samitapāpabāhitapāpā. Madappamādāpaṭiviratāti navavidhā mānamadā, pañcasu kāmaguṇesu cittavossajjanasaṅkhātā pamādā ca paṭiviratā. Khantisoracce niviṭṭhāti adhivāsanakhantiyañca suratabhāve ca patiṭṭhitā. Ekamattānanti attano rāgādīnaṃ damanādīhi ekamattānaṃ damenti samenti parinibbāpentīti vuccanti. Kālena kālanti kāle kāle . Abhinivajjeyyāsīti gūthaṃ viya visaṃ viya aggiṃ viya ca suṭṭhu vajjeyyāsi. Samādāyāti surabhikusumadāmaṃ viya amataṃ viya ca sammā ādāya pavatteyyāsi.

Vijite Adhammakāro Mā pavattitthā Samaṇabrāhmaṇā Madappamādā paṭiviratā Khantisoracce niviṭṭhā Ekamattāna Kālena kāla Abhinivajjeyyāsī Samādāyā

Idha ṭhatvā vattaṃ samānetabbaṃ. Antojanasmiṃ balakāyepi ekaṃ, khattiyesu ekaṃ, anuyantesu ekaṃ, brāhmaṇagahapatikesu ekaṃ, negamajānapadesu ekaṃ, samaṇabrāhmaṇesu ekaṃ, migapakkhīsu ekaṃ, adhammakārappaṭikkhepo ekaṃ, adhanānaṃ dhanānuppadānaṃ ekaṃ samaṇabrāhmaṇe upasaṅkamitvā pañhapucchanaṃ ekanti evametaṃ dasavidhaṃ hoti. Gahapatike pana pakkhijāte ca visuṃ katvā gaṇentassa dvādasavidhaṃ hoti. Pubbe avuttaṃ vā gaṇentena adhammarāgassa ca visamalobhassa ca pahānavasena dvādasavidhaṃ veditabbaṃ. Idaṃ kho tāta tanti idaṃ dasavidhaṃ dvādasavidhañca ariyacakkavattivattaṃ nāma. Vattamānassāti pūretvā vattamānassa. Tadahuposathetiādi mahāsudassane vuttaṃ.

Idaṃ kho tāta ta Vattamānassā Tadahuposathe
commentary_english:
84. "*Dharma*," means the *daśakuśalakarmapatha dharma*, the ten paths of wholesome actions.

"*Niśraya*," means having made that the support, with a mind of firm resolution, having made that itself the basis.

"*Dharmaṃ sakkaronto*," means as that which is done, that dharma is well done, thus he does this.

"*Dharmaṃ garuṃ karonto*," means in that, by the arising of respect, he makes that dharma heavy.

"*Dharmaṃ mānento*," means having made that very dharma dear and worthy of cultivation, he dwells [there].

"*Dharmaṃ pūjento*," means having designated that, performing its worship with worships of scents, garlands, and so forth.

"*Dharmaṃ apacayamāno*," means, of that very dharma, performing humbleness with folded hands and so forth, he makes lowliness.

"*Dharmaddhajo dharmaketū*," means, having honored that dharma as a flag, and having raised it up like a banner, by the continuity, he becomes a *dharmaddhaja* and a *dharmaketu*, this is the meaning.

"*Dharmādhipateyyo*," means, having become a *dharmādhipati*, with a nature that has come about, by the power of the dharma, by the doing of all actions, having become a *dharmādhipateyya*.

"*Dhammikaṃ rakkhāvaraṇaguttiṃ saṃvidahassū*," means because dharma exists for him, he is *dharmika*. Protection (*rakkhā*), a covering (*āvaraṇa*), and guarding (*gutti*) are protection and guarding.

There, “Protecting others, one protects oneself,” from the statement of the Saṃyutta Nikāya 5.385, patience and so forth are protection.

It was said, “And how, monks, does one who protects others protect oneself? By patience, non-violence, a mind of loving-kindness, and compassion," (Saṃyutta Nikāya 5.385).

*Nivāraṇa* is a shelter against clothing, covering, houses and so on. *Gutti* is guarding for the sake of preventing disturbances such as thieves and so on. Therefore, do all of that well, cause it to continue, establish it, this is the meaning.

Now, showing where that is to be arranged, [he] says, "*Antojanasmi*," and so forth.

There, this is the concise meaning: Establish your children and wife, who are known as *antojana*, in the restraint of morality (*śīla-saṃvara*), give them clothing, scents, garlands, and so forth, and prevent all disturbances for them.

This same method applies to armies and so forth.

However, this is the distinction: the army is to be supported by not transgressing time, by the provision of food and wages.

Anointed *kṣatriyas* are to be supported by the provision of auspicious horses, thoroughbreds, and so forth.

Following *kṣatriyas* are to be pleased by the provision of vehicles and conveyances appropriate to them.

*Brāhmaṇas* are to be [supported] with gifts of food, drink, clothing, and so on.

Householders are to be [supported] with the provision of food, seeds, plows, shares, oxen, and so forth.

Likewise, those dwelling in towns are *negama*, and those dwelling in the countryside are *jānapada*.

*Śramaṇas* and *brāhmaṇas* who have pacified evil and banished evil are to be honored by the provision of the requisites of a *śramaṇa*.

Birds and animals are to be comforted by the gift of fearlessness.

*Balakāyā vijite*, in one's own place of command and authority.

*Adhammakāro*, means *adharmakiryā*, doing what is not dharma.

*Mā pavattitthā*, means as it does not proceed, thus deal with it, this is the meaning.

*Śramaṇabrāhmaṇā*, means those who have pacified evil and banished evil.

*Madappamādā*.
" *Paṭiviratā* means they are abstaining from the nine kinds of pride and arrogance, the mental agitation regarding the five sense pleasures, which are called negligence, and they are abstaining.
*Khantisoracce niviṭṭhā* means they are established in patience and gentleness and in a loving state.
*Ekamattāna* means they tame, calm, and extinguish their own passions etc. with taming etc.
*Kālena kāla* means at the proper time.
*Abhinivajjeyyāsī* means you should avoid it well, like feces, poison, or fire.
*Samādāyā* means you should properly take and maintain it, like a fragrant flower garland or ambrosia.

In the conquered land, unrighteousness should not prevail; ascetics and Brahmins [should be free from] intoxication and negligence.
*Paṭiviratā khantisoracce niviṭṭhā ekamattāna kālena kāla*.
Here, having stayed, the proper conduct should be brought together.

There is one each for the inner circle and the armed forces; one each for the nobles; one each for the followers; one each for the Brahmins and householders; one each for the merchants and rural areas; one each for the ascetics and Brahmins; one each for animals and birds; one each for the rejection of unrighteous deeds; one each for providing wealth to the poor; after approaching the ascetics and Brahmins, there is one for asking questions; thus, this is tenfold.

However, if the householders and the bird species are made distinct and counted, it is twelvefold.

Or, by one who counts what was not said before, and by the abandonment of unrighteous passion and uneven greed, it should be known as twelvefold.

*Idaṃ kho tāta ta* means this is called the tenfold and twelvefold practice of the noble wheel-turning monarch.

*Vattamānassā* means after completing, of the present.

*Tadahuposathe* etc. is said in the Mahāsudassana [Sutta].

mula_pali:
85. ‘‘‘Evaṃ, devā’ti kho, bhikkhave, rājā khattiyo muddhābhisitto rājisissa paṭissutvā ariye cakkavattivatte ariyaṃ cakkavattivattaṃ (ka.) vatti. Tassa ariye cakkavattivatte vattamānassa tadahuposathe pannarase sīsaṃnhātassa uposathikassa uparipāsādavaragatassa dibbaṃ cakkaratanaṃ pāturahosi sahassāraṃ sanemikaṃ sanābhikaṃ sabbākāraparipūraṃ. Disvāna rañño khattiyassa muddhābhisittassa etadahosi – ‘sutaṃ kho pana metaṃ – yassa rañño khattiyassa muddhābhisittassa tadahuposathe pannarase sīsaṃnhātassa uposathikassa uparipāsādavaragatassa dibbaṃ cakkaratanaṃ pātubhavati sahassāraṃ sanemikaṃ sanābhikaṃ sabbākāraparipūraṃ , so hoti rājā cakkavattī’ti. Assaṃ nu kho ahaṃ rājā cakkavattīti.

‘‘Atha kho, bhikkhave, rājā khattiyo muddhābhisitto uṭṭhāyāsanā ekaṃsaṃ utarāsaṅgaṃ karitvā vāmena hatthena bhiṅkāraṃ gahetvā dakkhiṇena hatthena cakkaratanaṃ abbhukkiri – ‘pavattatu bhavaṃ cakkaratanaṃ, abhivijinātu bhavaṃ cakkaratana’nti.

‘‘Atha kho taṃ, bhikkhave, cakkaratanaṃ puratthimaṃ disaṃ pavatti, anvadeva rājā cakkavattī saddhiṃ caturaṅginiyā senāya. Yasmiṃ kho pana, bhikkhave, padese cakkaratanaṃ patiṭṭhāsi, tattha rājā cakkavattī vāsaṃ upagacchi saddhiṃ caturaṅginiyā senāya. Ye kho pana, bhikkhave, puratthimāya disāya paṭirājāno, te rājānaṃ cakkavattiṃ upasaṅkamitvā evamāhaṃsu – ‘ehi kho, mahārāja, svāgataṃ te sāgataṃ (sī. pī.) mahārāja, sakaṃ te, mahārāja, anusāsa, mahārājā’ti. Rājā cakkavattī evamāha – ‘pāṇo na hantabbo, adinnaṃ nādātabbaṃ, kāmesumicchā na caritabbā, musā na bhāsitabbā, majjaṃ na pātabbaṃ, yathābhuttañca bhuñjathā’ti. Ye kho pana, bhikkhave, puratthimāya disāya paṭirājāno, te rañño cakkavattissa anuyantā anuyuttā (sī. pī.) ahesuṃ.

sāgataṃ (sī. pī.) anuyuttā (sī. pī.)
mula_english:
85. "‘So it is, gods,’ the noble wheel-turning practice, monks, the anointed Khattiya king, promised to the royal sage. As he was following the noble wheel-turning practice, on the fast day of the fifteenth, when he had washed his head and was observing the fast, there appeared to him on the upper terrace of the palace, the divine Wheel-Treasure, thousand-spoked, complete with felloe, hub and all appurtenances. Seeing it, the anointed Khattiya king thought: ‘I have heard that when an anointed Khattiya king sees such a wheel on the fast day of the fifteenth, having washed his head and while observing the fast, there appears to him on the upper terrace of the palace, the divine Wheel-Treasure, thousand-spoked, complete with felloe, hub and all appurtenances, he becomes a wheel-turning monarch (cakravartin). Might I be such a wheel-turning monarch?’

"Then, monks, the anointed Khattiya king, rising from his seat, covering one shoulder with his robe, took a gold vessel (bhiṅkāra) in his left hand, sprinkled the Wheel-Treasure with his right hand, and said: ‘May the honored Wheel-Treasure turn, may the honored Wheel-Treasure conquer!’

"Then, monks, the Wheel-Treasure turned to the east, and the wheel-turning monarch (cakravartin) followed it with his fourfold army. And in whatever place, monks, the Wheel-Treasure stopped, there the wheel-turning monarch (cakravartin) took up residence with his fourfold army. And those opposing kings in the eastern direction came to the wheel-turning monarch (cakravartin) and said: ‘Come, great king (mahārāja), welcome to you, great king (mahārāja)! We are yours, great king (mahārāja)! Rule us, great king (mahārāja)!’ The wheel-turning monarch (cakravartin) said: ‘Life should not be taken, what is not given should not be taken, misconduct in sensual pleasures should not be practiced, lies should not be spoken, intoxicants should not be drunk, and you should eat what you are accustomed to eat.’ And those opposing kings in the eastern direction became followers of the wheel-turning monarch (cakravartin).

mula_pali: 86. ‘‘Atha kho taṃ, bhikkhave, cakkaratanaṃ puratthimaṃ samuddaṃ ajjhogāhetvā ajjhogahetvā (sī. syā. pī.) paccuttaritvā dakkhiṇaṃ disaṃ pavatti…pe… dakkhiṇaṃ samuddaṃ ajjhogāhetvā paccuttaritvā pacchimaṃ disaṃ pavatti, anvadeva rājā cakkavattī saddhiṃ caturaṅginiyā senāya. Yasmiṃ kho pana, bhikkhave, padese cakkaratanaṃ patiṭṭhāsi, tattha rājā cakkavattī vāsaṃ upagacchi saddhiṃ caturaṅginiyā senāya. Ye kho pana, bhikkhave, pacchimāya disāya paṭirājāno, te rājānaṃ cakkavattiṃ upasaṅkamitvā evamāhaṃsu – ‘ehi kho, mahārāja, svāgataṃ te, mahārāja, sakaṃ te, mahārāja, anusāsa, mahārājā’ti. Rājā cakkavattī evamāha – ‘pāṇo na hantabbo, adinnaṃ nādātabbaṃ, kāmesumicchā na caritabbā, musā na bhāsitabbā, majjaṃ na pātabbaṃ, yathābhuttañca bhuñjathā’ti. Ye kho pana, bhikkhave, pacchimāya disāya paṭirājāno, te rañño cakkavattissa anuyantā ahesuṃ.
mula_english:
86. Then, O monks, the wheel-treasure, having plunged into the eastern ocean, and having emerged again, turned to the southern direction... and having plunged into the southern ocean, and having emerged again, turned to the western direction, and the Wheel-turning Monarch ( *rājā cakkavattī*) followed along with his four-constituent army ( *caturaṅginiyā senāya*).

Now in whatever region ( *padese*) the wheel-treasure paused ( *cakkaratanaṃ patiṭṭhāsi*), there the Wheel-turning Monarch ( *rājā cakkavattī*) took up his abode ( *vāsaṃ upagacchi*) with his four-constituent army ( *caturaṅginiyā senāya*).

And those opposing kings ( *paṭirājāno*) in the western direction, approached the Wheel-turning Monarch ( *cakkavattiṃ upasaṅkamitvā*) and said thus: 'Come, great king ( *mahārāja*), welcome ( *svāgataṃ te*), great king ( *mahārāja*), we are yours ( *sakaṃ te*), great king ( *mahārāja*), rule ( *anusāsa*), great king ( *mahārājā*).'

The Wheel-turning Monarch ( *rājā cakkavattī*), said thus: ‘Living beings (*pāṇo*) should not be killed ( *na hantabbo*), what is not given ( *adinnaṃ*) should not be taken ( *nādātabbaṃ*), you should not misconduct yourselves in sensual pleasures ( *kāmesumicchā na caritabbā*), you should not speak falsehood ( *musā na bhāsitabbā*), you should not drink intoxicants ( *majjaṃ na pātabbaṃ*), and you should eat what you are accustomed to eat ( *yathābhuttañca bhuñjathā’ti*).’

And those opposing kings ( *paṭirājāno*) in the western direction, became followers (*anuyantā*) of the Wheel-turning Monarch ( *cakkavattissa*).

mula_pali:
87. ‘‘Atha kho taṃ, bhikkhave, cakkaratanaṃ pacchimaṃ samuddaṃ ajjhogāhetvā paccuttaritvā uttaraṃ disaṃ pavatti, anvadeva rājā cakkavattī saddhiṃ caturaṅginiyā senāya. Yasmiṃ kho pana, bhikkhave, padese cakkaratanaṃ patiṭṭhāsi, tattha rājā cakkavattī vāsaṃ upagacchi saddhiṃ caturaṅginiyā senāya. Ye kho pana, bhikkhave, uttarāya disāya paṭirājāno, te rājānaṃ cakkavattiṃ upasaṅkamitvā evamāhaṃsu – ‘ehi kho, mahārāja, svāgataṃ te, mahārāja , sakaṃ te, mahārāja, anusāsa, mahārājā’ti. Rājā cakkavattī evamāha – ‘pāṇo na hantabbo, adinnaṃ nādātabbaṃ, kāmesumicchā na caritabbā, musā na bhāsitabbā, majjaṃ na pātabbaṃ, yathābhuttañca bhuñjathā’ti. Ye kho pana, bhikkhave, uttarāya disāya paṭirājāno, te rañño cakkavattissa anuyantā ahesuṃ.

‘‘Atha kho taṃ, bhikkhave, cakkaratanaṃ samuddapariyantaṃ pathaviṃ abhivijinitvā tameva rājadhāniṃ paccāgantvā rañño cakkavattissa antepuradvāre atthakaraṇapamukhe aḍḍakaraṇapamukhe (ka.) akkhāhataṃ maññe aṭṭhāsi rañño cakkavattissa antepuraṃ upasobhayamānaṃ.

aḍḍakaraṇapamukhe (ka.)

Dutiyādicakkavattikathā
mula_english:
Then, mendicants, the wheel-treasure, having plunged into the western ocean, emerged and turned north. And King *Cakkavattī* followed it with his fourfold army.

Now in whatever region, mendicants, the wheel-treasure paused, there the Wheel-turning Monarch took up his abode with his four-constituent army.

And those opposing kings in the northern direction came to the Wheel-turning Monarch and spoke thus: ‘Come, great king, welcome! We are yours, Your Majesty. Rule us, Your Majesty!’

The Wheel-turning Monarch spoke thus: ‘You should not kill living beings *(*prāṇo na hantabbo*)*; you should not take what has not been given *(*adinnaṃ nādātabbaṃ*)*; you should not misconduct yourselves in sensual pleasures *(*kāmesumicchā na caritabbā*)*; you should not speak falsehood *(*musā na bhāsitabbā*)*; you should not drink intoxicants *(*majjaṃ na pātabbaṃ*)*; you should eat what you are accustomed to eat *(*yathābhuttañca bhuñjathā’ti*)*.’

And those who had opposed him in the northern direction became his subjects.

Then, mendicants, the wheel-treasure, having conquered the earth to the limits of the ocean, returned to that very same capital and, I believe, stood still at the inner gate of King *Cakkavattī*, embellishing the inner chambers.

On the succeeding Wheel-turning Monarchs.

mula_pali: 88. ‘‘Dutiyopi kho, bhikkhave, rājā cakkavattī…pe… tatiyopi kho, bhikkhave, rājā cakkavattī… catutthopi kho, bhikkhave, rājā cakkavattī… pañcamopi kho, bhikkhave, rājā cakkavattī… chaṭṭhopi kho, bhikkhave, rājā cakkavattī… sattamopi kho, bhikkhave, rājā cakkavattī bahunnaṃ vassānaṃ bahunnaṃ vassasatānaṃ bahunnaṃ vassasahassānaṃ accayena aññataraṃ purisaṃ āmantesi – ‘yadā tvaṃ, ambho purisa, passeyyāsi dibbaṃ cakkaratanaṃ osakkitaṃ ṭhānā cutaṃ, atha me āroceyyāsī’ti. ‘Evaṃ, devā’ti kho, bhikkhave, so puriso rañño cakkavattissa paccassosi. Addasā kho , bhikkhave, so puriso bahunnaṃ vassānaṃ bahunnaṃ vassasatānaṃ bahunnaṃ vassasahassānaṃ accayena dibbaṃ cakkaratanaṃ osakkitaṃ ṭhānā cutaṃ. Disvāna yena rājā cakkavattī tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā rājānaṃ cakkavattiṃ etadavoca – ‘yagghe , deva, jāneyyāsi, dibbaṃ te cakkaratanaṃ osakkitaṃ ṭhānā cuta’nti?
mula_english:
"Monks, a second wheel-turning monarch, and a third, a fourth, a fifth, a sixth, and a seventh wheel-turning monarch, after the lapse of many years, many hundreds of years, many thousands of years, addressed a certain man: ‘Good man, when you see the divine wheel-jewel (cakkaratana) dislodged and fallen from its place, then inform me.’

‘Yes, your majesty (deva),’ monks, that man replied to the wheel-turning monarch.

Then, monks, after the lapse of many years, many hundreds of years, many thousands of years, that man saw the divine wheel-jewel dislodged and fallen from its place.

Having seen it, he went to the wheel-turning monarch and said this to the wheel-turning monarch: ‘Your majesty, may you know that your divine wheel-jewel is dislodged and fallen from its place.’"

mula_pali:
89. ‘‘Atha kho, bhikkhave, rājā cakkavattī jeṭṭhaputtaṃ kumāraṃ āmantāpetvā etadavoca – ‘dibbaṃ kira me, tāta kumāra, cakkaratanaṃ osakkitaṃ, ṭhānā cutaṃ, sutaṃ kho pana metaṃ – yassa rañño cakkavattissa dibbaṃ cakkaratanaṃ osakkati, ṭhānā cavati, na dāni tena raññā ciraṃ jīvitabbaṃ hotīti. Bhuttā kho pana me mānusakā kāmā, samayo dāni me dibbe kāme pariyesituṃ, ehi tvaṃ, tāta kumāra, imaṃ samuddapariyantaṃ pathaviṃ paṭipajja . Ahaṃ pana kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissāmī’ti.

‘‘Atha kho, bhikkhave, rājā cakkavattī jeṭṭhaputtaṃ kumāraṃ sādhukaṃ rajje samanusāsitvā kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbaji. Sattāhapabbajite kho pana, bhikkhave, rājisimhi dibbaṃ cakkaratanaṃ antaradhāyi.
mula_english:
"Then, monks, the wheel-turning king summoned his eldest son, the prince, and said to him: 'It seems, dear prince, that my celestial wheel-treasure has receded, has fallen from its place. I have heard that when the celestial wheel-treasure of a wheel-turning king recedes, falls from its place, the king does not have long to live. I have enjoyed human pleasures; now is the time for me to seek divine pleasures. Come, dear prince, take charge of this earth bounded by the sea. I shall shave off my hair and beard, put on the ochre robes, and go forth from the household life into homelessness.'

"Then, monks, the wheel-turning king duly instructed his eldest son, the prince, in kingship, shaved off his hair and beard, put on the ochre robes, and went forth from the household life into homelessness ( *agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajji*). And, monks, seven days after the royal sage had gone forth, the celestial wheel-treasure disappeared ( *dibbaṃ cakkaratanaṃ antaradhāyi*).
"

mula_pali:
90. ‘‘Atha kho, bhikkhave, aññataro puriso yena rājā khattiyo muddhābhisitto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā rājānaṃ khattiyaṃ muddhābhisittaṃ etadavoca – ‘yagghe, deva, jāneyyāsi, dibbaṃ cakkaratanaṃ antarahita’nti? Atha kho, bhikkhave, rājā khattiyo muddhābhisitto dibbe cakkaratane antarahite anattamano ahosi. Anattamanatañca paṭisaṃvedesi; no ca kho rājisiṃ upasaṅkamitvā ariyaṃ cakkavattivattaṃ pucchi. So samateneva sudaṃ janapadaṃ pasāsati. Tassa samatena janapadaṃ pasāsato pubbenāparaṃ janapadā na pabbanti, yathā taṃ pubbakānaṃ rājūnaṃ ariye cakkavattivatte vattamānānaṃ.

‘‘Atha kho, bhikkhave, amaccā pārisajjā gaṇakamahāmattā anīkaṭṭhā dovārikā mantassājīvino sannipatitvā rājānaṃ khattiyaṃ muddhābhisittaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘na kho te, deva, samatena (sudaṃ) janapadaṃ pasāsato pubbenāparaṃ janapadā pabbanti, yathā taṃ pubbakānaṃ rājūnaṃ ariye cakkavattivatte vattamānānaṃ. Saṃvijjanti kho te, deva, vijite amaccā pārisajjā gaṇakamahāmattā anīkaṭṭhā dovārikā mantassājīvino mayañceva aññe ca aññe ca paṇḍite samaṇabrāhmaṇe puccheyyāsi (ka.) ye mayaṃ ariyaṃ cakkavattivattaṃ dhārema. Iṅgha tvaṃ, deva, amhe ariyaṃ cakkavattivattaṃ puccha. Tassa te mayaṃ ariyaṃ cakkavattivattaṃ puṭṭhā byākarissāmā’ti.

aññe ca paṇḍite samaṇabrāhmaṇe puccheyyāsi (ka.)

Āyuvaṇṇādipariyānikathā
mula_english:
‘Then, monks, a certain man approached the anointed Kṣatriya king and said: “Sire, you should know that the divine Wheel-Treasure (*cakraratna*) has disappeared!” Then, monks, when the divine Wheel-Treasure had disappeared, the anointed Kṣatriya king was unhappy and felt regret. But he did not go to the royal sage and ask him about the duties of a noble wheel-turning monarch (*cakravartivatta*). Instead, he ruled the people according to his own ideas. And, being so ruled, the people did not prosper so well as they had done under the previous kings who had performed the duties of a noble wheel-turning monarch.

Then, monks, the ministers, counsellors, treasury officials, guards and doorkeepers, and the chanters of *mantras* came together and said to the anointed Kṣatriya king: “Sire, as long as you rule the people according to your own ideas, and differently from the way they were ruled before under previous wheel-turning monarchs, the people do not prosper so well. In your realm, sire, there still exist ministers, counsellors, treasury officials, guards and doorkeepers, and chanters of *mantras*, and also other wise *śramaṇas* and *brāhmaṇas* who remember the duties of a noble wheel-turning monarch. Please ask us, sire, about the duties of a noble wheel-turning monarch, and we will explain them to you.”

The Discourse on the Completion of Life, Beauty, etc.
commentary_pali:
90.Samatenāti attano matiyā. Sudanti nipātamattaṃ. Pasāsatīti anusāsati. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – porāṇakaṃ rājavaṃsaṃ rājapaveṇiṃ rājadhammaṃ pahāya attano matimatte ṭhatvā janapadaṃ anusāsatīti. Evamayaṃ maghadevavaṃsassa kaḷārajanako viya daḷhanemivaṃsassa upacchedako antimapuriso hutvā uppanno. Pubbenāparanti pubbakālena sadisā hutvā aparakālaṃ. Janapadā na pabbantīti na vaḍḍhanti. Yathā taṃ pubbakānanti yathā pubbakānaṃ rājūnaṃ pubbe ca pacchā ca sadisāyeva hutvā pabbiṃsu, tathā na pabbanti. Katthaci suññā honti hataviluttā, telamadhuphāṇitādīsu ceva yāgubhattādīsu ca ojāpi parihāyitthāti attho.

Amaccā pārisajjāti amaccā ceva parisāvacarā ca. Gaṇakamahāmattāti acchiddakādipāṭhagaṇakā ceva mahāamaccā ca. Anīkaṭṭhāti hatthiācariyādayo. Dovārikāti dvārarakkhino. Mantassājīvinoti mantā vuccati paññā, taṃ nissayaṃ katvā ye jīvanti paṇḍitā mahāmattā, tesaṃ etaṃ nāmaṃ.

Amaccā pārisajjā Gaṇakamahāmattā Anīkaṭṭhā Dovārikā Mantassājīvino

Āyuvaṇṇādiparihānikathāvaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
90. *Samatena* means according to one's own opinion. *Suda* means merely a particle. *Pasasati* means teaches. This is what was said: having abandoned the ancient royal lineage, the royal tradition, and the royal law, and having remained in accordance with his own opinion, he teaches the country. In this way, this one was born as the last man, the destroyer of the Daḷhanemi lineage, like a *kaḷārajanaka* of the Maghadeva lineage. *Pubbenāpara* means having been similar to the previous time, to the subsequent time. *Janapadā na pabbantī* means they do not increase. *Yathā taṃ pubbakāna* means just as those previous kings increased having been similar both before and after, thus they do not increase. Somewhere they are empty, destroyed and plundered; in oil, honey, *phāṇita*, etc., and also in *yāgubhatta*, etc., even the essence diminishes; that is the meaning.

*Amaccā pārisajjā* means ministers and attendants. *Gaṇakamahāmattā* means mathematicians who are faultless in reciting, etc., and great ministers. *Anīkaṭṭhā* means elephant trainers, etc. *Dovārikā* means doorkeepers. *Mantassājīvino* means *mantā* is said to be wisdom (prajñā), and those learned great ministers who live relying on that, this is their name.

Ministers, attendants, mathematicians and great ministers, elephant trainers, doorkeepers, those who live by wisdom. Description of the discourse on the decline of life, complexion, etc.

mula_pali:
91. ‘‘Atha kho, bhikkhave, rājā khattiyo muddhābhisitto amacce pārisajje gaṇakamahāmatte anīkaṭṭhe dovārike mantassājīvino sannipātetvā ariyaṃ cakkavattivattaṃ pucchi. Tassa te ariyaṃ cakkavattivattaṃ puṭṭhā byākariṃsu. Tesaṃ sutvā dhammikañhi kho rakkhāvaraṇaguttiṃ saṃvidahi, no ca kho adhanānaṃ dhanamanuppadāsi. Adhanānaṃ dhane ananuppadiyamāne dāliddiyaṃ vepullamagamāsi. Dāliddiye vepullaṃ gate aññataro puriso paresaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyi. Tamenaṃ aggahesuṃ. Gahetvā rañño khattiyassa muddhābhisittassa dassesuṃ – ‘ayaṃ, deva, puriso paresaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyī’ti. Evaṃ vutte, bhikkhave, rājā khattiyo muddhābhisitto taṃ purisaṃ etadavoca – ‘saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, ambho purisa, paresaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyī’ti ādiyasīti (syā.)? ‘Saccaṃ, devā’ti. ‘Kiṃ kāraṇā’ti? ‘Na hi, deva, jīvāmī’ti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, rājā khattiyo muddhābhisitto tassa purisassa dhanamanuppadāsi – ‘iminā tvaṃ, ambho purisa, dhanena attanā ca jīvāhi, mātāpitaro ca posehi, puttadārañca posehi, kammante ca payojehi, samaṇabrāhmaṇesu samaṇesu brāhmaṇesu (bahūsu) uddhaggikaṃ dakkhiṇaṃ patiṭṭhāpehi sovaggikaṃ sukhavipākaṃ saggasaṃvattanika’nti. ‘Evaṃ, devā’ti kho, bhikkhave, so puriso rañño khattiyassa muddhābhisittassa paccassosi.

‘‘Aññataropi kho, bhikkhave, puriso paresaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyi. Tamenaṃ aggahesuṃ. Gahetvā rañño khattiyassa muddhābhisittassa dassesuṃ – ‘ayaṃ, deva, puriso paresaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyī’ti. Evaṃ vutte, bhikkhave, rājā khattiyo muddhābhisitto taṃ purisaṃ etadavoca – ‘saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, ambho purisa, paresaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyī’ti? ‘Saccaṃ, devā’ti. ‘Kiṃ kāraṇā’ti? ‘Na hi, deva, jīvāmī’ti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, rājā khattiyo muddhābhisitto tassa purisassa dhanamanuppadāsi – ‘iminā tvaṃ, ambho purisa, dhanena attanā ca jīvāhi, mātāpitaro ca posehi, puttadārañca posehi, kammante ca payojehi, samaṇabrāhmaṇesu uddhaggikaṃ dakkhiṇaṃ patiṭṭhāpehi sovaggikaṃ sukhavipākaṃ saggasaṃvattanika’nti. ‘Evaṃ, devā’ti kho, bhikkhave, so puriso rañño khattiyassa muddhābhisittassa paccassosi .
mula_english:
Then, the King, the Kṣatriya, the one who had been anointed on the head, having assembled the ministers, courtiers, accountants, chief ministers, soldiers, gatekeepers, and those who lived by counsel, asked about the noble duty of a wheel-turning monarch ( *cakkavattivattaṃ*).

And being asked, they explained to him the noble duty of a wheel-turning monarch.

Having listened to them, he established righteous guard and protection, but he did not give property (*dhana*) to the needy.

From the not giving of property (*dhana*) to the needy, poverty increased greatly.

When poverty had become great, a certain man took what was not given by others, which is known as theft (*theyyasaṅkhātaṃ*).

They arrested him.

Having arrested him, they showed him to the King, the Kṣatriya, the one who had been anointed on the head, saying: "This man, O King (*deva*), took what was not given by others, which is known as theft (*theyyasaṅkhātaṃ*)."

When this had been said, the King, the Kṣatriya, the one who had been anointed on the head, said to that man: "Is it true that you, good man, took what was not given by others, which is known as theft (*theyyasaṅkhātaṃ*)?"

"It is true, Your Majesty (*deva*)," he said.

"Why?"

"Because I have nothing to live on, Your Majesty (*deva*)," he replied.

Then, the King, the Kṣatriya, the one who had been anointed on the head, gave property (*dhana*) to that man, saying: "With this property (*dhana*), good man, may you support yourself, and support your mother and father, and support your wife and children, and engage in business, and establish an excellent gift to ascetics and Brahmins, which will lead to heavenly rebirth and a pleasant result."

"As you say, Your Majesty (*deva*)," the man replied to the King, the Kṣatriya, the one who had been anointed on the head.

Again, a certain man took what was not given by others, which is known as theft (*theyyasaṅkhātaṃ*).

They arrested him.

Having arrested him, they showed him to the King, the Kṣatriya, the one who had been anointed on the head, saying: "This man, O King (*deva*), took what was not given by others, which is known as theft (*theyyasaṅkhātaṃ*)."

When this had been said, the King, the Kṣatriya, the one who had been anointed on the head, said to that man: "Is it true that you, good man, took what was not given by others, which is known as theft (*theyyasaṅkhātaṃ*)?"

"It is true, Your Majesty (*deva*)," he said.

"Why?"

"Because I have nothing to live on, Your Majesty (*deva*)," he replied.

Then, the King, the Kṣatriya, the one who had been anointed on the head, gave property (*dhana*) to that man, saying: "With this property (*dhana*), good man, may you support yourself, and support your mother and father, and support your wife and children, and engage in business, and establish an excellent gift to ascetics and Brahmins, which will lead to heavenly rebirth and a pleasant result."

"As you say, Your Majesty (*deva*)," the man replied to the King, the Kṣatriya, the one who had been anointed on the head.
commentary_pali: 91.Noca kho adhanānanti balavalobhattā pana adhanānaṃ daliddamanussānaṃ dhanaṃ nānuppadāsi. Nānuppadiyamāneti ananuppadiyamāne, ayameva vā pāṭho. Dāliddiyanti daliddabhāvo. Attanā ca jīvāhīti sayañca jīvaṃ yāpehīti attho. Uddhaggikantiādīsu uparūparibhūmīsu phaladānavasena uddhamaggamassāti uddhaggikā. Saggassa hitā tatrupapattijananatoti sovaggikā. Nibbattaṭṭhāne sukho vipāko assāti sukhavipākā. Suṭṭhu aggānaṃ dibbavaṇṇādīnaṃ dasannaṃ visesānaṃ nibbattanato saggasaṃvattanikā. Evarūpaṃ dakkhiṇaṃ dānaṃ patiṭṭhapetīti attho.
commentary_english:
91.
"But not to the propertyless" (*ca kho adhanāna*). Because, due to the strength of greed, wealth was not produced for the propertyless, the poor people.
"When not produced" (*nānuppadiyamāne*) means when not being produced, this is just the reading.
"*Dāliddiya*" means the state of poverty (*daliddabhāvo*).
"*Attanā ca jīvāhī*" means "you should maintain your life yourself" (*sayañca jīvaṃ yāpehīti attho*).
"*Uddhaggika*," etc. Among those with higher and higher levels, by way of giving fruit, *uddhaggika* is one who possesses the supreme path (*uddhamaggamassāti uddhaggikā*).
*Sovaggikā* is conducive to happiness (*sagga*) and to rebirth there (*saggassa hitā tatrupapattijananatoti sovaggikā*).
*Sukhā vipākā* is one whose result (*vipāko*) is happy (*sukho*) in the place of arising (*nibbattaṭṭhāne sukho vipāko assāti sukhavipākā*).
*Saggasaṃvattanikā* arises from the production (*nibbattanato*) of the ten distinctions (*dasannaṃ visesānaṃ*) of the best (*aggānaṃ*) divine colors (*dibbavaṇṇādīnaṃ*).
"He establishes such a gift (*dakkhiṇaṃ dānaṃ*)," is the meaning (*evarūpaṃ dakkhiṇaṃ dānaṃ patiṭṭhapetīti attho*).

mula_pali: 92. ‘‘Assosuṃ kho, bhikkhave, manussā – ‘ye kira, bho, paresaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyanti, tesaṃ rājā dhanamanuppadetī’ti. Sutvāna tesaṃ etadahosi – ‘yaṃnūna mayampi paresaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyeyyāmā’ti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, aññataro puriso paresaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyi. Tamenaṃ aggahesuṃ. Gahetvā rañño khattiyassa muddhābhisittassa dassesuṃ – ‘ayaṃ, deva, puriso paresaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyī’ti. Evaṃ vutte, bhikkhave, rājā khattiyo muddhābhisitto taṃ purisaṃ etadavoca – ‘saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, ambho purisa, paresaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyī’ti? ‘Saccaṃ, devā’ti. ‘Kiṃ kāraṇā’ti? ‘Na hi, deva, jīvāmī’ti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, rañño khattiyassa muddhābhisittassa etadahosi – ‘sace kho ahaṃ yo yo paresaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyissati, tassa tassa dhanamanuppadassāmi, evamidaṃ adinnādānaṃ pavaḍḍhissati. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ imaṃ purisaṃ sunisedhaṃ nisedheyyaṃ, mūlaghaccaṃ mūlaghacchaṃ (syā.), mūlachejja (ka.) kareyyaṃ, sīsamassa chindeyya’nti. Atha kho, bhikkhave, rājā khattiyo muddhābhisitto purise āṇāpesi – ‘tena hi, bhaṇe, imaṃ purisaṃ daḷhāya rajjuyā pacchābāhaṃ pacchābāhuṃ (syā.) gāḷhabandhanaṃ bandhitvā khuramuṇḍaṃ karitvā kharassarena paṇavena rathikāya rathikaṃ siṅghāṭakena siṅghāṭakaṃ parinetvā dakkhiṇena dvārena nikkhamitvā dakkhiṇato nagarassa sunisedhaṃ nisedhetha, mūlaghaccaṃ karotha, sīsamassa chindathā’ti. ‘Evaṃ, devā’ti kho, bhikkhave, te purisā rañño khattiyassa muddhābhisittassa paṭissutvā taṃ purisaṃ daḷhāya rajjuyā pacchābāhaṃ gāḷhabandhanaṃ bandhitvā khuramuṇḍaṃ karitvā kharassarena paṇavena rathikāya rathikaṃ siṅghāṭakena siṅghāṭakaṃ parinetvā dakkhiṇena dvārena nikkhamitvā dakkhiṇato nagarassa sunisedhaṃ nisedhesuṃ, mūlaghaccaṃ akaṃsu, sīsamassa chindiṃsu.
mula_english:
‘Monks, people heard that the king was giving property to those who took what was not given, that is, theft.’

Having heard this, they thought, ‘Suppose we also take what is not given, that is, theft.’

Then, monks, another man took what was not given, that is, theft.

They arrested him.

Having arrested him, they showed him to the anointed Kṣatriya king, saying, ‘This man, your majesty, took what was not given, that is, theft.’

When this was said, monks, the anointed Kṣatriya king said to that man, ‘Is it true that you, fellow, took what was not given, that is, theft?’ ‘It is true, your majesty.’

‘What is the reason?’ ‘Your Majesty, I have nothing to live on.’

Then, monks, the anointed Kṣatriya king thought, ‘If I give property to everyone who takes what is not given, that is, theft, then this taking of what is not given will increase.

I had better put an end to this man, finish him off once and for all, and cut off his head.’

Then, monks, the anointed Kṣatriya king commanded his men: ‘Bind this man’s arms tightly behind him with a strong rope, tie him with a tight binding, shave his head closely, lead him to the rough sound of a drum through the streets and squares, lead him out through the southern gate, and there to the south of the city put an end to him, finish him off once and for all, and cut off his head!’

‘Yes, your majesty,’ monks, those men, having promised the anointed Kṣatriya king, bound that man’s arms tightly behind him with a strong rope, tied him with a tight binding, shaved his head closely, led him to the rough sound of a drum through the streets and squares, led him out through the southern gate, and there to the south of the city they put an end to him, finished him off once and for all, and cut off his head.
commentary_pali: 92.Pavaḍḍhissatīti vaḍḍhissati bahuṃ bhavissati. Sunisedhaṃ nisedheyyanti suṭṭhu nisiddhaṃ nisedheyyaṃ. Mūlaghaccanti mūlahataṃ. Kharassarenāti pharusasaddena. Paṇavenāti vajjhabheriyā.
commentary_english: 92. pavaḍḍhissatīti means it will increase, it will become much. sunisedhaṃ nisedheyyanti means it should be well prohibited. mūlaghaccanti means struck at the root. kharassarenāti means with a harsh sound. paṇavenāti means with a war drum.

mula_pali: 93. ‘‘Assosuṃ kho, bhikkhave, manussā – ‘ye kira, bho, paresaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyanti, te rājā sunisedhaṃ nisedheti, mūlaghaccaṃ karoti, sīsāni tesaṃ chindatī’ti. Sutvāna tesaṃ etadahosi – ‘yaṃnūna mayampi tiṇhāni satthāni kārāpessāma kārāpeyyāma (syā. pī.) kārāpeyyāmāti (ka. sī.), tiṇhāni satthāni kārāpetvā yesaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyissāma, te sunisedhaṃ nisedhessāma, mūlaghaccaṃ karissāma, sīsāni tesaṃ chindissāmā’ti. Te tiṇhāni satthāni kārāpesuṃ, tiṇhāni satthāni kārāpetvā gāmaghātampi upakkamiṃsu kātuṃ, nigamaghātampi upakkamiṃsu kātuṃ, nagaraghātampi upakkamiṃsu kātuṃ, panthaduhanampi panthadūhanaṃpi (sī. syā. pī.) upakkamiṃsu kātuṃ. Yesaṃ te adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyanti, te sunisedhaṃ nisedhenti, mūlaghaccaṃ karonti, sīsāni tesaṃ chindanti.
mula_english:
"

93. Monks, humans heard: ‘Those who take what is not given, which is called theft, the king strictly punishes them, makes them uprooted, and cuts off their heads.’ Having heard this, they thought: ‘Why don't we also have sharp swords made?’, and having had sharp swords made, [they thought:] ‘From whomever we will take what is not given, which is called theft, we will strictly punish them, make them uprooted, [and] cut off their heads.’ They had sharp swords made, and having had sharp swords made, they began to commit village slaughter, they began to commit town slaughter, they began to commit city slaughter, and they began to commit highway robbery. From whomever they take what is not given, which is called theft, they strictly punish them, make them uprooted, [and] cut off their heads.

"
commentary_pali: 93.Sīsāninesaṃ chindissāmāti yesaṃ antamaso mūlakamuṭṭhimpi harissāma, tesaṃ tatheva sīsāni chindissāma, yathā koci haṭabhāvampi na jānissati, amhākaṃ dāni kimettha rājāpi evaṃ uṭṭhāya paraṃ māretīti ayaṃ nesaṃ adhippāyo. Upakkamiṃsūti ārabhiṃsu. Panthaduhananti panthaghātaṃ, panthe ṭhatvā corakammaṃ.
commentary_english:
93.
"We will cut off their heads" ( *sīsāni chindissāma* ) means: even the least of those whose radish root we would steal, we will cut off their heads in just that way, so that no one will even know what violence is. What now is the king to us here, even if he rises up and kills others? This is their intention.
"They began" (*upakkamiṃsū*) means they commenced (*ārabhiṃsu*).
"Way-robbery" (*panthaduhana*) means way-slaughter (*panthaghātaṃ*), standing on the road and doing thievery (*panthe ṭhatvā corakammaṃ*).

mula_pali:
94. ‘‘Iti kho, bhikkhave, adhanānaṃ dhane ananuppadiyamāne dāliddiyaṃ vepullamagamāsi, dāliddiye vepullaṃ gate adinnādānaṃ vepullamagamāsi, adinnādāne vepullaṃ gate satthaṃ vepullamagamāsi, satthe vepullaṃ gate pāṇātipāto vepullamagamāsi, pāṇātipāte vepullaṃ gate tesaṃ sattānaṃ āyupi parihāyi, vaṇṇopi parihāyi. Tesaṃ āyunāpi parihāyamānānaṃ vaṇṇenapi parihāyamānānaṃ asītivassasahassāyukānaṃ manussānaṃ cattārīsavassasahassāyukā puttā ahesuṃ.

‘‘Cattārīsavassasahassāyukesu, bhikkhave, manussesu aññataro puriso paresaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyi. Tamenaṃ aggahesuṃ. Gahetvā rañño khattiyassa muddhābhisittassa dassesuṃ – ‘ayaṃ, deva, puriso paresaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyī’ti. Evaṃ vutte, bhikkhave, rājā khattiyo muddhābhisitto taṃ purisaṃ etadavoca – ‘saccaṃ kira tvaṃ, ambho purisa, paresaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyī’ti? ‘Na hi, devā’ti sampajānamusā abhāsi.
mula_english:
“Thus, from the not giving of property to the needy, poverty became rife; from the growth of poverty, the taking of what was not given increased; from the increase of theft, the use of weapons increased; from the increased use of weapons, the taking of life increased—and from the increase in the taking of life, people’s life-span decreased, their beauty decreased. And as a result of this decrease of life-span and beauty, the children of those whose life-span had been eighty thousand years lived for only forty thousand.

“And a man of the generation that lived for forty thousand years took what was not given, which is called theft (*theyya-saṃkhāta*). They arrested him, and brought him before the king, a Kṣatriya (*khattiya*) who had been consecrated (*muddhābhisitta*), saying: ‘Your Majesty (*deva*), this man took what was not given, which we call theft.’ When this was said, the Kṣatriya (*khattiya*) king who had been consecrated (*muddhābhisitta*) said to that man: ‘Is it true, fellow (*ambho*), that you took what was not given, which we call theft?’ ‘No, your majesty (*deva*),’ he lied, fully aware.
commentary_pali: 94.Na hi, devāti so kira cintesi – ‘‘ayaṃ rājā saccaṃ devāti mukhapaṭiññāya dinnāya mārāpeti, handāhaṃ musāvādaṃ karomī’’ti, maraṇabhayā ‘‘na hi devā’’ti avoca.
commentary_english: 94. "No, god," so he thought, "this king, having been given a declaration with his mouth that he is truly a god, will have me killed. Come, let me speak falsely." Out of fear of death, he said, "No, god."

mula_pali:
95. ‘‘Iti kho, bhikkhave, adhanānaṃ dhane ananuppadiyamāne dāliddiyaṃ vepullamagamāsi. Dāliddiye vepullaṃ gate adinnādānaṃ vepullamagamāsi, adinnādāne vepullaṃ gate satthaṃ vepullamagamāsi. Satthe vepullaṃ gate pāṇātipāto vepullamagamāsi, pāṇātipāte vepullaṃ gate musāvādo vepullamagamāsi , musāvāde vepullaṃ gate tesaṃ sattānaṃ āyupi parihāyi, vaṇṇopi parihāyi. Tesaṃ āyunāpi parihāyamānānaṃ vaṇṇenapi parihāyamānānaṃ cattārīsavassasahassāyukānaṃ manussānaṃ vīsativassasahassāyukā puttā ahesuṃ.

‘‘Vīsativassasahassāyukesu , bhikkhave, manussesu aññataro puriso paresaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyi. Tamenaṃ aññataro puriso rañño khattiyassa muddhābhisittassa ārocesi – ‘itthannāmo, deva, puriso paresaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyī’ti pesuññamakāsi.
mula_english:
95. It is by this, monks, that when wealth is not given to the poor ( *adhanānāṃ dhane ananuppadiyamāne*), poverty (*dāliddiyaṃ*) becomes widespread (*vepullamagamāsi*).

With poverty widespread, taking what was not given (*adinnādānaṃ*) becomes widespread. With taking what was not given widespread, weapons (*sattham*) become widespread.

With weapons widespread, the taking of life (*pāṇātipāto*) becomes widespread. With the taking of life widespread, lying (*musāvādo*) becomes widespread. With lying widespread, the life-span (*āyupi*) and beauty (*vaṇṇopi*) of those beings decrease (*parihāyi*).

As their life-span and beauty decrease, the children of humans who lived for forty thousand years become those who live for twenty thousand years.

Monks, among humans who lived for twenty thousand years, a certain man took what was not given, that is, what was reckoned as theft (*paresam adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyi*).

Then, another man reported him to the king, a Kṣatriya (*khattiyassa*) who had been consecrated by sprinkling on the head (*muddhābhisittassa*), saying, "Your majesty, a man named so-and-so has taken what was not given, that is, what was reckoned as theft (*itthannāmo, deva, puriso paresaṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyī*," thus engaging in backbiting (*pesuññamakāsi*).

mula_pali:
96. ‘‘Iti kho, bhikkhave, adhanānaṃ dhane ananuppadiyamāne dāliddiyaṃ vepullamagamāsi. Dāliddiye vepullaṃ gate adinnādānaṃ vepullamagamāsi, adinnādāne vepullaṃ gate satthaṃ vepullamagamāsi, satthe vepullaṃ gate pāṇātipāto vepullamagamāsi, pāṇātipāte vepullaṃ gate musāvādo vepullamagamāsi, musāvāde vepullaṃ gate pisuṇā vācā vepullamagamāsi, pisuṇāya vācāya vepullaṃ gatāya tesaṃ sattānaṃ āyupi parihāyi, vaṇṇopi parihāyi. Tesaṃ āyunāpi parihāyamānānaṃ vaṇṇenapi parihāyamānānaṃ vīsativassasahassāyukānaṃ manussānaṃ dasavassasahassāyukā puttā ahesuṃ.

‘‘Dasavassasahassāyukesu, bhikkhave, manussesu ekidaṃ sattā vaṇṇavanto honti, ekidaṃ sattā dubbaṇṇā. Tattha ye te sattā dubbaṇṇā, te vaṇṇavante satte abhijjhāyantā paresaṃ dāresu cārittaṃ āpajjiṃsu.
mula_english:
“Thus, from the not giving of property to the needy, poverty became rife. From the growth of poverty, the taking of what was not given increased; from the increase of theft, the use of weapons increased; from the increased use of weapons, the taking of life increased; from the increase in the taking of life, lying increased; from the increase in lying, malicious speech increased; and from the increase in malicious speech, people’s life-span decreased, their beauty decreased. And as a result of this decrease of life-span and beauty, the children of those whose life-span had been twenty thousand years lived only for ten thousand.

‘And of the generation that lived for ten thousand years, some beings were beautiful, and some were ugly. And those who were ugly, being envious of those who were beautiful, committed adultery with others’ wives.
commentary_pali: 96.Ekidanti ettha idanti nipātamattaṃ, eke sattāti attho. Cārittanti micchācāraṃ. Abhijjhābyāpādāti abhijjhā ca byāpādo ca. Micchādiṭṭhīti natthi dinnantiādikā antaggāhikā paccanīkadiṭṭhi.
commentary_english: 96. "Ekida" means here "ida" is only a particle, the meaning is "some beings." "Cāritta" means wrong conduct. "Abhijjhābyāpādā" means covetousness and ill-will. "Micchādiṭṭhi" means wrong view, such as "there is no giving," etc., an extreme view, an opposing view.

mula_pali: 97. ‘‘Iti kho, bhikkhave, adhanānaṃ dhane ananuppadiyamāne dāliddiyaṃ vepullamagamāsi. Dāliddiye vepullaṃ gate…pe… kāmesumicchācāro vepullamagamāsi, kāmesumicchācāre vepullaṃ gate tesaṃ sattānaṃ āyupi parihāyi, vaṇṇopi parihāyi. Tesaṃ āyunāpi parihāyamānānaṃ vaṇṇenapi parihāyamānānaṃ dasavassasahassāyukānaṃ manussānaṃ pañcavassasahassāyukā puttā ahesuṃ.
mula_english: “Thus, monks, from the not giving of property to the needy, poverty became rife.
