As poverty grew… sexual misconduct increased, and as sexual misconduct increased, the life-span of those beings decreased, and their beauty decreased. As their life-span decreased and their beauty decreased, the children of those humans whose life-span had been ten thousand years lived for only five thousand years.

mula_pali: 98. ‘‘Pañcavassasahassāyukesu, bhikkhave , manussesu dve dhammā vepullamagamaṃsu – pharusāvācā samphappalāpo ca. Dvīsu dhammesu vepullaṃ gatesu tesaṃ sattānaṃ āyupi parihāyi, vaṇṇopi parihāyi. Tesaṃ āyunāpi parihāyamānānaṃ vaṇṇenapi parihāyamānānaṃ pañcavassasahassāyukānaṃ manussānaṃ appekacce aḍḍhateyyavassasahassāyukā, appekacce dvevassasahassāyukā puttā ahesuṃ.
mula_english: “Monks, among humans living for five thousand years, two things increased: harsh speech ( *pharusāvācā*) and idle chatter (*samphappalāpo*). When these two things increased, the life-span (*āyupi*) and beauty (*vaṇṇo*) of those beings decreased. As their life-span and beauty decreased, some of the children of those humans who lived for five thousand years lived for two and a half thousand years, and some lived for only two thousand years.

mula_pali: 99. ‘‘Aḍḍhateyyavassasahassāyukesu, bhikkhave, manussesu abhijjhābyāpādā vepullamagamaṃsu. Abhijjhābyāpādesu vepullaṃ gatesu tesaṃ sattānaṃ āyupi parihāyi, vaṇṇopi parihāyi. Tesaṃ āyunāpi parihāyamānānaṃ vaṇṇenapi parihāyamānānaṃ aḍḍhateyyavassasahassāyukānaṃ manussānaṃ vassasahassāyukā puttā ahesuṃ.
mula_english: 99. “And among humans, monks, whose life-span was two-and-a-half thousand years, covetousness (*abhijjhā*) and hatred (*byāpādā*) increased (*vepullamagamaṃsu*). When covetousness and hatred increased, the life-span (*āyupi*) and beauty (*vaṇṇopi*) of those beings decreased (*parihāyi*). And as the life-span and beauty of those beings decreased, the children of those humans whose life-span had been two-and-a-half thousand years had a life-span of one thousand years.

mula_pali: 100. ‘‘Vassasahassāyukesu, bhikkhave, manussesu micchādiṭṭhi vepullamagamāsi. Micchādiṭṭhiyā vepullaṃ gatāya tesaṃ sattānaṃ āyupi parihāyi, vaṇṇopi parihāyi. Tesaṃ āyunāpi parihāyamānānaṃ vaṇṇenapi parihāyamānānaṃ vassasahassāyukānaṃ manussānaṃ pañcavassasatāyukā puttā ahesuṃ.
mula_english: 100. "Among humans whose life-span was a thousand years, bhikkhus, false views ( *micchādiṭṭhi*) increased (*vepullamagamāsi*). As false views (*micchādiṭṭhiyā*) increased (*vepullaṃ gatāya*), the life (*āyupi*) of those beings (*tesaṃ sattānaṃ*) declined (*parihāyi*), and their beauty (*vaṇṇopi*) also declined (*parihāyi*). As their life (*āyunāpi*) was declining (*parihāyamānānaṃ*) and their beauty (*vaṇṇenapi*) was declining (*parihāyamānānaṃ*), the children (*puttā ahesuṃ*) of those humans (*manussānaṃ*) whose life-span was a thousand years (*vassasahassāyukānaṃ*) lived for five hundred years (*pañcavassasatāyukā*).

mula_pali:
101. ‘‘Pañcavassasatāyukesu, bhikkhave, manussesu tayo dhammā vepullamagamaṃsu. Adhammarāgo visamalobho micchādhammo. Tīsu dhammesu vepullaṃ gatesu tesaṃ sattānaṃ āyupi parihāyi, vaṇṇopi parihāyi. Tesaṃ āyunāpi parihāyamānānaṃ vaṇṇenapi parihāyamānānaṃ pañcavassasatāyukānaṃ manussānaṃ appekacce aḍḍhateyyavassasatāyukā, appekacce dvevassasatāyukā puttā ahesuṃ.

‘‘Aḍḍhateyyavassasatāyukesu, bhikkhave , manussesu ime dhammā vepullamagamaṃsu. Amatteyyatā apetteyyatā asāmaññatā abrahmaññatā na kule jeṭṭhāpacāyitā.
mula_english:
101. "Among the generation whose life-span was five hundred years, *bhikkhus*, three things increased: incestuous passion (*adhammarāga*), excessive greed (*visamalobha*), and wrong practice (*micchādhammo*).

When these three things increased, the life-span (*āyupi*) of those beings decreased, and their beauty (*vaṇṇopi*) decreased.

And as the life-span and beauty of those humans with a five-hundred-year life-span declined, some had children who lived for two hundred and fifty years (*aḍḍhateyyavassasatāyukā*), and some had children who lived for only two hundred years (*dvevassasatāyukā*).

"Among the generation whose life-span was two hundred and fifty years, *bhikkhus*, these things increased: lack of respect for mother (*amatteyyatā*), lack of respect for father (*apetteyyatā*), lack of respect for ascetics (*asāmaññatā*), lack of respect for Brahmins (*abrahmaññatā*), and lack of respect for the head of the clan (*na kule jeṭṭhāpacāyitā*).
commentary_pali:
101.Adhammarāgoti mātā mātucchā pitucchā mātulānītiādike ayuttaṭṭhāne rāgo. Visamalobhoti paribhogayuttesupi ṭhānesu atibalavalobho. Micchādhammoti purisānaṃ purisesu itthīnañca itthīsu chandarāgo.

Amatteyyatātiādīsu mātu hito matteyyo, tassa bhāvo matteyyatā, mātari sammā paṭipattiyā etaṃ nāmaṃ. Tassā abhāvo ceva tappaṭipakkhatā ca amatteyyatā. Apetteyyatādīsupi eseva nayo. Na kule jeṭṭhāpacāyitāti kule jeṭṭhānaṃ apacitiyā nīcavuttiyā akaraṇabhāvo.

Amatteyyatā Apetteyyatā Na kule jeṭṭhāpacāyitā

Dasavassāyukasamayavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
101.
*Adhammarāgo*: "Improper lust" is desire ( *rāga*) in inappropriate situations, such as with one's mother ( *mātā*), maternal aunt ( *mātucchā*), paternal aunt ( *pitucchā*), or maternal uncle's wife ( *mātulānī*), etc.
*Visamalobho*: "Excessive greed" is extreme ( *atibalava*) greed ( *lobho*) even in situations where enjoyment ( *paribhoga*) is appropriate ( *yuttesu*).
*Micchādhammo*: "Wrongeous behavior" is desire and lust (*chandarāgo*) of men (*purisānaṃ*) for men (*purisesu*), and of women (*itthīnaṃ*) for women (*itthīsu*).

*Amatteyyatā*: "Ingratitude to mother", *matteyyo* is one who is kind to his mother, *mātu hito*, his state (*bhāvo*) is *matteyyatā*, this designation is due to proper conduct (*sammā paṭipattiyā*) towards one's mother (*mātari*).
*Amatteyyatā* is the absence (*abhāvo*) of that, and indeed its opposite (*tappaṭipakkhatā*).
*Apetteyyatā*: "Ingratitude to father", this same method applies.
*Na kule jeṭṭhāpacāyitā*: "Not revering elders in the family" is the state (*bhāvo*) of not showing honor (*apacitiyā*) and behaving humbly (*nīcavuttiyā*) towards the elders (*jeṭṭhānam*) in the family (*kule*).

*Amatteyyatā*
*Apetteyyatā*
*Na kule jeṭṭhāpacāyitā* Description of the time of the ten-year life span.

mula_pali:
102. ‘‘Iti kho, bhikkhave, adhanānaṃ dhane ananuppadiyamāne dāliddiyaṃ vepullamagamāsi. Dāliddiye vepullaṃ gate adinnādānaṃ vepullamagamāsi. Adinnādāne vepullaṃ gate satthaṃ vepullamagamāsi. Satthe vepullaṃ gate pāṇātipāto vepullamagamāsi. Pāṇātipāte vepullaṃ gate musāvādo vepullamagamāsi. Musāvāde vepullaṃ gate pisuṇā vācā vepullamagamāsi. Pisuṇāya vācāya vepullaṃ gatāya kāmesumicchācāro vepullamagamāsi. Kāmesumicchācāre vepullaṃ gate dve dhammā vepullamagamaṃsu, pharusā vācā samphappalāpo ca. Dvīsu dhammesu vepullaṃ gatesu abhijjhābyāpādā vepullamagamaṃsu. Abhijjhābyāpādesu vepullaṃ gatesu micchādiṭṭhi vepullamagamāsi. Micchādiṭṭhiyā vepullaṃ gatāya tayo dhammā vepullamagamaṃsu, adhammarāgo visamalobho micchādhammo. Tīsu dhammesu vepullaṃ gatesu ime dhammā vepullamagamaṃsu, amatteyyatā apetteyyatā asāmaññatā abrahmaññatā na kule jeṭṭhāpacāyitā. Imesu dhammesu vepullaṃ gatesu tesaṃ sattānaṃ āyupi parihāyi, vaṇṇopi parihāyi. Tesaṃ āyunāpi parihāyamānānaṃ vaṇṇenapi parihāyamānānaṃ aḍḍhateyyavassasatāyukānaṃ manussānaṃ vassasatāyukā puttā ahesuṃ.

Dasavassāyukasamayo
mula_english:
‘Thus, from the not giving of property to the needy, poverty became rife. From the growth of poverty, the taking of what was not given increased. From the increase of theft, the use of weapons increased. From the increased use of weapons, the taking of life increased. From the increase in the taking of life, lying increased. From the increase in lying, the speaking evil of others increased. From the increase in speaking evil of others, sexual misconduct increased. From the increase in sexual misconduct, two things increased: harsh speech and idle chatter. As these two things increased, covetousness and ill-will increased. As covetousness and ill-will increased, wrong view increased. As wrong view increased, three things increased: unrighteous attachment, irregular greed, and false dharma. As these three things increased, these things increased: lack of respect for mother, lack of respect for father, lack of respect for ascetics, lack of respect for Brahmins, and failure to honor the elders in the family. As these things increased, people’s life-span decreased, their beauty decreased. And the children of those whose life-span had been two-and-a-half centuries lived for only a hundred years.

The Era of Ten-Year Lifespans

mula_pali:
103. ‘‘Bhavissati , bhikkhave, so samayo, yaṃ imesaṃ manussānaṃ dasavassāyukā puttā bhavissanti. Dasavassāyukesu, bhikkhave, manussesu pañcavassikā pañcamāsikā (ka. sī.) kumārikā alaṃpateyyā bhavissanti. Dasavassāyukesu, bhikkhave, manussesu imāni rasāni antaradhāyissanti, seyyathidaṃ, sappi navanītaṃ telaṃ madhu phāṇitaṃ loṇaṃ. Dasavassāyukesu, bhikkhave, manussesu kudrūsako aggaṃ bhojanānaṃ aggabhojanaṃ (syā.) bhavissati. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, etarahi sālimaṃsodano aggaṃ bhojanānaṃ; evameva kho, bhikkhave, dasavassāyukesu manussesu kudrūsako aggaṃ bhojanānaṃ bhavissati.

‘‘Dasavassāyukesu, bhikkhave, manussesu dasa kusalakammapathā sabbena sabbaṃ antaradhāyissanti, dasa akusalakammapathā atibyādippissanti ativiya dippissanti (syā. pī.), ativyādippissanti (sī.). Dasavassāyukesu , bhikkhave, manussesu kusalantipi na bhavissati, kuto pana kusalassa kārako. Dasavassāyukesu, bhikkhave, manussesu ye te bhavissanti amatteyyā apetteyyā asāmaññā abrahmaññā na kule jeṭṭhāpacāyino, te pujjā ca bhavissanti pāsaṃsā ca. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, etarahi matteyyā petteyyā sāmaññā brahmaññā kule jeṭṭhāpacāyino pujjā ca pāsaṃsā ca; evameva kho, bhikkhave, dasavassāyukesu manussesu ye te bhavissanti amatteyyā apetteyyā asāmaññā abrahmaññā na kule jeṭṭhāpacāyino, te pujjā ca bhavissanti pāsaṃsā ca.

ativiya dippissanti (syā. pī.), ativyādippissanti (sī.)

‘‘Dasavassāyukesu , bhikkhave, manussesu na bhavissati mātāti vā mātucchāti vā mātulānīti vā ācariyabhariyāti vā garūnaṃ dārāti vā. Sambhedaṃ loko gamissati yathā ajeḷakā kukkuṭasūkarā soṇasiṅgālā soṇasigālā (sī. pī.).

soṇasigālā (sī. pī.)

‘‘Dasavassāyukesu, bhikkhave, manussesu tesaṃ sattānaṃ aññamaññamhi tibbo āghāto paccupaṭṭhito bhavissati tibbo byāpādo tibbo manopadoso tibbaṃ vadhakacittaṃ. Mātupi puttamhi puttassapi mātari; pitupi puttamhi puttassapi pitari; bhātupi bhaginiyā bhaginiyāpi bhātari tibbo āghāto paccupaṭṭhito bhavissati tibbo byāpādo tibbo manopadoso tibbaṃ vadhakacittaṃ. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, māgavikassa migaṃ disvā tibbo āghāto paccupaṭṭhito hoti tibbo byāpādo tibbo manopadoso tibbaṃ vadhakacittaṃ; evameva kho, bhikkhave, dasavassāyukesu manussesu tesaṃ sattānaṃ aññamaññamhi tibbo āghāto paccupaṭṭhito bhavissati tibbo byāpādo tibbo manopadoso tibbaṃ vadhakacittaṃ. Mātupi puttamhi puttassapi mātari; pitupi puttamhi puttassapi pitari; bhātupi bhaginiyā bhaginiyāpi bhātari tibbo āghāto paccupaṭṭhito bhavissati tibbo byāpādo tibbo manopadoso tibbaṃ vadhakacittaṃ.
mula_english:
103. “Monks, a time will come when the children of these people will have a life-span of ten years. And with them, girls will be marriageable at five years old. And with them, these flavours will disappear: ghee ( *sarpi*), butter (*navanītaṃ*), sesame-oil (*tailaṃ*), honey (*madhu*) , molasses (*phāṇitaṃ*) and salt (*loṇaṃ*). Among them, *kudrusa*-grain will be the chief food, just as rice and curry are today.

“Monks, for those of a ten-year life-span the ten wholesome courses of action will entirely disappear, and the ten unwholesome courses of action will become exceedingly apparent. For those of a ten-year life­span there will be no word for “moral” ( *kusala*), so how can there be anyone who acts in a moral way? For those of a ten-year life-span, those people who have no respect for mother (*amatteyyā*) or father (*apetteyyā*), for ascetics (*asāmaññā*) and Brahmins (*abrahmaññā*), for the head of the clan, will be the ones who enjoy honour and prestige. Just as it is now the people who show respect for mother and father, for ascetics and Brahmins, for the head of the clan, who are praised and honoured, so it will be with those who do the opposite.

“Monks, for those of a ten-year life-span no account will be taken of mother (*mātā*) or aunt (*mātucchā*), of mother’s sister-in-law (*mātulānī*) , of teacher’s wife (*ācariyabhariyā*) or of one’s father’s wives (*garūnaṃ dārāti*) and so on. all will be promiscuous in the world like goats and sheep, fowl and pigs, dogs and jackals.

“Monks, among those of a ten-year life-span, fierce enmity will prevail one for another, fierce hatred (*āghāta*), fierce anger (*byāpāda*) and thoughts of killing (*vadhakacittaṃ*). Mother against child and child against mother, father against child and child against father, brother against brother, brother against sister, fierce enmity will prevail. Just as the hunter feels hatred for the beast he stalks, so it will be among those of a ten-year life-span. Mother against child and child against mother, father against child and child against father, brother against brother, brother against sister, fierce enmity will prevail.
0073
commentary_pali:
103.Yaṃ imesanti yasmiṃ samaye imesaṃ. Alaṃpateyyāti patino dātuṃ yuttā. Imāni rasānīti imāni loke aggarasāni. Atibyādippissantīti ativiya dippissanti, ayameva vā pāṭho. Kusalantipi na bhavissatīti kusalanti nāmampi na bhavissati, paññattimattampi na paññāyissatīti attho. Pujjā ca bhavissanti pāsaṃsā cāti pūjārahā ca bhavissanti pasaṃsārahā ca. Tadā kira manussā ‘‘asukena nāma mātā pahatā, pitā pahato, samaṇabrāhmaṇā jīvitā voropitā, kule jeṭṭhānaṃ atthibhāvampi na jānāti, aho puriso’’ti tameva pūjessanti ceva pasaṃsissanti ca.

Nabhavissati mātāti vāti ayaṃ mayhaṃ mātāti garucittaṃ na bhavissati. Gehe mātugāmaṃ viya nānāvidhaṃ asabbhikathaṃ kathayamānā agāravupacārena upasaṅkamissanti. Mātucchādīsupi eseva nayo. Ettha ca mātucchāti mātubhaginī. Mātulānīti mātulabhariyā. Ācariyabhariyāti sippāyatanāni sikkhāpakassa ācariyassa bhariyā. Garūnaṃ dārāti cūḷapitumahāpituādīnaṃ bhariyā. Sambhedanti missībhāvaṃ, mariyādabhedaṃ vā.

Na bhavissati mātāti vā Mātucchā mātucchā Mātulānī Ācariyabhariyā Garūnaṃ dārā Sambheda

Tibbo āghāto paccupaṭṭhito bhavissatīti balavakopo punappunaṃ uppattivasena paccupaṭṭhito bhavissati. Aparāni dve etasseva vevacanāni. Kopo hi cittaṃ āghātetīti āghāto. Attano ca parassa ca hitasukhaṃ byāpādetīti byāpādo. Manopadūsanato manopadosoti vuccati. Tibbaṃ vadhakacittanti piyamānassāpi paraṃ māraṇatthāya vadhakacittaṃ. Tassa vatthuṃ dassetuṃ mātupi puttamhītiādi vuttaṃ. Māgavikassāti migaluddakassa.

Tibbo āghāto paccupaṭṭhito bhavissatī āghāto. byāpādo. manopadoso Tibbaṃ vadhakacitta mātupi puttamhī Māgavikassā
commentary_english:
103. " *yaṃ imesa*nti" means *yasmiṃ samaye imesaṃ*, [that is,] at which time, of these.

"*alaṃpateyyā*ti" means *patino dātuṃ yuttā*, [that is,] fit to be given to the husband.

"*imāni rasānī*ti" means *imāni loke aggarasāni*, [that is,] these are the best tastes in the world.

"*atibyādippissantī*ti" means *ativiya dippissanti*, [that is,] they will shine exceedingly; or this very reading [is correct].

"*kusalantipi na bhavissatī*ti" means *kusalanti nāmampi na bhavissati, paññattimattampi na paññāyissatīti attho*, [that is,] there will not even be the name "skillful," let alone any designation; this is the meaning.

"*pujjā ca bhavissanti pāsaṃsā cā*ti" means *pūjārahā ca bhavissanti pasaṃsārahā ca*, [that is,] they will be worthy of worship and worthy of praise.

Then, it seems, people [will say,] "This so-and-so has struck his mother, struck his father, deprived ascetics and Brahmins of life, does not even know the existence of elders in his family; oh, what a man!" Thus they will worship and praise him.

Nay, "*bhavissati mātāti vā*ti" means *ayaṃ mayhaṃ mātāti garucittaṃ na bhavissati*, [that is,] there will not be the serious thought, "This is my mother."

In the house, resembling a women’s village, speaking various kinds of improper speech, they will approach without respect or courtesy.

"*mātucchā*dīsupi eseva nayo" means this is the same method with regard to maternal aunts, etc.

And here, "*mātucchā*ti" means *mātubhaginī*, [that is,] mother's sister.

"*mātulānī*ti" means *mātulabhariyā*, [that is,] maternal uncle’s wife.

"*ācariyabhariyā*ti" means *sippāyatanāni sikkhāpakassa ācariyassa bhariyā*, [that is,] the wife of the teacher of skills and crafts.

"*garūnaṃ dārā*ti" means *cūḷapitumahāpituādīnaṃ bhariyā*, [that is,] the wives of paternal great-grandfathers and grandfathers, and so forth.

"*sambheda*nti" means *missībhāvaṃ, mariyādabhedaṃ vā*, [that is,] mixture, or transgression of boundaries.

Nay, "*bhavissati mātāti vā*" [means] maternal aunt, maternal aunt, maternal uncle’s wife, teacher’s wife, wives of elders, mixture.

"*tibbo āghāto paccupaṭṭhito bhavissatī*ti" means *balavakopo punappunaṃ uppattivasena paccupaṭṭhito bhavissati*, [that is,] a strong anger will repeatedly arise and be present.

The other two are synonyms for this very thing.

*Kopo hi cittaṃ āghātetīti āghāto*: because anger strikes the mind, [it is called] *āghāta*.

*Attano ca parassa ca hitasukhaṃ byāpādetīti byāpādo*: because it destroys the welfare and happiness of oneself and others, [it is called] *byāpāda*.

*Manopadūsanato manopadoso*ti *vuccati*: because it corrupts the mind, it is called *manopadosa*.

"*tibbaṃ vadhakacitta*nti" means *piyamānassāpi paraṃ māraṇatthāya vadhakacittaṃ*, [that is,] even to someone dear, a murderous thought for the purpose of killing.

To show its object, it was said, "*mātupi puttamhī*tiādi vuttaṃ*, [that is] even in a mother towards her son, and so forth.

"*māgavikassā*ti" means *migaluddakassa*, [that is,] a hunter of deer.

Severe striking; striking.

Malice.

Corruption of the mind; severe murderous intent; even in a mother towards her son; of a hunter.

mula_pali:
104. ‘‘Dasavassāyukesu, bhikkhave, manussesu sattāhaṃ satthantarakappo bhavissati. Te aññamaññamhi migasaññaṃ paṭilabhissanti. Tesaṃ tiṇhāni satthāni hatthesu pātubhavissanti. Te tiṇhena satthena ‘esa migo esa migo’ti aññamaññaṃ jīvitā voropessanti.

‘‘Atha kho tesaṃ, bhikkhave, sattānaṃ ekaccānaṃ evaṃ bhavissati – ‘mā ca mayaṃ kañci kiñci (ka.), mā ca amhe koci, yaṃnūna mayaṃ tiṇagahanaṃ vā vanagahanaṃ vā rukkhagahanaṃ vā nadīviduggaṃ vā pabbatavisamaṃ vā pavisitvā vanamūlaphalāhārā yāpeyyāmā’ti. Te tiṇagahanaṃ vā vanagahanaṃ vā rukkhagahanaṃ vā nadīviduggaṃ vā pabbatavisamaṃ vā te tiṇagahanaṃ vanagahanaṃ rukkhagahanaṃ nadīviduggaṃ pabbatavisamaṃ (sī. pī.) pavisitvā sattāhaṃ vanamūlaphalāhārā yāpessanti. Te tassa sattāhassa accayena tiṇagahanā vanagahanā rukkhagahanā nadīviduggā pabbatavisamā nikkhamitvā aññamaññaṃ āliṅgitvā sabhāgāyissanti samassāsissanti – ‘diṭṭhā, bho, sattā jīvasi, diṭṭhā, bho, sattā jīvasī’ti.

kiñci (ka.) te tiṇagahanaṃ vanagahanaṃ rukkhagahanaṃ nadīviduggaṃ pabbatavisamaṃ (sī. pī.)

Āyuvaṇṇādivaḍḍhanakathā
mula_english:
104. Monks, for humans with a lifespan of ten years, there will be a "sword-interval" ( *satthantarakappa*) of seven days. They will perceive each other as wild beasts. Sharp swords (*satthāni*) will appear in their hands. Thinking, "There is a wild beast! There is a wild beast!" they will take each other’s lives with sharp swords (*tiṇhena satthena*).

Then, monks, some beings will think: “Let us not kill anyone, and let no one kill us! Let us go into a grassy thicket (*tiṇagahanaṃ*), a forest thicket (*vanagahanaṃ*), a tree thicket (*rukkhagahanaṃ*), a river ravine (*nadīviduggaṃ*), or an uneven mountain (*pabbatavisamaṃ*), and live on forest roots and fruits (*vanamūlaphalāhārā*)!”

They will enter a grassy thicket (*tiṇagahanaṃ*), a forest thicket (*vanagahanaṃ*), a tree thicket (*rukkhagahanaṃ*), a river ravine (*nadīviduggaṃ*), or an uneven mountain (*pabbatavisamaṃ*), and subsist on forest roots and fruits (*vanamūlaphalāhārā*) for seven days. After those seven days, they will emerge from the grassy thickets (*tiṇagahanā*), forest thickets (*vanagahanā*), tree thickets (*rukkhagahanā*), river ravines (*nadīviduggā*) and uneven mountains (*pabbatavisamā*), and embracing each other, they will rejoice together, comforting each other, saying: "Good beings, I see that you are alive! Good beings, I see that you are alive!"

A discourse on the increase of life and complexion (*āyuvaṇṇādivaḍḍhanakathā*).
commentary_pali:
104.Satthantarakappoti satthena antarakappo. Saṃvaṭṭakappaṃ appatvā antarāva lokavināso. Antarakappo ca nāmesa dubbhikkhantarakappo rogantarakappo satthantarakappoti tividho. Tattha lobhussadāya pajāya dubbhikkhantarakappo hoti. Mohussadāya rogantarakappo. Dosussadāya satthantarakappo. Tattha dubbhikkhantarakappena naṭṭhā yebhuyyena pettivisaye upapajjanti. Kasmā? Āhāranikantiyā balavattā. Rogantarakappena naṭṭhā yebhuyyena sagge nibbattanti kasmā? Tesañhi ‘‘aho vataññesaṃ sattānaṃ evarūpo rogo na bhaveyyā’’ti mettacittaṃ uppajjatīti. Satthantarakappena naṭṭhā yebhuyyena niraye upapajjanti. Kasmā? Aññamaññaṃ balavāghātatāya.

Migasaññanti ‘‘ayaṃ migo, ayaṃ migo’’ti saññaṃ. Tiṇhāni satthāni hatthesu pātubhavissantīti tesaṃ kira hatthena phuṭṭhamattaṃ yaṃkiñci antamaso tiṇapaṇṇaṃ upādāya āvudhameva bhavissati. Mā ca mayaṃ kañcīti mayaṃ kañci ekapurisampi jīvitā mā voropayimha. Mā ca amhe kocīti amhepi koci ekapuriso jīvitā mā voropayittha. Yaṃnūna mayanti ayaṃ lokavināso paccupaṭṭhito, na sakkā dvīhi ekaṭṭhāne ṭhitehi jīvitaṃ laddhunti maññamānā evaṃ cintayiṃsu. Vanagahananti vanasaṅkhātehi tiṇagumbalatādīhi gahanaṃ duppavesaṭṭhānaṃ. Rukkhagahananti rukkhehi gahanaṃ duppavesaṭṭhānaṃ. Nadīvidugganti nadīnaṃ antaradīpādīsu duggamanaṭṭhānaṃ. Pabbatavisamanti pabbatehi visamaṃ, pabbatesupi vā visamaṭṭhānaṃ. Sabhāgāyissantīti yathā ahaṃ jīvāmi diṭṭhā bho sattā, tvampi tathā jīvasīti evaṃ sammodanakathāya attanā sabhāge karissanti.

Migasañña Tiṇhāni satthāni hatthesu pātubhavissantī Mā ca mayaṃ kañcī Mā ca amhe kocī Yaṃnūna maya Vanagahana Rukkhagahana Nadīvidugga Pabbatavisama Sabhāgāyissantī

Āyuvaṇṇādivaḍḍhanakathāvaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
104. *Satthantarakappo* means *antarakappa* with weapons. Before reaching the *saṃvaṭṭakappa*, there is destruction of the world in between. And that *antarakappa* is threefold, namely, *dubbikkhantarakappa* (famine *antarakappa*), *rogantarakappa* (disease *antarakappa*), and *satthantarakappa* (weapon *antarakappa*). There, the *dubbikkhantarakappa* happens to a population with an excess of greed. The *rogantarakappa* [happens] with an excess of delusion. The *satthantarakappa* [happens] with an excess of hatred. There, those destroyed by the *dubbikkhantarakappa* mostly arise in the realm of the departed. Why? Because of the strength of [their] attachment to food. Those destroyed by the *rogantarakappa* are mostly reborn in heaven. Why? Because for them, a mind of loving-kindness arises, thinking, "Oh, may such a disease not happen to other sentient beings!" Those destroyed by the *satthantarakappa* mostly arise in hell. Why? Because of violently striking each other.

*Migasañña* means the perception, "This is a deer, this is a deer."

*Tiṇhāni satthāni hatthesu pātubhavissantī* means, it seems, whatever is touched by their hand, even just grass or a leaf, will become a weapon.

*Mā ca mayaṃ kañcī* means, may we not deprive anyone, even a single person, of life.

*Mā ca amhe kocī* means, may no one deprive us, even a single person, of life.

*Yaṃnūna maya*—"This destruction of the world is imminent; it is not possible to obtain life by staying in one place by twos"—thinking thus, they considered.

*Vanagahana* means a difficult-to-enter place dense with grass, bushes, vines, etc., known as forest.

*Rukkhagahana* means a difficult-to-enter place dense with trees.

*Nadīvidugga* means a difficult-to-reach place in the midst of rivers, such as islands.

*Pabbatavisama* means uneven with mountains, or even an uneven place among mountains.

*Sabhāgāyissantī* means, "As I live, O beings seen! May you also live thus!" Thus, with a speech of rejoicing, they will make [others] share in their [life].

*Migasañña tiṇhāni satthāni hatthesu pātubhavissantī mā ca mayaṃ kañcī mā ca amhe kocī yaṃnūna maya vanagahana rukkhagahana nadīvidugga pabbatavisama sabhāgāyissantī*

Description of the Discourse on Increasing Life, Beauty, etc.

mula_pali:
105. ‘‘Atha kho tesaṃ, bhikkhave, sattānaṃ evaṃ bhavissati – ‘mayaṃ kho akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ samādānahetu evarūpaṃ āyataṃ ñātikkhayaṃ pattā. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ kusalaṃ kareyyāma. Kiṃ kusalaṃ kareyyāma? Yaṃnūna mayaṃ pāṇātipātā virameyyāma, idaṃ kusalaṃ dhammaṃ samādāya vatteyyāmā’ti. Te pāṇātipātā viramissanti, idaṃ kusalaṃ dhammaṃ samādāya vattissanti. Te kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ samādānahetu āyunāpi vaḍḍhissanti, vaṇṇenapi vaḍḍhissanti . Tesaṃ āyunāpi vaḍḍhamānānaṃ vaṇṇenapi vaḍḍhamānānaṃ dasavassāyukānaṃ manussānaṃ vīsativassāyukā puttā bhavissanti.

‘‘Atha kho tesaṃ, bhikkhave, sattānaṃ evaṃ bhavissati – ‘mayaṃ kho kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ samādānahetu āyunāpi vaḍḍhāma, vaṇṇenapi vaḍḍhāma. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ bhiyyosomattāya kusalaṃ kareyyāma. Kiṃ kusalaṃ kareyyāma? Yaṃnūna mayaṃ adinnādānā virameyyāma… kāmesumicchācārā virameyyāma… musāvādā virameyyāma… pisuṇāya vācāya virameyyāma… pharusāya vācāya virameyyāma… samphappalāpā virameyyāma… abhijjhaṃ pajaheyyāma… byāpādaṃ pajaheyyāma… micchādiṭṭhiṃ pajaheyyāma… tayo dhamme pajaheyyāma – adhammarāgaṃ visamalobhaṃ micchādhammaṃ… yaṃnūna mayaṃ matteyyā assāma petteyyā sāmaññā brahmaññā kule jeṭṭhāpacāyino, idaṃ kusalaṃ dhammaṃ samādāya vatteyyāmā’ti. Te matteyyā bhavissanti petteyyā sāmaññā brahmaññā kule jeṭṭhāpacāyino, idaṃ kusalaṃ dhammaṃ samādāya vattissanti.

‘‘Te kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ samādānahetu āyunāpi vaḍḍhissanti, vaṇṇenapi vaḍḍhissanti. Tesaṃ āyunāpi vaḍḍhamānānaṃ vaṇṇenapi vaḍḍhamānānaṃ vīsativassāyukānaṃ manussānaṃ cattārīsavassāyukā puttā bhavissanti… cattārīsavassāyukānaṃ manussānaṃ asītivassāyukā puttā bhavissanti… asītivassāyukānaṃ manussānaṃ saṭṭhivassasatāyukā puttā bhavissanti… saṭṭhivassasatāyukānaṃ manussānaṃ vīsatitivassasatāyukā puttā bhavissanti… vīsatitivassasatāyukānaṃ manussānaṃ cattārīsachabbassasatāyukā puttā bhavissanti. Cattārīsachabbassasatāyukānaṃ manussānaṃ dvevassasahassāyukā puttā bhavissanti… dvevassasahassāyukānaṃ manussānaṃ cattārivassasahassāyukā puttā bhavissanti… cattārivassasahassāyukānaṃ manussānaṃ aṭṭhavassasahassāyukā puttā bhavissanti… aṭṭhavassasahassāyukānaṃ manussānaṃ vīsativassasahassāyukā puttā bhavissanti… vīsativassasahassāyukānaṃ manussānaṃ cattārīsavassasahassāyukā puttā bhavissanti… cattārīsavassasahassāyukānaṃ manussānaṃ asītivassasahassāyukā puttā bhavissanti… asītivassasahassāyukesu, bhikkhave, manussesu pañcavassasatikā kumārikā alaṃpateyyā bhavissanti.

Saṅkharājauppatti
mula_english:
105. “And then the thought will occur to those beings: “It is only because we became addicted to unwholesome practices (*akuśalā dharmā*) that we suffered this great loss of our kindred. So let us now do good! What good should we do? Let us abstain from the taking of life- that will be a good practice (*kuśalā dharmā*).” And so they will abstain from the taking of life, and, having undertaken this good thing, will practise it. And so, as a result of undertaking wholesome practices (*kuśalā dharmā*), they will increase in lifespan and beauty. And the children of those whose life-span was ten years will live for twenty years.

“And then the thought will occur to those beings: “It is only because we have undertaken wholesome practices (*kuśalā dharmā*) that we are increasing in lifespan and beauty. So let us perform still more wholesome practices (*kuśalaṃ kareyyāma*). What good should we do? Let us refrain from taking what is not given, from sexual misconduct, from lying speech, from slander, from harsh speech, from idle chatter, from covetousness, from ill-will, from wrong views; let us abstain from three things: incest, excessive greed, and deviant practices; let us respect our mothers and fathers, ascetics and Brahmins, and the head of the clan, and let us persevere in these wholesome actions (*kuśalā dharmā*).” And so they will respect their mothers and fathers, ascetics (*śramaṇa*) and Brahmins (*brāhmaṇa*), and the head of the clan, and they will persevere in these wholesome actions (*kuśalā dharmā*).

And so, as a result of undertaking these wholesome practices (*kuśalā dharmā*), they will increase in lifespan and beauty. The children of those whose life-span is twenty years will live to be forty, their children will live to be eighty, their children to be a hundred and sixty, their children to be three hundred and twenty, their children to be six hundred and forty; the children of those whose life-span is six hundred and forty years will live for two thousand years, their children for four thousand, their children for eight thousand, and their children for twenty thousand. The children of those whose life-span is twenty thousand years will live to be forty thousand, and their children will attain to eighty thousand years. Among the people with an eighty thousand-year life­span, girls will become marriageable at five hundred.

The Genesis of the World.
commentary_pali:
105.Āyatanti mahantaṃ. Pāṇātipātā virameyyāmāti pāṇātipātato osakkeyyāma. Pāṇātipātaṃ virameyyāmātipi sajjhāyanti, tattha pāṇātipātaṃ pajaheyyāmāti attho. Vīsativassāyukāti mātāpitaro pāṇātipātā paṭiviratā, puttā kasmā vīsativassāyukā ahesunti khettavisuddhiyā. Tesañhi mātāpitaro sīlavanto jātā. Iti sīlagabbhe vaḍḍhitattā imāya khettavisuddhiyā dīghāyukā ahesuṃ. Ye panettha kālaṃ katvā tattheva nibbattā, te attanova sīlasampattiyā dīghāyukā ahesuṃ.

Assāmāti bhaveyyāma. Cattārīsavassāyukātiādayo koṭṭhāsā adinnādānādīhi paṭiviratānaṃ vasena veditabbā.

Assāmā Cattārīsavassāyukā

Saṅkharājauppattivaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
105. "Extended" means large (*mahantam*).

"May we abstain from killing (*pāṇātipātā virameyyāmā*)" means we should avoid and turn away from killing.

They recite, "May I abstain from killing (*pāṇātipātaṃ virameyyāmāti*)"; there, the meaning is "I would abandon killing (*pāṇātipātaṃ pajaheyyāmāti*)."

"Having a life of twenty years (*vīsativassāyukā*)" means the mothers and fathers, abstaining from killing (*pāṇātipātā paṭiviratā*), why did the children have a life of twenty years (*vīsativassāyukā ahesunti*)? [It was] because of the purification of the field (*khettavisuddhiyā*).

For their mothers and fathers were virtuous (*sīlavanto jātā*).

Thus, having grown in the womb of virtue (*sīlagabbhe vaḍḍhitattā*), through this purification of the field (*imāya khettavisuddhiyā*), they had long lives (*dīghāyukā ahesuṃ*).

Those who, having died here (*ye panettha kālaṃ katvā*), were reborn there (*tattheva nibbattā*), they themselves, through the accomplishment of virtue (*attanova sīlasampattiyā*), had long lives (*dīghāyukā ahesuṃ*).

"We might be (*assāmā*)" means we should be.

The sections beginning with "having a life of forty years (*cattārīsavassāyukā*)" should be understood (*veditabbā*) in terms of the abstinence from stealing, etc. (*adinnādānādīhi paṭiviratānaṃ vasena*).

"We might be (*assāmā*)," "having a life of forty years (*cattārīsavassāyukā*)." Explanation of the arising of Saṅkharāja (*saṅkharājauppattivaṇṇanā*).

mula_pali:
106. ‘‘Asītivassasahassāyukesu, bhikkhave, manussesu tayo ābādhā bhavissanti, icchā, anasanaṃ, jarā. Asītivassasahassāyukesu, bhikkhave, manussesu ayaṃ jambudīpo iddho ceva bhavissati phīto ca, kukkuṭasampātikā gāmanigamarājadhāniyo gāmanigamajanapadā rājadhāniyo (ka.). Asītivassasahassāyukesu, bhikkhave, manussesu ayaṃ jambudīpo avīci maññe phuṭo bhavissati manussehi, seyyathāpi naḷavanaṃ vā saravanaṃ sāravanaṃ (syā.) vā. Asītivassasahassāyukesu, bhikkhave, manussesu ayaṃ bārāṇasī ketumatī nāma rājadhānī bhavissati iddhā ceva phītā ca bahujanā ca ākiṇṇamanussā ca subhikkhā ca. Asītivassasahassāyukesu, bhikkhave, manussesu imasmiṃ jambudīpe caturāsītinagarasahassāni bhavissanti ketumatīrājadhānīpamukhāni. Asītivassasahassāyukesu, bhikkhave, manussesu ketumatiyā rājadhāniyā saṅkho nāma rājā uppajjissati cakkavattī dhammiko dhammarājā cāturanto vijitāvī janapadatthāvariyappatto sattaratanasamannāgato. Tassimāni satta ratanāni bhavissanti, seyyathidaṃ, cakkaratanaṃ hatthiratanaṃ assaratanaṃ maṇiratanaṃ itthiratanaṃ gahapatiratanaṃ pariṇāyakaratanameva sattamaṃ. Parosahassaṃ kho panassa puttā bhavissanti sūrā vīraṅgarūpā parasenappamaddanā. So imaṃ pathaviṃ sāgarapariyantaṃ adaṇḍena asatthena dhammena abhivijiya ajjhāvasissati.

Metteyyabuddhuppādo
mula_english:
106.
"When people live for eighty thousand years, monks, there will be three illnesses: greed ( *icchā*), overeating (*anasanaṃ*), and old age (*jarā*).

When people live for eighty thousand years, monks, this Jambudīpa (*jambudīpo*) will be prosperous (*iddho*) and flourishing (*phīto*). Villages, towns, and royal capitals will be as close as a cock’s flight apart.

When people live for eighty thousand years, monks, this Jambudīpa (*jambudīpo*), I think, will be crowded with people like Avīci hell, as thick with people as a reed thicket (*naḷavanaṃ*) or a sara-thicket (*saravanaṃ*).

When people live for eighty thousand years, monks, this Bārāṇasī (*bārāṇasī*) will be a royal capital called Ketumatī (*ketumatī*), prosperous (*iddhā*) and flourishing (*phītā*), populous (*bahujanā*), crowded with people (*ākiṇṇamanussā*), and with abundant food (*subhikkhā*).

When people live for eighty thousand years, monks, in this Jambudīpa (*jambudīpe*) there will be eighty-four thousand cities, headed by the royal capital Ketumatī (*ketumatīrājadhānīpamukhāni*).

When people live for eighty thousand years, monks, in the royal capital Ketumatī (*ketumatiyā rājadhāniyā*) a king named Saṅkha (*saṅkho nāma rājā*) will arise, a wheel-turning monarch (*cakkavattī*), a righteous monarch (*dhammiko*), a king of the Dharma (*dhammarājā*), a conqueror of the four quarters (*cāturanto*), a victor (*vijitāvī*) who has attained stability in his realm (*janapadatthāvariyappatto*), and is endowed with the seven treasures (*sattaratanasamannāgato*).

He will have these seven treasures (*satta ratanāni*): namely, the wheel treasure (*cakkaratanaṃ*), the elephant treasure (*hatthiratanaṃ*), the horse treasure (*assaratanaṃ*), the jewel treasure (*maṇiratanaṃ*), the woman treasure (*itthiratanaṃ*), the householder treasure (*gahapatiratanaṃ*), and the counselor treasure (*pariṇāyakaratanameva*) as the seventh.

He will have more than a thousand sons (*parosahassaṃ puttā*), who are brave (*sūrā*), heroic in form (*vīraṅgarūpā*), and crushers of the armies of others (*parasenappamaddanā*).

He will dwell having conquered this earth (*pathaviṃ*) bounded by the ocean (*sāgarapariyantaṃ*) without stick (*adaṇḍena*) or sword (*asatthena*), by the Dharma (*dhammena*) having conquered (*abhivijiya*) he will dwell (*ajjhāvasissati*).

The arising of the Buddha Maitreya.
commentary_pali: 106.Icchāti mayhaṃ bhattaṃ dethāti evaṃ uppajjanakataṇhā. Anasananti na asanaṃ avipphārikabhāvo kāyālasiyaṃ, bhattaṃ bhuttānaṃ bhattasammadapaccayā nipajjitukāmatājanako kāyadubbalabhāvoti attho. Jarāti pākaṭajarā. Kukkuṭasampātikāti ekagāmassa chadanapiṭṭhato uppatitvā itaragāmassa chadanapiṭṭhe patanasaṅkhāto kukkuṭasampāto. Etāsu atthīti kukkuṭasampātikā. ‘‘Kukkuṭasampādikā’’tipi pāṭho, gāmantarato gāmantaraṃ kukkuṭānaṃ padasā gamanasaṅkhāto kukkuṭasampādo etāsu atthīti attho. Ubhayampetaṃ ghananivāsataṃyeva dīpeti. Avīci maññe phuṭo bhavissatīti avīcimahānirayo viya nirantarapūrito bhavissati.
commentary_english:
106. *Icchā* means the craving that arises, thinking, "May I receive food."

*Anasana* means not eating, a state without spreading, physical laziness. For those who have eaten food, it means the condition of physical weakness that generates the desire to lie down due to the influence of food-induced exhilaration; this is the meaning.

*Jarā* means evident old age.

*Kukkuṭasampātikā* means *kukkuṭasampāta*, which is defined as flying up from the roof of one village and landing on the roof of another village.

*Etāsu atthīti kukkuṭasampātikā* means because it exists in these [places], it is *kukkuṭasampātikā*.

"‘‘*Kukkuṭasampādikā*’’tipi pāṭho," also, there is a reading "*Kukkuṭasampādikā*," *gāmantarato gāmantaraṃ kukkuṭānaṃ padasā gamanasaṅkhāto kukkuṭasampādo etāsu atthīti attho* means the meaning is the *kukkuṭasampāda*, which is defined as the chickens going on foot from one village to another, exists in these [places].

*Ubhayampetaṃ ghananivāsataṃyeva dīpeti* illuminates the dense dwelling of both.

"*Avīci maññe phuṭo bhavissatī*" means it will be continuously filled, like the Avīci Great Hell (*avīcimahāniraya*).

mula_pali: 107. ‘‘Asītivassasahassāyukesu, bhikkhave, manussesu metteyyo nāma bhagavā loke uppajjissati arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā. Seyyathāpāhametarahi loke uppanno arahaṃ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṃ buddho bhagavā. So imaṃ lokaṃ sadevakaṃ samārakaṃ sabrahmakaṃ sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiṃ pajaṃ sadevamanussaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedessati, seyyathāpāhametarahi imaṃ lokaṃ sadevakaṃ samārakaṃ sabrahmakaṃ sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiṃ pajaṃ sadevamanussaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedemi. So dhammaṃ desessati ādikalyāṇaṃ majjhekalyāṇaṃ pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ pakāsessati; seyyathāpāhametarahi dhammaṃ desemi ādikalyāṇaṃ majjhekalyāṇaṃ pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ pakāsemi. So anekasahassaṃ anekasatasahassaṃ (ka.) bhikkhusaṃghaṃ pariharissati, seyyathāpāhametarahi anekasataṃ bhikkhusaṃghaṃ pariharāmi.
mula_english:
107. “Monks, in that time of people with a lifespan of eighty thousand years, a Blessed Lord named Maitreya (Metteyya) will arise in the world, a worthy one, a fully enlightened Buddha, endowed with wisdom and conduct (vijjācaraṇasampanno), a Well-Farer (sugato), Knower of the worlds (lokavidū), incomparable Trainer of men to be tamed (anuttaro purisadammasārathi), Teacher of gods and humans (satthā devamanussānaṃ), enlightened and blessed (buddho bhagavā).

Just as I am now arisen in the world, a worthy one (arahaṃ), a fully enlightened Buddha (sammāsambuddho), endowed with wisdom and conduct (vijjācaraṇasampanno), a Well-Farer (sugato), Knower of the worlds (lokavidū), incomparable Trainer of men to be tamed (anuttaro purisadammasārathi), Teacher of gods and humans (satthā devamanussānaṃ), enlightened and blessed (buddho bhagavā).

He, having realized it by his own super-knowledge (abhiññā sacchikatvā), will proclaim this world with its gods (sadevakaṃ), its Māras (samārakaṃ), and its Brahmās (sabrahmakaṃ), its ascetics (sassamaṇa) and Brahmins (brāhmaṇiṃ), this generation (pajaṃ) with its gods and humans (sadevamanussaṃ), just as I do now realize and proclaim this world with its gods, its Maras, and its Brahmas, its ascetics and Brahmins, this generation with its gods and humans.

He will teach the Dhamma, lovely in its beginning (ādikalyāṇaṃ), lovely in its middle (majjhekalyāṇaṃ), lovely in its ending (pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ), in the spirit (sātthaṃ) and in the letter (sabyañjanaṃ), and proclaim the holy life (brahmacariyaṃ) in its fullness (kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ) and purity (parisuddhaṃ); just as I do now teach the Dhamma, lovely in its beginning, lovely in its middle, lovely in its ending, in the spirit and in the letter, and proclaim the holy life in its fullness and purity.

He will be attended by a company of thousands of monks (bhikkhusaṃghaṃ), just as I am now attended by a company of hundreds of monks (bhikkhusaṃghaṃ).
commentary_pali:
107. ‘‘Asītivassasahassāyukesu, bhikkhave, manussesu metteyyo nāma bhagavā loke uppajjissatī’’ti na vaḍḍhamānakavasena vuttaṃ. Na hi buddhā vaḍḍhamāne āyumhi nibbattanti, hāyamāne pana nibbattanti. Tasmā yadā taṃ āyu vaḍḍhitvā asaṅkheyyataṃ patvā puna hāyamānaṃ asītivassasahassakāle ṭhassati, tadā uppajjissatīti attho. Pariharissatīti idaṃ pana parivāretvā vicarantānaṃ vasena vuttaṃ. Yūpoti pāsādo. Raññā mahāpanādena kārāpitoti raññā hetubhūtena tassatthāya sakkena devarājena vissakammadevaputtaṃ pesetvā kārāpito. Pubbe kira dve pitāputtā naḷakārā paccekabuddhassa naḷehi ca udumbarehi ca paṇṇasālaṃ kārāpetvā taṃ tattha vāsāpetvā catūhi paccayehi upaṭṭhahiṃsu. Te kālaṃ katvā devaloke nibbattā. Tesu pitā devalokeyeva aṭṭhāsi. Putto devalokā cavitvā surucissa rañño deviyā sumedhāya kucchismiṃ nibbatto. Mahāpanādo nāma kumāro ahosi. So aparabhāge chattaṃ ussāpetvā mahāpanādo nāma rājā jāto. Athassa puññānubhāvena sakko devarājā vissakammadevaputtaṃ rañño pāsādaṃ karohīti pahiṇi so tassa pāsādaṃ nimmini pañcavīsatiyojanubbedhaṃ sattaratanamayaṃ satabhūmakaṃ. Yaṃ sandhāya jātake vuttaṃ –

‘‘Panādo nāma so rājā, yassa yūpo suvaṇṇayo;

Tiriyaṃ soḷasubbedho, uddhamāhu sahassadhā.

Sahassakaṇḍo satageṇḍu, dhajālu haritāmayo;

Anaccuṃ tattha gandhabbā, cha sahassāni sattadhā.

Evametaṃ tadā āsi, yathā bhāsasi bhaddaji;

Sakko ahaṃ tadā āsiṃ, veyyāvaccakaro tavā’’ti. (jā. 5.3.42);

So rājā tattha yāvatāyukaṃ vasitvā kālaṃ katvā devaloke nibbatti. Tasmiṃ devaloke nibbatte so pāsādo mahāgaṅgāya anusotaṃ pati. Tassa dhurasopānasammukhaṭṭhāne payāgapatiṭṭhānaṃ nāma nagaraṃ māpitaṃ. Thupikāsammukhaṭṭhāne koṭigāmo nāma. Aparabhāge amhākaṃ bhagavato kāle so naḷakāradevaputto devalokato cavitvā manussapathe bhaddajiseṭṭhi nāma hutvā satthu santike pabbajitvā arahattaṃ pāpuṇi. So nāvāya gaṅgātaraṇadivase bhikkhusaṅghassa taṃ pāsādaṃ dassetīti vatthu vitthāretabbaṃ. Kasmā panesa pāsādo na antarahitoti? Itarassa ānubhāvā. Tena saddhiṃ puññaṃ katvā devaloke nibbattakulaputto anāgate saṅkho nāma rājā bhavissati. Tassa paribhogatthāya so pāsādo uṭṭhahissati, tasmā na antarahitoti.
commentary_english:
107. "In eighty-thousand-year lifespans, monks, the blessed *Maitreya* will arise in the world," this was not said in the context of an increasing lifespan.

Indeed, Buddhas are not reborn when lifespans are increasing, but they are reborn when they are decreasing.

Therefore, when that lifespan has increased to *asaṅkhyeyyata*, and then remains at eighty-thousand years while decreasing, then that is when they will arise, is the meaning.

"*Pariharissati* (He will avoid)," this, however, was said in the context of wandering around after surrounding [something].

"*Yūpo* (a sacrificial post)," means a palace (*pāsāda*).

"*Raññā mahāpanādena kārāpito* (Built by King *Mahāpanāda*)," means that it was built for him, who was the causal agent, by *Śakra*, the king of the gods, after sending *Viśvakarmadevaputta*.

Formerly, it is said, two father and son reed-makers, having had a leaf hut built for a *Pratyekabuddha* with reeds and *udumbara* wood, having caused him to dwell there, attended to him with the four requisites.

Having died, they were reborn in the world of the gods (*devaloka*).

Among them, the father remained in the world of the gods itself.

The son, having departed from the world of the gods, was reborn in the womb of *Sumedhā*, the queen of King *Suruci*.

He was a prince named *Mahāpanāda*.

He, in the latter part [of his life], having raised an umbrella, became a king named *Mahāpanāda*.

Then, by the power of his merit (*puṇya*), *Śakra*, the king of the gods, sent *Viśvakarmadevaputta*, saying, "Build a palace (*pāsāda*) for the king!" He built a palace for him, twenty-five *yojana*s in extent, made of seven jewels, and with a hundred stories.

With reference to this, it was said in the *Jātaka*:

"That king was named *Panāda*, whose *yūpa* (sacrificial post) was golden;

Sixteen *ubbedha*s across, they say it was a thousandfold upwards.

A thousand sections, a hundred divisions, its banner was made of green gold;

There, the *gandharva*s danced, six thousand and seven times.

Thus it was then, just as you say, *Bhaddaji*;

I was *Śakra* then, your servant."

(Jā. 5.3.42);

That king, having lived there as long as his life lasted, having died, was reborn in the world of the gods (*devaloka*).

Having been reborn in that world of the gods, that palace fell along the stream of the *Mahāgaṅgā*.

At the place facing its staircase, a city named *Prayāgapatiṣṭhāna* was built.

Facing the spire (*thūpikā*), there is a village named *Koṭigāma*.

In a later time, in the time of our Blessed One (*Bhagavat*), that *Naḷakāradevaputta*, having departed from the world of the gods (*devaloka*), having become a wealthy merchant named *Bhaddajiśreṣṭhi* on the path of humans (*manuṣyapathe*), having gone forth near the Teacher (*Śāstṛ*), attained *arhattva*.

"That, on the day of crossing the *Gaṅgā* by boat, he shows that palace (*pāsāda*) to the community of monks (*bhikṣusaṅgha*)," the story should be expanded.

Why then did that palace not disappear? Because of the power of the other [one's merit].

Having done merit (*puṇya*) together with him, the son of a good family (*kulaputta*) reborn in the world of the gods (*devaloka*) will be a king named *Saṅkha* in the future.

For the purpose of his enjoyment, that palace will arise; therefore, it did not disappear.

mula_pali: 108. ‘‘Atha kho, bhikkhave, saṅkho nāma rājā yo so yūpo raññā mahāpanādena kārāpito. Taṃ yūpaṃ ussāpetvā ajjhāvasitvā taṃ datvā vissajjitvā samaṇabrāhmaṇakapaṇaddhikavaṇibbakayācakānaṃ dānaṃ datvā metteyyassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa santike kesamassuṃ ohāretvā kāsāyāni vatthāni acchādetvā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajissati. So evaṃ pabbajito samāno eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto nacirasseva yassatthāya kulaputtā sammadeva agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajanti, tadanuttaraṃ brahmacariyapariyosānaṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharissati.
mula_english: “Then, monks, there was a king named Saṅkha who had a sacrificial post (*yūpa*) erected by King Mahāpanāda. Having raised that sacrificial post, having dwelt there, having given it up, having presented it to ascetics (*śramaṇa*), Brahmins (*brāhmaṇa*), the poor, travelers, merchants, beggars, having given alms (*dāna*), having shaved off his hair and beard in the presence of the blessed (*bhagavat*) Maitreya, the worthy one (*arhat*), the perfectly awakened one (*samyak-saṃbuddha*), having put on yellow robes (*kāṣāya vastra*), he will go forth from household life (*agāra*) into homelessness (*anagāriya*). Having thus gone forth, remaining alone, secluded (*vūpakaṭṭha*), diligent (*appamatta*), ardent (*ātāpī*), resolute (*pahitatta*), before long, for the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the household life (*agāra*) into homelessness (*anagāriya*), he will realize for himself with direct knowledge (*abhiññā*) and attain to that unsurpassed (*anuttara*) consummation of the holy life (*brahmacariya-pariyosāna*) in this very life (*dṛṣṭe dharme*)."
commentary_pali: 108.Ussāpetvāti taṃ pāsādaṃ uṭṭhāpetvā. Ajjhāvasitvāti tattha vasitvā. Taṃ datvā vissajjitvāti taṃ pāsādaṃ dānavasena datvā nirapekkho pariccāgavasena ca vissajjitvā. Kassa ca evaṃ datvāti? Samaṇādīnaṃ. Tenāha – ‘‘samaṇabrāhmaṇakapaṇaddhikavanibbakayācakānaṃ dānaṃ datvā’’ti. Kathaṃ pana so ekaṃ pāsādaṃ bahūnaṃ dassatīti? Evaṃ kirassa cittaṃ uppajjissati ‘‘ayaṃ pāsādo vippakiriyatū’’ti. So khaṇḍakhaṇḍaso vippakirissati. So taṃ alaggamānova hutvā ‘‘yo yattakaṃ icchati, so tattakaṃ gaṇhatū’’ti dānavasena vissajjissati. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘dānaṃ datvā metteyyassa bhagavato…pe… viharissatī’’ti. Ettakena bhagavā vaṭṭagāmikusalassa anusandhiṃ dasseti.
commentary_english:
108.
"Having raised up" means having erected that palace.
"Having dwelt in" means dwelling there.
"Having given that away, having relinquished it" means having given that palace as a gift, being without expectation, and having relinquished it through relinquishment.
To whom does one give in this way? To ascetics, and so forth.
Therefore, it was said: "Having given a gift to ascetics, *brāhmaṇas*, the wretched, beggars, and mendicants."
How, then, will he give one palace to many? It will occur to him, "Let this palace be scattered!"
He will scatter it in pieces.
He, being unattached, having become such, will relinquish it through giving, saying, "Whoever wants as much as they want, let them take that much."
Therefore, it was said: "Having given a gift, the Blessed Metteyya...pe... will dwell."
By this much, the Blessed One shows the connection of Vaṭṭagāmikusalassa.

mula_pali:
109. ‘‘Attadīpā, bhikkhave, viharatha attasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā, dhammadīpā dhammasaraṇā anaññasaraṇā. Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu attadīpo viharati attasaraṇo anaññasaraṇo dhammadīpo dhammasaraṇo anaññasaraṇo? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Vedanāsu vedanānupassī…pe… citte cittānupassī…pe… dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu attadīpo viharati attasaraṇo anaññasaraṇo dhammadīpo dhammasaraṇo anaññasaraṇo.

Bhikkhunoāyuvaṇṇādivaḍḍhanakathā
mula_english:
109. “Monks, live as islands unto yourselves, as refuges unto yourselves, with no other refuge. Let the Dharma ( *dharma*) be your island, let the Dharma ( *dharma*) be your refuge, with no other refuge.

And how, monks, does a monk live as an island unto himself, as a refuge unto himself, with no other refuge; with the Dharma (*dharma*) as his island, the Dharma (*dharma*) as his refuge, with no other refuge? Here, monks, a monk dwells contemplating the body in the body, earnestly, clearly comprehending, and mindfully, having overcome desire and sorrow in regard to the world (*loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ*).

He dwells contemplating feelings in feelings,… mind in the mind,… mental objects in mental objects, earnestly, clearly comprehending, and mindfully, having overcome desire and sorrow in regard to the world (*loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ*).

Thus, monks, a monk lives as an island unto himself, as a refuge unto himself, with no other refuge; with the Dharma (*dharma*) as his island, the Dharma (*dharma*) as his refuge, with no other refuge.

A talk on the increase of a monk's life, complexion, and so on.
commentary_pali:
109. Idāni vivaṭṭagāmikusalassa anusandhiṃ dassento puna attadīpā, bhikkhave, viharathātiādimāha.

Bhikkhuno āyuvaṇṇādivaḍḍhanakathāvaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
Now, showing the connection to skillful practice leading to liberation, he said again, "Be your own lamp, *bhikkhus*," and so forth.

Explanation of the talk on the increase of a *bhikkhu*'s life, beauty, and so forth.

mula_pali:
110. ‘‘Gocare, bhikkhave, caratha sake pettike visaye. Gocare, bhikkhave, carantā sake pettike visaye āyunāpi vaḍḍhissatha, vaṇṇenapi vaḍḍhissatha, sukhenapi vaḍḍhissatha, bhogenapi vaḍḍhissatha, balenapi vaḍḍhissatha.

‘‘Kiñca , bhikkhave, bhikkhuno āyusmiṃ? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu chandasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, vīriyasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, cittasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti, vīmaṃsāsamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti. So imesaṃ catunnaṃ iddhipādānaṃ bhāvitattā bahulīkatattā ākaṅkhamāno kappaṃ vā tiṭṭheyya kappāvasesaṃ vā. Idaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno āyusmiṃ.

‘‘Kiñca, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno vaṇṇasmiṃ? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti, pātimokkhasaṃvarasaṃvuto viharati ācāragocarasampanno, aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī, samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu. Idaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno vaṇṇasmiṃ.

‘‘Kiñca, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno sukhasmiṃ? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā…pe… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Idaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno, sukhasmiṃ.

‘‘Kiñca, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno bhogasmiṃ? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu mettāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati tathā dutiyaṃ. Tathā tatiyaṃ. Tathā catutthaṃ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ mettāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati. Karuṇāsahagatena cetasā…pe… muditāsahagatena cetasā…pe… upekkhāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati. Tathā dutiyaṃ. Tathā tatiyaṃ. Tathā catutthaṃ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ upekkhāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati. Idaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno bhogasmiṃ.

‘‘Kiñca , bhikkhave, bhikkhuno balasmiṃ? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati. Idaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno balasmiṃ.

‘‘Nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, aññaṃ ekabalampi samanupassāmi yaṃ evaṃ duppasahaṃ, yathayidaṃ, bhikkhave, mārabalaṃ. Kusalānaṃ , bhikkhave, dhammānaṃ samādānahetu evamidaṃ puññaṃ pavaḍḍhatī’’ti. Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Cakkavattisuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ tatiyaṃ.
mula_english:
110. “Keep to your own preserves, monks, to your ancestral haunts. If you do so, your life-span will increase, your beauty will increase, your happiness will increase, your wealth will increase, your power will increase.

‘And what is length of life for a monk? Here, a monk develops the road to power which is concentration of intention accompanied by effort of will (chandasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgataṃ iddhipādaṃ bhāveti), the road to power which is concentration of energy…, the road to power which is con­centration of consciousness…, the road to power which is concentration of investigation accompanied by effort of will. By frequently practising these four roads to power he can, if he wishes, live for a full aeon, or the remaining part of an aeon. That is what I call length of life for a monk.

‘And what is beauty for a monk? Here, a monk is virtuous, he dwells restrained by the restraint of the *pātimokkha*, accomplished in conduct and resort, seeing danger in the slightest faults, undertaking and training himself in the rules of training. That is beauty for a monk.

‘And what is happiness for a monk? Here, a monk, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, enters upon and abides in the first *jhāna*, which is accompanied by applied and sustained thought, with rapture and pleasure born of seclusion. With the stilling of applied and sustained thought…the second *jhāna*…the third *jhāna*…the fourth *jhāna* he enters upon and abides. That is happiness for a monk.

‘And what is wealth for a monk? Here, a monk abides pervading one quarter with a mind imbued with loving-kindness, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth; and so above, below, and around; everywhere and equally he dwells pervading the entire world with his heart endued with loving- kindness, abundant, exalted, measureless, free from enmity, and free from affliction”. He abides pervading one quarter with a mind imbued with compassion…with a mind imbued with appreciative joy…with a mind imbued with equanimity, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth; and so above, below, and around; everywhere and equally he dwells pervading the all-encompassing world with a mind imbued with equanimity, abundant, exalted, immeasurable, without hostility and without ill will. That is wealth for a monk.

‘And what is power for a monk? Here, a monk–with the ending of *āsavas*–remains in the *āsava*-free awareness-release & discernment-release, directly knowing & realizing it for himself right in the here-&-now. That is power for a monk.

‘Monks, I do not consider any power so hard to conquer as the power of Māra. It is just by the building-up of wholesome states (*kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ samādānahetu*) that this merit (*puññaṃ*) increases’’.

This is what the Buddha said. Elated, those monks delighted in the Blessed One’s statement.

The Cakkavatti Sutta, the third, is finished.
[p.]
commentary_pali:
110.Idaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno āyusminti bhikkhave yaṃ vo ahaṃ āyunāpi vaḍḍhissathāti avocaṃ, tattha idaṃ bhikkhuno āyusmiṃ idaṃ āyukāraṇanti attho. Tasmā tumhehi āyunā vaḍḍhitukāmehi ime cattāro iddhipādā bhāvetabbāti dasseti.

Vaṇṇasminti yaṃ vo ahaṃ vaṇṇenapi vaḍḍhissathāti avocaṃ, idaṃ tattha vaṇṇakāraṇaṃ. Sīlavato hi avippaṭisārādīnaṃ vasena sarīravaṇṇopi kittivasena guṇavaṇṇopi vaḍḍhati. Tasmā tumhehi vaṇṇena vaḍḍhitukāmehi sīlasampannehi bhavitabbanti dasseti.

Vaṇṇasmi

Sukhasminti yaṃ vo ahaṃ sukhenapi vaḍḍhissathāti avocaṃ, idaṃ tattha vivekajaṃ pītisukhādinānappakārakaṃ jhānasukhaṃ. Tasmā tumhehi sukhena vaḍḍhitukāmehi imāni cattāri jhānāni bhāvetabbāni.

Sukhasmi

Bhogasminti yaṃ vo ahaṃ bhogenapi vaḍḍhissathāti avocaṃ, ayaṃ so appamāṇānaṃ sattānaṃ appaṭikūlatāvaho sukhasayanādi ekādasānisaṃso sabbadisāvipphāritabrahmavihārabhogo. Tasmā tumhehi bhogena vaḍḍhitukāmehi ime brahmavihārā bhāvetabbā.

Bhogasmi

Balasminti yaṃ vo ahaṃ balenapi vaḍḍhissathāti avocaṃ, idaṃ āsavakkhayapariyosāne uppannaṃ arahattaphalasaṅkhātaṃ balaṃ. Tasmā tumhehi balena vaḍḍhitukāmehi arahattappattiyā yogo karaṇīyo.

Balasmi

Yathayidaṃ, bhikkhave, mārabalanti yathā idaṃ devaputtamāramaccumārakilesamārānaṃ balaṃ duppasahaṃ durabhisambhavaṃ, evaṃ aññaṃ loke ekabalampi na samanupassāmi. Tampi balaṃ idameva arahattaphalaṃ pasahati abhibhavati ajjhottharati. Tasmā ettheva yogo karaṇīyoti dasseti.

Yathayidaṃ, bhikkhave, mārabala

Evamidaṃ puññanti evaṃ idaṃ lokuttarapuññampi yāva āsavakkhayā pavaḍḍhatīti vivaṭṭagāmikusalānusandhiṃ niṭṭhapento arahattanikūṭena desanaṃ niṭṭhapesi. Suttapariyosāne vīsati bhikkhusahassāni arahattaṃ pāpuṇiṃsu. Caturāsīti pāṇasahassāni amatapānaṃ piviṃsūti.

Evamidaṃ puñña

Sumaṅgalavilāsiniyā dīghanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Cakkavattisuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
110. “Here, monks, in the monk’s increase in *āyusmi*,”— monks, what I said to you, “I will increase you in life-span (āyunāpi vaḍḍhissathāti),”—there, this is what is meant by "in the monk’s *āyusmi*," this is the cause of long life. Therefore, he shows that these four constituents of psychic power should be cultivated by you who desire to increase in life-span.

“In beauty (vaṇṇasmiṃ),”—what I said to you, “I will increase you in beauty (vaṇṇenapi vaḍḍhissathāti),”—this is the cause of beauty there. For the bodily beauty of the virtuous one increases by means of non-remorse, etc., and the beauty of qualities increases by means of the beauty of fame. Therefore, he shows that you who desire to increase in beauty should be endowed with virtue.

“In happiness (sukhasmiṃ),”—what I said to you, “I will increase you in happiness (sukhenapi vaḍḍhissathāti),”—there, this is the happiness of jhāna, which is of various kinds, such as the joy and happiness born of seclusion. Therefore, he shows that these four jhānas should be cultivated by you who desire to increase in happiness.

“In wealth (bhogasmiṃ),”—what I said to you, “I will increase you in wealth (bhogenapi vaḍḍhissathāti),”—this is the enjoyment of the divine abodes, which spreads in all directions, bringing non-opposition to limitless beings, and has eleven blessings, beginning with pleasant sleep. Therefore, he shows that these divine abodes should be cultivated by you who desire to increase in wealth.

“In strength (balasmiṃ),”— what I said to you, “I will increase you in strength (balenapi vaḍḍhissathāti),”—this is the strength known as the fruit of arahantship, which arises at the end of the destruction of the corruptions. Therefore, he shows that effort should be made to attain arahantship by you who desire to increase in strength.

“Just as this, monks, is the power of Māra (yathayidaṃ, bhikkhave, mārabalaṃ),”—just as this power of Māra, the son of the gods, the Māra of death, and the Māra of the corruptions, is difficult to endure and overcome, so I do not see even one other power in the world. This very fruit of arahantship overpowers, overcomes, and subdues that power as well. Therefore, he shows that effort should be made here itself.

“Thus is merit (evamidaṃ puññaṃ),”—thus also this supramundane merit increases up to the destruction of the corruptions. Concluding the connection of skillful things that lead to liberation, he concluded the teaching with the peak of arahantship. At the end of the discourse, twenty thousand monks attained arahantship, and eighty-four thousand beings drank the nectar of immortality.

The Cakkavattisutta Commentary in the Sumaṅgalavilāsinī, Commentary to the Dīgha Nikāya, is finished.

mula_pali: 111. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati pubbārāme migāramātupāsāde. Tena kho pana samayena vāseṭṭhabhāradvājā bhikkhūsu parivasanti bhikkhubhāvaṃ ākaṅkhamānā. Atha kho bhagavā sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito pāsādā orohitvā pāsādapacchāyāyaṃ pāsādacchāyāyaṃ (ka.) abbhokāse caṅkamati.
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling in Sāvatthī in the Eastern Park in Migāramātā’s mansion.

And at that time Vāseṭṭha and Bhāradvāja were living among the monks, hoping to become monks themselves.

And in the evening, the Blessed One rose from his secluded meditation and came out of the mansion, and started walking up and down in the open space in the shade of the mansion.
commentary_pali:
111.Evaṃme sutanti aggaññasuttaṃ. Tatrāyamanuttānapadavaṇṇanā – pubbārāme migāramātupāsādeti ettha ayaṃ anupubbikathā. Atīte satasahassakappamatthake ekā upāsikā padumuttaraṃ bhagavantaṃ nimantetvā buddhappamukhassa bhikkhusatasahassassa dānaṃ datvā bhagavato pādamūle nipajjitvā ‘‘anāgate tumhādisassa buddhassa aggupaṭṭhāyikā homī’’ti patthanaṃ akāsi. Sā kappasatasahassaṃ devesu ceva manussesu ca saṃsaritvā amhākaṃ bhagavato kāle bhaddiyanagare meṇḍakaseṭṭhiputtassa dhanañcayaseṭṭhino gehe sumanadeviyā kucchimhi paṭisandhiṃ gaṇhi. Jātakāle tassā visākhāti nāmaṃ akaṃsu. Sā yadā bhagavā bhaddiyanagaraṃ āgamāsi, tadā pañcadāsisatehi saddhiṃ bhagavato paccuggamanaṃ katvā paṭhamadassanamhiyeva sotāpannā ahosi.

Aparabhāge sāvatthiyaṃ migāraseṭṭhiputtassa puṇṇavaḍḍhanakumārassa gehaṃ gatā. Tattha naṃ migāraseṭṭhi mātuṭṭhāne ṭhapesi. Tasmā migāramātāti vuccati. Patikulaṃ gacchantiyā cassā pitā mahālatāpiḷandhanaṃ nāma kārāpesi. Tasmiṃ piḷandhane catasso vajiranāḷiyo upayogaṃ agamaṃsu, muttānaṃ ekādasa nāḷiyo, pavāḷassa dvāvīsati nāḷiyo, maṇīnaṃ tettiṃsa nāḷiyo. Iti etehi ca aññehi ca sattahi ratanehi niṭṭhānaṃ agamāsi. Taṃ sīse paṭimukkaṃ yāva pādapiṭṭhiyā bhassati. Pañcannaṃ hatthīnaṃ balaṃ dhārayamānāva naṃ itthī dhāretuṃ sakkoti. Sā aparabhāge dasabalassa aggupaṭṭhāyikā hutvā taṃ pasādhanaṃ vissajjetvā navahi koṭīhi bhagavato vihāraṃ kārayamānā karīsamatte bhūmibhāge pāsādaṃ kāresi . Tassa uparibhūmiyaṃ pañca gabbhasatāni honti, heṭṭhimabhūmiyaṃ pañcāti gabbhasahassappaṭimaṇḍito ahosi. Sā ‘‘suddhapāsādova na sobhatī’’ti taṃ parivāretvā pañca duvaḍḍhagehasatāni, pañca cūḷapāsādasatāni , pañca dīghasālasatāni ca kārāpesi. Vihāramaho catūhi māsehi niṭṭhānaṃ agamāsi.

Mātugāmattabhāve ṭhitāya visākhāya viya aññissā buddhasāsane dhanapariccāgo nāma natthi, purisattabhāve ṭhitassa anāthapiṇḍikassa viya aññassāti. So hi catupaṇṇāsakoṭiyo vissajjetvā sāvatthiyā dakkhiṇabhāge anurādhapurassa mahāvihārasadise ṭhāne jetavanamahāvihāraṃ nāma kāresi. Visākhā sāvatthiyā pācīnabhāge uttaradeviyā vihārasadise ṭhāne pubbārāmaṃ nāma kāresi. Bhagavā imesaṃ dvinnaṃ kulānaṃ anukampāya sāvatthiṃ nissāya viharanto imesu dvīsu vihāresu nibaddhavāsaṃ vasi. Ekaṃ antovassaṃ jetavane vasati, ekaṃ pubbārāme. Tasmiṃ samaye pana bhagavā pubbārāme viharati. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘pubbārāme migāramātupāsāde’’ti.

Vāseṭṭhabhāradvājāti vāseṭṭho ca sāmaṇero bhāradvājo ca. Bhikkhūsu parivasantīti te neva titthiyaparivāsaṃ vasanti, na āpattiparivāsaṃ. Aparipuṇṇavassattā pana bhikkhubhāvaṃ patthayamānā vasanti. Tenevāha ‘‘bhikkhubhāvaṃ ākaṅkhamānā’’ti. Ubhopi hete udiccabrāhmaṇamahāsālakule nibbattā, cattālīsa cattālīsa koṭivibhavā tiṇṇaṃ vedānaṃ pāragū majjhimanikāye vāseṭṭhasuttaṃ sutvā saraṇaṃ gatā, tevijjasuttaṃ sutvā pabbajitvā imasmiṃ kāle bhikkhubhāvaṃ ākaṅkhamānā parivasanti. Abbhokāse caṅkamatīti uttaradakkhiṇena āyatassa pāsādassa puratthimadisābhāge pāsādacchāyāyaṃ yantarajjūhi ākaḍḍhiyamānaṃ ratanasatubbedhaṃ suvaṇṇaagghikaṃ viya anilapathe vidhāvantīhi chabbaṇṇāhi buddharasmīhi sobhamāno aparāparaṃ caṅkamati.

Vāseṭṭhabhāradvājā Bhikkhūsu parivasantī vāseṭṭhasuttaṃ tevijjasuttaṃ Abbhokāse caṅkamatī
commentary_english:
111. It is like this.

This is what I have heard: the *Aggaññasutta*.

Here is an explanation of the words with obvious meaning: "In the Pūrvārāma (Eastern Garden), in the palace of Migāramātā," this is the sequential account.

In the distant past, at the culmination of one hundred thousand *kappas*, there was a female lay follower (*upāsikā*) who invited the Blessed One Padumuttara, and after giving alms to a hundred thousand monks headed by the Buddha, she knelt at the feet of the Blessed One and made the aspiration, "In the future, may I be foremost among the female attendants of a Buddha like you."

Having transmigrated for a hundred thousand *kappas* among gods and humans, in the time of our Blessed One, in the city of Bhaddiya, in the home of Dhanañcaya, the wealthy merchant, the son of Meṇḍaka, the wealthy merchant, she took rebirth in the womb of Sumanadevī.

At the time of her birth, they gave her the name Visākhā.

When the Blessed One arrived in the city of Bhaddiya, she, together with five hundred slave girls, went to greet the Blessed One, and at the very first sight, she became a *sotāpanna* (stream-enterer).

Later, in Śrāvastī, she went to the house of Puṇṇavaḍḍhana-kumāra, the son of Migāra, the wealthy merchant.

There, Migāra, the wealthy merchant, placed her in the position of a mother.

Therefore, she is called Migāramātā.

When she was going to her husband's family, her father had a great jeweled ornament (*mahālatāpiḷandhana*) made.

In that ornament, four diamond pipes (*vajiranāḷiyo*) were used, eleven pipes (*nāḷiyo*) of pearls (*muttānaṃ*), twenty-two pipes (*nāḷiyo*) of coral (*pavāḷassa*), and thirty-three pipes (*nāḷiyo*) of jewels (*maṇīnaṃ*).

Thus, it was completed with these seven jewels and other jewels.

When placed on her head, it would hang down to the instep of her feet.

Only a woman possessing the strength of five elephants was able to bear it.

Later, having become the chief attendant of the One with the Ten Powers (*dasabala*), she gave away that ornament, and while building a monastery (*vihāra*) for the Blessed One with nine *koṭīs*, she had a palace (*pāsādaṃ*) built on a plot of land equal to a *karīsa*.

In the upper story of that, there were five hundred chambers (*gabbhasatāni*), and in the lower story, there were five hundred, so it was adorned with a thousand chambers (*gabbhasahassappaṭimaṇḍito*).

She thought, "The pure palace is not beautiful," so surrounding it, she had five hundred two-and-a-half storied houses, five hundred small palaces, and five hundred long halls built.

The dedication ceremony (*vihāramaho*) was completed in four months.

In the state of being a woman, there is no giving of wealth (*dhanapariccāgo*) in the Buddha's Dispensation like that of Visākhā, and in the state of being a man, there is no giving like that of Anāthapiṇḍika.

For he, having given away fifty-four *koṭīs*, had the Jetavanamahāvihāra, resembling the Mahāvihāra of Anurādhapura, built in the southern part of Śrāvastī.

Visākhā had the Pūrvārāma (Eastern Garden) built in the eastern part of Śrāvastī, in a place resembling the monastery of Uttaradevi.

Out of compassion for these two families, the Blessed One, relying on Śrāvastī, while dwelling there, constantly resided in these two monasteries.

He spent one rainy season in Jetavana, and one in Pūrvārāma.

At that time, the Blessed One was dwelling in Pūrvārāma.

Therefore, it was said, "In the Pūrvārāma, in the palace of Migāramātā."

"Vāseṭṭha and Bhāradvāja" means Vāseṭṭha and the novice Bhāradvāja.

"Living among the monks" means they do not live the probationary period (*parivāsa*) of the sectarians (*titthiya*), nor the probationary period (*parivāsa*) for offenses (*āpatti*).

But, because their years are not complete (*aparipuṇṇavassattā*), they live desiring the state of a monk (*bhikkhubhāvaṃ*).

Therefore, he said, "Desiring the state of a monk (*bhikkhubhāvaṃ ākaṅkhamānā*)."

Both of them were born in noble families of Udicca Brahmins, possessing forty *koṭīs* each, were experts in the three Vedas, and having heard the *Vāseṭṭhasutta* in the *Majjhimanikāya*, they had gone for refuge. Having heard the *Tevijjasutta*, having gone forth, at this time, desiring the state of a monk (*bhikkhubhāvaṃ ākaṅkhamānā*), they are living the probationary period (*parivasanti*).
<hi rend="bold">"Abbhokāse caṅkamatī"</hi> means: shining with the six-colored rays of the Buddha, which appear to be golden lamps, inlaid with jewels, being pulled by machine-cords in the eastern part of the palace, in the shadow of the palace, which is long from north to south, he walks back and forth in the open air.

<hi rend="bold">vāseṭṭhabhāradvājā</hi> <hi rend="bold">bhikkhūsu parivasantī</hi> <hi rend="bold">vāseṭṭhasuttaṃ</hi> <hi rend="bold">tevijjasuttaṃ</hi> <hi rend="bold">abbhokāse caṅkamatī</hi>

mula_pali: 112. Addasā kho vāseṭṭho bhagavantaṃ sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhitaṃ pāsādā orohitvā pāsādapacchāyāyaṃ abbhokāse caṅkamantaṃ. Disvāna bhāradvājaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘ayaṃ, āvuso bhāradvāja, bhagavā sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito pāsādā orohitvā pāsādapacchāyāyaṃ abbhokāse caṅkamati. Āyāmāvuso bhāradvāja, yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamissāma; appeva nāma labheyyāma bhagavato santikā sammukhā (syā. ka.) dhammiṃ kathaṃ savanāyā’’ti. ‘‘Evamāvuso’’ti kho bhāradvājo vāseṭṭhassa paccassosi.
mula_english:
Vāseṭṭha saw the Blessed One who had arisen from seclusion in the evening, having descended from the palace and was walking up and down in the open space in the shadow of the palace.

Having seen Bhāradvāja, he addressed him, "Friend Bhāradvāja, the Blessed One has arisen from seclusion in the evening, having descended from the palace and is walking up and down in the open space in the shadow of the palace.

Let us approach him, friend Bhāradvāja; perhaps we may have the opportunity to hear a talk on the Dhamma from the Blessed One’s presence <note>face to face (syā.
ka.
)</note>."

"Yes, indeed, friend," Bhāradvāja replied to Vāseṭṭha.

mula_pali: 113. Atha kho vāseṭṭhabhāradvājā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā bhagavantaṃ caṅkamantaṃ anucaṅkamiṃsu. Atha kho bhagavā vāseṭṭhaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘tumhe khvattha, vāseṭṭha, brāhmaṇajaccā brāhmaṇakulīnā brāhmaṇakulā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā, kacci vo, vāseṭṭha, brāhmaṇā na akkosanti na paribhāsantī’’ti? ‘‘Taggha no, bhante, brāhmaṇā akkosanti paribhāsanti attarūpāya paribhāsāya paripuṇṇāya, no aparipuṇṇāyā’’ti. ‘‘Yathā kathaṃ pana vo, vāseṭṭha, brāhmaṇā akkosanti paribhāsanti attarūpāya paribhāsāya paripuṇṇāya, no aparipuṇṇāyā’’ti? ‘‘Brāhmaṇā, bhante, evamāhaṃsu – ‘brāhmaṇova seṭṭho vaṇṇo, hīnā aññe vaṇṇā hīno añño vaṇṇo (sī. pī. ma. ni. 2 madhurasutta). Brāhmaṇova sukko vaṇṇo , kaṇhā aññe vaṇṇā kaṇho añño vaṇṇo (sī. pī. ma. ni. 2 madhurasutta). Brāhmaṇāva sujjhanti, no abrāhmaṇā. Brāhmaṇāva brāhmaṇā (syā.) brahmuno puttā orasā mukhato jātā brahmajā brahmanimmitā brahmadāyādā. Te tumhe seṭṭhaṃ vaṇṇaṃ hitvā hīnamattha vaṇṇaṃ ajjhupagatā, yadidaṃ muṇḍake samaṇake ibbhe kaṇhe bandhupādāpacce. Tayidaṃ na sādhu, tayidaṃ nappatirūpaṃ, yaṃ tumhe seṭṭhaṃ vaṇṇaṃ hitvā hīnamattha vaṇṇaṃ ajjhupagatā yadidaṃ muṇḍake samaṇake ibbhe kaṇhe bandhupādāpacce’ti. Evaṃ kho no, bhante, brāhmaṇā akkosanti paribhāsanti attarūpāya paribhāsāya paripuṇṇāya, no aparipuṇṇāyā’’ti.
mula_english:
113. Then Vāseṭṭha and Bhāradvāja approached the Blessed One; having approached, having greeted the Blessed One, they followed the Blessed One as he was walking back and forth.

Then the Blessed One addressed Vāseṭṭha, "From what group do you come, Vāseṭṭha? You have gone forth from the household life into homelessness from the Brahmin (brāhmaṇa) caste, from a Brahmin family, from the Brahmin clan. Do the Brahmins (brāhmaṇā) not revile or speak disparagingly of you, Vāseṭṭha?"

"Indeed, they do, venerable sir. The Brahmins (brāhmaṇā) revile and speak disparagingly of us with complete and utter disparagement."

"But in what way, Vāseṭṭha, do the Brahmins (brāhmaṇā) revile and speak disparagingly of you with complete and utter disparagement?"

"Venerable sir, the Brahmins (brāhmaṇā) say thus: 'Only the Brahmins (brāhmaṇova) are the highest class (varṇa); other classes (vaṇṇā) are inferior. Only the Brahmins (brāhmaṇova) are the fair class (vaṇṇa); other classes (vaṇṇā) are dark. Only the Brahmins (brāhmaṇāva) are purified; non-Brahmins are not. The Brahmins (brāhmaṇāva) are the true children of Brahmā, born of his mouth, offspring of Brahmā, created by Brahmā, heirs of Brahmā.

You have abandoned the highest class (seṭṭhaṃ varṇaṃ) and have taken to the inferior class (hīnamattha vaṇṇaṃ), namely these shavelings, these ascetics, these servants, these dark fellows, these descendants of Bandhu's feet.

This is not right; this is not proper; you have abandoned the highest class (seṭṭhaṃ varṇaṃ) and have taken to the inferior class (hīnamattha vaṇṇaṃ), namely these shavelings, these ascetics, these servants, these dark fellows, these descendants of Bandhu's feet.’

In this way, venerable sir, the Brahmins (brāhmaṇā) revile and speak disparagingly of us with complete and utter disparagement."
commentary_pali:
113.Anucaṅkamiṃsūti añjaliṃ paggayha onatasarīrā hutvā anuvattamānā caṅkamiṃsu. Vāseṭṭhaṃ āmantesīti so tesaṃ paṇḍitataro gahetabbaṃ vissajjetabbañca jānāti, tasmā taṃ āmantesi. Tumhe khvatthāti tumhe kho attha. Brāhmaṇajaccāti, brāhmaṇajātikā. Brāhmaṇakulīnāti brāhmaṇesu kulīnā kulasampannā. Brāhmaṇakulāti brāhmaṇakulato, bhogādisampannaṃ brāhmaṇakulaṃ pahāyāti attho. Na akkosantīti dasavidhena akkosavatthunā na akkosanti. Na paribhāsantīti nānāvidhāya paribhavakathāya na paribhāsantīti attho. Iti bhagavā ‘‘brāhmaṇā ime sāmaṇere akkosanti paribhāsantī’’ti jānamānova pucchati. Kasmā? Ime mayā apucchitā paṭhamataraṃ na kathessanti, akathite kathā na samuṭṭhātīti kathāsamuṭṭhāpanatthāya. Tagghāti ekaṃsavacane nipāto, ekaṃseneva no, bhante, brāhmaṇā akkosanti paribhāsantīti vuttaṃ hoti. Attarūpāyāti attano anurūpāya. Paripuṇṇāyāti yathāruci padabyañjanāni āropetvā āropetvā paripūritāya. No aparipuṇṇāyāti antarā aṭṭhapitāya nirantaraṃ pavattāya.

Kasmā pana brāhmaṇā ime sāmaṇere akkosantīti? Appatiṭṭhatāya. Ime hi sāmaṇerā aggabrāhmaṇānaṃ puttā tiṇṇaṃ vedānaṃ pāragū jambudīpe brāhmaṇānaṃ antare pākaṭā sambhāvitā tesaṃ pabbajitattā aññe brāhmaṇaputtā pabbajiṃsu. Atha kho brāhmaṇā ‘‘apatiṭṭhā mayaṃ jātā’’ti imāya appatiṭṭhatāya gāmadvārepi antogāmepi te disvā ‘‘tumhehi brāhmaṇasamayo bhinno, muṇḍasamaṇakassa pacchato pacchato rasagiddhā hutvā vicarathā’’tiādīni ceva pāḷiyaṃ āgatāni ‘‘brāhmaṇova seṭṭho vaṇṇo’’tiādīni ca vatvā akkosanti. Sāmaṇerā tesu akkosantesupi kopaṃ vā āghātaṃ vā akatvā kevalaṃ bhagavatā puṭṭhā ‘‘taggha no, bhante, brāhmaṇā akkosanti paribhāsantī’’ti ārocesuṃ. Atha ne bhagavā akkosanākāraṃ pucchanto yathā kathaṃ pana voti pucchati. Te ācikkhantā brāhmaṇā bhantetiādimāhaṃsu.

yathā kathaṃ pana vo brāhmaṇā bhante

Tattha seṭṭho vaṇṇoti jātigottādīnaṃ paññāpanaṭṭhāne brāhmaṇova seṭṭhoti dassenti. Hīnā aññe vaṇṇāti itare tayo vaṇṇā hīnā lāmakāti vadanti. Sukkoti paṇḍaro. Kaṇhoti kāḷako. Sujjhantīti jātigottādīnaṃ paññāpanaṭṭhāne sujjhanti. Brahmuno puttāti mahābrahmuno puttā. Orasā mukhato jātāti ure vasitvā mukhato nikkhantā, ure katvā saṃvaḍḍhitāti vā orasā. Brahmajāti brahmato nibbattā. Brahmanimmitāti brahmunā nimmitā. Brahmadāyādāti brahmuno dāyādā. Hīnamattha vaṇṇaṃ ajjhupagatāti hīnaṃ vaṇṇaṃ ajjhupagatā attha. Muṇḍakesamaṇaketi nindantā jigucchantā vadanti, na muṇḍakamattañceva samaṇamattañca sandhāya. Ibbheti gahapatike. Kaṇheti kāḷake. Bandhūti mārassa bandhubhūte mārapakkhike. Pādāpacceti mahābrahmuno pādānaṃ apaccabhūte pādato jāteti adhippāyo.

seṭṭho vaṇṇo Hīnā aññe vaṇṇā Sukko Kaṇho Sujjhantī Brahmuno puttā Orasā mukhato jātā Brahmajā Brahmanimmitā Brahmadāyādā Hīnamattha vaṇṇaṃ ajjhupagatā Muṇḍake samaṇake Ibbhe Kaṇhe Bandhū Pādāpacce
commentary_english:
113.
*"Anucaṅkamiṃsū"* means they walked about, offering añjali, with bowed bodies, following along.

*"Vāseṭṭhaṃ āmantesī"* means he knows what should be taken and what should be rejected; therefore, he addressed Vāseṭṭha.

*"Tumhe khvatthā"* means you are indeed that.

*"Brāhmaṇajaccā"*, means of the brāhmaṇa caste.

*"Brāhmaṇakulīnā"* means well-born among the *brāhmaṇas*, possessing good family lineage.

*"Brāhmaṇakulā"* means from a *brāhmaṇa* family; it means having abandoned a *brāhmaṇa* family endowed with wealth, etc.

*"Na akkosantī"* means they do not insult with the ten kinds of grounds for insult.

*"Na paribhāsantī"* means they do not revile with various kinds of reviling talk.

Thus, the Blessed One asks, knowing, "These *brāhmaṇas* insult and revile the novices."

Why? Because if they are not asked by me, they will not speak first; speech does not arise when something is unsaid. [This is] for the purpose of arousing speech.

*"Tagghā"* is a particle in a one-sided statement; it means, "Indeed, *bhante*, the *brāhmaṇas* insult and revile," it is said.

*"Attarūpāyā"* means corresponding to oneself.

*"Paripuṇṇāyā"* means having fully filled [the bowl] by pouring in choice food and flavors according to one's liking.

*"No aparipuṇṇāyā"* means continuously flowing, not stopped in between.

Why then do the *brāhmaṇas* insult these novices? Because of non-establishment.

These novices are sons of eminent *brāhmaṇas*, masters of the three Vedas, well-known and esteemed among the *brāhmaṇas* in Jambudīpa; because of their having gone forth, other sons of *brāhmaṇas* went forth.

Then the *brāhmaṇas*, seeing them at the village gate or within the village, [thinking] "We are born unestablished," and with this non-establishment, they insult, saying, "Your *brāhmaṇa* tradition is broken; you wander about, following behind bald ascetics, greedy for flavors," etc., and those that have come in the Pāḷi, "The *brāhmaṇa* is the highest caste," etc.

The novices, even when they were being insulted in those ways, without making anger or animosity, only when asked by the Blessed One, reported, "Indeed, *bhante*, the *brāhmaṇas* insult and revile."

Then the Blessed One, asking about the manner of insulting, asks, "How, indeed, do they treat you?"

Those who were relating said, "*Brāhmaṇas*, *bhante*," etc.

How, indeed, do the *brāhmaṇas*, *bhante*…

There, *"Seṭṭho vaṇṇo"* means in the place of declaring caste, lineage, etc., they show that the *brāhmaṇa* is the highest.

*"Hīnā aññe vaṇṇā"* means the other three castes are inferior and base, they say.

*"Sukko"* means white.

*"Kaṇho"* means black.

*"Sujjhantī"* means they are purified, in the place of declaring caste, lineage, etc.

*"Brahmuno puttā"* means sons of Mahābrahmā.

*"Orasā mukhato jātā"* means born from the mouth, having dwelt in the breast; or, "orasā" means having made [them] in [their] breast and raised [them].

*"Brahmajā"* means born from Brahmā.

*"Brahmanimmitā"* means created by Brahmā.

*"Brahmadāyādā"* means heirs of Brahmā.

*"Hīnamattha vaṇṇaṃ ajjhupagatā"* means you have approached an inferior caste.

*"Muṇḍake samaṇake"* means they speak, disparaging and loathing, not referring to mere baldness or mere asceticism.

*"Ibbhe"* means householders.

*"Kaṇhe"* means black.
<hi rend="bold">Bandhū</hi>: "relative," meaning those who are relatives of Māra, belonging to Māra's side.
