<hi rend="bold">Pādāpacce</hi>: "offspring of the foot," meaning offspring from the feet of Mahābrahmā, the intention being "born from the foot."

<hi rend="bold">Seṭṭho vaṇṇo</hi>: "the best class." <hi rend="bold">Hīnā aññe vaṇṇā</hi>: "other classes are inferior." <hi rend="bold">Sukko</hi>: "white." <hi rend="bold">Kaṇho</hi>: "black." <hi rend="bold">Sujjhantī</hi>: "they purify." <hi rend="bold">Brahmuno puttā</hi>: "sons of Brahmā." <hi rend="bold">Orasā mukhato jātā</hi>: "genuine, born from the mouth." <hi rend="bold">Brahmajā</hi>: "born of Brahmā." <hi rend="bold">Brahmanimmitā</hi>: "created by Brahmā." <hi rend="bold">Brahmadāyādā</hi>: "heirs of Brahmā." <hi rend="bold">Hīnamattha vaṇṇaṃ ajjhupagatā</hi>: "having adopted an inferior state." <hi rend="bold">Muṇḍake</hi>: "shavelings."

<hi rend="bold">Samaṇake</hi>: "ascetics." <hi rend="bold">Ibbhe</hi>: "wealthy men." <hi rend="bold">Kaṇhe</hi>: "black ones." <hi rend="bold">Bandhū</hi>: "relatives." <hi rend="bold">Pādāpacce</hi>: "offspring of the foot."

mula_pali:
114. ‘‘Taggha vo, vāseṭṭha, brāhmaṇā porāṇaṃ assarantā evamāhaṃsu – ‘brāhmaṇova seṭṭho vaṇṇo, hīnā aññe vaṇṇā; brāhmaṇova sukko vaṇṇo, kaṇhā aññe vaṇṇā; brāhmaṇāva sujjhanti, no abrāhmaṇā; brāhmaṇāva brahmuno puttā orasā mukhato jātā brahmajā brahmanimmitā brahmadāyādā’ti. Dissanti kho pana, vāseṭṭha, brāhmaṇānaṃ brāhmaṇiyo utuniyopi gabbhiniyopi vijāyamānāpi pāyamānāpi. Te ca brāhmaṇā yonijāva samānā evamāhaṃsu – ‘brāhmaṇova seṭṭho vaṇṇo, hīnā aññe vaṇṇā; brāhmaṇova sukko vaṇṇo, kaṇhā aññe vaṇṇā; brāhmaṇāva sujjhanti, no abrāhmaṇā; brāhmaṇāva brahmuno puttā orasā mukhato jātā brahmajā brahmanimmitā brahmadāyādā’ti. Te te ca (syā. ka.) brahmānañceva abbhācikkhanti, musā ca bhāsanti, bahuñca apuññaṃ pasavanti.

Catuvaṇṇasuddhi
mula_english:
“Then, Vāseṭṭha, the *brāhmaṇas* (Brahmins), while reciting their ancient tradition, say thus: ‘The *brāhmaṇa* is the highest class (*varṇa*), other classes are inferior; the *brāhmaṇa* is the fairest class, other classes are dark; only *brāhmaṇas* are purified, not non-*brāhmaṇas*; only *brāhmaṇas* are the sons of Brahmā, his direct offspring, born from his mouth, born of Brahmā, created by Brahmā, heirs of Brahmā.’

But, Vāseṭṭha, the *brāhmaṇīs* (female Brahmins) of the *brāhmaṇas* are seen to have their periods, become pregnant, give birth, and nurse [their children].

And yet these womb-born *brāhmaṇas*, while being born of the womb, say thus: ‘The *brāhmaṇa* is the highest class, other classes are inferior; the *brāhmaṇa* is the fairest class, other classes are dark; only *brāhmaṇas* are purified, not non-*brāhmaṇas*; only *brāhmaṇas* are the sons of Brahmā, his direct offspring, born from his mouth, born of Brahmā, created by Brahmā, heirs of Brahmā.’

These *brāhmaṇas* misrepresent Brahmā, speak falsely, and generate much demerit.

The purification of the four classes.
commentary_pali:
114. ‘‘Taggha vo, vāseṭṭha, brāhmaṇā porāṇaṃ assarantā evamāhaṃsū’’ti ettha voti nipātamattaṃ, sāmivacanaṃ vā, tumhākaṃ brāhmaṇāti attho. Porāṇanti porāṇakaṃ aggaññaṃ lokuppatticariyavaṃsaṃ. Assarantāti assaramānā. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti, ekaṃsena vo, vāseṭṭha, brāhmaṇā porāṇaṃ lokuppattiṃ ananussarantā ajānantā evaṃ vadantīti. ‘‘Dissanti kho panā’’ti evamādi tesaṃ laddhibhindanatthāya vuttaṃ. Tattha brāhmaṇiyoti brāhmaṇānaṃ puttappaṭilābhatthāya āvāhavivāhavasena kulaṃ ānītā brāhmaṇiyo dissanti. Tā kho panetā aparena samayena utuniyopi honti, sañjātapupphāti attho. Gabbhiniyoti sañjātagabbhā. Vijāyamānāti puttadhītaro janayamānā. Pāyamānāti dārake thaññaṃ pāyantiyo. Yonijāva samānāti brāhmaṇīnaṃ passāvamaggena jātā samānā. Evamāhaṃsūti evaṃ vadanti. Kathaṃ? ‘‘Brāhmaṇova seṭṭho vaṇṇo…pe… brahmadāyādā’’ti. Yadi pana nesaṃ taṃ saccavacanaṃ siyā, brāhmaṇīnaṃ kucchi mahābrahmassa uro bhaveyya, brāhmaṇīnaṃ passāvamaggo mahābrahmuno mukhaṃ bhaveyya, na kho panetaṃ evaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Tenāha ‘‘te ca brahmūnañceva abbhācikkhantī’’tiādi.

Catuvaṇṇasuddhivaṇṇanā

Ettāvatā ‘‘mayaṃ mahābrahmuno ure vasitvā mukhato nikkhantāti vattuṃ mā labhantū’’ti imaṃ mukhacchedakavādaṃ vatvā puna cattāropi vaṇṇā kusale dhamme samādāya vattantāva sujjhantīti dassanatthaṃ cattārome, vāseṭṭha, vaṇṇātiādimāha. Akusalasaṅkhātāti akusalāti saṅkhātā akusalakoṭṭhāsabhūtā vā. Esa nayo sabbattha. Na alamariyāti ariyabhāve asamatthā. Kaṇhāti pakatikāḷakā. Kaṇhavipākāti vipākopi nesaṃ kaṇho dukkhoti attho. Khattiyepi teti khattiyamhipi te. Ekacceti ekasmiṃ. Esa nayo sabbattha.

cattārome, vāseṭṭha, vaṇṇā Akusalasaṅkhātā Na alamariyā Kaṇhā Kaṇhavipākā Khattiyepi te Ekacce

Sukkāti nikkilesabhāvena paṇḍarā. Sukkavipākāti vipākopi nesaṃ sukko sukhoti attho.

Sukkā Sukkavipākā
commentary_english:
114. "Indeed, Vāseṭṭha, when the Brahmins, unmindful of the ancient [teachings], say thus," here, *vo* is merely a particle, or a word of respect, meaning "your" Brahmins. *Porāṇa* means ancient, the *Aggañña* [Sūtra], the lineage of the world's origin and conduct. *Assarantā* means not remembering. This is said: "Certainly, Vāseṭṭha, the Brahmins, not recollecting the ancient origin of the world, say thus without knowing." "Do they appear," etc., was said to refute their views. There, *brāhmaṇiyo* means Brahmin women brought into the family through marriage for the sake of having children by the Brahmins are seen. These women, after some time, also become seasonal, meaning they have their menstruation. *Gabbhiniyo* means those who have become pregnant. *Vijāyamānā* means giving birth to sons and daughters. *Pāyamānā* means those who are feeding milk to infants. *Yonijāva samānā* means being born through the birth canal of Brahmin women. *Evamāhaṃsū* means they say thus. How? "A Brahmin is the highest caste...pe... heirs of Brahman." If that statement of theirs were true, the wombs of Brahmin women would be the chest of Mahābrahmā, and the birth canal of Brahmin women would be the mouth of Mahābrahmā, but this is not to be seen thus. Therefore, he said, "And they are accusing Brahmā himself," etc.

Description of the purity of the four castes

To prevent them from being able to say, "We lived in the chest of Mahābrahmā and came out of his mouth," after stating this mouth-cutting argument, he said "The four castes, Vāseṭṭha" etc., to show that even all four castes become pure by adopting skillful qualities and behaving accordingly. *Akusalasaṅkhātā* means those who are designated as unwholesome, or those who are part of the unwholesome group. This method applies everywhere. *Na alamariyā* means incapable of noble states. *Kaṇhā* means naturally black. *Kaṇhavipākā* means their result is also black, meaning suffering. *Khattiyepi te* means even among the Khattiyas. *Ekacce* means in one. This method applies everywhere.

The four castes, Vāseṭṭha, are designated as unwholesome, incapable of noble states, black, and have black results. Even among the Khattiyas, some. *Sukkā* means white due to being free from defilements. *Sukkavipākā* means their result is also white, meaning happiness.

White, having white results.

mula_pali:
115. ‘‘Cattārome, vāseṭṭha, vaṇṇā – khattiyā, brāhmaṇā, vessā, suddā. Khattiyopi kho, vāseṭṭha, idhekacco pāṇātipātī hoti adinnādāyī kāmesumicchācārī musāvādī pisuṇavāco pharusavāco samphappalāpī abhijjhālu byāpannacitto micchādiṭṭhī. Iti kho, vāseṭṭha, yeme dhammā akusalā akusalasaṅkhātā sāvajjā sāvajjasaṅkhātā asevitabbā asevitabbasaṅkhātā naalamariyā naalamariyasaṅkhātā kaṇhā kaṇhavipākā viññugarahitā, khattiyepi te kho vāseṭṭha (ka.) idhekacce sandissanti. Brāhmaṇopi kho, vāseṭṭha…pe… vessopi kho, vāseṭṭha…pe… suddopi kho, vāseṭṭha, idhekacco pāṇātipātī hoti adinnādāyī kāmesumicchācārī musāvādī pisuṇavāco pharusavāco samphappalāpī abhijjhālu byāpannacitto micchādiṭṭhī. Iti kho, vāseṭṭha, yeme dhammā akusalā akusalasaṅkhātā…pe… kaṇhā kaṇhavipākā viññugarahitā; suddepi te idhekacce sandissanti.

‘‘Khattiyopi kho, vāseṭṭha, idhekacco pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, adinnādānā paṭivirato, kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato, musāvādā paṭivirato, pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato, pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato, samphappalāpā paṭivirato, anabhijjhālu abyāpannacitto, sammādiṭṭhī. Iti kho, vāseṭṭha, yeme dhammā kusalā kusalasaṅkhātā anavajjā anavajjasaṅkhātā sevitabbā sevitabbasaṅkhātā alamariyā alamariyasaṅkhātā sukkā sukkavipākā viññuppasatthā, khattiyepi te idhekacce sandissanti. Brāhmaṇopi kho, vāseṭṭha…pe… vessopi kho, vāseṭṭha…pe… suddopi kho, vāseṭṭha, idhekacco pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti…pe… anabhijjhālu , abyāpannacitto, sammādiṭṭhī. Iti kho, vāseṭṭha, yeme dhammā kusalā kusalasaṅkhātā anavajjā anavajjasaṅkhātā sevitabbā sevitabbasaṅkhātā alamariyā alamariyasaṅkhātā sukkā sukkavipākā viññuppasatthā; suddepi te idhekacce sandissanti.
mula_english:
115. ‘There are, Vāseṭṭha, these four castes: the nobles (*khattiya*), the Brahmins (*brāhmaṇa*), the merchants (*vessa*) and the workers (*sudda*).

And sometimes a noble (*khattiya*) takes life (*pāṇātipātī*), takes what is not given (*adinnādāyī*), commits sexual misconduct (*kāmesumicchācārī*), tells lies (*musāvādī*), indulges in slander (*pisuṇavāco*), harsh speech (*pharusavāco*) or idle chatter (*samphappalāpī*), is grasping (*abhijjhālu*), malicious (*byāpannacitto*), or of wrong views (*micchādiṭṭhī*).

Thus such things as are immoral (*akusalā*) and considered so (*akusalasaṅkhātā*), blameworthy (*sāvajjā*) and considered so (*sāvajjasaṅkhātā*), to be avoided (*asevitabbā*) and considered so (*asevitabbasaṅkhātā*), ways unbefitting an Ariyan (*naalamariyā*) and considered so (*naalamariyasaṅkhātā*), black (*kaṇhā*) with black result (*kaṇhavipākā*) and blamed by the wise (*viññugarahitā*), are sometimes to be found among the nobles (*khattiya*).

A Brahmin (*brāhmaṇa*)… A merchant (*vessa*)… And sometimes a worker (*sudda*) takes life (*pāṇātipātī*), takes what is not given (*adinnādāyī*), commits sexual misconduct (*kāmesumicchācārī*), tells lies (*musāvādī*), indulges in slander (*pisuṇavāco*), harsh speech (*pharusavāco*) or idle chatter (*samphappalāpī*), is grasping (*abhijjhālu*), malicious (*byāpannacitto*), or of wrong views (*micchādiṭṭhī*).

Thus such things as are immoral (*akusalā*) and considered so (*akusalasaṅkhātā*), black (*kaṇhā*) with black result (*kaṇhavipākā*) and blamed by the wise (*viññugarahitā*), are sometimes to be found among the workers (*sudda*).

And sometimes a noble (*khattiya*) abstains from taking life (*pāṇātipātā paṭivirato*), from taking what is not given (*adinnādānā paṭivirato*), from misconduct in sensual pleasures (*kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato*), from false speech (*musāvādā paṭivirato*), from malicious speech (*pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato*), from harsh speech (*pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato*), and from gossip (*samphappalāpā paṭivirato*); he is not covetous (*anabhijjhālu*), his mind is without ill will (*abyāpannacitto*), and he holds right view (*sammādiṭṭhī*).

Thus such things as are moral (*kusalā*) and considered so (*kusalasaṅkhātā*), blameless (*anavajjā*) and considered so (*anavajjasaṅkhātā*), to be followed (*sevitabbā*) and considered so (*sevitabbasaṅkhātā*), ways befitting an Ariyan (*alamariyā*) and considered so (*alamariyasaṅkhātā*), bright (*sukkā*) with bright results (*sukkavipākā*) and praised by the wise (*viññuppasatthā*), are sometimes to be found among the nobles (*khattiya*).

A Brahmin (*brāhmaṇa*)… A merchant (*vessa*)… And sometimes a worker (*sudda*) abstains from taking life (*pāṇātipātā paṭivirato*)…he is not covetous (*anabhijjhālu*), his mind is without ill will (*abyāpannacitto*), and he holds right view (*sammādiṭṭhī*).

Thus such things as are moral (*kusalā*) and considered so (*kusalasaṅkhātā*), blameless (*anavajjā*) and considered so (*anavajjasaṅkhātā*), to be followed (*sevitabbā*) and considered so (*sevitabbasaṅkhātā*), ways befitting an Ariyan (*alamariyā*) and considered so (*alamariyasaṅkhātā*), bright (*sukkā*) with bright results (*sukkavipākā*) and praised by the wise (*viññuppasatthā*), are sometimes to be found among the workers (*sudda*).

mula_pali: 116. ‘‘Imesu kho, vāseṭṭha, catūsu vaṇṇesu evaṃ ubhayavokiṇṇesu vattamānesu kaṇhasukkesu dhammesu viññugarahitesu ceva viññuppasatthesu ca yadettha brāhmaṇā evamāhaṃsu – ‘brāhmaṇova seṭṭho vaṇṇo, hīnā aññe vaṇṇā; brāhmaṇova sukko vaṇṇo, kaṇhā aññe vaṇṇā; brāhmaṇāva sujjhanti, no abrāhmaṇā; brāhmaṇāva brahmuno puttā orasā mukhato jātā brahmajā brahmanimmitā brahmadāyādā’ti. Taṃ tesaṃ viññū nānujānanti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Imesañhi, vāseṭṭha, catunnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ yo hoti bhikkhu arahaṃ khīṇāsavo vusitavā katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano sammadaññāvimutto, so nesaṃ aggamakkhāyati dhammeneva, no adhammena. Dhammo hi, vāseṭṭha, seṭṭho janetasmiṃ, diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañca .
mula_english:
Now, Vāseṭṭha, since both dark and bright qualities, which are blamed and praised by the wise, are thus found mingled in the four castes, the Brahmins say: ‘The Brahmin is the best caste; other castes are inferior. The Brahmin is the fair caste; other castes are dark. Only Brahmins are purified, not non-Brahmins. Brahmins are the true sons of Brahmā, born from his mouth, offspring of Brahmā, created by Brahmā, heirs of Brahmā.’

The wise do not recognize this claim of theirs.

Why is that? Because, Vāseṭṭha, anyone from the four castes who becomes a *bhikkhu* (monk), an *arahaṃ* (Arahant) who has destroyed the *āsavas* (corruptions), who has lived the (holy) life, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, reached the highest goal, destroyed the fetter of becoming, and become emancipated through right knowledge – he is declared to be the foremost among them by virtue of the *Dhamma* (righteousness), and not by *adhamma* (unrighteousness).

Indeed, Vāseṭṭha, the *Dhamma* is the best thing for people in this life and in the next.
commentary_pali:
116.Ubhayavokiṇṇesu vattamānesūti ubhayesu vokiṇṇesu missībhūtesu hutvā vattamānesu. Katamesu ubhayesūti? Kaṇhasukkesu dhammesu viññugarahitesu ceva viññuppasatthesu ca. Yadettha brāhmaṇā evamāhaṃsūti ettha etesu kaṇhasukkadhammesu vattamānāpi brāhmaṇā yadetaṃ evaṃ vadanti ‘‘brāhmaṇova seṭṭho vaṇṇo’’tiādi. Taṃ nesaṃ viññū nānujānantīti ye loke paṇḍitā, te nānumodanti, na pasaṃsantīti attho. Taṃ kissa hetu? Imesañhi vāseṭṭhātiādimhi ayaṃ saṅkhepattho. Yaṃ vuttaṃ nānujānantīti, taṃ kasmāti ce? Yasmā imesaṃ catunnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ yo bhikkhu arahaṃ…pe… sammadaññā vimutto, so tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati, te ca na evarūpā. Tasmā nesaṃ viññū nānujānanti.

Arahantiādipadesu cettha kilesānaṃ ārakattādīhi kāraṇehi arahaṃ. Āsavānaṃ khīṇattā khīṇāsavo. Satta sekkhā puthujjanakalyāṇakā ca brahmacariyavāsaṃ vasanti nāma. Ayaṃ pana vutthavāsoti vusitavā. Catūhi maggehi catūsu saccesu parijānanādikaraṇīyaṃ kataṃ assāti katakaraṇīyo. Kilesabhāro ca khandhabhāro ca ohito assāti ohitabhāro. Ohitoti ohārito. Sundaro attho, sako vā attho sadattho, anuppatto sadattho etenāti anuppattasadattho. Bhavasaṃyojanaṃ vuccati taṇhā, sā parikkhīṇā assāti parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano. Sammadaññā vimuttoti sammā hetunā kāraṇena jānitvā vimutto. Janetasminti jane etasmiṃ, imasmiṃ loketi attho. Diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañcāti idhattabhāve ca parattabhāve.

Araha arahaṃ. khīṇāsavo vusitavā. katakaraṇīyo. ohitabhāro. anuppattasadattho. parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano. Sammadaññā vimutto Janetasmi Diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañcā
commentary_english:
116. "While living amongst those involved in both" means while living having become mixed, mingled in both.

In which both? In the case of dark and bright *dharmas*, both those despised by the wise and those praised by the wise.

"Whatever *brāhmaṇas* said in this regard" means even while living in these dark and bright *dharmas*, whatever *brāhmaṇas* say like this: "The *brāhmaṇa* is the best caste," and so forth.

"The wise do not approve of that for them" means those who are wise in the world, they do not approve, they do not praise, is the meaning.

"Why is that? In this which begins 'Indeed, for these, Vāseṭṭha'" is the condensed meaning.

That which was said, "They do not approve," why is that? Because of these four castes, whichever *bhikṣu* is an *arhat*… having been released through perfect knowledge, he is declared the foremost of them, and they are not of such a kind.

Therefore, the wise do not approve of that for them.

In the words beginning with "*arahaṃ*," here, because of the reasons such as being far from defilements, [he is an] *arhat*. Because of the destruction of the *āsavas*, [he is] *khīṇāsavo*.

Seven trainees, ordinary worldlings of good character, live the *brahmacarya*. But this one has lived the life, therefore [he is] *vusitavā*. Because he has done what needed to be done, such as completely understanding the four noble truths through the four paths, [he is] *katakaraṇīyo*. Because the burden of defilements and the burden of aggregates have been cast off by him, [he is] *ohitabhāro*. *Ohito* means discarded. Beautiful is the meaning, or one's own meaning is the true meaning; the true meaning has been attained by him, therefore [he is] *anuppattasadattho*. Craving is said to be the bond of existence; that has been completely destroyed by him, therefore [he is] *parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano*. *Sammadaññā vimutto* means released having known through a correct reason, a cause.

*Janetasmiṃ* means in this person, in this world, is the meaning. *Diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañcā* means in this existence and in the future existence.

*arahaṃ*. *khīṇāsavo* *vusitavā*. *katakaraṇīyo*. *ohitabhāro*. *anuppattasadattho*. *parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano*. *sammadaññā vimutto* *janetasmiṃ* *diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañcā*

mula_pali:
117. ‘‘Tadamināpetaṃ, vāseṭṭha, pariyāyena veditabbaṃ, yathā dhammova seṭṭho janetasmiṃ, diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañca.

‘‘Jānāti kho kho pana (ka.), vāseṭṭha, rājā pasenadi kosalo – ‘samaṇo gotamo anantarā anuttaro (bahūsu) sakyakulā pabbajito’ti. Sakyā kho pana, vāseṭṭha, rañño pasenadissa kosalassa anuyuttā anantarā anuyantā (syā.), anantarā anuyuttā (ka.) bhavanti. Karonti kho, vāseṭṭha, sakyā raññe pasenadimhi kosale nipaccakāraṃ abhivādanaṃ paccuṭṭhānaṃ añjalikammaṃ sāmīcikammaṃ. Iti kho, vāseṭṭha, yaṃ karonti sakyā raññe pasenadimhi kosale nipaccakāraṃ abhivādanaṃ paccuṭṭhānaṃ añjalikammaṃ sāmīcikammaṃ, karoti taṃ rājā pasenadi kosalo tathāgate nipaccakāraṃ abhivādanaṃ paccuṭṭhānaṃ añjalikammaṃ sāmīcikammaṃ, na naṃ nanu (bahūsu) ‘sujāto samaṇo gotamo, dujjātohamasmi. Balavā samaṇo gotamo, dubbalohamasmi. Pāsādiko samaṇo gotamo, dubbaṇṇohamasmi. Mahesakkho samaṇo gotamo, appesakkhohamasmī’ti. Atha kho naṃ dhammaṃyeva sakkaronto dhammaṃ garuṃ karonto dhammaṃ mānento dhammaṃ pūjento dhammaṃ apacāyamāno evaṃ rājā pasenadi kosalo tathāgate nipaccakāraṃ karoti, abhivādanaṃ paccuṭṭhānaṃ añjalikammaṃ sāmīcikammaṃ. Imināpi kho etaṃ, vāseṭṭha, pariyāyena veditabbaṃ, yathā dhammova seṭṭho janetasmiṃ, diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañca.

kho pana (ka.) anuttaro (bahūsu) anantarā anuyantā (syā.), anantarā anuyuttā (ka.) nanu (bahūsu)
mula_english:
117. "This illustration will make clear to you, Vāseṭṭha, how Dhamma is best in this world and in the next.

Vāseṭṭha, King Pasenadi of Kosala knows that ‘The ascetic Gotama went forth from the Sakyan clan.’ Now, Vāseṭṭha, the Sakyans are subservient to King Pasenadi of Kosala. Vāseṭṭha, the Sakyans offer King Pasenadi of Kosala humble service (nipaccakāraṃ), salutation (abhivādanaṃ), rising (paccuṭṭhānaṃ), homage with joined palms (añjalikammaṃ), and fitting service (sāmīcikammaṃ). Thus, Vāseṭṭha, King Pasenadi of Kosala offers the same humble service, salutation, rising, homage with joined palms, and fitting service to the Tathāgata as the Sakyans offer to King Pasenadi of Kosala, not [thinking]: ‘The ascetic Gotama is well-born, and I am ill-born; the ascetic Gotama is strong, and I am weak; the ascetic Gotama is pleasant to look at, and I am ill-favoured; the ascetic Gotama is influential, and I am of little influence.’ But rather, honouring the Dhamma, making much of the Dhamma, esteeming the Dhamma, doing reverent homage to the Dhamma, King Pasenadi of Kosala does humble service, salutation, rising, homage with joined palms, and fitting service to the Tathāgata. This illustration also will make clear to you, Vāseṭṭha, how Dhamma is best in this world and in the next.
commentary_pali: 117.Anantarāti antaravirahitā, attano kulena sadisāti attho. Anuyuttāti vasavattino. Nipaccakāranti mahallakatarā nipaccakāraṃ dassenti. Daharatarā abhivādanādīni karonti. Tattha sāmīcikammanti taṃtaṃvattakaraṇādi anucchavikakammaṃ.
commentary_english:
117. *anantarā* means without an interval, similar to one's own family, is the meaning.

*anuyuttā* means those who possess power.

*nipaccakāra* means the elders show *nipaccakāra*.

The younger ones perform salutations and so forth (*abhivādanādīni karonti*).

There, *sāmīcikamma* means doing what is appropriate, etc., doing what is suitable.

mula_pali: 118. ‘‘Tumhe khvattha, vāseṭṭha, nānājaccā nānānāmā nānāgottā nānākulā agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā. ‘Ke tumhe’ti – puṭṭhā samānā ‘samaṇā sakyaputtiyāmhā’ti – paṭijānātha. Yassa kho panassa, vāseṭṭha, tathāgate saddhā niviṭṭhā mūlajātā patiṭṭhitā daḷhā asaṃhāriyā samaṇena vā brāhmaṇena vā devena vā mārena vā brahmunā vā kenaci vā lokasmiṃ, tassetaṃ kallaṃ vacanāya – ‘bhagavatomhi putto oraso mukhato jāto dhammajo dhammanimmito dhammadāyādo’ti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Tathāgatassa hetaṃ, vāseṭṭha, adhivacanaṃ ‘dhammakāyo’ itipi, ‘brahmakāyo’ itipi, ‘dhammabhūto’ itipi, ‘brahmabhūto’ itipi.
mula_english:
118. Vāseṭṭha, all of you, though of different birth ( *nānājaccā* ), name (*nānānāmā*), clan (*nānāgottā*) and family (*nānākulā*), have gone forth from the household life (*agārasmā*) into homelessness (*anagāriyaṃ pabbajitā*).

If asked "Who are you? (*ke tumhe*)," you should reply: "We are ascetics (*samaṇā*), followers of the Sakyan (*sakyaputtiyāmhā*)."

He whose faith (*saddhā*) in the *Tathāgata* is settled (*niviṭṭhā*), rooted (*mūlajātā*), established (*patiṭṭhitā*), solid (*daḷhā*), unshakeable (*asaṃhāriyā*) by any ascetic (*samaṇena*) or *Brāhmaṇa* (*brāhmaṇena*) or deva (*devena*) or *Māra* (*mārena*) or *Brahmā* (*brahmunā*) or anyone (*kenaci*) in the world (*lokasmiṃ*), can truly say: “I am a true son (*putto oraso*) of the Blessed One (*bhagavato*), born of his mouth (*mukhato jāto*), born of the *Dharma* (*dhammajo*), created by the *Dharma* (*dhammanimmito*), an heir of the *Dharma* (*dhammadāyādo*).”

Why is this? Because this is the designation (*adhivacanaṃ*) of the *Tathāgata*, Vāseṭṭha: “*Dharmakāya*,” “*Brahmakāya*,” “*Dharmabhūta*,” “*Brahmabhūta*.”
commentary_pali:
118.Niviṭṭhāti abhiniviṭṭhā acalaṭṭhitā. Kassa pana evarūpā saddhā hotīti? Sotāpannassa. So hi niviṭṭhasaddho asinā sīse chejjamānepi buddho abuddhoti vā, dhammo adhammoti vā, saṅgho asaṅghoti vā na vadati. Patiṭṭhitasaddho hoti sūrambaṭṭho viya.

So kira satthu dhammadesanaṃ sutvā sotāpanno hutvā gehaṃ agamāsi. Atha māro dvattiṃsavaralakkhaṇappaṭimaṇḍitaṃ buddharūpaṃ māpetvā tassa gharadvāre ṭhatvā ‘‘satthā āgato’’ti sāsanaṃ pahiṇi. Sūrambaṭṭho cintesi ‘‘ahaṃ idāneva satthu santike dhammaṃ sutvā āgato, kiṃ nu kho bhavissatī’’ti upasaṅkamitvā satthusaññāya vanditvā aṭṭhāsi. Māro āha – ‘‘ambaṭṭha, yaṃ te mayā ‘rūpaṃ aniccaṃ…pe… viññāṇaṃ aniccanti kathitaṃ, taṃ dukkathitaṃ. Anupadhāretvāva hi mayā evaṃ vuttaṃ. Tasmā tvaṃ ‘rūpaṃ niccaṃ…pe… viññāṇaṃ nicca’nti gaṇhāhī’’ti. So cintesi – ‘‘aṭṭhānametaṃ yaṃ buddhā anupadhāretvā apaccakkhaṃ katvā kiñci katheyyuṃ, addhā ayaṃ mayhaṃ vicchindajananatthaṃ māro āgato’’ti. Tato naṃ ‘‘tvaṃ mārosī’’ti āha. So musāvādaṃ kātuṃ nāsakkhi. ‘‘Āma mārosmī’’ti paṭijānāti. ‘‘Kasmā āgatosī’’ti? Tava saddhācālanatthanti āha. ‘‘Kaṇha pāpima, tvaṃ tāva eko tiṭṭha, tādisānaṃ mārānaṃ satampi sahassampi satasahassampi mama saddhaṃ cāletuṃ asamatthaṃ, maggena āgatasaddhā nāma thirā silāpathaviyaṃ patiṭṭhitasineru viya acalā hoti, kiṃ tvaṃ etthā’’ti accharaṃ pahari. So ṭhātuṃ asakkonto tattheva antaradhāyi. Evarūpaṃ saddhaṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ ‘‘niviṭṭhā’’ti.

Mūlajātāpatiṭṭhitāti maggamūlassa sañjātattā tena maggamūlena patiṭṭhitā. Daḷhāti thirā. Asaṃhāriyāti sunikhātaindakhīlo viya kenaci cāletuṃ asakkuṇeyyā. Tassetaṃ kallaṃ vacanāyāti tassa ariyasāvakassa yuttametaṃ vattuṃ. Kinti? ‘‘Bhagavatomhi putto oraso’’ti evamādi. So hi bhagavantaṃ nissāya ariyabhūmiyaṃ jātoti bhagavato putto. Ure vasitvā mukhato nikkhantadhammaghosavasena maggaphalesu patiṭṭhitattā oraso mukhato jāto. Ariyadhammato jātattā ariyadhammena ca nimmitattā dhammajo dhammanimmito. Navalokuttaradhammadāyajjaṃ arahatīti dhammadāyādo. Taṃ kissa hetūti yadetaṃ ‘‘bhagavatomhi putto’’ti vatvā ‘‘dhammajo dhammanimmito’’ti vuttaṃ, taṃ kasmāti ce? Idānissa atthaṃ dassento tathāgatassa hetantiādimāha. Tattha ‘‘dhammakāyo itipī’’ti kasmā tathāgato ‘‘dhammakāyo’’ti vutto? Tathāgato hi tepiṭakaṃ buddhavacanaṃ hadayena cintetvā vācāya abhinīhari. Tenassa kāyo dhammamayattā dhammova. Iti dhammo kāyo assāti dhammakāyo. Dhammakāyattā eva brahmakāyo. Dhammo hi seṭṭhatthena brahmāti vuccati. Dhammabhūtoti dhammasabhāvo. Dhammabhūtattā eva brahmabhūto.

Mūlajātā patiṭṭhitā Daḷhā Asaṃhāriyā Tassetaṃ kallaṃ vacanāyā bhagavato putto. oraso mukhato jāto. dhammajo dhammanimmito. dhammadāyādo. Taṃ kissa hetū tathāgatassa heta dhammakāyo. brahmakāyo. Dhammabhūto brahmabhūto.
commentary_english:
118. "Firmly fixed" means thoroughly fixed, unshakeably established.

Whose is such faith? A stream-enterer's.

For, being firmly fixed in faith, even when his head is being cut off with a sword, he would not say, "The Buddha is not awakened," or "The Dharma is not the Dharma," or "The Saṅgha is not the Saṅgha."

He is established in faith, like Sūrambaṭṭha.

Sūrambaṭṭha, having heard the Dharma teaching of the Teacher, became a stream-enterer and went home. Then Māra, having fashioned a Buddha-image adorned with the thirty-two excellent marks, stood at the door of his house and sent a message, "The Teacher has arrived." Sūrambaṭṭha thought, "I have just now come, having heard the Dharma in the presence of the Teacher; what now could this be?" Approaching, reverently saluting it in the thought that it was the Teacher, he stood there.

Māra said: "Ambaṭṭha, what was said by me to you, 'Form is impermanent... and so on... consciousness is impermanent,' that was badly said. For I spoke thus without reflection. Therefore, you should accept 'Form is permanent... and so on... consciousness is permanent.'"

He thought: "This is impossible, that Buddhas, without reflection, having made no direct experience, should say anything. Truly, this Māra has come for the purpose of destroying my generation."

Then he said to him, "You are Māra!"

He was unable to speak a falsehood.

"Yes, I am Māra," he acknowledged.

"Why have you come?" "To shake your faith," he said.

"Kaṇha, evil one, you just stand there! Even a hundred, a thousand, a hundred thousand Māras like you are unable to shake my faith. The faith that has come by way of the path is steady, like Mount Sineru, established on the solid rock-earth. What are you here for?" He hurled an acchara (?).

Unable to stand, he vanished right there.

With reference to such faith, this was said: "Firmly fixed."

Root-born, established, means: because of its arising from the root of the path, it is established by that root of the path.

"Strong" means steady.

"Unshakeable" means: like an Aindra pillar well-sunk, it could not be shaken by anyone.

"This is fitting for utterance by him" means: it is proper for that noble disciple to say this.

What? "I am a legitimate son of the Blessed One," and so on.

For, having relied on the Blessed One, he is born in the noble ground; therefore, he is a son of the Blessed One.

Having dwelt in the breast, by way of the sound of the Dharma issuing from the mouth, he is established in the fruits of the path; therefore, he is legitimate, born from the mouth.

Having been born from the noble Dharma, and having been fashioned by the noble Dharma, he is Dharma-born, Dharma-fashioned.

He is worthy of the inheritance of the nine supramundane Dharmas; therefore, he is a Dharma-heir.

"Why is that?" Because this was said: "I am a legitimate son of the Blessed One," having said "Dharma-born, Dharma-fashioned" what is the reason for that? Now, showing its meaning, he said, "A cause of the Tathāgata," and so on.

There, "The Dharma-body, and so on," why is the Tathāgata called "Dharma-body"? The Tathāgata, having thought with his heart, brings forth with his voice the Buddha-word which is the Tipiṭaka.

Therefore, his body is Dharma-made, Dharma itself.

Thus, Dharma is his body; therefore, "Dharma-body."

By virtue of being a Dharma-body, he is indeed a Brahma-body.

For Dharma, in the sense of excellence, is called Brahma.

"Dharma-become" means having the nature of Dharma.

By virtue of being Dharma-become, he is indeed Brahma-become.

Root-born.
Firm, strong, unshakeable.
This is fit for speech.
A son of the Blessed One,
born of his breast, born of his mouth,
Dharma-born, Dharma-created,
a Dharma-heir.
For what reason? Because the body of the *Tathāgata* is a Dharma-body, a Brahma-body, Dharma-become, Brahma-become.

mula_pali:
119. ‘‘Hoti kho so, vāseṭṭha, samayo yaṃ kadāci karahaci dīghassa addhuno accayena ayaṃ loko saṃvaṭṭati. Saṃvaṭṭamāne loke yebhuyyena sattā ābhassarasaṃvattanikā honti. Te tattha honti manomayā pītibhakkhā sayaṃpabhā antalikkhacarā subhaṭṭhāyino ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ tiṭṭhanti.

‘‘Hoti kho so, vāseṭṭha, samayo yaṃ kadāci karahaci dīghassa addhuno accayena ayaṃ loko vivaṭṭati. Vivaṭṭamāne loke yebhuyyena sattā ābhassarakāyā cavitvā itthattaṃ āgacchanti. Tedha honti manomayā pītibhakkhā sayaṃpabhā antalikkhacarā subhaṭṭhāyino ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ tiṭṭhanti.

Rasapathavipātubhāvo
mula_english:
‘There comes a time, Vāseṭṭha, when, sooner or later after a long period, this world contracts (saṃvaṭṭati). While the world is contracting (saṃvaṭṭamāne loke), beings for the most part are reborn in the Ābhassara Brahma-world (ābhassarasaṃvattanikā honti). There they dwell, mind-made (manomayā), feeding on rapture (pītibhakkhā), self-luminous (sayaṃpabhā), moving through the air (antalikkhacarā), abiding in glory (subhaṭṭhāyino), and they stay like that for a very long time (ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ tiṭṭhanti).

But sooner or later, Vāseṭṭha, after a very long period, this world begins to expand again (vivaṭṭati). When this world expands (vivaṭṭamāne loke), beings for the most part, having passed away from the Ābhassara Brahma-world (ābhassarakāyā cavitvā), come to this world (itthattaṃ āgacchanti). Here they dwell, mind-made (manomayā), feeding on rapture (pītibhakkhā), self-luminous (sayaṃpabhā), moving through the air (antalikkhacarā), abiding in glory (subhaṭṭhāyino), and they stay like that for a very long time (ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ tiṭṭhanti).

The appearance of a change of taste.
commentary_pali:
119. Ettāvatā bhagavā seṭṭhacchedakavādaṃ dassetvā idāni aparenapi nayena seṭṭhacchedakavādameva dassetuṃ hoti kho so, vāseṭṭha, samayotiādimāha. Tattha saṃvaṭṭavivaṭṭakathā brahmajāle vitthāritāva. Itthattaṃ āgacchantīti itthabhāvaṃ manussattaṃ āgacchanti. Tedha honti manomayāti te idha manussaloke nibbattamānāpi opapātikā hutvā maneneva nibbattāti manomayā. Brahmaloke viya idhāpi nesaṃ pītiyeva āhārakiccaṃ sādhetīti pītibhakkhā. Eteneva nayena sayaṃpabhādīnipi veditabbānīti.

Rasapathavipātubhāvavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
119. Thus far, the Blessed One, having shown the doctrine of the division into superior and inferior, now, by another method, in order to show the doctrine of the division into superior and inferior, said, "There comes a time, Vāseṭṭha," and so forth.

There, the talk of the cycle of contraction and expansion is already extensively explained in the *Brahmajāla*.

"*Coming to this state*" means coming to this condition, to human existence (manuṣyatta).

"*They are here, mind-made*" means, even though they are reborn here in the human world (manuṣyaloke), they are spontaneously born (opapātikā), reborn by the mind alone, thus mind-made (manomayā).

Just as in the Brahma world (brahmaloke), here also, joy (pīti) alone accomplishes the function of nourishment for them, thus "*nourished by joy* (pītibhakkhā)."

By this same method, *sayaṃpabhā* and the others should be understood.

Explanation of the appearance of the downfall in the path of taste (rasapathavipātubhāvavaṇṇanā).

mula_pali:
120. ‘‘Ekodakībhūtaṃ kho pana, vāseṭṭha, tena samayena hoti andhakāro andhakāratimisā . Na candimasūriyā paññāyanti, na nakkhattāni tārakarūpāni paññāyanti, na rattindivā paññāyanti, na māsaḍḍhamāsā paññāyanti, na utusaṃvaccharā paññāyanti , na itthipumā paññāyanti, sattā sattātveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchanti. Atha kho tesaṃ, vāseṭṭha, sattānaṃ kadāci karahaci dīghassa addhuno accayena rasapathavī udakasmiṃ samatani samatāni (bahūsu); seyyathāpi nāma payaso tattassa payatattassa (syā.) nibbāyamānassa upari santānakaṃ hoti, evameva pāturahosi. Sā ahosi vaṇṇasampannā gandhasampannā rasasampannā, seyyathāpi nāma sampannaṃ vā sappi sampannaṃ vā navanītaṃ evaṃvaṇṇā ahosi. Seyyathāpi nāma khuddamadhuṃ khuddaṃ madhuṃ (ka. sī.) aneḷakaṃ anelakaṃ (sī. pī.), evamassādā ahosi. Atha kho, vāseṭṭha, aññataro satto lolajātiko – ‘ambho, kimevidaṃ bhavissatī’ti rasapathaviṃ aṅguliyā sāyi. Tassa rasapathaviṃ aṅguliyā sāyato acchādesi, taṇhā cassa okkami. Aññepi kho, vāseṭṭha, sattā tassa sattassa diṭṭhānugatiṃ āpajjamānā rasapathaviṃ aṅguliyā sāyiṃsu. Tesaṃ rasapathaviṃ aṅguliyā sāyataṃ acchādesi, taṇhā ca tesaṃ okkami.

Candimasūriyādipātubhāvo
mula_english:
120. At that time, Vāseṭṭha, there was a single mass of water, darkness, and dense darkness. Neither moon nor sun appeared, no constellations or stars appeared, night and day were not distinguished, nor months and fortnights, no years or seasons, no male and female appeared, beings being reckoned just as beings.

Then, Vāseṭṭha, after a long time, sooner or later that savory earth formed on the water. Just as a skin forms on top of hot milk as it cools, just so it appeared. It was endowed with colour, smell and taste. It was the colour of fine ghee or butter. It was very sweet, like pure wild honey.

Then some being of a greedy nature said: “I say, what can this be?" and tasted the savory earth on its finger. In so doing, it became taken with the flavour, and craving arose in it. Then other beings, taking their cue from that one, also tasted the stuff with their fingers. They too were taken with the flavour, and craving arose in them.

The Appearance of the Moon, Sun, and So On
commentary_pali:
120.Ekodakībhūtanti sabbaṃ cakkavāḷaṃ ekodakameva bhūtaṃ. Andhakāroti tamo. Andhakāratimisāti cakkhuviññāṇuppattinivāraṇena andhabhāvakaraṇaṃ bahalatamaṃ. Samatanīti patiṭṭhahi samantato patthari. Payasotattassāti tattassa khīrassa. Vaṇṇasampannāti vaṇṇena sampannā. Kaṇikārapupphasadiso hissā vaṇṇo ahosi. Gandhasampannāti gandhena sampannā dibbagandhaṃ vāyati. Rasasampannāti rasena sampannā pakkhittadibbojā viya hoti. Khuddamadhunti khuddakamakkhikāhi katamadhuṃ. Aneḷakanti niddosaṃ makkhikaṇḍakavirahitaṃ. Lolajātikoti lolasabhāvo. Atītānantarepi kappe loloyeva. Ambhoti acchariyajāto āha. Kimevidaṃ bhavissatīti vaṇṇopissā manāpo gandhopi, raso panassā kīdiso bhavissatīti attho. Yo tattha uppannalobho, so rasapathaviṃ aṅguliyā sāyi, aṅguliyā gahetvā jivhagge ṭhapesi.

Acchādesīti jivhagge ṭhapitamattā satta rasaharaṇīsahassāni pharitvā manāpā hutvā tiṭṭhati. Taṇhā cassa okkamīti tattha cassa taṇhā uppajji.

Acchādesī Taṇhā cassa okkamī

Candimasūriyādipātubhāvavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
120. "Eko-dakībhūta" means the entire *cakkavāḷa* became of one water.
"Andhakāro" means darkness (tamas).
"Andhakāratimisā" means the densest darkness preventing the arising of eye-consciousness, making one blind.
"Samatanī" means it was established, spread out everywhere.
"Payaso," "tattassā" means of hot milk (*khīrassa*).
"Vaṇṇasampannā" means endowed with color.
Its color was like that of a *kaṇikāra* flower.
"Gandhasampannā" means endowed with smell, it emits divine fragrance (dibbagandhaṃ vāyati).
"Rasasampannā" means endowed with taste, it is like divine ambrosia that has been placed [there].
"Khuddamadhu" means honey made by small bees (*khuddakamakkhikāhi katamadhuṃ*).
"Aneḷaka" means faultless, free from bee-larvae (*makkhikaṇḍakavirahitaṃ*).
"Lolajātiko" means having a restless nature (lolasabhāvo).
Even in a past, uninterrupted eon, he was only restless (loloyeva).
"Ambho" is an exclamation expressing amazement.
"Kimevidaṃ bhavissatī" the color of it is pleasing, and the smell also, but what will its taste be? This is the meaning.
He, overcome by greed that arose there, tasted the taste-earth (rasapathaviṃ) with his finger (aṅguliyā), having taken [some] with his finger (aṅguliyā gahetvā), he placed it on the tip of his tongue (jivhagge ṭhapesi).

"Acchādesī" means as soon as it is placed on the tip of the tongue (jivhagge ṭhapitamattā), it spreads through seven thousand taste-nerves (satta rasaharaṇīsahassāni pharitvā), becoming pleasing, it remains.
"Taṇhā cassa okkamī" means craving arose in him there (tattha cassa taṇhā uppajji).

"Acchādesī taṇhā cassa okkamī" is a description of the appearance of the moon, sun, etc. (candimasūriyādipātubhāvavaṇṇanā).

mula_pali: 121. ‘‘Atha kho te, vāseṭṭha, sattā rasapathaviṃ hatthehi āluppakārakaṃ upakkamiṃsu paribhuñjituṃ. Yato kho te yato kho (sī. syā. pī.), vāseṭṭha, sattā rasapathaviṃ hatthehi āluppakārakaṃ upakkamiṃsu paribhuñjituṃ. Atha tesaṃ sattānaṃ sayaṃpabhā antaradhāyi. Sayaṃpabhāya antarahitāya candimasūriyā pāturahesuṃ. Candimasūriyesu pātubhūtesu nakkhattāni tārakarūpāni pāturahesuṃ. Nakkhattesu tārakarūpesu pātubhūtesu rattindivā paññāyiṃsu. Rattindivesu paññāyamānesu māsaḍḍhamāsā paññāyiṃsu. Māsaḍḍhamāsesu paññāyamānesu utusaṃvaccharā paññāyiṃsu. Ettāvatā kho , vāseṭṭha, ayaṃ loko puna vivaṭṭo hoti.
mula_english:
121. Then, Vāseṭṭha, those beings set to with their hands, breaking off pieces of the savory earth (*rasapathaviṃ*) in order to eat it.

Because, Vāseṭṭha, those beings set to with their hands, breaking off pieces of the savory earth (*rasapathaviṃ*) in order to eat it, their self-luminance (*sayaṃpabhā*) disappeared. As a result of the disappearance of their self-luminance (*sayaṃpabhāya*), the moon and the sun (*candimasūriyā*) appeared. After the appearance of the moon and sun (*candimasūriyesu*), the stars (*nakkhattāni*) appeared in their constellations (*tārakarūpāni*). After the appearance of the stars (*nakkhattesu*) in their constellations (*tārakarūpesu*), night and day (*rattindivā*) were distinguished. As night and day (*rattindivesu*) were distinguished, months and fortnights (*māsaḍḍhamāsā*) appeared. As months and fortnights (*māsaḍḍhamāsesu*) appeared, seasons and years (*utusaṃvaccharā*) were distinguished. To that extent, Vāseṭṭha, the world re-evolved.
commentary_pali:
121.Āluppakārakaṃ upakkamiṃsu paribhuñjitunti ālopaṃ katvā piṇḍe piṇḍe chinditvā paribhuñjituṃ ārabhiṃsu. Candimasūriyāti candimā ca sūriyo ca. Pāturahesunti pātubhaviṃsu.

Ko pana tesaṃ paṭhamaṃ pātubhavi, ko kasmiṃ vasati, kassa kiṃ pamāṇaṃ, ko upari, ko sīghaṃ gacchati, kati nesaṃ vīthiyo, kathaṃ caranti, kittake ṭhāne ālokaṃ karontīti? Ubho ekato pātubhavanti. Sūriyo paṭhamataraṃ paññāyati. Tesañhi sattānaṃ sayaṃpabhāya antarahitāya andhakāro ahosi. Te bhītatasitā ‘‘bhaddakaṃ vatassa sace āloko pātubhaveyyā’’ti cintayiṃsu. Tato mahājanassa sūrabhāvaṃ janayamānaṃ sūriyamaṇḍalaṃ uṭṭhahi. Tenevassa sūriyoti nāmaṃ ahosi. Tasmiṃ divasaṃ ālokaṃ katvā atthaṅgate puna andhakāro ahosi. Te ‘‘bhaddakaṃ vatassa sace añño āloko uppajjeyyā’’ti cintayiṃsu. Atha nesaṃ chandaṃ ñatvāva candamaṇḍalaṃ uṭṭhahi. Tenevassa candoti nāmaṃ ahosi.

Tesu cando antomaṇivimāne vasati. Taṃ bahi rajatena parikkhittaṃ . Ubhayampi sītalameva ahosi. Sūriyo antokanakavimāne vasati. Taṃ bāhiraṃ phalikaparikkhittaṃ hoti. Ubhayampi uṇhameva.

Pamāṇato cando ujukaṃ ekūnapaññāsayojano. Parimaṇḍalato tīhi yojanehi ūnadiyaḍḍhasatayojano. Sūriyo ujukaṃ paññāsayojano, parimaṇḍalato diyaḍḍhasatayojano.

Cando heṭṭhā, sūriyo upari, antarā nesaṃ yojanaṃ hoti. Candassa heṭṭhimantato sūriyassa uparimantato yojanasataṃ hoti.

Cando ujukaṃ saṇikaṃ gacchati, tiriyaṃ sīghaṃ. Dvīsu passesu nakkhattatārakā gacchanti. Cando dhenu viya vacchaṃ taṃ taṃ nakkhattaṃ upasaṅkamati. Nakkhattāni pana attano ṭhānaṃ na vijahanti. Sūriyassa ujukaṃ gamanaṃ sīghaṃ, tiriyaṃ gamanaṃ dandhaṃ. So kāḷapakkhauposathato pāṭipadadivase yojanānaṃ satasahassaṃ candamaṇḍalaṃ ohāya gacchati. Atha cando lekhā viya paññāyati. Pakkhassa dutiyāya satasahassanti evaṃ yāva uposathadivasā satasahassaṃ satasahassaṃ ohāya gacchati. Atha cando anukkamena vaḍḍhitvā uposathadivase paripuṇṇo hoti. Puna pāṭipadadivase yojanānaṃ satasahassaṃ dhāvitvā gaṇhāti. Dutiyāya satasahassanti evaṃ yāva uposathadivasā satasahassaṃ satasahassaṃ dhāvitvā gaṇhāti. Atha cando anukkamena hāyitvā uposathadivase sabbaso na paññāyati. Candaṃ heṭṭhā katvā sūriyo upari hoti. Mahatiyā pātiyā khuddakabhājanaṃ viya candamaṇḍalaṃ pidhīyati. Majjhanhike gehacchāyā viya candassa chāyā na paññāyati. So chāyāya apaññāyamānāya dūre ṭhitānaṃ divā padīpo viya sayampi na paññāyati.

Kati nesaṃ vīthiyoti ettha pana ajavīthi, nāgavīthi, govīthīti tisso vīthiyo honti. Tattha ajānaṃ udakaṃ paṭikūlaṃ hoti, hatthināgānaṃ manāpaṃ. Gunnaṃ sītuṇhasamatāya phāsu hoti. Tasmā yaṃ kālaṃ candimasūriyā ajavīthiṃ āruhanti, tadā devo ekabindumpi na vassati. Yadā nāgavīthiṃ ārohanti, tadā bhinnaṃ viya nabhaṃ paggharati. Yadā govīthiṃ ārohanti, tadā utusamatā sampajjati. Candimasūriyā chamāse sineruto bahi nikkhamanti, chamāse anto vicaranti. Te hi āsāḷhamāse sinerusamīpena vicaranti. Tato pare dve māse nikkhamitvā bahi vicarantā paṭhamakattikamāse majjhena gacchanti. Tato cakkavāḷābhimukhā gantvā tayo māse cakkavāḷasamīpena caritvā puna nikkhamitvā citramāse majjhena gantvā tato dve māse sinerubhimukhā pakkhanditvā puna āsāḷhe sinerusamīpena caranti.

Kittake ṭhāne ālokaṃ karontīti? Ekappahārena tīsu dīpesu ālokaṃ karonti. Kathaṃ? Imasmiñhi dīpe sūriyuggamanakālo pubbavidehe majjhanhiko hoti, uttarakurūsu atthaṅgamanakālo, aparagoyāne majjhimayāmo. Pubbavidehamhi uggamanakālo uttarakurūsu majjhanhiko, aparagoyāne atthaṅgamanakālo, idha majjhimayāmo. Uttarakurūsu uggamanakālo aparagoyāne majjhanhiko, idha atthaṅgamanakālo, pubbavidehe majjhimayāmo. Aparagoyānadīpe uggamanakālo idha majjhanhiko, pubbavidehe atthaṅgamanakālo, uttarakurūsu majjhimayāmoti.

Nakkhattānitārakarūpānīti kattikādinakkhattāni ceva sesatārakarūpāni ca candimasūriyehi saddhiṃyeva pāturahesuṃ. Rattindivāti tato sūriyatthaṅgamanato yāva aruṇuggamanā ratti, aruṇuggamanato yāva sūriyatthaṅgamanā divāti evaṃ rattindivā paññāyiṃsu. Atha pañcadasa rattiyo aḍḍhamāso, dve aḍḍhamāsā māsoti evaṃ māsaḍḍhamāsā paññāyiṃsu. Atha cattāro māsā utu, tayo utū saṃvaccharoti evaṃ utusaṃvaccharā paññāyiṃsu.

Nakkhattāni tārakarūpānī Rattindivā
commentary_english:
121. “*Āluppakārakaṃ upakkamiṃsu paribhuñjitu*” means they began to consume [it] by making a morsel, cutting [it] into pieces. "*Candimasūriyā*" means the moon (*candimā*) and the sun (*sūriya*). "*Pāturahesu*" means they became visible. What first became visible among them, where does [each] dwell, what is the measure of each, which is above, which moves quickly, how many paths do they have, how do they travel, in how much space do they make light? Both become visible at the same time. The sun is perceived earlier. For those beings, when their inherent radiance disappeared, there was darkness. Those who were frightened and alarmed thought, "It would be good if light would appear." Then the solar orb (*sūriyamaṇḍalaṃ*), generating the state of being the sun, arose for the great multitude. Therefore, his name became Sun (*sūriyo*). Having made light during the day, when it set, again there was darkness. They thought, "It would be good if another light would arise." Then, having known their desire, the lunar orb (*candamaṇḍalaṃ*) arose. Therefore, his name became Moon (*cando*). Among them, the moon dwells in an inner jeweled mansion (*antomaṇivimāne*). That is surrounded on the outside by silver. Both were cool. The sun dwells in an inner golden mansion (*antokanakavimāne*). That is surrounded on the outside by crystal. Both were hot. In measure, the moon is directly forty-nine *yojanas* less one. In circumference, [it is] one hundred and fifty *yojanas* less three *yojanas*. The sun is directly fifty *yojanas*, in circumference one hundred and fifty *yojanas*. The moon is below, the sun is above; between them there is one *yojana*. From the lowest point of the moon to the highest point of the sun, there are one hundred *yojanas*. The moon moves slowly directly, quickly across. The constellation stars move in two directions. The moon approaches each constellation just as a cow [approaches] her calf. But the constellations do not leave their own place. The sun’s direct movement is fast, its transverse movement is slow. From the *kāḷapakkhauposatha* to the day of the *pāṭipada*, the lunar orb descends a hundred thousand *yojanas*. Then the moon appears like a line. On the second day of the [lunar] fortnight, one hundred thousand, thus until the *uposatha* day, it descends a hundred thousand, a hundred thousand. Then the moon, gradually increasing, is full on the *uposatha* day. Again, on the *pāṭipada* day, it runs and takes a hundred thousand *yojanas*. For the second hundred thousand, in this way, up to the **uposatha** day, having run a hundred thousand, a hundred thousand, he takes. Then the moon, gradually waning, on the **uposatha** day, is not seen at all. Having made the moon below, the sun is above. The lunar orb is covered by a large bowl, like a small vessel. At midday, the moon's shadow is not seen, like the shadow of a house. Because its shadow is not seen, even the lamp during the day is not seen by those standing far away.

How many paths are there for them? Here, however, there are three paths: the Goat Path ( *ajavīthi* ), the Serpent Path ( *nāgavīthi* ), and the Cow Path ( *govīthi* ). There, water is unfavorable to goats, but pleasing to elephant-serpents. For cows, comfort comes from the equilibrium of heat and cold. Therefore, at whatever time the moon and sun ascend the Goat Path, the god does not rain even a drop. When they ascend the Serpent Path, the sky pours down as if broken. When they ascend the Cow Path, then seasonal harmony is achieved. The moon and sun go out beyond Mount Meru ( *sineru* ) for six months, and for six months they wander within. Indeed, in the month of Āsāḷha, they wander near Mount Meru. Then, going out for two more months, wandering outside, they go through the middle in the first month of Kattika. Then, going towards the **cakkavāḷa**, for three months near the **cakkavāḷa**, after acting, again going out, in the month of Citra, going through the middle, then for two months, having moved towards Mount Meru, again in Āsāḷha, they act near Mount Meru.

How much space do they illuminate? With a single strike, they illuminate the three continents. How? In this continent, at the time of sunrise, it is midday in Pūrvavideha, at sunset in Uttarakuru, and midnight ( *majjhimayāma* ) in Aparagoyāna. At sunrise in Pūrvavideha, it is midday in Uttarakuru, at sunset in Aparagoyāna, and midnight here. At sunrise in Uttarakuru, it is midday in Aparagoyāna, at sunset here, and midnight in Pūrvavideha. At sunrise in the Aparagoyāna continent, it is midday here, at sunset in Pūrvavideha, and midnight in Uttarakuru.

Constellations and Star Forms: the constellations beginning with Kattikā, and the remaining star forms, appeared together with the moon and sun. Night and Day: from sunset until the dawn, it is night; from the dawn until sunset, it is day. Thus, night and day were distinguished. Then, fifteen nights are a half-month, two half-months are a month. Thus, months and half-months were distinguished. Then, four months are a season ( *utu* ), three seasons are a year ( *saṃvacchara* ). Thus, seasons and years were distinguished.

Constellations Star Forms Night and Day

mula_pali:
122. ‘‘Atha kho te, vāseṭṭha, sattā rasapathaviṃ paribhuñjantā taṃbhakkhā tabbhakkhā (syā.) tadāhārā ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu. Yathā yathā kho te, vāseṭṭha, sattā rasapathaviṃ paribhuñjantā taṃbhakkhā tadāhārā ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu, tathā tathā tesaṃ sattānaṃ (rasapathaviṃ paribhuñjantānaṃ) ( ) sī. syā. pī. potthakesu natthi kharattañceva kāyasmiṃ okkami, vaṇṇavevaṇṇatā vaṇṇavevajjatā (ṭīkā) ca paññāyittha. Ekidaṃ sattā vaṇṇavanto honti, ekidaṃ sattā dubbaṇṇā. Tattha ye te sattā vaṇṇavanto, te dubbaṇṇe satte atimaññanti – ‘mayametehi vaṇṇavantatarā, amhehete dubbaṇṇatarā’ti. Tesaṃ vaṇṇātimānapaccayā mānātimānajātikānaṃ rasapathavī antaradhāyi. Rasāya pathaviyā antarahitāya sannipatiṃsu. Sannipatitvā anutthuniṃsu – ‘aho rasaṃ, aho rasa’nti! Tadetarahipi manussā kañcideva surasaṃ sādhurasaṃ (sī. syā. pī.) labhitvā evamāhaṃsu – ‘aho rasaṃ, aho rasa’nti! Tadeva porāṇaṃ aggaññaṃ akkharaṃ anusaranti, na tvevassa atthaṃ ājānanti.

Bhūmipappaṭakapātubhāvo
mula_english:
122. Then, Vāseṭṭha, as those beings continued for a long time feasting on the savory earth (rasapathavī), feeding on it and being nourished by it, as they did so, their bodies became coarser, and a difference in looks developed among them. Some beings became good-looking (varṇavanto), others ugly (dubbaṇṇā). And the good-looking ones despised the others, saying: “We are better-looking (varṇavantatarā) than they are, and they are uglier (dubbaṇṇatarā) than we are.” Because they became arrogant and conceited (mānātimānajātikānaṃ) about their looks (varṇātimānapaccayā), the savory earth disappeared (rasapathavī antaradhāyi). With the savory earth gone, they gathered together. Having gathered, they exclaimed: ‘Ah, flavor! Ah, flavor!’ And even today, humans who find some tasty (surasaṃ) thing exclaim: ‘Ah, flavor! Ah, flavor!’ They are following that ancient term aggaññaṃ (aggaññaṃ akkharaṃ), but they do not understand its meaning (atthaṃ ājānanti).

The Appearance of Earth-Fungus (bhūmipappaṭakapātubhāvo)
commentary_pali:
122.Vaṇṇavevaṇṇatā cāti vaṇṇassa vivaṇṇabhāvo. Tesaṃ vaṇṇātimānapaccayāti tesaṃ vaṇṇaṃ ārabbha uppannaatimānapaccayā. Mānātimānajātikānanti punappunaṃ uppajjamānātimānasabhāvānaṃ. Rasāya pathaviyāti sampannarasattā rasāti laddhanāmāya pathaviyā. Anutthuniṃsūti anubhāsiṃsu. Aho rasanti aho amhākaṃ madhurarasaṃ antarahitaṃ. Aggaññaṃ akkharanti lokuppattivaṃsakathaṃ. Anusarantīti anugacchanti.

Bhūmipappaṭakapātubhāvādivaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
"vaṇṇavevaṇṇatā cā" means the state of being discolored from color.

"tesaṃ vaṇṇātimānapaccayā" means due to the excessive pride that arose in them concerning color.

"mānātimānajātikānaṃ" means those whose nature is to repeatedly generate excessive pride.

"rasāya pathaviyā" means of the earth called Rasa, which is endowed with excellent taste.

"anutthuniṃsū" means they spoke.

"aho rasaṃ" means "Oh, taste! Our sweet taste has disappeared!"

"aggaññaṃ akkharaṃ" means the story of the lineage of the world's origin.

"anusarantī" means following.

Description of the appearance of earth-cakes and so forth.

mula_pali:
123. ‘‘Atha kho tesaṃ, vāseṭṭha, sattānaṃ rasāya pathaviyā antarahitāya bhūmipappaṭako pāturahosi. Seyyathāpi nāma ahicchattako, evameva pāturahosi. So ahosi vaṇṇasampanno gandhasampanno rasasampanno, seyyathāpi nāma sampannaṃ vā sappi sampannaṃ vā navanītaṃ evaṃvaṇṇo ahosi. Seyyathāpi nāma khuddamadhuṃ aneḷakaṃ, evamassādo ahosi.

‘‘Atha kho te, vāseṭṭha, sattā bhūmipappaṭakaṃ upakkamiṃsu paribhuñjituṃ. Te taṃ paribhuñjantā taṃbhakkhā tadāhārā ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu. Yathā yathā kho te, vāseṭṭha, sattā bhūmipappaṭakaṃ paribhuñjantā taṃbhakkhā tadāhārā ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu, tathā tathā tesaṃ sattānaṃ bhiyyoso mattāya kharattañceva kāyasmiṃ okkami, vaṇṇavevaṇṇatā ca paññāyittha. Ekidaṃ sattā vaṇṇavanto honti, ekidaṃ sattā dubbaṇṇā. Tattha ye te sattā vaṇṇavanto, te dubbaṇṇe satte atimaññanti – ‘mayametehi vaṇṇavantatarā, amhehete dubbaṇṇatarā’ti. Tesaṃ vaṇṇātimānapaccayā mānātimānajātikānaṃ bhūmipappaṭako antaradhāyi.

Padālatāpātubhāvo
mula_english:
‘And then, Vāseṭṭha, when the savory earth had disappeared for those beings, a mushroom (bhūmipappaṭaka) appeared. Just like a mushroom (ahicchattaka), it appeared in the same way. It was endowed with color (varṇa), endowed with smell (gandha), endowed with taste (rasa), just like fine ghee (sarpis) or fine butter (navanīta), it was of that color (evaṃvarṇa). It had a taste like pure honey (khuddamadhu).

‘And then, Vāseṭṭha, those beings began to consume the mushroom (bhūmipappaṭaka). They continued for a long time feeding on it, eating it, and being nourished by it. As those beings continued for a long time eating the mushroom (bhūmipappaṭaka), feeding on it, and being nourished by it, so their bodies gradually became coarser, and a difference in looks (varṇavevarṇatā) became apparent. Some beings became good-looking (varṇavanto), and some beings became ugly (dubbaṇṇā). Then, those beings who were good-looking despised those beings who were ugly, saying, “We are better-looking than these, and these are uglier than us.” Because of their arrogance (māna) and conceit (atimāna) about their looks (varṇa), the mushroom (bhūmipappaṭaka) disappeared.

Appearance of creepers (padālatāpātubhāvo).
commentary_pali: 123.Evameva pāturahosīti ediso hutvā uṭṭhahi, antovāpiyaṃ udake chinne sukkhakalalapaṭalaṃ viya ca uṭṭhahi.
commentary_english: Just so, *evameva pāturahosī*—thus having become *ediso*, he arose; like a dry embryonic membrane ( *sukkha-kalala-paṭalam*) when the water in the inner well (*antovāpiyaṃ*) has been depleted, he arose.

mula_pali:
124. ‘‘Bhūmipappaṭake antarahite padālatā saddālatā (sī.) pāturahosi, seyyathāpi nāma kalambukā kalambakā (syā.), evameva pāturahosi. Sā ahosi vaṇṇasampannā gandhasampannā rasasampannā, seyyathāpi nāma sampannaṃ vā sappi sampannaṃ vā navanītaṃ evaṃvaṇṇā ahosi. Seyyathāpi nāma khuddamadhuṃ aneḷakaṃ, evamassādā ahosi.

‘‘Atha kho te, vāseṭṭha, sattā padālataṃ upakkamiṃsu paribhuñjituṃ. Te taṃ paribhuñjantā taṃbhakkhā tadāhārā ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu. Yathā yathā kho te, vāseṭṭha, sattā padālataṃ paribhuñjantā taṃbhakkhā tadāhārā ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu, tathā tathā tesaṃ sattānaṃ bhiyyosomattāya kharattañceva kāyasmiṃ okkami, vaṇṇavevaṇṇatā ca paññāyittha. Ekidaṃ sattā vaṇṇavanto honti, ekidaṃ sattā dubbaṇṇā. Tattha ye te sattā vaṇṇavanto, te dubbaṇṇe satte atimaññanti – ‘mayametehi vaṇṇavantatarā, amhehete dubbaṇṇatarā’ti. Tesaṃ vaṇṇātimānapaccayā mānātimānajātikānaṃ padālatā antaradhāyi.

‘‘Padālatāya antarahitāya sannipatiṃsu. Sannipatitvā anutthuniṃsu – ‘ahu vata no, ahāyi vata no padālatā’ti! Tadetarahipi manussā kenaci kenacideva (sī. syā. pī.) dukkhadhammena phuṭṭhā evamāhaṃsu – ‘ahu vata no, ahāyi vata no’ti! Tadeva porāṇaṃ aggaññaṃ akkharaṃ anusaranti, na tvevassa atthaṃ ājānanti.

kenacideva (sī. syā. pī.)

Akaṭṭhapākasālipātubhāvo
mula_english:
124. After the fungus of the earth had disappeared, creepers appeared, just like *kalambukā* creeper.

It was endowed with colour, smell, and taste. It was the colour of fine ghee or butter.

It was as sweet as the pure honey of the bee.

Then, Vāseṭṭha, those beings set to and began to feed on those creepers.

And as they fed on them, nourishing themselves on them, they continued for a very long time.

And as they continued for a very long time feeding on those creepers, nourishing themselves on them, their bodies became coarser still, and the difference in their looks increased still more.

Some beings became good-looking, others ugly.

And the good-looking ones despised the others, saying: “We are better-looking than they are. They are uglier than we are.”

And because they became arrogant and conceited about their looks, the creepers disappeared too.

After the creepers had disappeared, they gathered together.

Having gathered together, they lamented: “Alas, it is lost to us, the creeper is lost to us!” Even today, when humans are touched by some suffering, they say the same thing: “Alas, it is lost to us!”

They are repeating an ancient saying without realizing its meaning.

The appearance of rice that ripens without cultivation
commentary_pali: 124.Padālatāti ekā madhurarasā bhaddālatā. Kalambukāti nāḷikā. Ahu vata noti madhurarasā vata no padālatā ahosi. Ahāyi vata noti sā no etarahi antarahitāti.
commentary_english:
124. *padālatā* is one *madhurarasa* *bhaddālatā*.
*kalambukā* is *nāḷikā*.
*"ahu vata no"* is *madhurarasā vata no padālatā ahosi*.
*"ahāyi vata no"* is *sā no etarahi antarahitāti*.

mula_pali:
125. ‘‘Atha kho tesaṃ, vāseṭṭha, sattānaṃ padālatāya antarahitāya akaṭṭhapāko sāli pāturahosi akaṇo athuso suddho sugandho taṇḍulapphalo. Yaṃ taṃ sāyaṃ sāyamāsāya āharanti, pāto taṃ hoti pakkaṃ paṭivirūḷhaṃ. Yaṃ taṃ pāto pātarāsāya āharanti, sāyaṃ taṃ hoti pakkaṃ paṭivirūḷhaṃ; nāpadānaṃ paññāyati. Atha kho te, vāseṭṭha, sattā akaṭṭhapākaṃ sāliṃ paribhuñjantā taṃbhakkhā tadāhārā ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu.

Itthipurisaliṅgapātubhāvo
mula_english:
‘And then, Vāseṭṭha, after the creepers had disappeared, rice appeared in open spaces, unhusked, without powder, pure, fragrant, and with grains like pearls.

And what they had taken in the evening for supper had grown again and was ripe in the morning.

And what they had taken in the morning for breakfast was ripe again by evening, with no sign of reaping.

And these beings, Vāseṭṭha, set to and fed on this uncultivated rice, and this lasted for a very long time.

The manifestation of the signs of woman and man.
commentary_pali:
125.Akaṭṭhapākoti akaṭṭheyeva bhūmibhāge uppanno. Akaṇoti nikkuṇḍako. Athusoti nitthuso. Sugandhoti dibbagandhaṃ vāyati. Taṇḍulapphaloti suparisuddhaṃ paṇḍaraṃ taṇḍulameva phalati. Pakkaṃ paṭivirūḷhanti sāyaṃ gahitaṭṭhānaṃ pāto pakkaṃ hoti, puna virūḷhaṃ paṭipākatikameva gahitaṭṭhānaṃ na paññāyati. Nāpadānaṃ paññāyatīti alāyitaṃ hutvā anūnameva paññāyati.

Itthipurisaliṅgādipātubhāvavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
125. *Akaṭṭhapāko* means <pb ed="m" n="3. 0053"/> that which has arisen in a field that has not been ploughed.

*Akaṇo* means *nikkuṇḍako*.

*Athuso* means *nitthuso*.

*Sugandho* means it emits a divine fragrance ( *dibbagandhaṃ vāyati*).

*Taṇḍulapphalo* means it produces very pure, white rice (*suparisuddhaṃ paṇḍaraṃ taṇḍulameva phalati*).

*Pakkaṃ paṭivirūḷha* means the place taken in the evening becomes ripe in the morning; again, the sprouted place that has become grown does not appear.

*Nāpadānaṃ paññāyatī* means it appears to be not agitated, but complete.

Explanation of the manifestation of male and female characteristics, and so forth.

mula_pali:
126. ‘‘Yathā yathā kho te, vāseṭṭha, sattā akaṭṭhapākaṃ sāliṃ paribhuñjantā taṃbhakkhā tadāhārā ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu, tathā tathā tesaṃ sattānaṃ bhiyyosomattāya kharattañceva kāyasmiṃ okkami, vaṇṇavevaṇṇatā ca paññāyittha, itthiyā ca itthiliṅgaṃ pāturahosi purisassa ca purisaliṅgaṃ. Itthī ca purisaṃ ativelaṃ upanijjhāyati puriso ca itthiṃ. Tesaṃ ativelaṃ aññamaññaṃ upanijjhāyataṃ sārāgo udapādi, pariḷāho kāyasmiṃ okkami. Te pariḷāhapaccayā methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭiseviṃsu.

‘‘Ye kho pana te, vāseṭṭha, tena samayena sattā passanti methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevante, aññe paṃsuṃ khipanti, aññe seṭṭhiṃ khipanti , aññe gomayaṃ khipanti – ‘nassa asuci vasali (syā.), vasalī (ka.), nassa asucī’ti. ‘Kathañhi nāma satto sattassa evarūpaṃ karissatī’ti! Tadetarahipi manussā ekaccesu janapadesu vadhuyā nibbuyhamānāya nivayhamānāya, niggayhamānāya (ka.) aññe paṃsuṃ khipanti, aññe seṭṭhiṃ khipanti, aññe gomayaṃ khipanti. Tadeva porāṇaṃ aggaññaṃ akkharaṃ anusaranti, na tvevassa atthaṃ ājānanti.

vasali (syā.), vasalī (ka.) nivayhamānāya, niggayhamānāya (ka.)

Methunadhammasamācāro
mula_english:
And as they, Vāseṭṭha, continued to consume the self-grown rice, living on it, that being their food, for a long, long time, so their bodies became coarser to a greater extent, and a difference in looks became apparent. And females developed female characteristics, and males developed male characteristics.

And the women became excessively preoccupied with men, and the men with women.

Owing to this excessive preoccupation with each other, passion arose, and their bodies burned with lust ( *sārāgo udapādi, pariḷāho kāyasmiṃ okkami*).

And later, because of this burning, they indulged in sexual activity (*te pariḷāhapaccayā methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭiseviṃsu*).

But those beings, Vāseṭṭha, who at that time saw others indulging in sexual activity, threw dust, threw ashes, threw cow dung, [saying] ‘This is impure, this is impure.’

‘How can a being do such a thing to another being?’ Even now in some districts, when a bride is being led out, some throw dust, some throw ashes, some throw cow dung.

They are repeating an ancient saying without actually understanding its meaning.

The practice of sexual intercourse.
commentary_pali: 126.Itthiyā cāti yā pubbe manussakāle itthī, tassa itthiliṅgaṃ pātubhavati, pubbe purisassa purisaliṅgaṃ. Mātugāmo nāma hi purisattabhāvaṃ labhanto anupubbena purisattapaccaye dhamme pūretvā labhati. Puriso itthattabhāvaṃ labhanto kāmesumicchācāraṃ nissāya labhati. Tadā pana pakatiyā mātugāmassa itthiliṅgaṃ, purisassa purisaliṅgaṃ pāturahosi. Upanijjhāyatanti upanijjhāyantānaṃ olokentānaṃ. Pariḷāhoti rāgapariḷāho. Seṭṭhinti chārikaṃ. Nibbuyhamānāyāti niyyamānāya.
commentary_english:
126. "And as for a woman (itthiyā cā'ti)," that which was previously a woman in human time, the sign of a woman appears for her, and previously for a man, the sign of a man.

A "mother-being (mātugāmo)" by name, indeed, obtaining the state of being a man, gradually, through conditions for being a man, fulfilling the Dharma, obtains it.

A man, obtaining the state of being a woman, obtains it relying on misconduct in sensual pleasures (kāmesumicchācāraṃ).

Then, indeed, by nature, for the mother-being, the sign of a woman, for a man, the sign of a man, appeared.

"Observing (upanijjhāyata'nti)," for those who observe, for those who look.

"Burning (pariḷāho'ti)," burning with passion (rāgapariḷāho).

"Seṭṭhi'nti," ashes (chārikaṃ).

"Being carried away (nibbuyhamānāyā'ti)," being led away (niyyamānāya).

mula_pali:
127. ‘‘Adhammasammataṃ kho pana adhammasammataṃ taṃ kho pana (syā.), adhammasammataṃ kho pana taṃ (?), vāseṭṭha, tena samayena hoti, tadetarahi dhammasammataṃ. Ye kho pana, vāseṭṭha, tena samayena sattā methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevanti, te māsampi dvemāsampi na labhanti gāmaṃ vā nigamaṃ vā pavisituṃ. Yato kho te, vāseṭṭha, sattā tasmiṃ asaddhamme ativelaṃ pātabyataṃ āpajjiṃsu. Atha agārāni upakkamiṃsu kātuṃ tasseva asaddhammassa paṭicchādanatthaṃ. Atha kho, vāseṭṭha, aññatarassa sattassa alasajātikassa etadahosi – ‘ambho, kimevāhaṃ vihaññāmi sāliṃ āharanto sāyaṃ sāyamāsāya pāto pātarāsāya! Yaṃnūnāhaṃ sāliṃ āhareyyaṃ sakiṃdeva sakiṃdeva (ka.) sāyapātarāsāyā’ti !

‘‘Atha kho so, vāseṭṭha, satto sāliṃ āhāsi sakiṃdeva sāyapātarāsāya. Atha kho, vāseṭṭha, aññataro satto yena so satto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā taṃ sattaṃ etadavoca – ‘ehi, bho satta, sālāhāraṃ gamissāmā’ti. ‘Alaṃ, bho satta, āhato āhaṭo (syā.) me sāli sakiṃdeva sāyapātarāsāyā’ti. Atha kho so, vāseṭṭha, satto tassa sattassa diṭṭhānugatiṃ āpajjamāno sāliṃ āhāsi sakiṃdeva dvīhāya. ‘Evampi kira, bho, sādhū’ti.

āhaṭo (syā.)

‘‘Atha kho, vāseṭṭha, aññataro satto yena so satto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā taṃ sattaṃ etadavoca – ‘ehi, bho satta, sālāhāraṃ gamissāmā’ti. ‘Alaṃ, bho satta, āhato me sāli sakiṃdeva dvīhāyā’ti. Atha kho so, vāseṭṭha, satto tassa sattassa diṭṭhānugatiṃ āpajjamāno sāliṃ āhāsi sakiṃdeva catūhāya, ‘evampi kira, bho, sādhū’ti.

‘‘Atha kho, vāseṭṭha, aññataro satto yena so satto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā taṃ sattaṃ etadavoca – ‘ehi, bho satta, sālāhāraṃ gamissāmā’ti. ‘Alaṃ, bho satta, āhato me sāli sakideva catūhāyā’ti. Atha kho so, vāseṭṭha, satto tassa sattassa diṭṭhānugatiṃ āpajjamāno sāliṃ āhāsi sakideva aṭṭhāhāya, ‘evampi kira, bho, sādhū’ti.

‘‘Yato kho te, vāseṭṭha, sattā sannidhikārakaṃ sāliṃ upakkamiṃsu paribhuñjituṃ. Atha kaṇopi taṇḍulaṃ pariyonandhi, thusopi taṇḍulaṃ pariyonandhi; lūnampi nappaṭivirūḷhaṃ , apadānaṃ paññāyittha, saṇḍasaṇḍā sālayo aṭṭhaṃsu.

Sālivibhāgo
mula_english:
127. What was considered bad form in those days ( *adhammasammataṃ*) is now considered good form (*dhammasammataṃ*). And those beings who in those days indulged in sex (*methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevanti*) were not allowed into a village (*gāmaṃ*) or town (*nigamaṃ*) for one or two months (*māsampi dvemāsampi*). Accordingly those who indulged for an excessively long period (*ativelaṃ pātabyataṃ āpajjiṃsu*) in such immoral practices (*asaddhamme*) began to build themselves dwellings (*agārāni upakkamiṃsu kātuṃ*) so as to indulge under cover (*paṭicchādanatthaṃ*).

Now it occurred to one of those beings who was inclined to laziness (*alasajātikassa*): "Well now, why should I be bothered (*vihaññāmi*) to gather rice (*sāliṃ āharanto*) in the evening for supper (*sāyaṃ sāyamāsāya*) and in the morning for breakfast (*pāto pātarāsāya*)! Why don't I gather rice (*sāliṃ āhareyyaṃ*) just once (*sakiṃdeva*) for both supper and breakfast (*sāyapātarāsāyā’ti*)."

Then that being gathered rice (*sāliṃ āhāsi*) just once (*sakiṃdeva*) for both supper and breakfast (*sāyapātarāsāya*). Then another being came (*upasaṅkami* ) to him and said: "Come on, let’s go rice-gathering (*sālāhāraṃ gamissāma*)!" "No need, my friend (*alaṃ, bho satta*), I’ve gathered enough rice (*āhato me sāli*) just once (*sakiṃdeva*) for both supper and breakfast (*sāyapātarāsāyā’ti*)."

Then the other, following his example (*diṭṭhānugatiṃ āpajjamāno*), gathered rice (*sāliṃ āhāsi*) enough just for two days (*dvīhāya*). "That should be about enough (*evampi kira, bho, sādhū’ti*)."

Then another being came (*upasaṅkami*) to him and said: "Come on, let’s go rice-gathering (*sālāhāraṃ gamissāma*)!" "No need, my friend (*alaṃ, bho satta*), I’ve gathered enough rice (*āhato me sāli*) just for two days (*dvīhāyā’ti*)."

Then the other, following his example (*diṭṭhānugatiṃ āpajjamāno*), gathered rice (*sāliṃ āhāsi*) enough just for four days (*catūhāya*). "That should be about enough (*evampi kira, bho, sādhū’ti*)."

Then another being came (*upasaṅkami*) to him and said: "Come on, let’s go rice-gathering (*sālāhāraṃ gamissāma*)!" "No need, my friend (*alaṃ, bho satta*), I’ve gathered enough rice (*āhato me sāli*) just for four days (*catūhāyā’ti*)."

Then the other, following his example (*diṭṭhānugatiṃ āpajjamāno*), gathered rice (*sāliṃ āhāsi*) enough just for eight days (*aṭṭhāhāya*). "That should be about enough (*evampi kira, bho, sādhū’ti*)."

However, when those beings made a store of rice (*sannidhikārakaṃ sāliṃ*) and lived on that (*paribhuñjituṃ*), then the grain (*kaṇopi taṇḍulaṃ*) was enveloped, the husk (*thusopi taṇḍulaṃ*) was enveloped; even when cut (*lūnampi*) it did not grow again (*nappaṭivirūḷhaṃ*), the separation was evident (*apadānaṃ paññāyittha*), and the rice grew in separate clusters (*saṇḍasaṇḍā sālayo aṭṭhaṃsu*).

The Division of Rice (*sālivibhāgo*)
commentary_pali: 127.Adhammasammatanti taṃ paṃsukhipanādi adhammoti sammataṃ. Tadetarahi dhammasammatanti taṃ idāni dhammoti sammataṃ, dhammoti taṃ gahetvā vicaranti. Tathā hi ekaccesu jānapadesu kalahaṃ kurumānā itthiyo ‘‘tvaṃ kasmā kathesi? Yā gomayapiṇḍamattampi nālatthā’’ti vadanti. Pātabyatanti sevitabbataṃ. Sannidhikārakanti sannidhiṃ katvā. Apadānaṃ paññāyitthāti chinnaṭṭhānaṃ ūnameva hutvā paññāyittha. Saṇḍasaṇḍāti ekekasmiṃ ṭhāne kalāpabandhā viya gumbagumbā hutvā.
commentary_english:
127.
*Adhammasammata* means that which is considered immoral, such as throwing away rags.
*Tadetarahi dhammasammata* means that which is now considered moral; they live considering that to be the Dharma and holding it as such.
For example, in some rural areas, women, when quarreling, say, "Why did you speak? You who didn't even get a ball of cow dung!"
*Pātabyata* means that which should be practiced.
*Sannidhikāraka* means having made a deposition.
*Apadānaṃ paññāyitthā* means it appeared as if the cut-off place was deficient.
*Saṇḍasaṇḍā* means like bunches of branches, in each place, having become clumps.

mula_pali: 128. ‘‘Atha kho te, vāseṭṭha, sattā sannipatiṃsu, sannipatitvā anutthuniṃsu – ‘pāpakā vata, bho, dhammā sattesu pātubhūtā. Mayañhi pubbe manomayā ahumhā pītibhakkhā sayaṃpabhā antalikkhacarā subhaṭṭhāyino, ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ aṭṭhamhā. Tesaṃ no amhākaṃ kadāci karahaci dīghassa addhuno accayena rasapathavī udakasmiṃ samatani. Sā ahosi vaṇṇasampannā gandhasampannā rasasampannā. Te mayaṃ rasapathaviṃ hatthehi āluppakārakaṃ upakkamimha paribhuñjituṃ, tesaṃ no rasapathaviṃ hatthehi āluppakārakaṃ upakkamataṃ paribhuñjituṃ sayaṃpabhā antaradhāyi. Sayaṃpabhāya antarahitāya candimasūriyā pāturahesuṃ, candimasūriyesu pātubhūtesu nakkhattāni tārakarūpāni pāturahesuṃ, nakkhattesu tārakarūpesu pātubhūtesu rattindivā paññāyiṃsu, rattindivesu paññāyamānesu māsaḍḍhamāsā paññāyiṃsu. Māsaḍḍhamāsesu paññāyamānesu utusaṃvaccharā paññāyiṃsu. Te mayaṃ rasapathaviṃ paribhuñjantā taṃbhakkhā tadāhārā ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ aṭṭhamhā. Tesaṃ no pāpakānaṃyeva akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pātubhāvā rasapathavī antaradhāyi. Rasapathaviyā antarahitāya bhūmipappaṭako pāturahosi. So ahosi vaṇṇasampanno gandhasampanno rasasampanno. Te mayaṃ bhūmipappaṭakaṃ upakkamimha paribhuñjituṃ. Te mayaṃ taṃ paribhuñjantā taṃbhakkhā tadāhārā ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ aṭṭhamhā. Tesaṃ no pāpakānaṃyeva akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pātubhāvā bhūmipappaṭako antaradhāyi. Bhūmipappaṭake antarahite padālatā pāturahosi. Sā ahosi vaṇṇasampannā gandhasampannā rasasampannā. Te mayaṃ padālataṃ upakkamimha paribhuñjituṃ. Te mayaṃ taṃ paribhuñjantā taṃbhakkhā tadāhārā ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ aṭṭhamhā. Tesaṃ no pāpakānaṃyeva akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pātubhāvā padālatā antaradhāyi. Padālatāya antarahitāya akaṭṭhapāko sāli pāturahosi akaṇo athuso suddho sugandho taṇḍulapphalo. Yaṃ taṃ sāyaṃ sāyamāsāya āharāma, pāto taṃ hoti pakkaṃ paṭivirūḷhaṃ. Yaṃ taṃ pāto pātarāsāya āharāma, sāyaṃ taṃ hoti pakkaṃ paṭivirūḷhaṃ. Nāpadānaṃ paññāyittha. Te mayaṃ akaṭṭhapākaṃ sāliṃ paribhuñjantā taṃbhakkhā tadāhārā ciraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ aṭṭhamhā. Tesaṃ no pāpakānaṃyeva akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pātubhāvā kaṇopi taṇḍulaṃ pariyonandhi, thusopi taṇḍulaṃ pariyonandhi, lūnampi nappaṭivirūḷhaṃ, apadānaṃ paññāyittha, saṇḍasaṇḍā sālayo ṭhitā. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ sāliṃ vibhajeyyāma, mariyādaṃ ṭhapeyyāmā’ti! Atha kho te, vāseṭṭha, sattā sāliṃ vibhajiṃsu, mariyādaṃ ṭhapesuṃ.
mula_english:
‘And then those beings, Vāseṭṭha, came together and lamented: “Wicked ways have become rife among us.”

‘At first we were mind-made, feeding on delight, self-luminous, moving in the sky, abiding in beauty, for a very long time.

‘And sooner or later, after a very long period of time, savoury earth spread itself over the waters.

It was endowed with colour, smell and taste.

And then we set to and ate the savoury earth with our hands, breaking off pieces. As we continued to do so, the self-luminosity disappeared.

When the self-luminosity had disappeared, the moon and sun appeared. With the appearance of the moon and sun, the stars appeared, and with the appearance of the stars, night and day became distinct, and as night and day became distinct, fortnights and months became distinct, and as fortnights and months became distinct, the seasons and the year became distinct.

And this lasted for a very long time.

And as evil and unwholesome dharmas arose in us, the savoury earth disappeared.

‘And then, when the savoury earth had disappeared, a fungus cropped up.

It was endowed with colour, smell and taste.

And those beings set to and ate the fungus.

And this lasted for a very long time.

And as evil and unwholesome dharmas arose in us, the fungus disappeared.

When the fungus had disappeared, creepers appeared.

It was endowed with colour, smell and taste.

And those beings set to and fed on those creepers.

And this lasted for a very long time.

And as evil and unwholesome dharmas arose in us, the creepers disappeared.

And then, after the creepers had disappeared, rice appeared in open spaces, free from powder and from husks, fragrant and clean-grained.

What we took in the evening for supper had grown again and was ripe in the morning.

What we took in the morning for breakfast was ripe again by evening.

There was no sign of reaping.

And these beings set to and fed on this rice, and this lasted for a very long time.

And as evil and unwholesome *dharmas* arose in us, the grains of rice became enclosed in powder and husk, and what was reaped no longer grew again. There was a sign of reaping, and the rice grew in separate clusters.

“Suppose now that we were to divide up the rice and set boundaries.” And so, Vāseṭṭha, those beings divided up the rice and set boundaries.
commentary_pali:
128.Mariyādaṃṭhapeyyāmāti sīmaṃ ṭhapeyyāma. Yatra hi nāmāti yo hi nāma. Pāṇinā pahariṃsūti tayo vāre vacanaṃ agaṇhantaṃ pāṇinā pahariṃsu. Tadagge khoti taṃ aggaṃ katvā.

Mahāsammatarājavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
128. mariyādaṃṭhapeyyāmāti sīmaṃ ṭhapeyyāma. yatra hi nāmāti yo hi nāma. pāṇinā pahariṃsūti tayo vāre vacanaṃ agaṇhantaṃ pāṇinā pahariṃsu. tadagge khoti taṃ aggaṃ katvā.

mahāsammatarājavaṇṇanā

mula_pali:
129. ‘‘Atha kho, vāseṭṭha, aññataro satto lolajātiko sakaṃ bhāgaṃ parirakkhanto aññataraṃ aññassa (?) bhāgaṃ adinnaṃ ādiyitvā paribhuñji. Tamenaṃ aggahesuṃ, gahetvā etadavocuṃ – ‘pāpakaṃ vata, bho satta, karosi, yatra hi nāma sakaṃ bhāgaṃ parirakkhanto aññataraṃ bhāgaṃ adinnaṃ ādiyitvā paribhuñjasi. Māssu, bho satta, punapi evarūpamakāsī’ti. ‘Evaṃ, bho’ti kho, vāseṭṭha, so satto tesaṃ sattānaṃ paccassosi. Dutiyampi kho, vāseṭṭha, so satto…pe… tatiyampi kho, vāseṭṭha, so satto sakaṃ bhāgaṃ parirakkhanto aññataraṃ bhāgaṃ adinnaṃ ādiyitvā paribhuñji. Tamenaṃ aggahesuṃ, gahetvā etadavocuṃ – ‘pāpakaṃ vata, bho satta, karosi, yatra hi nāma sakaṃ bhāgaṃ parirakkhanto aññataraṃ bhāgaṃ adinnaṃ ādiyitvā paribhuñjasi. Māssu, bho satta, punapi evarūpamakāsī’ti. Aññe pāṇinā pahariṃsu, aññe leḍḍunā pahariṃsu, aññe daṇḍena pahariṃsu. Tadagge kho, vāseṭṭha, adinnādānaṃ paññāyati, garahā paññāyati, musāvādo paññāyati, daṇḍādānaṃ paññāyati.

Mahāsammatarājā
mula_english:
Then, Vāseṭṭha, one being, greedy by nature, while protecting his own share, took and enjoyed another share that was not given.

They seized him, and having seized him, said this: "You wicked being, you do wrong when, while protecting your own share, you take and enjoy another share that was not given."

"Don't ever do such a thing again!"

"Yes, sir," Vāseṭṭha, that being replied to those beings.

A second time, Vāseṭṭha, that being…and a third time, Vāseṭṭha, that being, while protecting his own share, took and enjoyed another share that was not given.

They seized him, and having seized him, said this: "You wicked being, you do wrong when, while protecting your own share, you take and enjoy another share that was not given."

"Don't ever do such a thing again!"

Some struck him with their hands (pāṇinā), some struck him with clods (leḍḍunā), and some struck him with sticks (daṇḍena).

From this origin, Vāseṭṭha, taking what was not given (*adinnādānaṃ*) became apparent, censure (*garahā*) became apparent, lying (*musāvādo*) became apparent, and punishment (*daṇḍādānaṃ*) became apparent.

Mahāsammatarāja

mula_pali:
130. ‘‘Atha kho te, vāseṭṭha, sattā sannipatiṃsu, sannipatitvā anutthuniṃsu – ‘pāpakā vata bho dhammā sattesu pātubhūtā, yatra hi nāma adinnādānaṃ paññāyissati, garahā paññāyissati, musāvādo paññāyissati, daṇḍādānaṃ paññāyissati. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ ekaṃ sattaṃ sammanneyyāma, yo no sammā khīyitabbaṃ khīyeyya, sammā garahitabbaṃ garaheyya, sammā pabbājetabbaṃ pabbājeyya. Mayaṃ panassa sālīnaṃ bhāgaṃ anuppadassāmā’ti.

‘‘Atha kho te, vāseṭṭha, sattā yo nesaṃ satto abhirūpataro ca dassanīyataro ca pāsādikataro ca mahesakkhataro ca taṃ sattaṃ upasaṅkamitvā etadavocuṃ – ‘ehi, bho satta, sammā khīyitabbaṃ khīya, sammā garahitabbaṃ garaha, sammā pabbājetabbaṃ pabbājehi. Mayaṃ pana te sālīnaṃ bhāgaṃ anuppadassāmā’ti. ‘Evaṃ, bho’ti kho, vāseṭṭha, so satto tesaṃ sattānaṃ paṭissuṇitvā sammā khīyitabbaṃ khīyi, sammā garahitabbaṃ garahi, sammā pabbājetabbaṃ pabbājesi. Te panassa sālīnaṃ bhāgaṃ anuppadaṃsu.
mula_english:
Then, Vāseṭṭha, those beings came together and lamented, saying: “Indeed, evil things have appeared among beings, where taking what is not given, censure, lying, and violence are evident. Suppose we were to appoint a certain being who would rightly show anger where anger is due, rightly censure those who deserve it, and rightly banish those who deserve banishment. And in return, we would grant him a share of the rice.”

Then, Vāseṭṭha, those beings went to the one among them who was the most handsome, the most pleasing to see, the most agreeable, and the most capable, and said to him: “Come, good being, rightly show anger where anger is due, rightly censure those who deserve it, and rightly banish those who deserve banishment. And in return, we will grant you a share of the rice.”

“So be it, good sirs,” Vāseṭṭha, that being replied to those beings, and he rightly showed anger where anger was due, rightly censured those who deserved it, and rightly banished those who deserved banishment. And they granted him a share of the rice.
commentary_pali: 130.Khīyitabbaṃ khīyeyyāti pakāsetabbaṃ pakāseyya khipitabbaṃ khipeyya, hāretabbaṃ hāreyyāti vuttaṃ hoti. Yo nesaṃ sattoti yo tesaṃ satto. Ko pana soti? Amhākaṃ bodhisatto. Sālīnaṃ bhāgaṃ anupadassāmāti mayaṃ ekekassa khettato ambaṇambaṇaṃ āharitvā tuyhaṃ sālibhāgaṃ dassāma, tayā kiñci kammaṃ na kātabbaṃ, tvaṃ amhākaṃ jeṭṭhakaṭṭhāne tiṭṭhāti.
commentary_english:
130. "One should be caused to be consumed; one should consume," that is to say, one should cause it to be manifested; one should manifest it; one should cause it to be thrown away; one should throw it away; one should cause it to be taken away; one should take it away.

"He is not theirs, but he is theirs."

Who is he? Our *bodhisattva*. (bodhisattvaḥ)

"We will show you a share of rice," that is to say, we will bring an *ambaṇa* measure from each field and give you a share of rice. No work should be done by you. You should remain in our chief place.

mula_pali:
131. ‘‘Mahājanasammatoti kho, vāseṭṭha, ‘mahāsammato, mahāsammato’ tveva paṭhamaṃ akkharaṃ upanibbattaṃ. Khettānaṃ adhipatīti kho, vāseṭṭha, ‘khattiyo, khattiyo’ tveva dutiyaṃ akkharaṃ upanibbattaṃ. Dhammena pare rañjetīti kho, vāseṭṭha, ‘rājā, rājā’ tveva tatiyaṃ akkharaṃ upanibbattaṃ. Iti kho, vāseṭṭha, evametassa khattiyamaṇḍalassa porāṇena aggaññena akkharena abhinibbatti ahosi tesaṃyeva sattānaṃ, anaññesaṃ. Sadisānaṃyeva, no asadisānaṃ. Dhammeneva, no adhammena. Dhammo hi, vāseṭṭha, seṭṭho janetasmiṃ diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañca.

Brāhmaṇamaṇḍalaṃ
mula_english:
"Vāseṭṭha, 'The People's Choice' (*mahājanasammato*) is the meaning of *Mahāsammata*, which was the first title to be introduced.

Vāseṭṭha, 'Lord of the Fields' (*khettānaṃ adhipati*) is the meaning of *Khattiya*, the second such title to be introduced.

Vāseṭṭha, 'He Gladdens Others With Dhamma' (*dhammena pare rañjeti*) is the meaning of *Rāja*, the third title to be introduced.

Thus, Vāseṭṭha, was the origin of the class of Khattiyas, in accordance with the ancient titles that were introduced for them. They originated among these very same beings, no different from themselves.

And in accordance with Dharma (*dhamma*), not otherwise (*adhamma*).

Vāseṭṭha, Dhamma (*dharma*) is the best thing for people, in this life and the next as well.

The section on the Brāhmaṇa (*brāhmaṇa*) class."
commentary_pali:
