131.Akkharaṃ upanibbattanti saṅkhā samaññā paññatti vohāro uppanno. Khattiyo khattiyotveva dutiyaṃ akkharanti na kevalaṃ akkharameva, te panassa khettasāmino tīhi saṅkhehi abhisekampi akaṃsu. Rañjetīti sukheti pineti. Aggaññenāti agganti ñātena, agge vā ñātena lokuppattisamaye uppannena abhinibbatti ahosīti.

Brāhmaṇamaṇḍalādivaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
<hi rend="paranum">131</hi><hi rend="dot">.
</hi><hi rend="bold">akkharam upanibbatta</hi>nti: "Saṅkhā" (calculation), "samaññā" (designation), "paññatti" (concept), "vohāro" (expression) arose.
<hi rend="bold">khattiyo khattiyotveva dutiyam akkhara</hi>nti: Not merely the letter "akkara", but the landowners anointed him with three saṅkhās (calculations).
<hi rend="bold">rañjetī</hi>ti: gladdens and pleases.
<hi rend="bold">aggaññenā</hi>ti: by what is known as "agga", or by what was known as "agga", at the time of the world's origin, there was arising.

Description of the Brāhmaṇa circle, etc.

mula_pali:
132. ‘‘Atha kho tesaṃ, vāseṭṭha, sattānaṃyeva tesaṃ yeva kho vāseṭṭha sattānaṃ (sī. pī.) ekaccānaṃ etadahosi – ‘pāpakā vata, bho, dhammā sattesu pātubhūtā, yatra hi nāma adinnādānaṃ paññāyissati, garahā paññāyissati, musāvādo paññāyissati, daṇḍādānaṃ paññāyissati, pabbājanaṃ paññāyissati. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ pāpake akusale dhamme vāheyyāmā’ti. Te pāpake akusale dhamme vāhesuṃ . Pāpake akusale dhamme vāhentīti kho, vāseṭṭha, ‘brāhmaṇā, brāhmaṇā’ tveva paṭhamaṃ akkharaṃ upanibbattaṃ. Te araññāyatane paṇṇakuṭiyo karitvā paṇṇakuṭīsu jhāyanti vītaṅgārā vītadhūmā pannamusalā sāyaṃ sāyamāsāya pāto pātarāsāya gāmanigamarājadhāniyo osaranti ghāsamesamānā ghāsamesanā (sī. syā. pī.). Te ghāsaṃ paṭilabhitvā punadeva araññāyatane paṇṇakuṭīsu jhāyanti. Tamenaṃ manussā disvā evamāhaṃsu – ‘ime kho, bho, sattā araññāyatane paṇṇakuṭiyo karitvā paṇṇakuṭīsu jhāyanti, vītaṅgārā vītadhūmā pannamusalā sāyaṃ sāyamāsāya pāto pātarāsāya gāmanigamarājadhāniyo osaranti ghāsamesamānā. Te ghāsaṃ paṭilabhitvā punadeva araññāyatane paṇṇakuṭīsu jhāyantī’ti, jhāyantīti kho paṇṇakuṭīsu jhāyanti jhāyantīti kho (sī. pī.), paṇṇakuṭīsu jhāyantīti kho (ka.), vāseṭṭha, ‘jhāyakā, jhāyakā’ tveva dutiyaṃ akkharaṃ upanibbattaṃ. Tesaṃyeva kho, vāseṭṭha, sattānaṃ ekacce sattā araññāyatane paṇṇakuṭīsu taṃ jhānaṃ anabhisambhuṇamānā anabhisaṃbhūnamānā (katthaci) gāmasāmantaṃ nigamasāmantaṃ osaritvā ganthe karontā acchanti. Tamenaṃ manussā disvā evamāhaṃsu – ‘ime kho, bho, sattā araññāyatane paṇṇakuṭīsu taṃ jhānaṃ anabhisambhuṇamānā gāmasāmantaṃ nigamasāmantaṃ osaritvā ganthe karontā acchanti, na dānime jhāyantī’ti. Na dānime na dānime jhāyantī na dānime (sī. pī. ka.) jhāyantīti kho, vāseṭṭha, ‘ajjhāyakā ajjhāyakā’ tveva tatiyaṃ akkharaṃ upanibbattaṃ. Hīnasammataṃ kho pana, vāseṭṭha, tena samayena hoti, tadetarahi seṭṭhasammataṃ. Iti kho, vāseṭṭha, evametassa brāhmaṇamaṇḍalassa porāṇena aggaññena akkharena abhinibbatti ahosi tesaṃyeva sattānaṃ , anaññesaṃ sadisānaṃyeva no asadisānaṃ dhammeneva , no adhammena. Dhammo hi, vāseṭṭha, seṭṭho janetasmiṃ diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañca.

Vessamaṇḍalaṃ
mula_english:
132. Then, Vāseṭṭha, some of those beings thought: “Evil things have appeared among beings, such as taking what is not given (adinnādāna), censure (garahā), lying (musāvāda), punishment (daṇḍādāna) and banishment (pabbājana).

We ought to put aside evil (pāpake) and unwholesome things (akusale dhamme)."

They put aside evil and unwholesome things.

“They Put Aside Evil And Unwholesome Things” is the meaning of *brāhmaṇa* "brahmins," which is the first regular title to be introduced.

They went to the forest abodes (araññāyatane), made leaf huts (*paṇṇakuṭiyo*) and meditated (*jhāyanti*) in the leaf huts, being without embers (vītaṅgārā), without smoke (vītadhūmā), having abandoned the pestle (pannamusalā), in the evening (sāyaṃ) for the evening meal (sāyamāsāya), in the morning (pāto) for the morning meal (pātarāsāya), they went down to villages (gāma), towns (nigama) and capital cities (rājadhāniyo), seeking food (ghāsamesamānā).

They, having obtained food, then again meditated in the leaf huts in the forest abodes.

People, having seen them, said thus: “These beings, having made leaf huts in the forest abodes, meditate in the leaf huts, being without embers, without smoke, having abandoned the pestle, in the evening for the evening meal, in the morning for the morning meal, they go down to villages, towns, and capital cities, seeking food.

They, having obtained food, then again meditate in the leaf huts in the forest abodes,” is the meaning of *jhāyaka* “meditators," which is the second regular title to be introduced.

However, some of those beings, not being able to meditate (jhānaṃ anabhisambhuṇamānā) in leaf-huts in the forest abodes, settled around the borders of villages (gāmasāmantaṃ), the borders of towns (nigamasāmantaṃ), and compiled books (ganthe karontā).

People, having seen them, said thus: “These beings, not being able to meditate in leaf huts in the forest abodes, settled around the borders of villages, the borders of towns, and compiled books, now these do not meditate (jhāyantī).”

“Now These Do Not Meditate” is the meaning of *ajjhāyakā* "non-meditators," which is the third regular title to be introduced.

At that time it was regarded as a low designation, but now it is the higher.

This, then, Vāseṭṭha, is the origin of the class of *brāhmaṇas* (brahmins) in accordance with the ancient titles that were introduced for them. Their origin was from among these very same beings, like themselves, no different, and in accordance with *dharma*, not otherwise.

Dhamma’s the best thing for people In this life and the next as well.

Vessamaṇḍalaṃ
commentary_pali: 132.Vītaṅgārāvītadhūmāti pacitvā khāditabbābhāvato vigatadhūmaṅgārā. Pannamusalāti koṭṭetvā pacitabbābhāvato patitamusalā. Ghāsamesamānāti bhikkhācariyavasena yāgubhattaṃ pariyesantā. Tamenaṃ manussā disvāti te ete manussā passitvā. Anabhisambhuṇamānāti asahamānā asakkontā. Ganthe karontāti tayo vede abhisaṅkharontā ceva vācentā ca. Acchantīti vasanti, ‘‘acchentī’’tipi pāṭho. Esevattho. Hīnasammatanti ‘‘mante dhārenti mante vācentī’’ti kho, vāseṭṭha, idaṃ tena samayena hīnasammataṃ. Tadetarahi seṭṭhasammatanti taṃ idāni ‘‘ettake mante dhārenti ettake mante vācentī’’ti seṭṭhasammataṃ jātaṃ. Brāhmaṇamaṇḍalassāti brāhmaṇagaṇassa.
commentary_english:
132. *vītaṅgārā*: *vītadhūmā* means without embers, because it has been cooked and should be eaten; without smoke.
*pannamusalā*: because it has been pounded (*koṭṭetvā*) and should be cooked (*pacitabbābhāvato*), the pestle has fallen (*patitamusalā*).
*ghāsamesamānā*: searching for rice gruel (*yāgubhattaṃ*), according to the mendicant’s way of life (*bhikkhācariyavasena*).
*tamenaṃ manussā disvā*: those people (*manussā*) having seen (*passitvā*) him.
*anabhisambhuṇamānā*: not enduring (*asahamānā*), not being able (*asakkontā*).
*ganthe karontā*: reciting (*vācentā*) and composing (*abhisaṅkharontā*) the three Vedas.
*acchantī*: they dwell, *‘‘acchentī’’* is also a reading (*pāṭho*).
This is the meaning (*attho*).
*hīnasammata*: “They uphold the mantras, they recite the mantras,” thus, O Vāseṭṭha, at that time this was considered inferior (*hīnasammataṃ*).
*tadetarahi seṭṭhasammata*: now (*idāni*) that very thing, “they uphold so many mantras, they recite so many mantras,” has become considered superior (*seṭṭhasammataṃ jātaṃ*).
*brāhmaṇamaṇḍalassā*: of the Brāhmin group (*brāhmaṇagaṇassa*).

mula_pali:
133. ‘‘Tesaṃyeva kho, vāseṭṭha, sattānaṃ ekacce sattā methunaṃ dhammaṃ samādāya visukammante vissutakammante (sī. pī.), vissukammante (ka. sī.), visuṃ kammante (syā. ka.) payojesuṃ. Methunaṃ dhammaṃ samādāya visukammante payojentīti kho, vāseṭṭha, ‘vessā, vessā’ tveva akkharaṃ upanibbattaṃ. Iti kho, vāseṭṭha, evametassa vessamaṇḍalassa porāṇena aggaññena akkharena abhinibbatti ahosi tesaññeva sattānaṃ anaññesaṃ sadisānaṃyeva , no asadisānaṃ, dhammeneva no adhammena. Dhammo hi, vāseṭṭha, seṭṭho janetasmiṃ diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañca.

Suddamaṇḍalaṃ
mula_english: ‘And then, Vāseṭṭha, some of those beings, having paired off, adopted various trades. Having adopted the practice of sexual activity, they engaged in various trades. And so, Vāseṭṭha, the term "Vessa, Vessa" arose. Thus, Vāseṭṭha, this is how the ancient term *aggañña* originated for this class of Vessas, specifically for those beings like themselves, not for dissimilar ones, and in accordance with *dharma* (dhamma), not otherwise (*adhammena*). For, Vāseṭṭha, *dharma* (dhammo) is the best thing for people in this life and in the next as well.
commentary_pali: 133.Methunaṃ dhammaṃ samādāyāti methunadhammaṃ samādiyitvā. Visukammantepayojesunti gorakkha vāṇijakammādike vissute uggate kammante payojesuṃ.
commentary_english: 133. *methunaṃ dhammaṃ samādāyā* means having undertaken the practice of sexual intercourse. *visukammante payojesu* means they engaged in well-known and prominent activities such as cattle-rearing and trade.

mula_pali: 134. ‘‘Tesaññeva kho, vāseṭṭha, sattānaṃ ye te sattā avasesā te luddācārā khuddācārā ahesuṃ. Luddācārā khuddācārāti kho, vāseṭṭha, ‘suddā, suddā’ tveva akkharaṃ upanibbattaṃ. Iti kho, vāseṭṭha, evametassa suddamaṇḍalassa porāṇena aggaññena akkharena abhinibbatti ahosi tesaṃyeva sattānaṃ anaññesaṃ, sadisānaṃyeva no asadisānaṃ, dhammeneva, no adhammena. Dhammo hi, vāseṭṭha, seṭṭho janetasmiṃ diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañca.
mula_english:
‘And then, Vāseṭṭha, those beings that remained went in for hunting, those beings that remained became base and followed base practices.

“They Are Base Who Live By The Chase”, and that is the meaning of *Śūdra*, which came to be the regular title for such people.

This, then, Vāseṭṭha, is the origin of the *Śūdra* class in accordance with the ancient titles that were introduced for them. Their origin was from among these very same beings, like themselves, no different, and in accordance with *dharma*, not otherwise.

Dhamma’s the best thing for people in this life and the next as well.
commentary_pali: 134.Suddā suddāti tena luddācārakammakhuddācārakammunā suddaṃ suddaṃ lahuṃ lahuṃ kucchitaṃ gacchanti, vinassantīti attho. Ahu khoti hoti kho.
commentary_english:
134. *Suddā suddā*: by that base conduct and bad behavior, they go basely, basely, quickly, quickly, despicably, they perish, is the meaning.

*Ahu kho* means *hoti kho*.

mula_pali:
135. ‘‘Ahu kho so, vāseṭṭha, samayo, yaṃ khattiyopi sakaṃ dhammaṃ garahamāno agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajati – ‘samaṇo bhavissāmī’ti. Brāhmaṇopi kho, vāseṭṭha…pe… vessopi kho, vāseṭṭha…pe… suddopi kho, vāseṭṭha, sakaṃ dhammaṃ garahamāno agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajati – ‘samaṇo bhavissāmī’ti. Imehi kho, vāseṭṭha, catūhi maṇḍalehi samaṇamaṇḍalassa abhinibbatti ahosi, tesaṃyeva sattānaṃ anaññesaṃ, sadisānaṃyeva no asadisānaṃ, dhammeneva no adhammena. Dhammo hi, vāseṭṭha, seṭṭho janetasmiṃ diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañca.

Duccaritādikathā
mula_english:
‘And then, Vāseṭṭha, it came about that some *Khattiya* (warrior), dissatisfied with his own *Dhamma* (teaching, law), went forth from the household life into homelessness, thinking: “I will become an ascetic (*śramaṇa*).”

“ And a *Brahmin* (priest) did likewise… a *Vessa* (merchant) did likewise… and so did a *Sudda* (laborer). dissatisfied with his own *Dhamma* (teaching, law), went forth from the household life into homelessness, thinking: “I will become an ascetic (*śramaṇa*).”

And from these four classes the class of ascetics (*śramaṇa*) came into existence. Their origin was from among these very same beings, like themselves, no different, and in accordance with *Dhamma* (teaching, law), not otherwise.

*Dhamma* (teaching, law)’s the best thing for people In this life and the next as well.

The discourse on evil conduct, and so forth.
commentary_pali:
135.Sakaṃdhammaṃ garahamānoti na setacchattaṃ ussāpanamattena sujjhituṃ sakkāti evaṃ attano khattiyadhammaṃ nindamāno. Esa nayo sabbattha. ‘‘Imehi kho, vāseṭṭha, catūhi maṇḍalehī’’ti iminā imaṃ dasseti ‘‘samaṇamaṇḍalaṃ nāma visuṃ natthi, yasmā pana na sakkā jātiyā sujjhituṃ, attano attano sammāpaṭipattiyā visuddhi hoti. Tasmā imehi catūhi maṇḍalehi samaṇamaṇḍalassa abhinibbatti hoti. Imāni maṇḍalāni samaṇamaṇḍalaṃ anuvattanti, anuvattantāni ca dhammeneva anuvattanti, no adhammena. Samaṇamaṇḍalañhi āgamma sammāpaṭipattiṃ pūretvā suddhiṃ pāpuṇantī’’ti.

Duccaritādikathāvaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
135. *sakaṃ dhammaṃ garahamāno* means disparaging his own dharma, thinking that it is not possible to be purified merely by raising a white parasol; thus, he is criticizing his own *khattiya-dharma* (the dharma of a warrior). This method applies to the other cases as well.
‘‘imehi kho, vāseṭṭha, catūhi maṇḍalehī’’ti -- by this, he shows this: “There is no separate *samaṇa-maṇḍala* (the circle of ascetics) because it is not possible to be purified by birth; purification comes from one’s own right practice. Therefore, the arising of the *samaṇa-maṇḍala* is from these four circles. These circles follow the *samaṇa-maṇḍala*, and following, they follow only the Dharma, not non-dharma. Indeed, having come to the *samaṇa-maṇḍala*, having fulfilled right practice, they attain purification."

Explanation of wrong conduct etc.

mula_pali:
136. ‘‘Khattiyopi kho, vāseṭṭha, kāyena duccaritaṃ caritvā vācāya duccaritaṃ caritvā manasā duccaritaṃ caritvā micchādiṭṭhiko micchādiṭṭhikammasamādāno idaṃ padaṃ sī. ipotthakesu natthi micchādiṭṭhikammasamādānahetu kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati. Brāhmaṇopi kho, vāseṭṭha…pe… vessopi kho, vāseṭṭha… suddopi kho, vāseṭṭha… samaṇopi kho, vāseṭṭha, kāyena duccaritaṃ caritvā vācāya duccaritaṃ caritvā manasā duccaritaṃ caritvā micchādiṭṭhiko micchādiṭṭhikammasamādāno micchādiṭṭhikammasamādānahetu kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati.

‘‘Khattiyopi kho, vāseṭṭha, kāyena sucaritaṃ caritvā vācāya sucaritaṃ caritvā manasā sucaritaṃ caritvā sammādiṭṭhiko sammādiṭṭhikammasamādāno idaṃ padaṃ sī. pī. potthakesu natthi sammādiṭṭhikammasamādānahetu kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati. Brāhmaṇopi kho, vāseṭṭha…pe… vessopi kho, vāseṭṭha… suddopi kho, vāseṭṭha… samaṇopi kho, vāseṭṭha, kāyena sucaritaṃ caritvā vācāya sucaritaṃ caritvā manasā sucaritaṃ caritvā sammādiṭṭhiko sammādiṭṭhikammasamādāno sammādiṭṭhikammasamādānahetu kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati.

idaṃ padaṃ sī. pī. potthakesu natthi
mula_english:
136. Furthermore, Vāseṭṭha, a Khattiya, having conducted himself badly through body (kāyena duccaritaṃ caritvā), having conducted himself badly through speech, having conducted himself badly through mind, holding wrong views (micchādiṭṭhiko), adhering to actions based on wrong views (micchādiṭṭhikammasamādāno), because of adhering to actions based on wrong views, on the dissolution of the body (kāyassa bhedā), after death, reappears in a state of deprivation (apāyaṃ), in an unhappy destination (duggatiṃ), perdition (vinipātaṃ), even in hell (nirayaṃ upapajjati).

So too will a Brāhmin, a Vessa, a Sudda, a Samaṇa, Vāseṭṭha, having conducted himself badly through body (kāyena duccaritaṃ caritvā), having conducted himself badly through speech, having conducted himself badly through mind, holding wrong views (micchādiṭṭhiko), adhering to actions based on wrong views (micchādiṭṭhikammasamādāno), because of adhering to actions based on wrong views, on the dissolution of the body (kāyassa bhedā), after death, reappears in a state of deprivation (apāyaṃ), in an unhappy destination (duggatiṃ), perdition (vinipātaṃ), even in hell (nirayaṃ upapajjati).

Furthermore, Vāseṭṭha, a Khattiya, having conducted himself well through body (kāyena sucaritaṃ caritvā), having conducted himself well through speech, having conducted himself well through mind, holding right views (sammādiṭṭhiko), adhering to actions based on right views (sammādiṭṭhikammasamādāno), because of adhering to actions based on right views, on the dissolution of the body (kāyassa bhedā), after death, reappears in a good destination (sugatiṃ), in a heavenly world (saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati).

So too will a Brāhmin, a Vessa, a Sudda, a Samaṇa, Vāseṭṭha… having conducted himself well through body (kāyena sucaritaṃ caritvā), having conducted himself well through speech, having conducted himself well through mind, holding right views (sammādiṭṭhiko), adhering to actions based on right views (sammādiṭṭhikammasamādāno), because of adhering to actions based on right views, on the dissolution of the body (kāyassa bhedā), after death, reappears in a good destination (sugatiṃ), in a heavenly world (saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati).
commentary_pali: 136. Idāni yathājātiyā na sakkā sujjhituṃ, sammāpaṭipattiyāva sujjhanti, tamatthaṃ pākaṭaṃ karonto khattiyopi kho, vāseṭṭhāti desanaṃ ārabhi. Tattha micchādiṭṭhikammasamādānahetūti micchādiṭṭhivasena samādinnakammahetu, micchādiṭṭhikammassa vā samādānahetu.
commentary_english:
Now, clarifying the meaning that it is not possible to be purified merely by birth, but they are purified only by right practice, he began the discourse, "<hi rend="bold">Even a noble warrior, Vāseṭṭha...</hi>."

There, <hi rend="bold">micchādiṭṭhikammasamādānahetū</hi> means because of the action undertaken through wrong view, or because of undertaking the action of wrong view.

mula_pali:
137. ‘‘Khattiyopi kho, vāseṭṭha, kāyena dvayakārī, vācāya dvayakārī, manasā dvayakārī, vimissadiṭṭhiko vimissadiṭṭhikammasamādāno vimissadiṭṭhikammasamādānahetu vimissadiṭṭhiko vimissakammasamādāno vimissakammasamādānahetu (syā.), vītimissadiṭṭhiko vītimissadiṭṭhikammasamādānahetu (sī. pī.) kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī hoti. Brāhmaṇopi kho, vāseṭṭha …pe… vessopi kho, vāseṭṭha… suddopi kho, vāseṭṭha… samaṇopi kho, vāseṭṭha, kāyena dvayakārī , vācāya dvayakārī, manasā dvayakārī, vimissadiṭṭhiko vimissadiṭṭhikammasamādāno vimissadiṭṭhikammasamādānahetu kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī hoti.

Bodhipakkhiyabhāvanā
mula_english:
‘And a Kṣatriya, Vāseṭṭha, who performs deeds of both kinds through body (kāyena), speech (vācāya), and mind (manasā); whose view is mixed (vimissadiṭṭhiko), whose undertaking of deeds is based on mixed views (vimissadiṭṭhikammasamādāno), and whose cause for undertaking deeds is mixed views, will, at the breaking up of the body (kāyassa bhedā), after death (paraṃ maraṇā), experience both pleasure (sukha) and pain (dukkha).

A Brāhmaṇa, Vāseṭṭha… a merchant, Vāseṭṭha… a Śūdra, Vāseṭṭha… a renunciate, Vāseṭṭha, who performs deeds of both kinds through body, speech, and mind; whose view is mixed, whose undertaking of deeds is based on mixed views, and whose cause for undertaking deeds is mixed views, will, at the breaking up of the body, after death, experience both pleasure and pain.

Cultivating the Qualities Conducive to Awakening (bodhipakkhiyabhāvanā).
commentary_pali:
137.Dvayakārīti kālena kusalaṃ karoti, kālena akusalanti evaṃ ubhayakārī. Sukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī hotīti ekakkhaṇe ubhayavipākadānaṭṭhānaṃ nāma natthi. Yena pana akusalaṃ bahuṃ kataṃ hoti, kusalaṃ mandaṃ, so taṃ kusalaṃ nissāya khattiyakule vā brāhmaṇakule vā nibbattati. Atha naṃ akusalakammaṃ kāṇampi karoti khujjampi pīṭhasappimpi. So rajjassa vā anaraho hoti, abhisittakāle vā evaṃbhūto bhoge paribhuñjituṃ na sakkoti. Aparassa maraṇakāle dve balavamallā viya te dvepi kusalākusalakammāni upaṭṭhahanti. Tesu akusalaṃ balavataraṃ hoti, taṃ kusalaṃ paṭibāhitvā tiracchānayoniyaṃ nibbattāpeti. Kusalakammampi pavattivedanīyaṃ hoti. Tamenaṃ maṅgalahatthiṃ vā karonti maṅgalaassaṃ vā maṅgalausabhaṃ vā. So sampattiṃ anubhavati . Idaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ ‘‘sukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī hotī’’ti.

Bodhipakkhiyabhāvanāvaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
137. "A doer of both [good and evil]" means that at times one does what is wholesome (*kuśala*), and at times one does what is unwholesome (*akuśala*); thus, one is a doer of both.

"Experiencing pleasure and pain" means there is no such thing as a place for giving two results, wholesome and unwholesome, in a single moment.

Moreover, someone who has done much that is unwholesome (*akuśala*) and little that is wholesome (*kuśala*), is reborn, relying on that wholesome karma, in a *kṣatriya* family or a *brāhmaṇa* family.

Then, unwholesome karma makes them blind (*kāṇa*), hunchbacked (*khujja*), or a "stool-serpent" (*pīṭhasappin*).

They are unworthy of kingship (*rājya*), or, at the time of consecration (*abhiṣeka-kāla*), being of such a nature, they are unable to enjoy possessions (*bhoga*).

At the time of death of another, two strong wrestlers, as it were, two wholesome and unwholesome actions (*kuśalākuśalakarmāṇi*) attend to them.

Among these, the unwholesome (*akuśala*) is stronger; having repelled the wholesome (*kuśala*), it causes rebirth in the animal realm (*tiracchānayoni*).

A wholesome action (*kuśalakarma*) is also something to be experienced as it matures.

They make them either an auspicious elephant (*maṅgalahastin*), an auspicious horse (*maṅgalaassa*), or an auspicious bull (*maṅgalausabha*).

They experience prosperity (*sampatti*).

This was said with reference to "experiencing pleasure and pain."

Explanation of the cultivation of the Wings to Awakening (*bodhipakkhiyabhāvanāvaṇṇanā*).

mula_pali: 138. ‘‘Khattiyopi kho, vāseṭṭha, kāyena saṃvuto vācāya saṃvuto manasā saṃvuto sattannaṃ bodhipakkhiyānaṃ dhammānaṃ bhāvanamanvāya diṭṭheva dhamme parinibbāyati parinibbāti (ka.). Brāhmaṇopi kho, vāseṭṭha…pe… vessopi kho vāseṭṭha… suddopi kho, vāseṭṭha … samaṇopi kho, vāseṭṭha, kāyena saṃvuto vācāya saṃvuto manasā saṃvuto sattannaṃ bodhipakkhiyānaṃ dhammānaṃ bhāvanamanvāya diṭṭheva dhamme parinibbāyati.
mula_english: ‘And a *Kṣatriya* (khattiyo) who is restrained in body (*kāyena saṃvuto*), speech (*vācāya saṃvuto*) and thought (*manasā saṃvuto*), and who has developed the seven requisites of enlightenment (*sattannaṃ bodhipakkhiyānaṃ dhammānaṃ bhāvanamanvāya*), will attain to *Parinirvāṇa* (*parinibbāyati*) in this very life (*diṭṭheva dhamme*). A *Brāhmaṇa* (brāhmaṇopi) also, O *Vāseṭṭha*…pe… A *Vaiśya* (vessopi) also, O *Vāseṭṭha*… A *Śūdra* (suddopi) also, O *Vāseṭṭha*… A *Śramaṇa* (samaṇopi) also, O *Vāseṭṭha*, who is restrained in body (*kāyena saṃvuto*), speech (*vācāya saṃvuto*) and thought (*manasā saṃvuto*), and who has developed the seven requisites of enlightenment (*sattannaṃ bodhipakkhiyānaṃ dhammānaṃ bhāvanamanvāya*), will attain to *Parinirvāṇa* (*parinibbāyati*) in this very life (*diṭṭheva dhamme*).
commentary_pali: 138.Sattannaṃ bodhipakkhiyānanti ‘‘cattāro satipaṭṭhānā’’ti ādikoṭṭhāsavasena sattannaṃ, paṭipāṭiyā pana sattatiṃsāya bodhipakkhiyānaṃ dhammānaṃ . Bhāvanamanvāyāti bhāvanaṃ anugantvā, paṭipajjitvāti attho. Parinibbāyatīti kilesaparinibbānena parinibbāyati. Iti bhagavā cattāro vaṇṇe dassetvā vinivattetvā paṭividdhacatusaccaṃ khīṇāsavameva devamanussesu seṭṭhaṃ katvā dassesi.
commentary_english: 138. *sattannaṃ bodhipakkhiyāna* means of the seven—as in, "the four establishments of mindfulness ( *cattāro satipaṭṭhānā* )"—in terms of the initial divisions; however, in order, of the thirty-seven qualities pertaining to enlightenment (*bodhipakkhiyānaṃ dhammānaṃ*). *bhāvanamanvāyā* means having followed after cultivation (*bhāvanaṃ anugantvā*), that is, having practiced. *parinibbāyatī* means attains final *nirvāṇa* (*parinibbāna*) through the *nirvāṇa* of defilements (*kilesaparinibbānena*). Thus, the Blessed One, having shown the four castes and having dismissed them, showed that only the one whose four truths have been penetrated, the one whose outflows are ended (*khīṇāsava*), is the best among gods and humans.

mula_pali: 139. ‘‘Imesañhi, vāseṭṭha, catunnaṃ vaṇṇānaṃ yo hoti bhikkhu arahaṃ khīṇāsavo vusitavā katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano sammadaññā vimutto so nesaṃ aggamakkhāyati dhammeneva. No adhammena. Dhammo hi, vāseṭṭha, seṭṭho janetasmiṃ diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañca.
mula_english: “Indeed, Vāseṭṭha, whichever bhikkhu among these four classes is an *arhat*, one who has destroyed the influxes, who has lived the life, done what was to be done, laid down the burden, attained his own welfare, utterly destroyed the fetters of becoming, is liberated by perfect knowledge, he is declared the best of them by Dhamma alone, and not otherwise. For, Vāseṭṭha, the *dharma* is the best thing for people in this life and in the next as well.

mula_pali:
140. ‘‘Brahmunā pesā, vāseṭṭha, sanaṅkumārena gāthā bhāsitā –

‘Khattiyo seṭṭho janetasmiṃ, ye gottapaṭisārino;

Vijjācaraṇasampanno, so seṭṭho devamānuse’ti.

‘‘Sā kho panesā, vāseṭṭha, brahmunā sanaṅkumārena gāthā sugītā, no duggītā. Subhāsitā, no dubbhāsitā. Atthasaṃhitā, no anatthasaṃhitā. Anumatā mayā. Ahampi, vāseṭṭha, evaṃ vadāmi –

‘Khattiyo seṭṭho janetasmiṃ, ye gottapaṭisārino;

Vijjācaraṇasampanno, so seṭṭho devamānuse’ti.

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā vāseṭṭhabhāradvājā bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Aggaññasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ catutthaṃ.
mula_english:
140. "The *gāthā* was spoken by Brahmā, Vāseṭṭha, by Sanankumāra:

'The *kṣatriya* is the best among the people who are defined by lineage;

He who is endowed with knowledge and conduct is the best among gods and humans.'"

"And that *gāthā*, Vāseṭṭha, by Brahmā, by Sanankumāra, is well sung, not badly sung, rightly spoken (*subhāṣitā*), not wrongly spoken (*dubbhāṣitā*), connected with profit (*arthasaṃhitā*), not unconnected (*anarthasaṃhitā*). It is approved by me.

I also, Vāseṭṭha, say thus:

'The *kṣatriya* is the best among the people who are defined by lineage;

He who is endowed with knowledge and conduct is the best among gods and humans.'"

Thus spoke the Blessed One (*Bhagavān*).

Vāseṭṭha and Bhāradvāja, pleased, rejoiced in the Blessed One’s words (*bhāṣitaṃ abhinandunti*).

The *Aggañña Sutta*, the fourth, is finished.
commentary_pali:
140. Idāni tamevatthaṃ lokasammatassa brahmunopi vacanadassanānusārena daḷhaṃ katvā dassento imesañhi vāseṭṭha catunnaṃ vaṇṇānantiādimāha. ‘‘Brahmunāpesā’’tiādi ambaṭṭhasutte vitthāritaṃ. Iti bhagavā ettakena iminā kathāmaggena seṭṭhacchedakavādameva dassetvā suttantaṃ vinivattetvā arahattanikūṭena desanaṃ niṭṭhāpesi. Attamanā vāseṭṭhabhāradvājāti vāseṭṭhabhāradvāja sāmaṇerāpi hi sakamanā tuṭṭhamanā ‘‘sādhu, sādhū’’ti bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandiṃsu. Idameva suttantaṃ āvajjantā anumajjantā saha paṭisambhidāhi arahattaṃ pāpuṇiṃsūti.

Sumaṅgalavilāsiniyā dīghanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Aggaññasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
140. Now, showing that same meaning, having made it firm according to the words and teachings of the world-approved Brahmā, he said, "<hi rend="bold">Indeed, these four classes of Vāseṭṭha</hi>," and so forth.

"Brahmunāpesā," and so on, is explained in detail in the Ambaṭṭha Sutta.

Thus, the Blessed One, with this much, with this method of discussion, having shown only the doctrine of the best destroyer, having turned away the Suttanta, concluded the teaching with the perfection of Arahantship.

<hi rend="bold">The Vāseṭṭha-bhāradvājas being pleased</hi>, the Vāseṭṭha-bhāradvāja novices, being of one mind, with satisfied minds, rejoiced in the Blessed One's words, saying "Good! Good!".

They attained Arahantship together with the discriminations, reflecting on and rejoicing in this very Suttanta.

The Commentary on the Long Discourses, *Sumaṅgalavilāsinīyā Dīghanikāyaṭṭhakathāya*

The Aggañña Sutta Commentary is concluded.

mula_pali: 141. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā nāḷandāyaṃ viharati pāvārikambavane. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā sāriputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘evaṃpasanno ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavati, na cāhu na ca bhavissati na cetarahi vijjati añño samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā bhagavatā bhiyyobhiññataro yadidaṃ sambodhiya’’nti.
mula_english:
141. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One (bhagavā) was staying at Nāḷandā in Pāvārika's mango-grove.

Then the venerable (āyasmā) Śāriputta approached the Blessed One (bhagavā); having approached, he bowed down to the Blessed One (bhagavantaṃ) and sat down at one side.

Seated at one side, the venerable (āyasmā) Śāriputta said this to the Blessed One (bhagavantaṃ): "I have such faith, venerable sir (bhante), in the Blessed One (bhagavati) that there never has been, nor will there be, nor is there now any other ascetic (samaṇo) or Brahmin (brāhmaṇo) with greater direct knowledge than the Blessed One (bhagavatā) with regard to awakening (sambodhiya)."
commentary_pali:
141.Evaṃme sutanti sampasādanīyasuttaṃ. Tatrāyamanuttānapadavaṇṇanā – nāḷandāyanti nāḷandāti evaṃnāmake nagare, taṃ nagaraṃ gocaragāmaṃ katvā. Pāvārikambavaneti dussapāvārikaseṭṭhino ambavane. Taṃ kira tassa uyyānaṃ ahosi. So bhagavato dhammadesanaṃ sutvā bhagavati pasanno tasmiṃ uyyāne kuṭileṇamaṇḍapādipaṭimaṇḍitaṃ bhagavato vihāraṃ katvā niyyātesi. So vihāro jīvakambavanaṃ viya ‘‘pāvārikambavana’’ntveva saṅkhyaṃ gato, tasmiṃ pāvārikambavane viharatīti attho. Bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘evaṃpasanno ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavatī’’ti. Kasmā evaṃ avoca? Attano uppannasomanassapavedanatthaṃ.

Tatrāyamanupubbikathā – thero kira taṃdivasaṃ kālasseva sarīrappaṭijagganaṃ katvā sunivatthanivāsano pattacīvaramādāya pāsādikehi abhikkantādīhi devamanussānaṃ pasādaṃ āvahanto nāḷandavāsīnaṃ hitasukhamanubrūhayanto piṇḍāya pavisitvā pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto vihāraṃ gantvā satthu vattaṃ dassetvā satthari gandhakuṭiṃ paviṭṭhe satthāraṃ vanditvā attano divāṭṭhānaṃ agamāsi. Tattha saddhivihārikantevāsikesu vattaṃ dassetvā paṭikkantesu divāṭṭhānaṃ sammajjitvā cammakkhaṇḍaṃ paññapetvā udakatumbato udakena hatthapāde sītale katvā tisandhipallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā kālaparicchedaṃ katvā phalasamāpattiṃ samāpajji.

So yathāparicchinnakālavasena samāpattito vuṭṭhāya attano guṇe anussaritumāraddho. Athassa guṇe anussarato sīlaṃ āpāthamāgataṃ. Tato paṭipāṭiyāva samādhi paññā vimutti vimuttiñāṇadassanaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ ākāsānañcāyatanasamāpatti viññānañcāyatanasamāpatti ākiñcaññāyatanasamāpatti nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasamāpatti vipassanāñāṇaṃ manomayiddhiñāṇaṃ iddhividhañāṇaṃ dibbasotañāṇaṃ cetopariyañāṇaṃ pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇaṃ dibbacakkhuñāṇaṃ…pe… sotāpattimaggo sotāpattiphalaṃ…pe… arahattamaggo arahattaphalaṃ atthapaṭisambhidā dhammapaṭisambhidā niruttipaṭisambhidā paṭibhānapaṭisambhidā sāvakapāramīñāṇaṃ. Ito paṭṭhāya kappasatasahassādhikassa asaṅkhyeyyassa upari anomadassībuddhassa pādamūle kataṃ abhinīhāraṃ ādiṃ katvā attano guṇe anussarato yāva nisinnapallaṅkā guṇā upaṭṭhahiṃsu.

Evaṃ thero attano guṇe anussaramāno guṇānaṃ pamāṇaṃ vā paricchedaṃ vā daṭṭhuṃ nāsakkhi. So cintesi – ‘‘mayhaṃ tāva padesañāṇe ṭhitassa sāvakassa guṇānaṃ pamāṇaṃ vā paricchedo vā natthi. Ahaṃ pana yaṃ satthāraṃ uddissa pabbajito, kīdisā nu kho tassa guṇā’’ti dasabalassa guṇe anussarituṃ āraddho. So bhagavato sīlaṃ nissāya, samādhiṃ paññaṃ vimuttiṃ vimuttiñāṇadassanaṃ nissāya, cattāro satipaṭṭhāne nissāya, cattāro sammappadhāne cattāro iddhipāde cattāro magge cattāri phalāni catasso paṭisambhidā catuyoniparicchedakañāṇaṃ cattāro ariyavaṃse nissāya dasabalassa guṇe anussaritumāraddho.

Tathā pañca padhāniyaṅgāni, pañcaṅgikaṃsammāsamādhiṃ, pañcindriyāni, pañca balāni, pañca nissaraṇiyā dhātuyo, pañca vimuttāyatanāni, pañca vimuttiparipācaniyā paññā, cha sāraṇīye dhamme, cha anussatiṭṭhānāni, cha gārave, cha nissaraṇiyā dhātuyo, cha satatavihāre, cha anuttariyāni, cha nibbedhabhāgiyā paññā, cha abhiññā, cha asādhāraṇañāṇāni, satta aparihāniye dhamme, satta ariyadhanāni, satta bojjhaṅge, satta sappurisadhamme, satta nijjaravatthūni, satta paññā, satta dakkhiṇeyyapuggale, satta khīṇāsavabalāni, aṭṭha paññāpaṭilābhahetū, aṭṭha sammattāni, aṭṭha lokadhammātikkame, aṭṭha ārambhavatthūni, aṭṭha akkhaṇadesanā, aṭṭha mahāpurisavitakke, aṭṭha abhibhāyatanāni, aṭṭha vimokkhe, nava yonisomanasikāramūlake dhamme, nava pārisuddhipadhāniyaṅgāni, nava sattāvāsadesanā, nava āghātappaṭivinaye, nava paññā, nava nānattāni, nava anupubbavihāre, dasa nāthakaraṇe dhamme, dasa kasiṇāyatanāni, dasa kusalakammapathe, dasa tathāgatabalāni, dasa sammattāni, dasa ariyavāse, dasa asekkhadhamme, ekādasa mettānisaṃse, dvādasa dhammacakkākāre, terasa dhutaṅgaguṇe , cuddasa buddhañāṇāni, pañcadasa vimuttiparipācaniye dhamme, soḷasavidhaṃ ānāpānassatiṃ, aṭṭhārasa buddhadhamme, ekūnavīsati paccavekkhaṇañāṇāni, catucattālīsa ñāṇavatthūni, paropaṇṇāsa kusaladhamme, sattasattati ñāṇavatthūni, catuvīsatikoṭisatasahassasamāpattisañcaramahāvajirañāṇaṃ nissāya dasabalassa guṇe anussarituṃ ārabhi.

Tasmiṃyeva ca divāṭṭhāne nisinnoyeva upari ‘‘aparaṃ pana, bhante, etadānuttariya’’nti āgamissanti soḷasa aparampariyadhammā, tepi nissāya anussarituṃ ārabhi. So ‘‘kusalapaññattiyaṃ anuttaro mayhaṃ satthā, āyatanapaññattiyaṃ anuttaro, gabbhāvakkantiyaṃ anuttaro, ādesanāvidhāsu anuttaro, dassanasamāpattiyaṃ anuttaro, puggalapaññattiyaṃ anuttaro, padhāne anuttaro, paṭipadāsu anuttaro, bhassasamācāre anuttaro, purisasīlasamācāre anuttaro, anusāsanīvidhāsu anuttaro, parapuggalavimuttiñāṇe anuttaro, sassatavādesu anuttaro, pubbenivāsañāṇe anuttaro, dibbacakkhuñāṇe anuttaro, iddhividhe anuttaro, iminā ca iminā ca anuttaro’’ti evaṃ dasabalassa guṇe anussaranto bhagavato guṇānaṃ neva antaṃ, na pamāṇaṃ passi. Thero attanopi tāva guṇānaṃ antaṃ vā pamāṇaṃ vā nāddasa, bhagavato guṇānaṃ kiṃ passissati? Yassa yassa hi paññā mahatī ñāṇaṃ visadaṃ, so so buddhaguṇe mahantato saddahati. Lokiyamahājano ukkāsitvāpi khipitvāpi ‘‘namo buddhāna’’nti attano attano upanissaye ṭhatvā buddhānaṃ guṇe anussarati. Sabbalokiyamahājanato eko sotāpanno buddhaguṇe mahantato saddahati. Sotāpannānaṃ satatopi sahassatopi eko sakadāgāmī. Sakadāgāmīnaṃ satatopi sahassatopi eko anāgāmī. Anāgāmīnaṃ satatopi sahassatopi eko arahā buddhaguṇe mahantato saddahati. Avasesaarahantehi asīti mahātherā buddhaguṇe mahantato saddahanti. Asītimahātherehi cattāro mahātherā. Catūhi mahātherehi dve aggasāvakā. Tesupi sāriputtatthero, sāriputtattheratopi eko paccekabuddho buddhaguṇe mahantato saddahati. Sace pana sakalacakkavāḷagabbhe saṅghāṭikaṇṇena saṅghāṭikaṇṇaṃ pahariyamānā nisinnā paccekabuddhā buddhaguṇe anussareyyuṃ, tehi sabbehipi eko sabbaññubuddhova buddhaguṇe mahantato saddahati.

Seyyathāpi nāma mahājano ‘‘mahāsamuddo gambhīro uttāno’’ti jānanatthaṃ yottāni vaṭṭeyya, tattha koci byāmappamāṇaṃ yottaṃ vaṭṭeyya, koci dve byāmaṃ, koci dasabyāmaṃ, koci vīsatibyāmaṃ, koci tiṃsabyāmaṃ, koci cattālīsabyāmaṃ, koci paññāsabyāmaṃ, koci satabyāmaṃ, koci sahassabyāmaṃ , koci caturāsītibyāmasahassaṃ. Te nāvaṃ āruyha, samuddamajjhe uggatapabbatādimhi vā ṭhatvā attano attano yottaṃ otāreyyuṃ, tesu yassa yottaṃ byāmamattaṃ, so byāmamattaṭṭhāneyeva udakaṃ jānāti…pe… yassa caturāsītibyāmasahassaṃ, so caturāsītibyāmasahassaṭṭhāneyeva udakaṃ jānāti. Parato udakaṃ ettakanti na jānāti. Mahāsamudde pana na tattakaṃyeva udakaṃ, atha kho anantamaparimāṇaṃ. Caturāsītiyojanasahassaṃ gambhīro hi mahāsamuddo, evameva ekabyāmayottato paṭṭhāya navabyāmayottena ñātaudakaṃ viya lokiyamahājanena diṭṭhabuddhaguṇā veditabbā. Dasabyāmayottena dasabyāmaṭṭhāne ñātaudakaṃ viya sotāpannena diṭṭhabuddhaguṇā. Vīsatibyāmayottena vīsatibyāmaṭṭhāne ñātaudakaṃ viya sakadāgāminā diṭṭhabuddhaguṇā. Tiṃsabyāmayottena tiṃsabyāmaṭṭhāne ñātaudakaṃ viya anāgāminā diṭṭhabuddhaguṇā. Cattālīsabyāmayottena cattālīsabyāmaṭṭhāne ñātaudakaṃ viya arahatā diṭṭhabuddhaguṇā. Paññāsabyāmayottena paññāsabyāmaṭṭhāne ñātaudakaṃ viya asītimahātherehi diṭṭhabuddhaguṇā. Satabyāmayottena satabyāmaṭṭhāne ñātaudakaṃ viya catūhi mahātherehi diṭṭhabuddhaguṇā. Sahassabyāmayottena sahassabyāmaṭṭhāne ñātaudakaṃ viya mahāmoggallānattherena diṭṭhabuddhaguṇā. Caturāsītibyāmasahassayottena caturāsītibyāmasahassaṭṭhāne ñātaudakaṃ viya dhammasenāpatinā sāriputtattherena diṭṭhabuddhaguṇā. Tattha yathā so puriso mahāsamudde udakaṃ nāma na ettakaṃyeva, anantamaparimāṇanti gaṇhāti, evameva āyasmā sāriputto dhammanvayena anvayabuddhiyā anumānena nayaggāhena sāvakapāramīñāṇe ṭhatvā dasabalassa guṇe anussaranto ‘‘buddhaguṇā anantā aparimāṇā’’ti saddahi.

Therena hi diṭṭhabuddhaguṇehi dhammanvayena gahetabbabuddhaguṇāyeva bahutarā. Yathā kathaṃ viya? Yathā ito nava ito navāti aṭṭhārasa yojanāni avattharitvā gacchantiyā candabhāgāya mahānadiyā puriso sūcipāsena udakaṃ gaṇheyya, sūcipāsena gahitaudakato aggahitameva bahu hoti. Yathā vā pana puriso mahāpathavito aṅguliyā paṃsuṃ gaṇheyya, aṅguliyā gahitapaṃsuto avasesapaṃsuyeva bahu hoti. Yathā vā pana puriso mahāsamuddābhimukhiṃ aṅguliṃ kareyya, aṅguliabhimukhaudakato avasesaṃ udakaṃyeva bahu hoti. Yathā ca puriso ākāsābhimukhiṃ aṅguliṃ kareyya, aṅguliabhimukhaākāsato sesaākāsappadesova bahu hoti. Evaṃ therena diṭṭhabuddhaguṇehi adiṭṭhā guṇāva bahūti veditabbā. Vuttampi cetaṃ –

‘‘Buddhopi buddhassa bhaṇeyya vaṇṇaṃ,

Kappampi ce aññamabhāsamāno;

Khīyetha kappo ciradīghamantare,

Vaṇṇo na khīyetha tathāgatassā’’ti.

Evaṃ therassa attano ca satthu ca guṇe anussarato yamakamahānadīmahogho viya abbhantare pītisomanassaṃ avattharamānaṃ vāto viya bhastaṃ, ubbhijjitvā uggataudakaṃ viya mahārahadaṃ sakalasarīraṃ pūreti. Tato therassa ‘‘supatthitā vata me patthanā, suladdhā me pabbajjā, yvāhaṃ evaṃvidhassa satthu santike pabbajito’’ti āvajjantassa balavataraṃ pītisomanassaṃ uppajji.

Atha thero ‘‘kassāhaṃ imaṃ pītisomanassaṃ āroceyya’’nti cintento añño koci samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā devo vā māro vā brahmā vā mama imaṃ pasādaṃ anucchavikaṃ katvā paṭiggahetuṃ na sakkhissati, ahaṃ imaṃ somanassaṃ satthunoyeva pavedeyyāmi, satthāva me paṭiggaṇhituṃ sakkhissati, so hi tiṭṭhatu mama pītisomanassaṃ, mādisassa samaṇasatassa vā samaṇasahassassa vā samaṇasatasahassassa vā somanassaṃ pavedentassa sabbesaṃ manaṃ gaṇhanto paṭiggahetuṃ sakkoti. Seyyathāpi nāma aṭṭhārasa yojanāni avattharamānaṃ gacchantiṃ candabhāgamahānadiṃ kusumbhā vā kandarā vā sampaṭicchituṃ na sakkonti, mahāsamuddova taṃ sampaṭicchati. Mahāsamuddo hi tiṭṭhatu candabhāgā, evarūpānaṃ nadīnaṃ satampi sahassampi satasahassampi sampaṭicchati, na cassa tena ūnattaṃ vā pūrattaṃ vā paññāyati, evameva satthā mādisassa samaṇasatassa samaṇasahassassa samaṇasatasahassassa vā pītisomanassaṃ pavedentassa sabbesaṃ manaṃ gaṇhanto paṭiggahetuṃ sakkoti. Sesā samaṇabrāhmaṇādayo candabhāgaṃ kusumbhakandarā viya mama somanassaṃ sampaṭicchituṃ na sakkonti . Handāhaṃ mama pītisomanassaṃ satthunova ārocemīti pallaṅkaṃ vinibbhujitvā cammakkhaṇḍaṃ papphoṭetvā ādāya sāyanhasamaye pupphānaṃ vaṇṭato chijjitvā paggharaṇakāle satthāraṃ upasaṅkamitvā attano somanassaṃ pavedento evaṃpasanno ahaṃ, bhantetiādimāha. Tattha evaṃpasannoti evaṃ uppannasaddho, evaṃ saddahāmīti attho. Bhiyyobhiññataroti bhiyyataro abhiññāto, bhiyyatarābhiñño vā, uttaritarañāṇoti attho. Sambodhiyanti sabbaññutaññāṇe arahattamaggañāṇe vā, arahattamaggeneva hi buddhaguṇā nippadesā gahitā honti. Dve hi aggasāvakā arahattamaggeneva sāvakapāramīñāṇaṃ paṭilabhanti. Paccekabuddhā paccekabodhiñāṇaṃ. Buddhā sabbaññutaññāṇañceva sakale ca buddhaguṇe. Sabbañhi nesaṃ arahattamaggeneva ijjhati. Tasmā arahattamaggañāṇaṃ sambodhi nāma hoti. Tena uttaritaro bhagavatā natthi. Tenāha ‘‘bhagavatā bhiyyobhiññataro yadidaṃ sambodhiya’’nti.

evaṃpasanno ahaṃ, bhante evaṃpasanno Bhiyyobhiññataro Sambodhiya
commentary_english:
141. "Thus I have heard" is the Sampasadanīya Sutta. Here is a word-by-word explanation of it: *nāḷandāya* means in a city of that name, Nāḷanda, after making that city a pasture village. *pāvārikambavane* means in the mango grove of Dussapāvārika the millionaire. It seems that this was his park. Having heard the Blessed One's teaching, he was pleased with the Blessed One. In that park, he had a monastery built for the Blessed One, adorned with a brick hut and a pavilion. That monastery, like Jīvaka's mango grove, went by the name "Pāvārikambavana." The meaning is that he lived in that Pāvārikambavana. He said this to the Blessed One: "I am thus pleased, venerable sir, with the Blessed One." Why did he say this? To announce the pleasure that had arisen in himself. Here is the connected story: It seems that early that day, after attending to his bodily needs, the elder, well-clothed and carrying his bowl and robe, entered for alms, inspiring faith in the pleasing (sight) of his going and so on for gods and humans, increasing the benefit and happiness of the residents of Nāḷanda. After the meal, returning from his alms round, he went to the monastery, showed the proper respect to the Teacher, and after the Teacher had entered the Perfumed Chamber, he paid homage to the Teacher and went to his day quarters. There, after showing the proper respect to his fellow residents and pupils and after they had departed, he swept the day quarters, spread out a leather mat, cooled his hands and feet with water from a water pot, folded his legs in the three-jointed lotus position, set a time limit, and attained the fruition attainment. Having arisen from the attainment according to the time he had determined, he began to recollect his own qualities. Then, as he recollected his qualities, morality came to mind. Then, in sequence, concentration, wisdom, liberation, the knowledge and vision of liberation, the first *jhāna*, the second *jhāna*, the third *jhāna*, the fourth *jhāna*, the attainment of the base of the infinity of space, the attainment of the base of the infinity of consciousness, the attainment of the base of nothingness, the attainment of the base of neither perception nor non-perception, insight knowledge, mind-made power knowledge, the knowledge of the varieties of magical power, divine-ear knowledge, mind-reading knowledge, knowledge of the recollection of past lives, divine-eye knowledge...pe...the path of stream-entry, the fruit of stream-entry...pe...the path of arahantship, the fruit of arahantship, knowledge of the meaning, knowledge of the Dhamma, knowledge of language, knowledge of ready wit, the knowledge of a disciple's perfections. From here on, starting with the aspiration he made at the feet of the Buddha Anomadassī, more than a hundred thousand aeons ago, as he recollected his own qualities, the qualities up to the lotus posture in which he was sitting presented themselves. In this way, as the elder recollected his own qualities, he was unable to see the measure or limit of his qualities. He thought: "Even for me, a disciple standing in the knowledge of a part (of the teaching), there is no measure or limit to my qualities. But what are the qualities of the Teacher for whom I went forth?" He began to recollect the qualities of the one with the ten powers. He began to recollect the qualities of the one with the ten powers, relying on the Blessed One's morality, relying on his concentration, wisdom, liberation, and the knowledge and vision of liberation, relying on the four establishments of mindfulness, relying on the four right exertions, the four bases of power, the four paths, the four fruits, the four kinds of special knowledge, the knowledge that distinguishes the four types of birth, and relying on the four noble lineages. Likewise, the five factors of exertion, right concentration with five factors, the five faculties, the five powers, the five elements of escape, the five abodes of the liberated, the five kinds of wisdom that ripen liberation, the six things that cause affection, the six places for recollection, the six grounds for respect, the six elements of escape, the six constant abodes, the six unsurpassed things, the six kinds of wisdom that lead to penetration, the six superknowledges, the six kinds of uncommon knowledge, the seven conditions for non-decline, the seven noble treasures, the seven factors of enlightenment, the seven qualities of a good person, the seven things for wearing away (defilements), the seven kinds of wisdom, the seven worthy of offerings, the seven powers of one who has destroyed the taints, the eight causes for the attainment of wisdom, the eight kinds of rightness, the eight ways of transcending worldly conditions, the eight grounds for initiative, the eight unsuitable times for teaching, the eight thoughts of a great man, the eight abodes of mastery, the eight liberations, the nine kinds of Dhamma rooted in appropriate attention, the nine factors for complete purification through exertion, the nine abodes of beings, the nine ways of removing malice, the nine kinds of wisdom, the nine diversities, the nine successive abodes, the ten things that create protection, the ten kasina spheres, the ten courses of skillful action, the ten powers of a Tathāgata, the ten kinds of rightness, the ten noble abodes, the ten things for one in higher training, the eleven benefits of loving-kindness, the twelve aspects of the wheel of Dhamma, the thirteen qualities of ascetic practices, the fourteen Buddha knowledges, the fifteen conditions for the ripening of liberation, mindfulness of breathing in sixteen ways, the eighteen Buddha-dharmas, the nineteen knowledges of reviewing, the forty-four objects of knowledge, the fifty excellent qualities, the seventy-seven objects of knowledge, relying on the great adamantine knowledge that traverses the one hundred and twenty-four million concentrations, he began to recollect the qualities of the one with the ten powers. And while he was sitting in those very day quarters, he began to recollect, relying on those sixteen further qualities that would come in the passage "Furthermore, venerable sir, this is unsurpassed." He said: "My teacher is unsurpassed in the exposition of skillful qualities, unsurpassed in the exposition of the bases, unsurpassed in entering the womb, unsurpassed in methods of instruction, unsurpassed in the attainment of vision, unsurpassed in the exposition of individuals, unsurpassed in exertion, unsurpassed in practice, unsurpassed in speaking and conduct, unsurpassed in the moral conduct of a man, unsurpassed in methods of advising, unsurpassed in the knowledge of the liberation of other individuals, unsurpassed in eternalist theories, unsurpassed in the knowledge of past lives, unsurpassed in divine-eye knowledge, unsurpassed in magical power, unsurpassed in this and in that." As he thus recollected the qualities of the one with the ten powers, he saw neither the end nor the measure of the Blessed One's qualities. If the elder did not see the end or measure of his own qualities, what would he see of the Blessed One's qualities? To the extent that someone's wisdom is great and their knowledge is clear, to that extent they have faith in the Buddha's qualities as being great. Ordinary worldly people, even after coughing or spitting, recollect the Buddhas' qualities by saying "Homage to the Buddhas," standing in their own respective grounds. A stream-enterer has more faith in the Buddhas' qualities as being great than all ordinary worldly people. One who returns only once (to this world) is one out of a hundred or a thousand stream-enterers. One who returns only once [to this world] is superior even to hundreds and thousands of those who will not return. One *arhat* who will not return is superior to hundreds and thousands on account of the greatness of the qualities of the Buddha. Eighty great *theras*, along with the remaining *arhats*, have faith in the greatness of the qualities of the Buddha. Four great *theras* [come] from eighty great *theras*. Two chief disciples [come] from four great *theras*. Sāriputta Thera is among these, but one solitary buddha has more faith in the greatness of the qualities of the Buddha than Sāriputta Thera. If *pratyekabuddhas* seated in the womb of the entire *cakravāḍa*, their shoulders touching, were to recollect the qualities of the Buddha, a single all-knowing Buddha would have more faith in the greatness of the qualities of the Buddha than all of them. Just as a great crowd might twist ropes to ascertain whether "the great ocean is deep or shallow," one person might twist a rope one *vyāma* in length, another two *vyāmas*, another ten *vyāmas*, another twenty *vyāmas*, another thirty *vyāmas*, another forty *vyāmas*, another fifty *vyāmas*, another one hundred *vyāmas*, another one thousand *vyāmas*, another eighty-four thousand *byāmas*. Embarking on a ship in the middle of the ocean, whether standing on a mountain that has emerged or elsewhere, they would cast their own ropes. Of these, he whose rope is one *vyāma* in length knows the water only to the extent of one *vyāma*. And he whose rope is eighty-four thousand *byāmas* [long] knows the water only to the extent of eighty-four thousand *byāmas*. He does not know how much water there is beyond. In the great ocean, however, the water is not just that much; rather, it is endless and immeasurable. Indeed, the great ocean is eighty-four thousand *yojanas* deep. Just so, the qualities of the Buddha, known by worldly people, should be understood like water that is known [to be of a certain depth] from one *vyāma*’s length of rope up to nine *vyāmas*. The qualities of the Buddha seen by a *srotāpanna* are like water known to be at a depth of ten *byāmas* by a rope of ten *byāmas*’ length. The qualities of the Buddha [seen] by a *sakadāgāmin* are like water known to be at a depth of twenty *byāmas* by a rope of twenty *byāmas*’ length. The qualities of the Buddha [seen] by an *anāgāmin* are like water known to be at a depth of thirty *byāmas* by a rope of thirty *byāmas*’ length. The qualities of the Buddha [seen] by an *arhat* are like water known to be at a depth of forty *byāmas* by a rope of forty *byāmas*’ length. The qualities of the Buddha [seen] by eighty great *theras* are like water known to be at a depth of fifty *byāmas* by a rope of fifty *byāmas*’ length. The qualities of the Buddha [seen] by four great *theras* are like water known to be at a depth of one hundred *byāmas* by a rope of one hundred *byāmas*’ length. The qualities of the Buddha [seen] by Mahāmoggallāna Thera are like water known to be at a depth of one thousand *byāmas* by a rope of one thousand *byāmas*’ length. The qualities of the Buddha [seen] by Dhammasenāpati Sāriputta Thera are like water known to be at a depth of eighty-four thousand *byāmas* by a rope of eighty-four thousand *byāmas*’ length. There, just as a man might assume that the water in the great ocean is only that much, and not endless and immeasurable, just so, Āyasmā Sāriputta, relying on the law of the *dharma*, through the intelligence of inference, through reasoning, through an understanding of method, standing in the knowledge of the *śrāvakapāramī*, recollecting the qualities of the ten powers, had faith that "the qualities of the Buddha are endless and immeasurable." Indeed, the qualities of the Buddha that must be apprehended through the law of the *dharma* are far more numerous than the qualities of the Buddha that have been seen by the *thera*. How so? Just as if a man were to take water with the tip of a blade of grass from the Candrabhāga *mahānadī*, which flows, spreading eighteen *yojanas* from here to there, the water not taken by the tip of the blade of grass would be far greater. Or just as if a man were to take dust with his finger from the great earth, the remaining dust would be far greater than the dust taken by his finger. Or just as if a man were to point his finger toward the great ocean, the remaining water would be far greater than the water facing his finger. Or just as if a man were to point his finger toward the sky, the remaining expanse of sky would be far greater than the sky facing his finger. Thus, the qualities that have not been seen are understood to be far greater than the qualities of the Buddha seen by the *thera*. It was also said: “Even if a Buddha should describe the glory of a Buddha, And not mention anything else for an *aeon*, That *aeon* might come to an end after a very long time, But the glory of the *Tathāgata* would not come to an end.” Thus, when the *thera* recollected the qualities of himself and of the Teacher, a flood of qualities, like a great current of the Yamaka *mahānadī*, [arose] within. 0055"/> He fills his whole body with joy and gladness, as the wind fills a bellows, or as a great lake bursts forth and its waters gush out. Then, the Elder, as he reflected, "Truly, my aspiration is well-established, my going forth is well-gained, since I went forth in the presence of such a Teacher," even greater joy and gladness arose.

Then the Elder, thinking, "To whom should I announce this joy and gladness?", [realized] "No other renunciate or *brāhmaṇa*, god, *Māra*, or *Brahmā* will be able to accept my satisfaction, considering it unsuitable. I shall announce this gladness to the Teacher alone. The Teacher alone will be able to accept it. Indeed, let my joy and gladness remain for the Teacher. The Teacher, accepting the minds of all, is capable of receiving the joy and gladness of a hundred, a thousand, or a hundred thousand such renunciates as myself.

is able. Just as the rivers Kusumbhā or Kandarā are unable to receive the Candabhāga great river that flows covering eighteen yojanas, but the great ocean receives it. Indeed, let the great ocean remain for the Candabhāgā; it receives a hundred, a thousand, a hundred thousand such rivers, and neither diminution nor fullness is apparent in it. Just so, the Teacher, accepting the minds of all, is capable of receiving the joy and gladness of a hundred, a thousand, or a hundred thousand such renunciates as myself. The remaining renunciates, *brāhmaṇas*, and so on, are unable to receive my gladness like the rivers Candabhāgā, Kusumbhā, and Kandarā . Then, thinking, "Come, I will announce my joy and gladness to the Teacher alone," having arranged his seat, spread out his leather garment, and taken it, in the evening, having cut off the stalks of the flowers at the time of dripping, approaching the Teacher, announcing his gladness, he said, *evaṃpasanno ahaṃ, bhante* and so on. There, *evaṃpasanno* means having faith that has arisen thus, "Thus I believe," is the meaning. *bhiyyobhiññataro* means better known, or having better knowledge, or having superior knowledge, is the meaning. *sambodhiya* means with all-knowledge or with the knowledge of the path of *arhatship*, for indeed, by the path of *arhatship*, the qualities of the Buddha are grasped without remainder. The two chief disciples attain the knowledge of the perfection of discipleship by the path of *arhatship* alone. Individual Buddhas [attain] individual Buddha knowledge. Buddhas [attain] all-knowledge as well as all the qualities of the Buddha. Indeed, all of this is accomplished by the path of *arhatship* alone. Therefore, the knowledge of the path of *arhatship* is called *saṃbodhi* (perfect knowledge). There is no one superior to the Blessed One in that. Therefore he said, "More exalted in Enlightenment than the Blessed One is what is called *sambodhi*."

evaṃpasanno ahaṃ, bhante evaṃpasanno bhiyyobhiññataro sambodhiya

mula_pali:
142. ‘‘Uḷārā kho te ayaṃ, sāriputta, āsabhī vācā bhāsitā, ekaṃso gahito, sīhanādo nadito – ‘evaṃpasanno ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavati; na cāhu na ca bhavissati na cetarahi vijjati añño samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā bhagavatā bhiyyobhiññataro yadidaṃ sambodhiya’nti. Kiṃ te kiṃ nu (sī. pī.), kiṃ nu kho te (syā.), sāriputta, ye te ahesuṃ atītamaddhānaṃ arahanto sammāsambuddhā, sabbe te bhagavanto cetasā ceto paricca viditā – ‘evaṃsīlā te bhagavanto ahesuṃ itipi, evaṃdhammā te bhagavanto ahesuṃ itipi , evaṃpaññā te bhagavanto ahesuṃ itipi, evaṃvihārī te bhagavanto ahesuṃ itipi, evaṃvimuttā te bhagavanto ahesuṃ itipī’’’ti? ‘‘No hetaṃ, bhante’’.

‘‘Kiṃ pana te kiṃ pana (sī. pī.), sāriputta, ye te bhavissanti anāgatamaddhānaṃ arahanto sammāsambuddhā , sabbe te bhagavanto cetasā ceto paricca viditā, `evaṃsīlā te bhagavanto bhavissanti itipi, evaṃdhammā…pe… evaṃpaññā… evaṃvihārī… evaṃvimuttā te bhagavanto bhavissanti itipī’’’ti? ‘‘No hetaṃ, bhante’’.

kiṃ pana (sī. pī.)

‘‘Kiṃ pana te kiṃ pana (sī. pī.), sāriputta, ahaṃ etarahi arahaṃ sammāsambuddho cetasā ceto paricca vidito – ‘evaṃsīlo bhagavā itipi, evaṃdhammo…pe… evaṃpañño … evaṃvihārī… evaṃvimutto bhagavā itipī’’’ti? ‘‘No hetaṃ, bhante’’.

kiṃ pana (sī. pī.)

‘‘Ettha ca hi te, sāriputta, atītānāgatapaccuppannesu arahantesu sammāsambuddhesu cetopariyañāṇaṃ natthi. Atha kiṃ carahi te ayaṃ, sāriputta, uḷārā āsabhī vācā bhāsitā, ekaṃso gahito, sīhanādo nadito – ‘evaṃpasanno ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavati, na cāhu na ca bhavissati na cetarahi vijjati añño samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā bhagavatā bhiyyobhiññataro yadidaṃ sambodhiya’’’nti?
mula_english:
142. “Lofty indeed is this speech of yours, Sāriputta, a bull’s statement ( *āsabhī vācā bhāsitā* ), categorical, a veritable sounding of the lion's roar ( *sīhanādo nadito* ): ‘Lord, I have confidence in the Blessed One ( *bhagavati* ) that there neither has been nor will be nor is currently found another contemplative ( *samaṇo* ) or Brahmin ( *brāhmaṇo* ) whose direct knowledge is greater than that of the Blessed One ( *bhagavatā* ) in regard to self-awakening ( *sambodhiya* )!’”

How is this? Have all the *arhats*, the Fully Awakened Ones ( *sammāsambuddhā* ) of the past appeared to you, and were the minds of all those Lords open to you, so as to say: “These Lords were of such virtue ( *evaṃsīlā* ), such was their teaching ( *evaṃdhammā* ), such their wisdom ( *evaṃpaññā* ), such their way ( *evaṃvihārī* ), such their liberation ( *evaṃvimuttā* )?” “No, Lord.”

“Then have you perceived all the *arhat* Buddhas, the Fully Awakened Ones ( *sammāsambuddhā* ) who will appear in the future, so as to say: ‘These Lords will be of such virtue ( *evaṃsīlā* ), such will be their teaching ( *evaṃdhammā* )… such their wisdom ( *evaṃpaññā* )… such their way ( *evaṃvihārī* )… such their liberation ( *evaṃvimuttā* )?’” “No, Lord.”

“How is this? Now, have I, the *arhat*, the Fully Awakened One ( *sammāsambuddho* ), at present, encompassed with my awareness, so as to say: ‘The Blessed One is of such virtue ( *evaṃsīlo* ), such his teaching ( *evaṃdhammo* )… such his wisdom ( *evaṃpañño* )… such his way ( *evaṃvihārī* )… such his liberation ( *evaṃvimutto* )?’” “No, Lord.”

“Then it is clear, Sāriputta, that you have no knowledge of the minds of the *arhats*, the Fully Awakened Ones ( *sammāsambuddhesu* ) of the past, future and present. How then do you set forth a speech so lofty, a bull’s statement ( *āsabhī vācā bhāsitā* ), categorical, a veritable sounding of the lion's roar ( *sīhanādo nadito* ), saying: ‘Lord, I have confidence in the Blessed One ( *bhagavati* ), that there has not been, there will not be, nor is there now another contemplative ( *samaṇo* ) or Brahmin ( *brāhmaṇo* ) more exalted in Enlightenment ( *sambodhiya* ) than the Blessed One ( *bhagavatā* )’?”
commentary_pali:
142.Uḷārāti seṭṭhā. Ayañhi uḷārasaddo ‘‘uḷārāni khādanīyāni khādantī’’tiādīsu (ma. ni. 1.366) madhure āgacchati. ‘‘Uḷārāya khalu bhavaṃ, vacchāyano , samaṇaṃ gotamaṃ pasaṃsāya pasaṃsatī’’tiādīsu (ma. ni. 3.280) seṭṭhe. ‘‘Appamāṇo uḷāro obhāso’’tiādīsu (dī. ni. 2.32) vipule. Svāyamidha seṭṭhe āgato. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘uḷārāti seṭṭhā’’ti. Āsabhīti usabhassa vācāsadisī acalā asampavedhī. Ekaṃso gahitoti anussavena vā ācariyaparamparāya vā itikirāya vā piṭakasampadānena vā ākāraparivitakkena vā diṭṭhinijjhānakkhantiyā vā takkahetu vā nayahetu vā akathetvā paccakkhato ñāṇena paṭivijjhitvā viya ekaṃso gahito, sanniṭṭhānakathāva kathitāti attho.

Sīhanādoti seṭṭhanādo, neva dandhāyantena na gaggarāyantena sīhena viya uttamanādo naditoti attho. Kiṃ te sāriputtāti imaṃ desanaṃ kasmā ārabhīti? Anuyogadāpanatthaṃ. Ekacco hi sīhanādaṃ naditvā attano sīhanāde anuyogaṃ dātuṃ na sakkoti, nighaṃsanaṃ nakkhamati, lepe patitamakkaṭo viya hoti. Yathā dhamamānaṃ aparisuddhalohaṃ jhāyitvā jhāmaaṅgāro hoti, evaṃ jhāmaṅgāro viya hoti . Eko sīhanāde anuyogaṃ dāpiyamāno dātuṃ sakkoti, nighaṃsanaṃ khamati, dhamamānaṃ niddosajātarūpaṃ viya adhikataraṃ sobhati, tādiso thero. Tena naṃ bhagavā ‘‘anuyogakkhamo aya’’nti ñatvā sīhanāde anuyogadāpanatthaṃ imampi desanaṃ ārabhi.

Sīhanādo Kiṃ te sāriputtā

Tattha sabbe teti sabbe te tayā. Evaṃsīlātiādīsu lokiyalokuttaravasena sīlādīni pucchati. Tesaṃ vitthārakathā mahāpadāne kathitāva.

sabbe te Evaṃsīlā

Kiṃ pana te, sāriputta, ye te bhavissantīti atītā ca tāva niruddhā, apaṇṇattikabhāvaṃ gatā dīpasikhā viya nibbutā, evaṃ niruddhe apaṇṇattikabhāvaṃ gate tvaṃ kathaṃ jānissasi, anāgatabuddhānaṃ pana guṇā kinti tayā attano cittena paricchinditvā viditāti pucchanto evamāha. Kiṃ pana te, sāriputta, ahaṃ etarahīti anāgatāpi buddhā ajātā anibbattā anuppannā, tepi kathaṃ tvaṃ jānissasi? Tesañhi jānanaṃ apade ākāse padadassanaṃ viya hoti. Idāni mayā saddhiṃ ekavihāre vasasi, ekato bhikkhāya carasi, dhammadesanākāle dakkhiṇapasse nisīdasi, kiṃ pana mayhaṃ guṇā attano cetasā paricchinditvā viditā tayāti anuyuñjanto evamāha.

Kiṃ pana te, sāriputta, ye te bhavissantī Kiṃ pana te, sāriputta, ahaṃ etarahī

Thero pana pucchite pucchite ‘‘no hetaṃ, bhante’’ti paṭikkhipati. Therassa ca viditampi atthi aviditampi atthi, kiṃ so attano viditaṭṭhāne paṭikkhepaṃ karoti, aviditaṭṭhāneti? Viditaṭṭhāne na karoti, aviditaṭṭhāneyeva karotīti. Thero kira anuyoge āraddheyeva aññāsi. Na ayaṃ anuyogo sāvakapāramīñāṇe, sabbaññutaññāṇe ayaṃ anuyogoti attano sāvakapāramīñāṇe paṭikkhepaṃ akatvā aviditaṭṭhāne sabbaññutaññāṇe paṭikkhepaṃ karoti. Tena idampi dīpeti ‘‘bhagavā mayhaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannānaṃ buddhānaṃ sīlasamādhipaññāvimuttikāraṇajānanasamatthaṃ sabbaññutaññāṇaṃ natthī’’ti.

Etthāti etesu atītādibhedesu buddhesu. Atha kiñcarahīti atha kasmā evaṃ ñāṇe asati tayā evaṃ kathitanti vadati.

Etthā Atha kiñcarahī
commentary_english:
142. Uḷārā means *seṭṭhā*, the best. Indeed, this term *uḷāra* appears in passages such as, "They eat excellent (*uḷārāni*) edibles," (Majjhima Nikāya 1.366) coming as *madhure*, sweet. [It also appears] in passages such as, "Indeed, Venerable Vacchāyana praises the *samaṇa* Gotama with excellent (*uḷārāya*) praise," (Majjhima Nikāya 3.280) as *seṭṭhe*, the best. [Again, it appears] in passages such as, "Immeasurable, excellent (*uḷāro*) radiance," (Dīgha Nikāya 2.32) as *vipule*, vast. Here, it has come in the sense of *seṭṭhe*, the best. Therefore, it was said: "*Uḷārā* means *seṭṭhā*." Āsabhī means like the speech of a bull (*usabhassa vācā*), unmoving (*acalā*), and unwavering (*asampavedhī*). Ekaṃso gahito means grasping one aspect, whether through hearsay (*anussavena*) or through the lineage of teachers (*ācariyaparamparāya*) or through tradition (*itikirāya*), or through the accomplishment of the Piṭaka, or through considering the forms, or through the acceptance of insight and contemplation, or through reasoning, or through method, without speaking, having pierced directly through knowledge (*ñāṇena paṭivijjhitvā*), like grasping one aspect; the meaning is that [it] is spoken like a conclusive statement (*sanniṭṭhānakathā*).

Sīhanādo means the roar of the best (*seṭṭhanādo*), a supreme roar like a lion (*sīhena viya uttamanādo*), not roaring slowly (*dandhāyantena*) nor roaring harshly (*gaggarāyantena*), that is the meaning. Kiṃ te sāriputtā: Why was this discourse begun? For the purpose of giving an opportunity for questioning (*anuyogadāpanatthaṃ*). For one person, having roared a lion's roar (*sīhanādaṃ naditvā*), is not able to give an opportunity for questioning (*anuyogaṃ dātuṃ na sakkoti*) regarding his own lion's roar, is not able to rub it down (*nighaṃsanaṃ nakkhamati*), is like a monkey fallen in mud (*lepe patitamakkaṭo viya hoti*). Just as having smelted impure iron (*aparisuddhalohaṃ jhāyitvā*), it becomes burnt charcoal (*jhāmaaṅgāro hoti*), so he is like burnt charcoal. One person, being made to give an opportunity for questioning (*anuyogaṃ dāpiyamāno*) regarding the lion's roar, is able to give it (*dātuṃ sakkoti*), is able to rub it down (*nighaṃsanaṃ khamati*), shines even more (*adhikataraṃ sobhati*) like refined gold (*niddosajātarūpaṃ viya*), such is the elder (*thero*). Therefore, the Blessed One (*bhagavā*), knowing him to be capable of questioning (*anuyogakkhamo ayaṃ*), began this discourse for the purpose of giving an opportunity for questioning (*anuyogadāpanatthaṃ*) regarding the lion's roar.

Sīhanādo Kiṃ te sāriputtā

There, sabbe te means all those by you (*sabbe te tayā*). Evaṃsīlā and so on: he asks about virtue (*sīlādīni*) in terms of mundane (*lokiya*) and supramundane (*lokuttara*). Their detailed discussion is stated in the Mahāpadāna.

Sabbe te Evaṃsīlā

Kiṃ pana te, sāriputta, ye te bhavissantī: Indeed, those past [Buddhas] are now stopped, having gone to a state of non-manifestation (*apaṇṇattikabhāvaṃ gatā*), extinguished (*nibbutā*) like a lamp flame (*dīpasikhā viya*). How will you know, having gone to such a stopped, non-manifest state? But how have you, by your own mind (*attano cittena*), discriminated and known what the qualities (*guṇā*) of future Buddhas are?, thus asking, he said this. Kiṃ pana te, sāriputta, ahaṃ etarahī: Indeed, also the future Buddhas are unborn (*ajātā*), unproduced (*anibbattā*), unarisen (*anuppannā*), how will you know those also? Indeed, their knowing is like seeing footprints (*padadassanaṃ viya hoti*) in a place without feet (*apade*) in the sky (*ākāse*). Now, you dwell in the same monastery (*ekavihāre vasasi*) with me, you go for alms in the same place (*ekato bhikkhāya carasi*), you sit on the right side (*dakkhiṇapasse nisīdasi*) at the time of teaching the Dharma (*dhammadesanākāle*), but how have you, by your own mind (*attano cetasā*), discriminated and known what my qualities (*guṇā*) are?, thus questioning, he said this.

Kiṃ pana te, sāriputta, ye te bhavissantī Kiṃ pana te, sāriputta, ahaṃ etarahī

But the elder (*thero*), when asked again and again, rejects [them], saying, "No, venerable one (*no hetaṃ, bhante*)." And the elder has both known things (*viditampi atthi*) and unknown things (*aviditampi atthi*). Does he make a rejection (*paṭikkhepaṃ karoti*) in his own known place (*viditaṭṭhāne*), or in an unknown place (*aviditaṭṭhāneti*)? He does not make [it] in a known place (*viditaṭṭhāne na karoti*), he makes [it] only in an unknown place (*aviditaṭṭhāneyeva karotīti*). The elder, indeed, knew that the questioning itself had begun (*anuyoge āraddheyeva aññāsi*). This questioning is not in the knowledge of the disciple's perfections (*sāvakapāramīñāṇe*), this questioning is in the knowledge of omniscience (*sabbaññutaññāṇe*), thus, without making a rejection (*paṭikkhepaṃ akatvā*) in his own knowledge of the disciple's perfections (*sāvakapāramīñāṇe*), he makes a rejection (*paṭikkhepaṃ karoti*) in the unknown place, the knowledge of omniscience (*sabbaññutaññāṇe*). Therefore, this also illuminates that “the Blessed One does not have the omniscient knowledge capable of knowing the causes of the morality, concentration, wisdom, and liberation of the past, future, and present Buddhas.” Here, "etthā" refers to these Buddhas with distinctions such as past, etc. Here, "atha kiñcarahī" means why does he say this when such knowledge does not exist?

mula_pali: 143. ‘‘Na kho me na kho panetaṃ (syā. ka.), bhante, atītānāgatapaccuppannesu arahantesu sammāsambuddhesu cetopariyañāṇaṃ atthi. Api ca, me me bhante (sī. pī. ka.) dhammanvayo vidito. Seyyathāpi, bhante , rañño paccantimaṃ nagaraṃ daḷhuddhāpaṃ daḷhuddāpaṃ (sī. pī. ka.) daḷhapākāratoraṇaṃ ekadvāraṃ. Tatrassa dovāriko paṇḍito byatto medhāvī aññātānaṃ nivāretā, ñātānaṃ pavesetā. So tassa nagarassa samantā anupariyāyapathaṃ anukkamamāno na passeyya pākārasandhiṃ vā pākāravivaraṃ vā antamaso biḷāranikkhamanamattampi. Tassa evamassa – ‘ye kho keci oḷārikā pāṇā imaṃ nagaraṃ pavisanti vā nikkhamanti vā, sabbe te imināva dvārena pavisanti vā nikkhamanti vā’ti. Evameva kho me, bhante, dhammanvayo vidito. Ye te, bhante, ahesuṃ atītamaddhānaṃ arahanto sammāsambuddhā, sabbe te bhagavanto pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya cetaso upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe catūsu satipaṭṭhānesu suppatiṭṭhitacittā, satta sambojjhaṅge yathābhūtaṃ bhāvetvā anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambujjhiṃsu. Yepi te, bhante, bhavissanti anāgatamaddhānaṃ arahanto sammāsambuddhā, sabbe te bhagavanto pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya cetaso upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe catūsu satipaṭṭhānesu suppatiṭṭhitacittā, satta sambojjhaṅge yathābhūtaṃ bhāvetvā anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambujjhissanti. Bhagavāpi, bhante, etarahi arahaṃ sammāsambuddho pañca nīvaraṇe pahāya cetaso upakkilese paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe catūsu satipaṭṭhānesu suppatiṭṭhitacitto satta sambojjhaṅge yathābhūtaṃ bhāvetvā anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambuddho.
mula_english:
“Lord, the minds of the *arhats* (*arahant*), the Perfectly Awakened Ones (*sammāsambuddha*) of the past, future and present, are not open to me. However, I understand (what I said) is in conformity with the Teaching.

Suppose, venerable sir, a king had a frontier city with strong ramparts, walls, and arches, and with a single gate. The gatekeeper posted there would be wise, competent, and intelligent; one who keeps out strangers and admits acquaintances. Walking along the path encircling the city, he wouldn’t see a crack or an opening in the walls big enough for even a cat to slip through.

He might think: ‘Whatever large creatures enter or leave this city, all enter and leave through this one gate.’ And it seems to me, Lord, that the drift of the *dharma* is the same.

All those Arahant Buddhas of the past attained to supreme enlightenment by abandoning the five hindrances (*pañca nīvaraṇe*), defilements of mind which weaken understanding, having firmly established the four foundations of mindfulness (*catūsu satipaṭṭhānesu*) in their minds, and realised the seven factors of enlightenment (*satta sambojjhaṅge*) as they really are.

All the Arahant Buddhas of the future will do likewise.

and you, Lord, who are now the *arhat*, fully-en­lightened Buddha, have done the same.
commentary_pali:
143.Dhammanvayoti dhammassa paccakkhato ñāṇassa anuyogaṃ anugantvā uppannaṃ anumānañāṇaṃ nayaggāho vidito. Sāvakapāramīñāṇe ṭhatvāva imināva ākārena jānāmi bhagavāti vadati. Therassa hi nayaggāho appamāṇo apariyanto. Yathā sabbaññutaññāṇassa pamāṇaṃ vā pariyanto vā natthi, evaṃ dhammasenāpatino nayaggāhassa. Tena so ‘‘iminā evaṃvidho, iminā anuttaro satthā’’ti jānāti. Therassa hi nayaggāho sabbaññutaññāṇagatiko eva. Idāni taṃ nayaggāhaṃ pākaṭaṃ kātuṃ upamāya dassento seyyathāpi, bhantetiādimāha. Tattha yasmā majjhimapadese nagarassa uddhāpapākārādīni thirāni vā hontu, dubbalāni vā, sabbaso vā pana mā hontu, corāsaṅkā na hoti, tasmā taṃ aggahetvā paccantimanagaranti āha. Daḷhuddhāpanti thirapākārapādaṃ. Daḷhapākāratoraṇanti thirapākārañceva thirapiṭṭhasaṅghāṭañca. Ekadvāranti kasmā āha? Bahudvāre hi nagare bahūhi paṇḍitadovārikehi bhavitabbaṃ. Ekadvāre ekova vaṭṭati. Therassa ca paññāya sadiso añño natthi. Tasmā attano paṇḍitabhāvassa opammatthaṃ ekaṃyeva dovārikaṃ dassetuṃ ekadvāra’’nti āha. Paṇḍitoti paṇḍiccena samannāgato. Byattoti veyyattiyena samannāgato visadañāṇo. Medhāvīti ṭhānuppattikapaññāsaṅkhātāya medhāya samannāgato. Anupariyāyapathanti anupariyāyanāmakaṃ pākāramaggaṃ. Pākārasandhinti dvinnaṃ iṭṭhakānaṃ apagataṭṭhānaṃ. Pākāravivaranti pākārassa chinnaṭṭhānaṃ.

Cetaso upakkileseti pañca nīvaraṇāni cittaṃ upakkilesenti kiliṭṭhaṃ karonti upatāpenti vibādhenti, tasmā ‘‘cetaso upakkilesā’’ti vuccanti. Paññāya dubbalīkaraṇeti nīvaraṇā uppajjamānā anuppannāya paññāya uppajjituṃ na denti, uppannāya paññāya vaḍḍhituṃ na denti, tasmā ‘‘paññāya dubbalīkaraṇā’’ti vuccanti. Suppatiṭṭhitacittāti catūsu satipaṭṭhānesu suṭṭhu ṭhapitacittā hutvā. Satta bojjhaṅge yathābhūtanti satta bojjhaṅge yathāsabhāvena bhāvetvā. Anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhinti arahattaṃ sabbaññutaññāṇaṃ vā paṭivijjhiṃsūti dasseti.

Cetaso upakkilese Paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe Suppatiṭṭhitacittā Satta bojjhaṅge yathābhūta Anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhi

Apicettha satipaṭṭhānāti vipassanā. Sambojjhaṅgā maggo. Anuttarāsammāsambodhi arahattaṃ. Satipaṭṭhānāti vā maggāti vā bojjhaṅgamissakā. Sammāsambodhi arahattameva. Dīghabhāṇakamahāsīvatthero panāha ‘‘satipaṭṭhāne vipassanāti gahetvā bojjhaṅge maggo ca sabbaññutaññāṇañcāti gahite sundaro pañho bhaveyya, na panevaṃ gahita’’nti. Iti thero sabbaññubuddhānaṃ nīvaraṇappahāne satipaṭṭhānabhāvanāya sambodhiyañca majjhe bhinnasuvaṇṇarajatānaṃ viya nānattābhāvaṃ dasseti.

Idha ṭhatvā upamā saṃsandetabbā – āyasmā hi sāriputto paccantanagaraṃ dassesi, pākāraṃ dassesi, pariyāyapathaṃ dassesi, dvāraṃ dassesi, paṇḍitadovārikaṃ dassesi, nagaraṃ pavesanakanikkhamanake oḷārike pāṇe dassesi, paṇḍitadovārikassa tesaṃ pāṇānaṃ pākaṭabhāvañca dassesi. Tattha kiṃ kena sadisanti ce. Nagaraṃ viya hi nibbānaṃ, pākāro viya sīlaṃ, pariyāyapatho viya hirī, dvāraṃ viya ariyamaggo, paṇḍitadovāriko viya dhammasenāpati, nagarappavisanakanikkhamanakaoḷārikapāṇā viya atītānāgatapaccuppannā buddhā, dovārikassa tesaṃ pāṇānaṃ pākaṭabhāvo viya āyasmato sāriputtassa atītānāgatapaccuppannabuddhānaṃ sīlasamathādīhi pākaṭabhāvo. Ettāvatā therena bhagavā evamahaṃ sāvakapāramīñāṇe ṭhatvā dhammanvayena nayaggāhena jānāmīti attano sīhanādassa anuyogo dinno hoti.
commentary_english:
143. *Dhammanvayo* means that the inference-knowledge (*anumānañāṇaṃ*) arisen following the application (*anuyogaṃ anugantvā*) of knowledge (*ñāṇassa*) to the Teaching (*dhammassa*) as directly experienced (*paccakkhato*) is known as grasping the method (*nayaggāho*). Standing in the knowledge of a disciple's perfection (*sāvakapāramīñāṇe ṭhatvāva*), he speaks, "I know the Blessed One in just this manner" (*imināva ākārena jānāmi bhagavāti vadati*). Indeed, the Elder's grasp of the method (*nayaggāho*) is immeasurable (*appamāṇo*) and endless (*apariyanto*). Just as there is no measure (*pamāṇaṃ*) or end (*pariyanto*) to the knowledge of omniscience (*sabbaññutaññāṇassa*), so too is the Dharma-general's (*dhammasenāpatino*) grasp of the method. Therefore, he knows, "The Teacher is like this (*iminā evaṃvidho*), the Teacher is unsurpassed (*iminā anuttaro satthā*)." Indeed, the Elder's grasp of the method (*nayaggāho*) invariably pertains to the knowledge of omniscience (*sabbaññutaññāṇagatiko eva*). Now, showing that grasp of the method by way of simile, he says, "Just as, venerable sir (*seyyathāpi, bhante*)," etc. There, because in the middle country (*majjhimapadese*), whether the fortifications, ramparts, etc. (*uddhāpapākārādīni*) of a city are strong (*thirāni*) or weak (*dubbalāni*), or even if they do not exist at all (*sabbaso vā pana mā hontu*), there is no fear of robbers (*corāsaṅkā na hoti*), therefore, not taking that, he says, "a border city (*paccantimanagaranti āha*)." *Daḷhuddhāpa* means a strong rampart-base (*thirapākārapādaṃ*). *Daḷhapākāratoraṇa* means a strong rampart (*thirapākārañceva*) and a strong lintel (*thirapiṭṭhasaṅghāṭañca*). Why does he say *ekadvāra*—"single-gated"? In a city with many gates (*bahudvāre hi nagare*) there must be many wise gatekeepers (*bahūhi paṇḍitadovārikehi bhavitabbaṃ*). In a single-gated city, one is sufficient (*ekova vaṭṭati*). And there is no other equal to the Elder's wisdom (*paññāya sadiso añño natthi*). Therefore, to show a comparison for his own wise state (*attano paṇḍitabhāvassa opammatthaṃ*), to show a single gatekeeper (*ekaṃyeva dovārikaṃ dassetuṃ*) he says, "single-gated (*ekadvāra’’nti āha*)." *Paṇḍito* means endowed with wisdom (*paṇḍiccena samannāgato*). *Byatto* means endowed with competence (*veyyattiyena samannāgato*), clear knowledge (*visadañāṇo*). *Medhāvī* means endowed with intelligence (*medhāya samannāgato*), reckoned as wisdom that arises in the right place (*ṭhānuppattikapaññāsaṅkhātāya medhāya*). *Anupariyāyapatha* means the rampart-path called *anupariyāya* (*anupariyāyanāmakaṃ pākāramaggaṃ*). *Pākārasandhi* means the place where two bricks no longer touch (*dvinnaṃ iṭṭhakānaṃ apagataṭṭhānaṃ*). *Pākāravivara* means the place where the rampart is broken (*pākārassa chinnaṭṭhānaṃ*).

*Chetaso upakkilese* means the five hindrances (*pañca nīvaraṇāni*) defile the mind (*cittaṃ upakkilesenti*), making it impure (*kiliṭṭhaṃ karonti*), afflicting (*upatāpenti*), and oppressing (*vibādhenti*), therefore they are called "defilements of the mind (*cetaso upakkilesā’’ti vuccanti*)." *Paññāya dubbalīkaraṇe* means the hindrances, when arising (*nīvaraṇā uppajjamānā*), do not allow unarisen wisdom to arise (*anuppannāya paññāya uppajjituṃ na denti*), nor do they allow arisen wisdom to increase (*uppannāya paññāya vaḍḍhituṃ na denti*), therefore they are called "making wisdom weak (*paññāya dubbalīkaraṇā’’ti vuccanti*)." *Suppatiṭṭhitacittā* means having a mind well-established (*suṭṭhu ṭhapitacittā hutvā*) in the four establishments of mindfulness (*catūsu satipaṭṭhānesu*). *Satta bojjhaṅge yathābhūta* means having cultivated the seven factors of enlightenment according to their own nature (*satta bojjhaṅge yathāsabhāvena bhāvetvā*). *Anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhi* indicates that they penetrated to arhatship or the knowledge of omniscience (*arahattaṃ sabbaññutaññāṇaṃ vā paṭivijjhiṃsūti dasseti*).

Moreover, here *satipaṭṭhāna* means insight (*vipassanā*). *Sambojjhaṅgā* means the path (*maggo*). *Anuttarāsammāsambodhi* means arhatship (*arahattaṃ*). *Satipaṭṭhāna* or the path are mixed with the factors of enlightenment (*bojjhaṅgamissakā*). *Sammāsambodhi* is arhatship alone (*arahattameva*). But the long-reciter, Mahāsīva Thera, said, "If, taking *satipaṭṭhāne* as insight (*vipassanāti gahetvā*), and taking the factors of enlightenment as the path and the knowledge of omniscience (*bojjhaṅge maggo ca sabbaññutaññāṇañcāti gahite*), the question would be beautiful (*sundaro pañho bhaveyya*), but it is not taken thus (*na panevaṃ gahita’’nti*)." Thus, the Thera shows the non-difference (*nānattābhāvaṃ dasseti*) between the removal of the hindrances (*nīvaraṇappahāne*), the cultivation of the establishments of mindfulness (*satipaṭṭhānabhāvanāya*), and enlightenment (*sambodhiyañca*) among the all-knowing Buddhas, like diverse gold and silver (*bhinnasuvaṇṇarajatānaṃ viya*).
Here, having remained, an analogy should be considered: Venerable Sāriputta showed a border city, he showed a rampart, he showed a path of circumambulation, he showed a gate, he showed a wise gatekeeper, he showed substantial beings entering and leaving the city, and he showed the manifestation of those beings to the wise gatekeeper.

There, if one asks, what is similar to what?

The city is like *nirvāṇa*; the rampart is like virtue (*śīla*); the path of circumambulation is like moral shame (*hrī*); the gate is like the Noble Path (*āryamārga*); the wise gatekeeper is like the general of the Dharma (*dharmasenāpati*); the substantial beings entering and leaving the city are like the Buddhas of the past, future, and present; the manifestation of those beings to the gatekeeper is like the manifestation of the Buddhas of the past, future, and present to Venerable Sāriputta through virtue, tranquility, and so on.

To this extent, by the Elder, the Blessed One gave an application of his roar of a lion, saying, "Thus, I, standing in the knowledge of the perfection of a disciple, know through the connection of the Dharma and the grasp of method."

mula_pali:
144. ‘‘Idhāhaṃ, bhante, yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃ dhammassavanāya. Tassa me, bhante, bhagavā dhammaṃ deseti uttaruttaraṃ paṇītapaṇītaṃ kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāgaṃ. Yathā yathā me, bhante, bhagavā dhammaṃ desesi uttaruttaraṃ paṇītapaṇītaṃ kaṇhasukkasappaṭibhāgaṃ, tathā tathāhaṃ tasmiṃ dhamme abhiññā idhekaccaṃ dhammaṃ dhammesu niṭṭhamagamaṃ; satthari pasīdiṃ – ‘sammāsambuddho bhagavā, svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo, suppaṭipanno sāvakasaṅgho’ti.

Kusaladhammadesanā
mula_english:
‘‘So I came once to the Blessed Lord to listen to Dhamma. And the Blessed Lord taught me Dhamma most excellently and perfectly, contrasting the dark with the light.
