Moreover, he is energetic in mental effort, preventing the arising of defilements in whatever way possible. *Jhāyī* means meditating by way of focusing on the characteristic of the object. *Satimā* means endowed with mindfulness, capable of recollecting what was done long ago, etc. *Indriyesu guttadvāro, bhojane mattaññū samakārī jāgariyānuyogamanuyutto atandito āraddhavīriyo* 0069"/> jhāyī satimā

kalyāṇapaṭibhānoti *vākkaraṇasampanno* *ceva* *hoti* *paṭibhānasampanno* *ca*. *yuttapaṭibhāno* *kho* *pana* *hoti* *no* *muttapaṭibhāno*. *sīlasamācārasmiñhi* *ṭhitabhikkhu* *muttapaṭibhāno* *na* *hoti*, *yuttapaṭibhāno* *pana* *hoti* *vaṅgīsatthero* *viya*. gatimāti possessed of the power of going is endowed with wisdom (*paññā*) through the power of going. dhitimāti possessed of firmness is endowed with wisdom (*paññā*) through the power of retention (*dhāraṇā*). matimāti here, *mati* itself is a name for wisdom (*paññā*), therefore, it means possessing wisdom (*paññā*). iti tīhipi imehi padehi paññāva kathitā. tattha heṭṭhā samaṇadhammakaraṇavīriyaṃ kathitaṃ, idha buddhavacanagaṇhanavīriyaṃ. tathā heṭṭhā vipassanāpaññā kathitā, idha buddhavacanagaṇhanapaññā. na ca kāmesu giddhoti he is not attached to the object of desire or defilement (*vatthukāmakilesakāmesu agiddho*). sato ca nipako cāti he is mindful, wise, and endowed with mindfulness (*sati*) and knowledge (*jñāna*) in the seven locations beginning with going forward and going back (*abhikkantapaṭikkantādīsu sattasu ṭhānesu satiyā ceva ñāṇena ca samannāgato caratīti attho*). *nepakkanti* *paññā*, *tāya* *samannāgatattā* *nipakoti* *vutto*. *sesamidhāpi* *purimanayeneva* *yojetabbaṃ*.

kalyāṇapaṭibhāno gatimā dhitimā matimā na ca kāmesu giddho sato ca nipako cā

anusāsanavidhādivaṇṇanā

mula_pali:
154. ‘‘Aparaṃ pana, bhante, etadānuttariyaṃ, yathā bhagavā dhammaṃ deseti anusāsanavidhāsu. Catasso imā bhante anusāsanavidhā – jānāti , bhante, bhagavā aparaṃ puggalaṃ paccattaṃ yonisomanasikārā ‘ayaṃ puggalo yathānusiṭṭhaṃ tathā paṭipajjamāno tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā sotāpanno bhavissati avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo’ti. Jānāti, bhante, bhagavā paraṃ puggalaṃ paccattaṃ yonisomanasikārā – ‘ayaṃ puggalo yathānusiṭṭhaṃ tathā paṭipajjamāno tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā sakadāgāmī bhavissati, sakideva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā dukkhassantaṃ karissatī’ti. Jānāti, bhante, bhagavā paraṃ puggalaṃ paccattaṃ yonisomanasikārā – ‘ayaṃ puggalo yathānusiṭṭhaṃ tathā paṭipajjamāno pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātiko bhavissati tattha parinibbāyī anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā’ti. Jānāti, bhante, bhagavā paraṃ puggalaṃ paccattaṃ yonisomanasikārā – ‘ayaṃ puggalo yathānusiṭṭhaṃ tathā paṭipajjamāno āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharissatī’ti. Etadānuttariyaṃ, bhante, anusāsanavidhāsu.

Parapuggalavimuttiñāṇadesanā
mula_english:
154. ‘Also unsurpassed, venerable sir, is the Blessed Lord’s way of teaching the *dharma* in regard to modes of receptivity to instruction.

There are these four modes of receptivity to instruction: The Blessed Lord knows by his own skilled observation: “That one will, by following instructions, by the complete destruction of three fetters, become a Stream-Winner (*sotāpanna*), no more subject to rebirth in lower worlds, firmly established, destined for full enlightenment” (*sambodhiparāyaṇo*)’ti.

“that one will, by following instructions, by the complete destruction of three fetters and the reduction of greed (*rāga*), hatred (*dosa*) and delusion (*moha*), become a Once-Retumer (*sakadāgāmī*), and having returned once more to this world, will put an end to suffering”;

“that one will, by following instructions, by the complete destruction of the five lower fetters, be spontaneously reborn (*opapātiko*), and there will reach *Nirvāṇa* (*parinibbāyī*) without returning from that world”;

“that one will, by following instructions, by the destruction of the corruptions (*āsavānaṃ khayā*), gain in this very life the deliverance of mind (*cetovimutti*), the deliverance through wisdom (*paññāvimutti*) which is uncorrupted, and which one has understood and realised by one’s own super-knowledge.”

This is the unsurpassed teaching in regard to the modes of receptivity to instruction.

Explanation of the Knowledge of the Deliverance of Another Person
commentary_pali: 154.Paccattaṃ yoniso manasikārāti attano upāyamanasikārena. Yathānusiṭṭhaṃ tathā paṭipajjamānoti yathā mayā anusiṭṭhaṃ anusāsanī dinnā, tathā paṭipajjamāno. Tiṇṇaṃsaṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayātiādi vuttatthameva. Sesamidhāpi purimanayeneva yojetabbaṃ.
commentary_english:
154. *paccattaṃ yoniso manasikārā* means by attending properly to one's own means.

*yathānusiṭṭhaṃ tathā paṭipajjamāno* means acting in accordance with how I have instructed, the instruction that was given.

*tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā* etc., the meaning has already been stated.

Here too in the section on the third quarter everything else should be construed just as above.

mula_pali:
155. ‘‘Aparaṃ pana, bhante, etadānuttariyaṃ, yathā bhagavā dhammaṃ deseti parapuggalavimuttiñāṇe. Jānāti, bhante, bhagavā paraṃ puggalaṃ paccattaṃ yonisomanasikārā – ‘ayaṃ puggalo tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā sotāpanno bhavissati avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo’ti. Jānāti, bhante, bhagavā paraṃ puggalaṃ paccattaṃ yonisomanasikārā – ‘ayaṃ puggalo tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā sakadāgāmī bhavissati, sakideva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā dukkhassantaṃ karissatī’ti. Jānāti, bhante, bhagavā paraṃ puggalaṃ paccattaṃ yonisomanasikārā – ‘ayaṃ puggalo pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātiko bhavissati tattha parinibbāyī anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā’ti. Jānāti, bhante, bhagavā paraṃ puggalaṃ paccattaṃ yonisomanasikārā – ‘ayaṃ puggalo āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharissatī’ti. Etadānuttariyaṃ, bhante, parapuggalavimuttiñāṇe.

Sassatavādadesanā
mula_english:
‘Furthermore, venerable sir, unsurpassed is the way the Blessed One teaches the Dharma in regard to the knowledge of the liberation of others (parapuggalavimuttiñāṇe).

The Blessed Lord knows, venerable sir, another person through his own careful consideration: “This person, through the destruction of the three fetters (tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā), will become a stream-enterer (sotāpanno bhavissati), no longer subject to downfall, certain, destined for full enlightenment (sambodhiparāyaṇo).”

The Blessed Lord knows, venerable sir, another person through his own careful consideration: “This person, through the destruction of the three fetters (tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā) and the attenuation of greed, hatred, and delusion (rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā), will become a once-returner (sakadāgāmī bhavissati), and having returned to this world only once (sakideva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā), will make an end of suffering (dukkhassantaṃ karissatī).”

The Blessed Lord knows, venerable sir, another person through his own careful consideration: “This person, through the destruction of the five lower fetters (pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā), will be reborn spontaneously (opapātiko bhavissati), and there attain final *nirvāṇa* (parinibbāyī), not liable to return from that world (anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā).”

The Blessed Lord knows, venerable sir, another person through his own careful consideration: “This person, through the destruction of the *āsavas* (āsavānaṃ khayā), will in this very life (diṭṭheva dhamme) realize for himself with higher knowledge (sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā) the liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom that are free from *āsavas* (anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ), and having attained it, will abide therein (upasampajja viharissatī).”

Unsurpassed, venerable sir, is the knowledge of the liberation of others (parapuggalavimuttiñāṇe).

The teaching concerning the eternalist doctrine (sassatavādadesanā).
commentary_pali: 155.Parapuggalavimuttiñāṇeti sotāpannādīnaṃ parapuggalānaṃ tena tena maggena kilesavimuttiñāṇe. Sesamidhāpi purimanayeneva yojetabbaṃ.
commentary_english:
155. *Parapuggalavimuttiñāṇe* means the knowledge of the deliverance of other individuals, namely, the knowledge of deliverance from defilements of other individuals, beginning with the stream-enterer, by that particular path.

Here too in this section, everything else should be construed just as above.

mula_pali:
156. ‘‘Aparaṃ pana, bhante, etadānuttariyaṃ, yathā bhagavā dhammaṃ deseti sassatavādesu. Tayome, bhante, sassatavādā. Idha, bhante, ekacco samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā ātappamanvāya…pe… tathārūpaṃ cetosamādhiṃ phusati, yathāsamāhite citte anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati. Seyyathidaṃ, ekampi jātiṃ dvepi jātiyo tissopi jātiyo catassopi jātiyo pañcapi jātiyo dasapi jātiyo vīsampi jātiyo tiṃsampi jātiyo cattālīsampi jātiyo paññāsampi jātiyo jātisatampi jātisahassampi jātisatasahassampi anekānipi jātisatāni anekānipi jātisahassāni anekānipi jātisatasahassāni, ‘amutrāsiṃ evaṃnāmo evaṃgotto evaṃvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṃsukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto amutra udapādiṃ; tatrāpāsiṃ evaṃnāmo evaṃgotto evaṃvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṃsukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto idhūpapanno’ti. Iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati. So evamāha – ‘atītaṃpāhaṃ addhānaṃ jānāmi – saṃvaṭṭi vā loko vivaṭṭi vāti. Anāgataṃpāhaṃ addhānaṃ jānāmi – saṃvaṭṭissati vā loko vivaṭṭissati vāti. Sassato attā ca loko ca vañjho kūṭaṭṭho esikaṭṭhāyiṭṭhito. Te ca sattā sandhāvanti saṃsaranti cavanti upapajjanti, atthitveva sassatisama’nti. Ayaṃ paṭhamo sassatavādo.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhante, idhekacco samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā ātappamanvāya…pe… tathārūpaṃ cetosamādhiṃ phusati, yathāsamāhite citte anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati. Seyyathidaṃ, ekampi saṃvaṭṭavivaṭṭaṃ dvepi saṃvaṭṭavivaṭṭāni tīṇipi saṃvaṭṭavivaṭṭāni cattāripi saṃvaṭṭavivaṭṭāni pañcapi saṃvaṭṭavivaṭṭāni dasapi saṃvaṭṭavivaṭṭāni, ‘amutrāsiṃ evaṃnāmo evaṃgotto evaṃvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṃsukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto amutra udapādiṃ; tatrāpāsiṃ evaṃnāmo evaṃgotto evaṃvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṃsukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto idhūpapanno’ti. Iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati. So evamāha – ‘atītaṃpāhaṃ addhānaṃ jānāmi saṃvaṭṭi vā loko vivaṭṭi vāti . Anāgataṃpāhaṃ addhānaṃ jānāmi saṃvaṭṭissati vā loko vivaṭṭissati vāti. Sassato attā ca loko ca vañjho kūṭaṭṭho esikaṭṭhāyiṭṭhito. Te ca sattā sandhāvanti saṃsaranti cavanti upapajjanti, atthitveva sassatisama’nti. Ayaṃ dutiyo sassatavādo.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhante, idhekacco samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā ātappamanvāya…pe… tathārūpaṃ cetosamādhiṃ phusati, yathāsamāhite citte anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati. Seyyathidaṃ, dasapi saṃvaṭṭavivaṭṭāni vīsampi saṃvaṭṭavivaṭṭāni tiṃsampi saṃvaṭṭavivaṭṭāni cattālīsampi saṃvaṭṭavivaṭṭāni, ‘amutrāsiṃ evaṃnāmo evaṃgotto evaṃvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṃsukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto amutra udapādiṃ; tatrāpāsiṃ evaṃnāmo evaṃgotto evaṃvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṃsukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto idhūpapanno’ti. Iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati. So evamāha – ‘atītaṃpāhaṃ addhānaṃ jānāmi saṃvaṭṭipi loko vivaṭṭipīti; anāgataṃpāhaṃ addhānaṃ jānāmi saṃvaṭṭissatipi loko vivaṭṭissatipīti. Sassato attā ca loko ca vañjho kūṭaṭṭho esikaṭṭhāyiṭṭhito. Te ca sattā sandhāvanti saṃsaranti cavanti upapajjanti, atthitveva sassatisama’nti. Ayaṃ tatiyo sassatavādo, etadānuttariyaṃ, bhante, sassatavādesu.

Pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇadesanā
mula_english:
‘Also unsurpassed, venerable sir, is the way the Blessed One teaches the Dhamma regarding the eternalist theories ( *sassatavāda* ).

There are three such eternalist theories, venerable sir.

Here, venerable sir, some ascetic or *brāhmaṇa*, by means of ardour, attains to such a state of mental concentration (*ceto-samādhi*) that with his mind thus concentrated, he recollects his numerous past lives (*pubbenivāsa*).

That is, one birth, two births, three, four, or five births; ten, twenty, thirty, forty, or fifty births; a hundred, a thousand, or a hundred thousand births; many hundreds of births, many thousands of births, many hundreds of thousands of births. ‘There I was so named, belonged to such a clan, had such an appearance; such was my food, such my experience of pleasure and pain, such my span of life. Passing away thence, I re-arose there. There too I had such a name, belonged to such a clan, had such an appearance; such was my food, such my experience of pleasure and pain, such my span of life. Passing away thence, I re-arose here.’

Thus he remembers his various past births, with their modes and their details.

He says: ‘I know the past – the world was contracting or expanding.

I know the future – the world will contract or expand.

The self (*atman*) and the world are eternal, barren, steady as a mountain peak, firmly fixed as a pillar.

Beings run on, transmigrate, pass away, and are reborn, yet they persist eternally.’

This is the first eternalist theory.

‘Furthermore, venerable sir, some ascetic or *brāhmaṇa*, by means of ardour, attains to such a state of mental concentration (*ceto-samādhi*) that with his mind thus concentrated, he recollects his numerous past lives (*pubbenivāsa*).

That is, one period of contraction and expansion, two periods of contraction and expansion, three, four, five, or ten periods of contraction and expansion. ‘There I was so named, belonged to such a clan, had such an appearance; such was my food, such my experience of pleasure and pain, such my span of life. Passing away thence, I re-arose there. There too I had such a name, belonged to such a clan, had such an appearance; such was my food, such my experience of pleasure and pain, such my span of life. Passing away thence, I re-arose here.’

Thus he remembers his various past births, with their modes and their details.

He says: ‘I know the past – the world was contracting or expanding.

I know the future – the world will contract or expand.

The self (*atman*) and the world are eternal, barren, steady as a mountain peak, firmly fixed as a pillar.

Beings run on, transmigrate, pass away, and are reborn, yet they persist eternally.’

This is the second eternalist theory.

‘Furthermore, venerable sir, some ascetic or *brāhmaṇa*, by means of ardour, attains to such a state of mental concentration (*ceto-samādhi*) that with his mind thus concentrated, he recollects his numerous past lives (*pubbenivāsa*).

That is, he recalls ten periods of contraction and expansion, twenty periods of contraction and expansion, thirty periods of contraction and expansion, forty periods of contraction and expansion. ‘There I was so named, belonged to such a clan, had such an appearance; such was my food, such my experience of pleasure and pain, such my span of life. Passing away thence, I re-arose there. There too I had such a name, belonged to such a clan, had such an appearance; such was my food, such my experience of pleasure and pain, such my span of life. Passing away thence, I re-arose here.’

Thus he remembers his various past births, with their modes and their details.

He says: ‘I know the past – the world was contracting or expanding. I know the future – the world will contract or expand.

The self (*atman*) and the world are eternal, barren, steady as a mountain peak, firmly fixed as a pillar.

Beings run on, transmigrate, pass away, and are reborn, yet they persist eternally.’

This is the third eternalist theory. It is unsurpassed in regard to the eternalist theories.

The exposition of the knowledge of the recollection of past lives (*pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇa*).
commentary_pali: 156.Amutrāsiṃ evaṃnāmoti eko pubbenivāsaṃ anussaranto nāmagottaṃ pariyādiyamāno gacchati. Eko suddhakhandheyeva anussarati, eko hi sakkoti, eko na sakkoti. Tattha yo sakkoti, tassa vasena aggahetvā asakkontassa vasena gahitaṃ. Asakkonto pana kiṃ karoti? Suddhakhandheyeva anussaranto gantvā anekajātisatasahassamatthake ṭhatvā nāmagottaṃ pariyādiyamāno otarati. Taṃ dassento evaṃnāmotiādimāha . So evamāhāti so diṭṭhigatiko evamāha. Tattha kiñcāpi sassatoti vatvā ‘‘te ca sattā saṃsarantī’’ti vadantassa vacanaṃ pubbāparaviruddhaṃ hoti. Diṭṭhigatikattā panesa etaṃ na sallakkhesi. Diṭṭhigatikassa hi ṭhānaṃ vā niyamo vā natthi. Imaṃ gahetvā imaṃ vissajjeti, imaṃ vissajjetvā imaṃ gaṇhātīti brahmajāle vitthāritamevetaṃ. Ayaṃ tatiyo sassatavādoti thero lābhisseva vasena tayo sassatavāde āha. Bhagavatā pana takkīvādampi gahetvā brahmajāle cattāro vuttā. Etesaṃ pana tiṇṇaṃ vādānaṃ vitthārakathā brahmajāle (dī. ni. aṭṭha. 1.30) vuttanayeneva veditabbā. Sesamidhāpi purimanayeneva vitthāretabbaṃ.
commentary_english:
156. “*amutrāsiṃ evaṃnāmo*” - thus, one, recalling a former dwelling, goes reciting the name and clan.

One recalls it purely by means of the aggregates. One is able, one is not able.

There, what one is able to do, through that power, without seizing, through the power of not being able, it is seized.

What is one unable to do? Recalling purely by means of the aggregates, having gone, standing at the summit of hundreds of thousands of births, reciting the name and clan, one descends.

Showing that, [he] says, beginning with "*evaṃnāmo*."

"*so evamāhā*"- thus speaks that one who is attached to views.

There, although having said, “eternal,” the statement of one saying, "and those beings transmigrate," is contradictory to what precedes and what follows.

Because of being attached to views, he does not consider this.

For one attached to views, there is neither a place (ṭhāna) nor a certainty (niyama).

“Having taken this, he rejects this, having rejected this, he takes this" - thus, this is explained in detail in the Brahma-jāla (Brahmajāla Sutta).

"*ayaṃ tatiyo sassatavādo*" - thus, the elder states the three eternalist doctrines (sassatavāda) simply on the basis of gain.

The Blessed One, moreover, having taken the reasoning doctrine (takkīvāda) as well, stated four in the Brahma-jāla.

But the detailed account of these three doctrines should be understood just as it is explained in the Brahma-jāla (Dīgha Nikāya, Aṭṭhakathā 1. 30).

Here also, the remainder should be elaborated according to the former method.

mula_pali:
157. ‘‘Aparaṃ pana, bhante, etadānuttariyaṃ, yathā bhagavā dhammaṃ deseti pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇe. Idha, bhante, ekacco samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā ātappamanvāya…pe… tathārūpaṃ cetosamādhiṃ phusati, yathāsamāhite citte anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati. Seyyathidaṃ, ekampi jātiṃ dvepi jātiyo tissopi jātiyo catassopi jātiyo pañcapi jātiyo dasapi jātiyo vīsampi jātiyo tiṃsampi jātiyo cattālīsampi jātiyo paññāsampi jātiyo jātisatampi jātisahassampi jātisatasahassampi anekepi saṃvaṭṭakappe anekepi vivaṭṭakappe anekepi saṃvaṭṭavivaṭṭakappe, ‘amutrāsiṃ evaṃnāmo evaṃgotto evaṃvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṃsukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto amutra udapādiṃ; tatrāpāsiṃ evaṃnāmo evaṃgotto evaṃvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṃsukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto idhūpapanno’ti. Iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati. Santi, bhante, devā sattā (syā.), yesaṃ na sakkā gaṇanāya vā saṅkhānena vā āyu saṅkhātuṃ. Api ca, yasmiṃ yasmiṃ attabhāve abhinivuṭṭhapubbo abhinivutthapubbo (sī. syā. pī.) hoti yadi vā rūpīsu yadi vā arūpīsu yadi vā saññīsu yadi vā asaññīsu yadi vā nevasaññīnāsaññīsu. Iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati. Etadānuttariyaṃ, bhante, pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇe.

Cutūpapātañāṇadesanā
mula_english:
‘Furthermore, venerable sir, unsurpassed is the way the Blessed One teaches the Dharma regarding the knowledge of the recollection of past lives ( *pūrvanivāsānusmṛti-jñāna*).

Here, venerable sir, some ascetic or Brahmin, by means of ardour,… attains to such a state of mental concentration (*ceto-samādhi*) that, with his mind thus concentrated, he recollects his numerous past lives.

That is to say, one birth, two births, three births, four births, five births, ten births, twenty births, thirty births, forty births, fifty births, a hundred births, a thousand births, a hundred thousand births; many eons of world contraction, many eons of world expansion, many eons of world contraction and expansion: ‘There I was so named, of such a clan, with such an appearance, such was my nutriment, such my experience of pleasure and pain, such my life-term. Passing away thence, I arose there; there too I was so named, of such a clan, with such an appearance, such was my nutriment, such my experience of pleasure and pain, such my life-term. Passing away thence, I have been reborn here.’

Thus he remembers various past births, their conditions and details.

There are, venerable sir, deities whose life-span cannot be reckoned by counting or calculation.

Moreover, whatever existence they have previously experienced, whether in the World of Form ( *rūpa* ) or in the Formless World ( *arūpa* ), whether conscious ( *saññī* ), unconscious ( *asaññī* ) or neither-conscious-nor-unconscious ( *nevasaññīnāsaññī* ).

Thus he remembers various past births, their conditions and details.

This is the unsurpassed teaching in regard to the knowledge of the recollection of past lives (*pūrvanivāsānusmṛti-jñāna*).

Exposition of the knowledge of the passing away and reappearance of beings.
commentary_pali: 157.Gaṇanāya vāti piṇḍagaṇanāya. Saṅkhānenāti acchiddakavasena manogaṇanāya. Ubhayathāpi piṇḍagaṇanameva dasseti. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti, vassānaṃ satavasena sahassavasena satasahassavasena koṭivasena piṇḍaṃ katvāpi ettakāni vassasatānīti vā ettakā vassakoṭiyoti vā evaṃ saṅkhātuṃ na sakkā. Tumhe pana attano dasannaṃ pāramīnaṃ pūritattā sabbaññutaññāṇassa suppaṭividdhattā yasmā vo anāvaraṇañāṇaṃ sūraṃ vahati. Tasmā desanāñāṇakusalataṃ purakkhatvā vassagaṇanāyapi pariyantikaṃ katvā kappagaṇanāyapi paricchinditvā ettakanti dassethāti dīpeti. Pāḷiyattho panettha vuttanayoyeva. Sesamidhāpi purimanayeneva yojetabbaṃ.
commentary_english:
157. *Gaṇanāya vā* means by reckoning of a lump (of something).

*Saṅkhānenā* means by mental reckoning in an unbroken sequence.

In both ways, it indicates reckoning by a lump sum.

This means that even if one makes a lump sum of hundreds of years, or thousands of years, or hundreds of thousands of years, or millions of years, it is not possible to calculate thus: "so many hundreds of years," or "so many millions of years."

But since you have perfected the ten *pāramīs*, and because the wisdom of omniscience is well-established, therefore your unobstructed wisdom bears the sun.

Therefore, giving precedence to skillfulness in the wisdom of teaching, and having made a limit even in the reckoning of years, and having discriminated even in the reckoning of *kappas*, it illuminates that one should show "this much."

The meaning of the Pāli text here is just as explained.

Here too, in this section, everything else should be construed just as above.

mula_pali:
158. ‘‘Aparaṃ pana, bhante, etadānuttariyaṃ, yathā bhagavā dhammaṃ deseti sattānaṃ cutūpapātañāṇe. Idha, bhante, ekacco samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā ātappamanvāya…pe… tathārūpaṃ cetosamādhiṃ phusati, yathāsamāhite citte dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passati cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajānāti – ‘ime vata bhonto sattā kāyaduccaritena samannāgatā vacīduccaritena samannāgatā manoduccaritena samannāgatā ariyānaṃ upavādakā micchādiṭṭhikā micchādiṭṭhikammasamādānā. Te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapannā. Ime vā pana bhonto sattā kāyasucaritena samannāgatā vacīsucaritena samannāgatā manosucaritena samannāgatā ariyānaṃ anupavādakā sammādiṭṭhikā sammādiṭṭhikammasamādānā. Te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapannā’ti. Iti dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passati cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajānāti. Etadānuttariyaṃ, bhante, sattānaṃ cutūpapātañāṇe.

Iddhividhadesanā
mula_english:
‘Also unsurpassed, venerable sir, is the way the Blessed One teaches the Dhamma in regard to knowledge of the death and rebirth of beings.

Here, venerable sir, some ascetic or Brahmin, developing ardour… attains to such concentration of mind that with the divine eye (dibbena cakkhunā), purified and surpassing the human, he sees beings passing away and reappearing, inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate, and he understands beings according to their deeds (yathākammūpage satte pajānāti): ‘These worthy beings who were ill-conducted in body (kāyaduccaritena), speech (vacīduccaritena), and mind (manoduccaritena), revilers of noble ones (ariyānaṃ upavādakā), wrong in their views (micchādiṭṭhikā), giving effect to wrong views in their actions (micchādiṭṭhikammasamādānā), on the dissolution of the body (kāyassa bhedā), after death (paraṃ maraṇā), have reappeared in the plane of deprivation (apāyaṃ), the bad destination (duggatiṃ), the lower realms (vinipātaṃ), in hell (nirayaṃ) .

But these worthy beings who were well-conducted in body (kāyasucaritena), speech (vacīsucaritena), and mind (manosucaritena), not revilers of noble ones (ariyānaṃ anupavādakā), right in their views (sammādiṭṭhikā), giving effect to right views in their actions (sammādiṭṭhikammasamādānā), on the dissolution of the body (kāyassa bhedā), after death (paraṃ maraṇā), have reappeared in a happy destination (sugatiṃ), in the heavenly world (saggaṃ lokaṃ).’

Thus–by means of the divine eye (dibbena cakkhunā), purified & surpassing the human–he sees beings passing away & re-appearing, and discerns how they are inferior & superior, beautiful & ugly, fortunate & unfortunate in accordance with their actions.

This is unsurpassed, venerable sir, teaching in regard to knowledge of the death and birth of beings.

Explanation of the varieties of supernormal power.
commentary_pali: 158.Etadānuttariyaṃ, bhante, sattānaṃ cutūpapātañāṇeti bhante yāpi ayaṃ sattānaṃ cutipaṭisandhivasena ñāṇadesanā, sāpi tumhākaṃyeva anuttarā. Atītabuddhāpi evameva desesuṃ. Anāgatāpi evameva desessanti. Tumhe tesaṃ atītānāgatabuddhānaṃ ñāṇena saṃsanditvāva desayittha. ‘‘Imināpi kāraṇena evaṃpasanno ahaṃ bhante bhagavatī’’ti dīpeti. Pāḷiyattho panettha vitthāritoyeva.
commentary_english: 158. This is unsurpassed, O venerable one, in the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings. O venerable one, this explanation of knowledge regarding the passing away and rebirth of beings is indeed unsurpassed by you. The past Buddhas also taught in this way. The future Buddhas will also teach in this way. You have taught after comparing it with the knowledge of those past and future Buddhas. "Because of this reason, I am thus devoted to the Blessed One," he reveals. Moreover, the meaning of the Pāli [text] is explained here in detail.

mula_pali:
159. ‘‘Aparaṃ pana, bhante, etadānuttariyaṃ, yathā bhagavā dhammaṃ deseti iddhividhāsu. Dvemā, bhante, iddhividhāyo – atthi, bhante, iddhi sāsavā saupadhikā, ‘no ariyā’ti vuccati. Atthi, bhante, iddhi anāsavā anupadhikā ‘ariyā’ti vuccati. ‘‘Katamā ca, bhante, iddhi sāsavā saupadhikā, ‘no ariyā’ti vuccati? Idha, bhante, ekacco samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā ātappamanvāya…pe… tathārūpaṃ cetosamādhiṃ phusati, yathāsamāhite citte anekavihitaṃ iddhividhaṃ paccanubhoti. Ekopi hutvā bahudhā hoti, bahudhāpi hutvā eko hoti; āvibhāvaṃ tirobhāvaṃ tirokuṭṭaṃ tiropākāraṃ tiropabbataṃ asajjamāno gacchati seyyathāpi ākāse. Pathaviyāpi ummujjanimujjaṃ karoti, seyyathāpi udake. Udakepi abhijjamāne gacchati, seyyathāpi pathaviyaṃ. Ākāsepi pallaṅkena kamati, seyyathāpi pakkhī sakuṇo. Imepi candimasūriye evaṃmahiddhike evaṃmahānubhāve pāṇinā parāmasati parimajjati. Yāva brahmalokāpi kāyena vasaṃ vatteti. Ayaṃ, bhante, iddhi sāsavā saupadhikā, ‘no ariyā’ti vuccati.

‘‘Katamā pana, bhante, iddhi anāsavā anupadhikā, ‘ariyā’ti vuccati? Idha, bhante, bhikkhu sace ākaṅkhati – ‘paṭikūle appaṭikūlasaññī vihareyya’nti, appaṭikūlasaññī tattha viharati. Sace ākaṅkhati – ‘appaṭikūle paṭikūlasaññī vihareyya’nti, paṭikūlasaññī tattha viharati. Sace ākaṅkhati – ‘paṭikūle ca appaṭikūle ca appaṭikūlasaññī vihareyya’nti, appaṭikūlasaññī tattha viharati. Sace ākaṅkhati – ‘paṭikūle ca appaṭikūle ca paṭikūlasaññī vihareyya’nti, paṭikūlasaññī tattha viharati. Sace ākaṅkhati – ‘paṭikūlañca appaṭikūlañca tadubhayaṃ abhinivajjetvā upekkhako vihareyyaṃ sato sampajāno’ti, upekkhako tattha viharati sato sampajāno. Ayaṃ, bhante, iddhi anāsavā anupadhikā ‘ariyā’ti vuccati. Etadānuttariyaṃ, bhante, iddhividhāsu . Taṃ bhagavā asesamabhijānāti, taṃ bhagavato asesamabhijānato uttari abhiññeyyaṃ natthi, yadabhijānaṃ añño samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā bhagavatā bhiyyobhiññataro assa yadidaṃ iddhividhāsu.

Aññathāsatthuguṇadassanaṃ
mula_english:
159. ‘Also unsurpassed, venerable sir, is how the Blessed One teaches the Dharma regarding supernormal powers (iddhi-vidhā).

These, venerable sir, are two kinds of supernormal powers: There is the supernormal power that is with defilements (sāsavā) and conducive to renewed existence (saupadhikā), called "un-Āriyan".

There is the supernormal power that is without defilements (anāsavā) and not conducive to renewed existence (anupadhikā), called "Āriyan".

‘And what, venerable sir, is the supernormal power that is with defilements (sāsavā) and conducive to renewed existence (saupadhikā), called "un-Āriyan"? Here, venerable sir, some ascetic (śramaṇa) or Brahmin (brāhmaṇa), applies effort…and attains such a concentration of mind (ceto-samādhi) that, with his mind thus concentrated, he experiences various kinds of supernormal power (iddhi-vidhā).

Being one, he becomes many; being many, he becomes one. He appears (āvibhāvaṃ) and disappears (tirobhāvaṃ). He goes unimpeded through walls (tirokuṭṭaṃ), ramparts (tiropākāraṃ), and mountains (tiropabbataṃ) as if through space (ākāse).

He dives in and out of the earth (pathaviyā) as if it were water (udake).

He walks on water (udake) without sinking as if it were dry land (pathaviyaṃ).

He travels through the air (ākāse) cross-legged (pallaṅkena), like a winged bird (pakkhī sakuṇo).

He touches and strokes with his hand (pāṇinā) even the moon (candima) and the sun (sūriya), so mighty (evaṃmahiddhike) and powerful (evaṃmahānubhāve).

He exercises influence with his body (kāyena) even as far as the Brahmā world (brahmalokā).

This, venerable sir, is the supernormal power that is with defilements (sāsavā) and conducive to renewed existence (saupadhikā), called "un-Āriyan".

‘And what, venerable sir, is the supernormal power that is without defilements (anāsavā) and not conducive to renewed existence (anupadhikā), called "Āriyan"? Here, venerable sir, a *bhikṣu* (bhikkhu) if he should wish: ‘May I abide perceiving the unrepulsive (appaṭikūlasaññī) in the repulsive (paṭikūle),’ he abides perceiving the unrepulsive (appaṭikūlasaññī) in that.

If he should wish: ‘May I abide perceiving the repulsive (paṭikūlasaññī) in the unrepulsive (appaṭikūle),’ he abides perceiving the repulsive (paṭikūlasaññī) in that.

If he should wish: ‘May I abide perceiving the unrepulsive (appaṭikūlasaññī) in the repulsive (paṭikūle) and the unrepulsive (appaṭikūle),’ he abides perceiving the unrepulsive (appaṭikūlasaññī) in that.

If he should wish: ‘May I abide perceiving the repulsive (paṭikūlasaññī) in the repulsive (paṭikūle) and the unrepulsive (appaṭikūle),’ he abides perceiving the repulsive (paṭikūlasaññī) in that.

If he should wish: ‘May I, avoiding both the repulsive (paṭikūlañca) and unrepulsive (appaṭikūlañca), abide in equanimity (upekkhako), mindful (sato) and fully aware (sampajāno),’ he abides in equanimity (upekkhako) towards that, mindful (sato) and fully aware (sampajāno).

This, venerable sir, is the supernormal power that is without defilements (anāsavā) and not conducive to renewed existence (anupadhikā), called "Āriyan".

This is the unsurpassed teaching in regard to the supernormal powers (iddhi-vidhā).

This the Blessed One (bhagavā) fully comprehends (asesamabhijānāti), and beyond it lies nothing further to be comprehended; and in such understanding there is no other ascetic (śramaṇa) or Brahmin (brāhmaṇa) who is greater or more enlightened than the Blessed One (bhagavatā), as regards the supernormal powers (iddhi-vidhāsu).

A Display of the Teacher's Qualities in Other Ways
commentary_pali:
159.Sāsavā saupadhikāti sadosā saupārambhā. No ariyāti vuccatīti ariyiddhīti na vuccati. Anāsavā anupadhikāti niddosā anupārambhā. Ariyāti vuccatīti ariyiddhīti vuccati. Appaṭikūlasaññītattha viharatīti kathaṃ appaṭikūlasaññī tattha viharatīti? Paṭikūle satte mettaṃ pharati, saṅkhāre dhātusaññaṃ upasaṃharati. Yathāha ‘‘kathaṃ paṭikūle appaṭikūlasaññī viharati (paṭi. ma. 3.97)? Aniṭṭhasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ mettāya vā pharati, dhātuto vā upasaṃharatī’’ti. Paṭikūlasaññī tattha viharatīti appaṭikūle satte asubhasaññaṃ pharati, saṅkhāre aniccasaññaṃ upasaṃharati. Yathāha ‘‘kathaṃ appaṭikūle paṭikūlasaññī viharati? Iṭṭhasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ asubhāya vā pharati, aniccato vā upasaṃharatī’’ti. Evaṃ sesapadesupi attho veditabbo.

Upekkhako tattha viharatīti iṭṭhe arajjanto aniṭṭhe adussanto yathā aññe asamapekkhanena mohaṃ uppādenti, evaṃ anuppādento chasu ārammaṇesu chaḷaṅgupekkhāya upekkhako viharati. Etadānuttariyaṃ, bhante, iddhividhāsūti, bhante, yā ayaṃ dvīsu iddhīsu evaṃdesanā, etadānuttariyaṃ. Taṃ bhagavāti taṃ desanaṃ bhagavā asesaṃ sakalaṃ abhijānāti. Taṃ bhagavatoti taṃ desanaṃ bhagavato asesaṃ abhijānato. Uttari abhiññeyyaṃ natthīti uttari abhijānitabbaṃ natthi. Ayaṃ nāma ito añño dhammo vā puggalo vā yaṃ bhagavā na jānāti idaṃ natthi. Yadabhijānaṃ añño samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vāti yaṃ tumhehi anabhiññātaṃ añño samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā abhijānanto bhagavatā bhiyyobhiññataro assa, adhikatarapañño bhaveyya. Yadidaṃ iddhividhāsūti ettha yadidanti nipātamattaṃ. Iddhividhāsu bhagavatā uttaritaro natthi. Atītabuddhāpi hi imā dve iddhiyo desesuṃ, anāgatāpi imāva desessanti. Tumhepi tesaṃ ñāṇena saṃsanditvā imāva desayittha. Iti bhagavā iddhividhāsu anuttaroti dassento ‘‘imināpi kāraṇena evaṃpasanno ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavatī’’ti dīpeti. Ettāvatā ye dhammasenāpati divāṭṭhāne nisīditvā soḷasa aparampariyadhamme sammasi, teva dassitā honti.

Upekkhako tattha viharatī Etadānuttariyaṃ, bhante, iddhividhāsū Taṃ bhagavā Taṃ bhagavato Uttari abhiññeyyaṃ natthī Yadabhijānaṃ añño samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā Yadidaṃ iddhividhāsū yadida

Aññathāsatthuguṇadassanādivaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
159. *sāsavā saupadhikā* means with āsavas, with upadhi; *sadosā saupārambhā* means with faults, with instigation.

*no ariyāti vuccatī* means it is not called noble; *ariyiddhīti na vuccati* means it is not called noble power.

*anāsavā anupadhikā* means without āsavas, without upadhi; *niddosā anupārambhā* means without faults, without instigation.

*ariyāti vuccatī* means it is called noble; *ariyiddhīti vuccati* means it is called noble power.

*appaṭikūlasaññī tattha viharatī* means he dwells there with a perception of non-repulsiveness. How does he dwell there with a perception of non-repulsiveness? Towards repulsive beings, he pervades with loving-kindness (mettā); with regard to conditioned things (saṅkhāra), he brings together the element-perception (dhātusaññaṃ).

As he said: "How does he dwell with a perception of non-repulsiveness towards the repulsive (paṭi. ma. 3.97)? In a disagreeable (aniṭṭha) object (vatthu), he pervades with loving-kindness (mettā), or he brings together the element (dhātu)."

*paṭikūlasaññī tattha viharatī* means he dwells there with a perception of repulsiveness. Towards non-repulsive beings, he pervades with the unbeautiful-perception (asubhasaññaṃ); with regard to conditioned things (saṅkhāra), he brings together the impermanence-perception (aniccasaññaṃ).

As he said: "How does he dwell with a perception of repulsiveness towards the non-repulsive (3.0071)? In an agreeable (iṭṭha) object (vatthu), he pervades with the unbeautiful (asubhāya), or he brings together with impermanence (aniccato)."

Thus, the meaning should be understood in the remaining passages as well.

*upekkhako tattha viharatī* means he dwells there with equanimity; not being attached to the agreeable (iṭṭhe arajjanto), not being hostile to the disagreeable (aniṭṭhe adussanto). Just as others generate delusion (mohaṃ uppādenti) through unwise contemplation (asamapekkhanena), so not generating it, with regard to the six sense-objects (chasu ārammaṇesu), he dwells with equanimity (upekkhako viharati) through six-factored equanimity (chaḷaṅgupekkhāya).

*etadānuttariyaṃ, bhante, iddhividhāsū* means "This is the unsurpassed, O venerable one, in the kinds of psychic power." O venerable one, that which is the exposition of this sort in the two kinds of psychic power, this is the unsurpassed.

*taṃ bhagavā* means the Blessed One (bhagavā) knows that exposition (desanaṃ) completely (asesaṃ), entirely (sakalaṃ) *taṃ bhagavato* means the Blessed One knows that exposition completely.

*uttari abhiññeyyaṃ natthī* means there is nothing further to be known.

There is no other quality (dhammo) or person (puggalo) other than this, which the Blessed One does not know.

*yadabhijānaṃ añño samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā* means that which is not directly known by you, another ascetic (śramaṇa) or a brāhmaṇa, while directly knowing, might be greater in direct knowledge than the Blessed One, might be of superior wisdom.

*yadidaṃ iddhividhāsū* here *yadida* is merely a particle.

There is no one superior to the Blessed One in the kinds of psychic power.

The past Buddhas also expounded these two kinds of psychic power, the future ones will also expound these.

You too, having compared with their knowledge, have expounded these.

Thus, the Blessed One, showing that he is unsurpassed in the kinds of psychic power, declares "Because of this reason also, I am thus pleased, O venerable one, with the Blessed One."

To this extent, those qualities which Dhammasenāpati, having sat down in the day-quarters, contemplated the sixteen unparalleled qualities, those are shown.

*upekkhako tattha viharatī etadānuttariyaṃ, bhante, iddhividhāsū taṃ bhagavā taṃ bhagavato uttari abhiññeyyaṃ natthī yadabhijānaṃ añño samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā yadidaṃ iddhividhāsū yadida*

Description of the qualities of the Teacher in another way.

mula_pali:
160. ‘‘Yaṃ taṃ, bhante, saddhena kulaputtena pattabbaṃ āraddhavīriyena thāmavatā purisathāmena purisavīriyena purisaparakkamena purisadhorayhena, anuppattaṃ taṃ bhagavatā. Na ca, bhante, bhagavā kāmesu kāmasukhallikānuyogamanuyutto hīnaṃ gammaṃ pothujjanikaṃ anariyaṃ anatthasaṃhitaṃ, na ca attakilamathānuyogamanuyutto dukkhaṃ anariyaṃ anatthasaṃhitaṃ. Catunnañca bhagavā jhānānaṃ ābhicetasikānaṃ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṃ nikāmalābhī akicchalābhī akasiralābhī.

Anuyogadānappakāro
mula_english:
160. Whatever, Lord (*bhante*), is attainable by a clansman (*kulaputta*) endowed with confidence (*saddhā*) by putting forth effort (*āraddhavīriya*) and by persistence (*thāmavatā*), by human effort (*purisathāma*), human exertion (*purisavīriya*) and human endurance (*purisaparakkama*), that the Blessed Lord (*bhagavatā*) has achieved (*anuppattaṃ*).

For the Blessed Lord (*bhagavā*) gives himself up neither to the pleasures of the senses (*kāmesu kāmasukhallikānuyoga*), which are base (*hīnaṃ*), vulgar (*gammaṃ*), for worldlings (*pothujjanikaṃ*) and not for the Noble (*anariyaṃ*), and unprofitable (*anatthasaṃhitaṃ*), nor to self-torment (*attakilamathānuyoga*), which is painful (*dukkhaṃ*), ignoble (*anariyaṃ*) and unprofitable (*anatthasaṃhitaṃ*).

The Blessed Lord (*bhagavā*) is able to enjoy the surpassing happiness of dwelling in the four *jhānas* (*jhānānaṃ*) that constitute the higher mind (*ābhicetasikānaṃ*) and provide a pleasant abiding here and now (*diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṃ*), he obtains at will (*nikāmalābhī*), without trouble (*akicchalābhī*) or difficulty (*akasiralābhī*).

The manner of giving instruction (*anuyogadānappakāro*).
commentary_pali:
160. Idāni aparenapi ākārena bhagavato guṇe dassento yaṃ taṃ bhantetiādimāha. Tattha saddhena kulaputtenāti saddhā kulaputtā nāma atītānāgatapaccuppannā bodhisattā. Tasmā yaṃ sabbaññubodhisattena pattabbanti vuttaṃ hoti. Kiṃ pana tena pattabbaṃ? Nava lokuttaradhammā. Āraddhavīriyenātiādīsu ‘‘vīriyaṃ thāmo’’tiādīni sabbāneva vīriyavevacanāni. Tattha āraddhavīriyenāti paggahitavīriyena. Thāmavatāti thāmasampannena thiravīriyena. Purisathāmenāti tena thāmavatā yaṃ purisathāmena pattabbanti vuttaṃ hoti. Anantarapadadvayepi eseva nayo. Purisadhorayhenāti yā asamadhurehi buddhehi vahitabbā dhurā, taṃ dhuraṃ vahanasamatthena mahāpurisena. Anuppattaṃ taṃ bhagavatāti taṃ sabbaṃ atītānāgatabuddhehi pattabbaṃ, sabbameva anuppattaṃ, bhagavato ekaguṇopi ūno natthīti dasseti. Kāmesu kāmasukhallikānuyoganti vatthukāmesu kāmasukhallikānuyogaṃ. Yathā aññe keṇiyajaṭilādayo samaṇabrāhmaṇā ‘‘ko jānāti paralokaṃ . Sukho imissā paribbājikāya mudukāya lomasāya bāhāya samphasso’’ti moḷibandhāhi paribbājikāhi paricārenti sampattaṃ sampattaṃ rūpādiārammaṇaṃ anubhavamānā kāmasukhamanuyuttā, na evamanuyuttoti dasseti.

Hīnanti lāmakaṃ. Gammanti gāmavāsīnaṃ dhammaṃ. Pothujjanikanti puthujjanehi sevitabbaṃ. Anariyanti na niddosaṃ. Na vā ariyehi sevitabbaṃ. Anatthasañhitanti anatthasaṃyuttaṃ. Attakilamathānuyoganti attano ātāpanaparitāpanānuyogaṃ. Dukkhanti dukkhayuttaṃ, dukkhamaṃ vā. Yathā eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā kāmasukhallikānuyogaṃ parivajjessāmāti kāyakilamathaṃ anudhāvanti, tato muñcissāmāti kāmasukhaṃ anudhāvanti, na evaṃ bhagavā. Bhagavā pana ubho ete ante vajjetvā yā sā ‘‘atthi, bhikkhave, majjhimā paṭipadā tathāgatena abhisambuddhā cakkhukaraṇī’’ti evaṃ vuttā sammāpaṭipatti, tameva paṭipanno. Tasmā ‘‘na ca attakilamathānuyoga’’ntiādimāha.

Hīna Gamma Pothujjanika Anariya Anatthasañhita Attakilamathānuyoga Dukkha

Ābhicetasikānanti abhicetasikānaṃ, kāmāvacaracittāni atikkamitvā ṭhitānanti attho. Diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānanti imasmiṃyeva attabhāve sukhavihārānaṃ. Poṭṭhapādasuttantasmiñhi sappītikadutiyajjhānaphalasamāpatti kathitā (dī. ni. 1.432). Pāsādikasuttante saha maggena vipassanāpādakajjhānaṃ. Dasuttarasuttante catutthajjhānikaphalasamāpatti. Imasmiṃ sampasādanīye diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārajjhānāni kathitāni. Nikāmalābhīti yathākāmalābhī. Akicchalābhīti adukkhalābhī. Akasiralābhīti vipulalābhī.

Ābhicetasikāna Diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārāna Poṭṭhapādasuttanta Pāsādikasuttante Nikāmalābhī Akicchalābhī Akasiralābhī

Anuyogadānappakāravaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
160. Now, in another way, showing the qualities of the Blessed One, he says, "What is that, *bhante*?" etc. There, "*saddhena kulaputtenā*" means faithful children of good families are the *bodhisattvas* of the past, future, and present. Therefore, it is said that it is attained by the all-knowing *bodhisattva*. What should be attained by that? The nine supramundane *dharmas*. "*āraddhavīriyenā*" etc. are all synonyms for vigor, such as "*vīriyaṃ thāmo*." There, "*āraddhavīriyenā*" means with aroused vigor. "*thāmavatā*" means endowed with strength, with steadfast vigor. "*purisathāmenā*" means that which is attained by a great being (mahāpuruṣa) with the strength of a man, by that strong one. The same method applies in the case of the two subsequent words. "*purisadhorayhenā*" means the burden that should be carried by unequalled Buddhas, by a great being who is capable of carrying that burden. "*anuppattaṃ taṃ bhagavatā*" means that all of that, everything that should be attained by the Buddhas of the past and future, all of it is attained, the Blessed One does not lack even a single quality, he shows. "*kāmesu kāmasukhallikānuyoga*" means indulgence in sensual pleasures in the objective sense. Just as other ascetics and Brahmins, such as the Keṇiya Jaṭila, [saying] "Who knows the next world?" Pleasant is the touch of this wandering woman's soft, hairy arm,” experiencing the form etc. that is attained by those who attend to the wandering women with braided hair, they are devoted to sensual pleasure, he shows that he is not devoted in that way. Lower (*hīna*) means inferior. Rustic (*gamma*) means the *dharma* of those who live in villages. Worldly (*pothujjanika*) means that which should be practiced by ordinary people (*pṛthagjana*). Un-Āryan (*anāriya*) means not faultless. Or, it should not be practiced by the *āryas*. Unconnected with the goal (*anatthasañhita*) means unconnected with the goal (*anatthasaṃyuttaṃ*). Self-mortification (*attakilamathānuyoga*) means devoting oneself to tormenting and torturing oneself. Suffering (*dukkha*) means connected with suffering (*dukkha-yuttaṃ*), or characterized by suffering (*dukkhaṃ*). Just as some ascetics and Brahmins, thinking, "We will avoid indulgence in sensual pleasures," pursue bodily mortification, and thinking, "We will be freed from that," they pursue sensual pleasure, the Blessed One is not like that. But the Blessed One, having avoided both of these extremes, that very "*madhyamā pratipadā*—the Middle Way—has been awakened to by the *Tathāgata*, which gives vision, gives knowledge," that is called right practice (*samyakpratipatti*), he has followed that very path. Therefore, he says "*na ca attakilamathānuyoga*" etc. Lower (*hīna*), rustic (*gamma*), worldly (*pothujjanika*), un-Āryan (*anāriya*), unconnected with the goal (*anatthasañhita*), self-mortification (*attakilamathānuyoga*), suffering (*dukkha*). "*ābhicetasikāna*" means those that are mental, the meaning is that they transcend the minds of the desire realm. "*diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārāna*" means abiding in happiness in this very existence. In the *Poṭṭhapādasuttanta*, the attainment of the fruit of the second *jhāna* with joy is described (Dī. Ni. 1. 432). In the *Pāsādikasuttanta*, the *jhāna* that is the basis for insight together with the path [is described]. In the *Dasuttarasuttanta*, the attainment of the fruit of the fourth *jhānic* [stage is described]. In this inspiring [text], the *jhānas* of abiding happily in this very life have been described. *Nikāmalābhī* means obtaining according to one's desire (*yathākāmalābhī*). *Akicchalābhī* means obtaining without difficulty (*adukkhalābhī*). *Akasiralābhī* means obtaining abundantly (*vipulalābhī*).

*Ābhicetasikāna*, *diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārāna*, *poṭṭhapādasuttanta*, *pāsādikasuttante* *Nikāmalābhī*, *akicchalābhī*, *akasiralābhī* anuyogadānappakāravaṇṇanā

mula_pali:
161. ‘‘Sace maṃ, bhante, evaṃ puccheyya – ‘kiṃ nu kho, āvuso sāriputta, ahesuṃ atītamaddhānaṃ aññe samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā bhagavatā bhiyyobhiññatarā sambodhiya’nti, evaṃ puṭṭho ahaṃ, bhante, ‘no’ti vadeyyaṃ. ‘Kiṃ panāvuso sāriputta, bhavissanti anāgatamaddhānaṃ aññe samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā bhagavatā bhiyyobhiññatarā sambodhiya’nti, evaṃ puṭṭho ahaṃ, bhante, ‘no’ti vadeyyaṃ . ‘Kiṃ panāvuso sāriputta, atthetarahi añño samaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā bhagavatā bhiyyobhiññataro sambodhiya’nti, evaṃ puṭṭho ahaṃ, bhante, ‘no’ti vadeyyaṃ.

‘‘Sace pana maṃ, bhante, evaṃ puccheyya – ‘kiṃ nu kho, āvuso sāriputta, ahesuṃ atītamaddhānaṃ aññe samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā bhagavatā samasamā sambodhiya’nti, evaṃ puṭṭho ahaṃ, bhante, ‘eva’nti vadeyyaṃ. ‘Kiṃ panāvuso sāriputta, bhavissanti anāgatamaddhānaṃ aññe samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā bhagavatā samasamā sambodhiya’nti, evaṃ puṭṭho ahaṃ, bhante, ‘‘eva’’nti vadeyyaṃ . ‘Kiṃ panāvuso sāriputta, atthetarahi aññe samaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā bhagavatā samasamā sambodhiya’nti, evaṃ puṭṭho ahaṃ bhante ‘no’ti vadeyyaṃ.

‘‘Sace pana maṃ, bhante, evaṃ puccheyya – ‘kiṃ panāyasmā sāriputto ekaccaṃ abbhanujānāti , ekaccaṃ na abbhanujānātī’ti, evaṃ puṭṭho ahaṃ, bhante, evaṃ byākareyyaṃ – ‘sammukhā metaṃ, āvuso, bhagavato sutaṃ, sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – ‘‘ahesuṃ atītamaddhānaṃ arahanto sammāsambuddhā mayā samasamā sambodhiya’’nti. Sammukhā metaṃ, āvuso, bhagavato sutaṃ, sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – ‘‘bhavissanti anāgatamaddhānaṃ arahanto sammāsambuddhā mayā samasamā sambodhiya’’nti. Sammukhā metaṃ, āvuso, bhagavato sutaṃ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṃ – ‘‘aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso yaṃ ekissā lokadhātuyā dve arahanto sammāsambuddhā apubbaṃ acarimaṃ uppajjeyyuṃ, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī’’’ti.

‘‘Kaccāhaṃ, bhante, evaṃ puṭṭho evaṃ byākaramāno vuttavādī ceva bhagavato homi, na ca bhagavantaṃ abhūtena abbhācikkhāmi, dhammassa cānudhammaṃ byākaromi, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānuvādo vādānupāto (sī.) gārayhaṃ ṭhānaṃ āgacchatī’’ti? ‘‘Taggha tvaṃ, sāriputta, evaṃ puṭṭho evaṃ byākaramāno vuttavādī ceva me hosi, na ca maṃ abhūtena abbhācikkhasi, dhammassa cānudhammaṃ byākarosi, na ca koci sahadhammiko vādānuvādo gārayhaṃ ṭhānaṃ āgacchatī’’ti.

vādānupāto (sī.)

Acchariyaabbhutaṃ
mula_english:
161. ‘If I were asked, venerable sir: “Well now, friend Śāriputra, have there been in the past any other ascetics or Brahmins more greatly endowed with higher knowledge in enlightenment than the Blessed One?”, being asked thus, venerable sir, I would say: “No.”

‘Again, if I were asked, friend Śāriputra: “Will there be in the future any other ascetics or Brahmins more greatly endowed with higher knowledge in enlightenment than the Blessed One?”, being asked thus, venerable sir, I would say: “No.”

‘Again, if I were asked, friend Śāriputra: “Are there at present any other ascetics or Brahmins more greatly endowed with higher knowledge in enlightenment than the Blessed One?”, being asked thus, venerable sir, I would say: “No.”

‘If, venerable sir, I were asked thus: “Well now, friend Śāriputra, have there been in the past any other ascetics or Brahmins equally endowed with enlightenment as the Blessed One?”, being asked thus, venerable sir, I would say: “Yes.”

‘Again, if I were asked, friend Śāriputra: “Will there be in the future any other ascetics or Brahmins equally endowed with enlightenment as the Blessed One?”, being asked thus, venerable sir, I would say: “Yes.”

‘Again, if I were asked, friend Śāriputra: “Are there at present any other ascetics or Brahmins equally endowed with enlightenment as the Blessed One?”, being asked thus, venerable sir, I would say: “No.”

‘If, venerable sir, I were asked thus: “Well now, venerable Śāriputra, why do you approve of some, and not approve of others?”, being asked thus, venerable sir, I would answer thus: “I have heard and received it in the presence of the Blessed One: ‘In the past there were arhats, perfectly awakened Buddhas, equally endowed with enlightenment as me.’

I have heard and received it in the presence of the Blessed One: ‘In the future there will be arhats, perfectly awakened Buddhas, equally endowed with enlightenment as me.’

I have heard and received it in the presence of the Blessed One: ‘It is impossible, there is no chance of such a thing, that in one world system two arhats, perfectly awakened Buddhas, should arise without precedence or subsequence; such a thing cannot be.’”

‘If, venerable sir, being asked thus, explaining thus, would I be one who speaks in accordance with the Blessed One’s words, and would I not misrepresent the Blessed One with what is untrue? Would I be explaining the *dharma* in accordance with the *dharma*, and would no fellow practitioner of the *dharma* arrive at a ground for censure regarding my statement?’

‘Indeed, Śāriputra, being asked thus, explaining thus, you would be one who speaks in accordance with my words, and you would not misrepresent me with what is untrue; you would be explaining the *dharma* in accordance with the *dharma*, and no fellow practitioner of the *dharma* would arrive at a ground for censure regarding your statement.’

Amazing and wonderful!
commentary_pali:
161.Ekissā lokadhātuyāti dasasahassilokadhātuyā. Tīṇi hi khettāni – jātikhettaṃ āṇākhettaṃ visayakhettaṃ. Tattha jātikhettaṃ nāma dasasahassī lokadhātu. Sā hi tathāgatassa mātukucchiṃ okkamanakāle nikkhamanakāle sambodhikāle dhammacakkappavattane āyusaṅkhārossajjane parinibbāne ca kampati. Koṭisatasahassacakkavāḷaṃ pana āṇākhettaṃ nāma. Āṭānāṭiyamoraparittadhajaggaparittaratanaparittādīnañhi ettha āṇā vattati. Visayakhettassa pana parimāṇaṃ natthi, buddhānañhi ‘‘yāvatakaṃ ñāṇaṃ, tāvatakaṃ ñeyyaṃ, yāvatakaṃ ñeyyaṃ tāvatakaṃ ñāṇaṃ, ñāṇapariyantikaṃ ñeyyaṃ, ñeyyapariyantikaṃ ñāṇa’’nti (mahāni. 55) vacanato avisayo nāma natthi.

Imesu pana tīsu khettesu ṭhapetvā imaṃ cakkavāḷaṃ aññasmiṃ cakkavāḷe buddhā uppajjantīti suttaṃ natthi, nuppañjantīti pana atthi. Tīṇi piṭakāni vinayapiṭakaṃ, suttantapiṭakaṃ abhidhammapiṭakaṃ. Tisso saṅgītiyo mahākassapattherassa saṅgīti, yasattherassa saṅgīti, moggaliputtatissattherassa saṅgītīti. Imā tisso saṅgītiyo āruḷhe tepiṭake buddhavacane ‘‘imaṃ cakkavāḷaṃ muñcitvā aññattha buddhā uppajjantī’’ti suttaṃ natthi, nuppajjantīti pana atthi.

Apubbaṃ acarimanti apure apacchā ekato nuppajjanti, pure vā pacchā vā uppajjantīti vuttaṃ hoti. Tattha bodhipallaṅke ‘‘bodhiṃ apatvā na uṭṭhahissāmī’’ti nisinnakālato paṭṭhāya yāva mātukucchismiṃ paṭisandhiggahaṇaṃ, tāva pubbeti na veditabbaṃ. Bodhisattassa hi paṭisandhiggahaṇe dasasahassacakkavāḷakampaneneva khettapariggaho kato. Aññassa buddhassa uppattipi nivāritā hoti. Parinibbānato paṭṭhāya ca yāva sāsapamattāpi dhātuyo tiṭṭhanti, tāva pacchāti na veditabbaṃ. Dhātūsu hi ṭhitāsu buddhāpi ṭhitāva honti. Tasmā etthantare aññassa buddhassa uppatti nivāritāva hoti. Dhātuparinibbāne pana jāte aññassa buddhassa uppatti na nivāritā.

Apubbaṃ acarima

Tipiṭakaantaradhānakathā

Tīṇi antaradhānāni nāma pariyattiantaradhānaṃ, paṭivedhaantaradhānaṃ, paṭipattiantaradhānanti. Tattha pariyattīti tīṇi piṭakāni. Paṭivedhoti saccappaṭivedho. Paṭipattīti paṭipadā. Tattha paṭivedho ca paṭipatti ca hotipi na hotipi. Ekasmiñhi kāle paṭivedhakarā bhikkhū bahū honti, esa bhikkhu puthujjanoti aṅguliṃ pasāretvā dassetabbo hoti. Imasmiṃyeva dīpe ekavāraṃ puthujjanabhikkhu nāma nāhosi. Paṭipattipūrakāpi kadāci bahū honti, kadāci appā. Iti paṭivedho ca paṭipatti ca hotipi na hotipi. Sāsanaṭṭhitiyā pana pariyatti pamāṇaṃ. Paṇḍito hi tepiṭakaṃ sutvā dvepi pūreti.

Tīṇi antaradhānāni pariyattī Paṭivedho Paṭipattī

Yathā amhākaṃ bodhisatto āḷārassa santike pañcābhiññā satta ca samāpattiyo nibbattetvā nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasamāpattiyā parikammaṃ pucchi, so na jānāmīti āha. Tato udakassa santikaṃ gantvā adhigatavisesaṃ saṃsanditvā nevasaññānāsaññāyatanassa parikammaṃ pucchi, so ācikkhi, tassa vacanasamanantarameva mahāsatto taṃ jhānaṃ sampādesi, evameva paññavā bhikkhu pariyattiṃ sutvā dvepi pūreti. Tasmā pariyattiyā ṭhitāya sāsanaṃ ṭhitaṃ hoti. Yadā pana sā antaradhāyati, tadā paṭhamaṃ abhidhammapiṭakaṃ nassati. Tattha paṭṭhānaṃ sabbapaṭhamaṃ antaradhāyati. Anukkamena pacchā dhammasaṅgaho , tasmiṃ antarahite itaresu dvīsu piṭakesu ṭhitesupi sāsanaṃ ṭhitameva hoti.

Tattha suttantapiṭake antaradhāyamāne paṭhamaṃ aṅguttaranikāyo ekādasakato paṭṭhāya yāva ekakā antaradhāyati, tadanantaraṃ saṃyuttanikāyo cakkapeyyālato paṭṭhāya yāva oghataraṇā antaradhāyati. Tadanantaraṃ majjhimanikāyo indriyabhāvanato paṭṭhāya yāva mūlapariyāyā antaradhāyati. Tadanantaraṃ dīghanikāyo dasuttarato paṭṭhāya yāva brahmajālā antaradhāyati. Ekissāpi dvinnampi gāthānaṃ pucchā addhānaṃ gacchati, sāsanaṃ dhāretuṃ na sakkoti, sabhiyapucchā āḷavakapucchā viya ca. Etā kira kassapabuddhakālikā antarā sāsanaṃ dhāretuṃ nāsakkhiṃsu.

Dvīsu pana piṭakesu antarahitesupi vinayapiṭake ṭhite sāsanaṃ tiṭṭhati. Parivārakkhandhakesu antarahitesu ubhatovibhaṅge ṭhite ṭhitameva hoti. Ubhatovibhaṅge antarahite mātikāyapi ṭhitāya ṭhitameva hoti. Mātikāya antarahitāya pātimokkhapabbajjāupasampadāsu ṭhitāsu sāsanaṃ tiṭṭhati. Liṅgaṃ addhānaṃ gacchati. Setavatthasamaṇavaṃso pana kassapabuddhakālato paṭṭhāya sāsanaṃ dhāretuṃ nāsakkhi. Paṭisambhidāpattehi vassasahassaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Chaḷabhiññehi vassasahassaṃ. Tevijjehi vassasahassaṃ. Sukkhavipassakehi vassasahassaṃ. Pātimokkhehi vassasahassaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Pacchimakassa pana saccappaṭivedhato pacchimakassa sīlabhedato paṭṭhāya sāsanaṃ osakkitaṃ nāma hoti. Tato paṭṭhāya aññassa buddhassa uppatti na nivāritā.

Paṭisambhidāpattehi Chaḷabhiññehi Tevijjehi Sukkhavipassakehi Pātimokkhehi

Sāsanaantarahitavaṇṇanā

Tīṇi parinibbānāni nāma kilesaparinibbānaṃ khandhaparinibbānaṃ dhātuparinibbānanti. Tattha kilesaparinibbānaṃ bodhipallaṅke ahosi. Khandhaparinibbānaṃ kusinārāyaṃ. Dhātuparinibbānaṃ anāgate bhavissati. Sāsanassa kira osakkanakāle imasmiṃ tambapaṇṇidīpe dhātuyo sannipatitvā mahācetiyaṃ gamissanti. Mahācetiyato nāgadīpe rājāyatanacetiyaṃ. Tato mahābodhipallaṅkaṃ gamissanti. Nāgabhavanatopi devalokatopi brahmalokatopi dhātuyo mahābodhipallaṅkameva gamissanti. Sāsapamattāpi dhātuyo na antarā nassissanti. Sabbadhātuyo mahābodhipallaṅke rāsibhūtā suvaṇṇakkhandho viya ekagghanā hutvā chabbaṇṇarasmiyo vissajjessanti.

Tīṇi parinibbānāni

Tā dasasahassilokadhātuṃ pharissanti, tato dasasahassacakkavāḷadevatā sannipatitvā ‘‘ajja satthā parinibbāti, ajja sāsanaṃ osakkati, pacchimadassanaṃ dāni idaṃ amhāka’’nti dasabalassa parinibbutadivasato mahantataraṃ kāruññaṃ karissanti. Ṭhapetvā anāgāmikhīṇāsave avasesā sakabhāvena sandhāretuṃ na sakkhissanti. Dhātūsu tejodhātu uṭṭhahitvā yāva brahmalokā uggacchissati. Sāsapamattāyapi dhātuyā sati ekajālā bhavissati. Dhātūsu pariyādānaṃ gatāsu upacchijjissati. Evaṃ mahantaṃ ānubhāvaṃ dassetvā dhātūsu antarahitāsu sāsanaṃ antarahitaṃ nāma hoti.

Yāva na evaṃ antaradhāyati, tāva acarimaṃ nāma hoti. Evaṃ apubbaṃ acarimaṃ uppajjeyyuṃ, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Kasmā pana apubbaṃ acarimaṃ nuppajjantīti? Anacchariyattā. Buddhā hi acchariyamanussā. Yathāha – ‘‘ekapuggalo, bhikkhave, loke uppajjamāno uppajjati acchariyamanusso. Katamo ekapuggalo? Tathāgato arahaṃ sammāsambuddho’’ti (a. ni. 1.172). Yadi ca dve vā cattāro vā aṭṭha vā soḷasa vā ekato uppajjeyyuṃ, anacchariyā bhaveyyuṃ. Ekasmiñhi vihāre dvinnaṃ cetiyānampi lābhasakkāro uḷāro na hoti. Bhikkhūpi bahutāya na acchariyā jātā, evaṃ buddhāpi bhaveyyuṃ, tasmā nuppajjanti. Desanāya ca visesābhāvato. Yañhi satipaṭṭhānādibhedaṃ dhammaṃ eko deseti. Aññena uppajjitvāpi sova desetabbo siyā, tato anacchariyo siyā. Ekasmiṃ pana dhammaṃ desente desanāpi acchariyā hoti, vivādabhāvato ca. Bahūsu hi buddhesu uppannesu bahūnaṃ ācariyānaṃ antevāsikā viya amhākaṃ buddho pāsādiko, amhākaṃ buddho madhurassaro lābhī puññavāti vivadeyyuṃ. Tasmāpi evaṃ nuppajjanti. Api cetaṃ kāraṇaṃ milindaraññāpi puṭṭhena nāgasenattherena vitthāritameva. Vuttañhi tattha –

Bhante, nāgasena, bhāsitampi hetaṃ bhagavatā ‘‘aṭṭhānametaṃ, bhikkhave, anavakāso, yaṃ ekissā lokadhātuyā dve arahanto sammāsambuddhā apubbaṃ acarimaṃ uppajjeyyuṃ, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatī’’ti. Desayantā ca, bhante nāgasena, sabbepi tathāgatā sattatiṃsa bodhipakkhiye dhamme desenti, kathayamānā ca cattāri ariyasaccāni kathenti, sikkhāpentā ca tīsu sikkhāsu sikkhāpenti, anusāsamānā ca appamādappaṭipattiyaṃ anusāsanti. Yadi, bhante nāgasena, sabbesampi tathāgatānaṃ ekā desanā ekā kathā ekasikkhā ekānusāsanī, kena kāraṇena dve tathāgatā ekakkhaṇe nuppajjanti. Ekenapi tāva buddhuppādena ayaṃ loko obhāsajāto, yadi dutiyo buddho bhaveyya, dvinnaṃ pabhāya ayaṃ loko bhiyyosomattāya obhāsajāto bhaveyya, ovadamānā ca dve tathāgatā sukhaṃ ovadeyyuṃ, anusāsamānā ca sukhaṃ anusāseyyuṃ, tattha me kāraṇaṃ desehi, yathāhaṃ nissaṃsayo bhaveyya’’nti.

Ayaṃ, mahārāja, dasasahassī lokadhātu ekabuddhadhāraṇī, ekasseva tathāgatassa guṇaṃ dhāreti, yadi dutiyo buddho uppajjeyya, nāyaṃ dasasahassī lokadhātu dhāreyya, caleyya, kampeyya, nameyya, oṇameyya, vinameyya, vikireyya, vidhameyya, viddhaṃseyya, na ṭhānamupagaccheyya.

Yathā, mahārāja, nāvā ekapurisasandhāraṇī bhaveyya, ekapurise abhirūḷhe sā nāvā samupādikā bhaveyya, atha dutiyo puriso āgaccheyya tādiso āyunā vaṇṇena vayena pamāṇena kisathūlena sabbaṅgapaccaṅgena, so taṃ nāvaṃ abhirūheyya, api nu sā, mahārāja, nāvā dvinnampi dhāreyyāti? Na hi, bhante, caleyya, kampeyya, nameyya, oṇameyya, vinameyya, vikireyya, vidhameyya, viddhaṃseyya, na ṭhānamupagaccheyya osīdeyya udaketi. Evameva kho, mahārāja, ayaṃ dasasahassī lokadhātu ekabuddhadhāraṇī, ekasseva tathāgatassa guṇaṃ dhāreti, yadi dutiyo buddho uppajjeyya, nāyaṃ dasasahassī lokadhātu dhāreyya…pe… na ṭhānamupagaccheyya.

Yathā vā pana, mahārāja, puriso yāvadatthaṃ bhojanaṃ bhuñjeyya chādentaṃ yāva kaṇṭhamabhipūrayitvā, so dhāto pīṇito paripuṇṇo nirantaro tandīkato anoṇamitadaṇḍajāto punadeva tāvatakaṃ bhojanaṃ bhuñjeyya, api nu kho so, mahārāja, puriso sukhito bhaveyyāti? Na hi, bhante , sakiṃ bhuttova mareyyāti; evameva kho, mahārāja, ayaṃ dasasahassī lokadhātu ekabuddhadhāraṇī …pe… na ṭhānamupagaccheyyāti.

Kiṃ nu kho, bhante nāgasena, atidhammabhārena pathavī calatīti? Idha, mahārāja, dve sakaṭā ratanapūritā bhaveyyuṃ yāva mukhasamā, ekasmā sakaṭato ratanaṃ gahetvā ekasmiṃ sakaṭe ākireyyuṃ, api nu kho taṃ, mahārāja, sakaṭaṃ dvinnampi sakaṭānaṃ ratanaṃ dhāreyyāti? Na hi, bhante, nābhipi tassa phaleyya, arāpi tassa bhijjeyyuṃ, nemipi tassa opateyya, akkhopi tassa bhijjeyyāti. Kiṃ nu kho, mahārāja, atiratanabhārena sakaṭaṃ bhijjatīti? Āma, bhante,ti. Evameva kho, mahārāja, atidhammabhārena pathavī calati.

Apica, mahārāja, imaṃ kāraṇaṃ buddhabalaparidīpanāya osāritaṃ aññampi tattha atirūpaṃ kāraṇaṃ suṇohi, yena kāraṇena dve sammāsambuddhā ekakkhaṇe nuppajjanti. Yadi, mahārāja, dve sammāsambuddhā ekakkhaṇe uppajjeyyuṃ, tesaṃ parisāya vivādo uppajjeyya ‘‘tumhākaṃ buddho amhākaṃ buddho’’ti, ubhato pakkhajātā bhaveyyuṃ. Yathā, mahārāja, dvinnaṃ balavāmaccānaṃ parisāya vivādo uppajjeyya ‘‘tumhākaṃ amacco amhākaṃ amacco’’ti, ubhato pakkhajātā honti; evameva kho, mahārāja, yadi dve sammāsambuddhā ekakkhaṇe uppajjeyyuṃ, tesaṃ parisāya vivādo uppajjeyya ‘‘tumhākaṃ buddho, amhākaṃ buddho’’ti, ubhato pakkhajātā bhaveyyuṃ, idaṃ tāva, mahārāja, ekaṃ kāraṇaṃ, yena kāraṇena dve sammāsambuddhā ekakkhaṇe nuppajjanti.

Aparampi, mahārāja, uttariṃ kāraṇaṃ suṇohi, yena kāraṇena dve sammāsambuddhā ekakkhaṇe nuppajjanti. Yadi, mahārāja, dve sammāsambuddhā ekakkhaṇe uppajjeyyuṃ, ‘‘aggo buddho’’ti yaṃ vacanaṃ, taṃ micchā bhaveyya, ‘‘jeṭṭho buddho’’ti, seṭṭho buddhoti, visiṭṭho buddhoti, uttamo buddhoti, pavaro buddhoti, asamo buddhoti , asamasamo buddhoti, appaṭimo buddhoti, appaṭibhāgo buddhoti, appaṭipuggalo buddhoti yaṃ vacanaṃ, taṃ micchā bhaveyya. Imampi kho tvaṃ, mahārāja, kāraṇaṃ atthato sampaṭiccha, yena kāraṇena dve sammāsambuddhā ekakkhaṇe nuppajjanti.

Apica kho, mahārāja, buddhānaṃ bhagavantānaṃ sabhāvapakati esā, yaṃ ekoyeva buddho loke uppajjati. Kasmā kāraṇā? Mahantatāya sabbaññubuddhaguṇānaṃ, yaṃ aññampi, mahārāja, mahantaṃ hoti, taṃ ekaṃyeva hoti. Pathavī, mahārāja, mahantī, sā ekāyeva. Sāgaro mahanto, so ekoyeva. Sineru girirājā mahanto, so ekoyeva. Ākāso mahanto, so ekoyeva. Sakko mahanto, so ekoyeva. Māro mahanto , so ekoyeva. Mahābrahmā mahanto, so ekoyeva. Tathāgato arahaṃ sammāsambuddho mahanto, so ekoyeva lokasmiṃ. Yattha te uppajjanti, tattha aññesaṃ okāso na hoti. Tasmā, mahārāja, tathāgato arahaṃ sammāsambuddho ekoyeva loke uppajjatīti. Sukathito, bhante nāgasena, pañho opammehi kāraṇehīti (mi. pa. 5.1.1).

Dhammassa cānudhammanti navavidhassa lokuttaradhammassa anudhammaṃ pubbabhāgappaṭipadaṃ. Sahadhammikoti sakāraṇo. Vādānuvādoti vādoyeva.

Dhammassa cānudhamma Sahadhammiko Vādānuvādo

161. *Ekissā lokadhātuyā* means the ten-thousandfold world system.

There are three fields: the birth field ( *jātikhettaṃ*), the command field (*āṇākhettaṃ*), and the range field (*visayakhettaṃ*).

There, *jātikhettaṃ* is the name for the ten-thousandfold world system.

Indeed, it trembles when the Tathāgata enters his mother's womb, at his birth, at the time of his enlightenment, at the turning of the wheel of the Dharma, at the rejection of his life span, and at his complete passing away.

Moreover, *āṇākhettaṃ* is the name for a hundred thousand million world-spheres.

Here, the command (*āṇā*) of the Āṭānāṭiya, the Peacock Protection (*moraparitta*), the Banner Top Protection (*dhajaggaparitta*), the Jewel Protection (*ratanaparitta*) and others takes effect.

However, there is no limit to the *visayakhettaṃ*, for there is no object (*avisayo*) because of the Buddha's saying, "As far as there is knowledge (*ñāṇaṃ*), so far is there knowable (*ñeyyaṃ*); as far as there is knowable, so far is there knowledge; the knowable is limited by knowledge, [and] knowledge is limited by the knowable" (Mahāniddesa 55).

But in these three fields, setting aside this world-sphere, there is no sutra saying that Buddhas arise in another world-sphere, but there is [a sutra saying that] they do not arise.

The three baskets (*piṭaka*): the Basket of Discipline (*vinayapiṭakaṃ*), the Basket of Discourses (*suttantapiṭakaṃ*), and the Basket of Abhidhamma (*abhidhammapiṭakaṃ*).

The three recitations (*saṅgīti*): the recitation of the Elder Mahākassapa, the recitation of the Elder Yasa, and the recitation of the Elder Moggaliputtatissa.

In these three recitations, which are established in the three baskets, there is no sutra in the word of the Buddha saying, "Having released this world-sphere, Buddhas arise elsewhere," but there is [a sutra saying that] they do not arise.

*Apubbaṃ acarima* means that [Buddhas] do not arise together, before or after, but they arise before or after.

There, it should not be understood that [the time] from when [the Buddha] sat on the seat of enlightenment (*bodhipallaṅke*), [thinking,] "I will not rise until I have attained enlightenment (*bodhiṃ*)," until the acceptance of rebirth in his mother's womb, is before.

Indeed, at the acceptance of rebirth of the Bodhisatta, the extent of the field was made known only by the trembling of the ten-thousandfold world-sphere.

Even the arising of another Buddha is prevented.

And it should not be understood that [the time] from his complete passing away (*parinibbāna*) until even mustard-seed-sized relics (*dhātuyo*) remain is after.

Indeed, when the relics remain, even Buddhas remain.

Therefore, the arising of another Buddha is prevented in this interval.

However, the arising of another Buddha is not prevented when the relics completely pass away (*dhātuparinibbāne*).

*Apubbaṃ acarima*

Account of the Disappearance of the Three Baskets (*tipiṭakaantaradhānakathā*)

*Tīṇi antaradhānāni* are the disappearance of learning (*pariyattiantaradhānaṃ*), the disappearance of realization (*paṭivedhaantaradhānaṃ*), [and] the disappearance of practice (*paṭipattiantaradhānaṃ*).

There, *pariyattī* means the three baskets.

*Paṭivedho* means the realization of the truths (*saccappaṭivedho*).

*Paṭipattī* means the practice (*paṭipadā*).

There, realization and practice both exist and do not exist.

Indeed, at one time, there are many monks who realize [the truth], [so many that] it is necessary to extend a finger and point out, "This monk is an ordinary person (*puthujjana*)."

At one time on this island, there were no monks who were ordinary people.

Sometimes there are many who fulfill the practice, sometimes few.

Thus, realization and practice both exist and do not exist.

However, for the stability of the Dispensation, learning is the measure.

Indeed, the wise person, having heard the three baskets, fulfills both.

*Tīṇi antaradhānāni*, *pariyattī*, *paṭivedho*, *paṭipattī*

Just as our Bodhisatta, having produced the five superknowledges (*pañcābhiññā*) and the seven attainments (*satta samāpattiyo*) in the presence of Āḷāra, asked about the preliminary practice (*parikammaṃ*) of the attainment of neither perception nor non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasamāpattiyā*), [and] he said, "I do not know."

Then, having gone to the presence of Udaka, having compared the distinction he had attained, he asked about the preliminary practice of the attainment of neither perception nor non-perception, [and] he told [him]. Immediately after his words, the great being accomplished that meditation (*jhānaṃ*).

A wise *bhikkhu*, having heard the doctrine, fulfills both.
Therefore, when the doctrine is established, the *sāsana* is established.
But when that disappears, then first the Abhidhamma Piṭaka vanishes.
There the *paṭṭhāna* disappears first of all.
Gradually afterwards the Dhammasaṅgaho, when that has disappeared, even if the other two Piṭakas remain, the *sāsana* is still established.


There, when the Suttanta Piṭaka is disappearing, first the Aṅguttara Nikāya disappears, starting from the eleventh, up to the first. After that, the Saṃyutta Nikāya disappears, starting from Cakkapeyyāla, up to Oghataraṇa.
After that, the Majjhima Nikāya disappears, starting from Indriyabhāvanā, up to Mūlapariyāya.
After that, the Dīgha Nikāya disappears, starting from Dasuttara, up to Brahmajāla.
Even a question of one or two verses goes on for a long time, it is not able to maintain the *sāsana*, like the questions of Sabhiya and Āḷavaka.
These, it seems, in the time of Kassapa Buddha, were not able to maintain the *sāsana*.


But even when two Piṭakas have disappeared, the *sāsana* remains when the Vinaya Piṭaka remains.
When the Parivāra Khandhakas have disappeared, it still remains when the Ubhatovibhaṅga remains.
When the Ubhatovibhaṅga has disappeared, it still remains when the Mātikā remains.
When the Mātikā has disappeared, the *sāsana* remains when the Pātimokkha, *pabbajjā*, and *upasampadā* remain.
The symbol goes a long way.
But the Setavatthasamana lineage, from the time of Kassapa Buddha, was not able to maintain the *sāsana*.
With *paṭisambhidāpattehi* it stood for a thousand years.
With *chaḷabhiññehi* a thousand years.
With *tevijjehi* a thousand years.
With *sukkhavipassakehi* a thousand years.
With *pātimokkhehi* it stood for a thousand years.
But from the time of the last attainment of truth, from the time of the last breach of morality, the *sāsana* is said to be declining.
From then on, the arising of another Buddha is not prevented.


*tīṇi parinibbānāni* are: the *kilesaparinibbānaṃ*, the *khandhaparinibbānaṃ*, and the *dhātuparinibbānaṃ*.
There, the *kilesaparinibbānaṃ* was at the Bodhi tree.
The *khandhaparinibbānaṃ* was at Kusinārā.
The *dhātuparinibbānaṃ* will be in the future.
It seems that at the time of the decline of the *sāsana*, in this Tambapaṇṇidīpa, the relics will gather together and go to the Mahācetiya.
From the Mahācetiya to the Rājāyatanacetiya in Nāgadīpa.
From there they will go to the Mahābodhi tree.
From the Nāga world, the Deva world, and the Brahma world, the relics will go to the Mahābodhi tree.
Even relics the size of a mustard seed will not disappear in between.
All the relics, having gathered together at the Mahābodhi tree, having become one solid mass like a golden trunk, will emit six-colored rays.

That they will pervade the ten-thousandfold world system, and then the deities of the ten-thousand world-sphere will gather together and think, “Today the Teacher will attain *parinirvāṇa*, today the Teaching will decline, this is our last sight," and they will show even greater compassion than on the day of the Ten-Powered One’s *parinirvāṇa*.

Except for non-returners and those who have destroyed the āsavas, the rest will not be able to maintain their own state.

When the elements are present, the fire element will rise up and ascend as far as the Brahma world.

Even with a mustard seed-sized element, there will be a single flame.

When the elements have reached complete consumption, it will cease.

Having shown such great power, when the elements have disappeared, it is said that the Teaching has disappeared.

As long as it does not thus disappear, it is said that it is not final.

Thus, unarisen and not final [Buddhas] should arise; such a thing is not possible.

Why then do unarisen and not final [Buddhas] not arise? Because of [their] non-extraordinary nature.

For Buddhas are extraordinary humans.

As he said: “There is one person, monks, who arises in the world and is an extraordinary human.

Which one person? The *tathāgata*, the *arhat*, the completely awakened one” (A.
Ni.

172).

And if two, four, eight, or sixteen were to arise together, they would not be extraordinary.

For in one monastery, even for two *caityas*, the gain and honor is not abundant.

Monks are also not born as extraordinary in great numbers, so too would Buddhas be; therefore they do not arise.

And because of the absence of distinction in the teaching.

For when one teaches the Dharma that is distinct in the *smṛtyupasthānas*, etc.

Even having arisen by another, he would have to be taught that way, therefore he would be unextraordinary.

But when one teaches the Dharma, the teaching is also extraordinary, and because of the presence of debate.

For when many Buddhas have arisen, the students of many teachers would dispute, saying, “Our Buddha is pleasing, our Buddha has a sweet voice, he is a gainer and virtuous.”

Therefore, they do not thus arise.

And this reason has also been extensively explained by the Elder Nāgasena, questioned by King Milinda.

For it was said there:

“Venerable Nāgasena, this was also spoken by the Blessed One: ‘This is impossible, monks, there is no opportunity, that in one world-element two *arhats*, completely awakened ones, should arise unarisen and not final; such a thing is not possible.’”

And when they are teaching, venerable Nāgasena, all *tathāgatas* teach the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, and when they are speaking, they speak the Four Noble Truths, and when they are training, they train in the three trainings, and when they are instructing, they instruct in the practice of diligence.

If, venerable Nāgasena, all the *tathāgatas* have one teaching, one talk, one training, one instruction, by what reason do two *tathāgatas* not arise at the same moment?

Even by the arising of just one Buddha, this world has become light-born; if there were a second Buddha, by the light of the two, this world would become even more light-born; and when two *tathāgatas* are exhorting, they could easily exhort, and when instructing, they could easily instruct, tell me the reason for this, so that I may be without doubt.”

This, great king, is a ten-thousandfold world system, the sustainer of one Buddha, it sustains the qualities of only one *tathāgata*, if a second Buddha were to arise, this ten-thousandfold world system would not sustain [it], it would shake, tremble, bend, incline, turn away, scatter, dissolve, shatter, it would not reach a place of rest.
As, great king, if there were a boat capable of carrying one man, and when one man had embarked, that boat were full, then a second man should come, like the first in age, complexion, stature, and size, with all his limbs and members, and should embark on that boat, would that boat, great king, bear the weight of both? No, revered sir. It would shake, tremble, bend, lean over, incline, scatter, break up, be shattered, and would not reach its place, but would sink in the water.

Even so, great king, this ten-thousandfold world-system is the sustainer of one Buddha, it sustains the special qualities of one *tathāgata* only. If a second Buddha were to arise, this ten-thousandfold world-system could not bear him...it would not reach its place.

Or again, great king, it is as if a man should eat his fill of food, filling himself right up to his throat, and being satisfied, replete, full, without interruption, made languid, no longer standing erect, should again eat just as much food, would that man, great king, be happy? No, revered sir, but having eaten once, he would die. Even so, great king, this ten-thousandfold world-system is the sustainer of one Buddha.

What now, revered Nāgasena, is it because of the excessive burden of the *dharma* that the earth trembles? Here, great king, if there were two carts filled with jewels right up to their brims, and taking the jewels from one cart, they were to heap them into the other, would that cart, great king, bear the jewels of both carts? No, revered sir, the nave of its wheel would break, the spokes of it would be shattered, the felly of it would give way, the axle of it would be broken.

What now, great king, is it because of the excessive burden of jewels that the cart breaks? Yes, revered sir.

Even so, great king, it is because of the excessive burden of the *dharma* that the earth trembles.

Moreover, great king, this reason has been brought forward to illustrate the power of a Buddha. Hear another, still more excellent, reason why two perfectly awakened Buddhas do not arise at the same time.

If, great king, two perfectly awakened Buddhas were to arise at the same moment, a dispute would arise in their assemblies, [some saying,] "Our Buddha!" [others,] "Our Buddha!" and partisanships would arise on both sides.

As, great king, if a dispute were to arise in the assemblies of two powerful ministers, [some saying,] "Your minister!" [others,] "Our minister!" and partisanships would arise on both sides; even so, great king, if two perfectly awakened Buddhas were to arise at the same moment, a dispute would arise in their assemblies, [some saying,] "Your Buddha!" [others,] "Our Buddha!" and partisanships would arise on both sides. This, great king, is the first reason why two perfectly awakened Buddhas do not arise at the same moment.

And again, great king, hear a further reason why two perfectly awakened Buddhas do not arise at the same moment.

If, great king, two perfectly awakened Buddhas were to arise at the same moment, that saying, "The foremost Buddha," would be false, [as would also the sayings,] "The eldest Buddha," "The best Buddha," "The distinguished Buddha," "The supreme Buddha," "The excellent Buddha," "The matchless Buddha," "The unequalled Buddha," "The peerless Buddha," "The unrivalled Buddha," "The individual without compare". That saying would be false.

Do you also, great king, rightly accept this reason as to why two perfectly awakened Buddhas do not arise at the same moment.

Moreover, great king, this is the natural order of Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, that one Buddha alone arises in the world.

For what reason? Because of the greatness of the qualities of the all-knowing Buddha. Whatever else, great king, is great, that is only one.

The earth, great king, is mighty, and it is only one.

The ocean is mighty, and it is only one.

Sineru, king of mountains, is mighty, and it is only one.

Space is mighty, and it is only one.

Sakka is mighty, and he is only one.

Māra is mighty, and he is only one.

Mahā-Brahmā is mighty, and he is only one.

The *tathāgata*, *arhat*, perfectly enlightened Buddha, is mighty, and he is alone in the world.

Where they arise, there is no opportunity for others.

Therefore, great king, the *tathāgata*, *arhat*, perfectly enlightened Buddha, one alone arises in the world.

Well discussed, revered Nāgasena, is the question with similes and reasons.
" *Dhammassa cānudhamma* " means the practice preceding the ninefold supramundane dharma (*lokuttaradhamma*), which is in accordance with the dharma (*anudhamma*).

" *Sahadhammiko* " means with reason (*sakāraṇo*).

" *Vādānuvādo* " means simply debate (*vādo eva*).

*Dhammassa cānudhamma, sahadhammiko, vādānuvādo*: Description of the wonderful and amazing (*acchariyaabbhutavaṇṇanā*).

mula_pali:
162. Evaṃ vutte, āyasmā udāyī bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘acchariyaṃ, bhante, abbhutaṃ, bhante, tathāgatassa appicchatā santuṭṭhitā sallekhatā. Yatra hi nāma tathāgato evaṃmahiddhiko evaṃmahānubhāvo, atha ca pana nevattānaṃ pātukarissati! Ekamekañcepi ito, bhante, dhammaṃ aññatitthiyā paribbājakā attani samanupasseyyuṃ, te tāvatakeneva paṭākaṃ parihareyyuṃ. Acchariyaṃ, bhante, abbhutaṃ, bhante, tathāgatassa appicchatā santuṭṭhitā sallekhatā. Yatra hi nāma tathāgato evaṃ mahiddhiko evaṃmahānubhāvo. Atha ca pana nevattānaṃ pātukarissatī’’ti!

‘‘Passa kho tvaṃ, udāyi, ‘tathāgatassa appicchatā santuṭṭhitā sallekhatā. Yatra hi nāma tathāgato evaṃmahiddhiko evaṃmahānubhāvo, atha ca pana nevattānaṃ pātukarissati’! Ekamekañcepi ito, udāyi, dhammaṃ aññatitthiyā paribbājakā attani samanupasseyyuṃ, te tāvatakeneva paṭākaṃ parihareyyuṃ. Passa kho tvaṃ, udāyi, ‘tathāgatassa appicchatā santuṭṭhitā sallekhatā.
