Yatra hi nāma tathāgato evaṃmahiddhiko evaṃmahānubhāvo, atha ca pana nevattānaṃ pātukarissatī’’’ti!
mula_english:
At this, the Venerable Udayi said to the Blessed One: "It is wonderful, venerable sir, it is marvelous, venerable sir, how the **Tathāgata's** ( *tathāgatassa*) frugality, contentment, and austerity."

"Where the **Tathāgata** ( *tathāgato*) is so mighty, so powerful, yet he does not reveal himself! Even if wanderers of other sects were to perceive a single one of these qualities in themselves, they would parade around with a banner on account of that alone."

"It is wonderful, venerable sir, it is marvelous, venerable sir, how the **Tathāgata's** ( *tathāgatassa*) frugality, contentment, and austerity."

"Where the **Tathāgata** ( *tathāgato*) is so mighty, so powerful, yet he does not reveal himself!"

"Therefore, Udayi, observe the **Tathāgata's** ( *tathāgatassa*) frugality, contentment and austerity."

"Where the **Tathāgata** ( *tathāgato*) is so mighty, so powerful, yet he does not reveal himself! Even if wanderers of other sects were to perceive a single one of these qualities in themselves, they would parade around with a banner on account of that alone."

"Therefore, Udayi, observe the **Tathāgata's** ( *tathāgatassa*) frugality, contentment and austerity."

"Where the **Tathāgata** ( *tathāgato*) is so mighty, so powerful, yet he does not reveal himself!"
commentary_pali:
162.Āyasmā udāyīti tayo therā udāyī nāma – lāḷudāyī, kāḷudāyī, mahāudāyīti. Idha mahāudāyī adhippeto. Tassa kira imaṃ suttaṃ ādito paṭṭhāya yāva pariyosānā suṇantassa abbhantare pañcavaṇṇā pīti uppajjitvā pādapiṭṭhito sīsamatthakaṃ gacchati, sīsamatthakato pādapiṭṭhiṃ āgacchati, ubhato paṭṭhāya majjhaṃ otarati, majjhato paṭṭhāya ubhato gacchati. So nirantaraṃ pītiyā phuṭasarīro balavasomanassena dasabalassa guṇaṃ kathento acchariyaṃ bhantetiādimāha. Appicchatāti nittaṇhatā. Santuṭṭhitāti catūsu paccayesu tīhākārehi santoso. Sallekhatāti sabbakilesānaṃ sallikhitabhāvo. Yatra hi nāmāti yo nāma. Na attānaṃ pātukarissatīti attano guṇe na āvi karissati. Paṭākaṃ parihareyyunti ‘‘ko amhehi sadiso atthī’’ti vadantā paṭākaṃ ukkhipitvā nāḷandaṃ vicareyyuṃ.

Passakho tvaṃ, udāyi, tathāgatassa appicchatāti passa udāyi yādisī tathāgatassa appicchatāti therassa vacanaṃ sampaṭicchanto āha. Kiṃ pana bhagavā neva attānaṃ pātukaroti, na attano guṇaṃ kathetīti ce? Na, na katheti. Appicchatādīhi kathetabbaṃ, cīvarādihetuṃ na katheti. Tenevāha – ‘‘passa kho tvaṃ, udāyi, tathāgatassa appicchatā’’tiādi. Bujjhanakasattaṃ pana āgamma veneyyavasena katheti. Yathāha –

Passa kho tvaṃ, udāyi, tathāgatassa appicchatā

‘‘Na me ācariyo atthi, sadiso me na vijjati;

Sadevakasmiṃ lokasmiṃ, natthi me paṭipuggalo’’ti. (mahāva. 11);

Evaṃ tathāgatassa guṇadīpikā bahū gāthāpi suttantāpi vitthāretabbā.
commentary_english:
162. Āyasmā Udāyī: These three elders are named Udāyī - Lāḷudāyī, Kāḷudāyī, Mahāudāyī. Here, Mahāudāyī is intended. When he listens to this *sūtra* from beginning to end, a five-colored joy (*pañcavaṇṇā pīti*) arises in him, going from the soles of his feet to the crown of his head, and from the crown of his head to the soles of his feet, descending from both sides to the middle, and going from the middle to both sides. He, with his body filled with constant joy, recounting the qualities (*guṇa*) of the Ten-Powered One (*dasabalassa*) with intense delight, says, "Amazing, *bhante*," and so on. Appicchatā: is non-craving (*nittaṇhatā*). Santuṭṭhitā: is contentment (*santoso*) with the four requisites in three ways. Sallekhatā: is the state of having scraped away all defilements (*sabbakilesānaṃ sallikhitabhāvo*). Yatra hi nāmā: is that which is name (*yo nāma*). Na attānaṃ pātukarissatī: he does not reveal his own good qualities (*attano guṇe na āvi karissati*). Paṭākaṃ parihareyyu: "Those who say, 'Who is equal to us?' should raise a flag (*paṭākaṃ ukkhipitvā*) and wander about in Nāḷanda."

Passa Look, kho tvaṃ, Udāyi, tathāgatassa appicchatā: Udāyi, see the desirelessness of the *Tathāgata*. Saying, "Udāyi, see the desirelessness of the *Tathāgata*," he approves of the elder's words and says: "But does the Blessed One (*bhagavā*) not reveal himself, does he not speak of his own good qualities?" No, he does not speak of them. He should speak of desirelessness and so on (*appicchatādīhi kathetabbaṃ*), he does not speak for the sake of robes and so on (*cīvarādihetuṃ na katheti*). Therefore he said, "Look, Udāyi, at the desirelessness of the *Tathāgata*," and so on. But he speaks according to the individual being guided, having approached those capable of understanding (*bujjhanakasattaṃ pana āgamma veneyyavasena katheti*). As he said: Passa Look, kho tvaṃ, Udāyi, tathāgatassa appicchatā "I have no teacher, no one like me exists; In the world with its gods, there is no one comparable to me." (Mahāva. 11);

Thus, many verses and *sūtras* should be elaborated as illuminations of the *Tathāgata*'s qualities (*tathāgatassa guṇadīpikā bahū gāthāpi suttantāpi vitthāretabbā*).

mula_pali:
163. Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘tasmā tiha tvaṃ, sāriputta, imaṃ dhammapariyāyaṃ abhikkhaṇaṃ bhāseyyāsi bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ upāsakānaṃ upāsikānaṃ. Yesampi hi, sāriputta, moghapurisānaṃ bhavissati tathāgate kaṅkhā vā vimati vā, tesamimaṃ dhammapariyāyaṃ sutvā tathāgate kaṅkhā vā vimati vā, sā pahīyissatī’’ti. Iti hidaṃ āyasmā sāriputto bhagavato sammukhā sampasādaṃ pavedesi. Tasmā imassa veyyākaraṇassa sampasādanīyaṃ tveva adhivacananti.

Sampasādanīyasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ pañcamaṃ.
mula_english:
Then, the Lord (bhagavā) addressed the Venerable (āyasmantaṃ) Śāriputta (sāriputtaṃ), saying: "Therefore (tasmā), Śāriputra (sāriputta), you should frequently (abhikkhaṇaṃ) speak (bhāseyyāsi) about this (imaṃ) exposition of the Dharma (dhammapariyāyaṃ) to monks (bhikkhūnaṃ), nuns (bhikkhunīnaṃ), male lay followers (upāsakānaṃ) and female lay followers (upāsikānaṃ).

Even though some foolish people (moghapurisānaṃ) may have perplexity (kaṅkhā) or uncertainty (vimati) regarding the *Tathāgata*, when they hear this exposition of the Dharma (dhammapariyāyaṃ), their perplexity (kaṅkhā) or uncertainty (vimati) regarding the *Tathāgata* will be abandoned (pahīyissati."

Thus (iti), the Venerable (āyasmā) Śāriputta (sāriputto) proclaimed (pavedesi) his confidence (sampasādaṃ) in the Lord (bhagavato) face to face (sammukhā).

And so one name for this exposition (imasassa veyyākaraṇassa) is ‘The Serene Faith’ (sampasādanīyaṃ tveva adhivacananti).

The *Sampasādanīya Sutta*, the fifth, is concluded (niṭṭhitaṃ pañcamaṃ).
commentary_pali:
163.Abhikkhaṇaṃ bhāseyyāsīti punappunaṃ bhāseyyāsi. Pubbaṇhasamaye me kathitanti mā majjhanhikādīsu na kathayittha. Ajja vā me kathitanti mā paradivasādīsu na kathayitthāti attho. Pavedesīti kathesi. Imassa veyyākaraṇassāti niggāthakattā idaṃ suttaṃ ‘‘veyyākaraṇa’’nti vuttaṃ. Adhivacananti nāmaṃ. Idaṃ pana ‘‘iti hida’’nti paṭṭhāya padaṃ saṅgītikārehi ṭhapitaṃ. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānatthamevāti.

Sumaṅgalavilāsiniyā dīghanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Sampasādanīyasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
163.
"You should speak frequently (abhikkhaṇaṃ bhāseyyāsī)" means you should speak repeatedly.
"It was told to me in the forenoon (pubbaṇhasamaye me kathitanti)," do not say it in the afternoon, etc.
"It was told to me today (ajja vā me kathitanti)," do not say it on the following days, etc., is the meaning (attho).
"He announced (pavedesī)," he said.
"Because of this explanation (imassa veyyākaraṇassā)," because it is the author of the Niggātha, this sutra is called "explanation (veyyākaraṇa)."
"Designation (adhivacana)" is a name (nāmaṃ).
Furthermore, this word (padaṃ) beginning with "iti hida" was established by the reciters (saṅgītikārehi ṭhapitaṃ).
The rest is clear throughout (sesaṃ sabbattha uttānatthamevāti).

The Sampasādanīyasuttavaṇṇanā, commentary on the Dīghanikāya by Sumaṅgalavilāsinī, is finished (niṭṭhitā).

mula_pali:
164. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sakkesu viharati vedhaññā nāma sakyā, tesaṃ ambavane pāsāde.

Nigaṇṭhanāṭaputtakālaṅkiriyā

Tena kho pana samayena nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto nāthaputto (sī. pī.) pāvāyaṃ adhunākālaṅkato hoti. Tassa kālaṅkiriyāya bhinnā nigaṇṭhā dvedhikajātā bhaṇḍanajātā kalahajātā vivādāpannā aññamaññaṃ mukhasattīhi vitudantā viharanti – ‘‘na tvaṃ imaṃ dhammavinayaṃ ājānāsi, ahaṃ imaṃ dhammavinayaṃ ājānāmi, kiṃ tvaṃ imaṃ dhammavinayaṃ ājānissasi? Micchāpaṭipanno tvamasi, ahamasmi sammāpaṭipanno. Sahitaṃ me, asahitaṃ te. Purevacanīyaṃ pacchā avaca, pacchāvacanīyaṃ pure avaca. Adhiciṇṇaṃ te viparāvattaṃ, āropito te vādo, niggahito tvamasi, cara vādappamokkhāya, nibbeṭhehi vā sace pahosī’’ti. Vadhoyeva kho vadhoyeveko (ka.) maññe nigaṇṭhesu nāṭaputtiyesu vattati anuvattati (syā. ka.). Yepi nigaṇṭhassa nāṭaputtassa sāvakā gihī odātavasanā , tepi te tesu (ka.) nigaṇṭhesu nāṭaputtiyesu nibbinnarūpā nibbindarūpā (ka.) virattarūpā paṭivānarūpā, yathā taṃ durakkhāte dhammavinaye duppavedite aniyyānike anupasamasaṃvattanike asammāsambuddhappavedite bhinnathūpe appaṭisaraṇe.

nāthaputto (sī. pī.) vadhoyeveko (ka.) anuvattati (syā. ka.) te tesu (ka.) nibbindarūpā (ka.)
mula_english:
Thus I have heard: On one occasion the Blessed One (Bhagavān) was staying among the Sakyans (Śākyas) in the mansion in the mango grove of the Sakyan family called Vedhañña.

Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta's Death

And on that occasion, Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta had just died in Pāvā.

On his death, the Nigaṇṭhas had split into two factions. They kept arguing, quarreling, & disputing, stabbing one another with weapons of the mouth: “You don’t understand this *Dhamma-Vinaya*. I understand this *Dhamma-Vinaya*. How could you understand this *Dhamma-Vinaya*? Your way is wrong. My way is right. I am consistent. You are inconsistent. What should have been said first you said last. What should have been said last you said first. What you cogitated so long has been turned inside out. Your position has been overthrown. You’re trapped, so go try to release your position or disentangle yourself if you can!”

It seems to me that only slaughter (vadho) goes on among the Nigaṇṭhas, the followers of Nāṭaputta.

And his white-clothed lay disciples were disgusted, dismayed, and disappointed with the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta’s pupils, as they were with his badly proclaimed and badly expounded *Dhamma-Vinaya*, which was unemancipating, unconducive to peace, expounded by one not fully enlightened, and was now with its shrine broken, left without a refuge.
commentary_pali:
164.Evaṃme sutanti pāsādikasuttaṃ. Tatrāyamanuttānapadavaṇṇanā – vedhaññā nāma sakyāti dhanumhi katasikkhā vedhaññanāmakā eke sakyā. Tesaṃ ambavane pāsādeti tesaṃ ambavane sippaṃ uggaṇhatthāya kato dīghapāsādo atthi, tattha viharati. Adhunā kālaṅkatoti sampati kālaṅkato. Dvedhikajātāti dvejjhajātā, dvebhāgā jātā. Bhaṇḍanādīsu bhaṇḍanaṃ pubbabhāgakalaho, taṃ daṇḍādānādivasena paṇṇattivītikkamavasena ca vaḍḍhitaṃ kalaho. ‘‘Na tvaṃ imaṃ dhammavinayaṃ ājānāsī’’tiādinā nayena viruddhavacanaṃ vivādo. Vitudantāti vijjhantā. Sahitaṃ meti mama vacanaṃ atthasañhitaṃ. Adhiciṇṇaṃ te viparāvattanti yaṃ tava adhiciṇṇaṃ cirakālāsevanavasena paguṇaṃ, taṃ mama vādaṃ āgamma nivattaṃ. Āropito te vādoti tuyhaṃ upari mayā doso āropito. Cara vādappamokkhāyāti bhattapuṭaṃ ādāya taṃ taṃ upasaṅkamitvā vādappamokkhatthāya uttari pariyesamāno vicara. Nibbeṭhehi vāti atha vā mayā āropitadosato attānaṃ mocehi. Sace pahosīti sace sakkosi. Vadhoyevāti maraṇameva. Nāṭaputtiyesūti nāṭaputtassa antevāsikesu. Nibbinnarūpāti ukkaṇṭhitasabhāvā abhivādanādīnipi na karonti. Virattarūpāti vigatapemā. Paṭivānarūpāti tesaṃ sakkaccakiriyato nivattanasabhāvā. Yathā tanti yathā durakkhātādisabhāve dhammavinaye nibbinnavirattappaṭivānarūpehi bhavitabbaṃ, tatheva jātāti attho. Durakkhāteti dukkathite. Duppavediteti duviññāpite. Anupasamasaṃvattaniketi rāgādīnaṃ upasamaṃ kātuṃ asamatthe. Bhinnathūpeti bhindappatiṭṭhe. Ettha hi nāṭaputtova nesaṃ patiṭṭhaṭṭhena thūpo. So pana bhinno mato. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘bhinnathūpe’’ti. Appaṭisaraṇeti tasseva abhāvena paṭisaraṇavirahite.

Nanu cāyaṃ nāṭaputto nāḷandavāsiko, so kasmā pāvāyaṃ kālaṅkatoti? So kira upālinā gahapatinā paṭividdhasaccena dasahi gāthāhi bhāsite buddhaguṇe sutvā uṇhaṃ lohitaṃ chaḍḍesi. Atha naṃ aphāsukaṃ gahetvā pāvaṃ agamaṃsu. So tattha kālamakāsi. Kālaṃ kurumāno ca cintesi – ‘‘mama laddhi aniyyānikā sāravirahitā, mayaṃ tāva naṭṭhā, avasesajanopi mā apāyapūrako ahosi, sace panāhaṃ ‘mama sāsanaṃ aniyyānika’nti vakkhāmi, na saddahissanti, yaṃnūnāhaṃ dvepi jane na ekanīhārena uggaṇhāpeyyaṃ, te mamaccayena aññamaññaṃ vivadissanti, satthā taṃ vivādaṃ paṭicca ekaṃ dhammakathaṃ kathessati, tato te sāsanassa mahantabhāvaṃ jānissantī’’ti.

Atha naṃ eko antevāsiko upasaṅkamitvā āha – ‘‘bhante tumhe dubbalā, mayhampi imasmiṃ dhamme sāraṃ ācikkhatha, ācariyappamāṇa’’nti. ‘‘Āvuso, tvaṃ mamaccayena sassatanti gaṇheyyāsī’’ti. Aparopi upasaṅkami, taṃ ucchedaṃ gaṇhāpesi. Evaṃ dvepi jane ekaladdhike akatvā bahū nānānīhārena uggaṇhāpetvā kālamakāsi. Te tassa sarīrakiccaṃ katvā sannipatitvā aññamaññaṃ pucchiṃsu – ‘‘kassāvuso, ācariyo sāraṃ ācikkhī’’ti? Eko uṭṭhahitvā mayhanti āha. Kiṃ ācikkhīti? Sassatanti. Aparo taṃ paṭibāhitvā ‘‘mayhaṃ sāraṃ ācikkhī’’ti āha. Evaṃ sabbe ‘‘mayhaṃ sāraṃ ācikkhi, ahaṃ jeṭṭhako’’ti aññamaññaṃ vivādaṃ vaḍḍhetvā akkose ceva paribhāse ca hatthapādappahārādīni ca pavattetvā ekamaggena dve agacchantā nānādisāsu pakkamiṃsu.
commentary_english:
164. It was heard by me thus: the *Pāsādikasutta*. Herein, the explanation of the terms that are not obvious: *vedhaññā nāma sakyā* means the Śākyas called *Vedhañña* who have practiced archery. *tesaṃ ambavane pāsāde* means that in their mango grove there is a long palace built for learning crafts, there [they] live. *adhunā kālaṅkato* means now he has died. *dvedhikajātā* means those born of two branches, those born of two parts. *bhaṇḍanādīsu* quarreling is the preliminary stage of strife; when that is increased by means of punishment, seizure, transgression of the precepts and so forth, [it is called] *kalaho*, strife. "You do not understand this Dharma-vinaya" and so forth; speech that is contradictory in such a way is *vivādo*, dispute. *vitudantā* means piercing. *sahitaṃ me* means my speech is connected with meaning (*attha*). *adhiciṇṇaṃ te viparāvatta* means that which is habitually done by you, [that which] is familiar through continuous practice over a long time, that, having come to my *vāda*, doctrine, has ceased. *āropito te vādo* means a fault has been imputed by me onto you. *cara vādappamokkhāyā* means having taken a bowl of food, wandering about seeking further means for release from the *vāda*, doctrine, approach them. *nibbeṭhehi vā* means or else free yourself from the fault imputed by me. *sace pahosī* means if you are able. *vadhoyevā* means it is just death. *nāṭaputtiyesū* means among the disciples of *Nāṭaputta*. *nibbinnarūpā* means because of [their] disgusted nature, they do not do even salutations and so forth. *virattarūpā* means devoid of affection. *paṭivānarūpā* means because of the nature of turning away from their respectful actions. *yathā ta* means just as, in a Dharma-vinaya that is badly proclaimed and so forth, one must be of a disgusted, detached, and averse nature; the meaning is that they are just like that. *durakkhāte* means badly spoken. *duppavedite* means badly explained. *anupasamasaṃvattanike* means unable to calm the passions and so forth. *bhinnathūpe* means with a broken stupa. Here, *Nāṭaputta* himself is their stupa in the sense of being a foundation. But he is thought of as broken. Therefore it was said, "with a broken stupa." *appaṭisaraṇe* means without a refuge because of the absence of that very thing. Now, why did this *Nāṭaputta*, a resident of Nāḷanda, die in Pāvā? It is said that Upāli, having heard the Buddha's virtues spoken in ten verses expressing the truth discerned by the householder, vomited hot blood. Then, having taken him away as he was unwell, they went to Pāvā. There he died. While dying, he thought: "My doctrine is not one that leads out [of suffering], it is devoid of essence. We, indeed, are destroyed. May others not be filled with misfortune. But if I say, 'My teaching does not lead out [of suffering],' they will not believe it. I will have two people learn [it] in a way that is not unified. They will dispute with each other at my passing away. The Teacher, having relied upon that dispute, will speak a discourse on the Dharma. Then they will know the greatness of the teaching." 0081"/>

Then, a certain pupil, approaching, said, "Bhante, you are weak, please explain to me the essence of this Dharma, according to the teacher's measure." "Āvuso, you should grasp it as eternal through my instruction." Another approached, he made him grasp annihilation. Thus, without making even two people attain a single gain, having made many grasp with various devices, he made an end of his time. They, having performed his bodily duties, gathered together and asked one another, "To whom, āvuso, did the teacher explain the essence?" One, rising up, said, "To me." What did he explain? The eternal. Another, rejecting him, said, "He explained the essence to me." Thus, all, saying, "He explained the essence to me, I am the eldest," having increased the dispute with insults and abuse, and blows with hands and feet, etc., and having set it in motion, not going by one way, the two departed in various directions.

mula_pali:
165. Atha kho cundo samaṇuddeso pāvāyaṃ vassaṃvuṭṭho vassaṃvuttho (sī. syā. pī.) yena sāmagāmo, yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho cundo samaṇuddeso āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘nigaṇṭho, bhante, nāṭaputto pāvāyaṃ adhunākālaṅkato. Tassa kālaṅkiriyāya bhinnā nigaṇṭhā dvedhikajātā…pe… bhinnathūpe appaṭisaraṇe’’ti.

Evaṃ vutte, āyasmā ānando cundaṃ samaṇuddesaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘atthi kho idaṃ, āvuso cunda, kathāpābhataṃ bhagavantaṃ dassanāya. Āyāmāvuso cunda, yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamissāma; upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṃ bhagavato ārocessāmā’’ti āroceyyāmāti (syā.). ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho cundo samaṇuddeso āyasmato ānandassa paccassosi.

āroceyyāmāti (syā.)

Atha kho āyasmā ca ānando cundo ca samaṇuddeso yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘ayaṃ, bhante, cundo samaṇuddeso evamāha, ‘nigaṇṭho, bhante, nāṭaputto pāvāyaṃ adhunākālaṅkato, tassa kālaṅkiriyāya bhinnā nigaṇṭhā…pe… bhinnathūpe appaṭisaraṇe’’’ti.

Asammāsambuddhappaveditadhammavinayo
mula_english:
Then, the novice Cunda, who had spent the rainy season at Pāvā, went to Sāmagāma, to the venerable Ānanda; having approached the venerable Ānanda, he paid homage and sat down at one side.

Seated at one side, the novice Cunda said this to the venerable Ānanda: "Bhante, Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta has just died in Pāvā. Due to his death, the Nigaṇṭhas are divided, split into two…and [the community] is now with its stupa broken, left without a refuge."

When this was said, the venerable Ānanda said to the novice Cunda: "Friend Cunda, there is cause here for relating this matter to the Blessed One. Come, friend Cunda, let's approach the Blessed One and inform him of this matter."

"Yes, venerable sir," the novice Cunda replied to the venerable Ānanda.

Then, the venerable Ānanda and the novice Cunda approached the Blessed One; having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down at one side.

Seated at one side, the venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One: "This, bhante, is what the novice Cunda said: 'Bhante, Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta has just died in Pāvā. Due to his death, the Nigaṇṭhas are divided...and [the community] is now with its *stūpa* broken, left without a refuge.'"

The *Dhamma-Vinaya* proclaimed by the Unenlightened Buddha.
commentary_pali:
165.Atha kho cundo samaṇuddesoti ayaṃ thero dhammasenāpatissa kaniṭṭhabhātiko. Taṃ bhikkhū anupasampannakāle ‘‘cundo samaṇuddeso’’ti samudācaritvā therakālepi tatheva samudācariṃsu. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘cundo samaṇuddeso’’ti.

‘‘Pāvāyaṃ vassaṃvuṭṭho yena sāmagāmo, yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkamī’’ti kasmā upasaṅkami? Nāṭaputte kira kālaṅkate jambudīpe manussā tattha tattha kathaṃ pavattayiṃsu ‘‘nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto eko satthāti paññāyittha, tassa kālaṅkiriyāya sāvakānaṃ evarūpo vivādo jāto. Samaṇo pana gotamo jambudīpe cando viya sūriyo viya ca pākaṭo, sāvakāpissa pākaṭāyeva. Kīdiso nu kho samaṇe gotame parinibbute sāvakānaṃ vivādo bhavissatī’’ti . Thero taṃ kathaṃ sutvā cintesi – ‘‘imaṃ kathaṃ gahetvā dasabalassa ārocessāmi, satthā etaṃ aṭṭhuppattiṃ katvā ekaṃ desanaṃ kathessatī’’ti. So nikkhamitvā yena sāmagāmo, yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami.

Sāmagāmoti sāmākānaṃ ussannattā tassa gāmassa nāmaṃ. Yenāyasmā ānandoti ujumeva bhagavato santikaṃ agantvā yenassa upajjhāyo āyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami.

Sāmagāmo Yenāyasmā ānando

Buddhakāle kira sāriputtatthero ca ānandatthero ca aññamaññaṃ mamāyiṃsu. Sāriputtatthero ‘‘mayā kātabbaṃ satthu upaṭṭhānaṃ karotī’’ti ānandattheraṃ mamāyi. Ānandatthero ‘‘bhagavato sāvakānaṃ aggo’’ti sāriputtattheraṃ mamāyi. Kuladārake ca pabbājetvā sāriputtattherassa santike upajjhaṃ gaṇhāpesi. Sāriputtattheropi tatheva akāsi. Evaṃ ekamekena attano pattacīvaraṃ datvā pabbājetvā upajjhaṃ gaṇhāpitāni pañca pañca bhikkhusatāni ahesuṃ. Āyasmā ānando paṇītāni cīvarādīnipi labhitvā therassa adāsi.

Dhammaratanapūjā

Eko kira brāhmaṇo cintesi – ‘‘buddharatanassa ca saṅgharatanassa ca pūjā paññāyati, kathaṃ nu kho dhammaratanaṃ pūjitaṃ hotī’’ti? So bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṃ pucchi. Bhagavā āha – ‘‘sacepi brāhmaṇa dhammaratanaṃ pūjetukāmo, ekaṃ bahussutaṃ pūjehī’’ti. Bahussutaṃ, bhante, ācikkhathāti. Bhikkhusaṅghaṃ pucchāti. So bhikkhusaṅghaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ‘‘bahussutaṃ, bhante, ācikkhathā’’ti āha. Ānandatthero brāhmaṇāti. Brāhmaṇo theraṃ sahassagghanikena ticīvarena pūjesi. Thero taṃ gahetvā bhagavato santikaṃ agamāsi. Bhagavā ‘‘kuto, ānanda, laddha’’nti āha? Ekena, bhante, brāhmaṇena dinnaṃ, idaṃ panāhaṃ āyasmato sāriputtassa dātukāmoti. Dehi, ānandāti. Cārikaṃ pakkanto bhanteti. Āgatakāle dehīti, sikkhāpadaṃ bhante, paññattanti. Kadā pana sāriputto āgamissatīti? Dasāhamattena bhanteti. ‘‘Anujānāmi, ānanda, dasāhaparamaṃ atirekacīvaraṃ nikkhipitu’’nti sikkhāpadaṃ paññāpesi.

Sāriputtattheropi tatheva yaṃkiñci manāpaṃ labhati, taṃ ānandattherassa deti. So imampi attano kaniṭṭhabhātikaṃ therasseva saddhivihārikaṃ adāsi. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘yenassa upajjhāyo āyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkamī’’ti. Evaṃ kirassa ahosi – ‘‘upajjhāyo me mahāpañño, so imaṃ kathaṃ satthu ārocessati, atha satthā tadanurūpaṃ dhammaṃ desessatī’’ti. Kathāpābhatanti kathāya mūlaṃ. Mūlañhi ‘‘pābhata’’nti vuccati. Yathāha –

Kathāpābhata

‘‘Appakenāpi medhāvī, pābhatena vicakkhaṇo;

Samuṭṭhāpeti attānaṃ, aṇuṃ aggiṃva sandhama’’nti. (jā. 1.1.4);

Bhagavantaṃ dassanāyāti bhagavantaṃ dassanatthāya. Kiṃ panānena bhagavā na diṭṭhapubboti? No na diṭṭhapubbo. Ayañhi āyasmā divā nava vāre, rattiṃ nava vāreti ekāhaṃ aṭṭhārasa vāre upaṭṭhānameva gacchati. Divasassa pana satavāraṃ vā sahassavāraṃ vā gantukāmo samānopi na akāraṇā gacchati, ekaṃ pañhuddhāraṃ gahetvāva gacchati. So taṃ divasaṃ tena kathāpābhatena gantukāmo evamāha.

Bhagavantaṃ dassanāyā

Asammāsambuddhappaveditadhammavinayavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
165. Now then, the elder Cunda the novice, was the younger brother of the general of the Dharma. The monks addressed him as "Cunda the novice" even after he had reached elderhood, just as they had addressed him when he had not yet received the higher ordination. Therefore it was said: "Cunda the novice."

"Having spent the rainy season at Pāvā, he went to Sāmagāma, to the venerable Ānanda." Why did he go? It is said that after the death of Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta, in Jambudīpa, people were saying here and there, "Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta was a single teacher," but with his death, such a dispute arose among his disciples. But the Śramaṇa Gotama is manifest in Jambudīpa like the moon and the sun, and his disciples are also manifest. What kind of dispute will arise among the disciples when the Śramaṇa Gotama has attained complete nirvāṇa?"

The elder, having heard that story, thought, "Having taken this story, I will announce it to the Ten-Powered One. The Teacher, having made this the origin of something, will deliver a discourse." Having gone forth, he went to Sāmagāma, to the venerable Ānanda.

Sāmagāma: The name of that village is because of the abundance of Sāmāka plants.

"To the venerable Ānanda": Not having gone directly to the Blessed One, he went to the venerable Ānanda, who was his preceptor.

Sāmagāma

To the venerable Ānanda: It is said that during the time of the Buddha, the elder Śāriputta and the elder Ānanda cherished each other. The elder Śāriputta cherished the elder Ānanda, thinking, "He is doing the service of the Teacher, which should be done by me." The elder Ānanda cherished the elder Śāriputta, thinking, "He is the foremost of the Blessed One's disciples." Having ordained boys from good families, he had them take the precepts in the presence of the elder Śāriputta. The elder Śāriputta also did likewise. Thus, having given their own bowl and robe, having ordained them, and having had them take the precepts, there were five hundred monks. The venerable Ānanda, having obtained excellent robes and other things, gave them to the elder.

Dharma Jewel Worship

It is said that a certain Brahmin thought: "The worship of the Buddha Jewel and the Saṃgha Jewel is known, but how is the Dharma Jewel worshiped?" He went to the Blessed One and asked about this matter. The Blessed One said, "If, O Brahmin, you wish to worship the Dharma Jewel, worship a learned person."

"A learned person, venerable sir, declare [to me]."

"Ask the Saṃgha of monks."

He went to the Saṃgha of monks and said, "Declare to me a learned person, venerable sirs."

"The elder Ānanda is a Brahmin."

The Brahmin worshiped the elder with a set of three robes worth a thousand [coins].

The elder, having taken it, went to the presence of the Blessed One.

The Blessed One said, "From where, Ānanda, was [this] obtained?"

"It was given by a Brahmin, venerable sir. But I intend to give this to the venerable Śāriputta."

"Give [it to him], Ānanda."

"He has gone forth on a journey, venerable sir."

"[Give it to him] at the time he returns."

"Is the precept, venerable sir, ordained?"

"When will Śāriputta return?"

"In ten days, venerable sir."

"I allow, Ānanda, [one] to keep an extra robe for a maximum of ten days." Thus, he ordained the precept.

The elder Śāriputta also, whatever is pleasing he obtains, that he gives to the elder Ānanda.
So he gave even his younger brother as a co-resident to the Elder.
Therefore, it was said: "He approached Ānanda, the venerable one, his preceptor."
Thus it occurred to him: "My preceptor is very wise; he will announce this matter to the Teacher. Then the Teacher will teach the Dharma in accordance with that."
*Kathāpābhata* means the root of the story.
Indeed, the root is called "*pābhata*."
As he said:

*Kathāpābhata*:
"Even with a little, the wise, discerning one through *pābhata*;
raises himself up, like a small fire that is fanned."
(Jā. 1.1.4);

*Bhagavantaṃ dassanāyā* means for the purpose of seeing the Blessed One.
Has the Blessed One not been seen by him before? No, he has not been seen before.
Indeed, this venerable one goes to attendance nine times during the day, nine times during the night, thus eighteen times in one day.
But even though he is one who desires to go a hundred or a thousand times a day, he does not go without a reason; he goes only after taking up a question.
So, desiring to go that day with that *kathāpābhata*, he spoke thus.

*Bhagavantaṃ dassanāyā*: Explanation of the Dharma and the Vinaya proclaimed by the Perfectly Awakened Buddha.

mula_pali: 166. ‘‘Evaṃ hetaṃ, cunda, hoti durakkhāte dhammavinaye duppavedite aniyyānike anupasamasaṃvattanike asammāsambuddhappavedite. Idha, cunda, satthā ca hoti asammāsambuddho, dhammo ca durakkhāto duppavedito aniyyāniko anupasamasaṃvattaniko asammāsambuddhappavedito, sāvako ca tasmiṃ dhamme na dhammānudhammappaṭipanno viharati na sāmīcippaṭipanno na anudhammacārī, vokkamma ca tamhā dhammā vattati. So evamassa vacanīyo – ‘tassa te, āvuso, lābhā, tassa te suladdhaṃ, satthā ca te asammāsambuddho, dhammo ca durakkhāto duppavedito aniyyāniko anupasamasaṃvattaniko asammāsambuddhappavedito. Tvañca tasmiṃ dhamme na dhammānudhammappaṭipanno viharasi, na sāmīcippaṭipanno, na anudhammacārī, vokkamma ca tamhā dhammā vattasī’ti. Iti kho, cunda, satthāpi tattha gārayho, dhammopi tattha gārayho, sāvako ca tattha evaṃ pāsaṃso. Yo kho, cunda, evarūpaṃ sāvakaṃ evaṃ vadeyya – ‘etāyasmā tathā paṭipajjatu, yathā te satthārā dhammo desito paññatto’ti. Yo ca samādapeti samādāpeti (sī. ṭṭha.), yañca samādapeti, yo ca samādapito samādāpito (sī. ṭṭha.) tathattāya paṭipajjati. Sabbe te bahuṃ apuññaṃ pasavanti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Evaṃ hetaṃ, cunda, hoti durakkhāte dhammavinaye duppavedite aniyyānike anupasamasaṃvattanike asammāsambuddhappavedite.
mula_english:
166. Thus it is, Cunda, when the *dharma-vinaya* is poorly proclaimed, poorly expounded, not leading out, not conducive to calming, expounded by one who is not rightly self-awakened (*asammāsambuddha*).

Here, Cunda, the teacher (*satthā*) is not rightly self-awakened (*asammāsambuddho*), and his *dharma* is poorly proclaimed, poorly expounded, not leading out, not conducive to calming, expounded by one who is not rightly self-awakened (*asammāsambuddha*). A disciple (*sāvako*) of that *dharma* does not dwell practicing the *dharma* in accordance with that *dharma* (*dhammānudhammappaṭipanno*), practicing masterfully (*sāmīcippaṭipanno*), living in line with the *dharma* (*anudhammacārī*), but deviates from it.

He is to be told, ‘It is a gain for you, friend (*āvus°, vocative of āyusmat*), well-gained by you, that—when your teacher (*satthā*) is not rightly self-awakened (*asammāsambuddho*), and his *dharma* is poorly proclaimed, poorly expounded, not leading out, not conducive to calming, expounded by one who is not rightly self-awakened (*asammāsambuddha*)—you are one who does not dwell practicing the *dharma* in accordance with the *dharma* (*dhammānudhammappaṭipanno*), practicing masterfully (*sāmīcippaṭipanno*), living in line with the *dharma* (*anudhammacārī*), but deviates from it.’

There, Cunda, the teacher is to be criticized (*gārayho*), the *dharma* is to be criticized (*gārayho*), but the disciple (*sāvako*) is to be thus praised (*pāsaṃso*).

“Whoever might say to such a disciple (*sāvakaṃ*), ‘Come, friend, practice in line with the *dharma* as taught and formulated by your teacher (*satthārā*’):

He who encourages, and he who is encouraged, and he who, being encouraged, practices for the sake of suchness (*tathattāya paṭipajjati*), all would produce much demerit (*apuññaṃ*).

Why is that? That’s the way it is, Cunda, with a poorly proclaimed *dharma-vinaya*, poorly expounded, not leading out, not conducive to calming, expounded by one who is not rightly self-awakened (*asammāsambuddha*).
commentary_pali:
166.Evañhetaṃ, cunda, hotīti bhagavā ānandattherena ārocitepi yasmā na ānandatthero imissā kathāya sāmiko, cundatthero pana sāmiko. Sova tassā ādimajjhapariyosānaṃ jānāti. Tasmā bhagavā tena saddhiṃ kathento ‘‘evañhetaṃ, cunda, hotī’’tiādimāha . Tassattho – cunda evañhetaṃ hoti durakkhātādisabhāve dhammavinaye sāvakā dvedhikajātā bhaṇḍanādīni katvā mukhasattīhi vitudantā viharanti.

Idāni yasmā aniyyānikasāsaneneva niyyānikasāsanaṃ pākaṭaṃ hoti, tasmā ādito aniyyānikasāsanameva dassento idha cunda satthā ca hoti asammāsambuddhotiādimāha. Tattha vokkamma ca tamhā dhammā vattatīti na nirantaraṃ pūreti, okkamitvā okkamitvā antarantaraṃ katvā vattatīti attho. Tassa te, āvuso, lābhāti tassa tuyhaṃ ete dhammānudhammappaṭipattiādayo lābhā. Suladdhanti manussattampi te suladdhaṃ. Tathā paṭipajjatūti evaṃ paṭipajjatu. Yathā te satthārā dhammo desitoti yena te ākārena satthārā dhammo kathito. Yo ca samādapetīti yo ca ācariyo samādapeti. Yañca samādapetīti yaṃ antevāsiṃ samādapeti. Yo ca samādapitoti yo ca evaṃ samādapito antevāsiko. Yathā ācariyena samādapitaṃ, tathatthāya paṭipajjati. Sabbe teti tayopi te. Ettha hi ācariyo samādapitattā apuññaṃ pasavati, samādinnantevāsiko samādinnattā, paṭipannako paṭipannattā. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘sabbe te bahuṃ apuññaṃ pasavantī’’ti. Etenupāyena sabbavāresu attho veditabbo.

idha cunda satthā ca hoti asammāsambuddho vokkamma ca tamhā dhammā vattatī Tassa te, āvuso, lābhā Suladdha Tathā paṭipajjatū Yathā te satthārā dhammo desito Yo ca samādapetī Yañca samādapetī Yo ca samādapito Sabbe te
commentary_english:
166. "It is indeed so, Cunda," though the Blessed One was informed by the Venerable Ānanda, the Venerable Ānanda was not the master of this statement, but the Venerable Cunda was the master.
He knows the beginning, middle, and end of it.
Therefore, the Blessed One, while conversing with him, said, "It is indeed so, Cunda," and so on.
The meaning of that is: Cunda, it is indeed so that in a Dhamma-Vinaya where the teachings are poorly expounded, disciples, divided, quarrelsome, and so on, live piercing each other with weapons of the mouth.

Now, since the teaching that leads out becomes clear only through the teaching that does not lead out, therefore, showing first only the teaching that does not lead out, he said, "Here, Cunda, the teacher is not a fully awakened Buddha," and so on.
There, "He turns away from that teaching," means he does not fulfill it uninterruptedly; having stepped aside, having stepped aside, doing it intermittently, he turns, is the meaning.
"Yours are the gains, friend," means these gains of following the Dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma, and so on, are yours.
"Well-gained" means even human existence is well-gained by you.
"Thus, he should practice," means he should practice thus.
"As the Dhamma was taught by your teacher," means the manner in which the Dhamma was spoken by the teacher to you.
"He encourages," means the teacher encourages.
"Whatever he encourages," means he encourages the resident student.
"He who is encouraged," means the resident student who is thus encouraged.
As it was encouraged by the teacher, he practices for that purpose.
"All of them" means those three too.
Here, the teacher, because of encouraging, generates demerit; the resident student who has undertaken, because of having undertaken; the one who practices, because of practicing.
Therefore, it was said: "All of them generate much demerit."
By this method, the meaning should be understood in all instances.

Here, Cunda, the teacher is not a fully awakened Buddha. He turns away from that teaching. Yours are the gains, friend. Well-gained. Thus, he should practice. As the Dhamma was taught by your teacher. He encourages. Whatever he encourages. He who is encouraged. All of them.

mula_pali:
167. ‘‘Idha pana, cunda, satthā ca hoti asammāsambuddho, dhammo ca durakkhāto duppavedito aniyyāniko anupasamasaṃvattaniko asammāsambuddhappavedito, sāvako ca tasmiṃ dhamme dhammānudhammappaṭipanno viharati sāmīcippaṭipanno anudhammacārī, samādāya taṃ dhammaṃ vattati. So evamassa vacanīyo – ‘tassa te, āvuso, alābhā, tassa te dulladdhaṃ, satthā ca te asammāsambuddho , dhammo ca durakkhāto duppavedito aniyyāniko anupasamasaṃvattaniko asammāsambuddhappavedito. Tvañca tasmiṃ dhamme dhammānudhammappaṭipanno viharasi sāmīcippaṭipanno anudhammacārī, samādāya taṃ dhammaṃ vattasī’ti. Iti kho, cunda, satthāpi tattha gārayho, dhammopi tattha gārayho, sāvakopi tattha evaṃ gārayho. Yo kho, cunda, evarūpaṃ sāvakaṃ evaṃ vadeyya – ‘addhāyasmā ñāyappaṭipanno ñāyamārādhessatī’ti. Yo ca pasaṃsati, yañca pasaṃsati, yo ca pasaṃsito bhiyyoso mattāya vīriyaṃ ārabhati. Sabbe te bahuṃ apuññaṃ pasavanti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Evañhetaṃ, cunda, hoti durakkhāte dhammavinaye duppavedite aniyyānike anupasamasaṃvattanike asammāsambuddhappavedite.

Sammāsambuddhappaveditadhammavinayo
mula_english:
“Here, Cunda, a teacher is not a rightly self-awakened one (*asammāsambuddho*), and his *Dhamma-Vinaya* is poorly proclaimed (*durakkhāto*), poorly expounded (*duppavedito*), not leading out (*aniyyāniko*), not conducive to calming (*anupasamasaṃvattaniko*), expounded by one who is not rightly self-awakened (*asammāsambuddhappavedito*). A disciple of that *Dhamma* dwells practicing the *Dhamma* in accordance with the *Dhamma* (*dhammānudhammappaṭipanno*), practicing masterfully (*sāmīcippaṭipanno*), living in line with the *Dhamma* (*anudhammacārī*), and acts to conform to it.

He is to be told, ‘It is no gain for you, friend (*āvuso*), poorly-gained by you, that—when your teacher is not rightly self-awakened (*asammāsambuddho*), and his *Dhamma* is poorly proclaimed (*durakkhāto*), poorly expounded (*duppavedito*), not leading out (*aniyyāniko*), not conducive to calming (*anupasamasaṃvattaniko*), expounded by one who is not rightly self-awakened (*asammāsambuddhappavedito*)—you are one who dwells practicing the *Dhamma* in accordance with that *Dhamma* (*dhammānudhammappaṭipanno*), practicing masterfully (*sāmīcippaṭipanno*), living in line with that *Dhamma* (*anudhammacārī*), and acts to conform to it.’

There, Cunda, the teacher is to be criticized (*gārayho*), the *Dhamma* is to be criticized (*gārayho*), and the disciple is to be thus criticized (*gārayho*).

“Whoever might say to such a disciple, ‘Yes, friend, practicing the right way (*ñāyappaṭipanno*), you will succeed in the right way (*ñāyamārādhessati*)’:

The person who praised him, the thing praised, and the person who, being praised, aroused even greater persistence (*vīriyaṃ ārabhati*), would all produce much demerit (*apuññaṃ pasavanti*).

What is the reason for that (*taṃ kissa hetu*)? Because that is how it is when the *Dhamma-Vinaya* is badly proclaimed (*durakkhāte*), badly expounded (*duppavedite*), unemancipating (*aniyyānike*), unconducive to peace (*anupasamasaṃvattanike*), expounded by one who is not fully enlightened (*asammāsambuddhappavedite*).

The Dhamma-Vinaya Expounded by a Rightly Self-Awakened One (*sammāsambuddhappaveditadhammavinayo*)
commentary_pali:
167. Apicettha ñāyappaṭipannoti kāraṇappaṭipanno. Ñāyamārādhessatīti kāraṇaṃ nipphādessati. Vīriyaṃ ārabhatīti attano dukkhanibbattakaṃ vīriyaṃ karoti. Vuttañhetaṃ ‘‘durakkhāte, bhikkhave, dhammavinaye yo āraddhavīriyo, so dukkhaṃ viharati. Yo kusīto, so sukhaṃ viharatī’’ti (a. ni. 1.318).

Sammāsambuddhappaveditadhammavinayādivaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
Moreover, *ñāyappaṭipanno* means one who is engaged in the cause.

*ñāyamārādhessati* means he will bring about the cause.

*vīriyaṃ ārabhati* means he exerts effort that is the producer of his own suffering.

And this was said: "In the Dharma-Vinaya that is badly proclaimed, monks, one who has aroused energy dwells in suffering.

One who is lazy dwells in happiness" (A.
Ni.
1.
318).

Explanation of the Dharma-Vinaya, etc., proclaimed by the truly awakened Buddha.

mula_pali: 168. ‘‘Idha pana, cunda, satthā ca hoti sammāsambuddho, dhammo ca svākkhāto suppavedito niyyāniko upasamasaṃvattaniko sammāsambuddhappavedito, sāvako ca tasmiṃ dhamme na dhammānudhammappaṭipanno viharati, na sāmīcippaṭipanno, na anudhammacārī, vokkamma ca tamhā dhammā vattati. So evamassa vacanīyo – ‘tassa te, āvuso, alābhā, tassa te dulladdhaṃ, satthā ca te sammāsambuddho, dhammo ca svākkhāto suppavedito niyyāniko upasamasaṃvattaniko sammāsambuddhappavedito. Tvañca tasmiṃ dhamme na dhammānudhammappaṭipanno viharasi, na sāmīcippaṭipanno, na anudhammacārī, vokkamma ca tamhā dhammā vattasī’ti. Iti kho, cunda, satthāpi tattha pāsaṃso, dhammopi tattha pāsaṃso, sāvako ca tattha evaṃ gārayho. Yo kho, cunda, evarūpaṃ sāvakaṃ evaṃ vadeyya – ‘etāyasmā tathā paṭipajjatu yathā te satthārā dhammo desito paññatto’ti. Yo ca samādapeti, yañca samādapeti, yo ca samādapito tathattāya paṭipajjati. Sabbe te bahuṃ puññaṃ pasavanti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Evañhetaṃ , cunda, hoti svākkhāte dhammavinaye suppavedite niyyānike upasamasaṃvattanike sammāsambuddhappavedite.
mula_english:
168. Furthermore, Cunda, there is the case where a teacher is a rightly self-awakened *sammāsambuddho*, and the *dharma* is well-proclaimed (*svākkhāto*), well-expounded (*suppavedito*), leading out (*niyyāniko*), conducive to calming (*upasamasaṃvattaniko*), expounded by one who is rightly self-awakened (*sammāsambuddhappavedito*). And a disciple in that *dharma* does not dwell practicing the *dharma* in accordance with the *dharma* (*dhammānudhammappaṭipanno*), practicing masterfully (*sāmīcippaṭipanno*), living in line with the *dharma* (*anudhammacārī*), but deviates (*vokkamma*) from that *dharma*.

He is to be told: ‘It is no gain for you, friend (*āvuso*), poorly-gained by you, that—when your teacher is rightly self-awakened *sammāsambuddho*, and the *dharma* is well-proclaimed (*svākkhāto*), well-expounded (*suppavedito*), leading out (*niyyāniko*), conducive to calming (*upasamasaṃvattaniko*), expounded by one who is rightly self-awakened (*sammāsambuddhappavedito*)—

you are one who does not dwell practicing the *dharma* in accordance with the *dharma* (*dhammānudhammappaṭipanno*), practicing masterfully (*sāmīcippaṭipanno*), living in line with the *dharma* (*anudhammacārī*), but deviates (*vokkamma*) from it.’

There, Cunda, the teacher is to be praised (*pāsaṃso*), the *dharma* is to be praised (*pāsaṃso*), but the disciple is to be thus criticized (*gārayho*).

Whoever might say to such a disciple, ‘Come, friend (*etāyasmā*), practice in line with the *dharma* as taught and formulated (*paññatto*) by your teacher’:

The person who urged, the thing urged, and the person who practiced in line with what was urged (*tathattāya paṭipajjati*)

would all produce much merit (*bahuṃ puññaṃ pasavanti*).

What is the reason for that (*taṃ kissa hetu*)? Because that is how it is, Cunda, when the *dharma-vinaya* is well-proclaimed (*svākkhāte*), well-expounded (*suppavedite*), emancipating (*niyyānike*), conducive to peace (*upasamasaṃvattanike*), expounded by one who is fully enlightened (*sammāsambuddhappavedite*).
commentary_pali: 168. Evaṃ aniyyānikasāsanaṃ dassetvā idāni niyyānikasāsanaṃ dassento idha pana, cunda, satthā ca hoti sammāsambuddhotiādimāha. Tattha niyyānikoti maggatthāya phalatthāya ca niyyāti.
commentary_english:
Thus, having shown the teaching that does not lead out [of *saṃsāra*], now, showing the teaching that leads out, he says, "<hi rend="bold">Here, Cunda, the Teacher is a fully awakened Buddha</hi>," etc.

There, <hi rend="bold">leading out</hi> means leading out for the sake of the path (*mārga*) and for the sake of the fruit (*phala*).

mula_pali:
169. ‘‘Idha pana, cunda, satthā ca hoti sammāsambuddho, dhammo ca svākkhāto suppavedito niyyāniko upasamasaṃvattaniko sammāsambuddhappavedito, sāvako ca tasmiṃ dhamme dhammānudhammappaṭipanno viharati sāmīcippaṭipanno anudhammacārī, samādāya taṃ dhammaṃ vattati. So evamassa vacanīyo – ‘tassa te, āvuso, lābhā, tassa te suladdhaṃ, satthā ca te satthā ca te arahaṃ (syā.) sammāsambuddho , dhammo ca svākkhāto suppavedito niyyāniko upasamasaṃvattaniko sammāsambuddhappavedito. Tvañca tasmiṃ dhamme dhammānudhammappaṭipanno viharasi sāmīcippaṭipanno anudhammacārī, samādāya taṃ dhammaṃ vattasī’ti. Iti kho, cunda, satthāpi tattha pāsaṃso, dhammopi tattha pāsaṃso, sāvakopi tattha evaṃ pāsaṃso. Yo kho, cunda, evarūpaṃ sāvakaṃ evaṃ vadeyya – ‘addhāyasmā ñāyappaṭipanno ñāyamārādhessatī’ti. Yo ca pasaṃsati, yañca pasaṃsati, yo ca pasaṃsito pasattho (syā.) bhiyyoso mattāya vīriyaṃ ārabhati. Sabbe te bahuṃ puññaṃ pasavanti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Evañhetaṃ, cunda, hoti svākkhāte dhammavinaye suppavedite niyyānike upasamasaṃvattanike sammāsambuddhappavedite.

Sāvakānutappasatthu
mula_english:
169. “Here, Cunda, a teacher is rightly self-awakened (sammāsambuddho), and his *dharma* (dhamma), is well-proclaimed (svākkhāto), well-expounded (suppavedito), leading out (niyyāniko), conducive to calming (upasamasaṃvattaniko), expounded by one who is rightly self-awakened (sammāsambuddhappavedito). A disciple (sāvako) of that *dharma* (dhamme) dwells practicing the *dharma* in accordance with the *dharma* (dhammānudhammappaṭipanno), practicing masterfully (sāmīcippaṭipanno), living in line with the *dharma* (anudhammacārī), and acts to conform to it (samādāya taṃ dhammaṃ vattati).

He is to be told, ‘It is a gain for you, friend (āvuso), well-gained by you (lābhā, tassa te suladdhaṃ), that—your teacher (satthā ca te) is rightly self-awakened (sammāsambuddho), and his *dharma* (dhammo ca) is well-proclaimed (svākkhāto), well-expounded (suppavedito), leading out (niyyāniko), conducive to calming (upasamasaṃvattaniko), expounded by one who is rightly self-awakened (sammāsambuddhappavedito). You are one who dwells practicing the *dharma* in accordance with that *dharma* (dhammānudhammappaṭipanno viharasi), practicing masterfully (sāmīcippaṭipanno), living in line with that *dharma* (anudhammacārī), and acts to conform to it (samādāya taṃ dhammaṃ vattasī).’

There, Cunda, the teacher (satthāpi) is to be praised (pāsaṃso), the *dharma* (dhammopi) is to be praised (pāsaṃso), and the disciple (sāvakopi) is to be thus praised (evaṃ pāsaṃso).

“Whoever might say to such a disciple (evarūpaṃ sāvakaṃ), ‘Yes, friend (addhāyasmā), practicing the right way (ñāyappaṭipanno), you will succeed in the right way (ñāyamārādhessatī)’:

The person who praised him (yo ca pasaṃsati), the thing praised (yañca pasaṃsati), and the person who, being praised (yo ca pasaṃsito), aroused even greater persistence (bhiyyoso mattāya vīriyaṃ ārabhati), would all produce much merit (sabbe te bahuṃ puññaṃ pasavanti).

What is the reason for this (taṃ kissa hetu)? That’s the way it is, Cunda, with a well-proclaimed (svākkhāte) *dharma-vinaya* (dhammavinaye), well-expounded (suppavedite), leading out (niyyānike), conducive to calming (upasamasaṃvattanike), expounded by one who is rightly self-awakened (sammāsambuddhappavedite).

The disciple who does not cause remorse for the teacher.
commentary_pali: 169.Vīriyaṃ ārabhatīti attano sukhanipphādakaṃ vīriyaṃ ārabhati. Vuttañhetaṃ ‘‘svākkhāte, bhikkhave, dhammavinaye yo kusīto, so dukkhaṃ viharati. Yo āraddhavīriyo, so sukhaṃ viharatī’’ti (a. ni. 1.319).
commentary_english: 169. vīriyaṃ ārabhatīti, one undertakes effort (vīriya) that produces happiness (sukha) for oneself. It is said, "O monks, in the well-proclaimed Dharma and Discipline, whoever is lazy (kusīto) dwells in suffering (dukkhaṃ viharati)." "Whoever has aroused effort (āraddhavīriyo) dwells in happiness (sukhaṃ viharati)" (A. Ni. 1. 319).

mula_pali:
170. ‘‘Idha pana, cunda, satthā ca loke udapādi arahaṃ sammāsambuddho, dhammo ca svākkhāto suppavedito niyyāniko upasamasaṃvattaniko sammāsambuddhappavedito, aviññāpitatthā cassa honti sāvakā saddhamme, na ca tesaṃ kevalaṃ paripūraṃ brahmacariyaṃ āvikataṃ hoti uttānīkataṃ sabbasaṅgāhapadakataṃ sappāṭihīrakataṃ yāva devamanussehi suppakāsitaṃ. Atha nesaṃ satthuno antaradhānaṃ hoti. Evarūpo kho, cunda, satthā sāvakānaṃ kālaṅkato anutappo hoti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Satthā ca no loke udapādi arahaṃ sammāsambuddho, dhammo ca svākkhāto suppavedito niyyāniko upasamasaṃvattaniko sammāsambuddhappavedito, aviññāpitatthā camha saddhamme, na ca no kevalaṃ paripūraṃ brahmacariyaṃ āvikataṃ hoti uttānīkataṃ sabbasaṅgāhapadakataṃ sappāṭihīrakataṃ yāva devamanussehi suppakāsitaṃ. Atha no satthuno antaradhānaṃ hotīti. Evarūpo kho, cunda, satthā sāvakānaṃ kālaṅkato anutappo hoti.

Sāvakānanutappasatthu
mula_english:
“Here, Cunda, a teacher has arisen in the world, a worthy one, a rightly self-awakened one (arahant sammāsambuddho), and the Dharma (dhamma) is well-proclaimed, well-expounded, leading outwards, conducive to calm, expounded by a rightly self-awakened one. But his disciples have not been instructed in the meaning of the True Dharma (saddhamme), nor has the complete holy life (brahmacariyaṃ) been entirely disclosed to them, made plain, with all its steps collected, complete with miracles, well-proclaimed as far as gods (deva) and humans. Then their teacher disappears (satthuno antaradhānaṃ hoti). When a teacher of that sort has died, it is a matter of regret for his disciples. Why is that? Because: ‘A teacher has appeared in the world, a worthy one, a rightly self-awakened one, and the Dharma is well-proclaimed, well-expounded, leading outwards, conducive to calming, expounded by a rightly self-awakened one. But we have not been instructed in the meaning of the True Dharma, nor has the complete holy life been entirely disclosed to us, made plain, with all its steps collected, complete with miracles, well-proclaimed as far as gods and humans. And now our teacher has disappeared (satthuno antaradhānaṃ hoti).’ When a teacher of that sort has died, it is a matter of regret for his disciples.

Teacher causing regret to disciples.
commentary_pali: 170. Iti bhagavā niyyānikasāsane sammāpaṭipannassa kulaputtassa pasaṃsaṃ dassetvā puna desanaṃ vaḍḍhento idha, cunda, satthā ca loke udapādītiādimāha. Tattha aviññāpitatthāti abodhitatthā. Sabbasaṅgāhapadakatanti sabbasaṅgahapadehi kataṃ, sabbasaṅgāhikaṃ kataṃ na hotīti attho. ‘‘Sabbasaṅgāhapadagata’’ntipi pāṭho, na sabbasaṅgāhapadesu gataṃ, na ekasaṅgahajātanti attho. Sappāṭihīrakatanti niyyānikaṃ. Yāvadevamanussehīti devalokato yāva manussalokā suppakāsitaṃ. Anutappo hotīti anutāpakaro hoti. Satthā ca no loketi idaṃ tesaṃ anutāpakāradassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Nānutappo hotīti satthāraṃ āgamma sāvakehi yaṃ pattabbaṃ, tassa pattattā anutāpakaro na hoti.
commentary_english:
170. Thus, the Blessed One, praising the son of a good family who has rightly practiced in the doctrine that leads out [of suffering], and further increasing the teaching, said, "Here, Cunda, the teacher has arisen in the world," and so on.

There, *aviññāpitatthā* means *abodhitatthā* (the meaning is not understood).

*sabbasaṅgāhapadakata* means done with words of complete collection, meaning it is not done with a complete collection.

" *sabbasaṅgāhapadagata* " is also a reading, meaning not gone to all collections, not of one collection.

*sappāṭihīrakata* means leading out [of suffering].

*yāva devamanussehī* means well proclaimed from the world of gods to the world of humans.

*anutappo hotī* means he is the cause of remorse.

*satthā ca no loke* means this was said to show the cause of their remorse.

*nānutappo hotī* means having come to the teacher, because of the attainment of what is to be attained by the disciples, he is not the cause of remorse.

mula_pali:
171. ‘‘Idha pana, cunda, satthā ca loke udapādi arahaṃ sammāsambuddho. Dhammo ca svākkhāto suppavedito niyyāniko upasamasaṃvattaniko sammāsambuddhappavedito. Viññāpitatthā cassa honti sāvakā saddhamme, kevalañca tesaṃ paripūraṃ brahmacariyaṃ āvikataṃ hoti uttānīkataṃ sabbasaṅgāhapadakataṃ sappāṭihīrakataṃ yāva devamanussehi suppakāsitaṃ. Atha nesaṃ satthuno antaradhānaṃ hoti. Evarūpo kho, cunda, satthā sāvakānaṃ kālaṅkato ananutappo hoti . Taṃ kissa hetu? Satthā ca no loke udapādi arahaṃ sammāsambuddho. Dhammo ca svākkhāto suppavedito niyyāniko upasamasaṃvattaniko sammāsambuddhappavedito. Viññāpitatthā camha saddhamme, kevalañca no paripūraṃ brahmacariyaṃ āvikataṃ hoti uttānīkataṃ sabbasaṅgāhapadakataṃ sappāṭihīrakataṃ yāva devamanussehi suppakāsitaṃ . Atha no satthuno antaradhānaṃ hotīti. Evarūpo kho, cunda, satthā sāvakānaṃ kālaṅkato ananutappo hoti.

Brahmacariyaaparipūrādikathā
mula_english: “But then, Cunda, there is the case where a teacher has arisen in the world, a worthy one, a rightly self-awakened one (arahaṃ sammāsambuddho). And the Dhamma is well-proclaimed (svākkhāto), well-expounded (suppavedito), leading out (niyyāniko), conducive to calming (upasamasaṃvattaniko), proclaimed by one who is rightly self-awakened (sammāsambuddhappavedito). And his disciples have been instructed in the meaning of the True Dhamma (saddhamme), and the complete holy life (brahmacariyaṃ) has been entirely disclosed to them, made plain, with all its steps collected, complete with miracles, well-proclaimed as far as human beings and gods. Then their teacher disappears. When a teacher of that sort has died, it is a matter of no regret for his disciples. Why is this? Because: ‘A teacher has appeared in the world, a worthy one, a rightly self-awakened one (arahaṃ sammāsambuddho). And the Dhamma is well-proclaimed (svākkhāto), well-expounded (suppavedito), leading out (niyyāniko), conducive to calming (upasamasaṃvattaniko), proclaimed by one who is rightly self-awakened (sammāsambuddhappavedito). And we have been instructed in the meaning of the True Dhamma (saddhamme), and the complete holy life (brahmacariyaṃ) has been entirely disclosed to us, made plain, with all its steps collected, complete with miracles, well-proclaimed as far as human beings and gods.’ And now our teacher has disappeared. When a teacher of that sort has died, it is a matter of no regret for his disciples. Talk on the incompleteness of the holy life, and so forth.

mula_pali:
172. ‘‘Etehi cepi, cunda, aṅgehi samannāgataṃ brahmacariyaṃ hoti, no ca kho satthā hoti thero rattaññū cirapabbajito addhagato vayoanuppatto. Evaṃ taṃ brahmacariyaṃ aparipūraṃ hoti tenaṅgena.

‘‘Yato ca kho, cunda, etehi ceva aṅgehi samannāgataṃ brahmacariyaṃ hoti, satthā ca hoti thero rattaññū cirapabbajito addhagato vayoanuppatto. Evaṃ taṃ brahmacariyaṃ paripūraṃ hoti tenaṅgena.
mula_english:
“Now, Cunda, even if a holy life (*brahmacariya*) is endowed with these qualities (*aṅga*), but there is no teacher (*satthā*) who is an elder (*thera*), who knows from long experience (*rattaññū*), long gone forth (*cirapabbajito*), advanced in years (*addhagato*), and has reached old age (*vayoanuppatto*), then that holy life (*brahmacariya*) is incomplete with regard to that quality (*aṅga*).

“But when a holy life (*brahmacariya*) is endowed with these very qualities (*aṅga*), and there is a teacher (*satthā*) who is an elder (*thera*), who knows from long experience (*rattaññū*), long gone forth (*cirapabbajito*), advanced in years (*addhagato*), and has reached old age (*vayoanuppatto*), then that holy life (*brahmacariya*) is complete with regard to that quality (*aṅga*).
commentary_pali: 172.Theroti thiro therakārakehi dhammehi samannāgato. ‘‘Rattaññū’’tiādīni vuttatthāneva. Etehi ce pīti etehi heṭṭhā vuttehi.
commentary_english: 172. thero means one who is steadfast (*thiro*) and endowed (*samannāgato*) with qualities that make one an elder (*therakārakehi dhammehi*). "Experienced" (*rattaññū*) etc. [should be understood] in the places where they have been spoken of (*vuttatthāneva*). "by these also" means by these mentioned previously (*etehi heṭṭhā vuttehi*).

mula_pali:
173. ‘‘Etehi cepi, cunda, aṅgehi samannāgataṃ brahmacariyaṃ hoti, satthā ca hoti thero rattaññū cirapabbajito addhagato vayoanuppatto , no ca khvassa therā bhikkhū sāvakā honti viyattā vinītā visāradā pattayogakkhemā. Alaṃ samakkhātuṃ saddhammassa, alaṃ uppannaṃ parappavādaṃ sahadhammehi suniggahitaṃ niggahetvā sappāṭihāriyaṃ dhammaṃ desetuṃ. Evaṃ taṃ brahmacariyaṃ aparipūraṃ hoti tenaṅgena.

‘‘Yato ca kho, cunda, etehi ceva aṅgehi samannāgataṃ brahmacariyaṃ hoti, satthā ca hoti thero rattaññū cirapabbajito addhagato vayoanuppatto, therā cassa bhikkhū sāvakā honti viyattā vinītā visāradā pattayogakkhemā. Alaṃ samakkhātuṃ saddhammassa, alaṃ uppannaṃ parappavādaṃ sahadhammehi suniggahitaṃ niggahetvā sappāṭihāriyaṃ dhammaṃ desetuṃ. Evaṃ taṃ brahmacariyaṃ paripūraṃ hoti tenaṅgena.
mula_english:
173. “Now, even if a holy life (brahmacariyaṃ) is endowed with those factors (aṅgehi samannāgataṃ), and there is a teacher (satthā) who is an elder (thero), one who knows about experience (rattaññū), of long standing (cirapabbajito), senior (addhagato), attained to old age (vayoanuppatto), yet there are no elder monk (therā bhikkhū) disciples of his who are experienced (viyattā), trained (vinītā), mature (visāradā), attained to security from the yoke (pattayogakkhemā), able to teach the True Dhamma (saddhammassa), able to trap with the True Dhamma (sahadhammehi) any opposing doctrines (parappavādaṃ) that have arisen and—having trapped them—to teach the Dhamma (dhammaṃ) complete with miracles (sappāṭihāriyaṃ), then a holy life (brahmacariyaṃ) of that sort is incomplete (aparipūraṃ) with regard to that factor (tenaṅgena).

“But when a holy life (brahmacariyaṃ) is endowed with those factors (aṅgehi samannāgataṃ), and there is a teacher (satthā) who is an elder (thero), one who knows about experience (rattaññū), of long standing (cirapabbajito), senior (addhagato), attained to old age (vayoanuppatto), and there are elder monk (therā bhikkhū) disciples of his who are experienced (viyattā), trained (vinītā), mature (visāradā), attained to security from the yoke (pattayogakkhemā), able to teach the True Dhamma (saddhammassa), able to trap with the True Dhamma (sahadhammehi) any opposing doctrines (parappavādaṃ) that have arisen and—having trapped them—to teach the Dhamma (dhammaṃ) complete with miracles (sappāṭihāriyaṃ), then a holy life (brahmacariyaṃ) of that sort is complete (paripūraṃ) with regard to that factor (tenaṅgena).
commentary_pali: 173.Pattayogakkhemāti catūhi yogehi khemattā arahattaṃ idha yogakkhemaṃ nāma, taṃ pattāti attho. Alaṃ samakkhātuṃ saddhammassāti sammukhā gahitattā assa saddhammaṃ sammā ācikkhituṃ samatthā.
commentary_english:
`pattayogakkhemā` means having attained security from the four yokes; in this context, *arahattaṃ* (arahatship) is called *yogakkhemaṃ* (security from the yokes), meaning having attained that.

`alaṃ samakkhātuṃ saddhammassā` means being capable of properly explaining the true Dharma, because it was directly received.

mula_pali:
174. ‘‘Etehi cepi, cunda, aṅgehi samannāgataṃ brahmacariyaṃ hoti, satthā ca hoti thero rattaññū cirapabbajito addhagato vayoanuppatto, therā cassa bhikkhū sāvakā honti viyattā vinītā visāradā pattayogakkhemā. Alaṃ samakkhātuṃ saddhammassa, alaṃ uppannaṃ parappavādaṃ sahadhammehi suniggahitaṃ niggahetvā sappāṭihāriyaṃ dhammaṃ desetuṃ. No ca khvassa majjhimā bhikkhū sāvakā honti…pe… majjhimā cassa bhikkhū sāvakā honti, no ca khvassa navā bhikkhū sāvakā honti…pe… navā cassa bhikkhū sāvakā honti, no ca khvassa therā bhikkhuniyo sāvikā honti…pe… therā cassa bhikkhuniyo sāvikā honti, no ca khvassa majjhimā bhikkhuniyo sāvikā honti…pe… majjhimā cassa bhikkhuniyo sāvikā honti , no ca khvassa navā bhikkhuniyo sāvikā honti…pe… navā cassa bhikkhuniyo sāvikā honti, no ca khvassa upāsakā sāvakā honti gihī odātavasanā brahmacārino…pe… upāsakā cassa sāvakā honti gihī odātavasanā brahmacārino, no ca khvassa upāsakā sāvakā honti gihī odātavasanā kāmabhogino…pe… upāsakā cassa sāvakā honti gihī odātavasanā kāmabhogino, no ca khvassa upāsikā sāvikā honti gihiniyo odātavasanā brahmacāriniyo…pe… upāsikā cassa sāvikā honti gihiniyo odātavasanā brahmacāriniyo, no ca khvassa upāsikā sāvikā honti gihiniyo odātavasanā kāmabhoginiyo…pe… upāsikā cassa sāvikā honti gihiniyo odātavasanā kāmabhoginiyo, no ca khvassa brahmacariyaṃ hoti iddhañceva phītañca vitthārikaṃ bāhujaññaṃ puthubhūtaṃ yāva devamanussehi suppakāsitaṃ…pe… brahmacariyañcassa hoti iddhañceva phītañca vitthārikaṃ bāhujaññaṃ puthubhūtaṃ yāva devamanussehi suppakāsitaṃ, no ca kho lābhaggayasaggappattaṃ. Evaṃ taṃ brahmacariyaṃ aparipūraṃ hoti tenaṅgena.

‘‘Yato ca kho, cunda, etehi ceva aṅgehi samannāgataṃ brahmacariyaṃ hoti, satthā ca hoti thero rattaññū cirapabbajito addhagato vayoanuppatto, therā cassa bhikkhū sāvakā honti viyattā vinītā visāradā pattayogakkhemā. Alaṃ samakkhātuṃ saddhammassa, alaṃ uppannaṃ parappavādaṃ sahadhammehi suniggahitaṃ niggahetvā sappāṭihāriyaṃ dhammaṃ desetuṃ. Majjhimā cassa bhikkhū sāvakā honti…pe… navā cassa bhikkhū sāvakā honti…pe… therā cassa bhikkhuniyo sāvikā honti…pe… majjhimā cassa bhikkhuniyo sāvikā honti…pe… navā cassa bhikkhuniyo sāvikā honti…pe… upāsakā cassa sāvakā honti…pe… gihī odātavasanā brahmacārino . Upāsakā cassa sāvakā honti gihī odātavasanā kāmabhogino…pe… upāsikā cassa sāvikā honti gihiniyo odātavasanā brahmacāriniyo…pe… upāsikā cassa sāvikā honti gihiniyo odātavasanā kāmabhoginiyo…pe… brahmacariyañcassa hoti iddhañceva phītañca vitthārikaṃ bāhujaññaṃ puthubhūtaṃ yāva devamanussehi suppakāsitaṃ, lābhaggappattañca yasaggappattañca. Evaṃ taṃ brahmacariyaṃ paripūraṃ hoti tenaṅgena.
mula_english:
174. “But even if a holy life is endowed with these factors, Cunda, and there is a teacher who is an elder, of long standing, long gone forth, senior, attained to old age, and there are elder monk disciples of his who are experienced, trained, mature, attained to security from the yoke.
able to teach the True Dhamma (saddharma), able to trap with the True Dhamma any opposing doctrines (parappavāda) that have arisen and—having trapped them—to teach the Dhamma complete with miracles,
yet there are no monk disciples of his of middle standing… there are monk disciples of his of middle standing, yet no junior monk disciples of his… there are junior monk disciples of his, yet no elder nun disciples of his… there are elder nun disciples of his, yet no nun disciples of his of middle standing… there are nun disciples of his of middle standing, yet no junior nun disciples of his… there are junior nun disciples of his, yet no male lay disciples of his, householders wearing white, following the celibate life… there are male lay disciples of his, householders wearing white, following the celibate life, yet no male lay disciples of his, householders wearing white, partaking of sensuality… there are male lay disciples of his, householders wearing white, partaking of sensuality, yet no female lay disciples of his, householders wearing white, following the celibate life… there are female lay disciples of his, householders wearing white, following the celibate life, yet no female lay disciples of his, householders wearing white, partaking of sensuality… there are female lay disciples of his, householders wearing white, partaking of sensuality, and his holy life (brahmacariya) has become powerful, prosperous, detailed, well-populated, wide-spread, proclaimed among devas and human beings, yet it has not attained supremacy in terms of gains nor supremacy in terms of status.
then a holy life (brahmacariya) of that sort is incomplete with regard to that factor.

“But when a holy life (brahmacariya) is endowed with these very factors, Cunda, and there is a teacher who is an elder, of long standing, long gone forth, senior, attained to old age, and there are elder monk disciples of his who are experienced, trained, mature, attained to security from the yoke,
able to teach the True Dhamma (saddharma), able to trap with the True Dhamma any opposing doctrines (parappavāda) that have arisen and—having trapped them—to teach the Dhamma complete with miracles,
there are monk disciples of his of middle standing… there are junior monk disciples of his… there are elder nun disciples of his… there are nun disciples of his of middle standing… there are junior nun disciples of his… there are male lay disciples of his, householders wearing white, following the celibate life.
there are male lay disciples of his, householders wearing white, partaking of sensuality… there are female lay disciples of his, householders wearing white, following the celibate life… there are female lay disciples of his, householders wearing white, partaking of sensuality, and his holy life (brahmacariya) has become powerful, prosperous, detailed,
well-populated, wide-spread, proclaimed among devas and human beings, and has attained supremacy in terms of gains and supremacy in terms of status.
then a holy life (brahmacariya) of that sort is complete with regard to that factor.
commentary_pali: 174.Brahmacārinoti brahmacariyavāsaṃ vasamānā ariyasāvakā. Kāmabhoginoti gihisotāpannā. ‘‘Iddhañcevā’’tiādīni mahāparinibbāne vitthāritāneva. Lābhaggayasaggapattanti lābhaggañceva yasaggañca pattaṃ.
commentary_english: 174. Brahmacārinoti *brahmacariyavāsaṃ vasamānā ariyasāvakā*: "Brahmacarins" means noble disciples who dwell in the practice of celibacy (brahmacarya). Kāmabhoginoti *gihisotāpannā*: "Those who enjoy sensual pleasures" means householder stream-enterers. "Iddhañcevā" and the rest are explained in detail in the Mahāparinibbāna Sutta. Lābhaggayasaggapattanti *lābhaggañceva yasaggañca pattaṃ*: "Attainment of the highest gain and the highest fame" means the attainment of the highest gain and the highest fame.

mula_pali:
175. ‘‘Ahaṃ kho pana, cunda, etarahi satthā loke uppanno arahaṃ sammāsambuddho. Dhammo ca svākkhāto suppavedito niyyāniko upasamasaṃvattaniko sammāsambuddhappavedito. Viññāpitatthā ca me sāvakā saddhamme, kevalañca tesaṃ paripūraṃ brahmacariyaṃ āvikataṃ uttānīkataṃ sabbasaṅgāhapadakataṃ sappāṭihīrakataṃ yāva devamanussehi suppakāsitaṃ. Ahaṃ kho pana, cunda, etarahi satthā thero rattaññū cirapabbajito addhagato vayoanuppatto.

‘‘Santi kho pana me, cunda, etarahi therā bhikkhū sāvakā honti viyattā vinītā visāradā pattayogakkhemā. Alaṃ samakkhātuṃ saddhammassa, alaṃ uppannaṃ parappavādaṃ sahadhammehi suniggahitaṃ niggahetvā sappāṭihāriyaṃ dhammaṃ desetuṃ. Santi kho pana me, cunda , etarahi majjhimā bhikkhū sāvakā…pe… santi kho pana me, cunda, etarahi navā bhikkhū sāvakā…pe… santi kho pana me, cunda, etarahi therā bhikkhuniyo sāvikā…pe… santi kho pana me, cunda, etarahi majjhimā bhikkhuniyo sāvikā…pe… santi kho pana me, cunda, etarahi navā bhikkhuniyo sāvikā…pe… santi kho pana me, cunda, etarahi upāsakā sāvakā gihī odātavasanā brahmacārino…pe… santi kho pana me, cunda, etarahi upāsakā sāvakā gihī odātavasanā kāmabhogino…pe… santi kho pana me, cunda, etarahi upāsikā sāvikā gihiniyo odātavasanā brahmacāriniyo…pe… santi kho pana me, cunda, etarahi upāsikā sāvikā gihiniyo odātavasanā kāmabhoginiyo…pe… etarahi kho pana me, cunda, brahmacariyaṃ iddhañceva phītañca vitthārikaṃ bāhujaññaṃ puthubhūtaṃ yāva devamanussehi suppakāsitaṃ.
mula_english:
“Cunda, I am now a teacher who has appeared in the world, worthy & rightly self-awakened ( *arahaṃ sammāsambuddho*).

And the *Dhamma* is well-proclaimed, well-expounded, leading out, conducive to calming, expounded by one who is rightly self-awakened (*sammāsambuddhappavedito*).

My disciples have been instructed in the meaning/goal of the True *Dhamma*, and the complete holy life (*brahmacariyaṃ*) has been entirely disclosed to them, made plain, with all its steps collected, complete with miracles, well-proclaimed as far as human beings & *devas*.

I am now a teacher who is an elder, of long standing, long gone forth, senior, attained to old age.

“There are now elder monk disciples of mine who are experienced, trained, mature, attained to security from the yoke,

able to teach the True *Dhamma*, able to trap with the True *Dhamma* any opposing doctrines that have arisen and—having trapped them—to teach the *Dhamma* complete with miracles.

There are now monk disciples of mine of middle standing… There are now junior monk disciples of mine… There are now elder nun disciples of mine… nun disciples of mine of middle standing… junior nun disciples of mine… male lay disciples of mine, householders wearing white, following the celibate life… male lay disciples of mine, householders wearing white, partaking of sensuality… female lay disciples of mine, householders wearing white, following the celibate life. There are now female lay disciples of mine, householders wearing white, partaking of sensuality… And now, Cunda, this holy life (*brahmacariyaṃ*) is both successful and prosperous, widespread, well-known, far-reaching, and well-proclaimed among gods and humans.
commentary_pali: 175.Santi kho pana me, cunda, etarahi therā bhikkhū sāvakāti sāriputtamoggallānādayo therā. Bhikkhuniyoti khemātherīuppalavaṇṇatherīādayo. Upāsakā sāvakā gihī odātavatthavasanā brahmacārinoti cittagahapatihatthakaāḷavakādayo. Kāmabhoginoti cūḷaanāthapiṇḍikamahāanāthapiṇḍikādayo. Brahmacāriniyoti nandamātādayo. Kāmabhoginiyoti khujjuttarādayo.
commentary_english:
175. There are, Cunda, at this time, elder monks who are disciples, such as the elders Śāriputta and Maudgalyāyana.

*Bhikkhunīs* are the elder Khemā, the elder Utpalavarṇā, and so forth.

*Upāsakas* (male lay followers) who are disciples, householders wearing white clothes, and celibates, such as Cittagahapati, Hatthaka Āḷavaka, and so forth.

*Kāmabhogins* (male enjoyers of sensual pleasures) are Cūḷa-anāthapiṇḍika, Mahā-anāthapiṇḍika, and so forth.

*Brahmacāriṇīs* (female celibates) are Nandamātā, and so forth.

*Kāmabhoginīs* (female enjoyers of sensual pleasures) are Khujjuttarā, and so forth.

mula_pali:
176. ‘‘Yāvatā kho, cunda, etarahi satthāro loke uppannā, nāhaṃ, cunda, aññaṃ ekasatthārampi samanupassāmi evaṃlābhaggayasaggappattaṃ yatharivāhaṃ. Yāvatā kho pana, cunda, etarahi saṅgho vā gaṇo vā loke uppanno; nāhaṃ, cunda, aññaṃ ekaṃ saṃghampi samanupassāmi evaṃlābhaggayasaggappattaṃ yatharivāyaṃ, cunda, bhikkhusaṅgho. Yaṃ kho taṃ, cunda, sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ‘sabbākārasampannaṃ sabbākāraparipūraṃ anūnamanadhikaṃ svākkhātaṃ kevalaṃ paripūraṃ brahmacariyaṃ suppakāsita’nti. Idameva taṃ sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ‘sabbākārasampannaṃ…pe… suppakāsita’nti.

‘‘Udako uddako (sī. syā. pī.) sudaṃ, cunda, rāmaputto evaṃ vācaṃ bhāsati – ‘passaṃ na passatī’ti. Kiñca passaṃ na passatīti? Khurassa sādhunisitassa talamassa passati, dhārañca khvassa na passati. Idaṃ vuccati – ‘passaṃ na passatī’ti. Yaṃ kho panetaṃ, cunda, udakena rāmaputtena bhāsitaṃ hīnaṃ gammaṃ pothujjanikaṃ anariyaṃ anatthasaṃhitaṃ khurameva sandhāya. Yañca taṃ yañcetaṃ (syā. ka.), cunda, sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ‘passaṃ na passatī’ti, idameva taṃ idamevetaṃ (ka.) sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ‘passaṃ na passatī’ti. Kiñca passaṃ na passatīti? Evaṃ sabbākārasampannaṃ sabbākāraparipūraṃ anūnamanadhikaṃ svākkhātaṃ kevalaṃ paripūraṃ brahmacariyaṃ suppakāsitanti, iti hetaṃ passati suppakāsitaṃ, iti hetaṃ na passatīti (syā. ka.). Idamettha apakaḍḍheyya, evaṃ taṃ parisuddhataraṃ assāti, iti hetaṃ na passati na passatīti (syā. ka.). Idamettha upakaḍḍheyya, evaṃ taṃ paripūraṃ parisuddhataraṃ (syā. ka.), paripūrataraṃ (?) assāti, iti hetaṃ na passati. Idaṃ vuccati cunda – ‘passaṃ na passatī’ti. Yaṃ kho taṃ, cunda, sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ‘sabbākārasampannaṃ…pe… brahmacariyaṃ suppakāsita’nti. Idameva taṃ sammā vadamāno vadeyya – ‘sabbākārasampannaṃ sabbākāraparipūraṃ anūnamanadhikaṃ svākkhātaṃ kevalaṃ paripūraṃ brahmacariyaṃ suppakāsita’nti.

uddako (sī. syā. pī.) yañcetaṃ (syā. ka.) idamevetaṃ (ka.) suppakāsitaṃ, iti hetaṃ na passatīti (syā. ka.) na passatīti (syā. ka.) parisuddhataraṃ (syā. ka.), paripūrataraṃ (?)

Saṅgāyitabbadhammo
mula_english:
176. “To the extent that there are now teachers who have arisen in the world, Cunda, I do not see any other teacher who has attained supremacy in terms of gains and supremacy in terms of status equal to what I have. And to the extent that there is now a *saṅgha* or group that has arisen in the world, Cunda, I do not see any other *saṅgha* that has attained supremacy in terms of gains and supremacy in terms of status equal to what this *bhikkhusaṅgha*, the community of monks, has. Cunda, if one speaking rightly were to say, ‘A well-expounded, entirely complete, well-proclaimed holy life, consummate in all its aspects (*sabbākārasampannaṃ*), complete in all its aspects, with nothing lacking (*anūnaṃ*) and nothing in excess (*anadhikaṃ*),’ he would, speaking rightly, say it of this: ‘Consummate in all its aspects (*sabbākārasampannaṃ*)…pe… well-proclaimed (*suppakāsitaṃ*)’.” “Udaka Rāmaputta once made this statement: ‘Seeing, one doesn’t see.’ Furthermore, what does it mean, ‘Seeing, one doesn’t see’? One sees the blade of a well-sharpened razor (*khurassa sādhunisitassa talamassa*), but one does not see the edge (*dhārañca khvassa na passati*). This is called, ‘Seeing, one doesn’t see.’ But this statement of Uddaka Rāmaputta, Cunda, is base, vulgar, common, ignoble, unprofitable, dealing only with a razor (*khurameva sandhāya*). And how would one, Cunda, speaking rightly, say, ‘Seeing, one doesn’t see’? He would, speaking rightly, say just this: ‘Seeing, one doesn’t see.’ Furthermore, what does it mean, ‘Seeing, one doesn’t see’? Thus, ‘Consummate in all its aspects (*sabbākārasampannaṃ*), complete in all its aspects (*sabbākāraparipūraṃ*), with nothing lacking (*anūnamanadhikaṃ*), well-proclaimed (*svākkhātaṃ*), entirely complete (*kevalaṃ paripūraṃ*), the holy life (*brahmacariyaṃ*) is well-proclaimed (*suppakāsitaṃ*)’. This is how one sees. If one were to remove this from here, thinking, ‘It would become purer,’ one does not see this. If one were to add this here, thinking, ‘It would become more complete (*paripūraṃ*),’ one does not see this. This is called, Cunda, ‘Seeing, one doesn’t see.’ Cunda, if one speaking rightly were to say, ‘Consummate in all its aspects (*sabbākārasampannaṃ*)…pe… the holy life (*brahmacariyaṃ*) is well-proclaimed (*suppakāsitaṃ*)’, he would, speaking rightly, say it of this: ‘Consummate in all its aspects (*sabbākārasampannaṃ*), complete in all its aspects (*sabbākāraparipūraṃ*), with nothing lacking (*anūnamanadhikaṃ*), well-proclaimed (*svākkhātaṃ*), entirely complete (*kevalaṃ paripūraṃ*), the holy life (*brahmacariyaṃ*) is well-proclaimed (*suppakāsitaṃ*)’." 0127"/> Note: *idamevetaṃ* (ka.) Note: *suppakāsitaṃ*, *iti hetaṃ na passatīti* (syā. ka.) Note: *na passatīti* (syā. ka.) Note: *parisuddhataraṃ* (syā. ka.), *paripūrataraṃ* (?)

*saṅgāyitabbadhammo*
commentary_pali:
176.Sabbākārasampannanti sabbakāraṇasampannaṃ. Idamevatanti idameva brahmacariyaṃ, imameva dhammaṃ sammā hetunā nayena vadamāno vadeyya. Udakāssudanti udako sudaṃ. Passaṃ na passatīti passanto na passati. So kira imaṃ pañhaṃ mahājanaṃ pucchi. Tehi ‘‘na jānāma, ācariya, kathehi no’’ti vutto so āha – ‘‘gambhīro ayaṃ pañho āhārasappāye sati thokaṃ cintetvā sakkā kathetu’’nti. Tato tehi cattāro māse mahāsakkāre kate taṃ pañhaṃ kathento kiñca passaṃ na passatītiādimāha. Tattha sādhunisitassāti suṭṭhunisitassa tikhiṇassa, sunisitakhurassa kira talaṃ paññāyati, dhārā na paññāyatīti ayamettha attho.

Saṅgāyitabbadhammādivaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
176. "Possessed of all aspects" [sabbākārasampanna] means possessed of all causes [sabakāraṇasampannaṃ].
"This very thing" [idameva] means this very celibate life (brahmacariya), he should speak declaring this very doctrine (dharma) with the right motive and method (sammā hetunā nayena vadamāno vadeyya).
"Water indeed" [udakāssuda] means water indeed [udako sudaṃ].
"Seeing, he does not see" [passaṃ na passatī] means seeing, he does not see [passanto na passati].
He asked the crowd this question.
They said, "We do not know, teacher (ācariya), tell us." He, having been told thus, said, "This question is profound (gambhīro), when there is a suitable opportunity for food (āhārasappāye sati), having thought a little (thokaṃ cintetvā), it is possible to tell (sakkā kathetu)."
Then, after four months (cattāro māse), a great honor (mahāsakkāre) having been done, while telling that question, he said beginning with, "Though seeing, he does not see" [kiñca passaṃ na passatī].
There, "Of one well sharpened" [sādhunisitassā] means of one very well sharpened [suṭṭhunisitassa], of one sharp (tikhiṇassa), it is said, the surface of a very well sharpened razor (sunisitakhurassa) appears (paññāyati), the edge (dhārā) does not appear (na paññāyatīti), this is its meaning (ayamettha attho).

Explanation of the things to be chanted, beginning with the Dharma (saṅgāyitabbadhammādivaṇṇanā).

mula_pali:
177. Tasmātiha, cunda, ye vo mayā dhammā abhiññā desitā, tattha sabbeheva saṅgamma samāgamma atthena atthaṃ byañjanena byañjanaṃ saṅgāyitabbaṃ na vivaditabbaṃ, yathayidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ addhaniyaṃ assa ciraṭṭhitikaṃ, tadassa bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ. Katame ca te, cunda , dhammā mayā abhiññā desitā, yattha sabbeheva saṅgamma samāgamma atthena atthaṃ byañjanena byañjanaṃ saṅgāyitabbaṃ na vivaditabbaṃ, yathayidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ addhaniyaṃ assa ciraṭṭhitikaṃ, tadassa bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ? Seyyathidaṃ – cattāro satipaṭṭhānā, cattāro sammappadhānā, cattāro iddhipādā, pañcindriyāni, pañca balāni, satta bojjhaṅgā , ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo. Ime kho te, cunda, dhammā mayā abhiññā desitā. Yattha sabbeheva saṅgamma samāgamma atthena atthaṃ byañjanena byañjanaṃ saṅgāyitabbaṃ na vivaditabbaṃ, yathayidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ addhaniyaṃ assa ciraṭṭhitikaṃ, tadassa bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ.

Saññāpetabbavidhi
mula_english:
“Therefore, Cunda, regarding those qualities ( *dhamma*) that I have taught, having directly known them (*abhiññā desitā*), you should all, having assembled & gathered together, recite & compare meaning with meaning (*atthena atthaṃ*), expression with expression (*byañjanena byañjanaṃ*), so that this holy life (*brahmacariyaṃ*) may long endure & remain steadfast for the benefit, welfare, & happiness of the multitude; out of sympathy for the world; for the benefit, welfare, & happiness of human beings & devas.

And which are the qualities (*dhammā*) I have taught, Cunda, that you should all, having assembled & gathered together, recite & compare meaning with meaning (*atthena atthaṃ*), expression with expression (*byañjanena byañjanaṃ*), so that this holy life (*brahmacariyaṃ*) may long endure & remain steadfast for the benefit, welfare, & happiness of the multitude; out of sympathy for the world; for the benefit, welfare, & happiness of human beings & devas? Namely: the four foundations of mindfulness (*cattāro satipaṭṭhānā*), the four right exertions (*cattāro sammappadhānā*), the four bases of power (*cattāro iddhipādā*), the five faculties (*pañcindriyāni*), the five strengths (*pañca balāni*), the seven factors of enlightenment (*satta bojjhaṅgā*), and the Noble Eightfold Path (*ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo*).

These, Cunda, are the qualities (*dhammā*) I have taught.

Those should all be recited together, without dispute, so that this holy life (*brahmacariyaṃ*) will endure & last a long time, and that will be for the benefit & happiness of many, out of sympathy for the world; for the welfare, benefit, & happiness of devas & human beings.

Method for making known.
commentary_pali: 177.Saṅgamma samāgammāti saṅgantvā samāgantvā. Atthena atthaṃ, byañjanena byañjananti atthena saha atthaṃ, byañjanenapi saha byañjanaṃ samānentehīti attho. Saṅgāyitabbanti vācetabbaṃ sajjhāyitabbaṃ. Yathayidaṃ brahmacariyanti yathā idaṃ sakalaṃ sāsanabrahmacariyaṃ.
commentary_english: 177. Saṅgamma samāgammā means having come together, having assembled. Atthena atthaṃ, byañjanena byañjana means meaning together with meaning, and expression together with expression, is the meaning. Saṅgāyitabba means should be recited, should be studied. Yathayidaṃ brahmacariya means just as this is the entire teaching of the holy life (brahmacarya).

mula_pali: 178. ‘‘Tesañca vo, cunda, samaggānaṃ sammodamānānaṃ avivadamānānaṃ sikkhataṃ sikkhitabbaṃ (bahūsu) aññataro sabrahmacārī saṅghe dhammaṃ bhāseyya. Tatra ce tumhākaṃ evamassa – ‘ayaṃ kho āyasmā atthañceva micchā gaṇhāti, byañjanāni ca micchā ropetī’ti. Tassa neva abhinanditabbaṃ na paṭikkositabbaṃ, anabhinanditvā appaṭikkositvā so evamassa vacanīyo – ‘imassa nu kho, āvuso, atthassa imāni vā byañjanāni etāni vā byañjanāni katamāni opāyikatarāni, imesañca imesaṃ vā (syā. pī. ka.), imesaṃ (sī.) byañjanānaṃ ayaṃ vā attho eso vā attho katamo opāyikataro’ti ? So ce evaṃ vadeyya – ‘imassa kho, āvuso, atthassa imāneva byañjanāni opāyikatarāni, yā ceva yañceva (sī. ka.), ṭīkā oloketabbā etāni; imesañca imedaṃ (sabbattha) byañjanānaṃ ayameva attho opāyikataro, yā ceva yañceva (sī. ka.), ṭīkā oloketabbā eso’ti.
