So neva ussādetabbo na apasādetabbo, anussādetvā anapasādetvā sveva sādhukaṃ saññāpetabbo tassa ca atthassa tesañca byañjanānaṃ nisantiyā.
mula_english:
178.
’’Furthermore, Cunda, while you are harmonious, rejoicing together, not quarreling, and training, if another fellow religious (sabrahmacārī) should speak Dharma (dhammaṃ bhāseyya) in the Sangha (saṅghe), and if the thought occurs to you, ‘Friends, this venerable one has grasped the wrong meaning (atthañceva micchā gaṇhāti), and picked up the wrong expression (byañjanāni ca micchā ropetī),’ then you should express neither delight (abhinanditabbaṃ) nor scorn (paṭikkositabbaṃ). Neither delighting (anabhinanditvā) nor scorning (appaṭikkositvā), you should say to him, ‘With regard to this meaning (atthassa), friend (āvuso), there are these expressions (imāni vā byañjanāni) or those expressions (etāni vā byañjanāni). Which are the more pertinent (katamāni opāyikatarāni)? And with regard to these expressions (byañjanānaṃ), there is this meaning (ayaṃ vā attho) or that meaning (eso vā attho). Which is the more pertinent (katamo opāyikataro)?’ If he should say, ‘Friends, with regard to this meaning (atthassa), these expressions (imāneva byañjanāni) are more pertinent (opāyikatarāni) than those (yā ceva etāni); and with regard to these expressions (byañjanānaṃ), this meaning (ayameva attho) is more pertinent (opāyikataro) than that (yā ceva eso),’ then he is neither to be praised (ussādetabbo) nor disparaged (apasādetabbo). Neither praising (anussādetvā) nor disparaging (anapasādetvā) him, you should show him how to examine that meaning (atthassa) & those expressions (byañjanānaṃ) properly (sādhukaṃ saññāpetabbo).
commentary_pali: 178.Tatra ceti tatra saṅghamajjhe, tassa vā bhāsite. Atthañceva micchā gaṇhāti, byañjanāni ca micchā ropetīti ‘‘cattāro satipaṭṭhānā’’ti ettha ārammaṇaṃ ‘‘satipaṭṭhāna’’nti atthaṃ gaṇhāti. ‘‘Satipaṭṭhānānī’’ti byañjanaṃ ropeti. Imassa nu kho, āvuso, atthassāti ‘‘satiyeva satipaṭṭhāna’’nti. Atthassa ‘‘cattāro satipaṭṭhānā’’ti kiṃ nu kho imāni byañjanāni, udāhu cattāri satipaṭṭhānānī’’ti etāni vā byañjanāni. Katamāni opāyikatarānīti imassa atthassa katamāni byañjanāni upapannatarāni allīnatarāni. Imesañcabyañjanānanti ‘‘cattāro satipaṭṭhānā’’ti byañjanānaṃ ‘‘satiyeva satipaṭṭhāna’’nti kiṃ nu kho ayaṃ attho, udāhu ‘‘ārammaṇaṃ satipaṭṭhāna’’nti eso atthoti? Imassa kho, āvuso, atthassāti ‘‘ārammaṇaṃ satipaṭṭhāna’’nti imassa atthassa. Yā ceva etānīti yāni ceva etāni mayā vuttāni. Yā ceva esoti yo ceva esa mayā vutto. So neva ussādetabboti tumhehi tāva sammā atthe ca sammā byañjane ca ṭhātabbaṃ. So pana neva ussādetabbo, na apasādetabbo. Saññāpetabboti jānāpetabbo. Tassa ca atthassāti ‘‘satiyeva satipaṭṭhāna’’nti atthassa ca. Tesañca byañjanānanti ‘‘satipaṭṭhānā’’ti byañjanānaṃ. Nisantiyāti nisāmanatthaṃ dhāraṇatthaṃ. Iminā nayena sabbavāresu attho veditabbo.
commentary_english:
178. *tatra ce*ti: There, in the midst of the *saṅgha*, or in his utterance.

*atthañceva micchā gaṇhāti, byañjanāni ca micchā ropetī*ti: Here, regarding "the four *satipaṭṭhāna*s," he grasps the meaning (attha) as "the object is *satipaṭṭhāna*." He applies the expression (*byañjana*) as "*satipaṭṭhānāni*."

*imassa nu kho, āvuso, atthassā*ti: Of this meaning, "*sati* alone is *satipaṭṭhāna*." Regarding the meaning, "the four *satipaṭṭhāna*s," what are these expressions (*byañjana*)? Or, are these the expressions, "the four *satipaṭṭhāna*s"?

*katamāni opāyikatarānī*ti: Of this meaning, which expressions are more fitting, more suitable?

*imesañca byañjanāna*nti: Of these expressions, "the four *satipaṭṭhāna*s," is this the meaning, "*sati* alone is *satipaṭṭhāna*," or is this the meaning, "the object is *satipaṭṭhāna*?"

*imassa kho, āvuso, atthassā*ti: Of this meaning, "the object is *satipaṭṭhāna*."

*yā ceva etānī*ti: Whatever things were spoken by me.

*yā ceva eso*ti: Whatever was spoken by me.

*so neva ussādetabbo*ti: You should remain with the meaning and the expression. However, that should not be removed, nor should it be rejected.

*saññāpetabbo*ti: It should be made known.

*tassa ca atthassā*ti: And of the meaning, "*sati* alone is *satipaṭṭhāna*."

*tesañca byañjanāna*nti: Of those expressions, "*satipaṭṭhāna*s."

*nisantiyā*ti: For the sake of contemplating, for the sake of retaining.

In this way, the meaning should be understood in all instances.

mula_pali: 179. ‘‘Aparopi ce, cunda, sabrahmacārī saṅghe dhammaṃ bhāseyya. Tatra ce tumhākaṃ evamassa – ‘ayaṃ kho āyasmā atthañhi kho micchā gaṇhāti byañjanāni sammā ropetī’ti. Tassa neva abhinanditabbaṃ na paṭikkositabbaṃ, anabhinanditvā appaṭikkositvā so evamassa vacanīyo – ‘imesaṃ nu kho, āvuso, byañjanānaṃ ayaṃ vā attho eso vā attho katamo opāyikataro’ti? So ce evaṃ vadeyya – ‘imesaṃ kho, āvuso, byañjanānaṃ ayameva attho opāyikataro, yā ceva eso’ti. So neva ussādetabbo na apasādetabbo, anussādetvā anapasādetvā sveva sādhukaṃ saññāpetabbo tasseva atthassa nisantiyā.
mula_english: “If another one of your fellows in the holy life, Cunda, should speak of the *dharma* in the *saṃgha*, and you should think, ‘This venerable one grasps the meaning incorrectly but utters the expressions correctly,’ you should express neither delight nor scorn. Neither delighting nor scorning, you should say to him, ‘With regard to these expressions, friend, there is this meaning or that meaning. Which is the more pertinent?’ If he should say, ‘With regard to these expressions, friend, this meaning is the more pertinent, namely, this,’ neither praising nor disparaging him, you should show him how to carefully examine that very meaning."

mula_pali: 180. ‘‘Aparopi ce, cunda, sabrahmacārī saṅghe dhammaṃ bhāseyya. Tatra ce tumhākaṃ evamassa – ‘ayaṃ kho āyasmā atthañhi kho sammā gaṇhāti byañjanāni micchā ropetī’ti. Tassa neva abhinanditabbaṃ na paṭikkositabbaṃ; anabhinanditvā appaṭikkositvā so evamassa vacanīyo – ‘imassa nu kho, āvuso, atthassa imāni vā byañjanāni etāni vā byañjanāni katamāni opāyikatarānī’ti? So ce evaṃ vadeyya – ‘imassa kho, āvuso, atthassa imāneva byañjanāni opayikatarāni, yāni ceva etānī’ti . So neva ussādetabbo na apasādetabbo; anussādetvā anapasādetvā sveva sādhukaṃ saññāpetabbo tesaññeva byañjanānaṃ nisantiyā.
mula_english: “Furthermore, Cunda, if a fellow practitioner of the holy life should speak about the *dharma* in the *saṅgha*, and if the thought should occur to you, ‘This venerable one grasps the meaning (*artha*) well, but applies the expressions (*byañjana*) incorrectly,’ that should neither be rejoiced at nor rejected. Without rejoicing or rejecting, you should say to him, ‘Friend, with regard to this meaning (*artha*), which of these expressions (*byañjana*) or those expressions (*byañjana*) are more fitting?’ If he should say, ‘Friend, with regard to this meaning (*artha*), these very expressions (*byañjana*) are more fitting than those,’ he should neither be encouraged nor discouraged. Without encouraging or discouraging him, you should carefully explain it to him precisely according to the arrangement of those very expressions (*byañjana*)."

mula_pali:
181. ‘‘Aparopi ce, cunda, sabrahmacārī saṅghe dhammaṃ bhāseyya. Tatra ce tumhākaṃ evamassa – ‘ayaṃ kho āyasmā atthañceva sammā gaṇhāti byañjanāni ca sammā ropetī’ti. Tassa ‘sādhū’ti bhāsitaṃ abhinanditabbaṃ anumoditabbaṃ; tassa ‘sādhū’ti bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā so evamassa vacanīyo – ‘lābhā no āvuso, suladdhaṃ no āvuso, ye mayaṃ āyasmantaṃ tādisaṃ sabrahmacāriṃ passāma evaṃ atthupetaṃ byañjanupeta’nti.

Paccayānuññātakāraṇaṃ
mula_english:
“Furthermore, Cunda, if another one of your fellows in the holy life should speak of the Dharma (dhammaṃ) in the Saṅgha (saṅghe), and it should occur to you, ‘This venerable one rightly grasps both the meaning (atthañceva) and the expression (byañjanāni) and rightly brings them into connection,’ you should express delight and rejoice in his statement, saying, ‘Excellent (sādhu).’ Expressing delight and rejoicing in his statement, saying, ‘Excellent,’ you should say to him, ‘It’s a gain for us, friend (āvuso), a great gain, that we see a venerable one like you who has entered into the meaning (atthupetaṃ) and the expression (byañjanupeta)’."

The reason for permission granted (paccayānuññātakāraṇaṃ).
commentary_pali:
181.Tādisanti tumhādisaṃ. Atthupetanti atthena upetaṃ atthassa viññātāraṃ. Byañjanupetanti byañjanehi upetaṃ byañjanānaṃ viññātāraṃ. Evaṃ etaṃ bhikkhuṃ pasaṃsatha. Eso hi bhikkhu na tumhākaṃ sāvako nāma, buddho nāma esa cundāti. Iti bhagavā bahussutaṃ bhikkhuṃ attano ṭhāne ṭhapesi.

Paccayānuññātakāraṇādivaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
*Tādisa*nti: like you.

*Atthupeta*nti: endowed with meaning, understanding the meaning.

*Byañjanupeta*nti: endowed with letters, understanding the letters.

Thus, praise this *bhikkhu*.

This *bhikkhu* is not your disciple, but is named Buddha, this is Cunda.

Thus, the Blessed One established the learned *bhikkhu* in his own place.

Explanation of the reasons for permission, etc.

mula_pali:
182. ‘‘Na vo ahaṃ, cunda, diṭṭhadhammikānaṃyeva āsavānaṃ saṃvarāya dhammaṃ desemi. Na panāhaṃ, cunda, samparāyikānaṃyeva āsavānaṃ paṭighātāya dhammaṃ desemi. Diṭṭhadhammikānaṃ cevāhaṃ, cunda, āsavānaṃ saṃvarāya dhammaṃ desemi; samparāyikānañca āsavānaṃ paṭighātāya. Tasmātiha, cunda, yaṃ vo mayā cīvaraṃ anuññātaṃ, alaṃ vo taṃ – yāvadeva sītassa paṭighātāya, uṇhassa paṭighātāya, ḍaṃsamakasavātātapasarīsapa siriṃsapa (syā.) samphassānaṃ paṭighātāya, yāvadeva hirikopīnapaṭicchādanatthaṃ. Yo vo mayā piṇḍapāto anuññāto, alaṃ vo so yāvadeva imassa kāyassa ṭhitiyā yāpanāya vihiṃsūparatiyā brahmacariyānuggahāya, iti purāṇañca vedanaṃ paṭihaṅkhāmi, navañca vedanaṃ na uppādessāmi, yātrā ca me bhavissati anavajjatā ca phāsuvihāro ca cāti (bahūsu). Yaṃ vo mayā senāsanaṃ anuññātaṃ, alaṃ vo taṃ yāvadeva sītassa paṭighātāya, uṇhassa paṭighātāya, ḍaṃsamakasavātātapasarīsapasamphassānaṃ paṭighātāya, yāvadeva utuparissayavinodana paṭisallānārāmatthaṃ. Yo vo mayā gilānapaccayabhesajja parikkhāro anuññāto, alaṃ vo so yāvadeva uppannānaṃ veyyābādhikānaṃ vedanānaṃ paṭighātāya abyāpajjaparamatāya abyāpajjhaparamatāyāti (sī. syā. pī.), abyābajjhaparamatāya (?).

Sukhallikānuyogo
mula_english:
“Cunda, I do not teach you the Dharma only for the restraint of *āsavas* (influxes, effluents) in the present life (*dṛṣṭadhārmika*), nor do I teach you the Dharma only for warding off the *āsavas* in the afterlife (*samparāyika*). But I teach you the Dharma both for the restraint of *āsavas* in the present life (*dṛṣṭadhārmika*) and for the warding off of *āsavas* in the afterlife (*samparāyika*).

Therefore, Cunda, the robe (*cīvara*) I have allowed you is enough simply to counteract cold (*sīta*), to counteract heat (*uṇha*), to counteract the touch (*samphassa*) of flies (*ḍaṃsa*), mosquitoes (*makasa*), wind (*vāta*), sun (*ātapa*), & reptiles (*sarīsapa*); simply for the purpose of covering the parts of the body that cause shame (*hiri-kopīna-praticchādanārtha*).

The alms food (*piṇḍapāta*) I have allowed you is enough simply for the survival & continuance of this body (*kāya*), for ending its afflictions (*vihiṃsūparati*), for the support of the holy life (*brahmacarya*), thinking, ‘Thus will I destroy old feelings (*vedanā*) and not create new feelings. I will maintain myself, be blameless (*anavajjatā*), & live in comfort (*phāsuvihāra*)’

The lodgings (*senāsana*) I have allowed you are enough simply to counteract cold (*sīta*), to counteract heat (*uṇha*), to counteract the touch (*samphassa*) of flies (*ḍaṃsa*), mosquitoes (*makasa*), wind (*vāta*), sun (*ātapa*), & reptiles (*sarīsapa*); simply for protection from the inclemencies of weather (*utuparissayavinodana*) and for the enjoyment of seclusion (*pratisallānārāmattha*).

The medicinal requisites (*gilānapaccayabhesajja parikkhāra*) used for curing the sick that I have allowed you are enough simply to counteract any pains (*vedanā*) of illness that have arisen and for maximum freedom from disease (*abyāpajjaparamatā*).

Indulgence in pleasure.
commentary_pali:
182. Idāni tatopi uttaritaraṃ desanaṃ vaḍḍhento na vo ahaṃ, cundātiādimāha. Tattha diṭṭhadhammikā āsavā nāma idhaloke paccayahetu uppajjanakā āsavā. Samparāyikā āsavā nāma paraloke bhaṇḍanahetu uppajjanakā āsavā. Saṃvarāyāti yathā te na pavisanti, evaṃ pidahanāya. Paṭighātāyāti mūlaghātena paṭihananāya. Alaṃ vo taṃ yāvadeva sītassa paṭighātāyāti taṃ tumhākaṃ sītassa paṭighātāya samatthaṃ. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti, yaṃ vo mayā cīvaraṃ anuññātaṃ, taṃ pārupitvā dappaṃ vā mānaṃ vā kurumānā viharissathāti na anuññātaṃ, taṃ pana pārupitvā sītappaṭighātādīni katvā sukhaṃ samaṇadhammaṃ yoniso manasikāraṃ karissathāti anuññātaṃ. Yathā ca cīvaraṃ, evaṃ piṇḍapātādayopi. Anupadasaṃvaṇṇanā panettha visuddhimagge vuttanayeneva veditabbā.

Sukhallikānuyogādivaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
182. Now, further increasing the teaching, he said, "Not to you am I, Cunda," and so on.

There, the *diṭṭhadhammikā āsavā*, the "defilements relating to the immediately visible dharma," are those defilements that arise in this world due to causes and conditions.

The *samparāyikā āsavā*, the "defilements relating to the future life," are those defilements that arise in the next world due to causes of strife.

*Saṃvarāyā* means for guarding, just as they do not enter, so for covering.

*Paṭighātāyā* means for warding off, by means of striking at the root, for repelling.

*Alaṃ vo taṃ yāvadeva sītassa paṭighātāyā* means that is sufficient for you for warding off the cold. That is effective for you to ward off the cold.

This is said: that the robe (*cīvara*) which I have allowed you, it is not allowed that having put it on, you live making arrogance or pride. But it is allowed that having put it on, having done such things as warding off the cold, you will carefully and systematically attend to the *śramaṇa-dharma*, the qualities of a contemplative.

And as with the robe (*cīvara*), so also with alms-food (*piṇḍapāta*) and so on.

The word-by-word commentary here should be understood according to the method stated in the *Visuddhimagga* (Path of Purification).

Explanation of indulgence in pleasure and so on.

mula_pali:
183. ‘‘Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, cunda, vijjati yaṃ aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ vadeyyuṃ – ‘sukhallikānuyogamanuyuttā samaṇā sakyaputtiyā viharantī’ti. Evaṃvādino vadamānā (syā.), cunda, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evamassu vacanīyā – ‘katamo so , āvuso, sukhallikānuyogo? Sukhallikānuyogā hi bahū anekavihitā nānappakārakā’ti.

‘‘Cattārome, cunda, sukhallikānuyogā hīnā gammā pothujjanikā anariyā anatthasaṃhitā na nibbidāya na virāgāya na nirodhāya na upasamāya na abhiññāya na sambodhāya na nibbānāya saṃvattanti. Katame cattāro?

‘‘Idha, cunda, ekacco bālo pāṇe vadhitvā vadhitvā attānaṃ sukheti pīṇeti. Ayaṃ paṭhamo sukhallikānuyogo.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, cunda, idhekacco adinnaṃ ādiyitvā ādiyitvā attānaṃ sukheti pīṇeti. Ayaṃ dutiyo sukhallikānuyogo.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, cunda, idhekacco musā bhaṇitvā bhaṇitvā attānaṃ sukheti pīṇeti. Ayaṃ tatiyo sukhallikānuyogo.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, cunda, idhekacco pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappito samaṅgībhūto paricāreti. Ayaṃ catuttho sukhallikānuyogo.

‘‘Ime kho, cunda, cattāro sukhallikānuyogā hīnā gammā pothujjanikā anariyā anatthasaṃhitā na nibbidāya na virāgāya na nirodhāya na upasamāya na abhiññāya na sambodhāya na nibbānāya saṃvattanti.

‘‘Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, cunda, vijjati yaṃ aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ vadeyyuṃ – ‘‘ime cattāro sukhallikānuyoge anuyuttā samaṇā sakyaputtiyā viharantī’ti. Te vo te (sī. pī.) ‘māhevaṃ’ tissu vacanīyā. Na te vo sammā vadamānā vadeyyuṃ, abbhācikkheyyuṃ asatā abhūtena.

te (sī. pī.)
mula_english:
183. “Now, it’s possible, Cunda, that wanderers of other sects might say, ‘The Sakyan-son contemplatives live devoted to the devotion to pleasure ( *sukhallikānuyoga* ).’"

Those speaking thus, Cunda, are wanderers of other sects to whom you should say, 'What is that devotion to pleasure, friends? For devotions to pleasure are many, performed in various ways and of diverse kinds.'"

“There are these four devotions to pleasure, Cunda, that are base, vulgar, common, ignoble, unprofitable, that do not lead to disenchantment ( *nirbidāya* ), dispassion ( *virāgāya* ), cessation ( *nirodhāya* ), calming ( *upaśamāya* ), direct knowledge ( *abhijñāya* ), self-awakening ( *sambodhāya* ), or unbinding ( *nirbānāya* ). What are the four?

“Here, Cunda, a certain foolish man finds pleasure and rapture in killing living beings. This is the first devotion to pleasure (*sukhallikānuyoga*).

“Further, Cunda, a certain person finds pleasure & rapture for himself in taking what is not given ( *adinnaṃ ādiyitvā* ). This is the second devotion to pleasure (*sukhallikānuyogo*).

“Further, Cunda, a certain person finds pleasure & rapture for himself in telling lies. This is the third devotion to pleasure (*sukhallikānuyogo*).

“Further, Cunda, a certain person goes about endowed & provided with the five strings of sensuality ( *pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappito* ). This is the fourth devotion to pleasure (*sukhallikānuyogo*).

“These are the four devotions to pleasure, Cunda, that are base, vulgar, common, ignoble, unprofitable, that do not lead to disenchantment ( *nirbidāya* ), dispassion ( *virāgāya* ), cessation ( *nirodhāya* ), calming ( *upaśamāya* ), direct knowledge ( *abhijñāya* ), self-awakening ( *sambodhāya* ), or unbinding ( *nirbānāya* ).

“Now, it’s possible, Cunda, that wanderers of other sects might say, ‘The Sakyan-son contemplatives live devoted to these four devotions to pleasure (*sukhallikānuyoga*).’ They are to be told, ‘Not so!’ They would not be speaking rightly of you. They would be slandering you with what is unfactual & untrue.
commentary_pali: 183.Sukhallikānuyoganti sukhalliyanānuyogaṃ, sukhasevanādhimuttanti attho. Sukhetīti sukhitaṃ karoti. Pīṇetīti pīṇitaṃ thūlaṃ karoti.
commentary_english: 183. sukhallikānuyoganti: *sukhallikānuyogaṃ*, meaning *sukha-sevanādhimutti*. sukhetīti: [It] makes happy (*sukhitam karoti*). pīṇetīti: [It] makes [something] fat and coarse (*pīṇitaṃ thūlaṃ karoti*).

mula_pali:
184. ‘‘Cattārome, cunda, sukhallikānuyogā ekantanibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattanti. Katame cattāro?

‘‘Idha , cunda, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ayaṃ paṭhamo sukhallikānuyogo.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, cunda, bhikkhu vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā…pe… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ayaṃ dutiyo sukhallikānuyogo.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, cunda, bhikkhu pītiyā ca virāgā…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ayaṃ tatiyo sukhallikānuyogo.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, cunda, bhikkhu sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā…pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ayaṃ catuttho sukhallikānuyogo.

‘‘Ime kho, cunda, cattāro sukhallikānuyogā ekantanibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattanti.

‘‘Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, cunda, vijjati yaṃ aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ vadeyyuṃ – ‘‘ime cattāro sukhallikānuyoge anuyuttā samaṇā sakyaputtiyā viharantī’ti. Te vo ‘evaṃ’ tissu vacanīyā. Sammā te vo vadamānā vadeyyuṃ, na te vo abbhācikkheyyuṃ asatā abhūtena.

Sukhallikānuyogānisaṃso
mula_english:
184. “There are these four devotions to pleasure, Cunda, that lead exclusively to disenchantment ( *nirbidā*), dispassion ( *virāga*), cessation ( *nirodha*), calming ( *upaśamā*), direct knowledge (*abhijñā*), self-awakening (*saṃbodha*), & unbinding (*nirvāṇa*). What are the four?

“Here, Cunda, a *bhikkhu*, quite secluded from sensual pleasures ( *kāmehi*), secluded from unwholesome states ( *akusalehi dhammehi*), enters upon and abides in the first *jhāna*: rapture (*pīti*) and pleasure (*sukha*) born of seclusion (*vivekajaṃ*), accompanied by applied thought (*savitakkaṃ*) & sustained thought (*savicāraṃ*). This is the first devotion to pleasure (*sukhallikānuyoga*).

“Again, Cunda, with the stilling of applied and sustained thought (*vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā*), the *bhikkhu* enters and remains in the second *jhāna*. This is the second devotion to pleasure (*sukhallikānuyoga*).

“Again, Cunda, with the fading away as well of rapture (*pītiyā ca virāgā*), the *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the third *jhāna*. This is the third devotion to pleasure (*sukhallikānuyoga*).

“Again, Cunda, with the abandoning of pleasure (*sukha*) and pain (*dukkha*), the *bhikkhu* enters upon and abides in the fourth *jhāna*. This is the fourth devotion to pleasure (*sukhallikānuyoga*).

“These are the four devotions to pleasure (*sukhallikānuyogā*), Cunda, that lead exclusively to disenchantment ( *nirbidā*), dispassion ( *virāga*), cessation ( *nirodha*), calming ( *upaśamā*), direct knowledge (*abhijñā*), self-awakening (*saṃbodha*), & unbinding (*nirvāṇa*).

“Now, it is possible, Cunda, that wanderers of other sects might say: ‘The Sakyan-son contemplatives live devoted to these four devotions to pleasure (*sukhallikānuyoga*)’. They are to be told, ‘Not so!’ They would be speaking rightly of you. They would not be slandering you with what is unfactual & untrue.

The Benefit of Devotions to Pleasure

mula_pali:
185. ‘‘Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, cunda, vijjati, yaṃ aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ vadeyyuṃ – ‘ime panāvuso, cattāro sukhallikānuyoge anuyuttānaṃ viharataṃ kati phalāni katānisaṃsā pāṭikaṅkhā’ti? Evaṃvādino, cunda, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evamassu vacanīyā – ‘ime kho, āvuso, cattāro sukhallikānuyoge anuyuttānaṃ viharataṃ cattāri phalāni cattāro ānisaṃsā pāṭikaṅkhā. Katame cattāro? Idhāvuso, bhikkhu tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā sotāpanno hoti avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo. Idaṃ paṭhamaṃ phalaṃ, paṭhamo ānisaṃso. Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu tiṇṇaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā rāgadosamohānaṃ tanuttā sakadāgāmī hoti, sakideva imaṃ lokaṃ āgantvā dukkhassantaṃ karoti. Idaṃ dutiyaṃ phalaṃ, dutiyo ānisaṃso. Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu pañcannaṃ orambhāgiyānaṃ saṃyojanānaṃ parikkhayā opapātiko hoti, tattha parinibbāyī anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā. Idaṃ tatiyaṃ phalaṃ, tatiyo ānisaṃso. Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati. Idaṃ catutthaṃ phalaṃ catuttho ānisaṃso. Ime kho, āvuso, cattāro sukhallikānuyoge anuyuttānaṃ viharataṃ imāni cattāri phalāni, cattāro ānisaṃsā pāṭikaṅkhā’’ti.

Khīṇāsavaabhabbaṭhānaṃ
mula_english:
185. It is possible, Cunda, that wanderers of other sects might say thus: 'Friends, how many fruits and rewards are to be expected for those who live devoted to these four devotions to pleasure?'

Those wanderers of other sects saying that are to be told: 'Living devoted to these four devotions to pleasure, friends, four fruits, four rewards can be expected.

What are the four? Here, friends, a monk, with the wasting away of three fetters ( *saṃyojana*), is a stream-enterer ( *sotāpanna*), certain, never again destined for the lower realms, headed for self-awakening ( *sambodhiparāyaṇa*). This is the first fruit ( *phala*), the first reward ( *ānisaṃsa*).

Further, friends, the monk—with the wasting away of three fetters, and with the attenuation of passion ( *rāga*), aversion ( *dosa*), & delusion ( *moha*)—is a once-returner ( *sakadāgāmī*); who, on returning only once more to this world, will make an ending to stress ( *dukkha*). This is the second fruit, the second reward.

Further, the monk—with the wasting away of the five lower fetters—is due to arise spontaneously ( *opapātika*), there to totally unbind ( *parinibbāyī*), destined never again to return from that world. This is the third fruit, the third reward.

Further, the monk—with the ending of effluents ( *āsava*)—enters & remains in the effluent-free awareness-release ( *cetovimutti*) & discernment-release ( *paññāvimutti*), having directly known & realized it for himself right in the here & now. This is the fourth fruit the fourth reward.

Living devoted to these four devotions to pleasure, friends, these four fruits, these four rewards can be expected.’

Condition of the destruction of the corruptions, and being incapable.

mula_pali:
186. ‘‘Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, cunda, vijjati yaṃ aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ vadeyyuṃ – ‘aṭṭhitadhammā samaṇā sakyaputtiyā viharantī’ti. Evaṃvādino, cunda, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evamassu vacanīyā – ‘atthi kho, āvuso, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena sāvakānaṃ dhammā desitā paññattā yāvajīvaṃ anatikkamanīyā. Seyyathāpi, āvuso, indakhīlo vā ayokhīlo vā gambhīranemo sunikhāto acalo asampavedhī. Evameva kho, āvuso, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena sāvakānaṃ dhammā desitā paññattā yāvajīvaṃ anatikkamanīyā. Yo so, āvuso, bhikkhu arahaṃ khīṇāsavo vusitavā katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano sammadaññā vimutto, abhabbo so nava ṭhānāni ajjhācarituṃ. Abhabbo, āvuso, khīṇāsavo bhikkhu sañcicca pāṇaṃ jīvitā voropetuṃ; abhabbo khīṇāsavo bhikkhu adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādiyituṃ; abhabbo khīṇāsavo bhikkhu methunaṃ dhammaṃ paṭisevituṃ; abhabbo khīṇāsavo bhikkhu sampajānamusā bhāsituṃ; abhabbo khīṇāsavo bhikkhu sannidhikārakaṃ kāme paribhuñjituṃ seyyathāpi pubbe āgārikabhūto; abhabbo khīṇāsavo bhikkhu chandāgatiṃ gantuṃ; abhabbo khīṇāsavo bhikkhu dosāgatiṃ gantuṃ; abhabbo khīṇāsavo bhikkhu mohāgatiṃ gantuṃ; abhabbo khīṇāsavo bhikkhu bhayāgatiṃ gantuṃ. Yo so, āvuso, bhikkhu arahaṃ khīṇāsavo vusitavā katakaraṇīyo ohitabhāro anuppattasadattho parikkhīṇabhavasaṃyojano sammadaññā vimutto, abhabbo so imāni nava ṭhānāni ajjhācaritu’’nti.

Pañhābyākaraṇaṃ
mula_english:
186. Now, Cunda, it is possible that wanderers of other sects might say: “The *śramaṇas* who are followers of the Sakyan live attached to the abandoned *dharmas*.”

Cunda, the wanderers of other sects who say this should be addressed thus: ‘Friends, there are *dharmas* taught and laid down by that Blessed One who knows, who sees, the *arhat*, the perfectly enlightened one, which are not to be transgressed by his disciples as long as they live.

Just as, friends, a gate post *Indrakhīla* or iron post *Ayokhīla* with a deep base is well planted, firm, and unshakeable.

In the same way, friends, there are *dharmas* taught and laid down by that Blessed One who knows, who sees, the *arhat*, the perfectly enlightened one, which are not to be transgressed by his disciples as long as they live.

That monk, friends, who is an *arhat*, one whose outflows are destroyed (*khīṇāsava*), who has lived the holy life, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, attained his own true goal, utterly destroyed the fetters of existence, and is liberated through perfect knowledge (*sammadaññā vimutto*) is incapable of transgressing these nine principles.

A *bhikṣu* whose *āsavas* are destroyed (*khīṇāsavo*) is incapable of intentionally taking the life of a living being; a *bhikṣu* whose *āsavas* are destroyed (*khīṇāsavo*) is incapable of taking what is not given, known as theft; a *bhikṣu* whose *āsavas* are destroyed (*khīṇāsavo*) is incapable of engaging in sexual intercourse (*maithuna dharma*); a *bhikṣu* whose *āsavas* are destroyed (*khīṇāsavo*) is incapable of uttering a deliberate lie; a *bhikṣu* whose *āsavas* are destroyed (*khīṇāsavo*) is incapable of enjoying stored-up sensual pleasures as he did when he was formerly a householder; a *bhikṣu* whose *āsavas* are destroyed (*khīṇāsavo*) is incapable of following the path of desire (*chandāgati*); a *bhikṣu* whose *āsavas* are destroyed (*khīṇāsavo*) is incapable of following the path of hatred (*dosāgati*); a *bhikṣu* whose *āsavas* are destroyed (*khīṇāsavo*) is incapable of following the path of delusion (*mohāgati*); a *bhikṣu* whose *āsavas* are destroyed (*khīṇāsavo*) is incapable of following the path of fear (*bhayāgati*).

That monk, friends, who is an *arhat*, one whose outflows are destroyed (*khīṇāsava*), who has lived the holy life, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, attained his own true goal, utterly destroyed the fetters of existence, and is liberated through perfect knowledge (*sammadaññā vimutto*) is incapable of transgressing these nine principles.”

Questions and Answers
commentary_pali:
186.Aṭṭhitadhammāti naṭṭhitasabhāvā. Jivhā no atthīti yaṃ yaṃ icchanti, taṃ taṃ kathenti, kadāci maggaṃ kathenti, kadāci phalaṃ kadāci nibbānanti adhippāyo. Jānatāti sabbaññutaññāṇena jānantena. Passatāti pañcahi cakkhūhi passantena. Gambhīranemoti gambhīrabhūmiṃ anupaviṭṭho. Sunikhātoti suṭṭhu nikhāto. Evameva kho, āvusoti evaṃ khīṇāsavo abhabbo nava ṭhānāni ajjhācarituṃ. Tasmiṃ anajjhācāro acalo asampavedhī. Tattha sañcicca pāṇaṃ jīvitā voropanādīsu sotāpannādayopi abhabbā. Sannidhikārakaṃ kāme paribhuñjitunti vatthukāme ca kilesakāme ca sannidhiṃ katvā paribhuñjituṃ. Seyyathāpi pubbe agārikabhūtoti yathā pubbe gihibhūto paribhuñjati, evaṃ paribhuñjituṃ abhabbo.

Pañhabyākaraṇavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
186. "Aṭṭhitadhammā" means one whose nature is not established.

"Because they have a tongue, whatever they wish, that they declare; sometimes they declare the path *mārga*, sometimes the fruit *phala*, and sometimes nirvāṇa, this is the meaning.

"Jānatā" means knowing with the knowledge of omniscience *sarvajñuta-jñāna*.

"Passatā" means seeing with the five eyes *pañcahi cakṣūhi*.

"Gambhīranemo" means one who has entered a profound state *gambhīrabhūmi*.

"Sunikhāto" means well-established.

"Evameva kho, āvuso" means thus, a person with destroyed outflows *khīṇāsava* is incapable *abhabbo* of committing nine offenses *nava ṭhānāni ajjhācarituṃ*.

In that, there is no transgression *anajjhācāro*, he is unwavering *acalo*, and unshakeable *asampavedhī*.

There, even those who have entered the stream *sotāpanna*, and so forth, are incapable *abhabbā* of intentionally taking life *pāṇaṃ jīvitā voropanādīsu*.

"Sannidhikārakaṃ kāme paribhuñjituṃ" means to enjoy objects of desire *vatthukāme* and defiled desires *kilesakāme* by accumulating them *ca sannidhiṃ katvā paribhuñjituṃ*.

"Seyyathāpi pubbe agārikabhūto" means just as formerly one who was a householder would enjoy, so he is incapable *abhabbo* of enjoying thus *evaṃ paribhuñjituṃ*.

Explanation of Questions.

mula_pali: 187. ‘‘Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, cunda, vijjati, yaṃ aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ vadeyyuṃ – ‘atītaṃ kho addhānaṃ ārabbha samaṇo gotamo atīrakaṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ paññapeti, no ca kho anāgataṃ addhānaṃ ārabbha atīrakaṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ paññapeti, tayidaṃ kiṃsu tayidaṃ kathaṃsū’ti? Te ca aññatitthiyā paribbājakā aññavihitakena ñāṇadassanena aññavihitakaṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ paññapetabbaṃ maññanti yathariva bālā abyattā. Atītaṃ kho, cunda, addhānaṃ ārabbha tathāgatassa satānusāri ñāṇaṃ hoti; so yāvatakaṃ ākaṅkhati tāvatakaṃ anussarati. Anāgatañca kho addhānaṃ ārabbha tathāgatassa bodhijaṃ ñāṇaṃ uppajjati – ‘ayamantimā jāti, natthidāni punabbhavo’ti. ‘Atītaṃ cepi, cunda, hoti abhūtaṃ atacchaṃ anatthasaṃhitaṃ, na taṃ tathāgato byākaroti. Atītaṃ cepi, cunda, hoti bhūtaṃ tacchaṃ anatthasaṃhitaṃ, tampi tathāgato na byākaroti. Atītaṃ cepi cunda, hoti bhūtaṃ tacchaṃ atthasaṃhitaṃ, tatra kālaññū tathāgato hoti tassa pañhassa veyyākaraṇāya. Anāgataṃ cepi, cunda, hoti abhūtaṃ atacchaṃ anatthasaṃhitaṃ, na taṃ tathāgato byākaroti…pe… tassa pañhassa veyyākaraṇāya. Paccuppannaṃ cepi, cunda, hoti abhūtaṃ atacchaṃ anatthasaṃhitaṃ, na taṃ tathāgato byākaroti. Paccuppannaṃ cepi, cunda, hoti bhūtaṃ tacchaṃ anatthasaṃhitaṃ, tampi tathāgato na byākaroti. Paccuppannaṃ cepi, cunda, hoti bhūtaṃ tacchaṃ atthasaṃhitaṃ, tatra kālaññū tathāgato hoti tassa pañhassa veyyākaraṇāya.
mula_english:
187.
“Now, it’s possible, Cunda, that some wanderers of other sects might say, ‘Gotama the *śramaṇa* describes unlimited knowledge and vision (*jñānadarśana*) with regard to the past (*atītaṃ kho addhānaṃ ārabbha*), but doesn’t describe unlimited knowledge and vision with regard to the future (*anāgataṃ addhānaṃ ārabbha*). What is this? How is this?’ Those wanderers of other sects construe the sort of knowing that is not knowledge and vision (*jñānadarśana*) to be the sort of knowing that is knowledge and vision, just like inexperienced fools (*bālā abyattā*).

The *Tathāgata’s* memory-&-recollection knowledge (*satānusāri ñāṇaṃ*) with regard to the past (*atītaṃ kho, cunda, addhānaṃ ārabbha*) is such that he recollects whatever he wants (*so yāvatakaṃ ākaṅkhati tāvatakaṃ anussarati*).

The *Tathāgata’s* *bodhi*-born knowledge (*bodhijaṃ ñāṇaṃ*) with regard to the future arises (*anāgatañca kho addhānaṃ ārabbha tathāgatassa*): ‘This is the last birth. There is now no further becoming (*natthidāni punabbhavo’ti*.’

“With regard to what is past: If it is unfactual (*abhūtaṃ*), untrue (*atacchaṃ*), & unbeneficial (*anatthasaṃhitaṃ*), the *Tathāgata* does not declare it (*na taṃ tathāgato byākaroti*).

If it is factual (*bhūtaṃ*), true (*tacchaṃ*), but unbeneficial (*anatthasaṃhitaṃ*), the *Tathāgata* does not declare it.

If it is factual (*bhūtaṃ*), true (*tacchaṃ*), & beneficial (*atthasaṃhitaṃ*), the *Tathāgata* has a sense of the proper time (*kālaññū*) for giving the answer to that question.

“With regard to what is future… If it is unfactual (*abhūtaṃ*), untrue (*atacchaṃ*), & unbeneficial (*anatthasaṃhitaṃ*), the *Tathāgata* does not declare it…for giving the answer to that question.

“With regard to what is present: If it is unfactual (*abhūtaṃ*), untrue (*atacchaṃ*), & unbeneficial (*anatthasaṃhitaṃ*), the *Tathāgata* does not declare it.

If it is factual (*bhūtaṃ*), true (*tacchaṃ*), but unbeneficial (*anatthasaṃhitaṃ*), the *Tathāgata* does not declare it.

If it is factual (*bhūtaṃ*), true (*tacchaṃ*), & beneficial (*atthasaṃhitaṃ*), the *Tathāgata* has a sense of the proper time (*kālaññū*) for giving the answer to that question.
commentary_pali:
187. Agāramajjhe vasantā hi sotāpannādayo yāvajīvaṃ gihibyañjanena tiṭṭhanti. Khīṇāsavo pana arahattaṃ patvāva manussabhūto parinibbāti vā pabbajati vā. Cātumahārājikādīsu kāmāvacaradevesu muhuttampi na tiṭṭhati. Kasmā? Vivekaṭṭhānassa abhāvā. Bhummadevattabhāve pana ṭhito arahattaṃ patvāpi tiṭṭhati. Tassa vasena ayaṃ pañho āgato. Bhinnadosattā panassa bhikkhubhāvo veditabbo. Atīrakanti atīraṃ aparicchedaṃ mahantaṃ. No ca kho anāgatanti anāgataṃ pana addhānaṃ ārabbha evaṃ na paññapeti, atītameva maññe samaṇo gotamo jānāti, na anāgataṃ. Tathā hissa atīte aḍḍhachaṭṭhasatajātakānussaraṇaṃ paññāyati. Anāgate evaṃ bahuṃ anussaraṇaṃ na paññāyatīti imamatthaṃ maññamānā evaṃ vadeyyuṃ. Tayidaṃ kiṃ sūti anāgate apaññāpanaṃ kiṃ nu kho? Kathaṃsūti kena nu kho kāraṇena ajānantoyeva nu kho anāgataṃ nānussarati, ananussaritukāmatāya nānussaratīti. Aññavihitakena ñāṇadassanenāti paccakkhaṃ viya katvā dassanasamatthatāya dassanabhūtena ñāṇena aññatthavihitakena ñāṇena aññaṃ ārabbha pavattena, aññavihitakaṃ aññaṃ ārabbha pavattamānaṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ saṅgāhetabbaṃ paññāpetabbaṃ maññanti. Te hi carato ca tiṭṭhato ca suttassa ca jāgarassa ca satataṃ samitaṃ ñāṇadassanaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ maññanti, tādisañca ñāṇaṃ nāma natthi. Tasmā yathariva bālā abyattā, evaṃ maññantīti veditabbo.

Satānusārīti pubbenivāsānussatisampayuttakaṃ. Yāvatakaṃ ākaṅkhatīti yattakaṃ ñātuṃ icchati, tattakaṃ jānissāmīti ñāṇaṃ pesesi. Athassa dubbalapattapuṭe pakkhandanārāco viya appaṭihataṃ anivāritaṃ ñāṇaṃ gacchati, tena yāvatakaṃ ākaṅkhati tāvatakaṃ anussarati. Bodhijanti bodhimūle jātaṃ. Ñāṇaṃ uppajjatīti catumaggañāṇaṃ uppajjati. Ayamantimā jātīti tena ñāṇena jātimūlassa pahīnattā puna ayamantimā jāti. Natthidāni punabbhavoti aparampi ñāṇaṃ uppajjati. Anatthasaṃhitanti na idhalokatthaṃ vā paralokatthaṃ vā nissitaṃ. Na taṃ tathāgato byākarotīti taṃ bhāratayuddhasītāharaṇasadisaṃ aniyyānikakathaṃ tathāgato na katheti. Bhūtaṃ tacchaṃ anatthasaṃhitanti rājakathāditiracchānakathaṃ. Kālaññū tathāgato hotīti kālaṃ jānāti. Sahetukaṃ sakāraṇaṃ katvā yuttapattakāleyeva katheti.

Satānusārī Yāvatakaṃ ākaṅkhatī Bodhija Ñāṇaṃ uppajjatī Ayamantimā jātī Natthidāni punabbhavo Anatthasaṃhita Na taṃ tathāgato byākarotī Bhūtaṃ tacchaṃ anatthasaṃhita Kālaññū tathāgato hotī
commentary_english:
187. Living in a house, the stream-enterers and so on remain householders as long as they live.

The one with destroyed asavas, having attained arhatship, as a human being, either attains final nirvāṇa or goes forth.

He does not remain even for a moment in the Cātumahārājika heavens and so on, in the desire-realm deities.

Why? Because of the absence of a place of seclusion (viveka).

However, one who is established in the state of being a terrestrial deity, having attained arhatship, remains.

Because of that reason, this question has come.

Because of the difference in faults, the state of being a *bhikkhu* should be understood.

*Atīraka* means boundless, unlimited, great.

*No ca kho anāgata* means, regarding the future, he does not declare thus, "I think only the *samaṇa* Gotama knows the past, not the future."

Thus, for him, in the past, the recollection of the Aḍḍhachaṭṭhasata Birth Stories (*jātaka*) is known.

In the future, such a great recollection is not known; thinking this, they might say thus.

*Tayidaṃ kiṃ sū* means, what is this non-declaration regarding the future? *Kathaṃsū* means, by what cause, not knowing, does he not recollect the future, or does he not recollect due to a desire not to recollect?

*Aññavihitakena ñāṇadassanenā* means, having made [it] as if directly perceived, by the knowledge (jñāna) that is the seeing (dassana), due to the capability of seeing, by the knowledge (jñāna) that is arranged elsewhere, by the knowledge (jñāna) that is occurring concerning something else, the knowledge-and-seeing (ñāṇadassana) that is arranged elsewhere, that is occurring concerning something else, they think should be gathered and declared.

They think that the knowledge-and-seeing (ñāṇadassana) that is constantly and always present for those who are walking, standing, sleeping, and waking is continuous, but such knowledge does not exist.

Therefore, just as infants [are] unskilled, so it should be understood that they think.

*Satānusārī* is connected with the recollection of former dwellings.

*Yāvatakaṃ ākaṅkhatī* means, “to whatever extent he desires to know, to that extent I will know,” he sends forth knowledge (jñāna).

Then, for him, in a weak bowl made of leaves, like an arrow that is shot forth, unimpeded, unrestricted knowledge (jñāna) goes; therefore, to whatever extent he desires, to that extent he recollects.

*Bodhija* means born at the foot of the *bodhi* tree.

*Ñāṇaṃ uppajjatī* means the fourfold path-knowledge (catumaggañāṇa) arises.

*Ayamantimā jātī* means, by that knowledge (jñāna), because the root of birth is abandoned, this is the last birth.

*Natthidāni punabbhavo* means another knowledge (*ñāṇa*) arises.

*Anatthasaṃhita* means not dependent on benefit in this world or benefit in another world.

*Na taṃ tathāgato byākarotī* means the *Tathāgata* does not speak of that which is like the Bhārata war or the abduction of Sītā, a story that does not lead to liberation.

*Bhūtaṃ tacchaṃ anatthasaṃhita* means talk of kings and so forth, animal talk.

*Kālaññū tathāgato hotī* means the *Tathāgata* knows the time.

Having made [it] with cause and reason, he speaks at the proper time.

mula_pali:
188. ‘‘Iti kho, cunda, atītānāgatapaccuppannesu dhammesu tathāgato kālavādī kālavādī saccavādī (syā.) bhūtavādī atthavādī dhammavādī vinayavādī, tasmā ‘tathāgato’ti vuccati. Yañca kho, cunda, sadevakassa lokassa samārakassa sabrahmakassa sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya diṭṭhaṃ sutaṃ mutaṃ viññātaṃ pattaṃ pariyesitaṃ anuvicaritaṃ manasā, sabbaṃ tathāgatena abhisambuddhaṃ, tasmā ‘tathāgato’ti vuccati. Yañca, cunda, rattiṃ tathāgato anuttaraṃ sammāsambodhiṃ abhisambujjhati, yañca rattiṃ anupādisesāya nibbānadhātuyā parinibbāyati, yaṃ etasmiṃ antare bhāsati lapati niddisati. Sabbaṃ taṃ tatheva hoti no aññathā, tasmā ‘tathāgato’ti vuccati. Yathāvādī, cunda, tathāgato tathākārī, yathākārī tathāvādī. Iti yathāvādī tathākārī, yathākārī tathāvādī, tasmā ‘tathāgato’ti vuccati. Sadevake loke, cunda, samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya tathāgato abhibhū anabhibhūto aññadatthudaso vasavattī, tasmā ‘tathāgato’ti vuccati.

Abyākataṭṭhānaṃ
mula_english:
“Thus, Cunda, with regard to things that are past, future, and present, the *tathāgata* is one who speaks at the proper time (*kālavādī*), speaks what is true, speaks what is factual, speaks the meaning (*atthavādī*), speaks the *dharma* (*dhammavādī*), speaks *vinaya* (*vinayavādī*). Therefore he is called the *tathāgata*.

“Cunda, whatever in this world—with its *devas*, *Māras*, & *Brahmās*, this generation with its contemplatives & *brāhmaṇas*, its royalty & common people—is seen, heard, sensed, cognized, attained, sought after, pondered by the intellect, that has been fully awakened to by the *tathāgata*. Therefore he is called the *tathāgata*.

“Cunda, from the night when the *tathāgata* fully awakens to the unsurpassed right self-awakening (*sammāsambodhi*) until the night he totally unbinds in the unbinding property (*nirvāṇadhātu*) with no fuel remaining (*anupādisesāya*), whatever the *tathāgata* has said, spoken, explained, all that is just so (*tatheva*) and not otherwise (*aññathā*). Therefore he is called the *tathāgata*.

“The *tathāgata* is one who does in line with what he teaches (*yathāvādī*), one who teaches in line with what he does (*tathākārī*). Because he is one who does in line with what he teaches, one who teaches in line with what he does, he is thus called the *tathāgata*.

“In this world with its *devas*, *Māras*, & *Brahmās*, this generation with its contemplatives & *brāhmaṇas*, its royalty & common people, the *tathāgata* is the unconquered conqueror (*abhibhū anabhibhūto*), all-seeing (*aññadatthudaso*), the wielder of power (*vasavattī*). Therefore he is called the *tathāgata*.

The Topic of the Unexplained. (*abyākataṭṭhānaṃ*)
commentary_pali:
188.Tasmā tathāgatoti vuccatīti yathā yathā gaditabbaṃ, tathā tatheva gadanato dakārassa takāraṃ katvā tathāgatoti vuccatīti attho. Diṭṭhanti rūpāyatanaṃ. Sutanti saddāyatanaṃ. Mutanti mutvā patvā gahetabbato gandhāyatanaṃ rasāyatanaṃ phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ. Viññātanti sukhadukkhādidhammāyatanaṃ. Pattanti pariyesitvā vā apariyesitvā vā pattaṃ. Pariyesitanti pattaṃ vā apattaṃ vā pariyesitaṃ. Anuvicaritaṃ manasāti cittena anusañcaritaṃ. ‘‘Tathāgatena abhisambuddha’’nti iminā etaṃ dasseti, yañhi aparimāṇāsu lokadhātūsu imassa sadevakassa lokassa nīlaṃ pītakantiādi rūpārammaṇaṃ cakkhudvāre āpāthamāgacchati, ‘‘ayaṃ satto imasmiṃ khaṇe imaṃ nāma rūpārammaṇaṃ disvā sumano vā dummano vā majjhatto vā jāto’’ti sabbaṃ taṃ tathāgatassa evaṃ abhisambuddhaṃ . Tathā yaṃ aparimāṇāsu lokadhātūsu imassa sadevakassa lokassa bherisaddo mudiṅgasaddotiādi saddārammaṇaṃ sotadvāre āpāthamāgacchati. Mūlagandho tacagandhotiādi gandhārammaṇaṃ ghānadvāre āpāthamāgacchati. Mūlaraso khandharasotiādi rasārammaṇaṃ jivhādvāre āpāthamāgacchati. Kakkhaḷaṃ mudukantiādi pathavīdhātutejodhātuvāyodhātubhedaṃ phoṭṭhabbārammaṇaṃ kāyadvāre āpāthamāgacchati. ‘‘Ayaṃ satto imasmiṃ khaṇe imaṃ nāma phoṭṭhabbārammaṇaṃ phusitvā sumano vā dummano vā majjhatto vā jāto’’ti sabbaṃ taṃ tathāgatassa evaṃ abhisambuddhaṃ. Tathā yaṃ aparimāṇāsu lokadhātūsu imassa sadevakassa lokassa sukhadukkhādibhedaṃ dhammārammaṇaṃ manodvārassa āpāthamāgacchati, ‘‘ayaṃ satto imasmiṃ khaṇe idaṃ nāma dhammārammaṇaṃ vijānitvā sumano vā dummano vā majjhatto vā jāto’’ti sabbaṃ taṃ tathāgatassa evaṃ abhisambuddhaṃ.

Yañhi , cunda, imesaṃ sattānaṃ diṭṭhaṃ sutaṃ mutaṃ viññātaṃ tattha tathāgatena adiṭṭhaṃ vā asutaṃ vā amutaṃ vā aviññātaṃ vā natthi. Imassa mahājanassa pariyesitvā pattampi atthi, pariyesitvā appattampi atthi. Apariyesitvā pattampi atthi, apariyesitvā appattampi atthi. Sabbampi taṃ tathāgatassa appattaṃ nāma natthi, ñāṇena asacchikataṃ nāma. ‘‘Tasmā tathāgatoti vuccatī’’ti. Yaṃ yathā lokena gataṃ tassa tatheva gatattā ‘‘tathāgato’’ti vuccati. Pāḷiyaṃ pana abhisambuddhanti vuttaṃ, taṃ gatasaddena ekatthaṃ. Iminā nayena sabbavāresu ‘‘tathāgato’’ti nigamanassa attho veditabbo, tassa yutti brahmajāle tathāgatasaddavitthāre vuttāyeva.

brahmajāle

Abyākataṭṭhānavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
188. Therefore, he is called the *tathāgata*.
Just as it should be spoken, so it is said; from speaking, having made the *takāra* from the *dakāra*, therefore, it is said that he is the *tathāgata*.
*Diṭṭha* means the *rūpāyatana* (sense-sphere of forms).
*Suta* means the *saddāyatana* (sense-sphere of sounds).
*Muta* means, having sensed, having attained, because it is apprehended, the *gandhāyatana* (sense-sphere of smells), the *rasāyatana* (sense-sphere of tastes), the *phoṭṭhabbāyatana* (sense-sphere of tangibles).
*Viññāta* means the *sukhadukkhādidhammāyatanaṃ* (sense-sphere of phenomena relating to pleasure, pain, etc.).
*Patta* means either by seeking, or without seeking, it is attained (*pattaṃ*).
*Pariyesita* means either attained (*pattaṃ*) or unattained (*apattaṃ*) by seeking (*pariyesitaṃ*).
*Anuvicaritaṃ manasā* means it is mentally traversed by the mind (*cittena anusañcaritaṃ*).

“The *tathāgata* is completely awakened (*abhisambuddha*)” is what this shows. Namely, in the immeasurable world-systems (*lokadhātūsu*), to this world together with the *devas* (*sadevakassa lokassa*), blue, yellow, and so forth—the *rūpārammaṇa* (object of visual form) comes into the range (*āpāthamāgacchati*) of the eye-door (*cakkhudvāre*); “This being (*satto*), in this moment (*khaṇe*), having seen this such-and-such *rūpārammaṇa* (object of visual form), has been born pleasant (*sumano*), or unpleasant (*dummano*), or neutral (*majjhatto*)”—all that is thus completely awakened to the *tathāgata* (*tathāgatassa evaṃ abhisambuddhaṃ*).

Similarly, that which, in the immeasurable world-systems (*lokadhātūsu*), to this world together with the *devas* (*sadevakassa lokassa*), the sound of the kettledrum, the sound of the *mudiṅga*, and so forth—the *saddārammaṇa* (object of sound) comes into the range (*āpāthamāgacchati*) of the ear-door (*sotadvāre*).

The root-smell, the bark-smell, and so forth—the *gandhārammaṇa* (object of smell) comes into the range (*āpāthamāgacchati*) of the nose-door (*ghānadvāre*).

The root-taste, the trunk-taste, and so forth—the *rasārammaṇa* (object of taste) comes into the range (*āpāthamāgacchati*) of the tongue-door (*jivhādvāre*).

Roughness, softness, and so forth—the earth-element, fire-element, air-element division—the *phoṭṭhabbārammaṇa* (object of tactile sensation) comes into the range (*āpāthamāgacchati*) of the body-door (*kāyadvāre*).

“This being (*satto*), in this moment (*khaṇe*), having touched this such-and-such *phoṭṭhabbārammaṇa* (object of tactile sensation), has been born pleasant (*sumano*), or unpleasant (*dummano*), or neutral (*majjhatto*)”—all that is thus completely awakened to the *tathāgata* (*tathāgatassa evaṃ abhisambuddhaṃ*).

Similarly, that which, in the immeasurable world-systems (*lokadhātūsu*), to this world together with the *devas* (*sadevakassa lokassa*), pleasure, pain, and so forth division—the *dhammārammaṇa* (object of phenomena) comes into the range (*āpāthamāgacchati*) of the mind-door (*manodvārassa*), “This being (*satto*), in this moment (*khaṇe*), having cognized this such-and-such *dhammārammaṇa* (object of phenomena), has been born pleasant (*sumano*), or unpleasant (*dummano*), or neutral (*majjhatto*)”—all that is thus completely awakened to the *tathāgata* (*tathāgatassa evaṃ abhisambuddhaṃ*).

Namely, Cunda, to these beings (*imesaṃ sattānaṃ*), what is seen (*diṭṭhaṃ*), heard (*sutaṃ*), sensed (*mutaṃ*), cognized (*viññātaṃ*) there, nothing is unseen (*adiṭṭhaṃ*), or unheard (*asutaṃ*), or unsensed (*amutaṃ*), or uncognized (*aviññātaṃ*) by the *tathāgata*.
To this great multitude (*imassa mahājanassa*), having sought, there is attainment (*pattampi atthi*); having sought, there is non-attainment (*appattampi atthi*).
Without seeking, there is attainment (*pattampi atthi*); without seeking, there is non-attainment (*appattampi atthi*).
All of that, there is nothing un-attained by the *tathāgata* (*tathāgatassa appattaṃ nāma natthi*), namely, un-experienced by knowledge (*ñāṇena asacchikataṃ nāma*).
‘‘Therefore, he is called the *tathāgata* (*tasmā tathāgatoti vuccatī*)’’.
That which is gone to by the world (*yaṃ yathā lokena gataṃ*), because of his having gone to that in just that way (*tassa tatheva gatattā*), ‘‘he is called the *tathāgata* (*tathāgato’’ti vuccati*)’’.
In the *pāḷi*, however, it is said completely awakened (*abhisambuddhanti vuttaṃ*); that is one in meaning with gone to (*gatasaddena ekatthaṃ*).
By this method (*iminā nayena*), in all instances (*sabbavāresu*), the meaning of the conclusion ‘‘*tathāgato* (*tathāgato’’ti nigamanassa attho*),’ is to be understood (*veditabbo*); its reasoning (*tassa yutti*) is stated in detail about the word *tathāgata* (*tathāgatasaddavitthāre vuttāyeva*) in the *brahmajāla*.

*brahmajāle*
Explanation of the Unexplained

mula_pali:
189. ‘‘Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, cunda, vijjati yaṃ aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ vadeyyuṃ – ‘kiṃ nu kho, āvuso, hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti? Evaṃvādino, cunda, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evamassu vacanīyā – ‘abyākataṃ kho, āvuso, bhagavatā – ‘‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’’’nti.

‘‘Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, cunda, vijjati, yaṃ aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ vadeyyuṃ – ‘kiṃ panāvuso, na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti? Evaṃvādino, cunda, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evamassu vacanīyā – ‘etampi kho, āvuso, bhagavatā abyākataṃ – ‘‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’’’nti.

‘‘Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, cunda, vijjati, yaṃ aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ vadeyyuṃ – ‘kiṃ panāvuso, hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti? Evaṃvādino, cunda, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evamassu vacanīyā – ‘abyākataṃ kho etaṃ, āvuso, bhagavatā – ‘‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’’’nti.

‘‘Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, cunda, vijjati, yaṃ aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ vadeyyuṃ – ‘kiṃ panāvuso, neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti? Evaṃvādino, cunda, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evamassu vacanīyā – ‘etampi kho, āvuso, bhagavatā abyākataṃ – ‘‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’’’nti.

‘‘Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, cunda, vijjati, yaṃ aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ vadeyyuṃ – ‘kasmā panetaṃ, āvuso, samaṇena gotamena abyākata’nti? Evaṃvādino, cunda, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evamassu vacanīyā – ‘na hetaṃ, āvuso, atthasaṃhitaṃ na dhammasaṃhitaṃ na ādibrahmacariyakaṃ na nibbidāya na virāgāya na nirodhāya na upasamāya na abhiññāya na sambodhāya na nibbānāya saṃvattati, tasmā taṃ bhagavatā abyākata’nti.

Byākataṭṭhānaṃ
mula_english:
189. It is possible, Cunda, that wanderers of other sects might say this: ‘But, friend, does the *tathāgata* exist after death (*tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā*)? Only this is true, anything otherwise is worthless.’ The wanderers of other sects who say this should be told: ‘But, friend, this is undeclared by the Blessed One: ‘The *tathāgata* exists after death (*tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā*): only this is true, anything otherwise is worthless."’

It is possible, Cunda, that wanderers of other sects might say this: ‘But, friend, does the *tathāgata* not exist after death (*tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā*)? Only this is true, anything otherwise is worthless.’ The wanderers of other sects who say this should be told: ‘But, friend, this is undeclared by the Blessed One: ‘The *tathāgata* does not exist after death (*tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā*): only this is true, anything otherwise is worthless."’

It is possible, Cunda, that wanderers of other sects might say this: ‘But, friend, does the *tathāgata* both exist and not exist after death (*tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā*)? Only this is true, anything otherwise is worthless.’ The wanderers of other sects who say this should be told: ‘But, friend, this is undeclared by the Blessed One: ‘The *tathāgata* both exists and does not exist after death (*tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā*): only this is true, anything otherwise is worthless."’

It is possible, Cunda, that wanderers of other sects might say this: ‘But, friend, does the *tathāgata* neither exist nor not exist after death (*tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā*)? Only this is true, anything otherwise is worthless.’ The wanderers of other sects who say this should be told: ‘But, friend, this is undeclared by the Blessed One: ‘The *tathāgata* neither exists nor does not exist after death (*tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā*): only this is true, anything otherwise is worthless."’

It is possible, Cunda, that wanderers of other sects might say this: ‘But why, friend, is this undeclared by the *samaṇa* Gotama?’ The wanderers of other sects who say this should be told: ‘Because, friend, it isn’t connected with the goal, isn’t connected with the *dharma*, isn’t fundamental to the holy life. It doesn’t lead to disenchantment (*nibbidā*), dispassion (*virāga*), cessation (*nirodha*), calming (*upasama*), direct knowledge (*abhijñā*), self-awakening (*saṃbodha*), or *nirvāṇa* (*nirvāṇa*). That’s why it’s undeclared by the Blessed One.’

Declared Instances
commentary_pali: 189. Evaṃ attano asamataṃ anuttarataṃ sabbaññutaṃ dhammarājabhāvaṃ kathetvā idāni ‘‘puthusamaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ laddhīsu mayā aññātaṃ adiṭṭhaṃ nāma natthi, sabbaṃ mama ñāṇassa antoyeva parivattatī’’ti sīhanādaṃ nadanto ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, cunda, vijjatītiādimāha. Tattha tathāgatoti satto. Na hetaṃ, āvuso, atthasaṃhitanti idhalokaparalokaatthasaṃhitaṃ na hoti. Na ca dhammasaṃhitanti navalokuttaradhammanissitaṃ na hoti. Naādibrahmacariyakanti sikkhattayasaṅgahitassa sakalasāsanabrahmacariyassa ādibhūtaṃ na hoti.
commentary_english:
Thus, having declared his unmatched, supreme, all-knowing state as the King of Dharma, he now roars the lion's roar, saying, "Among the doctrines of various ascetics and Brahmins, there is nothing unknown or unseen by me; everything revolves within the range of my knowledge." He then spoke, beginning with, "This is the place, Cunda, where..."

There, *tathāgata* means a being.

"*Na hetaṃ, āvuso, atthasaṃhita*," means it is not connected with benefit in this world and the next.

"*Na ca dhammasaṃhita*," means it is not based on the nine transcendental *dharmas*.

"*Na ādibrahmacariyaka*," means it is not the beginning of the entire *brahmacarya* of the teaching, which is encompassed by the three trainings (*śikṣā*).

mula_pali:
190. ‘‘Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, cunda, vijjati, yaṃ aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ vadeyyuṃ – ‘kiṃ panāvuso, samaṇena gotamena byākata’nti? Evaṃvādino, cunda, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evamassu vacanīyā – ‘idaṃ dukkhanti kho, āvuso, bhagavatā byākataṃ, ayaṃ dukkhasamudayoti kho, āvuso, bhagavatā byākataṃ, ayaṃ dukkhanirodhoti kho, āvuso, bhagavatā byākataṃ, ayaṃ dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadāti kho, āvuso, bhagavatā byākata’nti.

‘‘Ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ, cunda, vijjati, yaṃ aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ vadeyyuṃ – ‘kasmā panetaṃ, āvuso, samaṇena gotamena byākata’nti? Evaṃvādino, cunda, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evamassu vacanīyā – ‘etañhi, āvuso, atthasaṃhitaṃ, etaṃ dhammasaṃhitaṃ, etaṃ ādibrahmacariyakaṃ ekantanibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati. Tasmā taṃ bhagavatā byākata’nti.

Pubbantasahagatadiṭṭhinissayā
mula_english:
190. "But it happens, Cunda, that wanderers of other sects might say this: ‘What has been declared by the ascetic Gotama, friend?’ Wanderers of other sects who say this should be told: ‘This has been declared by the Blessed One: "This is suffering ( *duḥkha*)," friend. This has been declared by the Blessed One: "This is the origin of suffering ( *duḥkha-samudaya*)," friend. This has been declared by the Blessed One: "This is the cessation of suffering ( *duḥkha-nirodha*)," friend. This has been declared by the Blessed One: "This is the practice that leads to the cessation of suffering ( *duḥkha-nirodha-gāminī paṭipadā*)," friend.’

"But it happens, Cunda, that wanderers of other sects might say this: ‘Why has this been declared by the ascetic Gotama, friend?’ Wanderers of other sects who say this should be told: ‘Because this is connected with the goal, friend; this is connected with the Dharma, this is fundamental to the holy life. It leads solely to disenchantment, to dispassion, to cessation, to calming, to direct knowledge, to self-awakening, to nirvāṇa. That’s why it’s declared by the Blessed One.’"

Based on views that accord with former extremities.
commentary_pali:
190.Idaṃ dukkhanti khotiādīsu taṇhaṃ ṭhapetvā avasesā tebhummakā dhammā idaṃ dukkhanti byākataṃ. Tasseva dukkhassa pabhāvikā janikā taṇhā dukkhasamudayoti byākataṃ. Ubhinnaṃ appavatti dukkhanirodhoti byākataṃ. Dukkhaparijānano samudayapajahano nirodhasacchikaraṇo ariyamaggo dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadāti byākataṃ. ‘‘Etañhi, āvuso, atthasaṃhita’’ntiādīsu etaṃ idhalokaparalokaatthanissitaṃ navalokuttaradhammanissitaṃ sakalasāsanabrahmacariyassa ādi padhānaṃ pubbaṅgamanti ayamattho.

Pubbantasahagatadiṭṭhinissayavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
In the phrases beginning with "<hi rend="bold">idaṃ dukkhanti kho</hi>ti," the remaining threefold aggregates of *dharmas* are described as "<hi rend="bold">idaṃ dukkhaṃ</hi>" [this is suffering], except for craving.

Craving, which is the origin and cause of that suffering itself, is described as "<hi rend="bold">dukkhasamudayo</hi>" [the origin of suffering].

The non-arising of both [suffering and its origin] is described as "<hi rend="bold">dukkhanirodho</hi>" [the cessation of suffering].

The noble path of completely understanding suffering, abandoning its origin, and realizing its cessation, is described as "<hi rend="bold">dukkhanirodhagāminī paṭipadā</hi>" [the path leading to the cessation of suffering].

In the phrases beginning with "‘‘etañhi, āvuso, atthasaṃhita’’nti," the meaning is: this [teaching] is based on benefits in this world and the next, based on the nine supramundane *dharmas*, and is the beginning, the principal, and the forerunner of the entire dispensation and the holy life.

Explanation of the bases for views associated with the prior end.

mula_pali: 191. ‘‘Yepi te, cunda, pubbantasahagatā diṭṭhinissayā, tepi vo mayā byākatā, yathā te byākātabbā. Yathā ca te na byākātabbā, kiṃ vo ahaṃ te tathā tattha (syā. ka.) byākarissāmi? Yepi te, cunda, aparantasahagatā diṭṭhinissayā, tepi vo mayā byākatā, yathā te byākātabbā. Yathā ca te na byākātabbā, kiṃ vo ahaṃ te tathā byākarissāmi? Katame ca te, cunda, pubbantasahagatā diṭṭhinissayā, ye vo mayā byākatā, yathā te byākātabbā. (Yathā ca te na byākātabbā, kiṃ vo ahaṃ te tathā byākarissāmi) (yathā ca te na byākātabbā) sabbattha? Santi kho, cunda, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃvādino evaṃdiṭṭhino – ‘sassato attā ca loko ca, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti. Santi pana, cunda, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃvādino evaṃdiṭṭhino – ‘asassato attā ca loko ca…pe… sassato ca asassato ca attā ca loko ca… neva sassato nāsassato attā ca loko ca… sayaṃkato attā ca loko ca… paraṃkato attā ca loko ca… sayaṃkato ca paraṃkato ca attā ca loko ca… asayaṃkāro aparaṃkāro adhiccasamuppanno attā ca loko ca, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti. Sassataṃ sukhadukkhaṃ… asassataṃ sukhadukkhaṃ… sassatañca asassatañca sukhadukkhaṃ… nevasassataṃ nāsassataṃ sukhadukkhaṃ… sayaṃkataṃ sukhadukkhaṃ… paraṃkataṃ sukhadukkhaṃ… sayaṃkatañca paraṃkatañca sukhadukkhaṃ… asayaṃkāraṃ aparaṃkāraṃ adhiccasamuppannaṃ sukhadukkhaṃ, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti.
mula_english:
191. “Cunda, the view-dependencies (*dṛṣṭi-niśrayā*) concerning beginning-points (*pūrvānta-sahagatā*) that I have declared as they are to be declared.

And as they are not to be declared: Would I simply declare them to you? Cunda, the view-dependencies concerning endpoints (*aparantasahagatā*) that I have declared as they are to be declared.

And as they are not to be declared: Would I simply declare them to you? And which are the view-dependencies concerning beginning-points that I have declared as they are to be declared?

(And as they are not to be declared: Would I simply declare them to you?) There are certain contemplatives and *brāhmaṇas* who are of this view, this opinion: ‘The self (*ātmā*) and the world (*loka*) are eternal (*śāśvata*): only this is true, anything else is worthless.’

There are, Cunda, certain *śramaṇas* and *brāhmaṇas* who are of this view, this opinion: ‘The self and the world are not eternal (*aśāśvata*)’ … ‘The self and the world are both eternal and not eternal’ … ‘The self and the world are neither eternal nor not eternal’ … ‘The self and the world are self-made (*svayaṃkṛta*)’ … ‘The self and the world are other-made (*paraṃkṛta*)’ … ‘The self and the world are both self-made and other-made’ … ‘The self and the cosmos–without self-making (*asvayaṃkāra*), without other-making (*aparaṃkāra*)–are spontaneously arisen (*adhiccasamuppanna*)’: only this is true, anything else is worthless.’

Pleasure and pain (*sukhaduḥkha*) are eternal… Pleasure and pain are not eternal… Pleasure and pain are both eternal and not eternal… Pleasure and pain are neither eternal nor not eternal… Pleasure and pain are self-made… Pleasure and pain are other-made… Pleasure and pain are both self-made and other-made… Pleasure and pain–without self-making, without other-making–are spontaneously arisen: only this is true, anything else is worthless.
commentary_pali: 191. Idāni yaṃ taṃ mayā na byākataṃ, taṃ ajānantena na byākatanti mā evaṃ saññamakaṃsu. Jānantova ahaṃ evaṃ ‘‘etasmiṃ byākatepi attho natthī’’ti na byākariṃ. Yaṃ pana yathā byākātabbaṃ, taṃ mayā byākatamevāti sīhanādaṃ nadanto puna yepi te, cundātiādimāha. Tattha diṭṭhiyova diṭṭhinissayā, diṭṭhinissitakā diṭṭhigatikāti attho. Idameva saccanti idameva dassanaṃ saccaṃ. Moghamaññanti aññesaṃ vacanaṃ moghaṃ. Asayaṃkāroti asayaṃ kato.
commentary_english:
Now, what was not explained by me, they should not consider, "It was not explained by one who does not know."

Knowing thus, "Even in this explanation, there is no meaning," I did not explain.

But that which should be explained, that was indeed explained by me. Roaring the lion's roar, he then said, "Those too, Cunda," and so forth.

There, *dṛṣṭinissayā* means just dependent on views, *dṛṣṭinissitakā* means those who rely on views, *dṛṣṭigatikā* means having views as their course. This is the meaning.

"*Idameva sacca* (This alone is true)" means this very view is true.

"*Moghamañña* (Other [views] are vain)" means the speech of others is vain.

"*Asayaṃkāro* (Not self-made)" means not made by oneself.

mula_pali: 192. ‘‘Tatra, cunda, ye te samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃvādino evaṃdiṭṭhino – ‘sassato attā ca loko ca, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti. Tyāhaṃ upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ vadāmi – ‘atthi nu kho idaṃ, āvuso, vuccati – ‘‘sassato attā ca loko cā’’ti? Yañca kho te evamāhaṃsu – ‘idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti. Taṃ tesaṃ nānujānāmi. Taṃ kissa hetu? Aññathāsaññinopi hettha, cunda, santeke sattā. Imāyapi kho ahaṃ, cunda, paññattiyā neva attanā samasamaṃ samanupassāmi kuto bhiyyo. Atha kho ahameva tattha bhiyyo yadidaṃ adhipaññatti.
mula_english:
“There, Cunda, those ascetics and Brahmins who maintain such a view and opinion: ‘The self (*ātman*) and the world are eternal; only this is true, anything else is worthless.’

I approached them and said this: ‘Friends, is it the case that it is said, “The self (*ātman*) and the world are eternal”?’ And when they said this, ‘Only this is true, anything else is worthless,’

I do not grant them that point.

Why is that? Because there are beings here, Cunda, who have different perceptions.

And with this teaching as well, Cunda, I do not see myself as equal, much less superior.

In fact, I am superior in that regard, namely, in higher wisdom ( *adhiprajñapti*)."
commentary_pali: 192.Tatrāti tesu samaṇabrāhmaṇesu. Atthi nu kho idaṃ āvuso vuccatīti, āvuso, yaṃ tumhehi sassato attā ca loko cāti vuccati, idamatthi nu kho udāhu natthīti evamahaṃ te pucchāmīti attho. Yañca kho te evamāhaṃsūti yaṃ pana te ‘‘idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’’nti vadanti, taṃ tesaṃ nānujānāmi. Paññattiyāti diṭṭhipaññattiyā. Samasamanti samena ñāṇena samaṃ. Yadidaṃ adhipaññattīti yā ayaṃ adhipaññatti nāma. Ettha ahameva bhiyyo uttaritaro na mayā samo atthi. Tattha yañca vuttaṃ ‘‘paññattiyāti yañca adhipaññattī’’ti ubhayametaṃ atthato ekaṃ. Bhedato hi paññatti adhipaññattīti dvayaṃ hoti. Tattha paññatti nāma diṭṭhipaññatti. Adhipaññatti nāma khandhapaññatti dhātupaññatti āyatanapaññatti indriyapaññatti saccapaññatti puggalapaññattīti evaṃ vuttā cha paññattiyo. Idha pana paññattiyāti etthāpi paññatti ceva adhipaññatti ca adhippetā, adhipaññattīti etthāpi. Bhagavā hi paññattiyāpi anuttaro, adhipaññattiyāpi anuttaro. Tenāha – ‘‘ahameva tattha bhiyyo yadidaṃ adhipaññattī’’ti.
commentary_english:
192. "Tatrā"ti, at those *śramaṇa*s and *brāhmaṇa*s.

"Atthi nu kho idaṃ āvuso vuccatī"ti, friend, what you call the eternal *ātman* and the world, whether this exists or not, this is the meaning of "I ask you thus."

"Yañca kho te evamāhaṃsū"ti, but those who say, "This alone is true, other [teachings] are worthless," that, I do not allow them.

"Paññattiyā"ti, by designation of views (*dṛṣṭi-prajñapti*).

"Samasama"nti, equal through equal knowledge (*jñāna*).

"Yadidaṃ adhipaññattī"ti, that which is called higher designation (*adhiprajñapti*).

Here, I alone am superior, more excellent, there is none equal to me.

There, what was said, "by designation and by higher designation," both of these are one in meaning.

Indeed, by difference, designation and higher designation are two.

There, designation (*prajñapti*) is the designation of views (*dṛṣṭi-prajñapti*).

Higher designation (*adhiprajñapti*) is the designation of the aggregates (*skandha-prajñapti*), the designation of the elements (*dhātu-prajñapti*), the designation of the sources (*āyatana-prajñapti*), the designation of the faculties (*indriya-prajñapti*), the designation of the truths (*satya-prajñapti*), the designation of persons (*pudgala-prajñapti*). Thus, there are six designations that are spoken of.

Here, moreover, "by designation" here also both designation and higher designation are intended, and here also, "by higher designation".

Indeed, the Blessed One (*bhagavān*) is unsurpassed even by designation, unsurpassed even by higher designation.

Therefore, he said: "I alone am superior there, namely this higher designation (*adhiprajñapti*)."

mula_pali:
193. ‘‘Tatra, cunda, ye te samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃvādino evaṃdiṭṭhino – ‘asassato attā ca loko ca…pe… sassato ca asassato ca attā ca loko ca… nevasassato nāsassato attā ca loko ca… sayaṃkato attā ca loko ca… paraṃkato attā ca loko ca… sayaṃkato ca paraṃkato ca attā ca loko ca… asayaṃkāro aparaṃkāro adhiccasamuppanno attā ca loko ca… sassataṃ sukhadukkhaṃ… asassataṃ sukhadukkhaṃ… sassatañca asassatañca sukhadukkhaṃ… nevasassataṃ nāsassataṃ sukhadukkhaṃ… sayaṃkataṃ sukhadukkhaṃ… paraṃkataṃ sukhadukkhaṃ… sayaṃkatañca paraṃkatañca sukhadukkhaṃ… asayaṃkāraṃ aparaṃkāraṃ adhiccasamuppannaṃ sukhadukkhaṃ, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti. Tyāhaṃ upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ vadāmi – ‘atthi nu kho idaṃ, āvuso, vuccati – ‘‘asayaṃkāraṃ aparaṃkāraṃ adhiccasamuppannaṃ sukhadukkha’’’nti? Yañca kho te evamāhaṃsu – ‘idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti. Taṃ tesaṃ nānujānāmi. Taṃ kissa hetu? Aññathāsaññinopi hettha, cunda, santeke sattā. Imāyapi kho ahaṃ, cunda, paññattiyā neva attanā samasamaṃ samanupassāmi kuto bhiyyo. Atha kho ahameva tattha bhiyyo yadidaṃ adhipaññatti. Ime kho te, cunda, pubbantasahagatā diṭṭhinissayā, ye vo mayā byākatā, yathā te byākātabbā . Yathā ca te na byākātabbā, kiṃ vo ahaṃ te tathā byākarissāmīti byākarissāmīti (sī. ka.)?

Aparantasahagatadiṭṭhinissayā
mula_english:
193. “Here, Cunda, are those ascetics and Brahmins who maintain such views and opinions: ‘The self (*ātman*) and the world (*loka*) are not eternal’…and so on…‘The self and the world are eternal and not eternal’…‘The self is neither eternal nor not eternal’…
…the self and the world…‘The self and the world are self-made’…‘The self and the world are made by others’…‘The self and the world are both self-made and made by others’…‘The self and the world are without self-making or other-making, arising by chance’… ‘Pleasure and pain are eternal’…‘Pleasure and pain are not eternal’…‘Pleasure and pain are eternal and not eternal’…‘Pleasure and pain are neither eternal nor not eternal’…‘Pleasure and pain are self-made’…‘Pleasure and pain are made by others’…‘Pleasure and pain are both self-made and made by others’…‘Pleasure and pain are without self-making or other-making, arising by chance’; only this is true, anything else is worthless.”

Then I approached them and said this: “Is there such a thing, friends, that is called ‘pleasure and pain without self-making or other-making, arising by chance’?” And they replied to me thus: “Only this is true, anything else is worthless.”

I do not approve of that.

Why is that? Because there are beings here, Cunda, who have different perceptions.

And I do not regard this doctrine, Cunda, as even equal to my own, let alone better.

In fact, my doctrine is better, namely, super-wisdom (*adhipaññatti*).

These, Cunda, are the view-dependencies concerning beginning-points (*pubbantasahagatā diṭṭhinissayā*) that I have declared as they are to be declared.

And as they are not to be declared, would I simply declare them to you?

View-dependencies concerning end-points (*aparantasahagatadiṭṭhinissayā*).

mula_pali: 194. ‘‘Katame ca te, cunda, aparantasahagatā diṭṭhinissayā, ye vo mayā byākatā, yathā te byākātabbā. (Yathā ca te na byākātabbā, kiṃ vo ahaṃ te tathā byākarissāmī) ( ) etthantare pāṭho sabbatthapi paripuṇṇo dissati? Santi, cunda, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃvādino evaṃdiṭṭhino – ‘rūpī attā hoti arogo paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti. Santi pana, cunda, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃvādino evaṃdiṭṭhino – ‘arūpī attā hoti…pe… rūpī ca arūpī ca attā hoti… nevarūpī nārūpī attā hoti… saññī attā hoti… asaññī attā hoti… nevasaññīnāsaññī attā hoti… attā ucchijjati vinassati na hoti paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti. Tatra, cunda, ye te samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃvādino evaṃdiṭṭhino – ‘rūpī attā hoti arogo paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti. Tyāhaṃ upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ vadāmi – ‘atthi nu kho idaṃ, āvuso, vuccati – ‘‘rūpī attā hoti arogo paraṃ maraṇā’’’ti? Yañca kho te evamāhaṃsu – ‘idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti. Taṃ tesaṃ nānujānāmi. Taṃ kissa hetu? Aññathāsaññinopi hettha, cunda, santeke sattā. Imāyapi kho ahaṃ, cunda, paññattiyā neva attanā samasamaṃ samanupassāmi kuto bhiyyo. Atha kho ahameva tattha bhiyyo yadidaṃ adhipaññatti.
mula_english:
194. “And which are the view-dependencies (*dṛṣṭinissaya*) concerning endpoints (*aparantasahagata*) that I have declared as they are to be declared and as they are not to be declared?

(And how should I declare them to you?) Are there, Cunda, some ascetics and Brahmins (*śramaṇabrāhmaṇa*) who hold such views and opinions: ‘After death, the self (*āttā*) is possessed of form (*rūpī*) and free from disease (*arogo*): Only this is true, anything otherwise is worthless’ (*moghamañña*)?

Furthermore, are there, Cunda, some ascetics and Brahmins who hold such views and opinions: ‘After death, the self (*āttā*) is formless (*arūpī*)…pe… After death, the self is both possessed of form and formless… After death, the self is neither possessed of form nor formless… After death, the self is percipient (*saññī*)… After death, the self is not percipient (*asaññī*)… After death, the self is neither percipient nor not percipient… The self is annihilated (*ucchijjati*) and destroyed (*vinassati*) and does not exist after death: Only this is true, anything otherwise is worthless’?

As for the contemplatives and Brahmins who are of this view, this opinion, ‘After death, the self (*āttā*) is possessed of form (*rūpī*) and free from disease (*arogo*): Only this is true, anything otherwise is worthless’:

I, approaching them, say, ‘Friends, is it the case that this is said, “After death, the self (*āttā*) is possessed of form (*rūpī*) and free from disease (*arogo*)”’? And if they should say, ‘Only this is true, anything otherwise is worthless’.

I don’t grant their point.

Why is that? Because there are sentient beings (*sattā*) who have different perceptions.

And I do not see that this doctrine is even equal to mine, so how better?

In fact, my doctrine is the better one, that is, the super-wisdom (*adhiprajñāpti*)."

mula_pali: 195. ‘‘Tatra, cunda, ye te samaṇabrāhmaṇā evaṃvādino evaṃdiṭṭhino – ‘arūpī attā hoti…pe… rūpī ca arūpī ca attā hoti… nevarūpīnārūpī attā hoti… saññī attā hoti… asaññī attā hoti… nevasaññīnāsaññī attā hoti… attā ucchijjati vinassati na hoti paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti. Tyāhaṃ upasaṅkamitvā evaṃ vadāmi – ‘atthi nu kho idaṃ, āvuso, vuccati – ‘‘attā ucchijjati vinassati na hoti paraṃ maraṇā’’’ti? Yañca kho te, cunda, evamāhaṃsu – ‘idameva saccaṃ moghamañña’nti. Taṃ tesaṃ nānujānāmi. Taṃ kissa hetu? Aññathāsaññinopi hettha, cunda, santeke sattā. Imāyapi kho ahaṃ, cunda, paññattiyā neva attanā samasamaṃ samanupassāmi, kuto bhiyyo. Atha kho ahameva tattha bhiyyo yadidaṃ adhipaññatti. Ime kho te, cunda, aparantasahagatā diṭṭhinissayā, ye vo mayā byākatā , yathā te byākātabbā. Yathā ca te na byākātabbā, kiṃ vo ahaṃ te tathā byākarissāmīti byākarissāmīti (sī. ka.)?
mula_english:
195. There, Cunda, those ascetics and Brahmins who hold such views and opinions: ‘The self is formless ( *arūpī attā hoti* )…pe… The self is both with form and formless ( *rūpī ca arūpī ca attā hoti* )… The self is neither with form nor formless ( *nevarūpīnārūpī attā hoti* )… The self is percipient ( *saññī attā hoti* )… The self is non-percipient ( *asaññī attā hoti* )… The self is neither percipient nor non-percipient ( *nevasaññīnāsaññī attā hoti* )… The self is annihilated and destroyed at death, and does not exist beyond death ( *attā ucchijjati vinassati na hoti paraṃ maraṇā* ), only this is true, anything else is worthless.’

Approaching them, I say thus: ‘Is it the case, friend, that it is said: “The self is annihilated and destroyed at death, and does not exist beyond death ( *attā ucchijjati vinassati na hoti paraṃ maraṇā* )”’? And what they say thus, Cunda: ‘Only this is true, anything else is worthless.’

I don’t grant their point ( *taṃ tesaṃ nānujānāmi* ).

Why is that ( *taṃ kissa hetu* )? Because there are sentient beings here, Cunda, who are otherwise percipient.

And I do not consider this doctrine to be even equal to mine, let alone better.

In fact, my doctrine is the better one, which is super-wisdom ( *adhipaññatti* ).

These, Cunda, are the view-dependencies concerning endpoints, which have been declared by me, as they are to be declared ( *yathā te byākātabbā* ).

And as they are not to be declared, why would I declare them to you?

mula_pali: 196. ‘‘Imesañca, cunda, pubbantasahagatānaṃ diṭṭhinissayānaṃ imesañca aparantasahagatānaṃ diṭṭhinissayānaṃ pahānāya samatikkamāya evaṃ mayā cattāro satipaṭṭhānā desitā paññattā. Katame cattāro? Idha, cunda, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Vedanāsu vedanānupassī…pe… citte cittānupassī… dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṃ. Imesañca cunda, pubbantasahagatānaṃ diṭṭhinissayānaṃ imesañca aparantasahagatānaṃ diṭṭhinissayānaṃ pahānāya samatikkamāya. Evaṃ mayā ime cattāro satipaṭṭhānā desitā paññattā’’ti.
mula_english: “It’s for the abandoning & transcending of these view-dependencies concerning beginning-points and view-dependencies concerning endpoints that I have thus taught & formulated the four *satipaṭṭhānas*. Which four? Here, *Cunda*, a *bhikkhu* remains focused on the body in & of itself—ardent (*ātāpī*), alert (*sampajāno*), & mindful (*satimā*)—subduing greed (*abhijjhā*) & distress (*domanassa*) with reference to the world. He remains focused on feelings… mind… mental qualities in & of themselves—ardent, alert, & mindful—subduing greed & distress with reference to the world. It’s for the abandoning & transcending of these view-dependencies concerning beginning-points and view-dependencies concerning endpoints that I have thus taught & formulated these four *satipaṭṭhānas*.”
commentary_pali:
196.Pahānāyāti pajahanatthaṃ. Samatikkamāyāti tasseva vevacanaṃ. Desitāti kathitā. Paññattāti ṭhapitā. Satipaṭṭhānabhāvanāya hi ghanavinibbhogaṃ katvā sabbadhammesu yāthāvato diṭṭhesu ‘‘suddhasaṅkhārapuñjoyaṃ nayidha sattūpalabbhatī’’ti sanniṭṭhānato sabbadiṭṭhinissayānaṃ pahānaṃ hotīti. Tena vuttaṃ. Diṭṭhinissayānaṃ pahānāya samatikkamāya evaṃ mayā ime cattāro satipaṭṭhānā desitā paññattā’’ti. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānatthamevāti.

Sumaṅgalavilāsiniyā dīghanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Pāsādikasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
196. Pahānāyāti: with the meaning of abandoning (pajahanatthaṃ). Samatikkamāyāti: a synonym for that itself (tasseva vevacanaṃ). Desitāti: spoken (kathitā). Paññattāti: established (ṭhapitā). Indeed, through the cultivation of the establishments of mindfulness (satipaṭṭhānabhāvanāya), having made a solid discernment (ghanavinibbhogaṃ katvā), when all phenomena are seen as they actually are (sabbadhammesu yāthāvato diṭṭhesu), from the conviction that "this is merely a mass of pure formations (suddhasaṅkhārapuñjoyaṃ), no being is found here (nayidha sattūpalabbhatī)", the abandoning of all view-dependencies (sabbadiṭṭhinissayānaṃ pahānaṃ) occurs (hotīti). Therefore it has been said (tena vuttaṃ): "For the abandoning and transcending of view-dependencies (diṭṭhinissayānaṃ pahānāya samatikkamāya), thus, by me, these four establishments of mindfulness (ime cattāro satipaṭṭhānā) have been taught and established (desitā paññattā)." The rest is clear throughout (sesaṃ sabbattha uttānatthamevāti).

The Pāsādika Sutta Commentary (pāsādikasuttavaṇṇanā) in the Dīgha Nikāya Commentary, the Sumaṅgalavilāsinī (sumaṅgalavilāsiniyā dīghanikāyaṭṭhakathāya), is finished (niṭṭhitā).

mula_pali:
197. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā upavāṇo bhagavato piṭṭhito ṭhito hoti bhagavantaṃ bījayamāno. Atha kho āyasmā upavāṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘acchariyaṃ, bhante, abbhutaṃ, bhante! Pāsādiko vatāyaṃ, bhante, dhammapariyāyo; supāsādiko vatāyaṃ bhante, dhammapariyāyo, ko nāmāyaṃ bhante dhammapariyāyo’’ti? ‘‘Tasmātiha tvaṃ, upavāṇa, imaṃ dhammapariyāyaṃ ‘pāsādiko’ tveva naṃ dhārehī’’ti. Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamano āyasmā upavāṇo bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandīti.

Pāsādikasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ.
mula_english:
At that time, the venerable Upavāṇa was standing behind the Blessed One, fanning him.

Then the venerable Upavāṇa said this to the Blessed One: “Amazing, venerable sir, astonishing, venerable sir! How pleasing is this exposition of the Dharma, venerable sir; how very pleasing is this exposition of the Dharma, venerable sir. What is the name of this exposition of the Dharma, venerable sir?”

“Therefore, Upavāṇa, you should remember this exposition of the Dharma as ‘Pleasing (pāsādiko).’”

This is what the Buddha said.

The venerable Upavāṇa, pleased, rejoiced at the Blessed One’s words.

The Pāsādika Sutta, the sixth, is finished.

mula_pali: 198. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘bhikkhavo’’ti. ‘‘Bhaddante’’ti bhadanteti (sī. syā. pī.) te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. Once the Blessed One (bhagavān) was staying at Sāvatthi (śrāvastī) in the Jeta Grove (jetavana), in Anāthapindika’s park (anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme).

There the Fortunate One addressed the monks (bhikkhus), saying: “Bhikkhus.”

“Venerable sir (bhaddante),” those monks replied to the Blessed One.

The Blessed One said this (bhagavā etadavoca):
