mula_pali: 199. ‘‘Dvattiṃsimāni, bhikkhave, mahāpurisassa mahāpurisalakkhaṇāni, yehi samannāgatassa mahāpurisassa dveva gatiyo bhavanti anaññā. Sace agāraṃ ajjhāvasati, rājā hoti cakkavattī dhammiko dhammarājā cāturanto vijitāvī janapadatthāvariyappatto sattaratanasamannāgato. Tassimāni satta ratanāni bhavanti; seyyathidaṃ, cakkaratanaṃ hatthiratanaṃ assaratanaṃ maṇiratanaṃ itthiratanaṃ gahapatiratanaṃ pariṇāyakaratanameva sattamaṃ. Parosahassaṃ kho panassa puttā bhavanti sūrā vīraṅgarūpā parasenappamaddanā. So imaṃ pathaviṃ sāgarapariyantaṃ adaṇḍena asatthena dhammena abhivijiya ajjhāvasati. Sace kho pana agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajati, arahaṃ hoti sammāsambuddho loke vivaṭṭacchado vivaṭacchado (syā. ka.), vivattacchado (sī. pī.).
mula_english:
199. Monks, a great man (mahāpurisa) who possesses these thirty-two marks of a great man (mahāpurisalakkhaṇāni) has only two possible destinies.

If he lives the household life, he will become a king (rājā), a wheel-turning monarch (cakkavattī), a righteous monarch (dhāmmiko dhammarājā) of the Dharma, a conqueror of the four quarters (cāturanto vijitāvī), who has established the security of his realm (janapadatthāvariyappatto), and is possessed of the seven treasures (sattaratanasamannāgato).

He has these seven treasures (satta ratanāni): the wheel treasure (cakkaratana), the elephant treasure (hatthiratana), the horse treasure (assaratana), the jewel treasure (maṇiratana), the woman treasure (itthiratana), the steward treasure (gahapatiratana), and the counselor treasure (pariṇāyakaratanameva) as the seventh.

He has more than a thousand sons (parosahassaṃ puttā), who are brave (sūrā), of heroic stature (vīraṅgarūpā), and crush the armies of others (parasenappamaddanā).

He dwells having conquered this earth (pathaviṃ) bounded by the ocean (sāgarapariyantaṃ) without stick (adaṇḍena) or sword (asatthena), by the Dharma (dhammena).

But if he goes forth from the household life (agārasmā) into homelessness (anagāriyaṃ), he becomes an Arhat (arahaṃ), a Fully Enlightened Buddha (sammāsambuddho), one who draws back the veil from the world (loke vivaṭṭacchado).
commentary_pali:
199.Evaṃme sutanti lakkhaṇasuttaṃ. Tatrāyamanuttānapadavaṇṇanā. Dvattiṃsimānīti dvattiṃsa imāni. Mahāpurisalakkhaṇānīti mahāpurisabyañjanāni mahāpurisanimittāni ‘‘ayaṃ mahāpuriso’’ti sañjānanakāraṇāni. ‘‘Yehi samannāgatassa mahāpurisassā’’tiādi mahāpadāne vitthāritanayeneva veditabbaṃ.

‘‘Bāhirakāpi isayo dhārenti, no ca kho jānanti ‘imassa kammassa katattā imaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ paṭilabhatī’ti’’ kasmā āha? Aṭṭhuppattiyā anurūpattā. Idañhi suttaṃ saaṭṭhuppattikaṃ. Sā panassa aṭṭhuppatti kattha samuṭṭhitā? Antogāme manussānaṃ antare. Tadā kira sāvatthivāsino attano attano gehesu ca gehadvāresu ca santhāgārādīsu ca nisīditvā kathaṃ samuṭṭhāpesuṃ – ‘‘bhagavato asītianubyañjanāni byāmappabhā dvattiṃsamahāpurisalakkhaṇāni, yehi ca bhagavato kāyo, sabbaphāliphullo viya pāricchattako, vikasitamiva kamalavanaṃ, nānāratanavicittaṃ viya suvaṇṇatoraṇaṃ, tārāmaricivirocamiva gaganatalaṃ, ito cito ca vidhāvamānā vipphandamānā chabbaṇṇarasmiyo muñcanto ativiya sobhati. Bhagavato ca iminā nāma kammena idaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ nibbattanti kathitaṃ natthi, yāguuḷuṅkamattampi pana kaṭacchubhattamattaṃ vā pubbe dinnapaccayā evaṃ uppajjatīti bhagavatā vuttaṃ. Kiṃ nu kho satthā kammaṃ akāsi, yenassa imāni lakkhaṇāni nibbattantī’’ti.

Athāyasmā ānando antogāme caranto imaṃ kathāsallāpaṃ sutvā katabhattakicco vihāraṃ āgantvā satthu vattaṃ katvā vanditvā ṭhito ‘‘mayā, bhante, antogāme ekā kathā sutā’’ti āha. Tato bhagavatā ‘‘kiṃ te, ānanda, suta’’nti vutte sabbaṃ ārocesi. Satthā therassa vacanaṃ sutvā parivāretvā nisinne bhikkhū āmantetvā ‘‘dvattiṃsimāni, bhikkhave, mahāpurisassa mahāpurisalakkhaṇānī’’ti paṭipāṭiyā lakkhaṇāni dassetvā yena kammena yaṃ nibbattaṃ, tassa dassanatthaṃ evamāha.

Suppatiṭṭhitapādatālakkhaṇavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
199. ThusI have heard: the *lakṣaṇa-sūtra*. Herein is an explanation of the unelaborated terms. The thirty-two are these thirty-two. The marks of a great man (mahāpuruṣa) are the signs of a great man, the indications of a great man, the causes for recognizing "this is a great man (mahāpuruṣa)." "Possessing these, of a great man (mahāpuruṣa)" and so forth should be understood in the same way as explained in detail in the Great Legend (Mahāpadāna).

"Even non-Buddhists retain [them], but they do not know ‘because of doing this action, one obtains this mark (lakṣaṇa)’" Why [does he] say [this]? Because of conformity with the [actual] origin. For this sūtra is with [its] origin. Now, where did its origin arise? Among humans, in the inner village. Then, at that time, the inhabitants of Śrāvastī, having sat down in their own houses and in the doorways of [their] houses, and in assembly halls, and so forth, how did they bring it about? - "The eighty secondary marks (anubyañjana) of the Fortunate One (Bhagavat), the fathom-wide radiance, the thirty-two marks of a great man (mahāpuruṣa), by which, indeed, the body of the Fortunate One (Bhagavat), is like a fully blossoming pāricchattaka tree, like a blooming lotus grove, like a golden archway adorned with various jewels, like the surface of the sky gleaming with the rays of stars, sending forth excessively beautiful six-colored rays darting and flickering here and there. And it is said by the Fortunate One (Bhagavat) that this mark (lakṣaṇa) does not arise from this particular action (karma) by name; however, even a mouthful of rice gruel, or a spoonful of food, arises in this way due to a previously given condition." "What action (karma) did the Teacher (Śāstā) do, by which these marks (lakṣaṇa) arise for him?"

Then the venerable Ānanda, while wandering in the inner village, having heard this conversation, and having finished [his] meal duties, came to the monastery, and having performed the duties of the Teacher (Śāstā), and having paid homage, stood [there]. He said, "Venerable Sir (Bhante), a conversation was heard by me in the inner village." Then the Fortunate One (Bhagavat) said, "What was heard by you, Ānanda?" [and] he announced everything. The Teacher (Śāstā), having heard the elder's (sthavira) speech and having surrounded and addressed the monks (bhikṣu) who were sitting [there], showing in order the marks (lakṣaṇa), "These are the thirty-two marks of a great man (mahāpuruṣa) (mahāpurisalakkhaṇāni), O monks (bhikkhave)," in order to show that which arises from which action (karma), he spoke thus.

Explanation of the mark of well-established feet

mula_pali:
200. ‘‘Katamāni ca tāni, bhikkhave, dvattiṃsa mahāpurisassa mahāpurisalakkhaṇāni, yehi samannāgatassa mahāpurisassa dveva gatiyo bhavanti anaññā? Sace agāraṃ ajjhāvasati, rājā hoti cakkavattī…pe… sace kho pana agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajati, arahaṃ hoti sammāsambuddho loke vivaṭṭacchado.

‘‘Idha, bhikkhave, mahāpuriso suppatiṭṭhitapādo hoti. Yampi, bhikkhave, mahāpuriso suppatiṭṭhitapādo hoti, idampi, bhikkhave, mahāpurisassa mahāpurisalakkhaṇaṃ bhavati.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, mahāpurisassa heṭṭhāpādatalesu cakkāni jātāni honti sahassārāni sanemikāni sanābhikāni sabbākāraparipūrāni sabbākāraparipūrāni suvibhattantarāni (sī. pī.). Yampi , bhikkhave, mahāpurisassa heṭṭhāpādatalesu cakkāni jātāni honti sahassārāni sanemikāni sanābhikāni sabbākāraparipūrāni, idampi, bhikkhave, mahāpurisassa mahāpurisalakkhaṇaṃ bhavati.

sabbākāraparipūrāni suvibhattantarāni (sī. pī.)

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, mahāpuriso āyatapaṇhi hoti…pe… dīghaṅguli hoti… mudutalunahatthapādo hoti… jālahatthapādo hoti… ussaṅkhapādo hoti… eṇijaṅgho hoti… ṭhitakova anonamanto ubhohi pāṇitalehi jaṇṇukāni parimasati parimajjati… kosohitavatthaguyho hoti… suvaṇṇavaṇṇo hoti kañcanasannibhattaco… sukhumacchavi hoti, sukhumattā chaviyā rajojallaṃ kāye na upalimpati… ekekalomo hoti, ekekāni lomāni lomakūpesu jātāni… uddhaggalomo hoti, uddhaggāni lomāni jātāni nīlāni añjanavaṇṇāni kuṇḍalāvaṭṭāni kuṇḍalāvattāni (bahūsu) dakkhiṇāvaṭṭakajātāni dakkhiṇāvattakajātāni (sī. syā. pī.) … brahmujugatto hoti… sattussado hoti… sīhapubbaddhakāyo hoti… citantaraṃso pitantaraṃso (syā.) hoti… nigrodhaparimaṇḍalo hoti, yāvatakvassa kāyo tāvatakvassa byāmo yāvatakvassa byāmo tāvatakvassa kāyo… samavaṭṭakkhandho hoti… rasaggasaggī hoti… sīhahanu hoti… cattālīsadanto hoti … samadanto hoti… aviraḷadanto hoti… susukkadāṭho hoti… pahūtajivho hoti… brahmassaro hoti karavīkabhāṇī… abhinīlanetto hoti… gopakhumo hoti… uṇṇā bhamukantare jātā hoti, odātā mudutūlasannibhā. Yampi, bhikkhave, mahāpurisassa uṇṇā bhamukantare jātā hoti, odātā mudutūlasannibhā, idampi, bhikkhave, mahāpurisassa mahāpurisalakkhaṇaṃ bhavati.

kuṇḍalāvattāni (bahūsu) dakkhiṇāvattakajātāni (sī. syā. pī.) pitantaraṃso (syā.)

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, mahāpuriso uṇhīsasīso hoti. Yampi, bhikkhave, mahāpuriso uṇhīsasīso hoti, idampi, bhikkhave, mahāpurisassa mahāpurisalakkhaṇaṃ bhavati.

‘‘Imāni kho tāni, bhikkhave, dvattiṃsa mahāpurisassa mahāpurisalakkhaṇāni, yehi samannāgatassa mahāpurisassa dveva gatiyo bhavanti anaññā. Sace agāraṃ ajjhāvasati, rājā hoti cakkavattī…pe… sace kho pana agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajati, arahaṃ hoti sammāsambuddho loke vivaṭṭacchado.

‘‘Imāni kho, bhikkhave, dvattiṃsa mahāpurisassa mahāpurisalakkhaṇāni bāhirakāpi isayo dhārenti, no ca kho te jānanti – ‘imassa kammassa kaṭattā idaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ paṭilabhatī’ti.

(1) Suppatiṭṭhitapādatālakkhaṇaṃ
mula_english:
200. What, monks, are the thirty-two marks of a great man (*mahāpuruṣa*), with which a great man is endowed, that there are only two possible destinies, and no other? If he lives the household life, he becomes a wheel-turning monarch (*cakravartin*)… and so on… But if he goes forth from the household life into homelessness, then he becomes an *arhat*, a fully enlightened Buddha, one who draws back the veil from the world.

Here, monks, a great man has well-established feet. Monks, because a great man has well-established feet, this, monks, is a mark of a great man (*mahāpuruṣa-lakṣaṇa*).

Again, monks, on the soles of a great man’s feet, wheels are born, with a thousand spokes, complete with rims and hubs, complete in every way. Because of this...

Again, monks, a great man has projecting heels… and so on… he has long fingers… he has soft, tender hands and feet… he has webbed hands and feet… he has high-arched feet… he has antelope-like calves… standing without bending, he strokes and massages his knees with both palms… his genitals are concealed in a sheath… he has a golden complexion, with skin like burnished gold… he has delicate skin, and because of the delicacy of his skin, no dust or dirt clings to his body… he has single hairs in each pore… he has up-turned hairs, with up-turned hairs, dark blue, the color of *añjana*, curling in rings… He has a straight body like Brahmā… he has the seven *ussada*s… he has the torso of a lion… he has full shoulders… he is proportioned like a *nyagrodha* tree, the length of his body is the same as his wingspan, and his wingspan is the same as the length of his body… he has a level chest… he has a superior sense of taste… he has a lion’s jaw… he has forty teeth… he has even teeth… he has unbroken teeth… he has very white canine teeth… he has a large tongue… he has a Brahmā-like voice, with a *karavīka*-like quality… he has deep blue eyes… he has eyes like a cow… an *ūrṇā* hair grows between his eyebrows, white and soft like cotton. Because this, monks, is a mark of a great man (*mahāpuruṣa-lakṣaṇa*).

Again, monks, a great man has a protuberance on his head (*uṇhīsa-sīsa*). Monks, because a great man has a protuberance on his head (*uṇhīsa-sīsa*), this, monks, is a mark of a great man (*mahāpuruṣa-lakṣaṇa*).

These, monks, are the thirty-two marks of a great man (*mahāpuruṣa*), with which a great man is endowed, that there are only two possible destinies, and no other. If he lives the household life, he becomes a wheel-turning monarch (*cakravartin*)… and so on… But if he goes forth from the household life into homelessness, then he becomes an *arhat*, a fully enlightened Buddha, one who draws back the veil from the world.

These thirty-two marks of a great man (*mahāpuruṣa-lakṣaṇa*) are also known by outside seers, but they do not know that ‘because of doing this action, this mark is obtained.’
(1) *supratiṣṭhitapādatālakkhaṇaṃ*

mula_pali: 201. ‘‘Yampi, bhikkhave, tathāgato purimaṃ jātiṃ purimaṃ bhavaṃ purimaṃ niketaṃ pubbe manussabhūto samāno daḷhasamādāno ahosi kusalesu dhammesu, avatthitasamādāno kāyasucarite vacīsucarite manosucarite dānasaṃvibhāge sīlasamādāne uposathupavāse matteyyatāya petteyyatāya sāmaññatāya brahmaññatāya kule jeṭṭhāpacāyitāya aññataraññataresu ca adhikusalesu dhammesu . So tassa kammassa kaṭattā upacitattā ussannattā vipulattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati. So tattha aññe deve dasahi ṭhānehi adhiggaṇhāti dibbena āyunā dibbena vaṇṇena dibbena sukhena dibbena yasena dibbena ādhipateyyena dibbehi rūpehi dibbehi saddehi dibbehi gandhehi dibbehi rasehi dibbehi phoṭṭhabbehi. So tato cuto itthattaṃ āgato samāno imaṃ mahāpurisalakkhaṇaṃ paṭilabhati. Suppatiṭṭhitapādo hoti. Samaṃ pādaṃ bhūmiyaṃ nikkhipati, samaṃ uddharati, samaṃ sabbāvantehi pādatalehi bhūmiṃ phusati.
mula_english:
201.
"And also, monks, the *tathāgata*, in a former birth, a former existence, a former abode, having been previously a human being, was resolute in wholesome dharmas, steadfast in resolve, in good conduct of body (*kāyasucarita*), good conduct of speech (*vacīsucarita*), good conduct of mind (*manosucarita*), in the distribution of gifts (*dānasaṃvibhāga*), in the undertaking of morality (*śīlasamādāna*), in the observance of the *uposatha*, in affection for mother (*matteyyatā*), in affection for father (*petteyyatā*), in friendliness, in reverence for *brahmins*, in the family, in honoring elders, and in other superior wholesome dharmas.

Because of performing and accumulating that action, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in a happy destination, in a heavenly world (*sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati*).

There, he surpasses the other gods in ten respects: in divine lifespan (*dibbena āyunā*), in divine beauty (*dibbena vaṇṇena*), in divine pleasure (*dibbena sukhena*), in divine fame (*dibbena yasena*), and in divine sovereignty (*dibbena ādhipateyyena*); and in divine forms (*dibbehi rūpehi*), sounds (*dibbehi saddehi*), odors (*dibbehi gandhehi*), tastes (*dibbehi rasehi*), and tactile objects (*dibbehi phoṭṭhabbehi*).

Having fallen from there, and come again to this state, he acquires this characteristic of a great man (*mahāpurisalakkhaṇaṃ paṭilabhati*):

He has well-placed feet (*suppatiṭṭhitapādo hoti*).

He places his foot evenly on the ground, raises it evenly, and touches the ground evenly with the entire surface of the sole of his foot.
commentary_pali:
201.Purimaṃjātintiādīsu pubbe nivutthakkhandhā jātavasena ‘‘jātī’’ti vuttā. Tathā bhavanavasena ‘‘bhavo’’ti, nivutthavasena ālayaṭṭhena vā ‘‘niketo’’ti. Tiṇṇampi padānaṃ pubbe nivutthakkhandhasantāne ṭhitoti attho. Idāni yasmā taṃ khandhasantānaṃ devalokādīsupi vattati. Lakkhaṇanibbattanasamatthaṃ pana kusalakammaṃ tattha na sukaraṃ, manussabhūtasseva sukaraṃ. Tasmā yathābhūtena yaṃ kammaṃ kataṃ, taṃ dassento pubbe manussabhūto samānoti āha. Akāraṇaṃ vā etaṃ. Hatthiassamigamahiṃsavānarādibhūtopi mahāpuriso pāramiyo pūretiyeva. Yasmā pana evarūpe attabhāve ṭhitena katakammaṃ na sakkā sukhena dīpetuṃ, manussabhāve ṭhitena katakammaṃ pana sakkā sukhena dīpetuṃ. Tasmā ‘‘pubbe manussabhūto samāno’’ti āha.

Daḷhasamādānoti thiragahaṇo. Kusalesu dhammesūti dasakusalakammapathesu. Avatthitasamādānoti niccalagahaṇo anivattitagahaṇo. Mahāsattassa hi akusalakammato aggiṃ patvā kukkuṭapattaṃ viya cittaṃ paṭikuṭati, kusalaṃ patvā vitānaṃ viya pasāriyati. Tasmā daḷhasamādāno hoti avatthitasamādāno. Na sakkā kenaci samaṇena vā brāhmaṇena vā devena vā mārena vā brahmunā vā kusalasamādānaṃ vissajjāpetuṃ.

Daḷhasamādāno Kusalesu dhammesū Avatthitasamādāno

Tatrimāni vatthūni – pubbe kira mahāpuriso kalandakayoniyaṃ nibbatti. Atha deve vuṭṭhe ogho āgantvā kulāvakaṃ gahetvā samuddameva pavesesi. Mahāpuriso ‘‘puttake nīharissāmī’’ti naṅguṭṭhaṃ temetvā temetvā samuddato udakaṃ bahi khipi. Sattame divase sakko āvajjitvā tattha āgamma ‘‘kiṃ karosī’’ti pucchi? So tassa ārocesi. Sakko mahāsamuddato udakassa dunnīharaṇīyabhāvaṃ kathesi. Bodhisatto tādisena kusītena saddhiṃ kathetumpi na vaṭṭati. ‘‘Mā idha tiṭṭhā’’ti apasāresi. Sakko ‘‘anomapurisena gahitagahaṇaṃ na sakkā vissajjāpetu’’nti tuṭṭho tassa puttake ānetvā adāsi. Mahājanakakālepi mahāsamuddaṃ taramāno ‘‘kasmā mahāsamuddaṃ tarasī’’ti devatāya puṭṭho ‘‘pāraṃ gantvā kulasantake raṭṭhe rajjaṃ gahetvā dānaṃ dātuṃ tarāmī’’ti āha. Tato devatāya – ‘‘ayaṃ mahāsamuddo gambhīro ceva puthulo ca, kadā naṃ tarissatī’’ti vutte so āha ‘‘taveso mahāsamuddasadiso, mayhaṃ pana ajjhāsayaṃ āgamma khuddakamātikā viya khāyati. Tvaṃyeva maṃ dakkhissasi samuddaṃ taritvā samuddapārato dhanaṃ āharitvā kulasantakaṃ rajjaṃ gahetvā dānaṃ dadamāna’’nti. Devatā ‘‘anomapurisena gahitagahaṇaṃ na sakkā vissajjāpetu’’nti bodhisattaṃ āliṅgetvā haritvā uyyāne nipajjāpesi. So chattaṃ ussāpetvā divase divase pañcasatasahassapariccāgaṃ katvā aparabhāge nikkhamma pabbajito. Evaṃ mahāsatto na sakkā kenaci samaṇena vā…pe… brahmunā vā kusalasamādānaṃ vissajjāpetuṃ. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘daḷhasamādāno ahosi kusalesu dhammesu avatthitasamādāno’’ti.

Idāni yesu kusalesu dhammesu avatthitasamādāno ahosi, te dassetuṃ kāyasucaritetiādimāha. Dānasaṃvibhāgeti ettha ca dānameva diyyanavasena dānaṃ, saṃvibhāgakaraṇavasena saṃvibhāgo. Sīlasamādāneti pañcasīladasasīlacatupārisuddhisīlapūraṇakāle. Uposathūpavāseti cātuddasikādibhedassa uposathassa upavasanakāle. Matteyyatāyāti mātukātabbavatte. Sesapadesupi eseva nayo. Aññataraññataresu cāti aññesu ca evarūpesu. Adhikusalesūti ettha atthi kusalā, atthi adhikusalā. Sabbepi kāmāvacarā kusalā kusalā nāma, rūpāvacarā adhikusalā. Ubhopi te kusalā nāma, arūpāvacarā adhikusalā. Sabbepi te kusalā nāma, sāvakapāramīpaṭilābhapaccayā kusalā adhikusalā nāma. Tepi kusalā nāma, paccekabodhipaṭilābhapaccayā kusalā adhikusalā. Tepi kusalā nāma, sabbaññutaññāṇappaṭilābhapaccayā pana kusalā idha ‘‘adhikusalā’’ti adhippetā. Tesu adhikusalesu dhammesu daḷhasamādāno ahosi avatthitasamādāno.

kāyasucarite Dānasaṃvibhāge Sīlasamādāne Uposathūpavāse Matteyyatāyā Aññataraññataresu cā Adhikusalesū

Kaṭattā upacitattāti ettha sakimpi kataṃ katameva, abhiṇhakaraṇena pana upacitaṃ hoti. Ussannattāti piṇḍīkataṃ rāsīkataṃ kammaṃ ussannanti vuccati. Tasmā ‘‘ussannattā’’ti vadanto mayā katakammassa cakkavāḷaṃ atisambādhaṃ, bhavaggaṃ atinīcaṃ, evaṃ me ussannaṃ kammanti dasseti. Vipulattāti appamāṇattā. Iminā ‘‘anantaṃ aparimāṇaṃ mayā kataṃ kamma’’nti dasseti. Adhiggaṇhātīti adhibhavati, aññehi devehi atirekaṃ labhatīti attho. Paṭilabhatīti adhigacchati.

Kaṭattā upacitattā Ussannattā Vipulattā Adhiggaṇhātī Paṭilabhatī

Sabbāvantehi pādatalehīti idaṃ ‘‘samaṃ pādaṃ bhūmiyaṃ nikkhipatī’’ti etassa vitthāravacanaṃ. Tattha sabbāvantehīti sabbapadesavantehi, na ekena padesena paṭhamaṃ phusati, na ekena pacchā, sabbeheva pādatalehi samaṃ phusati, samaṃ uddharati. Sacepi hi tathāgato ‘‘anekasataporisaṃ narakaṃ akkamissāmī’’ti pādaṃ abhinīharati. Tāvadeva ninnaṭṭhānaṃ vātapūritā viya kammārabhastā unnamitvā pathavisamaṃ hoti. Unnataṭṭhānampi anto pavisati. ‘‘Dūre akkamissāmī’’ti abhinīharantassa sineruppamāṇopi pabbato suseditavettaṅkuro viya onamitvā pādasamīpaṃ āgacchati. Tathā hissa yamakapāṭihāriyaṃ katvā ‘‘yugandharapabbataṃ akkamissāmī’’ti pāde abhinīhaṭe pabbato onamitvā pādasamīpaṃ āgato. Sopi taṃ akkamitvā dutiyapādena tāvatiṃsabhavanaṃ akkami. Na hi cakkalakkhaṇena patiṭṭhātabbaṭṭhānaṃ visamaṃ bhavituṃ sakkoti. Khāṇu vā kaṇṭako vā sakkharā vā kathalā vā uccārapassāvakheḷasiṅghāṇikādīni vā purimataraṃ vā apagacchanti, tattha tattheva vā pathaviṃ pavisanti. Tathāgatassa hi sīlatejena puññatejena dhammatejena dasannaṃ pāramīnaṃ ānubhāvena ayaṃ mahāpathavī sammā mudupupphābhikiṇṇā hoti.

Sabbāvantehi pādatalehī
commentary_english:
201. Previously, the aggregates that have ceased are called "birth" (*jāti*) because of the condition of birth, etc. Similarly, because of the condition of becoming, it is called "becoming" (*bhava*), and because of the condition of having ceased, or due to the meaning of clinging, it is called "abode" (*niketo*). The meaning is that the three terms also abide in the continuum of aggregates that have ceased. Now, since that continuum of aggregates exists even in the heavens, etc., it is not easy there to perform wholesome actions capable of producing characteristics, but it is easy for one who has become a human being. Therefore, showing the action that was done in accordance with reality, he said, "previously, having become a human being." Or, this is without cause. Even having become an elephant, horse, deer, buffalo, monkey, etc., a great being fulfills the perfections. Since it is not possible to easily illuminate the action that was done by one abiding in such a form of self, but it is possible to easily illuminate the action that was done by one abiding in the state of a human being, therefore, he said, "previously, having become a human being." *Dṛḍhasamādāna* means firm grasping. *Kusalesu dhammesu* means in the paths of the ten wholesome actions. *Avatiṭṭhitasamādāna* means unwavering grasping, unshakeable grasping. For a great being, the mind recoils upon encountering unwholesome action, like a chicken feather encountering fire; upon encountering wholesome action, it spreads out like an awning. Therefore, he is firm in his resolve; he is unwavering in his resolve. It is not possible for any *śramaṇa*, *brāhmaṇa*, god, *Māra*, or *Brahmā* to cause him to abandon his wholesome resolve. Firm in resolve, in wholesome qualities, unwavering in resolve. These are the topics: It is said that previously a great being was born in a *kalandaka* womb. Then, when the god rose, a flood came, took the nest, and threw it into the ocean. The great being, thinking, "I will bring out my children," wetted his tail again and again and threw water out of the ocean. On the seventh day, *Śakra*, reflecting, came there and asked, "What are you doing?" He declared it to him. *Śakra* spoke of the difficult-to-remove nature of the water from the great ocean. The *bodhisattva* does not even deserve to converse with such a lazy person. He drove him away, saying, "Do not stand here!" *Śakra*, pleased, thinking, "It is not possible to make one abandon what has been grasped by an extraordinary person," brought his children and gave them to him. Even in the time of Mahājanaka, while crossing the great ocean, when asked by a deity, "Why are you crossing the great ocean?" he said, "Having gone to the other shore, having taken the kingdom in the realm belonging to my family, I am crossing over in order to give charity." Then the deity said, "This great ocean is deep and wide; when will you cross it?" He said, "This is like a great ocean to you, but having come into my intention, it appears like a small matika. You yourself will see me, having crossed the ocean, having brought wealth from beyond the ocean, having taken the kingdom belonging to my family, giving charity." The deity, thinking, "It is not possible to make one abandon what has been grasped by an extraordinary person," embraced the *bodhisattva*, carried him away, and laid him down in a garden. He raised a parasol, made a donation of five hundred thousand each day, and having gone out in the later part of the day, he went forth. Thus, it is not possible for any great being to be made to abandon his wholesome resolve by any *śramaṇa*, or…or…*Brahmā*. Therefore, it was said, "He was firm in his resolve; he was unwavering in his resolve in wholesome qualities." Now, in order to show in which wholesome qualities he was unwavering in his resolve, he said, "*kāyasucarita*, etc." "In giving and sharing," here, *dāna* is indeed giving in the sense of bestowing, while *saṃvibhāga* is sharing in the sense of dispensing. "In undertaking morality," at the time of fulfilling the five precepts (*pañca-śīla*), the ten precepts (*daśa-śīla*), the four-fold purity of morality (*catu-pārisuddhi-śīla*). "In observing the *uposatha*," at the time of fasting on the *uposatha*, which has distinctions beginning with the fourteenth day (*cātuddasika*). "In maternal regard," in conduct befitting a mother. The same principle applies to the remaining clauses as well. "And in one or another," means in other such cases. "In superior virtuous qualities," here, there are virtuous qualities (*kuśala*), and there are superior virtuous qualities (*adhikuśala*). All wholesome qualities in the desire realm (*kāmāvacarā*) are called wholesome (*kuśala*), while those in the form realm (*rūpāvacarā*) are superior wholesome qualities (*adhikuśala*). Both of these are called wholesome (*kuśala*), while those in the formless realm (*arūpāvacarā*) are superior wholesome qualities (*adhikuśala*). All of these are called wholesome, because of the conditions for obtaining the perfections of a disciple (*śrāvaka-pāramī*), wholesome qualities (*kuśala*) are called superior wholesome qualities (*adhikuśala*). These too are called wholesome, because of the conditions for obtaining the *pratyekabuddha*-enlightenment, wholesome qualities are superior wholesome qualities. These too are called wholesome, but because of the conditions for obtaining the all-knowing wisdom (*sarvajñuta-jñāna*), wholesome qualities here are "understood as superior wholesome qualities (*adhikusalā*)." In those superior wholesome qualities (*adhikuśalesu dhammesu*), he was firm in his resolve (*dṛḍha-samādāna*), he was unwavering in his resolve (*avastitha-samādāna*).

In bodily good conduct (*kāya-sucarite*), in giving and sharing (*dāna-saṃvibhāge*), in undertaking morality (*śīla-samādāne*), in observing the *uposatha* (*uposatha-upavāse*), in maternal regard (*matteyyatāyā*), and in one or another (*aññataraññataresu ca*), in superior wholesome qualities (*adhikusalā*).

In having done and accumulated," here, having done it even once is "having done" it, but through frequent doing, it becomes "accumulated." "Because of being heaped up," an action that is massed together and piled up is called "heaped up (*ussanna*)." Therefore, saying "because of being heaped up (*ussannattā*)," he shows that "the universe (*cakravāḷa*) is extremely crowded for the karma I have done (*kata-kammassa*), the peak of existence (*bhavagga*) is extremely low; thus, my karma is heaped up (*ussannaṃ kammanti*)." "Because of being extensive," because of being immeasurable (*appamāṇattā*). By this, he shows "I have done karma that is endless (*anantaṃ*), immeasurable (*aparimāṇaṃ*)." "He fully grasps," means he dominates, he obtains an excess over other gods, this is the meaning. "He obtains," means he attains.

In having done and accumulated, because of being heaped up, because of being extensive, he fully grasps. He obtains. In all the soles of his feet," this is an expanded explanation of "he places his foot evenly on the ground (*samaṃ pādaṃ bhūmiyaṃ nikkhipati*)." There, "in all the soles of his feet" means with all the surfaces of his feet; he does not first touch with one surface, nor later with one surface, but he touches evenly with all the soles of his feet, and he lifts up evenly. Even if the *Tathāgata* brings down his foot, thinking "I will tread on hell filled with hundreds of men (*anekasataporisaṃ narakaṃ akkamissāmī*)," at that very moment, a low place (*ninnaṭṭhānaṃ*) rises up like a bellows filled with wind (*vātapūritā viya kammārabhastā*), becoming level with the earth. Even a high place enters within. To one who intends, "I will step far away (*dūre akkamissāmī*)," even a mountain the size of Mount Meru, bends down like a well-trained rattan shoot, coming to the vicinity of his foot. Thus, for him, having performed the twin miracle (*yamaka-pāṭihāriyaṃ katvā*), when he brought down his foot, intending "I will step on Mount Yugandhara (*yugandharapabbataṃ akkamissāmī*)," the mountain bent down, coming to the vicinity of his foot. He too, having stepped on that, stepped with his second foot into the *Tāvatiṃsa* heaven. For a place that should be supported by the wheel marks cannot be uneven. A stump, or a thorn, or gravel, or a potsherd, or excrement, urine, saliva, mucus, and so forth either go away beforehand, or they enter the earth right there. For the *Tathāgata*, by the power of his moral conduct (*śīla-tejas*), by the power of his merit (*puṇya-tejas*), by the power of his *dharma* (*dhamma-tejas*), by the power of the ten perfections (*pāramī*), this great earth is strewn with soft, lovely flowers.

mula_pali: 202. ‘‘So tena lakkhaṇena samannāgato sace agāraṃ ajjhāvasati, rājā hoti cakkavattī dhammiko dhammarājā cāturanto vijitāvī janapadatthāvariyappatto sattaratanasamannāgato. Tassimāni satta ratanāni bhavanti; seyyathidaṃ, cakkaratanaṃ hatthiratanaṃ assaratanaṃ maṇiratanaṃ itthiratanaṃ gahapatiratanaṃ pariṇāyakaratanameva sattamaṃ. Parosahassaṃ kho panassa puttā bhavanti sūrā vīraṅgarūpā parasenappamaddanā. So imaṃ pathaviṃ sāgarapariyantaṃ akhilamanimittamakaṇṭakaṃ iddhaṃ phītaṃ khemaṃ sivaṃ nirabbudaṃ adaṇḍena asatthena dhammena abhivijiya ajjhāvasati . Rājā samāno kiṃ labhati? Akkhambhiyo avikkhambhiyo (sī. pī.) hoti kenaci manussabhūtena paccatthikena paccāmittena. Rājā samāno idaṃ labhati. ‘‘Sace kho pana agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajati, arahaṃ hoti sammāsambuddho loke vivaṭṭacchado. Buddho samāno kiṃ labhati? Akkhambhiyo hoti abbhantarehi vā bāhirehi vā paccatthikehi paccāmittehi rāgena vā dosena vā mohena vā samaṇena vā brāhmaṇena vā devena vā mārena vā brahmunā vā kenaci vā lokasmiṃ. Buddho samāno idaṃ labhati’’. Etamatthaṃ bhagavā avoca.
mula_english:
202.
"So, endowed with those marks, if he lives the household life, he becomes a ruler, a wheel-turning monarch ( *cakravartin*), a righteous king who rules by the *dharma*, master of the four quarters, all-victorious, who has stabilized his country and possesses the seven treasures (*saptaratnasamannāgata*).

He has these seven treasures (*sapta ratnani*): namely, the wheel-treasure (*cakraratna*), the elephant-treasure (*hatthiratna*), the horse-treasure (*assaratna*), the jewel-treasure (*maṇiratna*), the woman-treasure (*itthiratna*), the steward-treasure (*gahapatiratna*), and the counselor-treasure (*pariṇāyakaratanameva*) as the seventh.

He has more than a thousand sons who are heroes, of heroic stature (*vīraṅgarūpā*), conquerors of the hostile army (*parasenappamaddanā*).

Over this earth bounded by the ocean, he rules without a rod (*adaṇḍena*), without a weapon (*asatthena*), by means of the *dharma* (*dhammena*), having completely conquered it.

What does a king obtain? He cannot be shaken by any hostile human being.

This is what a king obtains.

"But if he goes forth from the household life into homelessness (*anagāriyaṃ pabbajati*), he becomes an *arhat*, a fully-enlightened Buddha (*sammāsambuddho*), one who draws back the veil from the world (*loke vivaṭṭacchado*).

What does a Buddha obtain? He cannot be shaken by any internal or external foes, by passion (*rāgena*) or aversion (*dosena*) or delusion (*mohena*) or by any recluse (*samaṇena*) or Brahmin (*brāhmaṇena*) or god (*devena*) or *Mara* (*māreṇa*) or *Brahma* (*brahmunā*) or anyone in the world.

This is what a Buddha obtains."

This is the meaning of what the Blessed One (*bhagavā*) said.
commentary_pali:
202.Sāgarapariyantanti sāgarasīmaṃ. Na hi tassa rajjaṃ karontassa antarā rukkho vā pabbato vā nadī vā sīmā hoti mahāsamuddova sīmā. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘sāgarapariyanta’’nti. Akhilamanimittamakaṇṭakanti niccoraṃ. Corā hi kharasamphassaṭṭhena khilā, upaddavapaccayaṭṭhena nimittā, vijjhanaṭṭhena kaṇṭakāti vuccanti. Iddhanti samiddhaṃ. Phītanti sabbasampattiphāliphullaṃ. Khemanti nibbhayaṃ. Sivanti nirupaddavaṃ. Nirabbudanti abbudavirahitaṃ, gumbaṃ gumbaṃ hutvā carantehi corehi virahitanti attho. Akkhambhiyoti avikkhambhanīyo. Na naṃ koci ṭhānato cāletuṃ sakkoti. Paccatthikenāti paṭipakkhaṃ icchantena. Paccāmittenāti paṭiviruddhena amittena. Ubhayampetaṃ sapattavevacanaṃ. Abbhantarehīti anto uṭṭhitehi rāgādīhi.

Bāhirehīti samaṇādīhi. Tathā hi naṃ bāhirā devadattakokālikādayo samaṇāpi soṇadaṇḍakūṭadaṇḍādayo brāhmaṇāpi sakkasadisā devatāpi satta vassāni anubandhamāno māropi bakādayo brahmānopi vikkhambhetuṃ nāsakkhiṃsu.

Bāhirehī

Ettāvatā bhagavatā kammañca kammasarikkhakañca lakkhaṇañca lakkhaṇānisaṃso ca vutto hoti. Kammaṃ nāma satasahassakappādhikāni cattāri asaṅkhyeyyāni daḷhavīriyena hutvā kataṃ kammaṃ. Kammasarikkhakaṃ nāma daḷhena hutvā katabhāvaṃ sadevako loko jānātūti suppatiṭṭhitapādamahāpurisalakkhaṇaṃ. Lakkhaṇaṃ nāma suppatiṭṭhitapādatā. Lakkhaṇānisaṃso nāma paccatthikehi avikkhambhanīyatā.

Kammaṃ Kammasarikkhakaṃ Lakkhaṇaṃ Lakkhaṇānisaṃso
commentary_english:
202. *Sāgarapariyanta* means *sāgarasīmaṃ* (ocean boundary).

Indeed, for one who rules, there is no tree, mountain, or river as a boundary, but the great ocean is the boundary.

Therefore it was said, "*sāgarapariyanta*."

*Akhilamanimittamakaṇṭaka* means constant thieves.

Thieves, indeed, are obstructions ( *khila*) because of their harsh touch, signs (*nimitta*) because of being the cause of misfortune, and they are called thorns (*kaṇṭaka*) because of piercing.

*Iddha* means prosperous.

*Phīta* means flourishing with all kinds of wealth and fruit.

*Khema* means fearless.

*Siva* means without distress.

*Nirabbuda* means without *abbuda*, meaning without thieves going about in groups; this is the meaning.

*Akkhambhiyo* means unshakeable.

No one is able to move him from his position.

*Paccatthikenā* means wishing for opposition (*paṭipakkhaṃ icchantena*).

*Paccāmittenā* means with an enemy who is opposed (*paṭiviruddhena amittena*).

Both of these are synonyms for an enemy (*sapattavevacanaṃ*).

*Abbhantarehī* means from internal, arisen things such as desire (*rāga*) etc.

*Bāhirehī* means from external *śramaṇa* ascetics, etc.

Thus, external Devadatta, Kokālika, etc., ascetics, Soṇadaṇḍa, Kūṭadaṇḍa, etc., *brāhmaṇa* priests, deities like Śakka, Māra who followed for seven years, Baka, etc., Brahmās, etc., were unable to shake him.

*Bāhirehī*

Thus, by the Blessed One, action (*karma*), similar action (*karmasarikkhaka*), characteristic (*lakṣaṇa*), and the benefit of the characteristic (*lakṣaṇānisaṃsa*) have been spoken.

*Karma* is an action done with firm effort for hundreds of thousands of *kalpa*s plus four *asaṅkhyeyya*s.

*Karmasarikkhaka* is that the world with the *deva*s knows the state of being done with firmness; [this is] the characteristic of a great person (*mahāpuruṣa*) with well-established feet (*supratiṭṭhitapāda*).

*Lakṣaṇa* is the state of having well-established feet (*supratiṭṭhitapādatā*).

*Lakṣaṇānisaṃsa* is the state of being unshakeable by opponents (*paccatthikehi avikkhambhanīyatā*).

*Karma*, *Karmasarikkhaka*, *Lakṣaṇa*, *Lakṣaṇānisaṃsa*

mula_pali:
203. Tatthetaṃ vuccati –

‘‘Sacce ca dhamme ca dame ca saṃyame,

Soceyyasīlālayuposathesu ca;

Dāne ahiṃsāya asāhase rato,

Daḷhaṃ samādāya samattamācari samantamācari (syā. ka.).

samantamācari (syā. ka.)

‘‘So tena kammena divaṃ samakkami apakkami (syā. ka.),

apakkami (syā. ka.)

Sukhañca khiḍḍāratiyo ca anvabhi aṃnvabhi (ṭīkā);

aṃnvabhi (ṭīkā)

Tato cavitvā punarāgato idha,

Samehi pādehi phusī vasundharaṃ.

‘‘Byākaṃsu veyyañjanikā samāgatā,

Samappatiṭṭhassa na hoti khambhanā;

Gihissa vā pabbajitassa vā puna pana (syā.),

pana (syā.)

Taṃ lakkhaṇaṃ bhavati tadatthajotakaṃ.

‘‘Akkhambhiyo hoti agāramāvasaṃ,

Parābhibhū sattubhi nappamaddano;

Manussabhūtenidha hoti kenaci,

Akkhambhiyo tassa phalena kammuno.

‘‘Sace ca pabbajjamupeti tādiso,

Nekkhammachandābhirato vicakkhaṇo;

Aggo na so gacchati jātu khambhanaṃ,

Naruttamo esa hi tassa dhammatā’’ti.

(2) Pādatalacakkalakkhaṇaṃ
mula_english:
203.
That is what is said there:

"In truth, in dharma, in self-control, and in restraint,
In purity, moral conduct, abiding place, and observance days,
In giving, non-violence, delighting in non-aggression,
Firmly undertaking, one practices completely.

Through that action, he ascends to heaven,
And experiences happiness, joy, and delight;
Then, having passed away from there and returned here,
He touches the earth with even feet.

The interpreters who have assembled declare,
“For one who is well-established, there is no obstruction;
Whether he is a householder or a renunciate again,
That characteristic is the illuminator of that meaning.”

Unobstructed, he dwells in a house,
Unconquered, not oppressed by enemies;
Being a human being here, by someone,
He is unobstructed by the fruit of his action.

If such a one goes forth into homelessness,
Delighting in renunciation and skilled,
That foremost one never goes to obstruction,
For this is the nature of that best of men."

(2) The characteristic of the wheel on the sole of the foot.
commentary_pali:
203.Tatthetaṃvuccatīti tattha vutte kammādibhede aparampi idaṃ vuccati, gāthābandhaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Etā pana gāthā porāṇakattherā ‘‘ānandattherena ṭhapitā vaṇṇanāgāthā’’ti vatvā gatā. Aparabhāge therā ‘‘ekapadiko atthuddhāro’’ti āhaṃsu.

Tattha sacceti vacīsacce. Dhammeti dasakusalakammapathadhamme. Dameti indriyadamane. Saṃyameti sīlasaṃyame. ‘‘Soceyyasīlālayuposathesu cā’’ti ettha kāyasoceyyādi tividhaṃ soceyyaṃ. Ālayabhūtaṃ sīlameva sīlālayo. Uposathakammaṃ uposatho. Ahiṃsāyāti avihiṃsāya. Samattamācarīti sakalaṃ acari.

sacce Dhamme Dame Saṃyame ‘‘Soceyyasīlālayuposathesu cā’’ soceyyaṃ. sīlālayo. uposatho. Ahiṃsāyā Samattamācarī

Anvabhīti anubhavi. Veyyañjanikāti lakkhaṇapāṭhakā. Parābhibhūti pare abhibhavanasamattho. Sattubhīti sapattehi akkhambhiyo hoti.

Anvabhī Veyyañjanikā Parābhibhū Sattubhī

Na so gacchati jātu khambhananti so ekaṃseneva aggapuggalo vikkhambhetabbataṃ na gacchati. Esā hi tassa dhammatāti tassa hi esā dhammatā ayaṃ sabhāvo.

Na so gacchati jātu khambhana Esā hi tassa dhammatā

Pādatalacakkalakkhaṇavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
203.

Thus, “*tatthetaṃ*,” it is said. There, having spoken, another thing is said in the distinction of karma and so forth; with reference to the structure of verses, it is spoken.
However, these verses, the old elders, having said, “The *vaṇṇanā* verses were established by Ānanda,” departed.
In another part, the elders said, “*ekapadiko atthuddhāro*.”

There, “*sacce*” means truthful speech (*vacīsacce*).
“*dhamme*” means the ten paths of wholesome action (*dasakusalakammapathadhamme*).
“*dame*” means the taming of the senses (*indriyadamane*).
“*saṃyame*” means restraint in ethics (*sīlasaṃyame*).
“*‘‘soceyyasīlālayuposathesu cā’’*” here, *soceyya*, threefold, such as purity of body and so forth.
Morality, which is the basis, is indeed the abode of morality (*sīlālayo*).
The *uposatha* action is the *uposatho*.
“*ahiṃsāyā*” means non-violence (*avihiṃsāya*).
“*samattamācarī*” means all (*sakalaṃ*) was practiced (*acari*).

*sacce*, *dhamme*, *dame*, *saṃyame*, *‘‘soceyyasīlālayuposathesu cā’’*, *soceyyaṃ*.
*sīlālayo*.
*uposatho*.
*ahiṃsāyā*, *samattamācarī* “*anvabhī*” means experience (*anubhavi*).
“*veyyañjanikā*” means those who recite the characteristics (*lakkhaṇapāṭhakā*).
“*parābhibhū*” means capable of overcoming the enemy (*pare abhibhavanasamattho*).
“*sattubhī*” means he is unshakeable by enemies (*sapattehi akkhambhiyo hoti*).

*anvabhī*, *veyyañjanikā*, *parābhibhū*, *sattubhī* “*na so gacchati jātu khambhana*” means that foremost person never goes to a state of being obstructed by anyone.
“*esā hi tassa dhammatā*” means this is his nature; this is his inherent quality (*ayaṃ sabhāvo*).

*na so gacchati jātu khambhana*, *esā hi tassa dhammatā*.
Explanation of the characteristics of the wheel-mark on the sole of the foot (*pādatalacakkalakkhaṇavaṇṇanā*).

mula_pali:
204. ‘‘Yampi, bhikkhave, tathāgato purimaṃ jātiṃ purimaṃ bhavaṃ purimaṃ niketaṃ pubbe manussabhūto samāno bahujanassa sukhāvaho ahosi, ubbegauttāsabhayaṃ apanuditā, dhammikañca rakkhāvaraṇaguttiṃ saṃvidhātā, saparivārañca dānaṃ adāsi. So tassa kammassa kaṭattā upacitattā ussannattā vipulattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati…pe… so tato cuto itthattaṃ āgato samāno imaṃ mahāpurisalakkhaṇaṃ paṭilabhati. Heṭṭhāpādatalesu cakkāni jātāni honti sahassārāni sanemikāni sanābhikāni sabbākāraparipūrāni suvibhattantarāni.

‘‘So tena lakkhaṇena samannāgato sace agāraṃ ajjhāvasati, rājā hoti cakkavattī…pe… rājā samāno kiṃ labhati? Mahāparivāro hoti; mahāssa honti parivārā brāhmaṇagahapatikā negamajānapadā gaṇakamahāmattā anīkaṭṭhā dovārikā amaccā pārisajjā rājāno bhogiyā kumārā. Rājā samāno idaṃ labhati. Sace kho pana agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajati, arahaṃ hoti sammāsambuddho loke vivaṭṭacchado. Buddho samāno kiṃ labhati? Mahāparivāro hoti; mahāssa honti parivārā bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo upāsakā upāsikāyo devā manussā asurā nāgā gandhabbā. Buddho samāno idaṃ labhati’’. Etamatthaṃ bhagavā avoca.
mula_english:
204.
’’And also, monks, the *tathāgata* in a former birth, a former existence, a former dwelling, having previously been a human being, was the bringer of ease to many people, he drove away agitation, terror, and fear, and he was a provider of just protection, warding and safety, and he gave gifts together with his retinue.

Through the effect, accumulation, abundance, and magnitude of that action, at the breaking up of the body, after death, he is reborn into a happy destination, a heavenly world…pe… having passed away from there and come to this state, he obtains this mark of a great man.

On the soles of his feet, wheels are born, with a thousand spokes, with rims, with hubs, complete in all aspects, with well-defined divisions.

’’He who possesses this mark, if he lives in the household, becomes a king, a wheel-turner…pe… What does the king obtain when he is in the same state? He has a large retinue; brahmins, householders, town and country people, accountants, high officials, army officers, gatekeepers, advisors, attendants, kings, enjoyers, and princes have a large retinue.

The king obtains this when he is in the same state.

But if he goes forth from the household life into homelessness, then he becomes an *arhat*, a perfectly awakened Buddha, one who draws back the veil in the world.

What does the Buddha obtain when he is in the same state? He has a large retinue; monks, nuns, male lay followers, female lay followers, gods, humans, *asuras*, *nāgas*, and *gandharvas* have a large retinue.

The Buddha obtains this when he is in the same state.’’

The Blessed One said this was the meaning.
commentary_pali:
204.Ubbegauttāsabhayanti ubbegabhayañceva uttāsabhayañca. Tattha corato vā rājato vā paccatthikato vā vilopanabandhanādinissayaṃ bhayaṃ ubbego nāma, taṃmuhuttikaṃ caṇḍahatthiassādīni vā ahiyakkhādayo vā paṭicca lomahaṃsanakaraṃ bhayaṃ uttāsabhayaṃ nāma. Taṃ sabbaṃ apanuditā vūpasametā. Saṃvidhātāti saṃvidahitā. Kathaṃ saṃvidahati? Aṭaviyaṃ sāsaṅkaṭṭhānesu dānasālaṃ kāretvā tattha āgate bhojetvā manusse datvā ativāheti, taṃ ṭhānaṃ pavisituṃ asakkontānaṃ manusse pesetvā paveseti. Nagarādīsupi tesu tesu ṭhānesu ārakkhaṃ ṭhapeti, evaṃ saṃvidahati. Saparivārañca dānaṃ adāsīti annaṃ pānanti dasavidhaṃ dānavatthuṃ.

Tattha annanti yāgubhattaṃ. Taṃ dadanto na dvāre ṭhapetvā adāsi, atha kho antonivesane haritupalittaṭṭhāne lājā ceva pupphāni ca vikiritvā āsanaṃ paññapetvā vitānaṃ bandhitvā gandhadhūmādīhi sakkāraṃ katvā bhikkhusaṅghaṃ nisīdāpetvā yāguṃ adāsi. Yāguṃ dento ca sabyañjanaṃ adāsi. Yāgupānāvasāne pāde dhovitvā telena makkhetvā nānappakārakaṃ anantaṃ khajjakaṃ datvā pariyosāne anekasūpaṃ anekabyañjanaṃ paṇītabhojanaṃ adāsi . Pānaṃ dento ambapānādiaṭṭhavidhaṃ pānaṃ adāsi, tampi yāgubhattaṃ datvā. Vatthaṃ dento na suddhavatthameva adāsi, ekapaṭṭadupaṭṭādipahonakaṃ pana datvā sucimpi adāsi, suttampi adāsi, suttaṃ vaṭṭesi, sūcikammakaraṇaṭṭhāne bhikkhūnaṃ āsanāni, yāgubhattaṃ, pādamakkhanaṃ, piṭṭhimakkhanaṃ, rajanaṃ, paṇḍupalāsaṃ, rajanadoṇikaṃ, antamaso cīvararajanakaṃ kappiyakārakampi adāsi.

anna

Yānanti upāhanaṃ. Taṃ dadantopi upāhanatthavikaṃ upāhanadaṇḍakaṃ makkhanatelaṃ heṭṭhā vuttāni ca annādīni tasseva parivāraṃ katvā adāsi. Mālaṃ dentopi na suddhamālameva adāsi, atha kho naṃ gandhehi missetvā heṭṭhimāni cattāri tasseva parivāraṃ katvā adāsi. Bodhicetiyaāsanapotthakādipūjanatthāya ceva cetiyagharadhūpanatthāya ca gandhaṃ dentopi na suddhagandhameva adāsi, gandhapisanakanisadāya ceva pakkhipanakabhājanena ca saddhiṃ heṭṭhimāni pañca tassa parivāraṃ katvā adāsi. Cetiyapūjādīnaṃ atthāya haritālamanosilācīnapiṭṭhādivilepanaṃ dentopi na suddhavilepanameva adāsi, vilepanabhājanena saddhiṃ heṭṭhimāni cha tassa parivāraṃ katvā adāsi. Seyyāti mañcapīṭhaṃ. Taṃ dentopi na suddhakameva adāsi, kojavakambalapaccattharaṇamañcappaṭipādakehi saddhiṃ antamaso maṅgulasodhanadaṇḍakaṃ heṭṭhimāni ca satta tassa parivāraṃ katvā adāsi. Āvasathaṃ dentopi na gehamattameva adāsi, atha kho naṃ mālākammalatākammapaṭimaṇḍitaṃ supaññattaṃ mañcapīṭhaṃ kāretvā heṭṭhimāni aṭṭha tassa parivāraṃ katvā adāsi. Padīpeyyanti padīpatelaṃ. Taṃ dento cetiyaṅgaṇe bodhiyaṅgaṇe dhammassavanagge vasanagehe potthakavācanaṭṭhāne iminā dīpaṃ jālāpethāti na suddhatelameva adāsi, vaṭṭi kapallakatelabhājanādīhi saddhiṃ heṭṭhimāni nava tassa parivāraṃ katvā adāsi. Suvibhattantarānīti suvibhattaantarāni.

Yāna Mālaṃ gandhaṃ vilepanaṃ Seyyā Āvasathaṃ Padīpeyya Suvibhattantarānī

Rājānoti abhisittā. Bhogiyāti bhojakā kumārāti rājakumārā. Idha kammaṃ nāma saparivāraṃ dānaṃ. Kammasarikkhakaṃ nāma saparivāraṃ katvā dānaṃ adāsīti iminā kāraṇena sadevako loko jānātūti nibbattaṃ cakkalakkhaṇaṃ. Lakkhaṇaṃ nāma tadeva cakkalakkhaṇaṃ. Ānisaṃso mahāparivāratā.

Rājāno Bhogiyā kumārā kammaṃ Kammasarikkhakaṃ Lakkhaṇaṃ Ānisaṃso
commentary_english:
204. *Ubbegauttāsabhaya* means *ubbegabhayañceva* and *uttāsabhayañca*.

Therein, fear that relies on robbery, imprisonment, and so on, from a thief, a king, or an enemy is called *ubbego*; fear that causes one’s hair to stand on end in that very moment, which comes from fierce elephants, horses, and so on, or from snakes, *yakṣas*, and so on, is called *uttāsabhaya*.

Having driven away all of that, they are calmed.

*Saṃvidhātā* means *saṃvidahitā*.

How does [one] arrange? Having had a gift hall made in a forest in dangerous places, having fed those who come there, having given to people, one spends time, sending people and causing [others] to enter that place which [they are] unable to enter.

Even in towns and so on, in those places, one stations a guard; thus, one arranges.

“And he gave gifts with a retinue” means ten kinds of gift items: food and drink.

Therein, *anna* means rice gruel.

When giving that, he did not give [it] having placed [them] at the door; rather, inside the residence, in a place smeared with green clay, having scattered fried grain as well as flowers, having prepared a seat, having hung an awning, having made an offering with scents, incense, and so on, having had the community of monks sit down, he gave rice gruel.

When giving rice gruel, he gave it with curry.

At the end of the rice gruel and drink, having washed [their] feet, having smeared [them] with oil, having given various kinds of endless snacks, at the end, he gave many soups, many curries, and delicious food.

When giving a drink, he gave eight kinds of drinks, beginning with mango drink, and he also gave that having given rice gruel.

When giving cloth, he did not give only pure cloth; but, having given what is sufficient for one or two cloths, and so on, he also gave a needle, he also gave thread, he twisted the thread, and in a place for needlework, he gave seats for the monks, rice gruel, foot ointment, back ointment, dye, yellow leaves, a dye trough, and even a *kappiyakāraka* for dyeing robes.

*Anna*.

*Yāna* means shoes.

When giving that, he also gave a shoe bag, a shoe stick, ointment oil, and the food and so on mentioned above, having made that itself into a retinue.

When giving a garland, he did not give only a pure garland; rather, having mixed that with scents, he made those four themselves into a retinue and gave [them].

When giving scents for the sake of honoring a Bodhi tree shrine, a seat, books, and so on, and for the sake of incensing a shrine house, he did not give only pure scent; but, along with a scent grinding stone and a vessel for putting [it] in, he made those five themselves into a retinue and gave [them].

When giving ointment for the sake of honoring a shrine, and so on, he did not give only pure ointment, such as yellow orpiment, realgar, Chinese flour paste, and so on; but, along with an ointment vessel, he made those six themselves into a retinue and gave [them].

*Seyyā* means a couch seat.

When giving that, he did not give only a pure one; but, along with a goat’s-hair blanket, a woolen blanket, a covering, a couch, and implements, at the very least, a *maṅgulasodhana* stick, he made those seven themselves into a retinue and gave [them].

*Āvasatha* means lodging.

When giving that, he did not give only a house; rather, having had a well-made and nicely appointed couch seat decorated with garlands, carvings, creeper carvings made, he made those eight themselves into a retinue and gave [them].

*Padīpeyya* means lamp oil.

When giving that, saying, "By this, light a lamp in a shrine courtyard, in a Bodhi tree courtyard, in a *dharmmasavana* hall, in a dwelling house, and in a book reading place," he did not give only pure oil; but, along with a wick, a potsherd, an oil vessel, and so on, he made those nine themselves into a retinue and gave [them].

*Suvibhattantarānī* means *suvibhattaantarāni*.

*Yāna*, *māla*, *gandha*, *vilepana*, *seyyā*, *āvasatha*, *padīpeyya*, *suvibhattantarānī*.

*Rājāno* means those anointed.

*Bhogiyā* means *bhojakā*; *kumārā* means princes.

Here, *kammaṃ* means a gift with a retinue.

*Kammasarikkhakaṃ* means that because he gave a gift having made a retinue, may the world with the gods know!—the wheel mark has arisen.

*Lakkhaṇaṃ* means that same wheel mark.

*Ānisaṃso* [is] having a large retinue.

*Rājāno*, *bhogiyā*, *kumārā*.
*karmaṃ karmasarikkhakaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ ānisaṃso*: action, its similar characteristic, its characteristic, and its benefit.

mula_pali:
205. Tatthetaṃ vuccati –

‘‘Pure puratthā purimāsu jātisu,

Manussabhūto bahunaṃ sukhāvaho;

Ubbhegauttāsabhayāpanūdano,

Guttīsu rakkhāvaraṇesu ussuko.

‘‘So tena kammena divaṃ samakkami,

Sukhañca khiḍḍāratiyo ca anvabhi;

Tato cavitvā punarāgato idha,

Cakkāni pādesu duvesu vindati.

‘‘Samantanemīni sahassarāni ca,

Byākaṃsu veyyañjanikā samāgatā;

Disvā kumāraṃ satapuññalakkhaṇaṃ,

Parivāravā hessati sattumaddano.

Tathā hī cakkāni samantanemini,

Sace na pabbajjamupeti tādiso;

Vatteti cakkaṃ pathaviṃ pasāsati,

Tassānuyantādha tassānuyuttā idha (sī. pī.), tassānuyantā idha (syā. ka.) bhavanti khattiyā.

tassānuyuttā idha (sī. pī.), tassānuyantā idha (syā. ka.)

‘‘Mahāyasaṃ saṃparivārayanti naṃ,

Sace ca pabbajjamupeti tādiso;

Nekkhammachandābhirato vicakkhaṇo,

Devāmanussāsurasakkarakkhasā sattarakkhasā (ka.) sī. syāaṭṭhakathā oloketabbā.

sattarakkhasā (ka.) sī. syāaṭṭhakathā oloketabbā

‘‘Gandhabbanāgā vihagā catuppadā,

Anuttaraṃ devamanussapūjitaṃ;

Mahāyasaṃ saṃparivārayanti na’’nti.

(3-5) Āyatapaṇhitāditilakkhaṇaṃ
mula_english:
205. Thus, it is said:

“In former births, long ago,
Having been a human, bringing joy to many,
Dispelling agitation, fright, and fear,
Diligent in guards, protections, and defenses.

“Through that action, he ascended to heaven,
Experienced happiness, sports, and delights;
Having passed away from there, returned again here,
He finds wheels on both feet.

“With rims all around and a thousand spokes,
The interpreters, having gathered, declared:
‘Having seen the prince, with a hundred meritorious marks,
He will have a retinue, a destroyer of enemies.’

“Thus, indeed, are the wheels with rims all around;
If he does not go forth into homelessness, being such;
He will turn the wheel, he will rule the earth,
To him will be subject the nobles.

“They attend upon him, greatly renowned,
And if he goes forth into homelessness, being such;
Delighting in the desire for renunciation, discerning,
Gods, humans, asuras, and *sakkara* demons.

“Gandharvas, nāgas, birds, quadrupeds,
The unsurpassed, worshipped by gods and humans;
They attend upon him, greatly renowned.”

(3-5) The characteristic marks beginning with long heels.
commentary_pali:
205.Tatthetaṃ vuccatīti imā tadatthaparidīpanā gāthā vuccanti. Duvidhā hi gāthā honti – tadatthaparidīpanā ca visesatthaparidīpanā ca. Tattha pāḷiāgatameva atthaṃ paridīpanā tadatthaparidīpanā nāma. Pāḷiyaṃ anāgataṃ paridīpanā visesatthaparidīpanā nāma. Imā pana tadatthaparidīpanā. Tattha pureti pubbe. Puratthāti tasseva vevacanaṃ. Purimāsu jātīsūti imissā jātiyā pubbekatakammapaṭikkhepadīpanaṃ. Ubbegauttāsabhayāpanūdanoti ubbegabhayassa ca uttāsabhayassa ca apanūdano. Ussukoti adhimutto.

Satapuññalakkhaṇanti satena satena puññakammena nibbattaṃ ekekaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ. Evaṃ sante yo koci buddho bhaveyyāti na rocayiṃsu, anantesu pana cakkavāḷesu sabbe sattā ekekaṃ kammaṃ satakkhattuṃ kareyyuṃ, ettakehi janehi kataṃ kammaṃ bodhisatto ekova ekekaṃ sataguṇaṃ katvā nibbatto. Tasmā ‘‘satapuññalakkhaṇo’’ti imamatthaṃ rocayiṃsu. Manussāsurasakkarakkhasāti manussā ca asurā ca sakkā ca rakkhasā ca.

Satapuññalakkhaṇa Manussāsurasakkarakkhasā

Āyatapaṇhitāditilakkhaṇavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
205. tatthetaṃ vuccatīti: These verses are called *tadatthaparidīpanā*, meaning they illuminate that meaning. Indeed, there are two kinds of verses: *tadatthaparidīpanā* (illuminating that meaning) and *visesatthaparidīpanā* (illuminating a specific meaning). There, *tadatthaparidīpanā* is the name for illuminating a meaning that has already appeared in the Pāli. *visesatthaparidīpanā* is the name for illuminating something that has not appeared in the Pāli. But these are *tadatthaparidīpanā*. There, pureti: *pubbe* (formerly). puratthāti: is a synonym of that. purimāsu jātīsūti: This shows the rejection of past actions of this birth. ubbegauttāsabhayāpanūdanoti: *apanūdano* (removing) of *ubbegabhayassa* (fear of agitation) and *uttāsabhayassa* (fear of anxiety). ussukoti: *adhimutto* (resolved).

satapuññalakkhaṇanti: Each mark (lakkhaṇa) is produced by a hundred, a hundred meritorious actions (puññakammena). When it is like this, they did not approve that just anyone could become a Buddha, but that in endless world-systems, all beings might do a single action a hundred times; the Bodhisattva alone, having done an action a hundred times over by so many people, was born. Therefore, they approved this meaning: "having marks produced by a hundred meritorious actions" (satapuññalakkhaṇo). manussāsurasakkarakkhasāti: humans (manussā), asuras, *sakkā* (Śākyas?) and *rakshasas*.

satapuññalakkhaṇa manussāsurasakkarakkhasā

Description of marks such as āyatapaṇhitāditilakkhaṇa

mula_pali:
206. ‘‘Yampi, bhikkhave, tathāgato purimaṃ jātiṃ purimaṃ bhavaṃ purimaṃ niketaṃ pubbe manussabhūto samāno pāṇātipātaṃ pahāya pāṇātipātā paṭivirato ahosi nihitadaṇḍo nihitasattho lajjī dayāpanno, sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampī vihāsi. So tassa kammassa kaṭattā upacitattā ussannattā vipulattā…pe… so tato cuto itthattaṃ āgato samāno imāni tīṇi mahāpurisalakkhaṇāni paṭilabhati. Āyatapaṇhi ca hoti, dīghaṅguli ca brahmujugatto ca.

‘‘So tehi lakkhaṇehi samannāgato sace agāraṃ ajjhāvasati, rājā hoti cakkavattī…pe… rājā samāno kiṃ labhati? Dīghāyuko hoti ciraṭṭhitiko, dīghamāyuṃ pāleti, na sakkā hoti antarā jīvitā voropetuṃ kenaci manussabhūtena paccatthikena paccāmittena . Rājā samāno idaṃ labhati… buddho samāno kiṃ labhati? Dīghāyuko hoti ciraṭṭhitiko, dīghamāyuṃ pāleti, na sakkā hoti antarā jīvitā voropetuṃ paccatthikehi paccāmittehi samaṇena vā brāhmaṇena vā devena vā mārena vā brahmunā vā kenaci vā lokasmiṃ. Buddho samāno idaṃ labhati’’. Etamatthaṃ bhagavā avoca.
mula_english:
206.

“And further, monks, the *tathāgata*, when in a former life, a former existence, a former abode, as a former human being, having abandoned the taking of life (*pāṇātipātaṃ pahāya*), abstained from taking life (*pāṇātipātā paṭivirato ahosi*), laid aside the stick, laid aside the sword, was conscientious, full of kindness, abiding as one who is compassionate for the welfare of all living beings (*sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampī vihāsi*).

Because of the completion, accumulation, abundance, and vastness of that karma… so, having passed away from there, having come to this state, he obtains these three marks of a great man (*mahāpurisalakkhaṇāni*).

He also has even heels (*āyatapaṇhi ca hoti*), and he has long fingers (*dīghaṅguli ca*) and a straight body like Brahmā (*brahmujugatto ca*).

“So, <pb ed="m" n="3. 0123"/> being endowed with these marks, if he lives in a house, he becomes a king, a wheel-turning monarch (*cakravartī*)…pe… what does a king obtain? He is long-lived (*dīghāyuko hoti*) and endures long (*ciraṭṭhitiko*), he protects his long life (*dīghamāyuṃ pāleti*), and it is not possible for any human being, an adversary or enemy (*paccatthikena paccāmittena*) to remove him from life prematurely.

What does a king obtain?… What does a Buddha obtain? He is long-lived (*dīghāyuko hoti*) and endures long (*ciraṭṭhitiko*), he protects his long life (*dīghamāyuṃ pāleti*), and it is not possible for adversaries or enemies (*paccatthikehi paccāmittehi*), or a *śramaṇa*, or a *brāhmaṇa*, or a *deva*, or a *māra*, or a *brahmā*, or anyone in the world to remove him from life prematurely.

A Buddha obtains this.’

This is the meaning of what the Blessed One (*bhagavā*) said (*etamatthaṃ bhagavā avoca*)."
commentary_pali: 206.Antarāti paṭisandhito sarasacutiyā antare. Idha kammaṃ nāma pāṇātipātā virati. Kammasarikkhakaṃ nāma pāṇātipātaṃ karonto padasaddasavanabhayā aggaggapādehi akkamantā gantvā paraṃ pātenti. Atha te iminā kāraṇena tesaṃ taṃ kammaṃ jano jānātūti antovaṅkapādā vā bahivaṅkapādā vā ukkuṭikapādā vā aggakoṇḍā vā paṇhikoṇḍā vā bhavanti. Aggapādehi gantvā parassa amāritabhāvaṃ pana tathāgatassa sadevako loko iminā kāraṇena jānātūti āyatapaṇhi mahāpurisalakkhaṇaṃ nibbattati . Tathā paraṃ ghātentā unnatakāyena gacchantā aññe passissantīti onatā gantvā paraṃ ghātenti. Atha te evamime gantvā paraṃ ghātayiṃsūti nesaṃ taṃ kammaṃ iminā kāraṇena paro jānātūti khujjā vā vāmanā vā pīṭhasappi vā bhavanti. Tathāgatassa pana evaṃ gantvā paresaṃ aghātitabhāvaṃ iminā kāraṇena sadevako loko jānātūti brahmujugattamahāpurisalakkhaṇaṃ nibbattati. Tathā paraṃ ghātentā āvudhaṃ vā muggaraṃ vā gaṇhitvā muṭṭhikatahatthā paraṃ ghātenti. Te evaṃ tesaṃ parassa ghātitabhāvaṃ iminā kāraṇena jano jānātūti rassaṅgulī vā rassahatthā vā vaṅkaṅgulī vā phaṇahatthakā vā bhavanti. Tathāgatassa pana evaṃ paresaṃ aghātitabhāvaṃ sadevako loko iminā kāraṇena jānātūti dīghaṅgulimahāpurisalakkhaṇaṃ nibbattati. Idamettha kammasarikkhakaṃ. Idameva pana lakkhaṇattayaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ nāma. Dīghāyukabhāvo lakkhaṇānisaṃso.
commentary_english:
206. *Antarā* means in the *paṭisandhi* between the *sarasacuti*.
Here, *kamma* is abstaining from injuring living beings (*pāṇātipātā virati*).
*Kammasarikkhakaṃ* means those who, committing injury to living beings (*pāṇātipātaṃ karonto*), go stepping with the tips of their toes for fear of the sound of footsteps, etc., and cause others to fall (*paraṃ pātenti*).
Then, because of this cause, people know their deed (*kamma*): they have feet that are turned inward (*antovaṅkapādā*), or feet that are turned outward (*bahivaṅkapādā*), or feet that are bent (*ukkuṭikapādā*), or pointed ankles (*aggakoṇḍā*), or heels that are bent (*paṇhikoṇḍā*).
Going on the tips of the toes (*aggapādehi gantvā*), the world with the gods knows that the Tathāgata never causes others to be injured (*parassa amāritabhāvaṃ*), thus the characteristic of having level heels (*āyatapaṇhi mahāpurisalakkhaṇaṃ*) arises.
Likewise, injuring others (*paraṃ ghātentā*), going with an elevated body, [thinking] “others will see,” they go bent over and injure others (*paraṃ ghātenti*).
Then, [thinking] "these, going thus, injured others (*paraṃ ghātayiṃsūti*)," others know their deed (*kamma*) because of this cause: they are hunchbacked (*khujjā*), or dwarfs (*vāmanā*), or have hunchbacks (*pīṭhasappi*).
The world with the gods knows that the Tathāgata, going thus, never causes others to be injured (*paresaṃ aghātitabhāvaṃ*), thus the characteristic of having an upright body (*brahmujugatta mahāpurisalakkhaṇaṃ*) arises.
Likewise, injuring others (*paraṃ ghātentā*), taking a weapon (*āvudhaṃ*) or a club (*muggaraṃ*), with fists clenched, they injure others (*paraṃ ghātenti*).
They, in this way, because of this cause, people know that they caused others to be injured (*parassa ghātitabhāvaṃ*): they have short fingers (*rassaṅgulī*), or short hands (*rassahatthā*), or crooked fingers (*vaṅkaṅgulī*), or hands like a snake's hood (*phaṇahatthakā*).
The world with the gods knows that the Tathāgata, likewise, never causes others to be injured (*paresaṃ aghātitabhāvaṃ*), thus the characteristic of having long fingers (*dīghaṅguli mahāpurisalakkhaṇaṃ*) arises.
This is the similarity to the deed (*kammasarikkhakaṃ*).
This triad of characteristics (*lakkhaṇattayaṃ*) is called a characteristic (*lakkhaṇaṃ nāma*).
Having a long life (*dīghāyukabhāvo*) is the benefit of the characteristics (*lakkhaṇānisaṃso*).

mula_pali:
207. Tatthetaṃ vuccati –

‘‘Māraṇavadhabhayattano maraṇavadhabhayattano (sī. pī. ka.), maraṇavadhabhayamattano (syā.) viditvā,

maraṇavadhabhayattano (sī. pī. ka.), maraṇavadhabhayamattano (syā.)

Paṭivirato paraṃ māraṇāyahosi;

Tena sucaritena saggamagamā tena so sucaritena saggamagamāsi (syā.),

tena so sucaritena saggamagamāsi (syā.)

Sukataphalavipākamanubhosi.

‘‘Caviya punaridhāgato samāno,

Paṭilabhati idha tīṇi lakkhaṇāni;

Bhavati vipuladīghapāsaṇhiko,

Brahmāva suju subho sujātagatto.

‘‘Subhujo susu susaṇṭhito sujāto,

Mudutalunaṅguliyassa honti;

Dīghā tībhi purisavaraggalakkhaṇehi,

Cirayapanāya cirayāpanāya (syā.) kumāramādisanti.

cirayāpanāya (syā.)

‘‘Bhavati yadi gihī ciraṃ yapeti,

Cirataraṃ pabbajati yadi tato hi;

Yāpayati ca vasiddhibhāvanāya,

Iti dīghāyukatāya taṃ nimitta’’nti.

(6) Sattussadatālakkhaṇaṃ
mula_english:
Section 207. Thus, it is said:

"Knowing the fear of death, slaughter, and danger,

Being completely averse to killing,

Through that good conduct, he went to heaven,

He experienced the ripening of wholesome deeds."

"Having died and been reborn here, being the same,

He obtains here three characteristics;

He becomes one who is large, long, and broad,

Like Brahmā, he is very straight, beautiful, and well-formed."

"He has good arms, is very well-established, and well-born,

He has soft and tender fingers;

Long [life] with three excellent characteristics of a man,

For the long duration, they teach the boy."

"If a householder lives long,

If he goes forth, even longer;

He maintains through the cultivation of powers,

Thus, that is the cause of longevity."

(6) The characteristic of constant delight.
commentary_pali:
207.Maraṇavadhabhayattanoti ettha maraṇasaṅkhāto vadho maraṇavadho, maraṇavadhato bhayaṃ maraṇavadhabhayaṃ, taṃ attano jānitvā. Paṭivirato paraṃmāraṇāyāti yathā mayhaṃ maraṇato bhayaṃ mama jīvitaṃ piyaṃ, evaṃ paresampīti ñatvā paraṃ māraṇato paṭivirato ahosi. Sucaritenāti suciṇṇena. Saggamagamāti saggaṃ gato.

Caviya punaridhāgatoti cavitvā puna idhāgato. Dīghapāsaṇhikoti dīghapaṇhiko. Brahmāva sujūti brahmā viya suṭṭhu uju.

Caviya punaridhāgato Dīghapāsaṇhiko Brahmāva sujū

Subhujoti sundarabhujo. Susūti mahallakakālepi taruṇarūpo. Susaṇṭhitoti susaṇṭhānasampanno. Mudutalunaṅguliyassāti mudū ca talunā ca aṅguliyo assa. Tībhīti tīhi. Purisavaraggalakkhaṇehīti purisavarassa aggalakkhaṇehi. Cirayapanāyāti ciraṃ yāpanāya, dīghāyukabhāvāya.

Subhujo Susū Susaṇṭhito Mudutalunaṅguliyassā Tībhī Purisavaraggalakkhaṇehī Cirayapanāyā

Ciraṃ yapetīti ciraṃ yāpeti. Cirataraṃ pabbajati yadi tatoti tato cirataraṃ yāpeti, yadi pabbajatīti attho. Yāpayatica vasiddhibhāvanāyāti vasippatto hutvā iddhibhāvanāya yāpeti.

Ciraṃ yapetī Cirataraṃ pabbajati yadi tato Yāpayati ca vasiddhibhāvanāyā

Sattussadatālakkhaṇavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
207. “*Maraṇavadhabhayattano*” means here *vadha*, which is reckoned as *maraṇa*, is *maraṇavadho*; fear from *maraṇavadhato* is “*maraṇavadhabhayaṃ*”; having known that oneself.

"*Paṭivirato paraṃmāraṇāyā*" means just as for me, there is fear from death, my life is dear, so also, having known that for others, he was abstinent from killing others.

"*Sucaritenā*" means by good conduct.

"*Saggamagamā*" means he went to heaven (svarga).

"*Caviya punaridhāgato*" means having passed away, again he came here.

"*Dīghapāsaṇhiko*" means *dīghapaṇhiko*.

"*Brahmāva sujū*" means just as Brahmā, very straight.

*Caviya punaridhāgato dīghapāsaṇhiko brahmāva sujū*

"*Subhujo*" means beautiful arms.

"*Susū*" means even in old age, having a youthful form.

"*Susaṇṭhito*" means well-established and accomplished.

"*Mudutalunaṅguliyassā*" means soft and tender fingers are his.

"*Tībhī*" means by the three.

"*Purisavaraggalakkhaṇehī*" means by the characteristics of the best of men...

"*Cirayapanāyā*" means for a long duration, for the state of having a long life (dīrghāyuṣ).

*Subhujo susū susaṇṭhito mudutalunaṅguliyassā tībhī purisavaraggalakkhaṇehī cirayapanāyā*

"*Ciraṃ yapetī*" means he maintains for a long time.

"*Cirataraṃ pabbajati yadi tato*" means therefore, he maintains for a very long time, if he goes forth, this is the meaning.

"*Yāpayati* and by the development of mastery, he maintains by means of the development ofiddhi.

*Ciraṃ yapetī cirataraṃ pabbajati yadi tato yāpayati ca vasiddhibhāvanāyā*

Description of the characteristics of taste.

mula_pali:
208. ‘‘Yampi , bhikkhave, tathāgato purimaṃ jātiṃ purimaṃ bhavaṃ purimaṃ niketaṃ pubbe manussabhūto samāno dātā ahosi paṇītānaṃ rasitānaṃ khādanīyānaṃ bhojanīyānaṃ sāyanīyānaṃ lehanīyānaṃ pānānaṃ. So tassa kammassa kaṭattā…pe… so tato cuto itthattaṃ āgato samāno imaṃ mahāpurisalakkhaṇaṃ paṭilabhati, sattussado hoti, sattassa ussadā honti; ubhosu hatthesu ussadā honti, ubhosu pādesu ussadā honti, ubhosu aṃsakūṭesu ussadā honti, khandhe ussado hoti.

‘‘So tena lakkhaṇena samannāgato sace agāraṃ ajjhāvasati, rājā hoti cakkavattī…pe… rājā samāno kiṃ labhati? Lābhī hoti paṇītānaṃ rasitānaṃ khādanīyānaṃ bhojanīyānaṃ sāyanīyānaṃ lehanīyānaṃ pānānaṃ. Rājā samāno idaṃ labhati… buddho samāno kiṃ labhati? Lābhī hoti paṇītānaṃ rasitānaṃ khādanīyānaṃ bhojanīyānaṃ sāyanīyānaṃ lehanīyānaṃ pānānaṃ. Buddho samāno idaṃ labhati’’. Etamatthaṃ bhagavā avoca.
mula_english:
208.
’ Bhikkhus, since a *Tathāgata* in a former birth, in a former existence, in a former dwelling place, formerly existing as a human being, was a giver of fine delicious things, of eatables, of edibles, of savouries, of lickables and of drinks.

Since he has performed this karma…so, passing from there and coming to this state, he obtains this mark of a great man (*mahāpurisalakkhaṇa*): he has seven raised places; he has seven raised places in seven places; he has raised places on both hands; he has raised places on both feet; he has raised places on both shoulder blades; he has a raised place on the neck.

’Possessing that mark, if he dwells in a house, he becomes a wheel-turning monarch (*cakravartin*)… What does a king obtain when he is a king? He obtains fine delicious things, eatables, edibles, savouries, lickables, and drinks.

What does a king obtain when he is a king?… What does a *Buddha* obtain when he is a *Buddha*? He obtains fine delicious things, eatables, edibles, savouries, lickables, and drinks.

What does a *Buddha* obtain when he is a *Buddha*?’

The Fortunate One said this.
commentary_pali:
208.Rasitānanti rasasampannānaṃ. ‘‘Khādanīyāna’’ntiādīsu khādanīyāni nāma piṭṭhakhajjakādīni. Bhojanīyānīti pañca bhojanāni. Sāyanīyānīti sāyitabbāni sappinavanītādīni. Lehanīyānīti nillehitabbāni piṭṭhapāyāsādīni. Pānānīti aṭṭha pānakāni.

Idha kammaṃ nāma kappasatasahassādhikāni cattāri asaṅkhyeyyāni dinnaṃ idaṃ paṇītabhojanadānaṃ. Kammasarikkhakaṃ nāma lūkhabhojane kucchigate lohitaṃ sussati, maṃsaṃ milāyati. Tasmā lūkhadāyakā sattā iminā kāraṇena nesaṃ lūkhabhojanassa dinnabhāvaṃ jano jānātūti appamaṃsā appalohitā manussapetā viya dullabhannapānā bhavanti. Paṇītabhojane pana kucchigate maṃsalohitaṃ vaḍḍhati, paripuṇṇakāyā pāsādikā abhirūpadassanā honti. Tasmā tathāgatassa dīgharattaṃ paṇītabhojanadāyakattaṃ sadevako loko iminā kāraṇena jānātūti sattussadamahāpurisalakkhaṇaṃ nibbattati. Lakkhaṇaṃ nāma sattussadalakkhaṇameva. Paṇītalābhitā ānisaṃso.

kammaṃ Kammasarikkhakaṃ Lakkhaṇaṃ ānisaṃso.
commentary_english:
208. *Rasitāna* means rich in flavor.

Among "khādanīyāni," etc., *khādanīyāni* are things like piṭṭhakhajjaka. *Bhojanīyāni* are the five foods. *Sāyanīyāni* are things to be tasted like ghee and butter. *Lehanīyāni* are things to be licked up, like piṭṭhapāyāsa. *Pānāni* are the eight drinks.

Here, *kammaṃ* (karma/action) means this offering of excellent food, which was given for four incalculable periods, each exceeding one hundred thousand aeons.

*Kammasarikkhakaṃ* means that when coarse food is taken into the stomach, blood dries up, and flesh withers. Therefore, beings who give coarse food, because of this reason—so that people will know that they gave coarse food—become human ghosts with little flesh and little blood, who are hard to find food and drink.

But when excellent food is taken into the stomach, flesh and blood increase, and they are of perfect form, lovely, and beautiful to see. Therefore, so that the world with the gods will know that the Tathāgata was a giver of excellent food for a long time, the characteristic of Sattussada-mahāpurisa arises.

*Lakkhaṇaṃ* (characteristic) means just the Sattussada characteristic.

*Ānisaṃso* is the benefit of obtaining excellent things.

Karma, its resemblance, characteristic, benefit.

mula_pali:
209. Tatthetaṃ vuccati –

‘‘Khajjabhojjamatha leyya sāyiyaṃ,

Uttamaggarasadāyako ahu;

Tena so sucaritena kammunā,

Nandane ciramabhippamodati.

‘‘Satta cussade idhādhigacchati,

Hatthapādamudutañca vindati;

Āhu byañjananimittakovidā,

Khajjabhojjarasalābhitāya naṃ.

‘‘Yaṃ gihissapi na taṃ gihissāpi (syā.) tadatthajotakaṃ,

na taṃ gihissāpi (syā.)

Pabbajjampi ca tadādhigacchati;

Khajjabhojjarasalābhiruttamaṃ,

Āhu sabbagihibandhanacchida’’nti.

(7-8) Karacaraṇamudujālatālakkhaṇāni
mula_english:
209. Thus it is said:

“Chewable food, edible food, linctuses and savouries,
He was a giver of the best and chief flavours;
By that good deed,
In Nandana he rejoices for a long time.

“A being here obtains fourfold birth,
And finds soft hands and feet;
The experts in the signs of characteristics say,
'For him there is the attainment of chewable food, edible food and flavours.'

“Even what does not belong to a householder
Is an indicator of that meaning,
And then he obtains the ascetic life;
'Through the best of chewable foods, edible foods and flavours,
He is said to be a cutter of all householder bonds.”

(7-8) The characteristics of soft hands and feet, and webbed fingers.
commentary_pali:
209.Khajjabhojjamathaleyyasāyitanti khajjakañca bhojanañca lehanīyañca sāyanīyañca. Uttamaggarasadāyakoti uttamo aggarasadāyako, uttamānaṃ vā aggarasānaṃ dāyako.

Satta cussadeti satta ca ussade. Tadatthajotakanti khajjabhojjādijotakaṃ, tesaṃ lābhasaṃvattanikanti attho. Pabbajampi cāti pabbajamānopi ca. Tadādhigacchatīti taṃ adhigacchati. Lābhiruttamanti lābhi uttamaṃ.

Satta cussade Tadatthajotaka Pabbajampi cā Tadādhigacchatī Lābhiruttama

Karacaraṇādilakkhaṇavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
209. khajjabhojjamathaleyyasāyitanti *khajjakañca bhojanañca lehanīyañca sāyanīyañca*. uttamaggarasadāyakoti *uttamo aggarasadāyako, uttamānaṃ vā aggarasānaṃ dāyako*.

satta cussadeti *satta ca ussade*. tadatthajotakanti *khajjabhojjādijotakaṃ, tesaṃ lābhasaṃvattanikanti attho*. pabbajampi cāti *pabbajamānopi ca*. tadādhigacchatīti *taṃ adhigacchati*. lābhiruttamanti *lābhi uttamaṃ*.

satta cussade tadatthajotaka pabbajampi cā tadādhigacchatī lābhiruttama

Description of the characteristics of hands, feet, etc.

mula_pali:
210. ‘‘Yampi , bhikkhave, tathāgato purimaṃ jātiṃ purimaṃ bhavaṃ purimaṃ niketaṃ pubbe manussabhūto samāno catūhi saṅgahavatthūhi janaṃ saṅgāhako ahosi – dānena peyyavajjena piyavācena (syā. ka.) atthacariyāya samānattatāya. So tassa kammassa kaṭattā…pe… so tato cuto itthattaṃ āgato samāno imāni dve mahāpurisalakkhaṇāni paṭilabhati. Mudutalunahatthapādo ca hoti jālahatthapādo ca.

‘‘So tehi lakkhaṇehi samannāgato sace agāraṃ ajjhāvasati, rājā hoti cakkavattī…pe… rājā samāno kiṃ labhati? Susaṅgahitaparijano hoti, susaṅgahitāssa honti brāhmaṇagahapatikā negamajānapadā gaṇakamahāmattā anīkaṭṭhā dovārikā amaccā pārisajjā rājāno bhogiyā kumārā. Rājā samāno idaṃ labhati… buddho samāno kiṃ labhati? Susaṅgahitaparijano hoti, susaṅgahitāssa honti bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo upāsakā upāsikāyo devā manussā asurā nāgā gandhabbā. Buddho samāno idaṃ labhati’’. Etamatthaṃ bhagavā avoca.
mula_english:
210.
Monks, the *tathāgata*, when he was formerly a human being, was a benefactor of people with the four bases of sympathy—through giving (**dāna**), through amiable speech, through beneficial conduct, and through equality.

Due to performing that action… he obtains these two marks of a great man: He has soft and tender hands and feet, and he has webbed hands and feet.

If he, endowed with those marks, remains in the household, he becomes a universal monarch (**cakravartin**)… What does a king obtain? He has a well-supported retinue. The *brāhmaṇa* householders, the townspeople and rural folk, accountants, high-ranking ministers, soldiers, gatekeepers, counselors, courtiers, kings, enjoyers, and princes are well-supported. What does a king obtain?… What does a buddha obtain? He has a well-supported retinue. The monks (**bhikkhū**), nuns (**bhikkhuniyo**), male lay devotees (*upāsaka*), female lay devotees (*upāsikā*), gods (**devā**), humans (*manussa*), *asuras*, *nāgas*, and *gandharvas* are well-supported. What does a buddha obtain?
This is the meaning of what the Blessed One (*bhagavā*) said.
commentary_pali:
210.Dānenātiādīsu ekacco dāneneva saṅgaṇhitabbo hoti, taṃ dānena saṅgahesi. Pabbajitānaṃ pabbajitaparikkhāraṃ, gihīnaṃ gihiparikkhāraṃ adāsi.

Peyyavajjenāti ekacco hi ‘‘ayaṃ dātabbaṃ nāma deti, ekena pana vacanena sabbaṃ makkhetvā nāseti, kiṃ etassa dāna’’nti vattā hoti. Ekacco ‘‘ayaṃ kiñcāpi dānaṃ na deti, kathento pana telena viya makkheti. Eso detu vā mā vā, vacanameva tassa sahassaṃ agghatī’’ti vattā hoti. Evarūpo puggalo dānaṃ na paccāsīsati, piyavacanameva paccāsīsati. Taṃ piyavacanena saṅgahesi.

Peyyavajjenā

Atthacariyāyāti atthasaṃvaḍḍhanakathāya. Ekacco hi neva dānaṃ, na piyavacanaṃ paccāsīsati. Attano hitakathaṃ vaḍḍhitakathameva paccāsīsati. Evarūpaṃ puggalaṃ ‘‘idaṃ te kātabbaṃ, idaṃ te na kātabbaṃ. Evarūpo puggalo sevitabbo, evarūpo puggalo na sevitabbo’’ti evaṃ atthacariyāya saṅgahesi.

Atthacariyāyā

Samānattatāyāti samānasukhadukkhabhāvena. Ekacco hi dānādīsu ekampi na paccāsīsati, ekāsane nisajjaṃ, ekapallaṅke sayanaṃ, ekato bhojananti evaṃ samānasukhadukkhataṃ paccāsīsati. Tattha jātiyā hīno bhogena adhiko dussaṅgaho hoti. Na hi sakkā tena saddhiṃ ekaparibhogo kātuṃ, tathā akariyamāne ca so kujjhati. Bhogena hīno jātiyā adhikopi dussaṅgaho hoti. So hi ‘‘ahaṃ jātimā’’ti bhogasampannena saddhiṃ ekaparibhogaṃ na icchati, tasmiṃ akariyamāne kujjhati. Ubhohipi hīno pana susaṅgaho hoti. Na hi so itarena saddhiṃ ekaparibhogaṃ icchati, na akariyamāne ca kujjhati. Ubhohi sadisopi susaṅgahoyeva. Bhikkhūsu dussīlo dussaṅgaho hoti. Na hi sakkā tena saddhiṃ ekaparibhogo kātuṃ, tathā akariyamāne ca kujjhati. Sīlavā susaṅgaho hoti. Sīlavā hi adīyamānepi akariyamānepi na kujjhati. Aññaṃ attanā saddhiṃ paribhogaṃ akarontampi na pāpakena cittena passati. Paribhogopi tena saddhiṃ sukaro hoti. Tasmā evarūpaṃ puggalaṃ evaṃ samānattatāya saṅgahesi.

Samānattatāyā

Susaṅgahitāssa hontīti susaṅgahitā assa honti. Detu vā mā vā detu, karotu vā mā vā karotu, susaṅgahitāva honti, na bhijjanti. ‘‘Yadāssa dātabbaṃ hoti, tadā deti. Idāni maññe natthi, tena na deti. Kiṃ mayaṃ dadamānameva upaṭṭhahāma? Adentaṃ akarontaṃ na upaṭṭhahāmā’’ti evaṃ cintenti.

Susaṅgahitāssa hontī

Idha kammaṃ nāma dīgharattaṃ kataṃ dānādisaṅgahakammaṃ. Kammasarikkhakaṃ nāma yo evaṃ asaṅgāhako hoti, so iminā kāraṇenassa asaṅgāhakabhāvaṃ jano jānātūti thaddhahatthapādo ceva hoti, visamaṭṭhitāvayavalakkhaṇo ca. Tathāgatassa pana dīgharattaṃ saṅgāhakabhāvaṃ sadevako loko iminā kāraṇena jānātūti imāni dve lakkhaṇāni nibbattanti. Lakkhaṇaṃ nāma idameva lakkhaṇadvayaṃ. Susaṅgahitaparijanatā ānisaṃso.

kammaṃ Kammasarikkhakaṃ Lakkhaṇaṃ ānisaṃso.
commentary_english:
210. "With giving" etc., on the one hand, one is to be helped by giving; he helps them by giving. He gave mendicant requisites to renunciates, and household requisites to householders.

"With gentle speech": On the one hand, one might say, "This person gives what should be given, but with one word, destroying all, ruining it. What use is his giving?"

On the other hand, one might say, "This person, although not giving a gift, spreads (happiness) with their speech like oil."

That person, whether giving or not, their speech is worth a thousand. That is what they say. Such a person does not expect gifts, but only expects affectionate speech. He helps them with affectionate speech.

With gentle speech, with helpful conduct, by speaking words that are beneficial.

On the one hand, one neither expects gifts, nor affectionate speech. One only expects words that are personally beneficial and promote one's own growth.

Such a person [is assisted] by saying, "This you should do, this you should not do. This kind of person should be associated with, and this kind of person should not be associated with." Thus, one helps them with helpful conduct.

With helpful conduct, with evenness, through a sharing of pleasure and pain.

On the one hand, one does not expect giving, etc. One expects sitting on the same seat, sleeping on the same couch, eating at the same place. Thus, one expects a sharing of pleasure and pain.

There, a person who is inferior by birth but superior in wealth is difficult to get along with. It is not possible to share the same things with him; if it is not done, he gets angry.

A person who is inferior in wealth but superior in birth is also difficult to get along with. He does not want to share the same things with someone wealthy because he thinks, "I am highborn." If it is not done, he gets angry.

However, one who is inferior in both ways is easy to get along with. He does not want to share the same things with the other person, and he does not get angry if it is not done.

One who is similar in both ways is very easy to get along with. Among monks, one of bad conduct is difficult to get along with. It is not possible to share the same things with him; if it is not done, he gets angry.

One who is virtuous is easy to get along with. A virtuous person does not get angry even if something is not given or done.

Even if another person does not share things with him, he does not look at them with an evil mind. Sharing with him is also easy. Therefore, he helps such a person with such evenness.

One is well-helped. They are well-helped. Whether he gives or does not give, whether he does or does not do, they are well-helped and do not break apart. "When it is time to give, he gives. Now, I think, there is nothing, so he does not give."
Why do we approach only those who are giving? We do not approach those who are not giving and not doing?' Thus, they think.

They are well-supported. Here, *karma*, namely, *karma* of prolonged giving, beginning with generosity and collection.
