Namely, *karma* is similar to this: one who is thus uncollecting, by this cause, the people know that he is uncollecting, he is stiff-handed and footed, and he has the characteristic of unevenly placed limbs.

Moreover, the world with the gods knows the *Tathāgata's* state of collecting for a long time by this cause. These two characteristics arise.

Namely, the characteristic is just this pair of characteristics.

Well-supported retinue is the benefit.

*Karma*, *karma* is similar, the characteristic is the benefit.

mula_pali:
211. Tatthetaṃ vuccati –

‘‘Dānampi catthacariyatañca dānampi ca atthacariyatampi ca (sī. pī.),

dānampi ca atthacariyatampi ca (sī. pī.)

Piyavāditañca samānattatañca piyavadatañca samānachandatañca (sī. pī.);

piyavadatañca samānachandatañca (sī. pī.)

Kariyacariyasusaṅgahaṃ bahūnaṃ,

Anavamatena guṇena yāti saggaṃ.

‘‘Caviya punaridhāgato samāno,

Karacaraṇamudutañca jālino ca;

Atirucirasuvaggudassaneyyaṃ,

Paṭilabhati daharo susu kumāro.

‘‘Bhavati parijanassavo vidheyyo,

Mahimaṃ āvasito susaṅgahito;

Piyavadū hitasukhataṃ jigīsamāno jigiṃ samāno (sī. syā. pī.),

jigiṃ samāno (sī. syā. pī.)

Abhirucitāni guṇāni ācarati.

‘‘Yadi ca jahati sabbakāmabhogaṃ,

Kathayati dhammakathaṃ jino janassa;

Vacanapaṭikarassābhippasannā ,

Sutvāna dhammānudhammamācarantī’’ti.

(9-10) Ussaṅkhapādauddhaggalomatālakkhaṇāni
mula_english:
211. Thus, it is said:

Generosity, beneficial conduct,

Pleasant speech, equality;

Gathering many through proper conduct,

One goes to heaven with unfailing qualities.

Having passed away and being reborn here,

With soft hands and feet and a net-like pattern,

Extremely beautiful, with a good complexion and pleasing to behold,

A young and tender boy obtains [these qualities].

He becomes obedient to his retinue,

His greatness is sustained and well-received;

Speaking pleasantly, desiring welfare and happiness,

He practices pleasing qualities.

If one abandons all sensual pleasures,

The Victorious One speaks the Dharma to the people;

Being very pleased with the response to his words,

Having heard, they practice the Dharma accordingly.

(9-10) The characteristics of elevated feet and upward-growing body hair.
commentary_pali:
211.Kariyāti karitvā. Cariyāti caritvā. Anavamatenāti anavaññātena. ‘‘Anapamodenā’’tipi pāṭho, na appamodena, na dīnena na gabbhitenāti attho.

Caviyāti cavitvā. Atirucira suvaggu dassaneyyanti atirucirañca supāsādikaṃ suvaggu ca suṭṭhu chekaṃ dassaneyyañca daṭṭhabbayuttaṃ. Susu kumāroti suṭṭhu sukumāro.

Caviyā Atirucira suvaggu dassaneyya Susu kumāro

Parijanassavoti parijano assavo vacanakaro. Vidheyyoti kattabbākattabbesu yathāruci vidhātabbo. Mahimanti mahiṃ imaṃ. Piyavadū hitasukhataṃ jigīsamānoti piyavado hutvā hitañca sukhañca pariyesamāno. Vacanapaṭikarassā bhippasannāti vacanapaṭikarā assa abhippasannā. Dhammānudhammanti dhammañca anudhammañca.

Parijanassavo Vidheyyo Mahima Piyavadū hitasukhataṃ jigīsamāno Vacanapaṭikarassā bhippasannā Dhammānudhamma

Ussaṅkhapādādilakkhaṇavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
211.

*kariyā* means having done.

*cariyā* means having behaved.

*anavamatenā* means not despised.

"anapamodenā''tipi pāṭho, na appamodena, na dīnena na gabbhitenāti attho.

*caviyā* means having moved.

*atirucira suvaggu dassaneyya* means exceedingly beautiful, very good, and worth seeing.

*susu kumāro* means very delicate.

*caviyā atirucira suvaggu dassaneyya susu kumāro parijanassavo* *vidheyyo mahima piyavadū hitasukhataṃ jigīsamāno vacanapaṭikarassā bhippasannā dhammānudhamma* *parijanassavo vidheyyo mahima piyavadū hitasukhataṃ jigīsamāno vacanapaṭikarassā bhippasannā dhammānudhamma*

*parijanassavo* means attendants are obedient and carry out orders.

*vidheyyo* means to be managed according to one's wishes in what should and should not be done.

*mahima* means this greatness.

*piyavadū hitasukhataṃ jigīsamāno* means speaking pleasantly and seeking benefit and happiness.

*vacanapaṭikarassā bhippasannā* means pleased with his responses.

*dhammānudhamma* means dharma and according to dharma.

Description of the characteristics of *ussaṅkhapādādi*

mula_pali:
212. ‘‘Yampi, bhikkhave, tathāgato purimaṃ jātiṃ purimaṃ bhavaṃ purimaṃ niketaṃ pubbe manussabhūto samāno samāno bahuno janassa (sī. pī.) atthūpasaṃhitaṃ dhammūpasaṃhitaṃ vācaṃ bhāsitā ahosi, bahujanaṃ nidaṃsesi, pāṇīnaṃ hitasukhāvaho dhammayāgī. So tassa kammassa kaṭattā…pe… so tato cuto itthattaṃ āgato samāno imāni dve mahāpurisalakkhaṇāni paṭilabhati. Ussaṅkhapādo ca hoti, uddhaggalomo ca.

‘‘So tehi lakkhaṇehi samannāgato, sace agāraṃ ajjhāvasati, rājā hoti cakkavattī…pe… rājā samāno kiṃ labhati? Aggo ca hoti seṭṭho ca pāmokkho ca uttamo ca pavaro ca kāmabhogīnaṃ. Rājā samāno idaṃ labhati… buddho samāno kiṃ labhati? Aggo ca hoti seṭṭho ca pāmokkho ca uttamo ca pavaro ca sabbasattānaṃ. Buddho samāno idaṃ labhati’’. Etamatthaṃ bhagavā avoca.
mula_english:
"Furthermore, monks, when the Tathāgata, in a former birth, a former existence, a former abode, having previously been a human being, spoke words connected with benefit or connected with the Dhamma to many people, pointed them out, and was a sacrificer of the Dhamma bringing benefit and happiness to beings, with that action performed... on his being come again to this same human state, he acquires these two characteristics of a Great Man: he has feet with high insteps, and he has upward-growing body hairs.

"So, endowed with those characteristics, if he lives the household life, he becomes a wheel-turning monarch... What does a king gain by being a king? He is the foremost, the best, the chief, the highest, and the most excellent of those who enjoy sensual pleasures. That is what a king gains by being a king... What does a Buddha gain by being a Buddha? He is the foremost, the best, the chief, the highest, and the most excellent of all beings. That is what a Buddha gains by being a Buddha."

This is the meaning of what the Blessed One said.
commentary_pali: 212.Atthūpasaṃhitanti idhalokaparalokatthanissitaṃ. Dhammūpasaṃhitanti dasakusalakammapathanissitaṃ. Bahujanaṃ nidaṃsesīti bahujanassa nidaṃsanakathaṃ kathesi. Pāṇīnanti sattānaṃ. ‘‘Aggo’’tiādīni sabbāni aññamaññavevacanāni. Idha kammaṃ nāma dīgharattaṃ bhāsitā uddhaṅgamanīyā atthūpasaṃhitā vācā. Kammasarikkhakaṃ nāma yo evarūpaṃ uggatavācaṃ na bhāsati, so iminā kāraṇena uggatavācāya abhāsanaṃ jano jānātūti adhosaṅkhapādo ca hoti adhonatalomo ca. Tathāgatassa pana dīgharattaṃ evarūpāya uggatavācāya bhāsitabhāvaṃ sadevako loko iminā kāraṇena jānātūti ussaṅkhapādalakkhaṇañca uddhaggalomalakkhaṇañca nibbattati. Lakkhaṇaṃ nāma idameva lakkhaṇadvayaṃ. Uttamabhāvo ānisaṃso.
commentary_english:
212.
*Atthūpasaṃhita* means that which is based on this world and the next.
*Dhammūpasaṃhita* means that which is based on the ten wholesome courses of action ( *dasakusalakammapatha*).
*Bahujanaṃ nidaṃsesī* means he related a demonstrative talk to many people (*bahujanassa nidaṃsanakathaṃ kathesi*).
*Pāṇīna* means of beings (*sattānaṃ*).
"The chief" and so on, all are synonyms for one another (*aññamaññavevacanāni*).
Here, *kammaṃ* (karma) means speech (*vācā*) that is uttered for a long time, exalting, and connected with meaning (*atthūpasaṃhitā*).
*Kammasarikkhakaṃ* means that a person who does not speak such exalted speech (*uggatavācaṃ*)—may people know that the non-speaking of exalted speech is for this reason (*iminā kāraṇena*)—he will have downcast feet (*adhosaṅkhapādo*) and downcast hair (*adhonatalomo*).
But that the state of the Tathāgata's speaking exalted speech (*uggatavācāya bhāsitabhāvaṃ*) for a long time, may the world with its gods (*sadevako loko*) know for this reason (*iminā kāraṇena*), results in the characteristics of uplifted feet and uplifted hair (*ussaṅkhapādalakkhaṇañca uddhaggalomalakkhaṇañca*).
*Lakkhaṇaṃ* (characteristic) means just these two characteristics (*lakkhaṇadvayaṃ*).
The highest state is *ānisaṃso* (benefit, advantage).

mula_pali:
213. Tatthetaṃ vuccati –

‘‘Atthadhammasahitaṃ atthadhammasaṃhitaṃ (ka. sī. pī.), atthadhammupasaṃhitaṃ (ka.) pure giraṃ,

atthadhammasaṃhitaṃ (ka. sī. pī.), atthadhammupasaṃhitaṃ (ka.)

Erayaṃ bahujanaṃ nidaṃsayi;

Pāṇinaṃ hitasukhāvaho ahu,

Dhammayāgamayajī dhammayāgaṃ assaji (ka.) amaccharī.

dhammayāgaṃ assaji (ka.)

‘‘Tena so sucaritena kammunā,

Suggatiṃ vajati tattha modati;

Lakkhaṇāni ca duve idhāgato,

Uttamappamukhatāya uttamasukhatāya (syā.), uttamapamukkhatāya (ka.) vindati.

uttamasukhatāya (syā.), uttamapamukkhatāya (ka.)

‘‘Ubbhamuppatitalomavā saso,

Pādagaṇṭhirahu sādhusaṇṭhitā;

Maṃsalohitācitā tacotthatā,

Uparicaraṇasobhanā uparijānusobhanā (syā.), upari ca pana sobhanā (sī. pī.) ahu.

uparijānusobhanā (syā.), upari ca pana sobhanā (sī. pī.)

‘‘Gehamāvasati ce tathāvidho,

Aggataṃ vajati kāmabhoginaṃ;

Tena uttaritaro na vijjati,

Jambudīpamabhibhuyya iriyati.

‘‘Pabbajampi ca anomanikkamo,

Aggataṃ vajati sabbapāṇinaṃ;

Tena uttaritaro na vijjati,

Sabbalokamabhibhuyya viharatī’’ti.

(11) Eṇijaṅghalakkhaṇaṃ
mula_english:
213. Thus, it is said:

“He uttered speech that was connected with meaning and the Dharma,
He cheered up many people, showing [them] the way;
He was the bringer of benefit and happiness to beings,
A non-avaricious sacrificer of the Dharma-sacrifice.

“Because of that well-done action,
He goes to a good destination, there he rejoices;
And having come here [he acquires] two characteristics,
He obtains pre-eminence.

“He has hair that grows upwards,
His ankles are well-formed;
His skin is filled with flesh and blood,
And his beautiful feet are well placed.

“If such a one lives at home,
He goes to the highest state of those who enjoy sensual pleasures;
There is no one superior to him,
He governs Jambudīpa.

“And even his renunciation, his blameless departure,
Goes to the highest state of all living beings;
There is no one superior to him,
He dwells having overcome the entire world.”

(11) The characteristic of deer-like shanks.
commentary_pali:
213.Erayanti bhaṇanto. Bahujanaṃ nidaṃsayīti bahujanassa hitaṃ dasseti. Dhammayāganti dhammadānayaññaṃ.

Ubbhamuppatitalomavā sasoti so esa uddhaggatalomavā hoti. Pādagaṇṭhirahūti pādagopphakā ahesuṃ. Sādhusaṇṭhitāti suṭṭhu saṇṭhitā. Maṃsalohitācitāti maṃsena ca lohitena ca ācitā. Tacotthatāti tacena pariyonaddhā niguḷhā. Vajatīti gacchati. Anomanikkamoti anomavihārī seṭṭhavihārī.

Ubbhamuppatitalomavā saso Pādagaṇṭhirahū Sādhusaṇṭhitā Maṃsalohitācitā Tacotthatā Vajatī Anomanikkamo

Eṇijaṅghalakkhaṇavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
erayanti bhaṇanto: saying "erayanti."
bahujanaṃ nidaṃsayīti: "nidaṃsayī to many people" means he shows benefit to many people.
dhammayāganti: *dharmayajña*, the sacrifice of the giving of Dharma.

ubbhamuppatitalomavā saso ti: "ubbhamuppatitalomavā saso" means he has uplifted hairs.
pādagaṇṭhirahū ti: "pādagaṇṭhirahū" means there were no ankle joints.
sādhusaṇṭhitā ti: "sādhusaṇṭhitā" means well-formed.
maṃsalohitācitā ti: "maṃsalohitācitā" means covered with flesh and blood.
tacotthatā ti: "tacotthatā" means concealed, covered with skin.
vajatī ti: "vajatī" means he goes.
anomanikkamo ti: "anomanikkamo" means one who dwells without fault, one who dwells excellently.

ubbhamuppatitalomavā saso pādagaṇṭhirahū sādhusaṇṭhitā maṃsalohitācitā tacotthatā vajatī anomanikkamo
Description of the deer-like calf characteristic.

mula_pali:
214. ‘‘Yampi, bhikkhave, tathāgato purimaṃ jātiṃ purimaṃ bhavaṃ purimaṃ niketaṃ pubbe manussabhūto samāno sakkaccaṃ vācetā ahosi sippaṃ vā vijjaṃ vā caraṇaṃ vā kammaṃ vā – ‘kiṃ time khippaṃ vijāneyyuṃ, khippaṃ paṭipajjeyyuṃ, na ciraṃ kilisseyyu’’nti. So tassa kammassa kaṭattā…pe… so tato cuto itthattaṃ āgato samāno imaṃ mahāpurisalakkhaṇaṃ paṭilabhati. Eṇijaṅgho hoti.

‘‘So tena lakkhaṇena samannāgato sace agāraṃ ajjhāvasati, rājā hoti cakkavattī…pe… rājā samāno kiṃ labhati? Yāni tāni rājārahāni rājaṅgāni rājūpabhogāni rājānucchavikāni tāni khippaṃ paṭilabhati. Rājā samāno idaṃ labhati… buddho samāno kiṃ labhati? Yāni tāni samaṇārahāni samaṇaṅgāni samaṇūpabhogāni samaṇānucchavikāni, tāni khippaṃ paṭilabhati. Buddho samāno idaṃ labhati’’. Etamatthaṃ bhagavā avoca.
mula_english:
214.

Furthermore, monks, the *tathāgata*, in a former birth, a former existence, a former abode, having previously been a human being, was a respectful instructor in crafts (*śilpa*), knowledge (*vidyā*), conduct (*caraṇa*), or action (*karma*), thinking, 'How may these quickly understand, quickly practice, and not be defiled for long?'

By performing that action, he, having departed from there and come to this state, acquires this characteristic of a great man (*mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa*).

He has antelope-like calves (*eṇijaṅgho*).

Furthermore, endowed with that characteristic, if he lives in a house, he becomes a wheel-turning monarch (*cakravartin*)... As a king, what does he obtain? He quickly obtains those royal requisites, royal limbs, royal enjoyments, and those suitable for a king.

As a king, he obtains this... As a Buddha, what does he obtain? He quickly obtains those requisites for ascetics (*śramaṇa*), limbs for ascetics, enjoyments for ascetics and those suitable for ascetics.

As a Buddha, he obtains this.

The Blessed One said this.
commentary_pali:
214.Sippaṃ vātiādīsu sippaṃ nāma dve sippāni – hīnañca sippaṃ, ukkaṭṭhañca sippaṃ. Hīnaṃ nāma sippaṃ naḷakārasippaṃ, kumbhakārasippaṃ pesakārasippaṃ nahāpitasippaṃ. Ukkaṭṭhaṃ nāma sippaṃ lekhā muddā gaṇanā. Vijjāti ahivijjādianekavidhā. Caraṇanti pañcasīlaṃ dasasīlaṃ pātimokkhasaṃvarasīlaṃ. Kammanti kammassakatājānanapaññā. Kilisseyyunti kilameyyuṃ. Antevāsikavattaṃ nāma dukkhaṃ, taṃ nesaṃ mā ciramahosīti cintesi.

Rājārahānīti rañño anurūpāni hatthiassādīni, tāniyeva rañño senāya aṅgabhūtattā rājaṅgānīti vuccanti. Rājūpabhogānīti rañño upabhogaparibhogabhaṇḍāni, tāni ceva sattaratanāni ca. Rājānucchavikānīti rañño anucchavikāni. Tesaṃyeva sabbesaṃ idaṃ gahaṇaṃ. Samaṇārahānīti samaṇānaṃ anurūpāni cīvarādīni. Samaṇaṅgānīti samaṇānaṃ koṭṭhāsabhūtā catasso parisā. Samaṇūpabhogānīti samaṇānaṃ upabhogaparikkhārā. Samaṇānucchavikānīti tesaṃyeva adhivacanaṃ.

Rājārahānī rājaṅgānī Rājūpabhogānī Rājānucchavikānī Samaṇārahānī Samaṇaṅgānī Samaṇūpabhogānī Samaṇānucchavikānī

Idha pana kammaṃ nāma dīgharattaṃ sakkaccaṃ sippādivācanaṃ. Kammasarikkhakaṃ nāma yo evaṃ sakkaccaṃ sippaṃ avācento antevāsike ukkuṭikāsanajaṅghapesanikādīhi kilameti, tassa jaṅghamaṃsaṃ likhitvā pātitaṃ viya hoti. Tathāgatassa pana sakkaccaṃ vācitabhāvaṃ sadevako loko iminā kāraṇena jānātūti anupubbauggatavaṭṭitaṃ eṇijaṅghalakkhaṇaṃ nibbattati. Lakkhaṇaṃ nāma idameva lakkhaṇaṃ. Anucchavikalābhitā ānisaṃso.

kammaṃ Kammasarikkhakaṃ eṇijaṅghalakkhaṇaṃ Lakkhaṇaṃ ānisaṃso.
commentary_english:
214.
"Craft or skill" (*śilpa*) etc.: *śilpa* means two kinds of crafts – low craft (*hīnaṃ ca śilpaṃ*) and high craft (*ukkaṭṭhañca śilpaṃ*).

Low craft (*hīnaṃ nāma śilpaṃ*) means reed work (*naḷakārasippaṃ*), pottery (*kumbhakārasippaṃ*), weaving (*pesakārasippaṃ*), and hairdressing (*nahāpitasilpaṃ*).

High craft (*ukkaṭṭhaṃ nāma śilpaṃ*) means writing (*lekhā*), accounting (*muddā*), and calculation (*gaṇanā*).

"Knowledge" (*vidyā*) means various kinds such as snake-charming knowledge (*ahividyādi*).

"Conduct" (*caraṇa*) means the five precepts (*pañcasīlaṃ*), the ten precepts (*dasasīlaṃ*), the precepts of the Prātimokṣa restraint (*pātimokkhasaṃvarasīlaṃ*).

"Action" (*karma*) means the wisdom of knowing ownership of action (*kammassakatājānanapaññā*).

"They might suffer" (*kilisseyyu*) means they might be exhausted (*kilameyyuṃ*).

The duty of a pupil (*antevāsikavattaṃ*) is called suffering (*dukkhaṃ*). He thought, "May that not be long for them" (*taṃ nesaṃ mā ciramahosīti cintesi*).

"Fit for a king" (*rājārahānī*) means elephants, horses, etc., which are suitable for a king (*rañño anurūpāni hatthiassādīni*). Because those very things are the essence of the king's army (*rañño senāya aṅgabhūtattā*), they are called "royal constituents" (*rājāṅgānīti*).

"Royal requisites" (*rājūpabhogānī*) means the king's (*rañño*) articles for enjoyment and use (*upabhogaparibhogabhaṇḍāni*), and those very seven jewels (*tāni ceva sattaratanāni ca*).

"Appropriate for a king" (*rājānucchavikānī*) means what is suitable for a king (*rañño anucchavikāni*).

This is the grasping of all of them (*tesaṃyeva sabbesaṃ idaṃ gahaṇaṃ*).

"Fit for ascetics" (*samaṇārahānī*) means robes etc., which are suitable for ascetics (*samaṇānaṃ anurūpāni cīvarādīni*).

"Constituents of an ascetic" (*samaṇaṅgānī*) means the four assemblies (*catasso parisā*) which are the portions of ascetics (*samaṇānaṃ koṭṭhāsabhūtā*).

"Requisites of an ascetic" (*samaṇūpabhogānī*) means the requisites for the use of ascetics (*samaṇānaṃ upabhogaparikkhārā*).

"Appropriate for ascetics" (*samaṇānucchavikānī*) means just an expression for those (*tesaṃyeva adhivacanaṃ*).

Fit for a king (*rājārahānī*), royal constituents (*rājaṅgānī*), royal requisites (*rājūpabhogānī*), appropriate for a king (*rājānucchavikānī*), fit for ascetics (*samaṇārahānī*), constituents of an ascetic (*samaṇaṅgānī*), requisites of an ascetic (*samaṇūpabhogānī*), appropriate for ascetics (*samaṇānucchavikānī*). Here, "action" (*karma*) means the repeated recitation of crafts and skills with reverence for a long time (*dīgharattaṃ sakkaccaṃ sippādivācanaṃ*).

"Similar to action" (*kammasarikkhakaṃ*) means that if someone, while not causing the pupils (*antevāsike*) to repeat the craft reverently in this way (*yo evaṃ sakkaccaṃ sippaṃ avācento*), exhausts them with squatting postures, seats, shanks, prostrations, etc. (*ukkuṭikāsanajaṅghapesanikādīhi kilameti*), it is as if the flesh of his shank has been scratched and cast down (*tassa jaṅghamaṃsaṃ likhitvā pātitaṃ viya hoti*).

However, the world with the gods (*sadevako loko*) knows that the Tathāgata's state of having caused recitation with reverence (*tathāgatassa pana sakkaccaṃ vācitabhāvaṃ*) is born from this cause (*iminā kāraṇena jānātūti*) - the characteristic of the antelope's shank, made orderly and raised (*anupubbauggatavaṭṭitaṃ eṇijaṅghalakkhaṇaṃ*).

"Characteristic" (*lakṣaṇaṃ*) means just this characteristic (*idameva lakṣaṇaṃ*).

The advantage (*ānisaṃso*) is non-acquisitiveness (*anucchavikalābhitā*).

Action (*karma*), similar to action (*kammasarikkhakaṃ*), characteristic of the antelope's shank (*eṇijaṅghalakkhaṇaṃ*), characteristic (*lakṣaṇaṃ*), advantage (*ānisaṃso*).

mula_pali:
215. Tatthetaṃ vuccati –

‘‘Sippesu vijjācaraṇesu kammesu kammasu (sī. pī.),

kammasu (sī. pī.)

Kathaṃ vijāneyyuṃ vijāneyya (sī. pī.), vijāneyyu (syā.) lahunti icchati;

vijāneyya (sī. pī.), vijāneyyu (syā.)

Yadūpaghātāya na hoti kassaci,

Vāceti khippaṃ na ciraṃ kilissati.

‘‘Taṃ kammaṃ katvā kusalaṃ sukhudrayaṃ sukhindriyaṃ (ka.),

sukhindriyaṃ (ka.)

Jaṅghā manuññā labhate susaṇṭhitā;

Vaṭṭā sujātā anupubbamuggatā,

Uddhaggalomā sukhumattacotthatā.

‘‘Eṇeyyajaṅghoti tamāhu puggalaṃ,

Sampattiyā khippamidhāhu khippamidāhu (?) lakkhaṇaṃ;

khippamidāhu (?)

Gehānulomāni yadābhikaṅkhati,

Apabbajaṃ khippamidhādhigacchati khippamidādhigacchati (?).

khippamidādhigacchati (?)

‘‘Sace ca pabbajjamupeti tādiso,

Nekkhammachandābhirato vicakkhaṇo;

Anucchavikassa yadānulomikaṃ,

Taṃ vindati khippamanomavikkamo nikkamo (sī. syā. pī.)’’ti.

nikkamo (sī. syā. pī.)

(12) Sukhumacchavilakkhaṇaṃ
mula_english:
Thus is it said:

"In crafts, knowledge, conduct, and deeds,
how they may quickly understand—so he wishes;
that no harm comes to anyone,
he quickly makes them recite, and does not long languish.

"Having done that wholesome deed, resulting in happiness,
he obtains fair shanks, well-formed;
rounded, well-shaped, gradually rising,
with upward-growing hairs, subtle, very smooth.

"‘Deer-like shanks’—they call that person,
here they quickly declare the sign of attainment;
when he desires things conforming to the household life,
he quickly attains non-renunciation here.

"And if such a one goes forth,
delighting in the joy of renunciation, discerning;
when something suitable arises for him,
he quickly finds that matchless prowess."

(12) The subtle-skinned characteristic
commentary_pali:
215.Yadūpaghātāyāti yaṃ sippaṃ kassaci upaghātāya na hoti. Kilissatīti kilamissati. Sukhumattacotthatāti sukhumattacena pariyonaddhā. Kiṃ pana aññena kammena aññaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ nibbattatīti? Na nibbattati. Yaṃ pana nibbattati, taṃ anubyañjanaṃ hoti, tasmā idha vuttaṃ.

Sukhumacchavilakkhaṇavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
215. *yadūpaghātāyā* means that skill which is not harmful to anyone.
*kilissatī* means will be weary.
*sukhumattacotthatā* means enveloped by delicate skin.
Now, does another characteristic arise from another action? It does not arise.
But that which arises is a minor mark, therefore it is said here.

Explanation of delicate skin with auspicious marks.

mula_pali:
216. ‘‘Yampi, bhikkhave, tathāgato purimaṃ jātiṃ purimaṃ bhavaṃ purimaṃ niketaṃ pubbe manussabhūto samāno samaṇaṃ vā brāhmaṇaṃ vā upasaṅkamitvā paripucchitā ahosi – ‘‘kiṃ, bhante, kusalaṃ, kiṃ akusalaṃ, kiṃ sāvajjaṃ, kiṃ anavajjaṃ, kiṃ sevitabbaṃ, kiṃ na sevitabbaṃ, kiṃ me karīyamānaṃ dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāya assa, kiṃ vā pana me karīyamānaṃ dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāya assā’’ti. So tassa kammassa kaṭattā…pe… so tato cuto itthattaṃ āgato samāno imaṃ mahāpurisalakkhaṇaṃ paṭilabhati. Sukhumacchavi hoti, sukhumattā chaviyā rajojallaṃ kāye na upalimpati.

‘‘So tena lakkhaṇena samannāgato sace agāraṃ ajjhāvasati, rājā hoti cakkavattī…pe… rājā samāno kiṃ labhati? Mahāpañño hoti, nāssa hoti koci paññāya sadiso vā seṭṭho vā kāmabhogīnaṃ. Rājā samāno idaṃ labhati… buddho samāno kiṃ labhati? Mahāpañño hoti puthupañño hāsapañño hāsupañño (sī. pī.) javanapañño tikkhapañño nibbedhikapañño, nāssa hoti koci paññāya sadiso vā seṭṭho vā sabbasattānaṃ. Buddho samāno idaṃ labhati’’. Etamatthaṃ bhagavā avoca.

hāsupañño (sī. pī.)
mula_english:
216.

“And also, monks, the *tathāgata*, when previously born, previously existing, previously established, having formerly been a human being, having approached a *śramaṇa* or a *brāhmaṇa* asked: ‘Venerable sir, what is wholesome (*kuśala*)? What is unwholesome (*akuśala*)? What is blameworthy (*sāvajja*)? What is blameless (*anavajja*)? What should be cultivated? What should not be cultivated? What kind of action will lead to my harm and suffering for a long time? What kind of action will lead to my welfare and happiness for a long time?’

With that action performed, stored up,… on his being come again to the same human state, he acquires these marks of a great man (*mahāpurisalakkhaṇa*).

He has fine skin (*sukhumacchavi*), and because of the fineness of his skin (*chaviyā*), dust and dirt do not stick on his body (*kāye*).

“So, endowed with these characteristics, if he lives in a house, he becomes a king, a wheel-turning monarch… What does the king gain? He becomes greatly wise (*mahāpañño*); no one is equal or superior to him in wisdom among those who enjoy sensual pleasures (*kāmabhogīnaṃ*).

The king gains this… What does the Buddha gain? He becomes greatly wise, widely wise (*puthupañño*), joyfully wise (*hāsapañño*)… swiftly wise, sharply wise (*tikkhapañño*), penetratingly wise; no one is equal or superior to him in wisdom among all beings (*sabbasattānaṃ*).

The Buddha gains this.”

This is the meaning of what the Blessed One (*bhagavā*) said.
commentary_pali:
216.Samaṇaṃ vāti samitapāpaṭṭhena samaṇaṃ. Brāhmaṇaṃ vāti bāhitapāpaṭṭhena brāhmaṇaṃ.

Mahāpaññotiādīsu mahāpaññādīhi samannāgato hotīti attho. Tatridaṃ mahāpaññādīnaṃ nānattaṃ.

Mahāpañño

Tattha katamā mahāpaññā? Mahante sīlakkhandhe pariggaṇhātīti mahāpaññā, mahante samādhikkhandhe paññākkhandhe vimuttikkhandhe vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhe pariggaṇhātīti mahāpaññā. Mahantāni ṭhānāṭhānāni mahantā vihārasamāpattiyo mahantāni ariyasaccāni mahante satipaṭṭhāne sammappadhāne iddhipāde mahantāni indriyāni balāni mahante bojjhaṅge mahante ariyamagge mahantāni sāmaññaphalāni mahantā abhiññāyo mahantaṃ paramatthaṃ nibbānaṃ pariggaṇhātīti mahāpaññā.

mahāpaññā? mahāpaññā,

Katamā puthupaññā? Puthunānākhandhesu ñāṇaṃ pavattatīti puthupaññā. Puthunānādhātūsu puthunānāāyatanesu puthunānāpaṭiccasamuppādesu puthunānāsuññatamanupalabbhesu puthunānāatthesu dhammesu niruttīsu paṭibhānesu. Puthunānāsīlakkhandhesu puthunānāsamādhipaññāvimuttivimuttiñādassanakkhandhesu puthunānāṭhānāṭhānesu puthunānāvihārasamāpattīsu puthunānāariyasaccesu puthunānāsatipaṭṭhānesu sammappadhānesu iddhipādesu indriyesu balesu bojjhaṅgesu puthunānāariyamaggesu sāmaññaphalesu abhiññāsu puthujjanasādhāraṇe dhamme samatikkamma paramatthe nibbāne ñāṇaṃ pavattatīti puthupaññā.

puthupaññā? puthupaññā.

Katamā hāsapaññā? Idhekacco hāsabahulo vedabahulo tuṭṭhibahulo pāmojjabahulo sīlaṃ paripūreti indriyasaṃvaraṃ paripūreti bhojane mattaññutaṃ jāgariyānuyogaṃ sīlakkhandhaṃ samādhikkhandhaṃ paññākkhandhaṃ vimuttikkhandhaṃ vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhaṃ paripūretīti hāsapaññā. Hāsabahulo…pe… pāmojjabahulo ṭhānāṭhānaṃ paṭivijjhatīti hāsapaññā. Hāsabahulo vihārasamāpattiyo paripūretīti hāsapaññā. Hāsabahulo ariyasaccāni paṭivijjhatīti hāsapaññā. Satipaṭṭhāne sammappadhāne iddhipāde indriyāni balāni bojjhaṅge ariyamaggaṃ bhāvetīti hāsapaññā. Hāsabahulo sāmaññaphalāni sacchikarotīti hāsapaññā. Abhiññāyo paṭivijjhatīti hāsapaññā. Hāsabahulo vedatuṭṭhipāmojjabahulo paramatthaṃ nibbānaṃ sacchikarotīti hāsapaññā.

hāsapaññā?

Katamā javanapaññā? Yaṃkiñci rūpaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ yaṃ dūre santike vā, sabbaṃ taṃ rūpaṃ aniccato khippaṃ javatīti javanapaññā. Dukkhato khippaṃ anattato khippaṃ javatīti javanapaññā. Yā kāci vedanā…pe… yaṃkiñci viññāṇaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ, sabbaṃ taṃ viññāṇaṃ aniccato dukkhato anattato khippaṃ javatīti javanapaññā. Cakkhu…pe… jarāmaraṇaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ aniccato dukkhato anattato khippaṃ javatīti javanapaññā. Rūpaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ aniccaṃ khayaṭṭhena dukkhaṃ bhayaṭṭhena anattā asārakaṭṭhenāti tulayitvā tīrayitvā vibhāvayitvā vibhūtaṃ katvā rūpanirodhe nibbāne khippaṃ javatīti javanapaññā. Vedanā saññā saṅkhārā viññāṇaṃ cakkhu…pe… jarāmaraṇaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ aniccaṃ khayaṭṭhena…pe… vibhūtaṃ katvā jarāmaraṇanirodhe nibbāne khippaṃ javatīti javanapaññā. Rūpaṃ atītānāgatapaccuppannaṃ . Cakkhuṃ…pe… jarāmaraṇaṃ aniccaṃ saṅkhataṃ paṭiccasamuppannaṃ khayadhammaṃ vayadhammaṃ virāgadhammaṃ nirodhadhammanti tulayitvā tīrayitvā vibhāvayitvā vibhūtaṃ katvā jarāmaraṇanirodhe nibbāne khippaṃ javatīti javanapaññā.

javanapaññā?

Katamā tikkhapaññā? Khippaṃ kilese chindatīti tikkhapaññā. Uppannaṃ kāmavitakkaṃ nādhivāseti, uppannaṃ byāpādavitakkaṃ, uppannaṃ vihiṃsāvitakkaṃ, uppannuppanne pāpake akusale dhamme uppannaṃ rāgaṃ dosaṃ mohaṃ kodhaṃ upanāhaṃ makkhaṃ paḷāsaṃ issaṃ macchariyaṃ māyaṃ sāṭheyyaṃ thambhaṃ sārambhaṃ mānaṃ atimānaṃ madaṃ pamādaṃ sabbe kilese sabbe duccarite sabbe abhisaṅkhāre sabbe bhavagāmikamme nādhivāseti pajahati vinodeti byantī karoti anabhāvaṃ gametīti tikkhapaññā. Ekasmiṃ āsane cattāro ariyamaggā cattāri sāmaññaphalāni catasso paṭisambhidāyo cha abhiññāyo adhigatā honti sacchikatā phassitā paññāyāti tikkhapaññā.

tikkhapaññā?

Katamā nibbedhikapaññā? Idhekacco sabbasaṅkhāresu ubbegabahulo hoti uttāsabahulo ukkaṇṭhanabahulo aratibahulo anabhiratibahulo bahimukho na ramati sabbasaṅkhāresu, anibbiddhapubbaṃ apadālitapubbaṃ lobhakkhandhaṃ nibbijjhati padāletīti nibbedhikapaññā. Anibbiddhapubbaṃ apadālitapubbaṃ dosakkhandhaṃ mohakkhandhaṃ kodhaṃ upanāhaṃ…pe… sabbe bhavagāmikamme nibbijjhati padāletīti nibbedhikapaññāti (paṭi. ma. 3.3).

nibbedhikapaññā?
commentary_english:
216. " *Samaṇaṃ vā* " means *samaṇa* because of having calmed ( *samita* ) evil.

" *Brāhmaṇaṃ vā* " means *brāhmaṇa* because of having warded off ( *bāhita* ) evil.

In " *mahāpañño* ", etc., the meaning is that he is endowed with great wisdom ( *mahāpaññā* ), etc.

Herein is the diversity of the types of great wisdom, etc.

Great wisdom:

What is great wisdom ( *mahāpaññā* )? *Mahāpaññā* because he takes up a great aggregate of morality ( *sīlakkhandha* ), he takes up a great aggregate of concentration, an aggregate of wisdom, an aggregate of liberation, an aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation.

*Mahāpaññā* because he takes up great possibilities and impossibilities, great attainments of dwelling, great noble truths ( *ariyasacca* ), great mindfulnesses ( *satipaṭṭhāne* ), right efforts ( *sammappadhāne* ), bases of psychic power ( *iddhipāde* ), great faculties ( *indriyāni* ), strengths ( *balāni* ), great factors of enlightenment ( *bojjhaṅge* ), great noble paths ( *ariyamagge* ), great fruits of contemplative life ( *sāmaññaphalāni* ), great super-knowledges ( *abhiññāyo* ), the great ultimate reality: nirvāṇa ( *nibbānaṃ* ).

What is diverse wisdom ( *puthupaññā* )? *Puthupaññā* because knowledge proceeds in diverse aggregates.

In diverse elements ( *dhātūsu* ), diverse sense-bases ( *āyatanesu* ), diverse dependent originations ( *paṭiccasamuppādesu* ), diverse unapprehended emptinesses, diverse meanings, diverse qualities ( *dhammesu* ), diverse expressions ( *niruttīsu* ), diverse eloquence ( *paṭibhānesu* ).

In diverse aggregates of morality, diverse aggregates of concentration, wisdom, liberation, knowledge and vision of liberation, diverse possibilities and impossibilities, diverse attainments of dwelling, diverse noble truths, diverse mindfulnesses, right efforts, bases of psychic power, faculties, strengths, factors of enlightenment, diverse noble paths, fruits of contemplative life, super-knowledges, having transcended qualities common to ordinary people, knowledge proceeds in the ultimate reality: nirvāṇa, therefore, it is diverse wisdom.

What is laughing wisdom ( *hāsapaññā* )? Here, someone is abundant in laughter, abundant in joy, abundant in satisfaction, abundant in gladness, he fulfills morality, he fulfills restraint of the senses, he fulfills moderation in eating, devotion to wakefulness, he fulfills the aggregate of morality, the aggregate of concentration, the aggregate of wisdom, the aggregate of liberation, the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation, therefore, it is laughing wisdom.

Abundant in laughter... abundant in gladness, he penetrates possibilities and impossibilities, therefore, it is laughing wisdom.

Abundant in laughter, he fulfills the attainments of dwelling, therefore, it is laughing wisdom.

Abundant in laughter, he penetrates the noble truths, therefore, it is laughing wisdom.

He develops mindfulnesses, right efforts, bases of psychic power, faculties, strengths, factors of enlightenment, the noble path, therefore, it is laughing wisdom.

Abundant in laughter, he realizes the fruits of the contemplative life, therefore, it is laughing wisdom.

He penetrates the super-knowledges, therefore, it is laughing wisdom.

Abundant in laughter, abundant in joy, satisfaction, gladness, he realizes the ultimate reality: nirvāṇa, therefore, it is laughing wisdom.

What is swift wisdom ( *javanapaññā* )? Whatever form there is, past, future, or present, whether far or near, all that form swiftly rushes away due to impermanence ( *anicca* ), therefore, it is swift wisdom.

Swiftly due to suffering ( *dukkha* ), swiftly due to non-self ( *anatta* ), therefore, it is swift wisdom.

Whatever feeling there is... whatever consciousness ( *viññāṇaṃ* ) there is, past, future, or present, all that consciousness swiftly rushes away due to impermanence, suffering, non-self, therefore, it is swift wisdom.

Eye ( *cakkhu* )... aging and death ( *jarāmaraṇaṃ* ), past, future, or present, swiftly rushes away due to impermanence, suffering, non-self, therefore, it is swift wisdom.

Form, past, future, or present, impermanent in the sense of destruction, suffering in the sense of fear, non-self in the sense of lacking essence, having weighed it, having examined it, having analyzed it, having made it distinct, swiftly rushes to nirvāṇa in the cessation of form, therefore, it is swift wisdom.

Feeling, perception ( *saññā* ), mental formations ( *saṅkhārā* ), consciousness, eye... aging and death, past, future, or present, impermanent in the sense of destruction... having made it distinct, swiftly rushes to nirvāṇa in the cessation of aging and death, therefore, it is swift wisdom.

Form, past, future, or present.

Eye... aging and death, impermanent, conditioned ( *saṅkhataṃ* ), dependently originated ( *paṭiccasamuppannaṃ* ), subject to destruction ( *khayadhammaṃ* ), subject to decay ( *vayadhammaṃ* ), subject to fading away ( *virāgadhammaṃ* ), subject to cessation ( *nirodhadhammaṃ* ), having weighed it, having examined it, having analyzed it, having made it distinct, swiftly rushes to nirvāṇa in the cessation of aging and death, therefore, it is swift wisdom.

What is sharp wisdom ( *tikkhapaññā* )? *Tikkhapaññā* because it quickly cuts off defilements ( *kilese* ).

He does not tolerate an arisen sensual thought ( *kāmavitakkaṃ* ), an arisen thought of ill-will ( *byāpādavitakkaṃ* ), an arisen thought of harm ( *vihiṃsāvitakkaṃ* ), arisen evil unwholesome qualities, arisen greed ( *rāgaṃ* ), hatred ( *dosaṃ* ), delusion ( *mohaṃ* ), anger ( *kodhaṃ* ), resentment ( *upanāhaṃ* ), contempt ( *makkhaṃ* ), insolence ( *paḷāsaṃ* ), envy ( *issaṃ* ), avarice ( *macchariyaṃ* ), deceit ( *māyaṃ* ), slyness ( *sāṭheyyaṃ* ), obstinacy ( *thambhaṃ* ), impetuosity ( *sārambhaṃ* ), conceit ( *mānaṃ* ), arrogance ( *atimānaṃ* ), intoxication ( *madaṃ* ), negligence ( *pamādaṃ* ), all defilements, all misconduct, all (evil) preparations, all karma leading to becoming, he does not tolerate, he abandons, he dispels, he eliminates, he causes to be non-existent, therefore, it is sharp wisdom.

In one seat, the four noble paths ( *ariyamaggā* ), the four fruits of the contemplative life, the four kinds of discrimination, the six super-knowledges are attained, realized, touched with wisdom, therefore, it is sharp wisdom.
Sharp wisdom? What is penetrative wisdom ( *nibbedhikapaññā*)? Here, someone is full of agitation (*ubbegabahulo*) towards all conditioned things (*sabbasankhāresu*), full of anxiety (*uttāsabahulo*), full of aversion (*ukkaṇṭhanabahulo*), full of discontent (*aratibahulo*), full of displeasure (*anabhiratibahulo*), turned away, not delighting in all conditioned things. They penetrate and split apart the mass of greed (*lobhakkhandhaṃ*) that has never been penetrated or split apart before. Therefore, it is penetrative wisdom.

They penetrate and split apart the mass of hatred (*dosakkhandhaṃ*), the mass of delusion (*mohakkhandhaṃ*), anger (*kodhaṃ*), resentment (*upanāhaṃ*)…pe… all deeds leading to becoming (*sabbe bhavagāmikamme*) . Therefore, it is penetrative wisdom (Paṭi.

mula_pali:
217. Tatthetaṃ vuccati –

‘‘Pure puratthā purimāsu jātisu,

Aññātukāmo paripucchitā ahu;

Sussūsitā pabbajitaṃ upāsitā,

Atthantaro atthakathaṃ nisāmayi.

‘‘Paññāpaṭilābhagatena paññāpaṭilābhakatena (sī. pī.) ṭīkā oloketabbā kammunā,

paññāpaṭilābhakatena (sī. pī.) ṭīkā oloketabbā

Manussabhūto sukhumacchavī ahu;

Byākaṃsu uppādanimittakovidā,

Sukhumāni atthāni avecca dakkhiti.

‘‘Sace na pabbajjamupeti tādiso,

Vatteti cakkaṃ pathaviṃ pasāsati;

Atthānusiṭṭhīsu pariggahesu ca,

Na tena seyyo sadiso ca vijjati.

‘‘Sace ca pabbajjamupeti tādiso,

Nekkhammachandābhirato vicakkhaṇo;

Paññāvisiṭṭhaṃ labhate anuttaraṃ,

Pappoti bodhiṃ varabhūrimedhaso’’ti.

(13) Suvaṇṇavaṇṇalakkhaṇaṃ
mula_english:
217.
That is what is said:

"In former births, in previous existences,
Being desirous of knowing, he asked questions;
He listened, attended to the renunciate,
Understood the meaning, heeded the exposition of the meaning.

"Through the action of gaining wisdom
A human being with delicate skin came to be;
The skilled in the cause of production declared,
'Having understood, he will see subtle meanings.'

"If such a one does not embrace the homeless life,
He turns the wheel, he rules the earth;
In instructions on the meaning, and in acquisitions,
None is better or equal to him.

"If such a one embraces the homeless life,
Delighting in renunciation and virtuous inclination, discerning;
He obtains the unsurpassed, distinguished by wisdom,
He attains enlightenment, of excellent, abundant intellect."

(13) The characteristic of golden color.
commentary_pali:
217.Pabbajitaṃ upāsitāti paṇḍitaṃ pabbajitaṃ upasaṅkamitvā payirupāsitā. Atthantaroti yathā eke randhagavesino upārambhacittatāya dosaṃ abbhantaraṃ karitvā nisāmayanti, evaṃ anisāmetvā atthaṃ abbhantaraṃ katvā atthayuttaṃ kathaṃ nisāmayi upadhārayi.

Paṭilābhagatenāti paṭilābhatthāya gatena. Uppādanimittakovidāti uppāde ca nimitte ca chekā. Avecca dakkhitīti ñatvā passissati.

Paṭilābhagatenā Uppādanimittakovidā Avecca dakkhitī

Atthānusiṭṭhīsu pariggahesu cāti ye atthānusāsanesu pariggahā atthānatthaṃ pariggāhakāni ñāṇāni, tesūti attho.

Atthānusiṭṭhīsu pariggahesu cā

Suvaṇṇavaṇṇalakkhaṇavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
217. "pabbajitaṃ upāsitā" means having approached and attended upon a learned renunciate.

"atthantaro" means, just as some, seeking faults, listen with a fault-finding mentality, making the fault internal, so without listening in that way, having made the meaning internal, how did he listen to and consider the meaningful speech?

"paṭilābhagatenā" means having gone for the sake of gain.

"uppādanimittakovidā" means skilled in production and in signs.

"avecca dakkhitī" means having known, he will see.

"paṭilābhagatenā uppādanimittakovidā avecca dakkhitī atthānusiṭṭhīsu pariggahesu cā" means, those insights in instructions about meaning, the knowledges that grasp what is meaningful and meaningless in instructions about meaning, that is the meaning.

"atthānusiṭṭhīsu pariggahesu cā"

Description of the characteristics and color of gold.

mula_pali:
218. ‘‘Yampi , bhikkhave, tathāgato purimaṃ jātiṃ purimaṃ bhavaṃ purimaṃ niketaṃ pubbe manussabhūto samāno akkodhano ahosi anupāyāsabahulo, bahumpi vutto samāno nābhisajji na kuppi na byāpajji na patitthīyi, na kopañca dosañca appaccayañca pātvākāsi. Dātā ca ahosi sukhumānaṃ mudukānaṃ attharaṇānaṃ pāvuraṇānaṃ pāpuraṇānaṃ (sī. syā. pī.) khomasukhumānaṃ kappāsikasukhumānaṃ koseyyasukhumānaṃ kambalasukhumānaṃ. So tassa kammassa kaṭattā upacitattā…pe… so tato cuto itthattaṃ āgato samāno imaṃ mahāpurisalakkhaṇaṃ paṭilabhati. Suvaṇṇavaṇṇo hoti kañcanasannibhattaco.

‘‘So tena lakkhaṇena samannāgato sace agāraṃ ajjhāvasati, rājā hoti cakkavattī…pe… rājā samāno kiṃ labhati? Lābhī hoti sukhumānaṃ mudukānaṃ attharaṇānaṃ pāvuraṇānaṃ khomasukhumānaṃ kappāsikasukhumānaṃ koseyyasukhumānaṃ kambalasukhumānaṃ. Rājā samāno idaṃ labhati… buddho samāno kiṃ labhati? Lābhī hoti sukhumānaṃ mudukānaṃ attharaṇānaṃ pāvuraṇānaṃ khomasukhumānaṃ kappāsikasukhumānaṃ koseyyasukhumānaṃ kambalasukhumānaṃ. Buddho samāno idaṃ labhati’’. Etamatthaṃ bhagavā avoca.
mula_english:
218. "Bhikkhus, since a *Tathāgata*, in a former birth, a former existence, a former abode, formerly existing as a human being, was unangered ( *akkodhana*) and little given to despair (*anupāyāsabahulo*), and since when much was said he never answered back, was never irritated, never felt ill will, never resented, and never manifested annoyance, irritation, hate and surliness, and since he was a giver of fine soft rugs (*sukhumānaṃ mudukānaṃ attharaṇānaṃ* ) and cloaks (*pāvuraṇānaṃ*) made of fine linen (*khomasukhumānaṃ*), fine cotton (*kappāsikasukhumānaṃ*), fine silk (*koseyyasukhumānaṃ*), [and] fine wool (*kambalasukhumānaṃ*).

with that action performed, stored up,… on his being come again to the same human state (*itthattaṃ āgato samāno*), he acquires these two characteristics of a Great Man (*mahāpurisalakkhaṇaṃ paṭilabhati*):

He is the color of gold (*suvaṇṇavaṇṇo hoti*), and his skin has a golden sheen (*kañcanasannibhattaco*).

"So, endowed with that characteristic, if he dwells in a house, he becomes a wheel-turning monarch (*rājā hoti cakkavattī*)… what does a king obtain (*kiṃ labhati*)? He obtains (*lābhī hoti*) fine soft rugs (*sukhumānaṃ mudukānaṃ attharaṇānaṃ*) and cloaks (*pāvuraṇānaṃ*) made of fine linen (*khomasukhumānaṃ*), fine cotton (*kappāsikasukhumānaṃ*), fine silk (*koseyyasukhumānaṃ*), [and] fine wool (*kambalasukhumānaṃ*).

A king obtains this (*idaṃ labhati*)… what does a Buddha obtain (*buddho samāno kiṃ labhati*)? He obtains (*lābhī hoti*) fine soft rugs (*sukhumānaṃ mudukānaṃ attharaṇānaṃ*) and cloaks (*pāvuraṇānaṃ*) made of fine linen (*khomasukhumānaṃ*), fine cotton (*kappāsikasukhumānaṃ*), fine silk (*koseyyasukhumānaṃ*), [and] fine wool (*kambalasukhumānaṃ*).

A Buddha obtains this (*buddho samāno idaṃ labhati*)."

This is the meaning of what the Blessed One said (*etamatthaṃ bhagavā avoca*).
commentary_pali:
218.Akkodhanoti na anāgāmimaggena kodhassa pahīnattā, atha kho sacepi me kodho uppajjeyya, khippameva naṃ paṭivinodeyyanti evaṃ akkodhavasikattā. Nābhisajjīti kuṭilakaṇṭako viya tattha tattha mammaṃ tudanto viya na laggi. Na kuppi na byāpajjītiādīsu pubbuppattiko kopo. Tato balavataro byāpādo. Tato balavatarā patitthiyanā. Taṃ sabbaṃ akaronto na kuppi na byāpajji na patitthiyi. Appaccayanti domanassaṃ. Na pātvākāsīti na kāyavikārena vā vacīvikārena vā pākaṭamakāsi.

Idha kammaṃ nāma dīgharattaṃ akkodhanatā ceva sukhumattharaṇādidānañca. Kammasarikkhakaṃ nāma kodhanassa chavivaṇṇo āvilo hoti mukhaṃ duddasiyaṃ vatthacchādanasadisañca maṇḍanaṃ nāma natthi. Tasmā yo kodhano ceva vatthacchādanānañca adātā, so iminā kāraṇenassa jano kodhanādibhāvaṃ jānātūti dubbaṇṇo hoti dussaṇṭhāno. Akkodhanassa pana mukhaṃ virocati, chavivaṇṇo vippasīdati. Sattā hi catūhi kāraṇehi pāsādikā honti āmisadānena vā vatthadānena vā sammajjanena vā akkodhanatāya vā. Imāni cattāripi kāraṇāni dīgharattaṃ tathāgatena katāneva. Tenassa imesaṃ katabhāvaṃ sadevako loko iminā kāraṇena jānātūti suvaṇṇavaṇṇaṃ mahāpurisalakkhaṇaṃ nibbattati. Lakkhaṇaṃ nāma idameva lakkhaṇaṃ. Sukhumattharaṇādilābhitā ānisaṃso.

Kammasarikkhakaṃ Lakkhaṇaṃ ānisaṃso.
commentary_english:
218. "Akkodhano" means at 3.0116: not because anger has been abandoned by the path of the non-returner (anāgāmin), but rather because, even if anger should arise in me, I would quickly dispel it; thus, through the practice of non-anger.

"Nābhisajjī" means he does not cling like a crooked thorn pricking at vital spots here and there.

"Na kuppi na byāpajjī" etc., at 3.0105:  The anger that arises initially is kopa. Thereafter, byāpādo is stronger. Thereafter, patitthiyanā is even stronger. Not doing all that, he is neither angry, nor malicious, nor resentful.

"Appaccaya" means dejection (domanassaṃ).

"Na pātvākāsī" means he did not make it manifest through bodily action or verbal action.

Here, karma means prolonged non-anger and at 3.0934: giving of soft bedding, etc.

"Kammasarikkhakaṃ" means, for an angry person, the color of the skin is murky, the face is unpleasant to look at, and there is no adornment like a cloth covering.

Therefore, whoever is angry and does not give cloth coverings, etc., people know his angry nature by this cause, that he is ugly and misshapen.

But for a non-angry person, the face shines, and the color of the skin is very clear.

Indeed, beings are pleasing through four causes: either through giving food (āmisadānena), or through giving cloth (vatthadānena), or through sweeping (sammajjanena), or through non-anger (akkodhanatāya).

These four causes have been practiced for a long time by the Tathāgata.

Therefore, the world with its gods knows by this cause that he has done these deeds, and thus a golden color, the marks of a great man (mahāpurisalakkhaṇaṃ), arise.

"Lakkhaṇaṃ" means this very mark.

The benefit (ānisaṃsaḥ) is the attainment of soft bedding, etc.

3.0934: Kammasarikkhakaṃ, lakkhaṇaṃ, ānisaṃsaḥ.

mula_pali:

‘‘Akkodhañca adhiṭṭhahi adāsi adāsi ca (sī. pī.),

upapajja (sī. pī.)

Kanakatanusannibho idhābhibhavati,

Suravarataroriva indo.

pasāsati (syā.)

pasayha abhivasana-varataraṃ (sī. pī.)

vipula (syā.), vipulaṃ (sī. pī.)

suhita (syā.), sa hi (sī. pī.)

(14) Kosohitavatthaguyhalakkhaṇaṃ
mula_english:
219.
That is why it is said:

“He mastered angerlessness and gave gifts,”

Gave gifts of fine, beautiful clothes;

In a former existence, standing, he generously bestowed,

Like a god raining down abundant wealth.

“Having done that, having passed away from here, to the divine,

He attained, having experienced the result of good deeds;

Possessing a body like refined gold, here he prevails,

Like the moon among the best of gods.

“A man, having left home, dwells in a house,”

He instructs those who are wrong with great authority;

Overpowering, he swiftly obtains the seven jewels,

He gains stainless, fine-skinned purity.

“He gains robes, clothes, freedom, and cloaks,

If he approaches homelessness;

United, he experiences the fruit of former deeds,

There is no destruction of what has been done."

(14) The characteristic of hidden meaning in clothing
commentary_pali:
219.Abhivissajīti abhivissajjesi. Mahimiva suro abhivassanti suro vuccati devo, mahāpathaviṃ abhivassanto devo viya.

Suravarataroriva indoti surānaṃ varataro indo viya.

Suravarataroriva indo

Kosohitavatthaguyhalakkhaṇavaṇṇanā

219. *abhivissajī* means *abhivissajessi*.

*mahimiva suro abhivassa* means *suro* is called *devo*, like a *devo* raining on the great earth (*mahāpathavīṃ*).

mula_pali:
220. Yampi, bhikkhave, tathāgato purimaṃ jātiṃ purimaṃ bhavaṃ purimaṃ niketaṃ pubbe manussabhūto samāno cirappanaṭṭhe sucirappavāsino ñātimitte suhajje sakhino samānetā ahosi. Mātarampi puttena samānetā ahosi, puttampi mātarā samānetā ahosi, pitarampi puttena samānetā ahosi, puttampi pitarā samānetā ahosi, bhātarampi bhātarā samānetā ahosi, bhātarampi bhaginiyā samānetā ahosi, bhaginimpi bhātarā samānetā ahosi, bhaginimpi bhaginiyā samānetā ahosi, samaṅgīkatvā samaggiṃ katvā (sī. syā. pī.) ca abbhanumoditā ahosi. So tassa kammassa kaṭattā…pe… so tato cuto itthattaṃ āgato samāno imaṃ mahāpurisalakkhaṇaṃ paṭilabhati – kosohitavatthaguyho hoti.

‘‘So tena lakkhaṇena samannāgato sace agāraṃ ajjhāvasati, rājā hoti cakkavattī…pe… rājā samāno kiṃ labhati? Pahūtaputto hoti, parosahassaṃ kho panassa puttā bhavanti sūrā vīraṅgarūpā parasenappamaddanā. Rājā samāno idaṃ labhati… buddho samāno kiṃ labhati? Pahūtaputto hoti, anekasahassaṃ kho panassa puttā bhavanti sūrā vīraṅgarūpā parasenappamaddanā. Buddho samāno idaṃ labhati’’. Etamatthaṃ bhagavā avoca.
mula_english:
220.

Even so, monks, the *tathāgata*, having been a human being in the past, in his previous birth, in his previous existence, in his previous abode, was one who brought together relatives, friends, companions, and associates for a long time established in long-term exile.

A mother would bring her son together, and a son his mother; a father would bring his son together, and a son his father; a brother would bring his brother together, and a brother his sister; a sister would bring her brother together, and a sister her sister, having made them harmonious, and they were rejoiced over.

He, through performing that action… he, fallen from there, having come to this state, obtains this mark of a great man—he has retracted his penis into its sheath.

‘‘He, endowed with that mark, if he lives in a house, becomes a king, a wheel-turning monarch… What does a king obtain? He has many sons; he has more than a thousand sons who are heroes, of heroic stature, conquerors of the hostile army.

A king obtains this… A *buddha* obtains what? He has many sons; he has many thousands of sons who are heroes, of heroic stature, conquerors of the hostile army.

A *buddha* obtains this.’’

The Blessed One said this.
commentary_pali:
220.Mātarampiputtena samānetā ahosīti imaṃ kammaṃ rajje patiṭṭhitena sakkā kātuṃ. Tasmā bodhisattopi rajjaṃ kārayamāno antonagare catukkādīsu catūsu nagaradvāresu bahinagare catūsu disāsu imaṃ kammaṃ karothāti manusse ṭhapesi. Te mātaraṃ kuhiṃ me putto puttaṃ na passāmīti vilapantiṃ pariyesamānaṃ disvā ehi, amma, puttaṃ dakkhasīti taṃ ādāya gantvā nahāpetvā bhojetvā puttamassā pariyesitvā dassenti. Esa nayo sabbattha.

Idha kammaṃ nāma dīgharattaṃ ñātīnaṃ samaṅgibhāvakaraṇaṃ. Kammasarikkhakaṃ nāma ñātayo hi samaṅgībhūtā aññamaññassa vajjaṃ paṭicchādenti. Kiñcāpi hi te kalahakāle kalahaṃ karonti, ekassa pana dose uppanne aññaṃ jānāpetuṃ na icchanti. Ayaṃ nāma etassa dosoti vutte sabbe uṭṭhahitvā kena diṭṭhaṃ kena sutaṃ, amhākaṃ ñātīsu evarūpaṃ kattā nāma natthīti. Tathāgatena ca taṃ ñātisaṅgahaṃ karontena dīgharattaṃ idaṃ vajjappaṭicchādanakammaṃ nāma kataṃ hoti. Athassa sadevako loko iminā kāraṇena evarūpassa kammassa katabhāvaṃ jānātūti kosohitavatthaguyhalakkhaṇaṃ nibbattati. Lakkhaṇaṃ nāma idameva lakkhaṇaṃ. Pahūtaputtatā ānisaṃso.

kammaṃ Kammasarikkhakaṃ Lakkhaṇaṃ ānisaṃso.
commentary_english:
220.
"[She] was equal to a son" — it is possible for one established in kingship to do this act.
Therefore, the bodhisattva, while ruling the kingdom, stationed men at the four city gates in the inner city, beginning with the crossroads, and in the four directions in the outer city, [saying,] "Do this act!"
They, having seen a mother wailing, "Where is my son, my son?," having searched for [him], having gone, having bathed [him], having fed [him], having searched for [him] with his mother, show [him to her].
This method applies to all instances.

Here, the meaning of *karma* is prolonged making of harmony among relatives.
The meaning of "similar to *karma*" is: relatives, having become harmonious, conceal each other’s faults.
Even though they quarrel at the time of strife, they do not want to make known another's fault if it has arisen.
"This is his fault" — when this has been said, all having risen up [say,] "By whom has it been seen? By whom has it been heard? Among our relatives, there is no one who does such a thing!"
And the *Tathāgata*, while making that collection of relatives, for a long time, this act of concealing faults is done.
Then, may the world with the gods know the state of having done this act of such *karma* by this cause. The characteristic of [having] a hidden vagina and garment arises.
The meaning of *lakṣaṇa* is just this characteristic.
The advantage is having many sons.

*Karma*. Similar to *karma*.
Characteristic. Advantage.

mula_pali:
221. Tatthetaṃ vuccati –

‘‘Pure puratthā purimāsu jātisu,

Cirappanaṭṭhe sucirappavāsino;

Ñātī suhajje sakhino samānayi,

Samaṅgikatvā anumoditā ahu.

‘‘So tena sa tena (ka.) kammena divaṃ samakkami,

sa tena (ka.)

Sukhañca khiḍḍāratiyo ca anvabhi;

Tato cavitvā punarāgato idha,

Kosohitaṃ vindati vatthachādiyaṃ.

‘‘Pahūtaputto bhavatī tathāvidho,

Parosahassañca parosahassassa (sī. pī.) bhavanti atrajā;

parosahassassa (sī. pī.)

Sūrā ca vīrā ca sūrā ca vīraṅgarūpā (ka.) amittatāpanā,

sūrā ca vīraṅgarūpā (ka.)

Gihissa pītiṃjananā piyaṃvadā.

‘‘Bahūtarā pabbajitassa iriyato,

Bhavanti puttā vacanānusārino;

Gihissa vā pabbajitassa vā puna,

Taṃ lakkhaṇaṃ jāyati tadatthajotaka’’nti.

Paṭhamabhāṇavāro niṭṭhito.

(15-16) Parimaṇḍalaanonamajaṇṇuparimasanalakkhaṇāni
mula_english:
221. That is what is said here:

“In former times, in previous births,
Having long been established and lived for a long time,
He brought together relatives, friends, and companions,
Having agreed, he rejoiced with them.

“Through that action, he attained heaven,
And experienced happiness, play, and delights;
Having passed away from there, he returned here again,
He obtains wealth hidden, covered with cloth.

“He becomes the father of many children,
And more than a thousand children are born to him;
They are heroes, brave, and tormentors of enemies,
Generators of joy for the householder, and speak pleasantly.

“Many more children of the renunciate who is behaving well,
Become sons who follow his word;
Whether for the householder or the renunciate,
That characteristic arises, revealing that meaning.”

The first recitation section is finished.

(15-16) The characteristics of being perfectly round, not leaning, and well-kneaded.
commentary_pali:
221.Vatthachādiyanti vatthena chādetabbaṃ vatthaguyhaṃ.

Amittatāpanāti amittānaṃ patāpanā. Gihissa pītiṃ jananāti gihibhūtassa sato pītijananā.

Amittatāpanā Gihissa pītiṃ jananā

Parimaṇḍalādilakkhaṇavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
vatthachādiya: "vatthena chādetabbaṃ vatthaguyhaṃ" means "that which should be covered with cloth, the secret of cloth."

amittatāpanā: "amittānaṃ patāpanā" means "tormenting enemies."

gihissa pītiṃ jananā: "gihibhūtassa sato pītijananā" means "generating joy for one who has become a householder."

amittatāpanā gihissa pītiṃ jananā

Description of the characteristics beginning with "perfectly round."

mula_pali:
222. ‘‘Yampi , bhikkhave, tathāgato purimaṃ jātiṃ purimaṃ bhavaṃ purimaṃ niketaṃ pubbe manussabhūto samāno mahājanasaṅgahaṃ mahājanasaṅgāhakaṃ (ka.) samekkhamāno samapekkhamāno (ka.) samaṃ jānāti sāmaṃ jānāti, purisaṃ jānāti purisavisesaṃ jānāti – ‘ayamidamarahati ayamidamarahatī’ti tattha tattha purisavisesakaro ahosi. So tassa kammassa kaṭattā…pe… so tato cuto itthattaṃ āgato samāno imāni dve mahāpurisalakkhaṇāni paṭilabhati. Nigrodha parimaṇḍalo ca hoti, ṭhitakoyeva ca anonamanto ubhohi pāṇitalehi jaṇṇukāni parimasati parimajjati.

‘‘So tehi lakkhaṇehi samannāgato sace agāraṃ ajjhāvasati, rājā hoti cakkavattī…pe… rājā samāno kiṃ labhati ? Aḍḍho hoti mahaddhano mahābhogo pahūtajātarūparajato pahūtavittūpakaraṇo pahūtadhanadhañño paripuṇṇakosakoṭṭhāgāro. Rājā samāno idaṃ labhati…pe… buddho samāno kiṃ labhati? Aḍḍho hoti mahaddhano mahābhogo. Tassimāni dhanāni honti, seyyathidaṃ, saddhādhanaṃ sīladhanaṃ hiridhanaṃ ottappadhanaṃ sutadhanaṃ cāgadhanaṃ paññādhanaṃ. Buddho samāno idaṃ labhati’’. Etamatthaṃ bhagavā avoca.
mula_english:
222.
’’And also, O monks, the Thus-Gone-One, in a prior birth, a prior existence, a prior abode, formerly being a human being, carefully considering the great multitude, knowing equally, knowing by himself, knowing a person, knowing a distinguished person— ‘This one is worthy of this, this one is worthy of that’— in that place, in that place, he was a maker of distinctions among persons.
He, by the performance of that action... having passed away from there, having come to this state, he acquires these two marks of a great man.
And he is of the measure of a banyan tree, and standing, without bending down, with both palms he touches and rubs his knees.

’’He, endowed with those marks, if he lives in a house, he is a wheel-turning monarch… a king being, what does he obtain? He is rich, of great wealth, of great possessions, with an abundance of gold and silver, with an abundance of possessions and requisites, with an abundance of money and grain, with a full treasury and storehouse.
A king being, this he obtains… a Buddha being, what does he obtain? He is rich, of great wealth, of great possessions.
These riches are his: namely, the wealth of faith (śraddhādhana), the wealth of virtue (śīladhana), the wealth of modesty (hirīdhana), the wealth of fear (ottappadhana), the wealth of learning (śrutadhana), the wealth of generosity (tyāgadhana), the wealth of wisdom (prajñādhana).
A Buddha being, this he obtains’’.
This meaning the Blessed One said.
commentary_pali:
222.Samaṃ jānātīti ‘‘ayaṃ tārukkhasamo ayaṃ pokkharasātisamo’’ti evaṃ tena tena samaṃ jānāti. Sāmaṃ jānātīti sayaṃ jānāti. Purisaṃ jānātīti ‘‘ayaṃ seṭṭhasammato’’ti purisaṃ jānāti. Purisavisesaṃ jānātīti muggaṃ māsena samaṃ akatvā guṇavisiṭṭhassa visesaṃ jānāti. Ayamidamarahatīti ayaṃ puriso idaṃ nāma dānasakkāraṃ arahati . Purisavisesakaro ahosīti purisavisesaṃ ñatvā kārako ahosi. Yo yaṃ arahati, tasseva taṃ adāsi. Yo hi kahāpaṇārahassa aḍḍhaṃ deti, so parassa aḍḍhaṃ nāseti. Yo dve kahāpaṇe deti, so attano kahāpaṇaṃ nāseti. Tasmā idaṃ ubhayampi akatvā yo yaṃ arahati, tassa tadeva adāsi. Saddhādhanantiādīsu sampattipaṭilābhaṭṭhena saddhādīnaṃ dhanabhāvo veditabbo.

Idha kammaṃ nāma dīgharattaṃ purisavisesaṃ ñatvā kataṃ samasaṅgahakammaṃ. Kammasarikkhakaṃ nāma tadassa kammaṃ sadevako loko iminā kāraṇena jānātūti imāni dve lakkhaṇāni nibbattanti. Lakkhaṇaṃ nāma idameva lakkhaṇadvayaṃ. Dhanasampatti ānisaṃso.

kammaṃ Kammasarikkhakaṃ Lakkhaṇaṃ ānisaṃso.
commentary_english:
222. *Samaṃ jānātī* means, "This is like a *tārukkha*, this is like a *pokkharasāti*," thus, in that way, he knows similarly.

*Sāmaṃ jānātī* means he knows himself.

*Purisaṃ jānātī* means, "This is highly regarded," thus he knows a man.

*Purisavisesaṃ jānātī* means, without making *mugga* equal to *māsa*, he knows the distinction of one endowed with good qualities.

*Ayamidamarahatī* means, this person deserves this gift and honor.

*Purisavisesakaro ahosī* means, having known the distinction of a person, he was a doer.

Whoever deserves what, to him he gave that very thing.

If he gives half to one who deserves a *kahāpaṇa*, he destroys half of another.

Whoever gives two *kahāpaṇa*s, he destroys his own *kahāpaṇa*.

Therefore, without doing both of these, whoever deserves what, to him he gave that very thing.

In *saddhādhana* etc., it should be understood that faith and so forth have the nature of wealth by way of obtaining prosperity.

Here, *kammaṃ* (karma) means a *samasaṅgahakammaṃ* (harmonious/unifying karma) done, having known a distinguished person for a long time.

*Kammasarikkhakaṃ* means, because of that, the world with the gods knows, "By this cause," thus these two characteristics arise.

*Lakkhaṇaṃ* means just this pair of characteristics.

Wealth-prosperity is *ānisaṃsa* (advantageous/beneficial).

*Kammaṃ* (karma), *kammasarikkhakaṃ*

*Lakkhaṇaṃ* (characteristic), *ānisaṃsa* (advantageous/beneficial).

mula_pali:
223. Tatthetaṃ vuccati –

‘‘Tuliya paṭivicaya cintayitvā,

Mahājanasaṅgahanaṃ mahājanaṃ saṅgāhakaṃ (ka.) samekkhamāno;

mahājanaṃ saṅgāhakaṃ (ka.)

Ayamidamarahati tattha tattha,

Purisavisesakaro pure ahosi.

‘‘Mahiñca pana samā ca pana (syā.), sa hi ca pana (sī. pī.) ṭhito anonamanto,

samā ca pana (syā.), sa hi ca pana (sī. pī.)

Phusati karehi ubhohi jaṇṇukāni;

Mahiruhaparimaṇḍalo ahosi,

Sucaritakammavipākasesakena.

‘‘Bahuvividhanimittalakkhaṇaññū,

Atinipuṇā manujā byākariṃsu;

Bahuvividhā gihīnaṃ arahāni,

Paṭilabhati daharo susu kumāro.

‘‘Idha ca mahīpatissa kāmabhogī,

Gihipatirūpakā bahū bhavanti;

Yadi ca jahati sabbakāmabhogaṃ,

Labhati anuttaraṃ uttamadhanagga’’nti.

(17-19) Sīhapubbaddhakāyāditilakkhaṇaṃ
mula_english:
That is what is said:

Having considered and investigated with measure,
Observing the consolidation of the great multitude,
"This is worthy of this, in that place,"
He was in the past a maker of distinctions among men.

And standing firm, unbending, on the earth,
He touches his knees with both hands;
He was perfectly round like a great tree,
Through the remainder of the ripening of well-done deeds.

Knowing various omens and signs,
Very skilled men declared:
"Various kinds of attainments of the worthy ones,
The young, very tender boy obtains."

And here, of the king, a enjoyer of sensual pleasures,
Many become householder-like lords;
And if he abandons all sensual pleasures,
He obtains the unsurpassed, the highest, excellent wealth.

(17-19) Characteristics beginning with having a body bound in the front like a lion
commentary_pali:
223.Tuliyāti tulayitvā. Paṭivicayāti paṭivicinitvā. Mahājanasaṅgāhakanti mahājanasaṅgahaṇaṃ. Samekkhamānoti samaṃ pekkhamāno. Atinipuṇāmanujāti atinipuṇā sukhumapaññā lakkhaṇapāṭhakamanussā. Bahuvividhā gihīnaṃ arahānīti bahū vividhāni gihīnaṃ anucchavikāni paṭilabhati. Daharo susu kumāro ‘‘ayaṃ daharo kumāro paṭilabhissatī’’ti byākaṃsu mahīpatissāti rañño.

Sīhapubbaddhakāyādilakkhaṇavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
223.
*tuliyā* means having compared.
*paṭivicayā* means having examined.
*mahājanasaṅgāhaka* means collecting a great multitude of people.
*samekkhamāno* means regarding equally.
*atinipuṇā manujā* means very clever, possessing subtle wisdom, people who are experts in লক্ষণ.
*bahuvividhā gihīnaṃ arahānī* means obtaining many various suitable things for householders.
*daharo susu kumāro* ‘‘ayaṃ daharo kumāro paṭilabhissatī’’ti byākaṃsu *mahīpatissā* means the king said, "This young boy will receive [it]."
Description of the characteristics beginning with the siṃhapubbaddhakāya.

mula_pali:
224. ‘‘Yampi , bhikkhave, tathāgato purimaṃ jātiṃ purimaṃ bhavaṃ purimaṃ niketaṃ pubbe manussabhūto samāno bahujanassa atthakāmo ahosi hitakāmo phāsukāmo yogakkhemakāmo – ‘kintime saddhāya vaḍḍheyyuṃ, sīlena vaḍḍheyyuṃ, sutena vaḍḍheyyuṃ sutena vaḍḍheyyuṃ, buddhiyā vaḍḍheyyuṃ (syā.), cāgena vaḍḍheyyuṃ, dhammena vaḍḍheyyuṃ, paññāya vaḍḍheyyuṃ, dhanadhaññena vaḍḍheyyuṃ, khettavatthunā vaḍḍheyyuṃ, dvipadacatuppadehi vaḍḍheyyuṃ, puttadārehi vaḍḍheyyuṃ, dāsakammakaraporisehi vaḍḍheyyuṃ, ñātīhi vaḍḍheyyuṃ, mittehi vaḍḍheyyuṃ, bandhavehi vaḍḍheyyu’nti. So tassa kammassa kaṭattā…pe… so tato cuto itthattaṃ āgato samāno imāni tīṇi mahāpurisalakkhaṇāni paṭilabhati. Sīhapubbaddhakāyo ca hoti citantaraṃso ca samavaṭṭakkhandho ca.

‘‘So tehi lakkhaṇehi samannāgato sace agāraṃ ajjhāvasati, rājā hoti cakkavattī…pe… rājā samāno kiṃ labhati? Aparihānadhammo hoti, na parihāyati dhanadhaññena khettavatthunā dvipadacatuppadehi puttadārehi dāsakammakaraporisehi ñātīhi mittehi bandhavehi, na parihāyati sabbasampattiyā. Rājā samāno idaṃ labhati… buddho samāno kiṃ labhati? Aparihānadhammo hoti, na parihāyati saddhāya sīlena sutena cāgena paññāya, na parihāyati sabbasampattiyā. Buddho samāno idaṃ labhati’’. Etamatthaṃ bhagavā avoca.
mula_english:
224.
‘‘Bhikkhus, since a *Tathāgata* in a former birth, formerly existing as a human being, sought the good, the welfare, the comfort, the safety from bondage, of the many, thinking “How shall these have increase in faith (*śraddhā*), in virtue (*śīla*), in learning, in generosity (*cāga*), in understanding (*prajñā*), in riches and corn, in fields and lands (*kṣetravastu*), in bipeds and quadrupeds, in wives and children, in bondsmen, servants and men, in relatives, in friends, in kinsmen?”

With that action performed, stored up, on his being come again to this state, he obtains these three marks of a great man (*mahāpurisalakkhaṇa*):

He has a body like the forepart of a lion (*sīhapubbaddhakāya*), he has evenly spaced shoulders, and he has a well-rounded neck.

‘‘So, endowed with those marks, if he dwells in a house, he becomes a king, a wheel-turner… What does a king obtain? He is one whose righteousness does not decline (*aparihāṇadhamma*), he does not fall away from riches and corn, from fields and lands (*kṣetravastu*), from bipeds and quadrupeds, from wives and children, from bondsmen, servants and men, from relatives, from friends, from kinsmen, he does not fall away from all prosperity (*sabbasampatti*). A king obtains this… What does a *Buddha* obtain? He is one whose righteousness does not decline (*aparihāṇadhamma*), he does not fall away from faith (*śraddhā*), virtue (*śīla*), learning, generosity (*cāga*), understanding (*prajñā*), he does not fall away from all prosperity (*sabbasampatti*). A *Buddha* obtains this’’.

This is the meaning of what the Blessed One (*bhagavā*) said.
commentary_pali: 224.Yogakkhemakāmoti yogato khemakāmo. Paññāyāti kammassakatapaññāya. Idha kammaṃ nāma mahājanassa atthakāmatā. Kammasarikkhakaṃ nāma taṃ mahājanassa atthakāmatāya vaḍḍhimeva paccāsīsitabhāvaṃ sadevako loko iminā kāraṇena jānātūti imāni samantaparipūrāni aparihīnāni tīṇi lakkhaṇāni nibbattanti. Lakkhaṇaṃ nāma idameva lakkhaṇattayaṃ. Dhanādīhi ceva saddhādīhi ca aparihāni ānisaṃso.
commentary_english:
224. *yogakkhemakāmo* means one who desires *yogakkhema* from yoga.

*paññāyā* means by wisdom (*prajñā*) that is one's own through action (*karma*).

Here, *kammaṃ* (karma) means the welfare desired by the *mahājanas*.

*kammasarikkhakaṃ* means that the world with the *devas* knows by this cause that the state of anticipating only growth for the sake of the welfare desired by the *mahājanas*. These three characteristics (*lakṣaṇā*) arise, being entirely full all around and not deficient.

*lakkhaṇaṃ* (characteristic) means just this triad of characteristics (*lakṣaṇatrayaṃ*).

The advantage (*ānisaṃsa*) of non-deficiency with wealth (*dhana*) and so on, and faith (*śraddhā*) and so on.

mula_pali:
225. Tatthetaṃ vuccati –

‘‘Saddhāya sīlena sutena buddhiyā,

Cāgena dhammena bahūhi sādhuhi;

Dhanena dhaññena ca khettavatthunā,

Puttehi dārehi catuppadehi ca.

‘‘Ñātīhi mittehi ca bandhavehi ca,

Balena vaṇṇena sukhena cūbhayaṃ;

Kathaṃ na hāyeyyuṃ pareti icchati,

Atthassa middhī ca idaṃ samiddhañca (ka.), addhaṃ samiddhañca (syā.) panābhikaṅkhati.

idaṃ samiddhañca (ka.), addhaṃ samiddhañca (syā.)

‘‘Sa sīhapubbaddhasusaṇṭhito ahu,

Samavaṭṭakkhandho ca citantaraṃso;

Pubbe suciṇṇena katena kammunā,

Ahāniyaṃ pubbanimittamassa taṃ.

‘‘Gihīpi dhaññena dhanena vaḍḍhati,

Puttehi dārehi catuppadehi ca;

Akiñcano pabbajito anuttaraṃ,

Pappoti bodhiṃ asahānadhammata’’nti sambodhimahānadhammatanti (syā. ka.) ṭīkā oloketabbā.

sambodhimahānadhammatanti (syā. ka.) ṭīkā oloketabbā

(20) Rasaggasaggitālakkhaṇaṃ
mula_english:
225. Thus it is said –

With faith (*śraddhā*), with morality (*śīla*), with learning (*śruta*), with wisdom (*buddhi*),
With generosity (*cāga*), with the law (*dharma*), with many virtuous qualities;
With wealth (*dhana*), with grain (*dhañña*), and with fields and property (*khettavatthu*),
With sons (*puttehi*), wives (*dārehi*), and quadrupeds (*catuppadehi*).

With relatives (*ñātīhi*), friends (*mittehi*), and kinsmen (*bandhavehi*),
With strength (*bala*), complexion (*vaṇṇa*), and happiness (*sukha*)—both;
"How should they not decline?" thus he wishes,
But he does not long for the sluggishness of wealth (*attha*).

He was well-established, a lion in his former existence (*sīhapubbaddhasusaṇṭhito*),

With well-rounded shoulders, and a mind full of light (*citta*);
By meritorious deeds well performed in the past (*pubbe suciṇṇena katena kammunā*),
That is an indestructible sign of his former existence (*pubbanimittamassa taṃ*).

Even a householder prospers with grain (*dhañña*) and wealth (*dhana*),
With sons (*puttehi*), wives (*dārehi*), and quadrupeds (*catuppadehi*);
The homeless wanderer attains the unsurpassed (*anuttaraṃ*),
Awakening (*bodhi*) overcoming the lawless state (*asahānadhammata*)." The commentary *sambodhimahānadhammatanti* should be consulted.

(20) The characteristic of the highest taste.
commentary_pali:
225.Saddhāyāti okappanasaddhāya pasādasaddhāya. Sīlenāti pañcasīlena dasasīlena. Sutenāti pariyattisavanena. Buddhiyāti etesaṃ buddhiyā , ‘‘kinti etehi vaḍḍheyyu’’nti evaṃ cintesīti attho. Dhammenāti lokiyadhammena. Bahūhi sādhūhīti aññehipi bahūhi uttamaguṇehi. Asahānadhammatanti aparihīnadhammaṃ.

Rasaggasaggitālakkhaṇavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
225.
*Śraddhāyā*: By *śraddhā* is meant conviction (*okappanasaddhāya*) and serene faith (*pasādasaddhāya*).
*Śīlenā*: By morality (*śīlenā*) is meant the five precepts (*pañcasīlena*) and the ten precepts (*dasasīlena*).
*Sutenā*: By learning (*sutenā*) is meant the teaching (*pariyattisavanena*).
*Buddhiyā*: By wisdom (*buddhiyā*) is meant their wisdom (*etesam buddhiyā*), thinking, "How may we grow by these means?" This is the meaning.
*Dhammenā*: By *dhammena* is meant worldly *dhamma* (*lokiyadhammena*).
*Bahūhi sādhūhī*: By "many virtuous ones" (*bahūhi sādhūhī*) is meant many others with supreme qualities (*aññehipi bahūhi uttamaguṇehi*).
*Asahānadhammata*: *Asahānadhammata* means undiminished quality (*aparihīnadhammaṃ*).

Explanation of the characteristic of taste (*rasaggasaggitālakkhaṇavaṇṇanā*).

mula_pali:
226. ‘‘Yampi , bhikkhave, tathāgato purimaṃ jātiṃ purimaṃ bhavaṃ purimaṃ niketaṃ pubbe manussabhūto samāno sattānaṃ aviheṭhakajātiko ahosi pāṇinā vā leḍḍunā vā daṇḍena vā satthena vā. So tassa kammassa kaṭattā upacitattā…pe… so tato cuto itthattaṃ āgato samāno imaṃ mahāpurisalakkhaṇaṃ paṭilabhati, rasaggasaggī hoti, uddhaggāssa rasaharaṇīyo gīvāya jātā honti samābhivāhiniyo samavāharasaharaṇiyo (syā.).

‘‘So tena lakkhaṇena samannāgato sace agāraṃ ajjhāvasati, rājā hoti cakkavattī…pe… rājā samāno kiṃ labhati? Appābādho hoti appātaṅko, samavepākiniyā gahaṇiyā samannāgato nātisītāya nāccuṇhāya. Rājā samāno idaṃ labhati… buddho samāno kiṃ labhati? Appābādho hoti appātaṅko samavepākiniyā gahaṇiyā samannāgato nātisītāya nāccuṇhāya majjhimāya padhānakkhamāya. Buddho samāno idaṃ labhati’’. Etamatthaṃ bhagavā avoca.
mula_english:
226.
"Furthermore, monks, when the *tathāgata* in a former life, a former existence, a former abode, having been a human being, was one who did not harm beings with his hand, with a clod, with a stick, or with a weapon,

he, as a result of the performance and accumulation of that action... he, passing away from there and being reborn here, obtains this mark of a great man: he is exquisite in taste, and taste-conducting channels arise in his neck that are evenly distributed.

"He who is endowed with that characteristic, if he lives at home, becomes a king, a wheel-turning monarch... What does a king obtain? He is free from illness and discomfort, endowed with good digestion—neither too cold nor too hot.
A king obtains this... What does a Buddha obtain? He is free from illness and discomfort, endowed with good digestion—neither too cold nor too hot, of moderate strength, fit for exertion.
A Buddha obtains this."

This is the meaning of what the Blessed One said.
commentary_pali: 226.Samābhivāhiniyoti yathā tilaphalamattampi jivhagge ṭhapitaṃ sabbattha pharati, evaṃ samā hutvā vahanti. Idha kammaṃ nāma aviheṭhanakammaṃ. Kammasarikkhakaṃ nāma pāṇiādīhi pahāraṃ laddhassa tattha tattha lohitaṃ saṇṭhāti, gaṇṭhi gaṇṭhi hutvā antova pubbaṃ gaṇhāti, antova bhijjati, evaṃ so bahurogo hoti. Tathāgatena pana dīgharattaṃ imaṃ ārogyakaraṇakammaṃ kataṃ. Tadassa sadevako loko iminā kāraṇena jānātūti ārogyakaraṃ rasaggasaggilakkhaṇaṃ nibbattati. Lakkhaṇaṃ nāma idameva lakkhaṇaṃ. Appābādhatā ānisaṃso.
commentary_english:
226. As, when a drop of sesame oil is placed on the tip of the tongue, it spreads everywhere, so they flow, having become unified.

Here, *karma* means non-injurious action.

*Kammasarikkhakaṃ* means that when someone who has been struck with hands etc., blood gathers in that spot, forming knots, and pus forms inside; it breaks open inside, and thus he has many diseases.

However, the *Tathāgata* has performed this health-giving action for a long time.

May the world with its gods know this reason: thus arises the characteristic of health-giving, excellent taste and heaven.

*Lakkhaṇaṃ* means just this characteristic.

Freedom from disease is the *ānisaṃsa* (benefit).

mula_pali:
227. Tatthetaṃ vuccati –

‘‘Na pāṇidaṇḍehi panātha leḍḍunā,

Satthena vā maraṇavadhena māraṇavadhena (ka.) vā pana;

māraṇavadhena (ka.)

Ubbādhanāya paritajjanāya vā,

Na heṭhayī janatamaheṭhako ahu.

‘‘Teneva so sugatimupecca modati,

Sukhapphalaṃ kariya sukhāni vindati;

Samojasā sampajjasā (sī. pī.), pāmuñjasā (syā.), sāmañca sā (ka.) rasaharaṇī susaṇṭhitā,

sampajjasā (sī. pī.), pāmuñjasā (syā.), sāmañca sā (ka.)

Idhāgato labhati rasaggasaggitaṃ.

‘‘Tenāhu naṃ atinipuṇā vicakkhaṇā,

Ayaṃ naro sukhabahulo bhavissati;

Gihissa vā pabbajitassa vā puna pana (syā.),

pana (syā.)

Taṃ lakkhaṇaṃ bhavati tadatthajotaka’’nti.

(21-22) Abhinīlanettagopakhumalakkhaṇāni
mula_english:
Herein it is said:

“Not with hand or stick, nor with a clod,
Nor with a weapon, or deadly violence,
Nor for inciting or vexing,
Should he inflict pain on any being.

Thus, attaining a good destiny (sugati), he rejoices,
Having performed deeds yielding pleasant fruit (sukhapphalaṃ), he obtains pleasures (sukhāni vindati);
With composure, well-established, are the flavors and essences,

Having come here, he obtains the best flavor (rasaggasaggitaṃ).

Therefore, those who are very clever and discerning say,
“This person will be abundant in happiness (sukhabahulo bhavissati);
Whether a householder (gihissa) or a renunciate (pabbajitassa),

That is a characteristic indicative of its meaning.”

(21-22) The characteristics of dark blue eyes and eyelashes.
commentary_pali:
227.Maraṇavadhenāti ‘‘etaṃ māretha etaṃ ghātethā’’ti evaṃ āṇattena maraṇavadhena. Ubbādhanāyāti bandhanāgārappavesanena.

Abhinīlanettādilakkhaṇavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
*maraṇavadhenā*ti, "kill him, strike him down," thus with the command of death. *ubbādhanāyā*ti, by imprisonment.

Description of characteristics, beginning with dark-blue eyes.

mula_pali:
228. ‘‘Yampi, bhikkhave, tathāgato purimaṃ jātiṃ purimaṃ bhavaṃ purimaṃ niketaṃ pubbe manussabhūto samāno na ca visaṭaṃ, na ca visāci na ca visācitaṃ (sī. pī.), na ca visāvi (syā.), na ca pana viceyya pekkhitā, ujuṃ tathā pasaṭamujumano, piyacakkhunā bahujanaṃ udikkhitā ahosi. So tassa kammassa kaṭattā…pe… so tato cuto itthattaṃ āgato samāno imāni dve mahāpurisalakkhaṇāni paṭilabhati. Abhinīlanetto ca hoti gopakhumo ca.

‘‘So tehi lakkhaṇehi samannāgato, sace agāraṃ ajjhāvasati, rājā hoti cakkavattī…pe… rājā samāno kiṃ labhati? Piyadassano hoti bahuno janassa, piyo hoti manāpo brāhmaṇagahapatikānaṃ negamajānapadānaṃ gaṇakamahāmattānaṃ anīkaṭṭhānaṃ dovārikānaṃ amaccānaṃ pārisajjānaṃ rājūnaṃ bhogiyānaṃ kumārānaṃ. Rājā samāno idaṃ labhati…pe… buddho samāno kiṃ labhati? Piyadassano hoti bahuno janassa, piyo hoti manāpo bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ upāsakānaṃ upāsikānaṃ devānaṃ manussānaṃ asurānaṃ nāgānaṃ gandhabbānaṃ. Buddho samāno idaṃ labhati’’. Etamatthaṃ bhagavā avoca.
mula_english:
228.

"And also, monks, the *tathāgata*, in a former birth, a former existence, a former abode, having been formerly a human being, was not deceitful, nor fraudulent, not hypercritical in his observation, but upright, thus straightforward of mind, he looked upon the multitude with loving eyes.
Through the performance of that action… and so on… having passed away from there, and being come to this state, he acquires these two characteristics of a Great Man: he has very blue eyes, and he has eyelashes like a cow's.

"So, being endowed with those characteristics, if he lives in a house, he becomes a wheel-turning monarch… and so on… being a king, what does he gain? He is pleasing to see, he is beloved by many people; he is agreeable to *brāhmaṇas*, householders, townsmen, country people, accountants, high-ranking officials, troops, gatekeepers, ministers, attendants, kings, enjoyers, and princes.
Being a king, he gains this… and so on… being a Buddha, what does he gain? He is pleasing to see, he is beloved by many people; he is agreeable to monks, nuns, male lay followers, female lay followers, gods, humans, *asuras*, *nāgas*, and *gandharvas*.
Being a Buddha, he gains this."
The Blessed One said this.
commentary_pali:
228.Na ca visaṭanti kakkaṭako viya akkhīni nīharitvā na kodhavasena pekkhitā ahosi. Na ca visācīti vaṅkakkhikoṭiyā pekkhitāpi nāhosi. Na ca pana viceyya pekkhitāti viceyya pekkhitā nāma yo kujjhitvā yadā naṃ paro oloketi, tadā nimmīleti na oloketi, puna gacchantaṃ kujjhitvā oloketi, evarūpo nāhosi. ‘‘Vineyyapekkhitā’’tipi pāṭho, ayamevattho. Ujuṃ tathā pasaṭamujumanoti ujumano hutvā uju pekkhitā hoti, yathā ca ujuṃ, tathā pasaṭaṃ vipulaṃ vitthataṃ pekkhitā hoti. Piyadassanoti piyāyamānehi passitabbo.

Idha kammaṃ nāma dīgharattaṃ mahājanassa piyacakkhunā olokanakammaṃ. Kammasarikkhakaṃ nāma kujjhitvā olokento kāṇo viya kākakkhi viya hoti, vaṅkakkhi pana āvilakkhi ca hotiyeva. Pasannacittassa pana olokayato akkhīnaṃ pañcavaṇṇo pasādo paññāyati. Tathāgato ca tathā olokesi. Athassa taṃ dīgharattaṃ piyacakkhunā olokitabhāvaṃ sadevako loko iminā kāraṇena jānātūti imāni nettasampattikarāni dve mahāpurisalakkhaṇāni nibbattanti. Lakkhaṇaṃ nāma idameva lakkhaṇadvayaṃ. Piyadassanatā ānisaṃso. Abhiyoginoti lakkhaṇasatthe yuttā.

kammaṃ Kammasarikkhakaṃ Lakkhaṇaṃ ānisaṃso. Abhiyogino

Uṇhīsasīsalakkhaṇavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
228. *Na ca visaṭā* means that he did not look with eyes popping out like a crab, nor did he look because of anger.

*Na ca visācī* means that he also did not look with the corner of his crooked eye.

*Na ca pana viceyya pekkhitā* means that looking after considering, means that when another person looks at one who is angry, then one closes one's eyes and does not look, and then, being angry, looks at the one who is going away; he was not of such a nature. The reading is also "vineyyapekkhitā," this is the same meaning.

*Ujuṃ tathā pasaṭamujumano* means having a straight mind, he is a straight looker; and just as he is straight, so also he is a broad, extensive, and widespread looker.

*Piyadassano* means one who should be seen by those who are dear.

Here, *kammaṃ* means the act of looking with loving eyes at the great multitude for a long time.

*Kammasarikkhakaṃ* means, while looking angrily, one is like a blind person, like the eye of a crow; however, one with a crooked eye is indeed one with disturbed eyes. But for one looking with a clear mind, a five-colored clarity of the eyes is evident. The Tathāgata looked in that way. In order that the world with the gods might know by this reason that he had looked with loving eyes for a long time, these two great-man characteristics productive of the accomplishment of eyes arise.

*Lakkhaṇaṃ* means just these two characteristics.

Being pleasing to see is the *ānisaṃso*. *Abhiyogino* means those who are engaged in the characteristic-doctrine.

*Kammaṃ*, *kammasarikkhakaṃ*, *lakkhaṇaṃ*, *ānisaṃso*. *Abhiyogino*

Description of the Uṇhīsaśīsa Characteristic

mula_pali:
229. Tatthetaṃ vuccati –

‘‘Na ca visaṭaṃ na ca visāci visācitaṃ (sī. pī.), visāvi (syā.), na ca pana viceyyapekkhitā;

visācitaṃ (sī. pī.), visāvi (syā.)

Ujuṃ tathā pasaṭamujumano, piyacakkhunā bahujanaṃ udikkhitā.

‘‘Sugatīsu so phalavipākaṃ,

Anubhavati tattha modati;

Idha ca pana bhavati gopakhumo,

Abhinīlanettanayano sudassano.

‘‘Abhiyogino ca nipuṇā,

Bahū pana nimittakovidā;

Sukhumanayanakusalā manujā,

Piyadassanoti abhiniddisanti naṃ.

‘‘Piyadassano gihīpi santo ca,

Bhavati bahujanapiyāyito;

Yadi ca na bhavati gihī samaṇo hoti,

Piyo bahūnaṃ sokanāsano’’ti.

(23) Uṇhīsasīsalakkhaṇaṃ

230. ‘‘Yampi, bhikkhave, tathāgato purimaṃ jātiṃ purimaṃ bhavaṃ purimaṃ niketaṃ pubbe manussabhūto samāno bahujanapubbaṅgamo ahosi kusalesu dhammesu bahujanapāmokkho kāyasucarite vacīsucarite manosucarite dānasaṃvibhāge sīlasamādāne uposathupavāse matteyyatāya petteyyatāya sāmaññatāya brahmaññatāya kule jeṭṭhāpacāyitāya aññataraññataresu ca adhikusalesu dhammesu. So tassa kammassa kaṭattā…pe… so tato cuto itthattaṃ āgato samāno imaṃ mahāpurisalakkhaṇaṃ paṭilabhati – uṇhīsasīso hoti.

‘‘So tena lakkhaṇena samannāgato sace agāraṃ ajjhāvasati, rājā hoti cakkavattī…pe… rājā samāno kiṃ labhati? Mahāssa jano anvāyiko hoti, brāhmaṇagahapatikā negamajānapadā gaṇakamahāmattā anīkaṭṭhā dovārikā amaccā pārisajjā rājāno bhogiyā kumārā. Rājā samāno idaṃ labhati… buddho samāno kiṃ labhati? Mahāssa jano anvāyiko hoti, bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo upāsakā upāsikāyo devā manussā asurā nāgā gandhabbā. Buddho samāno idaṃ labhati’’. Etamatthaṃ bhagavā avoca.
mula_english:
230.
"Bhikkhus, since a *Tathāgata* in a former birth, a former existence, a former abode, formerly existing as a human being, was one who went before many people, was preeminent among many people in wholesome qualities, in bodily good conduct, in verbal good conduct, in mental good conduct, in sharing gifts (*dānasaṃvibhāga*), in undertaking precepts (*śīlasamādāna*), in observing the *uposatha*, in maternal affection, in paternal affection, in recluseship, in *brahmaṇya*, in honoring elders in the family, and in other higher wholesome qualities;

through the accomplishment of that action... he, having passed away from there and come to this state, obtains this mark of a great man (*mahāpurisalakkhaṇa*)—he has a head with a protuberance (*uṇhīsasīsa*).

"He, endowed with that mark, if he lives the household life, becomes a king, a wheel-turning monarch (*cakkavattī*)... What does a king gain?
