A great following of people adheres to him: *brāhmaṇa* householders, town and country dwellers, accountants, great ministers, soldiers, gatekeepers, counselors, courtiers, kings, enjoyers, princes.

A king gains this... What does a Buddha gain? A great following of people adheres to him: monks (*bhikkhus*), nuns (*bhikkhunis*), laymen (*upāsakas*), laywomen (*upāsikās*), gods (*devas*), humans (*manussas*), *asuras*, *nāgas*, *gandharvas*.

A Buddha gains this."

The Blessed One (*bhagavā*) said this.
commentary_pali: 230.Bahujanapubbaṅgamo ahosīti bahujanassa pubbaṅgamo ahosi gaṇajeṭṭhako. Tassa diṭṭhānugatiṃ aññe āpajjiṃsu. Idha kammaṃ nāma pubbaṅgamatā. Kammasarikkhakaṃ nāma yo pubbaṅgamo hutvā dānādīni kusalakammāni karoti, so amaṅkubhūto sīsaṃ ukkhipitvā pītipāmojjena paripuṇṇasīso vicarati, mahāpuriso ca hoti. Tathāgato ca tathā akāsi. Athassa sadevako loko iminā kāraṇena idaṃ pubbaṅgamakammaṃ jānātūti uṇhīsasīsalakkhaṇaṃ nibbattati. Lakkhaṇaṃ nāma idameva lakkhaṇaṃ. Mahājanānuvattanatā ānisaṃso.
commentary_english: 230. "He was the *bahujanapubbaṅgamo*," that is, he was the *pubbaṅgamo* of many people, the chief of the group. Others followed his example and path (*diṭṭhānugati*). Here, *kammaṃ* (karma) means leadership (*pubbaṅgamatā*). *Kammasarikkhakaṃ* means that one who, having become a leader (*pubbaṅgamo*), performs meritorious actions such as giving *dānādīni*, that person, without being anxious (*amaṅkubhūto*), raises his head (*sīsaṃ ukkhipitvā*), lives happily (*pītipāmojjena*) with a fulfilled mind (*paripuṇṇasīso vicarati*), and becomes a great being (*mahāpuriso*). The *tathāgata* also did that (*tathā akāsi*). So that the world with its gods (*sadevako loko*) may know this leadership action (*idaṃ pubbaṅgamakammaṃ*) for this reason (*iminā kāraṇena*), the *uṇhīsasīsalakkhaṇaṃ* arises. *Lakkhaṇaṃ* means just this characteristic (*idameva lakkhaṇaṃ*). Following the great multitude (*mahājanānuvattanatā*) is a great benefit (*ānisaṃso*).

mula_pali:
231. Tatthetaṃ vuccati –

‘‘Pubbaṅgamo sucaritesu ahu,

Dhammesu dhammacariyābhirato;

Anvāyiko bahujanassa ahu,

Saggesu vedayittha puññaphalaṃ.

‘‘Veditvā so sucaritassa phalaṃ,

Uṇhīsasīsattamidhajjhagamā;

Byākaṃsu byañjananimittadharā,

Pubbaṅgamo bahujanaṃ hessati.

‘‘Paṭibhogiyā manujesu idha,

Pubbeva tassa abhiharanti tadā;

Yadi khattiyo bhavati bhūmipati,

Paṭihārakaṃ bahujane labhati.

‘‘Atha cepi pabbajati so manujo,

Dhammesu hoti paguṇo visavī;

Tassānusāsaniguṇābhirato,

Anvāyiko bahujano bhavatī’’ti.

(24-25) Ekekalomatāuṇṇālakkhaṇāni
mula_english:
231. Thus, it is said:

"He was foremost in good conduct (sucaritesu),
Devoted to the Dharma, delighting in conduct in accordance with the Dharma (dharmmacariyābhirato);
He was a follower of many people (bahujanassa),
In the heavens (saggesu), he experienced the fruit of merit (puññaphalaṃ)."

"Having experienced the fruit of good conduct (sucaritassa phalaṃ),
He attained the state of having a crown-protuberance (uṇhīsasīsattaṃ) here;
Those who bear the marks of the signs (byañjananimittadharā) declared,
'He will be foremost (pubbaṅgamo) for many people (bahujanaṃ)'."

"Here (idha) among humans (manujesu) those who are worthy of gifts (paṭibhogiyā),
Offer to him then (tadā) even before (pubbeva) his (tassa) arrival (abhiharanti);
If (yadi) he becomes (bhavati) a king (khattiyo), a lord of the earth (bhūmipati),
He obtains (labhati) attendants (paṭihārakaṃ) from many people (bahujane)."

"Then (atha), even if (cepi) that (so) man (manujo) goes forth (pabbajati),
In the doctrines (dhammesu) he is skilled (paguṇo), wise (visavī);
Delighting in the qualities of his (tassa) instruction (anusāsaniguṇābhirato),
He is a follower (anvāyiko), he becomes (bhavati) one of many people (bahujano," thus (iti).

(24-25) The characteristics of having one hair per pore, and the ūrṇā.
commentary_pali:
231.Bahujanaṃhessatīti bahujanassa bhavissati. Paṭibhogiyāti veyyāvaccakarā, etassa bahū veyyāvaccakarā bhavissantīti attho. Abhiharanti tadāti daharakāleyeva tadā evaṃ byākaronti. Paṭihārakanti veyyāvaccakarabhāvaṃ. Visavīti ciṇṇavasī.

Ekekalomatādilakkhaṇavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
[They] will abandon many people, it will be for many people.

Because they are to be partaken of, they are assistants. There will be many assistants for him, this is the meaning.

Because they bring it near at that time, then at that time, in their young age, they declare thus.

Because they are protectors, [it means] the state of being an assistant.

Because it is visavī, it is ciṇṇavasī.

Explanation of the characteristics beginning with one hair per pore.

mula_pali:
232. ‘‘Yampi, bhikkhave, tathāgato purimaṃ jātiṃ purimaṃ bhavaṃ purimaṃ niketaṃ pubbe manussabhūto samāno musāvādaṃ pahāya musāvādā paṭivirato ahosi, saccavādī saccasandho theto paccayiko avisaṃvādako lokassa . So tassa kammassa kaṭattā upacitattā…pe… so tato cuto itthattaṃ āgato samāno imāni dve mahāpurisalakkhaṇāni paṭilabhati. Ekekalomo ca hoti, uṇṇā ca bhamukantare jātā hoti odātā mudutūlasannibhā.

‘‘So tehi lakkhaṇehi samannāgato, sace agāraṃ ajjhāvasati, rājā hoti cakkavattī…pe… rājā samāno kiṃ labhati? Mahāssa jano upavattati, brāhmaṇagahapatikā negamajānapadā gaṇakamahāmattā anīkaṭṭhā dovārikā amaccā pārisajjā rājāno bhogiyā kumārā. Rājā samāno idaṃ labhati… buddho samāno kiṃ labhati? Mahāssa jano upavattati, bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo upāsakā upāsikāyo devā manussā asurā nāgā gandhabbā. Buddho samāno idaṃ labhati’’. Etamatthaṃ bhagavā avoca.
mula_english:
232.
’’Even so, *bhikkhus*, a *tathāgata*, in a former birth, a former existence, a former abode, having previously been a human being, abandoning false speech, refraining from false speech, was a speaker of truth, trustworthy, reliable, dependable, not deceitful to the world.

With that action performed, stored up,… on his being come again to this same human state, he acquires these two characteristics of a Great Man:

He has single hairs in each pore, and between the eyebrows there grows a white *uṇṇā* hair, soft like cotton-down.

’’So endowed with these characteristics, if he lives the household life, he becomes a wheel-turning monarch… A king, what does he acquire? A great populace attends upon him—*brāhmaṇa* householders, townsfolk, countryfolk, accountants, high officials, army officers, gatekeepers, ministers, courtiers, kings, enjoyers, princes.

A king, he acquires this… A buddha, what does he acquire? A great populace attends upon him—*bhikkhus*, *bhikkhuṇīs*, *upāsakas*, *upāsikās*, gods (devas), humans (*manuṣyās*), *asuras*, *nāgas*, *gandharvas*.

A buddha, he acquires this’’.

This is the meaning of what the Blessed One (*bhagavā*) said.
commentary_pali:
232.Upavattatīti ajjhāsayaṃ anuvattati, idha kammaṃ nāma dīgharattaṃ saccakathanaṃ. Kammasarikkhakaṃ nāma dīgharattaṃ advejjhakathāya parisuddhakathāya kathitabhāvamassa sadevako loko iminā kāraṇena jānātūti ekekalomalakkhaṇañca uṇṇālakkhaṇañca nibbattati. Lakkhaṇaṃ nāma idameva lakkhaṇadvayaṃ. Mahājanassa ajjhāsayānukūlena anuvattanatā ānisaṃso. Ekekalomūpacitaṅgavāti ekekehi lomehi upacitasarīro.

Cattālīsādilakkhaṇavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
Upavattatī means adhering to intention; here, *karma* (karman) means speaking the truth for a long time.

*Kammasarikkhakaṃ* means that the world with its deities knows, by this cause, that a state of being spoken about in undefiled and purified speech exists for a long time; thus, the characteristic of having each single hair (ekaikalomalakṣaṇa) and the characteristic of the ūrṇā (ūrṇālakṣaṇa) arise.

*Lakkhaṇaṃ* means just these two characteristics.

*Ānisaṃsa* is the tendency to conform with the favorable intentions of the great multitude.

Eкекаlоmūрасitaṅgavā means one whose body is covered with individual hairs.

Description of the characteristics beginning with the forty.

mula_pali:
233. Tatthetaṃ vuccati –

‘‘Saccappaṭiñño purimāsu jātisu,

Advejjhavāco alikaṃ vivajjayi;

Na so visaṃvādayitāpi kassaci,

Bhūtena tacchena tathena bhāsayi tosayi (sī. pī.).

tosayi (sī. pī.)

‘‘Setā susukkā mudutūlasannibhā,

Uṇṇā sujātā uṇṇāssa jātā (ka. sī.) bhamukantare ahu;

uṇṇāssa jātā (ka. sī.)

Na lomakūpesu duve ajāyisuṃ,

Ekekalomūpacitaṅgavā ahu.

‘‘Taṃ lakkhaṇaññū bahavo samāgatā,

Byākaṃsu uppādanimittakovidā;

Uṇṇā ca lomā ca yathā susaṇṭhitā,

Upavattatī īdisakaṃ bahujjano.

‘‘Gihimpi santaṃ upavattatī jano,

Bahu puratthāpakatena kammunā;

Akiñcanaṃ pabbajitaṃ anuttaraṃ,

Buddhampi santaṃ upavattati jano’’ti.

(26-27) Cattālīsaaviraḷadantalakkhaṇāni
mula_english:
233. Thus, it is said:

“Truthful in promises in former births,
With unwavering speech, he avoided falsehood;
He was not deceptive to anyone,
He spoke with truth, with accuracy, with fact.

“White, very white, like soft cotton,
A well-formed *ūrṇā* arose between his eyebrows;
Not two hairs grew in each hair follicle,
He had a body with one hair per follicle.

“Many experts in লক্ষণs (lakṣaṇas), gathered,
Explained, skilled in the causes of origination;
The *ūrṇā* and hairs, being well-placed,
‘He approaches such a state,’ many people say.

“Even a householder is approached by people,
Due to much meritorious action done in the past;
A mendicant with nothing, unsurpassed,
Even a Buddha is approached by people.”

(26-27) The forty unspaced teeth लक्षणs (lakṣaṇas).

mula_pali:
234. ‘‘Yampi, bhikkhave tathāgato purimaṃ jātiṃ purimaṃ bhavaṃ purimaṃ niketaṃ pubbe manussabhūto samāno pisuṇaṃ vācaṃ pahāya pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato ahosi. Ito sutvā na amutra akkhātā imesaṃ bhedāya, amutra vā sutvā na imesaṃ akkhātā amūsaṃ bhedāya , iti bhinnānaṃ vā sandhātā, sahitānaṃ vā anuppadātā, samaggārāmo samaggarato samagganandī samaggakaraṇiṃ vācaṃ bhāsitā ahosi. So tassa kammassa kaṭattā…pe… so tato cuto itthattaṃ āgato samāno imāni dve mahāpurisalakkhaṇāni paṭilabhati. Cattālīsadanto ca hoti aviraḷadanto ca.

‘‘So tehi lakkhaṇehi samannāgato sace agāraṃ ajjhāvasati, rājā hoti cakkavattī…pe… rājā samāno kiṃ labhati? Abhejjapariso hoti, abhejjāssa honti parisā, brāhmaṇagahapatikā negamajānapadā gaṇakamahāmattā anīkaṭṭhā dovārikā amaccā pārisajjā rājāno bhogiyā kumārā. Rājā samāno idaṃ labhati … buddho samāno kiṃ labhati? Abhejjapariso hoti, abhejjāssa honti parisā, bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo upāsakā upāsikāyo devā manussā asurā nāgā gandhabbā. Buddho samāno idaṃ labhati’’. Etamatthaṃ bhagavā avoca.
mula_english:
234.

"And further, monks, the *tathāgata*, in a former birth, a former existence, a former dwelling, having been previously a human being, abandoning malicious speech, abstained from malicious speech. Having heard something here, he did not repeat it there to the detriment of these people; or having heard something there, he did not repeat it here to the detriment of those people. Thus, he was a reconciler of those who were divided, a promoter of friendships. Rejoicing, delighting, and exulting in concord, he spoke only words that were conducive to concord.

With that action performed... he, having passed away from there, having come again to this same human state, he acquires these two characteristics of a Great Man: He has forty teeth, and his teeth are not widely spaced.

"He, endowed with these characteristics, if he lives the household life, becomes a king, a wheel-turning monarch... What does the king gain? He has an unassailable retinue; his retinues are unassailable: *brāhmaṇa* householders, town and country dwellers, accountants, high officials, troops, gatekeepers, counselors, courtiers, kings, those who enjoy, and princes.

The king gains this... What does the *buddha* gain? He has an unassailable retinue; his retinues are unassailable: monks (*bhikkhu*), nuns (*bhikkhunī*), laymen (*upāsaka*), laywomen (*upāsikā*), gods (*deva*), humans (*manussa*), *asura*s, *nāga*s, and *gandharva*s.

The *buddha* gains this."

This is the meaning of what the Blessed One (*bhagavā*) said.
commentary_pali:
234.Abhejjaparisoti abhinditabbapariso. Idha kammaṃ nāma dīgharattaṃ apisuṇavācāya kathanaṃ. Kammasarikkhakaṃ nāma pisuṇavācassa kira samaggabhāvaṃ bhindanato dantā aparipuṇṇā ceva honti viraḷā ca. Tathāgatassa pana dīgharattaṃ apisuṇavācataṃ sadevako loko iminā kāraṇena jānātūti idaṃ lakkhaṇadvayaṃ nibbattati. Lakkhaṇaṃ nāma idameva lakkhaṇadvayaṃ. Abhejjaparisatā ānisaṃso. Caturo dasāti cattāro dasa cattālīsaṃ.

Pahūtajivhādilakkhaṇavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
234. *Abhejjapariso* means *abhinditabbapariso*.

Here, *kammaṃ* means speaking without malicious intent for a long time.

*Kammasarikkhakaṃ* means that because malicious speech destroys harmony, the teeth become incomplete and sparse.

This two-fold characteristic arises so that the world with its gods may know that the Tathāgata has spoken without malicious intent for a long time.

*Lakkhaṇaṃ* means this very two-fold characteristic.

*Ānisaṃso* is the quality of having an unbreakble assembly. *Caturo dasā* means four tens, forty-four.

Description of the characteristics beginning with the abundant tongue.

mula_pali:
235. Tatthetaṃ vuccati –

‘‘Vebhūtiyaṃ sahitabhedakāriṃ,

Bhedappavaḍḍhanavivādakāriṃ;

Kalahappavaḍḍhanaākiccakāriṃ,

Sahitānaṃ bhedajananiṃ na bhaṇi.

‘‘Avivādavaḍḍhanakariṃ sugiraṃ,

Bhinnānusandhijananiṃ abhaṇi;

Kalahaṃ janassa panudī samaṅgī,

Sahitehi nandati pamodati ca.

‘‘Sugatīsu so phalavipākaṃ,

Anubhavati tattha modati;

Dantā idha honti aviraḷā sahitā,

Caturo dasassa mukhajā susaṇṭhitā.

‘‘Yadi khattiyo bhavati bhūmipati,

Avibhediyāssa parisā bhavati;

Samaṇo ca hoti virajo vimalo,

Parisāssa hoti anugatā acalā’’ti.

(28-29) Pahūtajivhābrahmassaralakkhaṇāni
mula_english:
235. That is said:

"He does not speak of making divisions among those united in harmony,
Causing disputes that increase division;
Causing trouble that increases strife,
Generating discord among those united.

"He speaks well, making for the increase of non-dispute,
He does not speak of generating broken connections;
He removes strife from the people, complete in all parts,
He rejoices and delights with those united.

"He experiences the ripening of the fruit in the happy realms,
He delights there;
Here the teeth are not sparse, [but] united,
Fourteen, born of the face, are well-formed.

"If a noble becomes the lord of the earth (bhūmipati),
His assembly is indivisible;
And the ascetic is without passion, stainless,
His assembly is following and unwavering."

(28-29) Characteristics of having an abundant tongue and a voice like Brahmā.

mula_pali:
236. ‘‘Yampi , bhikkhave, tathāgato purimaṃ jātiṃ purimaṃ bhavaṃ purimaṃ niketaṃ pubbe manussabhūto samāno pharusaṃ vācaṃ pahāya pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato ahosi. Yā sā vācā nelā kaṇṇasukhā pemanīyā hadayaṅgamā porī bahujanakantā bahujanamanāpā, tathārūpiṃ vācaṃ bhāsitā ahosi. So tassa kammassa kaṭattā upacitattā…pe… so tato cuto itthattaṃ āgato samāno imāni dve mahāpurisalakkhaṇāni paṭilabhati. Pahūtajivho ca hoti brahmassaro ca karavīkabhāṇī.

‘‘So tehi lakkhaṇehi samannāgato sace agāraṃ ajjhāvasati, rājā hoti cakkavattī…pe… rājā samāno kiṃ labhati? Ādeyyavāco hoti, ādiyantissa vacanaṃ brāhmaṇagahapatikā negamajānapadā gaṇakamahāmattā anīkaṭṭhā dovārikā amaccā pārisajjā rājāno bhogiyā kumārā. Rājā samāno idaṃ labhati… buddho samāno kiṃ labhati? Ādeyyavāco hoti, ādiyantissa vacanaṃ bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo upāsakā upāsikāyo devā manussā asurā nāgā gandhabbā. Buddho samāno idaṃ labhati’’. Etamatthaṃ bhagavā avoca.
mula_english:
236. "And further, monks, the *tathāgata*, in a former birth, a former existence, a former abode, having previously been a human being, abandoning harsh speech, abstained from harsh speech.

He spoke such words as were gentle, pleasing to the ear, and loveable, as go to the heart, are courteous, desired by many, and agreeable to many.

With that action performed, stored up, … on his being come again to this same human state, he acquires these two characteristics of a Great Man:

He has a large tongue, and he has a divine voice like the call of a *karavika* bird.

"So, endowed with these characteristics, if he lives the household life, he becomes a king, a wheel-turning monarch… What does the king, being the same, obtain? He is one whose word is to be heeded. Brāhmaṇas, householders, town and country folk, accountants, chief ministers, army officers, doorkeepers, counselors, courtiers, kings, princes, and youths heed his word.

The king, being the same, obtains this... What does the Buddha, being the same, obtain? He is one whose word is to be heeded. Monks, nuns, laymen, laywomen, gods, humans, *asuras*, *nāgas*, and *gandharvas* heed his word.

The Buddha, being the same, obtains this."

This is the meaning of what the Blessed One (bhagavā) said.
commentary_pali: 236.Ādeyyavāco hotīti gahetabbavacano hoti. Idha kammaṃ nāma dīgharattaṃ apharusavāditā. Kammasarikkhakaṃ nāma ye pharusavācā honti, te iminā kāraṇena nesaṃ jivhaṃ parivattetvā parivattetvā pharusavācāya kathitabhāvaṃ jano jānātūti baddhajivhā vā honti, gūḷhajivhā vā dvijivhā vā mammanā vā. Ye pana jivhaṃ parivattetvā parivattetvā pharusavācaṃ na vadanti, te baddhajivhā gūḷhajivhā dvijivhā na honti. Mudu nesaṃ jivhā hoti rattakambalavaṇṇā. Tasmā tathāgatassa dīgharattaṃ jivhaṃ parivattetvā pharusāya vācāya akathitabhāvaṃ sadevako loko iminā kāraṇena jānātūti pahūtajivhālakkhaṇaṃ nibbattati. Pharusavācaṃ kathentānañca saddo bhijjati. Te saddabhedaṃ katvā pharusavācāya kathitabhāvaṃ jano jānātūti chinnassarā vā honti bhinnassarā vā kākassarā vā. Ye pana sarabhedakaraṃ pharusavācaṃ na kathenti, tesaṃ saddo madhuro ca hoti pemanīyo. Tasmā tathāgatassa dīgharattaṃ sarabhedakarāya pharusavācāya akathitabhāvaṃ sadevako loko iminā kāraṇena jānātūti brahmassaralakkhaṇaṃ nibbattati. Lakkhaṇaṃ nāma idameva lakkhaṇadvayaṃ. Ādeyyavacanatā ānisaṃso.
commentary_english:
236. "'He is one whose words are worthy of being heeded' means that his words are worth taking to heart."

Here, *karma* means prolonged gentleness in speech.

*Karma*-similarity: Those who have harsh speech, due to this cause, people know that their tongues are twisted and turned to speak harsh speech, therefore they are either tongue-tied (baddhajivhā), or have a hidden tongue (gūḷhajivhā), or a double tongue (dvijivhā), or are stammerers (mammanā).

But those who, twisting and turning their tongues, do not speak harsh speech, are not tongue-tied, do not have a hidden tongue, and do not have a double tongue.

Their tongues are soft and the color of a red blanket (rattakambalavaṇṇā).

Therefore, because the *Tathāgata* has for a long time refrained from speaking harsh words by twisting the tongue, the world with the gods knows this to be the cause, thus the characteristic of having an abundant tongue (pahūtajivhālakkhaṇaṃ) comes into being.

The sound of those who speak harsh speech is broken.

They, having made a split in the sound, people know the state of having spoken harsh speech; they have broken sounds (chinnassarā), split sounds (bhinnassarā), or crow-like sounds (kākassarā).

Those who do not speak harsh speech that causes a split in the sound, their sound is sweet (madhuro) and beloved (pemanīyo).

Therefore, because the *Tathāgata* has for a long time refrained from harsh speech that causes a split in the sound, the world with the gods knows this to be the cause, thus the characteristic of having a Brahma-like voice (brahmassaralakkhaṇaṃ) comes into being.

*Lakṣaṇa* means just these two characteristics.

The advantage (ānisaṃso) is that the words are worth taking to heart (ādeyyavacanatā).

mula_pali:
237. Tatthetaṃ vuccati –

‘‘Akkosabhaṇḍanavihesakāriṃ,

Ubbādhikaṃ ubbādhakaraṃ (syā.) bahujanappamaddanaṃ;

ubbādhakaraṃ (syā.)

Abāḷhaṃ giraṃ so na bhaṇi pharusaṃ,

Madhuraṃ bhaṇi susaṃhitaṃ susahitaṃ (syā.) sakhilaṃ.

susahitaṃ (syā.)

‘‘Manaso piyā hadayagāminiyo,

Vācā so erayati kaṇṇasukhā;

Vācāsuciṇṇaphalamanubhavi,

Saggesu vedayatha vedayati (?) ṭīkā oloketabbā puññaphalaṃ.

vedayati (?) ṭīkā oloketabbā

‘‘Veditvā so sucaritassa phalaṃ,

Brahmassarattamidhamajjhagamā;

Jivhāssa hoti vipulā puthulā,

Ādeyyavākyavacano bhavati.

‘‘Gihinopi ijjhati yathā bhaṇato,

Atha ce pabbajati so manujo;

Ādiyantissa vacanaṃ janatā,

Bahuno bahuṃ subhaṇitaṃ bhaṇato’’ti.

(30) Sīhahanulakkhaṇaṃ
mula_english:
237. Thus is it said:

“One who causes abuse, contention, and injury,
An oppressor, a crusher of many people,
He does not utter rough, unrestrained speech,
He speaks sweetly, well-composed, and amiable.

“Speech that is pleasing to the mind, that goes to the heart,
He sends forth speech that is pleasing to the ear;
Experiencing the fruit of well-practiced speech,
He experiences the fruit of merit in the heavens.

“Having experienced the fruit of good conduct,
He attained the Brahma-like voice here;
His tongue is large and broad,
He becomes one whose words are worthy of acceptance.

“Even a householder succeeds when speaking thus,
And if that man goes forth;
People accept his words,
When speaking well, much by many.”

(30) The characteristic of a lion's jaw.
commentary_pali:
237.Ubbādhikanti akkosayuttattā ābādhakariṃ bahujanappamaddananti bahujanānaṃ pamaddaniṃ abāḷhaṃ giraṃ so na bhaṇi pharusanti ettha akāro parato bhaṇisaddena yojetabbo. Bāḷhanti balavaṃ atipharusaṃ. Bāḷhaṃ giraṃ so na abhaṇīti ayamettha attho. Susaṃhitanti suṭṭhu pemasañhitaṃ. Sakhilanti mudukaṃ. Vācāti vācāyo. Kaṇṇasukhāti kaṇṇasukhāyo. ‘‘Kaṇṇasukha’’ntipi pāṭho, yathā kaṇṇānaṃ sukhaṃ hoti, evaṃ erayatīti attho. Vedayathāti vedayittha. Brahmassarattanti brahmassarataṃ. Bahuno bahunti bahujanassa bahuṃ. ‘‘Bahūnaṃ bahunti’’pi pāṭho, bahujanānaṃ bahunti attho.

Sīhahanulakkhaṇavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
237. "Ubbādhika" means because it is connected with abuse, it causes distress. "Bahujanappamaddana" means the suppression of many people. "Abāḷhaṃ giraṃ so na bhaṇi pharusa" means here, the *akāra* should be connected with the word *bhaṇi* later on.

"Bāḷha" means strong, very harsh.

"Bāḷhaṃ giraṃ so na abhaṇī" this is the meaning here.

"Susaṃhita" means very well connected with love.

"Sakhila" means soft.

"Vācā" means by speech.

"Kaṇṇasukhā" means pleasing to the ear.

"Kaṇṇasukha'ntipi pāṭho, yathā kaṇṇānaṃ sukhaṃ hoti, evaṃ erayatīti attho" means, just as there is pleasure for the ears, so it is in this way.

"Vedayathā" means he made known.

"Brahmassaratta" means Brahmassarataṃ.

"Bahuno bahu" means much to many people.

"Bahūnaṃ bahunti'pi pāṭho, bahujanānaṃ bahunti attho" means much to many people.

Description of the lion's jaw characteristics.

mula_pali:
238. ‘‘Yampi , bhikkhave, tathāgato purimaṃ jātiṃ purimaṃ bhavaṃ purimaṃ niketaṃ pubbe manussabhūto samāno samphappalāpaṃ pahāya samphappalāpā paṭivirato ahosi kālavādī bhūtavādī atthavādī dhammavādī vinayavādī, nidhānavatiṃ vācaṃ bhāsitā ahosi kālena sāpadesaṃ pariyantavatiṃ atthasaṃhitaṃ. So tassa kammassa kaṭattā…pe… so tato cuto itthattaṃ āgato samāno imaṃ mahāpurisalakkhaṇaṃ paṭilabhati, sīhahanu hoti.

‘‘So tena lakkhaṇena samannāgato sace agāraṃ ajjhāvasati, rājā hoti cakkavattī…pe… rājā samāno kiṃ labhati? Appadhaṃsiyo hoti kenaci manussabhūtena paccatthikena paccāmittena. Rājā samāno idaṃ labhati… buddho samāno kiṃ labhati? Appadhaṃsiyo hoti abbhantarehi vā bāhirehi vā paccatthikehi paccāmittehi, rāgena vā dosena vā mohena vā samaṇena vā brāhmaṇena vā devena vā mārena vā brahmunā vā kenaci vā lokasmiṃ. Buddho samāno idaṃ labhati’’. Etamatthaṃ bhagavā avoca.
mula_english:
238.
"O monks, the *tathāgata*, having abandoned frivolous talk in his previous birth, previous existence, previous abode, as a human being, desisted from frivolous talk. He was a speaker of truth, a speaker of reality, a speaker of meaning, a speaker of the *dharma*, a speaker of discipline. His speech was treasured, timely, reasoned, limited, and connected with meaning.

By doing that deed, he... having passed away from there, having come to this state, obtains this mark of a great man, he has a lion's jaw.

"Being endowed with that mark, if he lives in a house, he becomes a king, a wheel-turning monarch... What does a king obtain? He is unassailable by any hostile or inimical human being.

What does a king obtain?… What does a Buddha obtain? He is unassailable by any internal or external hostile or inimical forces, by lust, hatred, or delusion, by any ascetic, *brāhmaṇa*, god, *māra*, or *brahmā* in the world.

A Buddha obtains this."

This is the meaning of what the Blessed One (*bhagavā*) said.
commentary_pali: 238.Appadhaṃsiko hotīti guṇato vā ṭhānato vā padhaṃsetuṃ cāvetuṃ asakkuṇeyyo. Idha kammaṃ nāma palāpakathāya akathanaṃ. Kammasarikkhakaṃ nāma ye taṃ kathenti, te iminā kāraṇena nesaṃ hanukaṃ cāletvā cāletvā palāpakathāya kathitabhāvaṃ jano jānātūti antopaviṭṭhahanukā vā vaṅkahanukā vā pabbhārahanukā vā honti. Tathāgato pana tathā na kathesi. Tenassa hanukaṃ cāletvā cāletvā dīgharattaṃ palāpakathāya akathitabhāvaṃ sadevako loko iminā kāraṇena jānātūti sīhahanulakkhaṇaṃ nibbattati. Lakkhaṇaṃ nāma idameva lakkhaṇaṃ. Appadhaṃsikatā ānisaṃso.
commentary_english:
238. *appadhaṃsiko hotī* means that one is not able to be ruined or removed, whether by qualities or by location.

Here, *kammaṃ* (karman) means not speaking about frivolous matters.

*kammasarikkhakaṃ* means those who speak of that, people know the state of having spoken of frivolous matters by moving their jaws with this reason; they are those whose jaws are set inwards, or whose jaws are crooked, or whose jaws are protruding.

However, the Tathāgata did not speak thus.

Therefore, because the world with the gods knows that he did not speak of frivolous matters for a long time by moving his jaw, the characteristic of a lion's jaw arises.

*lakkhaṇaṃ* (lakṣaṇa) means this very characteristic.

*appadhaṃsikatā ānisaṃso* (anuśaṃsa).

mula_pali:
239. Tatthetaṃ vuccati –

‘‘Na samphappalāpaṃ na muddhataṃ buddhatanti (ka.),

buddhatanti (ka.)

Avikiṇṇavacanabyappatho ahosi;

Ahitamapi ca apanudi,

Hitamapi ca bahujanasukhañca abhaṇi.

‘‘Taṃ katvā ito cuto divamupapajji,

Sukataphalavipākamanubhosi;

Caviya punaridhāgato samāno,

Dvidugamavaratarahanuttamalattha.

‘‘Rājā hoti suduppadhaṃsiyo,

Manujindo manujādhipati mahānubhāvo;

Tidivapuravarasamo bhavati,

Suravarataroriva indo.

‘‘Gandhabbāsurayakkharakkhasebhi surasakkarakkhasebhi (syā.),

surasakkarakkhasebhi (syā.)

Surehi na hi bhavati suppadhaṃsiyo;

Tathatto yadi bhavati tathāvidho,

Idha disā ca paṭidisā ca vidisā cā’’ti.

(31-32) Samadantasusukkadāṭhālakkhaṇāni
mula_english:
239. It is said thus:

"Not frivolous talk, not foolishness,
His speech was articulate and unscattered;
He warded off what was harmful,
And spoke what was beneficial and brought happiness to many.

Having done that, having passed away from here, he went to heaven,
He experienced the ripening of meritorious deeds;
Having passed away and being reborn here again,
He attained a twofold, excellent, superior, and unsurpassed state.

The king is very difficult to overcome,
The lord of men, the ruler of men, is of great power;
He is like the excellent city of the three heavens,
Like Indra among the best of the gods.

By gandharvas, asuras, yakṣas, and rākṣasas,
He is not easily overcome by the gods;
If he is truthful and of such a kind,
Here [are] the directions, the intermediate directions, and the subdivisions of the directions."

(31-32) The characteristics of having even teeth and very white canine teeth.
commentary_pali:
239.Avikiṇṇavacanabyappatho cāti avikiṇṇavacanānaṃ viya purimabodhisattānaṃ vacanapatho assāti avikiṇṇavacanabyappatho. Dvidugamavaratarahanuttamalatthāti dvīhi dvīhi gacchatīti dvidugamo, dvīhi dvīhīti catūhi, catuppadānaṃ varatarassa sīhasseva hanubhāvaṃ alatthāti attho. Manujādhipatīti manujānaṃ adhipati. Tathattoti tathasabhāvo.

Samadantādilakkhaṇavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
Avikiṇṇavacanabyappatho cāti: Avikiṇṇavacanānaṃ viya purimabodhisattānaṃ vacanapatho assāti avikiṇṇavacanabyappatho.

Dvidugamavaratarahanuttamalatthāti: Dvīhi dvīhi gacchatīti dvidugamo, dvīhi dvīhīti catūhi, catuppadānaṃ varatarassa sīhasseva hanubhāvaṃ alatthāti attho.

Manujādhipatīti: Manujānaṃ adhipati.

Tathattoti: Tathasabhāvo.

Samadantādilakkhaṇavaṇṇanā

mula_pali:
240. ‘‘Yampi, bhikkhave, tathāgato purimaṃ jātiṃ purimaṃ bhavaṃ purimaṃ niketaṃ pubbe manussabhūto samāno micchājīvaṃ pahāya sammāājīvena jīvikaṃ kappesi, tulākūṭa kaṃsakūṭa mānakūṭa ukkoṭana vañcana nikati sāciyoga chedana vadha bandhana viparāmosa ālopa sahasākārā sāhasākārā (sī. syā. pī.) paṭivirato ahosi. So tassa kammassa kaṭattā upacitattā ussannattā vipulattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati. So tattha aññe deve dasahi ṭhānehi adhigaṇhāti dibbena āyunā dibbena vaṇṇena dibbena sukhena dibbena yasena dibbena ādhipateyyena dibbehi rūpehi dibbehi saddehi dibbehi gandhehi dibbehi rasehi dibbehi phoṭṭhabbehi. So tato cuto itthattaṃ āgato samāno imāni dve mahāpurisalakkhaṇāni paṭilabhati, samadanto ca hoti susukkadāṭho ca.

‘‘So tehi lakkhaṇehi samannāgato sace agāraṃ ajjhāvasati, rājā hoti cakkavattī dhammiko dhammarājā cāturanto vijitāvī janapadatthāvariyappatto sattaratanasamannāgato. Tassimāni satta ratanāni bhavanti, seyyathidaṃ – cakkaratanaṃ hatthiratanaṃ assaratanaṃ maṇiratanaṃ itthiratanaṃ gahapatiratanaṃ pariṇāyakaratanameva sattamaṃ. Parosahassaṃ kho panassa puttā bhavanti sūrā vīraṅgarūpā parasenappamaddanā. So imaṃ pathaviṃ sāgarapariyantaṃ akhilamanimittamakaṇṭakaṃ iddhaṃ phītaṃ khemaṃ sivaṃ nirabbudaṃ adaṇḍena asatthena dhammena abhivijiya ajjhāvasati. Rājā samāno kiṃ labhati? Suciparivāro hoti sucissa honti parivārā brāhmaṇagahapatikā negamajānapadā gaṇakamahāmattā anīkaṭṭhā dovārikā amaccā pārisajjā rājāno bhogiyā kumārā. Rājā samāno idaṃ labhati.

‘‘Sace kho pana agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajati, arahaṃ hoti sammāsambuddho loke vivaṭṭacchado. Buddho samāno kiṃ labhati? Suciparivāro hoti, sucissa honti parivārā, bhikkhū bhikkhuniyo upāsakā upāsikāyo devā manussā asurā nāgā gandhabbā. Buddho samāno idaṃ labhati’’. Etamatthaṃ bhagavā avoca.
mula_english:
240. "And also, monks, the *tathāgata*, having been previously a human being, abandoning wrong livelihood, maintained his life with right livelihood, abstaining from false balances, false metal, false measures, bribery, deception, fraud, cutting off limbs, killing, imprisonment, robbery, plunder, and violent actions.

By the effect of that action, accumulated, increased, and grown great, at the breaking up of the body after death, he is reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. There, he surpasses the other gods in ten respects: in divine lifespan, in divine beauty, in divine happiness, in divine fame, in divine sovereignty, in divine forms, in divine sounds, in divine smells, in divine tastes, and in divine touches.

Having passed away from there and come to this state, he obtains these two marks of a great man (*mahāpurisa*): he has even teeth, and his teeth are very white.

"Endowed with these characteristics, if he lives the household life, he becomes a king, a wheel-turning monarch (*cakravartin*), a righteous king who rules according to Dharma, a conqueror of the four quarters, who has attained stability in his country, possessed of the seven treasures. These seven treasures are his: the wheel treasure (*cakraratna*), the elephant treasure (*hatthiratna*), the horse treasure (*assaratna*), the jewel treasure (*maṇiratna*), the woman treasure (*itthiratna*), the steward treasure (*gahapatiratna*), and the counselor treasure (*pariṇāyakaratana*) as the seventh. He has more than a thousand sons who are heroes, of heroic stature, conquerors of the hostile army. He conquers and rules this earth to its ocean borders, without violence or weapons, but by Dharma, a land that is unhindered, without misfortune, safe, secure, and free from trouble. What does a king obtain when he is a king? He has a pure retinue; brahmins and householders, townsfolk and countryfolk, accountants and high officials, troops, door-keepers, ministers, courtiers, tributary kings, and princes have a pure retinue. This is what a king obtains when he is a king.

"But if he goes forth from the household life into homelessness, he becomes an *arhat*, a fully enlightened Buddha (*sammāsambuddha*), one who draws back the veil from the world. What does a Buddha obtain when he is a Buddha? He has a pure retinue; monks (*bhikkhus*), nuns (*bhikkhunis*), laymen (*upāsakas*), laywomen (*upāsikās*), gods (*devas*), humans (*manussas*), *asuras*, *nāgas*, and *gandharvas* have a pure retinue. This is what a Buddha obtains when he is a Buddha."

This is the meaning of what the Blessed One (*bhagavā*) said.
commentary_pali: 240.Suciparivāroti parisuddhaparivāro. Idha kammaṃ nāma sammājīvatā. Kammasarikkhakaṃ nāma yo visamena saṃkiliṭṭhājīvena jīvitaṃ kappeti, tassa dantāpi visamā honti dāṭhāpi kiliṭṭhā. Tathāgatassa pana samena suddhājīvena jīvitaṃ kappitabhāvaṃ sadevako loko iminā kāraṇena jānātūti samadantalakkhaṇañca susukkadāṭhālakkhaṇañca nibbattati. Lakkhaṇaṃ nāma idameva lakkhaṇadvayaṃ. Suciparivāratā ānisaṃso.
commentary_english:
240. *suciparivāro* means *parisuddhaparivāro*.

Here, *kammaṃ* means right livelihood (*sammājīvatā*).

*kammasarikkhakaṃ* means, whoever maintains a livelihood with a corrupt and impure way of life (*visamena saṃkiliṭṭhājīvena jīvitaṃ kappeti*), their teeth become uneven (*visamā honti*) and their fangs impure (*dāṭhāpi kiliṭṭhā*).

Furthermore, because the *tathāgata*'s life is one of purity and righteousness (*samena suddhājīvena jīvitaṃ kappitabhāvaṃ*), the world with its gods knows this, thus resulting in even teeth and very white fangs (*samadantalakkhaṇañca susukkadāṭhālakkhaṇañca nibbattati*).

*lakkhaṇaṃ* means these two characteristics (*lakkhaṇadvayaṃ*).

*suciparivāratā* is a benefit (*ānisaṃso*).

mula_pali:
241. Tatthetaṃ vuccati –

‘‘Micchājīvañca avassaji samena vuttiṃ,

Sucinā so janayittha dhammikena;

Ahitamapi ca apanudi,

Hitamapi ca bahujanasukhañca acari.

‘‘Sagge vedayati naro sukhapphalāni,

Karitvā nipuṇebhi vidūhi sabbhi;

Vaṇṇitāni tidivapuravarasamo,

Abhiramati ratikhiḍḍāsamaṅgī.

‘‘Laddhānaṃ mānusakaṃ bhavaṃ tato,

Cavitvāna sukataphalavipākaṃ;

Sesakena paṭilabhati lapanajaṃ,

Samamapi sucisusukkaṃ laddhāna manussakaṃ bhavaṃ tato caviya, puna sukataphalavipākasesakena; paṭilabhati lapanajaṃ samamapi, suci ca suvisuddhasusukkaṃ (syā.).

laddhāna manussakaṃ bhavaṃ tato caviya, puna sukataphalavipākasesakena; paṭilabhati lapanajaṃ samamapi, suci ca suvisuddhasusukkaṃ (syā.)

‘‘Taṃ veyyañjanikā samāgatā bahavo,

Byākaṃsu nipuṇasammatā manujā;

Sucijanaparivāragaṇo bhavati,

Dijasamasukkasucisobhanadanto.

‘‘Rañño hoti bahujano,

Suciparivāro mahatiṃ mahiṃ anusāsato;

Pasayha na ca janapadatudanaṃ,

Hitamapi ca bahujanasukhañca caranti.

‘‘Atha ce pabbajati bhavati vipāpo,

Samaṇo samitarajo vivaṭṭacchado;

Vigatadarathakilamatho,

Imamapi ca paramapi ca imampi ca parampi ca (pī.), paraṃpi paramaṃpi ca (syā.) passati lokaṃ.

imampi ca parampi ca (pī.), paraṃpi paramaṃpi ca (syā.)

‘‘Tassovādakarā bahugihī ca pabbajitā ca,

Asuciṃ garahitaṃ dhunanti pāpaṃ;

Sa hi sucibhi parivuto bhavati,

Malakhilakalikilese panudehī’’ti tassovādakarā bahugihī ca, pabbajitā ca asucivigarahita; panudipāpassa hi sucibhiparivuto, bhavati malakhilakakilese panudeti (syā.).

tassovādakarā bahugihī ca, pabbajitā ca asucivigarahita; panudipāpassa hi sucibhiparivuto, bhavati malakhilakakilese panudeti (syā.)

Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Lakkhaṇasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ sattamaṃ.
mula_english:
241. So, that is said:

"Abandoning wrong livelihood and a blameless way of life,
He engendered purity through righteous means;
And he warded off what was harmful,
And practiced what was beneficial and brought happiness to many.

"In heaven, a man experiences pleasant fruits,
Having performed skillful deeds with knowledgeable companions;
He is praised as equal to the best celestial abodes,
He delights, endowed with pleasure, sport, and amusement.

"Having obtained a human existence from there,
Having passed away due to the ripening of wholesome deeds;
Through the remainder, he obtains speech-born qualities,
And even purity, utmost purity, and supreme purity.

"Those skilled in prognostication, assembled in large numbers,
Declared [him] to be one who is discerning and agreeable to the wise;
He becomes one whose retinue is of pure people,
His teeth are even, supremely white, pure, and beautiful.

"He is a king with many subjects,
Surrounded by pure followers, ruling the great earth;
Forcibly, and without causing distress to the people,
He acts in ways that are beneficial and bring happiness to many.

"And if he goes forth, he becomes free from evil,
An ascetic, calmed of passion, with his veil removed;
Devoid of anxiety, weariness, and fatigue,
He sees this world and the world beyond.

"Householders and renunciates, who act according to his advice,
Shake off impure, blameworthy evil;
He is surrounded by the pure,
Drive away the defilements of malice, stinginess, and torment!"

This the Blessed One said.
Elated, those monks delighted in the Blessed One’s statement.

The Lakkhaṇa-sutta, the seventh, is finished.
commentary_pali:
241.Avassajīti pahāsi tidivapuravarasamoti tidivapuravarena sakkena samo. Lapanajanti mukhajaṃ, dantanti attho. Dijasamasukkasucisobhanadantoti dve vāre jātattā dijanāmakā sukkā suci sobhanā ca dantā assāti dijasamasukkasucisobhanadanto. Na ca janapadatudananti yo tassa cakkavāḷaparicchinno janapado, tassa aññena tudanaṃ pīḷā vā ābādho vā natthi. Hitamapi ca bahujana sukhañca carantīti bahujanā samānasukhadukkhā hutvā tasmiṃ janapade aññamaññassa hitañceva sukhañca caranti. Vipāpoti vigatapāpo. Vigatadarathakilamathoti vigatakāyikadarathakilamatho. Malakhilakalikilese panudehīti rāgādimalānañceva rāgādikhilānañca dosakalīnañca sabbakilesānañca apanudehi. Sesaṃ sabbattha uttānatthamevāti.

Sumaṅgalavilāsiniyā dīghanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Lakkhaṇasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
241. "Avassajīti"…
Pahāsi, "tidivapuravarasamo" means equal to Sakka by the excellence of the heavenly city.
"Lapanaja" means born of the mouth, the meaning is teeth.
"Dijasamasukkasucisobhanadanto" means because the teeth are born twice, they are called dija, they are white, pure and beautiful, therefore dijasamasukkasucisobhanadanto.
"Na ca janapadatudana" means, that inhabited country which is bounded by the world-circle, in it there is no oppression, suffering or affliction from another.
"Hitamapi ca bahujana sukhañca carantī" means, many people, being alike in happiness and suffering, live in that country practicing benefit and happiness towards each other.
"Vipāpo" means vigatapāpo (one who is without evil).
"Vigatadarathakilamatho" means vigatakāyikadarathakilamatho (one who is without bodily anguish and fatigue).
"Malakhilakalikilese panudehī" means remove the impurities beginning with desire, remove the defects beginning with desire, remove the strife of faults, remove all defilements.
The rest is clear throughout.

The Lakkhaṇasuttavaṇṇanā is finished in the Sumaṅgalavilāsinī, commentary on the Dīghanikāya.

mula_pali: 242. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tena kho pana samayena siṅgālako sigālako (sī.) gahapatiputto kālasseva uṭṭhāya rājagahā nikkhamitvā allavattho allakeso pañjaliko puthudisā puthuddisā (sī. syā. pī.) namassati – puratthimaṃ disaṃ dakkhiṇaṃ disaṃ pacchimaṃ disaṃ uttaraṃ disaṃ heṭṭhimaṃ disaṃ uparimaṃ disaṃ.
mula_english:
Thus have I heard. Once the Blessed One was staying at Rājagaha, at the Squirrels’ Feeding Place in the Bamboo Grove.

At that time a young householder named Siṅgālaka arose early and set out from Rājagaha with freshly washed clothes and hair. With palms together held up in reverence, he was paying respect towards the six directions: that is east (*purastimaṃ diśaṃ*), south (*dakṣiṇaṃ diśaṃ*), west (*paścimaṃ diśaṃ*), north (*uttaraṃ diśaṃ*), lower (*heṭṭhimaṃ diśaṃ*) and upper (*uparimaṃ diśaṃ*).
commentary_pali:
242.Evaṃme sutanti siṅgālasuttaṃ. Tatrāyamanuttānapadavaṇṇanā – veḷuvane kalandakanivāpeti veḷuvananti tassa uyyānassa nāmaṃ. Taṃ kira veḷūhi parikkhittaṃ ahosi aṭṭhārasahatthena ca pākārena gopuraṭṭālakayuttaṃ nīlobhāsaṃ manoramaṃ, tena veḷuvananti vuccati. Kalandakānañcettha nivāpaṃ adaṃsu, tena kalandakanivāpoti vuccati.

Pubbe kira aññataro rājā tattha uyyānakīḷanatthaṃ āgato surāmadena matto divā niddaṃ okkami. Parijanopissa ‘‘sutto rājā’’ti pupphaphalādīhi palobhiyamāno ito cito ca pakkāmi. Atha surāgandhena aññatarasmā susirarukkhā kaṇhasappo nikkhamitvā rañño abhimukho āgacchati, taṃ disvā rukkhadevatā ‘‘rañño jīvitaṃ dammī’’ti kāḷakavesena āgantvā kaṇṇamūle saddamakāsi. Rājā paṭibujjhi. Kaṇhasappo nivatto. So taṃ disvā ‘‘imāya kāḷakāya mama jīvitaṃ dinna’’nti kāḷakānaṃ tattha nivāpaṃ paṭṭhapesi, abhayaghosañca ghosāpesi. Tasmā taṃ tato pabhuti ‘‘kalandakanivāpo’’ti saṅkhyaṃ gataṃ. Kalandakāti hi kāḷakānaṃ etaṃ nāmaṃ.

Kalandakā

Tena kho pana samayenāti yasmiṃ samaye bhagavā rājagahaṃ gocaragāmaṃ katvā veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe viharati, tena samayena. Siṅgālako gahapatiputtoti siṅgālakoti tassa nāmaṃ. Gahapatiputtoti gahapatissa putto gahapatiputto. Tassa kira pitā gahapatimahāsālo, nidahitvā ṭhapitā cassa gehe cattālīsa dhanakoṭiyo atthi. So bhagavati niṭṭhaṅgato upāsako sotāpanno, bhariyāpissa sotāpannāyeva. Putto panassa assaddho appasanno. Atha naṃ mātāpitaro abhikkhaṇaṃ evaṃ ovadanti – ‘‘tāta satthāraṃ upasaṅkama, dhammasenāpatiṃ mahāmoggallānaṃ mahākassapaṃ asītimahāsāvake upasaṅkamā’’ti. So evamāha – ‘‘natthi mama tumhākaṃ samaṇānaṃ upasaṅkamanakiccaṃ, samaṇānaṃ santikaṃ gantvā vanditabbaṃ hoti, onamitvā vandantassa piṭṭhi rujjati, jāṇukāni kharāni honti, bhūmiyaṃ nisīditabbaṃ hoti, tattha nisinnassa vatthāni kilissanti jīranti, samīpe nisinnakālato paṭṭhāya kathāsallāpo hoti, tasmiṃ sati vissāso uppajjati, tato nimantetvā cīvarapiṇḍapātādīni dātabbāni honti. Evaṃ sante attho parihāyati, natthi mayhaṃ tumhākaṃ samaṇānaṃ upasaṅkamanakicca’’nti. Iti naṃ yāvajīvaṃ ovadantāpi mātāpitaro sāsane upanetuṃ nāsakkhiṃsu.

Tena kho pana samayenā Siṅgālako gahapatiputto Gahapatiputto

Athassa pitā maraṇamañce nipanno ‘‘mama puttassa ovādaṃ dātuṃ vaṭṭatī’’ti cintetvā puna cintesi – ‘‘disā tāta namassāhī’’ti evamassa ovādaṃ dassāmi, so atthaṃ ajānanto disā namassissati, atha naṃ satthā vā sāvakā vā passitvā ‘‘kiṃ karosī’’ti pucchissanti. Tato ‘‘mayhaṃ pitā disā namassanaṃ karohīti maṃ ovadī’’ti vakkhati. Athassa te ‘‘na tuyhaṃ pitā etā disā namassāpeti, imā pana disā namassāpetī’’ti dhammaṃ desessanti. So buddhasāsane guṇaṃ ñatvā ‘‘puññakammaṃ karissatī’’ti. Atha naṃ āmantāpetvā ‘‘tāta, pātova uṭṭhāya cha disā namasseyyāsī’’ti āha. Maraṇamañce nipannassa kathā nāma yāvajīvaṃ anussaraṇīyā hoti. Tasmā so gahapatiputto taṃ pituvacanaṃ anussaranto tathā akāsi. Tasmā ‘‘kālasseva uṭṭhāya rājagahā nikkhamitvā’’tiādi vuttaṃ.
commentary_english:
242. Thus have I heard.

This is the explanation of the words that are not plain: *veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe*, "in the Bamboo Grove, at the Kalandaka feeding ground." *Veḷuvana* means the name of that park.

It was enclosed by bamboos, delightful to behold with a wall of eighteen *hatthas*, complete with a gateway and watchtower, and gleaming with blue. Therefore, it is called *Veḷuvana*.

There, they gave food to the *kalandakas*; therefore, it is called *Kalandakanivāpa*.

Once upon a time, a king came there to play in the park, and, drunk with liquor, fell asleep during the day.

His attendants, thinking, "The king is asleep," went away here and there, enticed by flowers and fruits, and so on.

Then, drawn by the smell of liquor, a black snake came out of a hollow tree and approached the king. Seeing this, the tree deity, thinking, "I will give the king life," came in the guise of a crow and made a sound in his ear.

The king awoke.

The black snake retreated.

Seeing it, he thought, "This crow gave me life." Therefore, he established a feeding ground there for crows, and proclaimed an assurance of safety.

Therefore, from that time on, it was called *Kalandakanivāpa*.

*Kalandaka* is a name for crows.

*kalandakā*.

"At that time," means at the time when the Blessed One, having made Rājagṛha his alms-gathering village, was dwelling in the Bamboo Grove, at the Kalandaka feeding ground.

"*Siṅgālako gahapatiputto*" means Siṅgālaka was his name.

"*Gahapatiputto*" means the son of the householder is the *gahapatiputto*.

His father was a very wealthy householder. Forty *dhanakoṭis* were deposited and stored in his house.

He was a lay follower who had gone for refuge to the Blessed One, a stream-enterer; his wife too was a stream-enterer.

But his son was faithless and displeased.

Then his mother and father constantly advised him thus: "Dear son, go to the Teacher, go to the general of the Dhamma, Mahāmoggallāna, go to Mahākassapa, [go] to the eighty great disciples."

He said thus: "I have no business going to your ascetics. Having gone to the presence of the ascetics, one must pay homage. As one bows down, one's back breaks, one's knees become stiff, one must sit on the ground.

Having sat there, one's clothes get soiled and worn out. From the time of sitting nearby onward, there is conversation and discussion. When that is the case, trust arises; then, having invited them, robes, alms-food, and so on must be given.

When that is the case, wealth declines. I have no business going to your ascetics."

Thus, though his mother and father advised him for as long as he lived, they were not able to bring him to the Teaching.

Then, when his father was lying on his deathbed, he thought, "It is fitting to give an instruction to my son." Thinking again, he decided: "I will give him this instruction: 'Dear son, worship the directions!'" Not understanding the meaning, he will worship the directions. Then the Teacher or a disciple will see him and ask, "What are you doing?"

Then he will say, "My father instructed me, 'Worship the directions!'"

Then they will teach him the Dhamma, saying, "Your father does not command you to worship these directions, but he commands you to worship *these* directions."

Having known the good qualities in the Buddha's teaching, he will do meritorious deeds.

Then, having summoned him, he said, "Dear son, having gotten up early in the morning, you should worship the six directions."

A word from one lying on one's deathbed is indeed something to be remembered for as long as life lasts.

Therefore, that householder's son, remembering that word of his father, did so.

Therefore, it was said, "Having gotten up early in the morning, having gone out from Rājagṛha," and so on.
[p.]

mula_pali:
243. Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya rājagahaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi. Addasā kho bhagavā siṅgālakaṃ gahapatiputtaṃ kālasseva vuṭṭhāya rājagahā nikkhamitvā allavatthaṃ allakesaṃ pañjalikaṃ puthudisā namassantaṃ – puratthimaṃ disaṃ dakkhiṇaṃ disaṃ pacchimaṃ disaṃ uttaraṃ disaṃ heṭṭhimaṃ disaṃ uparimaṃ disaṃ. Disvā siṅgālakaṃ gahapatiputtaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘kiṃ nu kho tvaṃ, gahapatiputta, kālasseva uṭṭhāya rājagahā nikkhamitvā allavattho allakeso pañjaliko puthudisā namassasi – puratthimaṃ disaṃ dakkhiṇaṃ disaṃ pacchimaṃ disaṃ uttaraṃ disaṃ heṭṭhimaṃ disaṃ uparimaṃ disa’’nti? ‘‘Pitā maṃ, bhante, kālaṃ karonto evaṃ avaca – ‘disā, tāta, namasseyyāsī’ti. So kho ahaṃ, bhante, pituvacanaṃ sakkaronto garuṃ karonto mānento pūjento kālasseva uṭṭhāya rājagahā nikkhamitvā allavattho allakeso pañjaliko puthudisā namassāmi – puratthimaṃ disaṃ dakkhiṇaṃ disaṃ pacchimaṃ disaṃ uttaraṃ disaṃ heṭṭhimaṃ disaṃ uparimaṃ disa’’nti.

Cha disā
mula_english:
Then, when it was morning, the Blessed One, having dressed, took his bowl and robe and entered Rājagaha for alms.

The Blessed One saw Sigālaka, a householder's son, who had risen early and left Rājagaha, with wet clothes and wet hair, paying homage to the different directions with his palms together—the east direction, the south direction, the west direction, the north direction, the lower direction, and the upper direction.

Seeing Sigālaka, the householder's son, the Blessed One said to him: "Young householder, why do you, having risen early and left Rājagaha, with wet clothes and wet hair, pay homage to the different directions with your palms together—the east direction, the south direction, the west direction, the north direction, the lower direction, and the upper direction?"

"Venerable Sir, my father, when he was about to die, told me: 'Dear son, you should pay homage to the directions.' And so, venerable sir, honoring, respecting, esteeming, and venerating my father's words, I rise early and leave Rājagaha, with wet clothes and wet hair, paying homage to the different directions with my palms together—the east direction, the south direction, the west direction, the north direction, the lower direction, and the upper direction."

The Six Directions ( *cha disā*)
commentary_pali:
243.Puthudisāti bahudisā. Idāni tā dassento puratthimaṃ disantiādimāha. Pāvisīti na tāva paviṭṭho, pavisissāmīti nikkhantattā pana antarāmagge vattamānopi evaṃ vuccati. Addasā kho bhagavāti na idāneva addasa, paccūsasamayepi buddhacakkhunā lokaṃ volokento etaṃ disā namassamānaṃ disvā ‘‘ajja ahaṃ siṅgālassa gahapatiputtassa gihivinayaṃ siṅgālasuttantaṃ kathessāmi, mahājanassa sā kathā saphalā bhavissati, gantabbaṃ mayā etthā’’ti. Tasmā pātova nikkhamitvā rājagahaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi, pavisanto ca naṃ tatheva addasa. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘addasā kho bhagavā’’ti. Etadavocāti so kira avidūre ṭhitampi satthāraṃ na passati, disāyeva namassati. Athaṃ naṃ bhagavā sūriyarasmisamphassena vikasamānaṃ mahāpadumaṃ viya mukhaṃ vivaritvā ‘‘kiṃ nu kho tvaṃ, gahapatiputtā’’tiādikaṃ etadavoca.

Chadisādivaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
243. *Puthudisā* means *bahudisā.*

Now, showing that, he says, "*Puratthimaṃ disa,* etc."

*Pāvisī* means he has not yet entered, but because of having left, even while proceeding on the intermediate path, it is said thus.

"*Addasā kho Bhagavā*," he did not see just now, even at dawn, with his Buddha-eye, looking at the world, having seen him bowing to this direction, "[Today] I will explain the *Siṅgālasuttanta*, the discipline for householders, to Siṅgāla, the householder's son. That talk will be fruitful for the great mass of people. I must go there."

Therefore, having left early in the morning, he entered Rājagaha for alms, and while entering, he saw him just like that.

Therefore it was said – "*Addasā kho Bhagavā*."

"*Etadavocā*" means he does not see the Teacher even though he is standing not far away, he bows to the direction itself.

Then the Blessed One, having opened his mouth like a great lotus blossoming with the touch of the sun's rays, said to him, "*Kiṃ nu kho tvaṃ, gahapatiputtā*, etc."

Explanation of *chadisādi.*

mula_pali:
244. ‘‘Na kho, gahapatiputta, ariyassa vinaye evaṃ cha disā chaddisā (sī. pī.) namassitabbā’’ti. ‘‘Yathā kathaṃ pana, bhante, ariyassa vinaye cha disā chaddisā (sī. pī.) namassitabbā? Sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā tathā dhammaṃ desetu, yathā ariyassa vinaye cha disā chaddisā (sī. pī.) namassitabbā’’ti.

‘‘Tena hi, gahapatiputta suṇohi sādhukaṃ manasikarohi bhāsissāmī’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho siṅgālako gahapatiputto bhagavato paccassosi. Bhagavā etadavoca –

‘‘Yato kho, gahapatiputta, ariyasāvakassa cattāro kammakilesā pahīnā honti, catūhi ca ṭhānehi pāpakammaṃ na karoti, cha ca bhogānaṃ apāyamukhāni na sevati, so evaṃ cuddasa pāpakāpagato chaddisāpaṭicchādī paṭicchādī hoti (syā.) ubholokavijayāya paṭipanno hoti. Tassa ayañceva loko āraddho hoti paro ca loko. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati.

paṭicchādī hoti (syā.)

Cattārokammakilesā
mula_english:
244. “Young householder, that is not how the six directions (*ṣaḍdiśa*, Sī., Pī.) should be worshipped according to the discipline (*vinaya*) of the noble ones (*ārya*).”

“Then how, dear sir (*bhante*), should the six directions (*ṣaḍdiśa*, Sī., Pī.) be worshipped according to the discipline (*vinaya*) of the noble ones (*ārya*)? It would be good if the Blessed One (*bhagavān*) would teach me the *dharma* in such a way that the six directions (*ṣaḍdiśa*, Sī., Pī.) are [properly] worshipped according to the discipline (*vinaya*) of the noble ones (*ārya*).”

“Very well, young man, listen and pay careful attention; I will speak.”

“Yes, dear sir (*bhante*),” replied Siṅgālaka, the householder's son, to the Blessed One (*bhagavat*).

The Blessed One (*bhagavān*) said this:

“Young man, when a noble disciple (*ariyasāvaka*) has abandoned the four defilements of action (*cattāro kammakilesā*), does not commit evil deeds from four causes, and does not pursue the six ways of wasting wealth, then, having avoided these fourteen evil ways, that noble disciple (*ariyasāvaka*) covers the six directions and has embarked on the path to conquer both worlds (*ubholoka*). For him, this world is secured, and the next world (*para loka*) as well. At the dissolution of the body (*kāyassa bhedā*), after death (*maraṇā*), he attains a good destiny (*sugati*), even a heavenly world (*saggaṃ lokaṃ*).

The Four Defilements of Action (*cattārokammakilesā*)
commentary_pali: 244.Yathākathaṃ pana, bhanteti so kira taṃ bhagavato vacanaṃ sutvāva cintesi ‘‘yā kira mama pitarā cha disā namassitabbā’’ti vuttā, na kira tā etā, aññā kira ariyasāvakena cha disā namassitabbā. Handāhaṃ ariyasāvakena namassitabbā disāyeva pucchitvā namassāmīti. So tā pucchanto yathā kathaṃ pana, bhantetiādimāha. Tattha yathāti nipātamattaṃ. Kathaṃ panāti idameva pucchāpadaṃ. Kammakilesāti tehi kammehi sattā kilissanti, tasmā kammakilesāti vuccanti. Ṭhānehīti kāraṇehi. Apāyamukhānīti vināsamukhāni. Soti so sotāpanno ariyasāvako. Cuddasa pāpakāpagatoti etehi cuddasahi pāpakehi lāmakehi apagato. Chaddisāpaṭicchādīti cha disā paṭicchādento. Ubholokavijayāyāti ubhinnaṃ idhalokaparalokānaṃ vijinanatthāya. Ayañceva loko āraddho hotīti evarūpassa hi idha loke pañca verāni na honti, tenassa ayañceva loko āraddho hoti paritosito ceva nipphādito ca. Paralokepi pañca verāni na honti, tenassa paro ca loko ārādhito hoti. Tasmā so kāyassa bhedā parammaraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati.
commentary_english:
244. *yathā*.
*kathaṃ pana, bhante* means: So, having heard that statement of the Blessed One, he thought, "Indeed, what my father said, 'The six directions should be worshipped,' are not these. The six directions should be worshipped by an noble disciple."

“Now, I will ask about the directions that should be worshipped by an noble disciple and then worship them.”

So, when asking about this, he said, "*yathā kathaṃ pana, bhante*, etc."

There, *yathā* is merely a particle.

*kathaṃ panā* is simply an interrogative phrase.

*kammakilesā* means: Beings are defiled by these actions, therefore they are called defilements of action. (karma).

*ṭhānehī* means: by reasons.

*apāyamukhānī* means: the entrances to ruin.

*so* means: that stream-enterer, the noble disciple (*āryasrāvaka*).

*cuddasa pāpakāpagato* means: he is devoid of these fourteen evil and base things.

*chaddisāpaṭicchādī* means: one who covers the six directions.

*ubholokavijayāyā* means: for the sake of conquering both, this world and the next.

*ayañceva loko āraddho hotī* means: for one of such a nature, there are no five forms of hatred in this world; therefore, this world is well begun, satisfied, and accomplished for him.

There are no five forms of hatred in the next world either; therefore, the next world is well cultivated for him.

Therefore, at the dissolution of the body, after death, he is reborn in a happy destination, even in the heavenly world ( *sugatiṃ svargaṃ lokam upapajjati* ).

mula_pali:
245. ‘‘Katamassa cattāro kammakilesā pahīnā honti? Pāṇātipāto kho, gahapatiputta, kammakileso, adinnādānaṃ kammakileso, kāmesumicchācāro kammakileso, musāvādo kammakileso. Imassa cattāro kammakilesā pahīnā hontī’’ti. Idamavoca bhagavā, idaṃ vatvāna idaṃ vatvā (sī. pī.) evamīdisesu ṭhānesu sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā –

‘‘Pāṇātipāto adinnādānaṃ, musāvādo ca vuccati;

Paradāragamanañceva, nappasaṃsanti paṇḍitā’’ti.

Catuṭṭhānaṃ
mula_english:
245.
"What four defilements of action (kammakilesā) are abandoned? Killing living beings (prāṇātipāta), householder's son, is a defilement of action, taking what is not given (adinnādāna) is a defilement of action, misconduct in sexual pleasures (kāmesumicchācāra) is a defilement of action, lying (musāvāda) is a defilement of action.

These four defilements of action are abandoned."
This the Blessed One (bhagavā) said. Having said this, the Well-Gone (sugato), the Teacher (satthā) then said further:

"Killing living beings (prāṇātipāto), taking what is not given (adinnādāna), and lying (musāvādo) are declared;

sensual misconduct with another's spouse (paradāragamanañceva) is not praised by the wise (paṇḍitā)."

Four bases (catuṭṭhānaṃ).
commentary_pali:
245. Iti bhagavā saṅkhepena mātikaṃ ṭhapetvā idāni tameva vitthārento katamassa cattāro kammakilesātiādimāha. Kammakilesoti kammañca taṃ kilesasampayuttattā kileso cāti kammakileso. Sakilesoyeva hi pāṇaṃ hanati, nikkileso na hanati, tasmā pāṇātipāto ‘‘kammakileso’’ti vutto. Adinnādānādīsupi eseva nayo. Athāparanti aparampi etadatthaparidīpakameva gāthābandhaṃ avocāti attho.

Catuṭhānādivaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
245. Thus, the Blessed One, having established the summary (mātikā) in brief, now expanding on that very thing, said, beginning with, "What are the four defilements of action (kammakilesā)?"

*Kammakileso* means action (kamma) and defilement (kilesa), since it is associated with defilements; therefore, it is a defilement of action (kammakileso).

Indeed, one kills a living being with defilement, not without defilement; therefore, taking life (pāṇātipāto) is called "defilement of action" (*kammakileso*).

The same method (naya) applies to taking what is not given (adinnādāna), and so forth (*adinnādānādīsu*).

*Athāparaṃ* means "Furthermore (aparaṃ)," he spoke another verse (gāthābandhaṃ) that illuminates this meaning (etadatthaparidīpakameva), that is the meaning (attho).

Description of the four bases (catuṭhānādivaṇṇanā)

mula_pali:
246. ‘‘Katamehi catūhi ṭhānehi pāpakammaṃ na karoti? Chandāgatiṃ gacchanto pāpakammaṃ karoti, dosāgatiṃ gacchanto pāpakammaṃ karoti, mohāgatiṃ gacchanto pāpakammaṃ karoti, bhayāgatiṃ gacchanto pāpakammaṃ karoti. Yato kho, gahapatiputta, ariyasāvako neva chandāgatiṃ gacchati, na dosāgatiṃ gacchati, na mohāgatiṃ gacchati, na bhayāgatiṃ gacchati; imehi catūhi ṭhānehi pāpakammaṃ na karotī’’ti. Idamavoca bhagavā, idaṃ vatvāna sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā –

‘‘Chandā dosā bhayā mohā, yo dhammaṃ ativattati;

Nihīyati yaso tassa tassa yeso (bahūsu, vinayepi), kāḷapakkheva candimā.

tassa yeso (bahūsu, vinayepi)

‘‘Chandā dosā bhayā mohā, yo dhammaṃ nātivattati;

Āpūrati yaso tassa tassa yeso (bahūsu, vinayepi), sukkapakkheva juṇhapakkheva (ka.) candimā’’ti.

tassa yeso (bahūsu, vinayepi) juṇhapakkheva (ka.)

Cha apāyamukhāni
mula_english:
246. Which are the four ways in which one does not commit evil deeds? Going astray through desire (*chandāgati*), one commits evil deeds; going astray through hatred (*dosāgati*), one commits evil deeds; going astray through delusion (*mohāgati*), one commits evil deeds; going astray through fear (*bhayāgati*), one commits evil deeds.

But, young man, when a noble disciple (*ariyasāvaka*) does not go astray through desire, does not go astray through hatred, does not go astray through delusion, does not go astray through fear, in these four ways, he does not commit evil deeds.

The Blessed One said this. Having spoken thus, the Well-Gone (*sugata*), the Teacher (*satthā*) then said further:

“Desire (*chandā*), hatred (*dosā*), fear (*bhayā*), delusion (*mohā*): whoever transgresses the Dharma (*dhamma*),

his glory wanes, like the moon in the dark fortnight."

Desire, hatred, fear, delusion: whoever does not transgress the Dharma,

his glory is increased, like the moon in the bright fortnight."

Six causes of ruin (*apāyamukhāni*).
commentary_pali:
246.Pāpakammaṃkarotīti idaṃ bhagavā yasmā kārake dassite akārako pākaṭo hoti, tasmā ‘‘pāpakammaṃ na karotī’’ti mātikaṃ ṭhapetvāpi desanākusalatāya paṭhamataraṃ kārakaṃ dassento āha . Tattha chandāgatiṃ gacchantoti chandena pemena agatiṃ gacchanto akattabbaṃ karonto. Parapadesupi eseva nayo. Tattha yo ‘‘ayaṃ me mitto vā sambhatto vā sandiṭṭho vā ñātako vā lañjaṃ vā pana me detī’’ti chandavasena assāmikaṃ sāmikaṃ karoti, ayaṃ chandāgatiṃ gacchanto pāpakammaṃ karoti nāma. Yo ‘‘ayaṃ me verī’’ti pakativeravasena taṅkhaṇuppannakodhavasena vā sāmikaṃ assāmikaṃ karoti, ayaṃ dosāgatiṃ gacchanto pāpakammaṃ karoti nāma. Yo pana mandattā momūhattā yaṃ vā taṃ vā vatvā assāmikaṃ sāmikaṃ karoti, ayaṃ mohāgatiṃ gacchanto pāpakammaṃ karoti nāma. Yo pana ‘‘ayaṃ rājavallabho vā visamanissito vā anatthampi me kareyyā’’ti bhīto assāmikaṃ sāmikaṃ karoti, ayaṃ bhayāgatiṃ gacchanto pāpakammaṃ karoti nāma. Yo pana yaṃkiñci bhājento ‘‘ayaṃ me sandiṭṭho vā sambhatto vā’’ti pemavasena atirekaṃ deti, ‘‘ayaṃ me verī’’ti dosavasena ūnakaṃ deti, momūhattā dinnādinnaṃ ajānamāno kassaci ūnaṃ kassaci adhikaṃ deti, ‘‘ayaṃ imasmiṃ adiyyamāne mayhaṃ anatthampi kareyyā’’ti bhīto kassaci atirekaṃ deti, so catubbidhopi yathānukkamena chandāgatiādīni gacchanto pāpakammaṃ karoti nāma.

Ariyasāvako pana jīvitakkhayaṃ pāpuṇantopi chandāgatiādīni na gacchati. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘imehi catūhi ṭhānehi pāpakammaṃ na karotī’’ti.

Nihīyati yaso tassāti tassa agatigāmino kittiyasopi parivārayasopi nihīyati parihāyati.

Nihīyati yaso tassā

Chaapāyamukhādivaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
246. *Pāpakammaṃ karotī* (he does an evil action): Because when the agent is shown, the non-agent becomes clear, therefore the Blessed One, after establishing the topic "he does not do an evil action," showing the agent first, said, out of skill in teaching.

There, *chandāgatiṃ gacchanto* (while taking a wrong course of action because of partiality): going the wrong course of action due to desire and affection, doing what should not be done.

And so with the other three wrong courses of action.

There, "This is my friend, my acquaintance, my companion, or my relative, or he is giving me a bribe," thus, because of partiality, he treats one who is not the owner as the owner; this one, while taking a wrong course of action because of partiality (*chandāgatiṃ gacchanto*), does an evil action (*pāpakammaṃ karoti*) indeed.

"This is my enemy," thus, because of natural hostility or because of an access of anger arisen in that moment, he treats one who is the owner as one who is not the owner; this one, while taking a wrong course of action because of hatred (*dosāgatiṃ gacchanto*), does an evil action (*pāpakammaṃ karoti*) indeed.

Furthermore, out of dullness or out of delusion, saying this or that, he treats one who is not the owner as the owner; this one, while taking a wrong course of action because of delusion (*mohāgatiṃ gacchanto*), does an evil action (*pāpakammaṃ karoti*) indeed.

Furthermore, fearing that "This is either a king's favourite or one who is entrenched in wrongdoing, he could even harm me," he treats one who is not the owner as the owner; this one, while taking a wrong course of action because of fear (*bhayāgatiṃ gacchanto*), does an evil action (*pāpakammaṃ karoti*) indeed.

Furthermore, while distributing something, "This is my acquaintance or my companion," thus, out of affection, he gives more; "This is my enemy," thus, out of hatred, he gives less; out of delusion, not knowing what is given and what is not given, he gives less to someone and more to someone else; fearing that "If this is not given to him, he could even harm me," he gives more to someone; this one, in all these four ways, following these wrong courses of action such as partiality, does an evil action (*pāpakammaṃ karoti*) indeed.

But a noble disciple (*ariyasāvako*), even reaching the destruction of life, does not take these wrong courses of action such as partiality.

Therefore it was said: "By these four conditions, he does not do an evil action (*pāpakammaṃ*)."

*Nihīyati yaso tassā* (his glory fades): his fame and his retinue, of one who goes the wrong course of action, decline and diminish.

*Nihīyati yaso tassā* (his glory fades)—description of the gates to the bad realms.

mula_pali:
247. ‘‘Katamāni cha bhogānaṃ apāyamukhāni na sevati? Surāmerayamajjappamādaṭṭhānānuyogo kho, gahapatiputta, bhogānaṃ apāyamukhaṃ, vikālavisikhācariyānuyogo bhogānaṃ apāyamukhaṃ, samajjābhicaraṇaṃ bhogānaṃ apāyamukhaṃ, jūtappamādaṭṭhānānuyogo bhogānaṃ apāyamukhaṃ, pāpamittānuyogo bhogānaṃ apāyamukhaṃ, ālasyānuyogo ālasānuyogo (sī. syā. pī.) bhogānaṃ apāyamukhaṃ.

Surāmerayassa cha ādīnavā
mula_english:
“And what six ways of squandering wealth (*bhogānaṃ apāyamukhāni*) are to be avoided? Indulgence in intoxicants and sloth, O householder's son (*gahapatiputta*), is a way of wasting one's substance (*bhogānaṃ apāyamukhaṃ*); strolling in the streets at unseasonable hours is a way of wasting one's substance; frequenting fairs is a way of wasting one's substance; indulgence in gambling is a way of wasting one's substance; association with evil companions is a way of wasting one's substance; and addiction to idleness (*ālasyānuyogo*) is a way of wasting one's substance.

The dangers of intoxicants and sloth.
commentary_pali:
247.Surāmerayamajjappamādaṭṭhānānuyogoti ettha surāti piṭṭhasurā pūvasurā odanasurā kiṇṇapakkhittā sambhārasaṃyuttāti pañca surā. Merayanti pupphāsavo phalāsavo madhvāsavo guḷāsavo sambhārasaṃyuttoti pañca āsavā. Taṃ sabbampi madakaraṇavasena majjaṃ. Pamādaṭṭhānanti pamādakāraṇaṃ. Yāya cetanāya taṃ majjaṃ pivati, tassa etaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Anuyogoti tassa surāmerayamajjappamādaṭṭhānassa anuanuyogo punappunaṃ karaṇaṃ. Yasmā panetaṃ anuyuttassa uppannā ceva bhogā parihāyanti, anuppannā ca nuppajjanti, tasmā ‘‘bhogānaṃ apāyamukha’’nti vuttaṃ. Vikālavisikhācariyānuyogoti avelāya visikhāsu cariyānuyuttatā.

Samajjābhicaraṇanti naccādidassanavasena samajjāgamanaṃ. Ālasyānuyogoti kāyālasiyatāya yuttappayuttatā.

Samajjābhicaraṇa Ālasyānuyogo

Surāmerayassa chaādīnavādivaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
247. surāmerayamajjappamādaṭṭhānānuyogo: Here, *surā* refers to *piṭṭhasurā*, *pūvasurā*, *odanasurā*, *kiṇṇapakkhittā*, and *sambhārasaṃyuttā*, these five are *surā*. meraya: *pupphāsavo*, *phalāsavo*, *madhvāsavo*, *guḷāsavo*, and *sambhārasaṃyutto*, these five are *āsavā*. All of that, due to causing intoxication, is majjaṃ. pamādaṭṭhāna means the cause of negligence (*pamādakāraṇaṃ*). That which one drinks, that *majjaṃ* with whatever intention (*cetanā*), that is its designation (*adhivacanaṃ*). anuyogo means repeatedly doing (*punappunaṃ karaṇaṃ*) that which pertains to *surāmerayamajjappamādaṭṭhānassa*. Because for one engaged in this, existing enjoyments ( *bhogā*) decline (*parihāyanti*), and non-existing ones do not arise (*nuppajjanti*), therefore it is said, "the gateway to the ruin of enjoyments (*bhogānaṃ apāyamukha*)". vikālavisikhācariyānuyogo means being engaged in wandering (*cariyānuyuttatā*) on the streets (*visikhāsu*) at an improper time (*avelāya*).

samajjābhicaraṇa means going to a festival (*samajjāgamanaṃ*) through seeing dance etc. (*naccādidassanavasena*). ālasyānuyogo means being associated with bodily laziness (*kāyālasiyatāya yuttappayuttatā*).

samajjābhicaraṇa ālasyānuyogo

Description of the faults etc. of *surāmerayassa*

mula_pali:
248. ‘‘Cha khome, gahapatiputta, ādīnavā surāmerayamajjappamādaṭṭhānānuyoge. Sandiṭṭhikā dhanajāni dhanañjāni (sī. pī.), kalahappavaḍḍhanī, rogānaṃ āyatanaṃ, akittisañjananī, kopīnanidaṃsanī , paññāya dubbalikaraṇītveva chaṭṭhaṃ padaṃ bhavati. Ime kho, gahapatiputta, cha ādīnavā surāmerayamajjappamādaṭṭhānānuyoge.

Vikālacariyāya cha ādīnavā
mula_english:
“These are the six dangers, householder, in addiction to intoxicants, liquor and sloth-producing drugs: visible loss of wealth, a source of quarreling, a breeding-ground of diseases, a cause of ill-repute, an indecent exposure, and weakening of intellect. These are the six dangers, householder, in addiction to intoxicants, liquor and sloth-producing drugs."

Six dangers of going around at unseemly hours.
commentary_pali: 248. Evaṃ channaṃ apāyamukhānaṃ mātikaṃ ṭhapetvā idāni tāni vibhajanto cha kho me, gahapatiputta ādīnavātiādimāha. Tattha sandiṭṭhikāti sāmaṃ passitabbā, idhalokabhāvinī. Dhanajānīti dhanahāni. Kalahappavaḍḍhanīti vācākalahassa ceva hatthaparāmāsādikāyakalahassa ca vaḍḍhanī. Rogānaṃ āyatananti tesaṃ tesaṃ akkhirogādīnaṃ khettaṃ. Akittisañjananīti suraṃ pivitvā hi mātarampi paharanti pitarampi, aññaṃ bahumpi avattabbaṃ vadanti, akattabbaṃ karonti. Tena garahampi daṇḍampi hatthapādādichedampi pāpuṇanti, idhalokepi paralokepi akittiṃ pāpuṇanti, iti tesaṃ sā surā akittisañjananī nāma hoti. Kopīnanidaṃsanīti guyhaṭṭhānañhi vivariyamānaṃ hiriṃ kopeti vināseti, tasmā ‘‘kopīna’’nti vuccati, surāmadamattā ca taṃ taṃ aṅgaṃ vivaritvā vicaranti, tena nesaṃ sā surā kopīnassa nidaṃsanato ‘‘kopīnanidaṃsanī’’ti vuccati. Paññāya dubbalikaraṇīti sāgatattherassa viya kammassakatapaññaṃ dubbalaṃ karoti, tasmā ‘‘paññāya dubbalikaraṇī’’ti vuccati. Maggapaññaṃ pana dubbalaṃ kātuṃ na sakkoti. Adhigatamaggānañhi sā antomukhameva na pavisati. Chaṭṭhaṃ padanti chaṭṭhaṃ kāraṇaṃ.
commentary_english:
248. Thus, having established the matrix of the six gateways to loss and now differentiating them, he said, "There are six dangers for me, son of the householder," and so on.

There, *sandiṭṭhikā* means visible in itself, pertaining to this world.

*dhanajānī* means loss of wealth (*dhanahāni*).

*kalahappavaḍḍhanī* means increase or quarrels (*vācākalahassa ceva hatthaparāmāsādikāyakalahassa ca vaḍḍhanī*): increase of verbal quarrels and bodily quarrels, with hand contact.

*rogānaṃ āyatana* means the site (*khettaṃ*) of those various diseases (*tesaṃ tesaṃ akkhirogādīnaṃ*), such as eye diseases and so on.

*akittisañjananī* means: having drunk liquor (*suraṃ pivitvā*), one hits both one’s mother (*mātarampi*) and one’s father (*pitarampi*), one says much not to be said (*aññaṃ bahumpi avattabbaṃ vadanti*), and one does much not to he done (*akattabbaṃ karonti*). Therefore, while incurring blame (*garahampi*), punishment (*daṇḍampi*), and mutilation of hands, feet, and other limbs (*hatthapādādichedampi*), they incur disrepute (*akittiṃ pāpuṇanti*) both in this world (*idhalokepi*) and in the other world (*paralokepi*). Therefore, that liquor is said to involve a “production of disrepute” (*akittisañjananī nāma hoti*) for them.

*kopīnanidaṃsanī* means: though they are parts of the body to be concealed (*guyhaṭṭhānaṃ*), when uncovered (*vivariyamānaṃ*), they disturb, i.e., eliminate, decency (*hiriṃ kopeti vināseti*); therefore, they are called “private parts” (*kopīna*). Indeed, men inebriated by liquor (*surāmadamattā*) walk with their member uncovered (*taṃ taṃ aṅgaṃ vivaritvā vicaranti*). Therefore, for them that liquor, in that it exposes their private parts (*kopīnassa nidaṃsanato*), is said to be causing the “exposure of the private parts” (*kopīnanidaṃsanī*).

*paññāya dubbalikaraṇī* means it makes weak the wisdom consisting of one’s own actions (*kammassakatapaññaṃ dubbalaṃ karoti*), like that of the Elder Sāgata (*sāgatattherassa viya*); therefore, it is called “causing the weakening of wisdom” (*paññāya dubbalikaraṇī*).

But it is not able to make weak the wisdom of the path (*maggapaññaṃ pana dubbalaṃ kātuṃ na sakkoti*).

Indeed, it does not enter solely into the interior (*antomukhameva na pavisati*) of those who have attained the paths (*adhigatamaggānaṃ*).

*chaṭṭhaṃ pada* means the sixth cause (*chaṭṭhaṃ kāraṇaṃ*).

mula_pali:
249. ‘‘Cha khome, gahapatiputta, ādīnavā vikālavisikhācariyānuyoge. Attāpissa agutto arakkhito hoti, puttadāropissa agutto arakkhito hoti, sāpateyyaṃpissa aguttaṃ arakkhitaṃ hoti, saṅkiyo ca hoti pāpakesu ṭhānesu tesu tesu ṭhānesu (syā.), abhūtavacanañca tasmiṃ rūhati, bahūnañca dukkhadhammānaṃ purakkhato hoti. Ime kho, gahapatiputta, cha ādīnavā vikālavisikhācariyānuyoge.

Samajjābhicaraṇassa cha ādīnavā
mula_english:
“There are these six dangers, householder, attached to haunting the streets at unfitting times.

oneself is defenceless and without protection, and so are one’s wife and children, and so is one’s property; one is suspected of crimes, and false reports are pinned on one, and one encounters all sorts of unpleasantness.

These are the six dangers, householder, attached to haunting the streets at unfitting times.

The six dangers of attending festivals:
commentary_pali: 249.Attāpissa agutto arakkhito hotīti avelāya caranto hi khāṇukaṇṭakādīnipi akkamati, ahināpi yakkhādīhipi samāgacchati, taṃ taṃ ṭhānaṃ gacchatīti ñatvā verinopi naṃ nilīyitvā gaṇhanti vā hananti vā. Evaṃ attāpissa agutto hoti arakkhito. Puttadārāpi ‘‘amhākaṃ pitā amhākaṃ sāmi rattiṃ vicarati, kimaṅgaṃ pana maya’’nti itissa puttadhītaropi bhariyāpi bahi patthanaṃ katvā rattiṃ carantā anayabyasanaṃ pāpuṇanti. Evaṃ puttadāropissa agutto arakkhito hoti. Sāpateyyanti tassa puttadāraparijanassa rattiṃ caraṇakabhāvaṃ ñatvā corā suññaṃ gehaṃ pavisitvā yaṃ icchanti, taṃ haranti. Evaṃ sāpateyyampissa aguttaṃ arakkhitaṃ hoti. Saṅkiyo ca hotīti aññehi katapāpakammesupi ‘‘iminā kataṃ bhavissatī’’ti saṅkitabbo hoti. Yassa yassa gharadvārena yāti, tattha yaṃ aññena corakammaṃ paradārikakammaṃ vā kataṃ, taṃ ‘‘iminā kata’’nti vutte abhūtaṃ asantampi tasmiṃ rūhati patiṭṭhāti. Bahūnañca dukkhadhammānanti ettakaṃ dukkhaṃ, ettakaṃ domanassanti vattuṃ na sakkā, aññasmiṃ puggale asati sabbaṃ vikālacārimhi āharitabbaṃ hoti, iti so bahūnaṃ dukkhadhammānaṃ purakkhato puregāmī hoti.
commentary_english:
“His body is unguarded, unprotected” means: while walking at the wrong time, he treads upon stumps, thorns, and the like (khāṇukaṇṭakādīni), and he comes across a snake or an ogre and the like. And his enemies, knowing that he is going to such-and-such place, rob him or kill him in an ambush.

In this sense, “his body is unguarded, unprotected”.

Also his children and wife think, "Our father, our lord, wanders at night, what then of us?" Therefore, his sons and daughters, and also his wife, make an assignation outside and, wandering at night, they meet with misfortune and disaster.

In this sense, “also his children and wife are unguarded, unprotected”.

“His property” means: knowing that his children, wife, and attendants are in the habit of wandering at night, thieves enter his empty house and take whatever they desire.

In this sense, “also his property is unguarded, unprotected”.

“He is suspected” means: he may be suspected even of evil actions done by others, for the people will say “He must have done it.”

If he crosses anybody’s threshold, and there someone else has committed theft (corakammaṃ) or adultery (paradārikakammaṃ), “He has done it,” they say, and albeit “false”, i.e., untrue, this rumour “grows”, is attached, to him.

“And many painful experiences” means: it is not possible to state the specific amount of suffering (dukkhaṃ) and the specific amount of sorrow (domanassaṃ). Lacking another man, all that must be related to one who wanders at unseemly hours.’ In this sense, “he faces, he confronts, many painful experiences”.

mula_pali:
250. ‘‘Cha khome, gahapatiputta, ādīnavā samajjābhicaraṇe. Kva kuvaṃ (ka. sī. pī.) naccaṃ, kva gītaṃ, kva vāditaṃ, kva akkhānaṃ, kva pāṇissaraṃ, kva kumbhathunanti. Ime kho, gahapatiputta, cha ādīnavā samajjābhicaraṇe.

Jūtappamādassa cha ādīnavā
mula_english:
“These are the six dangers, householder's son, inherent in habitual partying:

One is always thinking: “Where is there dancing? Where’ is there singing? Where are they playing music? Where are they reciting? Where is there hand-clapping? Where are the drums?”

‘There are these six dangers attached to frequenting fairs:

The six dangers of gambling.
commentary_pali: 250.Kvanaccanti ‘‘kasmiṃ ṭhāne naṭanāṭakādinaccaṃ atthī’’ti pucchitvā yasmiṃ gāme vā nigame vā taṃ atthi, tattha gantabbaṃ hoti, tassa ‘‘sve naccadassanaṃ gamissāmī’’ti ajja vatthagandhamālādīni paṭiyādentasseva sakaladivasampi kammacchedo hoti, naccadassanena ekāhampi dvīhampi tīhampi tattheva hoti, atha vuṭṭhisampattiyādīni labhitvāpi vappādikāle vappādīni akarontassa anuppannā bhogā nuppajjanti, tassa bahi gatabhāvaṃ ñatvā anārakkhe gehe corā yaṃ icchanti, taṃ karonti, tenassa uppannāpi bhogā vinassanti. Kva gītantiādīsupi eseva nayo. Tesaṃ nānākaraṇaṃ brahmajāle vuttameva.
commentary_english:
250. “Where is there dancing (nacca)?” means: having asked, "In what place (kasmiṃ ṭhāne) is there dancing (nacca) by dancers, actors, etc. (naṭanāṭakādi)?" and wherever there is that in a village (grāme) or town (nigame), one has to go there (tattha gantabbaṃ hoti). Thinking, "Tomorrow (sve) I am going to a dancing performance (naccadassanaṃ gamissāmī)," today (ajja) itself, he stops working (kammacchedo hoti) all day just to prepare his clothes, garlands, perfumes, etc. (vatthagandhamālādīni paṭiyādentasseva sakaladivasampi). He spends one day (ekāhampi), two days (dvīhampi), or three days (tīhampi) there itself at the dancing performance. Then, although he obtains abundant rains and other favorable conditions (vuṭṭhisampattiyādīni labhitvāpi), the wealth (bhogā) yet to be produced (anuppannā) is not produced (nuppajjanti), because he does not cultivate at the time for cultivating (vappādikāle vappādīni akarontassa). Knowing that he has gone out (tassa bahi gatabhāvaṃ ñatvā), in the unprotected house (anārakkhe gehe), thieves (corā) do what they want (yaṃ icchanti, taṃ karonti), and thus, his wealth (bhogā), even that which has already arisen (uppannāpi), is ruined (vinassanti).

The same exegesis (eseva nayo) applies to the following sentences, starting with “where is there singing (kva gīta)?”.

Their variations (tesaṃ nānākaraṇaṃ) have already been explained (vuttameva) in the *Brahmajāla*.

mula_pali:
251. ‘‘Cha khome, gahapatiputta, ādīnavā jūtappamādaṭṭhānānuyoge. Jayaṃ veraṃ pasavati, jino vittamanusocati, sandiṭṭhikā dhanajāni, sabhāgatassa sabhāye tassa (ka.) vacanaṃ na rūhati, mittāmaccānaṃ paribhūto hoti, āvāhavivāhakānaṃ apatthito hoti – ‘akkhadhutto ayaṃ purisapuggalo nālaṃ dārabharaṇāyā’ti. Ime kho, gahapatiputta, cha ādīnavā jūtappamādaṭṭhānānuyoge.

Pāpamittatāya cha ādīnavā
mula_english:
251. “These are the six dangers inherent in compulsive gambling, householder: winning breeds resentment; the loser mourns lost property; savings are lost; one’s word carries no weight in a public forum; friends and colleagues display their contempt; and one is not sought after for marriage, since a gambler cannot adequately support a family.

These, householder, are the six dangers inherent in compulsive gambling.

Six dangers of evil friendship.
commentary_pali:
251.Jayaṃ veranti ‘‘jitaṃ mayā’’ti parisamajjhe parassa sāṭakaṃ vā veṭhanaṃ vā gaṇhāti, so ‘‘parisamajjhe me avamānaṃ karosi, hotu, sikkhāpessāmi na’’nti tattha veraṃ bandhati, evaṃ jinanto sayaṃ veraṃ pasavati. Jinoti aññena jito samāno yaṃ tena tassa veṭhanaṃ vā sāṭako vā aññaṃ vā pana hiraññasuvaṇṇādivittaṃ gahitaṃ, taṃ anusocati ‘‘ahosi vata me, taṃ taṃ vata me natthī’’ti tappaccayā socati. Evaṃ so jino vittaṃ anusocati. Sabhāgatassa vacanaṃ na rūhatīti vinicchayaṭṭhāne sakkhipuṭṭhassa sato vacanaṃ na rūhati, na patiṭṭhāti, ‘‘ayaṃ akkhasoṇḍo jūtakaro, mā tassa vacanaṃ gaṇhitthā’’ti vattāro bhavanti. Mittāmaccānaṃparibhūto hotīti tañhi mitāmaccā evaṃ vadanti – ‘‘samma, tvampi nāma kulaputto jūtakaro chinnabhinnako hutvā vicarasi, na te idaṃ jātigottānaṃ anurūpaṃ, ito paṭṭhāya mā evaṃ kareyyāsī’’ti. So evaṃ vuttopi tesaṃ vacanaṃ na karoti. Tato tena saddhiṃ ekato na tiṭṭhanti na nisīdanti. Tassa kāraṇā sakkhipuṭṭhāpi na kathenti. Evaṃ mittāmaccānaṃ paribhūto hoti.
