Āvāhavivāhakānanti āvāhakā nāma ye tassa gharato dārikaṃ gahetukāmā. Vivāhakā nāma ye tassa gehe dārikaṃ dātukāmā. Apatthito hotīti anicchito hoti. Nālaṃ dārabharaṇāyāti dārabharaṇāya na samattho. Etassa gehe dārikā dinnāpi etassa gehato āgatāpi amhehi eva positabbā bhavissatiyeva.

Āvāhavivāhakāna Apatthito hotī Nālaṃ dārabharaṇāyā

Pāpamittatāya chaādīnavādivaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
251. When one says, "I have won ( jayaṃ )!", in the midst of the assembly, one grabs the cloak ( *sāṭakaṃ* ) or turban ( *veṭhanaṃ* ) of another. The latter, in the midst of the assembly, says: “You are disrespecting me. Very well, I will teach you a lesson (sikkhāpessāmi )!” Thus, one harbors ( *bandhati* ) hatred ( *veraṃ* ). Thus, if one wins ( *jinanto* ), one begets ( *pasavati* ) hatred ( *veraṃ* ) oneself.

“If one loses ( *jino* )” means: being defeated by another, one mourns for whatever was taken by him, be it his turban ( *veṭhanaṃ* ), cloak ( *sāṭako* ), or any other wealth such as gold ( *hirañña* ), silver ( *suvaṇṇa* ), and so on ( *ādī* ). One laments: “Alas! I had it ( *ahosi vata me* )! Alas! I don’t have it ( *natthī* )!” Therefore ( *tappaccayā* ), one grieves ( *socati* ).

Thus, if one loses ( *jino* ), one mourns ( *anusocati* ) for one’s wealth ( *vittaṃ* ).

“When one is in an assembly ( *sabhāgatassa* ), one’s word does not prevail ( *vacanaṃ na rūhati* )” means: in a court of law ( *vinicchayaṭṭhāne* ), when someone is questioned as a witness ( *sakkhipuṭṭhassa sato* ), their word ( *vacanaṃ* ) is not accepted ( *na rūhati* ), it does not stand ( *na patiṭṭhāti* ). People will say: “This is a dice addict ( *akkhasoṇḍo* ), a gambler ( *jūtakaro* ), do not accept his word ( *vacanaṃ gaṇhittha* )!” These are the kinds of things people say ( *vattāro bhavanti* ).

“One is despised by friends and companions ( *mittāmaccānaṃ paribhūto hotī* )” means that friends and companions ( *mitāmaccā* ) say thus: “Dear friend ( *samma* ), you, though the son of a good family ( *kulaputto* ) in name only ( *nāma* ), wander about ( *vicarasi* ) as a corrupt and degraded ( *chinnabhinnako hutvā* ) gambler ( *jūtakaro* ). This is not befitting ( *anurūpaṃ* ) your caste ( *jāti* ) and lineage ( *gottānaṃ* ). From now on ( *ito paṭṭhāya* ), do not do this ( *mā evaṃ kareyyāsī* )!”

Even though one is so spoken to ( *so evaṃ vuttopi* ), one does not follow ( *na karoti* ) their word ( *vacanaṃ* ).

Therefore ( *tato* ), they do not stay ( *na tiṭṭhanti* ) or sit ( *na nisīdanti* ) together ( *ekato* ) with him ( *tena saddhiṃ* ).

For that reason ( *tassa kāraṇā* ), even though they are asked as witnesses ( *sakkhipuṭṭhāpi* ), they do not speak ( *na kathenti* ).

Thus ( *evaṃ* ), one is despised ( *paribhūto hoti* ) by friends and companions ( *mittāmaccānaṃ* ).

“By those who take or give in marriage ( *āvāhavivāhakāna* )” means that *āvāhakā* are those who wish to get ( *gahetukāmā* ) a girl ( *dārikaṃ* ) from his house ( *gharato* ).

*Vivāhakā* are those who wish to give ( *dātukāmā* ) a girl ( *dārikaṃ* ) into his house ( *gehe* ).

“One is undesired ( *apatthito hotī* )” means that one is unwanted ( *anicchito hoti* ).

“Not sufficient for the support of a wife ( *nālaṃ dārabharaṇāyā* )” means one is not capable ( *na samattho* ) of supporting a wife ( *dārabharaṇāya* ).

People would think: “Even if a girl ( *dārikā* ) is given ( *dinnāpi* ) into his house ( *gehe* ) or taken ( *āgatāpi* ) from his house ( *gehato* ), we ( *amhehi* ) ourselves ( *eva* ) will have to provide for her ( *positabbā bhavissatiyeva* ).”

Those who take or give in marriage ( *āvāhavivāhakāna* ), one is undesired ( *apatthito hotī* ), not sufficient for the support of a wife ( *nālaṃ dārabharaṇāyā* ).

Description of the six disadvantages of bad friendship ( *pāpamittatāya chaādīnavādivaṇṇanā* ).

mula_pali:
252. ‘‘Cha khome, gahapatiputta, ādīnavā pāpamittānuyoge. Ye dhuttā, ye soṇḍā, ye pipāsā, ye nekatikā, ye vañcanikā, ye sāhasikā. Tyāssa mittā honti te sahāyā. Ime kho, gahapatiputta, cha ādīnavā pāpamittānuyoge.

Ālasyassa cha ādīnavā
mula_english:
“Householder’s son, there are these six dangers in associating with bad friends:

Any gambler (*dhūrta*), any glutton (*śauṇḍa*), any drunkard (*pipāsā*), any cheat (*naikatika*), any trickster (*vañcanika*), any bully (*sāhasika*).

They become his friends and companions (*sahāyā*).

Householder’s son, there are these six dangers in associating with bad friends.

Six dangers of laziness (*ālasya*).
commentary_pali: 252.Dhuttāti akkhadhuttā. Soṇḍāti itthisoṇḍā bhattasoṇḍā pūvasoṇḍā mūlakasoṇḍā. Pipāsāti pānasoṇḍā. Nekatikāti patirūpakena vañcanakā. Vañcanikāti sammukhāvañcanāhi vañcanikā. Sāhasikāti ekāgārikādisāhasikakammakārino. Tyāssa mittā hontīti te assa mittā honti. Aññehi sappurisehi saddhiṃ na ramati gandhamālādīhi alaṅkaritvā varasayanaṃ āropitasūkaro gūthakūpamiva, te pāpamitteyeva upasaṅkamati. Tasmā diṭṭhe ceva dhamme samparāyañca bahuṃ anatthaṃ nigacchati.
commentary_english:
252.
“Cheaters ( *dhuttā*)” means dice-cheaters (*akkhadhuttā*).

“Addicted fellows (*soṇḍā*)” means addicted to women (*itthisoṇḍā*), addicted to food (*bhattasoṇḍā*), addicted to cakes (*pūvasoṇḍā*), addicted to roots (*mūlakasoṇḍā*).

“Thirst (*pipāsā*)” means addicted to drinks (*pānasoṇḍā*).

“Hypocrites (*nekatikā*)” means swindlers by means of false appearances (*patirūpakena vañcanakā*).

“Swindlers (*vañcanikā*)” means swindlers in front (*sammukhāvañcanāhi vañcanikā*).

“Brutes (*sāhasikā*)” means men who rob isolated houses and do other brutal acts (*ekāgārikādisāhasikakammakārino*).

“These are one’s friends (*tyāssa mittā hontī*)” means: these are one’s friends (*te assa mittā honti*).

One does not enjoy oneself with other good men (*aññehi sappurisehi saddhiṃ na ramati*), but a pig, in spite of being led upon the best couch adorned with perfumed garlands and the like (*gandhamālādīhi alaṅkaritvā varasayanaṃ āropitasūkaro*), prefers a latrine (*gūthakūpamiva*); he approaches only evil friends (*te pāpamitteyeva upasaṅkamati*).

Therefore, in this very life and in the next, he incurs much misfortune (*tasmā diṭṭhe ceva dhamme samparāyañca bahuṃ anatthaṃ nigacchati*).

mula_pali:
253. ‘‘Cha khome, gahapatiputta, ādīnavā ālasyānuyoge. Atisītanti kammaṃ na karoti, atiuṇhanti kammaṃ na karoti, atisāyanti kammaṃ na karoti, atipātoti kammaṃ na karoti, atichātosmīti kammaṃ na karoti, atidhātosmīti kammaṃ na karoti. Tassa evaṃ kiccāpadesabahulassa viharato anuppannā ceva bhogā nuppajjanti, uppannā ca bhogā parikkhayaṃ gacchanti. Ime kho, gahapatiputta, cha ādīnavā ālasyānuyoge’’ti. Idamavoca bhagavā, idaṃ vatvāna sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā –

‘‘Hoti pānasakhā nāma,

Hoti sammiyasammiyo;

Yo ca atthesu jātesu,

Sahāyo hoti so sakhā.

‘‘Ussūraseyyā paradārasevanā,

Verappasavo verappasaṅgo (sī. syā. pī.) ca anatthatā ca;

verappasaṅgo (sī. syā. pī.)

Pāpā ca mittā sukadariyatā ca,

Ete cha ṭhānā purisaṃ dhaṃsayanti.

‘‘Pāpamitto pāpasakho,

Pāpaācāragocaro;

Asmā lokā paramhā ca,

Ubhayā dhaṃsate naro.

‘‘Akkhitthiyo vāruṇī naccagītaṃ,

Divā soppaṃ pāricariyā akāle;

Pāpā ca mittā sukadariyatā ca,

Ete cha ṭhānā purisaṃ dhaṃsayanti.

‘‘Akkhehi dibbanti suraṃ pivanti,

Yantitthiyo pāṇasamā paresaṃ;

Nihīnasevī na ca vuddhasevī vuddhisevī (syā.), buddhisevī (ka.),

vuddhisevī (syā.), buddhisevī (ka.)

Nihīyate kāḷapakkheva cando.

‘‘Yo vāruṇī addhano akiñcano,

Pipāso pivaṃ papāgato pipāsosi atthapāgato (syā.), pipāsopi samappapāgato (ka.);

pipāsosi atthapāgato (syā.), pipāsopi samappapāgato (ka.)

Udakamiva iṇaṃ vigāhati,

Akulaṃ ākulaṃ (syā. ka.) kāhiti khippamattano.

ākulaṃ (syā. ka.)

‘‘Na divā soppasīlena, rattimuṭṭhānadessinā rattinuṭṭhānadassinā (sī. pī.), rattinuṭṭhānasīlinā (?);

rattinuṭṭhānadassinā (sī. pī.), rattinuṭṭhānasīlinā (?)

Niccaṃ mattena soṇḍena, sakkā āvasituṃ gharaṃ.

‘‘Atisītaṃ atiuṇhaṃ, atisāyamidaṃ ahu;

Iti vissaṭṭhakammante, atthā accenti māṇave.

‘‘Yodha sītañca uṇhañca, tiṇā bhiyyo na maññati;

Karaṃ purisakiccāni, so sukhaṃ sukhā (sabbattha) aṭṭhakathā oloketabbā na vihāyatī’’ti.

sukhā (sabbattha) aṭṭhakathā oloketabbā

Mittapatirūpakā
mula_english:
“These are the six dangers inherent in laziness, householder’s son. Thinking: “It’s too cold”, one does not work; thinking: “It’s too hot”, one does not work; thinking: “It’s too early”, one does not work; thinking: “It’s too late”, one does not work; think­ing: “I’m too hungry”, one does not work; thinking: “I’m too full”, one does not work.’ While he lives with an abundance of excuses for not working, new wealth does not accrue, and existing wealth goes to waste. These, householder’s son, are the six dangers inherent in laziness.”

Thus spoke the Blessed One. Having said this, the Fortunate One, the Teacher, then said further:

“There is one called a drinking buddy, and there is one who is a ‘yes-man’; but he who is a friend in times of need, he is a true friend.

“Excessive sleep, sexual intercourse with another man's wife, quarrelsomeness, and ruinousness; evil friends and stinginess: these six things destroy a man.

“An evil friend, an evil companion, one whose behavior is evil: from this world and the next, that person declines in both ways.

“Gambling women, liquor, dancing, singing, sleeping by day, and attending on others at the wrong time; evil friends and stinginess: these six things destroy a man.

“They gamble with dice and drink liquor; they consider as dear as life, the wives of others. They associate with the inferior and not with their elders; he declines like the moon in the dark fortnight.

“One who is addicted to liquor, resourceless, and has nothing, drinks when thirsty, having come to a drinking-place; he incurs debt like water, and soon plunges himself into bewilderment.

“Not with a habit of sleeping by day, but showing vigilance at night…"

commentary_pali:
253.Atisītanti kammaṃ na karotīti manussehi kālasseva vuṭṭhāya ‘‘etha bho kammantaṃ gacchāmā’’ti vutto ‘‘atisītaṃ tāva, aṭṭhīni bhijjanti viya, gacchatha tumhe pacchā jānissāmī’’ti aggiṃ tapanto nisīdati. Te gantvā kammaṃ karonti. Itarassa kammaṃ parihāyati. Atiuṇhantiādīsupi eseva nayo.

Hoti pānasakhā nāmāti ekacco pānaṭṭhāne surāgeheyeva sahāyo hoti. ‘‘Pannasakhā’’tipi pāṭho, ayamevattho. Sammiyasammiyoti samma sammāti vadanto sammukheyeva sahāyo hoti, parammukhe verīsadiso otārameva gavesati. Atthesujātesūti tathārūpesu kiccesu samuppannesu. Verappasavoti verabahulatā. Anatthatāti anatthakāritā. Sukadariyatāti suṭṭhu kadariyatā thaddhamacchariyabhāvo . Udakamiva iṇaṃ vigāhatīti pāsāṇo udakaṃ viya saṃsīdanto iṇaṃ vigāhati.

Hoti pānasakhā nāmā Sammiyasammiyo Atthesu jātesū Verappasavo Anatthatā Sukadariyatā Udakamiva iṇaṃ vigāhatī

Rattinuṭṭhānadessināti rattiṃ anuṭṭhānasīlena. Atisāyamidaṃ ahūti idaṃ atisāyaṃ jātanti ye evaṃ vatvā kammaṃ na karonti. Iti vissaṭṭhakammanteti evaṃ vatvā pariccattakammante. Atthā accenti māṇaveti evarūpe puggale atthā atikkamanti, tesu na tiṭṭhanti.

Rattinuṭṭhānadessinā Atisāyamidaṃ ahū Iti vissaṭṭhakammante Atthā accenti māṇave

Mittapatirūpakādivaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
“One does not work because ‘It is too cold’” means: when other men, getting up early, say, “Hey, come on, let’s go to work”, one answers, “It is too cold, my bones hurt, you go, I will know later.” So, one sits down, tending the fire.
They go and work.
but the work of the other fellow falls behind.
"It is too hot" and so forth, the same method [applies].

“He is a drinking friend” means: a certain person is a companion only at the place of drinking, in the tavern.
“He is a friend in name only,” this is the meaning.
“He is a ‘yes-man’” means: saying “Yes, yes” he is a companion only to one's face; behind one's back he is like an enemy, seeking only an opportunity [to harm you].
"In matters that have arisen" means: in such and such circumstances, when [problems] have arisen.
“He is a breeder of animosity” means: he has much animosity.
“He is without benefit” means: he causes harm.
“He is very stingy” means: he is extremely stingy, he is rigid and miserly.
“He plumbs debt like water” means: like a stone sinking in water, he plumbs debt.

“He is a drinking friend,” “He is a ‘yes-man’,” “In matters that have arisen"
"He is a breeder of animosity," "He is without benefit," "He is very stingy,"
“One is known for not rising at night” means: one is in the habit of not rising at night.
“It is too late in the evening” means: saying “It is too late in the evening,” they do not work.
“Thus, work is given up” means: thus, work is relinquished.
“Wealth passes away from a young man” means: wealth passes away from a person of such character; it does not remain with them.

“One is known for not rising at night,” “It is too late in the evening,” “Thus, work is given up,” “Wealth passes away from a young man,”
“More than grass” means: more than grass.
“He does not abandon happiness” means: that man does not give up happiness; he is always endowed with happiness.
By this manner of speaking, he shows this meaning: “Being a householder, so much work should not be done; for one who does [too much], there is no increase.”
In this world and the next, one only obtains censure.

“More than grass,” “He does not abandon happiness.”
Description of a false friend, and so forth

mula_pali: 254. ‘‘Cattārome, gahapatiputta, amittā mittapatirūpakā veditabbā. Aññadatthuharo amitto mittapatirūpako veditabbo, vacīparamo amitto mittapatirūpako veditabbo, anuppiyabhāṇī amitto mittapatirūpako veditabbo, apāyasahāyo amitto mittapatirūpako veditabbo.
mula_english: “Young man, be aware of these four enemies disguised as friends: the taker, the talker, the flatterer, and the reckless companion."
commentary_pali: 254. Idāni yo evaṃ karoto anattho uppajjati, aññāni vā pana yāni kānici bhayāni yekeci upaddavā yekeci upasaggā, sabbe te bālaṃ nissāya uppajjanti. Tasmā ‘‘evarūpā bālā na sevitabbā’’ti bāle mittapatirūpake amitte dassetuṃ cattārome, gahapatiputta amittātiādimāha. Tattha aññadatthuharoti sayaṃ tucchahattho āgantvā ekaṃsena yaṃkiñci haratiyeva. Vacīparamoti vacanaparamo vacanamatteneva dāyako kārako viya hoti. Anuppiyabhāṇīti anuppiyaṃ bhaṇati. Apāyasahāyoti bhogānaṃ apāyesu sahāyo hoti.
commentary_english:
Now, if someone acting in this way encounters misfortune, or any other fears, calamities, or troubles whatsoever, all of these arise dependent on the fool.

Therefore, because "fools of this sort are not to be associated with," in order to point out those who are false friends disguised as friends, he said, "<hi rend="bold">These four, O son of a householder, are enemies</hi>," and so forth.

There, <hi rend="bold">"one who appropriates the possessions of another"</hi> means that he comes empty-handed himself and selfishly takes away whatever he can.

<hi rend="bold">"A master of words"</hi> means he is supreme in speech; he is like a giver and a doer merely by his words.

<hi rend="bold">"Speaking affectionately"</hi> means he speaks pleasingly.

<hi rend="bold">"A companion in ruin"</hi> means he is a companion in the dissipating of wealth.

mula_pali:
255. ‘‘Catūhi kho, gahapatiputta, ṭhānehi aññadatthuharo amitto mittapatirūpako veditabbo.

‘‘Aññadatthuharo hoti, appena bahumicchati ;

Bhayassa kiccaṃ karoti, sevati atthakāraṇā.

‘‘Imehi kho, gahapatiputta, catūhi ṭhānehi aññadatthuharo amitto mittapatirūpako veditabbo.
mula_english:
“The flatterer can be identified by four things, householder's son:

He takes everything (aññadatthuharo hoti), he wants a lot for very little (appena bahumicchati);

he does what needs to be done out of fear (bhayassa kiccaṃ karoti), he serves out of concern for his own advantage (sevati atthakāraṇā).

“The flatterer can be identified by these four things, householder's son.
commentary_pali: 255. Evaṃ cattāro amitte dassetvā puna tattha ekekaṃ catūhi kāraṇehi vibhajanto catūhi kho, gahapatiputtātiādimāha. Tattha aññadatthuharo hotīti ekaṃsena hārakoyeva hoti. Sahāyassa gehaṃ rittahattho āgantvā nivatthasāṭakādīnaṃ vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, so ‘‘ativiya tvaṃ samma imassa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsasī’’ti aññaṃ nivāsetvā taṃ deti. Appena bahumicchatīti yaṃkiñci appakaṃ datvā tassa santikā bahuṃ pattheti. Bhayassakiccaṃ karotīti attano bhaye uppanne tassa dāso viya hutvā taṃ taṃ kiccaṃ karoti, ayaṃ sabbadā na karoti, bhaye uppanne karoti, na pemenāti amitto nāma jāto. Sevati atthakāraṇāti mittasanthavavasena na sevati, attano atthameva paccāsīsanto sevati.
commentary_english:
255. Thus, having shown four enemies, again, dividing each one by four reasons, he said, "<hi rend="bold">By four, indeed, householders' sons</hi>," and so forth.

There, "<hi rend="bold">he is a taker of another's property</hi>," means he is entirely a taker.

He goes empty-handed to a friend's house, and praises his garment and other clothes that he is wearing. This one puts on another one and gives him that one. saying "My dear, you are praising this too much.”

"<hi rend="bold">He wants much for little</hi>" means: no matter how small a thing he has done, he asks much in return.

"<hi rend="bold">He does his duty out of fear</hi>" means: when fear arises concerning himself, he does this or that duty on his own as if he were a slave. He does not do it all the time on his own. He does it when fear arises, not out of love. Therefore he is called an “enemy”.

"<hi rend="bold">He offers his services to get an advantage</hi>" means: he does not offer his services because of intimacy with his friends. He offers his services hoping just for a personal advantage.

mula_pali: 256. ‘‘Catūhi kho, gahapatiputta, ṭhānehi vacīparamo amitto mittapatirūpako veditabbo. Atītena paṭisantharati paṭisandharati (ka.), anāgatena paṭisantharati, niratthakena saṅgaṇhāti, paccuppannesu kiccesu byasanaṃ dasseti. Imehi kho, gahapatiputta, catūhi ṭhānehi vacīparamo amitto mittapatirūpako veditabbo.
mula_english: ‘The great talker can be seen to be a false friend for four reasons: he talks of favours in the past (*atītena paṭisantharati*), and in the future (*anāgatena paṭisantharati*), he mouths empty phrases of goodwill (*niratthakena saṅgaṇhāti*), and when something needs to be done in the present, he pleads inability owing to some disaster (*paccuppannesu kiccesu byasanaṃ dasseti*). ‘The great talker can be seen to be a false friend for these four reasons.
commentary_pali: 256.Atītena paṭisantharatīti sahāye āgate ‘‘hiyyo vā pare vā na āgatosi, amhākaṃ imasmiṃ vāre sassaṃ ativiya nipphannaṃ, bahūni sāliyavabījādīni ṭhapetvā maggaṃ olokentā nisīdimha, ajja pana sabbaṃ khīṇa’’nti evaṃ atītena saṅgaṇhāti. Anāgatenāti ‘‘imasmiṃ vāre amhākaṃ sassaṃ manāpaṃ bhavissati, phalabhārabharitā sāliādayo, sassasaṅgahe kate tumhākaṃ saṅgahaṃ kātuṃ samatthā bhavissāmā’’ti evaṃ anāgatena saṅgaṇhāti. Niratthakenāti hatthikkhandhe vā assapiṭṭhe vā nisinno sahāyaṃ disvā ‘‘ehi, bho, idha nisīdā’’ti vadati. Manāpaṃ sāṭakaṃ nivāsetvā ‘‘sahāyakassa vata me anucchaviko añño pana mayhaṃ natthī’’ti vadati, evaṃ niratthakena saṅgaṇhāti nāma. Paccuppannesu kiccesu byasanaṃ dassetīti ‘‘sakaṭena me attho’’ti vutte ‘‘cakkamassa bhinnaṃ, akkho chinno’’tiādīni vadati.
commentary_english:
“Welcoming an incoming guest with past goods not available at present” (*atītena paṭisantharatī*) means: when a friend comes, he says: “You did not come yesterday or on another day. On that occasion the crop was very high. Having hoarded much rice, barley, seeds, and other produce (*sāli-yava-bījādīni*), we sat down watching the road. But today it’s all gone.” Thus, he welcomes an incoming guest with past goods not available at present.

“With future goods not available at present” (*anāgatenā*) means: “On that future occasion we will have a wonderful crop. Rice and the other plants (*sāliādayo*) will be heavy with the weight of their fruits. Once we have harvested the crop, we will be able to receive you.” Thus, he receives a guest with future goods not available at present.

“With worthless talk” (*niratthakenā*) means: sitting on the back of an elephant (*hatthikkhandhe*) or on the back of a horse (*assapiṭṭhe*), he says: “Come on, you, sit here!”

While wearing a wonderful garment, he says, “My dear, it would suit my companion (*sahāyakassa*), but I don’t have another one.” Thus, he receives a guest with worthless talk.

“Pointing out misfortune in present affairs” (*paccuppannesu kiccesu byasanaṃ dassetī*) means: When someone says, “I need a cart (*sakaṭena me attho*),” he says things like, “Its wheel is broken, and its axle is broken.”

mula_pali: 257. ‘‘Catūhi kho, gahapatiputta, ṭhānehi anuppiyabhāṇī amitto mittapatirūpako veditabbo. Pāpakaṃpissa pāpakammaṃpissa (syā.) anujānāti, kalyāṇaṃpissa anujānāti, sammukhāssa vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati, parammukhāssa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsati. Imehi kho, gahapatiputta, catūhi ṭhānehi anuppiyabhāṇī amitto mittapatirūpako veditabbo.
mula_english: "Householder's son, the flatterer can be identified as a false friend by four characteristics: He approves of his bad actions, he approves of his good actions, he praises him to his face, and he speaks disparagingly of him behind his back. Indeed, householder's son, the flatterer can be identified as a false friend by these four characteristics."
commentary_pali:
257.Pāpakampissa anujānātīti pāṇātipātādīsu yaṃkiñci karomāti vutte ‘‘sādhu samma karomā’’ti anujānāti. Kalyāṇepi eseva nayo. Sahāyo hotīti ‘‘asukaṭṭhāne suraṃ pivanti, ehi tattha gacchāmā’’ti vutte sādhūti gacchati. Esa nayo sabbattha. Iti viññāyāti ‘‘mittapatirūpakā ete’’ti evaṃ jānitvā.

Suhadamittādivaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
“He approves of what is evil for one who is unstable in wickedness (pāpakampissa anujānāti)” means: if one says, "Let us commit murder (prāṇātipāta) and other such evils," he approves, saying, "Very good, my dear (sādhu samma), let's do it (karomā'ti anujānāti)."

And the same rule (eva nayo) applies in the case of what is wholesome (kalyāṇepi).

“A companion (sahāyo hotī)” means: if some are drinking liquor (suraṃ pivanti) in such-and-such a place (asukaṭṭhāne), and one says, "Come (ehi), let's go there (tattha gacchāmā)," he arises saying, "Very well (sādhūti)," and goes (gacchati).

This method (esa nayo) applies in all instances (sabbattha).

“Having understood (iti viññāyā)” means: having known (jānitvā) thus (evaṃ), "These are only seeming friends (mittapatirūpakā ete)."

Description of sincere friends and so on (suhadamittādivaṇṇanā).

mula_pali: 258. ‘‘Catūhi kho, gahapatiputta, ṭhānehi apāyasahāyo amitto mittapatirūpako veditabbo . Surāmeraya majjappamādaṭṭhānānuyoge sahāyo hoti, vikāla visikhā cariyānuyoge sahāyo hoti, samajjābhicaraṇe sahāyo hoti, jūtappamādaṭṭhānānuyoge sahāyo hoti. Imehi kho, gahapatiputta, catūhi ṭhānehi apāyasahāyo amitto mittapatirūpako veditabbo’’ti.
mula_english: 258. “The reckless companion, householder's son, can be identified by four things: he is a companion when you indulge in strong drink (*surāmerayamajjapramādaṭṭhānānuyoge*), when you haunt the streets at unfitting times (*vikālavisikhācariyānuyoge*), when you frequent fairs (*samajjābhicaraṇe*), and when you indulge in gambling (*jūtappamādaṭṭhānānuyoge*). The reckless companion, householder's son, can be identified by these four things.”

mula_pali:
259. Idamavoca bhagavā, idaṃ vatvāna sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā –

‘‘Aññadatthuharo mitto, yo ca mitto vacīparo vacīparamo (syā.);

vacīparamo (syā.)

Anuppiyañca yo āha, apāyesu ca yo sakhā.

Ete amitte cattāro, iti viññāya paṇḍito;

Ārakā parivajjeyya, maggaṃ paṭibhayaṃ yathā’’ti.

Suhadamitto
mula_english:
Thus spoke the Blessed One. Having said this, the Sugata, the Teacher, then said further:

"The friend who takes away benefits, the friend who is only a speaker;
the one who says agreeable things, and the friend in misfortune:

These are the four kinds of foes in the guise of friends; having recognized this, the wise man
should avoid them from afar, like a path fraught with danger."

[Topic:] A true-hearted friend

mula_pali: 260. ‘‘Cattārome , gahapatiputta, mittā suhadā veditabbā. Upakāro upakārako (syā.) mitto suhado veditabbo, samānasukhadukkho mitto suhado veditabbo, atthakkhāyī mitto suhado veditabbo, anukampako mitto suhado veditabbo.
mula_english: 260. "These four, householder's son, are to be known as friends and good-hearted companions: the friend who is a helper ( *upakārako*), the friend who shares pleasure and pain equally (*samānasukhadukkho*), the friend who declares what is beneficial (*atthakkhāyī*), and the friend who is compassionate (*anukampako*)."
commentary_pali: 260. Evaṃ na sevitabbe pāpamitte dassetvā idāni sevitabbe kalyāṇamitte dassento puna cattārome, gahapatiputtātiādimāha. Tattha suhadāti sundarahadayā.
commentary_english:
Thus, having shown how evil friends should not be served, he now shows how good friends should be served, again beginning with "<hi rend="bold">these four, sons of householders</hi>," etc.

There, <hi rend="bold">suhadā</hi> means "having a beautiful heart" (*sundarahṛdayā*).

mula_pali: 261. ‘‘Catūhi kho, gahapatiputta, ṭhānehi upakāro mitto suhado veditabbo. Pamattaṃ rakkhati, pamattassa sāpateyyaṃ rakkhati, bhītassa saraṇaṃ hoti, uppannesu kiccakaraṇīyesu taddiguṇaṃ bhogaṃ anuppadeti. Imehi kho, gahapatiputta, catūhi ṭhānehi upakāro mitto suhado veditabbo.
mula_english: “Householder’s son, the helpful friend can be recognized by four qualities: He protects you when you are heedless, he protects your possessions when you are heedless, he is a refuge when you are afraid, and when there is some business to be done, he provides twice as much as is needed. Householder’s son, the helpful friend can be recognized by these four qualities.”
commentary_pali: 261.Pamattaṃ rakkhatīti majjaṃ pivitvā gāmamajjhe vā gāmadvāre vā magge vā nipannaṃ disvā ‘‘evaṃnipannassa kocideva nivāsanapārupanampi hareyyā’’ti samīpe nisīditvā pabuddhakāle gahetvā gacchati. Pamattassasāpateyyanti sahāyo bahigato vā hoti suraṃ pivitvā vā pamatto, gehaṃ anārakkhaṃ ‘‘kocideva yaṃkiñci hareyyā’’ti gehaṃ pavisitvā tassa dhanaṃ rakkhati. Bhītassāti kismiñcideva bhaye uppanne ‘‘mā bhāyi, mādise sahāye ṭhite kiṃ bhāyasī’’ti taṃ bhayaṃ haranto paṭisaraṇaṃ hoti. Taddiguṇaṃ bhoganti kiccakaraṇīye uppanne sahāyaṃ attano santikaṃ āgataṃ disvā vadati ‘‘kasmā āgatosī’’ti? Rājakule kammaṃ atthīti. Kiṃ laddhuṃ vaṭṭatīti? Eko kahāpaṇoti. ‘‘Nagare kammaṃ nāma na ekakahāpaṇena nipphajjati, dve gaṇhāhī’’ti evaṃ yattakaṃ vadati, tato diguṇaṃ deti.
commentary_english:
261. “He protects you when you are careless ( *pramattaṃ rakkhati* )” means that, having drunk liquor, if one sees him lying down in the middle of the village, or at the gate of the village, or on a road, thinking that someone could steal even his garment and cloak, his friend sits by him, and when he wakes up, his friend takes him away.

“He protects your property when you are careless ( *pamattassa sāpateyyaṃ* )” means that, thinking his friend is away or drunk, having drunk liquor, that his house is unguarded, and that someone could steal any of his goods, he enters his house and guards his property.

“When you are afraid ( *bhītassā* )” means that if any danger arises, he becomes a refuge by removing that fear, saying, “Don’t be afraid, why are you afraid when a friend like myself is standing by you?”

“Twice as much enjoyment ( *taddiguṇaṃ bhoga* )” means that when something needing to be done arises in the royal family, having seen his friend come to his side, he says, “Why have you come?” because there is work.

“What should you bring?”

“For one coin they do not stage a trial in the city. Take two!” Thus, however much his friend asks, he gives him twice as much.

mula_pali: 262. ‘‘Catūhi kho, gahapatiputta, ṭhānehi samānasukhadukkho mitto suhado veditabbo. Guyhamassa ācikkhati, guyhamassa parigūhati, āpadāsu na vijahati, jīvitaṃpissa atthāya pariccattaṃ hoti. Imehi kho, gahapatiputta, catūhi ṭhānehi samānasukhadukkho mitto suhado veditabbo.
mula_english: “Householder's son, the friend who shares the same happiness and sorrow can be identified by four things: He tells you his secrets, he guards your secrets, he does not abandon you in misfortune, and he would even sacrifice his life for you. Indeed, householder's son, the friend who shares the same happiness and sorrow can be identified by these four things.”
commentary_pali: 262.Guyhamassa ācikkhatīti attano guyhaṃ nigūhituṃ yuttakathaṃ aññassa akathetvā tasseva ācikkhati. Guyhamassa parigūhatīti tena kathitaṃ guyhaṃ yathā añño na jānāti, evaṃ rakkhati. Āpadāsu na vijahatīti uppanne bhaye na pariccajati. Jīvitampissa atthāyāti attano jīvitampi tassa sahāyassa atthāya pariccattameva hoti, attano jīvitaṃ agaṇetvāpi tassa kammaṃ karotiyeva.
commentary_english:
262. "He reveals what is secret" means he reveals a suitable topic for concealment to him, not telling it to another, but revealing it to him alone.

"He cherishes what is secret" means he protects the secret that has been spoken by him so that another does not know it.

"He does not abandon in adversity" means he does not abandon [him] in arising fear.

"For you, he abandons even his life" means: he abandons even his own life for him, for a friend. Disregarding even his life, he just does what is to be done for him. (jīvitampissa atthāyāti attano jīvitampi tassa sahāyassa atthāya pariccattameva hoti, attano jīvitaṃ agaṇetvāpi tassa kammaṃ karotiyeva.)

mula_pali: 263. ‘‘Catūhi kho, gahapatiputta, ṭhānehi atthakkhāyī mitto suhado veditabbo. Pāpā nivāreti, kalyāṇe niveseti, assutaṃ sāveti, saggassa maggaṃ ācikkhati. Imehi kho, gahapatiputta, catūhi ṭhānehi atthakkhāyī mitto suhado veditabbo.
mula_english: ‘The friend who points out what is good for you can be seen to be a loyal friend in four ways: by restraining you from wrongdoing, guiding you towards good actions, telling you what you ought to know, and showing you the path to heaven. In these four ways, a friend who points out what is beneficial, *gahapatiputta*, can be seen as a true friend.’
commentary_pali: 263.Pāpā nivāretīti amhesu passantesu passantesu tvaṃ evaṃ kātuṃ na labhasi, pañca verāni dasa akusalakammapathe mā karohīti nivāreti. Kalyāṇe nivesetīti kalyāṇakamme tīsu saraṇesu pañcasīlesu dasakusalakammapathesu vattassu, dānaṃ dehi puññaṃ karohi dhammaṃ suṇāhīti evaṃ kalyāṇe niyojeti. Assutaṃ sāvetīti assutapubbaṃ sukhumaṃ nipuṇaṃ kāraṇaṃ sāveti. Saggassa magganti idaṃ kammaṃ katvā sagge nibbattantīti evaṃ saggassa maggaṃ ācikkhati.
commentary_english:
263. “He keeps you away from evil (pāpā nivāretī)”: when we watch, you are not allowed to behave like that: do not do the five sins (pañca verāni), the ten courses of unwholesome action (dasa akusalakammapathe). Thus, he keeps him away.

“He leads you to what is good (kalyāṇe nivesetī)”: In wholesome actions (kalyāṇakamme), turn to the three refuges (tīsu saraṇesu) or the five precepts (pañcasīlesu), the ten courses of wholesome action (dasakusalakammapathesu); give donations (dānaṃ dehi), do meritorious deeds (puññaṃ karohi), listen to the Dharma (dhammaṃ suṇāhīti). Thus, he directs him to what is good (kalyāṇe niyojeti).

“He makes the unheard heard (assutaṃ sāvetī)”: he makes known subtle and refined causes which were previously unheard (assutapubbaṃ sukhumaṃ nipuṇaṃ kāraṇaṃ sāveti).

“The path to heaven (saggassa magga)”: By doing this action (idaṃ kammaṃ katvā), they are reborn in heaven (sagge nibbattantīti). Thus, he points out the path to heaven (saggassa maggaṃ ācikkhati).

mula_pali: 264. ‘‘Catūhi kho, gahapatiputta, ṭhānehi anukampako mitto suhado veditabbo. Abhavenassa na nandati, bhavenassa nandati, avaṇṇaṃ bhaṇamānaṃ nivāreti, vaṇṇaṃ bhaṇamānaṃ pasaṃsati. Imehi kho, gahapatiputta, catūhi ṭhānehi anukampako mitto suhado veditabbo’’ti.
mula_english:
“The compassionate friend can be identified by four things:

he does not rejoice at your misfortune, he rejoices at your good fortune, he stops others who speak against you, and he commends others who speak in praise of you.’

‘The sympathetic friend can be seen to be a loyal friend in four ways:
commentary_pali: 264.Abhavenassa na nandatīti tassa abhavena avuḍḍhiyā puttadārassa vā parijanassa vā tathārūpaṃ pārijuññaṃ disvā vā sutvā vā na nandati, anattamano hoti. Bhavenāti vuḍḍhiyā tathārūpassa sampattiṃ vā issariyappaṭilābhaṃ vā disvā vā sutvā vā nandati, attamano hoti. Avaṇṇaṃ bhaṇamānaṃ nivāretīti ‘‘asuko virūpo na pāsādiko dujjātiko dussīlo’’ti vā vutte ‘‘evaṃ mā bhaṇi, rūpavā ca so pāsādiko ca sujāto ca sīlasampanno cā’’tiādīhi vacanehi paraṃ attano sahāyassa avaṇṇaṃ bhaṇamānaṃ nivāreti. Vaṇṇaṃ bhaṇamānaṃ pasaṃsatīti ‘‘asuko rūpavā pāsādiko sujāto sīlasampanno’’ti vutte ‘‘aho suṭṭhu vadasi, subhāsitaṃ tayā, evametaṃ, esa puriso rūpavā pāsādiko sujāto sīlasampanno’’ti evaṃ attano sahāyakassa paraṃ vaṇṇaṃ bhaṇamānaṃ pasaṃsati.
commentary_english:
264. “He does not rejoice over your failure” (abhavenassa na nandatī) means: he does not rejoice, he is not happy over one’s failure, one’s misfortune, for he witnesses or hears of one’s loss of a child, a wife, or a servant as if it were his own loss; he is unhappy.

“With prosperity” (bhavenā) means: he rejoices, he is happy when he sees or hears of one’s success or the gaining of power; he is delighted.

“He stops anybody speaking ill of you” (avaṇṇaṃ bhaṇamānaṃ nivāretī) means: if anybody says that such-and-such a person is ugly (virūpo), unpleasant (na pāsādiko), born of a bad family (dujjātiko), or immoral (dussīlo), he stops his interlocutor who speaks ill of his own companion with words such as: “Don’t say that. He is handsome (rūpavā), pleasant (pāsādiko), born of a good family (sujāto), and perfectly moral (sīlasampanno).”

“He commends anybody praising you” (vaṇṇaṃ bhaṇamānaṃ pasaṃsatī) means: if anybody says that such-and-such a person is handsome (rūpavā), pleasant (pāsādiko), born of a good family (sujāto), and perfectly moral (sīlasampanno), he commends his interlocutor, who thus praises his own companion, saying, “Ah, well spoken! Well said by you! So it is! This man is handsome (rūpavā), pleasant (pāsādiko), born of a good family (sujāto), and perfectly moral (sīlasampanno).”

mula_pali:
265. Idamavoca bhagavā, idaṃ vatvāna sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā –

‘‘Upakāro ca yo mitto, sukhe dukkhe sukhadukkho (syā. ka.) ca yo sakhā yo ca mitto sukhe dukkhe (sī. pī.);

sukhadukkho (syā. ka.) yo ca mitto sukhe dukkhe (sī. pī.)

Atthakkhāyī ca yo mitto, yo ca mittānukampako.

‘‘Etepi mitte cattāro, iti viññāya paṇḍito;

Sakkaccaṃ payirupāseyya, mātā puttaṃ va orasaṃ;

Paṇḍito sīlasampanno, jalaṃ aggīva bhāsati.

‘‘Bhoge saṃharamānassa, bhamarasseva irīyato;

Bhogā sannicayaṃ yanti, vammikovupacīyati.

‘‘Evaṃ bhoge samāhatvā samāharitvā (syā.), alamatto kule gihī;

samāharitvā (syā.)

Catudhā vibhaje bhoge, sa ve mittāni ganthati.

‘‘Ekena bhoge bhuñjeyya, dvīhi kammaṃ payojaye;

Catutthañca nidhāpeyya, āpadāsu bhavissatī’’ti.

Chaddisāpaṭicchādanakaṇḍaṃ
mula_english:
The Blessed One said this. Having said this, the Sugata, the Teacher, then said further:

“The friend who is a helper, the friend in times both good and bad ( *sukhe dukkhe*), the friend who declares what is beneficial, and the friend who is compassionate.

“Knowing these four kinds of friends, a wise man should carefully attend to them, as a mother [attends to] her own son; a wise man, accomplished in virtue, shines like a fire.

“For one who is accumulating wealth, behaving like a bee; wealth gathers, [just as] an anthill grows.

“Having thus accumulated wealth, a householder in a family of sufficient means should divide his wealth into four parts; in that way he binds friends to himself.

“With one part he should enjoy wealth, with two he should pursue his livelihood, and the fourth he should save for times of distress.”

The Chapter on Covering the Six Directions.
commentary_pali:
265.Jalaṃ aggīva bhāsatīti rattiṃ pabbatamatthake jalamāno aggi viya virocati.

Bhoge saṃharamānassāti attānampi parampi apīḷetvā dhammena samena bhoge sampiṇḍentassa rāsiṃ karontassa. Bhamarasseva irīyatoti yathā bhamaro pupphānaṃ vaṇṇagandhaṃ apothayaṃ tuṇḍenapi pakkhehipi rasaṃ āharitvā anupubbena cakkappamāṇaṃ madhupaṭalaṃ karoti, evaṃ anupubbena mahantaṃ bhogarāsiṃ karontassa. Bhogā sannicayaṃ yantīti tassa bhogā nicayaṃ gacchanti. Kathaṃ? Anupubbena upacikāhi saṃvaḍḍhiyamāno vammiko viya. Tenāha ‘‘vammikovupacīyatī’’ti. Yathā vammiko upaciyati, evaṃ nicayaṃ yantīti attho.

Bhoge saṃharamānassā Bhamarasseva irīyato Bhogā sannicayaṃ yantī

Samāhatvāti samāharitvā. Alamatthoti yuttasabhāvo samattho vā pariyattarūpo gharāvāsaṃ saṇṭhāpetuṃ.

Samāhatvā Alamattho

Idāni yathā vā gharāvāso saṇṭhapetabbo, tathā ovadanto catudhā vibhaje bhogetiādimāha. Tattha sa ve mittāni ganthatīti so evaṃ vibhajanto mittāni ganthati nāma abhejjamānāni ṭhapeti. Yassa hi bhogā santi, so eva mitte ṭhapetuṃ sakkoti, na itaro.

catudhā vibhaje bhoge sa ve mittāni ganthatī

Ekenabhoge bhuñjeyyāti ekena koṭṭhāsena bhoge bhuñjeyya. Dvīhi kammaṃ payojayeti dvīhi koṭṭhāsehi kasivāṇijjādikammaṃ payojeyya. Catutthañca nidhāpeyyāti catutthaṃ koṭṭhāsaṃ nidhāpetvā ṭhapeyya. Āpadāsu bhavissatīti kulānañhi na sabbakālaṃ ekasadisaṃ vattati, kadāci rājādivasena āpadāpi uppajjanti, tasmā evaṃ āpadāsu uppannāsu bhavissatīti ‘‘ekaṃ koṭṭhāsaṃ nidhāpeyyā’’ti āha . Imesu pana catūsu koṭṭhāsesu katarakoṭṭhāsaṃ gahetvā kusalaṃ kātabbanti? ‘‘Bhoge bhuñjeyyā’’ti vuttakoṭṭhāsaṃ. Tato gaṇhitvā bhikkhūnampi kapaṇaddhikādīnampi dātabbaṃ, pesakāranhāpitādīnampi vetanaṃ dātabbaṃ.

Ekena bhoge bhuñjeyyā Dvīhi kammaṃ payojaye Catutthañca nidhāpeyyā Āpadāsu bhavissatī

Chaddisāpaṭicchādanakaṇḍavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
265. *jalaṃ aggīva bhāsatī* means it shines like a blazing fire on a mountain at night, appearing like fire.

*bhoge saṃharamānassā* means accumulating possessions without oppressing oneself or others, gathering possessions through just means, piling them up. *bhamarasseva irīyato* means just as a bee, without spoiling the color and fragrance of flowers, takes in their pollen with its mouth and wings, and gradually makes a honeycomb the size of a wheel, so too, gradually, one accumulates a great heap of possessions. *bhogā sannicayaṃ yantī* means possessions go to accumulation, that is, one's possessions go to a collection. How? Gradually, like an anthill that grows with small particles. Therefore, it is said, "The anthill grows." Just as an anthill grows, so it goes to accumulation, this is the meaning.

*bhoge saṃharamānassā bhamarasseva irīyato bhogā sannicayaṃ yantī samāhatvā* means having collected. *alamattho* means being capable, being fit in nature, or being qualified to establish a household.

*samāhatvā alamattho* Now, just as a household should be established, so advising, he says, "*catudhā vibhaje bhoge*," and so forth. There, *sa ve mittāni ganthatī* means he, thus dividing, binds friends, that is, he establishes unbreakable friendships. For he who has possessions is able to establish friends, not the other.

*catudhā vibhaje bhoge sa ve mittāni ganthatī* *ekena bhoge bhuñjeyyā* means with one part, he should enjoy possessions. *dvīhi kammaṃ payojaye* means with two parts, he should engage in work such as farming and trade. *catutthañca nidhāpeyyā* means and the fourth part, having stored the fourth portion, he should keep it aside. *āpadāsu bhavissatī* means it will be for times of adversity, for families do not always fare the same; sometimes adversities arise due to kings and so forth. Therefore, in this way, it will be for when adversities have arisen, thus he says, "One part should be stored away."

Among these four portions, which portion having taken, should skillful actions be done? The portion that was said, "*bhoge bhuñjeyyā*." Having taken from that, it should be given to monks and to the poor and needy, and wages should be given to servants and so forth.

*ekena bhoge bhuñjeyyā dvīhi kammaṃ payojaye catutthañca nidhāpeyyā āpadāsu bhavissatī*

Explanation of the section on garments used to cover the body in all directions

mula_pali: 266. ‘‘Kathañca, gahapatiputta, ariyasāvako chaddisāpaṭicchādī hoti? Cha imā, gahapatiputta, disā veditabbā. Puratthimā disā mātāpitaro veditabbā, dakkhiṇā disā ācariyā veditabbā, pacchimā disā puttadārā veditabbā, uttarā disā mittāmaccā veditabbā, heṭṭhimā disā dāsakammakarā veditabbā, uparimā disā samaṇabrāhmaṇā veditabbā.
mula_english: “And how, young householder, does the noble disciple protect the six directions (chaddisāpaṭicchādī)? These six directions (disā) should be known (veditabbā). The east (puratthimā disā) should be known as mother and father (mātāpitaro veditabbā), the south (dakkhiṇā disā) should be known as teachers (ācariyā veditabbā), the west (pacchimā disā) should be known as spouse and children (puttadārā veditabbā), the north (uttarā disā) should be known as friends and associates (mittāmaccā veditabbā), the lower direction (heṭṭhimā disā) should be known as servants and workers (dāsakammakarā veditabbā), and the upper direction (uparimā disā) should be known as ascetics and Brahmins (samaṇabrāhmaṇā veditabbā).
commentary_pali:
266. Iti bhagavā ettakena kathāmaggena evaṃ gahapatiputtassa ariyasāvako catūhi kāraṇehi akusalaṃ pahāya chahi kāraṇehi bhogānaṃ apāyamukhaṃ vajjetvā soḷasa mittāni sevanto gharāvāsaṃ saṇṭhapetvā dārabharaṇaṃ karonto dhammikena ājīvena jīvati, devamanussānañca antare aggikkhandho viya virocatīti vajjanīyadhammavajjanatthaṃ sevitabbadhammasevanatthañca ovādaṃ datvā idāni namassitabbā cha disā dassento kathañca gahapatiputtātiādimāha.

Tattha chaddisāpaṭicchādīti yathā chahi disāhi āgamanabhayaṃ na āgacchati, khemaṃ hoti nibbhayaṃ evaṃ viharanto ‘‘chaddisāpaṭicchādī’’ti vuccati. ‘‘Puratthimā disā mātāpitaro veditabbā’’tiādīsu mātāpitaro pubbupakāritāya puratthimā disāti veditabbā. Ācariyā dakkhiṇeyyatāya dakkhiṇā disāti. Puttadārā piṭṭhito anubandhanavasena pacchimā disāti. Mittāmaccā yasmā so mittāmacce nissāya te te dukkhavisese uttarati, tasmā uttarā disāti. Dāsakammakarā pādamūle patiṭṭhānavasena heṭṭhimā disāti. Samaṇabrāhmaṇā guṇehi upari ṭhitabhāvena uparimā disāti veditabbā.

chaddisāpaṭicchādī mātāpitaro puratthimā disā Ācariyā dakkhiṇā disā Puttadārā pacchimā disā Mittāmaccā uttarā disā Dāsakammakarā heṭṭhimā disā Samaṇabrāhmaṇā uparimā disā
commentary_english:
266. Thus, the Blessed One, by this method of exposition, having given advice to the householder's son, [saying that] a noble disciple ( *arya-śrāvaka* ) abandons demerit by four causes, avoids the gateways to ruin of possessions by six causes, cultivates sixteen friends, establishes a household, supports a wife, lives by a righteous livelihood, and shines forth like a blazing firebrand amidst gods and humans, in order to abandon what should be abandoned and to cultivate what should be cultivated, now, showing the six directions that should be venerated, said, "How, O householder's son…," and so forth.

There, *chaddisāpaṭicchādī* means that just as no fear of arrival comes from the six directions, [and] it is secure and free from fear, so one who lives in this way is called "protected by the six directions."

In the passage beginning "The eastern direction is to be known as parents," parents are to be known as the eastern direction ( *puratthimā disā* ) because of their prior kindness.

Teachers ( *ācārya* ) are the southern direction ( *dakṣiṇā disā* ) because of their claim to offerings ( *dakkhiṇeyyatāya* ).

Children and wives ( *putradārā* ) are the western direction ( *pacchimā disā* ) because of their continuous attachment from behind.

Friends and companions ( *mittāmaccā* ), because one relies on friends and companions and crosses over those particular sufferings, therefore [they are] the northern direction ( *uttarā disā* ).

Servants and workers ( *dāsakammakarā* ) are the lower direction ( *heṭṭhimā disā* ) because of their position at the base of the feet ( *pādamūle patiṭṭhānavasena* ).

Ascetics and Brahmins ( *śramaṇabrāhmaṇā* ) are to be known as the upper direction ( *uparimā disā* ) because of their being situated above by good qualities ( *guṇehi upari ṭhitabhāvena* ).

Protected by the six directions ( *chaddisāpaṭicchādī* ), parents ( *mātāpitaro* ), eastern direction ( *puratthimā disā* ), teachers ( *ācariyā* ), southern direction ( *dakṣiṇā disā* ), children and wives ( *putradārā* ), western direction ( *pacchimā disā* ), friends and companions ( *mittāmaccā* ), northern direction ( *uttarā disā* ), servants and workers ( *dāsakammakarā* ), lower direction ( *heṭṭhimā disā* ), ascetics and Brahmins ( *śramaṇabrāhmaṇā* ), upper direction ( *uparimā disā* ).

mula_pali: 267. ‘‘Pañcahi kho, gahapatiputta, ṭhānehi puttena puratthimā disā mātāpitaro paccupaṭṭhātabbā – bhato ne nesaṃ (bahūsu) bharissāmi, kiccaṃ nesaṃ karissāmi, kulavaṃsaṃ ṭhapessāmi, dāyajjaṃ paṭipajjāmi, atha vā pana petānaṃ kālaṅkatānaṃ dakkhiṇaṃ anuppadassāmīti. Imehi kho, gahapatiputta, pañcahi ṭhānehi puttena puratthimā disā mātāpitaro paccupaṭṭhitā pañcahi ṭhānehi puttaṃ anukampanti. Pāpā nivārenti, kalyāṇe nivesenti, sippaṃ sikkhāpenti, patirūpena dārena saṃyojenti, samaye dāyajjaṃ niyyādenti niyyātenti (ka. sī.). Imehi kho, gahapatiputta, pañcahi ṭhānehi puttena puratthimā disā mātāpitaro paccupaṭṭhitā imehi pañcahi ṭhānehi puttaṃ anukampanti. Evamassa esā puratthimā disā paṭicchannā hoti khemā appaṭibhayā.
mula_english:
“Householder’s son, mother and father, as the eastern direction, can be aided in five instances by a son: “I, who was given sustenance by them, shall sustain them, I shall perform their tasks for them, I shall maintain the traditions of their clan, I shall keep up their inheritance, and in addition I shall make continual offerings for them when they have passed on and completed their time.”

When mother and father, as the eastern direction, are aided by a son in these five instances they are sympathetic with their son in five instances: they protect him from evil, they encourage him to do good, they have him trained in a craft, they have him joined to a suitable wife, and when it is the occasion they hand over their inheritance to him’.

When mother and father are aided by a son in these five instances they are sympathetic with their son in these five instances.

In this way the eastern direction is covered, making it at peace and free from fear.
commentary_pali:
267.Bhato ne bharissāmīti ahaṃ mātāpitūhi thaññaṃ pāyetvā hatthapāde vaḍḍhetvā mukhena siṅghāṇikaṃ apanetvā nahāpetvā maṇḍetvā bhato bharito jaggito, svāhaṃ ajja te mahallake pādadhovananhāpanayāgubhattadānādīhi bharissāmi.

Kiccaṃ nesaṃ karissāmīti attano kammaṃ ṭhapetvā mātāpitūnaṃ rājakulādīsu uppannaṃ kiccaṃ gantvā karissāmi. Kulavaṃsaṃ saṇṭhapessāmīti mātāpitūnaṃ santakaṃ khettavatthuhiraññasuvaṇṇādiṃ avināsetvā rakkhantopi kulavaṃsaṃ saṇṭhapeti nāma. Mātāpitaro adhammikavaṃsato hāretvā dhammikavaṃse ṭhapentopi, kulavaṃsena āgatāni salākabhattādīni anupacchinditvā pavattentopi kulavaṃsaṃ saṇṭhapeti nāma. Idaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ – ‘‘kulavaṃsaṃ saṇṭhapessāmī’’ti.

Kiccaṃ nesaṃ karissāmī Kulavaṃsaṃ saṇṭhapessāmī

Dāyajjaṃ paṭipajjāmīti mātāpitaro attano ovāde avattamāne micchāpaṭipanne dārake vinicchayaṃ patvā aputte karonti, te dāyajjārahā na honti. Ovāde vattamāne pana kulasantakassa sāmike karonti, ahaṃ evaṃ vattissāmīti adhippāyena ‘‘dāyajjaṃ paṭipajjāmī’’ti vuttaṃ.

Dāyajjaṃ paṭipajjāmī

Dakkhiṇaṃ anuppadassāmīti tesaṃ pattidānaṃ katvā tatiyadivasato paṭṭhāya dānaṃ anuppadassāmi. Pāpā nivārentīti pāṇātipātādīnaṃ diṭṭhadhammikasamparāyikaṃ ādīnavaṃ vatvā, ‘‘tāta, mā evarūpaṃ karī’’ti nivārenti, katampi garahanti. Kalyāṇe nivesentīti anāthapiṇḍiko viya lañjaṃ datvāpi sīlasamādānādīsu nivesenti. Sippaṃ sikkhāpentīti attano ovāde ṭhitabhāvaṃ ñatvā vaṃsānugataṃ muddāgaṇanādisippaṃ sikkhāpenti. Patirūpenāti kulasīlarūpādīhi anurūpena.

Dakkhiṇaṃ anuppadassāmī Pāpā nivārentī Kalyāṇe nivesentī Sippaṃ sikkhāpentī Patirūpenā

Samaye dāyajjaṃ niyyādentīti samaye dhanaṃ denti. Tattha niccasamayo kālasamayoti dve samayā. Niccasamaye denti nāma ‘‘uṭṭhāya samuṭṭhāya imaṃ gaṇhitabbaṃ gaṇha, ayaṃ te paribbayo hotu, iminā kusalaṃ karohī’’ti denti. Kālasamaye denti nāma sikhāṭhapanaāvāhavivāhādisamaye denti. Apica pacchime kāle maraṇamañce nipannassa ‘‘iminā kusalaṃ karohī’’ti dentāpi samaye denti nāma. Paṭicchannā hotīti yaṃ puratthimadisato bhayaṃ āgaccheyya, yathā taṃ nāgacchati, evaṃ pihitā hoti. Sace hi puttā vippaṭipannā, assu, mātāpitaro daharakālato paṭṭhāya jagganādīhi sammā paṭipannā, ete dārakā, mātāpitūnaṃ appatirūpāti etaṃ bhayaṃ āgaccheyya. Puttā sammā paṭipannā, mātāpitaro vippaṭipannā, mātāpitaro puttānaṃ nānurūpāti etaṃ bhayaṃ āgaccheyya. Ubhosu vippaṭipannesu duvidhampi taṃ bhayaṃ hoti. Sammā paṭipannesu sabbaṃ na hoti. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘paṭicchannā hoti khemā appaṭibhayā’’ti.

Samaye dāyajjaṃ niyyādentī Niccasamaye Kālasamaye Paṭicchannā hotī

Evañca pana vatvā bhagavā siṅgālakaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘na kho te, gahapatiputta, pitā lokasammataṃ puratthimaṃ disaṃ namassāpeti. Mātāpitaro pana puratthimadisāsadise katvā namassāpeti. Ayañhi te pitarā puratthimā disā akkhātā, no aññā’’ti.
commentary_english:
267. “They supported me, I will not support them” means: I was supported, raised, brought up by my parents as they breastfed me, helped my hands and feet to grow, removed my nasal mucus with their mouth, bathed me and adorned me. I myself today will support them, old as they are, by washing their feet, bathing them, giving them rice meals etc.

“I will do what they are required to do” means: setting aside my own agenda, I will go and take care of any requirement incumbent upon my parents that might arise in the royal court and other official sites.

“I will further the tradition of my family” means: I will further the tradition of my family through not dissipating it, through protecting my parents’ property, their fields, goods, gold and money, etc.

The parents, having turned away from the unrighteous tradition, also establish their children in the righteous tradition. Moreover, by not interrupting the *salākabhatta* (food distributed by ticket) and other traditions that have come down through the family, they further the family tradition.

This is said with reference to the statement: “I will further the tradition of my family.”

“I will do what they are required to do.”

“I will further the tradition of my family.”

“I will worthily receive the inheritance” means: if their children do not abide by their instructions and misbehave, the parents pronounce a legal statement to repudiate them as their offspring. These are unfit to inherit.
If, on the other hand, their children abide by their instructions, the parents turn them into the owners of the family property. Thus, abiding by their instructions, I will worthily receive the inheritance.

“I will worthily receive the inheritance.”

“I will give them appropriate gifts” means: having made over to them the merit, I will give them gifts starting from the third day.

“They stop him from what is evil” means: they tell him how killing living beings and the other evil actions entail a danger for one’s present and future lives, and stop him, saying: “My dear, don’t do an action like this!” If it is already done,’ they disapprove of it.

“They establish him in virtue” means: like Anāthapiṇḍika, even having given wealth, they establish them in morality (*śīla*) and taking up vows (*samādāna*), and so on.

“They teach him some skill” means: having known that he is standing in their instruction, they teach him the skills appropriate to the family, such as accounting with seals and so forth.

“With a suitable wife” means: with a wife who is suitable in family, morality (*śīla*), beauty (*rūpa*), and so forth.

“I will give them appropriate gifts.”

“They stop him from what is evil.”

“They establish him in virtue.”

“They teach him some skill.”

“With a suitable wife.”

“They hand over the inheritance in due time” means: they give wealth in due time (*samaya*).

Here, there are two proper times (*samaya*): on a regular basis (*nityasamaya*) and on fixed occasions (*kālasamaya*).

They “give it on a regular basis” (*nityasamaya*) when they give it, saying, “Get up, stand up, and take this. It is yours to spend. Do anything good with it.”

They “give it at a proper time” (*kālasamaya*) when they give it at the time of tonsure, marriage, wedding, and so forth.

Moreover, they “give it at a proper time” (*samaya*) also when they give it at the time of their passing away, when one of them is lying on their deathbed, saying. “Do anything good with it!”

“She is sheltered” means: just as the fear that might come from the eastern direction does not come, in the same way she is shielded.

If, however, the sons are misbehaving, there might come this fear that, although the parents have properly attended to them with nursing and so forth from the time they were young, these children are not suitable to their parents.

[Alternatively,] if the sons are well-behaved, [there might come this fear] that the parents are misbehaving, [that] the parents are not suitable to their sons.

When both are misbehaving, this double fear exists.

When all are well-behaved, none of this exists.

Therefore it was said: “She is sheltered, secure, and free from fear.”

“They hand over the inheritance in due time.”

“On a regular basis” (*nityasamaya*).

“At a proper time” (*kālasamaya*).

“She is sheltered.”

Having spoken thus, the Blessed One said this to Siṅgālaka: “It was not, son of the householder, that your father paid homage to the eastern direction which is recognized by the world.

Rather, your parents, having made the eastern direction equivalent to themselves, paid homage.

This, indeed, is the eastern direction that was explained to you by your father, not another."

mula_pali: 268. ‘‘Pañcahi kho, gahapatiputta, ṭhānehi antevāsinā dakkhiṇā disā ācariyā paccupaṭṭhātabbā – uṭṭhānena upaṭṭhānena sussusāya pāricariyāya sakkaccaṃ sippapaṭiggahaṇena sippaṃ paṭiggahaṇena (syā.), sippauggahaṇena (ka.). Imehi kho, gahapatiputta, pañcahi ṭhānehi antevāsinā dakkhiṇā disā ācariyā paccupaṭṭhitā pañcahi ṭhānehi antevāsiṃ anukampanti – suvinītaṃ vinenti, suggahitaṃ gāhāpenti, sabbasippassutaṃ samakkhāyino bhavanti, mittāmaccesu paṭiyādenti paṭivedenti (syā.), disāsu parittāṇaṃ karonti. Imehi kho, gahapatiputta, pañcahi ṭhānehi antevāsinā dakkhiṇā disā ācariyā paccupaṭṭhitā imehi pañcahi ṭhānehi antevāsiṃ anukampanti. Evamassa esā dakkhiṇā disā paṭicchannā hoti khemā appaṭibhayā.
mula_english: “In five ways, householder’s son, should a pupil attend upon teachers as the southern direction: by rising (to greet them), by waiting on them, by being attentive, by serving them, by carefully receiving instruction in their craft. And in five ways, the teachers, thus attended to by the pupil as the southern direction, show compassion to the pupil: they train them in proper discipline, ensure they have grasped what they should have duly grasped, give them a thorough grounding in all skills, recommend them to their friends and colleagues, and provide them with security in all directions. In these five ways, householder’s son, the teachers as the southern direction are attended to by a pupil, and in these five ways they show compassion to the pupil. Thus, this southern direction is protected, made peaceful and free from fear.
commentary_pali:
268.Uṭṭhānenāti āsanā uṭṭhānena. Antevāsikena hi ācariyaṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ disvā āsanā vuṭṭhāya paccuggamanaṃ katvā hatthato bhaṇḍakaṃ gahetvā āsanaṃ paññapetvā nisīdāpetvā bījanapādadhovanapādamakkhanāni kātabbāni. Taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ ‘‘uṭṭhānenā’’ti. Upaṭṭhānenāti divasassa tikkhattuṃ upaṭṭhānagamanena. Sippuggahaṇakāle pana avassakameva gantabbaṃ hoti. Sussūsāyāti saddahitvā savanena. Asaddahitvā suṇanto hi visesaṃ nādhigacchati. Pāricariyāyāti avasesakhuddakapāricariyāya. Antevāsikena hi ācariyassa pātova vuṭṭhāya mukhodakadantakaṭṭhaṃ datvā bhattakiccakālepi pānīyaṃ gahetvā paccupaṭṭhānādīni katvā vanditvā gantabbaṃ. Kiliṭṭhavatthādīni dhovitabbāni, sāyaṃ nahānodakaṃ paccupaṭṭhapetabbaṃ. Aphāsukāle upaṭṭhātabbaṃ. Pabbajitenapi sabbaṃ antevāsikavattaṃ kātabbaṃ. Idaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ – ‘‘pāricariyāyā’’ti. Sakkaccaṃ sippapaṭiggahaṇenāti sakkaccaṃ paṭiggahaṇaṃ nāma thokaṃ gahetvā bahuvāre sajjhāyakaraṇaṃ, ekapadampi visuddhameva gahetabbaṃ.

Suvinītaṃ vinentīti ‘‘evaṃ te nisīditabbaṃ, evaṃ ṭhātabbaṃ, evaṃ khāditabbaṃ, evaṃ bhuñjitabbaṃ, pāpamittā vajjetabbā, kalyāṇamittā sevitabbā’’ti evaṃ ācāraṃ sikkhāpenti vinenti. Suggahitaṃ gāhāpentīti yathā suggahitaṃ gaṇhāti, evaṃ atthañca byañjanañca sodhetvā payogaṃ dassetvā gaṇhāpenti. Mittāmaccesu paṭiyādentīti ‘‘ayaṃ amhākaṃ antevāsiko byatto bahussuto mayā samasamo, etaṃ sallakkheyyāthā’’ti evaṃ guṇaṃ kathetvā mittāmaccesu patiṭṭhapenti.

Suvinītaṃ vinentī Suggahitaṃ gāhāpentī Mittāmaccesu paṭiyādentī

Disāsu parittāṇaṃ karontīti sippasikkhāpanenevassa sabbadisāsu rakkhaṃ karonti. Uggahitasippo hi yaṃ yaṃ disaṃ gantvā sippaṃ dasseti, tattha tatthassa lābhasakkāro uppajjati. So ācariyena kato nāma hoti, guṇaṃ kathentopissa mahājano ācariyapāde dhovitvā vasitaantevāsiko vata ayanti paṭhamaṃ ācariyasseva guṇaṃ kathenti, brahmalokappamāṇopissa lābho uppajjamāno ācariyasantakova hoti. Apica yaṃ vijjaṃ parijappitvā gacchantaṃ aṭaviyaṃ corā na passanti, amanussā vā dīghajātiādayo vā na viheṭhenti, taṃ sikkhāpentāpi disāsu parittāṇaṃ karonti. Yaṃ vā so disaṃ gato hoti, tato kaṅkhaṃ uppādetvā attano santikaṃ āgatamanusse ‘‘etissaṃ disāyaṃ amhākaṃ antevāsiko vasati, tassa ca mayhañca imasmiṃ sippe nānākaraṇaṃ natthi, gacchatha tameva pucchathā’’ti evaṃ antevāsikaṃ paggaṇhantāpi tassa tattha lābhasakkāruppattiyā parittāṇaṃ karonti nāma, patiṭṭhaṃ karontīti attho. Sesamettha purimanayeneva yojetabbaṃ.

Disāsu parittāṇaṃ karontī
commentary_english:
268. "By rising" means by rising from one's seat.

For a pupil ( *antevāsika*) having seen his teacher (*ācāriya*) coming from afar, must rise from his seat, approach him, make a greeting, take his bowl from his hands, prepare a seat, invite him to sit down, fan him, wash his feet, and anoint his feet.

The expression “by rising” refers to this.

"By ministering to them" means: by going to minister to to them three times a day.

And when one is learning a profession (*śilpa*), one must inevitably go.

"By diligence" means by listening with conviction.

for one who listens without conviction does not attain distinction.

"By attending upon him" refers to all the remaining minor services.

For a pupil must get up early in the morning, give water for rinsing his mouth and a tooth stick to his master, fetch water also at lunch, provide anything needed, etc., and revere him.

He must wash the dirty clothes, etc. At night, he must provide bathing water.

When his master is not well, he must minister to him.

As for an ordained person, he himself must undertake the duties related to the status of “pupil”.

The expression “by attending upon him” refers to all this.

"By respectfully accepting a profession" means respectfully accepting means taking a little and reviewing many times; even one word must be taken purely.

"By training the well-trained," means they train and discipline, saying, "You should sit like this, you should stand like this, you should eat like this, you should enjoy like this, bad friends should be avoided, good friends should be cultivated."

"By causing the well-grasped to be grasped," means just as he grasps the well-grasped, so too, having purified both the meaning ( *artha*) and the letter (*byañjana*), having shown the application, they cause him to grasp.

"They establish him among their friends and companions" means they establish him among their friends and companions, praising him thus: “this pupil of ours is skilled, learned, my equal; consider him as such!”

Ensuring the safety in every quarter, they protect him in all quarters by teaching him a profession.

For if one has learnt a profession, one obtains gain and honor everywhere, in whatever quarter one has gone to practice one’s profession.

He is called "made by a master". Even when praising him, the people first praise his master, saying, “This is indeed a pupil who has grown up washing his master’s feet.” The resulting gain, even if it reached the world of Brahmās, belongs to his master.

Moreover, they ensure his safety in every quarter also by teaching him the spell to mutter so that thieves do not see him going in the forest or so that he is not injured by non-human beings or by snakes and the like.

If he has gone to a different quarter, then they “ensure the safety” of - meaning, they provide help for - gain and honor accruing to him in that quarter, by favoring their pupil also in the following way: When a man comes to them because he has a doubt about him, they say a pupil of ours lives in this quarter; there is no difference between myself and him in this subject. Go and ask him.”

Here in the section on the previous method everything else should be construed just as above.

mula_pali: 269. ‘‘Pañcahi kho, gahapatiputta, ṭhānehi sāmikena pacchimā disā bhariyā paccupaṭṭhātabbā – sammānanāya anavamānanāya avimānanāya (syā. pī.) anaticariyāya issariyavossaggena alaṅkārānuppadānena. Imehi kho, gahapatiputta, pañcahi ṭhānehi sāmikena pacchimā disā bhariyā paccupaṭṭhitā pañcahi ṭhānehi sāmikaṃ anukampati – susaṃvihitakammantā ca hoti, saṅgahitaparijanā susaṅgahitaparijanā (sī. syā. pī.) ca, anaticārinī ca, sambhatañca anurakkhati, dakkhā ca hoti analasā sabbakiccesu. Imehi kho, gahapatiputta, pañcahi ṭhānehi sāmikena pacchimā disā bhariyā paccupaṭṭhitā imehi pañcahi ṭhānehi sāmikaṃ anukampati. Evamassa esā pacchimā disā paṭicchannā hoti khemā appaṭibhayā.
mula_english:
269. “In five ways, householder's son, should a wife as the western direction be attended to by a husband: by honoring (sammānanāya), by not despising (anavamānanāya), by not being unfaithful (anaticariyāya), by giving authority (issariyavossaggena), and by providing adornments (alaṅkārānuppadānena).

And in five ways, householder's son, a wife, thus ministered to by her husband as the western direction, reciprocates with compassion towards her husband: she is well-organized in her work (susaṃvihitakammantā ca hoti), her retainers are properly supported (saṅgahitaparijanā ca), she does not betray him (anaticārinī ca), she protects what has been earned (sambhatañca anurakkhati), and she is clever and industrious in all tasks (dakkhā ca hoti analasā sabbakiccesu).

And in five ways, householder's son, a wife, thus ministered to by her husband as the western direction, reciprocates with compassion towards her husband. In this way, the western direction is protected (paticchannā hoti), and made peaceful (khemā) and secure (appaṭibhayā).
commentary_pali: 269. Tatiyadisāvāre sammānanāyāti devamāte tissamāteti evaṃ sambhāvitakathākathanena. Anavamānanāyāti yathā dāsakammakarādayo pothetvā viheṭhetvā kathenti, evaṃ hīḷetvā vimānetvā akathanena. Anaticariyāyāti taṃ atikkamitvā bahi aññāya itthiyā saddhiṃ paricaranto taṃ aticarati nāma, tathā akaraṇena. Issariyavossaggenāti itthiyo hi mahālatāsadisampi ābharaṇaṃ labhitvā bhattaṃ vicāretuṃ alabhamānā kujjhanti, kaṭacchuṃ hatthe ṭhapetvā tava ruciyā karohīti bhattagehe vissaṭṭhe sabbaṃ issariyaṃ vissaṭṭhaṃ nāma hoti, evaṃ karaṇenāti attho. Alaṅkārānuppadānenāti attano vibhavānurūpena alaṅkāradānena. Susaṃvihitakammantāti yāgubhattapacanakālādīni anatikkamitvā tassa tassa sādhukaṃ karaṇena suṭṭhu saṃvihitakammantā. Saṅgahitaparijanāti sammānanādīhi ceva paheṇakapesanādīhi ca saṅgahitaparijanā. Idha parijano nāma sāmikassa ceva attano ca ñātijano. Anaticārinīti sāmikaṃ muñcitvā aññaṃ manasāpi na pattheti. Sambhatanti kasivāṇijjādīni katvā ābhatadhanaṃ. Dakkhāca hotīti yāgubhattasampādanādīsu chekā nipuṇā hoti. Analasāti nikkosajjā. Yathā aññā kusītā nisinnaṭṭhāne nisinnāva honti ṭhitaṭṭhāne ṭhitāva, evaṃ ahutvā vipphāritena cittena sabbakiccāni nipphādeti. Sesamidhāpi purimanayeneva yojetabbaṃ.
commentary_english:
269.
“By honoring her” means: by speaking words of respect, such as “Devamātā,” “Tissamātā,” and so forth.
“By not disrespecting her” means: by not referring to her despisingly, injuriously, lest servants, workmen, and others refer to her harassingly, injuriously.
“By not being unfaithful to her” means: by not transgressing against her, going outside and associating with another woman; that is called being unfaithful, and [is avoided] by not doing that.
“By handing over authority to her” means: Women, even though they receive an ornament as long as a creeper, if they are not allowed to look after the food, they are discontent. All authority is handed over when the kitchen is handed over by putting a ladle in their hands saying, “Do as you like!”
“By not failing to provide ornaments” means: by giving ornaments in accordance with her own means.
“Being of well-ordered activities” means: without overstepping the proper times for rice-gruel, cooked rice, cooking, and so forth, by doing each of these things properly, she is truly of well-ordered activities.
“Having gathered attendants” means: having gathered attendants with acts of respect, and with gifts and sending messages, and so forth.
Here ‘attendants’ are her husband’s and her own relatives.
“Not being unfaithful” means: without deserting her husband, she does not desire another even in her mind.
“Having acquired” means: having acquired wealth by doing farming, trade, and so forth.
“Being clever and skilled” means: she is clever and skilled in preparing rice-gruel, cooked rice, and so forth.
“Not being lazy” means: being without sloth.
Other indolent women just sit where they sit, and just stand where they stand; unlike them, she fulfils all her duties, thinking of everything.
Here too in the section on the third quarter everything else should be construed just as above.

mula_pali: 270. ‘‘Pañcahi kho, gahapatiputta, ṭhānehi kulaputtena uttarā disā mittāmaccā paccupaṭṭhātabbā – dānena peyyavajjena viyavajjena (syā. ka.) atthacariyāya samānattatāya avisaṃvādanatāya. Imehi kho, gahapatiputta, pañcahi ṭhānehi kulaputtena uttarā disā mittāmaccā paccupaṭṭhitā pañcahi ṭhānehi kulaputtaṃ anukampanti – pamattaṃ rakkhanti, pamattassa sāpateyyaṃ rakkhanti, bhītassa saraṇaṃ honti, āpadāsu na vijahanti, aparapajā cassa paṭipūjenti. Imehi kho, gahapatiputta, pañcahi ṭhānehi kulaputtena uttarā disā mittāmaccā paccupaṭṭhitā imehi pañcahi ṭhānehi kulaputtaṃ anukampanti. Evamassa esā uttarā disā paṭicchannā hoti khemā appaṭibhayā.
mula_english: “In five ways, householder's son, should a clansman minister to friends and colleagues as the northern direction: by giving (dānena), by amiable speech (peyyavajjena), by promoting their welfare (atthacariyāya), by treating them impartially (samānattatāya), and by being true to his word (avisaṃvādanatāya). And in five ways, householder's son, friends and colleagues, thus ministered to by a clansman as the northern direction, will reciprocate: they protect him when he is heedless (pamattaṃ rakkhanti), they protect his property when he is heedless (pamattassa sāpateyyaṃ rakkhanti), they are a refuge when he is afraid (bhītassa saraṇaṃ honti), they do not forsake him in adversities (āpadāsu na vijahanti), and they show consideration for his descendants (aparapajā cassa paṭipūjenti). In these five ways, householder's son, a clansman thus attends to friends and colleagues as the northern direction, and in these five ways they reciprocate. Thus, this northern direction is covered, secure, and free from fear (khemā appaṭibhayā)."
commentary_pali: 270. Catutthadisāvāre avisaṃvādanatāyāti yassa yassa nāmaṃ gaṇhāti, taṃ taṃ avisaṃvādetvā idampi amhākaṃ gehe atthi, idampi atthi, gahetvā gacchāhīti evaṃ avisaṃvādetvā dānena. Aparapajā cassa paṭipūjentīti sahāyassa puttadhītaro pajā nāma, tesaṃ pana puttadhītaro ca nattupanattakā ca aparapajā nāma. Te paṭipūjenti keḷāyanti mamāyanti maṅgalakālādīsu tesaṃ maṅgalādīni karonti. Sesamidhāpi purimanayeneva veditabbaṃ.
commentary_english:
270. "By not deceiving them" (avisaṃvādanatāyā) means: not deceiving about anything a needy friend mentions, e.g. by giving it without deceiving, thus: "I have it at home, I have it at home. Take it!" By *dāna*.

"And they honour his further descendants" (aparapajā cassa paṭipūjentī) means: a companion’s sons and daughters are called “descendants” (pajā nāma), and their sons, daughters, nephews, and nieces are called his “further descendants” (aparapajā nāma).

They cherish them, are fond of them (keḷāyanti), and love them (mamāyanti). On the date of ceremonies and other festivities (maṅgalakālādīsu), they take part in their ceremonies and in other festivities (maṅgalādīni karonti).

Here too in the section on the fourth quarter everything else should be construed just as above (purimanayeneva veditabbaṃ).

mula_pali: 271. ‘‘Pañcahi kho, gahapatiputta, ṭhānehi ayyirakena ayirakena (sī. syā. pī.) heṭṭhimā disā dāsakammakarā paccupaṭṭhātabbā – yathābalaṃ kammantasaṃvidhānena bhattavetanānuppadānena gilānupaṭṭhānena acchariyānaṃ rasānaṃ saṃvibhāgena samaye vossaggena. Imehi kho, gahapatiputta, pañcahi ṭhānehi ayyirakena heṭṭhimā disā dāsakammakarā paccupaṭṭhitā pañcahi ṭhānehi ayyirakaṃ anukampanti – pubbuṭṭhāyino ca honti, pacchā nipātino ca, dinnādāyino ca, sukatakammakarā ca, kittivaṇṇaharā ca. Imehi kho, gahapatiputta, pañcahi ṭhānehi ayyirakena heṭṭhimā disā dāsakammakarā paccupaṭṭhitā imehi pañcahi ṭhānehi ayyirakaṃ anukampanti. Evamassa esā heṭṭhimā disā paṭicchannā hoti khemā appaṭibhayā.
mula_english:
“Householder, there are five ways in which an employer should minister to their workers and servants who represent the lower direction: by organizing work according to their strength ( *yathābalaṃ kammantasaṃvidhānena*), by providing food and wages (*bhattavetanānuppadānena*), by looking after them when they are ill (*gilānupaṭṭhānena*), by sharing special treats (*acchariyānaṃ rasānaṃ saṃvibhāgena*), and by giving them reasonable time off (*samaye vossaggena*).

And, householder, workers and servants who are thus ministered to by their employer in these five ways will reciprocate with compassion in five ways: they will be willing to start work early, and finish late when necessary (*pubbuṭṭhāyino ca honti, pacchā nipātino ca*); they will take only what is given (*dinnādāyino ca*); they will do their work well (*sukatakammakarā ca*); and they will promote a good reputation (*kittivaṇṇaharā ca*).

And, householder, when workers and servants are ministered to by their employer in these five ways, they reciprocate with compassion in these same five ways.

In this way, this lower direction is protected, made peaceful and free from fear (*evamassa esā heṭṭhimā disā paṭicchannā hoti khemā appaṭibhayā*)."
commentary_pali: 271.Yathābalaṃ kammantasaṃvidhānenāti daharehi kātabbaṃ mahallakehi, mahallakehi vā kātabbaṃ daharehi, itthīhi kātabbaṃ purisehi, purisehi vā kātabbaṃ itthīhi akāretvā tassa tassa balānurūpeneva kammantasaṃvidhānena. Bhattavetanānuppadānenāti ayaṃ khuddakaputto, ayaṃ ekavihārīti tassa tassa anurūpaṃ sallakkhetvā bhattadānena ceva paribbayadānena ca. Gilānupaṭṭhānenāti aphāsukakāle kammaṃ akāretvā sappāyabhesajjādīni datvā paṭijagganena. Acchariyānaṃ rasānaṃ saṃvibhāgenāti acchariye madhurarase labhitvā sayameva akhāditvā tesampi tato saṃvibhāgakaraṇena. Samaye vossaggenāti niccasamaye ca kālasamaye ca vossajjanena. Niccasamaye vossajjanaṃ nāma sakaladivasaṃ kammaṃ karontā kilamanti. Tasmā yathā na kilamanti, evaṃ velaṃ ñatvā vissajjanaṃ. Kālasamaye vossaggo nāma chaṇanakkhattakīḷādīsu alaṅkārabhaṇḍakhādanīyabhojanīyādīni datvā vissajjanaṃ. Dinnādāyinoti corikāya kiñci agahetvā sāmikehi dinnasseva ādāyino. Sukatakammakarāti ‘‘kiṃ etassa kammena katena, na mayaṃ kiñci labhāmā’’ti anujjhāyitvā tuṭṭhahadayā yathā taṃ kammaṃ sukataṃ hoti, evaṃ kārakā. Kittivaṇṇaharāti parisamajjhe kathāya sampattāya ‘‘ko amhākaṃ sāmikehi sadiso atthi, mayaṃ attano dāsabhāvampi na jānāma, tesaṃ sāmikabhāvampi na jānāma, evaṃ no anukampantī’’ti guṇakathāhārakā. Sesamidhāpi purimanayeneva yojetabbaṃ.
commentary_english:
271. “By organizing their work according to their strength” ( *yathābalaṃ kammantasaṃvidhānenā* ) means: what should be done by the young (*daharehi kātabbaṃ mahallakehi*), or what should be done by the old be done by the young (*mahallakehi vā kātabbaṃ daharehi*), or what should be done by women be done by men (*itthīhi kātabbaṃ purisehi*), or what should be done by men be done by women (*purisehi vā kātabbaṃ itthīhi akāretvā*) by organizing their work just according to the strength of each of them (*tassa tassa balānurūpeneva kammantasaṃvidhānena*).

“By appropriately supplying them with food and salary” (*bhattavetanānuppadānenā* ) means: considering what is appropriate to this or that servant or employee, thinking, “This one has a small child; this one lives alone” (*ayaṃ khuddakaputto, ayaṃ ekavihārīti*), by giving food (*bhattadānena ceva*) and by giving a salary (*paribbayadānena ca*).

“Through tending to the sick” (*gilānupaṭṭhānenā*) means: without making them work at an unsuitable time (*aphāsukakāle kammaṃ akāretvā*), by giving suitable medicine and so on (*sappāyabhesajjādīni datvā*) and by tending to them (*paṭijagganena*).

“Through sharing extraordinary flavors” (*acchariyānaṃ rasānaṃ saṃvibhāgenā*) means: having obtained an extraordinary, delicious flavor (*acchariye madhurarase labhitvā*), without eating it oneself (*sayam eva akhāditvā*), by sharing it with them (*tesampi tato saṃvibhāgakaraṇena*).

“Through granting leave at the right time” (*samaye vossaggenā*) means: by granting leave at a fixed time and at a seasonal time (*niccasamaye ca kālasamaye ca vossajjanena*).

"At a fixed time ( *niccasamaye* )" granting leave means: those who do work all day become tired ( *vossajjanaṃ nāma sakaladivasaṃ kammaṃ karontā kilamanti*).

Therefore, knowing the time (*velaṃ ñatvā*) grant them leave (*vissajjanaṃ*) so that they will not be fatigued (*tasmā yathā na kilamanti, evaṃ*).

"At a seasonal time ( *kālasamaye* )" granting leave means: giving ornaments, goods, food, and nourishment, and so on (*chaṇanakkhattakīḷādīsu alaṅkārabhaṇḍakhādanīyabhojanīyādīni datvā*) at festivals, asterisms, games, and so on, grant leave (*vissajjanaṃ*).

“Those who take only what is given” (*dinnādāyino*) means: without taking anything by theft (*corikāya kiñci agahetvā*), they take only what is given by the masters (*sāmikehi dinnasseva ādāyino*).

“They work well” (*sukatakammakarā*) means: glad at heart (*tuṭṭhahadayā*), they work so that their job is well done (*yathā taṃ kammaṃ sukataṃ hoti*), without growing annoyed at the thought “Why am I doing this job? I don’t get anything” (*kiṃ etassa kammena katena, na mayaṃ kiñci labhāmāti anujjhāyitvā*), thus they are workers (*evaṃ kārakā*).

“They spread his prestige and fame” (*kittivaṇṇaharā*) means: when a conversation arises in the middle of an assembly (*parisamajjhe kathāya sampattāya*), they spread his praises saying, “Who is the like of our masters? We do not think of ourselves as their servants, nor do we think of them as our masters: so much they show us their affection!” (*ko amhākaṃ sāmikehi sadiso atthi, mayaṃ attano dāsabhāvampi na jānāma, tesaṃ sāmikabhāvampi na jānāma, evaṃ no anukampantīti guṇakathāhārakā*).

Here too in the section on the third quarter everything else should be construed just as above (*sesamidhāpi purimanayeneva yojetabbaṃ*).

mula_pali: 272. ‘‘Pañcahi kho, gahapatiputta, ṭhānehi kulaputtena uparimā disā samaṇabrāhmaṇā paccupaṭṭhātabbā – mettena kāyakammena mettena vacīkammena mettena manokammena anāvaṭadvāratāya āmisānuppadānena. Imehi kho, gahapatiputta, pañcahi ṭhānehi kulaputtena uparimā disā samaṇabrāhmaṇā paccupaṭṭhitā chahi ṭhānehi kulaputtaṃ anukampanti – pāpā nivārenti, kalyāṇe nivesenti, kalyāṇena manasā anukampanti, assutaṃ sāventi, sutaṃ pariyodāpenti, saggassa maggaṃ ācikkhanti. Imehi kho, gahapatiputta, pañcahi ṭhānehi kulaputtena uparimā disā samaṇabrāhmaṇā paccupaṭṭhitā imehi chahi ṭhānehi kulaputtaṃ anukampanti. Evamassa esā uparimā disā paṭicchannā hoti khemā appaṭibhayā’’ti.
mula_english: "Householder, a clansman should attend to ascetics and Brahmins as the upper direction in five ways: with loving physical actions, with loving verbal actions, with loving mental actions, with open doors, and by supplying their material needs. Householder, ascetics and Brahmins, thus attended to by a clansman as the upper direction, show their compassion to the clansman in six ways: they restrain him from evil, encourage him to do good, feel compassion for him with a compassionate heart, teach him what he has not heard, clarify what he has already heard, and point out the path to heaven. Householder, ascetics and Brahmins are thus attended to by a clansman as the upper direction and show their compassion to the clansman in these six ways. In this way, this upper direction is protected, safe, and free from fear."
commentary_pali:
272.Mettena kāyakammenātiādīsu mettacittaṃ paccupaṭṭhapetvā katāni kāyakammādīni mettāni nāma vuccanti. Tattha bhikkhū nimantessāmīti vihāragamanaṃ , dhamakaraṇaṃ gahetvā udakaparissāvanaṃ, piṭṭhiparikammapādaparikammādikaraṇañca mettaṃ kāyakammaṃ nāma. Bhikkhū piṇḍāya paviṭṭhe disvā ‘‘sakkaccaṃ yāguṃ detha, bhattaṃ dethā’’tiādivacanañceva, sādhukāraṃ datvā dhammasavanañca sakkaccaṃ paṭisanthārakaraṇādīni ca mettaṃ vacīkammaṃ nāma. ‘‘Amhākaṃ kulūpakattherā averā hontu abyāpajjā’’ti evaṃ cintanaṃ mettaṃ manokammaṃ nāma. Anāvaṭadvāratāyāti apihitadvāratāya. Tattha sabbadvārāni vivaritvāpi sīlavantānaṃ adāyako akārako pihitadvāroyeva. Sabbadvārāni pana pidahitvāpi tesaṃ dāyako kārako vivaṭadvāroyeva. Iti sīlavantesu gehadvāraṃ āgatesu santaṃyeva natthīti avatvā dātabbaṃ. Evaṃ anāvaṭadvāratā nāma hoti.

Āmisānuppadānenāti purebhattaṃ paribhuñjitabbakaṃ āmisaṃ nāma, tasmā sīlavantānaṃ yāgubhattasampadānenāti attho. Kalyāṇena manasā anukampantīti ‘‘sabbe sattā sukhitā hontu averā arogā abyāpajjā’’ti evaṃ hitapharaṇena. Apica upaṭṭhākānaṃ gehaṃ aññe sīlavante sabrahmacārī gahetvā pavisantāpi kalyāṇena cetasā anukampanti nāma. Sutaṃ pariyodāpentīti yaṃ tesaṃ pakatiyā sutaṃ atthi, tassa atthaṃ kathetvā kaṅkhaṃ vinodenti, tathattāya vā paṭipajjāpenti. Sesamidhāpi purimanayeneva yojetabbaṃ.

Āmisānuppadānenā Kalyāṇena manasā anukampantī Sutaṃ pariyodāpentī
commentary_english:
272. “With affectionate bodily action (mettena kāyakammenā)” and so forth, bodily actions (kāyakamma) and so on, which are done after establishing a mind of loving-kindness ( *mettacittaṃ*), are called actions of loving-kindness (mettāni).

There, going to the monastery thinking, "I will invite the monks," taking the water filter, filtering water, and also doing things like massaging the back and feet, is called affectionate bodily action (mettāṃ *kāyakammaṃ*).

Seeing the monks entering for alms food, saying, "Respectfully give rice gruel (yāgu)! Give food (bhatta)!" and so forth, and also giving approval, giving a religious sermon (dhammasavana) respectfully, actions such as respectfully preparing a reception, are called affectionate verbal action (mettaṃ *vacīkammaṃ*).

“May the elders who are of service to our families be without enmity, without malice, without oppression (amhākaṃ kulūpakattherā averā hontu abyāpajjā),” such thinking is called affectionate mental action (mettaṃ *manokammaṃ*).

“Non-closing of the door (anāvaṭadvāratāyā)” means having the door unopened (apihitadvāratāya).

There, even having opened all the doors, one who is not a giver and not an actor to those who observe the precepts is indeed "one whose door is closed" (pihitadvāroyeva).

Conversely, even having closed all the doors, one who gives and acts for them is indeed "one whose door is open" (vivaṭadvāroyeva).

Therefore, when those who observe the precepts come to the door of the house, one must give what one has, without saying, "I don't have it (natthīti)."

In this sense, it is called “non-closing the door (anāvaṭadvāratā)” .
