“By not giving material things (āmisānuppadānenā)” means material things (āmisa) that should be enjoyed before the meal; therefore, it means giving an abundance of rice gruel (yāgu) and food (bhatta) to those who observe the precepts.

“Showing affection with a benevolent mind (kalyāṇena manasā anukampantī)” means, "May all beings be happy, without enmity, without disease, without oppression (sabbe sattā sukhitā hontu averā arogā abyāpajjā)," with such benefit.

Moreover, also when they enter a house of supporters with other fellow practitioners who observe the precepts, they show them affection with benevolent thoughts (kalyāṇena cetasā anukampanti nāma).

“Purifying what they have heard (sutaṃ pariyodāpentī)” means that they eliminate doubts explaining the meaning of what is ordinarily heard by them (tesaṃ pakatiyā sutaṃ atthi), or else they cause them to practice accordingly (tathattāya vā paṭipajjāpenti).

Here too in the section on the third quarter everything else should be construed just as above (sesamidhāpi purimanayeneva yojetabbaṃ).

Not giving material things (āmisānuppadānenā), showing affection with a benevolent mind (kalyāṇena manasā anukampantī), purifying what they have heard (sutaṃ pariyodāpentī).

mula_pali:
273. Idamavoca bhagavā. Idaṃ vatvāna sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā –

‘‘Mātāpitā disā pubbā, ācariyā dakkhiṇā disā;

Puttadārā disā pacchā, mittāmaccā ca uttarā.

‘‘Dāsakammakarā heṭṭhā, uddhaṃ samaṇabrāhmaṇā;

Etā disā namasseyya, alamatto kule gihī.

‘‘Paṇḍito sīlasampanno, saṇho ca paṭibhānavā;

Nivātavutti atthaddho, tādiso labhate yasaṃ.

‘‘Uṭṭhānako analaso, āpadāsu na vedhati;

Acchinnavutti medhāvī, tādiso labhate yasaṃ.

‘‘Saṅgāhako mittakaro, vadaññū vītamaccharo;

Netā vinetā anunetā, tādiso labhate yasaṃ.

‘‘Dānañca peyyavajjañca, atthacariyā ca yā idha;

Samānattatā ca dhammesu, tattha tattha yathārahaṃ;

Ete kho saṅgahā loke, rathassāṇīva yāyato.

‘‘Ete ca saṅgahā nāssu, na mātā puttakāraṇā;

Labhetha mānaṃ pūjaṃ vā, pitā vā puttakāraṇā.

‘‘Yasmā ca saṅgahā saṅgahe (ka.) aṭṭhakathāyaṃ icchitapāṭho ete, sammapekkhanti samavekkhanti (sī. pī. ka.) paṇḍitā;

saṅgahe (ka.) aṭṭhakathāyaṃ icchitapāṭho samavekkhanti (sī. pī. ka.)

Tasmā mahattaṃ papponti, pāsaṃsā ca bhavanti te’’ti.
commentary_pali:
273.Alamattoti puttadārabharaṇaṃ katvā agāraṃ ajjhāvasanasamattho. Paṇḍitoti disānamassanaṭṭhāne paṇḍito hutvā. Saṇhoti sukhumatthadassanena saṇhavācābhaṇanena vā saṇho hutvā. Paṭibhānavāti disānamassanaṭṭhāne paṭibhānavā hutvā nivātavuttīti nīcavutti. Atthaddhoti thambharahito. Uṭṭhānakoti uṭṭhānavīriyasampanno. Analasoti nikkosajjo. Acchinnavuttīti nirantarakaraṇavasena akhaṇḍavutti. Medhāvīti ṭhānuppattiyā paññāya samannāgato.

Saṅgāhakoti catūhi saṅgahavatthūhi saṅgahakaro. Mittakaroti mittagavesano. Vadaññūti pubbakārinā, vuttavacanaṃ jānāti. Sahāyakassa gharaṃ gatakāle ‘‘mayhaṃ sahāyakassa veṭhanaṃ detha, sāṭakaṃ detha, manussānaṃ bhattavetanaṃ dethā’’ti vuttavacanamanussaranto tassa attano gehaṃ āgatassa tattakaṃ vā tato atirekaṃ vā paṭikattāti attho. Apica sahāyakassa gharaṃ gantvā imaṃ nāma gaṇhissāmīti āgataṃ sahāyakaṃ lajjāya gaṇhituṃ asakkontaṃ anicchāritampi tassa vācaṃ ñatvā yena atthena so āgato, taṃ nipphādento vadaññū nāma. Yena yena vā pana sahāyakassa ūnaṃ hoti, oloketvā taṃ taṃ dentopi vadaññūyeva. Netāti taṃ taṃ atthaṃ dassento paññāya netā. Vividhāni kāraṇāni dassento netīti vinetā. Punappunaṃ netīti anunetā.

Saṅgāhako Mittakaro Vadaññū Netā vinetā. anunetā.

Tattha tatthāti tasmiṃ tasmiṃ puggale. Rathassāṇīva yāyatoti yathā āṇiyā satiyeva ratho yāti, asati na yāti, evaṃ imesu saṅgahesu satiyeva loko vattati, asati na vattati. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘ete kho saṅgahā loke, rathassāṇīva yāyato’’ti.

Tattha tatthā Rathassāṇīva yāyato

Na mātā puttakāraṇāti yadi mātā ete saṅgahe puttassa na kareyya, puttakāraṇā mānaṃ vā pūjaṃ vā na labheyya.

Na mātā puttakāraṇā

Saṅgahā eteti upayogavacane paccattaṃ. ‘‘Saṅgahe ete’’ti vā pāṭho. Sammapekkhantīti sammā pekkhanti. Pāsaṃsā ca bhavantīti pasaṃsanīyā ca bhavanti.

Saṅgahā ete Sammapekkhantī Pāsaṃsā ca bhavantī
commentary_english:
273. *Alamatto* means capable of dwelling in a house after having made provision for sons and wife.

*Paṇḍito* means being wise in the place of honoring the directions.

*Saṇho* means being gentle by seeing subtle meanings and speaking gentle words, or having become gentle.

*Paṭibhānavā* means being quick-witted in the place of honoring the directions, *nivātavuttī* means humble conduct.

*Atthaddho* means without stiffness.

*Uṭṭhānako* means endowed with energetic vigor.

*Analaso* means without laziness.

*Acchinnavuttī* means unbroken conduct due to continuous action.

*Medhāvī* means endowed with wisdom through the attainment of a basis.

*Saṅgāhako* means one who gathers with the four bases of sympathy ( *saṃgrahavastu* ).

*Mittakaro* means seeking friends.

*Vadaññū* means, by a former act, knowing the spoken word.

When a friend has gone to his house, understanding the spoken word, recalling, "Give my friend a wrap, give a cloth, give the servants their food wages," he repays the arriving friend with that much or more, that is the meaning.

Moreover, *vadaññū* is the name of one who, going to a friend's house and being unable to receive the arriving friend out of shame, thinking, "I will take this name," knowing his speech even though it is unuttered, accomplishes that with which he has come.

Or whatever is lacking for a friend, looking after that, even giving that, is indeed *vadaññū*.

*Netā* means showing that meaning, a leader by wisdom.

Showing various reasons, *netīti vinetā* means a guide.

*Punaḥ punaḥ netīti anunetā* means repeatedly guiding.

*Saṅgāhako*, *mittakaro*, *vadaññū*, *netā*, *vinetā*, *anunetā*.

*Tattha tatthā* means in that that person.

*Rathassāṇīva yāyato* means just as a chariot goes only when there is a pin, and does not go when there is not, so also in these gatherings the world goes on only when there is, and does not go on when there is not.

Therefore it was said - "These gatherings in the world are like the pin of a chariot going."

*Tattha tatthā*, *rathassāṇīva yāyato*.

*Na mātā puttakāraṇā* means if a mother would not do these gatherings for her son, she would not gain honor or worship on account of her son.

*Na mātā puttakāraṇā*, *saṅgahā ete* means individually in the expression of use.

Or " *saṅgahe ete* " is the reading.

*Sammapekkhantī* means rightly regarding.

*Pāsaṃsā ca bhavantī* means and they are praiseworthy.

*Saṅgahā ete*, *sammapekkhantī*, *pāsaṃsā ca bhavantī*.

mula_pali:
274. Evaṃ vutte, siṅgālako gahapatiputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘abhikkantaṃ, bhante! Abhikkantaṃ, bhante! Seyyathāpi, bhante, nikkujjitaṃ vā ukkujjeyya, paṭicchannaṃ vā vivareyya, mūḷhassa vā maggaṃ ācikkheyya, andhakāre vā telapajjotaṃ dhāreyya ‘cakkhumanto rūpāni dakkhantī’ti. Evamevaṃ bhagavatā anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito. Esāhaṃ, bhante, bhagavantaṃ saraṇaṃ gacchāmi dhammañca bhikkhusaṃghañca. Upāsakaṃ maṃ bhagavā dhāretu, ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata’’nti.

Siṅgālasuttaṃ siṅgālovādasuttantaṃ (pī.) niṭṭhitaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ.

siṅgālovādasuttantaṃ (pī.)
mula_english:
274. Thus, when this was said, Siṅgālaka, the householder's son, said this to the Blessed One: “Excellent, venerable sir! Excellent, venerable sir! Just as, venerable sir, one might set upright what has been overturned, or reveal what has been hidden, or show the way to one who is lost, or carry an oil lamp into the darkness so that those with eyes might see what is there—just so has the Blessed Lord expounded the *dharma* in various ways (*anekapariyāyena dhammo pakāsito*). I go for refuge to the Buddha (*bhagavantam saraṇaṃ gacchāmi*), the *dharma* (*dhammañca*), and the Saṃgha of monks (*bhikkhusaṃghañca*). May the Blessed Lord accept me from this day forth as a lay-follower (*upāsakaṃ*) as long as life shall last!”

The Siṅgāla Suttaṃ (Siṅgālovādasuttantaṃ) is finished, the eighth.

Note: Siṅgālovādasuttantaṃ.
commentary_pali:
274. Iti bhagavā yā disā sandhāya te gahapatiputta pitā āha ‘‘disā namasseyyāsī’’ti, imā tā cha disā. Yadi tvaṃ pitu vacanaṃ karosi, imā disā namassāti dassento siṅgālassa pucchāya ṭhatvā desanaṃ matthakaṃ pāpetvā rājagahaṃ piṇḍāya pāvisi . Siṅgālakopi saraṇesu patiṭṭhāya cattālīsakoṭidhanaṃ buddhasāsane vikiritvā puññakammaṃ katvā saggaparāyaṇo ahosi. Imasmiñca pana sutte yaṃ gihīhi kattabbaṃ kammaṃ nāma, taṃ akathitaṃ natthi, gihivinayo nāmāyaṃ suttanto. Tasmā imaṃ sutvā yathānusiṭṭhaṃ paṭipajjamānassa vuddhiyeva pāṭikaṅkhā, no parihānīti.

Sumaṅgalavilāsiniyā dīghanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Siṅgālasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
Thus, the Bhagavān, referring to the direction that your householder son's father spoke of, said, "You should pay homage to the directions." These are the six directions.

If you do the word of your father, showing Siṅgāla that you should pay homage to these directions, having stood to ask, bringing the teaching to its peak, he entered Rājagaha for alms.

Siṅgālaka also, having been established in the refuges, having scattered forty million wealth in the Buddha's teaching, having done meritorious action, became destined for heaven.

Moreover, in this *sutta*, that action which should be done by householders, there is nothing that is not spoken of. This *sutta* is called the "Vinaya for Householders."

Therefore, having heard this, for one who practices according to the instruction, only growth is to be expected, not decline.

The Siṅgāla Sutta Commentary is finished.

mula_pali: 275. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā rājagahe viharati gijjhakūṭe pabbate. Atha kho cattāro mahārājā mahārājāno (ka.) mahatiyā ca yakkhasenāya mahatiyā ca gandhabbasenāya mahatiyā ca kumbhaṇḍasenāya mahatiyā ca nāgasenāya catuddisaṃ rakkhaṃ ṭhapetvā catuddisaṃ gumbaṃ ṭhapetvā catuddisaṃ ovaraṇaṃ ṭhapetvā abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṃ gijjhakūṭaṃ pabbataṃ obhāsetvā gijjhakūṭaṃ obhāsetvā (sī. syā. pī.) yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Tepi kho yakkhā appekacce bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu, appekacce bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodiṃsu, sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu, appekacce yena bhagavā tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu, appekacce nāmagottaṃ sāvetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu, appekacce tuṇhībhūtā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu.
mula_english:
275. Thus have I heard. On one occasion the Blessed One (bhagavā) was dwelling at Rājagṛha on the mountain Vulture Peak (Gṛdhrakūṭa).

Then, the Four Great Kings (cattāro mahārājā), with a large army of *yakṣas* (yakṣasenā), a large army of *gandharvas* (gandhabbasenā), a large army of *kumbhāṇḍas* (kumbhaṇḍasenā), and a large army of *nāgas* (nāgasenā), having placed a guard over the four quarters, having placed troops in the four directions, having placed a barricade on four sides, when the night was far advanced, illuminating the entire Vulture's Peak with their surpassing radiance, approached the Blessed One; having approached, they respectfully greeted the Blessed One and sat down on one side.

Then some of those *yakṣas*, after worshipping the Blessed One, sat down on one side; some exchanged greetings with the Blessed One, and after exchanging polite and courteous greetings, sat down on one side; some, after raising their hands in respectful salutation (añjali) to the Blessed One, sat down on one side; some, after announcing their name and clan, sat down on one side; some, remaining silent, sat down on one side.
commentary_pali:
275.Evaṃme sutanti āṭānāṭiyasuttaṃ. Tatrāyamapubbapadavaṇṇanā – catuddisaṃ rakkhaṃ ṭhapetvāti asurasenāya nivāraṇatthaṃ sakkassa devānamindassa catūsu disāsu ārakkhaṃ ṭhapetvā. Gumbaṃ ṭhapetvāti balagumbaṃ ṭhapetvā. Ovaraṇaṃ ṭhapetvāti catūsu disāsu ārakkhake ṭhapetvā. Evaṃ sakkassa devānamindassa ārakkhaṃ susaṃvihitaṃ katvā āṭānāṭanagare nisinnā satta buddhe ārabbha imaṃ parittaṃ bandhitvā ‘‘ye satthu dhammaāṇaṃ amhākañca rājaāṇaṃ na suṇanti, tesaṃ idañcidañca karissāmā’’ti sāvanaṃ katvā attanopi catūsu disāsu mahatiyā ca yakkhasenāyātiādīhi catūhi senāhi ārakkhaṃ saṃvidahitvā abhikkantāya rattiyā…pe… ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu.

Abhikkantāya rattiyāti ettha abhikkantasaddo khayasundarābhirūpaabbhanumodanādīsu dissati. Tattha ‘‘abhikkantā, bhante ratti, nikkhanto paṭhamo yāmo, ciranisinno bhikkhusaṅgho uddisatu, bhante, bhagavā bhikkhūnaṃ pātimokkha’’nti (a. ni. 8.20) evamādīsu khaye dissati. ‘‘Ayaṃ imesaṃ catunnaṃ puggalānaṃ abhikkantataro paṇītataro cā’’ti (a. ni. 4.100) evamādīsu sundare.

Abhikkantāya rattiyā

‘‘Ko me vandati pādāni, iddhiyā yasasā jalaṃ;

Abhikkantena vaṇṇena, sabbā obhāsayaṃ disā’’ti. (vi. va. 857);

Evamādīsu abhirūpe. ‘‘Abhikkantaṃ, bho gotamāti (pārā. 15) evamādīsu abbhanumodane . Idha pana khaye. Tena abhikkantāya rattiyā, parikkhīṇāya rattiyāti vuttaṃ hoti.

Abhikkantavaṇṇāti idha abhikkantasaddo abhirūpe. Vaṇṇasaddo pana chavithutikulavaggakāraṇasaṇṭhānapamāṇarūpāyatanādīsu dissati. Tattha ‘‘suvaṇṇavaṇṇosi bhagavā’’ti (ma. ni. 2.399) evamādīsu chaviyaṃ. ‘‘Kadā saññūḷhā pana te, gahapati, ime samaṇassa gotamassa vaṇṇā’’ti (ma. ni. 2.77) evamādīsu thutiyaṃ. ‘‘Cattārome , bho gotama, vaṇṇā’’ti (dī. ni. 1.266) evamādīsu kulavagge. ‘‘Atha kena nu vaṇṇena gandhathenoti vuccatī’’tiādīsu (saṃ. ni. 1.234) kāraṇe. ‘‘Mahantaṃ hatthirājavaṇṇaṃ abhinimminitvā’’ti (saṃ. ni. 1.138) evamādīsu saṇṭhāne. ‘‘Tayo pattassa vaṇṇā’’ti (pārā. 602) evamādīsu pamāṇe. ‘‘Vaṇṇo gandho raso ojā’’ti evamādīsu rūpāyatane. So idha chaviyaṃ daṭṭhabbo. Tena ‘‘abhikkantavaṇṇā abhirūpacchavī’’ti vuttaṃ hoti.

Abhikkantavaṇṇā

Kevalakappanti ettha kevalasaddo anavasesayebhuyyaabyāmissānatirekadaḷhatthavisaṃyogādianekattho. Tathā hissa ‘‘kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariya’’nti (pārā. 1) evamādīsu anavasesatā attho. ‘‘Kevalakappā ca aṅgamāgadhā pahūtaṃ khādanīyaṃ bhojanīyaṃ ādāya abhikkamitukāmā hontī’’ti (mahāva. 43) evamādīsu yebhuyyatā. ‘‘Kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hotī’’ti (mahāva. 1) evamādīsu abyāmissatā. ‘‘Kevalaṃ saddhāmattakaṃ nūna ayamāyasmā’’ti (a. ni. 6.55) evamādīsu anatirekatā. ‘‘Āyasmato, bhante, anuruddhassa bāhiko nāma saddhivihāriko kevalakappaṃ saṅghabhedāya ṭhito’’ti (a. ni. 4.243) evamādīsu daḷhatthatā. ‘‘Kevalī vusitavā uttamapurisoti vuccatī’’ti (a. ni. 10.12) evamādīsu visaṃyogo. Idha panassa anavasesattho adhippeto.

Kevalakappa

Kappasaddo panāyaṃ abhisaddahanavohārakālapaññattichedanavikappalesasamantabhāvādianekattho. Tathā hissa ‘‘okappaniyametaṃ bhoto gotamassa. Yathā taṃ arahato sammāsambuddhassā’’ti (ma. ni. 1.387) evamādīsu abhisaddahanamattho. ‘‘Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pañcahi samaṇakappehi phalaṃ paribhuñjitu’’nti (cūḷava. 250) evamādīsu vohāro. ‘‘Yena sudaṃ niccakappaṃ viharāmī’’ti (ma. ni. 1.387) evamādīsu kālo. ‘‘Iccāyasmā kappo’’ti (su. ni. 1098) evamādīsu paññatti. ‘‘Alaṅkato kappitakesamassū’’ti (vi. va. 1094) evamādīsu chedanaṃ. ‘‘Kappati dvaṅgulakappo’’ti (cūḷava. 446) evamādīsu vikappo, atthi kappo nipajjitu’’nti (a. ni. 8.80) evamādīsu leso. ‘‘Kevalakappaṃ veḷuvanaṃ obhāsetvā’’ti (saṃ. ni. 1.94) evamādīsu samantabhāvo. Idha pana samantabhāvo attho adhippeto. Tasmā ‘‘kevalakappaṃ gijjhakūṭa’’nti ettha anavasesaṃ samantato gijjhakūṭanti evamattho daṭṭhabbo.

Obhāsetvāti vatthamālālaṅkārasarīrasamuṭṭhitāya ābhāya pharitvā, candimā viya sūriyo viya ca ekobhāsaṃ ekapajjotaṃ karitvāti attho. Ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsūti devatānaṃ dasabalassa santike nisinnaṭṭhānaṃ nāma na bahu, imasmiṃ pana sutte parittagāravavasena nisīdiṃsu.

Obhāsetvā Ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsū
commentary_english:
275. Thus have I heard: the Āṭānāṭiya Sutta.

Here is the word-by-word commentary: "Having established a defense in the four directions" means for the purpose of preventing the army of *asuras*, Sakka, the lord of the gods, having established protection in the four directions.

"Having established a troop" means having established a troop of strength.

"Having established a barrier" means having established guards in the four directions.

Having thus made the defense of Sakka, the lord of the gods, very well arranged, the seven Buddhas residing in Āṭānāṭa city, having composed this *paritta*, "Those who do not listen to the command of the Teacher, the *dhamma*, and our royal command, we will do this and that to them," having made this proclamation, and having arranged a defense for themselves in the four directions with four armies, beginning with the great army of *yakkhas*, [they] sat down to one side as the night was passing away…

Here, *abhikkanta* appears in the sense of exhaustion, beauty, handsomeness, approval, etc.

Here, in such passages as "The night is far spent, venerable sir, the first watch has passed, the community of monks has been sitting for a long time, may the Blessed One recite the Pātimokkha to the monks," it appears in the sense of exhaustion.

In such passages as "This is the most outstanding and excellent of these four persons," it is good.

*abhikkantāya rattiyā*

"Who bows to my feet, blazing with power and glory;
With surpassing beauty, illuminating all directions."

In such passages, [it means] handsome.

In such passages as "It is superb, Gotama," [it means] approval.

Here, however, it is in the sense of exhaustion. Therefore, *abhikkantāya rattiyā* means *parikkhīṇāya rattiyāti*, "when the night was becoming exhausted."

Here, *abhikkanta* appears in the sense of handsomeness. But *vaṇṇa* appears in the sense of skin, praise, clan group, reason, shape, measure, the form base, and so on.

Here, in such passages as "The Blessed One is golden-skinned," it refers to skin.

In such passages as "When did you concoct that hymn of praise to the monk Gotama, householder?", it is eulogy.
“‘These four, oh Gotama, are colors’ etc. (Dīgha Nikāya 3.1.0143, in the section on families).

“‘Then by what token can one tell a man to be a thief of scents?’ etc. (Saṃyutta Nikāya 1.234), it is a reason.

“‘Having created a great elephant-king-color’ etc. (Saṃyutta Nikāya 1.138), it is in configuration.

“‘These three are the colors of a bowl’ etc. (Pārājika 602), it is in measure.

“‘Color, odor, taste, nutritive essence’ etc., it is in the visible-form base (rūpāyatana).

Here it should be understood as skin (chavi).

Consequently ‘the extreme of whose brilliance’ means ‘the beauty of whose skin’.

The word *kevalakappa* here has various meanings such as remainderlessness (anavasesa), the most part (yebhuyya), unmixedness (abyāmissa), nothing extra (anatireka), firmness (daḷhattha), dissociation (visaṃyoga), and so on.

For in such passages as ‘A Divine Life as utterly perfect (kevalaparipuṇṇa) and pure (parisuddha), the meaning is remainderlessness (anavasesatā).

In such passages as ‘The whole (kevalakappa) of Aṅga and Magadha will come bringing quantities of food’ it is the most part (yebhuyyatā).

In such passages as “Of the whole (kevalassa) mass of suffering (dukkakkhandha) there is origination (samudayo)", it means unmixedness (abyāmissatā).

In such passages as ‘Surely it is only (kevalaṃ) by mere faith that this venerable one…’ it is with nothing extra (anatirekatā).

In such passages as ‘This co-resident of the venerable Anuruddha’s named Bāhika has taken his stand entirely (kevalakappaṃ) for the schism in the Community’ it is firmness (daḷhatthatā).

In such passages as ‘One who has reached the absolute (kevalī) lived out the life, is called the Supreme Man’ it is dissociation (visaṃyoga).

Here, however, the meaning intended is remainderlessness (anavasesattha).

The word *kappa* has also many meanings such as exercise of faith (abhisaddahana), lawfulness (vohāra), time (kāla), description (paññatti), cutting (chedana), interpretation (vikappa), fraction (lesa), surroundings (samantabhāva), and so on.
And thus, in such passages as, “That must be believed as a statement of Master Gotama’s, since he is an *arhat*, a perfectly enlightened one" (Ma. Ni. 1.387), the meaning is the exercise of faith.

In such passages as, “I allow you, monks, to partake of the fruits with five types of *samaṇa-kappa*” (Cūḷava. 250), it is usage.

In such passages as, "In which I constantly abide" (Ma. Ni. 1.387), it is time.

In such passages as, "Thus spoke venerable Kappa" (Su. Ni. 1098), it is designation.

In such passages as, "Adorned, with trimmed hair and beard" (Vi. Va. 1094), it is cutting.

In such passages as, "A two-finger length is allowable" (Cūḷava. 446), it is alternative; and in such passages as, "Is there a possibility to lie down?" (A. Ni. 8.80), it is a hint.

In such passages as, "Having illuminated the entire *veḷuvana*" (Saṃ. Ni. 1.94), it is all-aroundness (*samantabhāva*).

Here, however, the meaning of all-aroundness is intended.

Therefore, "the entire *gijjhakūṭa*" should be regarded as meaning "Gijjhakūṭa together with its surroundings, without remainder."

*Obhāsetvā*: Having pervaded with the radiance arising from robes, garlands, ornaments, and the body, making it a single illumination, a single blaze, like the moon or the sun.

*Ekantaṃ nisīdiṃsū*: The place where the deities sat near the Ten-Powered One was not large, but in this *sutta*, they sat down out of slight reverence.

mula_pali:
276. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho vessavaṇo mahārājā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – ‘‘santi hi, bhante, uḷārā yakkhā bhagavato appasannā. Santi hi, bhante, uḷārā yakkhā bhagavato pasannā. Santi hi , bhante, majjhimā yakkhā bhagavato appasannā. Santi hi, bhante, majjhimā yakkhā bhagavato pasannā. Santi hi, bhante, nīcā yakkhā bhagavato appasannā. Santi hi, bhante, nīcā yakkhā bhagavato pasannā. Yebhuyyena kho pana, bhante, yakkhā appasannāyeva bhagavato. Taṃ kissa hetu? Bhagavā hi, bhante, pāṇātipātā veramaṇiyā dhammaṃ deseti, adinnādānā veramaṇiyā dhammaṃ deseti, kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇiyā dhammaṃ deseti, musāvādā veramaṇiyā dhammaṃ deseti, surāmerayamajjappamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇiyā dhammaṃ deseti. Yebhuyyena kho pana, bhante, yakkhā appaṭiviratāyeva pāṇātipātā, appaṭiviratā adinnādānā, appaṭiviratā kāmesumicchācārā, appaṭiviratā musāvādā, appaṭiviratā surāmerayamajjappamādaṭṭhānā . Tesaṃ taṃ hoti appiyaṃ amanāpaṃ. Santi hi, bhante, bhagavato sāvakā araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti appasaddāni appanigghosāni vijanavātāni manussarāhasseyyakāni manussarāhaseyyakāni (sī. syā. pī.) paṭisallānasāruppāni. Tattha santi uḷārā yakkhā nivāsino, ye imasmiṃ bhagavato pāvacane appasannā. Tesaṃ pasādāya uggaṇhātu, bhante, bhagavā āṭānāṭiyaṃ rakkhaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ upāsakānaṃ upāsikānaṃ guttiyā rakkhāya avihiṃsāya phāsuvihārāyā’’ti. Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena.

Atha kho vessavaṇo mahārājā bhagavato adhivāsanaṃ viditvā tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imaṃ āṭānāṭiyaṃ rakkhaṃ abhāsi –
mula_english:
Then the great King Vessavaṇa, who was seated to one side, said this to the Blessed One: “Indeed, reverend Sir, there are eminent *yakṣas* who are not pleased with the Blessed One.

There are also eminent *yakṣas* pleased with the Blessed One.

Indeed, reverend Sir, there are middling *yakṣas* who are not pleased with the Blessed One.

Indeed, reverend Sir, there are middling *yakṣas* who are pleased with the Blessed One.

Indeed, reverend Sir, there are low *yakṣas* who are not pleased with the Blessed One.

Indeed, reverend Sir, there are low *yakṣas* who are pleased with the Blessed One.

But, reverend Sir, for the most part, the *yakṣas* are not pleased with the Blessed One.

What is the reason for that? Because, reverend Sir, the Blessed One teaches the *dharma* of abstaining from killing living beings (*prāṇātipātā veramaṇiyā dharmaṃ deseti*), teaches the *dharma* of abstaining from taking what is not given (*adinnādānā veramaṇiyā dharmaṃ deseti*), teaches the *dharma* of abstaining from sexual misconduct (*kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇiyā dharmaṃ deseti*), teaches the *dharma* of abstaining from false speech (*musāvādā veramaṇiyā dharmaṃ deseti*), teaches the *dharma* of abstaining from liquor, wine, and intoxicants, the basis for heedlessness (*surāmerayamajjappamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇiyā dhammaṃ deseti*).

But, reverend Sir, for the most part, the *yakṣas* do not abstain from killing living beings (*appaṭiviratāyeva pāṇātipātā*), do not abstain from taking what is not given (*appaṭiviratā adinnādānā*), do not abstain from sexual misconduct (*appaṭiviratā kāmesumicchācārā*), do not abstain from false speech (*appaṭiviratā musāvādā*), [and] do not abstain from liquor, wine, and intoxicants, the basis for heedlessness (*appaṭiviratā surāmerayamajjappamādaṭṭhānā*).

To them, that is unappealing and displeasing.

Indeed, reverend Sir, there are disciples of the Blessed One who frequent remote forest and woodland dwelling places—places with little sound, little noise, free from drafts, hidden from men, suitable for seclusion.

There are eminent *yakṣas* dwelling there who are not pleased with the Blessed One’s teaching.

To please them, reverend Sir, may the Blessed One learn the Āṭānāṭiya protection, for the monks’, nuns’, laymen’s, and laywomen’s safety, shelter, non-harm, and comfortable dwelling.”

The Blessed One consented in silence (*adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena*).

Then, the great King Vessavaṇa, knowing the Blessed One’s consent, at that moment recited this Āṭānāṭiya protection:
commentary_pali: 276.Vessavaṇoti kiñcāpi cattāro mahārājāno āgatā, vessavaṇo pana dasabalassa vissāsiko kathāpavattane byatto susikkhito, tasmā vessavaṇo mahārājā bhagavantaṃ etadavoca. Uḷārāti mahesakkhānubhāvasampannā. Pāṇātipātā veramaṇiyāti pāṇātipāte diṭṭhadhammikasamparāyikaṃ ādīnavaṃ dassetvā tato veramaṇiyā dhammaṃ deseti. Sesesupi eseva nayo. Tattha santi uḷārā yakkhā nivāsinoti tesu senāsanesu santi uḷārā yakkhā nibaddhavāsino. Āṭānāṭiyanti āṭānāṭanagare baddhattā evaṃnāmaṃ. Kiṃ pana bhagavato apaccakkhadhammo nāma atthīti, natthi. Atha kasmā vessavaṇo ‘‘uggaṇhātu, bhante, bhagavā’’tiādimāha? Okāsakaraṇatthaṃ. So hi bhagavantaṃ imaṃ parittaṃ sāvetuṃ okāsaṃ kārento evamāha. Satthu kathite imaṃ parittaṃ garu bhavissatītipi āha. Phāsuvihārāyāti gamanaṭṭhānādīsu catūsu iriyāpathesu sukhavihārāya.
commentary_english:
276. "Vessavaṇo": Although the four great kings ( *catvāro mahārājāno*) came, Vessavaṇa was trustworthy to the one with the ten powers (*dasabalassa*), skilled in initiating conversation, and well-trained. Therefore, Vessavaṇa, the great king ( *mahārājā*), said this to the Blessed One (*bhagavantaṃ*).

"Uḷārā": possessing great power and influence (*mahesakkhānubhāvasampannā*).

"Pāṇātipātā veramaṇiyā": Having shown the immediate and future dangers (*diṭṭhadhammikasamparāyikaṃ ādīnavaṃ*) in taking life (*pāṇātipāte*), he then teaches the Dharma of abstaining from taking life (*pāṇātipātā veramaṇiyā*).

So with the rest (*sesesupi eseva nayo*).

"Tattha santi uḷārā yakkhā nivāsino": In those lodgings, there are magnificent *yakṣas* who dwell there permanently (*tesu senāsanesu santi uḷārā yakkhā nibaddhavāsino*).

"Āṭānāṭiya": because it is connected with the city of Āṭānāṭa, hence the name (*āṭānāṭanagare baddhattā evaṃnāmaṃ*).

But is there any teaching (*apaccakkhadhammo*) of the Blessed One (*bhagavato*) that is not directly known? No (*natthi*).

Then why did Vessavaṇa say, "May the Blessed One learn it, venerable sir (*bhante*)?" It was to make an opportunity (*okāsakaraṇatthaṃ*).

Because he, creating an opportunity (*okāsaṃ kārento*) to have the Blessed One (*bhagavantaṃ*) recite this protection (*parittaṃ sāvetuṃ*), spoke thus (*evamāha*).

He also said, "When spoken by the Teacher (*satthu kathite*), this protection (*parittaṃ*) will be weighty ( *garu bhavissati*)."

"Phāsuvihārāyā": for a pleasant dwelling (*sukhavihārāya*) in the four postures (*catūsu iriyāpathesu*), such as places for walking and standing, etc. (*gamanaṭṭhānādīsu*).

mula_pali:
277. ‘‘Vipassissa ca ime cakārā porāṇapotthakesu natthi namatthu, cakkhumantassa sirīmato.

Sikhissapi ca ime cakārā porāṇapotthakesu natthi namatthu, sabbabhūtānukampino.

‘‘Vessabhussa ca ime cakārā porāṇapotthakesu natthi namatthu, nhātakassa tapassino;

Namatthu kakusandhassa, mārasenāpamaddino.

‘‘Koṇāgamanassa namatthu, brāhmaṇassa vusīmato;

Kassapassa ca ime cakārā porāṇapotthakesu natthi namatthu, vippamuttassa sabbadhi.

‘‘Aṅgīrasassa namatthu, sakyaputtassa sirīmato;

Yo imaṃ dhammaṃ desesi dhammamadesesi (sī. syā. pī.), dhammaṃ deseti (?), sabbadukkhāpanūdanaṃ.

dhammamadesesi (sī. syā. pī.), dhammaṃ deseti (?)

‘‘Ye cāpi nibbutā loke, yathābhūtaṃ vipassisuṃ;

Te janā apisuṇātha apisuṇā (sī. syā. pī.), mahantā vītasāradā.

apisuṇā (sī. syā. pī.)

‘‘Hitaṃ devamanussānaṃ, yaṃ namassanti gotamaṃ;

Vijjācaraṇasampannaṃ, mahantaṃ vītasāradaṃ.
commentary_pali:
277.Cakkhumantassāti na vipassīyeva cakkhumā, sattapi buddhā cakkhumanto, tasmā ekekassa buddhassa etāni satta satta nāmāni honti. Sabbepi buddhā cakkhumanto, sabbe sabbabhūtānukampino, sabbe nhātakilesattā nhātakā. Sabbe mārasenāpamaddino, sabbe vusitavanto, sabbe vimuttā, sabbe aṅgato rasmīnaṃ nikkhantattā aṅgīrasā. Na kevalañca buddhānaṃ etāneva satta nāmāni asaṅkhyeyyāni nāmāni saguṇena mahesinoti vuttaṃ.

Vessavaṇo pana attano pākaṭanāmavasena evamāha. Te janāti idha khīṇāsavā janāti adhippetā. Apisuṇāthāti desanāsīsamattametaṃ, amusā apisuṇā apharusā mantabhāṇinoti attho . Mahattāti mahantabhāvaṃ pattā. ‘‘Mahantā’’tipi pāṭho, mahantāti attho. Vītasāradāti nissāradā vigatalomahaṃsā.

Te janā Apisuṇāthā Mahattā Vītasāradā

Hitanti mettāpharaṇena hitaṃ. Yaṃ namassantīti ettha yanti nipātamattaṃ. Mahattanti mahantaṃ. Ayameva vā pāṭho, idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti ‘‘ye cāpi loke kilesanibbānena nibbutā yathābhūtaṃ vipassisuṃ, vijjādiguṇasampannañca hitaṃ devamanussānaṃ gotamaṃ namassanti, te janā apisuṇā, tesampi namatthū’’ti. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana te janā apisuṇāti te buddhā apisuṇāti evaṃ paṭhamagāthāya buddhānaṃyeva vaṇṇo kathito, tasmā paṭhamagāthā sattannaṃ buddhānaṃ vasena vuttā. Dutiyagāthāya ‘‘gotama’’nti desanāmukhamattametaṃ. Ayampi hi sattannaṃyeva vasena vuttāti veditabbā. Ayañhettha attho – loke paṇḍitā devamanussā yaṃ namassanti gotamaṃ, tassa ca tato purimānañca buddhānaṃ namatthūti.

Hita Yaṃ namassantī Mahatta
commentary_english:
277. cakkhumantassāti: "Because he has eyes (cakkhumā)," he is not merely one who sees (vipassī). The seven Buddhas also have eyes (cakkhumanto). Therefore, each buddha has these seven names. All buddhas have eyes (cakkhumanto), all are compassionate to all beings (sabbabhūtānukampino), all are cleansed (nhātakā) of defilements (kilesa). All are vanquishers of Māra's army (mārasenāpamaddino), all have lived the holy life (vusitavanto), all are liberated (vimuttā), all are called Aṅgīrasa because rays of light (rasmīnaṃ) issue from their bodies (aṅgato). It is said that the Buddhas have not only these seven names, but also countless (asaṅkhyeyyāni) names with good qualities (saguṇena mahesinoti).

Vaiśravaṇa (vessavaṇo), however, spoke thus in accordance with his well-known name (pākaṭanāmavasena). te janāti: "Those people" (te janā) here refers to individuals whose āsavas are destroyed (khīṇāsavā janāti adhippetā). apisuṇāthāti: "They are not malicious (apisuṇāthā)." This is merely the essence of the teaching (desanāsīsamattametaṃ): they are not false (amusā), not malicious (apisuṇā), not harsh (apharusā), and speak truthfully (mantabhāṇinoti attho). mahattāti: Because they have attained greatness (mahantabhāvaṃ pattā). There is also the reading "mahantā," meaning "great (mahantāti)." vītasāradāti: "They are without arrogance (vītasāradā)," meaning they are without essence (nissāradā) and their hair does not stand on end (vigatalomahaṃsā).

te janā apisuṇāthā mahattā vītasāradā

hitanti: "Beneficial (hitaṃ)" means beneficial (hitaṃ) through the pervasion of loving-kindness (mettāpharaṇena). yaṃ namassantīti: "They worship (yaṃ namassantī)." Here, "yanti" is merely a particle (nipātamattaṃ). mahattanti: "Greatness (mahattaṃ)" means great (mahantaṃ). Or, this is the reading: "This was said: 'Those who, in the world (loke), have attained nirvāṇa (nibbānena nibbutā) by destroying the defilements (kilesa), have truly seen (yathābhūtaṃ vipassisuṃ), possess knowledge and good qualities (vijjādiguṇasampannañca), and worship Gotama (gotamaṃ namassanti), who is beneficial (hitaṃ) to gods and humans (devamanussānaṃ), those people (te janā) are not malicious (apisuṇā), and homage to them as well (tesampi namatthū).'" In the commentary (aṭṭhakathāyaṃ), "te janā apisuṇāti" means "those people are not malicious," and "te buddhā apisuṇāti" means "those buddhas are not malicious." Thus, in the first verse (paṭhamagāthāya), the praise (vaṇṇo kathito) is only of the Buddhas (buddhānaṃyeva). Therefore, the first verse (paṭhamagāthā) was spoken in relation to the seven Buddhas (sattannaṃ buddhānaṃ vasena vuttā). In the second verse (dutiyagāthāya), "Gotama (gotamaṃ)" is merely the beginning of the teaching (desanāmukhamattametaṃ). This too (ayampi hi) should be understood (veditabbā) as spoken in relation to the seven (sattannaṃyeva vasena vuttāti). Here, the meaning (attha) is this (ayañhettha): "In the world (loke), the wise (paṇḍitā), gods and humans (devamanussā), worship Gotama (gotamaṃ) and homage (namatthūti) to him and to the Buddhas (buddhānaṃ) before him (tato purimānañca)."

hita yaṃ namassantī mahatta

mula_pali:
278. ‘‘Yato uggacchati sūriyo suriyo (sī. syā. pī.), ādicco maṇḍalī mahā.

Yassa cuggacchamānassa, saṃvarīpi nirujjhati;

Yassa cuggate sūriye, ‘divaso’ti pavuccati.

‘‘Rahadopi tattha gambhīro, samuddo saritodako;

Evaṃ taṃ tattha jānanti, ‘samuddo saritodako’.

‘‘Ito ‘sā purimā disā’, iti naṃ ācikkhatī jano;

Yaṃ disaṃ abhipāleti, mahārājā yasassi so.

‘‘Gandhabbānaṃ adhipati ādhipati (sī. syā. pī.) evamuparipi, ‘dhataraṭṭho’ti nāmaso;

ādhipati (sī. syā. pī.) evamuparipi

Ramatī naccagītehi, gandhabbehi purakkhato.

‘‘Puttāpi tassa bahavo, ekanāmāti me sutaṃ;

Asīti dasa eko ca, indanāmā mahabbalā.

Te cāpi buddhaṃ disvāna, buddhaṃ ādiccabandhunaṃ;

Dūratova namassanti, mahantaṃ vītasāradaṃ.

‘‘Namo te purisājañña, namo te purisuttama;

Kusalena samekkhasi, amanussāpi taṃ vandanti;

Sutaṃ netaṃ abhiṇhaso, tasmā evaṃ vademase.

‘‘‘Jinaṃ vandatha gotamaṃ, jinaṃ vandāma gotamaṃ;

Vijjācaraṇasampannaṃ, buddhaṃ vandāma gotamaṃ’.
commentary_pali:
278.Yato uggacchatīti yato ṭhānato udeti. Ādiccoti aditiyā putto, vevacanamattaṃ vā etaṃ sūriyasaddassa. Mahantaṃ maṇḍalaṃ assāti maṇḍalīmahā. Yassa cuggacchamānassāti yamhi uggacchamāne. Saṃvarīpi nirujjhatīti ratti antaradhāyati. Yassa cuggateti yasmiṃ uggate.

Rahadoti udakarahado. Tatthāti yato uggacchati sūriyo, tasmiṃ ṭhāne. Samuddoti yo so rahadoti vutto, so na añño, atha kho samuddo. Saritodakoti visaṭodako, saritā nānappakārā nadiyo assa udake paviṭṭhāti vā saritodako. Evaṃ taṃ tattha jānantīti taṃ rahadaṃ tattha evaṃ jānanti . Kinti jānanti? Samuddo saritodakoti evaṃ jānanti.

Rahado Tatthā Samuddo Saritodako saritodako. Evaṃ taṃ tattha jānantī

Itoti sineruto vā tesaṃ nisinnaṭṭhānato vā. Janoti ayaṃ mahājano. Ekanāmāti indanāmena ekanāmā. Sabbesaṃ kira tesaṃ sakkassa devarañño nāmameva nāmamakaṃsu. Asīti dasa eko cāti ekanavutijanā. Indanāmāti indoti evaṃnāmā. Buddhaṃ ādiccabandhunanti kilesaniddāpagamanenāpi buddhaṃ. Ādiccena samānagottatāyapi ādiccabandhunaṃ. Kusalena samekkhasīti anavajjena nipuṇena vā sabbaññutaññāṇena mahājanaṃ olokesi. Amanussāpi taṃ vandantīti amanussāpi taṃ ‘‘sabbaññutaññāṇena mahājanaṃ olokesī’’ti vatvā vandanti. Sutaṃ netaṃ abhiṇhasoti etaṃ amhehi abhikkhaṇaṃ sutaṃ. Jinaṃ vandatha gotamaṃ, jinaṃ vandāma gotamanti amhehi puṭṭhā jinaṃ vandāma gotamanti vadanti.

Ito Jano Ekanāmā Asīti dasa eko cā Indanāmā Buddhaṃ ādiccabandhuna Kusalena samekkhasī Amanussāpi taṃ vandantī Sutaṃ netaṃ abhiṇhaso Jinaṃ vandatha gotamaṃ, jinaṃ vandāma gotama
commentary_english:
278. *Yato uggacchatī* means from which place (*ṭhānataḥ*) it rises (*udeti*).

*Ādicco* means the son of Aditi, or it is simply a synonym (*vevacanamattaṃ*) for the word sun (*sūriyassa*).

*Mahantaṃ maṇḍalaṃ assāti maṇḍalīmahā* means because it has a large sphere (*maṇḍalaṃ*), it is called *maṇḍalīmahā.*

*Yassa cuggacchamānassā* means when (*yamhi*) it is rising (*uggacchamāne*).

*Saṃvarīpi nirujjhatī* means the night (*ratti*) disappears (*antaradhāyati*).

*Yassa cuggate* means when (*yasmiṃ*) it has risen (*uggate*).

*Rahado* means water-lake (*udakarahado*).

*Tatthā* means in that place (*ṭhāne*) from which the sun (*sūriyo*) rises (*uggacchati*).

*Samuddo* means that which was called (*vutto*) *rahado*; that is not different (*añño*), but it is indeed the ocean (*samuddo*).

*Saritodako* means having scattered water (*visaṭodako*), or many different (*nānappakārā*) rivers (*nadiyo*) enter (*paviṭṭhāti*) into its water (*udake*); therefore, *saritodako*.

*Evaṃ taṃ tattha jānantī* means in this way, they know (*jānanti*) that *rahadaṃ* there (*tattha*).

How do they know (*jānanti*)? They know in this way: the ocean (*samuddo*) has river-water (*saritodako*).

*Rahado*, *Tatthā*, *Samuddo*, *Saritodako*, *Saritodako*.
*Evaṃ taṃ tattha jānantī*.

*Ito* means from Mount Meru (*sineruto*) or from their sitting place (*nisinnaṭṭhānato*).

*Jano* means this great multitude (*mahājano*).

*Ekanāmā* means having one name (*ekanāmā*) with the name of Indra (*indanāmena*).

Indeed, they made the name itself the name of Śakra, king of the gods (*sakkassa devarañño nāmameva nāmamakaṃsu*).

*Asīti dasa eko cā* means ninety-one people (*ekanavutijanā*).

*Indanāmā* means having the name of Indra (*indoti evaṃnāmā*).

*Buddhaṃ ādiccabandhuna* means having become a Buddha (*buddhaṃ*) even through the cessation (*apagamanena*) of the sleep of defilements (*kilesaniddā*).

Because of having the same lineage (*samānagottatāyapi*) as the sun (*ādiccena*), [it is called] *ādiccabandhunaṃ*.

*Kusalena samekkhasī* means he looked (*olokesi*) at the great multitude (*mahājanaṃ*) with faultless (*anavajjena*), skillful (*nipuṇena*) or all-knowing knowledge (*sabbaññutaññāṇena*).

*Amanussāpi taṃ vandantī* means even non-humans (*amanussāpi*) venerate (*vandantī*) him, saying, "He looks (*olokesi*) at the great multitude (*mahājanaṃ*) with all-knowing knowledge (*sabbaññutaññāṇena*)".

*Sutaṃ netaṃ abhiṇhaso* means this (*etaṃ*) has been frequently (*abhikkhaṇaṃ*) heard (*sutaṃ*) by us (*amhehi*).

*"Jinaṃ vandatha gotamaṃ, jinaṃ vandāma gotama"* means when asked by us (*amhehi puṭṭhā*), they say (*vadanti*), "We venerate the Victorious One, Gotama (*jinaṃ vandāma gotamanti*)."

*Ito*, *Jano*, *Ekanāmā*, *Asīti dasa eko cā*, *Indanāmā*, *Buddhaṃ ādiccabandhuna*, *Kusalena samekkhasī*, *Amanussāpi taṃ vandantī*,
*Sutaṃ netaṃ abhiṇhaso*, *Jinaṃ vandatha gotamaṃ, jinaṃ vandāma gotama*

mula_pali:
279. ‘‘Yena petā pavuccanti, pisuṇā piṭṭhimaṃsikā.

Pāṇātipātino luddā luddhā (pī. ka.), corā nekatikā janā.

luddhā (pī. ka.)

‘‘Ito ‘sā dakkhiṇā disā’, iti naṃ ācikkhatī jano;

Yaṃ disaṃ abhipāleti, mahārājā yasassi so.

‘‘Kumbhaṇḍānaṃ adhipati, ‘virūḷho’ iti nāmaso;

Ramatī naccagītehi, kumbhaṇḍehi purakkhato.

‘‘Puttāpi tassa bahavo, ekanāmāti me sutaṃ;

Asīti dasa eko ca, indanāmā mahabbalā.

Te cāpi buddhaṃ disvāna, buddhaṃ ādiccabandhunaṃ;

Dūratova namassanti, mahantaṃ vītasāradaṃ.

‘‘Namo te purisājañña, namo te purisuttama;

Kusalena samekkhasi, amanussāpi taṃ vandanti;

Sutaṃ netaṃ abhiṇhaso, tasmā evaṃ vademase.

‘‘‘Jinaṃ vandatha gotamaṃ, jinaṃ vandāma gotamaṃ;

Vijjācaraṇasampannaṃ, buddhaṃ vandāma gotamaṃ’.
commentary_pali: 279.Yenapetā pavuccantīti petā nāma kālaṅkatā, te yena disābhāgena nīhariyantūti vuccanti. Pisuṇā piṭṭhimaṃsikāti pisuṇāvācā ceva piṭṭhimaṃsaṃ khādantā viya parammukhā garahakā ca. Ete ca yena nīhariyantūti vuccanti, sabbepi hete dakkhiṇadvārena nīharitvā dakkhiṇato nagarassa ḍayhantu vā chijjantu vā haññantu vāti evaṃ vuccanti. Ito sā dakkhiṇā disāti yena disābhāgena te petā ca pisuṇādikā ca nīhariyantūti vuccanti, ito sā dakkhiṇā disā. Itoti sineruto vā tesaṃ nisinnaṭṭhānato vā. Kumbhaṇḍānanti te kira devā mahodarā honti, rahassaṅgampi ca nesaṃ kumbho viya mahantaṃ hoti. Tasmā kumbhaṇḍāti vuccanti.
commentary_english:
279.
Because by which *petas* are said to be led out. *Peta* means those whose time has passed; thus, they are called [petas] because they are led out by whatever direction.
*Pisuṇā piṭṭhimaṃsikā* means backbiting speech, and also like those eating back flesh, those who are critical behind one's back.
And these, by whichever [direction] they should be led out, therefore they are called [such] because they, all of them, having led [them] out through the southern gate, may be burned, cut, or killed to the south of the city, in this way they are called.
"From here [is] the southern direction" [means] because by whichever direction those *petas* and those beginning with *pisuṇa* are led out, from here [is] the southern direction.
"From here" [means] either from Mount *Sineru* or from their place of sitting.
*Kumbhaṇḍāna* means those gods are said to have large bellies; and also their secret parts are like a *kumbha*, they are large.
Therefore they are called *kumbhaṇḍa*.

mula_pali:
281. ‘‘Yena uttarakuruvho uttarakurū rammā (sī. syā. pī.), mahāneru sudassano.

Manussā tattha jāyanti, amamā apariggahā.

‘‘Na te bījaṃ pavapanti, napi nīyanti naṅgalā;

Akaṭṭhapākimaṃ sāliṃ, paribhuñjanti mānusā.

‘‘Akaṇaṃ athusaṃ suddhaṃ, sugandhaṃ taṇḍulapphalaṃ;

Tuṇḍikīre pacitvāna, tato bhuñjanti bhojanaṃ.

‘‘Gāviṃ ekakhuraṃ katvā, anuyanti disodisaṃ;

Pasuṃ ekakhuraṃ katvā, anuyanti disodisaṃ.

‘‘Itthiṃ vā vāhanaṃ itthī-vāhanaṃ (sī. pī.), itthīṃ vāhanaṃ (syā.) katvā, anuyanti disodisaṃ;

itthī-vāhanaṃ (sī. pī.), itthīṃ vāhanaṃ (syā.)

‘‘Kumāriṃ vāhanaṃ katvā, anuyanti disodisaṃ;

Kumāraṃ vāhanaṃ katvā, anuyanti disodisaṃ.

Sabbā disā anupariyāyanti anupariyanti (syā.);

anupariyanti (syā.)

Pāsādā sivikā ceva, mahārājassa yasassino.

‘‘Tassa ca nagarā ahu,

Antalikkhe sumāpitā;

Āṭānāṭā kusināṭā parakusināṭā,

Nāṭasuriyā nāṭapuriyā (sī. pī.), nāṭapariyā (syā.) parakusiṭanāṭā.

nāṭapuriyā (sī. pī.), nāṭapariyā (syā.)

‘‘Uttarena kasivanto kapivanto (sī. syā. pī),

kapivanto (sī. syā. pī)

Kukkuṭakā kukutthakā (sī. pī.) kuḷīrakā, vane pokkharasātakā.

kukutthakā (sī. pī.)

‘‘Ayaṃ kho sā, mārisa, āṭānāṭiyā rakkhā bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ upāsakānaṃ upāsikānaṃ guttiyā rakkhāya avihiṃsāya phāsuvihārāya.
mula_english:
281. Where delightful Uttarakuru is, and the good looking Mahāneru. People are born there, without ego, without possessions. They neither sow the seed nor use the plow; Humans enjoy the rice that ripens without tilling. Rice, purged of the red powder and of husk, clean and sweet-scented, having cooked it on hot rocks, they then enjoy their food. Having made a cow into a single hoof, they go in all directions; Having made an animal into a single hoof, they go in all directions. Having made a woman or conveyance , they go in all directions; Having made a man into a conveyance, they go in all directions. Having made a girl into a conveyance, they go in all directions; Having made a boy into a conveyance, they go in all directions. They, having mounted a vehicle, go around in all directions; the realm of that king. Elephant conveyances, horse conveyances, divine conveyances are prepared; palaces and palanquins, of the glorious great king. And to him there were cities, well-measured in the sky; Āṭānāṭā, Kusināṭā, Parakusināṭā, Nāṭasuriyā, Parakusiṭanāṭā. To the north are farmers, It should be; (syāḥ). (pī)

And with the multitude of people on the other side;

Navanavatiya, Ambara-ambaravatiyo,

is the king’s capital named Āḷakamandā.

‘‘To Kuvera Indeed, O venerable one, the great king's capital is named Visāṇā;

Therefore, the great king Kuvera is called ‘Vessavaṇa.’

‘‘Approaching they proclaim, Tatolā, Tattalā, Tatotalā;

Ojasi, Tejasi, Tatojasi, Sūra, Rājā, Ariṭṭha, Nemi.

‘‘There also is a lake named Dharaṇī, from which the clouds pour down;

Whence the rains rush forth, and there also is the assembly hall Sālavatī Bhagalavatī (Sī. syā. pī. ) by name.

Bhagalavatī (Sī. syā. pī. )

‘‘Where the yakṣas attend, there are trees with constant fruit;

Various flocks of birds are joined, resounding with peacocks and herons;

With cuckoos and other sweet-voiced birds.

‘‘Here are jīvañjīvaka sounds, and also oṭṭhavacittakā;

Jungle fowls Kukutthakā (Sī. pī. ), crabs, and in the woods, Pokkharasātakā.

Kukutthakā (Sī. pī. )

‘‘Here are the sounds of śuka and śālika birds, and daṇḍamāṇavakāni;

At all times, she shines, Kuvera’s lotus pool forever.

‘‘From here, ‘that is the northern direction,’ thus people declare it;

The direction which the great king, glorious one, protects.

‘‘And Kuvera is the lord of the yakṣas, by name;

He delights in dancing and songs, being honored by the yakṣas.

‘‘And he has many sons, all of one name, so I have heard;

Eighty, ten, and one, all named Indra, and very powerful.

‘‘And they too, having seen the Buddha, the Buddha, a relative of the sun;

Worship him from afar, the great one, devoid of arrogance.

‘‘Homage to you, O noble thoroughbred man, homage to you, O best of men;

You observe with skill, even non-humans worship you;

This is not heard frequently, therefore we speak thus.

‘‘‘Worship the Jina, Gotama, we worship the Jina, Gotama;

Accomplished in knowledge and conduct, we worship the Buddha, Gotama’’’nti.

‘‘This is the Āṭānāṭiyā protection, O venerable one, for the monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen, for their guard, protection, freedom from harm, and comfortable living.
commentary_pali:
281.Yenāti yena disābhāgena. Mahānerūti mahāsineru pabbatarājā. Sudassanoti sovaṇṇamayattā sundaradassano. Sinerussa hi pācīnapassaṃ rajatamayaṃ, dakkhiṇapassaṃ maṇimayaṃ , pacchimapassaṃ phalikamayaṃ, uttarapassaṃ sovaṇṇamayaṃ, taṃ manuññadassanaṃ hoti. Tasmā yena disābhāgena sineru sudassanoti ayametthattho. Manussā tattha jāyantīti tattha uttarakurumhi manussā jāyanti. Amamāti vatthābharaṇapānabhojanādīsupi mamattavirahitā. Apariggahāti itthipariggahena apariggahā. Tesaṃ kira ‘‘ayaṃ mayhaṃ bhariyā’’ti mamattaṃ na hoti, mātaraṃ vā bhaginiṃ vā disvā chandarāgo nuppajjati.

Napi nīyanti naṅgalāti naṅgalānipi tattha ‘‘kasikammaṃ karissāmā’’ti na khettaṃ nīyanti. Akaṭṭhapākimanti akaṭṭhe bhūmibhāge araññe sayameva jātaṃ. Taṇḍulapphalanti taṇḍulāva tassa phalaṃ hoti.

Napi nīyanti naṅgalā Akaṭṭhapākima Taṇḍulapphala

Tuṇḍikīre pacitvānāti ukkhaliyaṃ ākiritvā niddhumaṅgārena agginā pacitvā. Tattha kira jotikapāsāṇā nāma honti. Atha kho te tayo pāsāṇe ṭhapetvā taṃ ukkhaliṃ āropenti. Pāsāṇehi tejo samuṭṭhahitvā taṃ pacati. Tato bhuñjanti bhojananti tato ukkhalito bhojanameva bhuñjanti, añño sūpo vā byañjanaṃ vā na hoti, bhuñjantānaṃ cittānukūloyevassa raso hoti. Te taṃ ṭhānaṃ sampattānaṃ dentiyeva, macchariyacittaṃ nāma na hoti. Buddhapaccekabuddhādayopi mahiddhikā tattha gantvā piṇḍapātaṃ gaṇhanti.

Tuṇḍikīre pacitvānā Tato bhuñjanti bhojana

Gāviṃekakhuraṃ katvāti gāviṃ gahetvā ekakhuraṃ vāhanameva katvā. Taṃ abhiruyha vessavaṇassa paricārakā yakkhā. Anuyanti disodisanti tāya tāya disāya caranti. Pasuṃ ekakhuraṃ katvāti ṭhapetvā gāviṃ avasesacatuppadajātikaṃ pasuṃ ekakhuraṃ vāhanameva katvā disodisaṃ anuyanti.

Gāviṃ ekakhuraṃ katvā Anuyanti disodisa Pasuṃ ekakhuraṃ katvā

Itthiṃ vā vāhanaṃ katvāti yebhuyyena gabbhiniṃ mātugāmaṃ vāhanaṃ karitvā. Tassā piṭṭhiyā nisīditvā caranti. Tassā kira piṭṭhi onamituṃ sahati. Itarā pana itthiyo yāne yojenti. Purisaṃ vāhanaṃ katvāti purise gahetvā yāne yojenti. Gaṇhantā ca sammādiṭṭhike gahetuṃ na sakkonti. Yebhuyyena paccantimamilakkhuvāsike gaṇhanti. Aññataro kirettha jānapado ekassa therassa samīpe nisīditvā niddāyati, thero ‘‘upāsaka ativiya niddāyasī’’ti pucchi. ‘‘Ajja, bhante, sabbarattiṃ vessavaṇadāsehi kilamitomhī’’ti āha.

Itthiṃ vā vāhanaṃ katvā Purisaṃ vāhanaṃ katvā

Kumāriṃ vāhanaṃ katvāti kumāriyo gahetvā ekakhuraṃ vāhanaṃ katvā rathe yojenti. Kumāravāhanepi eseva nayo. Pacārā tassa rājinoti tassa rañño paricārikā. Hatthiyānaṃ assayānanti na kevalaṃ goyānādīniyeva, hatthiassayānādīnipi abhiruhitvā vicaranti. Dibbaṃ yānanti aññampi nesaṃ bahuvidhaṃ dibbayānaṃ upaṭṭhitameva hoti, etāni tāva nesaṃ upakappanayānāni. Te pana pāsāde varasayanamhi nipannāpi pīṭhasivikādīsu ca nisinnāpi vicaranti. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘pāsādā sivikā cevā’’ti. Mahārājassa yasassinoti evaṃ ānubhāvasampannassa yasassino mahārājassa etāni yānāni nibbattanti.

Kumāriṃ vāhanaṃ katvā Kumāravāhanepi Pacārā tassa rājino Hatthiyānaṃ assayāna Dibbaṃ yāna Mahārājassa yasassino

Tassaca nagarā ahu antalikkhe sumāpitāti tassa rañño ākāse suṭṭhu māpitā ete āṭānāṭādikā nagarā ahesuṃ, nagarāni bhaviṃsūti attho. Ekañhissa nagaraṃ āṭānāṭā nāma āsi, ekaṃ kusināṭā nāma, ekaṃ parakusināṭā nāma, ekaṃ nāṭasūriyā nāma, ekaṃ parakusiṭanāṭā nāma.

Tassa ca nagarā ahu antalikkhe sumāpitā

Uttarena kasivantoti tasmiṃ ṭhatvā ujuṃ uttaradisāya kasivanto nāma aññaṃ nagaraṃ. Janoghamaparena cāti etassa aparabhāge janoghaṃ nāma aññaṃ nagaraṃ. Navanavatiyoti aññampi navanavatiyo nāma ekaṃ nagaraṃ. Aparaṃ ambaraambaravatiyo nāma. Āḷakamandāti aparampi āḷakamandā nāma rājadhānī.

Uttarena kasivanto Janoghamaparena cā Navanavatiyo Āḷakamandā

Tasmākuvero mahārājāti ayaṃ kira anuppanne buddhe kuvero nāma brāhmaṇo hutvā ucchuvappaṃ kāretvā satta yantāni yojesi. Ekissāya yantasālāya uṭṭhitaṃ āyaṃ āgatāgatassa mahājanassa datvā puññaṃ akāsi. Avasesasālāhi tattheva bahutaro āyo uṭṭhāsi, so tena pasīditvā avasesasālāsupi uppajjanakaṃ gahetvā vīsati vassasahassāni dānaṃ adāsi. So kālaṃ katvā cātumahārājikesu kuvero nāma devaputto jāto. Aparabhāge visāṇāya rājadhāniyā rajjaṃ kāresi. Tato paṭṭhāya vessavaṇoti vuccati.

Tasmā kuvero mahārājā

Paccesanto pakāsentīti paṭiesanto visuṃ visuṃ atthe upaparikkhamānā anusāsamānā aññe dvādasa yakkharaṭṭhikā pakāsenti. Te kira yakkharaṭṭhikā sāsanaṃ gahetvā dvādasannaṃ yakkhadovārikānaṃ nivedenti. Yakkhadovārikā taṃ sāsanaṃ mahārājassa nivedenti. Idāni tesaṃ yakkharaṭṭhikānaṃ nāmaṃ dassento tatolātiādimāha. Tesu kira eko tatolā nāma, eko tattalā nāma, eko tatotalā nāma, eko ojasi nāma, eko tejasi nāma, eko tatojasī nāma. Sūro rājāti eko sūro nāma, eko rājā nāma, eko sūrorājā nāma, ariṭṭho nemīti eko ariṭṭho nāma, eko nemi nāma, eko ariṭṭhanemi nāma.

Paccesanto pakāsentī tatolā Sūro rājā ariṭṭho nemī

Rahadopitattha dharaṇī nāmāti tattha paneko nāmena dharaṇī nāma udakarahado atthi, paṇṇāsayojanā mahāpokkharaṇī atthīti vuttaṃ hoti. Yato meghā pavassantīti yato pokkharaṇito udakaṃ gahetvā meghā pavassanti. Vassā yato patāyantīti yato vuṭṭhiyo avattharamānā nigacchanti. Meghesu kira uṭṭhitesu tato pokkharaṇito purāṇaudakaṃ bhassati. Upari megho uṭṭhahitvā taṃ pokkharaṇiṃ navodakena pūreti. Purāṇodakaṃ heṭṭhimaṃ hutvā nikkhamati. Paripuṇṇāya pokkharaṇiyā valāhakā vigacchanti. Sabhāpīti sabhā. Tassā kira pokkharaṇiyā tīre sālavatiyā nāma latāya parikkhitto dvādasayojaniko ratanamaṇḍapo atthi, taṃ sandhāyetaṃ vuttaṃ.

Rahadopi tattha dharaṇī nāmā Yato meghā pavassantī Vassā yato patāyantī Sabhāpī

Payirupāsantīti nisīdanti. Tattha niccaphalā rukkhāti tasmiṃ ṭhāne taṃ maṇḍapaṃ parivāretvā sadā phalitā ambajambuādayo rukkhā niccapupphitā ca campakamālādayoti dasseti. Nānādijagaṇāyutāti vividhapakkhisaṅghasamākulā. Mayūrakoñcābhirudāti mayūrehi koñcasakuṇehi ca abhirudā upagītā.

Payirupāsantī Tattha niccaphalā rukkhā Nānādijagaṇāyutā Mayūrakoñcābhirudā

Jīvañjīvakasaddetthāti ‘‘jīva jīvā’’ti evaṃ viravantānaṃ jīvañjīvakasakuṇānampi ettha saddo atthi. Oṭṭhavacittakāti ‘‘uṭṭhehi, citta, uṭṭhehi cittā’’ti evaṃ vassamānā uṭṭhavacittakasakuṇāpi tattha vicaranti. Kukkuṭakāti vanakukkuṭakā. Kuḷīrakāti suvaṇṇakakkaṭakā. Vaneti padumavane. Pokkharasātakāti pokkharasātakā nāma sakuṇā.

Jīvañjīvakasaddetthā Oṭṭhavacittakā Kukkuṭakā Kuḷīrakā Vane Pokkharasātakā

Sukasāḷikasaddetthāti sukānañca sāḷikānañca saddo ettha. Daṇḍamāṇavakāni cāti manussamukhasakuṇā. Te kira dvīhi hatthehi suvaṇṇadaṇḍaṃ gahetvā ekaṃ pokkharapattaṃ akkamitvā anantare pokkharapatte suvaṇṇadaṇḍaṃ nikkhipantā vicaranti. Sobhati sabbakālaṃ sāti sā pokkharaṇī sabbakālaṃ sobhati. Kuveranaḷinīti kuverassa naḷinī padumasarabhūtā, sā dharaṇī nāma pokkharaṇī sadā nirantaraṃ sobhati.

Sukasāḷikasaddetthā Daṇḍamāṇavakāni cā Sobhati sabbakālaṃ sā Kuveranaḷinī
commentary_english:
281. "Yenā" means by which direction or part.
"Mahānerū" means the great Mount Meru, king of mountains.
"Sudassano" means of beautiful appearance because it is made of gold.
Mount Meru's eastern side is made of silver, the southern side is made of jewels, page 3.0965, the western side is made of crystal, the northern side is made of gold; it is of pleasing appearance.
Therefore, "Sineru Sudassana" means by which direction it is.
"Manussā tattha jāyantī" means humans are born there in Uttarakuru.
"Amamā" means they are without attachment even to clothing, ornaments, drinks, food, and so on.
"Apariggahā" means they are without possessions through possessing women.
It is said that for them, there is no attachment thinking, "This is my wife," and having seen a mother or sister, lust and passion do not arise.

"Napi nīyanti naṅgalā" means plows are not brought there thinking, "We will do agriculture," the field is not led [there].
"Akaṭṭhapākima" means it ripens without cultivation, in an uncultivated part of the earth, in the forest it is self-born.
"Taṇḍulapphala" means its fruit is just like rice.

"Tuṇḍikīre pacitvānā" means having scattered it in a pot, having cooked it with smokeless embers and fire.
There, it is said that there are luminous stones by name.
Then, page 3.0147, indeed, they place those three stones, and they place the pot on top.
Heat arising from the stones cooks it.
"Tato bhuñjanti bhojana" means then, having taken [that] food from the pot, they eat only that food; there is no other soup or curry, and the taste of it is just according to the minds of those eating.
They give that place to those who have attained accomplishment, and there is no such thing as a miserly mind.
Buddhas, Pratyekabuddhas, and others with great powers go there and receive alms.

"Gāviṃ ekakhuraṃ katvā" means having taken a cow, having made a single-hoofed vehicle.
Having climbed upon it, the attendants of Vaiśravaṇa are the *yakṣas*.
"Anuyanti disodisa" means they wander in that direction.
"Pasuṃ ekakhuraṃ katvā" means having placed a cow, having made the remaining four-footed species of animal a single-hoofed vehicle, they follow in every direction.

"Itthiṃ vā vāhanaṃ katvā" means generally, having made a pregnant woman a vehicle.
Having sat on her back, they travel.
It is said that her back is able to bend.
But the other women harness vehicles.
"Purisaṃ vāhanaṃ katvā" means having taken a man, they harness vehicles.
Those who take [others] do not succeed in taking those with right view.
Generally, they take those who dwell in the border regions among the barbarians.
Another person there, page 3.0966, a villager, sat down near a certain *thera* and was drowsy; the *thera* asked, "Layman, are you very drowsy?"
"Today, venerable sir, I have been exhausted by the servants of Vaiśravaṇa all night," he said.
"Having made the maiden a vehicle": Taking maidens, making a single-hoofed animal a vehicle, they yoke it to a chariot.

"Also the *kumāra* vehicle": This is the same method.

"The attendants of that king": The attendants of that king.

"Elephant vehicle, horse vehicle": Not only cow vehicles and so on, but also having mounted elephant vehicles, horse vehicles, and so on, they wander about.

"Divine vehicle": Another kind of manifold divine vehicle is also at hand for them; these, however, are their vehicles of preparation.

But they, even lying down in a palace on an excellent bed, and even sitting on couches, palanquins, and so on, wander about.

Therefore it was said, "Palaces, palanquins, and also..."

"Of the glorious great king": Thus, these vehicles come into being for the glorious great king who is endowed with such power.

Having made the maiden a vehicle. Also the *kumāra* vehicle. The attendants of that king. Elephant vehicle, horse vehicle. Divine vehicle. Of the glorious great king.

"And cities were in the sky, well-measured": In the sky of that king, these cities, Āṭānāṭa and so on, were well-measured; the meaning is, they were cities.

One city of his was named Āṭānāṭā, one was named Kusināṭā, one was named Parakusināṭā, one was named Nāṭasūriyā, one was named Parakusiṭanāṭā.

And cities were in the sky, well-measured.

"To the north, Kasivanto": Having stood in that, directly to the north direction [is] another city named Kasivanto.

"And Janoghama is beyond": On the other side of this [is] another city named Janoghama.

"Navanavatiyo": Also, another city named Navanavatiyo.

Another [is] named Ambaraambaravatiyo.

"Āḷakamandā": Also another capital named Āḷakamandā.

To the north, Kasivanto. And Janoghama is beyond. Navanavatiyo. Āḷakamandā.

"The *Mahārāja* Kuvera": It is said that this Kuvera, when the Buddhas had not arisen, having been a *brāhmaṇa* named Kuvera, having caused a sugarcane field to be made, yoked seven machines.

Having given the income that arose in one machine-hall to the great crowd of those who came and went, he performed merit.

From the remaining halls, even more income arose there; he, having been pleased by that, having taken the means of production even in the remaining halls, gave a gift for twenty thousand years.

Having died, he was born as a *devaputra* named Kuvera in the Cātumahārājika heavens.

In another part, he caused the kingdom of the capital of Visāṇā to be made.

From then on, he is called Vessavaṇa.

Therefore.

"Investigating and making clear": Examining the meanings separately, teaching, other twelve *yakṣa* generals make clear.

Those *yakṣa* generals, having taken the teaching, announce [it] to the twelve *yakṣa* gatekeepers.

The *yakṣa* gatekeepers announce that teaching to the Great King.

Now, showing the names of those *yakṣa* generals, he says, "Tatolā" and so on.

Among those, one was named Tatolā, one was named Tattalā, one was named Tatotalā, one was named Ojasi, one was named Tejasi, one was named Tatojasī.

"Sūra the king": One was named Sūra, one was named King, one was named Sūrorājā, "Ariṭṭha Nemi": one was named Ariṭṭha, one was named Nemi, one was named Ariṭṭhanemi.

Investigating and making clear.

Tatolā. Sūra the king. Ariṭṭha Nemi.

"There, a pool named Dharaṇī": There, indeed, is a water-lake named Dharaṇī by the name; it is said that there is a great lotus pond of fifty *yojana*s.

"From which the clouds pour down": From which, having taken water from the lotus pond, the clouds pour down.

"The rains from which rush down": From which the rains, rushing down, descend.

When the clouds have arisen, the old water vanishes from that lotus pond.

Having risen up, the cloud fills that lotus pond with new water.

The old water, having become lower, goes out.
Clouds depart from the full lotus pond.

"It is a gathering," that is, a meeting.

On the bank of that lotus pond, surrounded by a creeper named Sālavatī, there is a jeweled pavilion twelve *yojanas* in extent; referring to that, this was said.

A lake also.

There, the earth is named. Because clouds shower down; rains because they fly; it is a gathering.

"They sit respectfully near," that is, they sit down.

"There are trees with constant fruit," that is, having surrounded that pavilion in that place, always bearing fruit, such as mangoes and rose-apples, and always in bloom, such as *campaka* garlands, this shows.

"Endowed with various bird-flocks," that is, crowded with various bird-communities.

"Resounded by peacocks and cranes," that is, resounded and sung to by peacocks and crane-birds.

They sit respectfully near. There are trees with constant fruit. Endowed with various bird-flocks. Resounded by peacocks and cranes.

"There is the sound of *jīvañjīvaka* birds here," that is, the sound of *jīvañjīvaka* birds, chirping thus: "Live! Live!" is here also.

"Oṭṭhavacittaka birds," that is, *oṭṭhavacittaka* birds, chirping thus: "Get up, Citta! Get up, Cittā!" wander about there.

"*Kukkuṭaka* birds," that is, forest-fowl.

"*Kuḷīraka* birds," that is, golden crabs.

"In the forest," that is, in the lotus forest.

"*Pokkharasātaka* birds," that is, birds named *pokkharasātaka*.

There is the sound of *jīvañjīvaka* birds here.

Oṭṭhavacittaka birds. *Kukkuṭaka* birds. *Kuḷīraka* birds.

In the forest. *Pokkharasātaka* birds.

"There is the sound of parrots and *sāḷika* birds here," that is, the sound of parrots and *sāḷika* birds is here.

"And staff-youths," that is, birds with human faces.

It is said that those, holding a golden staff with both hands, stepping on one lotus leaf, and placing the golden staff on the next lotus leaf, wander about.

"It shines at all times," that is, that lotus pond shines at all times.

"*Kuveranaḷinī*," that is, the lotus pond of Kuvera, having the essence of a lotus marsh, that earth called lotus pond always shines uninterruptedly.

There is the sound of parrots and *sāḷika* birds here. And staff-youths. It shines at all times. *Kuveranaḷinī*.

mula_pali:
282. ‘‘Yassa kassaci, mārisa, bhikkhussa vā bhikkhuniyā vā upāsakassa vā upāsikāya vā ayaṃ āṭānāṭiyā rakkhā suggahitā bhavissati samattā pariyāputā pariyāpuṭā (ka.). Taṃ ce amanusso yakkho vā yakkhinī vā yakkhapotako vā yakkhapotikā vā yakkhamahāmatto vā yakkhapārisajjo vā yakkhapacāro vā, gandhabbo vā gandhabbī vā gandhabbapotako vā gandhabbapotikā vā gandhabbamahāmatto vā gandhabbapārisajjo vā gandhabbapacāro vā, kumbhaṇḍo vā kumbhaṇḍī vā kumbhaṇḍapotako vā kumbhaṇḍapotikā vā kumbhaṇḍamahāmatto vā kumbhaṇḍapārisajjo vā kumbhaṇḍapacāro vā, nāgo vā nāgī vā nāgapotako vā nāgapotikā vā nāgamahāmatto vā nāgapārisajjo vā nāgapacāro vā, paduṭṭhacitto bhikkhuṃ vā bhikkhuniṃ vā upāsakaṃ vā upāsikaṃ vā gacchantaṃ vā anugaccheyya, ṭhitaṃ vā upatiṭṭheyya, nisinnaṃ vā upanisīdeyya, nipannaṃ vā upanipajjeyya. Na me so, mārisa, amanusso labheyya gāmesu vā nigamesu vā sakkāraṃ vā garukāraṃ vā. Na me so, mārisa, amanusso labheyya āḷakamandāya nāma rājadhāniyā vatthuṃ vā vāsaṃ vā. Na me so, mārisa, amanusso labheyya yakkhānaṃ samitiṃ gantuṃ. Apissu naṃ, mārisa, amanussā anāvayhampi naṃ kareyyuṃ avivayhaṃ. Apissu naṃ, mārisa, amanussā attāhipi paripuṇṇāhi paribhāsāhi paribhāseyyuṃ. Apissu naṃ, mārisa, amanussā rittaṃpissa pattaṃ sīse nikkujjeyyuṃ. Apissu naṃ, mārisa, amanussā sattadhāpissa muddhaṃ phāleyyuṃ.

‘‘Santi hi, mārisa, amanussā caṇḍā ruddhā ruddā (sī. pī.) rabhasā, te neva mahārājānaṃ ādiyanti, na mahārājānaṃ purisakānaṃ ādiyanti, na mahārājānaṃ purisakānaṃ purisakānaṃ ādiyanti. Te kho te, mārisa, amanussā mahārājānaṃ avaruddhā nāma vuccanti. Seyyathāpi, mārisa, rañño māgadhassa vijite mahācorā. Te neva rañño māgadhassa ādiyanti, na rañño māgadhassa purisakānaṃ ādiyanti, na rañño māgadhassa purisakānaṃ purisakānaṃ ādiyanti. Te kho te, mārisa, mahācorā rañño māgadhassa avaruddhā nāma vuccanti. Evameva kho, mārisa, santi amanussā caṇḍā ruddhā rabhasā, te neva mahārājānaṃ ādiyanti, na mahārājānaṃ purisakānaṃ ādiyanti, na mahārājānaṃ purisakānaṃ purisakānaṃ ādiyanti. Te kho te, mārisa, amanussā mahārājānaṃ avaruddhā nāma vuccanti. Yo hi koci, mārisa, amanusso yakkho vā yakkhinī vā…pe… gandhabbo vā gandhabbī vā … kumbhaṇḍo vā kumbhaṇḍī vā… nāgo vā nāgī vā nāgapotako vā nāgapotikā vā nāgamahāmatto vā nāgapārisajjo vā nāgapacāro vā paduṭṭhacitto bhikkhuṃ vā bhikkhuniṃ vā upāsakaṃ vā upāsikaṃ vā gacchantaṃ vā anugaccheyya, ṭhitaṃ vā upatiṭṭheyya, nisinnaṃ vā upanisīdeyya, nipannaṃ vā upanipajjeyya. Imesaṃ yakkhānaṃ mahāyakkhānaṃ senāpatīnaṃ mahāsenāpatīnaṃ ujjhāpetabbaṃ vikkanditabbaṃ viravitabbaṃ – ‘ayaṃ yakkho gaṇhāti, ayaṃ yakkho āvisati, ayaṃ yakkho heṭheti, ayaṃ yakkho viheṭheti, ayaṃ yakkho hiṃsati, ayaṃ yakkho vihiṃsati, ayaṃ yakkho na muñcatī’ti.

ruddā (sī. pī.)
mula_english:
282. “Whoever, dear Sir—be they monk (*bhikkhu*) or nun (*bhikkhunī*) or layman (*upāsaka*) or laywoman (*upāsikā*)—learns this Āṭānāṭiya protection (*rakkhā*) well, and will master it in its entirety.

Then if a non-human being—be they male *yakkha* or female *yakkha* or *yakkha* boy or *yakkha* girl or *yakkha* minister or *yakkha* councillor or *yakkha* messenger or male *gandhabba* or female *gandhabba* or *gandhabba* boy or *gandhabba* girl or *gandhabba* minister or *gandhabba* councillor or *gandhabba* messenger or male *kumbhaṇḍa* or female *kumbhaṇḍa* or *kumbhaṇḍa* boy or *kumbhaṇḍa* girl or *kumbhaṇḍa* minister or *kumbhaṇḍa* councillor or *kumbhaṇḍa* messenger or male *nāga* or female *nāga* or *nāga* boy or *nāga* girl or *nāga* minister or *nāga* councillor or *nāga* messenger—with corrupted mind were to follow a monk (*bhikkhu*) or nun (*bhikkhunī*) or layman (*upāsaka*) or laywoman (*upāsikā*) who is walking, or stands by them, or sits down close by them, or lies down close by them,

then that non-human being, dear Sir, would not receive in my villages (*gāmesu*) and towns (*nigamesu*), honour (*sakkāraṃ*) or respect (*garukāraṃ*).

That non-human being, dear Sir, would not receive in my royal city Ālakamandā (*rājadhāniyā*), ground (*vatthuṃ*) or dwelling (*vāsaṃ*).

That non-human being, dear Sir, would not be able to go to the gathering (*samitiṃ*) of the *yakkhas*.

Further, dear Sir, non-human beings would not give or take him in marriage.

Further, dear Sir, non-human beings would abuse him with very personal abuse.

Further, dear Sir, non-human beings would drop an empty bowl (*pattaṃ*) over his head (*sīse*).

Further, dear Sir, non-human beings would split his head (*muddhaṃ*) into seven (*sattadhā*) pieces.

“There are non-human beings, dear Sir, who are fierce (*caṇḍā*), cruel (*ruddhā*), and violent (*rabhasā*), they do not take notice of the Great Kings (*mahārājānaṃ*), they do not take notice of the Great Kings’ men, they do not take notice of the Great Kings’ men’s men.

And those non-human beings, dear Sir, are said to be in revolt (*avaruddhā*) against the Great Kings (*mahārājānaṃ*).

Just as, dear Sir, there are great thieves (*mahācorā*) in the king of Magadha’s (*rañño māgadhassa*) realm (*vijite*),

who do not take notice of the king of Magadha, who do not take notice of the king of Magadha’s men, who do not take notice of the king of Magadha’s men’s men,

and those great thieves, dear Sir, are said to be in revolt (*avaruddhā*) against the king of Magadha.

Even so, dear Sir, there are non-human beings who are fierce (*caṇḍā*), cruel (*ruddhā*), and violent (*rabhasā*), they do not take notice of the Great Kings (*mahārājānaṃ*), they do not take notice of the Great Kings’ men, they do not take notice of the Great Kings’ men’s men.

And those non-human beings, dear Sir, are said to be in revolt (*avaruddhā*) against the Great Kings (*mahārājānaṃ*).

“Now, dear Sir, whatever non-human beings—be they male *yakkha* or female *yakkha* … male *gandhabba* or female *gandhabba* …male *kumbhaṇḍa* or female *kumbhaṇḍa* … male *nāga* or female *nāga* or *nāga* boy or *nāga* girl or *nāga* minister or *nāga* councillor or *nāga* messenger—with corrupted mind were to follow a monk (*bhikkhu*) or nun (*bhikkhunī*) or layman (*upāsaka*) or laywoman (*upāsikā*) who is walking, or stands by them, or sits down close by them, or lies down close by them,

then to these *yakkhas*, great *yakkhas*, generals (*senāpatīnaṃ*), and great generals (*mahāsenāpatīnaṃ*), one should call out, one should shout out, one should cry out: ‘This *yakkha* has seized me, this *yakkha* has grabbed me, this *yakkha* annoys me, this *yakkha* harasses me, this *yakkha* hurts me, this *yakkha* injures me, this *yakkha* will not release me.’"
commentary_pali:
282.Yassa kassacīti idaṃ vessavaṇo āṭānāṭiyaṃ rakkhaṃ niṭṭhapetvā tassā parikammaṃ dassento āha. Tattha suggahitāti atthañca byañjanañca parisodhetvā suṭṭhu uggahitā. Samattā pariyāputāti padabyañjanāni ahāpetvā paripuṇṇaṃ uggahitā. Atthampi pāḷimpi visaṃvādetvā sabbaso vā pana appaguṇaṃ katvā bhaṇantassa hi parittaṃ tejavantaṃ na hoti, sabbaso paguṇaṃ katvā bhaṇantasseva tejavantaṃ hoti. Lābhahetu uggahetvā bhaṇantassāpi atthaṃ na sādheti, nissaraṇapakkhe ṭhatvā mettaṃ purecārikaṃ katvā bhaṇantasseva atthāya hotīti dasseti. Yakkhapacāroti yakkhaparicārako.

Vatthuṃ vāti gharavatthuṃ vā. Vāsaṃ vāti tattha nibaddhavāsaṃ vā. Samitinti samāgamaṃ. Anāvayhanti na āvāhayuttaṃ. Avivayhanti na vivāhayuttaṃ. Tena saha āvāhavivāhaṃ na kareyyunti attho. Attāhipi paripuṇṇāhīti ‘‘kaḷārakkhi kaḷāradantā’’ti evaṃ etesaṃ attabhāvaṃ upanetvā vuttāhi paripuṇṇabyañjanāhi paribhāsāhi paribhāseyyuṃ yakkhaakkosehi nāma akkoseyyunti attho. Rittampissa pattanti bhikkhūnaṃ pattasadisameva lohapattaṃ hoti. Taṃ sīse nikkujjitaṃ yāva galavāṭakā bhassati. Atha naṃ majjhe ayokhīlena ākoṭenti.

Vatthuṃ vā Vāsaṃ vā Samiti Anāvayha Avivayha Attāhipi paripuṇṇāhī Rittampissa patta

Caṇḍāti kodhanā. Ruddhāti viruddhā. Rabhasāti karaṇuttariyā. Neva mahārājānaṃ ādiyantīti vacanaṃ na gaṇhanti, āṇaṃ na karonti. Mahārājānaṃ purisakānanti aṭṭhavīsatiyakkhasenāpatīnaṃ. Purisakānanti yakkhasenāpatīnaṃ ye manassā tesaṃ. Avaruddhā nāmāti paccāmittā verino. Ujjhāpetabbanti parittaṃ vatvā amanusse paṭikkamāpetuṃ asakkontena etesaṃ yakkhānaṃ ujjhāpetabbaṃ, ete jānāpetabbāti attho.

Caṇḍā Ruddhā Rabhasā Neva mahārājānaṃ ādiyantī Mahārājānaṃ purisakāna Purisakāna Avaruddhā nāmā Ujjhāpetabba

Parittaparikammakathā

Idha pana ṭhatvā parittassa parikammaṃ kathetabbaṃ. Paṭhamameva hi āṭānāṭiyasuttaṃ na bhaṇitabbaṃ, mettasuttaṃ dhajaggasuttaṃ ratanasuttanti imāni sattāhaṃ bhaṇitabbāni. Sace muñcati, sundaraṃ. No ce muñcati, āṭānāṭiyasuttaṃ bhaṇitabbaṃ, taṃ bhaṇantena bhikkhunā piṭṭhaṃ vā maṃsaṃ vā na khāditabbaṃ, susāne na vasitabbaṃ. Kasmā? Amanussā okāsaṃ labhanti. Parittakaraṇaṭṭhānaṃ haritupalittaṃ kāretvā tattha parisuddhaṃ āsanaṃ paññapetvā nisīditabbaṃ.

Parittakārako bhikkhu vihārato gharaṃ nentehi phalakāvudhehi parivāretvā netabbo. Abbhokāse nisīditvā na vattabbaṃ, dvāravātapānāni pidahitvā nisinnena āvudhahatthehi saṃparivāritena mettacittaṃ purecārikaṃ katvā vattabbaṃ. Paṭhamaṃ sikkhāpadāni gāhāpetvā sīle patiṭṭhitassa parittaṃ kātabbaṃ. Evampi mocetuṃ asakkontena vihāraṃ ānetvā cetiyaṅgaṇe nipajjāpetvā āsanapūjaṃ kāretvā dīpe jālāpetvā cetiyaṅgaṇaṃ sammajjitvā maṅgalakathā vattabbā. Sabbasannipāto ghosetabbo. Vihārassa upavane jeṭṭhakarukkho nāma hoti, tattha bhikkhusaṅgho tumhākaṃ āgamanaṃ paṭimānetīti pahiṇitabbaṃ. Sabbasannipātaṭṭhāne anāgantuṃ nāma na labbhati. Tato amanussagahitako ‘‘tvaṃ ko nāmā’’ti pucchitabbo. Nāme kathite nāmeneva ālapitabbo. Itthannāma tuyhaṃ mālāgandhādīsu patti āsanapūjāya patti piṇḍapāte patti, bhikkhusaṅghena tuyhaṃ paṇṇākāratthāya mahāmaṅgalakathā vuttā, bhikkhusaṅghe gāravena etaṃ muñcāhīti mocetabbo. Sace na muñcati, devatānaṃ ārocetabbaṃ ‘‘tumhe jānātha, ayaṃ amanusso amhākaṃ vacanaṃ na karoti, mayaṃ buddhaāṇaṃ karissāmā’’ti parittaṃ kātabbaṃ. Etaṃ tāva gihīnaṃ parikammaṃ. Sace pana bhikkhu amanussena gahito hoti, āsanāni dhovitvā sabbasannipātaṃ ghosāpetvā gandhamālādīsu pattiṃ datvā parittaṃ bhaṇitabbaṃ. Idaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ parikammaṃ.

Vikkanditabbanti sabbasannipātaṃ ghosāpetvā aṭṭhavīsati yakkhasenāpatayo kanditabbā. Viravitabbanti ‘‘ayaṃ yakkho gaṇhātī’’tiādīni bhaṇantena tehi saddhiṃ kathetabbaṃ. Tattha gaṇhātīti sarīre adhimuccati. Āvisatīti tasseva vevacanaṃ. Atha vā laggati na apetīti vuttaṃ hoti. Heṭhetīti uppannaṃ rogaṃ vaḍḍhento bādhati. Viheṭhetīti tasseva vevacanaṃ. Hiṃsatīti appamaṃsalohitaṃ karonto dukkhāpeti. Vihiṃsatīti tasseva vevacanaṃ. Na muñcatīti appamādagāho hutvā muñcituṃ na icchati, evaṃ etesaṃ viravitabbaṃ.

Vikkanditabba Viravitabba gaṇhātī Āvisatī Heṭhetī Viheṭhetī Hiṃsatī Vihiṃsatī Na muñcatī
commentary_english:
282. " *yassa kassacī* "—Vessavaṇa said this, finishing the protection in Āṭānāṭiya, showing the preliminary act for that. There, "*suggahitā*"—having purified the meaning and the letter, well grasped. "*samattā pariyāputā*"—without omitting the words and letters, fully grasped. Indeed, the protective verse of one speaking after contradicting the meaning and the text, or making it altogether inferior, is not powerful. The protective verse of one speaking after making it altogether excellent is powerful. He shows that even if one grasps and speaks for the sake of gain, it does not accomplish the meaning. It is only for the sake of one standing on the side of liberation, making loving-kindness a forerunner, that it is. "*yakkhapacāro*"—one who attends to yakkhas. "*vatthuṃ vā*"—or a house site. "*vāsaṃ vā*"—or a regular dwelling there. "*samiti*"—a gathering. "*anāvayha*"—not suitable for marriage. "*avivayha*"—not suitable for divorce. The meaning is that one should not engage in marriage or divorce with them. "*attāhipi paripuṇṇāhī*"—having brought their own existence near by saying, "Kaḷārakkhi Kaḷāradantā," they should revile them with complete letters, complete expressions, with the names of the yaksha curses. "*rittampissa patta*"—there is an iron bowl, just like the monks' bowl. Having turned it upside down on the head, it falls down to the throat. Then they strike it in the middle with an iron stake. *vatthuṃ vā vāsaṃ vā samiti anāvayha avivayha attāhipi paripuṇṇāhī rittampissa patta* *caṇḍā* — angry. *ruddhā* — opposed. *rabhasā* — excelling in action. "*neva mahārājānaṃ ādiyantī*"—they do not accept the word, they do not do the command. "*mahārājānaṃ purisakāna*"—of the twenty-eight yaksha generals. "*purisakāna*"—of those who are mindful of the yaksha generals. "*avaruddhā nāmā*"—called enemies, hostile. "*ujjhāpetabba*"—by one unable to turn back the non-humans by saying the protective verses, these yakkhas should be driven out; this is the meaning that they should be made to know. *caṇḍā ruddhā rabhasā neva mahārājānaṃ ādiyantī mahārājānaṃ purisakāna purisakāna avaruddhā nāmā ujjhāpetabba* The Talk about the Preliminary Activity for the Protective Verses Here, however, standing, the preliminary activity for the protective verses should be told. Indeed, first of all, the Āṭānāṭiya Sutta should not be spoken. The Mettā Sutta, the Dhajagga Sutta, the Ratana Sutta—these should be spoken for seven days. If it releases, excellent. If it does not release, the Āṭānāṭiya Sutta should be spoken. A monk speaking that should not eat meat or fish, and should not live in a cemetery. Why? Non-humans obtain an opportunity. Having had the place for doing the protective verses plastered with green, having prepared a pure seat there, one should sit down. The monk doing the protective verses should be led from the monastery to the house surrounded by those wielding wooden weapons. Sitting in the open air, it should not be said. Having closed the doors and windows, surrounded by those with weapons in their hands, making loving-kindness a forerunner, it should be said. First, having had the precepts taken, the protective verses should be done for one established in morality. Even if unable to free [him] in this way, having brought [him] to the monastery, having had [him] lie down in the temple courtyard, having performed the seat-offering, having lit lamps, having swept the temple courtyard, a *maṅgala* talk should be given. A general assembly should be announced. There is a *jeṭṭhakarukkha* tree named in the vicinity of the monastery; it should be sent [word] that "the monastic Saṅgha awaits your arrival there." In the place of the general assembly, it is not permitted for one not to come. Then, one possessed by a non-human should be asked, "Who are you?" When the name has been spoken, he should be addressed by that very name. "[So and so], you have merit in flowers, scents, and so forth; you have merit in the seat offering; you have merit in the alms-food. A great auspicious talk was spoken by the monastic Saṅgha for the purpose of your gift. In the monastic Saṅgha, with reverence, release this one!" Thus, he should be freed. If he does not release [him], the deities should be informed: "You know, this non-human does not do our bidding. We will do the Buddha's command!" Thus, a protective recitation should be done. This is the preliminary act for laypeople. But if a monk is seized by a non-human, having washed the seats, having announced a general assembly, having given merit in scents, garlands, and so forth, a protective recitation should be spoken. This is the preliminary act for monks.

vikkanditabbanti having announced a general assembly, twenty-eight *yakkha* generals should be made to wail. viravitabbanti, while saying "This *yakkha* seizes [him]," and so forth, it should be spoken with them. There, gaṇhātīti: adheres to the body. āvisatīti is a synonym for that very thing. Or, it means it clings, it does not go away. heṭhetīti, while increasing the disease that has arisen, it afflicts. viheṭhetīti is a synonym for that very thing. hiṃsatīti, while making [him have] little flesh and blood, he causes suffering. vihiṃsatīti is a synonym for that very thing. na muñcatīti, having become a seizure of negligence, he does not wish to release [him]. Thus, it should be cried to them.

vikkanditabba viravitabba gaṇhātī āvisatī heṭhetī viheṭhetī hiṃsatī vihiṃsatī na muñcatī

mula_pali:
283. ‘‘Katamesaṃ yakkhānaṃ mahāyakkhānaṃ senāpatīnaṃ mahāsenāpatīnaṃ?

‘‘Indo somo varuṇo ca, bhāradvājo pajāpati;

Candano kāmaseṭṭho ca, kinnughaṇḍu nighaṇḍu ca.

‘‘Panādo opamañño ca, devasūto ca mātali;

Cittaseno ca gandhabbo, naḷo rājā janesabho janosabho (syā.).

janosabho (syā.)

‘‘Sātāgiro hemavato, puṇṇako karatiyo guḷo;

Sivako mucalindo ca, vessāmitto yugandharo.

‘‘Gopālo supparodho ca suppagedho ca (sī. syā. pī.), hiri netti hirī nettī (sī. pī.) ca mandiyo;

suppagedho ca (sī. syā. pī.) hirī nettī (sī. pī.)

Pañcālacaṇḍo āḷavako, pajjunno sumano sumukho;

Dadhimukho maṇi māṇivaro maṇi mānicaro (syā. pī.) dīgho, atho serīsako saha.

maṇi mānicaro (syā. pī.)

‘‘Imesaṃ yakkhānaṃ mahāyakkhānaṃ senāpatīnaṃ mahāsenāpatīnaṃ ujjhāpetabbaṃ vikkanditabbaṃ viravitabbaṃ – ‘ayaṃ yakkho gaṇhāti, ayaṃ yakkho āvisati, ayaṃ yakkho heṭheti, ayaṃ yakkho viheṭheti, ayaṃ yakkho hiṃsati, ayaṃ yakkho vihiṃsati, ayaṃ yakkho na muñcatī’ti.

‘‘Ayaṃ kho sā, mārisa, āṭānāṭiyā rakkhā bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ upāsakānaṃ upāsikānaṃ guttiyā rakkhāya avihiṃsāya phāsuvihārāya. Handa ca dāni mayaṃ, mārisa, gacchāma bahukiccā mayaṃ bahukaraṇīyā’’ti. ‘‘Yassadāni tumhe mahārājāno kālaṃ maññathā’’ti.
commentary_pali:
283. Idāni yesaṃ evaṃ viravitabbaṃ, te dassetuṃ katamesaṃ yakkhānantiādimāha. Tattha indo somotiādīni tesaṃ nāmāni. Tesu vessāmittoti vessāmittapabbatavāsī eko yakkho. Yugandharopi yugandharapabbatavāsīyeva. Hiri netti ca mandiyoti hiri ca netti ca mandiyo ca. Maṇi māṇi varo dīghoti maṇi ca māṇi ca varo ca dīgho ca. Atho serīsako sahāti tehi saha añño serīsako nāma. ‘‘Imesaṃ yakkhānaṃ…pe… ujjhāpetabba’’nti ayaṃ yakkho imaṃ heṭheti viheṭheti na muñcatīti evaṃ etesaṃ yakkhasenāpatīnaṃ ārocetabbaṃ. Tato te bhikkhusaṅgho attano dhammaāṇaṃ karoti, mayampi amhākaṃ yakkharājaāṇaṃ karomāti ussukkaṃ karissanti. Evaṃ amanussānaṃ okāso na bhavissati, buddhasāvakānaṃ phāsuvihāro ca bhavissatīti dassento ‘‘ayaṃ kho sā, mārisa, āṭānāṭiyā rakkhā’’tiādimāha. Taṃ sabbaṃ, tato parañca uttānatthamevāti.

Sumaṅgalavilāsiniyā dīghanikāyaṭṭhakathāya

Āṭānāṭiyasuttavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.
commentary_english:
Now, to show those for whom such a request should be made, he says, "To which *yakṣas*?" etc.

There, *indo somo* etc., are their names.

Among them, *vessāmitto* means a certain *yakṣa* dwelling on Mount Vessāmitta.

*yugandharopi* means dwelling on Mount Yugandhara.

*hiri netti ca mandiyo* means Hiri, Netti, and Mandiyo.

*maṇi māṇi varo dīgho* means Maṇi, Māṇi, Varo, and Dīgho.

*atho serīsako sahā* means another named Serīsaka together with them.

"These *yakṣas*...should be incited" means, this *yakṣa* harasses, molests, and does not release him; in this way it should be announced to these *yakṣa* generals.

Then that *bhikkhu-saṅgha* makes its own *dhamma*-command; "We also will make our *yakṣa*-king's command," they will be eager.
