Thus, showing that an opportunity for non-humans will not occur, and there will be a comfortable dwelling for the Buddha's disciples, he says, "This, friend, is the *Āṭānāṭiya* protection," etc.

All of that, and what comes after, is easily understood.

The Commentary on the *Āṭānāṭiya Sutta* in the *Dīgha Nikāya* is finished in the *Sumangalavilāsinī*.

mula_pali:
284. Atha kho cattāro mahārājā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā tatthevantaradhāyiṃsu. Tepi kho yakkhā uṭṭhāyāsanā appekacce bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā tatthevantaradhāyiṃsu. Appekacce bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodiṃsu, sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā tatthevantaradhāyiṃsu . Appekacce yena bhagavā tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā tatthevantaradhāyiṃsu. Appekacce nāmagottaṃ sāvetvā tatthevantaradhāyiṃsu. Appekacce tuṇhībhūtā tatthevantaradhāyiṃsūti.

Paṭhamabhāṇavāro niṭṭhito.

Dutiyabhāṇavāro
mula_english:
Then, the Four Great Kings rose from their seats, and after worshipping the Blessed One (bhagavantam) and circumambulating him, they vanished right there.

Then, some *yakṣas* also rose from their seats, and after worshipping the Blessed One (bhagavantam) and circumambulating him, they vanished right there.

Some rejoiced with the Blessed One (bhagavatā), and after exchanging friendly conversation and polite discourse, they vanished right there.

Some, after raising their hands in respectful salutation (*añjali*) towards the Blessed One (bhagavā), vanished right there.

Some, after announcing their name (*nāma*) and clan (*gotta*), vanished right there.

And some, while remaining silent (*tuṇhībhūtā*), vanished right there.

The first recitation section is finished.

Second recitation section.

mula_pali: 285. Atha kho bhagavā tassā rattiyā accayena bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘imaṃ, bhikkhave, rattiṃ cattāro mahārājā mahatiyā ca yakkhasenāya mahatiyā ca gandhabbasenāya mahatiyā ca kumbhaṇḍasenāya mahatiyā ca nāgasenāya catuddisaṃ rakkhaṃ ṭhapetvā catuddisaṃ gumbaṃ ṭhapetvā catuddisaṃ ovaraṇaṃ ṭhapetvā abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇā kevalakappaṃ gijjhakūṭaṃ pabbataṃ obhāsetvā yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā maṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Tepi kho, bhikkhave, yakkhā appekacce maṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Appekacce mayā saddhiṃ sammodiṃsu, sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Appekacce yenāhaṃ tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Appekacce nāmagottaṃ sāvetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Appekacce tuṇhībhūtā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu.
mula_english:
Then, when that night had passed, the Blessed One addressed the monks, saying: "This night, monks, the Four Great Kings, with a great army of *yakkhas* (yakṣa), with a great army of *gandhabbas* (gandharva), with a great army of *kumbhaṇḍas* (kumbhāṇḍa), with a great army of *nāgas* (nāga), having set up a protection over the four quarters, having set serried troops at the four directions, having set up a barricade at the four directions, at the end of the night, having lit up the whole of Vulture's Peak (*Gijjhakūṭa*) with their surpassing beauty, approached me; after approaching, they worshipped me and sat down on one side.

Then of those *yakkhas* (yakṣa), monks, some, after worshipping me, sat down on one side.

Some exchanged greetings with me, and after exchanging polite and courteous greetings, sat down on one side.

Some, after raising their hands in respectful salutation to me, sat down on one side.

Some, after announcing their name and family (*nāmagotta*), sat down on one side.

Some kept silent and sat down on one side.

mula_pali: 286. ‘‘Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho, bhikkhave, vessavaṇo mahārājā maṃ etadavoca – ‘santi hi, bhante, uḷārā yakkhā bhagavato appasannā…pe… santi hi , bhante nīcā yakkhā bhagavato pasannā. Yebhuyyena kho pana, bhante, yakkhā appasannāyeva bhagavato. Taṃ kissa hetu? Bhagavā hi, bhante, pāṇātipātā veramaṇiyā dhammaṃ deseti… surāmerayamajjappamādaṭṭhānā veramaṇiyā dhammaṃ deseti. Yebhuyyena kho pana, bhante, yakkhā appaṭiviratāyeva pāṇātipātā… appaṭiviratā surāmerayamajjappamādaṭṭhānā. Tesaṃ taṃ hoti appiyaṃ amanāpaṃ. Santi hi, bhante, bhagavato sāvakā araññavanapatthāni pantāni senāsanāni paṭisevanti appasaddāni appanigghosāni vijanavātāni manussarāhasseyyakāni paṭisallānasāruppāni. Tattha santi uḷārā yakkhā nivāsino, ye imasmiṃ bhagavato pāvacane appasannā, tesaṃ pasādāya uggaṇhātu, bhante, bhagavā āṭānāṭiyaṃ rakkhaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ upāsakānaṃ upāsikānaṃ guttiyā rakkhāya avihiṃsāya phāsuvihārāyā’ti. Adhivāsesiṃ kho ahaṃ, bhikkhave, tuṇhībhāvena. Atha kho, bhikkhave, vessavaṇo mahārājā me adhivāsanaṃ viditvā tāyaṃ velāyaṃ imaṃ āṭānāṭiyaṃ rakkhaṃ abhāsi –
mula_english:
"Then, monks, the Great King Vessavaṇa, while sitting to one side, said this to me: 'There are, reverend Sir, high-ranking *yakkha*s who are displeased with the Blessed One... and there are, reverend Sir, low *yakkha*s who are pleased with the Blessed One. But, reverend Sir, for the most part, the *yakkha*s are displeased with the Blessed One. Why is that? Because, reverend Sir, the Blessed One teaches the Dharma (dhamma) of refraining from killing living beings... and teaches the Dharma of refraining from liquor, wines, or intoxicants that cause heedlessness. But, reverend Sir, for the most part, the *yakkha*s do not refrain from killing living beings... do not refrain from liquor, wines, or intoxicants that cause heedlessness. To them, that is displeasing and unpalatable. There are, reverend Sir, disciples of the Blessed One who frequent remote forest and woodland hermitages, quiet places with little noise, secluded spots sheltered from the wind, hidden from human contact, and suited to solitude. There reside high-ranking *yakkha*s who are displeased with the Blessed One’s teaching in those places. In order to please them, reverend Sir, may the Blessed One learn the Āṭānāṭiya protection (*Āṭānāṭiyaṃ rakkhaṃ*) for the safety, protection, non-violence, and comfortable dwelling of the monks (*bhikkhūnaṃ*), nuns (*bhikkhunīnaṃ*), laymen (*upāsakānaṃ*), and laywomen (*upāsikānaṃ*)'.

"And I, monks, consented in silence. Then, monks, the Great King Vessavaṇa, knowing of my consent, at that moment recited this Āṭānāṭiya protection (*Āṭānāṭiyaṃ rakkhaṃ*):"

mula_pali:
287. ‘Vipassissa ca namatthu, cakkhumantassa sirīmato.

Sikhissapi ca namatthu, sabbabhūtānukampino.

‘Vessabhussa ca namatthu, nhātakassa tapassino;

Namatthu kakusandhassa, mārasenāpamaddino.

‘Koṇāgamanassa namatthu, brāhmaṇassa vusīmato;

Kassapassa ca namatthu, vippamuttassa sabbadhi.

‘Aṅgīrasassa namatthu, sakyaputtassa sirīmato;

Yo imaṃ dhammaṃ desesi, sabbadukkhāpanūdanaṃ.

‘Ye cāpi nibbutā loke, yathābhūtaṃ vipassisuṃ;

Te janā apisuṇātha, mahantā vītasāradā.

‘Hitaṃ devamanussānaṃ, yaṃ namassanti gotamaṃ;

Vijjācaraṇasampannaṃ, mahantaṃ vītasāradaṃ.

288. ‘Yato uggacchati sūriyo, ādicco maṇḍalī mahā.

Yassa cuggacchamānassa, saṃvarīpi nirujjhati;

Yassa cuggate sūriye, ‘‘divaso’’ti pavuccati.

‘Rahadopi tattha gambhīro, samuddo saritodako;

Evaṃ taṃ tattha jānanti, ‘‘samuddo saritodako’’.

‘Ito ‘‘sā purimā disā’’, iti naṃ ācikkhatī jano;

Yaṃ disaṃ abhipāleti, mahārājā yasassi so.

‘Gandhabbānaṃ adhipati, ‘‘dhataraṭṭho’’ti nāmaso;

Ramatī naccagītehi, gandhabbehi purakkhato.

‘Puttāpi tassa bahavo, ekanāmāti me sutaṃ;

Asīti dasa eko ca, indanāmā mahabbalā.

‘Te cāpi buddhaṃ disvāna, buddhaṃ ādiccabandhunaṃ;

Dūratova namassanti, mahantaṃ vītasāradaṃ.

‘Namo te purisājañña, namo te purisuttama;

Kusalena samekkhasi, amanussāpi taṃ vandanti;

Sutaṃ netaṃ abhiṇhaso, tassā evaṃ vademase.

‘‘Jinaṃ vandatha gotamaṃ, jinaṃ vandāma gotamaṃ;

Vijjācaraṇasampannaṃ, buddhaṃ vandāma gotamaṃ’’.
mula_english:
288.
From where the sun arises, the son of Aditi, the great circle.

When he is arising, restraint ceases;

When the sun has risen, it is called "day."

'Even a lake there is deep, the ocean with flowing waters;'

Thus there they know it, "the ocean with flowing waters."

'From here "that is the eastern direction," thus people point to it;

That direction is governed by the great and glorious king.

'The overlord of the *gandharvas* is named "Dhṛtarāṣṭra";'

He delights in dance and song, attended by *gandharvas*.

'He has many sons, all of one name, so I have heard;'

They are eighty and ten and one, named Indra, of great strength.

'They also, seeing the Buddha, the Buddha, a relative of the sun,

From afar they bow, to the great one, devoid of arrogance.

'Homage to you, thoroughbred among men, homage to you, best of men;

With skill you consider, even non-humans bow to you;

This is not heard often, thus we speak to her.

"Bow to the Conqueror, Gotama, we bow to the Conqueror, Gotama;"

Endowed with knowledge and conduct, we bow to the Buddha, Gotama.'

mula_pali:
289. ‘Yena petā pavuccanti, pisuṇā piṭṭhimaṃsikā.

Pāṇātipātino luddā, corā nekatikā janā.

‘Ito ‘‘sā dakkhiṇā disā’’, iti naṃ ācikkhatī jano;

Yaṃ disaṃ abhipāleti, mahārājā yasassi so.

‘Kumbhaṇḍānaṃ adhipati, ‘‘virūḷho’’ iti nāmaso;

Ramatī naccagītehi, kumbhaṇḍehi purakkhato.

‘Puttāpi tassa bahavo, ekanāmāti me sutaṃ;

Asīti dasa eko ca, indanāmā mahabbalā.

‘Te cāpi buddhaṃ disvāna, buddhaṃ ādiccabandhunaṃ;

Dūratova namassanti, mahantaṃ vītasāradaṃ.

‘Namo te purisājañña, namo te purisuttama;

Kusalena samekkhasi, amanussāpi taṃ vandanti;

Sutaṃ netaṃ abhiṇhaso, tasmā evaṃ vademase.

‘‘Jinaṃ vandatha gotamaṃ, jinaṃ vandāma gotamaṃ;

Vijjācaraṇasampannaṃ, buddhaṃ vandāma gotamaṃ’’.

290. ‘Yattha coggacchati sūriyo, ādicco maṇḍalī mahā.

Yassa coggacchamānassa, divasopi nirujjhati;

Yassa coggate sūriye, ‘‘saṃvarī’’ti pavuccati.

‘Rahadopi tattha gambhīro, samuddo saritodako;

Evaṃ taṃ tattha jānanti, samuddo saritodako.

‘Ito ‘‘sā pacchimā disā’’, iti naṃ ācikkhatī jano;

Yaṃ disaṃ abhipāleti, mahārājā yasassi so.

‘Nāgānañca adhipati, ‘‘virūpakkho’’ti nāmaso;

Ramatī naccagītehi, nāgeheva purakkhato.

‘Puttāpi tassa bahavo, ekanāmāti me sutaṃ;

Asīti dasa eko ca, indanāmā mahabbalā.

‘Te cāpi buddhaṃ disvāna, buddhaṃ ādiccabandhunaṃ;

Dūratova namassanti, mahantaṃ vītasāradaṃ.

‘Namo te purisājañña, namo te purisuttama;

Kusalena samekkhasi, amanussāpi taṃ vandanti;

Sutaṃ netaṃ abhiṇhaso, tasmā evaṃ vademase.

‘‘Jinaṃ vandatha gotamaṃ, jinaṃ vandāma gotamaṃ;

Vijjācaraṇasampannaṃ, buddhaṃ vandāma gotamaṃ’’.

291. ‘Yena uttarakuruvho, mahāneru sudassano.

Manussā tattha jāyanti, amamā apariggahā.

‘Na te bījaṃ pavapanti, nāpi nīyanti naṅgalā;

Akaṭṭhapākimaṃ sāliṃ, paribhuñjanti mānusā.

‘Akaṇaṃ athusaṃ suddhaṃ, sugandhaṃ taṇḍulapphalaṃ;

Tuṇḍikīre pacitvāna, tato bhuñjanti bhojanaṃ.

‘Gāviṃ ekakhuraṃ katvā, anuyanti disodisaṃ;

Pasuṃ ekakhuraṃ katvā, anuyanti disodisaṃ.

‘Itthiṃ vā vāhanaṃ katvā, anuyanti disodisaṃ;

Purisaṃ vāhanaṃ katvā, anuyanti disodisaṃ.

‘Kumāriṃ vāhanaṃ katvā, anuyanti disodisaṃ;

Kumāraṃ vāhanaṃ katvā, anuyanti disodisaṃ.

‘Te yāne abhiruhitvā,

Sabbā disā anupariyāyanti;

Pacārā tassa rājino.

‘Hatthiyānaṃ assayānaṃ,

Dibbaṃ yānaṃ upaṭṭhitaṃ;

Pāsādā sivikā ceva,

Mahārājassa yasassino.

‘Tassa ca nagarā ahu,

Antalikkhe sumāpitā;

Āṭānāṭā kusināṭā parakusināṭā,

Nāṭasuriyā parakusiṭanāṭā.

‘Uttarena kasivanto,

Janoghamaparena ca;

Navanavutiyo ambaraambaravatiyo,

Āḷakamandā nāma rājadhānī.

‘Kuverassa kho pana, mārisa, mahārājassa visāṇā nāma rājadhānī;

Tasmā kuvero mahārājā, ‘‘vessavaṇo’’ti pavuccati.

‘Paccesanto pakāsenti, tatolā tattalā tatotalā;

Ojasi tejasi tatojasī, sūro rājā ariṭṭho nemi.

‘Rahadopi tattha dharaṇī nāma, yato meghā pavassanti;

Vassā yato patāyanti, sabhāpi tattha sālavatī nāma.

‘Yattha yakkhā payirupāsanti, tattha niccaphalā rukkhā;

Nānā dijagaṇā yutā, mayūrakoñcābhirudā;

Kokilādīhi vagguhi.

‘Jīvañjīvakasaddettha, atho oṭṭhavacittakā;

Kukkuṭakā kuḷīrakā, vane pokkharasātakā.

‘Sukasāḷika saddettha, daṇḍamāṇavakāni ca;

Sobhati sabbakālaṃ sā, kuveranaḷinī sadā.

‘Ito ‘‘sā uttarā disā’’, iti naṃ ācikkhatī jano;

Yaṃ disaṃ abhipāleti, mahārājā yasassi so.

‘Yakkhānañca adhipati, ‘‘kuvero’’ iti nāmaso;

Ramatī naccagītehi, yakkheheva purakkhato.

‘Puttāpi tassa bahavo, ekanāmāti me sutaṃ;

Asīti dasa eko ca, indanāmā mahabbalā.

‘Te cāpi buddhaṃ disvāna, buddhaṃ ādiccabandhunaṃ;

Dūratova namassanti, mahantaṃ vītasāradaṃ.

‘Namo te purisājañña, namo te purisuttama;

Kusalena samekkhasi, amanussāpi taṃ vandanti;

Sutaṃ netaṃ abhiṇhaso, tasmā evaṃ vademase.

‘‘Jinaṃ vandatha gotamaṃ, jinaṃ vandāma gotamaṃ;

Vijjācaraṇasampannaṃ, buddhaṃ vandāma gotama’’nti.

292. ‘Ayaṃ kho sā, mārisa , āṭānāṭiyā rakkhā bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ upāsakānaṃ upāsikānaṃ guttiyā rakkhāya avihiṃsāya phāsuvihārāya. Yassa kassaci, mārisa, bhikkhussa vā bhikkhuniyā vā upāsakassa vā upāsikāya vā ayaṃ āṭānāṭiyā rakkhā suggahitā bhavissati samattā pariyāputā taṃ ce amanusso yakkho vā yakkhinī vā…pe… gandhabbo vā gandhabbī vā…pe… kumbhaṇḍo vā kumbhaṇḍī vā…pe… nāgo vā nāgī vā nāgapotako vā nāgapotikā vā nāgamahāmatto vā nāgapārisajjo vā nāgapacāro vā, paduṭṭhacitto bhikkhuṃ vā bhikkhuniṃ vā upāsakaṃ vā upāsikaṃ vā gacchantaṃ vā anugaccheyya, ṭhitaṃ vā upatiṭṭheyya, nisinnaṃ vā upanisīdeyya, nipannaṃ vā upanipajjeyya. Na me so, mārisa, amanusso labheyya gāmesu vā nigamesu vā sakkāraṃ vā garukāraṃ vā. Na me so, mārisa, amanusso labheyya āḷakamandāya nāma rājadhāniyā vatthuṃ vā vāsaṃ vā. Na me so, mārisa, amanusso labheyya yakkhānaṃ samitiṃ gantuṃ. Apissu naṃ, mārisa, amanussā anāvayhampi naṃ kareyyuṃ avivayhaṃ. Apissu naṃ, mārisa, amanussā attāhi paripuṇṇāhi paribhāsāhi paribhāseyyuṃ. Apissu naṃ, mārisa, amanussā rittaṃpissa pattaṃ sīse nikkujjeyyuṃ. Apissu naṃ, mārisa, amanussā sattadhāpissa muddhaṃ phāleyyuṃ. Santi hi, mārisa, amanussā caṇḍā ruddhā rabhasā, te neva mahārājānaṃ ādiyanti, na mahārājānaṃ purisakānaṃ ādiyanti, na mahārājānaṃ purisakānaṃ purisakānaṃ ādiyanti. Te kho te, mārisa, amanussā mahārājānaṃ avaruddhā nāma vuccanti. Seyyathāpi, mārisa, rañño māgadhassa vijite mahācorā. Te neva rañño māgadhassa ādiyanti, na rañño māgadhassa purisakānaṃ ādiyanti, na rañño māgadhassa purisakānaṃ purisakānaṃ ādiyanti. Te kho te, mārisa, mahācorā rañño māgadhassa avaruddhā nāma vuccanti. Evameva kho, mārisa, santi amanussā caṇḍā ruddhā rabhasā, te neva mahārājānaṃ ādiyanti, na mahārājānaṃ purisakānaṃ ādiyanti, na mahārājānaṃ purisakānaṃ purisakānaṃ ādiyanti. Te kho te, mārisa, amanussā mahārājānaṃ avaruddhā nāma vuccanti. Yo hi koci, mārisa, amanusso yakkho vā yakkhinī vā…pe… gandhabbo vā gandhabbī vā…pe… kumbhaṇḍo vā kumbhaṇḍī vā…pe… nāgo vā nāgī vā…pe… paduṭṭhacitto bhikkhuṃ vā bhikkhuniṃ vā upāsakaṃ vā upāsikaṃ vā gacchantaṃ vā upagaccheyya, ṭhitaṃ vā upatiṭṭheyya, nisinnaṃ vā upanisīdeyya, nipannaṃ vā upanipajjeyya. Imesaṃ yakkhānaṃ mahāyakkhānaṃ senāpatīnaṃ mahāsenāpatīnaṃ ujjhāpetabbaṃ vikkanditabbaṃ viravitabbaṃ – ‘ayaṃ yakkho gaṇhāti, ayaṃ yakkho āvisati, ayaṃ yakkho heṭheti, ayaṃ yakkho viheṭheti, ayaṃ yakkho hiṃsati, ayaṃ yakkho vihiṃsati, ayaṃ yakkho na muñcatī’ti.
mula_english:
292. ‘This, dear Sir, is the Āṭānāṭiya protection, for the safety, defense, non-violence, and comfortable dwelling of the monks (bhikkhu), nuns (bhikkhunī), male lay practitioners (upāsaka), and female lay practitioners (upāsikā).

Whoever, dear Sir, be they monk (bhikkhu) or nun (bhikkhunī) or male lay practitioner (upāsaka) or female lay practitioner (upāsikā), if this Āṭānāṭiya protection is well-grasped, complete, and learned, then if any non-human being, be they male *yakṣa* or female *yakṣa*…pe… male *gandharva* or female *gandharva*…pe… male *kumbhāṇḍa* or female *kumbhāṇḍa*…pe… male *nāga* or female *nāga* or young *nāga* or young female *nāga* or great *nāga* minister or *nāga* councilor or *nāga* messenger, with corrupted mind, should follow or approach a monk (bhikkhu) or nun (bhikkhunī) or male lay practitioner (upāsaka) or female lay practitioner (upāsikā) who is walking, standing, sitting, or lying down,

that non-human being, dear Sir, would not receive honor or respect in my villages or towns.

That non-human being, dear Sir, would not receive ground or dwelling in my royal city, Āḷakamandā by name.

That non-human being, dear Sir, would not be able to go to the gathering of the *yakṣas*.

Further, dear Sir, non-human beings would not give or take him in marriage.

Further, dear Sir, non-human beings would abuse him with very personal abuse.

Further, dear Sir, non-human beings would drop an empty bowl over his head.

Further, dear Sir, non-human beings would split his head into seven pieces.

For there are non-human beings, dear Sir, who are fierce, cruel, and violent, they do not take notice of the Great Kings (mahārāja), they do not take notice of the Great Kings’ men, they do not take notice of the Great Kings’ men’s men.

And those non-human beings, dear Sir, are said to be in revolt against the Great Kings (mahārāja).

Just as, dear Sir, there are great thieves in the realm of the king of Magadha,

who do not take notice of the king of Magadha, who do not take notice of the king of Magadha’s men, who do not take notice of the king of Magadha’s men’s men,

and those great thieves, dear Sir, are said to be in revolt against the king of Magadha.

Even so, dear Sir, there are non-human beings who are fierce, cruel, and violent, they do not take notice of the Great Kings (mahārāja), they do not take notice of the Great Kings’ men, they do not take notice of the Great Kings’ men’s men.

And those non-human beings, dear Sir, are said to be in revolt against the Great Kings (mahārāja).

Now, dear Sir, whatever non-human being, be they male *yakṣa* or female *yakṣa*…pe… male *gandharva* or female *gandharva*…pe… male *kumbhāṇḍa* or female *kumbhāṇḍa*…pe… male *nāga* or female *nāga*…pe… with corrupted mind, should approach a monk (bhikkhu) or nun (bhikkhunī) or male lay practitioner (upāsaka) or female lay practitioner (upāsikā) who is walking, standing, sitting, or lying down,

then to these *yakṣas*, great *yakṣas*, generals, and great generals, one should call out, one should shout out, one should cry out: ‘This *yakṣa* has seized me, this *yakṣa* has grabbed me, this *yakṣa* annoys me, this *yakṣa* harasses me, this *yakṣa* hurts me, this *yakṣa* injures me, this *yakṣa* will not release me.’

mula_pali:
293. ‘Katamesaṃ yakkhānaṃ mahāyakkhānaṃ senāpatīnaṃ mahāsenāpatīnaṃ?

‘Indo somo varuṇo ca, bhāradvājo pajāpati;

Candano kāmaseṭṭho ca, kinnughaṇḍu nighaṇḍu ca.

‘Panādo opamañño ca, devasūto ca mātali;

Cittaseno ca gandhabbo, naḷo rājā janesabho.

‘Sātāgiro hevamato, puṇṇako karatiyo guḷo;

Sivako mucalindo ca, vessāmitto yugandharo.

‘Gopālo supparodho ca, hiri netti ca mandiyo;

Pañcālacaṇḍo āḷavako, pajjunno sumano sumukho;

Dadhimukho maṇi māṇivaro dīgho, atho serīsako saha.

‘Imesaṃ yakkhānaṃ mahāyakkhānaṃ senāpatīnaṃ mahāsenāpatīnaṃ ujjhāpetabbaṃ vikkanditabbaṃ viravitabbaṃ – ‘‘ayaṃ yakkho gaṇhāti, ayaṃ yakkho āvisati, ayaṃ yakkho heṭheti, ayaṃ yakkho viheṭheti, ayaṃ yakkho hiṃsati, ayaṃ yakkho vihiṃsati, ayaṃ yakkho na muñcatī’’ti. Ayaṃ kho, mārisa, āṭānāṭiyā rakkhā bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ upāsakānaṃ upāsikānaṃ guttiyā rakkhāya avihiṃsāya phāsuvihārāya. Handa ca dāni mayaṃ, mārisa, gacchāma, bahukiccā mayaṃ bahukaraṇīyā’’’ti. ‘‘‘Yassa dāni tumhe mahārājāno kālaṃ maññathā’’’ti.

294. ‘‘Atha kho, bhikkhave, cattāro mahārājā uṭṭhāyāsanā maṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā tatthevantaradhāyiṃsu. Tepi kho, bhikkhave, yakkhā uṭṭhāyāsanā appekacce maṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā tatthevantaradhāyiṃsu. Appekacce mayā saddhiṃ sammodiṃsu, sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā tatthevantaradhāyiṃsu. Appekacce yenāhaṃ tenañjaliṃ paṇāmetvā tatthevantaradhāyiṃsu. Appekacce nāmagottaṃ sāvetvā tatthevantaradhāyiṃsu. Appekacce tuṇhībhūtā tatthevantaradhāyiṃsu.
mula_english:
294. Then, O monks, the Four Great Kings (cattāro mahārājā) rose from their seats, and after worshipping me (maṃ abhivādetvā) and circumambulating (padakkhiṇaṃ katvā), they vanished right there (tatthevantaradhāyiṃsu).

Then, O monks, some *yakṣas* (yakkhā) rose from their seats, and after worshipping me (maṃ abhivādetvā) and circumambulating (padakkhiṇaṃ katvā), they vanished right there (tatthevantaradhāyiṃsu).

Some exchanged greetings (sammodiṃsu) with me (mayā saddhiṃ), and after exchanging polite and courteous greetings (sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā), vanished right there (tatthevantaradhāyiṃsu).

Some, after raising their hands in respectful salutation (añjaliṃ paṇāmetvā) to where I was (yenāhaṃ tena), vanished right there (tatthevantaradhāyiṃsu).

Some, after announcing their name and family (nāmagottaṃ sāvetvā), vanished right there (tatthevantaradhāyiṃsu).

Some, while keeping silent (tuṇhībhūtā), vanished right there (tatthevantaradhāyiṃsu).

mula_pali:
295. ‘‘Uggaṇhātha , bhikkhave, āṭānāṭiyaṃ rakkhaṃ. Pariyāpuṇātha, bhikkhave, āṭānāṭiyaṃ rakkhaṃ. Dhāretha, bhikkhave, āṭānāṭiyaṃ rakkhaṃ. Atthasaṃhitā atthasaṃhitāyaṃ (syā.), bhikkhave, āṭānāṭiyā rakkhā bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ upāsakānaṃ upāsikānaṃ guttiyā rakkhāya avihiṃsāya phāsuvihārāyā’’ti. Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti.

Āṭānāṭiyasuttaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ navamaṃ.
mula_english:
“Learn, monks, the Āṭānāṭiya protection. Master, monks, the Āṭānāṭiya protection. Bear in mind, monks, the Āṭānāṭiya protection. The Āṭānāṭiya protection, monks, is for the monks’, nuns’, laymen’s, and laywomen’s guard, protection, freedom from harm, and comfortable living.”

That is what the Blessed One said. Elated, those bhikkhus delighted in the Blessed One’s statement.

The Āṭānāṭiya Sutta, the ninth, is finished.

mula_pali:
296. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā mallesu cārikaṃ caramāno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi yena pāvā nāma mallānaṃ nagaraṃ tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā pāvāyaṃ viharati cundassa kammāraputtassa ambavane.

Ubbhatakanavasandhāgāraṃ
mula_english:
Thus have I heard:

On one occasion, the Blessed One was wandering among the Mallas, together with a large Saṅgha of monks, approximately five hundred monks, and he arrived at Pāvā, a city of the Mallas.

There, it is said, the Blessed One stayed near Pāvā in the mango grove of Cunda, the smith's son.

Ubbhatakanavasandhāgāraṃ
commentary_pali:
296.Evaṃme sutanti saṅgītisuttaṃ. Tatrāyamapubbapadavaṇṇanā – cārikaṃ caramānoti nibaddhacārikaṃ caramāno. Tadā kira satthā dasasahassacakkavāḷe ñāṇajālaṃ pattharitvā lokaṃ volokayamāno pāvānagaravāsino mallarājāno disvā ime rājāno mayhaṃ sabbaññutaññāṇajālassa anto paññāyanti, kiṃ nu khoti āvajjanto ‘‘rājāno ekaṃ sandhāgāraṃ kāresuṃ, mayi gate maṅgalaṃ bhaṇāpessanti, ahaṃ tesaṃ maṅgalaṃ vatvā uyyojetvā ‘bhikkhusaṅghassa dhammakathaṃ kathehī’ti sāriputtaṃ vakkhāmi, sāriputto tīhi piṭakehi sammasitvā cuddasapañhādhikena pañhasahassena paṭimaṇḍetvā bhikkhusaṅghassa saṅgītisuttaṃ nāma kathessati, suttantaṃ āvajjetvā pañca bhikkhusatāni saha paṭisambhidāhi arahattaṃ pāpuṇissantī’’ti imamatthaṃ disvā cārikaṃ pakkanto. Tena vuttaṃ – ‘‘mallesu cārikaṃ caramāno’’ti.

Ubbhatakanavasandhāgāravaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
296. Thus, *me suta* is the *saṅgītisuttaṃ*.

Here, the commentary on the *apubbapadavaṇṇanā* is: *cārikaṃ caramāno* means constantly wandering on *cārikaṃ*.

At that time, the teacher, having spread the net of knowledge in the ten thousand world-systems, gazed upon the world. Seeing the Malla kings dwelling in Pāvā city, and reflecting, "These kings appear within the net of my omniscient knowledge, what now?", [he thought,] "The kings have built a *sandhāgāraṃ*; when I go, they will have auspicious verses recited. I will speak auspicious verses to them and then dismiss them, and I will say to Śāriputra, 'Preach a *dhammakathaṃ* to the *bhikkhusaṅghassa*.' Śāriputra, having considered the three *piṭakas*, having adorned [the sermon] with a thousand questions along with fourteen additional questions, will preach the *saṅgītisuttaṃ* to the *bhikkhusaṅghassa*. Having reflected on the *suttantaṃ*, five hundred *bhikkhus* together with the *paṭisambhidā* will attain *arahattaṃ*," having seen this purpose, he departed on *cārikaṃ*.

Therefore, it was said: "wandering on *cārikaṃ* among the Mallas."

Commentary on the *ubbhatakanavasandhāgāravaṇṇanā*.

mula_pali: 297. Tena kho pana samayena pāveyyakānaṃ mallānaṃ ubbhatakaṃ nāma navaṃ sandhāgāraṃ santhāgāraṃ (sī. pī.), saṇṭhāgāraṃ (syā. kaṃ.) acirakāritaṃ hoti anajjhāvuṭṭhaṃ anajjhāvutthaṃ (sī. syā. pī. ka.) samaṇena vā brāhmaṇena vā kenaci vā manussabhūtena. Assosuṃ kho pāveyyakā mallā – ‘‘bhagavā kira mallesu cārikaṃ caramāno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi pāvaṃ anuppatto pāvāyaṃ viharati cundassa kammāraputtassa ambavane’’ti. Atha kho pāveyyakā mallā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho pāveyyakā mallā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘idha, bhante, pāveyyakānaṃ mallānaṃ ubbhatakaṃ nāma navaṃ sandhāgāraṃ acirakāritaṃ hoti anajjhāvuṭṭhaṃ samaṇena vā brāhmaṇena vā kenaci vā manussabhūtena. Tañca kho, bhante, bhagavā paṭhamaṃ paribhuñjatu, bhagavatā paṭhamaṃ paribhuttaṃ pacchā pāveyyakā mallā paribhuñjissanti. Tadassa pāveyyakānaṃ mallānaṃ dīgharattaṃ hitāya sukhāyā’’ti. Adhivāsesi kho bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena.
mula_english:
Now, at that time, the Mallas of Pāvā had just built a new reception hall named Ubbhataka, and it had not yet been dwelt in by any ascetic (*śramaṇa*) or *brāhmaṇa*, or anyone at all in human form.

The Pāvā Mallas heard, "The Blessed One (*bhagavā*), they say, wandering among the Mallas with a large *saṅgha* of monks—approximately 500 monks in all—has arrived at Pāvā and is staying near Pāvā in Cunda the silversmith’s mango grove."

Then the Pāvā Mallas went to the Blessed One (*bhagavā*) and, on arrival, having bowed down to him, sat to one side.

As they were sitting there, the Pāvā Mallas said to the Blessed One (*bhagavā*), "Here, venerable sir (*bhante*), the Mallas of Pāvā have a new reception hall named Ubbhataka, which has just been built, and it has not yet been dwelt in by any ascetic (*śramaṇa*) or *brāhmaṇa*, or anyone at all in human form.

May the Blessed One (*bhagavā*) be the first to use it, venerable sir (*bhante*). When the Blessed One (*bhagavatā*) has used it first, the Pāvā Mallas will use it afterwards.

That will be for their long-term welfare and happiness."

The Blessed One (*bhagavā*) assented by silence.
commentary_pali: 297.Ubbhatakanti tassa nāmaṃ, uccattā vā evaṃ vuttaṃ. Sandhāgāranti nagaramajjhe sandhāgārasālā. Samaṇena vāti ettha yasmā gharavatthupariggahakāleyeva devatā attano vasanaṭṭhānaṃ gaṇhanti. Tasmā devena vāti avatvā ‘‘samaṇena vā brāhmaṇena vā kenaci vā manussabhūtenā’’ti vuttaṃ. Yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsūti bhagavato āgamanaṃ sutvā ‘‘amhehi gantvāpi na bhagavā ānīto, dūtaṃ pesetvāpi na pakkosāpito, sayameva pana mahābhikkhusaṅghaparivāro amhākaṃ vasanaṭṭhānaṃ sampatto, amhehi ca sandhāgārasālā kāritā, ettha mayaṃ dasabalaṃ ānetvā maṅgalaṃ bhaṇāpessāmā’’ti cintetvā upasaṅkamiṃsu.
commentary_english:
297. *Ubbhataka* means "his name," or it is said thus because of height.

*Sandhāgāra* means "the *sandhāgāra* hall in the middle of the city."

"*Samaṇena vā*" here, because the deities take possession of their dwelling place at the very time of taking possession of the site of a house.

Therefore, instead of saying "by a god (devena)," it is said, "by a *śramaṇa*, or by a *brāhmaṇa*, or by anyone in human form."

"*Yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsū*" means, having heard of the arrival of the Blessed One (*bhagavat*), "even though we went, the Blessed One was not brought; even though a messenger was sent, he was not summoned; but the great retinue of *bhikṣus* (*mahābhikkhusaṅghaparivāra*) itself has arrived at our dwelling place, and we have had a *sandhāgāra* hall built, here we will bring the one with the ten powers (*dasabala*) and have auspicious things spoken," thinking thus, they approached.

mula_pali: 298. Atha kho pāveyyakā mallā bhagavato adhivāsanaṃ viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā yena sandhāgāraṃ tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā sabbasanthariṃ sabbasanthariṃ santhataṃ (ka.) sandhāgāraṃ santharitvā bhagavato āsanāni paññāpetvā udakamaṇikaṃ patiṭṭhapetvā telapadīpaṃ āropetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhaṃsu. Ekamantaṃ ṭhitā kho te pāveyyakā mallā bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ – ‘‘sabbasantharisanthataṃ sabbasanthariṃ santhataṃ (sī. pī. ka.), bhante, sandhāgāraṃ, bhagavato āsanāni paññattāni, udakamaṇiko patiṭṭhāpito, telapadīpo āropito. Yassadāni, bhante, bhagavā kālaṃ maññatī’’ti.
mula_english:
Then, the Mallans of Pāvā, knowing the Blessed One's acceptance, rose from their seats, bowed down to the Blessed One, circumambulated him, and went to the assembly hall (saṃdhāgāra). Having approached it, they covered the assembly hall (saṃdhāgāra) entirely with felt rugs, arranged the seats for the Blessed One, set out a water vessel (udakamaṇika), and lit an oil lamp (telapadīpa). Then they approached the Blessed One; having approached, bowed down to the Blessed One, and stood to one side.

Standing to one side, the Mallans of Pāvā said this to the Blessed One: "The assembly hall (saṃdhāgāra) is entirely covered with felt rugs, venerable sir (bhante). The seats for the Blessed One are arranged, the water vessel (udakamaṇika) is set out, and the oil lamp (telapadīpa) is lit. May the Blessed One do what he thinks it is now time to do."
commentary_pali: 298.Yena sandhāgāraṃ tenupasaṅkamiṃsūti taṃ divasaṃ kira sandhāgāre cittakammaṃ niṭṭhapetvā aṭṭakā muttamattā honti, buddhā ca nāma araññajjhāsayā araññārāmā, antogāme vaseyyuṃ vā no vā. Tasmā bhagavato manaṃ jānitvāva paṭijaggissāmāti cintetvā te bhagavantaṃ upasaṅkamiṃsu. Idāni pana manaṃ labhitvā paṭijaggitukāmā yena sandhāgāraṃ tenupasaṅkamiṃsu . Sabbasantharinti yathā sabbaṃ santhataṃ hoti, evaṃ. Yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsūti ettha pana te mallarājāno sandhāgāraṃ paṭijaggitvā nagaravīthiyopi sammajjāpetvā dhaje ussāpetvā gehadvāresu puṇṇaghaṭe ca kadaliyo ca ṭhapāpetvā sakalanagaraṃ dīpamālādīhi vippakiṇṇatārakaṃ viya katvā khīrapāyake dārake khīraṃ pāyyetha, dahare kumāre lahuṃ lahuṃ bhojāpetvā sayāpetha, uccāsaddaṃ mā karittha, ajja ekarattiṃ satthā antogāme vasissati, buddhā nāma appasaddakāmā hontīti bheriṃ carāpetvā sayaṃ daṇḍadīpikaṃ ādāya yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu.
commentary_english:
"Where the assembly hall was, there they approached," that day, it is said, having finished the painted work in the assembly hall, the upper stories were exceedingly full. For Buddhas are by nature those who dwell in the wilderness, delighting in the wilderness, and they may or may not dwell within a village. Therefore, thinking, "Having understood the mind of the Blessed One, we will attend upon him," they approached the Blessed One. Now, having obtained the mind, desiring to attend upon [him], they approached where the assembly hall was.

"<hi rend="bold">Sabbasanthari</hi>nti" means just as everything is spread out, so it is.

"<hi rend="bold">Yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsū</hi>ti" Here, those Malla kings, having prepared the assembly hall, and having caused the city streets to be swept, and having raised flags, and having placed full water pots and banana trees at the house doors, and having made the entire city like a scattering of stars with rows of lamps and so on, the milk-drinking boys were given milk to drink, the young boys were quickly fed and put to sleep, they did not make a loud noise, "Today, for one night, the Teacher will dwell within the village, for Buddhas are those who desire little noise," having caused the drum to be sounded, themselves taking a staff-torch, they approached where the Blessed One was.

mula_pali: 299. Atha kho bhagavā nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya saddhiṃ bhikkhusaṅghena yena sandhāgāraṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā pāde pakkhāletvā sandhāgāraṃ pavisitvā majjhimaṃ thambhaṃ nissāya puratthābhimukho nisīdi. Bhikkhusaṅghopi kho pāde pakkhāletvā sandhāgāraṃ pavisitvā pacchimaṃ bhittiṃ nissāya puratthābhimukho nisīdi bhagavantaṃyeva purakkhatvā. Pāveyyakāpi kho mallā pāde pakkhāletvā sandhāgāraṃ pavisitvā puratthimaṃ bhittiṃ nissāya pacchimābhimukhā nisīdiṃsu bhagavantaṃyeva purakkhatvā. Atha kho bhagavā pāveyyake malle bahudeva rattiṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṃsetvā uyyojesi – ‘‘abhikkantā kho, vāseṭṭhā, ratti. Yassadāni tumhe kālaṃ maññathā’’ti. ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho pāveyyakā mallā bhagavato paṭissutvā uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkamiṃsu.
mula_english:
Then the Blessed One, having dressed and taking his bowl and outer robe, went together with the Saṅgha of monks to the assembly hall ( *sandhāgāraṃ* ); having arrived, washed his feet, entered the assembly hall, and sat down facing east, leaning against the central pillar (*majjhimaṃ thambhaṃ*).

The Saṅgha of monks also washed their feet, entered the assembly hall, and sat down facing east, leaning against the western wall (*pacchimaṃ bhittiṃ*), with the Blessed One in front of them.

The Mallas of Pāvā also washed their feet, entered the assembly hall, and sat down facing west, leaning against the eastern wall (*puratthimaṃ bhittiṃ*), with the Blessed One in front of them.

Then the Blessed One, having instructed, encouraged, roused, and delighted the Mallas of Pāvā for much of the night with a Dhamma talk, dismissed them, saying, "The night is far gone, Vāseṭṭhas. Now is the time for you to do as you think fit." (*yassadāni tumhe kālaṃ maññatha*).

"Even so, venerable sir ( *bhante* )" the Mallas of Pāvā replied to the Blessed One, and rising from their seats, bowed down to the Blessed One, circumambulated him, and departed.
commentary_pali:
299.Bhagavantaṃyeva purakkhatvāti bhagavantaṃ purato katvā. Tattha bhagavā bhikkhūnañceva upāsakānañca majjhe nisinno ativiya virocati, samantapāsādiko suvaṇṇavaṇṇo abhirūpo dassanīyo. Purimakāyato suvaṇṇavaṇṇā rasmi uṭṭhahitvā asītihatthaṃ ṭhānaṃ gaṇhāti. Pacchimakāyato. Dakkhiṇahatthato. Vāmahatthato suvaṇṇavaṇṇā rasmi uṭṭhahitvā asītihatthaṃ ṭhānaṃ gaṇhāti. Upari kesantato paṭṭhāya sabbakesāvaṭṭehi moragīvavaṇṇā rasmi uṭṭhahitvā gaganatale asītihatthaṃ ṭhānaṃ gaṇhāti. Heṭṭhā pādatalehi pavāḷavaṇṇā rasmi uṭṭhahitvā ghanapathaviyaṃ asītihatthaṃ ṭhānaṃ gaṇhāti. Evaṃ samantā asīti hatthamattaṃ ṭhānaṃ chabbaṇṇā buddharasmiyo vijjotamānā vipphandamānā vidhāvanti. Sabbe disābhāgā suvaṇṇacampakapupphehi vikiriyamānā viya suvaṇṇaghaṭato nikkhantasuvaṇṇarasadhārāhi siñcamānā viya pasāritasuvaṇṇapaṭaparikkhittā viya verambhavātasamuṭṭhitakiṃsukakaṇikārapupphacuṇṇasamākiṇṇā viya ca vippakāsanti.

Bhagavatopi asītianubyañjanabyāmappabhādvattiṃsavaralakkhaṇasamujjalaṃ sarīraṃ samuggatatārakaṃ viya gaganatalaṃ, vikasitamiva padumavanaṃ , sabbapāliphullo viya yojanasatiko pāricchattako paṭipāṭiyā ṭhapitānaṃ dvattiṃsacandānaṃ dvattiṃsasūriyānaṃ dvattiṃsacakkavattirājānaṃ dvattiṃsadevarājānaṃ dvattiṃsamahābrahmānaṃ siriyā siriṃ abhibhavamānaṃ viya virocati. Parivāretvā nisinnā bhikkhūpi sabbeva appicchā santuṭṭhā pavivittā asaṃsaṭṭhā āraddhavīriyā vattāro vacanakkhamā codakā pāpagarahino sīlasampannā samādhisampannā paññāvimutti vimuttiñāṇadassanasampannā. Tehi parivārito bhagavā rattakambalaparikkhitto viya suvaṇṇakkhandho , rattapadumavanasaṇḍamajjhagatā viya suvaṇṇanāvā, pavāḷavedikāparikkhitto viya suvaṇṇapāsādo virocittha.

Asītimahātherāpi naṃ meghavaṇṇaṃ paṃsukūlaṃ pārupitvā maṇivammavammitā viya mahānāgā parivārayiṃsu vantarāgā bhinnakilesā vijaṭitajaṭā chinnabandhanā kule vā gaṇe vā alaggā. Iti bhagavā sayaṃ vītarāgo vītarāgehi, vītadoso vītadosehi, vītamoho vītamohehi, nittaṇho nittaṇhehi, nikkileso nikkilesehi, sayaṃ buddho bahussutabuddhehi parivārito pattaparivāritaṃ viya kesaraṃ, kesaraparivāritā viya kaṇṇikā, aṭṭhanāgasahassaparivārito viya chaddanto nāgarājā, navutihaṃsasahassaparivārito viya dhataraṭṭho haṃsarājā, senaṅgaparivārito viya cakkavattirājā, marugaṇaparivārito viya sakko devarājā, brahmagaṇaparivārito viya hārito mahābrahmā, asamena buddhavesena aparimāṇena buddhavilāsena tassaṃ parisati nisinno pāveyyake malle bahudeva rattiṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā uyyojesi.

Ettha ca dhammikathā nāma sandhāgāraanumodanappaṭisaṃyuttā pakiṇṇakakathā veditabbā. Tadā hi bhagavā ākāsagaṅgaṃ otārento viya pathavojaṃ ākaḍḍhanto viya mahājambuṃ matthake gahetvā cālento viya yojaniyamadhugaṇḍaṃ cakkayantena pīḷetvā madhupānaṃ pāyamāno viya ca pāveyyakānaṃ mallānaṃ hitasukhāvahaṃ pakiṇṇakakathaṃ kathesi.

dhammikathā
commentary_english:
299. *bhagavantaṃyeva purakkhatvā* means having put the Blessed One in front.

There, the Blessed One, seated in the midst of the monks and lay followers, exceedingly shone forth, being entirely pleasing, of golden color, beautiful, and worthy of being seen.

From the front of his body, a golden-colored ray arose and occupied a space of eighty cubits.

From the back of his body...

From the right hand...

From the left hand, a golden-colored ray arose and occupied a space of eighty cubits.

Starting from the top of his head, with all the whorls of hair, a ray the color of a peacock's neck arose and occupied a space of eighty cubits in the sky.

From beneath the soles of his feet, a coral-colored ray arose and occupied a space of eighty cubits in the solid earth.

Thus, on all sides, a space of eighty cubits was filled by the six-colored Buddha rays, which were shining, pulsating, and darting about.

All directions shone forth as if they were being scattered with golden *campaka* flowers, as if they were being sprinkled with streams of golden essence flowing from a golden pitcher, as if they were surrounded by a stretched-out golden cloth, and as if they were covered with a powder of *kiṃsuka* and *kaṇikāra* flowers stirred up by the *verambha* wind.

The Blessed One's body, resplendent with the eighty minor marks, a fathom's span of light, and the thirty-two excellent marks, shone forth as if it were the sky filled with rising stars, as if it were a blooming lotus grove, like a *pāricchatta* tree a hundred *yojanas* in height covered with all sorts of flowers, and as if it were surpassing the glory of the thirty-two moons, thirty-two suns, thirty-two universal monarchs, thirty-two divine kings, and thirty-two Great Brahmās arranged in order.

The monks who were sitting around him were all of few desires, content, secluded, unassociated, with aroused energy, eloquent, patient of speech, instigators, censurers of evil, accomplished in virtue, accomplished in concentration, accomplished in wisdom-deliverance and vision of the knowledge of deliverance.

The Blessed One, surrounded by them, shone like a golden mountain surrounded by a red blanket, like a golden ship in the middle of a grove of red lotuses, and like a golden palace surrounded by a coral terrace.

The eighty great elders, having put on dust-heap robes the color of clouds and armored with jewels, like great nāgas, surrounded him, free from passion, with broken defilements, with untangled matted hair, with severed bonds, unattached to family or group.

Thus, the Blessed One, himself free from passion, surrounded by those free from passion; free from hatred, surrounded by those free from hatred; free from delusion, surrounded by those free from delusion; free from craving, surrounded by those free from craving; free from defilement, surrounded by those free from defilement; himself awakened, surrounded by the much-learned awakened ones, [shone] like pollen surrounded by petals, like a pericarp surrounded by pollen, like the nāga king Chaddanta surrounded by eight thousand nāgas, like the swan king Dhataraṭṭha surrounded by ninety thousand swans, like a universal monarch surrounded by his army, like Śakra, the king of the gods, surrounded by the host of Maruts, and like Harita, the Great Brahmā, surrounded by the host of Brahmās. Seated in that assembly in an unequaled Buddha's guise, with immeasurable Buddha's splendor, he encouraged the Mallas of Pāveyyaka for much of the night with a *dhammī kathā* and then dismissed them.

Here, *dhammī kathā* should be understood as diverse talk connected with approval of the meeting hall.

Then, the Blessed One spoke talk that was diverse and conducive to the benefit and happiness of the Mallas of Pāveyyaka, as if he were letting down the Ganges of the sky, as if he were drawing up the essence of the earth, as if he were taking the great *jambu* fruit on his head and shaking it, and as if he were squeezing the honey sac of a *yojanīya* with a wheel press and giving them a drink of honey.

*Dhammī kathā*.

mula_pali:
300. Atha kho bhagavā acirapakkantesu pāveyyakesu mallesu tuṇhībhūtaṃ tuṇhībhūtaṃ bhikkhusaṃghaṃ anuviloketvā āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ āmantesi – ‘‘vigatathinamiddho vigatathīnamiddho (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) kho, sāriputta, bhikkhusaṅgho. Paṭibhātu taṃ, sāriputta, bhikkhūnaṃ dhammīkathā. Piṭṭhi me āgilāyati. Tamahaṃ āyamissāmī’’ti āyameyyāmīti (syā. kaṃ.). ‘‘Evaṃ, bhante’’ti kho āyasmā sāriputto bhagavato paccassosi. Atha kho bhagavā catugguṇaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ paññapetvā dakkhiṇena passena sīhaseyyaṃ kappesi pāde pādaṃ accādhāya, sato sampajāno uṭṭhānasaññaṃ manasi karitvā.

Bhinnanigaṇṭhavatthu
mula_english:
Then, not long after the Pāvā Mallans had departed, the Blessed One, surveying the silent Saṅgha of monks, addressed the venerable Sāriputta, saying: “Sāriputta, the Saṅgha of monks is free from sloth and torpor (vigatathinamiddho kho, sāriputta, bhikkhusaṅgho). Let a Dhamma talk occur to you, Sāriputta, for the monks. My back aches (piṭṭhi me āgilāyati). I will stretch it (tamahaṃ āyamissāmī’’ti).”

“As you say, venerable sir (evaṃ, bhante’ti), ” the venerable Sāriputta replied to the Blessed One.

Then the Blessed One folded his outer robe in four, and lay down on his right side in the lion's posture (sīhaseyyaṃ kappesi), placing one foot on top of the other, mindful and fully aware, keeping in mind the intention of rising.

The matter of the Dissension among the Nigaṇṭhas.
commentary_pali:
300.Tuṇhībhūtaṃ tuṇhībhūtanti yaṃ yaṃ disaṃ anuviloketi, tattha tattha tuṇhībhūtameva. Anuviloketvāti maṃsacakkhunā dibbacakkhunāti dvīhi cakkhūhi tato tato viloketvā. Maṃsacakkhunā hi nesaṃ bahiddhā iriyāpathaṃ pariggahesi. Tattha ekabhikkhussāpi neva hatthakukkuccaṃ na pādakukkuccaṃ ahosi, na koci sīsamukkhipi, na kathaṃ kathesi, na niddāyanto nisīdi. Sabbepi tīhi sikkhāhi sikkhitā nivāte padīpasikhā viya niccalā nisīdiṃsu. Iti nesaṃ imaṃ iriyāpathaṃ maṃsacakkhunā pariggahesi. Ālokaṃ pana vaḍḍhayitvā dibbacakkhunā hadayarūpaṃ disvā abbhantaragataṃ sīlaṃ olokesi. So anekasatānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ antokumbhiyaṃ jalamānaṃ padīpaṃ viya arahattupagaṃ sīlaṃ addasa. Āraddhavipassakā hi te bhikkhū. Iti nesaṃ sīlaṃ disvā ‘‘imepi bhikkhū mayhaṃ anucchavikā, ahampi imesaṃ anucchaviko’’ti cakkhutalesu nimittaṃ ṭhapetvā bhikkhusaṅghaṃ oloketvā āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ āmantesi ‘‘piṭṭhi me āgilāyatī’’ti. Kasmā āgilāyati? Bhagavato hi chabbassāni mahāpadhānaṃ padahantassa mahantaṃ kāyadukkhaṃ ahosi. Athassa aparabhāge mahallakakāle piṭṭhivāto uppajji.

Saṅghāṭiṃ paññāpetvāti sandhāgārassa kira ekapasse te rājāno kappiyamañcakaṃ paññapesuṃ ‘‘appeva nāma satthā nipajjeyyā’’ti. Satthāpi catūhi iriyāpathehi paribhuttaṃ imesaṃ mahapphalaṃ bhavissatīti tattha saṅghāṭiṃ paññāpetvā nipajji.

Saṅghāṭiṃ paññāpetvā

Bhinnanigaṇṭhavatthuvaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
"Being silent, being silent": Whatever direction he surveys, it is only silent.

"Having surveyed": Having looked around from there in various directions with two eyes, the physical eye and the divine eye.

With the physical eye, he ascertained their outward conduct.

There, not even for one monk was there hesitation regarding the hands or hesitation regarding the feet; no one lifted his head, no one spoke a word, no one sat dozing.

All, trained in the three trainings, sat still like a lamp flame in a windless place.

Thus, with the physical eye, he ascertained this conduct of theirs.

But increasing the light, with the divine eye, having seen the heart-form, he looked at the virtue gone within.

He saw the virtue leading to arahantship, like a lamp burning within the inner vessel of many hundreds of monks.

For those monks were beginning insight.

Thus, having seen their virtue, fixing the sign in the eye sockets, thinking, "These monks are suitable for me, and I am suitable for them," surveying the community of monks, he addressed the venerable Sāriputta, "My back is aching."

Why is it aching? For the Blessed One, while undertaking the great struggle for six years, there was great bodily pain.

Then in the latter part of his life, in old age, back-wind arose for him.

"Having prepared the double robe": It seems those kings prepared a suitable couch on one side of the assembly hall, thinking, "Perhaps the Teacher might lie down."

The Teacher, thinking that it would be of great fruit for them, having used it with the four postures, lay down there, having prepared the double robe (*saṃghāṭīṃ prajñāpetvā*).

"Having prepared the double robe"
Explanation of the Story of the Split Nigaṇṭha

mula_pali: 301. Tena kho pana samayena nigaṇṭho nāṭaputto pāvāyaṃ adhunākālaṅkato hoti. Tassa kālaṅkiriyāya bhinnā nigaṇṭhā dvedhikajātā ddheḷhakajātā (syā. kaṃ.) bhaṇḍanajātā kalahajātā vivādāpannā aññamaññaṃ mukhasattīhi vitudantā viharanti vicaranti (syā. kaṃ.) – ‘‘na tvaṃ imaṃ dhammavinayaṃ ājānāsi, ahaṃ imaṃ dhammavinayaṃ ājānāmi, kiṃ tvaṃ imaṃ dhammavinayaṃ ājānissasi! Micchāpaṭipanno tvamasi, ahamasmi sammāpaṭipanno. Sahitaṃ me, asahitaṃ te. Purevacanīyaṃ pacchā avaca, pacchāvacanīyaṃ pure avaca. Adhiciṇṇaṃ te viparāvattaṃ, āropito te vādo, niggahito tvamasi, cara vādappamokkhāya, nibbeṭhehi vā sace pahosī’’ti. Vadhoyeva kho maññe nigaṇṭhesu nāṭaputtiyesu vattati. Yepi yepi te (sī. pī.) nigaṇṭhassa nāṭaputtassa sāvakā gihī odātavasanā , tepi nigaṇṭhesu nāṭaputtiyesu nibbinnarūpā virattarūpā paṭivānarūpā, yathā taṃ durakkhāte dhammavinaye duppavedite aniyyānike anupasamasaṃvattanike asammāsambuddhappavedite bhinnathūpe appaṭisaraṇe.
mula_english:
301. At that time, Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta had recently died in Pāvā.

After his death, the Nigaṇṭhas were split into two factions, given to quarreling and disputing, stabbing one another with weapons of the mouth, saying, "You do not understand this *Dhamma-vinaya*; I understand this *Dhamma-vinaya*. How could you understand this *Dhamma-vinaya*? You are practicing wrongly; I am practicing rightly. I am consistent; you are inconsistent. You said last what should have been said first, and you said first what should have been said last. What you had so carefully thought out has been turned inside out. Your doctrine is refuted. You are proved wrong. Go and learn better, or disentangle yourself if you can!"

It seemed as though nothing but slaughter was being committed among the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputtas.

And even those lay disciples of Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta, dressed in white, were disgusted, dismayed, and disappointed with the Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputtas, and at how poorly proclaimed and poorly expounded that *Dhamma-vinaya* was, not leading out, not conducive to calming, expounded by one who was not rightly self-awakened, its foundation now broken, without an arbiter.
commentary_pali: 301.Tassa kālaṅkiriyāyātiādīsu yaṃ vattabbaṃ, taṃ sabbaṃ heṭṭhā vuttameva.
commentary_english: As for what is to be said regarding "tassa kālaṅkiriyāyā" and the like, all that has already been said below.

mula_pali:
302. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto bhikkhū āmantesi – ‘‘nigaṇṭho, āvuso, nāṭaputto pāvāyaṃ adhunākālaṅkato, tassa kālaṅkiriyāya bhinnā nigaṇṭhā dvedhikajātā…pe… bhinnathūpe appaṭisaraṇe’’. ‘‘Evañhetaṃ, āvuso, hoti durakkhāte dhammavinaye duppavedite aniyyānike anupasamasaṃvattanike asammāsambuddhappavedite. Ayaṃ kho panāvuso amhākaṃ asmākaṃ (pī.) bhagavatā bhagavato (ka. sī.) dhammo svākkhāto suppavedito niyyāniko upasamasaṃvattaniko sammāsambuddhappavedito. Tattha sabbeheva saṅgāyitabbaṃ, na vivaditabbaṃ, yathayidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ addhaniyaṃ assa ciraṭṭhitikaṃ, tadassa bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ.

‘‘Katamo cāvuso, amhākaṃ bhagavatā bhagavato (ka. sī.) dhammo svākkhāto suppavedito niyyāniko upasamasaṃvattaniko sammāsambuddhappavedito; yattha sabbeheva saṅgāyitabbaṃ, na vivaditabbaṃ, yathayidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ addhaniyaṃ assa ciraṭṭhitikaṃ, tadassa bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ?

Ekakaṃ
mula_english:
“Friends, Nigaṇṭha Nāṭaputta has recently died in Pāvā. On his death, the Nigaṇṭhas have split into two factions… their shrine is broken, left without a refuge.”

“That’s the way it is, friends, with a poorly proclaimed *Dhamma-Vinaya*, poorly expounded, not leading out, not conducive to calming, expounded by one who is not rightly self-awakened.

“But, friends, our *dharma* is well-proclaimed by the Blessed One, well-expounded, leading out, conducive to calming, expounded by one who is rightly self-awakened. There it should all be recited together, without dispute, so that this holy life (*brahmacariya*) will endure & last a long time, and that will be for the benefit & happiness of many, out of sympathy for the world, for the welfare, benefit, & happiness of *devas* and human beings.

“And which is our *dharma*, friends, that is well expounded by the Blessed One, leading out, conducive to calming, expounded by one who is rightly self-awakened, that should all be recited together, without dispute, so that this holy life (*brahmacariya*) will endure & last a long time, and that will be for the benefit & happiness of many, out of sympathy for the world, for the welfare, benefit, & happiness of *devas* and human beings?
commentary_pali:
302.Āmantesīti bhaṇḍanādivūpasamakaraṃ svākhyātaṃ dhammaṃ desetukāmo āmantesi.

Ekakavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
"āmantesī": He invited, meaning he invited, wishing to teach the well-proclaimed Dharma which pacifies quarrels, etc.

Explanation of the one.

mula_pali:
303. ‘‘Atthi kho, āvuso, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena eko dhammo sammadakkhāto. Tattha sabbeheva saṅgāyitabbaṃ, na vivaditabbaṃ, yathayidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ addhaniyaṃ assa ciraṭṭhitikaṃ , tadassa bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ. Katamo eko dhammo? Sabbe sattā āhāraṭṭhitikā. Sabbe sattā saṅkhāraṭṭhitikā. Ayaṃ kho, āvuso, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena eko dhammo sammadakkhāto. Tattha sabbeheva saṅgāyitabbaṃ, na vivaditabbaṃ , yathayidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ addhaniyaṃ assa ciraṭṭhitikaṃ, tadassa bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ.

Dukaṃ
mula_english:
303. “There is, friends (āvusho), one *dharma* that is rightly expounded by the Blessed One—the one who knows (jānatā), the one who sees (passatā), the Worthy One (arahatā), rightly self-awakened (sammāsambuddhena).

There all should recite together (saṅgāyitabbaṃ), without dispute (na vivaditabbaṃ), so that this holy life (*brahmacariya*) will endure & last a long time (ciraṭṭhitikaṃ), and that will be for the benefit (hitāya) & happiness (sukhāya) of many (bahujanā), out of sympathy (anukampāya) for the world (loka), for the welfare (atthaya), benefit (hitāya), & happiness (sukhāya) of gods (*deva*) & human beings (manussānaṃ).

What is that one *dharma* (eko dhammo)? All beings (sabbe sattā) are maintained by nutriment (āhāraṭṭhitikā).
All beings (sabbe sattā) are maintained by fabrication (saṅkhāraṭṭhitikā).

This, friends (āvusho), is one *dharma* that is rightly expounded by the Blessed One—the one who knows (jānatā), the one who sees (passatā), the Worthy One (arahatā), rightly self-awakened (sammāsambuddhena).
There all should recite together (saṅgāyitabbaṃ), without dispute (na vivaditabbaṃ), so that this holy life (*brahmacariya*) will endure & last a long time (ciraṭṭhitikaṃ), and that will be for the benefit (hitāya) & happiness (sukhāya) of many (bahujanā), out of sympathy (anukampāya) for the world (loka), for the welfare (atthaya), benefit (hitāya), & happiness (sukhāya) of gods (*deva*) & human beings (manussānaṃ).

Dukaṃ
commentary_pali:
303.Tatthāti tasmiṃ dhamme. Saṅgāyitabbanti samaggehi gāyitabbaṃ, ekavacanehi aviruddhavacanehi bhaṇitabbaṃ. Na vivaditabbanti atthe vā byañjane vā vivādo na kātabbo. Eko dhammoti ekakadukatikādivasena bahudhā sāmaggirasaṃ dassetukāmo paṭhamaṃ tāva ‘‘eko dhammo’’ti āha. Sabbe sattāti kāmabhavādīsu saññābhavādīsu ekavokārabhavādīsu ca sabbabhavesu sabbe sattā. Āhāraṭṭhitikāti āhārato ṭhiti etesanti āhāraṭṭhitikā. Iti sabbasattānaṃ ṭhiti hetu āhāro nāma eko dhammo amhākaṃ satthārā yāthāvato ñatvā sammadakkhāto āvusoti dīpeti.

Nanu ca evaṃ sante yaṃ vuttaṃ ‘‘asaññasattā devā ahetukā anāhārā aphassakā’’tiādi, (vibha. 1017) taṃ vacanaṃ virujjhatīti, na virujjhati. Tesañhi jhānaṃ āhāro hoti. Evaṃ santepi ‘‘cattārome, bhikkhave, āhārā bhūtānaṃ vā sattānaṃ ṭhitiyā sambhavesīnaṃ vā anuggahāya. Katame cattāro? Kabaḷīkāro āhāro oḷāriko vā sukhumo vā, phasso dutiyo, manosañcetanā tatiyā, viññāṇaṃ catuttha’’nti (saṃ. ni. 2.11) idampi virujjhatīti, idampi na virujjhati. Etasmiñhi sutte nippariyāyena āhāralakkhaṇāva dhammā āhārāti vuttā. Idha pana pariyāyena paccayo āhāroti vutto. Sabbadhammānañhi paccayo laddhuṃ vaṭṭati. So ca yaṃ yaṃ phalaṃ janeti, taṃ taṃ āharati nāma, tasmā āhāroti vuccati. Tenevāha ‘‘avijjampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sāhāraṃ vadāmi, no anāhāraṃ. Ko ca, bhikkhave, avijjāya āhāro? Pañcanīvaraṇātissa vacanīyaṃ. Pañcanīvaraṇepāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sāhāre vadāmi, no anāhāre. Ko ca, bhikkhave, pañcannaṃ nīvaraṇānaṃ āhāro? Ayonisomanasikārotissa vacanīya’’nti (a. ni. 10.61). Ayaṃ idha adhippeto.

Etasmiñhi paccayāhāre gahite pariyāyāhāropi nippariyāyāhāropi sabbo gahitova hoti. Tattha asaññabhave paccayāhāro labbhati. Anuppanne hi buddhe titthāyatane pabbajitā vāyokasiṇe parikammaṃ katvā catutthajjhānaṃ nibbattetvā tato vuṭṭhāya dhī cittaṃ, dhibbatetaṃ cittaṃ cittassa nāma abhāvoyeva sādhu, cittañhi nissāyeva vadhabandhādipaccayaṃ dukkhaṃ uppajjati. Citte asati natthetanti khantiṃ ruciṃ uppādetvā aparihīnajjhānā kālaṅkatvā asaññabhave nibbattanti. Yo yassa iriyāpatho manussaloke paṇihito ahosi, so tena iriyāpathena nibbattitvā pañca kappasatāni ṭhito vā nisinno vā nipanno vā hoti. Evarūpānampi sattānaṃ paccayāhāro labbhati. Te hi yaṃ jhānaṃ bhāvetvā nibbattā, tadeva nesaṃ paccayo hoti. Yathā jiyāvegena khittasaro yāva jiyāvego atthi, tāva gacchati, evaṃ yāva jhānapaccayo atthi, tāva tiṭṭhanti. Tasmiṃ niṭṭhite khīṇavego saro viya patanti. Ye pana te nerayikā neva uṭṭhānaphalūpajīvī na puññaphalūpajīvīti vuttā, tesaṃ ko āhāroti ? Tesaṃ kammameva āhāro. Kiṃ pañca āhārā atthīti ce. Pañca, na pañcāti idaṃ na vattabbaṃ. Nanu paccayo āhāroti vuttametaṃ. Tasmā yena kammena te niraye nibbattā, tadeva tesaṃ ṭhitipaccayattā āhāro hoti. Yaṃ sandhāya idaṃ vuttaṃ ‘‘na ca tāva kālaṅkaroti, yāva na taṃ pāpakammaṃ byantī hotī’’ti (ma. ni. 3.250).

Kabaḷīkāraṃ āhāraṃ ārabbha cettha vivādo na kātabbo. Mukhe uppanno kheḷopi hi tesaṃ āhārakiccaṃ sādheti. Kheḷopi hi niraye dukkhavedaniyo hutvā paccayo hoti, sagge sukhavedaniyo. Iti kāmabhave nippariyāyena cattāro āhārā. Rūpārūpabhavesu ṭhapetvā asaññaṃ sesānaṃ tayo. Asaññānañceva avasesānañca paccayāhāroti iminā āhārena ‘‘sabbe sattā āhāraṭṭhitikā’’ti etaṃ pañhaṃ kathetvā ‘‘ayaṃ kho āvuso’’ti evaṃ niyyātanampi ‘‘atthi kho āvuso’’ti puna uddharaṇampi akatvā ‘‘sabbe sattā saṅkhāraṭṭhitikā’’ti dutiyapañhaṃ vissajjesi.

Kasmā pana na niyyātesi na uddharittha? Tattha tattha niyyātiyamānepi uddhariyamānepi pariyāpuṇituṃ vācetuṃ dukkhaṃ hoti, tasmā dve ekābaddhe katvā vissajjesi. Imasmimpi vissajjane heṭṭhā vuttapaccayova attano phalassa saṅkharaṇato saṅkhāroti vutto. Iti heṭṭhā āhārapaccayo kathito, idha saṅkhārapaccayoti ayamettha heṭṭhimato viseso. ‘‘Heṭṭhā nippariyāyāhāro gahito, idha pariyāyāhāroti evaṃ gahite viseso pākaṭo bhaveyya, no ca gaṇhiṃsū’ti mahāsīvatthero āha. Indriyabaddhassapi hi anindriyabaddhassapi paccayo laddhuṃ vaṭṭati. Vinā paccayena dhammo nāma natthi. Tattha anindriyabaddhassa tiṇarukkhalatādino pathavīraso āporaso ca paccayo hoti. Deve avassante hi tiṇādīni milāyanti, vassante ca pana haritāni honti. Iti tesaṃ pathavīraso āporaso ca paccayo hoti. Indriyabaddhassa avijjā taṇhā kammaṃ āhāroti evamādayo paccayā, iti heṭṭhā paccayoyeva āhāroti kathito, idha saṅkhāroti. Ayamevettha viseso.

Ayaṃkho, āvusoti āvuso amhākaṃ satthārā mahābodhimaṇḍe nisīditvā sayaṃ sabbaññutaññāṇena sacchikatvā ayaṃ ekadhammo desito. Tattha ekadhamme tumhehi sabbeheva saṅgāyitabbaṃ na vivaditabbaṃ. Yathayidaṃ brahmacariyanti yathā saṅgāyamānānaṃ tumhākaṃ idaṃ sāsanabrahmacariyaṃ addhaniyaṃ assa. Ekena hi bhikkhunā ‘‘atthi, kho āvuso, eko dhammo sammadakkhāto. Katamo eko dhammo? Sabbe sattā āhāraṭṭhitikā. Sabbe sattā saṅkhāraṭṭhitikā’’ti kathite tassa kathaṃ sutvā añño kathessati. Tassapi aññoti evaṃ paramparakathāniyamena idaṃ brahmacariyaṃ ciraṃ tiṭṭhamānaṃ sadevakassa lokassa atthāya hitāya bhavissatīti ekakavasena dhammasenāpati sāriputtatthero sāmaggirasaṃ dassesīti.

Ayaṃ kho, āvuso Yathayidaṃ brahmacariya

Ekakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

Dukavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
Tatthā: That is, in that Dharma. Saṅgāyitabba: To be chanted by those in harmony, to be recited with concordant words in unison. Na vivaditabba: There should be no dispute in meaning or expression. Eko dhammo: "One Dharma," intending to show the taste of harmony in many ways by means of the one, the dyads, the triads, etc., first he said, "one Dharma." Sabbe sattā: "All beings," that is, all beings in all existences, in the desire realm and so on, in the realm of perception and so on, in the realm of one-idea and so on. Āhāraṭṭhitikā: Āhāraṭṭhitikā means the condition of being maintained by nutriment, of those beings. Thus, the Buddha, our teacher, illuminates that nutriment is one dharma for the sake of the maintenance of all beings, having known it as it is, and having well explained it, O friends. Now, if it is like that, the statement, "Unconscious beings, gods, are without cause, without nutriment, without contact," and so forth (Vibha. 1017), would be contradicted. It is not contradicted. For jhāna is their nutriment. Even when that exists, [the Buddha] said, "There are these four kinds of nutriment, monks, for the maintenance of beings that have already come to be and for the support of those seeking a new existence. What are the four? Edible food, coarse or subtle, is the first; contact is the second; mental volition is the third; and consciousness is the fourth" (Saṃ. Ni. 2.11). If this, too, is contradictory, this too is not contradictory. In this sūtra, the characteristics of nutriment themselves are called nutriment without qualification. Here, however, a condition is called nutriment in a qualified way. For a condition is suitable to be obtained by all things. And that which generates any fruit, that it brings, therefore it is called nutriment. Therefore, he said, "I say that ignorance, monks, has nutriment, not without nutriment. And what, monks, is the nutriment for ignorance? It should be said: the five hindrances. And I say that the five hindrances, monks, have nutriment, not without nutriment. And what, monks, is the nutriment for the five hindrances? It should be said: improper attention" (A. Ni. 10.61). This is the meaning intended here. When a conditional nutriment is taken, then qualified nutriment and unqualified nutriment are all taken. There, in the unconscious realm, conditional nutriment is obtained. Indeed, when Buddhas have not arisen, ascetics in other sects, having performed the preliminary act on the air kasina, having generated the fourth jhāna, and having arisen from that, [think]: "Consciousness is bad; this is consciousness; the non-existence of consciousness is good," for suffering arises only dependent on the condition of killing, binding, etc., because of consciousness. When there is no consciousness, they produce forbearance and inclination, and without decline of jhāna, having made an end of life, they are born in the unconscious realm. Whatever posture of his, standing, sitting or lying down, was practiced in the human world, in that same posture, having been born there, he remains for five hundred kalpas. Even to such beings, conditional nutriment is obtained. For the jhāna which they cultivated and in which they were born, that itself is their condition. Just as an arrow shot with the force of a bow travels as long as the force of the bow lasts, so too, [the beings] remain as long as the condition of jhāna lasts. When that is finished, they fall like an arrow whose force is spent. But what is the food of those hell-beings who are said to subsist neither on the fruit of effort nor on the fruit of merit? Their karma itself is their food. What, are there five kinds of food? It should not be said, "five, not five." Surely, it has been said that a condition is food. Therefore, by whatever karma they are reborn in hell, that itself is their food, because it is the condition for their existence. Referring to this, it was said: "And he does not die as long as that evil karma is not exhausted" (Majjhima Nikāya 3.250).

Here, no dispute should be made regarding the food of morsels. Even the saliva that arises in the mouth accomplishes their function of food. Even saliva, having become a condition, is painful to experience in hell, and pleasant to experience in heaven. Thus, in the realm of desire, there are four kinds of food, without any alternative. In the realms of form and formlessness, setting aside the non-percipient beings, there are three. Since *paccaya* is food, after stating the question, "All beings are sustained by food," with this food as *paccaya*, without stating "This is the cause, friend," nor again taking up "There is indeed, friend," he dismissed the second question: "All beings are sustained by formations."

Why then did he not state and take up [the questions] distinctly? Because it is difficult to learn and recite each one when stating and taking them up distinctly. Therefore, he dismissed [the two questions] by making them one. In this dismissal too, the *saṅkhāra* is stated to be the condition previously stated, since it produces the fruit of itself. Thus, *āhāra-paccaya* (food condition) has been spoken of previously; here, it is *saṅkhāra-paccaya* (formation condition). This is the difference between the former and the latter. "Previously, food without alternatives was taken; here, food with alternatives." Thus, if it is taken in this way, the distinction would be clear. But the Elder Mahāsīva said that they did not take it [in that way]. Even for one bound by the senses and for one not bound by the senses, it is fitting to obtain a condition. Without a condition, there is no *dharma*. There, for one not bound by the senses, earth-essence and water-essence are the condition for grass, trees, creepers, and so on. When the sky does not rain, grass and so on wither; and when it rains, they become green. Thus, for them, earth-essence and water-essence are the condition. For one bound by the senses, ignorance, craving, and karma are food. Thus, previously, it was said that *paccaya* itself is food; here, it is *saṅkhāra*. This alone is the distinction here.

"This, friend," means, friend, this one dharma was taught by our teacher after sitting at the great Bodhi-tree and realizing it himself through the knowledge of omniscience. There, in that one dharma, you should all be in harmony and not quarrel. "As this holy life..." means, as you are in harmony, may this holy life of the teaching be lasting. Indeed, by one monk, "There is, friend, one dharma rightly expounded..."

Which is the one principle? All beings are maintained by nutriment (āhāra). When it is said, "All beings are maintained by conditions (saṅkhāra)", how will another speak having heard that? Even of that other, thus, by the rule of continuous story, this religious life (brahmacariyaṃ), long enduring, will be for the welfare and benefit of the world with its gods (sadevakassa lokassa). Thus, in a singular way, the general of the Dhamma, the venerable Sāriputta, showed the taste of concord.

This Indeed, friend, just as this religious life (brahmacariya)

The section based on one item is finished (ekakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā).

Section based on two items

mula_pali:
304. ‘‘Atthi kho, āvuso, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena dve dhammā sammadakkhātā. Tattha sabbeheva saṅgāyitabbaṃ, na vivaditabbaṃ, yathayidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ addhaniyaṃ assa ciraṭṭhitikaṃ, tadassa bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ. Katame dve dve dhammo (syā. kaṃ.) evamuparipi?

‘‘Nāmañca rūpañca.

‘‘Avijjā ca bhavataṇhā ca.

‘‘Bhavadiṭṭhi ca vibhavadiṭṭhi ca.

‘‘Ahirikañca ahirīkañca (katthaci) anottappañca.

ahirīkañca (katthaci)

‘‘Hirī ca ottappañca.

‘‘Dovacassatā ca pāpamittatā ca.

‘‘Sovacassatā ca kalyāṇamittatā ca.

‘‘Āpattikusalatā ca āpattivuṭṭhānakusalatā ca.

‘‘Samāpattikusalatā ca samāpattivuṭṭhānakusalatā ca.

‘‘Dhātukusalatā ca manasikārakusalatā ca.

‘‘Āyatanakusalatā ca paṭiccasamuppādakusalatā ca.

‘‘Ṭhānakusalatā ca aṭṭhānakusalatā ca.

‘‘Ajjavañca lajjavañca.

‘‘Khanti ca soraccañca.

‘‘Sākhalyañca paṭisanthāro ca.

‘‘Avihiṃsā ca soceyyañca.

‘‘Muṭṭhassaccañca asampajaññañca.

‘‘Sati ca sampajaññañca .

‘‘Indriyesu aguttadvāratā ca bhojane amattaññutā ca.

‘‘Indriyesu guttadvāratā ca bhojane mattaññutā ca.

‘‘Paṭisaṅkhānabalañca paṭisandhānabalañca (syā.) bhāvanābalañca.

paṭisandhānabalañca (syā.)

‘‘Satibalañca samādhibalañca.

‘‘Samatho ca vipassanā ca.

‘‘Samathanimittañca paggahanimittañca.

‘‘Paggaho ca avikkhepo ca.

‘‘Sīlavipatti ca diṭṭhivipatti ca.

‘‘Sīlasampadā ca diṭṭhisampadā ca.

‘‘Sīlavisuddhi ca diṭṭhivisuddhi ca.

‘‘Diṭṭhivisuddhi kho pana yathā diṭṭhissa ca padhānaṃ.

‘‘Saṃvego ca saṃvejanīyesu ṭhānesu saṃviggassa ca yoniso padhānaṃ.
