‘‘Ime kho, āvuso, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena dve dhammā sammadakkhātā. Tattha sabbeheva saṅgāyitabbaṃ, na vivaditabbaṃ, yathayidaṃ brahmacariyaṃ addhaniyaṃ assa ciraṭṭhitikaṃ, tadassa bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ.

Tikaṃ
mula_english:
304. Friends, these are the two *dharmas* that are rightly expounded by the Blessed One—the one who knows, the one who sees, the Worthy One (*arhat*), rightly self-awakened (*sammāsambuddha*). That should all be recited together, without dispute, so that this holy life (*brahmacariya*) will endure & last a long time, and that will be for the benefit & happiness of many, out of sympathy for the world, for the welfare, benefit, & happiness of *devas* & human beings.

What are the two?

Name (*nāma*) and form (*rūpa*).

Ignorance (*avijjā*) and craving for becoming (*bhavataṇhā*).

The view of being (*bhavadiṭṭhi*) and the view of non-being (*vibhavadiṭṭhi*).

Shamelessness (*ahirikañca*) and recklessness (*anottappañca*).

Moral shame (*hirī*) and moral dread (*ottappañca*).

Being difficult to instruct (*dovacassatā*) & evil friendship (*pāpamittatā*).

Being easy to instruct (*sovacassatā*) & admirable friendship (*kalyāṇamittatā*).

Skill in offenses (*āpattikusalatā*) & skill in exiting from offenses (*āpattivuṭṭhānakusalatā*).

Skill in attainments (*samāpattikusalatā*) & skill in exiting from attainments (*samāpattivuṭṭhānakusalatā*).

Skill in properties (*dhātukusalatā*) & skill in attention (*manasikārakusalatā*).

Skill in sense media (*āyatanakusalatā*) & skill in dependent co-arising (*paṭiccasamuppādakusalatā*).

Skill in what is possible (*ṭhānakusalatā*) & skill in what is impossible (*aṭṭhānakusalatā*).

Uprightness (*ajjavañca*) & gentleness (*lajjavañca*).

Patience (*khanti*) & gentleness (*soraccañca*).

Sociability (*sākhalyañca*) and cordiality (*paṭisanthāro ca*).

Non-harming (*avihiṃsā*) and purity (*soceyyañca*).

Forgetfulness (*muṭṭhassaccañca*) and lack of clear comprehension (*asampajaññañca*).

Mindfulness (*sati*) and clear comprehension (*sampajaññañca*).

Unguarded sense doors (*indriyesu aguttadvāratā*) & not knowing moderation in eating (*bhojane amattaññutā*).

Guarded sense doors (*indriyesu guttadvāratā*) & knowing moderation in eating (*bhojane mattaññutā*).

Strength of reflection (*paṭisaṅkhānabalañca*) & strength of development (*bhāvanābalañca*).

Strength of mindfulness (*satibalañca*) & strength of *samādhi* (*samādhibalañca*).

Serenity (*samatho*) and insight (*vipassanā ca*).

The sign of serenity (*samathanimittañca*) and the sign of striving (*paggahanimittañca*).
• "Grasp and non-distraction, and

• "Failure of virtue and failure of view, and

• "Success of virtue and success of view, and

• "Purity of virtue and purity of view, and

• "Purity of view and the exertion of one with such a view.

• "Agitation, and appropriate exertion in places causing agitation for one who is agitated, and

• "Lack of satisfaction and non-opposition in wholesome qualities, and exertion, and

• "Clear knowing & release: (vijjā ca vimutti ca.)

• "Knowledge of cessation & knowledge of non-arising.

• “These, friends, are the two *dharmas* that are rightly expounded by the Blessed One—the one who knows, the one who sees, the Worthy One, rightly self-awakened.

That should all be recited together, without dispute, so that this holy life will endure & last a long time, and that will be for the benefit & happiness of many, out of sympathy for the world, for the welfare, benefit, & happiness of *devas* & human beings.

Tikaṃ
commentary_pali:
304. Iti ekakavasena sāmaggirasaṃ dassetvā idāni dukavasena dassetuṃ puna desanaṃ ārabhi. Tattha nāmarūpaduke nāmanti cattāro arūpino khandhā nibbānañca. Tattha cattāro khandhā nāmanaṭṭhena nāmaṃ. Nāmanaṭṭhenāti nāmakaraṇaṭṭhena. Yathā hi mahājanasammatattā mahāsammatassa ‘‘mahāsammato’’ti nāmaṃ ahosi, yathā mātāpitaro ‘‘ayaṃ tisso nāma hotu, phusso nāma hotū’’ti evaṃ puttassa kittimanāmaṃ karonti, yathā vā ‘‘dhammakathiko vinayadharo’’ti guṇato nāmaṃ āgacchati, na evaṃ vedanādīnaṃ. Vedanādayo hi mahāpathavīādayo viya attano nāmaṃ karontāva uppajjanti. Tesu uppannesu tesaṃ nāmaṃ uppannameva hoti. Na hi vedanaṃ uppannaṃ ‘‘tvaṃ vedanā nāma hohī’’ti, koci bhaṇati, na cassā yena kenaci kāraṇena nāmaggahaṇakiccaṃ atthi, yathā pathaviyā uppannāya ‘‘tvaṃ pathavī nāma hohī’’ti nāmaggahaṇakiccaṃ natthi, cakkavāḷasinerumhi candimasūriyanakkhattesu uppannesu ‘‘tvaṃ cakkavāḷaṃ nāma, tvaṃ nakkhattaṃ nāma hohī’’ti nāmaggahaṇakiccaṃ natthi, nāmaṃ uppannameva hoti, opapātikā paññatti nipatati, evaṃ vedanāya uppannāya ‘‘tvaṃ vedanā nāma hohī’’ti nāmaggahaṇakiccaṃ natthi, tāya uppannāya vedanāti nāmaṃ uppannameva hoti. Saññādīsupi eseva nayo atītepi hi vedanā vedanāyeva. Saññā. Saṅkhārā. Viññāṇaṃ viññāṇameva. Anāgatepi. Paccuppannepi. Nibbānaṃ pana sadāpi nibbānamevāti. Nāmanaṭṭhena nāmaṃ. Namanaṭṭhenāpi cettha cattāro khandhā nāmaṃ. Te hi ārammaṇābhimukhaṃ namanti. Nāmanaṭṭhena sabbampi nāmaṃ. Cattāro hi khandhā ārammaṇe aññamaññaṃ nāmenti , nibbānaṃ ārammaṇādhipatipaccayatāya attani anavajjadhamme nāmeti.

Rūpanti cattāro ca mahābhūtā catunnañca mahābhūtānaṃ upādāya rūpaṃ, taṃ sabbampi ruppanaṭṭhena rūpaṃ. Tassa vitthārakathā visuddhimagge vuttanayeneva veditabbā.

Rūpa rūpaṃ.

Avijjāti dukkhādīsu aññāṇaṃ. Ayampi vitthārato visuddhimagge kathitāyeva. Bhavataṇhāti bhavapatthanā. Yathāha ‘‘tattha katamā bhavataṇhā? Yo bhavesu bhavacchando’’tiādi (dha. sa. 1319).

Avijjā Bhavataṇhā

Bhavadiṭṭhīti bhavo vuccati sassataṃ, sassatavasena uppajjanakadiṭṭhi. Sā ‘‘tattha katamā bhavadiṭṭhi? ‘Bhavissati attā ca loko cā’ti yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigata’’ntiādinā (dha. sa. 1320) nayena abhidhamme vitthāritā. Vibhavadiṭṭhīti vibhavo vuccati ucchedaṃ, ucchedavasena uppajjanakadiṭṭhi. Sāpi ‘‘tattha katamā vibhavadiṭṭhi? ‘Na bhavissati attā ca loko cā’ti (dha. sa. 285). Yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigata’’ntiādinā (dha. sa. 1321) nayena tattheva vitthāritā.

Bhavadiṭṭhī Vibhavadiṭṭhī

Ahirikanti ‘‘yaṃ na hirīyati hirīyitabbenā’’ti (dha. sa. 1328) evaṃ vitthāritā nillajjatā. Anottappanti ‘‘yaṃ na ottappati ottappitabbenā’’ti (dha. sa. 1329) evaṃ vitthārito abhāyanakaākāro.

Ahirika Anottappa

Hirī ca ottappañcāti ‘‘yaṃ hirīyati hirīyitabbena, ottappati ottappitabbenā’’ti (dha. sa. 1330-31) evaṃ vitthāritāni hiriottappāni. Api cettha ajjhattasamuṭṭhānā hirī, bahiddhāsamuṭṭhānaṃ ottappaṃ. Attādhipateyyā hirī, lokādhipateyyaṃ ottappaṃ. Lajjāsabhāvasaṇṭhitā hirī, bhayasabhāvasaṇṭhitaṃ ottappaṃ. Vitthārakathā panettha sabbākārena visuddhimagge vuttā.

Hirī ca ottappañcā hirī, ottappaṃ.

Dovacassatāti dukkhaṃ vaco etasmiṃ vippaṭikūlagāhimhi vipaccanīkasāte anādare puggaleti dubbaco, tassa kammaṃ dovacassaṃ, tassa bhāvo dovacassatā. Vitthārato panesā ‘‘tattha katamā dovacassatā? Sahadhammike vuccamāne dovacassāya’’nti (dha. sa. 1332) abhidhamme āgatā. Sā atthato saṅkhārakkhandho hoti. ‘‘Catunnañca khandhānaṃ etenākārena pavattānaṃ etaṃ adhivacana’’nti vadanti. Pāpamittatāti pāpā assaddhādayo puggalā etassa mittāti pāpamitto, tassa bhāvo pāpamittatā. Vitthārato panesā – ‘‘tattha katamā pāpamittatā? Ye te puggalā assaddhā dussīlā appassutā maccharino duppaññā. Yā tesaṃ sevanā nisevanā saṃsevanā bhajanā saṃbhajanā bhatti saṃbhatti taṃsampavaṅkatā’’ti (dha. sa. 1333) evaṃ āgatā. Sāpi atthato dovacassatā viya daṭṭhabbā.

Dovacassatā dovacassatā. Pāpamittatā

Sovacassatā ca kalyāṇamittatā ca vuttappaṭipakkhanayena veditabbā. Ubhopi panetā idha lokiyalokuttaramissakā kathitā.

Sovacassatā ca kalyāṇamittatā

Āpattikusalatāti ‘‘pañcapi āpattikkhandhā āpattiyo, sattapi āpattikkhandhā āpattiyo. Yā tāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ āpattikusalatā paññā pajānanā’’ti (dha. sa. 1336) evaṃ vutto āpattikusalabhāvo.

Āpattikusalatā

Āpattivuṭṭhānakusalatāti ‘‘yā tāhi āpattīhi vuṭṭhānakusalatā paññā pajānanā’’ti (dha. sa. 1337) evaṃ vuttā saha kammavācāya āpattīhi vuṭṭhānaparicchedajānanā paññā.

Āpattivuṭṭhānakusalatā

Samāpattikusalatāti ‘‘atthi savitakkasavicārā samāpatti, atthi avitakkavicāramattā samāpatti, atthi avitakkaavicārā samāpatti. Yā tāsaṃ samāpattīnaṃ kusalatā paññā pajānanā’’ti (dha. sa. 1338) evaṃ vuttā saha parikammena appanāparicchedajānanā paññā. Samāpattivuṭṭhānakusalatāti ‘‘yā tāhi samāpattīhi vuṭṭhānakusalatā paññā pajānanā’’ti (dha. sa. 1339) evaṃ vuttā yathāparicchinnasamayavaseneva samāpattito vuṭṭhānasamatthā ‘‘ettakaṃ gate sūriye uṭṭhahissāmī’’ti vuṭṭhānakālaparicchedakā paññā.

Samāpattikusalatā Samāpattivuṭṭhānakusalatā

Dhātukusalatāti ‘‘aṭṭhārasa dhātuyo cakkhudhātu…pe… manoviññāṇadhātu. Yā tāsaṃ dhātūnaṃ kusalatā paññā pajānanā’’ti (dha. sa. 1340) evaṃ vuttā aṭṭhārasannaṃ dhātūnaṃ sabhāvaparicchedakā savanadhāraṇasammasanapaṭivedhapaññā. Manasikārakusalatāti ‘‘yā tāsaṃ dhātūnaṃ manasikārakusalatā paññā pajānanā’’ti (dha. sa. 1341) evaṃ vuttā tāsaṃyeva dhātūnaṃ sammasanapaṭivedhapaccavekkhaṇapaññā.

Dhātukusalatā Manasikārakusalatā

Āyatanakusalatāti ‘‘dvādasāyatanāni cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… dhammāyatanaṃ. Yā tesaṃ āyatanānaṃ āyatanakusalatā paññā pajānanā’’ti (dha. sa. 1342) evaṃ vuttā dvādasannaṃ āyatanānaṃ uggahamanasikārapajānanā paññā. Apica dhātukusalatāpi uggahamanasikārasavanasammasanapaṭivedhapaccavekkhaṇesu vattati manasikārakusalatāpi āyatanakusalatāpi. Ayaṃ panettha viseso, savanauggahapaccavekkhaṇā lokiyā, paṭivedho lokuttaro, sammasanamanasikārā lokiyalokuttaramissakā. Paṭiccasamuppādakusalatāti ‘‘avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā…pe… samudayo hotīti yā tattha paññā pajānanā’’ti (dha. sa. 1343) evaṃ vuttā dvādasannaṃ paccayākārānaṃ uggahādivasena pavattā paññā.

Āyatanakusalatā Paṭiccasamuppādakusalatā

Ṭhānakusalatāti ‘‘ye ye dhammā yesaṃ yesaṃ dhammānaṃ hetupaccayā uppādāya taṃ taṃ ṭhānanti yā tattha paññā pajānanā’’ti (dha. sa. 1344) evaṃ vuttā ‘‘cakkhuṃ vatthuṃ katvā rūpaṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā uppannassa cakkhuviññāṇassa cakkhurūpaṃ (dha. sa. aṭṭha. 1344) ṭhānañceva kāraṇañcā’’ti evaṃ ṭhānaparicchindanasamatthā paññā. Aṭṭhānakusalatāti ‘‘ye ye dhammā yesaṃ yesaṃ dhammānaṃ na hetū na paccayā uppādāya taṃ taṃ aṭṭhānanti yā tattha paññā pajānanā’’ti (dha. sa. 1345) evaṃ vuttā ‘‘cakkhuṃ vatthuṃ katvā rūpaṃ ārammaṇaṃ katvā sotaviññāṇādīni nuppajjanti, tasmā tesaṃ cakkhurūpaṃ na ṭhānaṃ na kāraṇa’’nti evaṃ aṭṭhānaparicchindanasamatthā paññā apica etasmiṃ duke ‘‘kittāvatā pana, bhante, ṭhānāṭhānakusalo bhikkhūti alaṃ vacanāyāti. Idhānanda, bhikkhu aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso, yaṃ diṭṭhisampanno puggalo kañci saṅkhāraṃ niccato upagaccheyya, netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjatīti pajānāti. Ṭhānañca kho etaṃ vijjati, yaṃ puthujjano kañci saṅkhāraṃ niccato upagaccheyyā’’ti (ma. ni. 3.127) imināpi suttena attho veditabbo.

Ṭhānakusalatā Aṭṭhānakusalatā

Ajjavanti gomuttavaṅkatā candavaṅkatā naṅgalakoṭivaṅkatāti tayo anajjavā. Ekacco hi bhikkhu paṭhamavaye ekavīsatiyā anesanāsu chasu ca agocaresu carati, majjhimapacchimavayesu lajjī kukkuccako sikkhākāmo hoti, ayaṃ gomuttavaṅkatā nāma. Eko paṭhamavayepi pacchimavayepi catupārisuddhisīlaṃ pūreti, lajjī kukkuccako sikkhākāmo hoti, majjhimavaye purimasadiso, ayaṃ candavaṅkatā nāma. Eko paṭhamavayepi majjhimavayepi catupārisuddhisīlaṃ pūreti, lajjī kukkuccako sikkhākāmo hoti, pacchimavaye purimasadiso ayaṃ naṅgalakoṭivaṅkatā nāma. Eko sabbametaṃ vaṅkataṃ pahāya tīsupi vayesu pesalo lajjī kukkuccako sikkhākāmo hoti. Tassa yo so ujubhāvo, idaṃ ajjavaṃ nāma. Abhidhammepi vuttaṃ – ‘‘tattha katamo ajjavo. Yā ajjavatā ajimhatā avaṅkatā akuṭilatā, ayaṃ vuccati ajjavo’’ti (dha. sa. 1346). Lajjavanti ‘‘tattha katamo lajjavo? Yo hirīyati hirīyitabbena hirīyati pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ samāpattiyā. Ayaṃ vuccati lajjavo’’ti evaṃ vutto lajjībhāvo.

Ajjava Lajjava

Khantīti ‘‘tattha katamā khanti? Yā khanti khamanatā adhivāsanatā acaṇḍikkaṃ anassuropo attamanatā cittassā’’ti (dha. sa. 1348) evaṃ vuttā adhivāsanakhanti. Soraccanti ‘‘tattha katamaṃ soraccaṃ? Yo kāyiko avītikkamo, vācasiko avītikkamo, kāyikavācasiko avītikkamo. Idaṃ vuccati soraccaṃ. Sabbopi sīlasaṃvaro soracca’’nti (dha. sa. 1349) evaṃ vutto suratabhāvo.

Khantī Soracca

Sākhalyanti ‘‘tattha katamaṃ sākhalyaṃ? Yā sā vācā aṇḍakā kakkasā parakaṭukā parābhisajjanī kodhasāmantā asamādhisaṃvattanikā, tathārūpiṃ vācaṃ pahāya yā sā vācā neḷā kaṇṇasukhā pemanīyā hadayaṅgamā porī bahujanakantā bahujanamanāpā, tathārūpiṃ vācaṃ bhāsitā hoti. Yā tattha saṇhavācatā sakhilavācatā apharusavācatā. Idaṃ vuccati sākhalya’’nti (dha. sa. 1350) evaṃ vutto sammodakamudukabhāvo. Paṭisanthāroti ayaṃ lokasannivāso āmisena dhammena cāti dvīhi chiddo, tassa taṃ chiddaṃ yathā na paññāyati, evaṃ pīṭhassa viya paccattharaṇena āmisena dhammena ca paṭisantharaṇaṃ. Abhidhammepi vuttaṃ ‘‘tattha katamo paṭisanthāro ? Āmisapaṭisanthāro ca dhammapaṭisanthāro ca. Idhekacco paṭisanthārako hoti āmisapaṭisanthārena vā dhammapaṭisanthārena vā. Ayaṃ vuccati paṭisanthāro’’ti (dha. sa. 1351). Ettha ca āmisena saṅgaho āmisapaṭisanthāro nāma. Taṃ karontena mātāpitūnaṃ bhikkhugatikassa veyyāvaccakarassa rañño corānañca aggaṃ aggahetvāpi dātuṃ vaṭṭati. Āmasitvā dinne hi rājāno ca corā ca anatthampi karonti jīvitakkhayampi pāpenti, anāmasitvā dinne attamanā honti. Coranāgavatthuādīni cettha vatthūni kathetabbāni. Tāni samantapāsādikāya vinayaṭṭhakathāyaṃ (pāci. aṭṭha. 185-7) vitthāritāni. Sakkaccaṃ uddesadānaṃ pāḷivaṇṇanā dhammakathākathananti evaṃ dhammena saṅgaho dhammapaṭisanthāro nāma.

Sākhalya Paṭisanthāro

Avihiṃsāti karuṇāpi karuṇāpubbabhāgopi. Vuttampi cetaṃ – ‘‘tattha katamā avihiṃsā? Yā sattesu karuṇā karuṇāyanā karuṇāyitattaṃ karuṇācetovimutti, ayaṃ vuccati avihiṃsā’’ti. Soceyyanti mettāya ca mettāpubbabhāgassa ca vasena sucibhāvo. Vuttampi cetaṃ – ‘‘tattha katamaṃ soceyyaṃ? Yā sattesu metti mettāyanā mettāyitattaṃ mettācetovimutti, idaṃ vuccati soceyya’’nti.

Avihiṃsā Soceyya

Muṭṭhassaccanti sativippavāso, yathāha ‘‘tattha katamaṃ muṭṭhassaccaṃ? Yā asati ananussati appaṭissati assaraṇatā adhāraṇatā pilāpanatā sammussanatā, idaṃ vuccati muṭṭhassaccaṃ’’ (dha. sa. 1356). Asampajaññanti, ‘‘tattha katamaṃ asampajaññaṃ? Yaṃ aññāṇaṃ adassanaṃ avijjālaṅgī moho akusalamūla’’nti evaṃ vuttā avijjāyeva. Sati satiyeva. Sampajaññaṃ ñāṇaṃ.

Muṭṭhassacca Asampajañña Sati Sampajaññaṃ

Indriyesu aguttadvāratāti ‘‘tattha katamā indriyesu aguttadvāratā? Idhekacco cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā nimittaggāhī hotī’’tiādinā (dha. sa. 1352) nayena vitthārito indriyasaṃvarabhedo. Bhojane amattaññutāti ‘‘tattha katamā bhojane amattaññutā? Idhekacco appaṭisaṅkhā ayoniso āhāraṃ āhāreti davāya madāya maṇḍanāya vibhūsanāya. Yā tattha asantuṭṭhitā amattaññutā appaṭisaṅkhā bhojane’’ti evaṃ āgato bhojane amattaññubhāvo. Anantaraduko vuttappaṭipakkhanayena veditabbo.

Indriyesu aguttadvāratā Bhojane amattaññutā

Paṭisaṅkhānabalanti ‘‘tattha katamaṃ paṭisaṅkhānabalaṃ? Yā paññā pajānanā’’ti evaṃ vitthāritaṃ appaṭisaṅkhāya akampanañāṇaṃ. Bhāvanābalanti bhāventassa uppannaṃ balaṃ. Atthato vīriyasambojjhaṅgasīsena satta bojjhaṅgā honti. Vuttampi cetaṃ – ‘‘tattha katamaṃ bhāvanābalaṃ? Yā kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ āsevanā bhāvanā bahulīkammaṃ, idaṃ vuccati bhāvanābalaṃ. Sattabojjhaṅgā bhāvanābala’’nti.

Paṭisaṅkhānabala Bhāvanābala

Satibalanti assatiyā akampanavasena satiyeva. Samādhibalanti uddhacce akampanavasena samādhiyeva. Samatho samādhi. Vipassanā paññā. Samathova taṃ ākāraṃ gahetvā puna pavattetabbassa samathassa nimittavasena samathanimittaṃ paggāhanimittepi eseva nayo. Paggāho vīriyaṃ. Avikkhepo ekaggatā. Imehi pana sati ca sampajaññañca paṭisaṅkhānabalañca bhāvanābalañca satibalañca samādhibalañca samatho ca vippassanā ca samathanimittañca paggāhanimittañca paggāho ca avikkhepo cāti chahi dukehi parato sīladiṭṭhisampadādukena ca lokiyalokuttaramissakā dhammā kathitā.

Satibala Samādhibala Samatho Vipassanā samathanimittaṃ paggāhanimittepi Paggāho Avikkhepo

Sīlavipattīti ‘‘tattha katamā sīlavipatti? Kāyiko vītikkamo…pe… sabbampi dussīlyaṃ sīlavipattī’’ti evaṃ vutto sīlavināsako asaṃvaro. Diṭṭhivipattīti ‘‘tattha katamā diṭṭhivipatti? Natthi dinnaṃ natthi yiṭṭha’’nti evaṃ āgatā sammādiṭṭhivināsikā micchādiṭṭhi.

Sīlavipattī Diṭṭhivipattī

Sīlasampadāti ‘‘tattha katamā sīlasampadā? Kāyiko avītikkamo’’ti evaṃ pubbe vuttasoraccameva sīlassa sampādanato paripūraṇato ‘‘sīlasampadā’’ti vuttaṃ. Ettha ca ‘‘sabbopi sīlasaṃvaro sīlasampadā’’ti idaṃ mānasikapariyādānatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Diṭṭhisampadāti ‘‘tattha katamā diṭṭhisampadā? Atthi dinnaṃ atthi yiṭṭhaṃ…pe… sacchikatvā pavedentīti yā evarūpā paññā pajānanā’’ti evaṃ āgataṃ diṭṭhipāripūribhūtaṃ ñāṇaṃ.

Sīlasampadā Diṭṭhisampadā

Sīlavisuddhīti visuddhiṃ pāpetuṃ samatthaṃ sīlaṃ. Abhidhamme panāyaṃ ‘‘tattha katamā sīlavisuddhi? Kāyiko avītikkamo vācasiko avītikkamo kāyikavācasiko avītikkamo, ayaṃ vuccati sīlavisuddhī’’ti evaṃ vibhattā. Diṭṭhivisuddhīti visuddhiṃ pāpetuṃ samatthaṃ dassanaṃ. Abhidhamme panāyaṃ ‘‘tattha katamā diṭṭhivisuddhi? Kammassakatañāṇaṃ saccānulomikañāṇaṃ maggasamaṅgissañāṇaṃ phalasamaṅgissañāṇa’’nti evaṃ vuttā. Ettha ca tividhaṃ duccaritaṃ attanā katampi parena katampi sakaṃ nāma na hoti atthabhañjanato. Sucaritaṃ sakaṃ nāma atthajananatoti evaṃ jānanaṃ kammassakatañāṇaṃ nāma. Tasmiṃ ṭhatvā bahuṃ vaṭṭagāmikammaṃ āyūhitvā sukhato sukheneva arahattaṃ pattā gaṇanapathaṃ vītivattā. Vipassanāñāṇaṃ pana vacīsaccañca anulometi, paramatthasaccañca na vilometīti saccānulomikaṃ ñāṇanti vuttaṃ.

Sīlavisuddhī Diṭṭhivisuddhī Vipassanāñāṇaṃ

‘‘Diṭṭhivisuddhi kho pana yathādiṭṭhissa ca padhāna’’nti ettha diṭṭhivisuddhīti ñāṇadassanaṃ kathitaṃ. Yathādiṭṭhissa ca padhānanti taṃsampayuttameva vīriyaṃ. Api ca purimapadena catumaggañāṇaṃ. Pacchimapadena taṃsampayuttaṃ vīriyaṃ. Abhidhamme pana ‘‘diṭṭhivisuddhi kho panāti yā paññā pajānanā amoho dhammavicayo sammādiṭṭhi. Yathādiṭṭhissa ca padhānanti yo cetasiko vīriyārambho sammāvāyāmo’’ti evaṃ ayaṃ duko vibhatto.

diṭṭhivisuddhī Yathādiṭṭhissa ca padhāna Abhidhamme

‘‘Saṃvego ca saṃvejanīyesu ṭhānesū’’ti ettha ‘‘saṃvegoti jātibhayaṃ jarābhayaṃ byādhibhayaṃ maraṇabhaya’’nti evaṃ jātiādīni bhayato dassanañāṇaṃ. Saṃvejanīyaṃ ṭhānanti jātijarābyādhimaraṇaṃ. Etāni hi cattāri jāti dukkhā, jarā dukkhā, byādhi dukkho, maraṇaṃ dukkhanti evaṃ saṃveguppattikāraṇattā saṃvejanīyaṃ ṭhānanti vuttāni. Saṃviggassa ca yoniso padhānanti evaṃ saṃvegajātassa upāyapadhānaṃ. ‘‘Idha bhikkhu anuppannānaṃ pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ anuppādāya chandaṃ janetī’’ti evaṃ āgatavīriyassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ.

‘‘saṃvego saṃvejanīyaṃ ṭhāna Saṃviggassa ca yoniso padhāna

Asantuṭṭhitā ca kusalesu dhammesūti yā kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ bhāvanāya asantuṭṭhassa bhiyyokamyatā, tāya hi samaṅgībhūto puggalo sīlaṃ pūretvā jhānaṃ uppādeti. Jhānaṃ labhitvā vipassanaṃ ārabhati. Āraddhavipassako arahattaṃ agahetvā antarā vosānaṃ nāpajjati. Appaṭivānitā ca padhānasminti ‘‘kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ bhāvanāya sakkaccakiriyatā sātaccakiriyatā aṭṭhitakiriyatā anolīnavuttitā anikkhittachandatā anikkhittadhuratā āsevanā bhāvanā bahulīkamma’’nti evaṃ vuttā rattindivaṃ cha koṭṭhāse katvā jāgariyānuyogavasena āraddhe padhānasmiṃ arahattaṃ apatvā anivattanatā.

Asantuṭṭhitā ca kusalesu dhammesū Appaṭivānitā ca padhānasmi

Vijjāti tisso vijjā. Vimuttīti dve vimuttiyo, cittassa ca adhimutti, nibbānañca. Ettha ca aṭṭha samāpattiyo nīvaraṇādīhi suṭṭhu muttattā adhimutti nāma. Nibbānaṃ sabbasaṅkhatato muttattā vimuttīti veditabbaṃ.

Vijjā Vimuttī

Khaye ñāṇanti kilesakkhayakare ariyamagge ñāṇaṃ. Anuppāde ñāṇanti paṭisandhivasena anuppādabhūte taṃtaṃmaggavajjhakilesānaṃ vā anuppādapariyosāne uppanne ariyaphale ñāṇaṃ. Tenevāha ‘‘khaye ñāṇanti maggasamaṅgissa ñāṇaṃ. Anuppāde ñāṇanti phalasamaṅgissa ñāṇa’’nti. Ime kho, āvusotiādi ekake vuttanayeneva yojetabbaṃ. Iti pañcatiṃsāya dukānaṃ vasena thero sāmaggirasaṃ dassesīti.

Khaye ñāṇa Anuppāde ñāṇa Ime kho, āvuso

Dukavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

Tikavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
304. Having shown the samaggirasaṃ by way of oneness, now, in order to show [it] by way of duality, [the text] again began a teaching. There, in the *nāmarūpaduke*, **name** means the four immaterial aggregates and *nirvāṇa*. There, the four aggregates are **name** because of the meaning of bending toward. *Nāmanaṭṭhena*: because of the meaning of naming. Just as, because of being agreed upon by many people, the name of Mahāsammata was [given]. Just as mothers and fathers do the made-up-name-making of a son, [saying,] "May this one be named Tissa, may [this one] be named Phussa," so too, when one says, "A *dharmakathika*, a *vinayadhara*," a name comes from a quality, but it is not like that for feeling and so on. Feelings and so on, like the great earth element and so on, arise only doing their own naming. When they have arisen, their name is just what has arisen. For, when a feeling has arisen, no one says, "May you, feeling, be named," nor does it have a name-taking function by any cause, just as when the earth element has arisen, there is no name-taking function [saying,] "May you, earth element, be named." When the *cakravāḷas*, Sineru, the moon, the sun, and the stars have arisen, there is no name-taking function [saying,] "May you be named *cakravāḷa*, may you be named star." Name is just what has arisen; the *aupapātikā* designation falls [on it]. Thus, when feeling has arisen, there is no name-taking function [saying,] "May you, feeling, be named." Because of that arisal, [it is] feeling. Name is just what has arisen. This same *naya* [applies] also to perception and so on. In the past, too, feeling was just feeling. Perception. Volitional processes. Consciousness was just consciousness. Also in the future. Also in the present. But *nirvāṇa* is always just *nirvāṇa*. *Nāmanaṭṭhena nāmaṃ*: name through the meaning of bending. *Namanatthenāpi*: also here, the four aggregates are name because of the meaning of bending. For they bend toward the object. *Nāmanaṭṭhena sabbampi nāmaṃ*: all name is through the meaning of bending. For the four aggregates bend each other in the object, *nirvāṇa* bends in itself [those] undefiled *dharmas* through the condition of object-domination. *Rūpa* means the four great elements and the *rūpa* that takes up the four great elements; all of that is **rūpa** by way of the meaning of "ruppana." The talk of its expansion should be understood in just the way it was said in the *Visuddhimagga*. **Rūpa** **rūpa**. ***Avijjā*** means non-knowing regarding suffering and so on. This, too, is just what was spoken in the *Visuddhimagga* in detail. ***Bhavataṇhā*** means desire for becoming. As it was said: "Therein, what is desire for becoming? That which is desire for becoming in becomings" and so on (Dha. Sa. 1319). ***Avijjā*** ***bhavataṇhā*** ***Bhavadiṭṭhī*** means becoming is called eternal, [it is] the view that arises by way of the eternal. That, "Therein, what is the view of becoming? 'Self and world will be,' this view, a view-gone-[wrong]" and so on, was expanded in the *Abhidhamma* by way of the *naya* (Dha. Sa. 1320). ***Vibhavadiṭṭhī*** means non-becoming is called annihilation; [it is] the view that arises by way of annihilation. That, too, "Therein, what is the view of non-becoming? 'Self and world will not be'" (Dha. Sa. 285). That such a view, a fixed view, etc., has been extensively explained there itself in the way of (Dha. Sa. 1321). *bhava-diṭṭhi* *vibhava-diṭṭhi* *ahirika* means, as it is expanded "Not being ashamed of what should be ashamed of" (Dha. Sa. 1328), thus shamelessness is explained. *anottappa* means, as it is expanded "Not being afraid of what should be afraid of" (Dha. Sa. 1329), thus the state of being fearless is explained. *ahirika* *anottappa* *hirī ca ottappañca* means, as it is expanded "Being ashamed of what should be ashamed of, being afraid of what should be afraid of" (Dha. Sa. 1330-31), thus shame and fear are explained. Moreover, *hirī* arises internally, *ottappa* arises externally. *Hirī* has self as its authority; *ottappa* has the world as its authority. *Hirī* is established in the nature of modesty, *ottappa* is established in the nature of fear. The detailed explanation of this is given in all respects in the Path of Purification (Visuddhimagga). *hirī ca ottappañca* *hirī,* *ottappaṃ.* *dovacassatā* means, a person who is difficult to instruct is *dubbaco*, because he speaks painfully, is averse to what is contrary, is indifferent to what is on the side of opposition; the action of that person is *dovacassaṃ*, the state of that is *dovacassatā*. In detail, this has come in the Abhidhamma as, "What is *dovacassatā* there? In *dovacassa*, when one is being told what is in accordance with the Dharma" (Dha. Sa. 1332). In meaning, that is the *saṅkhārakkhandha*. They say, "This designation applies to the occurrence of the four *khandhas* in this way." *pāpamittatā* means, a wicked person, faithless, etc., is a friend of this person, thus a bad friend (*pāpamitto*), the state of that is *pāpamittatā*. In detail, this has come as – "What is *pāpamittatā* there? Those people who are faithless, immoral, unlearned, miserly, unwise. Association with them, constant association, close association, intimacy, close intimacy, devotion, close devotion, inclination towards that." (Dha. Sa. 1333) That too should be regarded as being like *dovacassatā* in meaning. *dovacassatā* *dovacassatā.* *pāpamittatā* *sovacassatā ca kalyāṇamittatā* ca should be understood by way of the opposite of what has been said. However, both of these are said here as mixed with the mundane and supramundane. *sovacassatā ca kalyāṇamittatā* *āpattikusalatā* means, "The five aggregates of offenses are offenses, the seven aggregates of offenses are offenses. "That wisdom [ *paññā* ] and understanding [ *pajānanā* ] which is skill in offenses [ *āpattikusalatā* ] regarding those offenses [ *āpattīnaṃ* ]" (dha. sa. 1336) Thus is described the state of being skilled in offenses [ *āpattikusalabhāvo* ]. Skill in offenses [ *āpattikusalatā* ]. Skill in arising from offenses [ *āpattivuṭṭhānakusalatā* ]: "That wisdom [ *paññā* ] and understanding [ *pajānanā* ] which is skill in arising [ *vuṭṭhānakusalatā* ] from those offenses [ *āpattīhi* ]" (dha. sa. 1337) Thus described, along with the *kammavācā*, is the wisdom [ *paññā* ] that knows the demarcation of arising from offenses [ *āpattīhi vuṭṭhānaparicchedajānanā* ]. Skill in arising from offenses [ *āpattivuṭṭhānakusalatā* ]. Skill in *samāpatti* [ *samāpattikusalatā* ]: (pb ed="v" n="3. 0147") "There is *samāpatti* with initial application and sustained application [ *savitakkasavicārā samāpatti* ], there is *samāpatti* with only sustained application and without initial application [ *avitakkavicāramattā samāpatti* ], there is *samāpatti* without initial application and without sustained application [ *avitakkaavicārā samāpatti* ]. That wisdom [ *paññā* ] and understanding [ *pajānanā* ] which is skill [ *kusala* ] in those *samāpattis* [ *samāpattīnaṃ* ]" (dha. sa. 1338) Thus described, along with preliminary activity [ *parikammena* ], is the wisdom [ *paññā* ] that knows the demarcation of attainment [ *appanāparicchedajānanā* ]. Skill in arising from *samāpatti* [ *samāpattivuṭṭhānakusalatā* ]: "That wisdom [ *paññā* ] and understanding [ *pajānanā* ] which is skill in arising [ *vuṭṭhānakusalatā* ] from those *samāpattis* [ *samāpattīhi* ]" (dha. sa. 1339) Thus described, just as with the power of a time defined by accurate measure [ *yathāparicchinnasamayavaseneva* ], the wisdom [ *paññā* ] is skilled in arising from *samāpatti* [ *samāpattito vuṭṭhānasamatthā* ] and demarcates the time of arising [ *vuṭṭhānakālaparicchedakā* ], [thinking] "When the sun has reached so far [ *ettakaṃ gate sūriye* ], I will arise [ *uṭṭhahissāmī’ti* ]." Skill in *samāpatti* [ *samāpattikusalatā* ] (pb ed="v" n="3. 0147") Skill in arising from *samāpatti* [ *samāpattivuṭṭhānakusalatā* ]. Skill in the elements [ *dhātukusalatā* ]: "The eighteen elements [ *aṭṭhārasa dhātuyo* ]: the eye element [ *cakkhudhātu* ]…pe… the mind-consciousness element [ *manoviññāṇadhātu* ]. That wisdom [ *paññā* ] and understanding [ *pajānanā* ] which is skill [ *kusala* ] in those elements [ *dhātūnaṃ* ]" (dha. sa. 1340) Thus described is the wisdom [ *paññā* ] that demarcates the intrinsic nature [ *sabhāvaparicchedakā* ] of the eighteen elements [ *aṭṭhārasannaṃ dhātūnaṃ* ], that discerns, retains, completely cognizes, and penetrates. (pb ed="m" n="3. 0162") Skill in attention [ *manasikārakusalatā* ]: "That wisdom [ *paññā* ] and understanding [ *pajānanā* ] which is skill in attention [ *manasikārakusalatā* ] regarding those elements [ *dhātūnaṃ* ]" (dha. sa. 1341) Thus described is the wisdom [ *paññā* ] that completely cognizes, penetrates, and reflects upon just those elements [ *tāsaṃyeva dhātūnaṃ sammasanapaṭivedhapaccavekkhaṇapaññā* ]. Skill in the elements [ *dhātukusalatā* ] (pb ed="m" n="3. 0162") Skill in attention [ *manasikārakusalatā* ]. Skill in the *āyatanas* [ *āyatanakusalatā* ]: "The twelve *āyatanas* [ *dvādasāyatanāni* ]: the eye *āyatana* [ *cakkhāyatanaṃ* ]…pe… the *dharma āyatana* [ *dhammāyatanaṃ* ]. That wisdom [ *paññā* ] and understanding [ *pajānanā* ] which is skill in the *āyatanas* [ *āyatanakusalatā* ] regarding those *āyatanas* [ *āyatanānaṃ* ]" (dha. sa. 1342) Thus described is the wisdom [ *paññā* ] that knows the attention of grasping to mind [ *uggahamanasikārapajānanā* ] regarding the twelve *āyatanas* [ *dvādasannaṃ āyatanānaṃ* ]. Moreover, skill in the elements [ *dhātukusalatāpi* ], skill in attention [ *manasikārakusalatāpi* ], and skill in the *āyatanas* [ *āyatanakusalatāpi* ] occur in grasping to mind, discerning, completely cognizing, penetrating, and reflecting upon [ *uggahamanasikārasavanasammasanapaṭivedhapaccavekkhaṇesu* ]. (pb ed="p" n="3. 0980") Herein is a distinction [ *viseso* ]: discerning, grasping to mind, and reflecting upon [ *savanauggahapaccavekkhaṇā* ] are mundane [ *lokiyā* ], penetration [ *paṭivedho* ] is supramundane [ *lokuttaro* ], and completely cognizing and attention [ *sammasanamanasikārā* ] are mixed mundane and supramundane [ *lokiyalokuttaramissakā* ]. Skill in dependent origination [ *paṭiccasamuppādakusalatā* ]: "With ignorance as condition, volitional formations [arise]…pe… thus there is arising [ *samudayo hotīti* ]. That wisdom [ *paññā* ] and understanding [ *pajānanā* ] which is therein [ *tattha* ]" (dha. sa. 1343) Thus described is the wisdom [ *paññā* ] that proceeds by way of grasping, etc. [ *uggahādivasena pavattā* ], regarding the twelve aspects of conditions [ *dvādasannaṃ paccayākārānaṃ* ]. Skill in the *āyatanas* [ *āyatanakusalatā* ] (pb ed="p" n="3. 0980") Skill in dependent origination [ *paṭiccasamuppādakusalatā* ]. Skill in what is possible [ *ṭhānakusalatā* ]: "Because of what conditions [ *hetupaccayā* ] do these *dharmas* [ *dhammā* ] arise [ *uppādāya* ] for those *dharmas* [ *dhammānaṃ* ], that is the possible [ *ṭhānanti* ]. That wisdom [ *paññā* ] and understanding [ *pajānanā* ] which is therein [ *tattha* ]" (dha. sa. 1344) Thus described is "Having made the eye the thing [object], having made form the objective condition [ *ārammaṇaṃ katvā* ], the form of the eye [ *cakkhurūpaṃ* ] for the eye-consciousness that has arisen [ *uppannassa cakkhuviññāṇassa* ]" (dha. sa. aṭṭha. (1344) *ṭhānañceva kāraṇañcā’*ti: Thus, the wisdom that is capable of distinguishing causes is *ṭhāna* (basis, reason) and *kāraṇa* (cause). *aṭṭhānakusalatā*ti: "Those things that are not the cause or condition for the arising of those things are called *aṭṭhāna*; the wisdom and understanding there," (Dha. Sa. 1345) thus it is said, "Visual consciousness and so forth do not arise by making the eye the base and form the object, therefore, the eye and form are not the basis or cause for them." Thus, the wisdom that is capable of distinguishing non-causes. Moreover, in this pair, "To what extent, venerable sir, is a monk skilled in causes and non-causes?" "Here, Ānanda, a monk understands: 'It is impossible, it cannot happen that a person possessing right view could treat any formation as permanent - there is no such possibility.' And he understands: 'It is possible that an ordinary person might treat some formation as permanent'," (Ma. Ni. 3. 127) the meaning should be understood by this sutra as well. *ṭhānakusalatā*, *aṭṭhānakusalatā* *ajjava*nti: There are three kinds of non-straightness: cow-dung crookedness, moon crookedness, and plough-tip crookedness. A certain monk in his early years engages in the twenty-one wrong livelihoods and the six improper resorts; in his middle and later years he is conscientious, scrupulous, and desires training; this is called cow-dung crookedness. One who in his early and later years fulfills the fourfold purity of morality, is conscientious, scrupulous, and desires training, but is like the former in his middle years; this is called moon crookedness. One who in his early and middle years fulfills the fourfold purity of morality, is conscientious, scrupulous, and desires training, but is like the former in his later years; this is called plough-tip crookedness. One who abandons all this crookedness and is amiable, conscientious, scrupulous, and desires training in all three periods of life. That which is his straightness, that is called *ajjava* (honesty, integrity). It is also said in the Abhidhamma: "What is *ajjava*? It is honesty, un-deceitfulness, un-crookedness, un-kinkedness; this is called *ajjava*," (Dha. Sa. 1346). *lajjava*nti: "What is *lajjava*? One is ashamed of what should be ashamed of; one is ashamed of the attainment of evil, unwholesome states; this is called *lajjava*." Thus, the state of being ashamed. *ajjava*, *lajjava* *khantī*ti: "What is *khanti* (patience)? It is endurance, forbearance, acceptance, non-harshness, non-belligerence, and mental satisfaction," (Dha. Sa. 1348) thus it is called acceptance-patience. *soracca*nti: "What is *soracca* (gentleness, mildness)? It is non-transgression in body, non-transgression in speech, and non-transgression in body and speech. This is called *soracca*. All restraint in morality is *soracca*," (Dha. Sa. 1349) thus, the state of being gentle. *khantī*, *soracca* *sākhalya*nti: "What is *sākhalya* (friendliness, amiability)? Abandoning speech that is rough, harsh, hurtful, offensive, anger-related, and conducive to non-harmony; speech that is smooth, pleasing to the ear, lovely, heart-warming, urbane, pleasing to many, agreeable to many is spoken. That which is gentle speech, friendly speech, non-harsh speech, this is called *sākhalya*," (Dha. Sa. 1350) thus it is called the state of amicable-softness. "Refurbishment" means this dwelling in the world is fissured by both sensual pleasures and the Dharma. Just as the fissure of a seat is not apparent, so too, refurbishment with material things and the Dharma. It is also said in the *Abhidhamma*: "What is that refurbishment? It is the refurbishment of sensual pleasures and the refurbishment of the Dharma." Here, a certain person is a restorer by means of the refurbishment of sensual pleasures or by the refurbishment of the Dharma. This is called refurbishment. And here, gathering with sensual pleasures is called the refurbishment of sensual pleasures. In doing that, it is proper to give to one's parents, to one who does the duties of a monk, to one who performs services, to the king, and to thieves, even without taking the best. For kings and thieves, when given after being touched, cause harm and bring about loss of life. When given without being touched, they are pleased. Here, stories such as the story of the thief Nāga should be told. These have been expanded in the *Samantapāsādikā*, the commentary on the *Vinaya*. Giving offerings with reverence, explaining the *Pāli*, and telling a *Dharma* story: thus, gathering with the *Dharma* is called the refurbishment of the *Dharma*. "Non-violence" means compassion and what precedes compassion. It was said, "What is non-violence? It is compassion for beings, having compassion, the state of having compassion, and the liberation of the mind through compassion. This is called non-violence." "Purity" means purity by way of loving-kindness and what precedes loving-kindness. It was said, "What is purity? It is loving-kindness for beings, having loving-kindness, the state of having loving-kindness, and the liberation of the mind through loving-kindness. This is called purity." "Loss of mindfulness" means the loss of memory, as he said, "What is loss of mindfulness? It is unmindfulness, non-recollection, lack of attention, lack of memory, instability, confusion, and bewilderment. This is called loss of mindfulness." "Non-comprehension" means, "What is non-comprehension? It is ignorance, not seeing, delusion clinging to ignorance, and the unwholesome root." Thus, what is said is simply ignorance. Mindfulness is simply mindfulness. Comprehension is knowledge. "Unguardedness of the senses" means, "What is unguardedness of the senses? Here, a certain person, seeing a form with the eye, is fixated on the characteristics." The difference in sense restraint has been expanded in this way. "Not knowing moderation in food" means, "What is not knowing moderation in food? Here, a certain person partakes of food unwisely, unreflectively, for pleasure, for intoxication, for adornment, for beautification. That which is dissatisfaction and not knowing moderation in food, and unwisely with food is the state of not knowing moderation in food which has come about in this way. The subsequent pair should be understood by way of the opposite of what has been said. "Power of reflection" means, "What is the power of reflection? It is wisdom and understanding." Thus, unshakeable knowledge through lack of reflection has been expanded. "Power of cultivation" means the power that arises in one who cultivates. From effort, with effort as its chief, the seven factors of Awakening arise. It has also been said: "What is the power of development (bhāvanābala) there? It is the repetition, the development, the repeated practice of skillful qualities (kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ). This is called the power of development (bhāvanābala). The seven factors of Awakening [are] the power of development."

Power of reflection (paṭisaṅkhānabala) Power of development (bhāvanābala)

Power of mindfulness (satibala) means mindfulness itself, by way of non-wavering in regard to non-mindfulness. Power of concentration (samādhibala) means concentration itself, by way of non-wavering in regard to distraction. Serenity (samatho) [is] concentration (samādhi). Insight (vipassanā) [is] wisdom (paññā). Having taken that form of serenity (samatho), because of the aspect of the sign (nimittavasena) of serenity (samathassa) that should be repeatedly developed, this is the method even for the sign of serenity (samathanimitta) and the sign of exerting (paggāhanimittepi). Exertion (paggāho) [is] effort (vīriyaṃ). Non-distraction (avikkhepo) [is] one-pointedness (ekaggatā). Furthermore, through these six pairs—mindfulness (sati) and clear comprehension (sampajaññañca), power of reflection (paṭisaṅkhānabalañca) and power of development (bhāvanābalañca), power of mindfulness (satibalañca) and power of concentration (samādhibalañca), serenity (samatho) and insight (vippassanā), the sign of serenity (samathanimittañca) and the sign of exertion (paggāhanimittañca), exertion (paggāho) and non-distraction (avikkhepo)—and through the pair of ethical conduct (sīla) and accomplishment of view (diṭṭhisampadā), mixed mundane and supramundane qualities (dhammā) are spoken of.

Power of mindfulness (satibala) Power of concentration (samādhibala) Serenity (samatho) Insight (vipassanā) Sign of serenity (samathanimitta) and sign of exertion (paggāhanimittepi) Exertion (paggāho) Non-distraction (avikkhepo)

Moral failure (sīlavipattī) means: "What is moral failure (sīlavipatti) there? It is bodily transgression…pe… all immorality (dussīlyaṃ) [is] moral failure (sīlavipattī)," thus the destruction of morality (sīlavināsako), lack of restraint (asaṃvaro), is spoken of. Failure of view (diṭṭhivipattī) means: "What is failure of view (diṭṭhivipatti) there? 'There is no giving (natthi dinnaṃ), there is no sacrifice (natthi yiṭṭha)'," thus wrong view (micchādiṭṭhi), which destroys right view (sammādiṭṭhi), has come.

Moral failure (sīlavipattī) Failure of view (diṭṭhivipattī)

Moral accomplishment (sīlasampadā) means: "What is moral accomplishment (sīlasampadā) there? It is non-transgression in body (kāyiko avītikkamo)," thus, just the same innocence (soraccameva) previously spoken of, from accomplishing (sampādanato) and fulfilling (paripūraṇato) morality (sīlassa), is spoken of as "moral accomplishment (sīlasampadā)." And here, "all moral restraint (sīlasaṃvaro) [is] moral accomplishment (sīlasampadā)," this is spoken for the sake of the mental condition (mānasikapariyādānatthaṃ). Accomplishment of view (diṭṭhisampadā) means: "What is accomplishment of view (diṭṭhisampadā) there? 'There is giving (atthi dinnaṃ), there is sacrifice (atthi yiṭṭhaṃ)…pe… having realized, they declare (sacchikatvā pavedentīti),' that understanding (paññā) and knowing (pajānanā) of such a kind," thus knowledge (ñāṇaṃ) that has come to be the complete fulfillment of view (diṭṭhipāripūribhūtaṃ) is spoken of.

Moral accomplishment (sīlasampadā) Accomplishment of view (diṭṭhisampadā)

Moral purification (sīlavisuddhī) means morality (sīlaṃ) that is capable of bringing about purification (visuddhiṃ pāpetuṃ samatthaṃ). In the *Abhidhamma*, however, this is distinguished thus: "What is moral purification (sīlavisuddhi) there? It is non-transgression in body (kāyiko avītikkamo), non-transgression in speech (vācasiko avītikkamo), non-transgression in body and speech (kāyikavācasiko avītikkamo); this is called moral purification (sīlavisuddhī)." Purification of view (diṭṭhivisuddhī) means seeing (dassanaṃ) that is capable of bringing about purification (visuddhiṃ pāpetuṃ samatthaṃ). In the *Abhidhamma*, however, this is spoken of thus: "What is purification of view (diṭṭhivisuddhi) there? It is knowledge of the results of action (kammassakatañāṇaṃ), knowledge conforming to the truths (saccānulomikañāṇaṃ), knowledge belonging to the factors of the path (maggasamaṅgissañāṇaṃ), knowledge belonging to the factors of the fruit (phalasamaṅgissañāṇaṃ)." And here, threefold misconduct (duccaritaṃ) done (katampi) by oneself (attanā) or done (katampi) by another (parena) or one's own (sakaṃ) [is] not called (nāma na hoti) meaning (attha) because it destroys (bhañjanato). Right conduct (sucaritaṃ), one's own name, because it generates meaning (atthajananatoti), thus, knowing (jānanaṃ) [is] knowledge of the results of action (kammassakatañāṇaṃ) called (nāma). Having stood in that, having prepared much work at Vaṭṭagāma (vaṭṭagāmikammaṃ āyūhitvā), having attained ease from ease (sukhato sukheneva), having attained arhatship (arahattaṃ pattā), they passed beyond the path of reckoning (gaṇanapathaṃ vītivattā). Insight knowledge (vipassanāñāṇaṃ), however, conforms (anulometi) to truth of speech (vacīsaccañca), and does not go against (na vilometīti) ultimate truth (paramatthasaccañca), therefore (iti) it is said [to be] knowledge conforming to the truth (saccānulomikaṃ ñāṇanti vuttaṃ).

Moral purification (sīlavisuddhī) Purification of view (diṭṭhivisuddhī) Insight knowledge (vipassanāñāṇaṃ)

‘‘Purification of view (diṭṭhivisuddhi), however, [is] the effort with what has been seen (yathādiṭṭhissa ca padhāna)," thus, here, purification of view (diṭṭhivisuddhī) means knowledge and seeing (ñāṇadassanaṃ), it is said (kathitaṃ). The effort with what has been seen (yathādiṭṭhissa ca padhāna) means just effort (vīriyaṃ) connected with that (taṃsampayuttameva). Furthermore (api ca), by the former term (purimapadena) [is meant] the knowledge of the four paths (catumaggañāṇaṃ). By the latter term (pacchimapadena) [is meant] effort connected with that (taṃsampayuttaṃ vīriyaṃ). In the *Abhidhamma*, however, "purification of view (diṭṭhivisuddhi kho pana) [is] that wisdom (paññā), knowing (pajānanā), non-delusion (amoho), investigation of phenomena (dhammavicayo), right view (sammādiṭṭhi). The effort with what has been seen (yathādiṭṭhissa ca padhānanti) [is] that mental effort (cetasiko vīriyārambho) [which is] right effort (sammāvāyāmo)," thus this pair (ayaṃ duko) [is] distinguished (vibhatto). *Diṭṭhivisuddhi* *yathādiṭṭhissa ca padhāna abhidhamme*: "Saṃvego ca saṃvejanīyesu ṭhānesū" – here, *saṃvego* means the knowledge of seeing fear in birth, aging, sickness and death. *Saṃvejanīyaṃ ṭhāna* means birth, aging, sickness and death. These four, namely, birth is suffering, aging is suffering, sickness is suffering, and death is suffering, are called *saṃvejanīyaṃ ṭhāna* because they are the cause of the arising of anxiety. *Saṃviggassa ca yoniso padhāna* means the method of effort for one who has arisen with anxiety. "Here, a bhikkhu generates desire for the non-arising of evil, unwholesome states that have not yet arisen" – this is a designation for energy that has come. "*Saṃvego saṃvejanīyaṃ ṭhāna saṃviggassa ca yoniso padhāna* *asantuṭṭhitā ca kusalesu dhammesū*" – the eagerness of one who is not content in the cultivation of wholesome states, a person endowed with that quality, fulfilling virtue, generates jhāna. Having attained jhāna, he undertakes vipassanā (insight meditation). Having begun vipassanā, he does not come to an end in between without attaining arahantship. *Appaṭivānitā ca padhānasmiṃ* means "diligence in doing, continuous doing, unwavering doing, unyielding behavior, unabandoned desire, unabandoned burden, cultivation, development, frequent practice" in the cultivation of wholesome states. It means unremitting effort in the practice that has been started, dividing the day and night into six portions, in devotion to wakefulness, not turning back without attaining arahantship. "*Asantuṭṭhitā ca kusalesu dhammesū appaṭivānitā ca padhānasmiṃ* *vijjā*" – the three true knowledges ( *tisso vijjā*). "*Vimuttī*" – the two liberations (*dve vimuttiyo*): the mind's release and *nirvāṇa*. Here, the eight attainments (*aṭṭha samāpattiyo*) are called *adhimutti* because they are well freed from the hindrances and so on. *Nirvāṇa* should be understood as *vimutti* because it is freed from all conditioned things (*sabbasankhatato muttattā vimuttīti veditabbaṃ*). "*Vijjā vimuttī* *khaye ñāṇa*" means knowledge in the Noble Path (*ariyamagge ñāṇaṃ*) that destroys defilements (*kilesakkhayakare*). "*Anuppāde ñāṇa*" means knowledge in the Noble Fruit (*ariyaphale ñāṇaṃ*) that has arisen at the end of the non-arising of those defilements (*taṃtaṃmaggavajjhakilesānaṃ*) to be destroyed by that particular path, or in the state of non-arising in terms of rebirth. Therefore, it was said, " *khaye ñāṇa* means knowledge of one associated with the path (*maggasamaṅgissa ñāṇaṃ*). *Anuppāde ñāṇa* means knowledge of one associated with the fruit (*phalasamaṅgissa ñāṇaṃ*)." "*Ime kho, āvuso*…" should be connected in the same way as stated in the case of the single. Thus, the elder showed the essence of harmony by way of the thirty-five dyads. "*Khaye ñāṇa anuppāde ñāṇa* *ime kho, āvuso*" The explanation of the dyads is finished. Explanation of the triads

305. ‘‘Atthi kho, āvuso, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena tayo dhammā sammadakkhātā. Tattha sabbeheva saṅgāyitabbaṃ…pe… atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ. Katame tayo?

‘‘Tīṇi akusalamūlāni – lobho akusalamūlaṃ, doso akusalamūlaṃ, moho akusalamūlaṃ.

‘‘Tīṇi kusalamūlāni – alobho kusalamūlaṃ, adoso kusalamūlaṃ, amoho kusalamūlaṃ.

‘‘Tīṇi duccaritāni – kāyaduccaritaṃ, vacīduccaritaṃ, manoduccaritaṃ.

‘‘Tīṇi sucaritāni – kāyasucaritaṃ, vacīsucaritaṃ , manosucaritaṃ.

‘‘Tayo akusalavitakkā – kāmavitakko, byāpādavitakko, vihiṃsāvitakko.

‘‘Tayo kusalavitakkā – nekkhammavitakko, abyāpādavitakko, avihiṃsāvitakko.

‘‘Tayo akusalasaṅkappā – kāmasaṅkappo, byāpādasaṅkappo, vihiṃsāsaṅkappo.

‘‘Tayo kusalasaṅkappā – nekkhammasaṅkappo, abyāpādasaṅkappo, avihiṃsāsaṅkappo.

‘‘Tisso akusalasaññā – kāmasaññā, byāpādasaññā, vihiṃsāsaññā.

‘‘Tisso kusalasaññā – nekkhammasaññā, abyāpādasaññā, avihiṃsāsaññā.

‘‘Tisso akusaladhātuyo – kāmadhātu, byāpādadhātu, vihiṃsādhātu.

‘‘Tisso kusaladhātuyo – nekkhammadhātu, abyāpādadhātu, avihiṃsādhātu.

‘‘Aparāpi tisso dhātuyo – kāmadhātu, rūpadhātu, arūpadhātu.

‘‘Aparāpi tisso dhātuyo – rūpadhātu, arūpadhātu, nirodhadhātu.

‘‘Aparāpi tisso dhātuyo – hīnadhātu, majjhimadhātu, paṇītadhātu.

‘‘Tisso taṇhā – kāmataṇhā, bhavataṇhā, vibhavataṇhā.

‘‘Aparāpi tisso taṇhā – kāmataṇhā, rūpataṇhā, arūpataṇhā.

‘‘Aparāpi tisso taṇhā – rūpataṇhā, arūpataṇhā, nirodhataṇhā.

‘‘Tīṇi saṃyojanāni – sakkāyadiṭṭhi, vicikicchā, sīlabbataparāmāso.

‘‘Tayo āsavā – kāmāsavo, bhavāsavo, avijjāsavo.

‘‘Tayo bhavā – kāmabhavo, rūpabhavo, arūpabhavo.

‘‘Tisso esanā – kāmesanā, bhavesanā, brahmacariyesanā.

‘‘Tisso vidhā – seyyohamasmīti vidhā, sadisohamasmīti vidhā, hīnohamasmīti vidhā.

‘‘Tayo addhā – atīto addhā, anāgato addhā, paccuppanno addhā.

‘‘Tayo antā – sakkāyo anto, sakkāyasamudayo anto, sakkāyanirodho anto.

‘‘Tisso vedanā – sukhā vedanā, dukkhā vedanā, adukkhamasukhā vedanā.

‘‘Tisso dukkhatā – dukkhadukkhatā, saṅkhāradukkhatā, vipariṇāmadukkhatā.

‘‘Tayo rāsī – micchattaniyato rāsi, sammattaniyato rāsi, aniyato rāsi.

‘‘Tayo tamā tisso kaṅkhā (bahūsu) aṭṭhakathā oloketabbā – atītaṃ vā addhānaṃ ārabbha kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati, anāgataṃ vā addhānaṃ ārabbha kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati, etarahi vā paccuppannaṃ addhānaṃ ārabbha kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati.

tisso kaṅkhā (bahūsu) aṭṭhakathā oloketabbā

‘‘Tīṇi tathāgatassa arakkheyyāni – parisuddhakāyasamācāro āvuso tathāgato, natthi tathāgatassa kāyaduccaritaṃ, yaṃ tathāgato rakkheyya – ‘mā me idaṃ paro aññāsī’ti. Parisuddhavacīsamācāro āvuso, tathāgato, natthi tathāgatassa vacīduccaritaṃ, yaṃ tathāgato rakkheyya – ‘mā me idaṃ paro aññāsī’ti. Parisuddhamanosamācāro, āvuso, tathāgato, natthi tathāgatassa manoduccaritaṃ yaṃ tathāgato rakkheyya – ‘mā me idaṃ paro aññāsī’ti.

‘‘Tayo kiñcanā – rāgo kiñcanaṃ, doso kiñcanaṃ, moho kiñcanaṃ.

‘‘Tayo aggī – rāgaggi, dosaggi, mohaggi.

‘‘Aparepi tayo aggī – āhuneyyaggi, gahapataggi, dakkhiṇeyyaggi.

‘‘Tividhena rūpasaṅgaho – sanidassanasappaṭighaṃ rūpaṃ sanidassanasappaṭigharūpaṃ (syā. kaṃ.) evamitaradvayepi, anidassanasappaṭighaṃ rūpaṃ, anidassanaappaṭighaṃ rūpaṃ.

sanidassanasappaṭigharūpaṃ (syā. kaṃ.) evamitaradvayepi

‘‘Tayo saṅkhārā – puññābhisaṅkhāro, apuññābhisaṅkhāro , āneñjābhisaṅkhāro.

‘‘Tayo puggalā – sekkho puggalo, asekkho puggalo, nevasekkhonāsekkho puggalo.

‘‘Tayo therā – jātithero, dhammathero, sammutithero sammatithero (syā. kaṃ.).

sammatithero (syā. kaṃ.)

‘‘Tīṇi puññakiriyavatthūni – dānamayaṃ puññakiriyavatthu, sīlamayaṃ puññakiriyavatthu, bhāvanāmayaṃ puññakiriyavatthu.

‘‘Tīṇi codanāvatthūni – diṭṭhena, sutena, parisaṅkāya.

‘‘Tisso kāmūpapattiyo kāmuppattiyo (sī.), kāmupapattiyo (syā. pī. ka.) – santāvuso sattā paccupaṭṭhitakāmā, te paccupaṭṭhitesu kāmesu vasaṃ vattenti, seyyathāpi manussā ekacce ca devā ekacce ca vinipātikā. Ayaṃ paṭhamā kāmūpapatti. Santāvuso, sattā nimmitakāmā, te nimminitvā nimminitvā kāmesu vasaṃ vattenti, seyyathāpi devā nimmānaratī. Ayaṃ dutiyā kāmūpapatti. Santāvuso sattā paranimmitakāmā, te paranimmitesu kāmesu vasaṃ vattenti, seyyathāpi devā paranimmitavasavattī. Ayaṃ tatiyā kāmūpapatti.

kāmuppattiyo (sī.), kāmupapattiyo (syā. pī. ka.)

‘‘Tisso sukhūpapattiyo sukhupapattiyo (syā. pī. ka.) – santāvuso sattā sattā sukhaṃ (syā. kaṃ.) uppādetvā uppādetvā sukhaṃ viharanti, seyyathāpi devā brahmakāyikā. Ayaṃ paṭhamā sukhūpapatti. Santāvuso, sattā sukhena abhisannā parisannā paripūrā paripphuṭā. Te kadāci karahaci udānaṃ udānenti – ‘aho sukhaṃ, aho sukha’nti , seyyathāpi devā ābhassarā. Ayaṃ dutiyā sukhūpapatti. Santāvuso, sattā sukhena abhisannā parisannā paripūrā paripphuṭā. Te santaṃyeva tusitā santusitā (syā. kaṃ.) sukhaṃ cittasukhaṃ (syā. ka.) paṭisaṃvedenti, seyyathāpi devā subhakiṇhā. Ayaṃ tatiyā sukhūpapatti .

sukhupapattiyo (syā. pī. ka.) sattā sukhaṃ (syā. kaṃ.) santusitā (syā. kaṃ.) cittasukhaṃ (syā. ka.)

‘‘Tisso paññā – sekkhā paññā, asekkhā paññā, nevasekkhānāsekkhā paññā.

‘‘Aparāpi tisso paññā – cintāmayā paññā, sutamayā paññā, bhāvanāmayā paññā.

‘‘Tīṇāvudhāni – sutāvudhaṃ, pavivekāvudhaṃ, paññāvudhaṃ.

‘‘Tīṇindriyāni – anaññātaññassāmītindriyaṃ, aññindriyaṃ, aññātāvindriyaṃ.

‘‘Tīṇi cakkhūni – maṃsacakkhu, dibbacakkhu, paññācakkhu.

‘‘Tisso sikkhā – adhisīlasikkhā, adhicittasikkhā, adhipaññāsikkhā.

‘‘Tisso bhāvanā – kāyabhāvanā, cittabhāvanā, paññābhāvanā.

‘‘Tīṇi anuttariyāni – dassanānuttariyaṃ, paṭipadānuttariyaṃ, vimuttānuttariyaṃ.

‘‘Tayo samādhī – savitakkasavicāro samādhi, avitakkavicāramatto samādhi, avitakkaavicāro samādhi.

‘‘Aparepi tayo samādhī – suññato samādhi, animitto samādhi, appaṇihito samādhi.

‘‘Tīṇi soceyyāni – kāyasoceyyaṃ, vacīsoceyyaṃ, manosoceyyaṃ.

‘‘Tīṇi moneyyāni – kāyamoneyyaṃ, vacīmoneyyaṃ, manomoneyyaṃ.

‘‘Tīṇi kosallāni – āyakosallaṃ, apāyakosallaṃ, upāyakosallaṃ.

‘‘Tayo madā – ārogyamado, yobbanamado, jīvitamado.

‘‘Tīṇi ādhipateyyāni – attādhipateyyaṃ, lokādhipateyyaṃ, dhammādhipateyyaṃ.

‘‘Tīṇi kathāvatthūni – atītaṃ vā addhānaṃ ārabbha kathaṃ katheyya – ‘evaṃ ahosi atītamaddhāna’nti; anāgataṃ vā addhānaṃ ārabbha kathaṃ katheyya – ‘evaṃ bhavissati anāgatamaddhāna’nti; etarahi vā paccuppannaṃ addhānaṃ ārabbha kathaṃ katheyya – ‘evaṃ hoti etarahi paccuppannaṃ addhāna’nti.

‘‘Tisso vijjā – pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇaṃ vijjā, sattānaṃ cutūpapāteñāṇaṃ vijjā, āsavānaṃ khayeñāṇaṃ vijjā.

‘‘Tayo vihārā – dibbo vihāro, brahmā vihāro, ariyo vihāro.

‘‘Tīṇi pāṭihāriyāni – iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ, ādesanāpāṭihāriyaṃ, anusāsanīpāṭihāriyaṃ.

‘‘Ime kho, āvuso, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena tayo dhammā sammadakkhātā. Tattha sabbeheva saṅgāyitabbaṃ…pe… atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ.

305. “There are, friends, three *dhammas* that are rightly expounded by the Blessed One—the one who knows, the one who sees, the Worthy One, rightly self-awakened. There, all should chant together…for the benefit, for the welfare, for the happiness of gods and humans. Which three? “Three unwholesome roots: greed (*lobha*) is an unwholesome root, hatred (*dosa*) is an unwholesome root, delusion (*moha*) is an unwholesome root. “Three wholesome roots: non-greed (*alobha*) is a wholesome root, non-hatred (*adosa*) is a wholesome root, non-delusion (*amoha*) is a wholesome root. “Three kinds of misconduct: bodily misconduct (*kāyaduccaritaṃ*), verbal misconduct (*vacīduccaritaṃ*), mental misconduct (*manoduccaritaṃ*). “Three kinds of good conduct: bodily good conduct (*kāyasucaritaṃ*), verbal good conduct (*vacīsucaritaṃ*), mental good conduct (*manosucaritaṃ*). “Three unwholesome thoughts: sensual thought (*kāmavitakko*), thought of ill-will (*byāpādavitakko*), thought of harming (*vihiṃsāvitakko*). “Three wholesome thoughts: thought of renunciation (*nekkhammavitakko*), thought of non-ill-will (*abyāpādavitakko*), thought of non-harming (*avihiṃsāvitakko*). “Three unwholesome intentions: sensual intention (*kāmasaṅkappo*), intention of ill-will (*byāpādasaṅkappo*), intention of harming (*vihiṃsāsaṅkappo*). “Three wholesome intentions: intention of renunciation (*nekkhammasaṅkappo*), intention of non-ill-will (*abyāpādasaṅkappo*), intention of non-harming (*avihiṃsāsaṅkappo*). “Three unwholesome perceptions: perception of sensuality (*kāmasaññā*), perception of ill-will (*byāpādasaññā*), perception of harmfulness (*vihiṃsāsaññā*). “Three wholesome perceptions: perception of renunciation (*nekkhammasaññā*), perception of non-ill-will (*abyāpādasaññā*), perception of non-harming (*avihiṃsāsaññā*). “Three unwholesome elements: the element of sensuality (*kāmadhātu*), the element of ill-will (*byāpādadhātu*), the element of harming (*vihiṃsādhātu*). “Three wholesome elements: the element of renunciation (*nekkhammadhātu*), the element of non-ill-will (*abyāpādadhātu*), the element of non-harming (*avihiṃsādhātu*). “Three other elements: the element of sensuality (*kāmadhātu*), the element of form (*rūpadhātu*), the element of the formless (*arūpadhātu*). “Three other elements: the element of form (*rūpadhātu*), the element of the formless (*arūpadhātu*), the element of cessation (*nirodhadhātu*). “Three other elements: the inferior element (*hīnadhātu*), the middling element (*majjhimadhātu*), the excellent element (*paṇītadhātu*). “Three cravings: craving for sensuality (*kāmataṇhā*), craving for becoming (*bhavataṇhā*), craving for non-becoming (*vibhavataṇhā*). “Three other cravings: craving for sensuality (*kāmataṇhā*), craving for form (*rūpataṇhā*), craving for the formless (*arūpataṇhā*). “Three other cravings: craving for form (*rūpataṇhā*), craving for the formless (*arūpataṇhā*), craving for cessation (*nirodhataṇhā*). “Three fetters: self-identity view (*sakkāyadiṭṭhi*), uncertainty (*vicikicchā*), grasping at habits and practices (*sīlabbataparāmāso*). “Three outflows: the outflow of sensuality (*kāmāsavo*), the outflow of becoming (*bhavāsavo*), the outflow of ignorance (*avijjāsavo*). “Three becomings: becoming in the sensuality realm (*kāmabhavo*), becoming in the form realm (*rūpabhavo*), becoming in the formless realm (*arūpabhavo*). “Three searches: the search for sensuality (*kāmesanā*), the search for becoming (*bhavesanā*), the search for a life of ব্রহ্মচर्या (*brahmacariyesanā*). “Three types: the ‘I-am-better’ type (*seyyohamasmīti vidhā*), the ‘I-am-the-same’ type (*sadisohamasmīti vidhā*), the ‘I-am-lower’ type (*hīnohamasmīti vidhā*). “Three times: the past time (*atīto addhā*), the future time (*anāgato addhā*), the present time (*paccuppanno addhā*). ‘‘There are three ends: the end of personality belief (sakkāyo anto), the origin of personality belief (sakkāyasamudayo anto), and the cessation of personality belief (sakkāyanirodho anto). ‘‘There are three feelings: pleasant feeling (sukhā vedanā), painful feeling (duḥkhā vedanā), and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling (adukkhamasukhā vedanā). ‘‘There are three kinds of suffering: the suffering of suffering (duḥkhaduḥkhatā), the suffering of conditioned existence (saṃskāraduḥkhatā), and the suffering of change (vipariṇāmaduḥkhatā). ‘‘There are three destinies: the destiny of definite unenlightenment (micchattaniyato rāsi), the destiny of definite enlightenment (sammattaniyato rāsi), and the indeterminate destiny (aniyatā-niyāma) (aniyata rāsi). ‘‘There are three doubts: One doubts, is uncertain, is undecided, & is unconfident about the past (atītaṃ vā addhānaṃ ārabbha kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati), about the future (anāgataṃ vā addhānaṃ ārabbha kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati), or about the present right now (etarahi vā paccuppannaṃ addhānaṃ ārabbha kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati). ‘‘Three things the Tathāgata doesn’t have to protect against: The Tathāgata, friends, is one of pure bodily conduct (parisuddhakāyasamācāro āvuso tathāgato). He has no bodily misconduct that he would have to protect, ‘Don’t let anyone else know this of me.’ The Tathāgata is one of pure verbal conduct (parisuddhavacīsamācāro āvuso, tathāgato). He has no verbal misconduct that he would have to protect, ‘Don’t let anyone else know this of me.’ The Tathāgata is one of pure mental conduct (parisuddhamanosamācāro, āvuso, tathāgato). He has no mental misconduct that he would have to protect, ‘Don’t let anyone else know this of me.’ • “Three impediments: the impediment of passion (rāgo kiñcanaṃ), the impediment of aversion (doso kiñcanaṃ), the impediment of delusion (moho kiñcanaṃ). ‘‘There are three fires: the fire of greed (rāgaggi), the fire of hatred (dosaggi), and the fire of delusion (mohaggi). ‘‘There are three fires: the fire worthy of offerings (āhuneyyaggi), the fire of the householder (gahapataggi), the fire worthy of gifts (dakkhiṇeyyaggi). • “The threefold classification of form: form with a surface & offering resistance (sanidassanasappaṭighaṃ rūpaṃ), form with no surface & offering resistance (anidassanasappaṭighaṃ rūpaṃ), form with no surface & offering no resistance (anidassanaappaṭighaṃ rūpaṃ). If such ignorance exists, three types of formations arise: those leading to meritorious states (puññābhisaṅkhāro), those leading to unmeritorious states (apuññābhisaṅkhāro), and those leading to neutral states (āneñjābhisaṅkhāro). ‘‘Three persons: the person in training (sekkho puggalo), the person beyond training (asekkho puggalo), and the person neither in training nor beyond training (nevasekkhonāsekkho puggalo). ‘‘Three elders: elders by birth (jātithero), elders by Dharma (dhammathero), and elders by consensus (sammutithero). ‘‘Three bases for making merit: the base for making merit consisting of generosity (dānamayaṃ puññakiriyavatthu), the base for making merit consisting of morality (sīlamayaṃ puññakiriyavatthu), and the base for making merit consisting of meditation (bhāvanāmayaṃ puññakiriyavatthu). ‘‘Three grounds for accusation: what is seen (diṭṭhena), what is heard (sutena), and suspicion (parisaṅkāya). ‘‘Three kinds of existence in the realm of desire (kāmūpapattiyo). ka. ) – There are, friends, beings who desire what is readily available; they wield power over the desires that are readily available, for example, humans, some gods, and some beings in lower destinations. This is the first sensual-pleasure rebirth ( *kāmūpapatti*). There are, friends, beings who desire what they have created; having created and created again, they wield power over those desires, for example, the gods of delight in creation (*nimmāṇaratī*). This is the second sensual-pleasure rebirth. There are, friends, beings who desire what is created by others; they wield power over the desires created by others, for example, the gods who control what is created by others (*paranimmitavasavattī*). This is the third sensual-pleasure rebirth.

Sensual-pleasure rebirths ( *kāmuppattiyo*) (sī.), sensual-pleasure rebirths (syā. pī. ka. )

‘‘These three are blissful rebirths ( *sukhūpapattiyo*) blissful rebirths (syā. pī. ka. ) – There are, friends, beings beings, happiness (syā. kaṃ. ) who, having given rise to happiness again and again, dwell in happiness, for example, the gods of Brahmā's retinue (*brahmakāyikā*). This is the first blissful rebirth (*sukhūpapatti*). There are, friends, beings who are suffused, pervaded, filled, and overflowing with happiness ( *sukhena abhisannā parisannā paripūrā paripphuṭā*). From time to time, they utter the inspired utterance, 'Oh, bliss! Oh, bliss!' , just as the radiant gods (*ābhassarā*). This is the second blissful rebirth (*sukhūpapatti*). There are, friends, beings who are suffused, pervaded, filled, and overflowing with happiness ( *sukhena abhisannā parisannā paripūrā paripphuṭā*). They, being content, experience happiness mental happiness (syā. ka. ), just as the Beautifully Refulgent gods ( *subhakiṇhā*). This is the third blissful rebirth ( *sukhūpapatti*) .

Blissful rebirths (syā. pī. ka. ) Beings, happiness (syā. kaṃ. ) Content (syā. kaṃ. [Note:] *cittasukhaṃ* (syā. ka.) “Three types of discernment (*prajñā*): the discernment of a person in training (*śaikṣa prajñā*), the discernment of a person beyond training (*aśaikṣa prajñā*), and the discernment of a person neither in training nor beyond training (*naivaśaikṣa-nāśaikṣa prajñā*). “Three more types of discernment (*prajñā*): discernment acquired through contemplating (*cintāmayā prajñā*), discernment acquired through learning (*śrutamayā prajñā*), [and] discernment acquired through development (*bhāvanāmayā prajñā*). “Three weapons: the weapon of learning (*śrutāyudham*), the weapon of seclusion (*pravivekāyudham*), and the weapon of discernment (*prajñāyudham*). “Three faculties (*indriyāṇi*): the faculty of ‘I will know the unknown’ (*anajñātañjñāsyāmīndriyam*), the faculty of knowledge (*ājñendriyam*), and the faculty of ‘one who has known’ (*ājñātāvīndriyam*). “Three eyes (*cakṣūṇi*): the eye of flesh (*māṃsacakṣu*), the divine eye (*divyacakṣu*), and the eye of discernment (*prajñācakṣu*). “Three trainings (*śikṣā*): the higher training in morality (*adhiśīlaśikṣā*), the higher training in mind (*adhicittaśikṣā*), [and] the higher training in discernment (*adhiprajñāśikṣā*). “Three developments (*bhāvanā*): development of body (*kāyabhāvanā*), development of mind (*cittabhāvanā*), [and] development of discernment (*prajñābhāvanā*). “Three unsurpassed things (*anuttariyāṇi*): unsurpassed vision (*darśanānuttariyaṃ*), unsurpassed practice (*pratipadānuttariyaṃ*), [and] unsurpassed release (*vimuktānuttariyaṃ*). “Three concentrations (*samādhi*): concentration with initial and sustained application of thought (*savitarkasavicāro samādhi*), concentration without initial application of thought, but with sustained application of thought alone (*avitarkavicāramātro samādhi*), and concentration with neither initial nor sustained application of thought (*avitarkaavicāro samādhi*). “Three more concentrations (*samādhi*): emptiness concentration (*śūnyato samādhi*), signless concentration (*animitto samādhi*), [and] undirected concentration (*apraṇihito samādhi*). “Three kinds of purity (*śauceyāṇi*): purity of body (*kāyasoceyyaṃ*), purity of speech (*vacīsoceyyaṃ*), [and] purity of mind (*manosoceyyaṃ*). “Three forms of sagacity (*mauneyyāni*): bodily sagacity (*kāyamoneyyaṃ*), verbal sagacity (*vacīmoneyyaṃ*), [and] mental sagacity (*manomoneyyaṃ*). “Three forms of skillfulness (*kauśalyāni*): skillfulness in progress (*āyakosallaṃ*), skillfulness in decline (*apāyakosallaṃ*), [and] skillfulness in tactics (*upāyakosallaṃ*). “Three intoxications (*madā*): intoxication with health (*ārogyamado*), intoxication with youth (*yobbamado*), [and] intoxication with life (*jīvitamado*). “Three supremacies (*ādhipateyyāni*): supremacy of oneself (*attādhipateyyaṃ*), supremacy of the world (*lokādhipateyyaṃ*), [and] supremacy of the Dharma (*dhammādhipateyyaṃ*). “Three topics of conversation (*kathāvatthūni*): One might converse about the past, ‘That’s how it was in the past’ (*evaṃ ahosi atītamaddhāna’nti*); One might converse about the future, ‘That’s how it will be in the future’ (*evaṃ bhavissati anāgatamaddhāna’nti*); One might converse about the present, ‘That’s how it is in the present’ (*evaṃ hoti etarahi paccuppannaṃ addhāna’nti*). “Three forms of clear knowing (*vidyā*): the clear knowing of the knowledge of previous lifetimes (*pūrvenivāsānusmṛti-jñānaṃ vidyā*), the clear knowing of the knowledge of the passing away and arising of beings (*sattānāṃ cyutyupapāda-jñānaṃ vidyā*), [and] the clear knowing of the knowledge of the ending of the effluents (*āsavānāṃ kṣaye jñānaṃ vidyā*). “Three abodes (*vihārā*): the divine abode (*dibbo vihāro*), the Brahmā abode (*brahmā vihāro*), and the noble abode (*ariyo vihāro*). “Three miracles (*prātihāryāṇi*): the miracle of psychic power (*ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ*), the miracle of mind-reading (*ādeśanāprātihāryaṃ*), and the miracle of instruction (*anuśāsanīprātihāryaṃ*). “These, friends (*āvuso*), are the three *dharmas* that are rightly expounded by the Blessed One (*bhagavatā*)—the one who knows (*jānatā*), the one who sees (*passatā*), the Worthy One (*arhatā*), rightly self-awakened (*sammāsambuddhena*). There, all should chant in unison… for the benefit, welfare and happiness of gods and humans. The Quadruple
commentary_pali:
305. Iti dukavasena sāmaggirasaṃ dassetvā idāni tikavasena dassetuṃ puna ārabhi. Tattha lubbhatīti lobho. Akusalañca taṃ mūlañca, akusalānaṃ vā mūlanti akusalamūlaṃ. Dussatīti doso. Muyhatīti moho. Tesaṃ paṭipakkhanayena alobhādayo veditabbā.

Duṭṭhu caritāni, virūpāni vā caritānīti duccaritāni. Kāyena duccaritaṃ, kāyato vā pavattaṃ duccaritanti kāyaduccaritaṃ. Sesesupi eseva nayo. Suṭṭhu caritāni, sundarāni vā caritānīti sucaritāni. Dvepi cete tikā paṇṇattiyā vā kammapathehi vā kathetabbā. Paññattiyā tāva kāyadvāre paññattasikkhāpadassa vītikkamo kāyaduccaritaṃ. Avītikkamo kāyasucaritaṃ. Vacīdvāre paññattasikkhāpadassa vītikkamo vacīduccaritaṃ, avītikkamo vacīsucaritaṃ. Ubhayattha paññattassa sikkhāpadassa vītikkamova manoduccaritaṃ, avītikkamo manosucaritaṃ. Ayaṃ paṇṇattikathā. Pāṇātipātādayo pana tisso cetanā kāyadvārepi vacīdvārepi uppannā kāyaduccaritaṃ. Catasso musāvādādicetanā vacīduccaritaṃ. Abhijjhā byāpādo micchādiṭṭhīti tayo cetanāsampayuttadhammā manoduccaritaṃ. Pāṇātipātādīhi viramantassa uppannā tisso cetanāpi viratiyopi kāyasucaritaṃ. Musāvādādīhi viramantassa catasso cetanāpi viratiyopi vacīsucaritaṃ. Anabhijjhā abyāpādo sammādiṭṭhīti tayo cetanāsampayuttadhammā manosucaritanti ayaṃ kammapathakathā.

Kāmapaṭisaṃyutto vitakko kāmavitakko. Byāpādapaṭisaṃyutto vitakko byāpādavitakko. Vihiṃsāpaṭisaṃyutto vitakko vihiṃsāvitakko. Tesu dve sattesupi saṅkhāresupi uppajjanti. Kāmavitakko hi piye manāpe satte vā saṅkhāre vā vitakkentassa uppajjati. Byāpādavitakko appiye amanāpe satte vā saṅkhāre vā kujjhitvā olokanakālato paṭṭhāya yāva vināsanā uppajjati. Vihiṃsāvitakko saṅkhāresu nuppajjati. Saṅkhāro hi dukkhāpetabbo nāma natthi. Ime sattā haññantu vā ucchijjantu vā vinassantu vā mā vā ahesunti cintanakāle pana sattesu uppajjati.

kāmavitakko. byāpādavitakko. vihiṃsāvitakko.

Nekkhammapaṭisaṃyutto vitakko nekkhammavitakko. So asubhapubbabhāge kāmāvacaro hoti. Asubhajjhāne rūpāvacaro. Taṃ jhānaṃ pādakaṃ katvā uppannamaggaphalakāle lokuttaro. Abyāpādapaṭisaṃyutto vitakko abyāpādavitakko. So mettāpubbabhāge kāmāvacaro hoti. Mettājhāne rūpāvacaro. Taṃ jhānaṃ pādakaṃ katvā uppannamaggaphalakāle lokuttaro. Avihiṃsāpaṭisaṃyutto vitakko avihiṃsāvitakko. So karuṇāpubbabhāge kāmāvacaro. Karuṇājhāne rūpāvacaro. Taṃ jhānaṃ pādakaṃ katvā uppannamaggaphalakāle lokuttaro. Yadā alobho sīsaṃ hoti, tadā itare dve tadanvāyikā bhavanti. Yadā mettā sīsaṃ hoti, tadā itare dve tadanvāyikā bhavanti. Yadā karuṇā sīsaṃ hoti, tadā itare dve tadanvāyikā bhavantīti. Kāmasaṅkappādayo vuttanayeneva veditabbā. Desanāmattameva hetaṃ. Atthato pana kāmavitakkādīnañca kāmasaṅkappādīnañca nānākaraṇaṃ natthi.

nekkhammavitakko. abyāpādavitakko. avihiṃsāvitakko.

Kāmapaṭisaṃyuttā saññā kāmasaññā. Byāpādapaṭisaṃyuttā saññā byāpādasaññā. Vihiṃsāpaṭisaṃyuttā saññā vihiṃsāsaññā. Tāsampi kāmavitakkādīnaṃ viya uppajjanākāro veditabbo. Taṃsampayuttāyeva hi etā. Nekkhammasaññādayopi nekkhammavitakkādisampayuttāyeva. Tasmā tāsampi tatheva kāmāvacarādibhāvo veditabbo.

kāmasaññā. byāpādasaññā. vihiṃsāsaññā. Nekkhammasaññādayo

Kāmadhātuādīsu ‘‘kāmapaṭisaṃyutto takko vitakko micchāsaṅkappo. Ayaṃ vuccati kāmadhātu. Sabbepi akusalā dhammā kāmadhātū’’ti ayaṃ kāmadhātu. ‘‘Byāpādapaṭisaṃyutto takko vitakko micchāsaṅkappo. Ayaṃ vuccati byāpādadhātu. Dasasu āghātavatthūsu cittassa āghāto paṭighāto anattamanatā cittassā’’ti ayaṃ byāpādadhātu. ‘‘Vihiṃsā paṭisaṃyutto takko vitakko micchāsaṅkappo. Ayaṃ vuccati vihiṃsādhātu. Idhekacco pāṇinā vā leḍḍunā vā daṇḍena vā satthena vā rajjuyā vā aññataraññatarena vā satte viheṭhetī’’ti ayaṃ vihiṃsādhātu. Tattha dve kathā sabbasaṅgāhikā ca asambhinnā ca. Tattha kāmadhātuyā gahitāya itarā dve gahitāva honti, tato pana nīharitvā ayaṃ byāpādadhātu ayaṃ vihiṃsādhātūti dassetīti ayaṃ sabbasaṅgāhikakathā nāma. Kāmadhātuṃ kathento pana bhagavā byāpādadhātuṃ byāpādadhātuṭṭhāne , vihiṃsādhātuṃ vihiṃsādhātuṭṭhāne ṭhapetvā avasesaṃ kāmadhātu nāmāti kathesīti ayaṃ asambhinnakathā nāma.

kāmadhātu. byāpādadhātu. vihiṃsādhātu.

Nekkhammadhātuādīsu ‘‘nekkhammapaṭisaṃyutto takko vitakko sammāsaṅkappo. Ayaṃ vuccati nekkhammadhātu. Sabbepi kusalā dhammā nekkhammadhātū’’ti ayaṃ nekkhammadhātu. ‘‘Abyāpādapaṭisaṃyutto takko…pe… ayaṃ vuccati abyāpādadhātu. Yā sattesu metti…pe… mettācetovimuttī’’ti ayaṃ abyāpādadhātu. ‘‘Avihiṃsāpaṭisaṃyutto takko…pe… ayaṃ vuccati avihiṃsādhātu. Yā sattesu karuṇā…pe… karuṇācetovimuttī’’ti ayaṃ avihiṃsādhātu. Idhāpi vuttanayeneva dve kathā veditabbā.

nekkhammadhātu. abyāpādadhātu. avihiṃsādhātu.

Aparāpi tisso dhātuyoti aññāpi suññataṭṭhena tisso dhātuyo. Tāsu ‘‘tattha katamā kāmadhātu? Heṭṭhato avīcinirayaṃ pariyantaṃ karitvā’’ti evaṃ vitthārito kāmabhavo kāmadhātu nāma. ‘‘Heṭṭhato brahmalokaṃ pariyantaṃ karitvā ākāsānañcāyatanupage deve pariyantaṃ karitvā’’ti evaṃ vitthāritā pana rūpārūpabhavā itarā dve dhātuyo. Dhātuyā āgataṭṭhānamhi hi bhavena paricchinditabbā. Bhavassa āgataṭṭhāne dhātuyā paricchinditabbā. Idha bhavena paricchedo kathito. Rūpadhātuādīsu rūpārūpadhātuyo rūpārūpabhavāyeva. Nirodhadhātuyā nibbānaṃ kathitaṃ.

Aparāpi tisso dhātuyo kāmadhātu

Hīnādīsu hīnā dhātūti dvādasa akusalacittuppādā. Avasesā tebhūmakadhammā majjhimadhātu. Nava lokuttaradhammā paṇītadhātu.

Hīnā majjhimadhātu. paṇītadhātu.

Kāmataṇhāti pañcakāmaguṇiko rāgo. Rūpārūpabhavesu pana rāgo jhānanikantisassatadiṭṭhisahagato rāgo bhavavasena patthanā bhavataṇhā. Ucchedadiṭṭhisahagato rāgo vibhavataṇhā. Apica ṭhapetvā pacchimaṃ taṇhādvayaṃ sesataṇhā kāmataṇhā nāma. Yathāha ‘‘tattha katamā bhavataṇhā? Bhavadiṭṭhisahagato rāgo sārāgo cittassa sārāgo. Ayaṃ vuccati bhavataṇhā. Tattha katamā vibhavataṇhā? Ucchedadiṭṭhisahagato rāgo sārāgo cittassa sārāgo, ayaṃ vuccati vibhavataṇhā. Avasesā taṇhā kāmataṇhā’’ti. Puna kāmataṇhādīsu pañcakāmaguṇiko rāgo kāmataṇhā. Rūpārūpabhavesu chandarāgo itarā dve taṇhā. Abhidhamme panetā ‘‘kāmadhātupaṭisaṃyutto…pe… arūpadhātupaṭisaṃyutto’’ti evaṃ vitthāritā. Iminā vārena kiṃ dasseti? Sabbepi tebhūmakā dhammā rajanīyaṭṭhena taṇhāvatthukāti sabbataṇhā kāmataṇhāya pariyādiyitvā tato nīharitvā itarā dve taṇhā dasseti. Rūpataṇhādīsu rūpabhave chandarāgo rūpataṇhā. Arūpabhave chandarāgo arūpataṇhā. Ucchedadiṭṭhisahagato rāgo nirodhataṇhā.

Kāmataṇhā bhavataṇhā. vibhavataṇhā. rūpataṇhā. arūpataṇhā. nirodhataṇhā.

Saṃyojanattike vaṭṭasmiṃ saṃyojayanti bandhantīti saṃyojanāni. Sati rūpādibhede kāye diṭṭhi, vijjamānā vā kāye diṭṭhīti sakkāyadiṭṭhi. Vicinanto etāya kicchati, na sakkoti sanniṭṭhānaṃ kātunti vicikicchā. Sīlañca vatañca parāmasatīti sīlabbataparāmāso. Atthato pana ‘‘rūpaṃ attato samanupassatī’’tiādinā nayena āgatā vīsativatthukā diṭṭhi sakkāyadiṭṭhi nāma. ‘‘Satthari kaṅkhatī’’tiādinā nayena āgatā aṭṭhavatthukā vimati vicikicchā nāma. ‘‘Idhekacco sīlena suddhi vatena suddhi sīlabbatena suddhīti sīlaṃ parāmasati, vataṃ parāmasati, sīlabbataṃ parāmasati. Yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigata’’ntiādinā nayena āgato vipariyesaggāho sīlabbataparāmāso nāma.

Tayoāsavāti ettha cirapārivāsiyaṭṭhena vā āsavanaṭṭhena vā āsavā. Tattha ‘‘purimā, bhikkhave, koṭi na paññāyati avijjāya, ito pubbe avijjā nāhosi, atha pacchā samabhavī’’ti, ‘‘purimā , bhikkhave, koṭi na paññāyati bhavataṇhāya bhavadiṭṭhiyā, ito pubbe bhavadiṭṭhi nāhosi, atha pacchā samabhavī’’ti evaṃ tāva cirapārivāsiyaṭṭhena āsavā veditabbā. Cakkhuto rūpe savati āsavati sandati pavattati. Sotato sadde. Ghānato gandhe. Jivhāto rase. Kāyato phoṭṭhabbe. Manato dhamme savati āsavati sandati pavattatīti evaṃ āsavanaṭṭhena āsavāti veditabbā.

Tayo āsavā āsavā.

Pāḷiyaṃ pana katthaci dve āsavā āgatā ‘‘diṭṭhadhammikā ca āsavā samparāyikā ca āsavā’’ti, katthaci ‘‘tayome, bhikkhave, āsavā. Kāmāsavo bhavāsavo avijjāsavo’’ti tayo. Abhidhamme teyeva diṭṭhāsavena saddhiṃ cattāro. Nibbedhikapariyāye ‘‘atthi, bhikkhave, āsavā nirayagāminiyā, atthi āsavā tiracchānayonigāminiyā, atthi āsavā pettivisayagāminiyā, atthi āsavā manussalokagāminiyā atthi āsavā devalokagāminiyā’’ti evaṃ pañca. Chakkanipāte āhuneyyasutte ‘‘atthi, bhikkhave, āsavā saṃvarā pahātabbā, atthi āsavā paṭisevanā pahātabbā, atthi āsavā parivajjanā pahātabbā, atthi āsavā adhivāsanā pahātabbā, atthi āsavā vinodanā pahātabbā, atthi āsavā bhāvanā pahātabbā’’ti evaṃ cha. Sabbāsavapariyāye teyeva dassanāpahātabbehi saddhiṃ satta. Imasmiṃ pana saṅgītisutte tayo. Tattha ‘‘yo kāmesu kāmacchando’’ti evaṃ vutto pañcakāmaguṇiko rāgo kāmāsavo nāma. ‘‘Yo bhavesu bhavacchando’’ti evaṃ vutto sassatadiṭṭhisahagato rāgo, bhavavasena vā patthanā bhavāsavo nāma. ‘‘Dukkhe aññāṇa’’ntiādinā nayena āgatā avijjā avijjāsavo nāmāti. Kāmabhavādayo kāmadhātuādivasena vuttāyeva.

Kāmesanādīsu ‘‘tattha katamā kāmesanā? Yo kāmesu kāmacchando kāmajjhosānaṃ, ayaṃ vuccati kāmesanā’’ti evaṃ vutto kāmagavesanarāgo kāmesanā nāma. ‘‘Tattha katamā bhavesanā? Yo bhavesu bhavacchando bhavajjhosānaṃ, ayaṃ vuccati bhavesanā’’ti evaṃ vutto bhavagavesanarāgo bhavesanā nāma. ‘‘Tattha katamā brahmacariyesanā? Sassato lokoti vā…pe… neva hoti na nahoti tathāgato parammaraṇāti vā, yā evarūpā diṭṭhi diṭṭhigataṃ vipariyesaggāho , ayaṃ vuccati brahmacariyesanā’’ti evaṃ vuttā diṭṭhigatikasammatassa brahmacariyassa gavesanadiṭṭhi brahmacariyesanā nāma. Na kevalañca bhavarāgadiṭṭhiyova, tadekaṭṭhaṃ kammampi esanāyeva. Vuttañhetaṃ ‘‘tattha katamā kāmesanā? Kāmarāgo tadekaṭṭhaṃ akusalaṃ kāyakammaṃ vacīkammaṃ manokammaṃ, ayaṃ vuccati kāmesanā. Tattha katamā bhavesanā? Bhavarāgo tadekaṭṭhaṃ akusalaṃ kāyakammaṃ vacīkammaṃ manokammaṃ, ayaṃ vuccati bhavesanā. Tattha katamā brahmacariyesanā? Antaggāhikā diṭṭhi tadekaṭṭhaṃ akusalaṃ kāyakammaṃ vacīkammaṃ manokammaṃ, ayaṃ vuccati brahmacariyesanā’’ti.

Vidhāsu ‘‘kathaṃvidhaṃ sīlavantaṃ vadanti, kathaṃvidhaṃ paññavantaṃ vadantī’’tiādīsu (saṃ. ni. 1.95) ākārasaṇṭhānaṃ vidhā nāma. ‘‘Ekavidhena ñāṇavatthu duvidhena ñāṇavatthū’’tiādīsu (vibha. 751) koṭṭhāso. ‘‘Seyyohamasmīti vidhā’’tiādīsu (vibha. 920) māno vidhā nāma. Idha so adhippeto. Māno hi seyyādivasena vidahanato vidhāti vuccati. Seyyohamasmīti iminā seyyasadisahīnānaṃ vasena tayo mānā vuttā. Sadisahīnesupi eseva nayo.

vidhā Seyyohamasmī

Ayañhi māno nāma seyyassa tividho, sadisassa tividho, hīnassa tividhoti navavidho hoti. Tattha ‘‘seyyassa seyyohamasmī’’ti māno rājūnañceva pabbajitānañca uppajjati.

māno navavidho

Rājā hi raṭṭhena vā dhanavāhanehi vā ‘‘ko mayā sadiso atthī’’ti etaṃ mānaṃ karoti . Pabbajitopi sīladhutaṅgādīhi ‘‘ko mayā sadiso atthī’’ti etaṃ mānaṃ karoti. ‘‘Seyyassa sadisohamasmī’’ti mānopi etesaṃyeva uppajjati. Rājā hi raṭṭhena vā dhanavāhanehi vā aññarājūhi saddhiṃ mayhaṃ kiṃ nānākaraṇanti etaṃ mānaṃ karoti. Pabbajitopi sīladhutaṅgādīhipi aññena bhikkhunā mayhaṃ kiṃ nānākaraṇanti etaṃ mānaṃ karoti. ‘‘Seyyassa hīnohamasmī’’ti mānopi etesaṃyeva uppajjati. Yassa hi rañño raṭṭhaṃ vā dhanavāhanādīni vā nātisampannāni honti, so mayhaṃ rājāti vohāramukhamattameva, kiṃ rājā nāma ahanti etaṃ mānaṃ karoti. Pabbajitopi appalābhasakkāro ahaṃ dhammakathiko bahussuto mahātheroti kathāmattakameva, kiṃ dhammakathiko nāmāhaṃ kiṃ bahussuto kiṃ mahāthero yassa me lābhasakkāro natthīti etaṃ mānaṃ karoti.

‘‘Sadisassa seyyohamasmī’’ti mānādayo amaccādīnaṃ uppajjanti. Amacco vā hi raṭṭhiyo vā bhogayānavāhanādīhi ko mayā sadiso añño rājapuriso atthīti vā mayhaṃ aññehi saddhiṃ kiṃ nānākaraṇanti vā amaccoti nāmameva mayhaṃ, ghāsacchādanamattampi me natthi, kiṃ amacco nāmāhanti vā ete māne karoti.

‘‘Hīnassa seyyohamasmī’’ti mānādayo dāsādīnaṃ uppajjanti. Dāso hi mātito vā pitito vā ko mayā sadiso añño dāso nāma atthi, aññe jīvituṃ asakkontā kucchihetu dāsā jātā, ahaṃ pana paveṇīāgatattā seyyoti vā paveṇīāgatabhāvena ubhatosuddhikadāsattena asukadāsena nāma saddhiṃ kiṃ mayhaṃ nānākaraṇanti vā kucchivasenāhaṃ dāsabya upagato, mātāpitukoṭiyā pana me dāsaṭṭhānaṃ natthi, kiṃ dāso nāma ahanti vā ete māne karoti. Yathā ca dāso, evaṃ pukkusacaṇḍālādayopi ete māne karontiyeva.

Ettha ca seyyassa seyyohamasmīti, ca sadisassa sadisohamasmīti ca hīnassa hīnohamasmīti ca ime tayo mānā yāthāvamānā nāma arahattamaggavajjhā. Sesā cha mānā ayāthāvamānā nāma paṭhamamaggavajjhā.

Tayo addhāti tayo kālā. Atīto addhātiādīsu dvepariyāyā suttantapariyāyo ca abhidhammapariyāyo ca. Suttantapariyāyena paṭisandhito pubbe atīto addhā nāma. Cutito pacchā anāgato addhā nāma. Saha cutipaṭisandhīhi tadantaraṃ paccuppanno addhā nāma. Abhidhammapariyāyena tīsu khaṇesu bhaṅgato uddhaṃ atīto addhā nāma. Uppādato pubbe anāgatoaddhā nāma. Khaṇattaye paccuppanno addhā nāma. Atītādibhedo ca nāma ayaṃ dhammānaṃ hoti, na kālassa. Atītādibhede pana dhamme upādāya idha paramatthato avijjamānopi kālo teneva vohārena vuttoti veditabbo.
