‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhuno uppanno hoti appamattako ābādho. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘uppanno kho me ayaṃ appamattako ābādho, ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ vijjati yaṃ me ābādho pavaḍḍheyya, handāhaṃ vīriyaṃ ārabhāmi…pe… so vīriyaṃ ārabhati… idaṃ sattamaṃ ārambhavatthu.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu gilānā vuṭṭhito hoti aciravuṭṭhito gelaññā. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘ahaṃ kho gilānā vuṭṭhito aciravuṭṭhito gelaññā, ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ vijjati yaṃ me ābādho paccudāvatteyya, handāhaṃ vīriyaṃ ārabhāmi appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāyā’’ti! So vīriyaṃ ārabhati appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāya. Idaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ ārambhavatthu.
mula_english:
335. "Aṭṭha ārambhavatthūni. Furthermore, friends, there is the case where a monk has some work to do. The thought occurs to him: ‘I will have to do this work. But when I am doing this work, it will not be easy to attend to the Buddha’s message. Why don’t I make an effort beforehand for the attaining of the as-yet-unattained, the reaching of the as-yet-unreached, the realization of the as-yet-unrealized?’ So he makes an effort for the attaining of the as-yet-unattained, the reaching of the as-yet-unreached, the realization of the as-yet-unrealized. This is the first ground for the arousal of energy.

“Again, friends, there is the case where a monk has done some work. The thought occurs to him: ‘I have done some work. While I was doing work, I couldn’t attend to the Buddha’s message. Why don’t I make an effort for the attaining of the as-yet-unattained, the reaching of the as-yet-unreached, the realization of the as-yet-unrealized?’ So he makes an effort... This is the second ground for the arousal of energy.

“Again, friends, there is the case where a monk has to go on a journey. The thought occurs to him: ‘I will have to go on this journey. But when I am going on the journey, it will not be easy to attend to the Buddha’s message. Why don’t I make an effort beforehand for the attaining of the as-yet-unattained, the reaching of the as-yet-unreached, the realization of the as-yet-unrealized?’ So he makes an effort. This is the third ground for the arousal of energy.

“Again, friends, there is the case where a monk has gone on a journey. The thought occurs to him: ‘I have gone on a journey. While I was going on the journey, I couldn’t attend to the Buddha’s message. Why don’t I make an effort for the attaining of the as-yet-unattained, the reaching of the as-yet-unreached, the realization of the as-yet-unrealized?’ So he makes an effort… This is the fourth ground for the arousal of energy.

“Again, friends, there is the case where a monk, having gone for alms in a village or town, does not get as much coarse or refined food as he would like for his fill. The thought occurs to him: ‘I, having gone for alms in a village or town, have not gotten as much coarse or refined food as I would like for my fill. This body of mine is light & suitable for work. Why don’t I make an effort for the attaining of the as-yet-unattained, the reaching of the as-yet-unreached, the realization of the as-yet-unrealized?’ So he makes an effort… This is the fifth ground for the arousal of energy.

“Again, friends, there is the case where a monk, having gone for alms in a village or town, gets as much coarse or refined food as he would like for his fill. The thought occurs to him: ‘I, having gone for alms in a village or town, have gotten as much coarse or refined food as I would like for my fill. This body of mine is strong & suitable for work. Why don’t I make an effort for the attaining of the as-yet-unattained, the reaching of the as-yet-unreached, the realization of the as-yet-unrealized?’ So he makes an effort… This is the sixth ground for the arousal of energy.

“Again, friends, there is the case where a monk comes down with a slight illness. The thought occurs to him: ‘I have come down with a slight illness. Now, there’s the possibility that it could get worse. Why don’t I make an effort beforehand for the attaining of the as-yet-unattained, the reaching of the as-yet-unreached, the realization of the as-yet-unrealized?’ So he makes an effort… This is the seventh ground for the arousal of energy.

“Again, friends, there is the case where a monk has recovered from his illness, not long after his recovery. The thought occurs to him: ‘I have recovered from my illness. It’s not long after my recovery. Now, there’s the possibility that the illness could come back. Why don’t I make an effort beforehand for the attaining of the as-yet-unattained, the reaching of the as-yet-unreached, the realization of the as-yet-unrealized?’ So he makes an effort for the attaining of the as-yet-unattained, the reaching of the as-yet-unreached, the realization of the as-yet-unrealized. This is the eighth ground for the arousal of energy.
commentary_pali: 335.Ārambhavatthūnīti vīriyakāraṇāni. Tesampi imināva nayena attho veditabbo.
commentary_english:
The causes of exertion, namely, the *ārambhavatthūnī*.

In the same way, the meaning should be understood for them as well.

mula_pali: 336. ‘‘Aṭṭha dānavatthūni. Āsajja dānaṃ deti, bhayā dānaṃ deti, ‘adāsi me’ti dānaṃ deti, ‘dassati me’ti dānaṃ deti, ‘sāhu dāna’nti dānaṃ deti, ‘ahaṃ pacāmi, ime na pacanti, nārahāmi pacanto apacantānaṃ dānaṃ na dātu’nti dānaṃ deti, ‘idaṃ me dānaṃ dadato kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggacchatī’ti dānaṃ deti. Cittālaṅkāra-cittaparikkhāratthaṃ dānaṃ deti.
mula_english:
336. The eight bases for giving (*dānavatthūni*):

One gives a gift (*dānaṃ deti*) on impulse (*āsajja*); one gives a gift out of fear (*bhayā*); one gives a gift thinking, "He/she gave to me (*adāsi me*);" one gives a gift thinking, "He/she will give to me (*dassati me*);" one gives a gift thinking, "It is good to give (*sāhu dānaṃ*);" one gives a gift thinking, "I am cooking (*ahaṃ pacāmi*), these are not cooking (*ime na pacanti*), it is not right for me, while cooking, not to give to those who are not cooking (*nārahaṃ pacanto apacantānaṃ dānaṃ na dātuṃ*);" one gives a gift thinking, "When this gift has been given (*idaṃ me dānaṃ dadato*), my admirable reputation (*kalyāṇo kittisaddo*) will spread about (*abbhuggacchati*)."

One gives a gift as an ornament for the mind (*cittālaṅkāra*), as a support for the mind (*citta-parikkhāratthaṃ*).
commentary_pali:
336.Dānavatthūnīti dānakāraṇāni. Āsajja dānaṃ detīti patvā dānaṃ deti. Āgataṃ disvāva muhuttaṃyeva nisīdāpetvā sakkāraṃ katvā dānaṃ deti, dassāmi dassāmīti na kilameti. Iti ettha āsādanaṃ dānakāraṇaṃ nāma hoti. Bhayā dānaṃ detītiādīsupi bhayādīni dānakāraṇānīti veditabbāni. Tattha bhayaṃ nāma ayaṃ adāyako akārakoti garahābhayaṃ vā apāyabhayaṃ vā. Adāsi meti mayhaṃ pubbe esa idaṃ nāma adāsīti deti. Dassati meti anāgate idaṃ nāma dassatīti deti. Sāhu dānanti dānaṃ nāma sādhu sundaraṃ, buddhādīhi paṇḍitehi pasatthanti deti. Cittālaṅkāracittaparikkhāratthaṃ dānaṃ detīti samathavipassanācittassa alaṅkāratthañceva parivāratthañca deti. Dānañhi cittaṃ mudukaṃ karoti. Yena laddhaṃ hoti, sopi laddhaṃ meti muducitto hoti, yena dinnaṃ, sopi dinnaṃ mayāti muducitto hoti, iti ubhinnampi cittaṃ mudukaṃ karoti, teneva ‘‘adantadamanaṃ dāna’’nti vuccati. Yathāha –

‘‘Adantadamanaṃ dānaṃ, adānaṃ dantadūsakaṃ;

Dānena piyavācāya, unnamanti namanti cā’’ti.

Imesu pana aṭṭhasu dānesu cittālaṅkāradānameva uttamaṃ.
commentary_english:
336. "Dānavatthūnī" means the causes of generosity (dānakāraṇāni).

"Āsajja dānaṃ detī" means giving generosity, having attained [something].

Having seen someone arrive, having seated them for just a moment, having shown respect, one gives generosity (dānaṃ deti), without tiring of saying "I will give, I will give."

Thus, here, āsādanaṃ is said to be a cause of generosity (dānakāraṇaṃ nāma hoti).

"Bhayā dānaṃ detī," and so forth, it should be understood that fear and so on are causes of generosity (dānakāraṇāni).

There, *bhayaṃ*, namely, this giver is a non-giver, a non-doer; or fear of blame (garahābhayaṃ vā), or fear of the lower realms (apāyabhayaṃ vā).

"Adāsi me" means, "This one gave this to me before," thus he gives.

"Dassati me" means, "In the future, this one will give to me," thus he gives.

"Sāhu dāna" means generosity (dānaṃ) is good (sādhu), beautiful (sundaraṃ), praised by the Buddhas and wise people, thus he gives.

"Cittālaṅkāracittaparikkhāratthaṃ dānaṃ detī" means he gives for the sake of adorning and purifying the mind (*samathavipassanācittassa alaṅkāratthañceva parivāratthañca deti*).

Indeed, generosity (dānañhi) makes the mind soft (cittaṃ mudukaṃ karoti).

By whom it has been received (yena laddhaṃ hoti), he also has a softened mind (mudu-citto hoti) thinking, "I have received it" (laddhaṃ me iti); by whom it has been given (yena dinnaṃ), he also has a softened mind thinking, "It was given by me" (dinnaṃ mayāti); thus, it makes the mind soft for both (iti ubhinnampi cittaṃ mudukaṃ karoti), therefore it is said, "Generosity tames the untamed" (‘‘adantadamanaṃ dāna’’nti vuccati).

As it is said:

“Generosity tames the untamed, non-generosity corrupts the tamed;

Through generosity and kind speech, they rise up and bow down.”

Among these eight kinds of generosity (aṭṭhasu dānesu), generosity which adorns the mind (*cittālaṅkāradānameva*) is the best (uttamaṃ).

mula_pali:
337. ‘‘Aṭṭha dānūpapattiyo. Idhāvuso, ekacco dānaṃ deti samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā annaṃ pānaṃ vatthaṃ yānaṃ mālāgandhavilepanaṃ seyyāvasathapadīpeyyaṃ. So yaṃ deti taṃ paccāsīsati paccāsiṃsati (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.). So passati khattiyamahāsālaṃ vā brāhmaṇamahāsālaṃ vā gahapatimahāsālaṃ vā pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappitaṃ samaṅgībhūtaṃ paricārayamānaṃ. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘aho vatāhaṃ kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā khattiyamahāsālānaṃ vā brāhmaṇamahāsālānaṃ vā gahapatimahāsālānaṃ vā sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya’nti! So taṃ cittaṃ dahati, taṃ cittaṃ adhiṭṭhāti, taṃ cittaṃ bhāveti, tassa taṃ cittaṃ hīne vimuttaṃ uttari abhāvitaṃ tatrūpapattiyā saṃvattati . Tañca kho sīlavato vadāmi no dussīlassa. Ijjhatāvuso, sīlavato cetopaṇidhi visuddhattā.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, idhekacco dānaṃ deti samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā annaṃ pānaṃ…pe… seyyāvasathapadīpeyyaṃ. So yaṃ deti taṃ paccāsīsati. Tassa sutaṃ hoti – ‘cātumahārājikā cātummahārājikā (sī. syā. pī.) devā dīghāyukā vaṇṇavanto sukhabahulā’’ti. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘aho vatāhaṃ kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā cātumahārājikānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya’’nti! So taṃ cittaṃ dahati, taṃ cittaṃ adhiṭṭhāti, taṃ cittaṃ bhāveti, tassa taṃ cittaṃ hīne vimuttaṃ uttari abhāvitaṃ tatrūpapattiyā saṃvattati. Tañca kho sīlavato vadāmi no dussīlassa. Ijjhatāvuso, sīlavato cetopaṇidhi visuddhattā.

cātummahārājikā (sī. syā. pī.)

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, idhekacco dānaṃ deti samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā annaṃ pānaṃ…pe… seyyāvasathapadīpeyyaṃ. So yaṃ deti taṃ paccāsīsati. Tassa sutaṃ hoti – ‘tāvatiṃsā devā…pe… yāmā devā…pe… tusitā devā …pe… nimmānaratī devā…pe… paranimmitavasavattī devā dīghāyukā vaṇṇavanto sukhabahulā’ti. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘aho vatāhaṃ kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā paranimmitavasavattīnaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya’’nti! So taṃ cittaṃ dahati, taṃ cittaṃ adhiṭṭhāti, taṃ cittaṃ bhāveti, tassa taṃ cittaṃ hīne vimuttaṃ uttari abhāvitaṃ tatrūpapattiyā saṃvattati. Tañca kho sīlavato vadāmi no dussīlassa. Ijjhatāvuso, sīlavato cetopaṇidhi visuddhattā.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, idhekacco dānaṃ deti samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā annaṃ pānaṃ vatthaṃ yānaṃ mālāgandhavilepanaṃ seyyāvasathapadīpeyyaṃ. So yaṃ deti taṃ paccāsīsati. Tassa sutaṃ hoti – ‘brahmakāyikā devā dīghāyukā vaṇṇavanto sukhabahulā’ti. Tassa evaṃ hoti – ‘aho vatāhaṃ kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā brahmakāyikānaṃ devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjeyya’nti! So taṃ cittaṃ dahati, taṃ cittaṃ adhiṭṭhāti, taṃ cittaṃ bhāveti, tassa taṃ cittaṃ hīne vimuttaṃ uttari abhāvitaṃ tatrūpapattiyā saṃvattati. Tañca kho sīlavato vadāmi no dussīlassa; vītarāgassa no sarāgassa. Ijjhatāvuso, sīlavato cetopaṇidhi vītarāgattā.

‘‘Aṭṭha parisā – khattiyaparisā, brāhmaṇaparisā, gahapatiparisā, samaṇaparisā, cātumahārājikaparisā, tāvatiṃsaparisā, māraparisā, brahmaparisā .

parisā –

‘‘Aṭṭha lokadhammā – lābho ca, alābho ca, yaso ca, ayaso ca, nindā ca, pasaṃsā ca, sukhañca, dukkhañca.

lokadhammā –
mula_english:
337.
’’Eight grounds for giving ( *dānūpapattiyo* ).
Here, friends, a certain individual gives a gift to a *samaṇa* or a *brāhmaṇa*—food, drink, cloth, vehicles, garlands, scents, ointments, bedding, lodging, and lighting.
Whatever he gives, he expects something in return.
He sees a prosperous noble warrior, a prosperous *brāhman*, or a prosperous householder going about endowed & provided with the five strings of sensuality.
It occurs to him: ‘Oh, with the breakup of the body, after death, may I be reborn in companionship with the prosperous noble warriors, the prosperous *brāhmans*, or the prosperous householders!’ He fixes on that thought, determines on that thought, develops that thought. His mind—unreleased from what is inferior, uncultivated in what is higher— leads to his rebirth there.
But I say this of a virtuous person, not of an unvirtuous one.
A virtuous person’s act of directing awareness succeeds through purity.

’’And further, friends, a certain person gives a gift to a *samaṇa* or a *brāhmaṇa*—food, drink…and lighting.
Whatever he gives, he expects something in return.
He has heard: ‘The *Cātumahārājika* gods are long-lived, beautiful, and abound in happiness.’
It occurs to him: ‘Oh, with the breakup of the body, after death, may I be reborn in companionship with the *Cātumahārājika* gods!’ He fixes on that thought, determines on that thought, develops that thought. His mind—unreleased from what is inferior, uncultivated in what is higher— leads to his rebirth there.
But I say this of a virtuous person, not of an unvirtuous one.
A virtuous person’s act of directing awareness succeeds through purity.

’’And further, friends, a certain person gives a gift to a *samaṇa* or a *brāhmaṇa*—food, drink…and lighting.
Whatever he gives, he expects something in return.
He has heard: ‘The *Tāvatiṃsa* gods… the *Yāma* gods… the *Tusita* gods… the *Nimmānarati* gods… the *Paranimmitavasavattī* gods are long-lived, beautiful, and abound in happiness.’
It occurs to him: ‘Oh, with the breakup of the body, after death, may I be reborn in companionship with the *Paranimmitavasavattī* gods!’ He fixes on that thought, determines on that thought, develops that thought. His mind—unreleased from what is inferior, uncultivated in what is higher— leads to his rebirth there.
But I say this of a virtuous person, not of an unvirtuous one.
A virtuous person’s act of directing awareness succeeds through purity.

’’And further, friends, a certain person gives a gift to a *samaṇa* or a *brāhmaṇa*—food, drink, cloth, vehicles, garlands, scents, ointments, bedding, lodging, and lighting.
Whatever he gives, he expects something in return.
He has heard: ‘The *Brahmakāyika* gods are long-lived, beautiful, and abound in happiness.’
It occurs to him: ‘Oh, may I, on the dissolution of the body, after death, be reborn in companionship with the *Brahmakāyika* devas!’ He directs his mind towards this, he establishes his mind towards this, he develops his mind towards this. But that mind of his is inferior and not freed, undeveloped for rebirth there.

But I say this of a virtuous person (*śīlavat*), not of an unvirtuous one (*duḥśīla*); of one devoid of passion (*vītarāga*), not of one with passion (*sarāga*).

A virtuous person’s (*śīlavat*) act of directing awareness succeeds through absence of passion (*vītarāgattā*).

The eight assemblies (*aṭṭha parisā*) are the assembly of *Kṣatriyas* (*khattiyaparisā*), the assembly of *Brāhmaṇas* (*brāhmaṇaparisā*), the assembly of householders (*gahapatiparisā*), the assembly of ascetics (*samaṇaparisā*), the assembly of the *Cāturmahārājikas* (*cātumahārājikaparisā*), the assembly of the Thirty-Three Gods (*tāvatiṃsaparisā*), the assembly of *Māras* (*māraparisā*), the assembly of *Brahmās* (*brahmaparisā*).

The eight worldly conditions (*aṭṭha lokadhammā*) are: gain (*lābha*), and loss (*alābha*), fame (*yaśa*), and infamy (*ayaśa*), blame (*nindā*), and praise (*pasaṃsā*), pleasure (*sukha*), and pain (*duḥkha*).
commentary_pali:
337.Dānūpapattiyoti dānapaccayā upapattiyo. Dahatīti ṭhapeti. Adhiṭṭhātīti tasseva vevacanaṃ. Bhāvetīti vaḍḍheti. Hīne vimuttanti hīnesu pañcakāmaguṇesu vimuttaṃ. Uttari abhāvitanti tato uttari maggaphalatthāya abhāvitaṃ. Tatrūpapattiyā saṃvattatīti yaṃ patthetvā kusalaṃ kataṃ, tattha tattha nibbattanatthāya saṃvattati.

Vītarāgassāti maggena vā samucchinnarāgassa samāpattiyā vā vikkhambhitarāgassa. Dānamatteneva hi brahmaloke nibbattituṃ na sakkā. Dānaṃ pana samādhivipassanācittassa alaṅkāro parivāro hoti. Tato dānena muducitto brahmavihāre bhāvetvā brahmaloke nibbattati. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘vītarāgassa no sarāgassā’’ti.

Vītarāgassā

Khattiyānaṃ parisā khattiyaparisā, samūhoti attho. Esa nayo sabbattha.

khattiyaparisā,

Lokassa dhammā lokadhammā. Etehi mutto nāma natthi, buddhānampi hontiyeva. Vuttampi cetaṃ – ‘‘aṭṭhime, bhikkhave, lokadhammā lokaṃ anuparivattanti, loko ca aṭṭha lokadhamme anuparivattatī’’ti (a. ni. 8.5). Lābho alābhoti lābhe āgate alābho āgato evāti veditabbo. Yasādīsupi eseva nayo.

lokadhammā. Lābho alābho Yasā
commentary_english:
337. *Dānūpapattiyo*: rebirths due to giving are *dānapaccayā upapattiyo*.
*Dahatī*: he places.
*Adhiṭṭhātī*: that is its synonym.
*Bhāvetī*: he increases.
*Hīne vimuttaṃ*: liberated from inferior, the five sensory pleasures are *vimuttaṃ*.
*Uttari abhāvitaṃ*: further uncultivated, is uncultivated for the sake of the path and its fruit.
*Tatrūpapattiyā saṃvattatī*: it leads to rebirth there, means that which having desired, good was done, it leads to the sake of arising in that very place.

*Vītarāgassā*: by the path, or by the eradicated passion, or by the suppressed passion through attainment (samāpatti).
Merely by giving, it is not possible to be reborn in the Brahmā realm.
Giving, however, is an adornment, an entourage of the mind of concentration and insight.
Therefore, with a mind softened by giving, having cultivated the Brahmā abodes, one is reborn in the Brahmā realm.
Therefore, it was said, "of one without passion, not of one with passion."

*Vītarāgassā*:
A gathering of *kṣatriyas* is a *kṣatriyaparisā,* meaning a group.
This method applies everywhere.

*Kṣatriyaparisā*,
The *dharmas* of the world are *lokadhammā*.
There is no one freed from these; even the Buddhas have them.
It was also said: “These eight worldly conditions, monks, keep the world turning around, and the world turns around these eight worldly conditions” (A.
Ni.
8.5).
*Lābho alābho*: having gained, loss has come, thus it should be understood.
This same method applies to fame, etc.

*Lokadhammā*.
*Lābho alābho* *yasā*

mula_pali:
338. ‘‘Aṭṭha abhibhāyatanāni. Ajjhattaṃ rūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati parittāni suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇāni, ‘tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṃsaññī hoti. Idaṃ paṭhamaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ.

‘‘Ajjhattaṃ rūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati appamāṇāni suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇāni, ‘tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti – evaṃsaññī hoti. Idaṃ dutiyaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ.

‘‘Ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati parittāni suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇāni, ‘tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṃsaññī hoti. Idaṃ tatiyaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ.

‘‘Ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati appamāṇāni suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇāni, ‘tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṃsaññī hoti. Idaṃ catutthaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ.

‘‘Ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati nīlāni nīlavaṇṇāni nīlanidassanāni nīlanibhāsāni. Seyyathāpi nāma umāpupphaṃ nīlaṃ nīlavaṇṇaṃ nīlanidassanaṃ nīlanibhāsaṃ, seyyathā vā pana taṃ vatthaṃ bārāṇaseyyakaṃ ubhatobhāgavimaṭṭhaṃ nīlaṃ nīlavaṇṇaṃ nīlanidassanaṃ nīlanibhāsaṃ. Evameva evamevaṃ (ka.) ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati nīlāni nīlavaṇṇāni nīlanidassanāni nīlanibhāsāni, ‘tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṃsaññī hoti. Idaṃ pañcamaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ.

evamevaṃ (ka.)

‘‘Ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati pītāni pītavaṇṇāni pītanidassanāni pītanibhāsāni. Seyyathāpi nāma kaṇikārapupphaṃ kaṇṇikārapupphaṃ (syā. kaṃ.) pītaṃ pītavaṇṇaṃ pītanidassanaṃ pītanibhāsaṃ, seyyathā vā pana taṃ vatthaṃ bārāṇaseyyakaṃ ubhatobhāgavimaṭṭhaṃ pītaṃ pītavaṇṇaṃ pītanidassanaṃ pītanibhāsaṃ. Evameva ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati pītāni pītavaṇṇāni pītanidassanāni pītanibhāsāni, ‘tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṃsaññī hoti. Idaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ.

kaṇṇikārapupphaṃ (syā. kaṃ.)

‘‘Ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati lohitakāni lohitakavaṇṇāni lohitakanidassanāni lohitakanibhāsāni. Seyyathāpi nāma bandhujīvakapupphaṃ lohitakaṃ lohitakavaṇṇaṃ lohitakanidassanaṃ lohitakanibhāsaṃ, seyyathā vā pana taṃ vatthaṃ bārāṇaseyyakaṃ ubhatobhāgavimaṭṭhaṃ lohitakaṃ lohitakavaṇṇaṃ lohitakanidassanaṃ lohitakanibhāsaṃ. Evameva ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati lohitakāni lohitakavaṇṇāni lohitakanidassanāni lohitakanibhāsāni, ‘tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṃsaññī hoti. Idaṃ sattamaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ.

‘‘Ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati odātāni odātavaṇṇāni odātanidassanāni odātanibhāsāni. Seyyathāpi nāma osadhitārakā odātā odātavaṇṇā odātanidassanā odātanibhāsā, seyyathā vā pana taṃ vatthaṃ bārāṇaseyyakaṃ ubhatobhāgavimaṭṭhaṃ odātaṃ odātavaṇṇaṃ odātanidassanaṃ odātanibhāsaṃ. Evameva ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko bahiddhā rūpāni passati odātāni odātavaṇṇāni odātanidassanāni odātanibhāsāni , ‘tāni abhibhuyya jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṃsaññī hoti. Idaṃ aṭṭhamaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ.
mula_english:
338. Eight dimensions of mastery (*aṭṭha abhibhāyatanāni*): One percipient of form internally (*ajjhattaṃ rūpasaññī eko*) sees forms externally as limited (*parittāni*), beautiful & ugly (*suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇāni*). Mastering them (*tāni abhibhuyya*), he is percipient of ‘I know; I see’ (*jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṃsaññī hoti*). This is the first dimension of mastery (*idaṃ paṭhamaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ*).

One percipient of form internally (*ajjhattaṃ rūpasaññī eko*) sees forms externally as immeasurable (*appamāṇāni*), beautiful & ugly (*suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇāni*). Mastering them (*tāni abhibhuyya*), he is percipient of ‘I know; I see’ (*jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṃsaññī hoti*). This is the second dimension of mastery (*idaṃ dutiyaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ*).

One percipient of the formless internally (*ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko*) sees forms externally as limited (*parittāni*), beautiful & ugly (*suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇāni*). Mastering them (*tāni abhibhuyya*), he is percipient of ‘I know; I see’ (*jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṃsaññī hoti*). This is the third dimension of mastery (*idaṃ tatiyaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ*).

One percipient of the formless internally (*ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko*) sees forms externally as immeasurable (*appamāṇāni*), beautiful & ugly (*suvaṇṇadubbaṇṇāni*). Mastering them (*tāni abhibhuyya*), he is percipient of ‘I know; I see’ (*jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṃsaññī hoti*). This is the fourth dimension of mastery (*idaṃ catutthaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ*).

One percipient of the formless internally (*ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko*) sees forms externally as blue (*nīlāni*), blue in their color (*nīlavaṇṇāni*), blue in their features (*nīlanidassanāni*), blue in their glow (*nīlanibhāsāni*). Just as a flax-flower (*umāpupphaṃ*) is blue (*nīlaṃ*), blue in its color (*nīlavaṇṇaṃ*), blue in its features (*nīlanidassanaṃ*), blue in its glow (*nīlanibhāsaṃ*), or just as Vārāṇasī muslin (*vatthaṃ bārāṇaseyyakaṃ*) smooth on both sides (*ubhatobhāgavimaṭṭhaṃ*) is blue (*nīlaṃ*), blue in its color (*nīlavaṇṇaṃ*), blue in its features (*nīlanidassanaṃ*), blue in its glow (*nīlanibhāsaṃ*). In the same way (*evameva*) one percipient of the formless internally (*ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko*) sees forms externally as blue (*nīlāni*), blue in their color (*nīlavaṇṇāni*), blue in their features (*nīlanidassanāni*), blue in their glow (*nīlanibhāsāni*). Mastering them (*tāni abhibhuyya*), he is percipient of ‘I know; I see’ (*jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṃsaññī hoti*). This is the fifth dimension of mastery (*idaṃ pañcamaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ*).

One percipient of the formless internally (*ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko*) sees forms externally as yellow (*pītāni*), yellow in their color (*pītavaṇṇāni*), yellow in their features (*pītanidassanāni*), yellow in their glow (*pītanibhāsāni*). Just as a *kaṇikāra*-flower (*kaṇikārapupphaṃ*) is yellow (*pītaṃ*), yellow in its color (*pītavaṇṇaṃ*), yellow in its features (*pītanidassanaṃ*), yellow in its glow (*pītanibhāsaṃ*), or just as Vārāṇasī muslin (*vatthaṃ bārāṇaseyyakaṃ*) smooth on both sides (*ubhatobhāgavimaṭṭhaṃ*) is yellow (*pītaṃ*), yellow in its color (*pītavaṇṇaṃ*), yellow in its features (*pītanidassanaṃ*), yellow in its glow (*pītanibhāsaṃ*). In the same way (*evameva*) one percipient of the formless internally (*ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko*) sees forms externally as yellow (*pītāni*), yellow in their color (*pītavaṇṇāni*), yellow in their features (*pītanidassanāni*), yellow in their glow (*pītanibhāsāni*). Mastering them (*tāni abhibhuyya*), he is percipient of ‘I know; I see’ (*jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṃsaññī hoti*). This is the sixth dimension of mastery (*idaṃ chaṭṭhaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ*).

One percipient of the formless internally (*ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko*) sees forms externally as red (*lohitakāni*), red in their color (*lohitakavaṇṇāni*), red in their features (*lohitakanidassanāni*), red in their glow (*lohitakanibhāsāni*). Just as a *bandhujīvaka*-flower (*bandhujīvakapupphaṃ*) is red (*lohitakaṃ*), red in its color (*lohitakavaṇṇaṃ*), red in its features (*lohitakanidassanaṃ*), red in its glow (*lohitakanibhāsaṃ*), or just as Vārāṇasī muslin (*vatthaṃ bārāṇaseyyakaṃ*) smooth on both sides (*ubhatobhāgavimaṭṭhaṃ*) is red (*lohitakaṃ*), red in its color (*lohitakavaṇṇaṃ*), red in its features (*lohitakanidassanaṃ*), red in its glow (*lohitakanibhāsaṃ*). In the same way (*evameva*) one percipient of the formless internally (*ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko*) sees forms externally as red (*lohitakāni*), red in their color (*lohitakavaṇṇāni*), red in their features (*lohitakanidassanāni*), red in their glow (*lohitakanibhāsāni*). Mastering them (*tāni abhibhuyya*), he is percipient of ‘I know; I see’ (*jānāmi passāmī’ti evaṃsaññī hoti*). This is the seventh dimension of mastery (*idaṃ sattamaṃ abhibhāyatanaṃ*).

One percipient of the formless internally (*ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī eko*) sees forms externally as white (*odātāni*), white in their color (*odātavaṇṇāni*), white in their features (*odātanidassanāni*), white in their glow (*odātanibhāsāni*). Just as the morning star (*osadhitārakā*) is white (*odātā*), white in its color (*odātavaṇṇā*), white in its features (*odātanidassanā*), white in its glow (*odātanibhāsā*), or just as Vārāṇasī muslin (*vatthaṃ bārāṇaseyyakaṃ*) smooth on both sides (*ubhatobhāgavimaṭṭhaṃ*) is white (*odātaṃ*), white in its color (*odātavaṇṇaṃ*), white in its features (*odātanidassanaṃ*), white in its glow (*odātanibhāsaṃ*).
Just so, not perceiving form internally, one sees external forms that are white, white in color, white in appearance, white in radiance, and mastering them, one is aware that one knows and sees them. This is the eighth sphere of mastery (*abhibhāyatana*).
commentary_pali:
338. Abhibhāyatanavimokkhakathā heṭṭhā kathitā eva.

‘‘Ime kho, āvuso’’tiādi vuttanayeneva yojetabbaṃ. Iti ekādasannaṃ aṭṭhakānaṃ vasena aṭṭhāsīti pañhe kathento thero sāmaggirasaṃ dassesīti.

Aṭṭhakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

Navakavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
338. The discourse on the spheres of mastery and deliverance has already been spoken of earlier.

"These, friend," etc., should be connected in the same way as stated before.

Thus, the elder, while speaking of eighty-eight questions in terms of eleven groups of eight, showed the essence of concord.

The explanation of the groups of eight is finished.

Explanation of the groups of nine.

mula_pali:
339. ‘‘Aṭṭha vimokkhā. Rūpī rūpāni passati. Ayaṃ paṭhamo vimokkho.

‘‘Ajjhattaṃ arūpasaññī bahiddhā rūpāni passati. Ayaṃ dutiyo vimokkho.

‘‘Subhanteva adhimutto hoti. Ayaṃ tatiyo vimokkho.

‘‘Sabbaso rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṃ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṃ amanasikārā ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ayaṃ catuttho vimokkho.

‘‘Sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘anantaṃ viññāṇa’nti viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ayaṃ pañcamo vimokkho.

‘‘Sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ayaṃ chaṭṭho vimokkho.

‘‘Sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ayaṃ sattamo vimokkho.

‘‘Sabbaso nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma saññāvedayita nirodhaṃ upasampajja viharati. Ayaṃ aṭṭhamo vimokkho.

‘‘Ime kho, āvuso, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena aṭṭha dhammā sammadakkhātā; tattha sabbeheva saṅgāyitabbaṃ…pe… atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ.

Navakaṃ
mula_english:
339. Eight liberations (*aṣṭau vimokṣāḥ*): Possessed of form, one sees forms. This is the first liberation.

Not percipient of form internally, one sees forms externally. This is the second liberation.

“One is intent only on the beautiful. This is the third liberation.

“Through the complete surmounting of perceptions of material form, the passing away of perceptions of resistance, and non-attention to perceptions of diversity, ‘Space is infinite,’ one enters and dwells in the base of the infinity of space (*ākāśānantyāyatana*). This is the fourth liberation.

“Having completely surmounted the base of the infinity of space (*ākāśānantyāyatana*), ‘Consciousness is infinite,’ one enters and dwells in the base of the infinity of consciousness (*vijñānānantyāyatana*). This is the fifth liberation.

“Having completely surmounted the base of the infinity of consciousness (*vijñāṇānantyāyatana*), ‘There is nothing,’ one enters and dwells in the base of nothingness (*ākiñcaññāyatana*). This is the sixth liberation.

“Having completely surmounted the base of nothingness (*ākiñcaññāyatana*), one enters and dwells in the base of neither perception nor non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatana*). This is the seventh liberation.

“With the complete transcending of the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatana*), one enters and remains in the cessation of perception and feeling (*saññāvedayita nirodha*). This is the eighth liberation.

“These, friends, are the eight qualities (*aṭṭha dhammā*) that are rightly expounded by the Blessed One—the one who knows, the one who sees, the Worthy One, rightly self-awakened. Those should all be recited together… for the benefit & happiness of devas & human beings.

The Ninth

mula_pali:
340. ‘‘Atthi kho, āvuso, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena nava dhammā sammadakkhātā; tattha sabbeheva saṅgāyitabbaṃ…pe… atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ. Katame nava?

‘‘Nava āghātavatthūni. ‘Anatthaṃ me acarī’ti āghātaṃ bandhati; ‘anatthaṃ me caratī’ti āghātaṃ bandhati; ‘anatthaṃ me carissatī’ti āghātaṃ bandhati; ‘piyassa me manāpassa anatthaṃ acarī’ti āghātaṃ bandhati…pe… anatthaṃ caratīti āghātaṃ bandhati…pe… anatthaṃ carissatīti āghātaṃ bandhati; ‘appiyassa me amanāpassa atthaṃ acarī’ti āghātaṃ bandhati…pe… atthaṃ caratīti āghātaṃ bandhati…pe… atthaṃ carissatīti āghātaṃ bandhati.

āghātavatthūni.

‘‘Nava āghātapaṭivinayā. ‘Anatthaṃ me acari acarīti (syā. ka.) evaṃ ‘‘carati carissati’’ padesupi, taṃ kutettha labbhā’ti āghātaṃ paṭivineti ; ‘anatthaṃ me carati, taṃ kutettha labbhā’ti āghātaṃ paṭivineti; ‘anatthaṃ me carissati, taṃ kutettha labbhā’ti āghātaṃ paṭivineti; ‘piyassa me manāpassa anatthaṃ acari…pe… anatthaṃ carati…pe… anatthaṃ carissati, taṃ kutettha labbhā’ti āghātaṃ paṭivineti; ‘appiyassa me amanāpassa atthaṃ acari…pe… atthaṃ carati…pe… atthaṃ carissati, taṃ kutettha labbhā’ti āghātaṃ paṭivineti.

āghātapaṭivinayā. acarīti (syā. ka.) evaṃ ‘‘carati carissati’’ padesupi
mula_english:
340. “There are, friends, nine *dhamma*s that are rightly expounded by the Blessed One—the one who knows, the one who sees, the Worthy One, rightly self-awakened (*sammāsambuddha*); those should all be recited together...for the benefit, welfare and happiness of *deva*s and human beings (*devamanussānaṃ*). What are the nine?

“Nine grounds for resentment (*āghātavatthūni*). ‘He has done me harm,’ one binds hatred (*āghātaṃ bandhati*); ‘He is doing me harm,’ one binds hatred; ‘He is going to do me harm,’ one binds hatred; ‘He has done harm to people who are dear & pleasing to me,’ one binds hatred…‘He is doing harm,’ one binds hatred…‘He is going to do harm,’ one binds hatred; ‘He has aided people who are not dear or pleasing to me,’ one binds hatred…‘He is aiding,’ one binds hatred…‘He is going to aid,’ one binds hatred.

Grounds for resentment (*āghātavatthūni*).

“Nine ways of subduing hatred (*āghātapaṭivinayā*). ‘He has done me harm, but what should I expect?’ one subdues hatred; ‘He is doing me harm, but what should I expect?’ one subdues hatred; ‘He is going to do me harm, but what should I expect?’ one subdues hatred; ‘He has done harm to people who are dear & pleasing to me…He is doing harm…He is going to do harm, but what should I expect?’ one subdues hatred; ‘He has aided people who are not dear or pleasing to me…He is aiding…He is going to aid, but what should I expect?’ one subdues hatred.

Ways of subduing hatred (*āghātapaṭivinayā*).
commentary_pali:
340. Iti aṭṭhakavasena sāmaggirasaṃ dassetvā idāni navakavasena dassetuṃ puna desanaṃ ārabhi. Tattha āghātavatthūnīti āghātakāraṇāni. Āghātaṃ bandhatīti kopaṃ bandhati karoti uppādeti.

Taṃ kutettha labbhāti taṃ anatthacaraṇaṃ mā ahosīti etasmiṃ puggale kuto labbhā, kena kāraṇena sakkā laddhuṃ ? Paro nāma parassa attano cittaruciyā anatthaṃ karotīti evaṃ cintetvā āghātaṃ paṭivinodeti. Atha vā sacāhaṃ paṭikopaṃ kareyyaṃ, taṃ kopakaraṇaṃ ettha puggale kuto labbhā, kena kāraṇena laddhabbanti attho. Kuto lābhātipi pāṭho, sacāhaṃ ettha kopaṃ kareyyaṃ, tasmiṃ me kopakaraṇe kuto lābhā, lābhā nāma ke siyunti attho. Imasmiñca atthe tanti nipātamattameva hoti.

Taṃ kutettha labbhā ta
commentary_english:
340. Thus, having shown the entirety with the eightfold division, now, to show [it] with the ninefold division, again he began the teaching. There, āghātavatthūnī means causes of striking. āghātaṃ bandhatī means he binds anger, he does, he produces.

taṃ kutettha labbhā means may that non-benefit conduct not be; where is it obtained in this person, by what means is it possible to obtain? 1046"/>? "Another, named, by the mind-desire of another's self, does non-benefit" — having thought thus, he wards off striking. Or, if I should do counter-anger, where is that anger-instrument obtained in this person, by what means is it obtained?, is the meaning. "Where is gain?" is also a reading; if I should do anger here, where is gain for me in that anger-instrument, what are gains called?, is the meaning. And in this meaning, ta is merely an indeclinable.

taṃ kutettha labbhā 1046"/>

mula_pali:
341. ‘‘Nava sattāvāsā. Santāvuso, sattā nānattakāyā nānattasaññino, seyyathāpi manussā ekacce ca devā ekacce ca vinipātikā. Ayaṃ paṭhamo sattāvāso.

‘‘Santāvuso, sattā nānattakāyā ekattasaññino, seyyathāpi devā brahmakāyikā paṭhamābhinibbattā. Ayaṃ dutiyo sattāvāso.

‘‘Santāvuso, sattā ekattakāyā nānattasaññino, seyyathāpi devā ābhassarā. Ayaṃ tatiyo sattāvāso.

‘‘Santāvuso , sattā ekattakāyā ekattasaññino, seyyathāpi devā subhakiṇhā. Ayaṃ catuttho sattāvāso.

‘‘Santāvuso, sattā asaññino appaṭisaṃvedino, seyyathāpi devā asaññasattā asaññisattā (syā. kaṃ.). Ayaṃ pañcamo sattāvāso.

asaññisattā (syā. kaṃ.)

‘‘Santāvuso, sattā sabbaso rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā paṭighasaññānaṃ atthaṅgamā nānattasaññānaṃ amanasikārā ‘ananto ākāso’ti ākāsānañcāyatanūpagā. Ayaṃ chaṭṭho sattāvāso.

‘‘Santāvuso, sattā sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘anantaṃ viññāṇa’nti viññāṇañcāyatanūpagā. Ayaṃ sattamo sattāvāso.

‘‘Santāvuso, sattā sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcāññāyatanūpagā. Ayaṃ aṭṭhamo sattāvāso.

‘‘Santāvuso , sattā sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma samatikkamma santametaṃ paṇītametanti (syā. kaṃ.) nevasaññānāsaññāyatanūpagā. Ayaṃ navamo sattāvāso.

samatikkamma santametaṃ paṇītametanti (syā. kaṃ.)
mula_english:
"Friends, there are nine abodes of beings."

"Friends, there are beings with diversity of body and diversity of perception, such as human beings, some gods, and some beings in the lower realms. This is the first abode for beings."

"Friends, there are beings with diversity of body and unity of perception, such as the gods of Brahmā’s retinue generated by the first. This is the second abode for beings."

"Friends, there are beings with unity of body and diversity of perception, such as the Radiant Gods. This is the third abode for beings."

"Friends, there are beings with unity of body and unity of perception, such as the Beautifully Lustrous Gods. This is the fourth abode for beings."

"Friends, there are beings without perception, experiencing no feeling, namely, the Gods who are Non-percipient Creatures. This is the fifth abode for beings."

"Friends, there are beings who, by completely surmounting all perceptions of form, with the disappearance of perceptions of resistance, and by not attending to perceptions of diversity, [thinking,] ‘Space is endless,’ reach the base of the infinity of space. This is the sixth abode for beings."

"Friends, there are beings who, by completely surmounting the base of the infinity of space, [thinking,] ‘Consciousness is endless,’ reach the base of the infinity of consciousness. This is the seventh abode for beings."

"Friends, there are beings who, by completely surmounting the base of the infinity of consciousness, [thinking,] ‘There is nothing,’ reach the base of nothingness. This is the eighth abode for beings."

"Friends, there are beings who, by completely surmounting the base of nothingness, reach the base of neither perception nor non-perception. This is the ninth abode for beings."
commentary_pali: 341.Sattāvāsāti sattānaṃ āvāsā, vasanaṭṭhānānīti attho. Tattha suddhāvāsāpi sattāvāsova, asabbakālikattā pana na gahitā. Suddhāvāsā hi buddhānaṃ khandhāvārasadisā. Asaṅkhyeyyakappe buddhesu anibbattantesu taṃ ṭhānaṃ suññaṃ hotīti asabbakālikattā na gahitā. Sesamettha yaṃ vattabbaṃ, taṃ heṭṭhā vuttameva.
commentary_english:
" *Sattāvāsā* means the abodes ( *āvāsā*) of beings (*sattānaṃ*), that is, places of dwelling ( *vasanaṭṭhānāni*).

Here, the Pure Abodes (*suddhāvāsā*) are also abodes of beings (*sattāvāsova*), but they are not included because they are not always [inhabited].

The Pure Abodes are similar to the camps of Buddhas.

For countless aeons ( *asaṅkhyeyyakappe*) when Buddhas have not arisen ( *anibbattantesu*), that place is empty (*suññaṃ hoti*); therefore, they are not included because they are not always [inhabited].

Whatever else needs to be said about this has already been said below."

mula_pali:
342. ‘‘Nava akkhaṇā asamayā brahmacariyavāsāya. Idhāvuso , tathāgato ca loke uppanno hoti arahaṃ sammāsambuddho, dhammo ca desiyati opasamiko parinibbāniko sambodhagāmī sugatappavedito. Ayañca puggalo nirayaṃ upapanno hoti. Ayaṃ paṭhamo akkhaṇo asamayo brahmacariyavāsāya.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, tathāgato ca loke uppanno hoti arahaṃ sammāsambuddho, dhammo ca desiyati opasamiko parinibbāniko sambodhagāmī sugatappavedito. Ayañca puggalo tiracchānayoniṃ upapanno hoti. Ayaṃ dutiyo akkhaṇo asamayo brahmacariyavāsāya.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ…pe… pettivisayaṃ upapanno hoti. Ayaṃ tatiyo akkhaṇo asamayo brahmacariyavāsāya.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ…pe… asurakāyaṃ upapanno hoti. Ayaṃ catuttho akkhaṇo asamayo brahmacariyavāsāya.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ…pe… aññataraṃ dīghāyukaṃ devanikāyaṃ upapanno hoti. Ayaṃ pañcamo akkhaṇo asamayo brahmacariyavāsāya.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ…pe… paccantimesu janapadesu paccājāto hoti milakkhesu milakkhakesu (syā. kaṃ.) milakkhūsu (ka.) aviññātāresu, yattha natthi gati bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ upāsakānaṃ upāsikānaṃ. Ayaṃ chaṭṭho akkhaṇo asamayo brahmacariyavāsāya.

milakkhakesu (syā. kaṃ.) milakkhūsu (ka.)

‘‘Puna caparaṃ…pe… majjhimesu janapadesu paccājāto hoti. So ca hoti micchādiṭṭhiko viparītadassano – ‘natthi dinnaṃ, natthi yiṭṭhaṃ, natthi hutaṃ, natthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ sukaṭa dukkaṭānaṃ (sī. pī.) kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko, natthi ayaṃ loko, natthi paro loko, natthi mātā, natthi pitā, natthi sattā opapātikā, natthi loke samaṇabrāhmaṇā sammaggatā sammāpaṭipannā ye imañca lokaṃ parañca lokaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentī’ti. Ayaṃ sattamo akkhaṇo asamayo brahmacariyavāsāya.

sukaṭa dukkaṭānaṃ (sī. pī.)

‘‘Puna caparaṃ…pe… majjhimesu janapadesu paccājāto hoti. So ca hoti duppañño jaḷo eḷamūgo, nappaṭibalo subhāsitadubbhāsitānamatthamaññātuṃ. Ayaṃ aṭṭhamo akkhaṇo asamayo brahmacariyavāsāya.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, tathāgato ca loke na katthaci nakāro na dissati uppanno hoti arahaṃ sammāsambuddho, dhammo ca na desiyati opasamiko parinibbāniko sambodhagāmī sugatappavedito. Ayañca puggalo majjhimesu janapadesu paccājāto hoti, so ca hoti paññavā ajaḷo aneḷamūgo, paṭibalo subhāsita-dubbhāsitānamatthamaññātuṃ. Ayaṃ navamo akkhaṇo asamayo brahmacariyavāsāya.

katthaci nakāro na dissati
mula_english:
342. Nine inopportune, untimely situations for leading the holy life.

Friends, there is the case where a *Tathāgata* appears in the world, worthy & rightly self-awakened ( *arahaṃ sammāsambuddho*). The *Dharma* is taught that leads to stilling, to total unbinding, to self-awakening as declared by One Well-gone (*sugatappavedito*). But this person is reborn in hell. This is the first inopportune, untimely situation for leading the holy life.

“And further, friends, there is the case where a *Tathāgata* appears in the world, worthy & rightly self-awakened. The *Dharma* is taught that leads to stilling, to total unbinding, to self-awakening as declared by One Well-gone. but this person is reborn in an animal womb… This is the second inopportune, untimely situation for leading the holy life.

“And further, …he is reborn in the realm of the hungry ghosts… This is the third inopportune, untimely situation for leading the holy life.

“And further, … in the host of the *asuras*… This is the fourth inopportune, untimely situation for leading the holy life.

“And further, … in a certain host of long-lived *devas*… This is the fifth inopportune, untimely situation for leading the holy life.

“And further, … he is born in a border region among ignorant barbarians where there is no opening for monks, nuns, male lay followers, or female lay followers to go.… This is the sixth inopportune, untimely situation for leading the holy life.

“And further, … Or he is born in the Middle Country (*majjhimesu janapadesu paccājāto hoti*). but he has wrong views & skewed vision: ‘There is nothing given (*natthi dinnaṃ*), nothing offered, nothing sacrificed (*natthi hutaṃ*). There is no fruit or result of good or bad actions. There is no this world, no next world, no mother, no father; there are no spontaneously reborn beings; there are no contemplatives or *brāhmaṇas* who, faring rightly & practicing rightly, proclaim this world & the next after having directly known & realized it for themselves.’ This is the seventh inopportune, untimely situation for leading the holy life.

“And further, … Or he is born in the Middle Country (*majjhimesu janapadesu paccājāto hoti*). but he is undiscerning, dull, drooling, incapable of knowing the meaning of what is well-said or ill-said.
This is the eighth inopportune, untimely situation for leading the holy life.

“And further, friend, a *Tathāgata* does not arise in the world, a worthy (*arhat*) and rightly self-awakened one (*sammāsambuddha*), and the *dharma* is not taught, which leads to stilling (*opaśamika*), to complete liberation (*parinirvāṇika*), to awakening (*sambodhi-gāmī*), proclaimed by the Well-Gone (*sugata*).

This person is reborn in the Middle Country and is discerning (*paññavā*), not dull (*ajaḷa*), not drooling and mute (*aneḷamūga*), capable of understanding the meaning of what is well-spoken (*subhāṣita*) and poorly-spoken (*dubbhāṣita*).

This is the ninth inopportune, untimely situation for leading the holy life.
commentary_pali: 342. Akkhaṇesu dhammo ca desiyatīti catusaccadhammo desiyati. Opasamikoti kilesūpasamakaro. Parinibbānikoti kilesaparinibbānena parinibbānāvaho. Sambodhagāmīti catumaggañāṇapaṭivedhagāmī. Aññataranti asaññabhavaṃ vā arūpabhavaṃ vā.
commentary_english:
342. "And the *dharma* is taught at the right times" means the *dharma* of the four noble truths is taught.

"*Opasamiko*" means the one who pacifies the defilements (*kleśa*).

"*Parinibbāniko*" means bringing about *parinirvāṇa* through the *parinirvāṇa* of the defilements.

"*Sambodhagāmī*" means leading to the realization of the knowledge of the four paths (*catumaggañāṇa*).

"*Aññatara*" means either the realm of non-perception (*asaññabhava*) or the formless realm (*arūpabhava*).

mula_pali: 343. ‘‘Nava anupubbavihārā. Idhāvuso, bhikkhu vivicceva kāmehi vivicca akusalehi dhammehi savitakkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ pītisukhaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Vitakkavicārānaṃ vūpasamā…pe… dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Pītiyā ca virāgā…pe… tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Sukhassa ca pahānā …pe… catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Sabbaso rūpasaññānaṃ samatikkamā…pe… ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. Sabbaso ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘anantaṃ viññāṇa’nti viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. Sabbaso viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samatikkamma ‘natthi kiñcī’ti ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. Sabbaso ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ upasampajja viharati. Sabbaso nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samatikkamma saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ upasampajja viharati.
mula_english: 343. “Nine step-by-step dwellings: Here, a *bhikṣu*, quite secluded from sense pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, enters and dwells in the first *jhāna*, which is accompanied by thought and examination, born of seclusion, filled with joy and happiness. With the stilling of thought and examination, he enters and dwells in the second *jhāna*. With the fading away of joy, he enters and dwells in the third *jhāna*. With the abandoning of pleasure, he enters and dwells in the fourth *jhāna*. With the complete transcending of perceptions of form, he enters and dwells in the dimension of the infinitude of space (*ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ*). With the complete transcending of the dimension of the infinitude of space, aware that ‘consciousness is infinite,’ he enters and dwells in the dimension of the infinitude of consciousness (*viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ*). With the complete transcending of the dimension of the infinitude of consciousness, aware that ‘there is nothing,’ he enters and dwells in the dimension of nothingness (*ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ*). With the complete transcending of the dimension of nothingness, he enters and dwells in the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ*). With the complete transcending of the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception, he enters and dwells in the cessation of perception and feeling (*saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ*).
commentary_pali: 343.Anupubbavihārāti anupaṭipāṭiyā samāpajjitabbavihārā.
commentary_english: 343. *Anupubbavihārā* means *vihārā* to be attained in due order.

mula_pali:
344. ‘‘Nava anupubbanirodhā. Paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa kāmasaññā niruddhā hoti. Dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa vitakkavicārā niruddhā honti. Tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa pīti niruddhā hoti. Catutthaṃ jhānaṃ samāpannassa assāsapassāssā niruddhā honti. Ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samāpannassa rūpasaññā niruddhā hoti. Viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samāpannassa ākāsānañcāyatanasaññā niruddhā hoti. Ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samāpannassa viññāṇañcāyatanasaññā niruddhā hoti. Nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samāpannassa ākiñcaññāyatanasaññā niruddhā hoti. Saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpannassa saññā ca vedanā ca niruddhā honti.

‘‘Ime kho, āvuso, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena nava dhammā sammadakkhātā. Tattha sabbeheva saṅgāyitabbaṃ…pe… atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ.

Dasakaṃ
mula_english:
344. "Nine step-by-step cessations:
When one has attained the first *jhāna* (first dhyāna), the perception of sensuality has ceased.
When one has attained the second *jhāna* (second dhyāna), directed thoughts & evaluations have ceased.
When one has attained the third *jhāna* (third dhyāna), rapture has ceased.
When one has attained the fourth *jhāna* (fourth dhyāna), in-&-out breaths have ceased.
When one has attained the dimension of the infinitude of space (*ākāsānañcāyatana*), the perception of forms has ceased.
When one has attained the dimension of the infinitude of consciousness (*viññāṇañcāyatana*), the perception of the dimension of the infinitude of space has ceased.
When one has attained the dimension of nothingness (*ākiñcaññāyatana*), the perception of the dimension of the infinitude of consciousness has ceased.
When one has attained the dimension of neither perception nor non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatana*), the perception of the dimension of nothingness has ceased.
When one has attained the cessation of perception & feeling (*saññāvedayitanirodha*), perceptions & feelings have ceased.

"These, friends, are the nine *dharmas* (nine things) that are rightly expounded by the Blessed One—the one who knows, the one who sees, the Worthy One, rightly self-awakened (*sammāsambuddha*).
There all should sing together… for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.

The tenth.
commentary_pali:
344.Anupubbanirodhāti anupaṭipāṭiyā nirodhā.

‘‘Ime, kho āvuso’’tiādi vuttanayeneva yojetabbaṃ. Iti channaṃ navakānaṃ vasena catupaṇṇāsa pañhe kathento thero sāmaggirasaṃ dassesīti.

Navakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

Dasakavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
344. *Anupubbanirodhā* means cessation in due order.

“These, friend,” etc., should be connected in the manner previously stated. Thus, while explaining forty-four questions based on six groups of nine, the elder showed the taste of concord.

The Commentary on the Nines is finished.

Commentary on the Tens

mula_pali:
345. ‘‘Atthi kho, āvuso, tena bhagavatā jānatā passatā arahatā sammāsambuddhena dasa dhammā sammadakkhātā. Tattha sabbeheva saṅgāyitabbaṃ…pe… atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṃ. Katame dasa?

‘‘Dasa nāthakaraṇā dhammā. Idhāvuso, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti. Pātimokkhasaṃvarasaṃvuto viharati ācāragocarasampanno, aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu. Yaṃpāvuso, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti, pātimokkhasaṃvarasaṃvuto viharati, ācāragocarasampanno, aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu. Ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo.

nāthakaraṇā dhammā.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu bahussuto hoti sutadharo sutasannicayo. Ye te dhammā ādikalyāṇā majjhekalyāṇā pariyosānakalyāṇā sātthā sabyañjanā sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ (sī. syā. pī.) kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ abhivadanti, tathārūpāssa dhammā bahussutā honti dhatā (ka. sī. syā. kaṃ.) dhātā vacasā paricitā manasānupekkhitā diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā, yaṃpāvuso, bhikkhu bahussuto hoti…pe… diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā. Ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo.

sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ (sī. syā. pī.) dhatā (ka. sī. syā. kaṃ.)

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu kalyāṇamitto hoti kalyāṇasahāyo kalyāṇasampavaṅko. Yaṃpāvuso, bhikkhu kalyāṇamitto hoti kalyāṇasahāyo kalyāṇasampavaṅko. Ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu suvaco hoti sovacassakaraṇehi dhammehi samannāgato khamo padakkhiṇaggāhī anusāsaniṃ. Yaṃpāvuso, bhikkhu suvaco hoti…pe… padakkhiṇaggāhī anusāsaniṃ. Ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu yāni tāni sabrahmacārīnaṃ uccāvacāni kiṃkaraṇīyāni, tattha dakkho hoti analaso tatrupāyāya vīmaṃsāya samannāgato, alaṃ kātuṃ alaṃ saṃvidhātuṃ. Yaṃpāvuso, bhikkhu yāni tāni sabrahmacārīnaṃ…pe… alaṃ saṃvidhātuṃ. Ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu dhammakāmo hoti piyasamudāhāro, abhidhamme abhivinaye uḷārapāmojjo uḷārapāmujjo (sī. pī.), oḷārapāmojjo (syā. kaṃ.). Yaṃpāvuso, bhikkhu dhammakāmo hoti…pe… uḷārapāmojjo uḷārapāmujjo (sī. pī.), oḷārapāmojjo (syā. kaṃ.). Ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo.

uḷārapāmujjo (sī. pī.), oḷārapāmojjo (syā. kaṃ.) uḷārapāmujjo (sī. pī.), oḷārapāmojjo (syā. kaṃ.)

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso , bhikkhu santuṭṭho hoti itarītarehi cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānappaccayabhesajjaparikkhārehi . Yaṃpāvuso, bhikkhu santuṭṭho hoti…pe… parikkhārehi. Ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu āraddhavīriyo viharati akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ upasampadāya, thāmavā daḷhaparakkamo anikkhittadhuro kusalesu dhammesu. Yaṃpāvuso, bhikkhu āraddhavīriyo viharati…pe… anikkhittadhuro kusalesu dhammesu. Ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu satimā hoti paramena satinepakkena samannāgato cirakatampi cirabhāsitampi saritā anussaritā. Yaṃpāvuso, bhikkhu satimā hoti…pe… saritā anussaritā. Ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo.

‘‘Puna caparaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu paññavā hoti, udayatthagāminiyā paññāya samannāgato ariyāya nibbedhikāya sammādukkhakkhayagāminiyā. Yaṃpāvuso, bhikkhu paññavā hoti…pe… sammādukkhakkhayagāminiyā. Ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo.
mula_english:
345. “There are, friends, ten *dharmas* that are rightly expounded by the Blessed One—the one who knows, the one who sees, the Worthy One, rightly self-awakened.

There, all should be chanted together… for the benefit, for the happiness of gods and humans.
What are the ten?

“Ten qualities creating a protector (*nāthakaraṇā dhammā*).
Here, friends, a monk (*bhikkhu*) is virtuous (*sīlavā* *hoti*).
He dwells restrained in accordance with the Pāṭimokkha (*pātimokkhasaṃvarasaṃvuto*), consummate in his behavior & sphere of activity (*ācāragocarasampanno*). He trains himself, having undertaken the training rules, seeing danger in the slightest faults (*aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu*).
And the fact that he is virtuous, friends, a monk is virtuous, he dwells restrained in accordance with the Pāṭimokkha, consummate in his behavior & sphere of activity. He trains himself, having undertaken the training rules, seeing danger in the slightest faults.
This quality also creates a protector (*ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo*).

Qualities creating a protector (*nāthakaraṇā dhammā*).

“And further, friends, a monk has heard much (*bahussuto hoti*), has retained what he has heard (*sutadharo*), has stored what he has heard (*sutasannicayo*).
Those *dharmas* that are admirable in the beginning (*ādikalyāṇā*), admirable in the middle (*majjhekalyāṇā*), admirable in the end (*pariyosānakalyāṇā*), that—in their meaning (*sātthā*) and expression (*sabyañjanā*)—proclaim the holy life (*brahmacariyaṃ*) that is entirely perfect (*kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ*), surpassingly pure (*parisuddhaṃ abhivadanti*): those teachings he has listened to often, retained, discussed, accumulated, examined with his mind, & well-penetrated in terms of his views (*dhammā bahussutā honti dhātā vacasā paricitā manasānupekkhitā diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā*). And the fact that he has heard much, friends, a monk has heard much…well-penetrated in terms of his views.
This quality also creates a protector (*ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo*).

“And further, friends, a monk has admirable friends (*kalyāṇamitto*), admirable comrades (*kalyāṇasahāyo*), admirable companions (*kalyāṇasampavaṅko*).
And the fact that he has admirable friends, friends, a monk has admirable friends, admirable comrades, admirable companions.
This quality also creates a protector (*ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo*).

“And further, friends, a monk is easy to speak to (*suvaco hoti*), endowed with qualities that make him easy to speak to (*sovacassakaraṇehi dhammehi samannāgato*), patient (*khamo*), respectful to instruction (*padakkhiṇaggāhī anusāsaniṃ*).
And the fact that he is easy to speak to, friends, a monk is easy to speak to…respectful to instruction.
This quality also creates a protector (*ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo*).
“And furthermore, the monk, friend, is skilled in the various tasks that are to be done for his fellow monks in the holy life. He is energetic, endowed with the wisdom to use the appropriate means in those tasks, capable of doing them and arranging them. And the fact that the monk is skilled in those various tasks for his fellows in the holy life…capable of arranging them, this is a quality creating a protector (nāthakaraṇo dhammo).

“And furthermore, the monk, friend, is one who desires the Dhamma, speaks in an endearing way, and takes great joy in the Abhidhamma and Abhivinaya. And the fact that the monk is one who desires the Dhamma…takes great joy, this is a quality creating a protector.

“And furthermore, the monk, friend, is content with any kind of robe cloth, alms food, lodging, and medicinal requisites for curing sickness. And the fact that the monk is content…requisites, this is a quality creating a protector.

“And furthermore, the monk, friend, dwells with aroused energy for the abandoning of unwholesome qualities and the undertaking of wholesome qualities; strong, firm in his effort, not laying down the burden in regard to wholesome qualities. And the fact that the monk dwells with aroused energy…not laying down the burden, this is a quality creating a protector.

“And furthermore, the monk, friend, is mindful (satimā), endowed with supreme skill in mindfulness, remembering and recollecting what was done and said long ago. And the fact that the monk is mindful…recollecting, this is a quality creating a protector.

“And furthermore, the monk, friend, is wise (paññavā), endowed with wisdom (paññā) that leads to the arising and passing away of phenomena, noble, penetrative, leading to the complete destruction of suffering (sammādukkhakkhayagāminiyā). And the fact that the monk is wise…leading to the complete destruction of suffering, this is a quality creating a protector.
[p.]
commentary_pali:
345. Iti navakavasena sāmaggirasaṃ dassetvā idāni dasakavasena dassetuṃ puna desanaṃ ārabhi. Tattha nāthakaraṇāti ‘‘sanāthā, bhikkhave, viharatha mā anāthā, dasa ime, bhikkhave, dhammā nāthakaraṇā’’ti (a. ni. 10.18) evaṃ akkhātā attano patiṭṭhākarā dhammā.

Kalyāṇamittotiādīsu sīlādiguṇasampannā kalyāṇā assa mittāti kalyāṇamitto. Te cassa ṭhānanisajjādīsu saha ayanato sahāyāti kalyāṇasahāyo. Cittena ceva kāyena ca kalyāṇamittesu eva sampavaṅko onatoti kalyāṇasampavaṅko. Suvacohotīti sukhena vattabbo hoti sukhena anusāsitabbo. Khamoti gāḷhena pharusena kakkhaḷena vuccamāno khamati, na kuppati. Padakkhiṇaggāhī anusāsaninti yathā ekacco ovadiyamāno vāmato gaṇhāti, paṭippharati vā asuṇanto vā gacchati, evaṃ akatvā ‘‘ovadatha, bhante , anusāsatha, tumhesu anovadantesu ko añño ovadissatī’’ti padakkhiṇaṃ gaṇhāti.

Kalyāṇamitto kalyāṇamitto. kalyāṇasahāyo. kalyāṇasampavaṅko. Suvaco hotī Khamo Padakkhiṇaggāhī anusāsani

Uccāvacānīti uccāni ca avacāni ca. Kiṃ karaṇīyānīti kiṃ karomīti evaṃ vatvā kattabbakammāni. Tattha uccakammāni nāma cīvarassa karaṇaṃ rajanaṃ cetiye sudhākammaṃ uposathāgāracetiyagharabodhiyagharesu kattabbanti evamādi. Avacakammaṃ nāma pādadhovanamakkhanādikhuddakakammaṃ. Tatrupāyāyāti tatrupagamanīyā. Alaṃ kātunti kātuṃ samattho hoti. Alaṃ saṃvidhātunti vicāretuṃ samattho.

Uccāvacānī Kiṃ karaṇīyānī uccakammāni Avacakammaṃ Tatrupāyāyā Alaṃ kātu Alaṃ saṃvidhātu

Dhamme assa kāmo sinehoti dhammakāmo, tepiṭakaṃ buddhavacanaṃ piyāyatīti attho. Piyasamudāhāroti parasmiṃ kathente sakkaccaṃ suṇāti, sayañca paresaṃ desetukāmo hotīti attho. ‘‘Abhidhamme abhivinaye’’ti ettha dhammo abhidhammo, vinayo abhivinayoti catukkaṃ veditabbaṃ. Tattha dhammoti suttantapiṭakaṃ. Abhidhammoti satta pakaraṇāni. Vinayoti ubhatovibhaṅgā. Abhivinayoti khandhakaparivārā. Atha vā suttantapiṭakampi abhidhammapiṭakampi dhammo eva. Maggaphalāni abhidhammo. Sakalaṃ vinayapiṭakaṃ vinayo. Kilesavūpasamakāraṇaṃ abhivinayo. Iti sabbasmimpi ettha dhamme abhidhamme vinaye abhivinaye ca. Uḷārapāmojjoti bahulapāmojjo hotīti attho.

Kusalesudhammesūti kāraṇatthe bhummaṃ, catubhūmakakusaladhammakāraṇā, tesaṃ adhigamatthāya anikkhittadhuro hotīti attho.

Kusalesu dhammesū
commentary_english:
345. Thus, having shown the taste of harmony by means of the group of nine, now, in order to show [it] by means of the group of ten, again he began the teaching.

There, *nāthakaraṇā* means, "Monks, live with support, not without support. These ten things, monks, are supportive" (A. Ni. 10.18). Thus, the qualities that are declared as making one's own support.

*Kalyāṇamitto* etc., [means] "He has good qualities such as moral conduct, etc., he is a good friend," [therefore] *kalyāṇamitto*. And for him, in places such as sitting and lying down, he is a companion in going together, [therefore] *kalyāṇasahāyo*. With mind and body, he is inclined to good friends, so he is *kalyāṇasampavaṅko*. *Suvaco* means he is easy to speak to and easy to instruct. *Khamo* means when being spoken to harshly, coarsely, and severely, he is patient, he does not get angry. *Padakkhiṇaggāhī anusāsani* means, just as some, when being advised, grasp it from the left, or refute it, or go away without listening, not doing thus, [but thinking,] "Advise me, venerable sir, instruct me; when you do not advise, who else will advise?" he grasps it from the right.

*Kalyāṇamitto* *Kalyāṇamitto*. *Kalyāṇasahāyo*. *Kalyāṇasampavaṅko*. *Suvaco*. *Khamo*. *Padakkhiṇaggāhī anusāsani*.

*Uccāvacānī* means high and low. *Kiṃ karaṇīyānī* means saying "What should I do?" [and doing] the tasks to be done. There, *uccakammāni* are namely, making a robe, dyeing, doing plaster work on a *cetiya*, and doing work in the *uposatha* hall, *cetiya* house, and *bodhi* tree house, and so forth. *Avacakammaṃ* is namely, washing the feet, anointing, and other small tasks. *Tatrupāyāyā* means those who should be approached there. *Alaṃ kātu* means he is capable of doing. *Alaṃ saṃvidhātu* means he is capable of considering.

*Uccāvacānī* *Kiṃ karaṇīyānī* *Uccakammāni* *Avacakammaṃ* *Tatrupāyāyā* *Alaṃ kātu* *Alaṃ saṃvidhātu* He has desire and affection for the Dharma, therefore [he is a] *dharmakāmo*, meaning he loves the *Tripiṭaka*, the word of the Buddha. *Piyasamudāhāro* means when another is speaking, he listens respectfully, and he himself wants to teach others, this is the meaning. "In *abhidhamma* and *abhivinaya*," here, *dharma* is *abhidhamma*, and *vinaya* is *abhivinaya*, this tetrad should be understood. There, *dharma* is the *sūtrānta-piṭaka*. *Abhidhamma* is the seven treatises. *Vinaya* is the *ubhatovibhaṅga*. *Abhivinaya* is the *khandhaka-parivāra*. Or else, the *sūtrānta-piṭaka* and the *abhidhamma-piṭaka* are also simply the *dharma*. The paths and fruits [are] *abhidhamma*. The entire *vinaya-piṭaka* is *vinaya*. The cause of pacifying defilements is *abhivinaya*. Thus, in all of this, here, in *dharma*, *abhidhamma*, *vinaya*, and *abhivinaya*. *Uḷārapāmojjo* means he has abundant joy, this is the meaning.
He is a lover of the Dharma (*dhammakāmo*), one whose speech is affectionate (*piyasamudāhāro*), [skilled in] the Dharma (*dhammo*), the Abhidhamma (*abhidhammo*), the Vinaya (*vinayo*), the Abhivinaya (*abhivinayo*), the Dharma (*dhammo*), the Abhidhamma (*abhidhammo*), the Vinaya (*vinayo*), the Abhivinaya (*abhivinayo*), one who has lofty joy (*uḷārapāmojjo*).

"In wholesome qualities (*kusalesu dhammesū*)": a pleonasm in the sense of cause, because of the wholesome qualities of the four planes, meaning he does not lay aside the burden for the sake of attaining them.

In wholesome qualities (*kusalesu dhammesū*).

mula_pali: 346. Dasa kasiṇāyatanāni. Pathavīkasiṇameko sañjānāti, uddhaṃ adho tiriyaṃ advayaṃ appamāṇaṃ. Āpokasiṇameko sañjānāti…pe… tejokasiṇameko sañjānāti… vāyokasiṇameko sañjānāti… nīlakasiṇameko sañjānāti… pītakasiṇameko sañjānāti… lohitakasiṇameko sañjānāti… odātakasiṇameko sañjānāti… ākāsakasiṇameko sañjānāti… viññāṇakasiṇameko sañjānāti, uddhaṃ adho tiriyaṃ advayaṃ appamāṇaṃ.
mula_english:
346. The ten *kasiṇa* spheres of perception (*kasiṇāyatanāni*).

One perceives the earth *kasiṇa* (*pathavīkasiṇa*), above, below, and across, undivided and immeasurable.
One perceives the water *kasiṇa* (*āpokasiṇa*) ... the fire *kasiṇa* (*tejokasiṇa*) ... the wind *kasiṇa* (*vāyokasiṇa*) ... the blue *kasiṇa* (*nīlakasiṇa*) ... the yellow *kasiṇa* (*pītakasiṇa*) ... the red *kasiṇa* (*lohitakasiṇa*) ... the white *kasiṇa* (*odātakasiṇa*) ... the space *kasiṇa* (*ākāsakasiṇa*) ... the consciousness *kasiṇa* (*viññāṇakasiṇa*), above, below, and across, undivided and immeasurable.
commentary_pali:
346. Kasiṇadasake sakalaṭṭhena kasiṇāni. Tadārammaṇānaṃ dhammānaṃ khettaṭṭhena vā adhiṭṭhānaṭṭhena vā āyatanāni. Uddhanti upari gaganatalābhimukhaṃ. Adhoti heṭṭhā bhūmitalābhimukhaṃ. Tiriyanti khettamaṇḍalamiva samantā paricchinditvā. Ekacco hi uddhameva kasiṇaṃ vaḍḍheti, ekacco adho, ekacco samantato. Tena tena vā kāraṇena evaṃ pasāreti ālokamiva rūpadassanakāmo. Tena vuttaṃ ‘‘pathavīkasiṇameko sañjānāti uddhaṃ adho tiriya’’nti. Advayanti idaṃ pana ekassa aññabhāvānupagamanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Yathā hi udakaṃ paviṭṭhassa sabbadisāsu udakameva hoti, na aññaṃ, evameva pathavīkasiṇaṃ pathavīkasiṇameva hoti , natthi tassa añño kasiṇasambhedoti. Esa nayo sabbattha. Appamāṇanti idaṃ tassa tassa pharaṇaappamāṇavasena vuttaṃ. Tañhi cetasā pharanto sakalameva pharati, na ‘‘ayamassa ādi, idaṃ majjha’’nti pamāṇaṃ gaṇhātīti. Viññāṇakasiṇanti cettha kasiṇugghāṭimākāse pavattaviññāṇaṃ. Tattha kasiṇavasena kasiṇugghāṭimākāse kasiṇugghāṭimākāsavasena tattha pavattaviññāṇe uddhaṃ adho tiriyatā veditabbā. Ayamettha saṅkhepo. Kammaṭṭhānabhāvanānayena panetāni pathavīkasiṇādīni vitthārato visuddhimagge vuttāneva.

Akusalakammapathadasakavaṇṇanā
commentary_english:
346. In the *kasiṇa* decade, the *kasiṇas* are so called in the sense of totality. The sense spheres (*āyatana*) [are so called] in the sense of the field or in the sense of the basis of phenomena with that as their object. "Upward" (*uddhaṃ*) means facing the upper sky. "Downward" (*adho*) means facing the lower ground. "Across" (*tiriyaṃ*) means having delimited all around, like a field circle. For one extends a *kasiṇa* upwards only, another downwards, another all round. Or, for some reason or another, one projects it thus, like a person wanting to see forms [projects] light. Therefore, it was said, "One perceives the earth *kasiṇa* upward, downward, across."

"Non-dual" (*advayaṃ*) is said here in order to avoid the acceptance of otherness of one. Just as there is water and nothing else in all directions for one who has entered into water, so too, the earth *kasiṇa* is the earth *kasiṇa* only; there is no mixture of it with any other *kasiṇa*. This method applies to all [the other *kasiṇas*].

"Immeasurable" (*appamāṇaṃ*) is said with reference to the immeasurable extent of the spreading of that, that is, the spreading of each of them. For, spreading it with the mind, one spreads it entirely; one does not take a measure, thinking, "This is its beginning, this its middle."

Here, the "consciousness *kasiṇa*" (*viññāṇakasiṇa*) is the consciousness occurring in the space of the removed *kasiṇa*. There, upwardness, downwardness, and acrossness should be understood with respect to the *kasiṇa*, with respect to the space of the removed *kasiṇa* in terms of the *kasiṇa*, and with respect to the consciousness occurring there in terms of the space of the removed *kasiṇa*.

This is a brief explanation (*ayaṃ ettha saṅkhepo*).

But these earth *kasiṇa*s and so on have been spoken of extensively in the *Visuddhimagga* according to the method of meditation subject and cultivation.

Explanation of the decade of unwholesome paths of action

mula_pali:
347. ‘‘Dasa akusalakammapathā – pāṇātipāto, adinnādānaṃ, kāmesumicchācāro, musāvādo, pisuṇā vācā, pharusā vācā, samphappalāpo, abhijjhā, byāpādo, micchādiṭṭhi.

‘‘Dasa kusalakammapathā – pāṇātipātā veramaṇī, adinnādānā veramaṇī, kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇī, musāvādā veramaṇī, pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇī, pharusāya vācāya veramaṇī, samphappalāpā veramaṇī, anabhijjhā, abyāpādo, sammādiṭṭhi.

kusalakammapathā –
mula_english:
“Ten unskillful courses of action ( *akuśalakammapathā*): taking life ( *pāṇātipāto*), taking what is not given (*adinnādānaṃ*), sexual misconduct (*kāmesumicchācāro*), telling lies (*musāvādo*), divisive speech (*pisuṇā vācā*), harsh speech (*pharusā vācā*), idle chatter (*samphappalāpo*), greed (*abhijjhā*), ill will (*byāpādo*), wrong view (*micchādiṭṭhi*).

“Ten skillful courses of action (*kusalakammapathā*): refraining from taking life (*pāṇātipātā veramaṇī*), refraining from taking what is not given (*adinnādānā veramaṇī*), refraining from sexual misconduct (*kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇī*), refraining from telling lies (*musāvādā veramaṇī*), refraining from divisive speech (*pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇī*), refraining from harsh speech (*pharusāya vācāya veramaṇī*), refraining from idle chatter (*samphappalāpā veramaṇī*), non-greed (*anabhijjhā*), non-ill will (*abyāpādo*), right view (*sammādiṭṭhi*).
commentary_pali:
347. Kammapathesu kammāneva sugatiduggatīnaṃ pathabhūtattā kammapathā nāma. Tesu pāṇātipāto adinnādānaṃ musāvādādayo ca cattāro brahmajāle vitthāritā eva. Kāmesumicchācāroti ettha pana kāmesūti methunasamācāresu methunavatthūsu vā. Micchācāroti ekantanindito lāmakācāro. Lakkhaṇato pana asaddhammādhippāyena kāyadvārappavattā agamanīyaṭṭhānavītikkamacetanā kāmesumicchācāro.

Tattha agamanīyaṭṭhānaṃ nāma purisānaṃ tāva māturakkhitā, piturakkhitā, mātāpiturakkhitā, bhāturakkhitā, bhaginirakkhitā, ñātirakkhitā, gottarakkhitā, dhammarakkhitā, sārakkhā, saparidaṇḍāti māturakkhitādayo dasa. Dhanakkītā, chandavāsinī, bhogavāsinī, paṭavāsinī, odapattakinī, obhatacumbaṭā, dāsī ca bhariyā ca, kammakārī ca bhariyā ca, dhajāhaṭā, muhuttikāti etā dhanakkītādayo dasāti vīsati. Itthīsu pana dvinnaṃ sārakkhasaparidaṇḍānaṃ dasannañca dhanakkītādīnanti dvādasannaṃ itthīnaṃ aññe purisā. Idaṃ agamanīyaṭṭhānaṃ nāma. So panesa micchācāro sīlādiguṇarahite agamanīyaṭṭhāne appasāvajjo. Sīlādiguṇasampanne mahāsāvajjo. Tassa cattāro sambhārā agamanīyavatthu, tasmiṃ sevanacittaṃ, sevanappayogo, maggenamaggappaṭipattiadhivāsananti. Eko payogo sāhatthiko eva.

agamanīyaṭṭhānaṃ

Abhijjhāyatīti abhijjhā, parabhaṇḍābhimukhī hutvā tanninnatāya pavattatīti attho. Sā ‘‘aho vata idaṃ mamassā’’ti evaṃ parabhaṇḍābhijjhāyanalakkhaṇā adinnādānaṃ viya appasāvajjā mahāsāvajjā ca. Tassā dve sambhārā parabhaṇḍaṃ, attano pariṇāmanañca. Parabhaṇḍavatthuke hi lobhe uppannepi na tāva kammapathabhedo hoti, yāva ‘‘aho vatīdaṃ mamassā’’ti attano na pariṇāmeti.

abhijjhā,

Hitasukhaṃ byāpādayatīti byāpādo. So paraṃ vināsāya manopadosalakkhaṇo pharusāvācā viya appasāvajjo mahāsāvajjo ca. Tassa dve sambhārā parasatto ca, tassa vināsacintā ca. Parasattavatthuke hi kodhe uppannepi na tāva kammapathabhedo hoti, yāva ‘‘aho vatāyaṃ ucchijjheyya vinasseyyā’’ti tassa vināsaṃ na cinteti.

byāpādo.

Yathābhuccagahaṇābhāvena micchā passatīti micchādiṭṭhi. Sā ‘‘natthi dinna’’ntiādinā nayena viparītadassanalakkhaṇā. Samphappalāpo viya appasāvajjā mahāsāvajjā ca. Apica aniyatā appasāvajjā, niyatā mahāsāvajjā. Tassā dve sambhārā vatthuno ca gahitākāraviparītatā, yathā ca taṃ gaṇhāti, tathābhāvena tassūpaṭṭhānanti.

micchādiṭṭhi.

Imesaṃ pana dasannaṃ akusalakammapathānaṃ dhammato koṭṭhāsato ārammaṇato vedanāto mūlatoti pañcahākārehi vinicchayo veditabbo.

Tattha dhammatoti etesu hi paṭipāṭiyā satta cetanādhammāva honti. Abhijjhādayo tayo cetanāsampayuttā.

dhammato

Koṭṭhāsatoti paṭipāṭiyā satta, micchādiṭṭhi cāti ime aṭṭha kammapathā eva honti, no mūlāni. Abhijjhābyāpādā kammapathā ceva mūlāni ca. Abhijjhā hi mūlaṃ patvā lobho akusalamūlaṃ hoti. Byāpādo doso akusalamūlaṃ hoti.

Koṭṭhāsato

Ārammaṇatoti pāṇātipāto jīvitindriyārammaṇato saṅkhārārammaṇo hoti. Adinnādānaṃ sattārammaṇaṃ vā saṅkhārārammaṇaṃ vā, micchācāro phoṭṭhabbavasena saṅkhārārammaṇo. ‘‘Sattārammaṇo’’tipi eke. Musāvādo sattārammaṇo vā saṅkhārārammaṇo vā, tathā pisuṇavācā. Pharusavācā sattārammaṇāva. Samphappalāpo diṭṭhasutamutaviññātavasena sattārammaṇo vā saṅkhārārammaṇo vā. Tathā abhijjhā. Byāpādo sattārammaṇova. Micchādiṭṭhi tebhūmakadhammavasena saṅkhārārammaṇā.

Ārammaṇato

Vedanātoti pāṇātipāto dukkhavedano hoti. Kiñcāpi hi rājāno coraṃ disvā hasamānāpi ‘‘gacchatha naṃ ghātethā’’ti vadanti, sanniṭṭhāpakacetanā pana dukkhasampayuttāva hoti. Adinnādānaṃ tivedanaṃ. Micchācāro sukhamajjhattavasena dvivedano. Sanniṭṭhāpakacitte pana majjhattavedano na hoti. Musāvādo tivedano. Tathā pisuṇavācā. Pharusavācā dukkhavedanā. Samphappalāpo tivedano. Abhijjhā sukhamajjhattavasena dvivedanā tathā micchādiṭṭhi. Byāpādo dukkhavedano.

Vedanāto

Mūlatoti pāṇātipāto dosamohavasena dvimūlako hoti. Adinnādānaṃ dosamohavasena vā lobhamohavasena vā. Micchācāro lobhamohavasena. Musāvādo dosamohavasena vā lobhamohavasena vā tathā pisuṇavācā samphappalāpo ca. Pharusavācā dosamohavasena. Abhijjhā mohavasena ekamūlā. Tathā byāpādo. Micchādiṭṭhi lobhamohavasena dvimūlāti.

Mūlato

Pāṇātipātā veramaṇiādīni samādānasampattasamucchedavirativasena veditabbāni.

Pāṇātipātā veramaṇi

Dhammato pana etesupi paṭipāṭiyā satta cetanāpi vattanti viratiyopi. Ante tayo cetanāsampayuttāva.

Dhammato

Koṭṭhāsatoti paṭipāṭiyā satta kammapathā eva, no mūlāni. Ante tayo kammapathā ceva mūlāni ca. Anabhijjhā hi mūlaṃ patvā alobho kusalamūlaṃ hoti. Abyāpādo adoso kusalamūlaṃ. Sammādiṭṭhi amoho kusalamūlaṃ.

Koṭṭhāsato

Ārammaṇatoti pāṇātipātādīnaṃ ārammaṇāneva etesaṃ ārammaṇāni. Vītikkamitabbatoyeva hi veramaṇī nāma hoti. Yathā pana nibbānārammaṇo ariyamaggo kilese pajahati, evaṃ jīvitindriyādiārammaṇāpete kammapathā pāṇātipātādīni dussīlyāni pajahantīti veditabbā.

Ārammaṇato

Vedanātoti sabbe sukhavedanā honti majjhattavedanā vā. Kusalaṃ patvā hi dukkhavedanā nāma natthi.

Vedanāto

Mūlatoti paṭipāṭiyā satta ñāṇasampayuttacittena viramantassa alobhaadosaamohavasena timūlāni honti, ñāṇavippayuttacittena viramantassa dvimūlāni. Anabhijjhā ñāṇasampayuttacittena viramantassa dvimūlā, ñāṇavippayuttacittena ekamūlā. Alobho pana attanāva attano mūlaṃ na hoti. Abyāpādepi eseva nayo. Sammādiṭṭhi alobhādosavasena dvimūlā evāti.
